While it demonstrates white matter microstructural changes correlating with fatigue in long COVID patients, it is an observational cross-sectional study without any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Diógenes Diego de Carvalho Bispo; Pedro Renato de Paula Brandão; Danilo Assis Pereira; Fernando Bisinoto Maluf; Bruna Arrais Dias; Hugo Rafael Paranhos; Felipe von Glehn; Augusto César Penalva de Oliveira; Neysa Aparecida Tinoco Regattieri; Lucas Scardua Silva; Clarissa Lin Yasuda; Alexandre Anderson de Sousa Munhoz Soares; Maxime Descoteaux
paper_title: Brain microstructural changes and fatigue after COVID-19

summary: This study evaluates motor fatigue in 29 non-hospitalized post-COVID patients using treadmill walking tests and the FSMC questionnaire. Despite severe subjective fatigue scores, only 2 subjects showed objective motor fatigability, suggesting functional capacity is better preserved than patients perceive.
paper_authors: Christian Weich; Christian Dettmers; Romina Saile; Luise Schleicher; Manfred Vieten; Michael Joebges
paper_title: Prominent Fatigue but No Motor Fatigability in Non-Hospitalized Patients With Post-COVID-Syndrome

summary: This prospective study compared perivascular space (PVS) quantification on 7T MRI between 10 COVID-19 patients and controls to determine if PVS could serve as a biomarker of neuroinflammation. Results showed significantly elevated PVS count and altered white matter volume in COVID-19 patients compared to controls, though no correlation with symptom severity was observed.
paper_authors: Mackenzie T. Langan; Derek A. Smith; Gaurav Verma; Oleksandr Khegai; Sera Saju; Shams Rashid; Daniel Ranti; Matthew Markowitz; Puneet Belani; Nathalie Jette; Brian Mathew; Jonathan Goldstein; Claudia F. E. Kirsch; Laurel S. Morris; Jacqueline H. Becker; Bradley N. Delman; Priti Balchandani
paper_title: Semi-automated Segmentation and Quantification of Perivascular Spaces at 7 Tesla in COVID-19

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluated 77 post-COVID patients using oculomotor, vestibular, reaction time, and cognitive (OVRT-C) testing via eye-tracking to identify objective neural deficits. While demonstrating feasibility of OVRT-C testing for screening neurological deficits post-COVID (88% sensitivity, 98% specificity), the study is purely diagnostic/observational with no treatment intervention tested.
paper_authors: Kelly KM; Anghinah R.; Kullmann A.; Ashmore RC; Synowiec AS; Gibson LC; Manfrinati L.; de Araújo A.; Spera RR; Brucki SMD; Tuma RL; Braverman A.; Kiderman A.
paper_title: Oculomotor, vestibular, reaction time, and cognitive tests as objective measures of neural deficits in patients post COVID-19 infection

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluated vestibular function in 58 patients with persistent vertigo/dizziness 6 months after COVID-19 infection using comprehensive otoneurological assessment and videonystagmography. The findings demonstrate high prevalence of vestibular dysfunction (nystagmus, unilateral weakness, impaired tracking) suggesting COVID-19 can cause inner ear damage and post-infectious neuroinflammation, but the study does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Katarzyna Pazdro-Zastawny; Karolina Dorobisz; Paula Misiak; Anna Kruk-Krzemień; Tomasz Zatoński
paper_title: Vestibular disorders in patients after COVID-19 infection

summary: This study evaluated cognitive deficits in 29 post-acute COVID-19 and post-vaccination syndrome patients and tested the efficacy of phosphatidylcholine and computer-assisted cognitive training for treatment. While all treatment groups showed cognitive improvement with positive trends, no statistically significant differences were found between groups, suggesting possible spontaneous remission of cognitive deficits.
paper_authors: Julian Frederic Hotz; Sophie Kellerberger; Sara Elea Jöchlinger; Iren Danielova; Hanife Temizsoy; Sandra Ötsch; Jürgen Goller; Muhammad Yacob; Udo Zifko
paper_title: Exploring cognitive impairments and the efficacy of phosphatidylcholine and computer-assisted cognitive training in post-acute COVID-19 and post-acute COVID-19 Vaccination Syndrome

summary: A multimodal MRI study comparing 14 long COVID patients with cognitive impairment to 10 healthy controls, measuring blood-brain barrier permeability, brain metabolites, and white matter integrity at 3 and 12 months post-infection. PASC patients showed elevated blood-brain barrier permeability, elevated inflammation markers, reduced glutamate/glutamine levels, and white matter loss, with partial improvement at 12 months.
paper_authors: Joga Chaganti; Govinda Poudel; Lucette Adeline Cysique; Gregory J. Dore; Anthony Kelleher; Gael Matthews; David Darley; Anthony Byrne; David Jakabek; Xin Zhang; Marrissa Lewis; Nikhil Jha; Bruce James Brew
paper_title: Blood brain barrier disruption and glutamatergic excitotoxicity in post-acute sequelae of SARS COV-2 infection cognitive impairment: potential biomarkers and a window into pathogenesis

summary: This cross-sectional study identified two neurocognitive domains in PASC patients using factor analysis: classic memory/concentration symptoms and sensory overload phenomena. The study characterizes symptoms but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Ariadna Sandoval; Mingqi Li; Leonard A. Jason
paper_title: Two neurocognitive domains identified for patients with myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome and post-acute sequelae of COVID-19

summary: This cross-sectional study compared white matter microstructural integrity in 22 recovered COVID-19 patients versus 16 healthy controls using advanced MRI diffusion techniques (DTI, DKI, NODDI). Results showed reduced white matter structural complexity in certain regions of recovered COVID-19 patients, suggesting potential long-term neurological sequelae from COVID-19.
paper_authors: Manxi Yuan; Ruiqi Lu; Yu Liu; Hui Zhu; Hao Wang; Jingzhi Wang; Yang Song; Lei Yang; Mingzhong Xiao
paper_title: White matter changes in recovered COVID-19 patients: insights from DTI, DKI, and NODDI metrics

summary: A bioinformatics study identifying co-expressed genes and molecular mechanisms linking post-COVID-19 and Guillain-Barre syndrome through analysis of GEO datasets and protein-protein interaction networks. The study identifies MMP9, CASP1, and CAMP as potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets but does not test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Jie-Hua Su; Dan-Yu Lin; Xiao-Huan Liu; Jie-Li Zhang; Zhong-Gui Li; En-Xiang Tao; Kai-Xun Huang
paper_title: Identifying potential co-expressed genes and molecular mechanisms linking post-COVID-19 and Guillain-Barre syndrome through neutrophil extracellular trap-related genes

summary: This cross-sectional study examines cerebrovascular reactivity (CVR) differences between 31 older adults with long-COVID and 31 unaffected controls, finding that the long-COVID group showed greater extreme CVR clusters in attention and executive function networks. The study links CVR abnormalities to cognitive symptoms and neuropsychological performance but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Jessica M. Pommy; Alexander Cohen; Amarpreet Mahil; Laura Glass Umfleet; Sara J. Swanson; Malgorzata Franczak; Shawn Obarski; Kelly Ristow; Yang Wang
paper_title: Changes in cerebrovascular reactivity within functional networks in older adults with long-COVID

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed cognitive functioning in 106 outpatients with neuro-PASC, comparing those with and without prior COVID-19 hospitalization. Findings showed subjective cognitive concerns were more pronounced than objective deficits and were primarily associated with fatigue and depression/mood symptoms rather than hospitalization status.
paper_authors: Joshua Cahan; John-Christopher A. Finley; Erica Cotton; Zachary S. Orban; Millenia Jimenez; Sandra Weintraub; Tali Sorets; Igor J. Koralnik
paper_title: Cognitive functioning in patients with neuro-PASC: the role of fatigue, mood, and hospitalization status

summary: This case-control study compared brain structural MRI features between adolescents with long COVID headaches and those with primary headaches, using machine learning to distinguish between the two groups. While it identified distinct gray matter changes associated with long COVID headaches, it is a diagnostic/prognostic study rather than a treatment intervention study.
paper_authors: Minhoe Kim; Sunkyung Sim; Jaeseok Yang; Minchul Kim; Minchul Kim; Minchul Kim
paper_title: Multivariate prediction of long COVID headache in adolescents using gray matter structural MRI features

summary: This cross-sectional study compared neurophysiological and cognitive function between 32 post-COVID-19 patients with persistent hyposmia and 16 controls using EEG/fNIRS during cognitive tasks and olfactory testing. The study found deficits in prefrontal function and olfactory performance in post-COVID patients but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Livio Clemente; Marianna La Rocca; Nicola Quaranta; Lucia Iannuzzi; Eleonora Vecchio; Antonio Brunetti; Eleonora Gentile; Michele Dibattista; Simona Lobasso; Vitoantonio Bevilacqua; Sebastiano Stramaglia; Marina de Tommaso
paper_title: Prefrontal dysfunction in post-COVID-19 hyposmia: an EEG/fNIRS study

summary: This study examines post-exertional malaise (PEM) in Long COVID by comparing self-reported PEM prevalence across cohorts and assessing symptom responses to standardized exercise testing (CPET). While the paper includes Long COVID patients undergoing exercise testing, it does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention—it is a descriptive/comparative assessment study without therapeutic intent or control groups receiving differential treatments.
paper_authors: Stussman B.; Camarillo N.; McCrossin G.; Stockman M.; Norato G.; Vetter CS; Ferrufino A.; Adedamola A.; Grayson N.; Nath A.; Chan L.; Walitt B.; Chin LMK
paper_title: Post-exertional malaise in Long COVID: subjective reporting versus objective assessment

summary: This paper develops machine learning models trained on EEG data to detect PASC/ME using a wearable headband, achieving 93% accuracy with synthetic data augmentation. The study demonstrates a diagnostic tool for identifying PASC but does not evaluate any treatment intervention or therapeutic outcome.
paper_authors: Harit Ahuja; Smriti Badhwar; Heather Edgell; Marin Litoiu; Lauren E. Sergio
paper_title: Machine learning algorithms for detection of visuomotor neural control differences in individuals with PASC and ME

summary: This exploratory cross-sectional study compared EEG neurodynamics during resting state and olfactory stimulation across three groups: severe COVID-19 patients, recovered moderate COVID-19 patients, and healthy controls. The study found differential patterns of cortical rigidity and neurodynamic adaptation in COVID-19 groups but explicitly notes the absence of behavioral or neuropsychological testing limits interpretations of cognitive status.
paper_authors: Mariia Chernykh; Ihor Zyma; Bohdan Vodianyk; Yaroslav Subin; Ivan Seleznov; Anton Popov; Ken Kiyono
paper_title: Comparative EEG study of neurodynamics upon olfactory stimulation in COVID-19 patients

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing memory consolidation and cognitive function in 42 long-COVID patients (with and without anosmia) versus 30 healthy controls. Found that long-COVID patients, particularly those with anosmia, show deficits in consolidation of declarative and procedural memories, suggesting limbic system dysfunction.
paper_authors: Tania Llana; Marta Mendez; Candela Zorzo; Camino Fidalgo; M.-Carmen Juan; Magdalena Mendez-Lopez
paper_title: Anosmia in COVID-19 could be associated with long-term deficits in the consolidation of procedural and verbal declarative memories

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing cortical gray matter volume, thickness, and surface area between 33 COVID-19 patients with neurological symptoms and 33 healthy controls using MRI. Found reduced cortical volume in orbitofrontal, frontal, and cingulate regions in patients, with associations to CSF inflammatory biomarkers, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Gretel Sanabria-Diaz; Manina Maja Etter; Lester Melie-Garcia; Johanna M. Lieb; Marios-Nikos Psychogios; Gregor Hutter; Cristina Granziera
paper_title: Brain cortical alterations in COVID-19 patients with neurological symptoms

summary: This cross-sectional study compared brainstem volumes on 7T MRI between 10 ME/CFS patients, 8 long COVID patients, and 10 healthy controls. Both patient groups showed significantly enlarged brainstem regions (pons, whole brainstem) and correlations with symptom severity (pain, breathing difficulty), but this is observational research without any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Kiran Thapaliya; Sonya Marshall-Gradisnik; Markus Barth; Natalie Eaton-Fitch; Leighton Barnden
paper_title: Brainstem volume changes in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome and long COVID patients

summary: Retrospective analysis of skin biopsy samples from 31 long COVID patients comparing autonomic small fiber density (piloerector and sweat gland innervation) to healthy controls. Findings show significantly reduced nerve fiber density in long COVID patients, providing histological evidence of autonomic small fiber involvement independent of somatic nerve fiber loss.
paper_authors: Pietro Falco; Eleonora Galosi; Daniel Litewczuk; Enrico Evangelisti; Giulia Di Stefano; Lars Arendt-Nielsen; Andrea Truini; Caterina Maria Leone
paper_title: Autonomic small fiber involvement in painful long COVID: a histological and clinical study

summary: This pilot study compares brain connectivity patterns during cognitive tasks between 10 long COVID patients and 13 healthy controls using 7 Tesla fMRI, finding altered connectivity in brainstem and default-mode network regions. The findings suggest brainstem circuit dysfunction may underlie cognitive and autonomic symptoms in long COVID, but the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Leighton Barnden; Kiran Thapaliya; Natalie Eaton-Fitch; Markus Barth; Sonya Marshall-Gradisnik
paper_title: Altered brain connectivity in Long Covid during cognitive exertion: a pilot study

summary: This cross-sectional study examined functional brain connectivity in non-hospitalized adults with post-COVID cognitive complaints using fMRI and neuropsychological testing. The findings showed preserved default mode network connectivity positively correlated with cognitive performance, providing neuroimaging evidence of brain function in individuals recovering from mild COVID.
paper_authors: Derek Madden; Tressie M. Stephens; Jim Scott; Christen O’Neal Swann; Kiana Prather; Jordan Hoffmeister; Lei Ding; Ian F. Dunn; Andrew K. Conner; Han Yuan
paper_title: Functional connectivity of default mode network in non-hospitalized patients with post-COVID cognitive complaints

summary: This pilot study analyzes plasma fatty acid profiles in COVID-19 patients with varying disease severity and examines associations with post-acute sequelae (PASC). The paper reports observational findings linking fatty acid depletion to PASC development but appears to be a registered protocol without intervention or clinical trial results.
paper_authors: Sophia Stromberg; Bridget A. Baxter; Gregory Dooley; Stephanie M. LaVergne; Emily Gallichotte; Taru Dutt; Madison Tipton; Kailey Berry; Jared Haberman; Nicole Natter; Tracy L. Webb; Kim McFann; Marcela Henao-Tamayo; Greg Ebel; Sangeeta Rao; Julie Dunn; Elizabeth P. Ryan
paper_title: Relationships between plasma fatty acids in adults with mild, moderate, or severe COVID-19 and the development of post-acute sequelae

summary: Cross-sectional study measuring serum tryptophan catabolites, inflammatory markers, and insulin resistance in 90 long COVID patients 3-10 months post-infection to identify biomarkers associated with chronic fatigue and affective symptoms. Identified three biomarkers (CRP, KYN/TRY ratio, insulin resistance) that explained ~40% of variance in physio-affective symptoms, suggesting inflammatory dysregulation from acute infection contributes to long COVID pathophysiology.
paper_authors: Hussein Kadhem Al-Hakeim; Anwar Khairi Abed; Shatha Rouf Moustafa; Abbas F. Almulla; Michael Maes
paper_title: Tryptophan catabolites, inflammation, and insulin resistance as determinants of chronic fatigue syndrome and affective symptoms in long COVID

summary: This metabolomics study compares serum metabolite profiles between COVID-19 patients with negative nucleic acid tests and healthy controls, identifying dysregulation in amino acid and lipid metabolism. Although the authors suggest metabolic changes could underlie long COVID pathophysiology, the study is a descriptive cross-sectional analysis with no intervention or treatment being tested.
paper_authors: Wenyu Chen; Ming Yao; Miaomiao Chen; Zhao Ou; Qi Yang; Yanbin He; Ning Zhang; Min Deng; Yuqi Wu; Rongchang Chen; Xiaoli Tan; Ziqing Kong
paper_title: Using an untargeted metabolomics approach to analyze serum metabolites in COVID-19 patients with nucleic acid turning negative

summary: This study describes acute SARS-CoV-2 infection symptoms and persistent symptoms 4-12 weeks post-infection in 2,001 children aged 0-17 years in Beijing. While it characterizes long COVID prevalence and symptom patterns, it is a descriptive observational study without any intervention or treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Jing Li; Jingjing Li; Ling Cao; Lin Wang; Xiaobo Chen; Wenquan Niu; Li Dang; Shuzhi Dai; Ying Wang; Menglei Ge; Weijie Liu; Qinwei Song; Wenjian Xu; Lijuan Ma
paper_title: Clinical manifestations and long-term symptoms associated with SARS-CoV-2 omicron infection in children aged 0–17 years in Beijing: a single-center study

summary: This study evaluates Qimai Feiluoping decoction (QM), a traditional Chinese medicine formula, for treating pulmonary fibrosis in COVID-19 convalescent patients through clinical observation and network pharmacology analysis. The work identifies active compounds in QM and demonstrates that it inhibits fibrosis progression by suppressing the TGF-β/Smad3 pathway and promoting epithelial-mesenchymal transition reversal in cell culture models.

paper_title: Network Pharmacology and Experimental Assessment to Explore the Pharmacological Mechanism of Qimai Feiluoping Decoction Against Pulmonary Fibrosis

summary: This is an in vitro mechanistic study investigating how histamine potentiates SARS-CoV-2 spike protein entry into endothelial cells and how the H2R blocker famotidine can block this effect. While relevant to long COVID pathophysiology, it is a basic science study without patient treatment or clinical outcomes, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: Raghavan S.; Leo MD
paper_title: Histamine Potentiates SARS-CoV-2 Spike Protein Entry Into Endothelial Cells

summary: This is a computational study identifying shared gene signatures between COVID-19 and major depressive disorder using machine learning and bioinformatics. It proposes trichostatin A as a potential therapeutic candidate through molecular docking simulations, but conducts no actual clinical or biological validation of treatment effects.
paper_authors: Shaojun Chen; Yiyuan Luo; Lihua Zhang
paper_title: Identification of gene signatures and potential pharmaceutical candidates linked to COVID-19-related depression based on gene expression profiles

summary: This paper analyzes publicly available data to investigate the effect of SARS-CoV-2 infection on mitochondrial non-coding RNA expression in COVID-19 recovery patients. The study is a secondary analysis of existing datasets examining molecular mechanisms rather than testing an intervention, and constitutes a review of published data rather than original research with patient cohorts.
paper_authors: Andrea Pozzi
paper_title: COVID-19 and Mitochondrial Non-Coding RNAs: New Insights From Published Data

summary: This mechanistic study investigates how adenosine deaminase (ADA1) promotes endothelial inflammation in post-COVID syndrome through in vitro experiments using serum from post-COVID patients and human lung microvascular endothelial cells. The findings identify the ADA1-CD26 interaction as a key pathway in vascular dysfunction, but this is basic research with no patient treatment or intervention tested.

paper_title: Adenosine deaminase mediates endothelial inflammation via an ADA1-CD26 interaction in post-COVID

summary: Experimental study in rats examining histological changes in reproductive tissues and hormone levels after exposure to SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein. While the authors speculate a link to post-COVID hypogonadism, the study is an animal model experiment with no human long COVID participants or treatment evaluation.

paper_title: SARS-CoV-2 Nucleocapsid Protein is Associated With Lower Testosterone Levels: An Experimental Study

summary: This paper develops a deep learning model using contrastive learning to differentiate post-COVID-19 patients from healthy controls and identify subtypes based on lung CT scans. It identifies two distinct post-COVID-19 phenotypes characterized by either small airways disease with air-trapping or airway-associated interstitial fibrotic patterns, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Frank Li; Xuan Zhang; Alejandro P. Comellas; Eric A. Hoffman; Tianbao Yang; Ching-Long Lin
paper_title: Contrastive learning and subtyping of post-COVID-19 lung computed tomography images

summary: This cross-sectional study compares pulmonary diffusing capacity measurements (DLCO and DLNO) between 37 long COVID patients and 37 symptom-free controls to characterize respiratory dysfunction in long COVID. The findings show significantly reduced DLCO, DLNO, pulmonary capillary blood volume, and alveolar volume in the long COVID group, suggesting impaired lung perfusion as a key mechanism.
paper_authors: Jordan K. Parks; Bruce D. Johnson; Meredith G. Shea; Chul-Ho Kim; Jessica I. Johnston; Alex Carlson; Jesse C. Schwartz; Courtney M. Wheatley-Guy
paper_title: Interrogating pulmonary diffusing capacity in long COVID: insights from DLCO and DLNO testing

summary: This cross-sectional study compared cardiorespiratory fitness and running biomechanics between 14 female recreational runners who had recovered from COVID-19 and 14 healthy controls. Results showed that recovered COVID-19 runners had reduced running endurance, increased ground contact time, and weaker propulsion forces compared to controls.
paper_authors: Amir Ali Jafarnezhadgero; Raha Noroozi; Ehsan Fakhri; Urs Granacher; Anderson Souza Oliveira
paper_title: The Impact of COVID-19 and Muscle Fatigue on Cardiorespiratory Fitness and Running Kinetics in Female Recreational Runners

summary: This cross-sectional study examined the association between olfactory dysfunction and quality of life in 58 individuals with post-COVID olfactory symptoms. While it identifies correlations between smell impairment and daily life problems, it is not a treatment trial—it documents impairment without testing any intervention.
paper_authors: Anja L. Winter; Sofie Henecke; Johan N. Lundström; Evelina Thunell
paper_title: Impairment of quality of life due to COVID-19-induced long-term olfactory dysfunction

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluated cognitive and neurological features in 406 COVID-19 patients at ~98 days post-symptom onset using neuropsychological tests and self-reported symptoms. The study found persistent cognitive alterations in 20.7% of patients, particularly in attention and working memory, associated with cardiovascular disease history, persistent fatigue, female sex, age, anxiety, and mental health stress.

paper_title: Neuropsychological measures of post-COVID-19 cognitive status

summary: This cross-sectional study compares maximal fat oxidation and exercise intensity at fat oxidation between endurance-trained and recreationally active subjects with post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection. While the paper addresses long COVID-related exercise intolerance, it is a descriptive physiological comparison without testing any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Andrea Meloni; Roberto Codella; Daniel Gotti; Simone Di Gennaro; Livio Luzi; Luca Filipas
paper_title: Fat oxidation rates and cardiorespiratory responses during exercise in different subject populations with post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection: a comparison with normative percentile values

summary: This observational study evaluated sleep quality via wrist actigraphy and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index in 49 post-COVID-19 patients from the NAUTILUS Project, correlating objective sleep measures with cognitive performance. The study found divergent results between self-reported and objective sleep measures, with a trend toward reduced cognitive performance in those with lower sleep efficiency.
paper_authors: Carnes-Vendrell, Anna; Piñol-Ripoll, Gerard; Targa, Adriano; Tahan, Nuria; Ariza, Mar; Cano, Neus; Segura, Barbara; Junque, Carme; Béjar, Javier; Barrue, Cristian; Nautilus Project Collaborative Group; Garolera, Maite
paper_title: Cognition and objective sleep quality in post-COVID-19 patients

summary: This cross-sectional study compared cardiovascular and autonomic nervous system responses to acute submaximal exercise in 27 individuals: 9 never infected (controls), 9 previously asymptomatic COVID-19 positive, and 9 previously symptomatic COVID-19 positive. Symptomatic COVID-19 survivors showed significantly reduced heart rate variability during exercise compared to controls and asymptomatic individuals, suggesting altered cardiovascular regulation.
paper_authors: Jillian Chan; Hailey Senior; Jessica Homitz; Niamh Cashin; John J. Guers
paper_title: Individuals with a previous symptomatic COVID-19 infection have altered heart rate and blood pressure variability during acute exercise

summary: This structural MRI pilot study examines differences in gray matter thickness and volume in cortical limbic and prefrontal regions between long COVID patients and healthy controls. The study found increased cortical thickness in specific brain regions (cingulate gyrus, middle frontal gyrus) and associations with cognitive and anxiety severity measures, but it is a cross-sectional observational study with no treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Shantanu H. Joshi; Prabha Siddarth; Helen Lavretsky
paper_title: Structural MRI correlates of cognitive and neuropsychiatric symptoms in Long COVID: a pilot study

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed IgG antibody levels and psychological measures in COVID-19 patients approximately 2 months post-diagnosis in Northern Cyprus. While it examines post-infection recovery, it does not focus on persistent long COVID symptoms (which typically manifest weeks to months after acute infection) and does not test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Burc Barin; Banu Elcin Yoldascan; Fatma Savaskan; Goncagul Ozbalikci; Tugce Karaderi; Hüseyin Çakal
paper_title: Joint Investigation of 2-Month Post-diagnosis IgG Antibody Levels and Psychological Measures for Assessing Longer Term Multi-Faceted Recovery Among COVID-19 Cases in Northern Cyprus

summary: This pilot study assessed emotional, cognitive, and somatic concerns in 26 Long COVID patients using neuropsychological screening and the Personality Assessment Inventory. The study found elevated somatic and cognitive concerns in >50% of participants, but is descriptive and non-interventional, providing no treatment outcomes or comparative data.
paper_authors: Sorets TR; Finley JA; LaFrance WC Jr; Patten RV; Mordecai K.; Jimenez M.; Suchy S.; Cahan J.; Koralnik IJ; Cherney LR; Cotton E.
paper_title: Beyond mood screening: a pilot study of emotional, cognitive, and somatic concerns in patients with Long COVID

summary: This study validates the German version of the DSQ-PEM (DePaul Symptom Questionnaire for Post-Exertional Malaise) in a representative general population sample and a clinical post-COVID sample. It demonstrates the instrument's reliability and validity for measuring PEM in German-speaking populations but does not test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Charlotte Kuczyk; Mariel Nöhre; Christoph Herrmann-Lingen; Maike Stolz; Christian Krauth; Elmar Brähler; Leonard A. Jason; Martina de Zwaan
paper_title: Reliability and validity of the German version of the DePaul Symptom Questionnaire Post-Exertional Malaise (DSQ-PEM)

summary: This cross-sectional study examines cognitive dysfunction in 41 long COVID patients using neuropsychological testing, psychiatric assessments, and inflammatory markers. The authors find that cognitive symptoms are more strongly associated with objective neuropsychological impairment than with depression, fatigue, or inflammatory cytokine levels.
paper_authors: Luke S. Watson; Youssef Toubouti; Sarah M. Gray; Núria Guillén; Agnès Pérez-Millan; Lorena Rami; Raquel Sanchez-Valle; Jason K. Johannesen
paper_title: Evaluating contributions of neuropsychological, psychiatric, and inflammatory processes to the expression of cognitive symptoms in post-acute COVID-19 syndrome

summary: A cross-sectional network analysis of 535 COVID-19 survivors 1 year post-hospitalization examining symptom-symptom interactions between mental distress (depression, anxiety, PTSD, sleep disturbance, fatigue) and quality of life. The study identifies key central and bridge symptoms (daytime dysfunction, fatigue) but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Pu Peng; Yaqi Wang; Zhuqing Li; Yanan Zhou; Ji Wang; Miao Qu; Tieqiao Liu
paper_title: A network analysis of the long-term quality of life and mental distress of COVID-19 survivors 1 year after hospital discharge

summary: This feasibility study evaluated an 8-week interprofessional group therapy program for post-COVID patients delivered in both face-to-face and online formats, targeting fatigue, stress intolerance, and symptom management. Among 57 participants (36 online, 21 face-to-face), the intervention was well-accepted and predominantly rated as helpful, with particular value in peer support, though the authors note that controlled studies are needed to formally evaluate efficacy.
paper_authors: Verena Zimmermann-Schlegel; Nadine Gronewold; Sandra Stengel; Mechthild Hartmann; Uta Merle; Hans-Christoph Friederich; Beate Ditzen; Jonas Tesarz
paper_title: Outpatient group therapy for post-COVID patients - a naturalistic feasibility study of a face-to-face and online group concept

summary: This cross-sectional MRI study investigates sex-specific differences in gray matter volume alterations associated with cognitive impairment in long-COVID patients compared to healthy controls. The authors found that cognitive impairment manifests through sex-specific brain structural changes, with females showing more restricted alterations in frontal and limbic regions, while males displayed widespread neocortical involvement.

paper_title: Cognition-associated gray matter volume alterations in long-COVID show sex-specific patterns

summary: This study develops a machine learning model to predict post-COVID-19 syndrome development in 221 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors using pre-discharge and 1-month follow-up clinical data. It identifies early predictors of PCS (75% prevalence at 3 months) but does not test or evaluate a specific intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Oleksii Honchar; Tetiana Ashcheulova; Tetyana Chumachenko; Dmytro Chumachenko; Alla Bobeiko; Viktor Blazhko; Eduard Khodosh; Nataliia Matiash; Tetiana Ambrosova; Nina Herasymchuk; Oksana Kochubiei; Viktoriia Smyrnova
paper_title: A prognostic model and pre-discharge predictors of post-COVID-19 syndrome after hospitalization for SARS-CoV-2 infection

summary: Post-hoc analysis of the COMET-ICE trial examining health-related quality of life and predictors of long COVID development among patients with mild-to-moderate COVID-19. The study identifies acute phase symptom severity and COPD as significant predictors of long COVID but does not test a long COVID treatment.
paper_authors: Heather L. Gelhorn; Parima Ghafoori; Katelyn Cutts; Helen Birch; Yulia Savva; Sacha Satram; Emily Lloyd; Wen-Hung Chen
paper_title: Characterizing health-related quality of life and identifying disease predictors among patients suspected of having long COVID: an analysis of COMET-ICE clinical trial data

summary: This cross-sectional study compared olfactory function, cognitive performance, and neuropsychiatric symptoms in 121 post-COVID patients versus 51 healthy controls. While it found significant cognitive and psychiatric sequelae in post-COVID patients, it is an observational study without any treatment intervention and therefore does not meet criteria for the clinical trials pipeline.

paper_title: Understanding the olfactory role in post-COVID cognitive and neuropsychiatric manifestations

summary: This study validates a German translation of the PAC-19QoL instrument, a quality-of-life measurement tool for long COVID patients. The instrument demonstrates good reliability and validity but this is a validation/psychometric study with no treatment intervention tested.
paper_authors: Srikanth Umakanthan; Mariam Monice; Salona Mehboob; Cheryl Linda Jones; Sam Lawrence
paper_title: RETRACTED: Post-acute (long) COVID-19 quality of life: validation of the German version of (PAC19QoL) instrument

summary: A multicentric cross-sectional study of 2,445 COVID-19 patients across LMICs assessing symptom persistence, depression, and chronic fatigue using validated instruments and deep learning models. Vaccinated individuals showed lower odds of prolonged symptoms and depression, and the study developed a predictive risk calculator for chronic fatigue and prolonged COVID-19 symptoms.
paper_authors: Shaheen, Ahmed; Shaheen, Nour; Long Covid Collaboration Study Group In The LMICs; Shoib, Sheikh; Saeed, Fahimeh; Buhari, Mudathiru; Bharmauria, Vishal; Flouty, Oliver
paper_title: Deep learning analysis of long COVID and vaccine impact in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs): development of a risk calculator in a multicentric study

summary: This paper describes the infrastructure, database, and biobank established at a major Brazilian academic health center to support COVID-19 research, including follow-up assessments of 700 hospitalized patients 6-11 months post-discharge. While it includes longitudinal follow-up of post-COVID patients, it is a descriptive paper about research systems and infrastructure rather than a treatment intervention study, and is excluded as a secondary/infrastructure analysis.

paper_title: Data-driven, cross-disciplinary collaboration: lessons learned at the largest academic health center in Latin America during the COVID-19 pandemic

summary: A cross-sectional analysis of 27,216 Reddit posts documenting long COVID patient experiences and symptom profiles using natural language processing and clustering. Identifies fatigue, pain, and neurological symptoms as most prevalent but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Hanin Ayadi; Charline Bour; Aurélie Fischer; Mohammad Ghoniem; Guy Fagherazzi
paper_title: The Long COVID experience from a patient's perspective: a clustering analysis of 27,216 Reddit posts

summary: The ECHOES dataset links national COVID-19 testing data with electronic health records for 44 million individuals in England to monitor health outcomes following SARS-CoV-2 infection. This is a descriptive epidemiological resource for investigating post-acute COVID-19 health conditions and mortality patterns, not a treatment trial or intervention study.
paper_authors: Hester Allen; Katie Hassell; Christopher Rawlinson; Owen Pullen; Colin Campbell; Annika M. Jödicke; Martí Català; Albert Prats-Uribe; Gavin Dabrera; Daniel Prieto-Alhambra; Ines Campos-Matos
paper_title: Development of the ECHOES national dataset: a resource for monitoring post-acute and long-term COVID-19 health outcomes in England

summary: This study uses machine learning (random forest classification) on longitudinal cohort data from the UK's Understanding Society COVID-19 Study to identify risk factors for long COVID-19. The analysis identifies sociodemographic and health-related predictors including early pandemic infection timing, work hours, age, and financial insecurity, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Rhea Machado; Reshen Soorinarain Dodhy; Atharve Sehgal; Kate Rattigan; Aparna Lalwani; David Waynforth
paper_title: A Machine Learning Approach to Identifying Risk Factors for Long COVID-19

summary: A cross-sectional study evaluating a 12-session physiotherapy protocol in 42 post-COVID-19 patients over 4 weeks. The intervention improved lung function (FEV1 +7.16%, FVC +7.56%), exercise capacity (6-min walk +13%), and reduced post-COVID sequelae by ~50%, with improvements in psychoemotional status and handgrip strength.
paper_authors: Silvia Denise Ponce-Campos; Juan Manuel Díaz; Daniela Moreno-Agundis; Ana Laura González-Delgado; Paulina Andrade-Lozano; Francisco Javier Avelar-González; Eduardo Hernández-Cuellar; Fernando Torres-Flores
paper_title: A Physiotherapy Treatment Plan for Post-COVID-19 Patients That Improves the FEV1, FVC, and 6-Min Walk Values, and Reduces the Sequelae in 12 Sessions

summary: This paper investigates potential autoimmune cross-reactivity of antibodies against the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (N) protein with human self-antigens using Western blot and mass spectrometry in animal models (mice, rabbits, hamsters). The findings highlight differences in anti-N antibody responses across species and provide implications for vaccine design, but do not test or evaluate any treatment intervention in long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Alexandra Rak; Yana Zabrodskaya; Pei-Fong Wong; Irina Isakova-Sivak
paper_title: Antibodies Against SARS-CoV-2 Nucleocapsid Protein Possess Autoimmune Properties

summary: This paper develops a Fuzzy Cognitive Map Decision Support System to model causal relationships between post-COVID syndrome symptoms and recommend specialist referrals for speech-language pathology problems. It uses a systematic review of 19 studies to identify symptom prevalence and demonstrates preliminary validation on four case studies, but does not evaluate an intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Manila Tola; Voula Chris Georgopoulos; Eleftheria Geronikou; Panagiotis Plotas; Chrysostomos Stylios
paper_title: Fuzzy Cognitive Maps for Decision Support in Post-COVID Syndrome with Speech-Language Pathology-Related Problems

summary: In vitro study examining how SARS-CoV-2 PLpro impairs interferon-related genes in epithelial cells and testing hydroxytyrosol as a potential therapeutic agent. This is a basic science mechanistic study with no patient intervention or clinical trial component.
paper_authors: Annalisa Crudele; Antonella Smeriglio; Mariarosaria Ingegneri; Nadia Panera; Marzia Bianchi; Maria Rita Braghini; Anna Pastore; Valeria Tocco; Rita Carsetti; Salvatore Zaffina; Anna Alisi; Domenico Trombetta
paper_title: Hydroxytyrosol Recovers SARS-CoV-2-PLpro-Dependent Impairment of Interferon Related Genes in Polarized Human Airway, Intestinal and Liver Epithelial Cells

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluates the test-retest reliability and minimal detectable change of two exercise tolerance tests (Chester Step Test and 1-Minute Sit-to-Stand) in 42 long COVID patients. While the tests show excellent reliability, this is a methodological validation study without evaluating any intervention outcomes, so it falls outside the treatment trial scope despite being directly relevant to long COVID assessment.
paper_authors: Ana Isabel Sevillano-Castaño; Renata Peroy-Badal; Rodrigo Torres-Castro; Ana María Cañuelo-Márquez; Manuel Rozalén-Bustín; Ángel Modrego-Navarro; Luis De Sousa-De Sousa; Juan José Ramos-Álvarez; José Luis Maté-Muñoz; Pablo García-Fernández
paper_title: Test–Retest Reliability and Minimal Detectable Change in Chester Step Test and 1-Minute Sit-to-Stand Test in Long COVID Patients

summary: This cross-sectional study examined whether genetic variations in antioxidant enzymes (SOD2, GPX, GST, Nrf2, ACE2) are associated with neurological sequelae in long-COVID patients. Specific polymorphisms in GSTP1 and GSTO1 were found to independently or cumulatively affect the risk of developing long-COVID myalgia and brain fog, supporting genetic susceptibility as a factor in long-COVID manifestations.
paper_authors: Marko Ercegovac; Milika Asanin; Ana Savic-Radojevic; Jovan Ranin; Marija Matic; Tatjana Djukic; Vesna Coric; Djurdja Jerotic; Nevena Todorovic; Ivana Milosevic; Goran Stevanovic; Tatjana Simic; Zoran Bukumiric; Marija Pljesa-Ercegovac
paper_title: Antioxidant Genetic Profile Modifies Probability of Developing Neurological Sequelae in Long-COVID

summary: This is a computational/in silico study using molecular dynamics simulations to predict the binding affinity and stability of apigenin and related flavonoids to the Nrf2 pathway as potential therapeutic candidates for long COVID. The study presents only molecular modeling results and predictions with no human participants, clinical trials, or experimental validation of therapeutic efficacy.
paper_authors: Muchtaridi Muchtaridi; Riska Prasetiawati; Siti Ajah Alawiah; Shela Salsabila; Taufik Muhammad Fakih; Rina Fajri Nuwarda; Nur Kusaira Khairul Ikram
paper_title: Revitalizing Recovery: Unveiling the Potential of Apigenin and Related Flavonoids in Long COVID-19 Therapy Through Molecular Dynamics Simulation

summary: This prospective observational study validates an energy level diary tool for fatigue management in post-COVID syndrome patients across two German rehabilitation centers, using a codesign approach with feedback from participants. The diary effectively tracks daily energy fluctuations, correlates with the MFI-20 fatigue scale, and patients rated it as a useful tool for learning pacing strategies and adapting rehabilitation therapies.
paper_authors: Maryam Balke; René Garbsch; Jessica Cormann; Pantea Pape; Frank C. Mooren; Boris Schmitz
paper_title: Design and validation of an energy level diary for fatigue management in patients with post-COVID syndrome

summary: A feasibility pilot study examining how secondary motor and cognitive tasks affect gait in 30 participants across six groups including long COVID patients, using wearable sensors to measure spatiotemporal parameters. The study found the incongruent dual-task condition most sensitive for differentiating clinical groups, with all participants completing the protocol successfully.
paper_authors: Daniela De Bartolo; Liliana Baleca; Domenico De Angelis; Ugo Nocentini; Marco Iosa
paper_title: The Effects of Secondary Motor and Cognitive Tasks on Gait Depend on Functional Walking Ability in Non-Traumatic Neurological Patients: A Feasibility Pilot Study

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluates small airways dysfunction and lung hyperinflation in 33 long COVID patients using pulmonary function tests and nitrogen washout techniques. The study demonstrates associations between small airways impairment and persistent dyspnea but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Angelos Vontetsianos; Nikolaos Chynkiamis; Christina Anagnostopoulou; Christiana Lekka; Stavrina Zaneli; Nektarios Anagnostopoulos; Nikoleta Rovina; Christos F. Kampolis; Andriana I. Papaioannou; Georgios Kaltsakas; Ioannis Vogiatzis; Grigorios Stratakos; Petros Bakakos; Nikolaos Koulouris
paper_title: Small Airways Dysfunction and Lung Hyperinflation in Long COVID-19 Patients as Potential Mechanisms of Persistent Dyspnoea

summary: This paper analyzes 1.2 million tweets about long COVID posted on Twitter between May 2020 and January 2023 using sentiment analysis and text mining techniques. It finds high tweet volume in 2022, mixed sentiment distribution (43% positive, 43% negative, 14% neutral), and that sadness was the most commonly expressed emotion.
paper_authors: Nirmalya Thakur
paper_title: Investigating and Analyzing Self-Reporting of Long COVID on Twitter: Findings from Sentiment Analysis

summary: This exploratory study compared chemosensory event-related potentials (CSERP) in 18 long COVID patients, 12 mild cognitive impairment patients, and 10 healthy controls to investigate shared neurobiological pathways. The study found reduced N1 amplitude and P3 latency abnormalities in long COVID patients, suggesting CSERPs could serve as biomarkers for cognitive and olfactory dysfunction, but does not test or evaluate any intervention.
paper_authors: Sara Invitto; Paolo Boscolo-Rizzo; Francesco Fantin; Domenico Marco Bonifati; Cosimo de Filippis; Enzo Emanuelli; Daniele Frezza; Federico Giopato; Marcella Caggiula; Andrea Schito; Vincenzo Ciccarese; Giacomo Spinato
paper_title: Exploratory Study on Chemosensory Event-Related Potentials in Long COVID-19 and Mild Cognitive Impairment: A Common Pathway?

summary: This paper investigates sesamin's anti-inflammatory and anti-COVID-19 properties through in vitro cell line assays and in silico molecular docking analyses, not through clinical trials or patient treatment. While it mentions long COVID symptoms, it does not test any intervention on actual long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Shu-Ming Huang; Cheng-Yang Hsieh; Jasmine U. Ting; Kathlia A. De Castro-Cruz; Ching-Chiung Wang; Chia-Jung Lee; Po-Wei Tsai
paper_title: Anti-COVID-19, Anti-Inflammatory, and Anti-Osteoarthritis Activities of Sesamin from Sesamum indicum L.

summary: A pilot study examining whether dietary habits and vitamin levels predict long COVID development in mild COVID-19 cases. Found that higher symptom count and fatigue predicted long COVID, while certain nutrients (vitamin E, PUFAs, fiber, iron) were associated with lower symptom severity.
paper_authors: Kaine Moreno McDaid; Mridula Chopra
paper_title: A Pilot Study to Examine If Dietary Habits Can Affect Symptomology in Mild Pre-Vaccination COVID-19 Cases

summary: This cross-sectional immunoassay study investigates the presence of autoantibodies against vagal nucleus proteins in long-COVID patients, vaccinated subjects, and unvaccinated controls. The findings suggest molecular mimicry may contribute to neurovegetative symptoms in long COVID, but the study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Silvestro Ennio D’Anna; Alessandra Maria Vitale; Giuseppa D’Amico; Celeste Caruso Bavisotto; Pasquale Ambrosino; Francesco Cappello; Mauro Maniscalco; Antonella Marino Gammazza
paper_title: Autoimmunity against Nucleus Ambiguous Is Putatively Possible in Both Long-COVID-19 and Vaccinated Subjects: Scientific Evidence and Working Hypothesis

summary: This case-control study compares red blood cell morphology, deformability, and aggregation between 30 long COVID patients and 30 controls to investigate the relationship between RBC abnormalities and fatigue. The study finds that LC patients have higher RBC aggregation, morphological abnormalities, and limited functional capacity to deform, which correlates with fatigue severity, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Marijke Grau; Alena Presche; Anna-Lena Krüger; Wilhelm Bloch; Björn Haiduk
paper_title: Red Blood Cell Morphology Is Associated with Altered Hemorheological Properties and Fatigue in Patients with Long COVID

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed heart rate variability, peripheral body temperature, and serum cytokine levels in 202 long COVID patients (stratified by symptom duration) compared to 95 healthy controls. The findings indicate reduced parasympathetic activation, elevated body temperature, and distinct inflammatory cytokine profiles (elevated IL-17/IL-2, low IL-4) in long COVID, suggesting potential treatment targets.
paper_authors: Pablo Fabiano Moura das Neves; Juarez Antônio Simões Quaresma; Maria Alice Freitas Queiroz; Camilla Costa Silva; Enzo Varela Maia; João Sergio de Sousa Oliveira; Carla Manuela Almeida das Neves; Suellen da Silva Mendonça; Aline Semblano Carreira Falcão; Giovana Salomão Melo; Isabella Boechat Faria Santos; Jorge Rodrigues de Sousa; Eduardo José Melo dos Santos; Pedro Fernando da Costa Vasconcelos; Antonio Carlos Rosário Vallinoto; Luiz Fábio Magno Falcão
paper_title: Imbalance of Peripheral Temperature, Sympathovagal, and Cytokine Profile in Long COVID

summary: This paper investigates the role of toxin-like peptides produced by gut bacteria in long COVID patients, comparing plasma, urine, and fecal samples from COVID-19 and long COVID patients. The study is an in vitro proteomics analysis of bacterial cultures without any intervention or treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Carlo Brogna; Simone Cristoni; Barbara Brogna; Domenico Rocco Bisaccia; Giuliano Marino; Valentina Viduto; Luigi Montano; Marina Piscopo
paper_title: Toxin-like Peptides from the Bacterial Cultures Derived from Gut Microbiome Infected by SARS-CoV-2—New Data for a Possible Role in the Long COVID Pattern

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing fecal microbiome composition and serum cytokine profiles in PASC and ME/CFS patients versus controls, using longitudinal databases and newly collected samples. Findings show significant dysbiosis and altered cytokine expression (elevated MIP-1β, reduced TARC) in PASC patients, with correlations to chronic fatigue symptoms.
paper_authors: Martin Tobi; Diptaraj Chaudhari; Elizabeth P. Ryan; Noreen F. Rossi; Orena Koka; Bridget Baxter; Madison Tipton; Taru S. Dutt; Yosef Tobi; Benita McVicker; Mariana Angoa-Perez
paper_title: Immune Signatures in Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) and Myalgia/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS): Insights from the Fecal Microbiome and Serum Cytokine Profiles

summary: This cross-sectional study examines inflammatory biomarkers and their relationship to depression and cognitive impairment in 101 COVID-19 survivors at one and three months post-infection. While it identifies sex-specific inflammatory pathways associated with neuropsychiatric outcomes, it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Mariagrazia Palladini; Mario Gennaro Mazza; Beatrice Bravi; Margherita Bessi; Maria Cristina Lorenzi; Sara Spadini; Rebecca De Lorenzo; Patrizia Rovere-Querini; Roberto Furlan; Francesco Benedetti
paper_title: Sex-Specific Inflammatory Profiles Affect Neuropsychiatric Issues in COVID-19 Survivors

summary: This paper explores potential therapeutic approaches against long COVID by analyzing blood pH, temperature variations, and molecular interactions using NMR spectroscopy and computational modeling. The work proposes incretin mimetics as potential preventive agents but presents only in silico and in vitro experiments without any clinical trial data or patient outcomes.
paper_authors: Hans-Christian Siebert; Thomas Eckert; Anirban Bhunia; Nele Klatte; Marzieh Mohri; Simone Siebert; Anna Kozarova; John W. paper_title: Blood pH Analysis in Combination with Molecular Medical Tools in Relation to COVID-19 Symptoms

summary: This study compares brain source activity at rest using high-density EEG between 18 post-COVID patients with cognitive deficits/fatigue and 18 healthy controls. The findings show reduced delta activity in executive function regions in post-COVID patients, but this is a diagnostic/mechanistic study without any intervention or treatment being tested.
paper_authors: Paola Ortelli; Angelica Quercia; Antonio Cerasa; Sabrina Dezi; Davide Ferrazzoli; Luca Sebastianelli; Leopold Saltuari; Viviana Versace; Angelo Quartarone
paper_title: Lowered Delta Activity in Post-COVID-19 Patients with Fatigue and Cognitive Impairment

summary: This study investigates kidney pathology in mice infected with mouse hepatitis virus-1 (MHV-1) as a model for long COVID kidney injury, identifying elevated markers of fibrosis and inflammation. The authors test a synthetic peptide (SPIKENET) that reduces several pathogenic markers in the mouse model, suggesting potential therapeutic targets for COVID-associated kidney complications.
paper_authors: Rajalakshmi Ramamoorthy; Hussain Hussain; Natalia Ravelo; Kannappan Sriramajayam; Dibe M. Di Gregorio; Kodisundaram Paulrasu; Pingping Chen; Karen Young; Andrew D. Masciarella; Arumugam R. Jayakumar; Michael J. Paidas
paper_title: Kidney Damage in Long COVID: Studies in Experimental Mice

summary: This cross-sectional study develops a metabolic fingerprinting approach using portable FT-MIR spectroscopy to differentiate long COVID from fibromyalgia based on blood samples. While it identifies distinct metabolic signatures between the two conditions, it is a diagnostic study, not a treatment intervention trial, and thus falls outside the scope of the screening criteria for intervention trials.
paper_authors: Hackshaw KV; Yao S.; Bao H.; de Lamo Castellvi S.; Aziz R.; Nuguri SM; Yu L.; Osuna-Diaz MM; Brode WM; Sebastian KR; Giusti MM; Rodriguez-Saona L.
paper_title: Metabolic Fingerprinting for the Diagnosis of Clinically Similar Long COVID and Fibromyalgia Using a Portable FT-MIR Spectroscopic Combined with Chemometrics

summary: This study investigates abnormal immunological factors in autoimmune disease patients after COVID-19 recovery, comparing 11 patients with various autoimmune diseases and 16 SLE patients. It found increased follicular T helper cells and decreased regulatory T cells post-infection, but this is an observational cross-sectional study with no treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the intervention trials database.
paper_authors: Siyue Yu; Hao Li; Kai Zhang; Gong Cheng; Yifan Wang; Yuan Jia; Linchong Su; Yuebo Jin; Miao Shao; Jing He
paper_title: Aberrant Immune Features after Recovery from COVID-19 in Patients with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus and Other Autoimmune Diseases

summary: This cross-sectional study measured adenine nucleotide levels in red blood cells and endothelial/microvascular function parameters in long COVID patients 12 weeks post-infection. The study found correlations between RBC ATP levels and vascular dysfunction markers but did not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Marzena Romanowska-Kocejko; Agata Jędrzejewska; Alicja Braczko; Klaudia Stawarska; Oliwia Król; Marika Frańczak; Gabriela Harasim; Ryszard T. Smoleński; Marcin Hellmann; Barbara Kutryb-Zając
paper_title: Red Blood Cell Adenylate Energetics Is Related to Endothelial and Microvascular Function in Long COVID

summary: This cross-sectional study compares immune cell profiles and checkpoint expression in post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis (PCPF) patients versus idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and healthy controls. While the paper investigates long COVID sequelae, it is observational and does not evaluate any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for a treatment trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: Sara Gangi; Laura Bergantini; Paolo Cameli; Irene Paggi; Marco Spalletti; Fabrizio Mezzasalma; Elena Bargagli; Miriana d’Alessandro
paper_title: Immunological Similarities and Differences between Post-COVID-19 Lung Sequelae and Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis

summary: This prospective cohort study examined myokine levels (myostatin, agrin, irisin, myonectin) in post-COVID-19 patients undergoing comprehensive rehabilitation and their correlation with rehabilitation duration. Lower irisin and myonectin and higher myostatin levels correlated with longer rehabilitation time, suggesting baseline myokine profiles could predict recovery trajectory.
paper_authors: Alicja Mińko; Agnieszka Turoń-Skrzypińska; Aleksandra Rył; Katarzyna Mańkowska; Aneta Cymbaluk-Płoska; Iwona Rotter
paper_title: The Significance of Selected Myokines in Predicting the Length of Rehabilitation of Patients after COVID-19 Infection

summary: This study uses surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) combined with multivariate analysis to develop classification models that differentiate long COVID from fibromyalgia based on blood metabolite profiles. The research demonstrates the feasibility of identifying spectral biomarkers in blood samples with high accuracy (100% validation performance) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Nuguri SM; Hackshaw KV; Castellvi SL; Wu Y.; Gonzalez CM; Goetzman CM; Schultz ZD; Yu L.; Aziz R.; Osuna-Diaz MM; Sebastian KR; Brode WM; Giusti MM; Rodriguez-Saona L.
paper_title: Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy Combined with Multivariate Analysis for Fingerprinting Clinically Similar Fibromyalgia and Long COVID Syndromes

summary: This proteomics study analyzes plasma samples from 28 COVID-19 patients with and without comorbidities to identify protein signatures and early diagnostic biomarkers. The research identifies alterations in coagulation, complement, and acute-phase response pathways, with potential relevance to long-COVID complications, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Víctor Urbiola-Salvador; Suiane Lima de Souza; Katarzyna Macur; Paulina Czaplewska; Zhi Chen
paper_title: Plasma Proteomics Elucidated a Protein Signature in COVID-19 Patients with Comorbidities and Early-Diagnosis Biomarkers

summary: This study investigates the mechanism by which SARS-CoV-2 spike protein induces α-synuclein aggregation in rodent models and neuronal cell cultures via microglia-mediated inflammation and mitochondrial ROS production. The authors evaluate metformin as a potential therapeutic intervention, finding it suppresses spike protein-induced inflammatory response and α-synucleinopathy in preclinical models.
paper_authors: Moon Han Chang; Jung Hyun Park; Hye Kyung Lee; Ji Young Choi; Young Ho Koh
paper_title: SARS-CoV-2 Spike Protein 1 Causes Aggregation of α-Synuclein via Microglia-Induced Inflammation and Production of Mitochondrial ROS: Potential Therapeutic Applications of Metformin

summary: This paper develops a machine learning clinical decision support system using fuzzy inference engines to predict dyspnea 12 months after acute COVID-19, based on retrospective patient data from the SeguiCovid database. The system is not a treatment trial but rather a diagnostic/predictive tool for identifying long COVID patients at risk of persistent dyspnea.
paper_authors: Manuel Casal-Guisande; Alberto Comesaña-Campos; Marta Núñez-Fernández; María Torres-Durán; Alberto Fernández-Villar
paper_title: Proposal and Definition of an Intelligent Clinical Decision Support System Applied to the Prediction of Dyspnea after 12 Months of an Acute Episode of COVID-19

summary: This cross-sectional study compared DNA methylation levels of the ACE2 promoter in 279 COVID-19 survivors who were hospitalized, stratified by presence or absence of post-COVID-19 pain symptoms. The study found no significant differences in ACE2 promoter methylation between those with and without post-COVID pain, failing to support the DNA methylation hypothesis for post-COVID pain development.
paper_authors: César Fernández-de-las-Peñas; Gema Díaz-Gil; Antonio Gil-Crujera; Stella M. Gómez-Sánchez; Silvia Ambite-Quesada; Anabel Franco-Moreno; Pablo Ryan-Murua; Juan Torres-Macho; Oscar J. Pellicer-Valero; Lars Arendt-Nielsen; Rocco Giordano
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 Pain Is Not Associated with DNA Methylation Levels of the ACE2 Promoter in COVID-19 Survivors Hospitalized Due to SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: This study characterizes new-onset chronic musculoskeletal pain in post-COVID patients and assesses overlap with fibromyalgia syndrome using ACR 2010 criteria. Thirteen of eighteen patients (72.2%) met fibromyalgia criteria, suggesting FMS may develop as a long-term sequela of viral infection.
paper_authors: Omar Khoja; Matthew Mulvey; Sarah Astill; Ai Lyn Tan; Manoj Sivan
paper_title: New-Onset Chronic Musculoskeletal Pain Following COVID-19 Infection Fulfils the Fibromyalgia Clinical Syndrome Criteria: A Preliminary Study

summary: This study examines the effects of CSD peptide LTI-2355 on myeloid cell function in lung tissue from PASC-F patients, demonstrating that LTI-2355 improves phagocytic activity and reduces pro-inflammatory cytokine production. However, this is an in vitro mechanistic study using donor lung explant tissue rather than a clinical trial with human subjects receiving treatment.
paper_authors: Brecht Creyns; BreAnne MacKenzie; Yago Amigo Pinho Jannini Sa; Ana Lucia Coelho; Dale Christensen; Tanyalak Parimon; Brian Windsor; Cory M. Hogaboam
paper_title: Caveolin Scaffolding Domain (CSD) Peptide LTI-2355 Modulates the Phagocytic and Synthetic Activity of Lung-Derived Myeloid Cells in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) and Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID Fibrosis (PASC-F)

summary: This is a preclinical study using hamster and cell line models to investigate the mechanisms of muscle fatigue in long COVID, showing SARS-CoV-2 causes myofiber atrophy and mitochondrial dysfunction without direct viral invasion. The study does not test a treatment intervention on patients; it is mechanistic research in animal and cell models.
paper_authors: Sachiko T. Homma; Xingyu Wang; Justin J. Frere; Adam C. Gower; Jingsong Zhou; Jean K. Lim; Benjamin R. tenOever; Lan Zhou
paper_title: Respiratory SARS-CoV-2 Infection Causes Skeletal Muscle Atrophy and Long-Lasting Energy Metabolism Suppression

summary: Cross-sectional observational study comparing leukocyte telomere length (LTL) and cognitive function in 256 post-COVID-19 subjects versus uninfected controls using MoCA and MMSE scales. Found decreased LTL in post-COVID subjects but no significant association between telomere length and cognitive impairment.
paper_authors: Villar-Juárez GE; Genis-Mendoza AD; Martínez-López JNI; Fresan A.; Tovilla-Zaráte CA; Nolasco-Rosales GA; Juárez-De la Cruz GI; Ramos DR; Villar-Soto M.; Mejía-Ortiz P.; Gómez Mendiola M.; Juárez-Rojop IE; Nicolini H.
paper_title: Exploring the Relationship between Telomere Length and Cognitive Changes in Post-COVID-19 Subjects

summary: This cross-sectional study examines autonomic dysfunction and cardio-respiratory fitness in 192 subjects with post-COVID syndrome, comparing symptomatic and asymptomatic groups. While the paper characterizes autonomic abnormalities and their association with exercise capacity, it is not a treatment trial—it is a descriptive observational study without intervention or treatment evaluation.
