paper_authors: Sophia Hofmann; Marianna Lucio; Gerd Wallukat; Jakob Hoffmanns; Thora Schröder; Franziska Raith; Charlotte Szewczykowski; Adam Skornia; Juergen Rech; Julia Schottenhamml; Thomas Harrer; Marion Ganslmayer; Christian Mardin; Merle Flecks; Petra Lakatos; Bettina Hohberger
paper_title: Functional Autoantibodies Targeting G-Protein-Coupled Receptors and Their Clinical Phenotype in Patients with Long-COVID

summary: Cross-sectional study examining associations between insomnia/depression and cognitive impairments, white matter changes, and serum biomarkers in 76 long COVID patients and 22 controls. Finds demyelination in specific brain regions correlates with insomnia and depression severity, with elevated myelin-specific autoantibodies in the insomnia group.
paper_authors: Marina Khodanovich; Daria Kamaeva; Anna Usova; Valentina Pashkevich; Marina Moshkina; Victoria Obukhovskaya; Nadezhda Kataeva; Anastasia Levina; Yana Tumentceva; Maria Shadrina; Ariuna Ranzaeva; Svetlana Vasilieva; Evgeny Schastnyy; Anna Naumova; Mikhail Svetlik
paper_title: Demyelination and Cognitive Performance in Long COVID Patients with Insomnia and/or Depression

summary: This study measures peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) mitochondrial respiration in COVID-19 patients and correlates these measurements with mortality and long COVID severity at three years post-hospitalization. The research identifies impaired mitochondrial respiration as a potential biomarker associated with COVID severity and long COVID symptoms, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Anne-Laure Charles; Léa Debrut; Walid Oulehri; Véronique Vincent; Héloise Delagreverie; Pauline Asael; Marianne Riou; Margherita Giannini; Alain Meyer; Bernard Geny
paper_title: Impaired Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cell (PBMC) Mitochondrial Respiration Is Associated with Mortality and Long COVID Syndrome Severity in COVID-19 Patients

summary: This cross-sectional study examined T cell dynamics and immune responses in 231 participants across acute COVID-19, convalescent, long COVID, and healthy control groups using flow cytometry and TREC assessment. The findings reveal distinct immune dysregulation in long COVID patients, including increased naïve CTLs, Th2 polarization, and reduced effector memory cells, suggesting ongoing immune dysfunction possibly driven by persistent antigen exposure or autoimmune mechanisms.
paper_authors: Zoia R. Korobova; Natalia A. Arsentieva; Anastasia A. Butenko; Igor V. Kudryavtsev; Artem A. Rubinstein; Anastasia S. Turenko; Yulia V. Ostankova; Ekaterina V. Boeva; Anastasia A. Knizhnikova; Anna O. Norka; Vadim V. Rassokhin; Nikolay A. Belyakov; Areg A. Totolian
paper_title: T Cell Dynamics in COVID-19, Long COVID and Successful Recovery

summary: This is a preclinical mechanistic study in K18-hACE2 transgenic mice investigating how SARS-CoV-2 spike protein S1 induces ferroptosis-related alterations in brain regions relevant to post-COVID neuropsychiatric symptoms. The study does not test any treatment intervention on long COVID patients—it is an exploratory animal model study examining biological pathways, not a clinical or observational trial.
paper_authors: Asmaa Yehia; Chirine Toufaily; Dalia M. Abdel Ghaffar; Gehan El Wakeel; Mohamed Adel; Abeer F. Mostafa; Osama A. Abulseoud
paper_title: SARS-CoV-2 Spike Protein Induces Time-Dependent and Brain-Region-Specific Alterations in Ferroptosis Markers: A Preliminary Study in K18-hACE2 Mice

summary: This study evaluates thermal nociception and inflammatory biomarkers in a female mouse model of post-COVID-19 condition following Omicron variant infection. The results showed only a trend toward lower heat nociceptive thresholds and slight systemic inflammation, with no significant alterations in neural inflammatory markers, suggesting the animal model does not fully reproduce the pain syndromes observed in human long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Eva M. Sánchez-Robles; Carmen Rodríguez-Rivera; Nancy Paniagua Lora; Esperanza Herradón Pliego; Carlos Goicoechea Garcia; Lars Arendt-Nielsen; Cesar Fernández-de-las-Peñas; Visitación López-Miranda
paper_title: Assessment of Nociception and Inflammatory/Tissue Damage Biomarkers in a Post-COVID-19 Animal Model

summary: This pilot study evaluated cardiac and hepatic abnormalities in 97 patients with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (3-11 weeks post-infection) using echocardiography and liver elastography. Approximately one-third of patients showed pulmonary hypertension, diastolic dysfunction, increased liver stiffness and steatosis, with more severe findings in those with prior pulmonary injury.
paper_authors: Felix Bende; Cristina Tudoran; Ioan Sporea; Renata Fofiu; Victor Bâldea; Radu Cotrău; Alina Popescu; Roxana Sirli; Bogdan Silviu Ungureanu; Mariana Tudoran
paper_title: A Multidisciplinary Approach to Evaluate the Presence of Hepatic and Cardiac Abnormalities in Patients with Post-Acute COVID-19 Syndrome—A Pilot Study

summary: This cross-sectional study examined 32 non-hospitalized post-COVID patients to identify cardiopulmonary causes of persistent dyspnea and fatigue through clinical examination, echocardiography, and exercise testing. The study identified chronotropic incompetence in 4 patients (12.5%) but did not test or evaluate any intervention—it was purely diagnostic/observational in nature.
paper_authors: Amaya Jimeno-Almazán; Jesús G. Pallarés; Ángel Buendía-Romero; Alejandro Martínez-Cava; Javier Courel-Ibáñez
paper_title: Chronotropic Incompetence in Non-Hospitalized Patients with Post-COVID-19 Syndrome

summary: This study evaluated a stepwise diagnostic approach for long COVID patients with cardiopulmonary symptoms, examining 231 reconvalescent COVID-19 patients to distinguish between actual organ damage and functional complaints. About 34.6% had suspicious findings on initial screening, with 44.4% of further-tested patients showing pathological findings on cardiopulmonary exercise testing and cardiac MRI, while others had functional long COVID without organ damage.
paper_authors: Johannes Kersten; Michael Baumhardt; Paul Hartveg; Luis Hoyo; Elina Hüll; Armin Imhof; Cornelia Kropf-Sanchen; Nicoleta Nita; Johannes Mörike; Manuel Rattka; Stefanie Andreß; Dominik Scharnbeck; Gerlinde Schmidtke-Schrezenmeier; Marijana Tadic; Alexander Wolf; Wolfgang Rottbauer; Dominik Buckert
paper_title: Long COVID: Distinction between Organ Damage and Deconditioning

summary: This cross-sectional study investigates the relationship between pain extent and sensory, cognitive, and psychological variables in 146 COVID-19 survivors with post-COVID pain. The analysis found that pain extent was not significantly associated with sensitization, cognitive impairment, or psychological distress, though females reported higher pain intensity and anxiety than males.
paper_authors: César Fernández-de-las-Peñas; Stella Fuensalida-Novo; Ricardo Ortega-Santiago; Juan Valera-Calero; Corrado Cescon; Marco Derboni; Vincenzo Giuffrida; Marco Barbero
paper_title: Pain Extent Is Not Associated with Sensory-Associated Symptoms, Cognitive or Psychological Variables in COVID-19 Survivors Suffering from Post-COVID Pain

summary: Retrospective study comparing cardiopulmonary exercise testing and oxidative stress markers in COVID-19 ICU survivors, mild long COVID patients, and obese controls. While it documents exercise limitation in long COVID, it is a descriptive observational study without any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Maurice Joris; Joël Pincemail; Camille Colson; Jean Joris; Doriane Calmes; Etienne Cavalier; Benoit Misset; Julien Guiot; Grégory Minguet; Anne-Françoise Rousseau
paper_title: Exercise Limitation after Critical versus Mild COVID-19 Infection: A Metabolic Perspective

summary: This cross-sectional study characterizes brain fog in 108 long COVID patients through questionnaires, cognitive assessments, and physical performance tests. While providing valuable clinical insights into brain fog as a symptom cluster linked to fatigue, dizziness, and myalgia, it does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Glenn Jennings; Ann Monaghan; Feng Xue; Eoin Duggan; Román Romero-Ortuño
paper_title: Comprehensive Clinical Characterisation of Brain Fog in Adults Reporting Long COVID Symptoms

summary: A retrospective analysis of 39 male long COVID patients examining the prevalence of late-onset hypogonadism (LOH) and its association with clinical symptoms. The study found that 48.7% of male patients met LOH criteria and that low testosterone correlated with increased fatigue, anxiety, cough, and hair loss, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Yukichika Yamamoto; Yuki Otsuka; Naruhiko Sunada; Kazuki Tokumasu; Yasuhiro Nakano; Hiroyuki Honda; Yasue Sakurada; Hideharu Hagiya; Yoshihisa Hanayama; Fumio Otsuka
paper_title: Detection of Male Hypogonadism in Patients with Post COVID-19 Condition

summary: This study objectively assessed physical activity patterns and sedentary behavior in 37 patients 3-6 months after COVID-19 hospitalization. Patients exhibited high levels of sedentary time (9.8 h/day) and moderate physical activity levels, with no significant differences across patient or disease severity subgroups.
paper_authors: Bram M. A. van Bakel; Frederik M. A. van den Heuvel; Jacqueline L. Vos; Hajar Rotbi; Esmée A. Bakker; Robin Nijveldt; Dick H. J. Thijssen; Thijs M. H. Eijsvogels
paper_title: High Levels of Sedentary Time in Patients with COVID-19 after Hospitalisation

summary: This cross-sectional study examined vascular endothelium dysfunction in 22 frail elderly patients recovering from COVID-19 pneumonia (84+ days post-hospitalization) using passive leg movement testing, compared to matched controls. Results show significantly altered blood velocity and femoral blood flow in COVID-19 patients, suggesting vascular dysfunction may contribute to long COVID symptoms including fatigue and exercise intolerance.
paper_authors: Mara Paneroni; Evasio Pasini; Michele Vitacca; Simonetta Scalvini; Laura Comini; Anna Pedrinolla; Massimo Venturelli
paper_title: Altered Vascular Endothelium-Dependent Responsiveness in Frail Elderly Patients Recovering from COVID-19 Pneumonia: Preliminary Evidence

summary: This study examined 154 long COVID patients enrolled in a 7-week rehabilitation program, investigating how post-traumatic stress symptoms (PTSS) and breathlessness interact to affect fatigue severity. Results showed a significant interaction between PTSS and breathlessness in predicting fatigue, with improvements in PTSS associated with fatigue improvement, supporting a biopsychosocial approach to long COVID rehabilitation.
paper_authors: Sari Harenwall; Suzanne Heywood-Everett; Rebecca Henderson; Joanne Smith; Rachel McEnery; Amy R. Bland
paper_title: The Interactive Effects of Post-Traumatic Stress Symptoms and Breathlessness on Fatigue Severity in Post-COVID-19 Syndrome

summary: This study compares immunological profiles across children with acute COVID-19, recovered from COVID-19, and with Long COVID, examining cytokine levels and immune cell subsets. The findings suggest Long COVID patients have impaired adaptive immune responses with reduced regulatory T cells and altered B cell compartments, but the study is observational without any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Danilo Buonsenso; Piero Valentini; Cristina De Rose; Maria Tredicine; Maria del Carmen Pereyra Boza; Chiara Camponeschi; Rosa Morello; Giuseppe Zampino; Anna E. S. Brooks; Mario Rende; Francesco Ria; Maurizio Sanguinetti; Giovanni Delogu; Michela Sali; Gabriele Di Sante
paper_title: Recovering or Persisting: The Immunopathological Features of SARS-CoV-2 Infection in Children

summary: This study validates the hyperventilation provocation test (HPTest) and PETCO2 kinetics as a diagnostic tool for idiopathic hyperventilation syndrome in long-COVID patients. While it identifies a diagnostic threshold with high sensitivity/specificity, it is a diagnostic validation study, not a treatment intervention trial, and does not meet inclusion criteria for the clinical trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: Nathalie Yaël Pauwen; Vitalie Faoro; Françoise Boucharessas; Thierry Colot; Alexis Guillaume; Roger Sergysels; Vincent Ninane
paper_title: Validation Criteria for PETCO2 Kinetics during the Hyperventilation Provocation Test in the Diagnosis of Idiopathic Hyperventilation Syndrome

summary: This cross-sectional study compared endothelial injury markers (CRP, ICAM-1, VCAM-1, E-selectin, syndecan-1) in COVID-19 convalescents versus healthy controls at least 6 months post-infection. The authors found only slight evidence of endothelial dysfunction in generally healthy convalescents without comorbidities.
paper_authors: Paweł Kozłowski; Marcin Śmiarowski; Wiktoria Przyborska; Karolina Zemlik; Milena Małecka-Giełdowska; Aleksandra Leszczyńska; Marzena Garley; Olga Ciepiela
paper_title: Mild-to-Moderate COVID-19 Convalescents May Present Pro-Longed Endothelium Injury

summary: Pilot study validating a free mobile application (RUNZI®) to measure aerobic capacity and endurance in post-COVID-19 patients using the 6-Minute Walking Test. The app showed excellent correlation with conventional 6MWT but no treatment intervention was tested; this is a diagnostic/measurement validation study only.
paper_authors: Roberto Cano-de-la-Cuerda; Carmen Jiménez-Antona; Alberto Melián-Ortiz; Alberto Molero-Sánchez; Ángel Gil-de Miguel; Ángel Lizcano-Álvarez; Valentín Hernández-Barrera; David Varillas-Delgado; Sofía Laguarta-Val
paper_title: Construct Validity and Test–Retest Reliability of a Free Mobile Application to Evaluate Aerobic Capacity and Endurance in Post-COVID-19 Syndrome Patients—A Pilot Study

summary: This study evaluated a 6-week multidisciplinary rehabilitation program (physical training, education, psychotherapy) in 97 long COVID-19 patients. The program significantly improved body composition, dyspnea, fatigue, and physical capacity, with no control group.
paper_authors: Małgorzata Ostrowska; Alicja Rzepka-Cholasińska; Łukasz Pietrzykowski; Piotr Michalski; Agata Kosobucka-Ozdoba; Małgorzata Jasiewicz; Michał Kasprzak; Jacek Kryś; Aldona Kubica
paper_title: Effects of Multidisciplinary Rehabilitation Program in Patients with Long COVID-19: Post-COVID-19 Rehabilitation (PCR SIRIO 8) Study

summary: This cross-sectional study examined 86 long COVID patients and 39 healthy controls to identify biomarkers and immune pathways predicting chronic fatigue, depression, and anxiety symptoms. Results showed that 34.9% of patients had elevated neurotoxicity markers, with immune-inflammatory and oxidative stress pathways explaining 61.6% of symptom variance.
paper_authors: Hussein Kadhem Al-Hakeim; Haneen Tahseen Al-Rubaye; Abbas F. Almulla; Dhurgham Shihab Al-Hadrawi; Michael Maes
paper_title: Chronic Fatigue, Depression and Anxiety Symptoms in Long COVID Are Strongly Predicted by Neuroimmune and Neuro-Oxidative Pathways Which Are Caused by the Inflammation during Acute Infection

summary: Secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial examining minimal clinically important differences (MCID) in inspiratory muscle function variables after an 8-week respiratory muscle training program in long COVID patients. The study establishes MCID thresholds for MIP and IME and demonstrates that MIP has the best discriminative ability for assessing training efficacy.
paper_authors: Tamara del Corral; Raúl Fabero-Garrido; Gustavo Plaza-Manzano; César Fernández-de-las-Peñas; Marcos José Navarro-Santana; Ibai López-de-Uralde-Villanueva
paper_title: Minimal Clinically Important Differences in Inspiratory Muscle Function Variables after a Respiratory Muscle Training Programme in Individuals with Long-Term Post-COVID-19 Symptoms

summary: This cross-sectional study compared oxidative stress biomarkers and mitochondrial regulatory proteins in post-COVID patients with and without long-term pulmonary complications. The study found elevated mitochondrial biomarkers (PINK1, DNM1L, MFN2) and inflammatory cytokines in patients with pulmonary sequelae, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Kamil Siekacz; Anna Kumor-Kisielewska; Joanna Miłkowska-Dymanowska; Małgorzata Pietrusińska; Krystian Bartczak; Sebastian Majewski; Adam Stańczyk; Wojciech Piotrowski; Adam Białas
paper_title: Oxidative Biomarkers Associated with the Pulmonary Manifestation of Post-COVID-19 Complications

summary: This cross-sectional study used cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) to profile elite and recreational athletes with post-exertional malaise (PEM) after COVID-19 infection. The study found that most athletes with PEM did not meet ESC criteria for adequate cardiopulmonary response, with perturbed ventilation/CO2 ratio and O2 pulse plateauing being key markers of exercise limitation, but it is a diagnostic/assessment study with no treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Simon Wernhart; Eberhard Weihe; Matthias Totzeck; Bastian Balcer; Tienush Rassaf; Peter Luedike
paper_title: Cardiopulmonary Profiling of Athletes with Post-Exertional Malaise after COVID-19 Infection—A Single-Center Experience

summary: This study analyzed electronic health records from 92,301 COVID-19 patients to identify predictive factors for PASC diagnoses using a Super Learner algorithm. The researchers developed a composite risk score with moderate discriminatory ability (AUC 0.66) to identify individuals at higher risk for long COVID, but the study does not evaluate a treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Weijia Jin; Wei Hao; Xu Shi; Lars G. Fritsche; Maxwell Salvatore; Andrew J. Admon; Christopher R. Friese; Bhramar Mukherjee
paper_title: Using Multi-Modal Electronic Health Record Data for the Development and Validation of Risk Prediction Models for Long COVID Using the Super Learner Algorithm

summary: This cross-sectional study compares gait and functional mobility (Timed-Up and Go test) between 15 COVID-19 hospitalized patients and 15 healthy controls using inertial motion sensors. COVID-19 survivors showed significantly impaired mobility with 46% longer task completion time, reduced walking speed, and altered gait kinematics despite at least 8 weeks post-discharge recovery.
paper_authors: Mateusz Kowal; Ewa Morgiel; Sławomir Winiarski; Ewa Gieysztor; Marta Madej; Agata Sebastian; Marcin Madziarski; Nicole Wedel; Krzysztof Proc; Katarzyna Madziarska; Piotr Wiland; Małgorzata Paprocka-Borowicz
paper_title: Effect of COVID-19 on Musculoskeletal Performance in Gait and the Timed-Up and Go Test

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed cognitive performance in 25 post-COVID depression (PCD) patients compared to recovered COVID-19 controls and non-infected controls using neuropsychological testing. PCD patients showed gender-dependent cognitive impairment in memory, processing speed, and attention, but the study does not test or evaluate a treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Marina Khodanovich; Anna Naumova; Daria Kamaeva; Victoria Obukhovskaya; Svetlana Vasilieva; Evgeny Schastnyy; Nadezhda Kataeva; Anastasia Levina; Marina Kudabaeva; Valentina Pashkevich; Marina Moshkina; Yana Tumentceva; Mikhail Svetlik
paper_title: Neurocognitive Changes in Patients with Post-COVID Depression

summary: This study uses machine learning on German primary care electronic medical records to predict which COVID-19 patients will develop long COVID based on pre-infection medical history and demographics. It is a retrospective analysis of existing data without any treatment intervention, focusing on risk factor identification rather than treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Roman Kessler; Jos Philipp; Joanna Wilfer; Karel Kostev
paper_title: Predictive Attributes for Developing Long COVID—A Study Using Machine Learning and Real-World Data from Primary Care Physicians in Germany

summary: This cross-sectional study measured serum NGAL levels in 146 COVID-19 patients three months post-infection to identify associations with disease severity and post-COVID symptoms. The authors found elevated NGAL levels associated with acute disease severity, prolonged dyspnea, and metabolic dysfunction, suggesting immune dysregulation persists in post-COVID syndrome.
paper_authors: Karol Żmudka; Alicja Gałeczka-Turkiewicz; Aleksandra Wroniecka; Aleksandra Włosowicz; Barbara Sobala-Szczygieł; Jolanta Mrochem-Kwarciak; Zenon P. Czuba; Jerzy Jaroszewicz
paper_title: Neutrophil Gelatinase-Associated Lipocalin as a Biomarker in Post-Acute COVID-19 Syndrome

summary: This study uses quantitative muscle MRI (qMRI) to evaluate and characterize muscle involvement in various neuromuscular disorders, including post-COVID-19 myalgia, comparing findings across dystrophic, inflammatory, and metabolic myopathies versus healthy controls. qMRI metrics were found to correlate with clinical assessments and show distinct involvement patterns across different disease types, supporting their potential for monitoring neuromuscular conditions.
paper_authors: Lara Schlaffke; Robert Rehmann; Anne-Katrin Güttsches; Matthias Vorgerd; Christine H. Meyer-Frießem; Hubert R. Dinse; Elena Enax-Krumova; Martijn Froeling; Johannes Forsting
paper_title: Evaluation of Neuromuscular Diseases and Complaints by Quantitative Muscle MRI

summary: This study analyzes cytokine profiles in 294 acute COVID-19 and post-COVID patients to identify immune biomarkers associated with disease severity and post-COVID complications. It identifies distinct cytokine signatures that correlate with complications like hypertension and diabetes but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Makhabbat Bekbossynova; Ainur Tauekelova; Aliya Sailybayeva; Samat Kozhakhmetov; Karakoz Mussabay; Laura Chulenbayeva; Alibek Kossumov; Zhanagul Khassenbekova; Elizaveta Vinogradova; Almagul Kushugulova
paper_title: Unraveling Acute and Post-COVID Cytokine Patterns to Anticipate Future Challenges

summary: Cross-sectional study of 144 post-COVID patients examining the relationship between hand grip strength and symptom severity, with 78 meeting ME/CFS criteria. Findings show impaired grip strength correlates with disability and physical dysfunction, particularly in ME/CFS patients, suggesting a common mechanism for muscle fatigue in this subtype.
paper_authors: Anna Paffrath; Laura Kim; Claudia Kedor; Elisa Stein; Rebekka Rust; Helma Freitag; Uta Hoppmann; Leif G. Hanitsch; Judith Bellmann-Strobl; Kirsten Wittke; Carmen Scheibenbogen; Franziska Sotzny
paper_title: Impaired Hand Grip Strength Correlates with Greater Disability and Symptom Severity in Post-COVID Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome

summary: This study measured aminothiol concentrations (cysteine, homocysteine, glutathione) in blood plasma of 212 COVID-19 convalescents using HPLC, stratified by sex, time since infection, and initial severity. While it addresses post-COVID pathophysiology and CVD risk factors, it is a descriptive biomarker study with no intervention or treatment evaluation, making it ineligible for the intervention trials pipeline.
paper_authors: Izabela Szołtysek-Bołdys; Wioleta Zielińska-Danch; Danuta Łoboda; Krzysztof S. Gołba; Beata Sarecka-Hujar
paper_title: Assessment of the Concentrations of Selected Aminothiols in Patients after COVID-19

summary: This cross-sectional study compared organ-dysfunction biomarkers (Lp-PLA2, S100, NGAL, NCAM-1, and others) in 215 mild-to-moderate COVID-19 convalescents versus 79 healthy controls at least 6 months post-infection. The study found lower Lp-PLA2 and NCAM-1 but elevated S100 in convalescents, suggesting low risk of lung fibrosis or chronic kidney disease, and no intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Aleksandra Wiśniewska; Aleksandra Kijak; Karolina Nowak; Michalina Lulek; Agata Skwarek; Milena Małecka-Giełdowska; Marcin Śmiarowski; Szczepan Wąsik; Olga Ciepiela
paper_title: Organ-Dysfunction Markers in Mild-to-Moderate COVID-19 Convalescents

summary: This cross-sectional study compares cardiorespiratory function and exercise capacity in 42 long COVID patients versus 10 healthy controls using echocardiography and cardiopulmonary exercise testing. The study identifies associations between impaired left and right ventricular performance and reduced exercise tolerance, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Angelos Vontetsianos; Nikolaos Chynkiamis; Maria Gounaridi; Christina Anagnostopoulou; Christiana Lekka; Stavroula Zaneli; Nektarios Anagnostopoulos; Evangelos Oikonomou; Manolis Vavuranakis; Nikoletta Rovina; Andriana Papaioannou; Georgios Kaltsakas; Nikolaos Koulouris; Ioannis Vogiatzis
paper_title: Exercise Intolerance Is Associated with Cardiovascular Dysfunction in Long COVID-19 Syndrome

summary: This cross-sectional study compared brain myelination using MRI in 25 post-COVID depression patients versus 38 COVID-recovered controls without depression at ~13.5 months post-infection. The study identified extensive demyelination in white and grey matter structures in depressed patients, with inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus demyelination as a key biomarker for post-COVID depression.
paper_authors: Marina Khodanovich; Mikhail Svetlik; Daria Kamaeva; Anna Usova; Marina Kudabaeva; Tatyana Anan’ina; Irina Vasserlauf; Valentina Pashkevich; Marina Moshkina; Victoria Obukhovskaya; Nadezhda Kataeva; Anastasia Levina; Yana Tumentceva; Svetlana Vasilieva; Evgeny Schastnyy; Anna Naumova
paper_title: Demyelination in Patients with POST-COVID Depression

summary: Prospective controlled study comparing metabolic inflammation, long COVID, and systemic lupus erythematosus across 272 adults with varying BMI to identify differential diagnostic tools and inflammatory markers. Findings show BMI-dependent effects on inflammatory variables and mental health quality of life, but the study is observational/cross-sectional without testing any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Chero-Sandoval L.; Martínez-Urbistondo M.; Cuevas-Sierra A.; Higuera-Gómez A.; Martin-Domenech E.; Castejón R.; Mellor-Pita S.; Moreno-Torres V.; Ramos-Lopez O.; de Luis D.; Vargas JA; Martínez JA
paper_title: Comparison of Metabolic Syndrome, Autoimmune and Viral Distinctive Inflammatory Related Conditions as Affected by Body Mass Index

summary: This cross-sectional study analyzes blood samples from 97 post-COVID syndrome patients to investigate hypercoagulability and endothelial dysfunction through thrombin generation and von Willebrand factor/ADAMTS13 measurements. The study found elevated thrombin production and abnormal coagulation markers in a subset of patients, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Maxim Muys; Anne Demulder; Tatiana Besse-Hammer; Nathalie Ghorra; Laurence Rozen
paper_title: Exploring Hypercoagulability in Post-COVID Syndrome (PCS): An Attempt at Unraveling the Endothelial Dysfunction

summary: This cross-sectional study compares brain MRI findings between 23 post-COVID patients and 20 controls, using vessel wall imaging (VWI) and complementary MRI methods to assess neurological changes. The authors identified several radiological abnormalities in post-COVID patients including white matter changes, vessel thickening, and hippocampal/cortical atrophy, but this is a diagnostic imaging study with no intervention or treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Jakub Okrzeja; Maciej Alimowski; Adam Garkowski; Marcin Hładuński; Bożena Kubas; Justyna Adamczuk; Piotr Czupryna; Karolina Narejko; Anna Moniuszko-Malinowska
paper_title: Assessment of Post-COVID-19 Changes in Brain—Clinical and Imaging Evaluation Using MRI Vessel Wall Imaging and Complementary MRI Methods

summary: This study examines reduced salivary gustin and statherin levels in long COVID patients with impaired taste dysfunction, comparing unstimulated whole saliva samples from long COVID cohort to pre-2019 controls. The research identifies salivary gustin as a potential biomarker for taste impairment but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Harika Chowdary; Naomi Riley; Parul Patel; Ana G. Gossweiler; Cordelia A. Running; Mythily Srinivasan
paper_title: Reduced Salivary Gustin and Statherin in Long-COVID Cohort with Impaired Bitter Taste

summary: This cross-sectional study from the Nautilus Project examines personality traits and sleep quality in 599 post-COVID patients versus healthy controls, finding that neuroticism correlates with poor sleep quality more strongly in PCC patients. However, this is a secondary analysis of data from existing clinical trials (NCT05307549 and NCT05307575) rather than a primary treatment trial, and it does not test or evaluate an intervention.
paper_authors: Anna Carnes-Vendrell; Gerard Piñol-Ripoll; Mar Ariza; Neus Cano; Barbara Segura; Carme Junque; Javier Béjar; Cristian Barrue; Maite Garolera
paper_title: Can Personality Traits Affect Sleep Quality in Post-COVID-19 Patients?

summary: This cross-sectional study examines the immunocytological profile of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid in 58 post-COVID patients with new-onset interstitial lung disease to identify biomarkers predictive of persistent lung disease. The authors found that elevated neutrophil counts, Th17 cell markers, and IL-8 levels are associated with worse prognosis in persistent PCS.
paper_authors: Justyna Dolna-Michno; Piotr Kopiński; Grzegorz Przybylski; Ewa Wypasek; Magdalena Szymańska; Ewelina Wędrowska; Klaudia Mikołajczyk; Tomasz Senderek; Maciej Gagat
paper_title: Cytoimmunological Profile of Lower Airways in Post-COVID-19 Syndrome (PCS): Predictive Value of Bronchoalveolar Lavage

summary: An exploratory pre-post study of 17 women with long COVID evaluated the effects of a 12-week non-aerobic motor control exercise program on body composition and fatigue. The intervention significantly reduced body fat and fatigue, improved pain perception, and increased physical activity, supporting structured exercise as part of long COVID rehabilitation.
paper_authors: María Miana; César Moreta-Fuentes; Ricardo Moreta-Fuentes; David Varillas-Delgado; Carmen Jiménez-Antona; Sofía Laguarta-Val
paper_title: Clinical Improvements Following a Non-Aerobic Therapeutic Exercise in Women with Long COVID

summary: This case-control study compares serum spike protein levels in 72 ME/CFS patients, 49 PCS patients without ME/CFS, and 69 controls (both pre-pandemic and post-COVID recovered) 4-31 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study evaluates immunoglobulin depletion as a potential treatment in 22 patients and finds that while spike protein is detectable in some patients, it does not correlate with ME/CFS severity or functional disability.
paper_authors: Annick Fehrer; Franziska Sotzny; Laura Kim; Claudia Kedor; Helma Freitag; Cornelia Heindrich; Patricia Grabowski; Nina Babel; Carmen Scheibenbogen; Kirsten Wittke
paper_title: Serum Spike Protein Persistence Post COVID Is Not Associated with ME/CFS

summary: An 8-week unsupervised pulmonary rehabilitation program for 20 COVID-19 recovering patients, evaluating changes in cardiopulmonary function, exercise capacity, and body composition. The program significantly improved hemodynamic parameters, oxygen saturation, 6-minute walk distance, VO2 uptake, body composition, and sleep quality.
paper_authors: Vasileios T. Stavrou; Konstantinos N. Tourlakopoulos; George D. Vavougios; Eirini Papayianni; Katerina Kiribesi; Stavros Maggoutas; Konstantinos Nikolaidis; Evangelos C. Fradelos; Ilias Dimeas; Zoe Daniil; Konstantinos I. Gourgoulianis; Stylianos Boutlas
paper_title: Eight Weeks Unsupervised Pulmonary Rehabilitation in Previously Hospitalized of SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: This economic modeling study estimates the workplace burden of COVID-19 including long COVID cases in the US and evaluates the health and economic benefits of workplace COVID-19 vaccination programs. While it addresses long COVID as a cost component in disease burden calculations, it is not a treatment trial but rather a health economic analysis of vaccination as a prevention strategy.
paper_authors: Ekkehard Beck; Keya Joshi; Darshan Mehta; Stephane Lorenc; Bishoy Rizkalla; Nicolas Van de Velde
paper_title: Workplace Vaccination Against COVID-19 and Seasonal Influenza in the United States: A Modeling-Based Estimation of the Health and Economic Benefits for Employers and Employees
paper_journal: Journal of Market Access & Health Policy

summary: This study used machine learning algorithms to predict rehabilitation outcomes in 189 convalescent COVID-19 patients undergoing pulmonary rehabilitation, with 6-minute walking test performance as the primary outcome. A random forest model achieved 83.7% accuracy in predicting three classes of rehabilitation improvement (low, medium, high).
paper_authors: Sarah Adamo; Pasquale Ambrosino; Carlo Ricciardi; Mariasofia Accardo; Marco Mosella; Mario Cesarelli; Giovanni d’Addio; Mauro Maniscalco
paper_title: A Machine Learning Approach to Predict the Rehabilitation Outcome in Convalescent COVID-19 Patients

summary: This study compared pulmonary and cardiac function in patients with post-mild COVID-19 dyspnea to those with moderate/severe COVID-19 and unexplained dyspnea using exercise testing and imaging. The findings show that mild post-COVID dyspnea patients had normal cardiopulmonary exercise test results similar to controls, suggesting mechanisms other than physiologic limitation.
paper_authors: Yaniv Dotan; Elite Weiner; Merav Zucker-Toledano; Anna Solomonov; Eyal Fuchs; Hanna Dawood; Elad Mor; Moneera Hanna; Rihan Naser-Aldeen; Lea Bentur; Ronen Bar-Yoseph
paper_title: Functional Capacity in Patients Who Recovered from Mild COVID-19 with Exertional Dyspnea

summary: Cross-sectional assessment of 1,588 post-COVID-19 patients examining the relationship between persistent symptoms and suicide risk using standardized psychiatric interviews. Found that greater physical complaints and psychopathology during post-COVID syndrome were associated with elevated suicide risk, with psychotherapy suggested as a potential risk reduction strategy.
paper_authors: Alessio Simonetti; Evelina Bernardi; Delfina Janiri; Marianna Mazza; Silvia Montanari; Antonello Catinari; Beatrice Terenzi; Matteo Tosato; Vincenzo Galluzzo; Francesca Ciciarello; Francesco Landi; Gabriele Sani
paper_title: Suicide Risk in Post-COVID-19 Syndrome

summary: This study evaluated clinical features and paraclinical findings in 106 post-COVID-19 patients with pneumonia, with 26 patients enrolled in a pulmonary rehabilitation program. After 2 weeks of rehabilitation, approximately 50% of patients showed improvement in instrumental activities of daily living (eating, washing, dressing), demonstrating the impact of structured rehabilitation on functional recovery in long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Paraschiva A. Postolache; Alexandru Nechifor; Ioana Buculei; Ioana Soare; Horia Mocanu; Florin Dumitru Petrariu
paper_title: Clinical Features and Paraclinical Findings in Patients with SARS CoV-2 Pneumonia and the Impact of Pulmonary Rehabilitation on the Instrumental Activities of Daily Living in POST-COVID-19 Patients

summary: This study evaluated a 14-day complex rehabilitation program in 39 post-COVID-19 patients, measuring clinical symptoms, laboratory biomarkers, and gut microbiota composition before and after the intervention. The program improved respiratory function and mood, though certain inflammatory markers and gut dysbiosis remained abnormal compared to healthy controls, suggesting personalized rehabilitation approaches may be needed.
paper_authors: Ekaterina Sorokina; Alisa Pautova; Oleg Fatuev; Vladislav Zakharchenko; Alexander Onufrievich; Andrey Grechko; Natalia Beloborodova; Ekaterina Chernevskaya
paper_title: Promising Markers of Inflammatory and Gut Dysbiosis in Patients with Post-COVID-19 Syndrome

summary: This study investigates sleep patterns in pediatric post-COVID-19 patients using EEG recordings and parent-reported sleep quality questionnaires. The analysis focuses on sleep spindles in NREM2 sleep, comparing recordings within three months after infection to pre-infection baseline data; preliminary findings suggest increased slow spindle components in right-frontal leads.
paper_authors: Paolo Di Bella; Anna Gaia Attardi; Ambra Butera; Arianna Mancini; Nunzia Calabrò; Elisa Giuseppa Lo Re; Giuseppe Trimarchi; Antonio Gennaro Nicotera; Gabriella Di Rosa; Daniela Lo Giudice
paper_title: Semi-Automatic Analysis of Specific Electroencephalographic Patterns during NREM2 Sleep in a Pediatric Population after SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: A genetic association study examining SNP variants linked to COVID-19 outcomes and their association with neurological complications and long-term post-COVID symptoms in young adults. The study is observational (cross-sectional) and does not test any treatment or intervention, making it ineligible for the treatment trial screening pipeline.
paper_authors: Anastasiya Kazantseva; Renata Enikeeva; Zalina Takhirova; Yuliya Davydova; Rustam Mustafin; Sergey Malykh; Alexandra Karunas; Alexander Kanapin; Elza Khusnutdinova
paper_title: Host Genetic Variants Linked to COVID-19 Neurological Complications and Susceptibility in Young Adults—A Preliminary Analysis

summary: This cross-sectional study investigates biological predictors and risk factors in post-COVID-19 syndrome among asthmatic patients with various comorbidities. The findings show elevated serum glucose, lactate dehydrogenase, and C-reactive protein in moderate-to-severe COVID-19 cases, with ALT activity and age identified as key variables distinguishing comorbidity profiles.
paper_authors: Oana Elena Melinte; Daniela Robu Popa; Mona Elisabeta Dobrin; Andrei Tudor Cernomaz; Cristina Grigorescu; Alexandra Floriana Nemes; Adina Catinca Gradinaru; Cristina Vicol; Doina Adina Todea; Damiana Maria Vulturar; Ionel Bogdan Cioroiu; Antigona Carmen Trofor
paper_title: Assessment of Some Risk Factors and Biological Predictors in the Post COVID-19 Syndrome in Asthmatic Patients

summary: This cross-sectional study investigated associations between vitamin D receptor (VDR) genetic variants (ApaI, FokI, TaqI) and COVID-19 severity and long-COVID symptoms in 100 Jordanian patients. The study found significant associations between VDR TaqI polymorphisms and persistent fatigue, muscle pain, and shortness of breath lasting >4 weeks post-infection, but no intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Ghayda’ Alhammadin; Yazun Jarrar; Abdalla Madani; Su-Jun Lee
paper_title: Exploring the Influence of VDR Genetic Variants TaqI, ApaI, and FokI on COVID-19 Severity and Long-COVID-19 Symptoms

summary: This study examines SARS-CoV-2 presence in endothelial tissue and alterations in PROS1 plasma levels in COVID-19 patients with coagulopathies, comparing infected and non-infected cohorts. While mechanistic research relevant to long COVID complications, this is a descriptive pathophysiology study examining biomarkers rather than evaluating a treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Marcello Baroni; Silvia Beltrami; Giovanna Schiuma; Paolo Ferraresi; Sabrina Rizzo; Angelina Passaro; Juana Maria Sanz Molina; Roberta Rizzo; Dario Di Luca; Daria Bortolotti
paper_title: In Situ Endothelial SARS-CoV-2 Presence and PROS1 Plasma Levels Alteration in SARS-CoV-2-Associated Coagulopathies

summary: This cross-sectional study measured lung gas transfer (DLNO-DLCO) in 118 post-COVID-19 patients (4.6 months post-infection) and 28 healthy controls to characterize alveolo-capillary gas exchange disturbances. Patients across all severity groups showed impaired pulmonary diffusion capacity, reduced membrane conductance, and abnormal vascular capacitance, indicating persistent lung dysfunction in long COVID.
paper_authors: Thông Hua-Huy; Hà Pham-Ngoc; Frédérique Aubourg; Christine Lorut; Nicolas Roche; Anh Tuan Dinh-Xuan
paper_title: Deciphering Alveolo-Capillary Gas Transfer Disturbances in Patients Recovering from COVID-19 Lung Disease

summary: This study analyzes whole-genome sequencing data from 153 patients with persistent COVID-19-related olfactory dysfunction to identify genetic factors associated with olfactory performance. The research found that ACE2 gene variants correlate with worse olfactory function, while IFI44 and NDUFAF4 variants correlate with better function, suggesting host genetic factors influence post-COVID olfactory dysfunction heterogeneity.
paper_authors: Beatrice Spedicati; Alessandro Pecori; Maria Pina Concas; Aurora Santin; Romina Ruberto; Giuseppe Giovanni Nardone; Andrea D’Alessandro; Giancarlo Tirelli; Paolo Boscolo-Rizzo; Giorgia Girotto
paper_title: Scent of COVID-19: Whole-Genome Sequencing Analysis Reveals the Role of ACE2, IFI44, and NDUFAF4 in Long-Lasting Olfactory Dysfunction

summary: This study evaluates laboratory diagnostic tests (complete blood count, ESR, biochemical markers, neutrophil/lymphocyte ratio) in 182 patients with COVID-19 and post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCI) to compare diagnostic performance and identify risk factors. The study does not test any intervention or treatment, making it an observational diagnostic study rather than a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Daniela Robu Popa; Oana Elena Melinte; Mona-Elisabeta Dobrin; Andrei Tudor Cernomaz; Cristina Grigorescu; Alexandra Floriana Nemes; Doina Adina Todea; Damiana Maria Vulturar; Ionela Alina Grosu-Creangă; Tiberiu Lunguleac; Antigona Carmen Trofor
paper_title: Laboratory Diagnostics Accuracy for COVID-19 versus Post-COVID-19 Syndrome in Lung Disease Patients with Multimorbidity

summary: This study evaluated diaphragm muscle function in 46 post-COVID-19 patients undergoing pulmonary rehabilitation using ultrasonography and functional assessments. While it identified significant diaphragm atrophy (69.5%) and paralysis (6.5%) associated with exercise intolerance, it is a descriptive cross-sectional study without an intervention or control group, making it observational rather than a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Janusz Kocjan; Mateusz Rydel; Jan Szczegielniak; Katarzyna Bogacz; Mariusz Adamek
paper_title: Diaphragm Muscle Atrophy Contributes to Low Physical Capacity in COVID-19 Survivors

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed olfactory and taste dysfunction in 81 post-COVID patients using standardized tests (Sniffin' Sticks and Taste Strip). The results showed that post-COVID olfactory dysfunction was predominantly peripheral rather than central, but the paper describes the problem rather than testing a treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Malgorzata Buksinska; Piotr Henryk Skarzynski; Danuta Raj-Koziak; Elzbieta Gos; Malgorzata Talarek
paper_title: Persistent Olfactory and Taste Dysfunction after COVID-19

summary: This study compared cognitive function (verbal working memory, divided attention, response inhibition) in 107 young adults across three groups: COVID-19-negative controls, COVID-19-recovered without PCC, and those with Post COVID-19 Condition. The PCC group showed significantly impaired cognitive performance and increased reaction times, indicating long-lasting cognitive slowing and dysfunction two years post-infection.
paper_authors: Johanna Takács; Darina Deák; Beáta Seregély; Akos Koller
paper_title: Cognitive Slowing, Dysfunction in Verbal Working Memory, Divided Attention and Response Inhibition in Post COVID-19 Condition in Young Adults

summary: In vitro study using COVID-19 pseudovirus-infected cell model to simulate long COVID pathology, demonstrating ferrous ion accumulation and mitochondrial dysfunction. Tests nutritional interventions (lactoferrin, Q10, Echinacea purpurea extract) to reduce iron accumulation and oxidative stress in infected cells.
paper_authors: Bo-Kai Chen; Chi-Ho Chan; Chin-Kun Wang
paper_title: Improvement on Ferrous Ion Accumulation and Mitochondrial Dysfunction in the COVID-19 Pseudovirus-Infected Cell Model Simulating the Long COVID Status by Nutritional Strategy

summary: This paper proposes a path module correlation coefficient to analyze the correlation between SARS-CoV-2 infection and long-COVID symptom manifestation using statistical analysis of gene networks. It identifies potential COVID-related genes like CTSC that may induce long-COVID symptoms but does not study any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Ziqi Liu; Ziqiao Yin; Zhilong Mi; Binghui Guo
paper_title: Long-COVID Inducement Mechanism Based on the Path Module Correlation Coefficient

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between different levels and domains of physical activity and mental health outcomes (anxiety, depression, stress) in individuals who recovered from COVID-19. While the paper touches on post-COVID recovery, it is primarily an observational assessment of PA-mental health associations rather than a treatment trial—participants' activity levels were measured, not assigned.
paper_authors: Miloš Stamenković; Saša Pantelić; Saša Bubanj; Bojan Bjelica; Nikola Aksović; Ovidiu Galeru; Tatiana-Nela Balint; Alina-Mihaela Cristuță; Carmina-Mihaela Gorgan; Tatiana Dobrescu
paper_title: Physical Activity and Mental Health After COVID-19: The Role of Levels and Domains of Physical Activity

summary: This ex vivo study evaluates the effects of fucoidan, a marine polysaccharide with anti-inflammatory and immune-enhancing properties, on mitochondrial membrane potential in peripheral blood mononuclear cells from COVID-19 patients and recovered subjects. Findings show that SARS-CoV-2 infection induces mitochondrial dysfunction persisting 11 months post-infection, and fucoidan treatment promotes recovery of mitochondrial membrane potential in recovered subjects, suggesting potential therapeutic value for long-term COVID-19 sequelae.
paper_authors: Karina Janice Guadalupe Díaz-Resendiz; Carlos Eduardo Covantes-Rosales; Alma Betsaida Benítez-Trinidad; Migdalia Sarahy Navidad-Murrieta; Francisco Fabian Razura-Carmona; Christian Daniel Carrillo-Cruz; Edwin Jaime Frias-Delgadillo; Daniela Alejandra Pérez-Díaz; Matxil Violeta Díaz-Benavides; Mercedes Zambrano-Soria; Guadalupe Herminia Ventura-Ramón; Aurelio Romero-Castro; David Alam-Escamilla; Manuel Iván Girón-Pérez
paper_title: Effect of Fucoidan on the Mitochondrial Membrane Potential (ΔΨm) of Leukocytes from Patients with Active COVID-19 and Subjects That Recovered from SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: This paper develops a qualitative phenomenological mathematical model exploring how vitamin D supplementation and degradation affect innate immune system response to SARS-CoV-2. The study identifies hysteretic phenomena when vitamin D influx is too low as potentially related to long COVID onset, but conducts no empirical treatment study or clinical trial.
paper_authors: Deborah Lacitignola; Fasma Diele; Carmela Marangi; Angela Monti; Teresa Serini; Simonetta Vernocchi
paper_title: Effects of Vitamin D Supplementation and Degradation on the Innate Immune System Response: Insights on SARS-CoV-2

summary: This study compares cardiac autonomic function via heart rate variability (HRV) in 37 COVID-19 recovered individuals versus 37 healthy controls at rest and during a 6-minute walk test. It identifies significant differences in HRV measures between groups and after exercise, suggesting HRV analysis could monitor post-COVID cardiovascular recovery, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Sakshi Garg; Preeti Saini; Moattar Raza Rizvi; Fuzail Ahmad; Mohammed AlTaweel; Zia Ul Sabah; Humayoun K. Durrani; Shatha A. Almasswary; Mohamed K. Seyam; Ankita Sharma; Irshad Ahmad; Sara Al Marzoogi; Mohammad A. Shaphe; Shadab Uddin; Irshad Ahmad
paper_title: The Cardiac Comeback-Beating Stronger: Exploring the Remarkable Resilience of the Heart in COVID-19 Recovery through Cardiac Autonomic Analysis

summary: Retrospective study examining serum IgE, immunoglobulin levels, and mast cell infiltration in 21 severe COVID-19 patients and 30 autopsies, finding elevated IgE and mast cell accumulation suggesting IgE-driven allergic mechanisms. While the study includes long COVID patients and discusses post-COVID immune dysregulation, it is a passive observational analysis without any intervention or treatment evaluation, so it does not meet the criteria for the intervention trials pipeline.
paper_authors: Sylvia Genova; Mina Pencheva; Hasan Burnusuzov; Martina Bozhkova; Georgi Kulinski; Stefka Kostyaneva; Eduard Tilkiyan; Tsvetana Abadjieva
paper_title: High Free IgE and Mast Cell Activation in Long COVID: Mechanisms of Persistent Immune Dysregulation

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence and predictors of dizziness and hearing loss in 209 long COVID patients. Found dizziness in 26% and hearing loss in 15.3% of participants, with female sex, fatigue severity, and acute neurological symptoms as significant predictors.
paper_authors: Faten S. Obeidat; Alia A. Alghwiri; Susan L. Whitney
paper_title: Predictors of Dizziness and Hearing Disorders in People with Long COVID

summary: This study compares orthostatic symptoms, hemodynamic responses to head-up tilt, and cerebral blood flow reductions in long-haul COVID-19 patients versus ME/CFS patients and healthy controls. It is a descriptive cross-sectional comparison study with no treatment intervention, therefore excluded from the treatment trials pipeline.
paper_authors: Campen CLMCV; Rowe PC; Visser FC
paper_title: Orthostatic Symptoms and Reductions in Cerebral Blood Flow in Long-Haul COVID-19 Patients: Similarities with Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome

summary: This study examines the anti-inflammatory properties of luteolin-rich extract from Harrisonia perforata root against SARS-CoV-2 spike protein-induced lung inflammation in vitro. The work demonstrates dose-dependent reduction in inflammatory cytokines in cultured lung epithelial cells, but presents no human trial data or clinical outcomes for long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Warathit Semmarath; Punnida Arjsri; Kamonwan Srisawad; Sonthaya Umsumarng; Pornngarm Dejkriengkraikul
paper_title: Luteolin-Rich Extract from Harrisonia perforata (Blanco) Merr. Root Alleviates SARS-CoV-2 Spike Protein-Stimulated Lung Inflammation via Inhibition of MAPK/NLRP3 Inflammasome Signaling Pathways

summary: This paper develops a mechanistic differential equation model to investigate population-level dynamics of long COVID, incorporating COVID-19 transmission, vaccination, and long COVID progression. The work is a theoretical modeling study validated with US and UK data, not an empirical treatment trial or intervention study.
paper_authors: Jacob Derrick; Ben Patterson; Jie Bai; Jin Wang
paper_title: A Mechanistic Model for Long COVID Dynamics

summary: Longitudinal observational study comparing inflammatory biomarker profiles in long COVID patients versus controls at 3 and 6 months post-infection. Findings suggest immune exhaustion rather than elevated inflammation may characterize long COVID, with predictive models combining cytokine signatures and acute disease severity.
paper_authors: Anne Kallaste; Kalle Kisand; Agnes Aart; Ahto Salumets; Kai Kisand; Pärt Peterson; Margus Lember
paper_title: Long COVID and Biomarker Dysregulation—A Shift Toward Immune Exhaustion?

summary: This study compares plasma metabolomic profiles of PASC patients (n=29), recovered COVID-19 patients (n=16), and healthy controls (n=30) to identify biomarkers of mitochondrial dysfunction. The findings show PASC patients have altered fatty acid metabolism and depleted tryptophan levels consistent with mitochondrial dysfunction, but no intervention or treatment is tested.
paper_authors: Vamsi P. Guntur; Travis Nemkov; Esther de Boer; Michael P. Mohning; David Baraghoshi; Francesca I. Cendali; Inigo San-Millán; Irina Petrache; Angelo D’Alessandro
paper_title: Signatures of Mitochondrial Dysfunction and Impaired Fatty Acid Metabolism in Plasma of Patients with Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC)

summary: A prospective single-center study evaluated the effects of 6-week pulmonary rehabilitation on 46 long-COVID patients using pre/post measurements of respiratory function, exercise capacity, and psychological outcomes. The structured rehabilitation program showed significant improvements in functional capacity (6MWT distance, Sit-to-Stand test), pain (VAS scores), psychological measures (PHQ-9, GAD), and respiratory parameters.
paper_authors: Natasa Mujovic; Dejan Nikolic; Filip Markovic; Mihailo Stjepanovic; Milica Zekovic; Hussain Saleh H. Ali; Dubravka Zivanovic; Milan Savic; Marija Laban
paper_title: The Effects of Six Weeks Pulmonary Rehabilitation on Functional and Psychological Outcomes in Long-COVID Patients: Preliminary Results from Serbian Single Center Study

summary: This cross-sectional study compares salivary metabolite profiles in 30 long COVID patients versus 7 controls, measuring respiratory function and physical capacity. While it identifies biomarker differences (lower creatine, Gly Pro Lys, and calenduloside G), it does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Luiz Machado; Robson Prudente; Estefânia Franco; Mariana Gatto; Gustavo Mota; Luana Pagan; Luís Brizola; Maércio dos Santos; Thulio Cunha; Robinson Sabino-Silva; Luiz Goulart; Mario Martins; Paula Santos; Larissa Maia; André Albuquerque; Eloara Ferreira; Bruno Baldi; Marina Okoshi; Suzana Tanni
paper_title: Salivary Metabolomics in Patients with Long COVID-19 Infection

summary: This study develops a machine-learning model using metabolomic data to distinguish long COVID (PASC) from similar conditions like ME/CFS, Lyme disease, POTS, and IBS. The model achieves high diagnostic accuracy (AUC-ROC 0.8991) but does not evaluate any treatment intervention or patient outcomes.
paper_authors: Ethan Cai; Valentina L. Kouznetsova; Igor F. Tsigelny
paper_title: Metabolomics-Based Machine Learning Diagnostics of Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: This paper evaluates the clinical performance of two neutralizing antibody tests (pseudovirus and surrogate virus neutralization tests) in a COVID-19 long-term follow-up cohort. It is a methods/validation study comparing diagnostic test sensitivity and specificity, not a treatment intervention trial.
paper_authors: Constant Gillot; Julien Favresse; Clara David; Vincent Maloteau; Jean-Michel Dogne; Jonathan Douxfils
paper_title: An Evaluation of a SARS-CoV-2 Pseudovirus Neutralization Test and A Comparison to a SARS-CoV-2 Surrogate Virus Neutralization Test in a COVID-19 Long-Term Follow-Up Cohort

summary: This study investigates dermatologic changes in mice infected with murine hepatitis virus-1 (MHV-1) as an experimental model of long COVID, documenting skin damage across acute and chronic phases. The authors test treatment with a synthetic peptide (SPIKENET/SPK) designed to block Spike glycoprotein binding and demonstrate it restores hair follicles and repairs epidermal/dermal layers in infected mice.
paper_authors: Hussain Hussain; Michael J. Paidas; Ramamoorthy Rajalakshmi; Aya Fadel; Misha Ali; Pingping Chen; Arumugam R. Jayakumar
paper_title: Dermatologic Changes in Experimental Model of Long COVID

summary: This paper investigates the mechanism by which SARS-CoV-2 may interfere with hematopoietic stem cell differentiation and cause thrombocytopenia and thrombophilia in long COVID patients. It is an ex vivo mechanistic study using cell lines and primary CD34+ HSCs, not a clinical trial or treatment intervention study.
paper_authors: Mario Giosuè Balzanelli; Pietro Distratis; Gianna Dipalma; Luigi Vimercati; Alessio Danilo Inchingolo; Rita Lazzaro; Sergey Khachatur Aityan; Maria Elena Maggiore; Antonio Mancini; Rita Laforgia; Angela Pezzolla; Diego Tomassone; Van Hung Pham; Donatello Iacobone; Annalisa Castrignano; Antonio Scarano; Felice Lorusso; Silvio Tafuri; Giovanni Migliore; Angelo Michele Inchingolo; Kieu Cao Diem Nguyen; Tran Cong Toai; Francesco Inchingolo; Ciro Gargiulo Isacco
paper_title: Sars-CoV-2 Virus Infection May Interfere CD34+ Hematopoietic Stem Cells and Megakaryocyte–Erythroid Progenitors Differentiation Contributing to Platelet Defection towards Insurgence of Thrombocytopenia and Thrombophilia

summary: This is an in vitro mechanistic study examining how the SARS-CoV-2 S1 spike protein activates inflammatory signaling and cytokine production in human lung and intestinal epithelial cells cultured in the laboratory. It does not test any treatment or intervention on long COVID patients, making it a mechanistic research paper rather than a clinical trial or treatment study.
paper_authors: Christopher B. Forsyth; Lijuan Zhang; Abhinav Bhushan; Barbara Swanson; Li Zhang; João I. Mamede; Robin M. Voigt; Maliha Shaikh; Phillip A. Engen; Ali Keshavarzian
paper_title: The SARS-CoV-2 S1 Spike Protein Promotes MAPK and NF-kB Activation in Human Lung Cells and Inflammatory Cytokine Production in Human Lung and Intestinal Epithelial Cells

summary: This study investigated the presence of SARS-CoV-2 microRNA-like small RNAs in serum samples from 24 COVID-19 patients, comparing those with and without PASC symptoms. The research found reduced small RNA positivity in PASC patients at later timepoints but found no significant differences in host target expression between groups.
paper_authors: Maria Alfreda Stincarelli; Isabella Abbate; Giulia Matusali; Michele Tanturli; Marta Camici; Rosaria Arvia; Elisabetta Lazzari; Eleonora Cimini; Alessandra Vergori; Fabrizio Maggi; Simone Giannecchini
paper_title: Reduced Presence of SARS-CoV-2 microRNA-like Small RNA in the Serum of Patients with Post-Acute Sequelae SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: This prospective longitudinal study examines predisposing and precipitating factors for ME/CFS development following infectious mononucleosis in college students, with planned inclusion of long COVID cases. The research identifies baseline and acute-phase predictors of non-recovery but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Leonard A. Jason; Ben Z. Katz
paper_title: Predisposing and Precipitating Factors in Epstein–Barr Virus-Caused Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome

summary: Analyzes the proteome of amyloid microclots found in long COVID and sepsis patients, identifying proteins that distinguish amyloid from normal clots. Identifies galectin-3-binding protein and thrombospondin-1 as potential biomarkers for amyloid-type clotting abnormalities in coagulopathies.
paper_authors: Douglas B. Kell; Etheresia Pretorius
paper_title: The Proteome Content of Blood Clots Observed Under Different Conditions: Successful Role in Predicting Clot Amyloid(ogenicity)

summary: This study compared circulating microRNA (miRNA) expression patterns in plasma from long COVID patients with rheumatological symptoms, recovered COVID-19 patients, and healthy controls. The research identified differential miRNA expression and antibody-mediated hydrolysis activity associated with immune response pathways, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Anna M. Timofeeva; Artem O. Nikitin; Georgy A. Nevinsky
paper_title: Circulating miRNAs in the Plasma of Post-COVID-19 Patients with Typical Recovery and Those with Long-COVID Symptoms: Regulation of Immune Response-Associated Pathways

summary: This computational and experimental study investigates how SARS-CoV-2 nucleoprotein binds neuropeptides and proposes mechanisms linking viral replication to long COVID symptoms through altered neurotransmission pathways. The work speculates on potential therapeutic targets but presents no clinical trial data or treatment outcomes in patients.
paper_authors: Julien Henri; Laetitia Minder; Kevin Mohanasundaram; Sébastien Dilly; Anne Goupil-Lamy; Carmelo Di Primo; Anny Slama Schwok
paper_title: Neuropeptides, New Ligands of SARS-CoV-2 Nucleoprotein, a Potential Link between Replication, Inflammation and Neurotransmission

summary: This pilot study compared cerebrovascular reactivity (CVR) measured by breath-hold fMRI in 14 patients with neurological post-COVID syndrome (PCS) with fatigue/memory/concentration symptoms, 11 with PCS with myopathy/neuropathy symptoms, and 17 healthy controls. No significant differences in CVR or time-to-peak were found between groups, suggesting endothelial dysfunction may not be the primary pathomechanism of neurological PCS symptoms.
paper_authors: Leonie Zerweck; Uwe Klose; Annerose Mengel; Tobias Hoheisel; Melinda Eikemeier; Vivien Richter; Natalie Sophie Joos; Ulrike Ernemann; Benjamin Bender; Till-Karsten Hauser
paper_title: Cerebrovascular Reactivity Assessed by Breath-Hold Functional MRI in Patients with Neurological Post-COVID-19 Syndrome—A Pilot Study

summary: This study compares gut bacteriome composition, intestinal permeability, and inflammatory cytokine profiles between acute COVID-19 patients, post-COVID patients, and healthy controls using 16S sequencing and serological assays. The findings show dysbiosis and increased zonulin levels in infected groups, suggesting that gut dysbiosis may contribute to systemic inflammation, but no treatment intervention is tested or evaluated.
paper_authors: Larissa S. Souza; Alexandre S. Ferreira-Junior; Pedro C. Estella; Ricardo K. Noda; Lhorena F. Sousa; Miguel T. Y. Murata; Lucas A. L. Carvalho; João L. Brisotti; Daniel G. Pinheiro; Josias Rodrigues; Carlos M. C. B. Fortaleza; Gislane L. V. de Oliveira
paper_title: Bacteriome Signature in SARS-CoV-2-Infected Patients Correlates with Increased Gut Permeability and Systemic Inflammatory Cytokines

summary: This exploratory study examines changes in appetite and eating behavior in 55 post-COVID-19 patients compared to controls, measuring appetite-related hormones and brain activity patterns. The findings show increased appetite hormone levels (NPY, ghrelin) persisting long after infection, correlating with specific activity in brain regions involved in appetite regulation.
paper_authors: Georgeta Inceu; Ruben Emanuel Nechifor; Adriana Rusu; Dana Mihaela Ciobanu; Nicu Catalin Draghici; Raluca Maria Pop; Anca Elena Craciun; Mihai Porojan; Matei Negrut; Gabriela Roman; Adriana Fodor; Cornelia Bala
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 Changes in Appetite—An Exploratory Study

summary: This cross-sectional study examined associations between sensory, psychological, and cognitive variables in 149 COVID-19 survivors with post-COVID pain using structural equation modeling. The analysis found that depressive symptoms were the strongest predictor of post-COVID pain, with psychological factors linked to central sensitization and sleep quality, but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: César Fernández-de-las-Peñas; Bernard X. W. Liew; Manuel Herrero-Montes; Pablo del-Valle-Loarte; Rafael Rodríguez-Rosado; Diego Ferrer-Pargada; Randy Neblett; Paula Paras-Bravo
paper_title: Data-Driven Path Analytic Modeling to Understand Underlying Mechanisms in COVID-19 Survivors Suffering from Long-Term Post-COVID Pain: A Spanish Cohort Study

summary: This secondary analysis compares serological biomarkers before and after SARS-CoV-2 infection in 76 ILD patients, with 79% developing post-COVID symptoms. CPK levels were significantly elevated in patients with post-COVID fatigue and dyspnea, but no other biomarkers showed significant changes.
paper_authors: Paula Parás-Bravo; César Fernández-de-las-Peñas; Diego Ferrer-Pargada; Sheila Izquierdo-Cuervo; Luis M. Fernández-Cacho; José M. Cifrián-Martínez; Patricia Druet-Toquero; Oscar Pellicer-Valero; Manuel Herrero-Montes
paper_title: Serological Biomarkers in Individuals with Interstitial Lung Disease after SARS-CoV-2 Infection and Association with Post-COVID-19 Symptoms

summary: This study investigates the prevalence of long COVID symptoms in 185 surveyed COVID-19 patients and examines the association between long COVID and Epstein-Barr virus reactivation in a subset of 68 patients. paper_title:
Complex inflammation indexes in patients with post-COVID syndromeНа сегодняшний день в мире активно занимаются выделением новых маркеров, характеризующих тяжесть состояния после перенесенного COVID-19. Для более детального понимания того, какие изменения вызывает вирус SARS-CoV-2 в организме человека и с чем взаимосвязано длительное сохранение симптомов после перенесенной новой коронавирусной инфекции, необходимо оценить связь между степенью тяжести после заболевания и показателями клинического анализа крови. Цель работы – выделение прогностических маркеров по клиническому анализу крови, коррелирующих с тяжестью состояния пациентов после перенесенной новой коронавирусной инфекции.
В исследование включены 372 пациента в постковидный период. Исходное течение заболевания оценивалось с использованием шкалы клинического прогрессирования ВОЗ. Разделение пациентов на группы осуществлялось по шкале функционального состояния после COVID-19 (PCFS). В анализе крови обследуемых были выделены критические значения лабораторных показателей, которые были проанализированы на предмет наличия взаимосвязей с тяжестью синдрома. Проведен качественный анализ типов реакции иммунной системы в программе «Протист».
Установлены наиболее статистически выраженные изменения у пациентов группы 1. Коэффициенты NLR, LMR, SII при сравнении с группой пациентов 1, 2, 3 были ниже. Индекс PLR был ниже при сравнении с группой пациентов 0. Других статистических различий между группами не выявлено. Поэтому интерес вызывает исследования качественных показателей. В группах больных 0, 1, 2 в основном определяется ареактивность иммунитета (71-92%), а в группах пациентов 3 и 4 уже у половины обследуемых наблюдается активация врожденного иммунитета, активация адаптивного иммунитета и иммунодефицит (угнетение иммунитета). Пациенты группы 2 занимали промежуточное состояние.
В постковидный период общие гематологические нарушения не являются выраженными и достаточными для постановки диагноза. В большей степени необходимо ориентироваться на комплексные качественные показатели. Как один из основных качественных параметров у пациентов в постковидный период имеет смысл использовать «Методику определения типа реакции иммунитета по развернутому анализу крови» При этом оценка типа иммунной реакции позволяет не только выявить пациентов с постковидным синдромом, но и провести отбор пациентов, нуждающихся в противовоспалительной и детоксикационной терапии.

paper_title: Analysis of the Study of the Expression of Apoptosis Markers (CD95) and Intercellular Adhesion Markers (CD54) in Healthy Individuals and Patients Who Underwent COVID-19 When Using the Drug Mercureid

The study also examined immune marker changes (CD3, CD4, CD8, CD25, CD38, CD54, CD95) and their correlation with COVID-19-related chronic inflammatory manifestations.
paper_authors: Sergey N. Gusev; Velichko LN; Bogdanova AV; Khramenko NI; Konovalova NV
paper_title: Analysis Study of Visual and Physiological Functions, Expression of Various CD Markers of the Immune System, Clinical Course and Treatment of Complications in Patients with COVID-19 When Using Drug Mercureid

summary: This paper develops an automated deep learning approach (DeepLabv3+) to segment pathologically altered lung tissue on chest CT scans in post-COVID syndrome patients. paper_authors: Daniel Štifanić; Tin Nadarević; Jelena Štifanić; Igor Barković; Zlatan Car
paper_title: Semantic segmentation of chest computed tomography scans for quantifying pathologically altered lung parenchyma in patients with post-COVID syndrome

summary: This cross-sectional study examines 131 post-COVID patients to assess the relationship between acute COVID-19 severity and post-COVID immune-mediated disorders, including autoimmune conditions, proliferative diseases, and allergopathology. paper_title: Immune-mediated disorders in post-COVID patients and their relationship with impaired complement system activity

summary: This study evaluates changes in immune markers (complement system, neutrophil phagocytic activity) in post-COVID syndrome patients with laboratory-confirmed herpes virus type 6 co-infection using immunological assays and statistical analysis. The findings show more pronounced immune system disorders in post-COVID patients with herpesvirus history, suggesting the need for individualized immunocorrection approaches, but this is a descriptive cross-sectional immunological assessment without a treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Maria D. Verkhovskaya; V. S. Marchenko
paper_title: Features of immune response in patients with post-COVID syndrome and a history of type 6 herpes

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluated computed tomography characteristics of sinonasal structures in 130 patients with olfactory dysfunction following COVID-19. The study identified correlations between olfactory fossa morphology and severity of olfactory dysfunction but did not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Yu.V. Svitlychna; Andriy V. Lupyr; Н. О. Шушляпина; Олег Аврунін
paper_title: Computed tomography characteristics of sinonasal structures in acute rhinosinusitis associated with olfactory dysfunction caused by COVID-19

summary: This study examines immunological differences between patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) who had prior COVID-19 infection and compares immune markers (TREC/KREC levels, lymphocyte subpopulations) between groups stratified by TREC status. The research identifies associations between reduced TREC levels and more severe clinical presentations, but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

paper_title: Screening of immune status in patients with acute coronary syndrome

summary: Study of 414 patients examining IgG antibody levels and lymphocyte activation markers (CD25, CD54, CD95) in those who recovered from COVID-19, had acute respiratory infections, or were uninfected. The Results of the Correction of Impaired Immune Homeostasis Using the Multitarget Immunotherapy Drug Mercureid

summary: A case series of 30 long COVID patients treated with laser therapy and high-intensity electromagnetic stimulation for respiratory symptoms and chest pain. The treatment showed statistically significant improvements in chest pain, anxiety scores, and oxygen saturation levels.
paper_authors: Juan José Bernal Arreola
paper_title: The Development of Pulmonary Rehabilitation Protocol for Long Covid Patients
paper_journal: International Journal of Clinical Studies and Medical Case Reports

summary: Study of 49 patients with ophthalmic pathologies who previously had COVID-19, examining eye disorders to assess vascular and CNS effects and immunological responses post-infection. No specific treatment intervention tested; descriptive assessment of long COVID sequelae in ophthalmologic manifestations.
paper_authors: Sergey N. Gusev; Velichko LN; Bogdanova AV; Khramenko NI; Konovalova NV; Kovtun AV
paper_title: Mercureid Gives New Opportunities for Treatment and Prevention of Complications Caused by COVID-19 in Patients with Ophthalmic Pathologies
paper_journal: Journal of Ophthalmology and Advance Research

summary: This retrospective study analyzes the correlation between circulating SARS-CoV-2 variants and chronic disease incidence in COVID-19 patients in the Dominican Republic (2020–2024). paper_title: ANÁLISIS DEL SÍNDROME LONG COVID:  CORRELACIÓN DE SU INCIDENCIA CON LAS VARIANTES DE SARS-COV-2 CIRCULANTES Y LA INCIDENCIA DE ENFERMEDADES CRÓNICAS EN PACIENTES DIAGNOSTICADOS EN LOS CENTROS DE SALUD EN LA REPÚBLICA DOMINICANA 2020-2024
paper_journal: Actas del Congreso de Investigación, Desarrollo e Innovación

summary: This cross-sectional study used exploratory factor analysis to identify latent symptom dimensions in long COVID among 480 survey participants. The analysis revealed a three-factor model (General, PEM/Fatigue/Cognitive Dysfunction, and Psychological symptoms) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Joseph A. Dorri; Leonard A. Jason
paper_title: AN EXPLORATORY FACTOR ANALYSIS OF LONG COVID

summary: This cross-sectional study examines immunological changes in 125 COVID-19 patients 1-4 months after recovery, measuring T-lymphocytes, B-lymphocytes, and circulating immune complexes using flow cytometry and ELISA. paper_authors: Glazanova, Tv; Shilova, Er; Efremova, Ys; Chubukina, Jb; Bessmeltsev, Ss
paper_title: Changes in some immunological parameters after COVID-19: general trends and individual characteristics

The study found significantly lower flow-mediated vasodilation (FMD) and elevated systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) in post-COVID patients, suggesting persistent cardiovascular risk, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

paper_title: Evaluation of endothelial dysfunction and inflammation in recovered COVID-19 patients
paper_journal: Journal of Medicine and Palliative Care

summary: This paper proposes a 5-part classification system for post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) based on a self-report survey dataset, distinguishing mild, moderate, and severe cases with overlap to ME/CFS criteria. It is a classification/consensus framework rather than an intervention trial or treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Leonard A. Jason; Mohammed F. Islam
paper_title: A CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM FOR POST-ACUTE SEQUELAE OF SARS CoV-2 INFECTION
paper_journal: Central Asian Journal of Medical Hypotheses and Ethics

summary: This study examines age-dependent changes in immune markers in patients with comorbid post-COVID syndrome and gastric adenocarcinoma, exploring the inflammation-ageing-carcinogenesis pathway. The authors characterize dysregulation of innate immunity, oxidative stress, and inflammatory cascades in this patient population.
paper_authors: Olena Klimova; Larisa Drozdova; Olena Lavinska; Serhii Savvy; Olga Merezhko; Alla Agarkova
paper_title: Age-Dependent Changes in Prognostic Immune Markers in Patients with Comorbid Post-COVID Syndrome and Gastric Adenocarcinoma

summary: This retrospective study examined heart-type fatty acid binding protein (HFABP) as a predictor of myocardial injury severity and long-term cardiac function changes in COVID-19 patients over a two-year follow-up period. HFABP levels were significantly elevated in severe cases and predicted long-term cardiac dysfunction, suggesting it as a biomarker for COVID-related cardiac complications.
paper_authors: Yin L.; Wang H.; Shao J.; Mou H.; Su L.
paper_title: The independent prediction study of the effect of heart-type fatty acid binding protein on the severity and long-term cardiac function in Covid-19 patients.

summary: This cross-sectional study compared immune responses and post-COVID symptom development in 24 patients (unvaccinated, twice-vaccinated, and thrice-vaccinated) at 4 and 16 weeks following acute Omicron infection. The study found that vaccinated patients experienced prolonged disease and higher rates of post-COVID symptoms (60-78%) compared to unvaccinated patients (50%), with stronger autoantibody responses to G-protein coupled receptors correlating with POST-COVID risk.
paper_authors: Erpenbach K.; Erpenbach AS; Mayer W.; Weck M.
paper_title: SARS-CoV-2-Omicron-variant Induced COVID-19-Infection in Unvaccinated and Vaccinated Patients: Impact on Immune Response, Symptomatology, and Risk of POST-COVID Syndrome

paper_title: The Impact of COVID-19 Severity on TNF-α and IFN-γ in T2DM Patients' PBMC Monocytes
paper_journal: Journal Of The Indonesian Medical Association

paper_title: Oxi-Inflammatory Stress and Biomolecular  Deterioration: A Mysterious Convergence in  Post COVID Patients

paper_title: Improving Quality of Life for Long COVID Patients: The Benefits of Rehabilitation

summary: Doctoral thesis analyzing baseline data from the EXER-COVID cohort study, comparing physical condition, ventilatory efficiency, muscle strength, autonomic function, and oxidative metabolism in long COVID patients versus healthy controls. paper_authors: Sergio Oscoz Ochandorena
paper_title: COVID-19 sequelae on physical condition, autonomic function and oxidative metabolism: a comparative analysis

paper_title: The adapted Autonomic Profile (aAP) home-based test for the evaluation of neuro-cardiovascular autonomic dysfunction

paper_authors: Guocheng Feng; Huaiyu Cai; Wei Quan
paper_title: Exploring the Emotional and Mental Well-Being of Individuals with Long COVID Through Twitter Analysis

It is a retrospective data analysis focused on model development for early detection, not a treatment study or clinical trial, and does not present original treatment outcomes or interventions.
paper_authors: Hector J. Castro; Maitham G. Yousif
paper_title: Cognizance of Post-COVID-19 Multi-Organ Dysfunction through Machine Learning Analysis

Machine learning analysis identified age, gender, disease severity, comorbidities, and illness duration as significant predictive factors for GI symptoms like diarrhea, abdominal pain, and nausea.
paper_authors: Maitham G. Yousif; Fadhil G. Al-Amran; Salman Rawaf; Mohammad Abdulla Grmt
paper_title: Machine Learning-driven Analysis of Gastrointestinal Symptoms in Post-COVID-19 Patients

paper_authors: Leyli-abadi, Milad; Brunet, Jean-Patrick; Tahmasebimoradi, Axel
paper_title: Statistical and Predictive Analysis to Identify Risk Factors and Effects of Post COVID-19 Syndrome

paper_title: Demo: Guide-RAG: Evidence-Driven Corpus Curation for Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Long COVID

paper_title: A Hybrid Enumeration Framework for Optimal Counterfactual Generation in Post-Acute COVID-19 Heart Failure

paper_title: System and Method to Determine ME/CFS and Long COVID Disease Severity Using a Wearable Sensor

paper_title: Exploring the Impact of Residual Symptoms of COVID-19 on Work Participation

paper_title: Peculiarities of clinical signs, course and treatment of musculoskeletal system lesions in post-COVID syndrome

paper_title: Network analysis of host response to SARS-CoV-2 reveals a new set of genes with therapeutic and long term implications for COVID-19 disease.
