summary: This cross-sectional study evaluates liver function markers and cardiac isoenzymes in 150 COVID-19 recovered patients to assess long-term organ damage. Elevated liver enzymes (GPT/GOT) and cardiac isoenzymes (LDH1/LDH2) were found in 12-20% of patients, suggesting persistent dysfunction even after symptom resolution.
paper_authors: Sara Alsaid Ali Algool; Najwa Abdullah Mohammed Almozogy; Amna Mohamed Saud; Fathi Maftah Abu Saa
paper_title: Evaluation of Liver Function Markers and Cardiac Isoenzymes in Recovered COVID-19 Patients
paper_journal: Libyan Journal of Medical and Applied Sciences

summary: A Mendelian randomization study using GWAS data to assess causal associations between COVID-19 genetic susceptibility and post-COVID-19 syndrome symptoms. The analysis identifies potential causal links between COVID-19 and specific PCS symptoms like myalgia, erectile dysfunction, and heart arrhythmia, with social factors as mediators.
paper_authors: Yiming Tao; Rui Zhao; Jie Han; Yongsheng Li
paper_title: Assessing the causal relationship between COVID-19 and post-COVID-19 syndrome: A Mendelian randomisation study

summary: This is a basic neuroscience dissertation using mouse models to investigate sex differences in neuroimmune modulation of learning and memory, with long COVID mentioned only as a motivation/context. It does not study long COVID patients or test treatments for long COVID—it is a preclinical mechanistic study in animals.
paper_authors: Posillico, Caitlin
paper_title: Sex Differences in the Neuroimmune Modulation of Learning and Memory

summary: This study examines neuropathophysiological consequences of SARS-CoV-2 infection by comparing transcriptional and cellular signatures in brain regions of SARS-CoV-2-infected subjects, AD patients, and controls. The findings reveal similar neuroinflammation and blood-brain barrier alterations in SARS-CoV-2 and AD, with potential implications for understanding neuro-PASC and therapeutic approaches.
paper_authors: Elizabeth Griggs; Kyle Trageser; Sean Naughton; Eun-Jeong Yang; Brian Mathew; Grace Van Hyfte; Linh Hellmers; Nathalie Jette; Molly Estill; Li Shen; Tracy Fischer; Giulio Maria Pasinetti
paper_title: Recapitulation of pathophysiological features of AD in SARS-CoV-2-infected subjects

summary: This study assessed immune activation markers (T-cell activation, cytokines) at 3-12 months post-infection in 63 patients with varying COVID-19 severity and investigated associations with long COVID symptoms. While it confirms that severe disease correlates with persistent immune activation and long COVID symptoms, it is an observational study measuring associations, not testing any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Marianna Santopaolo; Michaela Gregorova; Fergus Hamilton; David Arnold; Anna Long; Aurora Lacey; Elizabeth Oliver; Alice Halliday; Holly Baum; Kristy Hamilton; Rachel Milligan; Olivia Pearce; Lea Knezevic; Begonia Morales Aza; Alice Milne; Emily Milodowski; Eben Jones; Rajeka Lazarus; Anu Goenka; Adam Finn; Nicholas Maskell; Andrew D. Davidson; Kathleen Gillespie; Linda Wooldridge; Laura Rivino
paper_title: Prolonged T-cell activation and long COVID symptoms independently associate with severe COVID-19 at 3 months

summary: This study validates the A-B Neuropsychological Assessment Schedule (ABNAS) as a screening tool for long COVID by testing its sensitivity and specificity in 235 participants (LC patients and controls). The ABNAS total score and subscales (fatigue, mental slowing) demonstrated good sensitivity and specificity for identifying long COVID, but this is a diagnostic validation study, not a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Kishen Radhakrishna; Jessica Holland; Fiadhnait O'Keeffe; Keith Gaynor; Justin Kinsella; Jessica Bramham
paper_title: Analysis of the A-B Neuropsychological Assessment Schedule as a Cognitive Screener for Long COVID

summary: This study validates the sit-to-stand test as a remote assessment tool for evaluating functional capacity in post-COVID-19 patients, comparing in-person, synchronous, and asynchronous tele-assessment methods. While it demonstrates good reliability for remote assessment, it is a methodological validation study rather than a treatment intervention trial.
paper_authors: Juliane Machado Marques; Matheus Brasiliano da Paz; Rodrigo Rodrigues Gomes Costa; Frederico Ribeiro Neto
paper_title: Validity, reliability and minimal detectable change in the sit-to-stand test for synchronous and asynchronous tele-assessment in post-COVID-19 condition

summary: This cross-sectional study compares the prevalence of ME/CFS in long COVID patients versus controls, finding that while LC patients report significantly higher rates of PEM and other ME/CFS-like symptoms, only 18.8% meet formal ME/CFS diagnostic criteria. The study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Joao A. Kouyoumdjian; Leticia A. Yamamoto; Carla R. Graca
paper_title: Exploration of Intersections and Divergences of Long COVID and Chronic Fatigue Syndrome

summary: This paper evaluates the Breathing Pattern Assessment Tool (BPAT) for diagnosing breathing pattern disorders in post-COVID patients attending a respiratory clinic. BPAT showed high sensitivity (89.5%) and moderate specificity (78.3%) but this is a diagnostic validation study, not a treatment intervention trial.
paper_authors: Hannah Hylton; Alex Long; Charlotte Francis; Rebecca R. Taylor; William M. Ricketts; Richa Singh; Paul E. Pfeffer
paper_title: Real-world use of the Breathing Pattern Assessment Tool in assessment of breathlessness post-COVID-19

summary: A prospective cross-sectional study using multidetector CT scanning and 3D volumetric assessment to evaluate post-COVID-19 pulmonary complications in 30 patients >3 months post-infection. The study demonstrates CT's utility in detecting volume loss and fibrosis but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Amira Magdy Tourky; Amr Ahmed Mubarak; Ali Ali El-Barbary; Hanan Mohamed El-Ahwal
paper_title: Multidetector CT in Evaluation of Post COVID-19 Pulmonary Complications with 3D CT Volumetric Assessment  of Post COVID-19 Fibrosis
paper_journal: Journal of Advances in Medicine and Medical Research

summary: This study compares biomarker levels (GIP-10, Gal-3, HIF-1) in vaccinated vs non-vaccinated COVID-19 patients with pulmonary fibrosis to assess vaccine effects on inflammation. While it examines post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis, it focuses on vaccine status as a natural grouping rather than testing a treatment intervention for long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Maha R. Al-Sammarraie; Fatma D. Azaiez; Hejer Litaiem
paper_title: mRNA Vaccination for COVID-19 Lowers the Risk for Pulmonary Fibrosis Through GIP-10/Gal-3/HIF-1 Downregulation

summary: This cross-sectional study compares HDL lipoprotein functions and PON1 activity between post-COVID-19 syndrome patients, asymptomatic post-COVID individuals, and healthy controls. The study found increased PON1 antioxidant activity in asymptomatic patients and correlations between HDL components and inflammatory markers, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Belén Davico; Maximiliano Martín; Ezequiel Lozano Chiappe; Rodrigo Esparza Iraola; Marina Marchesini; María Pérez; Leonardo Gómez Rosso; Laura Boero; Gustavo Giunta; Fernando Brites
paper_title: Diferencia en las distintas funciones de las lipoproteínas de alta densidad en respuesta a la infección por SARS-CoV-2.

summary: A QC/QI project analyzing hospital readmission patterns in COVID-19 patients, identifying respiratory failure and COVID-19 sequelae as primary readmission diagnoses. The study examines risk factors and outcomes in readmitted patients but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Jagdeesh Natesan; Suganthini Krishnan; Teena Chopra
paper_title: Risk Factors for Re-admission in Covid-19 Patients from a Tertiary Care Health System: Quality Control (QC) and Quality Improvement (QI) Project
paper_journal: International Journal of TROPICAL DISEASE & Health

summary: This study uses Golden Syrian hamsters as an animal model to characterize cardiovascular complications associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection and post-COVID sequelae. The research documents pathological changes and identifies metabolic markers but does not test any therapeutic intervention in patients.

paper_title: Golden Syrian hamster as a model to study cardiovascular complications associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection

summary: Prospective observational cohort study of 478 COVID-19 hospitalization survivors assessed at 4 months post-discharge, documenting prevalence of persistent symptoms including fatigue (31%), cognitive impairment (21%), and dyspnea (16%), along with imaging abnormalities and psychological sequelae. This is a descriptive epidemiological study without any treatment intervention or control comparison group.

paper_title: Four-Month Clinical Status of a Cohort of Patients After Hospitalization for COVID-19

summary: This is an in vitro experimental study examining how the SARS-CoV-2 spike S1 protein affects hemichannel activity in HeLa cells transfected with connexin-43. The authors propose that persistent hemichannel opening could contribute to long COVID pathology and might represent a therapeutic target, but the work is basic laboratory research without any human subjects or treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Juan Carlos Prieto Villalobos; Juan Carlos Prieto Villalobos
paper_title: Role of the glycoprotein Spike S1 of the SARS-CoV-2 virus on the function of hemichannels formed by Cx43

summary: This is an editorial commentary on the COMEBAC study that describes long COVID prevalence and symptoms in hospital survivors at 4-month follow-up. It discusses general observations about long COVID sequelae but is not itself a primary research study with original data collection.
paper_authors: Hallie C. Prescott
paper_title: Outcomes for Patients Following Hospitalization for COVID-19

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines whether mRNA vaccination (BNT162b2) reduces the risk of long COVID in health care workers who experienced COVID-19 infection. The study compares long COVID incidence between vaccinated and unvaccinated groups but does not constitute a treatment trial, as vaccination is evaluated for its preventive effect rather than as a therapeutic intervention for existing long COVID.
paper_authors: Elena Azzolini; Riccardo Levi; Riccardo Sarti; Chiara Pozzi; Maximiliano Mollura; Alberto Mantovani; Maria Rescigno
paper_title: Association Between BNT162b2 Vaccination and Long COVID After Infections Not Requiring Hospitalization in Health Care Workers

summary: Prospective cohort study examining the association between pre-infection healthy lifestyle factors and risk of post-COVID-19 condition in 32,249 women from the Nurses' Health Study II. summary: Case-control study comparing 1-year adverse health outcomes between 13,435 adults with post-COVID-19 condition and 26,870 matched controls without COVID-19 using commercial insurance claims data. Post-COVID cohort showed significantly elevated risks for cardiac arrhythmias (RR 2.35), pulmonary embolism (RR 3.64), stroke, heart failure, COPD, and mortality (2.8% vs 1.2%), indicating substantial long-term cardiovascular and pulmonary complications.

summary: Cohort study examining whether nirmatrelvir treatment during acute COVID-19 reduces the risk of developing post-COVID condition using VA healthcare databases. Nirmatrelvir was associated with a 26% reduction in post-COVID risk and reduced risk across 10 of 13 post-acute sequelae components.

summary: This retrospective cohort study used linked Swedish healthcare data to compare kidney function decline after COVID-19 versus pneumonia in 134,565 individuals, finding that COVID-19 was associated with greater accelerated annual eGFR decline (3.4% vs 2.3%), particularly among hospitalized patients (5.4%). summary: This prospective cohort study from the RECOVER-Adult initiative characterizes olfactory dysfunction in 3,525 long COVID patients using formal smell testing (UPSIT) at a mean of 671 days post-infection. While it documents high rates of hyposmia (79.8% among those with self-reported change/loss) and associations with cognitive problems, it is an observational study with no treatment intervention and therefore ineligible for the intervention trials meta-analysis.

summary: This paper examines one-year outcomes in children with multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS-C) following acute COVID-19 infection. MIS-C is an acute post-infection complication occurring weeks after initial infection, distinct from long COVID's chronic ongoing symptoms; this study focuses on acute critical care outcomes rather than long-term persistent illness management or treatment interventions.

summary: This multisite longitudinal cohort study characterized long COVID symptoms in early childhood (infants/toddlers 0-2 years and preschool-aged children 3-5 years) by comparing infected and uninfected children. The study derived age-specific symptom indices to identify probable LC cases, finding 14% of infected infants/toddlers and 15% of infected preschool-aged children had probable LC based on distinct symptom patterns.

summary: Retrospective cohort study using QResearch and linked health records to quantify neuropsychiatric risks after severe COVID-19 hospitalization compared to other severe acute respiratory infections. Found elevated risks of anxiety, dementia, depression, and neuropsychiatric medication prescriptions in COVID-19 survivors, similar to SARI survivors.

paper_title: Neuropsychiatric Ramifications of Severe COVID-19 and Other Severe Acute Respiratory Infections

summary: This prospective cohort study examines whether pre-infection psychological distress (depression, anxiety, worry, stress, loneliness) is associated with increased risk of developing long COVID. The study found that participants with high psychological distress prior to infection had 32-46% increased risk of post-COVID conditions, with those experiencing multiple types of distress having nearly 50% increased risk.
paper_authors: Siwen Wang; Luwei Quan; Jorge E. Chavarro; Natalie Slopen; Laura D. Kubzansky; Karestan C. Koenen; Jae Hee Kang; Marc G. Weisskopf; Westyn Branch-Elliman; Andrea L. Roberts

summary: This Danish nationwide cohort study examined the risk of new-onset mental disorders following SARS-CoV-2 infection compared to negative test results and non-COVID hospitalizations. While the paper studies psychiatric sequelae post-infection, it does not focus on long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-months post-infection) and does not test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Vardan Nersesjan; Rune H. B. Christensen; Daniel Kondziella; Michael E. Benros
paper_title: COVID-19 and Risk for Mental Disorders Among Adults in Denmark

summary: A prospective cross-sectional study characterizing neurologic manifestations in 100 non-hospitalized long COVID patients (50 confirmed SARS-CoV-2+ and 50 negative controls) presenting to a Neuro-COVID clinic. Findings show prevalent brain fog (81%), headache (68%), and cognitive deficits in attention and working memory, with SARS-CoV-2+ patients showing significantly higher rates of anosmia.

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines the association between COVID-19 diagnosis and subsequent mental illness across vaccinated and unvaccinated populations in England. summary: A prospective follow-up study assessing dyspnea prevalence and predictors in 327 COVID-19 patients at 2 months post-infection. While relevant to long COVID, this is an observational study with no treatment intervention—it documents symptom outcomes rather than evaluating any therapeutic approach.
paper_authors: Md. Khairul Islam; Mohammad Faisal Hossain; Md. Maruf Ahmed Molla; Md. Mohiuddin Sharif; Pratyay Hasan; Fahima Sharmin Hossain; Ayesha Sikder; Md Gias Uddin; Md. Robed Amin
paper_title: A 2‐month post‐<scp>COVID</scp>‐19 follow‐up study on patients with dyspnea

summary: This longitudinal observational study examined 169 COVID-19 patients to assess whether ABO blood group is associated with in-hospital adverse outcomes and long-term persistent symptoms. The study found blood groups AB and B were associated with higher rates of respiratory support/death acutely, and AB with persistent palpitation and dizziness at 6-month follow-up, but it is an observational cohort study without treatment intervention and thus ineligible for the clinical trials pipeline.
paper_authors: Ahmed Nafakhi; Ihsan S. Rabeea; Rasha Al‐Darraji; Hussein Nafakhi; Ahmed Mechi; Alhan Al‐Khalidi; Mohammed alareedh
paper_title: Association of ABO blood group with in‐hospital adverse outcome and long term persistent symptoms of COVID‐19 infection: A single‐center longitudinal observational study

summary: A retrospective case-control study examining the association between acute COVID-19 severity and symptoms with the development of long COVID in a non-hospitalized population. The study found that severe acute infection and higher symptom burden during acute phase were strongly associated with long COVID development, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Nicolás Escrivá; Laura Moreno‐Galarraga; Elena Barado; María Gabriela Torres; Alejandro Fernandez‐Montero
paper_title: Association Between Acute COVID‐19 Infection and Long COVID in a Non‐Hospitalized Population: A Retrospective Case‐Control Study

summary: Longitudinal cohort study examining T-cell immune responses in COVID-19 survivors at 1 and 6-8 months post-infection using flow cytometry analysis. Found sustained T-cell responses and immune recovery patterns at 6-8 months, but this is purely observational characterization with no treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Poonam Suryawanshi; Bhagyashri Patil‐Takbhate; Prachi Athavale; Shahzad Mirza; Anuradha Tripathy; Shubhangi Kanitkar; Sachin Shivnitwar; Madhusudan S. Barthwal; Sachin Dole; Hanumant Chavan; Priyanka Jali; Sujata Pawale; Dhanashree Kakad; Arjun Lal Kakrani; Jitendra Bhawalkar; Madhura Gandhi; Sarika Chaturvedi; Mahesh Karandikar; Srikanth Tripathy
paper_title: T‐cell responses in COVID‐19 survivors 6−8 months after infection: A longitudinal cohort study in Pune

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining associations between acute inflammatory biomarkers (IL-6, CRP, ferritin) during COVID-19 hospitalization and long-COVID symptoms at 3-month follow-up in 144 patients. Found counterintuitive inverse associations between admission biomarker levels and subsequent myalgia, low mood, and anxiety, with gender confounding the relationships.
paper_authors: Dominic L. Sykes; Christina M. Van der Feltz‐Cornelis; Luke Holdsworth; Simon P. Hart; Joseph O'Halloran; Steve Holding; Michael G. Crooks
paper_title: Examining the relationship between inflammatory biomarkers during COVID‐19 hospitalization and subsequent long‐COVID symptoms: A longitudinal and retrospective study

summary: This observational study assessed the prevalence and characteristics of long COVID among people living with HIV in a tertiary clinic in western India, screening 94 PLHIV with confirmed COVID-19 history. Long COVID prevalence was 43.6%, with moderate-severe acute illness as a significant risk factor, and fatigue and cough as the most common persistent symptoms.
paper_authors: Sanjay Pujari; Sunil Gaikwad; Abhishek Chitalikar; Digamber Dabhade; Kedar Joshi; Vivek Bele
paper_title: Long‐coronavirus disease among people living with HIV in western India: An observational study

summary: Retrospective cross-sectional study assessing health-related quality of life (HRQoL) using EQ-5D-3L questionnaires in 105 COVID-19 ICU survivors at 1 year follow-up. Found that 69% reported pain/discomfort problems and 51% reported anxiety/depression, with diabetes, longer ICU stay, younger age, and male sex associated with impaired HRQoL.
paper_authors: Carina M. Samuelsson; Netha Hussain; Avril Drummond; Carina U. Persson
paper_title: Health‐Related Quality of Life One Year After Intensive Care Unit Admission for COVID‐19: A Retrospective, Cross‐Sectional, Longitudinal Observational Study

summary: Cohort study comparing obese and non-obese COVID-19 patients discharged from hospital to assess long-term effects of obesity on clinical manifestations and immune function. Found that obese patients had more severe clinical manifestations, abnormal metabolic indicators, and inversely correlated antibody titers with BMI.
paper_authors: Luorui Shang; Li Wang; Fangyuan Zhou; Jinxiao Li; Yuhan Liu; Shenglan Yang
paper_title: Long‐term effects of obesity on COVID‐19 patients discharged from hospital

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of sarcopenia in 541 COVID-19 survivors and examined its relationship to persistent long COVID symptoms. Sarcopenia was present in 19.5% of patients and was associated with higher numbers of persistent symptoms, particularly fatigue and dyspnea, suggesting it may be a biological mechanism underlying long COVID syndrome.
paper_authors: Anna Maria Martone; Matteo Tosato; Francesca Ciciarello; Vincenzo Galluzzo; Maria Beatrice Zazzara; Cristina Pais; Giulia Savera; Riccardo Calvani; Emanuele Marzetti; Maria Camprubi Robles; Maria Ramirez; Francesco Landi
paper_title: Sarcopenia as potential biological substrate of long COVID‐19 syndrome: prevalence, clinical features, and risk factors
paper_journal: Journal of Cachexia, Sarcopenia and Muscle

summary: This nested case-control study of 94 participants examines demographic, clinical, and immunological factors associated with long COVID, finding that HIV infection is an independent predictor of long COVID (OR=2.7) and that inflammatory marker patterns differ between HIV+ and HIV- individuals. The study identifies respiratory and musculoskeletal symptoms as most common in long COVID patients and reveals differential cytokine responses by HIV status (IL-6 in HIV- group, IFN-β in HIV+ group).
paper_authors: Patrick Kamanzi; Gina Mulundu; Keagan Mutale; Chibamba Mumba; Owen Ngalamika
paper_title: HIV and inflammatory markers are associated with persistent COVID‐19 symptoms

summary: Prospective cohort study of 104 renal transplant recipients followed for a median of 64 days after acute COVID-19 to identify post-COVID complications. 88.5% of survivors developed clinical or laboratory complications including shortness of breath, tiredness, and coagulopathy; most improved by 6 months with persistent elevated D-dimers in some patients.
paper_authors: Nikolina Basic‐Jukic; Ivana Juric; Vesna Furic‐Cunko; Lea Katalinic; Josipa Radic; Zrinka Bosnjak; Bojan Jelakovic; Zeljko Kastelan
paper_title: Follow‐up of renal transplant recipients after acute COVID‐19—A prospective cohort single‐center study

summary: Retrospective chart review of 798 long COVID patients describing symptom prevalence and complicating diseases, with emphasis on differential diagnosis rather than treatment evaluation. Study identifies non-COVID-related conditions mimicking long COVID symptoms but does not test or evaluate any intervention.
paper_authors: Tomoya Tsuchida; Masanori Hirose; Hirotoshi Fujii; Ryunosuke Hisatomi; Kosuke Ishizuka; Yoko Inoue; Kohta Katayama; Yu Nakagama; Yasutoshi Kido; Takahide Matsuda; Yoshiyuki Ohira
paper_title: Evaluation of diseases complicating long <scp>COVID</scp>: A retrospective chart review
paper_journal: Journal of General and Family Medicine

summary: This cross-sectional study uses cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging to characterize myocardial findings in patients with suspected myocarditis during acute COVID-19 (AMCovS) and post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (cPACS). The paper reports diagnostic imaging findings rather than testing or evaluating a treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Anna Palmisano; Davide Vignale; Elisa Bruno; Giovanni Peretto; Giacomo De Luca; Corrado Campochiaro; Alessandro Tomelleri; Eustachio Agricola; Matteo Montorfano; Antonio Esposito
paper_title: Cardiac magnetic resonance findings in acute and post‐acute <scp>COVID</scp>‐19 patients with suspected myocarditis

summary: This prospective cohort study examined the clinical features of 58 patients with gastrointestinal long-COVID symptoms out of 943 COVID-19 patients in Japan. The study found that patients with GI long-COVID symptoms had significantly lower quality of life measures (SF-8, EQ-5D-5L) at 12 months and experienced more varied long-COVID symptoms than those without GI symptoms.
paper_authors: Kazuma Yagi; Takanori Asakura; Hideki Terai; Keiko Ohgino; Katsunori Masaki; Ho Namkoong; Shotaro Chubachi; Jun Miyata; Ichiro Kawada; Nobuhiro Kodama; Satoshi Sakamoto; Akira Umeda; Takashi Ishiguro; Makoto Ishii; Koichi Fukunaga
paper_title: Clinical features of Japanese patients with gastrointestinal <scp>long‐COVID</scp> symptoms

summary: This study evaluates fetal cardiac morphology and function in pregnant women 4 weeks after recovery from moderate COVID-19 infection using echocardiography. The findings show no significant cardiac effects in the fetus, with only a minor difference in mitral E/A ratio that does not indicate clinical harm.
paper_authors: Sule Goncu Ayhan; Ezgi Turgut; Eda Ozden Tokalioglu; Deniz Oluklu; Bedri Sakcak; Derya Uyan Hendem; Atakan Tanacan; Ozlem Moraloglu Tekin; Dilek Sahin
paper_title: Post‐COVID‐19 fetal cardiac evaluation in moderate infection group of pregnant women

summary: This retrospective cohort study examined 51 Wilson disease patients before and ~11 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection to assess physical and mental health outcomes using validated scales. 39.2% were classified as having long COVID, with high rates of concentration disorders (60%), fatigue (55%), and reduced exercise capacity (50%), suggesting WD patients may be particularly vulnerable to long COVID complications.
paper_authors: Isabelle Mohr; Maximilian Brand; Christophe Weber; Andrea Langel; Jessica Langel; Patrick Michl; Viola Yuriko Leidner; Alexander Olkus; Sebastian Köhrer; Uta Merle
paper_title: Mental and Physical Health in Wilson Disease Patients With <scp>SARS</scp>‐<scp>CoV</scp>‐2 Infection and Relevance of Long‐<scp>COVID</scp>

summary: This study compares mitochondrial membrane potential in leukocytes between healthy controls, acute COVID-19 patients, and recovered individuals at 40 and 335 days post-infection. The findings suggest persistent loss of mitochondrial function in long COVID patients, particularly in females, potentially linking mitochondrial dysfunction to post-COVID sequelae.
paper_authors: Karina Janice Guadalupe Díaz-Resendiz; Alma Betsaida Benitez-Trinidad; Carlos Eduardo Covantes-Rosales; Gladys Alejandra Toledo-Ibarra; Pablo Cesar Ortiz-Lazareno; Daniel Alberto Girón-Pérez; Adela Yolanda Bueno-Durán; Daniela Alejandra Pérez-Díaz; Rocío Guadalupe Barcelos-García; Manuel Iván Girón-Pérez
paper_title: Loss of mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm) in leucocytes as post-COVID-19 sequelae

summary: This prospective cross-sectional study compares brain gray matter morphology in 38 young adults who recovered from mild COVID-19 without long COVID symptoms against 37 healthy controls using MRI-based morphometry. The study found gray matter alterations including reduced cortical thickness and subcortical volume in the COVID group despite subjects having no subjective neurological complaints at examination, suggesting subclinical CNS changes following mild infection.
paper_authors: Gábor Perlaki; Gergely Darnai; Ákos Arató; Husamalddin Ali Alhour; Anna Szente; Eszter Áfra; Szilvia Anett Nagy; Réka Horváth; Norbert Kovács; Tamás Dóczi; Gergely Orsi; József Janszky
paper_title: Gray Matter Changes Following Mild <scp>COVID</scp>‐19: An <scp>MR</scp> Morphometric Study in Healthy Young People

summary: Propensity-matched observational study comparing cirrhosis patients with COVID-19 vs. non-COVID sepsis, followed for 1 year to assess decompensation and mortality. Long COVID occurred in 33.3% of COVID-19 survivors with cirrhosis, with higher late mortality compared to non-COVID sepsis controls.
paper_authors: Prerna Sharma; Madhumita Premkumar; Rashmi Ranjan Guru; Anchal Sandhu; Kamal Kajal; Arka De; Sahaj Rathi; Nipun Verma; Sunil Taneja; Virendra Singh; Ajay Kumar Duseja
paper_title: Post <scp>COVID</scp> Condition and Long‐Term <scp>COVID</scp>‐19 Impact on Hepatic Decompensation and Survival in Cirrhosis: A Propensity Matched Observational Study

summary: This prospective study evaluated whether quantitative respiratory pattern measures from dynamic high-temporal resolution MRI can stratify postacute COVID-19 patients by cardiopulmonary symptom burden. The analysis found that tidal lung area, lung area coefficient of variability, and respiratory incoherence were significantly higher in patients with two or more cardiopulmonary symptoms, suggesting MRI-derived metrics may help characterize symptom severity.
paper_authors: Lea Azour; Henry Rusinek; Artem Mikheev; Nicholas Landini; Mahesh Bharath Keerthivasan; Christoph Maier; Barun Bagga; Mary Bruno; Rany Condos; William H. Moore; Hersh Chandarana
paper_title: Quantitative Characterization of Respiratory Patterns on Dynamic Higher Temporal Resolution <scp>MRI</scp> to Stratify Postacute Covid‐19 Patients by Cardiopulmonary Symptom Burden

summary: This cross-sectional MRI study compared cerebral blood flow (CBF) in 39 adults weeks to months post-COVID-19 versus 11 controls with flu-like symptoms but negative COVID tests. The COVID-19 group showed significantly reduced CBF in subcortical regions (thalamus, orbitofrontal cortex, basal ganglia), with additional CBF differences in those reporting ongoing fatigue, suggesting brain physiology changes underlie post-COVID symptoms.
paper_authors: Kim WSH; Ji X.; Roudaia E.; Chen JJ; Gilboa A.; Sekuler A.; Gao F.; Lin Z.; Jegatheesan A.; Masellis M.; Goubran M.; Rabin JS; Lam B.; Cheng I.; Fowler R.; Heyn C.; Black SE; Graham SJ; MacIntosh BJ
paper_title: <scp>MRI</scp> Assessment of Cerebral Blood Flow in Nonhospitalized Adults Who Self‐Isolated Due to <scp>COVID</scp>‐19

summary: This retrospective analysis examines KL-6 as a biomarker for COVID-19 severity and lung injury in 166 acute COVID-19 patients. While it mentions long-term lung injury prognosis, the study focuses on acute COVID-19 disease severity rather than long COVID syndrome, and it is purely observational with no treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Kai Deng; Qinghong Fan; Yanhong Yang; Xizi Deng; Ruiying He; Yizhou Tan; Yun Lan; Xilong Deng; Yuejun Pan; Yaping Wang; Yujuan Guan; Huiyuan Liu; Fengjuan Chen; Xiaoneng Mo; Xinghua Tan; Chun Luo; Xueliang Wen; Ying Liu; Jinxin Liu; Lieguang Zhang; Xiaoping Tang; Fengyu Hu; Feng Li
paper_title: Prognostic roles of KL‐6 in disease severity and lung injury in COVID‐19 patients: A longitudinal retrospective analysis

summary: A prospective cohort study following 172 COVID-19 patients for 8-10 months to characterize persistent symptoms post-recovery, finding 61% reported one or more long COVID symptoms with fatigue, dyspnea, and depression most common, and age as a significant risk factor. The study documents symptom prevalence and re-infection rates but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Mona Mohammed Abdelrahman; Noha Mohammed Abd‐Elrahman; Tasneem Mohammed Bakheet
paper_title: Persistence of symptoms after improvement of acute COVID19 infection, a longitudinal study

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluated radiological findings, pulmonary function, and health-related quality of life in 65 severe COVID-19 survivors at 6 months post-discharge. The paper found pulmonary abnormalities (fibrosis, reduced FEV1/FVC) and impaired quality of life but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Mustafa Ilteris Bardakci; Esin Nagihan Ozturk; Mufide Arzu Ozkarafakili; Huseyin Ozkurt; Ugur Yanc; Dilek Yildiz Sevgi
paper_title: Evaluation of long‐term radiological findings, pulmonary functions, and health‐related quality of life in survivors of severe COVID‐19

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 328 COVID-19 patients from Johns Hopkins Health System evaluated symptom persistence a median of 242 days post-infection. 33.2% reported incomplete recovery with women disproportionately reporting activity-limiting symptoms, though the study does not test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Priya Duggal; Tristan Penson; Hannah N. Manley; Candelaria Vergara; Rebecca M. Munday; Dylan Duchen; Elizabeth A. Linton; Amber Zurn; Jeanne C. Keruly; Shruti H. Mehta; David L. Thomas
paper_title: Post‐sequelae symptoms and comorbidities after COVID‐19

summary: Observational cohort study of 76 COVID-19 patients followed 1 year post-admission to examine long-term symptom persistence and quality of life, with comparison between those who did and did not receive systemic corticosteroids during acute infection. Patients receiving corticosteroids showed significantly lower rates of headache, dysphagia, chest pain, and depression, with improved quality of life scores in bodily pain and mental health domains.
paper_authors: Ignacio Pérez Catalán; Celia Roig Martí; Daniela Palomo de la Sota; Alejandro Cardenal Álvarez; Maria José Esteve Gimeno; Sergio Fabra Juana; Germán Herrero Rodríguez; Elena Domínguez Bajo; Nuria Tornador Gaya; Jorge Usó Blasco; Jose Manuel Ramos Rincón
paper_title: Corticosteroids for COVID‐19 symptoms and quality of life at 1 year from admission

summary: This cross-sectional study investigated the frequency and risk factors of brain fog in 2,696 COVID-19 survivors from Iran, finding that 62.3% reported long COVID syndrome and 7.2% experienced chronic brain fog. The study identified female sex, respiratory problems at onset, and ICU admission as significant risk factors for post-COVID brain fog.
paper_authors: Ali A. Asadi‐Pooya; Ali Akbari; Amir Emami; Mehrzad Lotfi; Mahtab Rostamihosseinkhani; Hamid Nemati; Zohreh Barzegar; Maryam Kabiri; Zahra Zeraatpisheh; Mohsen Farjoud‐Kouhanjani; Anahita Jafari; Sarvin Sasannia; Shayan Ashrafi; Masoume Nazeri; Sara Nasiri; Mina Shahisavandi
paper_title: Long COVID syndrome‐associated brain fog

summary: This cross-sectional study examined inflammatory biomarkers (ESR, CRP) and serum albumin levels in patients following recovery from severe versus mild-to-moderate COVID-19. The findings show sustained elevation of inflammatory markers and reduced albumin in severe COVID-19 post-recovery patients, but this is an observational characterization study without any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Kameran M. Ali; Ayad M. Ali; Hassan M. Tawfeeq; Grazziela P. Figueredo; Hassan M. Rostam
paper_title: Hypoalbuminemia in patients following their recovery from severe coronavirus disease 2019

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 524 COVID-19 patients in Eastern India followed up ~73 days post-infection during the Omicron wave to estimate long COVID incidence and identify predictors. Found 8.2% self-reported long COVID symptoms with fatigue and cough most common; prior infection and ≥5 acute COVID symptoms were significant predictors.
paper_authors: Arjun MC; Singh AK; Roy P.; Ravichandran M.; Mandal S.; Pal D.; Das K.; Gajjala A.; Venkateshan M.; Mishra B.; Patro BK; Mohapatra PR; Subba SH
paper_title: Long COVID following Omicron wave in Eastern India—A retrospective cohort study

summary: Observational study examining symptom changes and antibody titers in 42 long COVID patients after receiving their first COVID-19 vaccination. Found that vaccination increased antibody titers significantly, with worsening symptoms associated with the highest antibody titer increases.
paper_authors: Tomoya Tsuchida; Masanori Hirose; Yoko Inoue; Hiroyuki Kunishima; Takehito Otsubo; Takahide Matsuda
paper_title: Relationship between changes in symptoms and antibody titers after a single vaccination in patients with Long COVID

summary: This multicenter observational study tracked gastrointestinal and other post-COVID symptoms in 1,593 previously hospitalized patients at two timepoints (8.4 and 13.2 months post-infection) to characterize recovery trajectories. The study found an overall decline in symptom burden over time but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: César Fernández‐de‐las‐Peñas; José D. Martín‐Guerrero; Esperanza Navarro‐Pardo; Juan Torres‐Macho; Carlos Guijarro; Oscar J. Pellicer‐Valero
paper_title: Exploring the recovery curve for gastrointestinal symptoms from the acute COVID‐19 phase to long‐term post‐COVID: The LONG‐COVID‐EXP‐CM Multicenter Study

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 286 long COVID patients attending an outpatient clinic characterizing clinical features, symptom recovery periods, and factors affecting recovery. Respiratory symptoms and fatigue were most common, with COVID-19 severity, symptom burden, delayed treatment initiation, and smoking identified as independent factors slowing recovery.
paper_authors: Kazuki Takakura; Machi Suka; Mikio Kajihara; Shigeo Koido
paper_title: Clinical features, therapeutic outcomes, and recovery period of long COVID

summary: This study evaluates the psychometric properties and clinical usefulness of the COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale (C19-YRS) in 187 patients with post-COVID syndrome attending a rehabilitation clinic. The C19-YRS demonstrated good internal consistency and validity as an outcome measurement tool, but the paper does not test or evaluate a specific intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Rory J. O'Connor; Nick Preston; Amy Parkin; Sophie Makower; Denise Ross; Jeremy Gee; Stephen J. Halpin; Mike Horton; Manoj Sivan
paper_title: The COVID‐19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale (C19‐YRS): Application and psychometric analysis in a post‐COVID‐19 syndrome cohort

summary: This cross-sectional biomarker study profiled plasma from 181 individuals in the DigiHero cohort to characterize immune dysregulation in post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), including monocyte/macrophage dysfunction and circulating SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. The study found pronounced dysregulation in pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic cytokines with PASC-specific patterns, and identified circulating spike protein as an independent biomarker in a subset of PASC patients, illustrating biological heterogeneity in the condition.
paper_authors: Christoph Schultheiß; Edith Willscher; Lisa Paschold; Cornelia Gottschick; Bianca Klee; Lidia Bosurgi; Jochen Dutzmann; Daniel Sedding; Thomas Frese; Matthias Girndt; Jessica I. Höll; Michael Gekle; Rafael Mikolajczyk; Mascha Binder
paper_title: Liquid biomarkers of macrophage dysregulation and circulating spike protein illustrate the biological heterogeneity in patients with post‐acute sequelae of COVID‐19

summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 211 non-ICU COVID-19 survivors at 8-week outpatient follow-up to assess recovery, symptoms, and mental health outcomes. The study found persistent physical symptoms (fatigue 68%, dyspnea 56%) and cognitive problems (memory impairment 33%, concentration problems 28%) in most patients, with 7.8% meeting anxiety criteria and correlations between physical and mental symptom burden.
paper_authors: Karen Keijsers; Marielle Broeders; Vania Baptista Lopes; Aryan Klinkert; Janwillem van Baar; Lenny Nahar‐van Venrooij; Angèle Kerckhoffs
paper_title: Memory impairment and concentration problems in COVID‐19 survivors 8 weeks after non‐ICU hospitalization: A retrospective cohort study

summary: This retrospective cohort study follows 47 Omicron COVID-19 patients for 6 months post-discharge to assess dynamic changes in renal function and cytokine profiles. The study finds declining renal function at follow-up with altered cytokine levels, particularly elevated TGF-β in patients with kidney involvement, suggesting a potential manifestation of long COVID.
paper_authors: Lanbo Teng; Xinyuan Song; Miaomiao Zhang; Yingying Han; Ge Chang; Wenxiu Chang; Zhongyang Shen
paper_title: The pattern of cytokines expression and dynamic changes of renal function at 6 months in patients with Omicron COVID‐19

summary: Prospective cohort study following 233 hospitalized COVID-19 pneumonia patients for 12 months post-discharge, stratified by ventilation severity, measuring clinical symptoms, radiological findings, and pulmonary function. Most symptoms resolved by month 12, though brain fog, memory loss, and anosmia/dysgeusia persisted in some patients, and CT abnormalities remained common despite normalized pulmonary function in most cases.
paper_authors: Marco Bongiovanni; Giuseppe Barilaro; Francesco Bini
paper_title: Twelve‐month clinical, functional, and radiological outcomes in patients hospitalized for SARS‐CoV‐2 pneumonia

summary: This retrospective cohort study evaluated the efficacy of nirmatrelvir-ritonavir treatment on post-acute COVID-19 symptoms beyond 3 months using propensity score matching on 12,245 matched pairs. Early NMV-r treatment reduced hospitalization and ER visits but did not significantly reduce post-acute COVID-19 symptoms or mortality risk.
paper_authors: Min‐Hsiang Chuang; Jheng‐Yan Wu; Ting‐Hui Liu; Wan‐Hsuan Hsu; Ya‐Wen Tsai; Po‐Yu Huang; Chih‐Cheng Lai
paper_title: Efficacy of nirmatrelvir and ritonavir for post‐acute COVID‐19 sequelae beyond 3 months of SARS‐CoV‐2 infection

summary: This retrospective cohort study of 2.4 million patients examines the long-term risk of herpes zoster (HZ) infection following COVID-19 recovery, finding a significantly elevated HZ risk in the COVID-19 cohort (HR 1.59) over 12 months. The study does not test a treatment intervention but rather observes the natural epidemiological association between COVID-19 and HZ risk.
paper_authors: Yi‐Chen Chen; Chung‐Han Ho; Ting‐Hui Liu; Jheng‐Yan Wu; Po‐Yu Huang; Ya‐Wen Tsai; Chih‐Cheng Lai
paper_title: Long‐term risk of herpes zoster following COVID‐19: A retrospective cohort study of 2 442 686 patients

summary: Prospective longitudinal study tracking hospitalized COVID-19 patients over 24 months to examine post-COVID symptoms and inflammatory markers. Findings show 37-39% of patients had persistent symptoms associated with prolonged inflammation, which gradually resolved by 24 months post-infection and after vaccination.
paper_authors: Siew‐Wai Fong; Yun Shan Goh; Anthony Torres‐Ruesta; Zi Wei Chang; Yi‐Hao Chan; Vanessa Kexin Neo; Bernett Lee; Kaibo Duan; Siti Naqiah Amrun; Nicholas Kim‐Wah Yeo; Hsiuyi V. Chen; Matthew Zirui Tay; Guillaume Carissimo; Seow Yen Tan; Yee‐Sin Leo; David C. Lye; Laurent Renia; Barnaby Edward Young; Lisa F. P. Ng
paper_title: Prolonged inflammation in patients hospitalized for coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID‐19) resolves 2 years after infection

summary: Large-scale retrospective study examining prevalence and risk factors for long COVID 6-12 months after Omicron infection in 6,242 nonhospitalized patients in Hong Kong. Found 55% reported long COVID symptoms with fatigue most common; identified female gender, middle age, obesity, comorbidities, and specific acute-phase symptoms as significant risk factors.
paper_authors: Jingyuan Luo; Jialing Zhang; Hiu To Tang; Hoi Ki Wong; Aiping Lyu; Chun Hoi Cheung; Zhaoxiang Bian
paper_title: Prevalence and risk factors of long COVID 6–12 months after infection with the Omicron variant among nonhospitalized patients in Hong Kong

summary: Retrospective cohort study using propensity score matching to evaluate whether nirmatrelvir-ritonavir treatment reduces the long-term risk of neuropsychiatric sequelae in nonhospitalized COVID-19 patients. Treatment with nirmatrelvir-ritonavir was associated with significantly reduced risks of neuropsychiatric complications including dementia, depression, insomnia, and anxiety disorder during the 90-day to 1-year follow-up period.
paper_authors: Ting‐Hui Liu; Jheng‐Yan Wu; Po‐Yu Huang; Ya‐Wen Tsai; Chih‐Cheng Lai
paper_title: The effect of nirmatrelvir‐ritonavir on the long‐term risk of neuropsychiatric sequelae following COVID‐19

summary: Prospective cohort study evaluated Paxlovid (nirmatrelvir/ritonavir) effects on long COVID risk in 647 high-risk COVID-19 patients followed 6 months post-discharge. Paxlovid treatment was associated with reduced long COVID incidence and lower COPD assessment test scores compared to untreated patients.
paper_authors: Yu Wang; Danyang Zhao; Wenying Xiao; Jun Shi; Wei Chen; Qin Jia; Ying Zhou; Rongyu Wang; Xubo Chen; Liuliu Feng
paper_title: Paxlovid reduces the risk of Long COVID in patients six months after hospital discharge

summary: This study examines the prevalence of neutralizing autoantibodies against type I interferons in a Danish cohort of 279 long COVID patients compared to 94 controls with mild COVID-19. The findings show that anti-type I IFN autoantibodies are rare and no more prevalent in long COVID patients than controls, suggesting they are unlikely to drive long COVID symptoms.
paper_authors: Kristoffer Skaalum Hansen; Sofie Eg Jørgensen; Morten Kelder Skouboe; Jane Agergaard; Berit Schiøttz‐Christensen; Line Khalidan Vibholm; Martin Tolstrup; Lars Østergaard; Steffen Leth; Trine H. Mogensen
paper_title: Examination of autoantibodies to type I interferon in patients suffering from long COVID

summary: This study compares semen parameters before and after COVID-19 diagnosis in 114 patients and a control group to assess the impact of SARS-CoV-2 on male reproductive function. The findings show significant decreases in semen volume and sperm quality post-infection, with fever during acute infection being a negative risk factor, but this focuses on acute COVID-19 effects rather than long COVID sequelae or treatment interventions.
paper_authors: Cihan Cakir; Goktan Kuspinar; Gizem Kurt; Miray Berber; Kiper Aslan; Isil Kasapoglu; Gurkan Uncu; Berrin Avcı
paper_title: Comparison of semen parameters in the same patients before and after diagnosis of COVID‐19

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining the effect of oral antiviral agents (nirmatrelvir-ritonavir and molnupiravir) on major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) in nonhospitalized COVID-19 patients over 30 days to 1 year. While the study shows antivirals reduced MACE risk, it focuses on acute COVID-19 outcomes and prevention of short-term cardiovascular complications, not long COVID treatment or sequelae.
paper_authors: Ting‐Hui Liu; Min‐Hsiang Chuang; Jheng‐Yan Wu; Po‐Yu Huang; Ya‐Wen Tsai; Wan‐Hsuan Hsu; Chih‐Cheng Lai
paper_title: Effectiveness of oral antiviral agents on long‐term cardiovascular risk in nonhospitalized patients with COVID‐19: A multicenter matched cohort study

summary: This comparative study assessed retinal and vitreous alterations in 38 participants before and after COVID-19 infection using swept-source OCT and angiography, with follow-up imaging at 1 and 3 months post-infection. Findings showed significant retinal changes including ganglion cell thinning, vascular density alterations, and vitreous hyper-reflective dots in 71.1% of patients, suggesting direct or indirect virus-induced ocular injury.
paper_authors: Yuzhu Gao; Yifan Zhang; Kefan Mou; Yilin Liu; Qing Chen; Shulei Man; Hanyue Xu; Jiaming Zhou; Ting Wang; Yating Li; Yi Chen; Ming Zhang
paper_title: Assessment of alterations in the retina and vitreous in pre‐ and post‐COVID‐19 patients using swept‐source optical coherence tomography and angiography: A comparative study

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 30,892 COVID-19 patients examining the association between nutritional deficiency anemia (NDA) and post-acute sequelae using propensity score matching. Patients with NDA had significantly higher risk of post-COVID-19 condition, all-cause hospitalization, and mortality during 90-180 day follow-up.

paper_title: Prior COVID‐19 vaccination and reduced risk of cerebrovascular diseases among COVID‐19 survivors

paper_title: The association of multiple sclerosis, traumatic brain injury, and spinal cord injury to acute and long <scp>COVID</scp>‐19 outcomes

summary: Prospective cohort study tracking functional recovery and fatigue in 92 COVID-19 survivors at 1 and 6 months post-hospitalization. Found that while 50-79% of patients with new impairments at 1 month partially or fully recovered by 6 months, 21-50% did not recover, with lower socioeconomic status and age ≥65 associated with worse outcomes.

paper_title: Physical function and fatigue recovery at <scp>6 months</scp> after hospitalization for <scp>COVID</scp>‐19

summary: Retrospective chart review of 23 children with long COVID examined using cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) to identify mechanisms of exertional symptoms and exercise intolerance. summary: Retrospective cohort study of 82 adolescents with persistent pulmonary symptoms ≥4 weeks post-SARS-CoV-2 infection, followed for ~6.5 months. paper_title: Long‐term pulmonary sequelae in adolescents post‐SARS‐CoV‐2 infection

summary: This observational study followed 41 children hospitalized with COVID-19 pneumonia, assessing pulmonary sequelae at 3 and 6 months post-discharge through clinical assessment, lung ultrasound, and pulmonary function tests. paper_title: The outcomes of COVID‐19 pneumonia in children—clinical, radiographic, and pulmonary function assessment

paper_title: Lung function assessment in children with Long‐Covid syndrome

paper_title: Assessment of dynamic hepatic and renal imaging changes in COVID-19 survivors using T1 mapping and IVIM-DWI

summary: This study describes paired inspiratory/expiratory CT imaging findings in 48 long COVID patients with persistent respiratory symptoms, performed 72 days after symptom onset and at least 30 days after hospital discharge. The study documents high prevalence of air trapping (77%) and other parenchymal abnormalities, but is a descriptive cross-sectional imaging study without any treatment intervention and therefore excluded from the trials pipeline.

paper_title: Air trapping in COVID-19 patients following hospital discharge: retrospective evaluation with paired inspiratory/expiratory thin-section CT

summary: This prospective longitudinal study used hyperpolarized 129Xe MRI to investigate pulmonary diffusion and microvascular perfusion in COVID-19 convalescents, comparing them to healthy controls at baseline (~12.6 weeks) and follow-up (~38 weeks post-symptom onset. While the study documents natural recovery of microvascular function over time, it is an observational cohort study with no treatment intervention—participants were simply followed longitudinally without receiving any treatment as part of the study protocol.

paper_title: Alveolar membrane and capillary function in COVID-19 convalescents: insights from chest MRI

summary: Prospective cohort study examining pulmonary diffusing capacity (DLCO) changes and imaging findings (HRCT, V/Q SPECT) in 153 COVID-19 patients at short-term (5.6 months) and intermediate follow-up (12.5 months). The study found severity-dependent DLCO reduction at short-term follow-up that recovered by intermediate follow-up, though restrictive ventilatory disturbances and morphological changes persisted.

paper_title: Relation of pulmonary diffusing capacity changes to HRCT chest and V/Q SPECT findings at short-term and intermediate follow-up after COVID-19: a prospective cohort study (The secure study)

summary: This retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX research network investigates the association between vitamin D deficiency and post-acute outcomes of COVID-19 in 16,600 propensity-matched patients. The study found that vitamin D deficiency was associated with higher risk of ED visits, hospitalization, and death during 90-180 day follow-up, but not with post-COVID-19 condition diagnosis.

paper_title: Association between vitamin D deficiency and post-acute outcomes of SARS-CoV-2 infection

summary: This pilot observational study examined 88 patients with post-COVID manifestations, comparing 68 with herpesvirus reactivation (CMV, EBV, HHV6) to 20 controls without detectable herpesvirus DNA. Patients with herpesvirus reactivation showed more frequent fever, headache, neuropsychological disorders, pulmonary abnormalities, myalgia, and elevated inflammatory markers, suggesting herpesvirus reactivation may contribute to post-COVID syndrome severity.

paper_title: Herpesvirus infections and post-COVID-19 manifestations: a pilot observational study

summary: This cross-sectional study recruited 80 long COVID patients without prior rheumatic disease diagnosis to assess the prevalence and overlap of inflammatory rheumatic diseases (IRD) symptoms and biomarkers. The study found IRD in 6.25% of patients and documented significant symptom and biomarker overlap between long COVID and rheumatic diseases, but did not test any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Entzündlich rheumatische Erkrankungen bei PatientInnen mit Post-COVID-Syndrom

summary: This study investigates DNA damage in COVID-19 survivors using the comet assay method, comparing damage levels during the acute infection period versus the post-COVID period across ICU and non-ICU patients. paper_title: Investigating DNA damage caused by COVID-19 and influenza in post COVID-19

summary: Retrospective observational study of 85 severe/critical COVID-19 patients who received inpatient rehabilitation targeting neuromuscular and respiratory recovery in a Turkish hospital. paper_title: Rehabilitative management of post-acute COVID-19: clinical pictures and outcomes

summary: Prospective cohort study evaluating olfactory and chemosensory function recovery in 72 patients with sudden smell loss due to acute COVID-19 infection. At 5 weeks post-infection, 37% had persistent olfactory dysfunction, with odor threshold detection more affected than odor identification.

paper_title: Long-standing gustatory and olfactory dysfunction in COVID-19 patients: a prospective study

summary: Nationwide cohort study comparing long COVID symptoms in 37,522 SARS-CoV-2 positive children (0-17 years) to 78,037 controls via electronic questionnaire. Found that long COVID symptoms lasting >4 weeks were common in both groups but more frequent in infected school-age children (0.8% difference), with most symptoms resolving within 1-5 months.
paper_authors: Luise Borch; Mette Holm; Maria Knudsen; Svend Ellermann-Eriksen; Soeren Hagstroem
paper_title: Long COVID symptoms and duration in SARS-CoV-2 positive children — a nationwide cohort study

summary: The NEUROCOG-COVID study evaluated long-term cognitive and psychiatric outcomes in 74 patients hospitalized for severe COVID-19, finding that 73% presented with cognitive disorders including executive dysfunction (66%), memory disorders (31%), and language disorders (19%). The study characterizes the neuropsychological profile of post-COVID cognitive impairment but does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

paper_title: Long-term neuropsychological consequences of severe COVID-19 infection: the NEUROCOG-COVID study

summary: This prospective follow-up study assessed persistent respiratory symptoms and pulmonary function in 50 children 3 months post-COVID-19 infection. The study found respiratory symptoms persisted in 28% of patients with abnormalities in FEV1/FVC, lung clearance index, and DLCO, suggesting ongoing inflammatory effects despite mild acute disease.
paper_authors: Gökçen Kartal Öztürk; Burçin Beken; Sümeyra Doğan; Himmet Haluk Akar
paper_title: Pulmonary function tests in the follow-up of children with COVID-19

summary: This prospective study compared post-COVID-19 symptoms in 200 children infected with Delta vs Omicron variants, assessed via questionnaire >12 weeks after infection. Delta variant infections showed significantly higher rates of weakness, fatigue, anxiety disorder, and gastrointestinal changes compared to Omicron.
paper_authors: Sema Yildirim Arslan; Gulhadiye Avcu; Zumrut Sahbudak Bal; Asli Arslan; Feristah Ferda Ozkinay; Zafer Kurugol
paper_title: Evaluation of post-COVID symptoms of the SARS-CoV-2 Delta and Omicron variants in children: a prospective study

summary: Prospective cohort study examining age-related prevalence and symptoms of post-COVID-19 condition in 785 children followed for 6 months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection. Found 8% incidence of PCC with fatigue as the most common symptom, and identified age-group-specific associated factors (gastrointestinal/neurological symptoms in ages 0-2, comorbidities in older children).
paper_authors: Yixin Wu; Xiangrong Sun; Jingyun Yang; Hailin Fan; Ouxuan Jin; Liwei Tang; Meixian Zhang; Lizhen Wang
paper_title: Age differences in prevalence and symptoms of post-COVID-19 condition among children: a prospective cohort study

summary: A prospective multicenter registry study of 458 children with preceding COVID-19 assessed the prevalence of thyroid autoimmunity and dysfunction, finding 6.6% newly diagnosed thyroid autoimmunity and 4.0% ultrasound-proven autoimmune thyroiditis with no association to vaccination. The study documents long-lasting thyroid alterations in 73.3% of affected children but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

paper_title: Thyroid disturbances after COVID-19 and the effect of vaccination in children: a prospective tri-center registry analysis

summary: Longitudinal study reassessing cardiopulmonary function in 13 children with post-COVID-19 and 23 matched controls at baseline and 6-month follow-up using exercise testing. While this is a valid longitudinal observational study, it does not evaluate a specific intervention or treatment—it passively follows natural recovery without assigning any treatment to participants.

paper_title: Light at the end of the tunnel? Follow-up of cardiopulmonary function in children with post-COVID-19

summary: A retrospective clinical analysis of 44 long COVID patients presenting with neurologic symptoms at a Chicago neuro-infectious disease clinic between 2020-2022. The study documents presentation patterns, diagnostic findings (cognitive assessments, EEG, autoantibodies, CSF), and 12-month outcomes, finding that most patients continued experiencing neurologic symptoms though over half reported moderate or marked improvement.
paper_authors: Lauren E. Brandes; Daniel Orme; Adriana Bermeo-Ovalle; Fabian Sierra Morales
paper_title: Clinical and diagnostic features of long-COVID patients presenting with neurologic symptoms in Chicago

summary: This multicenter study (PoCoRe) examined dysfunctional coping patterns (avoidance-endurance model) in 481 post-COVID syndrome patients at the start and end of multimodal rehabilitation. The majority of patients (81.8%) exhibited dysfunctional illness behavior at baseline, with significant shifts toward adaptive/functional patterns during rehabilitation, though 10-15% deteriorated.
paper_authors: Alexa Kupferschmitt; Christoph Herrmann; Michael Jöbges; Stefan Kelm; Gerhard Sütfels; Thomas H. Loew; Monika Hasenbring; Volker Köllner
paper_title: Bedeutung von „avoidance“ und „endurance“ beim Post-COVID-Syndrom

summary: Extension cohort study documenting rheumatic and musculoskeletal symptoms in hospitalized COVID-19 survivors at 3 and 6 months post-hospitalization via telephone surveys. Found that 59.6% had persistent symptoms at 6 months, with fatigue (31.6%), joint pain (18.6%), and myalgia (15.1%) being the most common rheumatologic manifestations, with female patients at higher risk.
paper_authors: Fatih Karaarslan; Fulya Demircioğlu Güneri; Sinan Kardeş
paper_title: Long COVID: rheumatologic/musculoskeletal symptoms in hospitalized COVID-19 survivors at 3 and 6 months

summary: Observational cohort study examining associations between COVID-19 vaccination and long COVID symptoms in 28,356 UK participants infected with SARS-CoV-2 prior to vaccination. First and second vaccination doses were associated with 12.8% and 8.8% reductions in long COVID odds respectively, with sustained improvement after the second dose.
paper_authors: Alexandros A. Drosos; Eleftherios Pelechas; Paraskevi V. Voulgari
paper_title: Long COVID from rheumatology perspective: a simple mimicker or promoter of autoimmunity?

summary: This longitudinal descriptive study evaluated swallowing abnormalities in 127 post-COVID-19 patients with oropharyngeal dysphagia using fiberoptic endoscopic assessment at 1-4 weeks post-discharge. The study identified risk factors for aspiration (higher EAT-10 scores, dysphonia, respiratory rate, mechanical ventilation duration) and found associations with ageusia/anosmia, but is observational without testing any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Ahmed Mohamed Zayed; Omayma Afsah; Tamer Elhadidy; Tamer Abou-Elsaad
paper_title: Swallowing Evaluation in Post-COVID-19 Patients with Oropharyngeal Dysphagia

summary: Prospective cohort study of 26 post-COVID patients examining bronchoalveolar lavage cellularity, lung function impairment, and HRCT findings. Found that persistent inflammatory responses with CD4+ T-cell lymphocytosis in the lungs were associated with reduced lung function, suggesting a role for alveolar inflammation in post-COVID pathogenesis.
paper_authors: Maximilian Robert Gysan; Antje Lehmann; Dominik Bernitzky; Andreas Zech; Jonas Brugger; Helmut Prosch; Marco Idzko; Daniela Gompelmann
paper_title: Immunophenotyping of bronchoalveolar lavage and functional impairment in post-COVID syndrome

summary: This cross-sectional study compared olfactory function in acutely ill COVID-19 patients versus recovered patients using a psychophysical identification test. While it documents persistent olfactory dysfunction as a long-COVID sequela, it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Jacopo Pasquini; Carlo Maremmani; Stefano Salvadori; Vincenzo Silani; Nicola Ticozzi
paper_title: Testing olfactory dysfunction in acute and recovered COVID-19 patients: a single center study in Italy

summary: This study followed 165 COVID-19 survivors at 6 months post-hospitalization to assess the prevalence and predictors of long-term neurological manifestations. Fatigue (34%), memory/attention problems (31%), and sleep disorders (30%) were common, with 40% exhibiting neurological abnormalities; older age, comorbidities, and COVID-19 severity were independent predictors.
paper_authors: Andrea Pilotto; Viviana Cristillo; Stefano Cotti Piccinelli; Nicola Zoppi; Giulio Bonzi; Davide Sattin; Silvia Schiavolin; Alberto Raggi; Antonio Canale; Stefano Gipponi; Ilenia Libri; Martina Frigerio; Michela Bezzi; Matilde Leonardi; Alessandro Padovani
paper_title: Long-term neurological manifestations of COVID-19: prevalence and predictive factors

summary: This observational study evaluated a neuropsychological assessment model in 12 post-acute COVID-19 patients receiving rehabilitation, using cognitive tests (MMSE, MoCA) and psychological scales (AD-R, NPI) at baseline, discharge, and 3-month follow-up. Patients showed cognitive impairment at baseline with improvement in depression and behavioral scores, suggesting rehabilitation may benefit psychological and behavioral outcomes in post-COVID patients.
paper_authors: Silvia Bonizzato; Ada Ghiggia; Francesco Ferraro; Emanuela Galante
paper_title: Cognitive, behavioral, and psychological manifestations of COVID-19 in post-acute rehabilitation setting: preliminary data of an observational study

summary: A 9-month prospective follow-up study of 95 COVID-19 patients examining the prevalence and predictors of long-COVID symptoms. Found that female sex, higher symptom burden, and acute neuropsychiatric manifestations were associated with chronic fatigue syndrome and cognitive deficits at follow-up, but this is an observational study with no treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Fatemeh Sadat Mirfazeli; Atiye Sarabi-Jamab; Victor Pereira-Sanchez; Alireza Kordi; Behnam Shariati; Seyed Vahid Shariat; Salar Bahrami; Shabnam Nohesara; Mostafa Almasi-Dooghaee; Seyed Hamid Reza Faiz
paper_title: Chronic fatigue syndrome and cognitive deficit are associated with acute-phase neuropsychiatric manifestations of COVID-19: A 9-month follow-up study

summary: This cross-sectional study compared long COVID prevalence and symptoms in 118 healthcare workers with prior COVID-19 infection versus 118 matched controls without infection in Morocco. The study found 47.4% long COVID prevalence with predominant symptoms of asthenia, myalgia, and brain fog, but does not test any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Hicham El Otmani; Salma Nabili; Malika Berrada; Salma Bellakhdar; Bouchra El Moutawakil; Mohammed Abdoh Rafai
paper_title: Prevalence, characteristics and risk factors in a Moroccan cohort of Long-Covid-19

summary: A retrospective cohort study of 137 COVID-19 patients evaluated 1 year post-discharge to identify predictors of persistent brain fog using cognitive and psychological assessments. Depression was identified as the strongest independent predictor of cognitive complaints after adjusting for demographic and clinical variables.
paper_authors: Viviana Cristillo; Andrea Pilotto; Stefano Cotti Piccinelli; Stefano Gipponi; Matilde Leonardi; Michela Bezzi; Alessandro Padovani
paper_title: Predictors of “brain fog” 1 year after COVID-19 disease

summary: A matched cohort study using German health care data comparing incident autoimmune disease rates between 641,704 COVID-19 patients and matched controls followed 3-15 months post-infection. Patients with prior COVID-19 had 43% higher likelihood of developing new-onset autoimmune diseases, with strongest associations for vasculitis.
paper_authors: Falko Tesch; Franz Ehm; Annika Vivirito; Danny Wende; Manuel Batram; Friedrich Loser; Simone Menzer; Josephine Jacob; Martin Roessler; Martin Seifert; Barbara Kind; Christina König; Claudia Schulte; Tilo Buschmann; Dagmar Hertle; Pedro Ballesteros; Stefan Baßler; Barbara Bertele; Thomas Bitterer; Cordula Riederer; Franziska Sobik; Lukas Reitzle; Christa Scheidt-Nave; Jochen Schmitt
paper_title: Incident autoimmune diseases in association with SARS-CoV-2 infection: a matched cohort study

summary: Prospective cohort study following 191 mild-to-moderate COVID-19 patients for 1.5 years to assess prevalence and characteristics of persistent pain symptoms. Found 31.9% experienced persistent pain (headache 29.8%, myalgia 5.8%, neuropathic pain 4.2%) with female gender and neuropathic pain as predictors of long-term headaches.
paper_authors: Emel Oguz-Akarsu; Gizem Gullu; Erhan Kilic; Yasemin Dinç; Gonul Akdag; Cansu Rehber; Necdet Karli
paper_title: Beyond the acute: pain in long COVID survivors at 1.5 years

summary: This prospective observational cohort study examines perioperative outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer patients with prior COVID-19 infection versus unexposed controls. While the paper documents increased pulmonary complications and longer operative times in COVID-exposed patients, it is not about long COVID treatment—it focuses on acute surgical risk in cancer patients, not long COVID symptoms or interventions.
paper_authors: Hanbo Pan; Fan Shen; Ningyuan Zou; Yu Tian; Jiaqi Zhang; Yixing Tao; Hongda Zhu; Jia Huang; Qingquan Luo
paper_title: Impact of prior COVID-19 infection on perioperative outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer patients: a prospective observational cohort study

summary: This retrospective cohort study compares cerebrospinal fluid and serum cytokine profiles in post- versus para-infectious Guillain-Barré syndrome associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection. While the paper studies a COVID-related neurological complication, it is not about long COVID (which focuses on persistent multi-system symptoms weeks to months post-infection) and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

paper_title: COVID-19-associated serum and cerebrospinal fluid cytokines in post- versus para-infectious SARS-CoV-2-related Guillain–Barré syndrome

summary: Observational cohort study of 275 patients 3 months post-COVID-19 evaluating serological markers, pulmonary function tests, and chest CT findings. Anti-S antibody levels were independently associated with reduced diffusing capacity and severe acute COVID-19, but the study did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Interactions and clinical implications of serological and respiratory variables 3 months after acute COVID-19

summary: A prospective observational study evaluating coenzyme Q10 and alpha lipoic acid (Requpero) in 174 chronic COVID syndrome patients, comparing 116 treated patients with 58 untreated controls. While it clearly characterizes the fatigue phenotype in long COVID, it does not evaluate any treatment intervention and is a non-interventional descriptive study rather than a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Isabelle V. Carter; Anna May; Isabella C. Hsieh; Juliane Torer; David Rosenberg; Kingman P. Strohl
paper_title: The fatigue spectrum in a community-based long haul COVID cohort

summary: Longitudinal study profiling lipoproteins and inflammatory cytokines in long COVID patients at multiple timepoints (5-20 months post-infection) using NMR spectroscopy and flow cytometry. Found persistent hyperlipidemia and altered inflammatory markers in LC compared to acute COVID and healthy controls, but does not test or evaluate any intervention.
paper_authors: Gyuntae Bae; Zhiqi Yang; Daniele Bucci; Claire Wegner; Hartmut Schäfer; Yogesh Singh; Caterina Lonati; Christoph Trautwein
paper_title: Longitudinal lipoprotein and inflammatory mediators analysis uncover persisting inflammation and hyperlipidemia following SARS-CoV-2 infection in long COVID-19

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing circadian rhythm disorders and anxiety levels in 278 patients with and without COVID-19 history. Found that post-COVID patients had significantly higher rates of delayed sleep phase disorder and elevated anxiety levels, establishing an association between post-COVID anxiety and circadian rhythm disturbances.
paper_authors: Dmytro I. Boiko; Andrii M. Skrypnikov; Anastasiia D. Shkodina; Mohammad Mehedi Hasan; Ghulam Md. Ashraf; Md. Habibur Rahman
paper_title: RETRACTED ARTICLE: Circadian rhythm disorder and anxiety as mental health complications in post-COVID-19

summary: This observational cohort study followed 76 elite athletes infected with SARS-CoV-2 and 51 uninfected controls, assessing cardiac function via echocardiography at 1, 5, and 9 months post-infection. The study found elevated global longitudinal strain shortly after infection but within normal ranges, with no cardiac injury detected and no adverse effects from return to training.
paper_authors: Jonas Zacher; Niklas Joisten; Thomas Schmidt; Hans-Georg Predel
paper_title: Subacute and long-term effects of COVID-19 on cardiac health and function in German elite athletes assessed by strain analysis: a speckle tracking echocardiography observational trial

summary: This pilot study evaluated mountain spa rehabilitation (high-altitude environment combined with targeted spa therapy) in 14 post-COVID-19 patients compared to 15 healthy controls. The intervention resulted in significant improvements in clinical symptoms, lung function, and platelet mitochondrial respiration markers.
paper_authors: Anna Gvozdjáková; Zuzana Sumbalová; Jarmila Kucharská; Zuzana Rausová; Eleonóra Kovalčíková; Timea Takácsová; Plácido Navas; Guillermo López-Lluch; Viliam Mojto; Patrik Palacka
paper_title: Mountain spa rehabilitation improved health of patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome: pilot study

summary: Prospective cohort study examining renal function changes in young healthy adults following mild or asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection over 6 months. Finds mild COVID-19 associated with reduced creatinine clearance and albumin leakage without acute kidney injury.
paper_authors: Khalid Al Rumaihi; Kareim Khalafalla; Mohamed Arafa; Arun Nair; Ahmad Al Bishawi; Areen Fino; Faheem Sirtaj; Mohamed Khair Ella; Haitham ElBardisi; Muhammad Abu Khattab; Ahmad Majzoub
paper_title: COVID-19 and renal involvement: a prospective cohort study assessing the impact of mild SARS-CoV-2 infection on the kidney function of young healthy males

summary: Naturalistic observational study evaluating cytokine-blocking agents (anakinra, tocilizumab, sarilumab, reparixin, mavrilimumab) for preventing post-COVID depression in 588 COVID-19 survivors (131 treated with cytokine blockers). Cytokine-blocking treatment reduced depressive symptomatology severity and development of clinically relevant depression, with effects mediated by lowering systemic inflammation.
paper_authors: Mariagrazia Palladini; Alessia A. Azzalin; Margherita Bessi; Rebecca De Lorenzo; Patrizia Rovere-Querini; Francesco Benedetti; Mario Gennaro Mazza
paper_title: Cytokine Blockade Attenuates Inflammation and Improves Depressive Psychopathology After COVID-19: A Naturalistic Observational Study

summary: This study examines variation in primary care scheduling and follow-up after COVID-19 hospitalization in Michigan during 2020, focusing on patterns of outpatient care rather than testing a treatment intervention. It does not evaluate a specific treatment or intervention but rather describes existing follow-up practices and their variation across hospitals.
paper_authors: Hallie C. Prescott; Bonnie Cheng; Chelsea Abshire; Megan O’Malley; Scott A. Flanders; Renuka Tipirneni; Vineet Chopra
paper_title: Variation in Scheduling and Receipt of Primary Care Follow-up After Hospitalization for COVID-19 in Michigan

summary: A 3-year longitudinal study examining epigenetic aging in 54 volunteers (27 with COVID-19 history) using eight different epigenetic clocks. COVID-19 exposure was associated with accelerated epigenetic aging in several clocks (DNAmGrimAge, DNAmGrimAge2, DNAmFitAge), suggesting mild long-term effects on aging trajectories.
paper_authors: Gabor Farkas; Zahira El Mahdaouy; Gergely Babszky; Matyas Jokai; Ferenc Torma; Yaodong Gu; Ricardo Pinho; Ildiko Miklossy; Juozas Gordevicius; András Benczúr; Csaba Kerepesi; Zsolt Radak
paper_title: Associations of epigenetic aging and COVID- 19: A 3-year longitudinal study

summary: A monocentric cohort study characterizing post-COVID-19 syndrome in outpatients 3-10 months after mild infection, comparing COVID-positive (n=418) and COVID-negative (n=89) patients. Found that 53% of COVID-positive patients reported persistent symptoms, with fatigue, smell/taste disorder, dyspnea, and memory impairment independently associated with COVID-19.
paper_authors: Florian Desgranges; Eliana Tadini; Aline Munting; Jean Regina; Paraskevas Filippidis; Benjamin Viala; Eleftherios Karachalias; Véronique Suttels; David Haefliger; Eleftheria Kampouri; Mathias Van Singer; Jonathan Tschopp; Laurence Rochat Stettler; Siméon Schaad; Thomas Brahier; Olivier Hugli; Yolanda Mueller; Alexandre Gouveia; Onya Opota; Pierre-Nicolas Carron; Benoît Guery; Matthaios Papadimitriou-Olivgeris; Noémie Boillat-Blanco
paper_title: Post‑COVID‑19 Syndrome in Outpatients: a Cohort Study

summary: This study examines whether COVID-19 vaccination affects the evolution of six cardinal symptoms in patients with post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (long COVID). The authors assess the association between vaccination status and symptom progression over time in a cohort of long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Mayssam Nehme; Olivia Braillard; Julien Salamun; Frédérique Jacquerioz; Delphine S. Courvoisier; Hervé Spechbach; Idris Guessous
paper_title: Symptoms After COVID-19 Vaccination in Patients with Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2

summary: Multicenter observational study tracking recovery trajectories of loss of smell and taste in previously hospitalized COVID-19 survivors over multiple timepoints. Describes natural recovery patterns rather than evaluating any intervention, with most patients recovering by follow-up but some developing symptoms de novo.
paper_authors: César Fernández-de-las-Peñas; José D. Martín-Guerrero; Esperanza Navarro-Pardo; Ignacio Cancela-Cilleruelo; Paloma Moro-López-Menchero; Oscar J. Pellicer-Valero
paper_title: Exploring Trajectory Curves from Loss of Smell and Taste in Previously Hospitalized COVID-19 Survivors: the LONG-COVID-EXP-CM Multicenter Study

summary: A cross-sectional study of 441 adults presenting to a COVID-19 recovery clinic that identifies two distinct symptom clusters in long COVID patients: neuropsychiatric and pulmonary presentations. The study characterizes demographic and clinical differences between clusters but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Valerie Danesh; Alejandro C. Arroliga; James A. Bourgeois; Leanne M. Boehm; Michael J. McNeal; Andrew J. Widmer; Tresa M. McNeal; Shelli R. Kesler
paper_title: Symptom Clusters Seen in Adult COVID-19 Recovery Clinic Care Seekers

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining racial/ethnic differences in post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection using EHR data from 62,339 COVID-19 patients in New York City. Black and Hispanic patients showed significantly different odds of developing PASC symptoms and conditions (diabetes, headaches, dyspnea, chest pain) compared to white patients.
paper_authors: Dhruv Khullar; Yongkang Zhang; Chengxi Zang; Zhenxing Xu; Fei Wang; Mark G. Weiner; Thomas W. Carton; Russell L. Rothman; Jason P. Block; Rainu Kaushal
paper_title: Racial/Ethnic Disparities in Post-acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Infection in New York: an EHR-Based Cohort Study from the RECOVER Program

summary: Retrospective observational cohort study of 530 acute COVID-19 survivors followed ~1 year post-infection to assess persistent symptoms and functional limitations. Found 41.5% reported worse health, 44.2% reported persistent symptoms, and significant limitations in physical effort tolerance, with no intervention tested.
