paper_title: Health Status, Persistent Symptoms, and Effort Intolerance One Year After Acute COVID-19 Infection

summary: Prospective observational cohort study of 1,038 COVID-19 patients (hospitalized and outpatient) followed for 60-90 days to assess PASC development and associated demographic/clinical factors. Found 29.8% developed PASC with fatigue and dyspnea as most common symptoms; hospitalization, diabetes, and higher BMI were independent risk factors, while certain populations (organ transplant recipients, Medicaid insured) had lower PASC rates.
paper_authors: Sun M. Yoo; Teresa C. Liu; Yash Motwani; Myung S. Sim; Nisha Viswanathan; Nathan Samras; Felicia Hsu; Neil S. Wenger
paper_title: Factors Associated with Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC) After Diagnosis of Symptomatic COVID-19 in the Inpatient and Outpatient Setting in a Diverse Cohort

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining the incidence of chronic kidney disease (CKD) following acute COVID-19 using South Carolina statewide registry data from March 2020 to January 2022. Findings show COVID-19 was not independently associated with CKD after accounting for severity of illness and acute kidney injury.
paper_authors: Roy O. Mathew; Jiajia Zhang; Xueying Yang; Shujie Chen; Bankole Olatosi; Xiaoming Li
paper_title: Incidence of Chronic Kidney Disease Following Acute Coronavirus Disease 2019 Based on South Carolina Statewide Data

summary: This paper analyzes data from the RECOVER-Adult observational cohort to determine the incidence and prevalence of post-COVID ME/CFS among adults infected with SARS-CoV-2. The study found that ME/CFS develops at a significantly higher rate in COVID-infected participants (2.66 per 100 person-years) compared to uninfected controls (0.93 per 100 person-years), with 4.5% of infected participants meeting diagnostic criteria.
paper_authors: Suzanne D. Vernon; Tianyu Zheng; Hyungrok Do; Vincent C. Marconi; Leonard A. Jason; Nora G. Singer; Benjamin H. Natelson; Zaki A. Sherif; Hector Fabio Bonilla; Emily Taylor; Janet M. paper_title: Incidence and Prevalence of Post-COVID-19 Myalgic Encephalomyelitis: A Report from the Observational RECOVER-Adult Study

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining PASC prevalence 1 year post-infection in 863 diverse urban adults, with logistic regression identifying predictors. Reveals 54.1% PASC prevalence with significant racial/ethnic disparities and higher odds in females and those experiencing loneliness.
paper_authors: Christopher J. Gonzalez; Jennifer D. Lau; Mangala Rajan; Assem Jabri; Erica Phillips
paper_title: Predictors of Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19 in a Diverse Urban Population

summary: Observational cohort study of 1,407 PASC patients identifying four distinct health-related quality of life profiles using PROMIS-GH items at baseline and 12-month follow-up. Patients improved modestly over time with improvement varying by symptom profile, but no treatment intervention was delivered or evaluated.
paper_authors: Brittany Lapin; Yadi Li; Kristin Englund; Irene L. Katzan
paper_title: Health-Related Quality of Life for Patients with Post-Acute COVID-19 Syndrome: Identification of Symptom Clusters and Predictors of Long-Term Outcomes

summary: This cross-sectional study examines sleep disturbance severity and its correlates in post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) patients, with focus on racial disparities. Findings emphasize the importance of identifying sleep disturbances in PASC and highlight racial inequities, informing the need for interventions to reduce PASC-related disparities.
paper_authors: Cinthya Pena-Orbea; Brittany Lapin; Yadi Li; Kristin Englund; Catherine Heinzinger; Nancy Foldvary-Schaefer; Reena Mehra
paper_title: Sleep Disturbance Severity and Correlates in Post-acute Sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC)

summary: A prospective cohort study following 64 patients hospitalized for severe COVID-19 at 6 and 12 months post-discharge to assess long-term symptoms and respiratory outcomes. The study found persistent dyspnea, fatigue, anxiety, depression, and pulmonary deficits in significant proportions of patients, without any intervention being tested.
paper_authors: Giuseppe Pio Martino; Devis Benfaremo; Giuseppina Bitti; Gianluca Valeri; Laura Postacchini; Annalisa Marchetti; Stefano Angelici; Gianluca Moroncini
paper_title: 6 and 12 month outcomes in patients following COVID-19-related hospitalization: a prospective monocentric study

summary: This cross-sectional study examined 72 ambulatory post-COVID-19 patients to determine relationships between physical fitness, cardiopulmonary function, and patient-reported symptom severity. Greater physical fitness and cardiopulmonary function were associated with lower severity of symptoms including fatigue and dyspnea, suggesting exercise and physical conditioning may help reduce persistent post-COVID symptoms.

paper_title: Relationship between the severity of persistent symptoms, physical fitness, and cardiopulmonary function in post-COVID-19 condition. A population-based analysis

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining the risk of new-onset type 2 diabetes after SARS-CoV-2 infection using EHR data from over 247,000 patients across three cohorts (exposed, unexposed, and historical controls). Found that individuals exposed to SARS-CoV-2 had 1.64× higher risk of new-onset diabetes compared to historical controls, with findings consistent across sociodemographic subgroups.
paper_authors: Jithin Sam Varghese; Mohammed K. Ali; Yi Guo; William T. Donahoo; Rosette J. Chakkalakal
paper_title: Risk of New-Onset Diabetes Before and During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Real-World Cohort Study

summary: Prospective observational study evaluating lung ultrasound as a tool for detecting fibrotic-like changes 6 months after severe COVID-19 pneumonia compared to CT imaging. Found that LUS score was significantly associated with CT fibrotic patterns, but this is a diagnostic/prognostic study without any treatment intervention—patients were only assessed, not treated.

paper_title: Lung ultrasound in the follow-up of severe COVID-19 pneumonia: six months evaluation and comparison with CT

summary: Population-based cohort study in Ontario comparing health service use within 12 months post-discharge between adults with and without pre-existing disabilities hospitalized for COVID-19. Finds that people with disabilities had significantly higher rates of ambulatory care, ED visits, and hospital admissions even after adjustment for sociodemographic factors and comorbidities.

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines ethnic differences in long COVID symptom burden and impact on daily life among 864 patients attending a Long COVID Clinic in Denmark. The study describes symptom prevalence and disparities rather than evaluating any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Ethnic Differences in Symptom Burden, Work and Daily Life: A Study of Long COVID Patients in Denmark

summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 294 COVID-19 survivors (89 ICU, 205 non-ICU) for up to 24 months post-discharge to characterize persistent symptoms and medical specialty usage patterns. The study documented high incidence of ongoing symptoms (neuromuscular, respiratory, fatigue, cardiovascular) and associated specialty care needs but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Benjamin Musheyev; Montek S. Boparai; Reona Kimura; Rebeca Janowicz; Stacey Pamlanye; Wei Hou; Tim Q. Duong
paper_title: Longitudinal medical subspecialty follow-up of critically and non-critically ill hospitalized COVID-19 survivors up to 24 months after discharge

summary: Retrospective analysis of administrative claims data from Lombardy examining drug dispensation and diagnostic test usage in 46,574 COVID-19 recovered patients over 18 months post-infection as proxies for post-COVID healthcare impact. Findings show sustained elevated dispensation of drugs for specific conditions (anticoagulants, antidepressants, diabetes, airways disease) indicating ongoing post-COVID morbidity, but this is not a treatment intervention trial.

paper_title: Post-COVID condition: dispensation of drugs and diagnostic tests as proxies of healthcare impact

summary: Observational study of 55 older patients (mean age 82.3) assessing lung CT findings and functional status 3-6 months after COVID-19 pneumonia hospitalization. Most acute CT abnormalities resolved by 6 months; mild fibrotic changes persisted in 40% but were not associated with functional decline, which correlated instead with pre-existing comorbidities.
paper_authors: Chiara Di Pentima; Sara Cecchini; Francesco Spannella; Federico Giulietti; Massimiliano Allevi; Paola Schiavi; Francesca Carnevali; Lorenzo Zoppi; Maria Carmela Ciociola; Fiammetta Ventura; Gina Dragano; Piero Giordano; Enrico Paci; Riccardo Sarzani
paper_title: Radiological lung sequelae, functional status and symptoms in older patients 3 and 6 months after hospitalization for COVID-19 pneumonia

summary: This retrospective cohort study used administrative claims data from Lombardy, Italy to assess healthcare resource utilization in 315,593 individuals who recovered from the second COVID-19 wave and 269,605 from the third wave. The study found that hospitalizations, emergency room visits, and outpatient visits post-infection were similar to pre-pandemic levels, but drug dispensation and diagnostic testing increased notably for cardiorespiratory and blood system conditions.

paper_title: Post-recovery impact of the second and third SARS-CoV-2 infection waves on healthcare resource utilization in Lombardy, Italy

summary: This study analyzed blood cell counts and haematological parameters in 83 long COVID patients compared to 70 healthy controls, finding persistent abnormalities in 81% of patients. The findings suggest impaired immune responses including reduced lymphocytes and IgM memory B cells may contribute to long-term symptoms.
paper_authors: Gaetano Bergamaschi; Chiara Barteselli; Francesca Calabretta; Marco Vincenzo Lenti; Stefania Merli; Carlo Maria Rossi; Antonio Di Sabatino
paper_title: Haematological sequelae in the post-acute phase of symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection

summary: This is a prospective follow-up study of 755 long COVID patients from Italy, tracking symptom persistence at two timepoints (mean 223 days and 453 days post-infection). The study documents natural symptom trajectories and risk factors for persistence without testing any intervention, making it a natural history observational study rather than a treatment trial.

summary: This retrospective cohort study compared hypertensive patients with recent COVID-19 infection (within 6 months) to those without infection to evaluate blood pressure control and vascular stiffness. While the study shows COVID-19 increases arterial stiffness and blood pressure readings, it does not study long COVID (chronic post-COVID syndrome) or test any treatment intervention for long COVID patients.

paper_title: COVID-19 induces greater difficulty in blood pressure control due to increased arterial stiffness

summary: Longitudinal follow-up study of 5,610 COVID-19 patients tracking symptom presence at 1, 3, and 6 months post-infection. Identifies risk factors associated with persistent post-COVID symptoms (female gender, older age, hospitalization, comorbidities) but does not test any intervention or treatment.

paper_title: The presence of symptoms within 6 months after COVID-19: a single-center longitudinal study

summary: This study followed 222 ICU patients hospitalized for severe SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia over 24 months, assessing ventilatory function and diffusion capacity at multiple timepoints. The majority (63%) achieved normalization of lung function by 24 months, with male sex, age, and obesity negatively impacting recovery rates; however, this is a prospective follow-up study documenting natural recovery patterns without any intervention or treatment being tested.

Found that most acute thyroid abnormalities resolved, interferon treatment was associated with modest increases in anti-thyroid antibodies, but thyroid markers did not predict long COVID development.

summary: Retrospective study of 511 COVID-19 survivors examining the incidence of newly diagnosed hyperglycemia and diabetes mellitus and their association with obesity and lipid profiles. Found 3.32% developed new-onset T2DM and 16.82% developed hyperglycemia, with obesity and dyslipidemia as risk factors, but no intervention was tested.

paper_title: Association between newly diagnosed hyperglycemia/diabetes mellitus, atherogenic index of plasma and obesity in post-COVID-19 syndrome patients

summary: This prospective cohort study examines long-term functional outcomes in older adults who received inpatient geriatric rehabilitation following acute COVID-19 infection. While participants were treated with rehabilitation, the study focuses on acute COVID-19 recovery rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks/months post-infection), making it outside the scope of long COVID intervention trials.

paper_title: Long-term outcomes of older adults with acute COVID-19 following inpatient geriatric rehabilitation: a prospective cohort study from the Republic of Ireland

summary: Observational follow-up study investigating new-onset diabetes after COVID-19 (NODAC) and its recovery at 6 months in 1,310 patients. Finds NODAC prevalence of 8.5% with persistence driven by insulin resistance rather than beta-cell dysfunction, but does not test any treatment intervention.

paper_title: New Onset Diabetes After COVID 19 (NODAC) is predominantly due to exacerbated Insulin Resistance (IR) rather than beta cell dysfunction: Lessons from tertiary care hospital data during confluence of two epidemics

summary: Prospective observational study of 21 children with neuro-COVID-19 (with or without MIS-C) admitted to a hospital from January 2021 to January 2022, documenting neurological manifestations and their persistence up to 7 months post-discharge. summary: Observational study of 104 post-acute COVID-19 patients followed with low-field MRI exams over 6-24 months to assess lung opacity severity and evolution. Initial COVID-19 disease severity was associated with increased MRI opacity scores, and moderate to severe opacities persisted in 37% of exams beyond 6 months with no significant change over time.
paper_authors: Lea Azour; Hersh Chandarana; Christoph Maier; James Babb; William Moore
paper_title: Low Field MRI Surveillance 6-24 Months Post-acute COVID-19 Pneumonia: Factors Influencing Severity and Evolution of Lung Opacities

summary: A three-year longitudinal observational study of 47 COVID-19 patients using single-cell RNA sequencing and cytokine profiling to characterize immune dysregulation in long COVID. The study identifies persistent immune abnormalities and Th17-driven chronic inflammation as key features of post-COVID convalescence, but does not test or evaluate any therapeutic intervention.
paper_authors: Tian Zheng; Ru Gao; Yiwei Liu; Yeming Wang; Chao Wu; Li Guo; Lan Chen; Xinming Wang; Yan Xiao; Jingchuan Zhong; Rongling Zhang; Ying Wang; Xianwen Ren; Bin Cao; Lili Ren; Jianwei Wang
paper_title: T cell-driven sustained inflammation and immune dysregulation mimicking immunosenescence for up to three years post-COVID-19

summary: Retrospective observational study of 29 hospital staff with long COVID who underwent physiological assessment (spirometry, 6-minute walk test, exercise testing) followed by an exercise rehabilitation program. The rehabilitation program resulted in significant improvements in 6-minute walk distance and maximum power output, suggesting benefits for physical conditioning and work capacity in long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Y. Crosson Du Cormier; Mélanie Prudent; J.-B. Fassier; Émeric Stauffer
paper_title: Fonction respiratoire et aptitude physique du personnel des Hospices Civils de Lyon présentant un Covid long ; effets d’un programme de réhabilitation à l’effort
paper_journal: Archives des Maladies Professionnelles et de l'Environnement

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed behavioral and emotional problems in 122 children recovered from acute COVID-19 hospitalization in Wuhan, China using parent-reported questionnaires. While the paper follows children post-discharge, it focuses on acute infection recovery and behavioral sequelae rather than persistent long COVID syndrome, and does not test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Han Xiao; Qi Liu; Hong Mei; Qi Xue; Xiaonan Cai; Xinyan Xie; Zhiguo Xia; Yu Zhou; Hui Li; Kaiheng Zhu; Zihao Wan; Ranran Song; Zhisheng Liu
paper_title: Behavioral problems of pediatric patients recovered from COVID-19 in Wuhan, China

summary: Observational study examining cardiac abnormalities in 2,338 COVID-19 patients with long COVID symptoms, focusing on palpitations and arrhythmias detected via 24-hour Holter monitoring and echocardiography. Found inappropriate sinus tachycardia in 60% of symptomatic patients and significant correlation between arrhythmias and reduced myocardial strain.
paper_authors: Rania Hammami; Amine Bahloul; S. Charfeddine; R. Gargouri; Leïla Abid
paper_title: The long COVID: Findings of 24 rhythmic Holter in patients suffering from palpitations

summary: Observational study characterizing cardiovascular manifestations in 126 long COVID patients referred to a specialized cardiovascular clinic. Describes symptoms, diagnostic findings, and identifies that 77% had no new cardiac diagnosis but exhibited exercise intolerance and cardiovascular symptoms without identifiable pathology.
paper_authors: Stephen Y. Wang; Philip Adejumo; Claudia See; Oyere K. Onuma; Edward J. Miller; Erica S. Spatz
paper_title: Characteristics of patients referred to a cardiovascular disease clinic for post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection
paper_journal: American Heart Journal Plus: Cardiology Research and Practice

summary: A prospective case series of 630 young COVID-19 patients evaluated 2 weeks to 1 month post-infection for left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LV-GLS) alterations and correlation with long COVID symptoms. The study found LV-GLS alterations in 52.5% of patients, correlated with dyspnea and chest pain, with 87.5% showing spontaneous improvement at one-month follow-up without intervention.
paper_authors: Hassen Ibn Hadj Amor; S. Charfeddine; K. Salma; Imen Trabelsi; Tansim Slim; H. Rania; Amine Bahloul; Krifa Nesrine; Mely Nadia; Sami Milouchi; G. Jamel; Modarresi Mosalla Zeinab; T. Yemina; Jihen Jdidi; Bishoy Kamel; Adrien Salem; Leïla Abid
paper_title: Left ventricular global longitudinal strain alteration in young patient and correlation with post-COVID syndrome (TUN END COV Study)

summary: This retrospective case series evaluates Enhanced External Counterpulsation (EECP) as a treatment for long COVID symptoms in 7 outpatient centers. Results show significant improvements in fatigue, cardiovascular markers, activity status, and 6-minute walk distance, with all previously unable-to-work patients returning to work post-therapy.
paper_authors: Mohanakrishnan Sathyamoorthy; Monica Verduzco-Gutierrez; Swathi Varanasi; Robyn Ward; John Spertus; Sachin Shah
paper_title: Enhanced external counterpulsation for management of symptoms associated with long COVID
paper_journal: American Heart Journal Plus: Cardiology Research and Practice

summary: Prospective multicenter cohort study examining long-term pulmonary sequelae in COVID-19 survivors over 3 years, comparing outcomes between those with and without diabetes. Diabetes was identified as an independent predictor of persistent radiological abnormalities and pulmonary diffusion dysfunction, but no intervention or treatment was tested.
paper_authors: Linxia Wu; Xiaoyu Han; Lu Chen; Liyan Guo; Yumin Li; Osamah Alwalid; Tong Nie; Feihong Wu; Xiaoling Zhi; Yanqing Fan; Heshui Shi; Chuansheng Zheng
paper_title: Impact of Diabetes on Persistent Radiological Abnormalities and Pulmonary Diffusion Dysfunction in COVID-19 Survivors: A 3-Year Prospective Cohort Study

summary: Retrospective descriptive study of healthcare workers at Charles Nicolle Hospital who experienced persistent dyspnea upon return to work after COVID-19 infection between September-December 2020. The study documents prevalence (13.7% of 588 infected staff), demographic characteristics, and clinical features of post-COVID dyspnea but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Anja Mghirbi; Imen Youssef; Siwar Chemingui; Hiba Ziedi; Dorra Aouida; Nizar Ladhari
paper_title: Persistance de la dyspnée à la reprise du travail chez le personnel de soins
paper_journal: Archives des Maladies Professionnelles et de l'Environnement

summary: This study documents the prevalence of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection and associated symptoms in 760 healthcare workers during Omicron BA.5/BF.7 and XBB.1.5 waves between December 2022 and July 2023. While it identifies long COVID symptoms (fatigue, memory loss, cough) as secondary observations, the paper does not evaluate or test any treatment or intervention—it is primarily an epidemiological survey of infection patterns and symptom prevalence.
paper_authors: Xue-Dong Song; Hui-Xia Gao; Hao Tan; Yan-Yan Xie; Xin Zhang; Chen-Min Zhang; Yu-Ling Wang; Er-Hei Dai
paper_title: Prevalence of infection and reinfection among health care workers in a hospital of Northern China between BA.5/BF.7 and XBB.1.5 wave

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed pulmonary function in 53 healthcare professionals with persistent post-COVID complaints at ~3 months post-infection. Key findings include decreased DLCO in 39.6% of participants and persistent symptoms in 47.2%, with correlations between delayed return to work and lower DLCO values.
paper_authors: Pınar Y. Gülhan; Peri M. Arbak; Ali N. Annakkaya; Ege G. Balbay; Öner A. Balbay
paper_title: An assessment of post-COVID-19 infection pulmonary functions in healthcare professionals

summary: Longitudinal study comparing cognitive performance before and after COVID-19 infection in 276 essential workers with COVID-19 versus 217 controls without infection. Found significant decline in cognitive throughput post-infection, particularly in those with severe COVID-19 and PASC, equivalent to 10.6 years of normal aging.
paper_authors: Zennur Sekendiz; Olga Morozova; Melissa A. Carr; Ashley Fontana; Nikhil Mehta; Alina Ali; Eugene Jiang; Tesleem Babalola; Sean A.P. Clouston; Benjamin J. Luft
paper_title: Characterization of Change in Cognition Before and After COVID-19 Infection in Essential Workers at Midlife

summary: This prospective multicenter cohort study examines endothelial function in 798 long COVID patients using digital thermal monitoring (E4-Diagnose Polymath). The study found that 77.4% of patients had long COVID symptoms, with fatigue (42.2%) and chest pain being significantly associated with endothelial dysfunction.
paper_authors: S. Charfeddine; Hassen Ibn Hadj Amor; Slim Torjmen; S. Kraïem; Rania Hammami; Amine Bahloul; N. Kallel; N. Moussa; I. Touil; Sami Milouchi; Jamel Elghoul; Zina Meddeb; Yamina Thabet; Jihen Jdidi; K. Bouslema; Salem Abdesselem; Leïla Abid
paper_title: Endothelial dysfunction is the key of long COVID-19 symptoms: The results of TUN-EndCOV study

summary: A retrospective cohort study examining long COVID presentation and risk factors in an underserved urban population in Chicago using manual extraction from electronic health records. The study found that hospitalization, BMI >30, and female sex were associated with increased odds of long COVID, with certain preexisting conditions predicting analogous long COVID symptoms.
paper_authors: John Musachia; Jon Radosta; Dirin Ukwade; Shahrukh Rizvi; Romani Wahba
paper_title: Postacute Sequelae From SARS-CoV-2 at the University of Illinois Hospital and Clinics: An Examination of the Effects of Long COVID in an Underserved Population Utilizing Manual Extraction of Electronic Health Records

summary: Prospective cohort study examining menstrual cycle changes following SARS-CoV-2 infection in 127 women from the Arizona CoVHORT study. Found that 16% reported menstrual changes (primarily irregular menstruation and increased PMS symptoms) and those with changes reported more COVID-19 symptoms including fatigue, headache, and shortness of breath.
paper_authors: Sana M. Khan; Alexandra Shilen; Kelly M. Heslin; Providence Ishimwe; Alicia M. Allen; Elizabeth T. Jacobs; Leslie V. Farland
paper_title: SARS-CoV-2 infection and subsequent changes in the menstrual cycle among participants in the Arizona CoVHORT study
paper_journal: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology

summary: Prospective cohort study of 46,579 women examining whether pre-existing endometriosis is associated with increased risk of long COVID-19. Found that women with laparoscopically-confirmed endometriosis had a 22% higher risk of developing long COVID-19 compared to those without endometriosis history.
paper_authors: Siwen Wang; Leslie V. Farland; Audrey J. Gaskins; Jasmine Mortazavi; Yi-Xin Wang; Rulla M. Tamimi; Janet W. Rich-Edwards; Dan Zhang; Kathryn L. Terry; Jorge E. Chavarro; Stacey A. Missmer
paper_title: Association of laparoscopically-confirmed endometriosis with long COVID-19: a prospective cohort study
paper_journal: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology

summary: This cross-sectional study compared cognitive function and inflammatory markers in 66 COVID-19 survivors versus 79 healthy controls at 15 months post-discharge, finding impaired executive function on the Trails test and elevated TNF-α levels negatively correlated with cognitive performance. The study identifies inflammation as a potential mechanism underlying long-term cognitive impairment but does not test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Danmei He; Minlan Yuan; Wen Dang; Lin Bai; Runnan Yang; Jingyi Wang; Yao Ma; Bo Liu; Shiyu Liu; Simai Zhang; Xiao Liao; Wei Zhang
paper_title: Long term neuropsychiatric consequences in COVID-19 survivors: Cognitive impairment and inflammatory underpinnings fifteen months after discharge

summary: Retrospective analysis of 809 COVID-19 events in 778 kidney transplant recipients characterizing post-COVID-19 cardiovascular disease incidence and risk factors over 1 year. Post-COVID-19 CVD occurred in 8.7% of patients, with COVID-19 hospitalization conferring equivalent cardiovascular risk as previous CVD history.
paper_authors: Mary G. Bowring; Kasama Manothummetha; Veraprapas Kittipibul; Lucy X. Li; Robin K. Avery; Willa Cochran; Sean Ellis; Ilan S. Wittstein; Dorry L. Segev; Christine M. Durand; Daniel C. Brennan; Nitipong Permpalung
paper_title: Post–COVID-19 cardiovascular disease risk in kidney transplant recipients

summary: Prospective observational study of 930 liver transplant recipients infected with Omicron in China, following outcomes and post-COVID-19 symptoms through May 2023. While the study documents common post-COVID symptoms (fatigue 36.9%, memory loss 35.7%, sleep disturbance 23.9%) and finds protective effects of vaccination, it is a passive observational cohort with no active treatment intervention evaluated.
paper_authors: Wei Zhang; Rongrong Wang; Pingbo Jin; Xinyu Yu; Weili Wang; Yuntao Zhang; Xueli Bai; Tingbo Liang
paper_title: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of liver transplant recipients infected by Omicron during the opening up of the dynamic zero-coronavirus disease policy in China: A prospective, observational study

summary: Retrospective population-based cohort study examining long-term sequelae risk following SARS-CoV-2 Delta/Omicron infection in pregnant women compared to test-negative pregnant women and non-pregnant infected women. Found pregnant women had 1.6× higher risk of postacute sequelae vs uninfected pregnant controls and 13.4× higher risk vs non-pregnant infected women, though absolute incidence was <1%.
paper_authors: Yong Yi Tan; Enoch Xue Heng Loy; Wei Zhi Tan; An Ting Tay; Jue Tao Lim; Calvin J. Chiew; Mahesh Choolani; David Chien Lye; Kelvin Bryan Tan; Liang En Wee
paper_title: Long COVID-19 in pregnancy: increased risk but modest incidence following mild Omicron infection in a boosted obstetric cohort during endemicity
paper_journal: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology

summary: This retrospective cohort study uses the National COVID Cohort Collaborative to compare PASC prevalence between solid organ transplant recipients and non-immunosuppressed patients using propensity score matching. It identifies transplant status, infection severity, age, and immunosuppressive medications as independent risk factors for PASC but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

summary: Retrospective population-based cohort study comparing long COVID risk in Singaporean transplant recipients infected with Omicron vs test-negatives during 2022. Found no significantly elevated overall risk of postacute sequelae in the vaccinated/boosted transplant cohort, though autoimmune and neurologic sequelae showed increased risk compared to test-negatives.
paper_authors: Liang En Wee; Yong Yi Tan; Muhammad Ismail Bin Abdul Malek; Jue Tao Lim; Calvin J. Chiew; David Chien Lye; Kelvin Bryan Tan
paper_title: Postacute sequelae following Omicron SARS-CoV-2 infection in transplant recipients: a population -based cohort study

summary: Population-based cohort study assessing the prevalence of ongoing long COVID symptoms and related disability ~2 years after initial SARS-CoV-2 infection in Michigan adults. Found that 24% reported ongoing long COVID with substantial increases in cognition, mobility, independent living, and self-care disability compared to pre-infection baseline.
paper_authors: Nancy L. Fleischer; Elizabeth Slocum; Akash Patel; Yanmei Xie; Patricia McKane; Sarah Lyon-Callo; Jana L. Hirschtick
paper_title: Long COVID and New Onset Disability Nearly 2 Years After Initial Infection

summary: A retrospective cohort study of 1,802 patients evaluated at a comprehensive post-COVID center in Chicago, assessing specialty clinic utilization and clinical testing patterns. While it documents high prevalence of neurologic, pulmonary, and cardiac abnormalities in long COVID patients, it does not test or evaluate a specific intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Bailey J.; Lavelle B.; Miller J.; Jimenez M.; Lim PH; Orban ZS; Clark JR; Tomar R.; Ludwig A.; Ali ST; Lank GK; Zielinski A.; Mylvaganam R.; Kalhan R.; El Muayed M.; Mutharasan RK; Liotta EM; Sznajder JI; Davidson C.; Koralnik IJ; Sala MA
paper_title: Multidisciplinary Center Care for Long COVID Syndrome–A Retrospective Cohort Study

summary: This study compared autonomic dysfunction prevalence and severity in 33 long COVID (PASC) patients versus 33 POTS patients and 33 healthy controls using beat-to-beat hemodynamic monitoring and symptom scales. The majority (79%) of PASC patients met criteria for POTS and showed significantly impaired autonomic function and quality of life compared to controls, supporting routine autonomic testing in long COVID management.
paper_authors: Marie-Claire Seeley; Celine Gallagher; Eric Ong; Amy Langdon; Jonathan Chieng; Danielle Bailey; Amanda Page; Han S. Lim; Dennis H. Lau
paper_title: High Incidence of Autonomic Dysfunction and Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome in Patients with Long COVID: Implications for Management and Health Care Planning

summary: A Japanese multicenter cohort study of 26 institutions followed hospitalized COVID-19 patients over 12 months to identify risk factors for prolonged fatigue in long COVID. The study found that asthma was an independent risk factor for persistent general fatigue, which was the most interfering long COVID symptom in daily life.
paper_authors: Keeya Sunata; Jun Miyata; Hideki Terai; Emiko Matsuyama; Mayuko Watase; Ho Namkoong; Takanori Asakura; Katsunori Masaki; Shotaro Chubachi; Keiko Ohgino; Ichiro Kawada; Norihiro Harada; Hitoshi Sasano; Ai Nakamura; Yu Kusaka; Takehiko Ohba; Yasushi Nakano; Kazumi Nishio; Yukiko Nakajima; Shoji Suzuki; Shuichi Yoshida; Hiroki Tateno; Makoto Ishii; Koichi Fukunaga
paper_title: Asthma is a risk factor for general fatigue of long COVID in Japanese nation-wide cohort study

summary: Retrospective analysis of 2,389 COVID-19 survivors examining the impact of cardiac and cerebrovascular complications during acute hospitalization on long-term mortality outcomes. Study found that myocardial infarction during hospitalization was an independent predictor of increased mortality at 2.4-year follow-up, but does not study long COVID interventions or sequelae.
paper_authors: Kazuya Tateishi; Hosam Hmoud; Lucius De Gregorio; Isabella De Gregorio; Chantal Y. Asselin; Joseph De Gregorio
paper_title: Impact of Cardiac and Cerebrovascular Complications During Hospitalization on Long-Term Prognosis in Patients With COVID-19

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing cardiovascular event risk in 319 COVID-19+ patients versus 1,036 COVID-19- controls from a healthcare system, followed for median 6 months post-infection. Found that SARS-CoV-2 infection was associated with increased risk of cardiovascular morbidity/mortality and all-cause mortality in the late post-COVID period.
paper_authors: Tereshchenko LG; Bishop A.; Fisher-Campbell N.; Levene J.; Morris CC; Patel H.; Beeson E.; Blank JA; Bradner JN; Coblens M.; Corpron JW; Davison JM; Denny K.; Earp MS; Florea S.; Freeman H.; Fuson O.; Guillot FH; Haq KT; Kim M.; Kolseth C.; Krol O.; Lin L.; Litwin L.; Malik A.; Mitchell E.; Mohapatra A.; Mullen C.; Nix CD; Oyeyemi A.; Rutlen C.; Tam AE; Van Buren I.; Wallace J.; Khan A.
paper_title: Risk of Cardiovascular Events After COVID-19

summary: This US nationwide cohort study characterizes disability burden in 7,926 long COVID patients at baseline, measuring physical mobility, instrumental activities of daily living, and mental fatigue. The study finds 65% of long COVID participants have at least one disability compared to 6% in resolved COVID controls, identifying risk factors and protective factors like vaccination.
paper_authors: Bryan Lau; Eryka Wentz; Zhanmo Ni; Karine Yenokyan; Candelaria Vergara; Shruti H. Mehta; Priya Duggal
paper_title: Physical Health and Mental Fatigue Disability Associated with Long COVID: Baseline Results from a US Nationwide Cohort

summary: This cross-sectional study compared cognitive function in 210 long COVID patients versus 369 normal controls using comprehensive neuropsychological testing. Patients with long COVID had 3.6× higher odds of cognitive impairment, with 44% showing cognitive deficits ~7 months post-infection; higher BMI was the only differentiator among cognitively impaired long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Aaron Bonner-Jackson; Rohun Vangal; Yadi Li; Nicolas Thompson; Shinjon Chakrabarti; Kamini Krishnan
paper_title: Factors Associated with Cognitive Impairment in Patients with Persisting Sequelae of COVID-19

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining the association between sedentary lifestyle and risk of acute and post-acute COVID-19 sequelae in 4,850 participants. Finds that prolonged sedentary behavior is independently associated with higher risk of multiple post-COVID symptoms, while physical inactivity showed contradictory protective effects for some outcomes like insomnia.
paper_authors: Chen Zheng; Wendy Ya-Jun Huang; Feng-Hua Sun; Martin Chi-Sang Wong; Parco Ming-Fai Siu; Xiang-Ke Chen; Stephen Heung-Sang Wong
paper_title: Association of Sedentary Lifestyle with Risk of Acute and Post-Acute COVID-19 Sequelae: A Retrospective Cohort Study

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 363 long COVID patients referred for cardiovascular evaluation to assess whether persistent cardiovascular symptoms are associated with objective cardiac abnormalities. Found that only 23.4% had cardiac causes, with 14.3% attributed to COVID, suggesting most symptoms lack objective cardiac explanation.
paper_authors: James F. Howick; Petar Saric; Mohamed Elwazir; Darrell B. Newman; Patricia A. Pellikka; Annelise S. Howick; John C. O'Horo; Leslie T. Cooper; Abhishek J. Deshmukh; Ravindra Ganesh; Ryan Hurt; Bernard Gersh; John P. Bois
paper_title: A Pragmatic Study of Cardiovascular Disease During Long-Term COVID-19

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 364 COVID-19 patients characterizing persistent symptoms, radiological findings, and functional outcomes at follow-up. Identified fatigue as the most common symptom, chest CT alterations in 76% of patients, and pulmonary dysfunction in 44.7%, with higher risk in hospitalized patients and those receiving corticosteroids or hydroxychloroquine.
paper_authors: Patrizia Pasculli; Maria Antonella Zingaropoli; Federica Dominelli; Angelo Giuseppe Solimini; Giorgio Maria Masci; Lucia Ilaria Birtolo; Lara Pasquariello; Filippo Paribeni; Franco Iafrate; Valeria Panebianco; Gioacchino Galardo; Massimo Mancone; Carlo Catalano; Francesco Pugliese; Paolo Palange; Claudio Maria Mastroianni; Maria Rosa Ciardi
paper_title: Insights into Long COVID: Unraveling Risk Factors, Clinical Features, Radiological Findings, Functional Sequelae and Correlations: A Retrospective Cohort Study

summary: Prospective cohort study examining the correlation between pulmonary function test (PFT) abnormalities and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) measures in COVID-19 patients at 3, 6, and ≥12 months post-infection. Found that patients with normal PFTs had worse mobility impairment and anxiety scores, while HRQoL impairment was not explained by PFT abnormalities alone.
paper_authors: James Bradley; Qian Xu; Nikolas Touloumes; Eugene Lusciks; T'shura Ali; Emma C. Huang; James Chen; Shahab Ghafghazi; Forest W. Arnold; Maiying Kong; Jiapeng Huang; Rodrigo Cavallazzi
paper_title: Association of pulmonary function test abnormalities and quality-of-life measures after COVID-19 infection
paper_journal: The American Journal of the Medical Sciences

summary: Population-based cohort study comparing cardiovascular outcomes in 129,864 SARS-CoV-2-infected individuals versus 519,456 matched uninfected controls over 260 days median follow-up. Found significantly elevated risk of major adverse cardiovascular events and myocardial infarction in infected individuals, particularly those with severe acute COVID-19.
paper_authors: Héctor Alexander Velásquez García; Stanley Wong; Dahn Jeong; Mawuena Binka; Zaeema Naveed; James Wilton; Nathaniel Mark Hawkins; Naveed Zafar Janjua
paper_title: Risk of Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events After SARS-CoV-2 Infection in British Columbia: A Population-Based Study

summary: This cross-sectional study recruited long COVID patients from an online survey and compared objective and subjective audiological measurements (hearing thresholds, otoacoustic emissions) across three groups: long COVID, recovered COVID, and non-COVID controls. No clinically significant hearing loss was detected in long COVID patients, though minor frequency-specific differences were observed.
paper_authors: Degen CV; Mikuteit M.; Niewolik J.; Joosten T.; Schröder D.; Vahldiek K.; Mücke U.; Heinemann S.; Müller F.; Behrens GMN; Klawonn F.; Lenarz T.; Dopfer-Jablonka A.; Steffens S.
paper_title: Audiological profile of adult Long COVID patients

summary: A prospective cohort study following 254 COVID-19 hospitalized patients over 12 months to characterize functional recovery trajectory and identify predictors of recovery. At 12 months, over half demonstrated clinically important deficits in mobility and cognition, with persistent fatigue, dyspnea, and psychological distress.
paper_authors: Marla Beauchamp; Renata Kirkwood; MyLinh Duong; Terence Ho; Parminder Raina; Rebecca Kruisselbrink; Aaron Jones; Carla Girolametto; Andrew Costa
paper_title: Long-Term Functional Limitations and Predictors of Recovery After COVID-19: A Multicenter Prospective Cohort Study

summary: This case-control study compared recurrence of audio-vestibular disorders in 50 patients following COVID-19 breakthrough infection versus 50 patients following vaccination. While the paper addresses long COVID sequelae, it is excluded as a secondary analysis comparing outcomes between two groups rather than testing a specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Chih-Ching Wang; Yi-Ho Young
paper_title: Comparing the recurrence of audio-vestibular disorders following breakthrough infection of COVID-19 vs. those following vaccine administration

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 57 COVID-19 patients with laryngeal dysfunction, examining prevalence of dysphonia, dysphagia, and stenosis, and evaluating outcomes of voice therapy and procedural interventions. Voice therapy improved symptoms in 65% of patients, with improvements also seen in quality of life measures for those with laryngotracheal stenosis.
paper_authors: Hemali P. Shah; Alexandra T. Bourdillon; Neelima Panth; Jacqueline Ihnat; Nikita Kohli
paper_title: Long-term laryngological sequelae and patient-reported outcomes after COVID-19 infection

summary: A single-center prospective cohort study characterizing post-COVID-19 syndrome (PASC) in an ethnically diverse population over one year of follow-up. The study aims to identify clinical phenotypes and biomarkers to predict and manage post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
paper_authors: Xiaona Jia; Sanjie Cao; Ashley Sang Eun Lee; R. Sharon Chinthrajah; C. Yoffe; Sharie Boyd; Benjamin A. Pinsky; Kari C. Nadeau
paper_title: A080 A COMPREHENSIVE CHARACTERIZATION OF POST-COVID-19 SYNDROME IN A DIVERSE POPULATION

summary: Retrospective chart review of tracheostomy and ventilation management in 213 COVID-19 patients admitted to a long-term acute care hospital from April 2020 to November 2021. Study focuses on acute-phase respiratory management and laryngeal findings in hospitalized patients, not long COVID sequelae or post-acute treatment interventions.
paper_authors: Alvin Nguyen; Barbara Rajski; Vicki Furey; Lisa Duffner; Bryce Young; Inna A. Husain
paper_title: Upper airway and tracheostomy management in patients with COVID-19: A long-term acute care hospital (LTACH)

summary: A retrospective observational study evaluating specialized outpatient rehabilitation programs for long COVID in Alberta, Canada, examining program utilization, patient-reported outcomes, and healthcare costs over 180-day pre/post-enrollment periods. Results showed small but statistically significant improvements in functional status and quality of life, modest reductions in healthcare costs, and an ICER approaching the Canadian cost-effectiveness threshold, though authors note these represent preliminary associations rather than causal effects.
paper_authors: Azita Zahiriharsini; Mahnoush Rostami; Caitlin Hurd; Fatemeh Vakilian; Gurpreet Brar; Ting Wang; Thomas Mullie; Suzanne Basiuk; Balraj Mann; Colin Del Castilho; Maeve Smith; Grace Lam; Chester Ho; Kiran Pohar Manhas
paper_title: Evaluating medical and rehabilitation programs for long COVID: utilization, health outcomes, and healthcare costs
paper_journal: The American Journal of the Medical Sciences

summary: Prospective case-controlled study examining olfactory bulb morphology changes in 29 COVID-19 patients with anosmia/hyposmia (Group 1) compared to 24 normosmic post-COVID patients (Group 2) and 25 uninfected controls (Group 3), with 12 weeks of olfactory training intervention. Following olfactory training, Group 1 showed significant improvements in olfactory bulb volume and olfactory function scores, providing evidence for the effectiveness of olfactory training in treating long-lasting post-COVID olfactory loss.
paper_authors: Mustafa Baran; Mahmut Tayyar Kalcioglu; Ahmet Mutlu; Basak Atalay; Mahmut Bilal Dogan; Guler Ozturk
paper_title: Association of olfactory training with olfactory bulb morphology in adults with post-viral long-lasting olfactory dysfunction: A COVID-19 related prospective study

summary: Population-based observational study examining the association between pre-infection COVID-19 vaccination status and long COVID prevalence in Michigan adults. Reports that vaccinated individuals had 40-60% lower long COVID prevalence compared to unvaccinated controls, but this is a secondary analysis of existing surveillance data without testing an intervention in long COVID patients.

The study found that one-third of patients reported subjective cognitive impairment regardless of acute disease severity, which was associated with depression and PTSD but not objective cognitive test results.

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing subjective cognitive complaints and objective cognitive screening results in 87 African American post-COVID patients at a PASC clinic. Found high concordance between self-reported cognitive concerns and objective impairment, with depression and anxiety associated with subjective complaints.
paper_authors: Goldstein FC; Hajjar I.; Summers A.; Truong AD; Lee FFE; Han JE; Walker TA
paper_title: Frequency and correlates of subjective cognitive complaints and objective cognitive screening results in African American adults following COVID-19 infection

summary: This study uses diffusion basis spectrum imaging (DBSI) to examine neuroinflammatory markers in COVID-19 cases versus controls using pre- and post-infection UK Biobank neuroimaging data (N=416). summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 223 non-severe COVID-19 patients in Shanghai for 9 months to characterize long COVID sequelae and identify predictors of fatigue symptoms. The study found that 48.4% reported sequelae lasting >4 weeks, with fatigue being the most common (15.7%), and identified hospitalization duration, non-use of antivirals, and immune markers (IL-6, CD16+CD56+ NK cells) as independent risk factors.

paper_title: Clinical features and predictive nomogram for fatigue sequelae in non-severe patients infected with SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in Shanghai, China

summary: Prospective controlled cohort study of 404 SARS-CoV-2-positive and 105 negative youth (ages 12-25) investigating risk factors for fatigue severity at 6 months post-infection. Baseline symptom severity and psychosocial factors (loneliness, neuroticism) were major risk factors for persistent fatigue, rather than biomarkers or infection status.

paper_title: Risk factors for fatigue severity in the post-COVID-19 condition: A prospective controlled cohort study of nonhospitalised adolescents and young adults

summary: This study examined acute serum protein biomarkers and the prevalence of persistent neuropsychiatric symptoms in 97 South African SARS-CoV-2 positive patients at least 6 months post-infection. Over half of participants had persistent neuropsychiatric symptoms including cognitive impairment (44%), though acute biomarkers were not significantly associated with these outcomes.

paper_title: Acute serum protein biomarker profile and prevalence of persistent (>6 months) neuropsychiatric symptoms in a cohort of SARS-CoV-2 PCR positive patients in Cape Town, South Africa

summary: This longitudinal cohort study from the LoTECA project followed 93 young people with long COVID to identify predictors of fatigue progression from 6 to 12 months post-infection. Non-European ethnicity, higher interferon gamma levels, and lower RR-interval (higher resting heart rate) during acute infection were significant predictors of worsening fatigue, explaining 21% of variance.

paper_title: Predictors of fatigue progression in long COVID among young people

summary: A prospective cohort study of 63 COVID-19 patients examining the association between post-acute olfactory impairment and long-term physical capacity over 24 months. The study found that olfactory impairment in the early post-acute phase was significantly associated with reduced physical capacity at all follow-ups, with the association strengthening over time.
paper_authors: Christoffer Granvik; Alicia Lind; Guilherme W.F. Barros; Clas Ahlm; Sara Anderson; Linus Andersson; Johan Normark
paper_title: Olfactory impairment associated with reduced physical capacity 24 months after COVID-19

summary: This study examines dual inflammation (schizophrenia + COVID-19) and its impact on cognitive function in 119 schizophrenia patients with COVID-19 history versus controls. While the paper includes long COVID patients (70 recruited 2 years post-recovery), it is primarily focused on schizophrenia-specific cognitive impairment and inflammation, not on long COVID as the main condition or on evaluating a treatment intervention for long COVID.

paper_title: Dual inflammation in schizophrenia infected with COVID-19: Impact on cognitive function

summary: Prospective cohort study tracking cognitive function over 42 months in 1,553 long COVID patients from the Mount Sinai registry, assessing attention, working memory, processing speed, executive function, and memory. While most cognitive domains improved over time, processing speed and executive functioning remained significantly below normative values, indicating lasting cognitive burden of long COVID.

paper_title: Neurocognitive trajectories in long COVID: Evidence from longitudinal analyses

summary: Prospective observational study of COVID-19 ICU survivors examining cognitive impairment and subjective cognitive complaints at 6 and 12 months post-discharge. Cognitive impairment declined from 23.1% at 6 months to 11.1% at 12 months, while subjective complaints remained high and were associated with mental health problems and fatigue.

paper_title: Objective and subjective cognitive status after intensive care unit treatment for COVID-19

summary: This study analyzes immune markers from acute COVID-19 hospitalization to identify predictors of post-COVID fatigue 6-9 months later. While it studies long COVID outcomes, it is a secondary analysis examining associations in existing patient data rather than testing a treatment intervention.

paper_title: Inflammatory predictors of Post-COVID fatigue

summary: This observational study measured plasma levels of orexin A, substance P, bradykinin, and DABK in 78 acute COVID-19 ICU patients, 14 severe COVID-19 survivors at 2.5-year follow-up, and 14 healthy controls. paper_title: Systemic role of orexin A, substance P, bradykinin, and DABK in severe COVID-19 and 2.5-yr follow-ups: an observational study

summary: Prospective multicenter study following 211 severe COVID-19 patients (112 ward, 99 ICU) at 45 days and 6 months post-hospital discharge to assess respiratory sequelae and lung function recovery. paper_title: Lung function six months after severe COVID-19: Does time, in fact, heal all wounds?

paper_journal: The Brazilian Journal of Infectious Diseases

paper_title: Pulmonary function and exercise capacity six months after hospital discharge of patients with severe COVID-19

summary: An observational study evaluating the effect of a nutritional supplement (Apportal®) on chronic fatigue and quality of life in 201 subjects after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Results showed statistically significant improvements in fatigue, mental fatigue, and health status measures at both 14 and 28 days of supplementation.
paper_authors: Maria Sole Rossato; Elisa Brilli; Nicola Ferri; Giulio Giordano; Germano Tarantino
paper_title: Observational study on the benefit of a nutritional supplement, supporting immune function and energy metabolism, on chronic fatigue associated with the SARS-CoV-2 post-infection progress

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing treatments (low-dose naltrexone, amitriptyline, duloxetine, physical therapy) in 108 post-COVID-19 patients, evaluating improvements in fatigue, pain, dyspnea, and brain fog. Low-dose naltrexone showed significantly higher hazard of improvement (HR=5.04) compared to physical therapy alone.
paper_authors: Leonardo Tamariz; Elizabeth Bast; Nancy Klimas; Ana Palacio
paper_title: Low-dose Naltrexone Improves post–COVID-19 condition Symptoms

summary: Prospective cohort study measuring Myl9 serum concentrations in 195 COVID-19 patients during hospitalization and at 3- and 6-month follow-up to investigate the association between Myl9 levels and post-acute COVID-19 syndrome. Study identifies prolonged high Myl9 levels as associated with residual respiratory symptoms at 6 months, suggesting involvement of prolonged inflammation or endothelial damage in PACS pathogenesis.

paper_title: Prolonged high Myl9 levels are associated with the pathogenesis and respiratory symptom of post-acute COVID-19 syndrome: A 6-month follow-up study

summary: This prospective cohort study examined fat oxidation capacity as a marker of mitochondrial function in 187 post-COVID syndrome patients undergoing inpatient rehabilitation. Exercise-based rehabilitation significantly improved fat oxidation capacity (+44.2% overall, p<0.0001) and exercise tolerance, suggesting that metabolic disturbance in PCS patients is partially reversible through rehabilitation.
paper_authors: René Garbsch; Hendrik Schäfer; Frank C. Mooren; Boris Schmitz
paper_title: Analysis of fat oxidation capacity during cardiopulmonary exercise testing indicates long-lasting metabolic disturbance in patients with post-covid-19 syndrome

summary: This case-control study compared vitamin D levels in 75-73 post-COVID syndrome (PCS) patients versus non-PCS controls measured from 2019-2022, finding significantly lower vitamin D in the PCS cohort (17.0-17.6 ng/ml vs 22.3-23.7 ng/ml). paper_authors: Jens Bräunlich; Alexander Dinse-Lambracht
paper_title: Decreased levels of vitamin D in Post–Corona Virus-19 Disease syndrome (PCS) patients compared to a control group

summary: A prospective observational cohort study of 199 critically ill COVID-19 ICU survivors in Spain tracking nutritional, functional, and quality-of-life outcomes over 12 months post-discharge. summary: This retrospective cohort study compared mesotherapy with oral medication (diclofenac, thiocolchicoside, cyanocobalamin) for treating post-COVID pain syndrome in 96 patients. summary: Prospective cohort study following 103 mild COVID-19 patients over 6 months via phone interviews to characterize symptom onset, duration, and resolution. Found that 46% of patients had at least one unresolved symptom at 6-month follow-up, with fatigue, smell/taste changes, and breathing difficulties being most common.

Treatment did not significantly reduce risk of postacute cardiovascular, neurological, respiratory, autoimmune diagnoses, or symptoms up to 180 days post-infection.

While pulmonary perfusion impairment persists at 12 months and is associated with developing long COVID, this is an observational descriptive study with no treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Tao Ouyang; Zhenghui Huang; Shuxing Wei; Jun Yang; Andreas Voskrebenzev; Jens Vogel-Claussen; Shubin Guo; Qi Yang

summary: This retrospective cohort study examined the association between SARS-CoV-2 vaccination status and the risk of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 in South Korea during the Omicron-predominant period (January-March 2022). Vaccination with at least two doses was associated with significantly reduced risk of multiple post-acute conditions including cardiac events, venous thromboembolism, renal failure, and pulmonary complications.
paper_authors: Kyungmin Huh; Young-Eun Kim; Gi Hwan Bae; Jong Youn Moon; Ji-Man Kang; Jacob Lee; Jang-Whan Bae; Kyong Ran Peck; Jaehun Jung

summary: Retrospective cohort study evaluating whether intravenous remdesivir reduces long-term multisystemic sequelae (cardiovascular, neurological, respiratory, autoimmune diagnoses and symptom persistence) in 30,175 COVID-19 hospitalized adults in Singapore. Remdesivir treatment did not significantly reduce the risk of long-term diagnoses or symptom persistence compared to untreated individuals at 300 days post-hospitalization.
paper_authors: Liang En Wee; Jue Tao Lim; An Ting Tay; Calvin J. Chiew; Barnaby Edward Young; Shawn Vasoo; Huei Xin Lou; David Chien Lye; Kelvin Bryan Tan
paper_title: Remdesivir and risk of long-term multi-systemic sequelae following COVID-19 hospitalization

summary: This cross-sectional study compared resting-state functional MRI patterns in 39 long-COVID patients with and without cognitive impairment, finding altered default mode network connectivity and stronger visual-ventral stream connectivity in cognitively impaired patients. The study is observational and non-interventional, examining neurobiological correlates of cognitive dysfunction rather than testing a treatment.
paper_authors: Manuel Leitner; Daniela Pinter; Stefan Ropele; Marisa Koini
paper_title: Functional connectivity changes in long-Covid patients with and without cognitive impairment

summary: This cross-sectional study examined 52 adults (COVID-positive and COVID-negative controls) to investigate the relationship between inflammatory factors and neuropsychiatric symptoms in long COVID (neuro-PASC). The study found elevated neuropsychiatric symptoms and altered immune profiles (particularly elevated MIG/CXCL9) in COVID-positive participants with neuro-PASC, supporting the role of immune dysregulation in long COVID neuropsychiatric sequelae.
paper_authors: Jennifer M. Loftis; Evan Firsick; Kate Shirley; James L. Adkins; Anh Le-Cook; Emily Sano; Rebekah Hudson; Jonathan Moorman
paper_title: Inflammatory and mental health sequelae of COVID-19

summary: This cross-sectional study uses a custom olfactory-action meter to quantify olfactory detectabilities and neurocognitive impairments in COVID-19 patients during and post-infection (4-18 months), comparing symptomatic patients, asymptomatic carriers, and healthy controls. Results show persistent olfactory learning deficits in both symptomatic patients and recovered subjects during and after infection, suggesting long-term neurocognitive impairment from COVID-19.
paper_authors: Rajdeep Bhowmik; Meenakshi Pardasani; Sarang Mahajan; Rahul Magar; Samir V. Joshi; Ganesh Ashish Nair; Anindya S. Bhattacharjee; Nixon M. Abraham
paper_title: Persistent olfactory learning deficits during and post-COVID-19 infection

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining long-term multi-systemic complications in Singaporean children aged 1-17 years infected with SARS-CoV-2 Delta/Omicron variants compared to test-negative controls. Found modestly increased risk of respiratory sequelae (particularly bronchitis) post-infection, with reduced chronic sequelae in predominantly mild Omicron cases compared to historical influenza hospitalizations.
paper_authors: Liang En Wee; Jue Tao Lim; Janice Yu Jin Tan; Jiahui Li; Calvin Chiew; Chee-Fu Yung; Chia Yin Chong; David Chien Lye; Kelvin Bryan Tan
paper_title: Long-term multi-systemic complications after SARS-CoV-2 Omicron and Delta infection in children: a retrospective cohort study

summary: This retrospective cohort study uses real-world clinical data from the National COVID Cohort Collaborative to evaluate whether selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), particularly those with sigma-1 receptor agonist activity, reduce the risk of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC). The analysis of 17,908 patients found that SSRIs with S1R agonist activity reduced PASC risk by 29% and non-S1R agonist SSRIs by 21%, suggesting a potential preventive benefit of SSRIs in PASC.

paper_title: Assessing the effect of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors in the prevention of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19

summary: Population-based study examining the association between COVID-19 booster vaccination and risk of post-COVID condition during the Omicron wave in 7,936 infected participants. paper_title: Booster vaccination and post-COVID-19 condition during the Omicron variant-dominant wave: a large population-based study

summary: Retrospective study of 1,426 long COVID patients treated with traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) or Western medicine at a Chinese hospital between December 2022 and June 2023. summary: Prospective cohort study examining pathophysiological mechanisms of post-acute sequelae following COVID-19 (PASC) in non-hospitalized patients, comparing 311 PASC participants with 490 recovered controls across biomarkers and symptoms. summary: Retrospective cohort study using electronic health records from Hong Kong and UK to assess post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 infection in 551,586 patients with COVID-19 and matched controls. Study documents increased risk of cardiovascular, pulmonary, neuropsychiatric, renal, and other complications during the post-acute phase, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

summary: This prospective cohort study assessed cognitive performance (working memory, attention, reasoning, motor control) in 3,335 UK COVID Symptom Study participants, comparing those with and without prior SARS-CoV-2 infection. Cognitive deficits were detected in individuals with long COVID symptoms (~2 years post-infection), particularly those with ≥12 weeks of ongoing symptoms, but not in those who reported full recovery.

summary: This prospective cohort study develops and validates the Post COVID-19 Condition Stigma Questionnaire (PCCSQ) to measure stigma experienced by long COVID patients, finding high reliability and validity. summary: This retrospective multi-centre cohort study used electronic health records from 30,422 COVID-19 patients to characterize seven distinct long COVID (PASC) sub-phenotypes and their temporal attributes using distributed representation learning. Found that 46% recovered from fatigue and 57% from cognitive deficits within two years, with depression, headache, male sex, older age, and lower education as risk factors for non-recovery.

summary: Prospective observational cohort study tracking 106 post-COVID-19 patients with moderate-to-severe fatigue over 20 months, measuring symptom severity and biomarkers (hand grip strength, cardiovascular function, laboratory parameters). Patients meeting ME/CFS criteria showed persistent high symptom severity and fatigue/PEM, while general PCS patients improved; lower grip strength at onset correlated with symptom persistence.

summary: Prospective observational cohort study following 111 hospitalized COVID-19 patients in South Africa for up to 40 days post-discharge to assess lung outcomes and functional impairment. Found substantial pulmonary and functional morbidity, with 78.9% elevated respiratory symptom scores and 49.5% with spirometry abnormalities, particularly in patients with pre-existing TB, HIV, or extreme BMI.

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining the prevalence of long COVID in people with type 1 and type 2 diabetes compared to matched controls in a UK population. The study found similar or lower long COVID prevalence in diabetic individuals, with some sex-specific differences and associations with age and BMI.
paper_authors: Adrian H. Heald; Richard Williams; David A. Jenkins; Stuart Stewart; Nawar Diar Bakerly; Kevin Mccay; William Ollier
paper_title: The prevalence of long COVID in people with diabetes mellitus–evidence from a UK cohort

summary: This national retrospective cohort study analyzed electronic health records for 4.7 million Scottish adults to estimate long COVID prevalence (0.02-1.7% depending on identification method) and identify associated risk factors. The study found long COVID more common in females, middle-aged adults, those with comorbidities, immunosuppression, or prior hospitalization, but is not a treatment study and should be excluded from the intervention trials dataset.

summary: This retrospective cohort study from the RECOVER Initiative compares the incidence of post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) in females who acquired SARS-CoV-2 during pregnancy versus outside of pregnancy using electronic health record data from 19 U.S. health systems. The study found that SARS-CoV-2 infection acquired during pregnancy was associated with lower overall PASC risk (25.5% vs 33.9%) but increased risk for specific complications including abnormal heartbeat and thromboembolism.

summary: A 3-year prospective cohort study following 1,319 children post-SARS-CoV-2 infection to characterize long COVID prevalence, predictors, and outcomes. Found that age >12 years, infection with original/alpha variants, and lack of vaccination were significant risk factors for long COVID duration, with vaccination associated with lower risk at 3, 6, and 12 months.

summary: This study evaluates BNT162b2 vaccine effectiveness in reducing long COVID risk in children and adolescents using real-world EHR data from the RECOVER PCORnet. The vaccine showed 95.4% effectiveness during Delta and 60-75% during Omicron, with mediation analysis indicating protection is primarily through preventing initial SARS-CoV-2 infection rather than direct mitigation of post-infection sequelae.

paper_title: Long term health outcomes in people with diabetes 12 months after hospitalisation with COVID-19 in the UK: a prospective cohort study

summary: This retrospective cohort study analyzed electronic health records from 771,725 children across 24 U.S. health systems to examine racial and ethnic differences in long COVID (respiratory and neurological PASC). Among children with documented SARS-CoV-2 infection, the study found that Hispanic White children and those under 5 years had higher odds of respiratory PASC, while older children and those with pre-existing neurologic conditions were more likely to have neurologic PASC, with disparities potentially reflecting inequities in healthcare access.
