The study identifies oxygen desaturation during exercise as a predictor of abnormal heart rate response, showing EET is associated with impaired pulmonary function and reduced cardiac systolic/diastolic function.
paper_authors: Giovanna Pelà; Annalisa Frizzelli; Roberta Pisi; Luigino Calzetta; Alessandra Marchese; Alfredo Chetta; Marina Aiello
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 exaggerated exertional tachycardia: Relationship with pulmonary and cardiac sequelae

summary: Prospective cohort study of 46 former ICU patients treated for COVID-19, assessed at 4 and 12 months post-discharge using validated instruments. Study found persistent fatigue (82%), cognitive impairment improving from 52% to 31%, and low employment rates, indicating poor long-term recovery without clear improvement in physical or psychological outcomes.
paper_authors: Ing-Marie Larsson; Michael Hultström; Miklos Lipcsey; Robert Frithiof; Sten Rubertsson; Ewa Wallin
paper_title: Poor long-term recovery after critical COVID-19 during 12 months longitudinal follow-up

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 494 COVID-19 patients followed for ~1 year to identify risk factors for long COVID affecting the digestive system. Found that liver function abnormality on admission was associated with a 3.5-fold increased risk of developing digestive long COVID syndrome.
paper_authors: Huibin Wu; Yunjie Zhang; Wenqing Tang; Minzhi Lv; Zhixue Chen; Fansheng Meng; Yitong Zhao; Huajie Xu; Yuxin Dai; Jindan Xue; Jingya Wang; Ling Dong; Dejun Wu; Si Zhang; Ruyi Xue
paper_title: Liver function abnormality on admission predicts long COVID syndrome in digestive system

summary: This retrospective observational study describes the 3-month sequelae in 51 young, comorbid patients who recovered from severe COVID-19, including persistent symptoms (fatigue 74.5%, dyspnea 66%), pulmonary imaging abnormalities (64.7%), diffusion impairment (46.3%), and anxiety (51%). The study is a descriptive cohort follow-up without any intervention or treatment evaluation, making it ineligible for intervention trial analysis.
paper_authors: Caroline Granger; O. Hlal; Élisabeth Mercier; E. Bordart; Lauranne Teule; L. Colombain; Hugues Aumaître
paper_title: Description des séquelles à 3 mois d’une COVID grave chez une population jeune et comorbide

summary: A systematic assessment of 116 healthcare workers infected with COVID-19 in March-April 2020, evaluated at a mean of 67 days post-infection for physical and psychological outcomes. The study found persistent symptoms in 64 participants (55%) including fatigue and dyspnea, significant anxiety in one-third, and overall high satisfaction with the multidisciplinary assessment program, but it is a descriptive follow-up survey without treatment intervention.
paper_authors: M.-A. Khuong-Josses; M. Poupard; Q. Bougault; N. Sayre
paper_title: Bilan post-COVID-19 systématique dans une cohorte de plus de 100 soignants

summary: Prospective cohort study of 641 sailors (413 COVID-positive, 206 COVID-negative) followed for 12 months post-outbreak to characterize long COVID symptoms and their prevalence. Found that 53.7-55.2% of COVID-positive participants reported persistent symptoms at 6-9 months, with common symptoms including concentration/memory difficulties, fatigue, and sleep disorders.
paper_authors: Perisse A.; De Cacqueray F.; Delarbre D.; Marsaa H.; Bergmann C.; Da Silva V.; Bronstein A.; Paleiron N.; Menoud N.; Cobola J.; Verret C.; Mayet A.; Bylicki O.
paper_title: Symptoms of Long-COVID 1-Year after a COVID-19 outbreak among sailors on a French aircraft carrier

summary: Retrospective study comparing long COVID risk across SARS-CoV-2 variants (Alpha, Delta, Omicron) in 325 hospitalized patients with genomic sequencing. Found Omicron associated with lower odds of long-term sequelae compared to Alpha, while ICU admission and antiviral/immunomodulatory treatment predicted higher risk.
paper_authors: Ana Hernández-Aceituno; Abigail García-Hernández; Eneko Larumbe-Zabala
paper_title: COVID-19 long-term sequelae: Omicron versus Alpha and Delta variants

summary: A prospective cohort study that followed 51 COVID-19 patients with impaired lung diffusion capacity (DLCO) from 3 months to 1 year post-infection. While some patients showed improvement, 71% still had abnormal DLCO at 1 year, with obesity associated with lack of improvement—a natural history study without an intervention.
paper_authors: Nitzan Karny Epstein; Dana Yelin; Dorit Shitenberg; Dafna Yahav; Leonard Leibovici; Vered Daitch; Ili Margalit
paper_title: One-year follow-up of COVID-19 recoverees with impaired pulmonary function: A prospective cohort study

summary: This prospective cohort study followed 129 ambulatory COVID-19 patients using telemedicine software to monitor symptom evolution over time. At 3+ months follow-up, 43% of patients remained symptomatic with persistent fatigue, anosmia/ageusia, respiratory symptoms, and other long COVID manifestations, demonstrating high symptom persistence in non-hospitalized cases.
paper_authors: Alexandra Martin; Erika Nogué; M. Morell; Jacques Reynes; Vincent Le Moing; M.-C. Picot; Alain Makinson
paper_title: Suivi ambulatoire des patients COVID-19 via l’application MH LINK

summary: Longitudinal serological and immunological follow-up of 256 SARS-CoV-2 positive healthcare workers over 7 months, examining antibody dynamics and persistence of symptoms. 32.4% of followed participants reported persistent symptoms consistent with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome, with no active treatment intervention studied.
paper_authors: Pilmis B.; Elkaibi I.; Péan de Ponfilly G.; Daikha H.; Bouzid A.; Guihot A.; Castreau N.; Pradere P.; Ketatni H.; Mondragon A.; Hayem G.; Le Pavec J.; Laplanche S.; Le Monnier A.
paper_title: Evolution of anti-SARS-CoV-2 immune response in a cohort of French healthcare workers followed for 7 months

summary: Prospective multicenter follow-up study of 179 COVID-19 hospitalized patients at 12 months post-discharge, assessing pulmonary function, exercise capacity, and symptom burden. While pulmonary physiology improved (6MWT distance increased significantly), persistent symptoms including fatigue, depression, and anxiety did not improve over the follow-up period.
paper_authors: Søren Sperling; Steffen Leth; Andreas Fløe; Charlotte Hyldgaard; Tina Gissel; Ayfer Topcu; Lars Kristensen; Lene Sønderskov Dahl; Johannes Martin Schmid; Søren Jensen-Fangel; Elisabeth Bendstrup
paper_title: Twelve-month follow-up after hospitalization for SARS-COV-2: Physiology improves, symptoms remain

summary: This study assessed functional capacity and exercise tolerance in 200 COVID-19 survivors at 3 months post-discharge using cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) and related measurements. About one-third showed functional limitations, primarily due to muscular impairment, with the study calling for future research on targeted rehabilitation rather than testing an intervention.
paper_authors: Piero Clavario; Vincenzo De Marzo; Roberta Lotti; Cristina Barbara; Annalisa Porcile; Carmelo Russo; Federica Beccaria; Marco Bonavia; Luigi Carlo Bottaro; Marta Caltabellotta; Flavia Chioni; Monica Santangelo; Arto J. Hautala; Raffaele Griffo; Gianfranco Parati; Ugo Corrà; Italo Porto
paper_title: Cardiopulmonary exercise testing in COVID-19 patients at 3 months follow-up

summary: Observational study of 63 non-severe COVID-19 outpatients followed for 6 months to characterize persistent symptoms and document natural recovery rates. At 6 months, 30% had complete recovery, 57% partial recovery, and 13% no recovery, with dyspnea and asthenia/myalgia being the most persistent symptoms.
paper_authors: Seang S.; Itani O.; Monsel G.; Abdi B.; Marcelin AG; Valantin MA; Palich R.; Fayçal A.; Pourcher V.; Katlama C.; Tubiana R.
paper_title: Long COVID-19 symptoms: Clinical characteristics and recovery rate among non-severe outpatients over a six-month follow-up

summary: Retrospective study of 180 long COVID patients examining the prevalence and clinical characteristics of acute pericarditis as a manifestation of long COVID-19 syndrome. Found pericarditis in 22% of patients, with heart palpitations/arrhythmias and autoimmune/allergic disorders as independent risk factors.
paper_authors: Frank Lloyd Dini; Umberto Baldini; Ibadete Bytyçi; Nicola Riccardo Pugliese; Gani Bajraktari; Michael Y. Henein
paper_title: Acute pericarditis as a major clinical manifestation of long COVID-19 syndrome

summary: Prospective case-control study comparing endothelial vascular function in acute COVID-19, post-COVID patients, and matched controls using reactive hyperemia peripheral arterial tonometry. Found significantly impaired endothelial function in post-COVID patients (101.5 days post-symptom onset) compared to acute and control groups, suggesting persistent systemic vascular dysfunction.
paper_authors: Hernan Mejia-Renteria; Alejandro Travieso; Adam Sagir; Eduardo Martínez-Gómez; Angela Carrascosa-Granada; Takumi Toya; Iván J. Núñez-Gil; Vicente Estrada; Amir Lerman; Javier Escaned
paper_title: In-vivo evidence of systemic endothelial vascular dysfunction in COVID-19

summary: This cross-sectional study compared exercise capacity and cardiopulmonary function in UK military personnel with and without post-COVID syndrome using imaging and exercise testing. Results showed stepwise declines in exercise capacity and cardiac/pulmonary function in those with prolonged post-COVID symptoms, though findings may reflect deconditioning as well as direct COVID-19 pathology.
paper_authors: Rebecca R. Chamley; Jennifer L. Holland; Jonathan Collins; Kayleigh Pierce; William D. Watson; Peregrine G. Green; David O'Brien; Oliver O'Sullivan; Robert Barker-Davies; Peter Ladlow; Stefan Neubauer; Alexander Bennett; Edward D. Nicol; David A. Holdsworth; Oliver J. Rider
paper_title: Exercise capacity following SARS-CoV-2 infection is related to changes in cardiovascular and lung function in military personnel

summary: This retrospective study of 51 pediatric patients examines cardiovascular complications in PIMS-TS (pediatric multisystem inflammatory syndrome temporally associated with COVID-19), a serious acute inflammatory complication occurring weeks after COVID-19 infection. While PIMS-TS is technically temporally associated with prior COVID-19, this paper is fundamentally about acute post-infection inflammatory syndrome rather than long COVID, and contains no intervention or treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Aleksandra Stasiak; Piotr Kędziora; Beata Kierzkowska; Katarzyna Niewiadomska-Jarosik; Ewelina Perdas; Elżbieta Smolewska
paper_title: Changes in the cardiovascular system in children with pediatric multisystem inflammatory syndrome temporally associated with COVID-19 – A single center experience

summary: This prospective study examined cardiac inflammation and remodeling in COVID-19 survivors with myocardial injury during acute infection using cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. Findings showed high prevalence of myocardial and pericardial involvement (43-50% of patients), with some partial reversal on follow-up imaging.
paper_authors: Eduardo B. Schaustz; José Carlos P. Secco; Julia M. Barroso; Juliana R. Ferreira; Mariana B. Tortelly; Adriana L. Pimentel; Ana Cristina B.S. Figueiredo; Denilson C. Albuquerque; Allan R. Kluser Sales; Paulo H. Rosado de-Castro; Martha V.T. Pinheiro; Olga F. Souza; Emiliano Medei; Ronir R. Luiz; Andréa Silvestre-Sousa; Gabriel C. Camargo; Renata Moll-Bernardes
paper_title: Cardiac remodeling and inflammation detected by magnetic resonance imaging in COVID-19 survivors

summary: Observational study evaluating myocardial injury in 20 non-hospitalised patients with persistent symptoms >4 months after mild COVID-19 using cardiac MRI and pulmonary investigations. Found a higher-than-expected burden of myocardial fibrosis (scar on LGE imaging) in this long COVID cohort despite absence of abnormal T1/T2 values.
paper_authors: Krishnan A.; Ellenberger KA; Phetsouphanh C.; Kelleher AP; Matthews GV; Darley DR; Holloway CJ
paper_title: Myocardial fibrosis occurs in non-hospitalised patients with chronic symptoms after COVID-19

summary: ARCA post-COVID is an observational study investigating the prevalence of new cardiac alterations (NCA) in 502 COVID-19 recovered patients between June 2020 and December 2022. The study found NCA in 27.49% of patients, with pericardial effusion in 11.95%, and identified risk factors including older age, smoking, prior CAD, and stroke/TIA history.
paper_authors: Valeria Antoncecchi; Ettore Antoncecchi; Enrico Orsini; Giuseppe D'Ascenzo; Ugo Oliviero; Ketty Savino; Angelo Aloisio; Laura Casalino; Adele Lillo; Emilia Chiuini; Giosuè Santoro; Vincenzo Manfrè; Valeria Rizzo; Giovanni Battista Zito
paper_title: High prevalence of cardiac post-acute sequelae in patients recovered from Covid-19. Results from the ARCA post-COVID study
paper_journal: International Journal of Cardiology Cardiovascular Risk and Prevention

summary: This cross-sectional study compared circulating angiogenic progenitor cells (CAC) and endothelial cells (CEC) in 14 post-hospitalized post-COVID syndrome (PH-PCS) patients versus 7 matched controls at ≥18 months post-infection. The study found suggestive but imprecise evidence of unbalanced CAC and CEC apoptosis in PH-PCS patients, with possible associations between reduced flow-mediated dilation and cellular markers.
paper_authors: Julia M. Kröpfl; Christoph Hauser; Luca Beugger; Henner Hanssen; Fabian Schwendinger; Arno Schmidt-Trucksäss
paper_title: Circulating angiogenic progenitor cell apoptosis in Post-COVID-19 syndrome

summary: Longitudinal study tracking anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibody levels in 61 convalescent patients over 8 months and their association with post-COVID syndrome symptoms. Found stable antibody titers in 92% of participants and 46.8% prevalence of post-COVID syndrome, primarily affecting olfactory and gustatory function.
paper_authors: Catharina Gerhards; Margot Thiaucourt; Maximilian Kittel; Celine Becker; Volker Ast; Michael Hetjens; Michael Neumaier; Verena Haselmann
paper_title: Longitudinal assessment of anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibody dynamics and clinical features following convalescence from a COVID-19 infection

summary: A 90-day prospective cohort study comparing symptom trajectories in 210 SARS-CoV-2 positive vs 630 negative healthcare workers. Found persistent loss of taste/smell in 30% of positive cases and prolonged dyspnea at low levels, while most other acute symptoms resolved by 30 days.
paper_authors: Kent J. Nielsen; Jesper Medom Vestergaard; Vivi Schlünssen; Jens Peter Bonde; Kathrine Agergård Kaspersen; Karin Biering; Ole Carstensen; Thomas Greve; Karoline Kærgaard Hansen; Annett Dalbøge; Esben Meulengracht Flachs; Sanne Jespersen; Mette Lausten Hansen; Susan Mikkelsen; Marianne Kragh Thomsen; Jacob Dvinge Redder; Else Toft Würtz; Lars Østergaard; Christian Erikstrup; Henrik Albert Kolstad
paper_title: Day-by-day symptoms following positive and negative PCR tests for SARS-CoV-2 in non-hospitalized healthcare workers: A 90-day follow-up study

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines the prevalence of long-term sick leave (≥4 weeks) among 30,950 working-age COVID-19 patients in German general practices and identifies associated risk factors. The study is observational without treatment evaluation, making it ineligible for the intervention trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: Louis Jacob; Ai Koyanagi; Lee Smith; Christian Tanislav; Marcel Konrad; Susanne van der Beck; Karel Kostev
paper_title: Prevalence of, and factors associated with, long-term COVID-19 sick leave in working-age patients followed in general practices in Germany

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining associations between post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) and cardiac outcomes in 997,785 U.S. military members. PASC was significantly associated with increased odds of multiple cardiac events including myocarditis, heart failure, and arrhythmias.
paper_authors: Sithembile Mabila; Deven Patel; Michael Fan; Shauna Stahlman; Nicholas Seliga; Gosia Nowak; Natalie Wells
paper_title: Post –acute sequalae of COVID-19 and cardiac outcomes in U. S. military members
paper_journal: International Journal of Cardiology Cardiovascular Risk and Prevention

summary: Prospective follow-up study of 94 COVID-19 survivors one year post-hospitalization, assessing symptoms, imaging, and pulmonary function. Found high prevalence of chest CT abnormalities (71%) and muscle fatigue/insomnia as most common symptoms, with urea nitrogen associated with impaired lung diffusion capacity.
paper_authors: Yumiao Zhao; Chunxia Yang; Xiaocai An; Yajun Xiong; Yaomin Shang; Jiarong He; Yan Qiu; Ning Zhang; Lisha Huang; Junli Jia; Qinfu Xu; Long Zhang; Junjie Zhao; Guangzhong Pei; Hong Luo; Jun Wang; Qingquan Li; Yanfeng Gao; Aiguo Xu
paper_title: Follow-up study on COVID-19 survivors one year after discharge from hospital

summary: This study measured serum biomarkers (laminin, vWF, SP-D, RAGE) in 52 COVID-19 survivors 6 months post-discharge compared to 30 healthy controls. No treatment was administered; it is a purely observational study examining persistent lung injury indicators rather than evaluating any intervention.
paper_authors: Hongwei Li; Qian Wu; Zhonghua Qin; Xinwei Hou; Limin Zhang; Jin Guo; Yajie Li; Fangfei Yang; Yan Zhang; Qi Wu; Li Li; Huaiyong Chen; Li Li; Huaiyong Chen
paper_title: Serum levels of laminin and von Willebrand factor in COVID-19 survivors 6 months after discharge

summary: A 6-month prospective study of 75 patients with non-severe acute COVID-19, tracking long COVID symptoms occurring 1-12 weeks post-infection. Documents prevalence of fatigue (33%), anxiety (40%), brain fog (20%), respiratory symptoms, and other manifestations, with findings that symptom burden correlates with patient age.
paper_authors: N. Negrut; Tobias Ivan
paper_title: Long COVID-19 - a pathology of concern

summary: Prospective observational cohort study following 199 patients hospitalized with moderate-to-severe COVID-19 at 3 and 6 months post-discharge to characterize long-term sequelae. At 6 months, 47% had persistent exertional dyspnea and 32% had fatigue; imaging showed high prevalence of persistent abnormalities despite some functional improvement over time.
paper_authors: Gilles Darcis; Antoine Bouquegneau; Nathalie Maes; Marie Thys; Monique Henket; Florence Labye; Anne-Françoise Rousseau; Perrine Canivet; Colin Desir; Doriane Calmes; Raphael Schils; Sophie De Worm; Philippe Léonard; Paul Meunier; Michel Moutschen; Renaud Louis; Julien Guiot
paper_title: Long-term clinical follow-up of patients suffering from moderate-to-severe COVID-19 infection: a monocentric prospective observational cohort study

summary: Multicenter observational study tracking the recovery trajectory of post-COVID-19 symptoms in 1,593 previously hospitalized patients at two timepoints (8.4 and 13.2 months post-hospitalization). Found that symptom burden decreased over time, with 61.8% of patients reporting fewer symptoms at the later follow-up.
paper_authors: César Fernández-de-las-Peñas; José D. Martín-Guerrero; Ignacio Cancela-Cilleruelo; Paloma Moro-López-Menchero; Jorge Rodríguez-Jiménez; Oscar J. Pellicer-Valero
paper_title: Exploring the trajectory recovery curve of the number of post-COVID Symptoms: The LONG-COVID-EXP-CM Multicenter Study

summary: Multicenter retrospective cohort study of 1,969 COVID-19 patients hospitalized in Madrid, assessing clinical risk factors associated with long-term post-COVID symptoms at 8.4 months follow-up. Found that higher symptom load during acute phase (female gender, comorbidities, specific symptoms like vomiting, dyspnea, headache) predicted greater number of long-term symptoms, but the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: César Fernández-de-las-Peñas; Oscar J. Pellicer-Valero; Esperanza Navarro-Pardo; Domingo Palacios-Ceña; Lidiane L. Florencio; Carlos Guijarro; José D. Martín-Guerrero
paper_title: Symptoms Experienced at the Acute Phase of SARS-CoV-2 Infection as Risk Factor of Long-term Post-COVID Symptoms: The LONG-COVID-EXP-CM Multicenter Study

summary: Prospective cohort study of 316 hospitalized COVID-19 patients followed 4 months post-discharge to identify risk factors for long COVID-19 persistence. Found that female sex, hypertension, and higher number of initial symptoms were significantly associated with persistent symptoms, but acute severity measures were not.
paper_authors: Adrien Chan Sui Ko; Alexandre Candellier; Marie Mercier; Cédric Joseph; Jean-Luc Schmit; Jean-Philippe Lanoix; Claire Andrejak
paper_title: Number of initial symptoms is more related to long COVID-19 than acute severity of infection: a prospective cohort of hospitalized patients

summary: Longitudinal surveillance study tracking post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC) in Long Beach residents from April-December 2020, with follow-up at 1 and 2 months post-testing. Identified prevalence of PASC, associated risk factors (age, gender, race, comorbidities), and most common symptoms (fatigue, anosmia, dyspnea).
paper_authors: Kyle Shinji Yomogida; Shu‐Hong Zhu; Francesca Rubino; W Figueroa; N. Barin; E. Alison Holman
paper_title: Longitudinal surveillance of Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 among Long Beach City residents, April-December, 2020

summary: Multicenter prospective cohort study describing long-COVID symptoms in older adults (>65 years) versus younger individuals across Israel, Switzerland, Spain, and Italy. Found older adults more symptomatic with higher rates of fatigue (38%) and dyspnea (30%), plus pulmonary impairment, while female gender and obesity emerged as independent risk factors across age groups.

paper_title: Characteristics of long-COVID among older adults: a cross-sectional study

summary: Longitudinal cohort study following 226 nonhospitalized COVID-19 patients from the Faroe Islands with up to 8 months follow-up to assess long COVID prevalence and symptom burden. Found 39% reported persistent symptoms and 8% reported severe persistent symptoms, with fatigue and smell/taste dysfunction being most common.
paper_authors: Maria Skaalum Petersen; Marnar Fríðheim Kristiansen; Katrin Dahl Hanusson; Billa Mouritsardóttir Foldbo; Marjun Eivindardóttir Danielsen; Bjarni á. Steig; Shahin Gaini; Marin Strøm; Pál Weihe
paper_title: Prevalence of long COVID in a national cohort: longitudinal measures from disease onset until 8 months’ follow-up

summary: This study compares post-acute COVID-19 symptoms 3-15 months after infection between unvaccinated and vaccinated individuals with breakthrough infections using questionnaire data from the Norwegian COVID-19 cohort. Vaccination offered minor protection against PASC symptoms overall, with vaccinated participants reporting fewer memory problems than unvaccinated participants.
paper_authors: Sonja H. Brunvoll; Anders B. Nygaard; Morten W. Fagerland; Petter Holland; Merete Ellingjord-Dale; John Arne Dahl; Arne Søraas
paper_title: Post-acute symptoms 3-15 months after COVID-19 among unvaccinated and vaccinated individuals with a breakthrough infection

summary: Prospective observational cohort study following 155 COVID-19 patients at 2-4 months and 7-14 months post-infection to assess health-related quality of life using the SF-12 questionnaire and identify predictors of post-COVID syndrome. Patients with persistent symptoms had significantly lower physical composite scores that did not improve over time, with lower baseline physical function and elevated resting heart rate identified as predictors of long COVID at 1 year.
paper_authors: Brendan O'Kelly; Louise Vidal; Gordana Avramovic; John Broughan; Stephen Peter Connolly; Aoife G. Cotter; Walter Cullen; Shannon Glaspy; Tina McHugh; James Woo; John S. Lambert
paper_title: Assessing the impact of COVID-19 at 1-year using the SF-12 questionnaire: Data from the Anticipate longitudinal cohort study

summary: Prospective study examining short- and long-term immune changes across COVID-19 severity groups at presentation, week 2, and week 24. Findings show differential immune responses by severity, with severe/critical patients showing initial dysfunction but partial normalization by 24 weeks.
paper_authors: Khuloud Al Maamari; Ibrahim Al Busaidi; Mahmood Al Kindi; Fahad Zadjali; Fatma BaAlawi; Wijesinghe Anesta; Kawthar Al Amri; Wafa Albalushi; Hamed Al Balushi; Ayman Al Amri; Mahmood Aljufaili; Mujahid Al-Busaidi; Zakariya Al Muharrmi; Abdullah Balkhair; Nafila Al Riyami; Zahraa Ghanim; Jalila Alshekaili
paper_title: Short and long-term immune changes in different severity groups of COVID-19 disease

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines the prevalence, risk factors, and healthcare costs of long COVID in 180,759 Israeli COVID-19 patients, identifying 14,088 cases (7.8%). Long COVID was associated with increased hospitalizations and significantly higher direct medical costs ($2,810 vs $1,021 for non-long COVID patients), highlighting the substantial economic burden of the condition.
paper_authors: Lilac Tene; Tobias Bergroth; Anna Eisenberg; Shirley Shapiro Ben David; Gabriel Chodick
paper_title: Risk factors, health outcomes, healthcare services utilization, and direct medical costs of patients with long COVID

summary: Population-based cohort study characterizing 10,196 Swedish patients diagnosed with post-COVID-19 condition (U09.9) during the first 16 months of ICD-10 code implementation. Study describes sociodemographic characteristics, comorbidities, and disease patterns but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Maria Bygdell; Susannah Leach; Lisa Lundberg; David Gyll; Jari Martikainen; Ailiana Santosa; Huiqi Li; Magnus Gisslén; Fredrik Nyberg
paper_title: A comprehensive characterization of patients diagnosed with post-COVID-19 condition in Sweden 16 months after the introduction of the International Classification of Diseases Tenth Revision diagnosis code (U09.9): a population-based cohort study

summary: An 18.5-month prospective cohort study of 208 COVID-19 convalescents documenting sequential improvements in physical and psychological sequelae, but with persistent symptoms in 45.2% and abnormal lung imaging in ~30% at the final timepoint. The study identifies ongoing pathophysiological alterations and risk factors for symptom persistence but does not test any intervention.

paper_title: Long-term outcomes of COVID-19 convalescents: An 18.5-month longitudinal study in Wuhan

summary: Prospective cohort study following hospitalized and nonhospitalized COVID-19 patients in South Africa across three variant waves to assess post-COVID-19 condition prevalence at 6 months. Found 46.7% of hospitalized and 18.5% of nonhospitalized participants had persistent symptoms; identified risk factors including age, sex, comorbidities, and severity but found no intervention or treatment being tested.
paper_authors: Waasila Jassat; Caroline Mudara; Caroline Vika; Richard Welch; Tracy Arendse; Murray Dryden; Lucille Blumberg; Natalie Mayet; Stefano Tempia; Arifa Parker; Jeremy Nel; Rubeshan Perumal; Michelle J. Groome; Francesca Conradie; Norbert Ndjeka; Louise Sigfrid; Laura Merson; Cheryl Cohen
paper_title: A cohort study of post-COVID-19 condition across the Beta, Delta, and Omicron waves in South Africa: 6-month follow-up of hospitalized and nonhospitalized participants

summary: Population-based retrospective cohort study examining incident diabetes risk following COVID-19 infection using BC COVID-19 Cohort data. Finds increased diabetes incidence in COVID-19 infected individuals, particularly among males and those with severe disease (HR=1.16-3.32).
paper_authors: Zaeema Naveed; Héctor Alexander Velásquez García; Stanley Wong; James Wilton; Geoffrey McKee; Bushra Mahmood; Mawuena Binka; Drona Rasali; Naveed Z. Janjua
paper_title: RISK OF INCIDENT DIABETES FOLLOWING COVID-19 INFECTION: A POPULATION-BASED COHORT STUDY

summary: Observational study comparing persistent symptoms in 639 Argentine children with prior COVID-19 versus 577 uninfected controls. One-third of infected children experienced long COVID symptoms; older age, symptomatic infection, and comorbidities were independent risk factors.
paper_authors: Vanesa Seery; Silvina Raiden; Juan Martín Gómez Penedo; Mauricio Borda; Largión Herrera; Macarena Uranga; María Marcó del Pont; Carina Chirino; Constanza Erramuspe; Laura Silvana Alvarez; Melisa Lenoir; Laura Daniela Morales; Carolina Davenport; Soledad Huespe Auchter; Liliana Monsalvo; Laura Sastoque; Magalí Gavazzi; Constanza Russo; Inés Sananez; María de los Ángeles Pando; Natalia Laufer; Roberto Muiños; Fernando Ferrero; Jorge Geffner; Lourdes Arruvito
paper_title: Persistent symptoms after COVID-19 in children and adolescents from Argentina

summary: Retrospective analysis of 83 cases of Clostridium difficile colitis occurring during or after COVID-19 infection in post-COVID patients, examining risk factors and therapeutic outcomes. The study found that prior broad-spectrum antibiotic use was a major risk factor (occurring in 55% of cases), and demonstrated efficacy of vancomycin, metronidazole, and fidaxonicin treatments with 14% recurrence rate and FMT used in severe cases.
paper_authors: Silvia Cveková; Květoslava Aiglová
paper_title: CLOSTRIDIUM DIFFICILLAE INFECTION IN POST-COVID PATIENTS

summary: This prospective cohort study tracks 2,197 long COVID patients over 2 years to identify symptom evolution patterns using trajectory modeling. The study identifies three trajectories: 91% with slowly decreasing symptoms, 5% with rapid improvement, and 4% with persistent symptoms, but does not test any intervention.
paper_authors: Clemence Servier; Raphael Porcher; Isabelle Pane; Philippe Ravaud; Viet-Thi Tran
paper_title: Trajectories of the evolution of post-COVID-19 condition, up to two years after symptoms onset

summary: This is a secondary analysis of the DigiHero cohort study examining how SARS-CoV-2 variants, vaccination, and previous infections affect post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) risk. The study does not test or evaluate any intervention—it is purely observational, comparing PCC risk across variant exposures and vaccination histories.
paper_authors: Sophie Diexer; Bianca Klee; Cornelia Gottschick; Chao Xu; Anja Broda; Oliver Purschke; Mascha Binder; Thomas Frese; Matthias Girndt; Jessica I. Hoell; Irene Moor; Michael Gekle; Rafael Mikolajczyk
paper_title: Association between virus variants, vaccination, previous infections, and post-COVID-19 risk

summary: Prospective observational cohort study evaluating the impact of COVID-19 vaccination on long COVID (post-COVID condition) symptoms, immune responses, and viral persistence in 86 patients. Vaccination was associated with significant decreases in symptom count and organ system involvement, increased well-being scores, and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine levels, though SARS-CoV-2 viral antigens persisted in blood regardless of vaccination status.

paper_title: Vaccination after developing long COVID: Impact on clinical presentation, viral persistence, and immune responses

summary: A prospective cohort study of 806 long COVID patients followed for 1.5 years post-infection, comparing symptom severity and prognosis across SARS-CoV-2 variants (wild-type, Alpha, Delta, Omicron). The study found no clinically meaningful improvement over 1.5 years, with >57% of patients showing persistent severe symptoms regardless of infection variant.
paper_authors: Jane Agergaard; Jesper Damsgaard Gunst; Berit Schiøttz-Christensen; Lars Østergaard; Christian Wejse
paper_title: Long-term prognosis at 1.5 years after infection with wild-type strain of SARS-CoV-2 and Alpha, Delta, as well as Omicron variants

summary: Prospective multicenter cohort study of 502 patients hospitalized for COVID-19, examining whether in-hospital treatments (steroids, anti-inflammatory, antiviral) predict long-term health problems at 2-year follow-up. Found that in-hospital COVID-19 treatments were not significantly associated with long-term health problems including dyspnea, fatigue, cognitive failures, or quality of life.
paper_authors: Berentschot JC; Martine Bek L.; Heijenbrok-Kal MH; van den Berg-Emons RJG; Ribbers GM; Aerts JGJV; Hellemons ME
paper_title: Acute COVID-19 treatment is not associated with health problems 2 years after hospitalization

summary: A prospective cohort study of 231 French long COVID patients followed for 12 months to examine symptom course, impact on daily life, and factors associated with improvement. Found that only 8.7% achieved complete remission, 28.6% improved significantly, and most symptoms persisted; presence of pre-vaccination SARS-CoV-2 antibodies predicted improvement while ageusia predicted worse outcomes.
paper_authors: Dominique Salmon; Dorsaf Slama; Françoise Linard; Nicolas Dumesges; Valérie Le Baut; Florence Hakim; Pauline Oustric; Emilie Seyrat; Patricia Thoreux; Esaie Marshall
paper_title: Patients with Long COVID continue to experience significant symptoms at 12 months and factors associated with improvement: A prospective cohort study in France (PERSICOR)

summary: This study analyzed pre-pandemic predictors of long COVID in a representative Dutch population of 3,022 participants, identifying sociodemographic, medical, and psychosocial factors associated with long COVID development. The authors used K-means clustering to identify four distinct symptom clusters and their respective predictors, revealing heterogeneous presentations of long COVID.
paper_authors: Isabel A.L. Slurink; Sophie C.M. van den Houdt; Gaëtan Mertens
paper_title: Who develops long COVID? Longitudinal pre-pandemic predictors of long COVID and symptom clusters in a representative Dutch population

summary: Prospective cohort study tracking 14 somatic and cognitive symptoms in 120,605 Norwegian adults with pre-infection baseline measurements and follow-up for up to 22 months. Study confirms COVID-19 associated with persistent cognitive symptoms, anosmia, dysgeusia, dyspnea, and fatigue, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Temporal trajectories of long-COVID symptoms in adults with 22 months follow-up in a prospective cohort study in Norway

summary: This retrospective cohort study analyzed data from South Korean COVID-19 patients aged >60 years to investigate whether oral antivirals (nirmatrelvir/ritonavir and molnupiravir) reduce the risk of postacute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) within 30-120 days post-infection. Both antivirals showed significant protective effects against multiple PASC outcomes, including cardiovascular complications, respiratory diseases, and renal disorders, suggesting oral antivirals may mitigate long-term COVID-19 effects.
paper_authors: Hyejin Joo; Eunji Kim; Kyungmin Huh; Gi Hwan Bae; Hyungmin Lee; Jungyeon Kim; Dong-Hwi Kim; Min-Gyu Yoo; Il Uk Jo; Poong Hoon Lee; Geun Woo Lee; Hee Sun Jung; Jaehun Jung
paper_title: Risk of postacute sequelae of COVID-19 and oral antivirals in adults aged over 60 years: A nationwide retrospective cohort study

summary: Prospective cohort study comparing post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) prevalence in Delta- vs Omicron-infected adults over 12 months with population controls. PASC prevalence was higher for Delta initially (34.3% at 3 months) than Omicron (18.7%), but both declined over time and converged by 12 months.
paper_authors: Siméon de Bruijn; Anna D. Tulen; Jeroen Rodenburg; Hendriek Boshuizen; Maarten Schipper; Elizabeth N. Mutubuki; Hans Knoop; Eelco Franz; Tessa van der Maaden; Susan van den Hof; Albert Jan van Hoek; Cees C. van den Wijngaard
paper_title: Post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 3 to 12 months after infection: Delta vs Omicron

summary: This is a secondary analysis of national electronic health records examining hospitalization and mortality outcomes in COVID-19 and Long COVID patients, stratified by vaccination status and cardiovascular disease. While about Long COVID, it analyzes existing data rather than testing a specific intervention, making it ineligible for a treatment trials meta-analysis.

paper_title: Vaccinations, cardiovascular drugs, hospitalization, and mortality in COVID-19 and Long COVID

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing long-term sequelae 31-300 days post-hospitalization between Omicron COVID-19 (n=70,628) and influenza (n=10,454) patients in Singapore, stratified by vaccination status. Found higher risks of cognitive impairment and fatigue post-COVID-19 vs influenza, but lower cardiac sequelae risk, with vaccination modifying outcomes.
paper_authors: Liang En Wee; Reen Wan Li Ho; Jue Tao Lim; Calvin J. Chiew; David Chien Boon Lye; Kelvin Bryan Tan
paper_title: Long-term multisystemic sequelae post-hospitalisation for Omicron COVID-19 vs influenza: A retrospective cohort study

summary: Retrospective survey-based cohort study of 26,474 Quebec healthcare workers examining long COVID risk, prevalence (5.6%), and severity in relation to reinfections, variants, and acute infection severity. Reinfections, Omicron variant, and nonsevere acute infection were associated with lower long COVID risk, but the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Long COVID risk and severity after COVID-19 infections and reinfections: A retrospective cohort study among healthcare workers

summary: This binational cohort study in South Korea and Japan examined the long-term risk of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 in 1.1M individuals with type 2 diabetes, using propensity score weighting and Cox proportional hazards models. The study found increased risks of sequelae across 8 organ systems in COVID-infected vs non-infected individuals, with risks peaking within 12 months, but does not test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Jiyeon Oh; Soeun Kim; Hyesu Jo; Jaeyu Park; Yejun Son; Sooji Lee; Jinseok Lee; Lee Smith; Jiseung Kang; Junyang Jung; Hayeon Lee; Dong Keon Yon
paper_title: Burden of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 in patients with type 2 diabetes: a binational cohort study in South Korea and Japan

summary: Retrospective cohort study analyzing PASC prevalence and risk factors using Dutch primary care EHR data from 19,638 SARS-CoV-2 positive patients. Identifies comorbidities (lung disease, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, kidney disease) and demographics (age ≥45, female gender) as significant predictors of long COVID onset and duration.
paper_authors: Matthijs S. Berends; Maarten Homburg; Thijmen Kupers; Eline N. Meijer; Isabelle Bos; Robert Verheij; Jeroen Kuiper; Marjolein Y. Berger; Lilian L. Peters
paper_title: Impact of pre-existing comorbidities and multimorbidities, demography and viral variants on post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (‘Long COVID’) in Dutch primary care: A retrospective cohort study

summary: This study compares nasal microbiota and clinical features in 291 individuals with acute flu-like illness, stratified by COVID-19 status and long COVID outcomes (persistent symptoms >3 months). While COVID-19-positive individuals showed lower nasal microbiota diversity and those who developed LC had more acute cardiorespiratory symptoms, no LC-specific microbial profile was identified.
paper_authors: Carolina Alves Costa Silva; Adriele Pinheiro Bomfim; Julliane Dutra Medeiros; Jéssica de Jesus Silva; Ana Beatriz Cazé-Ceron; Thiago Cerqueira-Silva; Ricardo Khouri; Aldina Barral; Manoel Barral-Netto; Gabriel da Rocha Fernandes; Cynara Gomes Barbosa; Viviane S․ Boaventura
paper_title: Nasal microbiota and clinical features in acute flu-like illness: COVID-19 status and long COVID follow-up

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines all-cause mortality risk in COVID-19 hospitalization survivors versus matched uninfected controls over 3.5 years of follow-up. The study found elevated mortality in hospitalized patients (HR 1.69) with differential risk by age group, but does not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Wiessam Abu Ahmad; Yael Wolff-Sagy; Erez Battat; Ronen Arbel; Gil Lavie
paper_title: Mortality following recovery from COVID-19 hospitalization: A long-term cohort study

summary: This retrospective cohort study analyzed lymphocyte subset counts in 40,537 patients across pre-COVID, mass infection, and post-COVID phases to assess persistence of immune alterations. The findings demonstrate sustained lymphopenia 20 months post-infection, particularly in older adults, males, and cardiovascular disease patients, characterizing long COVID as a condition of long-lasting immune compromise.
paper_authors: Zhengqi Jiang; Tichao Shan; Yucan Li; Fengjiao Han; Baobao Feng; Xiaohui Zhen; Ji Ma; Heyu Ni; Jun Peng; Miao Xu
paper_title: Persistent attenuation of lymphocyte subsets after mass SARS-CoV-2 infection

summary: Develops and validates static and dynamic PASC scoring systems in a multicenter Korean cohort of 4,668 participants (4,388 infected, 280 controls) followed for up to 24 months. Identifies nine symptoms associated with long COVID and establishes quantitative diagnostic criteria, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

paper_title: Static and dynamic scoring systems for post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 in a Korean Cohort

summary: Retrospective cohort study evaluating whether early neutralizing monoclonal antibody (mAb) treatment reduces post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) in high-risk unvaccinated or immunocompromised individuals in Singapore. While mAb therapy did not significantly reduce overall PASC risk, it was associated with increased autoimmune complications and elevated thrombosis risk.
paper_authors: Jinghao Nicholas Ngiam; Liang En Wee; Jue Tao Lim; Enoch Xueheng Loy; Matthew Chung Yi Koh; An Ting Tay; Huei Xin Lou; Phyllis Kim; Calvin J. Chiew; Barnaby Edward Young; Shawn Vasoo; David Chien Boon Lye; Kelvin Bryan Tan
paper_title: Early administration of neutralizing monoclonal antibodies and post-acute sequelae of COVID-19

summary: Prospective cohort study examining the incidence of post-COVID-19 syndrome and its association with acute COVID-19 severity in 280 discharged patients. Found 71.43% developed post-COVID-19 syndrome with higher rates in severe cases, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Ericka Lyn A. Monzon; Kingbherly L. Li
paper_title: Incidence of post-COVID-19 syndrome and its association with COVID-19 severity in a tertiary private hospital: Prospective cohort study

summary: A prospective cohort study following 310 Greenlandic adults over 12 months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection to assess acute and long-term COVID-19 outcomes. Found that 53.7% recovered within 4 weeks, but long COVID symptoms (fatigue, mental exhaustion) persisted in a subset up to 12 months post-infection.
paper_authors: Mie Møller; Trine Abelsen; Anna Irene Vedel Sørensen; Mikael Andersson; Lennart Friis-Hansen; Christine Dilling-Hansen; Nikolai Kirkby; Peter Vedsted; Kåre Mølbak; Anders Koch
paper_title: Exploring the dynamics of COVID-19 in a Greenlandic cohort: Mild acute illness and moderate risk of long COVID

summary: This prospective cohort study tracked 396 Japanese patients for up to 12 months post-COVID to examine labor productivity changes and economic impacts across three symptom progression groups (non-long COVID, recovered, persistent). The persistent long COVID group showed significantly reduced work productivity compared to other groups, highlighting the substantial socioeconomic burden of ongoing long COVID symptoms.

paper_title: The relationship between long COVID, labor productivity, and socioeconomic losses in Japan: A cohort study

summary: This cross-sectional study characterizes monocyte subpopulation patterns in 89 patients across acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, long COVID-19 syndrome, and viral controls (Zika/CHIKV) using flow cytometry. The study found elevated classical and intermediate monocyte counts in acute infection and long COVID patients compared to other viral infections, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Monocytes subpopulations pattern in the acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 virus infection and after long COVID-19

summary: This study examines B cell dynamics and herpesvirus reactivation during acute COVID-19 and long-term follow-up (up to 460 days) in 120 patients. While the paper measures long COVID proxy (anosmia) and discusses PASC pathophysiology, it is a natural history observational study that does not evaluate or test any intervention or treatment.

paper_title: B cell dysregulation during acute COVID-19 is transient

summary: This study identifies neural injury biomarkers (GFAP and NF-L) associated with neurologic sequelae one year after SARS-CoV-2 hospitalization, comparing COVID-19 patients to historical pre-COVID controls. Elevated biomarker levels remained significantly associated with long-term neurological symptoms after adjusting for demographic and severity factors.
paper_authors: Spanos M.; Shachar S.; Sweeney T.; Lehmann HI; Gokulnath P.; Li G.; Sigal GB; Nagaraj R.; Bathala P.; Rana F.; Shah RV; Routenberg DA; Das S.
paper_title: Elevation of neural injury markers in patients with neurologic sequelae after hospitalization for SARS-CoV-2 infection

summary: This prospective cohort study uses target trial emulation to compare the risk of new-onset long COVID symptoms between 1,055 SARS-CoV-2 infected individuals and 52,310 uninfected controls from the CHASING COVID Cohort. The study found infected participants had significantly higher risks of long COVID symptoms (22.6% vs 11.3% at 4-8 months) across neurological, autonomic, and exercise intolerance clusters, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Yanhan Shen; Zach Shahn; McKaylee M. Robertson; Kelly Gebo; Denis Nash
paper_title: Natural history of self-reported symptoms following SARS-CoV-2 infection: A target trial emulation in a prospective community-recruited cohort

summary: Prospective cohort study following 2,524 hospitalized COVID-19 patients for 12 months to assess long COVID prevalence across different SARS-CoV-2 variants and lineages. Found 35.2% prevalence at one month with similar overall rates across variants, though specific lineages (Delta AY.126, AY.43, Omicron BA.1.17, BA.2.56, BA.5.1) showed stronger symptom severity correlations.
paper_authors: Sergio Padilla; Christian Ledesma; Javier García-Abellán; José Alberto García; Marta Fernández-González; Alba de la Rica; Antonio Galiana; Félix Gutiérrez; Mar Masiá
paper_title: Long COVID across SARS-CoV-2 variants, lineages, and sublineages

summary: Prospective longitudinal study of adolescents (12-17 years) with anxiety disorders treated with duloxetine or escitalopram, examining the impact of SARS-CoV-2 infection on anxiety and depressive symptoms over time. Found that COVID-19 infection was associated with worsening anxiety symptoms and a 33% worsening in syndromic severity in this anxious youth population.
paper_authors: Jeffrey R. Strawn; Jeffrey A. Mills; Heidi K. Schroeder; Zoe A. Neptune; Ashley Specht; Susana W. Keeshin
paper_title: The Impact of COVID-19 Infection and Characterization of Long COVID in Adolescents With Anxiety Disorders: A Prospective Longitudinal Study
paper_journal: Journal of the American Academy of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry

summary: Population-based cohort study (BAMSE) comparing lung function in young adults before and after COVID-19 infection using spirometry and serology. Found no significant differences in lung function decline between seropositive and seronegative participants, and asthma/ICS use did not modify outcomes.

paper_journal: Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology: Global

summary: This prospective observational study evaluated 24 long COVID patients with symptoms of orthostatic intolerance using head-up tilt table testing to characterize autonomic dysfunction. Nearly all patients demonstrated orthostatic intolerance on testing, with those having provoked orthostatic intolerance showing earlier symptom improvement compared to those with POTS.
paper_authors: Sameer M. Jamal; David B. Landers; Steven M. Hollenberg; Zoltan G. Turi; Taya V. Glotzer; Jana Tancredi; Joseph E. Parrillo
paper_title: Prospective Evaluation of Autonomic Dysfunction in Post-Acute Sequela of COVID-19
paper_journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

summary: Observational study of 408 long COVID patients with persistent chemosensory dysfunction (smell/taste loss) followed across 2021-2023, assessing predictors of recovery and symptom characteristics. Finds that cigarette smoke phantosmia predicts persistence while environmental allergies and hypertension predict recovery; no treatments resolved the dysfunction, though nasal steroids were reported helpful by recovered patients.
paper_authors: Dante G. Minichetti; Amelia Boyd; Evan Lemire; Jonathan Hacker; Adam L. Haber; Rachel E. Roditi; Mark W. Albers; Stella Lee; Kathleen M. Buchheit; Tanya M. Laidlaw; Lora G. Bankova
paper_title: Determinants of persistence and recovery of chronic coronavirus disease 2019 chemosensory dysfunction
paper_journal: Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology

summary: This retrospective cohort study examined whether nirmatrelvir-ritonavir (Paxlovid) reduced the incidence of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) in vaccinated patients with pre-existing cardiovascular disease. The treatment group showed a significantly lower rate of PASC (26% vs 30.6%) compared to untreated controls over 6 months of follow-up.

paper_title: Nirmatrelvir-Ritonavir for Acute COVID-19 in Patients With Cardiovascular Disease and Postacute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: This longitudinal observational cohort study followed 89 patients from an original cohort of 144 at 1-year and 2-year visits to investigate pulmonary and renal long COVID manifestations. The study identified fibrous lung stripes in 17.8% and renal involvement in 23.9% of patients at 2-year follow-up, with machine learning models predicting these outcomes from early clinical and multi-omics data, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

paper_title: Pulmonary and renal long COVID at two-year revisit

summary: This cross-sectional study compares autonomic function measures in patients with long COVID, healthy controls, and patients with pure autonomic failure using quantitative autonomic testing including heart rate, blood pressure, Valsalva, and tilt-table assessments. Patients with long COVID showed autonomic dysfunction patterns similar to pure autonomic failure patients when adjusted for age and sex, with abnormalities persisting up to 40 months post-infection.
paper_authors: Ciana Keller; Lorraine Mascarenhas; Jorge L. Reyes; Sue Duval; David G. Benditt
paper_title: Association of Autonomic Dysfunction With Long COVID

summary: This observational study characterizes postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) in long COVID patients using self-reported data from the Yale LISTEN cohort (n=578, surveyed May 2022–July 2023). Findings show 28.9% reported new-onset POTS with significantly worse health outcomes, higher symptom burden, and greater psychosocial distress compared to long COVID patients without POTS.

paper_title: Characterization of Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome in Long COVID

summary: A prospective cross-sectional assessment of cognitive function, mental health symptoms, and functional decline in 82 COVID-19 survivors (~4 months post-diagnosis) at Johns Hopkins Post-Acute COVID-19 Team clinic. Found 67% had abnormal cognitive scores (primarily processing speed, verbal fluency, learning, memory), with 35% reporting depression, anxiety, or functional decline; ICU patients showed greater severity of cognitive impairment.
paper_authors: Tracy D. Vannorsdall; Emily Brigham; Ashraf Fawzy; Sarath Raju; Alesandra Gorgone; Alexandra Pletnikova; Constantine G. Lyketsos; Ann M. Parker; Esther S. Oh
paper_title: Cognitive Dysfunction, Psychiatric Distress, and Functional Decline After COVID-19
paper_journal: Journal of the Academy of Consultation-Liaison Psychiatry

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing emergency visits and hospitalizations for cardiovascular diagnoses between 177,892 SARS-CoV-2 positive adults and matched negative controls in the postacute phase (>3 months). Found significantly elevated risks for diabetes, hypertension, heart failure, and kidney injury in COVID-19 survivors, particularly those hospitalized during acute infection.
paper_authors: Finlay A. McAlister; Majid Nabipoor; Ting Wang; Jeffrey A. Bakal
paper_title: Emergency Visits or Hospitalizations for Cardiovascular Diagnoses in the Post-Acute Phase of COVID-19

summary: Longitudinal observational study of 75 long COVID patients undergoing neuropsychological testing at ~7 months post-infection and 6-month follow-up. Found that 38.7% had low NP performance initially; while some domains improved by follow-up, persistent neuropsychiatric symptoms remained in most participants with minimal clinical improvement.
paper_authors: Sean T. Lynch; Rhea Dornbush; Sivan Shahar; Rayah Mansour; Lidia Klepacz; Louis H. Primavera; Stephen J. Ferrando
paper_title: Change in Neuropsychological Test Performance Seen in a Longitudinal Study of Patients With Post-acute Sequelae of COVID-19: A 6-Month Follow-up Study
paper_journal: Journal of the Academy of Consultation-Liaison Psychiatry

summary: This retrospective cohort study examined associations between post-traumatic stress disorder symptom trajectories and long COVID risk among 5,361 World Trade Center Health Registry enrollees with COVID-19 infection. All PTSS trajectory groups showed elevated risk of long COVID compared to the resilient group, with RRs ranging from 1.46-1.86, suggesting that pre-existing mental health conditions are a significant risk factor for developing long COVID.
paper_authors: Julia S. Sisti; Samuel E. Packard; Janette Yung; Janna Metzler
paper_title: Trajectories of post-traumatic stress disorder symptoms and subsequent risk of long COVID in the World Trade Center Health Registry

summary: Cross-sectional assessment of cognitive, depressive, and anxiety symptoms in 90 previously independent mild COVID-19 patients during hospitalization (Nov 2020–Mar 2021). Found 66.7% had impaired cognition (MoCA < 23), particularly in executive function and memory, with age-related severity differences, but no elevated depression or anxiety.
paper_authors: Giulia Gamberini; Fabio Giuseppe Masuccio; Marta Cerrato; Mara Strazzacappa; Diana Ferraro; Claudio Solaro
paper_title: Previously independent patients with mild-symptomatic COVID-19 are at high risk of developing cognitive impairment but not depression or anxiety

summary: This cross-sectional study examines the association between loneliness (overall, emotional, and social subtypes) and cognitive function in long COVID patients versus recovered controls. The findings show that emotional and overall loneliness are independently linked to objective cognitive difficulties like reduced verbal fluency and memory, suggesting loneliness as a potential intervention target for cognitive outcomes in long COVID.

paper_title: Cognitive sequala of loneliness in long COVID: Differential associations by loneliness subtypes

summary: Observational study analyzing Reddit posts to examine the association between COVID-19-induced loss of smell/taste and subsequent depression or suicidal ideation risk. The study found users reporting anosmia/ageusia had 30% higher risk of mental health crises, with peak risk occurring >100 days post-infection.
paper_authors: Elad Yom-Tov; Damien Lekkas; Nicholas C. Jacobson
paper_title: Association of COVID19-induced anosmia and ageusia with depression and suicidal ideation

summary: This nationwide population-based cohort study examines long-term impacts of prior COVID-19 on severe asthma exacerbations and mortality in Korean adults. While it studies post-COVID outcomes, it focuses on asthma complications rather than long COVID syndrome itself, and is an observational cohort study with no treatment intervention tested.
paper_authors: Hyun Lee; Bo-Guen Kim; Cho Yun Jeong; Dong Won Park; Tai Sun Park; Ji-Yong Moon; Tae-Hyung Kim; Jang Won Sohn; Ho Joo Yoon; Jong Seung Kim; Sang-Heon Kim
paper_title: Long-Term Impacts of COVID-19 on Severe Exacerbation and Mortality in Adult Asthma: A Nationwide Population-Based Cohort Study
paper_journal: The Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology: In Practice

summary: Prospective cohort study examining mental health outcomes (anxiety, depression, PTSD) and health-related quality of life in COVID-19 survivors stratified by disease severity (moderate, severe, critical) at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months post-infection. Found persistent mental health burden and reduced quality of life across all severity groups at 2 years, with no significant differences between severity groups except lower PTSD in critically ill patients.

paper_title: Long-term consequences on mental health and health related quality of life among COVID-19 patients with different disease severities

summary: This study evaluated the impact of add-on Ayurveda regimen (Dasamoolkadutrayadi Kashayam and Guluchyadi Kwatham) combined with standard care in acute COVID-19 patients, with extended 9-month follow-up to assess for post-COVID sequelae. paper_authors: Christoffer Granvik; Ida-Lisa Persson; Guilherme W.F. Barros; Clas Ahlm; Mattias N.E. Forsell; Staffan Tevell; Josefin Sundh; Anders Blomberg; Alicia Lind; Sara Cajander; Johan Normark
paper_title: Long-term physical capacity following COVID-19: A prospective, three-year study

summary: Retrospective cohort study analyzing Hong Kong electronic health records to examine whether SARS-CoV-2 infection increases multimorbidity risk in patients with pre-existing chronic conditions, stratified by vaccination status. Found COVID-19 infection associated with increased multimorbidity incidence (1.26× unvaccinated, 1.08× vaccinated vs. non-infected controls), demonstrating vaccination's protective effect.

paper_title: Post-COVID-19 multimorbidity incidence by prior vaccination status in people with a pre-existing comorbidity: A population-based cohort study

summary: Retrospective cohort study analyzing risk of chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS) in 3.2 million COVID-19 patients versus matched non-COVID controls using electronic health records. Found COVID-19 patients have significantly higher CFS risk (HR 1.59) across age groups and comorbid conditions, but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Chih-Wei Chen; Hsun-Hua Lee; Shu-Hao Chang; Yi-Ling Chen; Yu-Hsun Wang; Pui-Ying Leong; James Cheng-Chung Wei
paper_title: Risk of chronic fatigue syndrome after COVID-19: A retrospective cohort study of 3227281 patients
paper_journal: Journal of Infection and Public Health

summary: Prospective cohort study of 276 adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection during the Omicron period, tracking symptom persistence and IgG antibody titers over time. Female sex, incomplete vaccination, and comorbidities were risk factors for long COVID persistence (5% at ≥12 months), with lower anti-S1 IgG titers associated with persistent fatigue.

paper_title: Sex, vaccination status, and comorbidities influence long COVID persistence
paper_journal: Journal of Infection and Public Health

summary: Track PCC is a surveillance network study examining the incidence of post-COVID conditions across five U.S. geographic sites during the Omicron period (2022-2023). The study found PCC incidence highest 31-90 days post-infection, with no increase during the Omicron era compared to earlier variants, providing epidemiological data on disease burden rather than evaluating any treatment intervention.

paper_journal: Journal of Infection and Public Health

summary: Ambidirectional cohort study of 222 hospitalized COVID-19 patients followed for a median of 122 days post-discharge to identify predictors of post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PACS) outcomes including dyspnea, exercise intolerance, chronic fatigue, and well-being. Female gender, pre-existing lung disease, ICU admission, and critical illness were significant predictors of worse functional outcomes and mental health.

paper_title: Long term predictors of breathlessness, exercise intolerance, chronic fatigue and well-being in hospitalized patients with COVID-19: A cohort study with 4 months median follow-up
paper_journal: Journal of Infection and Public Health

summary: A prospective cohort study of 470 Swedish COVID-19 patients followed for up to 3 years post-infection, identifying four distinct symptom clusters (Few Symptoms, Respiratory, Neurocognitive, Multisystem) and their trajectories over time. While most participants improved, a subset experienced persistent symptoms at 3 years, with hospitalisation during acute COVID predicting worse outcomes.

paper_title: Post COVID-19 condition phenotypes: A prospective cohort study identifying four symptom clusters and their impact on long-term outcomes
paper_journal: Journal of Infection and Public Health

summary: This study tracked changes in the oral microbiome of COVID-19 recovered patients at 1, 3, and 5 months post-infection using 16S rRNA sequencing of tongue samples. The results show gradual restoration of oral microbiome diversity over 5 months of rehabilitation, with significant increases by month 5 compared to month 1.

paper_title: Alterations in the oral microbiome detected during long-term follow-up of COVID-19 recovered patients

summary: Longitudinal study comparing innate immune cell profiles in COVID-19 recovered patients (mild, moderate, severe) at 1 and 3 months post-recovery against controls. Found persistent immune dysregulation including elevated monocytes, PMN-MDSCs, and inflammatory cytokines associated with long COVID symptoms, but no intervention was tested.

paper_title: Impact of SARS-CoV-2 infection on the profiles and responses of innate immune cells after recovery
paper_journal: Journal of Microbiology, Immunology and Infection

summary: This study examines clinical and immunological characteristics of pediatric post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) in 92 children from the DISCOVER cohort, measuring blood biomarkers and immune responses. The researchers identified elevated anti-nucleocapsid IgG as a potential biomarker for stratifying PASC severity in children, with higher antibody levels correlating with greater symptom burden and monocyte counts.

paper_journal: Journal of Infection and Public Health

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence and severity of neurological and psychiatric long COVID symptoms among 467 vaccinated healthcare workers stratified by COVID-19 status. The study found no statistically significant differences in symptom severity across groups, highlighting potential biases in symptom reporting rather than evaluating any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Yi-Chun Chen; Cheng-Hsun Chiu; Chih-Jung Chen
paper_title: Neurological and psychiatric aspects of long COVID among vaccinated healthcare workers: An assessment of prevalence and reporting biases
paper_journal: Journal of Microbiology, Immunology and Infection

summary: Prospective cohort study of 625 PCR-confirmed COVID-19 patients in Northern Taiwan monitored for 3-6 months to assess long COVID symptoms and quality of life impacts using EQ-5D questionnaire. Found that older age (≥65 years) and hospitalization significantly predicted greater quality of life impairment, but the study passively follows patients without providing any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Liu Chia-ying; Hsu Hsin-sui; Liao Chun-hsing
paper_title: Long COVID Clinical Features in Northern Taiwan: Insights from a Single Medical Center Study
paper_journal: Journal of Microbiology, Immunology and Infection

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 82,070 U.S. veterans examining whether non-severe COVID-19 infection increases risk of developing frailty or pre-frailty over 36 months. Found that positive COVID-19 testing was associated with 66% increase in hazard of becoming frail and 68% increase in pre-frailty, with stronger effects in female patients (330% increase).
paper_authors: Natasha M. Resendes; Jerry Bradley; Fei Tang; Iriana S. Hammel; Jorge G. Ruiz
paper_title: The association of non-severe COVID-19 infection and progression to frailty among robust older veterans
paper_journal: The Journal of nutrition, health and aging

summary: This prospective follow-up study examined cognitive impairment and inflammatory markers in individuals with mild COVID-19 over six months. The paper found that 26% experienced persistent visuospatial difficulties, but 66% of those with initial impairments showed improvement, with changes in cytokine levels (CCL11, HGF, CXCL10) suggesting a link between cognitive issues and pro-inflammatory markers.

paper_title: Follow-up of cognitive impairment and inflammatory profile in individuals with mild COVID-19

summary: A prospective cohort study following 791 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors for 6 months, comparing 196 with neurological complications to 186 matched controls without complications. Patients with neurological complications had significantly worse functional outcomes, activities of daily living, and work capacity at 6-month follow-up, though cognitive and quality-of-life metrics were similar between groups.

Found high prevalence of executive dysfunction (45%), memory problems (25%), and mood disorders (16-18%), particularly in younger patients, with cognitive impairment independent of structural brain changes.

Found that ~50% had cognitive deficits at baseline (primarily verbal memory), with significant improvements over time but persistent borderline scores; depression and PTSD symptoms were present in 30% and decreased over time.

summary: Retrospective analysis of 272 COVID-19 patients examining the relationship between chest CT pneumonia severity and neuroimaging findings in the post-acute period. paper_authors: Luca Vannini; Ana Laynez-Carnicero; Carlos Bobis-Alvarez; Angelica Figueroa-Mora; Javier Poncela-Mireles; Francisca Gonzalvo Hernandez

paper_title: Comparative imaging study of patients with persistent olfactory dysfunction due to mild COVID-19 using structural and functional MRI

paper_title: The prevalence of psychiatric symptoms and their correlates as part of the long-COVID syndrome

summary: This prospective study followed COVID-19 survivors at 1 and 2 years post-discharge to examine brain structural changes using voxel-based morphometry. While it documents reduced gray matter volume in the cerebellum and temporal regions associated with immune-inflammatory markers, it is a natural history observational study without any treatment intervention and should be excluded from the treatment trials meta-analysis.

paper_title: Two-year follow-up of brain structural changes in patients who recovered from COVID-19: A prospective study

summary: This two-year longitudinal cohort study examined post-traumatic stress symptoms (PTSS), depression, and anxiety in COVID-19 survivors compared to non-infected controls, with neuroimaging data collected at 6 months. Female survivors showed sustained PTSS and depression for up to 2 years, and neuroimaging revealed altered amygdala and hippocampus activity correlated with mental health outcomes and social support.
paper_authors: Yanzhi Bi; Yian Xiao; Xinyu Pan; Yuqi Zhang; Quanqi Yang; Li Hu
paper_title: Long-term post-traumatic stress symptoms in COVID-19 survivors and its risk factors: a two-year longitudinal cohort study

summary: This retrospective cohort study uses propensity score matching on EHR data to compare stimulant prescribing rates between long-COVID patients and acute COVID-19 controls. It is excluded as a secondary analysis of existing EHR data without an intervention trial design.
paper_authors: Ruston M. Koonce; Bradley C. Martin
paper_title: The association between suspected long–COVID and stimulant prescribing in the United States

summary: This retrospective cohort study analyzes TriNetX data (33 million records, 2020-2022) to examine how substance use disorder exacerbates taste and olfactory disorders in long-COVID patients. The study identified epidemiological associations but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Ru-Yin Tsai; Shuo-Yan Gau; Ying-Jui Ho; Sheng-Yi Lin; Chung-Yao Ku; Shiow-Ing Wang; James Cheng-Chung Wei
paper_title: Long-COVID impacts taste and olfactory in individuals with substance use disorder: A retrospective cohort study from the TriNetX US Collaborative Networks

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines long-term renal consequences in COVID-19 patients who experienced acute kidney injury (AKI) during hospitalization, using data from the AP-HP health data warehouse. While the study follows patients longitudinally and documents renal outcomes, it is a secondary analysis of hospitalization data and does not involve testing or evaluating a specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Mohamad Zaidan; F. Gaillard; A. Barnoud; Y. Darhi; P. Samb; L. Grimaldi
paper_title: Conséquences à long terme de l’insuffisance rénale aiguë au cours de la COVID-19 : données de l’entrepôt de données de santé de l’AP–HP

summary: This longitudinal study followed 70 post-acute COVID-19 patients over 6 months to investigate how trauma exposure influences psychological outcomes using standardized psychiatric assessment tools. Results showed that patients with trauma history had significantly worse psychological outcomes across multiple dimensions including anxiety and obsessive-compulsive difficulties, highlighting the importance of trauma assessment for tailored psychological interventions.

paper_title: Trauma Shaping the Psychopathological Correlates of Patients with Long-COVID: A 6-Months Longitudinal Study with Repeated Measures Mixed Models

summary: A 3-year prospective follow-up study of 100 COVID-19 survivors examining associations between baseline biochemical parameters and psychiatric outcomes, measuring HbA1c, electrolytes, and tau protein levels. Severe cases showed elevated p-tau and HbA1c levels, with baseline electrolyte imbalances predicting long-term depression, anxiety, and somatization symptoms.
paper_authors: Shivani Jaiswal; Swapnajeet Sahoo; Vandana Dhiman; Naresh Sachdeva; Mini P. Singh; Sant Ram; Gaurav Sharma; Sanjay Kumar Bhadada
paper_title: Long COVID psychiatric sequelae, biochemical markers & tau protein: A 3-year follow-up study

summary: This study recruited long COVID patients and controls to characterize predictors of brain fog using questionnaires and cognitive tasks, developing classification and regression models. While it identified biopsychosocial factors associated with brain fog and documented high non-remission rates (82.4%), it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Halee Staggs; Ansgar Furst; Colleen Mills-Finnerty
paper_title: Characterizing predictors and chronicity of brain fog in long COVID

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing neuropsychiatric outcomes in 50,805 hospitalized COVID-19 patients versus matched controls from the Veterans Health Administration. Found significantly higher rates of psychiatry-related hospitalizations, mental health visits, new-onset depression, and new-onset dementia in the COVID-19 group at 90-180 days, but this is an observational study without any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Evaluation of Neuropsychiatric outcomes in patients hospitalized with COVID-19 in a nationwide Veterans Health Administration cohort

summary: A cross-sectional study comparing cognitive and reward processing in 24 post-COVID syndrome patients versus 24 healthy controls using fMRI and the Monetary Incentive Delay Task. The study found that post-COVID patients showed slower task performance and temporally altered brain activity in frontal regions, but normal reward circuit function, suggesting neural hypoarousal rather than reward system dysfunction.

paper_title: Cognitive impairment and associated neurobehavioral dysfunction in post-COVID syndrome

summary: A prospective cohort study of 109 COVID-19 ICU patients followed one year post-discharge to identify inflammatory biomarkers predictive of long-term functional outcomes. paper_title: Association of systemic inflammation and long-term dysfunction in COVID-19 patients: A prospective cohort

summary: This prospective cohort study examined the association between physical activity and long COVID risk in 237 Brazilian adults who recovered from COVID-19. paper_title: Physical activity and long COVID: findings from the Prospective Study About Mental and Physical Health in Adults cohort

Found 20% and 17% of participants reported persistent symptoms at 6 and 12 months respectively, with illness severity and hospitalization at diagnosis being significant risk factors.

paper_title: Long COVID prevalence and associated characteristics among a South Alabama population

paper_title: Post-COVID onset of psychiatric complications and associated COVID-related symptom impairment and organ system complications over 24 months

paper_title: Risk factors and early preventive measures for long COVID in non-hospitalized patients: analysis of a large cohort in the United Arab Emirates

paper_title: The predisposing factors to having a coded diagnosis of Long COVID

paper_title: COVID-19 follow-up: Chest X-ray findings with clinical and radiological relationship three months after recovery
