summary: Prospective observational study of 100 long COVID patients with exertional dyspnea, assessing ventilatory efficiency via cardiopulmonary exercise testing at 18 and 36 months post-COVID-19 pneumonia. Found persistently reduced ventilatory efficiency correlating with acute-phase lung involvement, but no intervention or treatment was tested.
paper_authors: Daniel Piamonti; Luigi Panza; Roberto Flore; Valentina Baccolini; Daniela Pellegrino; Arianna Sanna; Altea Lecci; Giulia Lo Muzio; Dario Angelone; Flavio Marco Mirabelli; Matteo Morviducci; Paolo Onorati; Emanuele Messina; Valeria Panebianco; Carlo Catalano; Matteo Bonini; Paolo Palange
paper_title: Ventilatory efficiency in long-term dyspnoeic patients following COVID-19 pneumonia

summary: This cross-sectional study compared cardiorespiratory patterns and exercise capacity among 94 individuals with long COVID, 100 with resolved symptoms, and 70 healthy controls using 6-minute walk tests and oxygen uptake measurements. While the study found significant impairments in oxygen consumption, ventilatory efficiency, and exercise capacity in long COVID patients with minimal change over six months, it is an observational assessment study without an intervention or treatment component.
paper_authors: Imane Salmam; Jean Tittley; Gilles Drouin; Kadija Perreault; François Desmeules; Jean-Sébastien Paquette; Jean-Sébastien Roy; Krista L. Best
paper_title: Metabolic and ventilatory constraints in long COVID individuals

summary: Prospective study evaluating long-term sequelae in 86 critically ill COVID-19 patients 6-9 months after hospitalization using standardized clinical assessments, pulmonary function tests, imaging, and psychological screening. Found high prevalence of fatigue (71%), weakness (48%), reduced diffusion capacity (64%), and psychological symptoms (depression 38%, anxiety 24%), with quality of life generally satisfactory.
paper_authors: Marie Berger; Delphine Daubin; Jérémy Charriot; Kada Klouche; Vincent Le Moing; B. Arnaud; David Morquin; Audrey Jaussent; Patrice Taourel; Maurice Hayot; Nicolas Nagot; Pierre Fesler; C. Roubille
paper_title: Devenir des patients hospitalisés en soins critiques pour infection à SARS-COV2 : évaluation standardisée des séquelles à 6–9 mois

summary: This retrospective cohort study compares neuromuscular abnormalities (M-wave alterations) between 55 post-COVID patients and 62 ME/CFS patients with recent severe infections, examining symptom prevalence and exercise-induced muscle dysfunction. The study found similar frequencies of neuromuscular symptoms and M-wave alterations (~48% vs 41%) in both groups, suggesting post-COVID syndrome shares early neuromusculature pathophysiology with ME/CFS.
paper_authors: F. Rétornaz; Stanislas Rebaudet; C. Stavris; Yves Jammes
paper_title: Conséquences neuromusculaires à long terme de la COVID-19 : analogies avec l’encéphalomyélite myalgique/syndrome de fatigue chronique

summary: Prospective single-center cohort study evaluating persistent auto-immunity and pulmonary sequelae in 101 COVID-19 patients hospitalized for pneumonia, assessed 3-4 months post-symptom onset. Found 34.5% had detectable auto-antibodies with association between auto-antibodies and parenchymal lung abnormalities on imaging, but no treatment intervention was evaluated.
paper_authors: V. Salle; Damien Basille; M. Auquier; C. Lateur; Gwladys Bourdenet; Brigitte Gubler; S. Devaux; Antoine Galmiche; V. Jounieaux; Claire Andréjak
paper_title: Auto-immunité persistante après COVID-19 : étude de cohorte prospective monocentrique

summary: Post-hoc analysis of a prospective cohort evaluating a respiratory rehabilitation program (RRP) in 110 long COVID patients, with stratification by disease duration and clinical presentation. RRP produced significant improvements in dyspnea, 6-minute walk distance, respiratory pressures, and muscle strength, with benefits observed across disease duration and severity subgroups.
paper_authors: Rodríguez-Hernández C.; Guillén-Solà A.; Curbelo YG; Boza R.; Acuña-Pardo C.; Tejero-Sánchez M.
paper_title: Beneficios de un programa de rehabilitación pulmonar para pacientes con COVID persistente: impacto de la gravedad inicial, tiempo de evolución y forma de presentación en los resultados clínicos

summary: Prospective cohort study (ALCOVID) evaluating clinical, functional, respiratory, and neuropsychological sequelae 3-6 months post-COVID-19 in 100 patients across initial severity levels. Found persistent clinical signs in 50%, abnormal 6-minute walk test in 65%, reduced DLCO in 63%, and significant PTSD scores in 31% of patients.
paper_authors: L. Chiche; Hervé Faralli; C. Stavris; Stanislas Rebaudet; J. Allemand; Francine Béhar‐Cohen; Diane Balma; Hervé Pegliasco; HORACIO DROUET; Marc Delord; P. Halfon; F. Rétornaz
paper_title: Séquelles physiques et psychiques 3–6 mois après la COVID-19 : premiers résultats de la cohorte prospective ALCOVID

summary: Prospective cohort study evaluating a personalized rehabilitation program (outpatient, home-based, and self-administered modalities) in 101 post-acute COVID syndrome patients. The program significantly improved inspiratory muscle strength, muscle function, dyspnea, and exercise capacity at 3-6 months, though health-related quality of life improvements were limited to 3 months.
paper_authors: Perrot JC; Segura M.; Flotats G.; Closa C.; Gich I.; Garcia C.; Alba A.; Nadal MJ; Pintor A.; Terra J.; Ramirez E.; Beranuy M.; Bascuñana H.; Plaza V.; Güell-Rous MR
paper_title: Long COVID-19: Impact of a personalized rehabilitation program

summary: Prospective follow-up study of 33 hospitalized COVID-19 patients (not requiring mechanical ventilation) assessed 6 weeks post-discharge for pulmonary and extrapulmonary sequelae. Patients showed reduced exercise capacity and fatigue (45%), with mild impairment in diffusion capacity but no thromboembolic, cardiac, or significant pulmonary impairments.
paper_authors: Ayham Daher; Paul Balfanz; Christian Cornelissen; Annegret Müller; Ingmar Bergs; Nikolaus Marx; Dirk Müller-Wieland; Bojan Hartmann; Michael Dreher; Tobias Müller
paper_title: Follow up of patients with severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19): Pulmonary and extrapulmonary disease sequelae

summary: This prospective observational study compares lung ultrasonography (LUS) and chest CT for evaluating respiratory outcomes in 38 COVID-19 survivors 3 months post-discharge. LUS demonstrated superior discrimination ability for identifying interstitial lung disease (AUC 0.94-0.95) compared to CT, suggesting it could be a first-line follow-up tool for post-COVID respiratory monitoring.
paper_authors: Guido Giovannetti; Lucrezia De Michele; Michele De Ceglie; Paola Pierucci; Alessandra Mirabile; Marco Vita; Vincenzo Ostilio Palmieri; Giovanna Elisiana Carpagnano; Arnaldo Scardapane; Carlo D'Agostino
paper_title: Lung ultrasonography for long-term follow-up of COVID-19 survivors compared to chest CT scan

summary: A longitudinal study of 39 long COVID patients receiving ambulatory respiratory rehabilitation over one year, with most patients presenting dyspnoea (90%) and fatigue (77%). Rehabilitation was associated with significant improvements in exertional dyspnoea, walking distance, and quality of life, with hyperventilation syndrome identified as a frequent contributor to persistent symptoms.
paper_authors: Benoit Bouteleux; Pauline Henrot; Rachel Ernst; Léo Grassion; Chantal Raherison-Semjen; Fabien Beaufils; Maéva Zysman; Mathieu Delorme
paper_title: Respiratory rehabilitation for Covid-19 related persistent dyspnoea: A one-year experience

summary: This single-center cohort study followed 126 severe COVID-19 survivors at three months post-hospitalization to assess respiratory sequelae through clinical evaluation, pulmonary function tests, and high-resolution CT imaging. While 25% reported dyspnea and 35% reported fatigue, with 45% showing decreased DLCO and 21% signs of fibrosis, this is a descriptive observational study documenting natural recovery outcomes rather than evaluating a treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Antoine Froidure; Amin Mahsouli; Giuseppe Liistro; Julien De Greef; Leila Belkhir; Ludovic Gérard; Aurélie Bertrand; Sandra Koenig; Lucie Pothen; Halil Yildiz; Benny Mwenge; Frank Aboubakar; Sophie Gohy; Charles Pilette; Gregory Reychler; Emmanuel Coche; Jean-Cyr Yombi; Benoit Ghaye
paper_title: Integrative respiratory follow-up of severe COVID-19 reveals common functional and lung imaging sequelae

summary: This prospective observational study followed COVID-19 patients for 12 months post-infection to assess pulmonary function, imaging changes, and respiratory symptoms across different acute disease severity groups. Patients with more severe acute COVID-19 showed greater correlation between initial respiratory failure severity and persistent pulmonary impairment, though respiratory symptoms generally improved during follow-up.
paper_authors: Fridolin Steinbeis; Charlotte Thibeault; Felix Doellinger; Raphaela Maria Ring; Mirja Mittermaier; Christoph Ruwwe-Glösenkamp; Florian Alius; Philipp Knape; Hans-Jakob Meyer; Lena Johanna Lippert; Elisa Theresa Helbig; Daniel Grund; Bettina Temmesfeld-Wollbrück; Norbert Suttorp; Leif Erik Sander; Florian Kurth; Tobias Penzkofer; Martin Witzenrath; Thomas Zoller
paper_title: Severity of respiratory failure and computed chest tomography in acute COVID-19 correlates with pulmonary function and respiratory symptoms after infection with SARS-CoV-2: An observational longitudinal study over 12 months

summary: This observational study examines lung function impairments in 128 COVID-19 hospitalized patients at 6 months post-discharge, stratified by race/ethnicity. It documents that ~22% of patients have persistent lung dysfunction across multiple domains, with non-Hispanic Black patients showing significantly lower diffusion capacity compared to White and Hispanic patients.
paper_authors: Samuel B. Konkol; Chintan Ramani; David N. Martin; Carissa K. Harnish-Cruz; Kelsie M. Mietla; Ryan F. Sessums; John C. Widere; Alexandra Kadl
paper_title: Differences in lung function between major race/ethnicity groups following hospitalization with COVID-19

summary: This observational cohort study tracked 21 recently hospitalized COVID-19 pneumonia patients using serial lung ultrasound, CT imaging, and physiological measures at discharge and follow-up timepoints (days 41 and 83). The study demonstrates that lung ultrasound can monitor early recovery of interstitial changes post-hospitalization, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Tuck-Kay Loke; Naomi Earl; Austin C.H. Begbey; Naveen Sharma; Niklas R. Wakeham; Hyon-Mok Sohn; Sarah J. Greenslade; Emma Ince; Miriam Davey; Karina Cox
paper_title: Lung ultrasound as a tool for monitoring the interstitial changes in recently hospitalised patients with COVID-19 pneumonia - The COVIDLUS study

summary: A prospective cross-sectional study of 440 long COVID patients examining the relationship between healthcare setting during acute COVID-19 and post-COVID mood disorders. Patients admitted to respiratory ICU showed higher incidence of mental alterations compared to general ICU patients, with female gender and specific post-COVID symptoms as additional risk factors.
paper_authors: Andrea Portacci; Vitaliano Nicola Quaranta; Ilaria Iorillo; Enrico Buonamico; Fabrizio Diaferia; Sara Quaranta; Cristian Locorotondo; Silvano Dragonieri; Giovanna Elisiana Carpagnano
paper_title: The impact of healthcare setting on post-COVID mood disorders: a single-centre perspective from Southern Italy Respiratory Intensive Care Unit

summary: This prospective observational study evaluated Galectin-3 blood concentrations as a predictive biomarker for post-COVID syndrome development in 437 patients. While Galectin-3 showed correlation with post-COVID outcomes and potential as a predictive marker, the study is observational/diagnostic only and does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Andrea Portacci; Monica Amendolara; Vitaliano Nicola Quaranta; Ilaria Iorillo; Enrico Buonamico; Fabrizio Diaferia; Sara Quaranta; Cristian Locorotondo; Annalisa Schirinzi; Esterina Boniello; Silvano Dragonieri; Giovanna Elisiana Carpagnano
paper_title: Can Galectin-3 be a reliable predictive biomarker for post-COVID syndrome development?

summary: Longitudinal Q-SPECT/CT imaging study of 105 severe COVID-19 patients at baseline and 3-month follow-up to evaluate pulmonary perfusion defects and their correlation with symptoms. While the study mentions potential relevance to understanding long COVID mechanisms, it is an observational diagnostic study without any active treatment intervention—patients with perfusion defects received standard anticoagulation rather than an experimental treatment being tested.
paper_authors: Nevenka Piskac Zivkovic; Andrea Mutvar; Dinka Kuster; Marko Lucijanic; Anja Ljilja Posavec; Daria Cvetkovic Kucic; Kristina Lalic; Mirna Vergles; Mario Udovicic; Bruno Barsic; Diana Rudan; Ivica Luksic; Irene Marthe Lang; Nika Skoro-Sajer
paper_title: Longitudinal analysis of chest Q-SPECT/CT in patients with severe COVID-19

summary: A prospective cohort study evaluating respiratory follow-up protocols at 3 and 6 months post-acute COVID-19 in 168 patients. The study found minimal changes in pulmonary function tests and clinical variables during follow-up, concluding that intensive monitoring may not be necessary.
paper_authors: Ophir Freund; Anna Breslavsky; Rotem Givoli-Vilensky; Nadav Zacks; Evgeni Gershman; Ariel Melloul; Ori Wand; Natalya Bilenko; Amir Bar-Shai
paper_title: Assessment of a close respiratory follow-up schedule at 3 and 6 months after acute COVID-19 and its related investigations

summary: A non-randomized trial evaluating multidisciplinary rehabilitation outcomes in 95 post-COVID-19 patients, comparing 49 patients without preexisting comorbidities to 46 with underlying cardiorespiratory disease. Rehabilitation produced significant improvements in respiratory function, blood gases, and exercise capacity in both groups, suggesting multidisciplinary rehabilitation is effective regardless of preexisting cardiorespiratory comorbidity.
paper_authors: Mauro Maniscalco; Salvatore Fuschillo; Pasquale Ambrosino; Michele Martucci; Antimo Papa; Maria Gabriella Matera; Mario Cazzola
paper_title: Preexisting cardiorespiratory comorbidity does not preclude the success of multidisciplinary rehabilitation in post-COVID-19 patients

summary: Prospective cohort study following 307 COVID-19 patients hospitalized during the first pandemic wave for up to 24 months post-discharge, assessing pulmonary phenotypes and recovery patterns using spirometry, lung volumes, DLCO, and chest CT. Identified three distinct phenotypes and four longitudinal recovery patterns, with persistent pulmonary symptoms and impaired lung function associated with longer hospitalization, more comorbidities, and severe acute disease.
paper_authors: Davide Chimera; Sara Maio; Chiara Romei; Annalisa De Liperi; Greta Barbieri; Laura Tavanti; Roberta Pancani; Guido Marchi; Massimiliano Desideri; Nicoletta Carpenè; Luciano Gabbrielli; Alessandro Celi; Ferruccio Aquilini; Sandra Baldacci; Michele Cristofano; Lorenzo Ghiadoni; Laura Carrozzi; Francesco Pistelli
paper_title: COVID-19 pulmonary phenotypes and longitudinal patterns in the first wave of the pandemic

summary: Cross-sectional study of 417 COVID-19 survivors in Lebanon assessing post-COVID syndrome symptom prevalence and impacts on quality of life and mental health using SF-36 and HADS instruments. Found fatigue, dyspnea, and cough as most common symptoms, with severe acute infection associated with worse physical functioning and role limitations.
paper_authors: Hisham Bou Fakhreddine; Salah Zeineldine; Hassan Itani; Jawad Abdul Sater; Pierre BouKhalil; Bassem Al Harfani; Imad Bouakl
paper_title: Impact of Post-COVID syndrome on quality of life and mental health among COVID-19 survivors: A study from a tertiary care center in Lebanon

summary: Prospective cohort study examining Long COVID as a predictor of myasthenia gravis (MG) exacerbation in 180 MG patients with COVID-19 co-infection, using machine learning for risk stratification. Found Long COVID was the strongest predictor of MG exacerbation (aHR=2.55), but this is observational epidemiology, not a treatment intervention trial.
paper_authors: Yan Li; Yimin Tao; Zhilan Zhao; Pei Zhong; Liyan Zhong; Hui Yang; Mingjie Yu; Sisi Liu; Kawai Lei; Qiong Zhao; Rui Wang; Jun Wang; Qibing Zeng; Shixiang Kuang; Ting Li
paper_title: Long COVID as an independent predictor of myasthenia gravis exacerbation: A prospective cohort study integrating machine learning for risk stratification

summary: Retrospective analysis of 213 patients hospitalized for COVID-19 pneumonia to identify predictive factors for long-term home oxygen therapy prescription. Study identifies advanced age, comorbidities, inflammatory syndrome, and extent of thoracic lesions as predictive factors but does not evaluate a specific intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: S. Bouchareb; N. Boudawara; S. Ksissa; Harinder K. Bali; S. Tliba; I. Belhaj; I. Touil; F.E. Dabbebi; R. Bouguezzi; Jalel Knani; L. Boussouffara; F. Boubaker
paper_title: Facteurs prédictifs de prescription d’oxygénothérapie au long cours après une infection à la COVID-19

summary: Retrospective analysis of 343 chest CT scans from patients over 40 years old comparing interstitial lung abnormality (ILA) prevalence in the post-COVID-19 era to pre-pandemic studies. Found 18% ILA prevalence (double the pre-pandemic ~7%), with increased fibrosing ILAs potentially linked to post-COVID lung changes, but this is an observational study without treatment intervention or control groups.
paper_authors: Chahbi Z.; Bigi S.; Adnor S.; Salek M.; Wakrim S.
paper_title: Anomalies pulmonaires interstitielles (ILA) dans l’ère post-COVID-19 : appel à une vigilance accrue des radiologues

summary: Prospective descriptive study of 150 hospitalized COVID-19 patients followed for 3 months to assess prevalence and characterize persistent symptoms. 34.5% of patients retained persistent symptoms at 3 months, with fatigue (19%), dyspnea (19.9%), and arthralgia (11.8%) being most common.
paper_authors: Mariem Friha; Tasnim Znegui; S. Maazoui; Slim Ghedira; A. Touil; Mariem Chaaben; Sonia Hbibech; H. Racil; N. Chaouech
paper_title: Les symptômes persistants de la COVID-19 à 3 mois

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed post-traumatic stress and psychological distress in 36 COVID-19 patients who had been intubated in ICU and were admitted to a respiratory rehabilitation center. While it documents long COVID sequelae (fatigue, dyspnea, anxiety, cognitive dysfunction), it is observational without any treatment intervention—patients were passively assessed during rehabilitation without being assigned to a specific treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Yara Al Chikhanie; L. Aujogue; David Veale; Samuel Vergès; F. Hérengt
paper_title: La détresse psychologique et le stress post-traumatique chez les patients post-COVID-19 réanimés intubés

summary: Prospective cohort study of 40 long COVID patients at 3 months post-infection, assessing persistence and types of symptoms. Found 70% had persistent clinical abnormalities, with fatigue (63%), headaches (48%), and neurocognitive dysfunction (38%) being most common; symptoms were more prevalent in women.
paper_authors: Arkan Jarrar; W. Benzarti; Amina Omrane; I. Gargouri; A. Knaz; A. Abdelghani; S. Aîssa; A. Hayouni
paper_title: Long COVID : qu’en est-il de l’évolution nos patients après 3 mois de leur sortie ? Résultats préliminaires

summary: Prospective cohort study of 279 COVID-19 pneumonia patients followed at 1 and 3 months post-hospitalization to characterize post-COVID fibrosis clinical and radiological profiles. Identified 10 patients with post-COVID fibrosis and respiratory impairment who received corticosteroid treatment (0.5 mg/kg/day prednisone equivalent per SPLF protocol), with fibrosis associated with severe initial COVID-19 pneumonia and extensive parenchymal lesions.
paper_authors: B. Said; N. Chaouech; N. Mechergui; I. Yousfi; J. Rejeb; D. Aouida; N. Ladhari; Al Chikhanie; L. Aujogue; D. Veale; S. Vergés; F. Herengt
paper_title: Diagnostic et prise en charge de la fibrose post-COVID

summary: Retrospective observational study examining the impact of systemic corticosteroid therapy during acute SARS-CoV-2 infection on respiratory sequelae at 3, 6, and 12 months follow-up in hospitalized patients. While patients receiving corticosteroids showed more ground-glass opacities at 3 months, no significant long-term functional differences were found between treatment groups.
paper_authors: J. Delomez; Marie Le Mercier; Damien Basille; V. Jounieaux; Claire Andréjak
paper_title: Impact de la corticothérapie systémique sur les séquelles respiratoires des infections à SARS-CoV-2

summary: Prospective study of 45 COVID-19 patients assessed 3 months post-infection with chest CT scans to characterize pulmonary sequelae and associated factors. Found parenchymal abnormalities in 75% of patients with regression in 91% of cases, most commonly ground-glass opacities, reticulations, and septal thickening.
paper_authors: C. Ben Rhouma; A. Migaou; E. Zaara; N. Fahem; W. Fekih; R. Kaddoussi; A. Ben Saad; W. Ghribi; I. Ben Limem; J. Elayeb; S. Joober; S. Cheikh Mhammed; N. Rouatbi; A. Achour; Mabrouk Abdelali; K. Ben Abdejelil; Ahmed Zrig; Mezri Maâtouk
paper_title: Le scanner thoracique lève le voile sur les séquelles pulmonaires du COVID

summary: Prospective observational study of 67 COVID-19 patients followed 3 months post-infection to characterize persistent clinical symptoms and identify risk factors. Found 61.8% retained >3 symptoms, with dyspnea, fatigue, and cognitive impairment as most common; no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: A. Migaou; C. Ben Rhouma; W. Feki; A. Ben Saad; R. Kaddoussi; N. Fahem; I. Ben Limem; J. Elayeb; E. Zaara; W. Ghribi; S. Joober; S. Cheikh Mhammed; N. Rouatbi; A. Achour; K. Benabdejelil; Mabrouk Abdelali; Ahlem Zrig; Mezri Maâtouk
paper_title: Le post-COVID : maladie à multiple facettes

summary: The COMEBAC cohort study evaluated respiratory symptoms and radiological abnormalities in 478 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors at 4 months post-discharge, with detailed assessment of 177 who had ICU admission or persistent symptoms. New-onset dyspnea was present in 16.3% of patients, and pulmonary fibrotic lesions were detected in 19.3% of those reassessed, though their extent was typically minimal and rarely accompanied by both dyspnea and impaired diffusion.
paper_authors: Étienne-Marie Jutant; Olivier Meyrignac; Antoine Beurnier; Xavier Jaïs; Tài Pham; Luc Morin; Athénaïs Boucly; Sophie Bulifon; F. Samy; Anatole Harrois; Mitja Jevnikar; Nicolas Noël; Jérémie Pichon; A. Roche; A. Seferian; Samer Soliman; Jacques Duranteau; Laurent Becquemont; Xavier Monnet; Olivier Sitbon; Marie‐France Bellin; Marc Humbert; Laurent Savale; David Montani
paper_title: Symptômes respiratoires et anomalies radiologiques dans le COVID long

summary: This prospective cross-sectional study evaluated the prevalence of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and its risk factors in 157 COVID-19 patients during acute hospitalization, using the PCL-5 questionnaire. PTSD was diagnosed in 36.9% of patients, with female sex and history of severe COVID-19 being significant risk factors.
paper_authors: Honar Cherif; S. Kalboussi; W. Fenina; Mohamed Amine Triki; F. Yangui; M.R. Charfi
paper_title: État de stress post-traumatique après une infection à COVID-19

summary: Retrospective study of 423 COVID-19 patients assessing chest CT findings at admission and 3-month follow-up to evaluate prognostic factors and long-term sequelae. Demonstrates that initial CT extent of lung damage correlates with severe COVID-19 and subsequent imaging abnormalities at 3 months.
paper_authors: I. El Wadhane; Mohamed Bouattour; R. Khemekhem; Hoda A. Makhlouf; M. Hamoudi; N. Kallel; Wiem Feki
paper_title: Intérêt pronostique à cours et à long terme du scanner thoracique chez les patients atteints de COVID-19

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 300 COVID-19 pneumonia patients followed at 3 and 6 months post-discharge, with CT imaging in a subset (n=60 at 3 months, n=9 at 6 months) to assess radiological sequelae. At 6 months, 9 patients had persistent radiological lesions consistent with early pulmonary fibrosis; ground-glass opacities, bronchiolectasis, and septal thickening were most common, associated with older age, longer initial hospitalization, and ICU admission.
paper_authors: Marwa Kalila; S. Toujeni; A. Hédhli; Améni Nâaroura; A. Ghourabi; A. Allouche; S. Cheikhrouhou; M. Mjid; Y. Ouahchi; S. Meraï; Besma Dhahri
paper_title: Évolution de l’atteinte pulmonaire au scanner thoracique 6 mois après une pneumonie à COVID-19

summary: Descriptive observational study of 39 post-COVID patients with sleep disorders who underwent polysomnography testing in Madagascar from July 2020 to August 2021. Sleep apnea was diagnosed in 71.8% of patients, with significant correlation between Epworth sleepiness scale and apnea-hypopnea index, but no specific intervention or treatment was tested.
paper_authors: L. Rebasy; A.H. Ranivoson; N.L. Rafitoharson; R.M. Andrianasolo; K. Ravahatra; H.M. Tiaray; J.L. Rakotoson; R.N. Raharimanana
paper_title: Résultats des examens de polygraphie ventilatoire réalisés chez les patients ayant présenté un trouble de sommeil après une infection à SARS-CoV-2 à Antananarivo Madagascar

summary: Prospective longitudinal cohort study of 155 hospital staff members with long COVID symptoms, following them over 2 years. Documents symptom persistence and prevalence across multiple organ systems (respiratory, neurological, cardiovascular, psychiatric), with most symptoms resolving by 6-12 months, and identifies need for multidisciplinary evaluation.
paper_authors: N. Hammache; A. Arib; R. Abdellaziz
paper_title: Étude du COVID long chez un personnel hospitalier

summary: Prospective cohort study evaluating post-COVID-19 clinical manifestations and respiratory function in 96 Madagascar patients over 6 months across 3 consultations. Study documents persistent fatigue (50-68%), neurological symptoms (memory loss, insomnia, tremor), respiratory dysfunction, and socioeconomic impact, with 2/3 patient loss to follow-up limiting statistical analysis.
paper_authors: J. Ratomaharo; V. Andriananja; R.T. Randriamahenintsoa; A.J.N. Andriamamonjisoa; M. Raberahona; Rivo Andry Rakotoarivelo; R. Andriamihaja; M.J. Randria
paper_title: Première évaluation médicale du post-COVID-19 à Madagascar

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 77 patients with severe COVID-19 pneumonia followed at 30 and 90 days post-discharge to identify predictive factors of persistent long COVID symptoms. Tobacco consumption emerged as a significant predictor of symptom persistence and worsening, while asthma history and advanced age correlated with symptom improvement.
paper_authors: T. Béjaoui; Houda Rouis; C. Moussa; Leila Bayahi; A. Khattab; I. Khouaja; I. Zendah; S. Maâlej
paper_title: Facteurs prédictifs du long COVID-19 : expérience d’un service de pneumologie en Tunisie

summary: Observational study of 20 patients admitted for respiratory and neuromuscular rehabilitation after acute COVID-19 hospitalization. Patients received physiotherapy interventions during acute phase recovery (not post-COVID/long COVID), showing improvements in 6-minute walk test and oxygen saturation.
paper_authors: S. Koné; Christine Ekono; E. Leblic; T. Kanouté; E. Decelle; D. Soumaré; F. Murielle; K. Ouattara; Y. Toloba
paper_title: Place de la kinésithérapie respiratoire et neuromusculaire chez les patients atteints de COVID-19

summary: Retrospective longitudinal study of 70 patients with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia followed at 3 months post-discharge to assess respiratory functional impairment. Found persistent diffusion abnormalities (DLCO reduction in 44.3%) and restrictive ventilatory patterns, with severity of initial lung involvement correlating with reduced FEV1.
paper_authors: I. Sahnoun; M. Bougacha; I. Moussa; S. Rejab; R. Jebali; C. maherssia; Asma Chaker; Saloua Ben Khamsa Jamelleddine; S. Maâlej; L. Douik El Gharbi
paper_title: Impact à long terme de la pneumonie à Sars-CoV-2 sur la fonction respiratoire

summary: This study follows 149 hospitalized and 141 non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients for 18-30 months to assess long-term survival, functional dependency, and reinfection rates. It is a passive observational follow-up study with no treatment intervention tested, showing that functional dependency improved over time in both groups but reinfection rates were similar (~20%) regardless of initial severity.
paper_authors: A. El Kik; H. Eid; Albert Riachy; Elio Mekhael; Karim Hoyek; Nabil Nassim; Maria Saadé; B. Habr; G. Sleilaty; M. Riachy
paper_title: Devenir au long cours des patients COVID-19 hospitalisés et non hospitalisés : décès, dépendance et réinfection

summary: Prospective study of 52 patients who had SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia, re-evaluated 6 months post-infection with chest CT scans to characterize pulmonary sequelae. Found pathological CT findings in 44% of cases, most commonly ground-glass opacities, micronodules, and honeycombing patterns.
paper_authors: E.L.P. Bemba; A.A.P. Hobie; R.G. Bopaka; P.P. Koumeka; K.B. Ossale-Abacka; F.H. Okemba-Okombi; M. Illoye-Ayet; J. Mboussa
paper_title: Profil scanographique des séquelles de la pneumonie à SARS-CoV-2 à Brazzaville

summary: A prospective cohort study of 292 patients hospitalized for SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia, followed at 3, 6, and 12 months post-infection to assess respiratory sequelae including DLCO impairment, persistent symptoms, and CT imaging findings. The study is observational with no intervention—it documents natural disease progression rather than testing a treatment.
paper_authors: Marie Le Mercier; Damien Basille; A. Chan Sui Ko; M. Auquier; H. Carette; S. Lion-Daolio; S. Devaux; V. Jounieaux; Claire Andréjak
paper_title: Évaluation des séquelles respiratoires des patients hospitalisés pour une pneumonie à SARS-CoV-2 au CHU d’Amiens 2020

summary: Prospective analytical study of 1,124 mild COVID-19 patients (outpatient, no oxygen therapy) assessing predictors of persistent symptoms ≥12 months post-infection. Found 23.8% had persistent symptoms; obesity, comorbidities, and acute-phase symptom burden were significant predictive factors.
paper_authors: A. Touil; E. Nemsi; S. Maazaoui; S. Maddeh; Tasnim Znegui; M. Chaabane; Yosor Ayedi; S. Habibèch; R. Fakhfakh; H. Racil; N. Chaouch
paper_title: Facteurs prédictifs de symptômes persistants une année ou plus après une forme légère de COVID-19

summary: Retrospective study of 41 post-COVID-19 patients rehospitalized at a Moroccan pneumology service, examining clinical characteristics, inflammatory/coagulation abnormalities, imaging findings, and therapeutic interventions including oxygen therapy, corticosteroids, antibiotics, and anticoagulation. Most patients (70%) had favorable outcomes, though 24% experienced thromboembolic complications and 14% died.

paper_title: Caractéristiques et prise en charge des patients réhospitalisés en post-COVID-19 au service de pneumologie du CHR-Hassan II d’Agadir

summary: This study examines the impact of long COVID on disease activity, disability, and quality of life in patients with inflammatory arthritis using data from RheumCARD, a prospective cohort study. The findings show that long COVID patients have significantly worse fatigue, pain, and quality of life compared to those without long COVID, but no treatment intervention is being tested or evaluated.

summary: This study compares long-term functional disability and oxygen dependence between hospitalized and non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients at a Lebanese hospital, following 290 patients over 18-30 months. While it documents significant differences in functional disability outcomes, it is a secondary analysis of patient cohorts rather than a treatment intervention trial.

paper_title: Différence au long cours dans la dépendance fonctionnelle et dans la dépendance à l’oxygène des patients Covid-19 hospitalisés et non hospitalisés

summary: Prospective survey of 174 COVID-19 survivors with pre-existing systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases examining DMARD disruption, disease flare, and prolonged COVID-19 symptoms. Identifies hospitalization and initial symptom count as predictors of prolonged symptom duration (≥28 days) but does not test or evaluate any specific intervention.

paper_title: DMARD disruption, rheumatic disease flare, and prolonged COVID-19 symptom duration after acute COVID-19 among patients with rheumatic disease: A prospective study

summary: Prospective cohort study following 29 COVID-19 participants with taste and smell assessments at baseline and 6-month follow-up using objective chemosensory tests and questionnaires. Study demonstrates significant improvement in olfactory function and modest improvement in taste intensity over 6 months post-infection.

paper_title: Long-term recovery of taste and smell following acute COVID-19 infection in a New Jersey cohort

summary: This population-based cohort study examines long-term venous thromboembolism risk (pulmonary embolism and deep venous thrombosis) following COVID-19 hospitalization in Swedish citizens over 180+ days. While it documents elevated VTE risk as a post-COVID sequela, the paper is fundamentally an epidemiological study of disease complications rather than a treatment/intervention trial for long COVID patients.

paper_title: Pulmonary embolism and deep venous thrombosis after COVID-19: long-term risk in a population-based cohort study

summary: This cross-sectional study characterized the prevalence and clinical features of persistent COVID-19 symptoms in 1,542 primary care patients, analyzing gender-specific differences in symptom clusters and functional status. While about long COVID, it is an observational characterization study that does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Rodríguez Onieva A.; Soto Castro CA; García Morales V.; Aneri Vacas M.; Hidalgo Requena A.
paper_title: Long COVID: Factors influencing persistent symptoms and the impact of gender

summary: This cross-sectional study from the ICOSS-2 collaboration assessed excessive daytime sleepiness and fatigue in 13,656 participants across multiple countries, comparing long COVID (LC), short COVID (SC), and COVID-negative groups. The study found that LC participants had significantly higher ESS and FSS scores and increased odds of severe fatigue and excessive sleep duration compared to SC and COVID-negative controls, highlighting sleep and fatigue as long COVID symptoms rather than evaluating any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Long COVID as a risk factor for hypersomnolence and fatigue: insights from the 2nd International Covid Sleep Study Collaboration (ICOSS-2)

summary: This prospective cohort study surveyed 2,980 US adults at two time points during the COVID-19 pandemic to assess insomnia prevalence and its association with COVID-19 outcomes. Among the 149 participants who contracted COVID-19, those with insomnia reported significantly longer symptom duration (24.8 vs 16.1 sick days), suggesting insomnia is associated with more chronic COVID-19 symptoms.
paper_authors: Ivan Vargas; Alexandria Muench; Michael A. Grandner; Michael R. Irwin; Michael L. Perlis
paper_title: Insomnia symptoms predict longer COVID-19 symptom duration

summary: This study examined respiratory and cardiovascular function in 87 young athletes (52 with prior mild COVID-19, 37 controls) during cycling ergometric testing at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months. All athletes recovered fully with no significant functional differences by 6 months, indicating complete normalization of cardiorespiratory parameters post-infection.

paper_title: The functional state of athletes who have undergone coronavirus infection (COVID-19)

summary: Register-based cohort study examining socioeconomic disparities in long COVID diagnosis among ethnic minorities in Denmark, comparing COVID-19 cases (n=2,287,175) by income, education, and ethnicity. Found migrants with low income had higher long COVID risk than native Danes, and certain migrant worker occupations showed elevated risk.

paper_title: Socioeconomic disparities in long COVID diagnosis among ethnic minorities in Denmark

summary: This prospective cohort study followed 14,421 Japanese workers over one year to assess the impact of COVID-19 infection on work functioning. COVID-19 infected workers showed significantly higher incidence of new work functioning impairment (adjusted IRR: 2.18), demonstrating persistent post-acute infection symptoms affecting work capacity.

summary: This prospective cohort study assessed endothelial dysfunction, coagulation activation, and inflammatory markers in 203 COVID-19 patients at 3 months post-infection compared to historic controls. The study found no macrovascular dysfunction but detected sustained inflammation, elevated endothelin-1, and coagulation abnormalities, highlighting vascular involvement in post-COVID recovery.

paper_title: Sustained inflammation, coagulation activation and elevated endothelin-1 levels without macrovascular dysfunction at 3 months after COVID-19

summary: Population-wide cohort study examining arterial and venous thrombotic event risks following hospitalization for COVID-19, pneumonia, and influenza in 2.6 million Welsh residents. While the study covers post-hospitalization sequelae, it focuses on thrombotic complications rather than long COVID symptoms and does not evaluate any treatment interventions.

summary: This prospective multicenter cohort study examined bleeding risk in pulmonary embolism patients receiving anticoagulation, comparing those with and without COVID-19 infection. While long COVID patients showed significantly higher bleeding rates, this is a secondary analysis of anticoagulation outcomes in PE patients rather than a treatment trial for long COVID itself.

summary: Longitudinal prospective cohort study following 71 COVID-19 pneumonia survivors for up to 12 months to identify sequelae and associated factors. Found that 29.7% developed hypertension and 45.9% developed type 2 diabetes by 5 months, with cognitive dysfunction and memory loss persisting, though some metabolic changes reversed by 12 months.

paper_title: Cognitive dysfunction, diabetes mellitus 2 and arterial hypertension: Sequelae up to one year of COVID-19

summary: Retrospective cohort study of kidney transplant recipients hospitalized with severe COVID-19, examining long-term graft function decline over 4 years. While it documents post-COVID renal complications in transplant patients, it does not study long COVID as a syndrome and does not test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Suzimar Silveira Rioja; Amanda Orlando Reis; Conrado Lysandro Rodrigues Gomes
paper_title: Long-Term Decline in Renal Allograft Function After Severe COVID-19 in Kidney Transplant Recipients: Evidence From a Four-Year Retrospective Cohort Study

summary: Prospective cohort study evaluating whether SARS-CoV-2 vaccination improves symptoms in participants with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC). Found no significant difference in symptom improvement or full recovery between vaccinated and unvaccinated matched pairs over 3 months, with comparable antibody decay trajectories.

summary: This retrospective cohort study evaluates the relationship between COVID-19 vaccination status and the prevalence of post-COVID cardiac complications and persistent symptoms in 1,883 patients. Vaccinated patients showed significantly lower rates of cardiac injury (1.35% vs 4.11%) and persistent long-COVID symptoms (10.7% vs 18.3%) compared to unvaccinated patients.

paper_title: Impact of COVID-19 vaccination in post-COVID cardiac complications

summary: This retrospective cohort study examined whether COVID-19 vaccination reduces the risk of developing post-COVID conditions in 84,464 Japanese participants. The study found that recent vaccination (14-149 days before infection) significantly lowered the 8-month incidence of 28 post-COVID conditions, but this is an observational analysis of vaccine effects on disease prevention, not a treatment intervention trial for patients with existing long COVID.

summary: This study examines whether COVID-19 vaccination reduces long COVID risk among adolescents who were infected with SARS-CoV-2, using matched retrospective cohorts. While 9 proteins showed associations with Long COVID and 10 with fatigue severity before multiple testing correction, only SRPK2 and ITGA6 remained significant after FDR-adjustment, suggesting limited predictive value of individual plasma proteins.

paper_title: Can inflammatory plasma proteins predict Long COVID or Fatigue severity after SARS-CoV-2 infection?

summary: This retrospective cohort study uses ultrasound shear wave elastography to assess liver stiffness in 30 post-COVID-19 patients compared to 100 controls at an average of 44 weeks post-infection. The study found COVID-19 infection is associated with increased liver stiffness (1.5 kPa increase, p=0.006), suggesting lasting hepatic injury, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

paper_title: Lasting liver injury following COVID-19 infection characterized by ultrasound shear wave elastography

summary: A prospective cohort study examining endothelial dysfunction in COVID-19 patients followed up to 6 months post-discharge, comparing acute and long-standing effects. summary: This population-based cross-sectional study examined associations between social vulnerability and new-onset mobility disability among 4,295 adults with PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection in Michigan. Living in high social vulnerability counties was associated with 1.38 times higher odds of reporting new mobility disability post-COVID, but the study is observational without treatment intervention.

paper_title: Social vulnerability and new mobility disability among adults with polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-confirmed SARS-CoV-2: Michigan COVID-19 Recovery Surveillance Study

summary: Prospective cohort study examining the association between mRNA vaccination status and post-COVID condition (PCC) prevalence in 288 Thai patients with mild COVID-19. Vaccination was associated with reduced PCC risk (43.5% vs 67.3% unvaccinated), but this is an observational analysis of vaccination exposure rather than a treatment intervention trial.

paper_title: The association between COVID-19 vaccination with the prevalence of post-COVID conditions in Thai patients with mild COVID-19

The study found 67% reported persistent symptoms (29% met post-COVID criteria) and identified associations between acute symptoms and symptom persistence duration, but did not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

paper_journal: Zeitschrift für Evidenz, Fortbildung und Qualität im Gesundheitswesen

summary: DigiHero is a digital epidemiology cohort study recruiting 318 long COVID patients in Germany to investigate molecular drivers of PASC through questionnaires, surveys, and blood biomarker profiling. The study found elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF) associated with long COVID symptoms that persist independently of post-infection vaccination.
paper_authors: Clare Wilson
paper_title: Vaccines may help clear up long-term covid-19 symptoms

summary: Prospective cohort study of 291 long COVID patients in Nairobi followed for 12 months, measuring health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and economic burden (catastrophic expenditures/costs) at 3-month intervals. summary: This study compares major adverse cardiac events (MACE) at 6-month follow-up between COVID-19 positive and negative patients from early pandemic (March-April 2020). summary: Registry analysis documenting the duration of dermatological manifestations in COVID-19 patients, including those with persistent symptoms (long-haulers defined as >60 days). This is a descriptive observational study tracking symptom duration, not an intervention trial.

summary: Staggered cohort study examining whether COVID-19 vaccination prevents long COVID symptoms in data from the UK, Spain, and Estonia. This is an observational cohort study examining outcomes in vaccinated vs unvaccinated populations rather than evaluating a treatment intervention for long COVID patients.

summary: This retrospective registry study examines COVID-19 sequelae prevalence and impact on survival in cancer patients who recovered from SARS-CoV-2 infection across 35 European institutions. While it documents long COVID symptoms (respiratory, fatigue) in 15% of cancer survivors, it is a secondary analysis of a cancer-oncology registry (OnCovid) and does not test or evaluate a specific long COVID treatment intervention.

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining rates of subsequent infections in 231,899 US veterans with positive COVID-19 tests versus 605,014 with negative tests between November 2021 and December 2023. Found that COVID-19 positive individuals had significantly increased risk of bacterial, viral, and fungal infections in the 12 months following infection, suggesting long-term immune system effects from SARS-CoV-2.

summary: This is a 3-year longitudinal cohort study of COVID-19 survivors from Wuhan following disease trajectory naturally, without any intervention or treatment. The study found most long COVID symptoms were mild-to-moderate at 3 years, with higher reinfection rates and symptom worsening in those with baseline long COVID.

summary: This prospective UK-wide multicentre MRI follow-up study (C-MORE) evaluates multiorgan abnormalities in 259 hospitalized COVID-19 patients at 5 months post-discharge compared to 52 non-COVID controls. The study documents higher prevalence of lung, brain, and kidney MRI abnormalities in COVID-19 patients but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Matthew R. Baldwin
paper_title: Making sense of multiorgan MRI imaging for post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection

summary: This longitudinal cohort study followed 1,192 COVID-19 hospital survivors for 2 years post-infection, measuring symptoms, lung function, quality of life, and return to work. While symptoms improved over time, the study found persistent sequelae in 55% at 2 years and significantly worse health status compared to matched controls, highlighting the burden of long COVID but not testing any specific intervention.

paper_title: Health outcomes in people 2 years after surviving hospitalisation with COVID-19: a longitudinal cohort study

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining whether molnupiravir treatment within 5 days of SARS-CoV-2 infection reduces the risk of post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC/long COVID) in high-risk patients. Results show molnupiravir was associated with reduced risk of PASC (14% relative risk reduction) and 8 of 13 measured post-acute sequelae including fatigue, dysrhythmia, thromboembolism, and neurocognitive impairment.
paper_authors: Yan Xie; Ziyad Al-Aly
paper_title: Risks and burdens of incident diabetes in long COVID: a cohort study

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining the association between COVID-19 vaccination status and risk of cardiovascular disease and mortality in post-COVID-19 patients using Hong Kong electronic health records. The study found that vaccinated patients had lower CVD and mortality risk compared to unvaccinated patients, with a dose-response relationship.

It is an observational epidemiological study comparing outcomes between groups but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Maxime Taquet; Rebecca Sillett; Lena Zhu; Jacob Mendel; Isabella Camplisson; Quentin Dercon; Paul J. Harrison
paper_title: Neurological and psychiatric risk trajectories after SARS-CoV-2 infection: an analysis of 2-year retrospective cohort studies including 1 284 437 patients

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines whether early treatment with molnupiravir (within 5 days of SARS-CoV-2 infection) reduces the risk of post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC/long COVID) in 229,286 US veterans with risk factors for severe COVID-19. Molnupiravir was associated with a 14% relative risk reduction for PASC, reduced mortality, and reduced risk of eight specific post-acute sequelae including fatigue, dysrhythmia, and neurocognitive impairment.
paper_authors: Evan Xu; Yan Xie; Ziyad Al-Aly
paper_title: Risks and burdens of incident dyslipidaemia in long COVID: a cohort study

summary: Prospective cohort study examining post-COVID condition prevalence and characteristics in patients with inflammatory rheumatic diseases in the Netherlands. The study follows patients over time to assess long COVID outcomes in this vulnerable population.

summary: A retrospective cohort study examining the association between nirmatrelvir-ritonavir treatment and post-acute sequelae outcomes in immunocompromised patients hospitalized with COVID-19 using Hong Kong Hospital Authority data. Among immunocompromised patients, nirmatrelvir-ritonavir was associated with significantly lower risk of post-acute inpatient death (HR 0.58) and acute respiratory distress syndrome, though effectiveness on post-acute hospitalization outcomes was less pronounced than in immunocompetent patients.

summary: A retrospective cohort study investigating associations between HLA alleles and severe COVID-19 outcomes, including PASC (post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection), using the All of Us dataset. The study aims to identify genetic risk factors for severe COVID-19 and PASC but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Grace Kim; Grace J. Kim; Nayane Brito; San Chu; Ronald Horswell; Nicolas Vince; Lucio Miele
paper_title: 483 Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) alleles associated with severe COVID-19 outcomes in the All of Us cohort
paper_journal: Journal of Clinical and Translational Science

summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 157 COVID-19 patients hospitalized in March-April 2020 and assessed them 12 months later for chronic pain and fatigue symptoms. The study found that 27.4% reported chronic fatigue, 25.5% met criteria for chronic fatigue syndrome, and 15.3% experienced severe chronic pain, with women more affected than men.
paper_authors: Sultan Fahad Madani; L Janbazi; A Kazemian; K Mansouri; Nima Yousefi; G Raissi; F Vahedifard
paper_title: P.038 The incidence and characteristics of chronic pain and fatigue after 12 months later admitting with COVID-19; The Post- COVID 19 syndrome
paper_journal: Canadian Journal of Neurological Sciences / Journal Canadien des Sciences Neurologiques

summary: Target trial emulation study comparing metformin users to controls (fluvoxamine, fluticasone, ivermectin, montelukast) using N3C data to assess metformin's effect on long COVID or death within 180 days post-infection. Metformin showed 53% risk reduction (aRR 0.47, 95% CI 0.25-0.89) compared to controls, with consistent results across subgroups and sensitivity analyses.
paper_authors: Steve Johnson; Carolyn Bramante; Til Stürmer; John Buse; Talia Wiggen; Jared Huling; Andrew Toler
paper_title: 595 Is PHASTR faster? A target trial emulation case study in the N3C
paper_journal: Journal of Clinical and Translational Science

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines the temporal relationship between new type 2 diabetes diagnosis and SARS-CoV-2 infection using nationwide EHR data from the RECOVER program. The study found that new diabetes diagnoses were paradoxically 83% lower in the 6 months post-infection compared to pre-infection, suggesting complex metabolic sequelae of COVID-19 rather than straightforward diabetes risk elevation.

paper_title: Are fewer cases of diabetes mellitus diagnosed in the months after SARS-CoV-2 infection? A population-level view in the EHR-based RECOVER program
paper_journal: Journal of Clinical and Translational Science

summary: A 2-year prospective cohort study following 230 COVID-19 survivors to assess prevalence of persistent neuropsychiatric symptoms and identify biobehavioral risk factors. Found that 39.1% had fatigue, 18.3% cognitive failure, and 11.3% depression at 2 years, with female gender, comorbidities, and acute phase severity as key risk factors.

paper_title: COVID-19-induced neuropsychiatric symptoms can persist long after acute infection: a 2-year prospective study of biobehavioral risk factors and psychometric outcomes

summary: This retrospective cohort study analyzes SARS-CoV-2 sequences linked to electronic health records to examine Long COVID incidence across viral lineages and identify conserved spike protein regions for vaccine development. While it characterizes Long COVID epidemiology by variant, it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention for long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Grace Jaeyoon Kim; Md Ashad Alam; Judy S. Crabtree; Rebecca Rose; Susanna L. Lamers; San Chu; Ronald Horswell; Daniel Fort; Lucio Miele
paper_title: Long COVID incidence across SARS-CoV-2 lineages and identification of conserved spike targets for multivalent vaccines
paper_journal: Journal of Clinical and Translational Science

summary: A 12-month prospective cohort study of 144 SARS-CoV-2 infected individuals examining psychiatric sequelae using validated questionnaires (SPHERE, DMI, EQ-5D-5L) and inflammatory biomarkers at 6 timepoints. Long COVID status emerged as the strongest predictor of neuropsychiatric symptoms, with robust inverse associations found between inflammatory biomarkers and mental health outcomes.
paper_authors: Seetal Dodd; Mohammedreza Mohebbi; Josie O’Donohue; Gail Matthews; David R. Darley; Michael Berk
paper_title: Psychiatric sequelae after SARS-Cov-2 infection: trajectory, predictors and associations in a longitudinal Australian cohort

summary: This retrospective VA database study characterizes long COVID by analyzing new diagnoses in 316,782 COVID-positive veterans from 2020-2022, defining long COVID subtypes by organ system and identifying demographic risk factors. While it provides evidence for long COVID case definition and clinical characterization, it is a secondary analysis of existing EHR data without testing or evaluating any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Peter L. Elkin; Skyler Resendez; H. Sebastian Ruiz; Wilmon McCray; Steven H. Brown; Jonathan Nebeker; Diane Montella
paper_title: 58 Utilizing VA Data to Define Long COVID and Identify Patients at Risk
paper_journal: Journal of Clinical and Translational Science

summary: This cross-sectional study examines how acute-phase oxygen saturation and body temperature predict long COVID symptoms (fatigue, depression, anxiety) in 120 LC patients and 36 controls 3-4 months post-infection. The study identifies an endophenotype class characterized by very low SpO2 and high body temperature associated with psychiatric and autonomic symptoms, but does not test or evaluate any intervention.
paper_authors: Dhurgham Shihab Al-Hadrawi; Haneen Tahseen Al-Rubaye; Abbas F. Almulla; Hussein Kadhem Al-Hakeim; Michael Maes
paper_title: Lowered oxygen saturation and increased body temperature in acute COVID-19 largely predict chronic fatigue syndrome and affective symptoms due to Long COVID: A precision nomothetic approach

summary: UK Biobank describes a large prospective cohort study (500,000 participants) repurposed to investigate COVID-19 and its long-term health effects through repeated blood samples, imaging, and data linkages. The paper outlines study protocols and sub-studies investigating long COVID sequelae but does not present results from completed interventions or treatments.

paper_title: UK biobank: Enhanced assessment of the epidemiology and long-term impact of coronavirus disease-2019

summary: This multicenter study tracks trajectories of anxiety, depressive symptoms, and sleep quality over time in previously hospitalized COVID-19 survivors as part of the LONG-COVID-EXP-CM cohort. It is an observational follow-up study without intervention assignment, focusing on characterizing the natural course of post-COVID psychological and sleep symptoms.

paper_title: Trajectory curves of post-COVID anxiety/depressive symptoms and sleep quality in previously hospitalized COVID-19 survivors: the LONG-COVID-EXP-CM multicenter study

summary: Retrospective observational study of 146 COVID-19 patients with anosmia, tracking olfactory recovery rates and predictors of poor long-term restoration over a mean 5.6-month follow-up. Study found that 36.7% had persistent olfactory disorders, with prolonged anosmia duration as the only significant predictor of incomplete recovery, but no intervention was tested.

paper_title: Delayed recovery from severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 related anosmia predicts incomplete olfactory restoration

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining associations between psychiatric disorders and long COVID diagnosis in 660,217 US veterans. summary: Prospective cohort study following 81 adults for 12 months after mild COVID-19 infection, assessing quality of life, respiratory symptoms, and healthcare utilization. summary: This cross-sectional study compares gut microbiota composition and gastrointestinal symptoms in patients with POTS and post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PACS) versus healthy controls using fecal DNA sequencing and symptom questionnaires. paper_authors: Viktor Hamrefors; Fredrik Kahn; Madlene Holmqvist; Katherine Carlson; Roosa Varjus; Alexander Gudjonsson; Artur Fedorowski; Bodil Ohlsson
paper_title: Gut microbiota composition is altered in postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome and post-acute COVID-19 syndrome

summary: Prospective cohort study following 121 long COVID patients for 24 months post-infection to characterize long COVID symptoms and assess the impact of COVID-19 vaccination. summary: This retrospective study examined 731 post-COVID patients to identify newly diagnosed alternative disorders that might explain their symptoms. paper_title: Occult endocrine disorders newly diagnosed in patients with post-COVID-19 symptoms

summary: Prospective observational study of COVID-19 pneumonia survivors followed at 3 and 12 months post-discharge to assess health-related quality of life (HRQoL) using SF-36 and pulmonary function tests in 130 patients. paper_title: Impact of COVID-19 on quality of life in survivors with pulmonary sequelae

summary: This study investigates molecular and metabolic changes in COVID-19 patients through a one-year follow-up period, examining inflammatory markers, amino acids, and micronutrients related to disease severity and physical recovery. summary: A prospective cohort study from the German DigiHero study examining early recovery factors in 5,098 SARS-CoV-2-infected individuals who developed early symptoms (4-12 weeks post-infection). paper_title: Insights into early recovery from Long COVID—results from the German DigiHero Cohort

summary: This study analyzes long COVID outcomes in 643 CORE clinic patients versus 52,089 non-CORE COVID-19 patients to identify associations between health-related social needs (HRSNs) and symptom severity. paper_title: Patients with unmet social needs are at higher risks of developing severe long COVID-19 symptoms and neuropsychiatric sequela

summary: This prospective cohort study followed 271 COVID-19 pneumonia patients with CT imaging at 6 months post-hospitalization to assess pulmonary residual abnormalities and fibrotic-like changes. While the study mentions paxlovid as a predictor, it is an observational follow-up study without an assigned treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the treatment trials analysis.
paper_authors: Xingyu Fang; Yuan Lv; Wei Lv; Lin Liu; Yun Feng; Li Liu; Feng Pan; Yijun Zhang
paper_title: CT-based Assessment at 6-Month Follow-up of COVID-19 Pneumonia patients in China

summary: Retrospective observational study of 609 nursing personnel assessing the relationship between post-COVID infection and work ability using the Work Ability Index. paper_title: Long-COVID autonomic syndrome in working age and work ability impairment

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 623 pregnant women comparing maternal and fetal complications across acute COVID-19, long-term COVID-19, and non-COVID-19 groups. paper_title: Cognitive profile, neuroimaging and fluid biomarkers in post-acute COVID-19 syndrome

summary: This ecological analysis compares the epidemiological and economic burden of post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) in Italy and the United States from 2020–2023, estimating incidence rates, quality-adjusted life years lost, and productivity losses. summary: A prospective cohort study examining the relationship between olfactory bulb volume (via MRI) and olfactory dysfunction in 233 individuals recovering from mild-to-moderate COVID-19, with follow-up assessments 1-2 years post-infection. It finds a possible association between vaccination and POTS incidence, though lower than post-infection POTS risk, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

paper_title: COVID-19 infection associated with increased risk of new-onset vascular dementia in adults ≥50 years

paper_title: Optimizing the schedule of BNT162b2 COVID-19 against long COVID and associated quality of life losses

summary: This study analyzed sex differences in outcomes from a standardized 3-week pulmonary rehabilitation program in 233 post-acute COVID-19 patients. Females showed smaller improvements in lung function parameters but greater overall progress toward reference values compared to males, suggesting sex-specific rehabilitation requirements.

paper_title:

                    COVID-19

summary: Observational study of long COVID patients treated with naturopathic complex therapy at a German natural medicine hospital, with whole-body hyperthermia as a central component. Early results from up to 6-month follow-up suggest patients improved with treatment, warranting further analysis.

summary: Retrospective analysis of 132 long COVID patients presenting to a post-COVID clinic ≥6 months after acute COVID-19, characterizing persistent symptoms and diagnostic findings. Most common complaints were fatigue (82%), dyspnea on exertion (61%), and cognitive impairment (54%), with significantly reduced quality of life across SF-36 domains.
paper_authors: Dietrich August; Katarina Stete; Hanna Hilger; Veronika Götz; Paul Biever; Jonas Hosp; Dirk Wagner; Thomas Christian Köhler; Kathrin Gerstacker; Jochen Seufert; Katharina Laubner; Winfried Kern; Siegbert Rieg

summary: This paper reports on the treatment of long COVID patients at a hospital for naturopathic medicine (KfN) in Germany, which offers individualized treatment concepts combining classical naturopathic approaches, neural therapy, and homeopathy alongside conventional internal medicine care. The authors present a study evaluating the outcomes of their comprehensive treatment approach, aimed at symptom relief and improving patient energy levels.
paper_authors: Robert Schmidt
paper_title:
Long/Post Covid im Krankenhaus für Naturheilweisen
                    unter besonderer Berücksichtigung der
                    Homöopathie

summary: A prospective observational study evaluating occupational outcomes in 173 long COVID patients undergoing pneumological rehabilitation, with follow-up assessments at baseline, end of rehabilitation, and 6 months post-intervention. Results show 85.5% returned to work at 6-month follow-up with significant improvements in work ability and reduced participation limitations, though 41.3% remained at risk for early retirement due to persistent cognitive symptoms and fatigue.
paper_authors: Mercedes Rutsch; Ruth Deck
paper_title:
Berufliche Belastungen von Long-Covid-Rehabilitand*innen und
                    Rückkehr zur Arbeit nach einer pneumologischen
                    Rehabilitation

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed olfactory and gustatory function in 48 long-COVID patients using validated tests (Sniffin' Sticks, 3-drop taste test) and self-reported ratings. The study found 90% of patients had pathological chemosensory diagnoses, but it is observational without any treatment intervention or control group.

summary: This within-subjects study evaluated the effect of COVID-19 on the auditory efferent system by measuring transient evoked otoacoustic emissions and contralateral suppression before and after COVID-19 in 11 adults. The study found no significant difference in auditory efferent function between pre- and post-COVID measurements, though it notes that severe COVID-19 can affect cochlear and auditory efferent system function.

summary: This cross-sectional study compared olfactory dysfunction (via U-sniff test) and subjective smell complaints across children with acute SARS-CoV-2, other URTIs, recovered COVID-19, and long COVID. The study found no significant between-group differences in hyposmia frequency (11-17%), but noted poor correspondence between objective test results and subjective complaints, particularly in the long COVID group.

summary: This pilot study followed 110 pregnant women from the CRONOS registry who had SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy to assess long-term post-COVID symptoms and quality of life. The study found that 63.6% of women experienced symptoms lasting longer than 12 weeks, with fatigue being the most common symptom (88%), significantly impacting quality of life in affected women.

paper_title:

summary: This prospective observational study examined diaphragmatic function using sonography in 54 post-COVID patients, stratifying them by presence or absence of dyspnea. Patients with dyspnea showed significantly reduced diaphragm thickness, mobility, and elasticity compared to those without dyspnea, suggesting diaphragm dysfunction as a potential mechanism underlying respiratory symptoms in post-COVID condition.

summary: A multicentre longitudinal observational study comparing pulmonary rehabilitation outcomes in 172 long COVID patients versus 133 asthma/COPD patients over 12 months. summary: Prospective observational study examining hypogonadism and testosterone levels in male COVID-19 survivors at 3 and 12 months post-infection. summary: A prospective observational study of 224 long COVID patients undergoing pulmonary rehabilitation, measuring patient-reported outcomes (dyspnea, quality of life, pain, fatigue, depression, anxiety) at baseline, end of rehabilitation, and at 3 and 6 months post-treatment. Patient-Reported Outcomes (PROs) 3 und 6 Monate nach pneumologischer

summary: This study evaluates the prevalence of persistent chemosensory symptoms in post-COVID patients across a cohort of 4,062 acutely infected individuals and 909 follow-up respondents at 14.5 months post-infection. The authors found that while subjective chemosensory complaints are common during and after acute infection, only 1.2% have objective quantifiable chemosensory damage and few seek specialized treatment, suggesting lower healthcare burden compared to other long COVID complications.
paper_authors: Hilmar Gudziol; Benjamin Giszas; Ulrike Schade; Thomas Bitter; Philipp A. Reuken; Andreas Stallmach; Orlando Guntinas-Lichius
paper_title: Post-COVID-Patienten mit persistierenden chemosensorischen Symptomen sind in der Bevölkerung selten
