summary: Longitudinal study following 20 hospitalized COVID-19 patients from discharge to three months post-discharge, assessing exercise capacity and occupational competence using standardized measures. While patients showed some improvement over time, the study is observational without any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the intervention trials pipeline.
paper_authors: Vildan Fidanoglu; Melda Saglam; Serkan Pekcetin; Naciye Vardar Yagli; Birsen Pinar Yildiz; Mesut Bayraktaroglu; Esra Ergun Alis
paper_title: Exercise Capacity and Occupational Competence Sequelae in COVID-19 Survivors: A Longitudinal Study

summary: This prospective observational study compared mitochondrial function in isolated PBMCs from 27 long COVID patients versus 16 healthy controls using Seahorse flux analysis. The study found distinctive changes in ATP synthase function in long COVID cases that correlated with autonomic health, quality of life, and time since infection, but did not test or evaluate any intervention.
paper_authors: Jane Macnaughtan; Kai-Yin Chau; Ewen Brennan; Marco Toffoli; Antonella Spinazzola; Toby Hillman; Melissa Heightman; Anthony Henry Vernon Schapira
paper_title: Mitochondrial function is impaired in long COVID patients

summary: This registry-based cohort study examines pre-pandemic care-seeking patterns in 208,050 Swedish women and their association with subsequent post-COVID condition, post-viral fatigue syndrome, and exhaustion disorder diagnoses. The study is observational/analytical rather than an intervention trial, analyzing historical primary-care data to identify risk factors for symptom-based diagnoses.
paper_authors: Agnes af Geijerstam; Kirsten Mehlig; Fredrik Nyberg; Annika Rosengren; Ailiana Santosa; Maria Åberg; Lauren Lissner
paper_title: Pre-pandemic care-seeking patterns and subsequent diagnoses of post-COVID condition, post viral fatigue syndrome, and exhaustion disorder: a registry-based cohort study of 208,050 Swedish women
paper_journal: Scandinavian Journal of Primary Health Care

summary: Prospective cohort study of 84 elite football players assessing persistent performance deficits after SARS-CoV-2 infection, with 22 infections during follow-up. Found transient compromise in aerobic performance (elevated heart rate during exertion) 52 days post-infection, resolved by 128 days, with no deficits in anaerobic performance or strength.
paper_authors: Wezenbeek E.; Denolf S.; Bourgois JG; Philippaerts RM; De Winne B.; Willems TM; Witvrouw E.; Verstockt S.; Schuermans J.
paper_title: Impact of (long) COVID on athletes’ performance: a prospective study in elite football players

summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 365,354 individuals in Stockholm matched on age, sex, and baseline healthcare use to compare healthcare utilization in 2021/22 between those with SARS-CoV-2 seropositivity in 2020 versus seronegative controls. The study found no overall increase in healthcare use in the general seropositive population, with increased healthcare use restricted only to individuals hospitalized for COVID-19 in 2020.
paper_authors: Nicholas Baltzer; Pontus Hedberg; Sara Nordqvist Kleppe; Joakim Dillner; Anders Sönnerborg; Jan Albert; Kristoffer Strålin; Pär Sparén; Pontus Nauclér
paper_title: Long-term healthcare use of COVID-19 cases in 2020: a two-year follow-up in Stockholm, Sweden

summary: This prospective cohort study investigates circadian rhythm alterations and sleep patterns in ME/CFS and post-COVID fatigue patients compared to healthy controls, examining associations with cardiovascular risk factors. While about long COVID, it is observational without any intervention—patients are monitored but not given a treatment, so it does not meet the inclusion criteria for treatment/intervention trials.
paper_authors: María Fernanda Zerón-Rugerio; Maria Cleofé Zaragozá; Joan Carles Domingo; Ramon Sanmartín-Sentañes; Jose Alegre-Martin; Jesús Castro-Marrero; Trinitat Cambras
paper_title: Sleep and circadian rhythm alterations in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome and post-COVID fatigue syndrome and its association with cardiovascular risk factors: A prospective cohort study

summary: This comparative effectiveness study evaluates allied healthcare (physiotherapy, occupational therapy, etc.) versus no treatment for long COVID patients using data from two cohorts (ParaCOV n=1,451 with allied healthcare and LongCOVID n=1,427 controls) followed for 12 months. Allied healthcare showed significant improvements in physical functioning and quality of life, though between-group differences were not considered clinically relevant by pre-specified thresholds.
paper_authors: Ângela Jornada Ben; Anita Natalia Varga; Siméon de Bruijn; Willem Bastiaan Dekker; Cees C. van den Wijngaard; Arie Cornelis Verburg; Thomas Johannes Hoogeboom; Philip van der Wees; Raymond W. J. G. Ostelo; Judith E. Bosmans; Johanna Maria van Dongen
paper_title: A comparison of allied healthcare versus no allied healthcare on participation, fatigue, physical functioning and health-related quality of life for patients with persistent complaints after a COVID-19 infection

summary: This observational cohort study evaluates vision-related symptoms and visual/oculomotor function in 38 non-hospitalised long COVID patients referred for neurocognitive assessment. The study validates clinical assessment tools (Developmental Eye Movement Test, Visual Motion Sensitivity Clinical Test Protocol) but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Jan Johansson; Marika Möller; Gabriela Markovic; Kristian Borg
paper_title: Vision impairment is common in non-hospitalised patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome

summary: This retrospective observational study compares cardiovascular disease risk and mortality outcomes between hemodialysis patients with and without prior mild COVID-19 infection during the post-Omicron era. The study found no significant increase in long-term cardiovascular or non-cardiovascular mortality risk associated with mild COVID-19 in this population.
paper_authors: Akiko Okamoto; Teppei Okamoto; Takaki Ichiyama; Takafumi Fukushima; Sosuke Omizo; Himawari Asanuma; Hiroyuki Sato; Hisashi Sakurai; Anna Yoneyama; Fumiya Yoneyama; Noritaka Ishii; Takuya Oishi; Ryuma Tanaka; Hikari Miura; Tomoko Hamaya; Hirotake Kodama; Naoki Fujita; Hiromi Murasawa; Hayato Yamamoto; Atsushi Imai; Hisao Saitoh; Shingo Hatakeyama; Chikara Ohyama; Tadashi Suzuki
paper_title: The long-term impact of mild COVID-19 on cardiovascular disease and mortality in patients on hemodialysis: a post-Omicron era retrospective observational study

summary: This study compared respiratory function, muscle strength, exercise capacity, and chronotropic response between post-COVID-19 patients with pulmonary involvement and healthy controls. Patients demonstrated significantly impaired respiratory function, exercise capacity, and chronotropic response, with most displaying sedentary lifestyle and elevated dyspnea; the authors recommend comprehensive pulmonary rehabilitation to prevent long-term impairments.
paper_authors: Ece Baytok; Meral Boşnak Güçlü; Başak Kavalcı Kol; Nilgün Yılmaz Demirci
paper_title: Oxygen consumption chronotropic response to maximal exercise and physical activity level in patients with post-COVID-19 and pulmonary involvement

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 12,000+ persons with HIV in Washington, DC that characterizes the prevalence (46%), symptom clustering, and risk factors for post-COVID conditions. The study found that asthma history and retired/disabled status were associated with post-COVID conditions, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Shannon Barth; Paige Kulie; Anne Monroe; Michael Horberg; Amanda Castel
paper_title: Prevalence and risk factors for post-COVID conditions of COVID-19 among persons with HIV in Washington, DC

summary: This observational study assessed objective neurocognitive deficits in 133 COVID-19 patients five months after hospitalization using standardized neuropsychological tests (RBANS and CWIT). Findings showed 37% of patients had cognitive impairment below cutoff, with attention and memory deficits most common, though no clear associations with disease severity indicators were found.
paper_authors: Ulrika Birberg Thornberg; Agnes Andersson; Malin Lindh; Lovisa Hellgren; Anestis Divanoglou; Richard Levi
paper_title: Neurocognitive deficits in COVID-19 patients five months after discharge from hospital

summary: This cohort follow-up study compares psychological impacts (anxiety, depression, PTSD) of COVID-19 on patients with and without chronic medical illnesses, with assessments at acute infection and 6-month follow-up. While it addresses long-term psychological sequelae, it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment or intervention for these conditions.
paper_authors: Hend Ibrahim Shousha; Nagwan Madbouly; Shimaa Afify; Noha Asem; Eman Fouad; Rabab Maher; Suaad Sayed Moussa; Amr Abdelazeem; Eslam Mohamed Youssif; Khalid Yousef Harhira; Kariman Kamal; Hazem Elmorsy; Hassan Elgarem; Dalia Omran; Mohamed Hassany; Basem Eysa; Mohamed El Kassas
paper_title: Anxiety, depression and coping strategies among chronic medical patients with coronavirus disease-2019: a multicenter follow-up cohort study

summary: A prospective cohort study examining platelet function and activation markers in mild COVID-19 convalescents at 2-15 weeks and 6-10 months post-infection compared to matched controls. The study found increased platelet sensitization and elevated inflammatory mediators (S1P, MRP4) but no altered platelet aggregation or thrombin formation, suggesting a persistent pro-inflammatory state after convalescence.
paper_authors: Céline Tolksdorf; Andrea Seidel; Christian Baume; Eileen Moritz; Karen Saljé; Kathrin Lehmann; Karsten Becker; Ulrike Garscha; Thomas Thiele; Edzard Schwedhelm; Mirjam von Lucadou; Mladen V. Tzvetkov; Stefan Engeli; Gabriele Jedlitschky; Bernhard H. Rauch
paper_title: Enhanced platelet sensitization is accompanied by increased expression of the transporter MRP4 and elevated plasma S1P levels in mild COVID-19 convalescents

summary: Prospective cohort study following 34 COVID-19 hospitalized patients who received early rehabilitation, with 17 completing 12-month follow-up. While quadriceps strength and functional capacity improved significantly, the study focuses on acute COVID-19 recovery during hospitalization rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks/months post-infection).
paper_authors: Tathyana Emília Neves de Figueiredo; Lívia Maria Petilli Zopelari; Valéria Amorim Pires Di Lorenzo
paper_title: Comparison of quadriceps muscle strength, functional capacity and fatigue at hospital discharge and after 12 months in COVID-19 hospitalized patients undergoing early rehabilitation: a follow-up study

summary: Prospective study evaluating the impact of an intensive, interdisciplinary inpatient rehabilitation program on 42 post-ICU COVID-19 survivors. The program resulted in significant improvements in muscle strength, respiratory function, fatigue, balance, exercise capacity, and ability to perform daily activities.
paper_authors: Margarida Rodrigues; Ana João Costa; Rui Santos; Pedro Diogo; Eugénio Gonçalves; Denise Barroso; Miguel P. Almeida; Inês Machado Vaz; Ana Lima
paper_title: Inpatient rehabilitation can improve functional outcomes of post-intensive care unit COVID-19 patients—a prospective study

summary: A prospective cohort study comparing psychological and biological assessments in 104 adults with tobacco use disorder before and four months after long COVID diagnosis. The study documents significant increases in depressive symptoms, anxiety, insomnia, and perceived stress, with decreased serum cortisol levels, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Thiago P. Fernandes; Natanael A. Santos; Linnea N. Dahlgren
paper_title: Prospective study of long COVID-related psychological and biological outcomes in individuals with tobacco use disorder

summary: This study examines immune response changes in 23 patients with cardiovascular disease during acute SARS-CoV-2 infection and 3-month recovery, measuring monocyte phenotypes and cytokine profiles. The findings suggest persistent pro-inflammatory monocyte dysfunction post-infection, but the study focuses on acute infection rather than long COVID syndrome.
paper_authors: Carolin Langnau; Henrik Janing; Hüseyin Kocaman; Sarah Gekeler; Manina Günter; Álvaro Petersen-Uribe; Philippa Jaeger; Barbara Koch; Klaus-Peter Kreisselmeier; Tatsiana Castor; Dominik Rath; Meinrad Paul Gawaz; Stella E. Autenrieth; Karin Anne Lydia Mueller
paper_title: Recovery of systemic hyperinflammation in patients with severe SARS-CoV-2 infection

summary: Prospective cohort study following COVID-19 ICU survivors in Congo for 2 years to assess kidney function decline and chronic kidney disease incidence, comparing patients with and without acute kidney injury. Finds that 23% experienced kidney function decline and 0.73% developed CKD, with prior AKI significantly increasing risk.
paper_authors: Yannick Mayamba Nlandu; Jean-Robert Rissassi Makulo; Marie Essig; Yannick Mompango Engole; Marie-France Ingole Mboliasa; Aliocha Natuhoyila Nkodila; Vieux Momeme Mokoli; Clarisse Nsenga Nkondi; Augustin Luzayadio Longo; François Musungayi Kajingulu; Cédric Kabemba Ilunga; Chantal Vuvu Zinga; Evariste Mukendi Kadima; Justine Busanga Bukabau; Steve Mundeke Ahuka; Aimé Lumaka; Nazaire Mangani Nseka; Ernest Kiswaya Sumaili
paper_title: Longitudinal kidney outcomes in surviving COVID-19 patients in Africa: a prospective Congolese single-center cohort study

summary: This is a secondary analysis from the COVID-19 RECOVERY STUDY II (CORES II) that performed cluster analysis on long COVID symptom phenotypes and their association with one-year psychosocial outcomes (anxiety, depression, PTSD, QOL) in 746 patients. The study identified five symptom clusters and found that multi-organ dysfunction and olfactory/gustatory disturbance phenotypes were associated with worse psychosocial outcomes, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Muneaki Hemmi; Naoki Kanda; Kensuke Nakamura; Shinya Suganuma; Keiichiro Kawabata; Hideaki Kato; Nao Ichihara; Takeshi Asami; Keiko Ide; Yoko Muto; Miyuki Hori; Arisa Iba; Mariko Hosozawa; Hiroyasu Iso
paper_title: The relationship between the phenotype of long COVID symptoms and one-year psychosocial outcomes: an exploratory clustering analysis

summary: This case-control study compares psychological and neurological symptoms between 62 long COVID-recovered individuals and 36 healthy controls, identifying unrefreshing sleep as a significant predictor of attention and anxiety issues. The study is excluded because it is observational without an intervention—it characterizes symptoms and risk factors rather than testing any treatment.
paper_authors: Sapna S. Mishra; Hritik Gupta; Tapan K. Gandhi; Bharat B. Biswal
paper_title: Psychological symptoms and risk factors associated with long COVID: a study on the Indian cohort

summary: This prospective observational study assessed thyroid dysfunction in 113 COVID-19 survivors two months post-infection, finding thyroid dysfunction in 61.1% of patients, predominantly subclinical hypothyroidism. The study documents the long-term effects of COVID-19 on thyroid function but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Vesselina Yanachkova; Teodora Stankova; Radiana Staynova
paper_title: Thyroid dysfunction as a long-term post-COVID-19 complication in mild-to-moderate COVID-19

summary: Retrospective database analysis of work absence claims among US employees with COVID-19 from 2018-2022, examining disability benefit utilization, claim duration, and costs. Findings show COVID-19 caused significant work loss extending beyond acute infection, ranking as the second most common reason for short-term disability claims during the study period.
paper_authors: Jennifer Judy; Alon Yehoshua; Julie Gouveia-Pisano; Richard A. Brook; Nathan L. Kleinman; Alek A. Drnach; Eric M. Rosenberg; Tanya Ghanjanasak; Deborah A. Winter; Feng Dai; Jannette M. Escobar; Heather Sell
paper_title: Impact of COVID-19 on work loss in the United States- A retrospective database analysis

summary: Retrospective cohort study using French primary care EHRs to assess healthcare resource utilization and costs among 30,122 adults with long COVID between 2020-2023. Found that long COVID patients incurred €2,443 per patient per year in healthcare costs, with 97.3% using GP services and 62.4% using nursing care.
paper_authors: Jingyan Yang; Cheikh Tamberou; Elise Arnee; Pierre-Alexandre Squara; Ayoub Boukhlal; Jennifer L. Nguyen; Hannah R. Volkman; Stéphane Fiévez; Marina Lepoutre-Bourguet; Jinma Ren; Haifa Ben Romdhane; Pascal Crépey; Olivier Robineau
paper_title: All-cause healthcare resource utilization and costs among community-managed adults with long-COVID in France, 2020–2023

summary: This retrospective cohort study quantifies healthcare resource utilization and direct medical costs for children with mild-to-moderate long COVID in France using primary care electronic health records. Among 27,537 children with COVID-19, 3,888 (14.1%) developed long COVID with mean first-year costs of €823 per patient, representing an incremental increase of €98 compared to non-long COVID controls.
paper_authors: Jingyan Yang; Cheikh Tamberou; Elise Arnee; Pierre-Alexandre Squara; Ayoub Boukhlal; Jennifer L. Nguyen; Hannah R. Volkman; Stephane Fievez; Marina Lepoutre-Bourguet; Haifa Ben Romdhane; Charlotte Renaudat; Pascal Crépey; Olivier Robineau
paper_title: Quantifying all-cause healthcare resource utilization and costs of children with mild-to-moderate long COVID in France

summary: Cross-sectional comparison of neuropsychological functioning between long COVID patients with persistent severe fatigue/concentration difficulties and those without complaints, assessed median 23 months post-infection. No significant cognitive impairment was found on most tests, with only minimal differences in processing speed.
paper_authors: Anouk Verveen; Sander C.J Verfaillie; Denise Visser; Dook W. Koch; Esmée Verwijk; Gert J. Geurtsen; Jeroen Roor; Brent Appelman; Ronald Boellaard; Caroline M. van Heugten; Janneke Horn; Hanneke E. Hulst; Menno D. de Jong; Tanja A. paper_title: Neuropsychological functioning after COVID-19: Minor differences between individuals with and without persistent complaints after SARS-CoV-2 infection

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluates performance validity testing (PVT) in 247 long COVID patients undergoing neuropsychological evaluation, examining the relationship between PVT failures, external incentives (disability claims), and cognitive performance. Results show that external incentives are associated with PVT failures, but this is an observational assessment study without any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Douglas M. Whiteside; Michael R. Basso; Chen Shen; Laura Fry; Savana Naini; Eric J. Waldron; Erin Holker; Jim Porter; Courtney Eskridge; Allison Logemann; Greta N. Minor
paper_title: The relationship between performance validity testing, external incentives, and cognitive functioning in long COVID
paper_journal: Journal of Clinical and Experimental Neuropsychology

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining the association between COVID-19 vaccination status and long COVID incidence and healthcare resource utilization in UK primary care data from 2022-2023. Vaccination was not associated with long COVID incidence, though some subgroup-specific benefits in specialist referrals were observed.
paper_authors: Kiran K. Rai; Hannah Gowman; Cale S. Harrison; David C. Gruben; Rebecca Butfield; Rosie Hulme; Hannah R. Volkman; Jennifer L. Nguyen; Jingyan Yang
paper_title: Understanding the role of COVID-19 vaccination in all-cause healthcare resource utilisation among adults with long COVID in the UK primary care setting: data from the 2022–2023 respiratory virus season

summary: Prospective cohort study of non-hospitalised COVID-19 patients across 11 European countries followed for 12 weeks to assess long-COVID prevalence, symptom characteristics, and risk factors. Found 52% developed long-COVID with fatigue as the most common lingering symptom; no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Katarina Hedin; Alike W. van der Velden; Malene Plejdrup Hansen; Anna B. Moberg; Anca Balan; Pascale Bruno; Samuel Coenen; Eskild Johansen; Anna Kowalczyk; Peter Konstantin Kurotschka; Sanne R. van der Linde; Lile Malania; Jörn Rohde; Jan Verbakel; Heike Vornhagen; Akke Vellinga
paper_title: Initial symptoms and three months follow-up after acute COVID-19 in outpatients: An international prospective cohort study

summary: This cross-sectional study compared psychological functioning in 201 long COVID patients versus 102 post-concussion syndrome patients using the Personality Assessment Inventory, finding similar patterns of emotional distress and psychological symptoms between groups. The study suggests psychological treatment strategies used for PCS may benefit long COVID patients but does not test or evaluate a treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Laura Fry; Allison Logemann; Eric Waldron; Erin Holker; Jim Porter; Courtney Eskridge; Savana Naini; Michael R. Basso; Sarah E. Taylor; Tanya Melnik; Douglas M. Whiteside
paper_title: Emotional functioning in long COVID: Comparison to post-concussion syndrome using the Personality Assessment Inventory

summary: A retrospective cohort study evaluating the prevalence of post-COVID-19 syndrome and associated risk factors in 463 healthcare workers followed for 18 months. Female sex and obesity were identified as statistically significant risk factors, with fatigue (32.5%) and memory disorders (21.5%) being the most common persistent symptoms.
paper_authors: Ana Cláudia Vasconcellos Azeredo; André Külzer Santos; Raimunda Sinthia Lima de Braga; João Vitor Vigne Duz; Marina Scheffer de Souza; Denise Rossato Silva
paper_title: Prevalence and associated risk factors of post-COVID-19 syndrome in healthcare workers
paper_journal: Journal of Occupational and Environmental Hygiene

summary: This pre-registered controlled study compared auditory function between 57 hospitalized COVID-19 patients and 40 matched non-COVID controls using comprehensive behavioral, physiological, and self-report measures. The study found no significant differences in auditory function between groups, concluding that COVID-19 infection does not have a significant long-term impact on hearing.
paper_authors: Visram AS; Jackson IR; Guest H.; Plack CJ; Brij S.; Chaudhuri N.; Munro KJ
paper_title: Pre-registered controlled comparison of auditory function reveals no difference between hospitalised adults with and without COVID-19

summary: Longitudinal neuropsychological assessment of 46 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors at 1 and 2.5 years post-infection, examining objective cognitive functioning across multiple domains. Found no consistent objective cognitive deficits or major cognitive disorders in the majority of cases, with stable performance over time except for improvement in phonemic fluency.
paper_authors: Dook W. Koch; Simona Klinkhammer; Anouk Verveen; Denise Visser; Pythia T. Nieuwkerk; Esmée Verwijk; Bart N.M. van Berckel; Janneke Horn; Nelleke Tolboom; Caroline M. van Heugten; Sander C.J. Verfaillie; Hans Knoop
paper_title: Long-term cognitive functioning following COVID-19: Negligible neuropsychological changes over time

summary: This prospective cohort study followed 291 SARS-CoV-2 positive individuals in Kenya for up to 16 months to characterize long COVID symptoms and recovery patterns. The study found that half had lingering symptoms at 6 months and a third at 12 months, with slower recovery in older adults, women, and those with comorbidities, but does not test any interventions or treatments.

Mohamed; Gershim Asiki; Constance Schultsz
paper_title: Recovery and long-term health outcomes of SARS-CoV-2 infection in a prospective cohort in an urban setting, Kenya

summary: This retrospective cohort study compares lung perfusion scintigraphy findings between 30 post-COVID patients with persistent dyspnea and 30 controls without prior COVID-19. The study investigates diagnostic imaging markers rather than evaluating a treatment intervention, making it a diagnostic/observational assessment study excluded from the trial analysis.
paper_authors: Francesco Lanfranchi; Sara Maggio; Carlo Delucchi; Francesca Bertoldi; Ferdinando Corica; Maria Silvia De Feo; Cecilia Marini; Teresita Aloè; Viviana Frantellizzi; Giuseppe De Vincentis; Silvia Morbelli; Gianmario Sambuceti; Emanuela Barisione; Matteo Bauckneht
paper_title: The added value of lung perfusion scintigraphy semiquantitative measures in post-COVID patients with persistent dyspnea without pulmonary embolism

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing chest CT airway and vascular measurements in females with long-COVID, COPD, and ex-smokers. Found significant differences in airway lumen area, wall thickness, and pulmonary vessel volume in long-COVID patients but no evidence of pulmonary vascular remodeling.
paper_authors: Kooner HK; Wyszkiewicz PV; Matheson AM; McIntosh MJ; Abdelrazek M.; Dhaliwal I.; Nicholson JM; Kirby M.; Svenningsen S.; Parraga G.
paper_title: Chest CT Airway and Vascular Measurements in Females with COPD or Long-COVID
paper_journal: COPD: Journal of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease

summary: Prospective cohort study of 327 long COVID patients receiving SPA (spa water therapy) rehabilitation, examining dyspnea and fatigue outcomes in relation to pulmonary function, obesity, and comorbidities. SPA therapy showed benefit for alleviating fatigue and improving well-being in selected subgroups, particularly those with chronic respiratory conditions, though not in patients with impaired DLCO and obesity.
paper_authors: Emanuela Resta; Chiara Noviello; Preethymol Peter; Giusi Graziano; Valeria Dalena; Alessia Caputi; Giorgio Castellana; Giacomo Riformato; Silvio Tafuri; Pierucci Pierucci
paper_title: Respiratory post COVID sequelae: the role of pulmonary function impairment, fatigue and obesity in dyspnea and the impact of SPA rehabilitation

summary: This cross-sectional study compares neural mechanosensitivity and peripheral nerve function between 33 long COVID patients and 31 healthy controls using standardized clinical assessments and neurodynamic tests. Long COVID patients showed significantly worse neural mechanosensitivity, functionality, and quality of life, but the study does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Andrés Calvache-Mateo; Alberto Rodríguez-López; Alba Navas-Otero; Javier Martín Núñez; Alejandro Heredia-Ciuró; Laura López-López; Marie Carmen Valenza
paper_title: Impairment of neural mechanosensitivity in the Long COVID haulers

summary: A prospective observational cohort study assessing long-term consequences of severe COVID-19 hospitalization at 4-5 months post-discharge in 128 patients. Findings show high prevalence of fatigue, dyspnea, and cognitive dysfunction with impaired quality of life and lung function (45% with reduced diffusing capacity), but no intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Marie Vejen; Ejvind Frausing Hansen; Bakir Nabil Ibrahim Al-Jarah; Casper Jensen; Pia Thaning; Klaus Nielsen Jeschke; Charlotte Suppli Ulrik
paper_title: Hospital admission for COVID-19 pneumonitis – long-term impairment in quality of life and lung function

summary: Retrospective cohort study analyzing pre- and post-COVID medication and disease burden in older adults using health system data from 2020-2024. Finds significant increases in diagnoses and medication use post-COVID, with disparities by age, race, and gender, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Shaminul H. Shakib; Demetra Antimisiaris
paper_title: Analysis of polypharmacy in older adults pre- and post-COVID-19

summary: Prospective observational study examining depression and PTSD symptoms in COVID-19 critical illness survivors at 1 and 12 months post-ICU discharge. Found that 29-32% had depression and 31-36% had PTSD symptoms, with mechanical ventilation predicting symptom persistence, but no intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Guillem Navarra-Ventura; Marta Godoy-González; Gemma Gomà; Mercè Jodar; Leonardo Sarlabous; Verónica Santos-Pulpón; Alba Xifra-Porxas; Candelaria de Haro; Oriol Roca; Lluís Blanch; Josefina López-Aguilar; Sol Fernández-Gonzalo
paper_title: Occurrence, co-occurrence and persistence of symptoms of depression and post-traumatic stress disorder in survivors of COVID-19 critical illness

summary: Longitudinal metagenomic study of 142 COVID-19 patients tracking antimicrobial resistance genes in gut microbiota from acute infection through 6 months post-viral clearance, with intervention groups receiving antibiotics or probiotics. Probiotics (synbiotic formula SIM01) significantly reduced antimicrobial resistance gene burden compared to antibiotic treatment, with expanded resistome associated with increased post-acute COVID-19 syndrome prevalence.
paper_authors: Qi Su; Qin Liu; Lin Zhang; Zhilu Xu; Chenyu Liu; Wenqi Lu; Jessica YL Ching; Amy Li; Joyce Wing Yan Mak; Grace Chung Yan Lui; Susanna So Shan Ng; Kai Ming Chow; David SC Hui; Paul KS Chan; Francis Ka Leung Chan; Siew C. Ng
paper_title: Antibiotics and probiotics impact gut antimicrobial resistance gene reservoir in COVID-19 patients

summary: Retrospective observational study evaluating post-COVID health status in 123 recovered patients using the EuroQol-5D-5L scale at discharge and 4-8 weeks post-discharge. Found significant improvements over time in anxiety/depression and other dimensions, with smoking associated with reduced activity levels at 4 weeks.
paper_authors: Siddhi Hegde; Shreya Sreeram; Kaushik R. Bhat; Vaishnavi Satish; Sujith Shekar; Mahesh Babu
paper_title: Evaluation of post-COVID health status using the EuroQol-5D-5L scale

summary: This is a prospective follow-up study of lung function in COVID-19 ICU survivors at 4 months, 1 year, and 2 years post-discharge. While it documents persistent pulmonary deficits in post-acute COVID-19, it does not focus on long COVID per se and contains no treatment or intervention component—it is purely observational follow-up of ICU survivors from acute COVID-19.
paper_authors: Marta A. Kisiel; Emil Ekbom; Christer Janson; Össur Emilsson; Miklos Lipcsey; Robert Frithiof; Michael Marks-Hultström; Andrei Malinovschi
paper_title: Long-term lung function trajectories in Swedish COVID-19 ICU survivors: a two-year follow-up study

summary: Prospective observational cohort of 34 long COVID patients receiving 12 weeks of telerehabilitation based on the STOP-REST-PACE approach, assessing post-exertional malaise (PEM), quality of life, respiratory symptoms, and return to work outcomes. Despite therapy, PEM persisted in 19/30 completers; respiratory symptoms improved significantly, but fatigue, quality of life, and return to work showed minimal improvement.
paper_authors: Pamela Tanguay; Isabelle Gaboury; Frédérique Daigle; Anne Bhéreur; Olivia Dubois; Émilie Lagueux; Florian Naye; Michel Tousignant; Nicole Marquis; Simon Décary
paper_title: Post-exertional malaise may persist in Long COVID despite learning STOP-REST-PACE

summary: A cross-sectional study comparing symptom trajectories in 278 long-COVID patients over ~21.7 weeks against 502 ME/CFS patients using standardized questionnaires. The study documents natural symptom evolution (improvement in most domains, worsening in neurocognitive) but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Leonard A. Jason; Mohammed F. Islam; Karl Conroy; Joseph Cotler; Chelsea Torres; Mady Johnson; Brianna Mabie
paper_title: COVID-19 symptoms over time: comparing long-haulers to ME/CFS

summary: This cross-sectional study from the SHARE survey examined associations between preexisting depression and COVID-19 vaccination uptake, SARS-CoV-2 infection risk, and long COVID development in 31,115 middle-aged and older Europeans. Depression was associated with reduced vaccination odds (OR=0.72), increased infection risk (OR=1.15), and increased long COVID risk (OR=1.21), with associations strengthening with depression severity.
paper_authors: Yumeng Gao; Chunxiao Duan; Tongtong Miao; Qian Shen; Jia Yu; Suwen Shen; Yujun Chen; Yuan Shen; Kaixin Zhang
paper_title: Association between depression and three key COVID-19-related outcomes: The SHARE study

summary: This study examines changes in thyroid function in hypothyroid patients during acute COVID-19 infection in Shanghai, comparing pre-infection baseline to 1-month and 3-month follow-up. It is not a long COVID study as it focuses on acute infection effects in a specific patient population rather than persistent post-COVID sequelae.
paper_authors: Bingxin Li; Xiaoyun Feng; Yihan Zhang; Yunhong Huang; Mingyu Gu; Haiyan Sun; Wenqian Ren; Qin Zhen; Tingting Shen; Ling Pan; Tingting Fan; Qin Qin; Fang Liu; Yongde Peng; Yufan Wang; Huanbai Xu
paper_title: Effect of COVID-19 infection on thyroid function status and clinical indexes among hypothyroid outpatients

summary: This 1-year longitudinal study tracks immune responses (antibodies, B cells, T cells) in 65 COVID-19 convalescents, finding that 48% retain post-acute sequelae symptoms and all maintain immune memory components. The study documents kinetics of SARS-CoV-2 immunity but does not test or evaluate any treatment or intervention for long COVID.
paper_authors: Yang Li; Xi Wang; Xu-Rui Shen; Rong Geng; Nan Xie; Jun-Feng Han; Qing-Miao Zhang; Zheng-Li Shi; Peng Zhou
paper_title: A 1-year longitudinal study on COVID-19 convalescents reveals persistence of anti-SARS-CoV-2 humoral and cellular immunity

summary: A prospective cohort pilot study evaluating stellate ganglion block (SGB) treatment in 10 patients with Long COVID/ME/CFS. Results showed significant improvements in post-exertional malaise, unrefreshing sleep, cognitive impairment, orthostatic intolerance, and quality of life measures, with objective resolution of POTS symptoms.
paper_authors: Deborah L. Duricka; Luke D. Liu
paper_title: Stellate Ganglion Block reduces symptoms of SARS-CoV-2-induced ME/CFS: A prospective cohort pilot study

summary: Prospective cohort study following 155 COVID-19 survivors for 2 years post-infection to assess persistent symptoms and health outcomes. Found that 36.6% had long COVID symptoms, 35.0% had psychological symptoms, and 50.7% had radiographic abnormalities, but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Dapeng Li; Xuejiao Liao; Zhi Liu; Zhenghua Ma; Jingke Dong; Guoqin Zheng; Mei Zi; Fang Wang; Qing He; Guobao Li; Zheng Zhang; Lei Liu
paper_title: Healthy outcomes of patients with COVID-19 two years after the infection: a prospective cohort study

summary: A prospective cohort study following 20,000+ COVID-19 patients in Shanghai for one year to assess long COVID prevalence and impact. Found 8.89% with self-reported long COVID symptoms at 6 months, with 68.5% achieving symptom resolution by 12 months; no treatments were administered.
paper_authors: Jianpeng Cai; Ke Lin; Haocheng Zhang; Quanlin Xue; Kun Zhu; Guanmin Yuan; Yuhan Sun; Feng Zhu; Jingwen Ai; Sen Wang; Wenhong Zhang
paper_title: A one-year follow-up study of systematic impact of long COVID symptoms among patients post SARS-CoV-2 omicron variants infection in Shanghai, China

summary: Prospective cohort study of 6,412 Omicron COVID-19 patients in Shanghai followed from November 2022 to February 2023, examining long COVID sequelae and reinfection rates. Found 9.4% experienced sequelae (primarily fatigue and mental symptoms) and 12.1% experienced reinfection; hybrid immunity with vaccination reduced reinfection risk and was associated with higher neutralizing antibody titers.
paper_authors: Mengna Lin; Kangli Cao; Feixiang Xu; Xueling Wu; Yao Shen; Su Lu; Zhongshu Kuang; Hailin Ding; Shuyun Yuan; Mian Shao; Guorong Gu; Lingyu Xing; Tianwen Gu; Shaodie Chen; Jian Sun; Jiamin Zhu; Xiaoyan Zhang; Yilin Yang; Guoping Zhao; Lihong Huang; Jianqing Xu; Zhenju Song
paper_title: A follow-up study on the recovery and reinfection of Omicron COVID-19 patients in Shanghai, China

summary: This observational study using target trial emulation compared nirmatrelvir/ritonavir and molnupiravir versus no antiviral treatment for post-COVID-19 outcomes among 140,477 and 96,030 outpatients respectively in Hong Kong. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir significantly reduced post-acute mortality and all-cause hospitalization at 31-180 and 181-360 days, while molnupiravir showed only short-term mortality benefit with no protective effect on long-term post-COVID outcomes.
paper_authors: Yuchen Wei; Christopher Boyer; Katherine Min Jia; Guozhang Lin; Huwen Wang; Conglu Li; Chi Tim Hung; Xiaoting Jiang; Carrie Ho Kwan Yam; Tsz Yu Chow; Yawen Wang; Shi Zhao; Zihao Guo; Kehang Li; Aimin Yang; Chris Ka Pun Mok; David S. C. Hui; Ka Chun Chong; Eng Kiong Yeoh
paper_title: Effectiveness of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir and molnupiravir on post-COVID-19 outcomes among outpatients: a target trial emulation investigation

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 1,530 COVID-19 patients examining the predictive role of baseline chest radiograph severity on short- and long-term outcomes. Found that CXR severity (Brixia score) was a significant independent predictor of mortality and presence of long-term residual symptoms at 5-6 month follow-up, with 36% of survivors symptomatic.
paper_authors: Maria M. D’souza; Aruna Kaushik; Jeanne Maria Dsouza; Ratnesh Kanwar; Vivek Lodhi; Rajnish Sharma; Anil Kumar Mishra
paper_title: Does the initial chest radiograph severity in COVID-19 impact the short- and long-term outcome? – a perspective from India

summary: This retrospective cohort study of 50,438 COVID-19 patients examines whether complete COVID-19 vaccination modifies the protective effect of nirmatrelvir-ritonavir treatment on post-acute mortality and rehospitalization outcomes. The study found a significant additive interaction between nirmatrelvir-ritonavir and complete vaccination on post-acute rehospitalization, with greater antiviral benefits in fully vaccinated individuals, particularly among older adults and females.
paper_authors: Huwen Wang; Yuchen Wei; Guozhang Lin; Christopher Boyer; Katherine Min Jia; Chi Tim Hung; Xiaoting Jiang; Conglu Li; Carrie Ho Kwan Yam; Tsz Yu Chow; Yawen Wang; Shi Zhao; Zihao Guo; Kehang Li; Aimin Yang; Chris Ka Pun Mok; David S. C. Hui; Ka Chun Chong; Eng Kiong Yeoh
paper_title: COVID-19 vaccination modified the effect of nirmatrelvir–ritonavir on post-acute mortality and rehospitalization: a retrospective cohort study

summary: This cross-sectional study examined 305 healthcare workers at least 12 weeks post-COVID-19 to identify characteristics and predictors of post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PCS). Female sex and increasing age were identified as statistically significant predictors of PCS, with fatigue, shortness of breath, and muscle/joint aches being the most common symptoms.
paper_authors: Ladislav Štěpánek; Marie Nakládalová; Magdaléna Janošíková; Lubomír Štěpánek; Kateřina Kabrhelová; Alena Boriková
paper_title: Predictors and characteristics of post-acute COVID-19 syndrome in healthcare workers

summary: Prospective cohort study of 154 non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients examining long-term symptoms and health-related quality of life over time. Found that ~10% developed long-term symptoms with significant negative impact on EQ5D-VAS scores, but this is an observational study with no treatment intervention—patients were passively followed, not actively treated.
paper_authors: Emma Löfström; Stefan Kunkel; Arne Kötz; Markus Lingman; Johan Undén; Jens M. Nygren
paper_title: Health-related quality of life and long-term symptoms among patients with non-severe covid-19 – a prospective cohort study

summary: A prospective cohort study of 102 COVID-19 patients assessing clinical and immunological features associated with persistence of post-COVID-19 syndrome at six months follow-up. The study identified that pro-inflammatory markers (IL-1α, IP-10, elevated CD57 expression in CD8+ T cells) and obesity were independently associated with symptom persistence.

paper_title: Novel clinical and immunological features associated with persistent post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 after six months of follow-up: a pilot study

summary: This retrospective cohort study compared cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2 max) measured via repeated cardiopulmonary exercise tests in 40 healthcare workers who had COVID-19 versus 87 controls over a mean interval of 762 days. COVID-19 survivors showed a statistically significant decline in VO2 max (3.12 mL/kg/min reduction) compared to controls, indicating that mild-to-moderate COVID-19 persistently reduces cardiorespiratory fitness even months after infection.
paper_authors: Ladislav Štěpánek; Marie Nakládalová; Eliška Sovová; Lubomír Štěpánek; Alena Boriková; Markéta Sovová; Katarína Moravcová; Jaromír Ožana; Libor Jelínek
paper_title: COVID-19 reduces cardiorespiratory fitness even months after a mild to moderate acute phase: a retrospective cohort study

summary: A 30-month nationwide French cohort study of 63,990 COVID-19 hospitalized patients matched to 319,891 controls, examining excess risks of death and organ-related hospitalizations. Findings show persistent increased risks for neurological, respiratory, and psychiatric disorders up to 30 months post-discharge, but this is an observational study with no treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Sarah Tubiana; Maryam Rontani; Philippe Herlemont; Rosemary Dray-Spira; Mahmoud Zureik; Alain Weill; Xavier Duval; Charles Burdet
paper_title: Long-term health outcomes following hospitalisation for COVID-19: a 30- month cohort analysis

summary: Prospective cohort study of 1,666 COVID-19 survivors hospitalized in Italy followed for 12 months to identify factors associated with persistent symptoms including fatigue, dyspnoea, insomnia, and mental confusion. Female sex and older age were independently associated with symptom persistence, while greater acute severity markers paradoxically predicted symptom improvement over time.

paper_title: Factors associated with persistent symptoms after COVID-19 infection: a longitudinal study on an Italian cohort of patients discharged from hospital

summary: This prospective/retrospective cohort study enrolled 223 long COVID patients (89 female, 134 male) to characterize sex-related differences in persistent symptoms at 5-month follow-up. Women were significantly more likely to report dyspnea, fatigue, chest pain, and palpitations, but the study does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Giovanna Pelà; Matteo Goldoni; Emila Solinas; Chiara Cavalli; Sara Tagliaferri; Silvia Ranzieri; Annalisa Frizzelli; Laura Marchi; Pier Anselmo Mori; Maria Majori; Marina Aiello; Massimo Corradi; Alfredo Chetta
paper_title: Sex-Related Differences in Long-COVID-19 Syndrome

summary: A retrospective cross-sectional study developing machine learning models to predict COVID-19 outcomes (hospitalization, ICU admission, long COVID) using viral sequencing and clinical data from 4,450 individuals. The study identifies risk factors and predictors but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Cynthia Y. Tang; Cheng Gao; Kritika Prasai; Tao Li; Shreya Dash; Jane A. McElroy; Jun Hang; Xiu-Feng Wan
paper_title: Prediction models for COVID-19 disease outcomes

summary: This observational study compared neurocognitive function and language performance in 47 COVID-19 survivors (12 weeks post-infection) versus 51 healthy controls, assessing associations with disease severity, BMI, and inflammatory markers. While the study documents significant cognitive deficits in long COVID patients, particularly in processing speed and memory, it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment or intervention—making it an observational assessment rather than a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Evgenia Panagea; Lambros Messinis; Panayiotis Patrikelis; Sonia Malefaki; Maria Christina Petri; Grigorios Nasios; Angelos Liontos; Dimitris Biros; Mary H. Kosmidis; Haralampos Milionis
paper_title: Persistent neuropsychological deficits in recovered COVID-19 patients: Correlations with disease biomarkers

summary: Retrospective analysis of 157 COVID-19 pneumonia patients evaluated at a Post-COVID clinic at 4 months follow-up, comparing pulmonary function and exercise capacity between males and females. Findings show women had more severe alveolar diffusion impairment and reduced exercise tolerance than men despite similar acute illness severity.
paper_authors: Lucia Spicuzza; Raffaele Campisi; Stefano Alia; Simone Prestifilippo; Maria Luisa Giuffrida; Lisa Angileri; Nicola Ciancio; Carlo Vancheri
paper_title: Female Sex Affects Respiratory Function and Exercise Ability in Patients Recovered from COVID-19 Pneumonia

summary: Prospective cohort study following 81 hospitalized COVID-19 patients over 12 months to track changes in pulmonary function, imaging, and patient-reported outcomes. Found pulmonary function improved between 3-6 months with plateauing thereafter, while 60% continued reporting abnormal quality of life at 12 months, but no intervention or treatment was tested.
paper_authors: Alyson W. Wong; Aditi S. Shah; Cameron J. Hague; James C. Johnston; Christopher J. Ryerson; Christopher Carlsten
paper_title: Natural history of COVID-19 recovery: Changes in physiologic, radiologic and patient-reported outcomes 12 months after symptom onset
paper_journal: Canadian Journal of Respiratory, Critical Care, and Sleep Medicine

summary: This retrospective cohort study using TriNetX data compared thyroid dysfunction risk in COVID-19 patients versus matched controls over 12 months. The study found a significant 2-fold increased risk of thyroid dysfunction (both thyrotoxicosis and hypothyroidism) in COVID-19 patients, with higher risk in older adults and females.
paper_authors: Li-An Huang; Shih-Chang Lo; Yi-Sun Yang; Chien-Ning Huang; Chi-Chih Wang; Yu-Hsun Wang; Edy Kornelius
paper_title: Association of COVID-19 Infection with Subsequent Thyroid Dysfunction: An International Population-Based Propensity Score Matched Analysis

summary: This cross-sectional study compared spleen size and T lymphocyte counts in 76 COVID-19 recovered patients versus 55 healthy controls. While it found reduced spleen size and decreased T lymphocytes in recovered patients, it addresses acute COVID-19 sequelae during the recovery phase, not persistent long COVID symptoms weeks-to-months post-infection, and does not study any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Lixia Xie; Yuanlan Lin; Yushu Deng; Bin Lei
paper_title: The Effect of SARS-CoV-2 on the Spleen and T Lymphocytes

summary: This observational cohort study examined whether daily emotional exertions (stress, worry, rumination) are associated with symptom severity in 376 UK Long COVID patients using intensive daily smartphone assessments. Results showed stress and worry are distinct factors linked to same-day and next-day symptom fluctuations, with implications for stress management in Long COVID self-care.

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed post-COVID-19 symptoms and functional capacity in 394 hospitalized and nonhospitalized survivors using tele-assessment methods at 1-6 months post-infection. The study found high prevalence of anxiety (47.7%), fatigue (46.7%), and muscle pain (45.7%), with significantly reduced functional capacity in the hospitalized group, highlighting the need for comprehensive multidisciplinary rehabilitation programs.
paper_authors: Gulhan Yilmaz Gokmen; Dilber Durmaz; Canan Demir; Fatma Nur Yilmaz
paper_title: Determining Post-COVID-19 Symptoms and Rehabilitation Needs in Hospitalized and Nonhospitalized COVID-19 Survivors with Tele-Assessment Methods

summary: Real-world analysis comparing post-COVID-19 condition risk in older patients (≥65 years) with influenza survivors using the TriNetX network. COVID-19 survivors showed significantly higher risk of multiple post-COVID conditions including abnormal breathing, fatigue, anxiety/depression, and cognitive symptoms, with age-related differences in cognitive symptom incidence.
paper_authors: Ting-Hui Liu; Po-Yu Huang; Jheng-Yan Wu; Min-Hsiang Chuang; Wan-Hsuan Hsu; Ya-Wen Tsai; Meng-Hsiu Tsai; Chih-Cheng Lai
paper_title: Real-world data analysis of post-COVID-19 condition risk in older patients

summary: This cross-sectional study examined associations between acute-phase bed rest duration and grip strength in 49 post-COVID-19 patients reporting ongoing symptoms and fatigue. Findings showed that each additional day of bed rest during acute illness was independently associated with lower grip strength (~150g per day), highlighting the importance of early mobilization during acute COVID-19.
paper_authors: Ann Monaghan; Glenn Jennings; Xue Feng; Silvin P. Knight; Rossella Rizzo; James Davis; Edel Duggan; Rose Anne Kenny; Román Romero‐Ortuño
paper_title: 123 ACUTE-PHASE BED-REST DURATION WAS ASSOCIATED WITH LOWER GRIP STRENGTH IN A POST-COVID-19 COHORT

summary: This retrospective cohort study follows 360 hospitalized COVID-19 patients for six months after discharge to assess longer-term outcomes including readmissions, mortality, and changes in residential status. While it documents significant post-discharge morbidity and mortality, it is an observational study without any treatment intervention and therefore does not meet criteria for inclusion in a treatment trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: Ellen Tullo; Catherine Dotchin; Somil Jaiswal
paper_title: 502 OUTCOMES OF HOSPITALISED PATIENTS WITH COVID-19 SIX MONTHS AFTER INDEX ADMISSION

summary: A prospective cohort study of 30 older Irish adults who received inpatient geriatric rehabilitation following acute COVID-19 infection, with follow-up assessment at six months post-discharge. Patients regained pre-admission functional ability but experienced persistent symptoms and reduced quality of life compared to baseline.
paper_authors: Aoife McCarthy; Katie Robinson; Frances Dockery; Kara McLoughlin; Margaret O'Connor; Antonella Milos; Gillian Corey; Leonora Carey; Fiona Steed; Miriam Haaksma; Aoife Whiston; Audrey Tierney; Rose Galvin
paper_title: Long-Term Outcomes of Older Adults in Ireland after Geriatric Rehabilitation for COVID-19: A Prospective Cohort Study

summary: Population-based cross-sectional analysis of 4,004 Europeans aged 50+ from the SHARE Corona Survey examining the prevalence of Long COVID and its association with multimorbidity and socioeconomic factors. Found 71.6% of COVID-19 survivors reported at least one Long COVID symptom, with significant cross-country variation and associations with education, employment, and age, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Piotr Wilk; Valerie Moran; Maria N. Pi Alperin; Torsten Bohn; Guy Fagherazzi; Maurice P. Zeegers; Maria Ruiz-Castell
paper_title: The role of multimorbidity and socio-economic characteristics as potential risk factors for Long Covid: evidence from the multilevel analysis of the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe’s corona surveys (2020–2021)

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining the incidence of long COVID symptoms 12-20 weeks post-diagnosis in a large US ambulatory care database of 916,894 COVID-19 patients. Identifies risk factors associated with long COVID development but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Robert Sedgley; Jessamine Winer-Jones; Machaon Bonafede
paper_title: Long COVID Incidence in a Large US Ambulatory Electronic Health Record System

summary: Retrospective cohort study using Oracle EHR data comparing thyroid disease risk (hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism) in 1.8M COVID-19 patients versus 3.7M matched controls from 2019-2024. COVID-19 was associated with significantly elevated risk of both conditions, with severity-dependent increases up to 9.87x for ECMO-dependent patients, and additional risk in long COVID-19 and reinfection cases.
paper_authors: Fares Qeadan; Benjamin Tingey; Jamie Egbert; Aisha Arshad; Trenton Honda
paper_title: SARS-CoV-2 and thyroid disease: a nationwide study on hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism using Oracle EHR Real-World Data

summary: Population-based cohort study comparing six-month post-COVID symptom risk between the first and second COVID-19 waves in France before vaccine rollout. Finds higher post-COVID risk during the first wave (14.6%) vs second wave (7.0%), with risk factors including baseline physical/mental conditions, female sex, and acute symptom severity.
paper_authors: Anne Pastorello; Laurence Meyer; Joël Coste; Camille Davisse-Paturet; Xavier de Lamballerie; Maria Melchior; Sophie Novelli; Delphine Rahib; Nathalie Bajos; Cécile Vuillermoz; Jeanna-Eve Franck; Carmelite Manto; Alexandra Rouquette; Josiane Warszawski
paper_title: Temporal changes in the risk of six-month post-COVID symptoms: a national population-based cohort study

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing risk of geriatric syndromes (cognitive impairment, depression, pressure injury) in older adults (65+) with and without COVID-19 using propensity score matching from US TriNetX data (2020-2022). The study found significantly elevated risk of multiple geriatric syndromes in COVID-19 survivors but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Chien-Chou Su; Yi-Ching Yang; Yu-Huai Yu; Yu-Hsuan Tsai; Deng-Chi Yang
paper_title: The risk of geriatric syndromes in older COVID-19 survivors among the nonvaccinated population: a real world retrospective cohort study

summary: Prospective longitudinal cohort study examining the association between pre-infection binge alcohol use and functional outcomes (mental and physical) among COVID-19-positive individuals measured at 3 and 6 months post-infection. Binge drinking showed statistically significant but clinically irrelevant associations with improved function at 3 months that were not sustained at 6 months.

paper_title: Association of binge alcohol use with functional outcomes among individuals with COVID-19 infection

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluated grip strength and associated factors among 93 post-COVID-19 older adults (mean age 73) recruited at an average of 55 days after hospital discharge. The study found that 74.2% had low grip strength, with age, hospital stay duration, and comorbidity burden as significant negative correlates, highlighting the need for rehabilitation monitoring in this population.
paper_authors: M H Tai; Safiyyah Nurnajah Wan; Julia Patrick Engkasan; T. Ong
paper_title: 1041 HAND GRIP STRENGTH AMONG POST-ACUTE COVID-19 OLDER ADULTS

summary: A cross-sectional study assessing cumulative neuropsychological deficits in 121 post-COVID patients using validated test batteries and Monte-Carlo simulation methods. Finds that moderate and severe COVID-19 cases show significantly greater long-term cognitive deficits (memory, executive function, perception, reasoning) compared to normative populations, while mild cases do not.
paper_authors: Voruz P.; Jacot de Alcântara I.; Nuber-Champier A.; Cionca A.; Allali G.; Benzakour L.; Lalive PH; Lövblad KO; Braillard O.; Nehme M.; Coen M.; Serratrice J.; Reny JL; Pugin J.; Guessous I.; Ptak R.; Landis BN; Assal F.; Péron JA
paper_title: Frequency of Abnormally Low Neuropsychological Scores in Post-COVID-19 Syndrome: the Geneva COVID-COG Cohort

summary: This study examined executive functioning and processing speed changes in 9 older adults with mild cognitive impairment who contracted COVID-19 between two assessment timepoints. Results showed significant decline in one cognitive measure post-infection, but the paper focuses on acute COVID-19 infection effects in MCI patients, not long COVID syndrome or treatment interventions.
paper_authors: Danna Torres; Sarah Langdon; Adriana Savettiere; Devon Delaney; J. Kaci Fairchild
paper_title: A - 105 Impact of COVID-19 on Executive Functioning and Processing Speed in Older Adults with Mild Cognitive Impairment

summary: Retrospective analysis of 205 long COVID patients using factorial analysis and hierarchical clustering to identify distinct clinical forms and patient clusters. Study identifies three clinical phenotypes (long, persistent, post-viral syndrome) associated with different pathophysiological mechanisms but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Pamela Mfouth Kemajou; Tatiana Besse-Hammer; Claire Lebouc; Yves Coppieters
paper_title: Cluster analysis identifies long COVID subtypes in Belgian patients

summary: This study examines cognitive performance validity test (PVT) failure rates in 323 long COVID patients receiving care at a specialized clinic, finding that failure on both PVTs was uncommon (6.3%) and unrelated to COVID severity or cognitive complaints. The paper characterizes patterns of validity test failure rather than evaluating a treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Phoebe A. Clark; Samantha Horn; Natalie Wang; Constantine G. Lyketsos; Ann M. Parker; Esther S. Oh; Tracy D. Vannorsdall
paper_title: Rates and Predictors of Performance Validity Test Failure in Adults Treated for Post-COVID-19 Condition: a Brief Report

summary: Prospective cohort study of acute COVID-19 inpatients (not long COVID patients) examining neurological symptoms and cerebral glucose metabolism in the subacute stage of active infection. Study focuses on acute COVID-19 pathophysiology, not persistent post-COVID syndrome or interventions for long COVID.
paper_authors: Jonas A. Hosp; Andrea Dressing; Ganna Blazhenets; Tobias Bormann; Alexander Rau; Marius Schwabenland; Johannes Thurow; Dirk Wagner; Cornelius Waller; Wolf D. Niesen; Lars Frings; Horst Urbach; Marco Prinz; Cornelius Weiller; Nils Schroeter; Philipp T. Meyer
paper_title: Cognitive impairment and altered cerebral glucose metabolism in the subacute stage of COVID-19

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining the risk of psoriatic arthritis and uveitis in patients with psoriasis after COVID-19 infection using propensity score matching. The study is not about long COVID treatment or management; instead, it investigates whether acute COVID-19 increases the risk of dermatological complications in psoriasis patients.
paper_authors: Tai-Li Chen; Chen-Yi Wu; Wei-Chuen Chang; Chih-Chiang Chen
paper_title: P076 Risk of psoriatic arthritis and uveitis among patients with psoriasis after COVID-19 infection: a nationwide cohort study

summary: This retrospective audit compares the incidence of chronic fungal sinusitis at a UK tertiary center before and after the COVID-19 pandemic (2018-2022). While it observes a higher post-pandemic incidence, the paper does not study long COVID specifically—it examines an opportunistic fungal infection that may have increased during the pandemic, not a persistent symptom or sequela of COVID-19 infection itself.
paper_authors: Arya Anthony Kamyab; William Ansley; Tiffany Munroe-Gray; Sarah Little; Dominic Jaikaransingh
paper_title: 219 Chronic Fungal Sinusitis: Pre and Post COVID-19, A single UK Tertiary Centre study

summary: Prospective cohort study examining humoral immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 and other coronaviruses in 112 infected individuals, comparing those who developed neuroPASC (n=18) versus those who did not (n=94). Finds that neuroPASC patients show attenuated anti-SARS-CoV-2 responses but expanded responses to other coronaviruses, suggesting immunologic imprinting as a pathogenic mechanism, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Marianna Spatola; Nadège Nziza; Wonyeong Jung; Yixiang Deng; Dansu Yuan; Alessandro Dinoto; Silvia Bozzetti; Vanessa Chiodega; Sergio Ferrari; Douglas A. Lauffenburger; Sara Mariotto; Galit Alter
paper_title: Neurologic sequelae of COVID-19 are determined by immunologic imprinting from previous coronaviruses

summary: This retrospective cohort study used electronic health records to compare cognitive outcomes in epilepsy patients taking phenytoin versus other anticonvulsants at the time of COVID-19 infection, testing whether phenytoin's receptor-interacting protein kinase inhibition could prevent post-COVID cognitive deficits. Patients on phenytoin had significantly lower risk of cognitive deficits in the 6 months post-infection compared to those on levetiracetam or valproate, suggesting potential protective effects of this drug class.
paper_authors: Maxime Taquet; Paul J. Harrison
paper_title: Exposure to phenytoin associates with a lower risk of post-COVID cognitive deficits: a cohort study

summary: This study compares white matter changes and cognitive function in 22 recovered COVID-19 patients at 1-year follow-up versus 21 healthy controls using advanced diffusion imaging techniques. While white matter abnormalities were detected in COVID-19 patients (particularly in those with ICU admission), no significant decline in cognitive function was found, and the paper does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Sihong Huang; Zhiguo Zhou; Danhui Yang; Wei Zhao; Mu Zeng; Xingzhi Xie; Yanyao Du; Yingjia Jiang; Xianglin Zhou; Wenhan Yang; Hu Guo; Hui Sun; Ping Liu; Jiyang Liu; Hong Luo; Jun Liu
paper_title: Persistent white matter changes in recovered COVID-19 patients at the 1-year follow-up

summary: This observational case-control study compared brain white matter microstructure in 16 long COVID patients versus 16 matched controls using advanced diffusion MRI techniques. The study found widespread white matter abnormalities in the patient group indicative of vasogenic edema, demyelination, and axonal damage, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Deneb Boito; Anders Eklund; Anders Tisell; Richard Levi; Evren Özarslan; Ida Blystad
paper_title: MRI with generalized diffusion encoding reveals damaged white matter in patients previously hospitalized for COVID-19 and with persisting symptoms at follow-up

summary: This study investigated limbic system damage and emotion recognition abilities in 105 long COVID patients at 6-9 months post-infection, stratified by acute respiratory severity. Moderate and severe patients showed impaired emotion recognition compared to mild cases, with findings linked to decreased episodic memory and anosmia rather than psychiatric symptoms.

paper_title: Markers of limbic system damage following SARS-CoV-2 infection

summary: Prospective cohort study measuring plasma biomarkers of nervous system injury (neurofilament light, GFAP, tau) in hospitalized COVID-19 survivors at 6 months and 1 year post-discharge. Found no robust associations between biomarkers and acute COVID-19 severity or post-acute neuropsychiatric symptoms, suggesting ongoing symptoms are not due to ongoing neural injury.

paper_title: Post-acute COVID-19 neuropsychiatric symptoms are not associated with ongoing nervous system injury

summary: International prospective cohort study of 6,862 hospitalized COVID-19 patients tracked for up to 12 months to assess post-acute neurological sequelae (PANSC) and sex differences in symptom resolution. Found that ~70% had multiple neurological symptoms at follow-up, with fatigue and myalgia most common; females experienced longer symptom resolution times than males, and ICU admission was associated with prolonged recovery.

While the study identifies elevated risk in hospitalized COVID-19 patients, it focuses on acute infection consequences rather than long COVID syndrome or any treatment interventions.

summary: Longitudinal observational study tracking brain imaging, clinical symptoms, and biomarkers in 51 post-COVID patients over 3 years compared to healthy controls. Study documents slow clinical improvement and brain recovery patterns with structural stabilization and increased connectivity, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

summary: This retrospective cohort study examined the association between COVID-19 infection and inflammatory dermatoses in 204,241 patients using electronic health records. The study found significantly elevated risks for several dermatological conditions (atopic dermatitis, acne, rosacea, alopecia areata, seborrheic dermatitis) following COVID-19 infection, but did not evaluate any treatment interventions.

paper_title: Risk of Inflammatory Dermatoses Following Covid-19 Infection: A cohort Study of 204,241 Patients

summary: This retrospective cohort study compared neurological manifestations of long COVID between patients with pre-vaccination and breakthrough SARS-CoV-2 infections, evaluating 1,300 Neuro-PASC patients at a neuro-COVID clinic. The study found that vaccination prior to infection does not significantly affect neurologic symptoms or cognitive outcomes, though breakthrough infection patients had higher comorbidity burden.

The study found persistent smell dysfunction in 60% of participants despite many self-reporting normal smell, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Found arrhythmias in 27% of participants, primarily ventricular premature contractions and non-sustained ventricular tachycardia, with associations to pre-existing cardiovascular disease and elevated cardiac troponin levels.
paper_authors: Charlotte Björk Ingul; Jostein Grimsmo; Albulena Mecinaj; Divna Trebinjac; Magnus Nossen; Simon Andrup; Knut Stavem; Tony Josefsen; Torbjørn Omland; Tomas Ø. Jensen
paper_title: Cardiac arrhythmias 3 months after hospitalization for COVID-19

summary: Prospective cohort study examining cardiac dysfunction in 50 patients with chronic heart failure following COVID-19 infection with lung involvement. Found worsening heart failure features including increased pulmonary artery pressure, ventricular dilation, valvular regurgitation, and left ventricular diastolic dysfunction one month post-infection.
paper_authors: E. Grigoricheva; G.R Gessen
paper_title: Features of chronic heart failure in COVID-19 pandemic

summary: This observational study evaluates cardiovascular sequelae in COVID-19 survivors with elevated biomarkers using advanced echocardiography. The study found minimal cardiac abnormalities in survivors without pre-existing cardiovascular disease and did not support routine screening programs post-discharge.
paper_authors: Eduard Ródenas‐Alesina; J Rodriguez-Palomares; M Oller-Bach; P Jordan; Carme Macià Badia; Lorena Herrador; Marina García-de-Acilu; Fernando Clau-Terré; Maribel González‐Del‐Hoyo; Rubén Fernández‐Galera; L Servato; Guillem Casas; Jordi Bañeras; Ignacio Ferreira‐González
paper_title: Routine advanced echocardiography in the evaluation of cardiovascular sequelae of COVID19 survivors with elevated cardiovascular biomarkers

summary: A prospective follow-up study assessing cardiopulmonary exercise capacity at 6 months post-hospitalization in 40 COVID-19 patients, comparing outcomes between those who received oxygen therapy versus those who did not. The study found no statistically significant differences in long-term cardiopulmonary limitations between groups, though 7.5% of patients showed asymptomatic cardiopulmonary limitations.
paper_authors: Roza Badr Eslam; Christina Binder; A Iscel; Josef Niebauer; Roya Anahita Mousavi; Christina Kronberger; Christoph Wenisch; Diana Bonderman
paper_title: Are there any long-term cardio-pulmonary limitations of hospitalized Covid-19 patients?

summary: Prospective observational cohort study evaluating cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) findings in 389 patients recovered from COVID-19, with 77% experiencing ongoing cardiovascular symptoms (long COVID). CMR findings of myopericardial inflammation, elevated native T1/T2, and pericardial changes were associated with long COVID status and symptom severity, but no differences in cardiac function were observed.
paper_authors: Valentina O. Püntmann; Simon S. Martin; Byambasuren Vanchin; Niels Ramsing Holm; Eleni Giokoglu; Jedrzej Hoffmann; Argyro Karyou; Christophe Arendt; Yascha Khodamoradi; Maria J. G. T. Vehreschild; Axel Braner; Gernot Rohde; Andreas M. Zeiher; Thomas J. Vogl; Eike Nagel
paper_title: Patterns of cardiac involvement in patients with long COVID syndrome using cardiovascular magnetic resonance

summary: This is an interim analysis of an ongoing prospective multicenter registry study examining long-term cardiopulmonary effects in 65 COVID-19 patients at 6 months post-discharge. The study documents persistent symptoms (fatigue 40%, dyspnea 36%) and imaging abnormalities (ground glass opacities 45%, cardiac MRI findings 11-19%) but reports no results yet, making it a protocol/interim analysis without complete trial data.
paper_authors: J H Niebauer; C Binder- Rodriguez; A Iscel; S Klenk; R Badr-Eslam; S Cadjo; M Kahr; S Hoffman; S Reiter-Malqvist; Robin N. Boeck; Christoph Wenisch; C Krestan; Michael Lichtenauer; Diana Bonderman
paper_title: Long-term cardiopulmonary effects after Covid-19 infection

summary: Cross-sectional observational study measuring endothelial dysfunction, coagulation markers, and inflammatory cytokines in 203 patients 3 months after COVID-19 infection compared to historical controls. Found sustained thrombo-inflammation (elevated ET-1, vWF:Ag, proinflammatory cytokines) but no macrovascular dysfunction.

paper_title: Sustained endothelial, coagulation and inflammatory cytokine activation without macrovascular dysfunction at 3 months after COVID-19: a reflection on SARS-CoV-2 induced thrombo-inflammation

summary: Prospective observational cohort study of 105 COVID-19 patients (63.5% with postcovid syndrome) evaluated ~107 days post-infection using cardiac imaging (echocardiography, ECG monitoring) and blood markers. Study found cardiac impairment is rare despite high symptom burden, with only 4 patients requiring cardiac intervention and no evidence of ventricular dysfunction.

paper_title: Echocardiography and ECG monitoring not very beneficial in COVID-19 follow-up even in long haulers

summary: This study examines inflammatory markers and cardiac function in 63 patients (26 without CVD, 37 with CVD) at 3 months after COVID-19-associated pneumonia. It is a passive observational follow-up study without any intervention, measuring associations between inflammation biomarkers and ventricular systolic function rather than testing a treatment.
paper_authors: N. Musikhina; T. Petelina; E. Yaroslavskaya; D. Krinochkin; N. Shirokov; N. Osokina; E. Gorbatenko
paper_title: Laboratory indicators of inflammation and systolic function of the left and right ventricles in patients with cardiovascular disease who have undergone COVID-19-associated pneumonia

summary: This study follows COVID-19 reconvalescents at 2-5 months post-discharge to assess coagulation abnormalities and endothelial function. The findings show suppressed clot formation but enhanced fibrinolysis compared to controls, with no thrombotic complications observed.
paper_authors: Galina Artemyeva; Anna Kalinskaya; Oleg Dukhin; А. И. Лебедева; Aviram Rozin; A. Shpektor; Elena Vasilieva
paper_title: Long-term post-discharge coagulation abnormalities in patients with moderate to severe COVID-19

summary: Prospective analysis comparing inflammatory, endothelial, and hemostasis parameters in COVID-19 pneumonia patients with and without type 2 diabetes, assessed at baseline and 3 months post-hospitalization. Found elevated inflammatory markers (CRP, homocysteine) and thrombophilia indicators at 3 months, particularly in diabetic patients, suggesting increased risk of adverse cardiovascular events during the post-COVID recovery period.

paper_title: Prospective analysis of inflammatory response markers, endothelial dysfunction and hemostasis parameters in COVID-19 associated pneumonia patients with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines the risk of incident diabetes in long COVID patients using Veterans Health Administration data, comparing 181,280 COVID-19 survivors with contemporary and historical controls. The study found a 40% increased risk of new-onset diabetes and 85% increased risk of antihyperglycemic medication use in COVID-19 patients at 12 months follow-up.
paper_authors: Francesco Paneni; Carlo Patrono
paper_title: Increased risk of incident diabetes in patients with long COVID

summary: This study develops a prognostic score (HOPE-2) for predicting long-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in 2,575 COVID-19 patients using multivariable regression analysis on retrospective registry data. The score stratifies patients into low, intermediate, and high-risk groups based on clinical factors, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

paper_title: Long-term mayor adverse cardiovascular events after COVID-19 infection: a clinical score from a cohort of 2575 patients enrolled in the multicenter international HOPE 2 registry

summary: Prospective cohort study of 70 COVID-19 survivors (41 with persistent dyspnea, 29 asymptomatic) evaluated at 3 months post-hospitalization using cardiopulmonary exercise testing, imaging, and functional assessments. Symptomatic patients showed reduced peak oxygen consumption and potential ventilatory inefficiency compared to asymptomatic patients, with >50% of survivors experiencing functional impairment regardless of hospitalization history.

paper_title: Post-COVID-19 syndrome: prospective evaluation of clinical and functional outcomes

summary: This study evaluates atrio-ventricular mechanics using speckle-tracking echocardiography in 157 children 4-5 months after asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection, compared to 107 healthy controls. Results show subtle subclinical left ventricular systolic dysfunction in 60% of post-COVID children despite normal ejection fraction, with worse impairment in those infected during the second pandemic wave.

paper_title: Mid- and long-term atrio-ventricular mechanics in children after recovery from asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection

summary: Prospective longitudinal study investigating cardiac impairment in 534 long COVID patients using cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging at baseline and 12-month follow-up. Found that 19% had cardiac impairment at baseline, persisting in 58% of those with paired 12-month data, but this is a natural history/observational study with no intervention.

paper_title: Cardiac impairment in Long Covid 1-year post SARS-CoV-2 infection

summary: Prospective observational study of 488 non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients without comorbidities followed for 3 months to identify predictors of long COVID. Found that severe acute COVID course, higher BMI, and arthralgia during acute phase were independent risk factors for developing long COVID symptoms.
paper_authors: Michał Chudzik; Maciej Banach; Joanna Lewek; Joanna Kapusta; Agata Bielecka‐Dąbrowa; Piotr Jankowski
paper_title: Independent predictors of long-COVID in patients without comorbidities. Data from the Polish long-COVID cardiovascular (PoLoCOV-CVD) study

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing right ventricular function via echocardiography in 263 CKD patients, with 168 post-COVID-19 and 95 controls, measured at mean 2.2 months post-infection. Found statistically significant differences in TAPSE, Tei index, and RVFWLS between groups, suggesting cardiovascular sequelae in CKD populations post-infection.
paper_authors: L Tapoi; C Ureche; A Diaconu; Vlad Vasiliu; Lucian Sirițeanu; T. Andrian; Anca-Elena Stefan; Cezar Valeriu Băluţă; Mugurel Apetrii; Gianina Dodi; Ionuţ Nistor; Mihai Onofriescu; R Sascau; C Statescu; Adrian Covic
paper_title: The impact of COVID-19 on right ventricular function in chronic kidney disease patients

summary: A prospective observational study of 158 COVID-19 survivors assessed at 3 months post-infection using cardiac imaging (ECG, echocardiography) and pulmonary function tests. Found no significant differences in cardiac or left/right ventricular function parameters across disease severity groups, arguing against significant cardiac sequelae.
paper_authors: Phyoe Kyaw Pyae; Alessio Navarra; R Webb; A Newland-Smith; Rama Vancheeswaran; Joban Sehmi; Andrew Barlow
paper_title: Three-month cardiac outcomes of survivors of COVID-19 presenting to a district general hospital in West Hertfordshire, UK

summary: Multicenter retrospective registry comparing cardiovascular outcomes in 3,578 COVID-19 patients vs. 849 controls at 1-year follow-up across 17 Spanish and Italian centers. Found no increased CV death but higher rates of VTE, major bleeding, and cardiac arrhythmias in COVID-19 patients.
paper_authors: V Arevalos Rivas; Luis Ortega‐Paz; Diego Fernández-Rodríguez; Víctor Alfonso Jiménez Díaz; J Baneras Rius; Gianluca Campo; José Francisco Díaz Fernández; Claudia Scardino; Miguel Rodríguez-Santamarta; Nieves Gonzalo; A Perginotti; F Alfonso; Ignacio J. Amat‐Santos; Manel Sabaté; Salvatore Brugaletta
paper_title: Long-term effects of coronavirus disease 2019 on the cardiovascular system: the CV COVID-19 registry

summary: This study investigates cardiac and vascular abnormalities in 25 COVID-19 patients at 1 and 6 months post-hospitalization, measuring ventricular-arterial coupling (VAC), arterial stiffness, and left ventricular function. Results show significant impairment in post-COVID patients compared to controls at both timepoints, with correlations between VAC and inflammatory markers (IL-6, CRP).
paper_authors: Stamatios Lampsas; Eleni Oikonomou; Nektarios Souvaliotis; Artemis Anastasiou; Ουρανία Κατσαρού; Anastasios Marathonitis; Antonios Lysandrou; Ioanna Tzima; Savvas Sarantos; Kostas Kalogeras; Aikaterini Tsatsaragkou; Vasiliki-Chara Mystakidi; Gerasimos Siasos; Dimitris Tousoulis; Manolis Vavuranakis

summary: This study evaluated 246 post-COVID patients using a stepwise cardiac diagnostic sequence to determine the prevalence of de novo cardiological alterations at least 30 days after discharge. While 25% had cardiac findings, only 6.5% were clinically relevant and the paper focuses on diagnostic prevalence rather than testing any intervention or treatment.
