paper_title: Pragmatic observations from a post-COVID-19 cardiac evaluation register: prevalence of cardiological alterations from a basic diagnostic sequence and contribution of the clinical hystory

summary: This case-control study compared coronary microvascular function between patients with prior COVID-19 infection and matched controls without prior infection using PET imaging. The study found higher rates of coronary microvascular dysfunction in post-COVID patients, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: A I Ahmed; Jean Michel Saad; Yushui Han; Fares Alahdab; Maan Malahfji; Faisal Nabi; John J. Mahmarian; John P. Cooke; William A. Zoghbi; Mouaz H. Al‐Mallah
paper_title: Coronary microvascular health in patients with prior COVID-19 infection and no known CAD

summary: A prospective cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of cardiac dysrhythmias in 87 long COVID patients using echocardiography and Holter monitoring. Found that 90.8% had normal sinus rhythm, but 80.5% had atrial premature beats and 57.5% had ventricular premature beats, with 8% presenting sustained atrial dysrhythmias.
paper_authors: David Shamia; Gal Tsaban; L Baham; Yael Raviv; Moti Haim
paper_title: Cardiac dysrhythmias among coronavirus-19 recovered symptomatic patients

summary: A prospective cohort study of 140 COVID-19 survivors at one-year follow-up examining cardiac dysfunction in long COVID patients using myocardial work parameters (GWI and GCW) on echocardiography. The study found that reduced myocardial work indices were independently associated with long COVID diagnosis, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: M L Luchian; A Motoc; B Roosens; Julien Magné; Karen Van den Bussche; H Chameleva; Tom De Potter; L Houard; S Droogmans; B Cosyns
paper_title: The impact of long COVID on myocardial work performance

summary: Prospective multicenter registry study following 150 COVID-19 hospitalized patients (~6 months post-discharge) with comprehensive cardiopulmonary assessments including echocardiography, cardiac MRI, CT imaging, and lung function tests. Found 75% met long COVID criteria with persistent symptoms, identified cardiac (reduced GLS, pericardial effusion, myocarditis) and pulmonary abnormalities (ground glass opacities, fibrosis), and determined independent predictors of long COVID including disease severity markers and elevated biomarkers.
paper_authors: J. Niebauer; C. Binder; A. Iscel; S. Klenk; C. Capelle; M. Kahr; S. Cadjo; M. Lichtenauer; A. Toma; A. Zoufaly; S. Hoffman; S. Charwat-Resl; C. Krestan; C. Wenisch; D. Bonderman
paper_title: Cardiopulmonary long-term effects in patients after hospitalization due to COVID-19 infection

summary: Prospective follow-up study of 34 COVID-19 hospitalized patients examining heart rate variability (HRV) at 1 and 6 months post-discharge compared to age/sex-matched controls. Found reduced SDNN (autonomic dysfunction marker) in COVID-19 group with partial recovery at 6 months, and lower SDNN values in patients with long COVID symptoms, suggesting a link between autonomic dysfunction and long COVID.
paper_authors: Stamatios Lampsas; Evangelos Oikonomou; Nektarios Souvaliotis; Athina Goliopoulou; George-Angelo Papamikroulis; Artemis Anastasiou; Panagiotis Theofilis; George Ε. paper_title: Impaired heart rate variability one and six months post acute COVID-19

summary: Prospective observational study comparing acute coronary syndrome presentation and outcomes in patients with prior COVID-19 infection versus uninfected and vaccinated patients. Finds that prior COVID-19 infection is associated with higher rates of coronary ectasia, thrombosis, and thrombectomy requirement, but does not study treatment of long COVID.
paper_authors: B To-Dang; Mark Zuckerman; Stefano Cannata; Roman Roy; Richard Dalton; Antonio Cannatà; I Webb; Narbeh Melikian; Jonathan Byrne; Philip MacCarthy; Ajay M. Shah; Rafał Dworakowski; Nilesh Pareek
paper_title: Prior COVID-19 infection is associated with persistent and higher thrombus burden in acute coronary syndromes

summary: This single-centre retrospective cohort study examined 169 COVID-19 patients to determine whether late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac MRI predicts long-term outcomes including mortality and cardiovascular events. The study found no significant association between the presence of myocardial scarring and adverse outcomes over 2-3 years of follow-up, suggesting larger multicentre studies are needed.
paper_authors: Kavitha Vimalesvaran; JP Howard; S Zaman; Ben Ariff; Anil A. Bharath; Graham Cole
paper_title: Late gadolinium enhancement following Covid-19 infection does not predict outcome: a single-centre study

summary: Prospective observational study comparing viral IgG/IgM titers (EBV, CMV, HSV, VZV, Parvo-B19) in 105 long COVID patients versus 105 healthy controls. Found significantly elevated EBV IgG and Parvo-B19 IgM in long COVID patients, suggesting viral reactivation linked to symptom domains (EBV with respiratory, Parvo-B19 with cardiovascular), but no intervention or treatment was administered.
paper_authors: Mariann Gyöngyösi; Ena Hašimbegović; Dominika Lukovic; Katrin Zlabinger; Andreas Spannbauer; E Samaha; Jutta Bergler‐Klein; Christian Hengstenberg; Patrick Mucher; Helmuth Haslacher; Monika Breuer; Robert Straßl; Martin Riesenhuber; Christoph Nitsche; Thomas A. Zelniker
paper_title: Sequential activation of DNA viruses by the RNA virus SARS-CoV-2 in patients with long COVID syndrome

summary: A case-control study comparing 1,195 female long-COVID patients with 718 controls to identify age-independent predictors of long-COVID occurrence. Found that HDL cholesterol and 24-hour pulse pressure are independent predictors in younger women, while cardiovascular abnormalities and severe acute COVID-19 course are associated with long-COVID in all females.
paper_authors: Michał Chudzik; Joanna Kapusta; Agata Sakowicz; Maciej Banach; Piotr Jankowski; Mateusz Babicki; Agata Bielecka‐Dąbrowa
paper_title: Age-independent predictors of Long-COVID in females. Data from the Polish Long-COVID Cardiovascular (PoLoCOV-CVD) Study

summary: A prospective cohort study of 252 post-COVID-19 patients followed for up to 428 days examining associations between socioeconomic deprivation and illness trajectory using imaging, biomarkers, and patient-reported outcomes. Greater deprivation was associated with worse health status, more lung/cardiac/renal imaging abnormalities, higher anxiety/depression, and more secondary care referrals.
paper_authors: Andrew Morrow; R.A. Sykes; Kenneth Mangion; Colin Berry
paper_title: Socioeconomic status and post-covid illness trajectory

summary: Population-based Swedish cohort study examining long-term venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk after COVID-19 in hospitalized and non-hospitalized patients. Hospitalized COVID-19 patients retained elevated PE and DVT risk for >180 days post-infection, while non-hospitalized individuals had similar risk to unexposed controls.
paper_authors: Helén Sjöland; Martin Lindgren; Triantafyllia Toska; Per‐Olof Hansson; Katarina Glise Sandblad; Lena Björck; C. Lundberg; Martin Adiels; Annika Rosengren
paper_title: Long-term risk of pulmonary embolism and deep venous thrombosis after COVID-19: a population-based cohort study

summary: Prospective registry study following 200 severe COVID-19 patients at 6 and 18 months post-discharge to assess cardiopulmonary impairment through clinical examination, imaging, and functional testing. Study is excluded because it does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment—it is a passive observational follow-up study documenting natural recovery patterns without assigning patients to treatment groups.
paper_authors: J H Niebauer; A Iscel; Sarah Schedl; C Capelle; M Kahr; Simon Schamilow; R Badr-Eslam; Michael Lichtenauer; A Zoufaly; Rudolf Valenta; S Charwat-Resl; C Krestan; Wolfgang Hitzl; C Wenisch; D Bonderman
paper_title: Cardiopulmonary long-term impairment in patients 6 and 18 months post severe Covid-19 infection

summary: This observational study compares long COVID symptom prevalence and cardiovascular complications between healthy women and men without comorbidities at 12 weeks and one year post-COVID. It finds women more frequently reported long COVID symptoms (63% vs 59%) and specific symptoms like fatigue and hair loss, while men showed more ECG abnormalities.
paper_authors: Agata Bielecka‐Dąbrowa; Agata Sakowicz; Joanna Kapusta; Maciej Banach; Piotr Jankowski; Michał Chudzik
paper_title: The effect of the gender on the risk of long-covid and cardiovascular complications in healthy patients without comorbidities- data from the polish long-COVID cardiovascular (PoLoCOV-CVD) study

summary: Longitudinal observational study assessing the prevalence of cardiovascular symptoms in 643 patients at 3 and 12 months following COVID-19 infection. Found that 65.7% had at least one post-COVID symptom at 12 months, with cardiovascular symptoms present in 60.1% at 3 months and 33.9% at 12 months; female sex and severe infection were predictive of persistent symptoms.

paper_title: The prevalence and assessment of cardiovascular symptoms as the risk factors for post-COVID syndrome at 12-month follow-up. Data from the Polish Long-COVID Cardiovascular (PoLoCOV-CVD) Study

summary: This retro-prospective study evaluated 793 long COVID patients to assess the incidence of postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) and other autonomic dysfunction symptoms, finding a 1.5% incidence of autonomic dysfunction and 0.1% incidence of POTS. The study identified elevated C-reactive protein as an associated factor and fatigue and orthostatic intolerance as the most common symptoms.

paper_title: Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) and other autonomic dysfunction following COVID-19 infection: incidence, characteristic and associating factors

summary: A prospective cohort study following 1,474 COVID-19 hospitalized patients across 16 countries at 3 months post-discharge to assess persistent long COVID symptoms, cardiovascular complications, and mortality. The study found 38% reported long COVID symptoms (primarily fatigue, cognitive impairment, and anxiety) and a 3% mortality rate, mostly from cardiac arrest and other severe complications.

paper_title: Mortality, cardiovascular disease and long covid at 3 months in individuals hospitalized with covid-19- a whf study

summary: Prospective cohort study following 2,504 COVID-19 hospitalized patients from 16 countries at 1, 3, 6, and 9-12 months post-discharge to assess long-term sequelae and burden of disease. Found persistent symptoms in 63% at 1 month declining to 28% at 9-12 months, with 12% mortality by one year primarily due to cardiovascular events, highlighting significant post-COVID complications requiring preventive strategies.

paper_title: Substantial morbidity and mortality due to cardiovascular diseases in hospitalized vaccinated and un-vaccinated patients with COVID-19 from 16 countries: the WHF COVID-19 Long-term study

summary: This prospective registry study followed 200 patients hospitalized for severe COVID-19 at 6, 18, and 30 months post-discharge to assess cardiopulmonary long-term effects and symptom burden. While long COVID prevalence decreased over time (73% at 6 months to 49% at 30 months), structural and functional abnormalities persisted, though at lower rates than reported symptoms.
paper_authors: J H Niebauer; A Iscel; Sarah Schedl; S Charwat-Resl; C Capelle; Maike Kahr; Simon Schamilow; Marc Srdits; John Faltas; Michael Lichtenauer; Alexander Zoufaly; Rudolf Valenta; Christian Krestan; Christoph Wenisch; D Bonderman
paper_title: Cardiopulmonary long-term effects 6, 18 and 30 months after severe COVID-19 infection

summary: This 2-year retrospective cohort study of 17 million individuals in England examines the association between COVID-19/influenza vaccinations, cardiovascular drugs, and hospitalisation/mortality outcomes in both COVID-19 and Long COVID populations. The study finds that COVID-19 vaccination (≥2 doses), influenza vaccination, and cardiovascular preventive therapies (particularly anticoagulants) significantly reduce mortality and hospitalisation risk, with greatest benefits in those with prior cardiovascular disease.

paper_title: Association of COVID-19 and influenza vaccinations and cardiovascular drugs with hospitalisation and mortality in COVID-19 and Long COVID: 2-year follow-up of 17 million individuals in England

summary: This study evaluates pericoronary adipose tissue attenuation as a marker of vascular inflammation in post-COVID patients using ultra-high-resolution CT imaging. The abstract indicates this is a study protocol describing enrollment and methods, with results presented only as baseline data and preliminary findings.
paper_authors: B Romanelli Scarpa Matuck; A. Ostovaneh; M Matheson; Thierry Thomas; Jason Ortman; C V Serrano Jr; Armin Arbab‐Zadeh; J A C Lima
paper_title: Pericoronary adipose tissue attenuation assessed by ultra-high-resolution CT post COVID-19

summary: Prospective observational follow-up study comparing long COVID symptoms and cardiovascular outcomes between vaccinated and unvaccinated COVID-19 hospitalized patients across 16 countries at 1, 3, 6, and 9-12 months post-discharge. Study found unvaccinated patients had higher rates of long COVID symptoms (fatigue, palpitations, anxiety), MACE, and mortality, but does not test a specific intervention—it passively compares outcomes by pre-existing vaccination status.
paper_authors: Kalpana Singh; Dorairaj Prabhakaran; Kalyani Nikhare; Lana Raspail; Arghya Banerjee; Jagat Narula; Daniel Piñeiro; Pablo Perel; K Sliwa Hahnle
paper_title: Vaccination status and long COVID symptoms among patients hospitalized with COVID-19: the WHF COVID-19 Long-term Study

summary: This cross-sectional study examines myocardial injury in young adults (ages 18-44) 2-6 months after COVID-19 recovery using cardiac MRI and inflammatory biomarkers, comparing them to two control groups. One-third of COVID-19 patients with cardiovascular risk factors showed myocardial damage (interstitial edema and/or fibrosis), with correlations found between biomarkers and imaging findings.
paper_authors: K. Abdulalimova
paper_title: Prognostic role of advanced cardiac imaging in assessing myocardial injury and its correlation with biomarkers in young patients recovering from COVID 19

summary: This prospective multicentric cohort study investigates accelerated vascular ageing in COVID-19 survivors across 2,390 participants in 16 countries, measuring carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity as a biomarker of large artery stiffness. The study finds that COVID-19 survivors, particularly women with persistent symptoms, show significantly higher PWV indicating early vascular ageing compared to controls, though PWV stabilizes or improves at 12-month follow-up.

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 863 ICU COVID-19 survivors followed for median 4.1 years to identify predictors of long-term mortality. Study found age, dementia, and COPD were significant mortality predictors, but myocardial injury and classical cardiovascular risk factors were not.

summary: Observational study comparing coronary ectasia prevalence in acute coronary syndrome patients before (2017-2019) and after (2020-2023) COVID-19 pandemic, finding increased ectasia rates post-pandemic (62% vs 12%). Study documents a post-COVID cardiovascular complication but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: J. Cecily Mary Majella; A. Anteena Stefanie; A. Anteena Stefanie
paper_title: Ectatic coronary arteries - increasing trends post covid 19 infection

summary: A prospective longitudinal study examining long-term cardiovascular consequences of COVID-19 using cardiac MRI and exercise testing in 138 individuals 3+ years post-infection. The study identifies native T1 as an independent predictor of reduced aerobic capacity (VO2max) in post-COVID patients, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

summary: This cross-sectional study examines how pre-existing cardiovascular disease (CVD) affects symptoms, quality of life, and functional outcomes in 668 long COVID (PASC) patients in Australia. The study finds that while prior CVD does not worsen PASC symptoms or functional capacity, it is associated with elevated blood pressure and cardiac troponin levels, and significantly impairs quality of life in long COVID patients.
paper_authors: J. Smith; T. H. Marwick
paper_title: Pre-existing cardiovascular disease does not augment the post-acute sequalae of SARS-CoV-2

summary: This cross-sectional study characterizes and compares clinical and hemodynamic profiles among 270 long COVID patients diagnosed with POTS, IST, or dual pathology using tilt testing and ECG monitoring. The findings show distinct phenotypes with different clinical presentations, particularly highlighting that IST patients have higher hypertension and resting blood pressure, while POTS and dual pathology patients experience more presyncope/syncope and cognitive impairment.

paper_title: Post-COVID postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome and inappropriate sinus tachycardia: prevalence, overlap and clinical characteristics

summary: This observational cohort study assessed long-term cardiac arrhythmias in 63 patients 6 months after severe COVID-19 infection using 24-h Holter monitoring. The study identified new diagnoses of atrial fibrillation in 4.8% of patients, asymptomatic bradycardia in 18%, and moderate-to-severe sleep apnea in 53%, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

summary: A prospective multicentre cohort study of 155 post-COVID-19 patients undergoing serial assessments with plasma proteomics and multisystem imaging to identify dysregulation of catecholamine pathways. The study identified a distinct proteomic cluster characterized by heightened catecholamine activity and oxidative stress, associated with heightened illness perception and reduced cardiorespiratory function despite absence of objective imaging abnormalities.

summary: This study evaluated cardiac involvement in patients recovered from COVID-19 using echocardiography, comparing 41 COVID-19 patients (15 hospitalized, 26 home-treated) with 13 healthy volunteers at median 5.9 months post-infection. paper_title: 761 Echocardiographic evaluation in patients recovered from COVID-19

summary: This prospective follow-up study assessed functional capacity using cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) in 198 COVID-19 survivors at 3 months post-discharge. paper_title: 782 Cardiopulmonary exercise testing in patients with COVID-19 at 3 months from hospital discharge

summary: A prospective/retrospective cohort study of 160 COVID-19 patients followed for a median of 5 months post-infection, examining cardiac structural and functional changes using echocardiography and imaging. Females reported significantly higher rates of dyspnoea, fatigue, chest pain, and palpitations compared to males, suggesting sex as an important determinant of persistent symptoms.

paper_title: P307 POST–COVID–19 SYNDROME: CAN IT BE CAUSED BY MYOCARDIAL INVOLVEMENT?

summary: Longitudinal cohort study of 5,181 Belgian COVID-19 patients followed for 3 months to assess the prevalence, symptom patterns, and risk factors of post-COVID-19 condition. Found that 49.6% reported PCC with fatigue, headache, and memory problems most common; identified female sex, lower education, obesity, chronic disease, and hospitalization as significant risk factors.
paper_authors: Smith P.
paper_title: Classification and risk factors of Post COVID-19 condition: a longitudinal study in the Belgian population

summary: Prospective cohort study of 1,029 COVID-19 patients followed at 1 and 3 months post-diagnosis to characterize persistent symptoms. Found that 27.6% reported at least one persistent symptom by 3 months, with muscle aches, shortness of breath, and fatigue being most common; persistent symptoms were more prevalent in women, older patients, and those with comorbidities.
paper_authors: Başoğlu Şensoy, Ecem; EMECEN, AHMET NACİ; KESKİN, SALİH; Süner, Ahmet Furkan; TURUNÇ, ÖYKÜ; ÜNAL, BELGİN; ŞİYVE, NESLİŞAH
paper_title: Persistent symptoms after three months follow-up of in and out-patient COVID-19 cases

summary: Prospective cohort study following 5,083 SARS-CoV-2 positive patients for 6 months to characterize post-COVID conditions and identify risk factors. Found 21.8% prevalence of post-COVID with fatigue, myalgia, and dyspnea as most common symptoms; older age, female gender, poor economic status, comorbidities, and ICU admission were significant risk factors.
paper_authors: AN Emecen; Ö Turunç; N Sivye; AF Süner; Ecem BAŞOĞLU ŞENSOY; Salih Keskin; Barış Ünal
paper_title: Characterizing post-covid conditions in a Turkish cohort: A prospective study

summary: This Dutch longitudinal cohort study (N=76,503) identified four distinct symptom profiles of post-COVID-19 condition (muscle pain, fatigue, cardiorespiratory, ageusia/anosmia) and characterized their shared and unique risk factors including sex, weight status, chronic disease, and vaccination status. The study provides epidemiological characterization of long COVID subtypes but does not test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Ballering, Aranka V; Boulogne, Floranne; Brouwer, Sandra; Claringbould, Annique; Deelen, Patrick; Dekens, Jackie; Dijkema, Marjolein X L; Jankipersadsing, Soesma A; Lanting, Pauline; Lifelines Corona Research Initiative; Lude Franke, H; Marike Boezen, H; Mierau, Jochen O; Nolte, Ilja; Ori, Anil P S; Rosmalen, Judith G M; Rosmalen, Judith G M; Vonk, Judith M; Warmerdam, Robert; Wiersma, Henry H; Wijmenga, Cisca; De Bock, Geertruida H; Van Blokland, Irene; Van Zon, Sander K R
paper_title: Symptom profiles and their risk factors in patients with post-COVID-19 condition: a Dutch longitudinal cohort study

summary: Longitudinal analysis of 47,964 Europeans aged 50+ examining how the COVID-19 pandemic impacted well-being across 2020-2021, with 73% of infected respondents reporting persistent Long COVID symptoms. The study found that individuals with COVID-19 and Long COVID experienced significantly larger declines in well-being than unaffected individuals, but does not test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Piotr Wilk; Sarah Cuschieri
paper_title: Effect of the COVID-19 Pandemic on the Well-Being of Middle-Aged and Older Adults from 27 European Countries: Evidence from a Longitudinal Analysis of Population-Based Surveys

summary: Prospective cohort study following 5,446 COVID-19 patients for 6 months to assess prevalence and predictors of self-reported anxiety and depression using the EQ-5D-3L scale. Found anxiety/depression decreased from 18.5% at 1 month to 15.4% at 6 months, with associations to female gender, economic status, disease severity, and ICU admission.
paper_authors: Neslişah Şiyve; AN Emecen; Salih Keskin; Ecem BAŞOĞLU ŞENSOY; Ö Turunç; AF Süner; Can Cimilli; Belgin Ünal
paper_title: Self-reported anxiety and depression among COVID-19 patients: A prospective cohort study from Turkey

summary: Population-based German cohort study comparing health outcomes in 350 SARS-CoV-2 infected and 4467 non-infected adults at >1 year follow-up. Found infected individuals had significantly higher rates of persistent health complaints (fatigue, dyspnea, smell/taste disorders) and incident diseases, but no intervention was tested or evaluated.
paper_authors: Christin Heidemann; Giselle Sarganas; Yong Du; Beate Gaertner; Christina Poethko‐Müller; Caroline Cohrdes; Sein Schmidt; Martin Schlaud; Christa Scheidt‐Nave
paper_title: Long-term health consequences in persons with and without SARS-CoV-2 infection in Germany

summary: A longitudinal online survey following 1,153 long COVID patients from November 2020 to November 2021, characterizing symptom patterns and identifying common triggers for symptom exacerbation. Findings show 95% of participants had not fully recovered, with 45% reporting constant illness patterns and common triggers including physical activity (44%), stress (40%), cognitive effort (27%), and social effort (25%).
paper_authors: Nida Ziauddeen; Marija Pantelic; Margaret O’Hara; Claire E. Hastie; Nisreen A Alwan
paper_title: Symptom patterns and triggers of Long Covid: findings from a longitudinal online survey

summary: A matched cohort study using German healthcare data comparing incidence of post-COVID-19 condition diagnoses in COVID-19 patients versus matched controls over one year. The study found serious diagnoses like chronic fatigue syndrome and cognitive impairment persisted longer in the COVID-19 group, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Falko Tesch; Danny Wende; Friedrich Loser; Annika Vivirito; Simone Menzer; Manuel Batram; Tilo Buschmann; Giselle Sarganas; Christa Scheidt‐Nave; Jochen Schmitt
paper_title: Incidence and persistence of post-COVID-19 condition in adults– a matched cohort study in Germany

summary: This matched cohort study used German healthcare insurance data to compare long COVID incidence and persistence in children/adolescents with COVID-19 versus matched controls through 2021. About 40% more COVID-infected individuals had post-COVID diagnoses at 3 months, with most resolving within 12 months, though a notable minority persisted longer in younger children.
paper_authors: Franz Ehm; Danny Wende; Friedrich Loser; Annika Vivirito; Simone Menzer; Manuel Batram; Tilo Buschmann; Giselle Sarganas; Christa Scheidt‐Nave; Jochen Schmitt
paper_title: Incidence and persistence of post-COVID condition in children – a matched cohort study in Germany

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 1,378 workers exposed to biohazards assessed post-COVID syndrome prevalence and symptoms in workers who developed COVID-19, with 70% (115/164) reporting persistent symptoms one month after infection. The study describes symptom patterns, comorbidity burden, sleep quality, fatigue, anxiety, and work ability impairment at follow-up but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Nicola Magnavita; Gabriele Arnesano; Reparata Rosa Di Prinzio; Igor Meraglia; Marco Merella; Maria Eugenia Vacca
paper_title: Post-Covid syndrome in the workplace

summary: This retrospective cohort study used Polish social insurance data (2020-2022) to quantify COVID-19-related work absence and associated economic costs, including post-COVID-19 condition. It found 52.9 million total work absence days with €4.3 billion in indirect costs, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Błażej Łyszczarz
paper_title: Incidence and cost of COVID-19-related work absence based on social insurance data from Poland

summary: Population-based retrospective cohort study comparing healthcare utilization in 307,994 Italian adults previously infected with SARS-CoV-2 versus matched uninfected controls over 6 months. Found that SARS-CoV-2 infected individuals, particularly those hospitalized or admitted to ICU, had significantly higher outpatient visits, diagnostic tests, and hospitalizations.
paper_authors: Luigi Castriotta; Graziano Onder; Valentina Rosolen; Yvonne Beorchia; Caterina Fanizza; Benedetta Bellini; Marco Floridia; Marina Giuliano; Andrea Silenzi; Flavia Pricci; Tiziana Grisetti; Tiziana Grassi; Dorina Tiple; Marika Villa; Francesco Profili; Paolo Francesconi; Fabio Barbone; Lucia Bisceglia; Silvio Brusaferro
paper_title: Examining potential Long COVID effects through utilization of healthcare resources: a retrospective, population-based, matched cohort study comparing individuals with and without prior SARS-CoV-2 infection

summary: A multicenter retrospective cohort study characterizing long COVID in 533 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors in the UAE, documenting symptom prevalence, demographic associations, and impact on daily functioning. The study identifies risk factors (female gender, ICU admission, comorbidities) but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Basema Saddik; Rouba Karen Zeidan; Ankita Shukla; Manal Awad; Hamzah Alzubaidi; Najlaa Al-Bluwi; Riaz Agha; Zahraa AlHano; Ghada Mohammed; Iffat Elbarazi
paper_title: Long COVID in the UAE: symptomatology, gender gaps, and health implications among COVID-19 survivors

summary: This study analyzes SHARE survey data from 1,909 European adults aged 50+ who reported a positive COVID-19 test to identify sociodemographic and health factors protective against post-COVID conditions. The findings show that male sex, higher education, healthy BMI, absence of comorbidities, COVID-19 vaccination, and non-Visegrad country residence are protective factors, with education level showing strong association with health outcomes.
paper_authors: Masasuke Ohno; Dagmar Dzúrová
paper_title: Health inequality and protective factors for post COVID-19 condition among older adults in Europe

summary: This is an observational cohort study examining employment outcomes in 206,299 UK survey participants with long COVID compared to pre-infection baseline. The study documents associations between long COVID status and labour market inactivity/workplace absence, estimating ~27,000 UK working-age adults were inactive due to long COVID in July 2022, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Ayoubkhani D.; Zaccardi F.; Pouwels KB; Walker AS; Houston D.; Alwan NA; Martin J.; Khunti K.; Nafilyan V.
paper_title: Employment outcomes of people with Long Covid symptoms: community-based cohort study

summary: This case-control study compared memory impairment rates between 140 COVID-19 survivors and 139 unexposed controls at one year post-infection in Tunisia. The study found a significantly higher incidence of memory impairment in the COVID-19 group (17.9% vs 9.4%), with age, female gender, diabetes, anxiety/depression, and obesity as risk factors.
paper_authors: Imen Zemni; M. Kacem; Cyrine Bennasrallah; Wafa Dhouib; Manel Ben Fredj; Héla Abroug; N. Ben Rached; Ahmed Mhalla; Inès Bouanène; Asma Belguith Sriha
paper_title: Memory impairment after one year of the acute episode of Covid-19 infection

summary: A retrospective cohort study analyzing determinants of long COVID illness duration and healthcare service use in an Irish community sample (n=1,505). The study identifies factors associated with recovery (marital status, prior physical activity, COVID-19 infection count) and patterns of service utilization, finding that recent variants are associated with faster recovery.
paper_authors: Patricia I. Carney; Fiona McGuire; Caitlin Carroll; Phillip S. Kavanagh; U Fallon
paper_title: Determinants of Long COVID illness duration and service use-an Irish retrospective cohort study

summary: Longitudinal cohort study identifying four distinct symptom profiles in post COVID-19 condition patients (muscle pain, fatigue, cardiorespiratory, ageusia/anosmia) using latent profile analysis on 642 cases from the Lifelines COVID-19 cohort. Examines demographic, lifestyle, and health-related risk factors associated with each symptom profile rather than evaluating any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: SKR van Zon; Aranka Ballering; Sandra Brouwer; JGM Rosmalen
paper_title: A longitudinal study on symptom profiles and risk factors in patients with post COVID-19 condition

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 1,648 COVID-19 patients hospitalized in Copenhagen examining ethnic disparities in disease severity as predictors of long COVID diagnosis. Found no excess long COVID risk among migrants (RR=1.20) but identified ethnic disparities in acute disease severity (oxygen requirements, inflammation markers) that may predict subsequent long COVID.
paper_authors: Maria Ingeborg Goldschmidt; Thomas Benfield; Marie Nørredam
paper_title: Ethnic disparities in clinical severity of COVID-19 as predictor of long COVID

summary: This study examines productivity loss in Dutch workers with acute COVID-19 and post-COVID condition using data from the Lifelines COVID-19 cohort across 31 waves (March 2020–October 2022). Workers with post-COVID condition experienced twice the average productivity loss (€7,118) compared to those with acute COVID-19 (€3,410), highlighting the chronic economic burden of long COVID.
paper_authors: G Monteiro Sanchez; Raun van Ooijen; JGM Rosmalen; Tanja Fens; Antoinette D. I. van Asselt; Sharon Brouwer; SKR van Zon
paper_title: Productivity loss due to acute COVID-19 and post COVID-19 condition in the Northern Netherlands

summary: Danish nationwide cohort study examining long COVID risk and symptoms among ethnic minorities compared to native Danes using register-based data from 2,334,271 COVID-19 diagnosed individuals. Found that ethnic minorities from North Africa, Middle East, Eastern Europe, and Asia had significantly higher risk of long COVID diagnosis, with hospitalization as a significant risk factor.
paper_authors: George Frederick Mkoma; Maria Ingeborg Goldschmidt; Jørgen Holm Petersen; Thomas Benfield; Agneta Cederström; Mikael Rostila; Charles Agyemang; Marie Nørredam
paper_title: Risk of long COVID and associated symptoms after acute SARS-COV-2 infection in ethnic minorities: a Danish nationwide cohort study

summary: Population-based descriptive study of long COVID patients included in Belgium's post-COVID care trajectory program in primary care during 2023. Reports demographic characteristics, treatment types (mainly monodisciplinary with physiotherapy focus), and program uptake but does not evaluate treatment outcomes or compare intervention effects.
paper_authors: Sarah Moreels; R De Schreye; Sherihane Bensemmane
paper_title: Inclusion of Long Covid patients in the care trajectory post-Covid-19: evidence from Belgium

summary: Swedish register-based retrospective cohort study examining long COVID risk in migrants compared to Swedish-born individuals. Found higher long COVID rates among migrants from multiple regions, primarily driven by greater disease severity rather than vaccinations or social inequalities.
paper_authors: Agneta Cederström; Mikael Rostila
paper_title: Risk of long COVID in migrants and the contribution of vaccinations, disease severity, social inequalities and preexisting health: A nationwide register study in Sweden

summary: Prospective observational study following working-age COVID-19 patients for 1 year post-discharge to assess autonomic syndrome occurrence and impact on work ability. Found autonomic syndrome in one in three patients at 1, 6, and 12 months, associated with reduced work ability, but no intervention was tested or evaluated.
paper_authors: F. Barbic; L. Rinaldi; S. Rigo; R. Furlan; E. Riboli; S. Stranges; C. Lampl; A. Simmet; Germany
paper_title: Long Covid autonomic syndrome and his impact on workability: results of observational prospective study and 1-year FU in patients admitted to hospital with COVID19

summary: This retrospective cohort study of 3.6 million Medicare beneficiaries examines the incidence of Long COVID and its association with prior COVID-19 vaccination. Findings show that those with 4+ vaccine doses had a 39% lower adjusted rate of Long COVID compared to unvaccinated beneficiaries.
paper_authors: Yasin Abul; Daniel A. Harris; Preeti Chachlani; Kaleen N. Hayes; Andrew R. Zullo; Vincent Mor; Stefan Gravenstein
paper_title: Incidence of Long COVID Diagnoses in 3.6 Million U.S. Medicare Beneficiaries With COVID-19
paper_journal: The Journals of Gerontology, Series A: Biological Sciences and Medical Sciences

summary: Secondary analysis of the FADA retrospective cohort study characterizing long COVID symptoms, severity, and associated factors in an Irish sample of 2,338 long COVID patients. Study found fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, and breathlessness as predominant symptoms, with baseline comorbidities and smoking as risk factors for persistence and severity.
paper_authors: Fiona McGuire; U Fallon; Phillip S. Kavanagh; Patricia I. Carney
paper_title: Characterising Long COVID in an Irish cohort: a study of symptom type, severity and determinants

summary: This observational study examines the prevalence and characteristics of long COVID symptoms across age groups using a nationally representative US sample from 2020. It finds that approximately 48% of COVID-diagnosed individuals reported symptoms three months post-infection, with no significant age-related differences in symptom burden.
paper_authors: Qiao Wu; Eileen Crimmins
paper_title: Age Differences in Becoming COVID Long-Haulers and in Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 86 older adults in Brazil examining the impact of physiotherapy rehabilitation on functional recovery after COVID-19. Found that while those recommended for physiotherapy had worse initial functional status, long-term functional capacity showed no significant difference between those who received treatment and those who did not.
paper_authors: Gabriela Ochiai; Erika Gouveia E. Silva; Daniella De Melo; Diêgo Araújo Ramos; Fabio Cavalcanti Freitas; Vivian Cintra Sousa; Ana Carolina Schmitt; Jose Pompeu
paper_title: INFLUENCE OF PHYSICAL THERAPY REHABILITATION ON FUNCTIONAL RECOVERY OF OLDER PEOPLE AFTER COVID-19

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining long COVID incidence and symptom patterns among 1,886 hospitalized COVID-19 patients in the Netherlands, stratified by migration background. Reports 26% long COVID prevalence at 12 weeks post-discharge with differences in symptom presentation and risk by migration status, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Felix P. Chilunga; B Appleman; M. van Vugt; K Klaverda; Patrick Smeele; Johan H. van Es; W. Joost Wiersinga; Mikael Rostila; Maria Prins; Karien Stronks
paper_title: Differences in incidence, nature of symptoms, and duration of long COVID among hospitalised migrant and non-migrant patients in the Netherland: a retrospective cohort study

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining the use of Long COVID Clinics (LCCs) in the Veterans Health Administration among 494,547 veterans with documented SARS-CoV-2 infection. Found that only 2% of the cohort used LCCs and 17.4% of those with a long COVID diagnosis used them, with significant geographic disparities in access.
paper_authors: David P. Bui; Elizabeth Bast; Hanh Trinh; Alexandra Fox; Theodore S. Z. Berkowitz; Ana Palacio; Pandora L. Wander; Ann M. O’Hare; Edward J. Boyko; George N. Ioannou; Matthew L. Maciejewski; Denise M. Hynes
paper_title: Use of Long COVID Clinics in the Veterans Health Administration: Implications for the path forward

summary: Prospective cohort study examining effects of acute COVID-19 infection on male reproductive and hormonal parameters in 50 recovered men followed for 3 months post-recovery. Findings show erectile dysfunction and spermatogenesis impairment gradually improve over time, with hormonal recovery within 3 months.
paper_authors: Abdullah Luay; Ula Al-Kawaz; E Mohsin
paper_title: O-253 Impact of Covid-19 Infection on Male Seminal and Hormonal Parameters

summary: Cross-sectional study examining sperm count changes in 20 Indian men post-COVID-19 recovery, finding 70% had reduced sperm counts with a mean reduction of 48.83% at 74 days post-recovery. This is an observational study documenting a post-COVID symptom without testing any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Gaurav Mittal; K.C Mantravadi; D.R Gedela
paper_title: P-051 Reduced sperm count in Indian men post recovery from SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) infection: a worrying trend

summary: This cross-sectional study examines associations between Post-Acute COVID-19 Syndrome (PACS) symptoms and risk factors in 108 patients from the Rutgers Post-COVID Recovery Program, stratifying participants by cognitive complaint status and test performance. The analysis identifies age, depression, anxiety, and fatigue as risk factors associated with cognitive impairment in long COVID, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Alice Dawson; William Hu
paper_title: Associations between PACS symptoms and risk factors among Long Haulers in the Rutgers Post-COVID Recovery Program

summary: Prospective cross-sectional study evaluating semen parameters and inflammation in men 1 and 3 months after COVID-19 recovery. Found that 25% of recovered men had semen impairment with elevated inflammatory markers, though parameters improved by 3-month follow-up.
paper_authors: Mauro Gacci; Marco Coppi; Elisabetta Baldi; A Sebastianelli; Claudia Zaccaro; Simone Morselli; Alessio Pecoraro; Alekseja Manera; Rossella Nicoletti; Andrea Liaci; Claudio Bisegna; Luca Gemma; S. Giancane; Simona Pollini; Alberto Antonelli; Filippo Lagi; Sara Marchiani; S Dabizzi; S Degl'Innocenti; Francesco Annunziato; Mario Maggi; L Vignozzi; A. Bartoloni; Gian María Rossolini; Sergio Serni
paper_title: O-001 Semen impairment and occurrence of SARS-CoV-2 virus in semen after recovery from COVID-19

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines cardiovascular event risk in COVID-19 patients with pre-existing chronic respiratory disease using NHS England data from 2020-2021. While it studies post-COVID outcomes, it focuses on general post-COVID cardiovascular complications rather than long COVID-specific persistent symptoms, and does not evaluate any treatment interventions.
paper_authors: Whittaker, Hannah; Kallis, Constantinos; Bolton, Thomas; Wood, Angela; Walker, Samantha; Sheikh, Aziz; Brownrigg, Alex; Akbari, Ashley; Sterniczuk, Kamil; Quint, Jennifer K; Cvd-Covid-Uk/Covid-Impact Consortium
paper_title: Risk of cardiovascular events following COVID-19 in people with and without pre-existing chronic respiratory disease

summary: Longitudinal study of healthcare workers who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2, tracking their antibody titers and symptoms over 7-8 months to investigate the relationship between immune response and post-COVID-19 syndrome development. Found no statistically significant difference in initial viral titers or antibody levels between those who developed PCS and those who did not.
paper_authors: Christopher Pereira; Benjamin H. L. Harris; Matteo Di Giovannantonio; Carolina Rosadas; Charlotte-Eve Short; Rachael Quinlan; Macià Sureda-Vives; Natalia Fernandez; Isaac Day-Weber; Maryam Khan; Federica Marchesin; Ksenia Katsanovskaja; Eleanor Parker; Graham P. Taylor; Richard S. Tedder; Myra O. McClure; Melanie Dani; Michael Fertleman
paper_title: The Association Between Antibody Response to Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 Infection and Post–COVID-19 Syndrome in Healthcare Workers

summary: Prospective study examining sperm parameter changes in 45 men with mild COVID-19 infection, measured before infection and 17-516 days post-infection. Study found significant decreases in sperm concentration, motility, and vitality persisting beyond 100 days post-infection, but this is observational follow-up of natural disease sequelae rather than an intervention trial for long COVID treatment.
paper_authors: R Nunez - Calonge; J. A. Guijarro; Thomas Rubio; P Alberola; Gabriela Veiga Fernández; N. Santamaría; Sergio Alonso; Inácio de Barros
paper_title: O-020 What is the recovery time for sperm parameters in men who have suffered a mild Covid-19 infection?

summary: This cross-sectional study of 508 Omicron-infected adults examines whether chronic post-COVID neuropsychiatric symptoms form distinct clusters with different risk factors, replicating earlier pre-Omicron findings. While confirming two separate symptom clusters (cognitive complaints and anxiety-depression), the study is observational without treatment intervention and therefore excluded from the intervention trials pipeline.
paper_authors: *Steven Wai Ho Chau; Timothy Mitchell Chue; Yee Lok Lai; Ling Tsui; Tsz Ching Lam; Rachel Ngai Yin Chan
paper_title: CHRONIC POST-COVID NEUROPSYCHIATRIC SYMPTOM CLUSTERS DO NOT SHARE THE SAME RISK FACTORS IN A COHORT INFECTED BY THE OMICRON VARIANT

summary: A prospective cohort study comparing prevalence and severity of symptoms 3 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection in cases versus test-negative and population controls in the Netherlands. Finds that 48.5% of cases report significantly elevated symptoms, with vaccination protective against loss of smell and taste but not other long COVID symptoms.
paper_authors: Tessa van der Maaden; Elizabeth N. Mutubuki; Siméon de Bruijn; Ka Yin Leung; Hans Knoop; Jaap Slootweg; Anna D. Tulen; Albert Wong; Albert Jan van Hoek; Eelco Franz; Cees C. van den Wijngaard
paper_title: Prevalence and Severity of Symptoms 3 Months After Infection With SARS-CoV-2 Compared to Test-Negative and Population Controls in the Netherlands

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 94,595 COVID-19 patients examining associations between COVID-19 severity and long-term cardiovascular and mortality outcomes 31-120 days post-infection. Study identifies increased risk of stroke, MI, PE/DVT, heart failure, and death following severe COVID-19, with most events occurring 31-60 days post-infection.
paper_authors: Galloway A.; Park Y.; Tanukonda V.; Ho YL; Nguyen XT; Maripuri M.; Dey AT; Gerlovin H.; Posner D.; Lynch KE; Cai T.; Luoh SW; Whitbourne S.; Gagnon DR; Muralidhar S.; Tsao PS; Casas JP; Gaziano JM; Wilson PWF; Hung AM; Cho K.
paper_title: Impact of Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) Severity on Long-term Events in United States Veterans Using the Veterans Affairs Severity Index for COVID-19 (VASIC)

summary: Longitudinal analysis of 33 long COVID patients examining autoimmune activation and cytokine profiles over 7-11 months post-acute infection. Found persistent autoimmunity, elevated proinflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α, G-CSF, IL-17A), and increased effector T cells; suggests immunomodulation as potential treatment target but does not test any intervention.
paper_authors: Yeny Acosta-Ampudia; Diana M. Monsalve; Manuel Rojas; Yhojan Rodríguez; Elizabeth Zapata; Carolina Ramírez-Santana; Juan-Manuel Anaya
paper_title: Persistent Autoimmune Activation and Proinflammatory State in Post-Coronavirus Disease 2019 Syndrome

summary: Population-based cohort study comparing the risk of post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) diagnosis after Omicron infections versus Delta, Alpha, and wild-type variants in Stockholm, Sweden. Found significantly lower PCC risk following Omicron infection (0.2%) compared to earlier variants (0.5-1.3%), with adjusted hazard ratios ranging from 3.26 to 6.31.
paper_authors: Pontus Hedberg; Pontus Nauclér
paper_title: Post–COVID-19 Condition After SARS-CoV-2 Infections During the Omicron Surge vs the Delta, Alpha, and Wild Type Periods in Stockholm, Sweden

summary: This study measured soluble markers of inflammation in a SARS-CoV-2 recovery cohort at early and late timepoints to identify biological processes associated with PASC. The findings showed that individuals who developed PASC had higher levels of inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IFN-γ-induced protein 10, IL-6) during recovery, suggesting persistent immune activation may underlie ongoing symptoms.
paper_authors: Peluso MJ; Lu S.; Tang AF; Durstenfeld MS; Ho HE; Goldberg SA; Forman CA; Munter SE; Hoh R.; Tai V.; Chenna A.; Yee BC; Winslow JW; Petropoulos CJ; Greenhouse B.; Hunt PW; Hsue PY; Martin JN; Daniel Kelly J.; Glidden DV; Deeks SG; Henrich TJ
paper_title: Markers of Immune Activation and Inflammation in Individuals With Postacute Sequelae of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 Infection

summary: A prospective cohort study following 52 individuals with mild COVID-19 and uninfected controls from pre-infection through 2 years post-infection to characterize lung function trajectories. Results show mild COVID-19 causes excess decline in FEV1 and FVC in the first 6 months post-infection with limited recovery, while DLco showed improvement between 6-24 months.
paper_authors: Katrine K. Iversen; Andreas Ronit; Magnus G. Ahlström; Børge G. Nordestgaard; Shoaib Afzal; Thomas Benfield
paper_title: Lung Function Trajectories in Mild COVID-19 With 2-year Follow-up

summary: This observational cohort study followed 102 participants with documented SARS-CoV-2 infection to characterize mucosal viral RNA clearance and symptom persistence over time. The study identified obesity as a risk factor for prolonged mucosal viral RNA (≥1 month) and symptom persistence (≥3 months), and found lower anti-spike IgG levels associated with reinfection risk.
paper_authors: Mars Stone; Bryan R. Spencer; Donald E. Warden; Rebecca V. Fink; Paula Saa; Jennifer Leddy; Jackie Mulach-Vannoy; Rebecca Townsend; David Krysztof; Alexandria N. Hughes; Clara Di Germanio; Debra A. Kessler; Steven Kleinman; Michael P. Busch; Philip J. Norris
paper_title: Patient and Immunological Factors Associated With Delayed Clearance of Mucosal Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 RNA and Symptom Persistence

summary: This cross-sectional study examined the association between prior SARS-CoV-2 infection and post-COVID symptoms among fully vaccinated Canadian paramedics. It found no significant association between known or unknown prior infection and the presence of post-COVID symptoms.
paper_authors: Michael Asamoah-Boaheng; Brian Grunau; Mohammad Ehsanul Karim; Tracy L. Kirkham; Paul A. Demers; Chris MacDonald; David M. Goldfarb
paper_title: The Association of Post-COVID-19–Related Symptoms and Preceding Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 Infection Among Fully Vaccinated Paramedics in Canada

summary: Prospective cohort study of 2,960 non-hospitalized adults examining risk factors for postacute sequelae (long COVID) following acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. Identified older age, female sex, rural residence, high BMI, greater acute severity, chronic lung disease, and poor baseline health as risk factors; recent vaccination reduced risk while antiviral therapy did not.
paper_authors: Dan-Yu Lin; Melissa A. Mischell; Xinyu Zhang; Katie R. Mollan; Ning Zhang; Dinelka Nanyakkara; Jessica R. Keys; Becky Straub; David Wohl; William Fischer
paper_title: Incidence and Severity of Postacute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Infection in the Omicron Era: A Prospective Cohort Study

summary: Population-based cohort study of 331,042 individuals in Stockholm examining the effect of COVID-19 vaccination on the risk of developing persistent post-COVID condition (PCC) after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Vaccination significantly reduced PCC risk, with 2-3 doses showing 58-63% risk reduction compared to unvaccinated individuals.
paper_authors: Pontus Hedberg; Suzanne Desirée van der Werff; Pontus Nauclér
paper_title: The Effect of COVID-19 Vaccination on the Risk of Persistent Post–COVID-19 Condition: Cohort Study

summary: This cross-sectional study of 4,108 mild COVID-19 patients investigates the association between post-COVID syndrome (PCS) symptoms and chronic low-grade inflammation in blood cells, comparing samples from 12-24 weeks before and 24 weeks after infection. The findings suggest that PCS symptoms including fatigue, cough, dizziness, and palpitations are associated with elevated inflammatory markers (hs-CRP, NLR, PLR) and immune cells, with women and healthcare workers showing higher symptom prevalence.
paper_authors: Lin Yanhui; Wang Jiangang; Gao Jianping; Wang Tao
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 syndrome and low-grade inflammation: exploring gender and occupational inequalities in a retrospective cohort study

summary: Uses temporal-informed PheWAS to identify new diagnoses occurring after COVID-19 in a large EHR cohort of 30,088 COVID-positive patients. Identifies increased risk for 43 diagnoses across respiratory, cardiovascular, neurological, and other systems, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

summary: Retrospective study of 139 pediatric long COVID patients evaluated in a rehabilitation clinic, assessing prevalence of anxious and depressive symptoms using validated scales. Found 40% had elevated anxiety/depression scores, with prior mental health diagnoses associated with higher symptom severity.
paper_authors: Ellen Henning; Rashelle Musci; Sara B. Johnson; Cindy Villatoro; Laura A. Malone
paper_title: Pediatric long COVID: relationships with premorbid history of anxiety or depression and health-related quality of life

summary: This retrospective claims database analysis compares erectile dysfunction risk following COVID-19 infection to other common viral infections (influenza, RSV, enterovirus, etc.) using propensity score matching. paper_authors: Upeka Rathnayaka; Deepika; Vidanage
paper_title: #60 TWO MONTH FOLLOW-UP OF PATIENTS WITH ACUTE COVID-19 AND MULTISYSTEM INFLAMMATORY SYNDROME IN CHILDREN
paper_journal: Journal of the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Society

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing long-term complications and mortality in older adults (≥60 years) with and without COVID-19 infection using UK Biobank and Hong Kong electronic health records. COVID-19 infection was significantly associated with higher risks of cardiovascular disease, respiratory disease, neuropsychiatric outcomes, renal disease, and all-cause mortality over 18-28 months of follow-up.

summary: This retrospective cohort study analyzed Military Health System records from October 2021–October 2022 to determine the incidence of diagnosed post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) among active duty service members and identify demographic risk factors and co-occurring diagnoses. Among 7,171 ADSM diagnosed with PCC, females had 3.7× higher incidence than males, older service members (55–64 years) had the greatest risk, and respiratory symptoms (particularly shortness of breath) were the most common co-occurring diagnosis.
paper_authors: Tonay Flattum-Riemers; Apryl Susi; Cade Nylund
paper_title: Incidence Trends and Co-Diagnosis of Post–COVID-19 Condition in the Active Duty Population

summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 1,000 hospitalized COVID-19 patients to evaluate long-term kidney outcomes in those who experienced acute kidney injury (AKI) versus those without AKI. Patients with COVID-19-associated AKI had significantly worse kidney function at 180-day follow-up, with higher rates of chronic kidney disease development and greater GFR decline.
paper_authors: Yulia Khruleva; Marina Efremovtseva; Zhanna Kobalava
paper_title: MO338: Long-Term Kidney Outcomes After Acute Kidney Injury in Patients With COVID-19

summary: This prospective observational study examined the fungal etiology and clinical profile of suspected mucormycosis in post-COVID patients, identifying Rhizopus arrhizus as the most common causative agent with rhino-orbital-cerebral mycormycosis as the most frequent clinical form. While the paper involves post-COVID patients, it is primarily a mycological epidemiology study of a secondary opportunistic fungal infection rather than a treatment trial for long COVID itself, and mucormycosis is an acute post-COVID complication rather than persistent long COVID syndrome.
paper_authors: Kiran Tak; Vijaylatha Rastogi; Pushpanjali Verma; Vikas Gehlot; Mansi Gupta; Digvijay Rawat; Shailja Prajapati; Geeta Parihar
paper_title: P299 A clinicomycological study of suspected mucormycosis in post-COVID patients attending a tertiary care hospital

summary: Cross-sectional study examining erectile dysfunction prevalence in 33 men recovered from COVID-19 using questionnaires and penile duplex ultrasonography. Found 64.3% had erectile dysfunction with significant vascular abnormalities, suggesting tissue hypoxia during acute infection may contribute to persistent sexual dysfunction.
paper_authors: Dr Davide Menafra; Cristina de Angelis; Dr Michele Castoro; Dr Francesco Garifalos; Dr Nunzia Verde; Prof Ivan Gentile; Prof Marialuisa Bocchino; Prof Lucia Ruggiero; Prof Emmanuele AF Jannini; Prof Annamaria Colao; Prof Rosario Pivonello

summary: This retrospective cohort study of 1,000 hospitalized COVID-19 patients examines the association between acute kidney injury (AKI) during acute infection and long-term mortality outcomes over 180 days post-discharge. The study finds that AKI during acute COVID-19 is independently associated with higher 180-day mortality (11.8% vs 4.5%), but focuses entirely on acute-phase complications rather than long COVID syndrome.
paper_authors: Yulia Khruleva; Marina Efremovtseva; Zhanna Kobalava
paper_title: MO332: Acute Kidney Injury is Associated With Poor Long-Term Outcomes in Hospitalized Patients With COVID-19

summary: A retrospective cohort study of 93 COVID-19 hospitalized patients followed for 12 months to assess whether acute infection severity predicts chronic kidney disease progression. The study found no significant association between COVID-19 severity and CKD progression, with 21.5% of survivors developing CKD progression regardless of initial disease severity.
paper_authors: Arturo Lorenzo; María Martínez Manrique; Paula Ardura; Isabel Acosta-Ochoa; Ana Lucía Valencia; Alicia Mendiluce; Veronica Fidalgo; Jimmy Reinaldo Sanchez Gil; Armando Coca
paper_title: MO442: COVID-19 Disease Severity and Risk of 12-Month CKD Progression

summary: Retrospective observational study examining outcomes in 12 advanced chronic kidney disease patients hospitalized with COVID-19 from March-December 2020. 42% experienced post-infection pneumology symptoms (cough, dyspnea), 8% neurological symptoms, and 8% loss of smell, but no treatment intervention was tested.

paper_title: MO470: Outcomes of Patients in Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease (ACKD) Consultation With Covid-19 Infection

summary: This multicenter registry study examines how chronic kidney disease and glomerular filtration rate affect the course of acute COVID-19 infection and post-COVID outcomes in 8,496 patients across 7 countries. The study found that CKD significantly increased severity during acute infection and mortality risk within 12 months post-COVID, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

summary: Retrospective study of 77 CKD patients presenting with post-COVID-19 sequelae (hematuria, proteinuria, kidney dysfunction) at 56 days post-infection. paper_authors: Erjola Likaj; Larisa Shehaj
paper_title: MO845: COVID-19 Sequels in Nephrology CKD Patients More Prone to Fatality

summary: This is a multicenter observational cohort study analyzing acute kidney injury (AKI) incidence in COVID-19 patients and its impact on post-COVID outcomes using the ACTIV international register. The study found AKI in 11.6% of hospitalized COVID-19 patients and was associated with higher mortality risk both during acute infection and at 3-month follow-up, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

paper_title: #4725 INCIDENCE OF ACUTE KIDNEY INJURY IN PATIENTS WITH COVID-19 AND ITS IMPACT ON THE COURSE OF THE ACUTE INFECTION AND POST-COVID PERIOD

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining the impact of acute COVID-19 infection on renal function in patients with pre-existing glomerular disease, evaluating eGFR changes and the effect of Paxlovid treatment. Findings show accelerated renal function deterioration in proteinuric patients following acute infection, not long COVID sequelae.

paper_title: #5532 COVID-19 INFECTION MODIFIES GLOMERULAR DISEASE EVOLUTION

summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 2,212 long-COVID patients in post-COVID recovery clinics to assess kidney function changes over 12 months. Patients experienced a 2.96 mL/min/1.73 m² decline in eGFR (3.39% reduction), with higher declines in hospitalized and diabetic patients, indicating long-COVID's impact on renal function.

summary: This retrospective cohort study from Stockholm examines whether COVID-19 infection is associated with accelerated kidney function decline compared to pneumonia survivors. The study found that COVID-19 survivors showed greater acceleration in eGFR decline, particularly among those with severe infection requiring hospitalization, suggesting a need for post-COVID kidney function monitoring.

summary: The CARTESIAN study is a prospective multicenter cohort of 938 COVID-19 survivors followed at 6 and 12 months post-infection to assess arterial stiffness and its relationship with kidney function. The study found that individuals with lower kidney function and severe COVID-19 history exhibit higher arterial stiffness and accelerated vascular aging, but this is an observational follow-up study with no treatment intervention tested.

paper_title: #723 The impact of kidney function on arterial stiffness in COVID-19 survivors: an analysis from CARTESIAN Study

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining acute kidney injury (AKI) in 409 hospitalized COVID-19 patients and its association with long-term renal and mortality outcomes over two years. paper_title: #3498 LONG-COVID IN PATIENTS ON HEMODIALYSIS: A SINGLE CENTER ANALYSIS

paper_title: #109 Managing PASC in CKD patients: implications for long-term care and health outcomes

summary: This nationwide Swedish registry study examines the risk of kidney injury following acute COVID-19 infection up to 6 months post-onset using the Self-Controlled Case Series method. While it documents an association between COVID-19 severity and kidney injury risk, it focuses on acute post-infection complications rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months later).
paper_authors: Hanna Jerndal; Angele Ahelba; Sebastian Kalucza; Ioannis Katsoularis; Bernd Stegmayr; Marie Eriksson; Osvaldo Fonseca Rodriguez; Anne-Marie Fors Connolly
paper_title: #680 Kidney injury post Covid-19—a nationwide Swedish register study

summary: This cross-sectional study of 214 long COVID patients assessed the impact of post-COVID-19 syndrome on occupational status and quality of life. While relevant to long COVID, it is observational only (no treatment intervention) and therefore excluded from the treatment trial pipeline.

paper_title: Occupational effects in patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome

summary: Prospective cohort study examining associations between night shift work, sleep disruption, and COVID-19 outcomes in 3,319 Spanish adults. paper_authors: Vandersmissen G.; Verbeeck J.; Henckens P.; Van Dyck J.; Wuytens C.; Molenberghs G.; Godderis L.

summary: This retrospective cohort study examined the long-term effect of COVID-19 on kidney function (eGFR trajectory) in patients with chronic kidney disease, comparing 268 COVID-infected cases to 534 matched controls followed over ~3 years. summary: This cross-sectional study examined 216 long COVID workers attending a multidisciplinary day-hospital program to identify factors associated with sick leave and sick leave duration. paper_authors: Lyubov Shpagina; Igor Bukhtiyarov; Liudmila Kuzmina; Evgeny Shigan; Elena Kondyurina; Ilya Shpagin; Olga Kotova; Galina Kuznetsova; Natalya Kamneva; Ekaterina Anikina; Kristina Likhenko-Logvinenko

summary: This is a workplace health surveillance study examining post-COVID syndrome prevalence, symptom patterns, and associations with occupational factors and mental health in 1,378 workers. It does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment for long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Nicola Magnavita; Igor Meraglia; Gabriele Arnesano; Marco Merella; Maria Eugenia Vacca
paper_title: P-543 WORK-RELATED FACTORS IN POST-COVID SYNDROME

summary: Retrospective telephone follow-up of 266 COVID-19 patients discharged from Henry Ford Hospital, assessing 30-day outcomes including symptoms, oxygen requirements, and readmissions. No active intervention or treatment was administered; this is a passive observational assessment of natural recovery patterns.
paper_authors: Smitha Gudipati; Judith L. Ranger; Amit T. Vahia; Tommy J. Parraga Acosta; Zachary W. Hanna; Sashi N. Nair; Nicholas F. Yared; Geehan Suleyman; Indira Brar

paper_title: Clinical Features and Follow-up of Referred Children and Young People With Long COVID

summary: This retrospective cohort study evaluates the safety of tranexamic acid (TXA) in post-COVID patients undergoing major arthroplasty, using propensity-matched data from the TriNetX database. summary: This prospective follow-up study compares cognitive function and mood changes in 90 older COVID-19 survivors versus 90 healthy controls at 1, 6, and 12 months post-infection. paper_title: Assessment of Cognitive and Mood Changes in Older Survivors of COVID-19

summary: Prospective cohort study of 303 COVID-19 hospitalized patients followed after discharge to assess incidence of post-COVID-19 IBS using Rome-IV criteria. paper_title: Incidence and predisposing factors for de novo post-COVID-19 irritable bowel syndrome

summary: Retrospective cohort study using N3C database to compare incidence of vestibular disorders in COVID-19 positive patients versus controls across different viral variants. paper_authors: Lawrance Lee; Evan French; Daniel H. Coelho; Nauman F. Manzoor
paper_title: Increased Incidence of Vestibular Disorders in Patients With SARS-CoV-2

summary: A retrospective observational study of 50 long COVID patients undergoing a rehabilitation program targeting fatigue, breathlessness, and pain. The program showed feasibility with significant improvements in symptom intensity and health-related quality of life.

paper_title: Post–COVID-19 Ongoing Symptoms and Health-Related Quality of Life: Does Rehabilitation Matter?

While 21% of iRD patients vs. 13% of controls met WHO long-COVID criteria, the difference was not statistically significant after adjusting for BMI and acute infection severity, concluding iRD patients are not more susceptible to long-COVID than the general population.
