summary: Prospective cohort study developing machine learning models to predict fatigue in COVID-19 patients using vocal biomarkers from 296 participants with 1772 voice recordings. The study demonstrates feasibility of remote fatigue monitoring via voice analysis but does not test any therapeutic intervention.
paper_authors: Abir Elbéji; Lu Zhang; Eduardo Higa; Aurélie Fischer; Vladimir Despotovic; Petr V. Nazarov; Gloria Aguayo; Guy Fagherazzi
paper_title: Vocal biomarker predicts fatigue in people with COVID-19: results from the prospective Predi-COVID cohort study

summary: Retrospective cohort study evaluating the effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccines and monoclonal antibodies in preventing post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC) in 53,239 patients across a US hospital system. Vaccination significantly reduced the likelihood of developing PASC (aOR 0.58) compared to both unvaccinated controls and monoclonal antibody treatment (aOR 0.77).
paper_authors: Jonika Tannous; Alan P. Pan; Thomas Potter; Abdulaziz T. Bako; Katharine Dlouhy; Ashley Drews; Henry Dirk Sostman; Farhaan S. Vahidy
paper_title: Real-world effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccines and anti-SARS-CoV-2 monoclonal antibodies against postacute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2: analysis of a COVID-19 observational registry for a diverse US metropolitan population

summary: Prospective cohort study following 67 COVID-19 ICU survivors for 1 year to assess recovery of participation in society and identify early determinants of recovery. While the study examines long-term post-COVID sequelae in ICU survivors, it is observational without an intervention component—patients received standard rehabilitation care rather than a tested treatment, making it ineligible as a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Carolina M. H. Wiertz; Bena Hemmen; Simone J. S. Sep; Susanne van Santen; Yvette Y. van Horn; Sander M. J. van Kuijk; Jeanine A. Verbunt
paper_title: Life after COVID-19: the road from intensive care back to living – a prospective cohort study

summary: Prospective observational study of 801 COVID-19 survivors assessed 3-11 months after hospital discharge to evaluate their long-term functional status. Found prevalent conditions including muscle weakness, pain, anxiety, depression, breathlessness, and reduced mobility, with no clear trends of improvement over the follow-up period.
paper_authors: Linamara Rizzo Battistella; Marta Imamura; Lucas Ramos De Pretto; Simon K. H. A. A. Van Cauwenbergh; Vinicius Delgado Ramos; Sabrina Saemy Tome Uchiyama; Denise Matheus; Flavia Kuhn; Ana Alice Amaral de Oliveira; Gabriella Souza Naves; Aline Rossetti Mirisola; Fernando de Quadros Ribeiro; Andre Tadeu Sugawara; Mauricio Cantarino; Rafael Andrade Santos Antunes Cavalca; Vanessa Pagano; Melina Valentim Marques; Elizabeth Mendes da Silva; Alessandra Pereira Gomes; Felipe Fregni
paper_title: Long-term functioning status of COVID-19 survivors: a prospective observational evaluation of a cohort of patients surviving hospitalisation

summary: Longitudinal observational study examining economic impacts of COVID-19 using monthly questionnaire data from 16,910 UK residents. Finds that incident COVID-19 and long COVID are associated with economic vulnerability (inadequate household income, sickness absence) in the short and long term, but this is an epidemiological/economic analysis, not a treatment intervention study.
paper_authors: Anne E. Williamson; Florence Tydeman; Alec Miners; Kate Pyper; Adrian R. Martineau
paper_title: Short-term and long-term impacts of COVID-19 on economic vulnerability: a population-based longitudinal study (COVIDENCE UK)

summary: A prospective, multicentre cohort study in French primary care examining initial symptoms and 3-month persistent symptoms in 521 patients with suspected COVID-19, comparing confirmed cases, no-COVID cases, and uncertain cases. While the study identifies persistent symptoms in ~one-third of confirmed cases at 3 months, it is purely observational with no treatment intervention—patients were simply followed up to assess symptom persistence without any therapeutic intervention being tested or evaluated.
paper_authors: Tan-Trung Phan; William Mirat; Sophie Brossier; Emmanuelle Boutin; Julie Fabre; Jean-Denis Hoonakker; Sylvie Bastuji-Garin; Vincent Renard; Emilie Ferrat
paper_title: Initial characteristics and course of disease in patients with suspected COVID-19 managed in general practice: a prospective, multicentre cohort study

summary: Retrospective cohort study analyzing routinely collected claims data from Bavaria, Germany to estimate the incidence of post-COVID syndrome and associated symptoms in ambulatory care. Found 14.2% of COVID-19 patients received a post-COVID diagnosis, with higher rates of fatigue, dyspnea, and smell/taste disturbances compared to controls, but the study does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Ewan Donnachie; Alexander Hapfelmeier; Klaus Linde; Martin Tauscher; Roman Gerlach; Anna Greissel; Antonius Schneider
paper_title: Incidence of post-COVID syndrome and associated symptoms in outpatient care in Bavaria, Germany: a retrospective cohort study using routinely collected claims data

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 3,809 patients who received monoclonal antibodies (MAbs) during acute COVID-19 compared to 3,809 matched controls, evaluating whether early MAb treatment prevents long COVID (postacute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection). MAb treatment reduced acute complications (hospitalization 28%, ICU admission 41% at 30 days) but did not reduce postacute clinical sequelae or long COVID risk.
paper_authors: Daniel Griffin; Chace McNeil; James Okusa; Diana Berrent; Yinglong Guo; Sarah E. Daugherty
paper_title: Does monoclonal antibody treatment for COVID-19 impact short and long-term outcomes in a large generalisable population? A retrospective cohort study in the USA

summary: A longitudinal cohort study of 3,039 Belgian adults with recent SARS-CoV-2 infection followed for 3 months post-infection to characterize the distribution and classification of post-COVID-19 condition symptoms. Using latent class analysis, the study identified three distinct symptom classes (anosmia/ageusia, neurological symptoms, and other symptoms) with different risk factors, but did not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Sarah Nayani; Diego Castanares-Zapatero; Robby De Pauw; Dieter Van Cauteren; Stefaan Demarest; Sabine Drieskens; Laura Cornelissen; Brecht Devleesschauwer; Karin De Ridder; Rana Charafeddine; Pierre Smith
paper_title: Classification of post COVID-19 condition symptoms: a longitudinal study in the Belgian population

summary: Prospective cohort study comparing health-related quality of life and respiratory outcomes 6 months after ICU discharge in critically ill COVID-19 survivors across different pandemic waves. The study found minimal differences in long-term HRQL between first and second/third wave survivors, with second/third wave patients showing slightly better role function and physical outcomes.
paper_authors: Pernilla Darlington; Mari Roël; Maria Cronhjort; Gabriel Hanna; Anders Hedman; Eva Joelsson-Alm; Anna Schandl
paper_title: Comparing severe COVID-19 outcomes of first and second/third waves: a prospective single-centre cohort study of health-related quality of life and pulmonary outcomes 6 months after infection

summary: A prospective longitudinal cohort study of 575 and 793 long COVID patients followed from May 2020 to October 2022 that identified three macro symptom clusters (neurological, sensorial, physical) and associated predictive factors. The study found associations between long COVID symptoms and comorbidities, acute-phase medications (ACE inhibitors, inhaled steroids), and demographic factors, but did not test a specific intervention.
paper_authors: Fabio Borgonovo; Pietro Giorgio Lovaglio; Chiara Mariani; Paolo Berta; Maria Vittoria Cossu; Giuliano Rizzardini; Giorgio Vittadini; Amedeo Ferdinando Capetti
paper_title: Analysis and clinical determinants of post-COVID-19 syndrome in the Lombardy region: evidence from a longitudinal cohort study

summary: This retrospective cohort study assessed health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in 1,207 patients hospitalized with COVID-19-related SARI at 1 year post-discharge using SF-36 questionnaires, examining associations with age, frailty, and disease severity. The study found significant correlations between baseline disease factors and physical functioning outcomes at 1-year follow-up.
paper_authors: Gavin Wright; Keerthi Senthil; Amir Zadeh-Kochek; Jonathan Heung-san Au; Jufen Zhang; Jiawei Huang; Ravi Saripalli; Mohiuddin Khan; Omar Ghauri; San Kim; Zakiuddin Mohammed; Carol Alves; Gouri Koduri
paper_title: Health-related quality of life after 12 months post discharge in patients hospitalised with COVID-19-related severe acute respiratory infection (SARI): a prospective analysis of SF-36 data and correlation with retrospective admission data on age, disease severity, and frailty

summary: Retrospective cohort study using real-world data (TriNetX) examining the association between Long COVID diagnosis and increased risk of mental health disorders in US patients. Found Long COVID patients had 2.6-fold increased risk of mental health disorders, with particularly strong associations for major depression (3.36×) and generalized anxiety disorder (3.44×).
paper_authors: Yue Zhang; Vernon M. Chinchilli; Paddy Ssentongo; Djibril M. Ba
paper_title: Association of Long COVID with mental health disorders: a retrospective cohort study using real-world data from the USA

summary: Longitudinal cohort study (n=19,545) examining the association between COVID-19 severity and somatic symptoms in the Japanese general population over 1-year follow-up using the SSS-8 scale. Found that COVID-19 cases requiring O2 therapy were significantly associated with very high somatic symptom burden (OR 7.60), identifying severity of acute infection and pre-existing conditions as risk factors for long COVID symptoms.
paper_authors: Norio Sugawara; Takahiro Tabuchi; Keita Tokumitsu; Norio Yasui-Furukori
paper_title: Predictors of somatic symptoms during the COVID-19 pandemic: a national longitudinal survey in Japan

summary: A 9-month prospective cohort study of 287 individuals in Scotland tracking COVID-19 recovery and long COVID symptom persistence using a mobile app. Only 3.1% met long COVID criteria at 9 months; fatigue was the most persistent symptom, and older age and female gender were associated with higher symptom burden.
paper_authors: Nicholas F. Sculthorpe; Marie McLaughlin; Luke Cerexhe; Eilidh Macdonald; Antonio Dello Iacono; Nilihan E. M. Sanal-Hayes; Joanne Ingram; Rachel Meach; David Carless; Jane Ormerod; Lawrence D. Hayes
paper_title: Tracking Persistent Symptoms in Scotland (TraPSS): a longitudinal prospective cohort study of COVID-19 recovery after mild acute infection

summary: This retrospective cohort study analyzed sick note rates in 24 million primary care patients with COVID-19 in 2020-2022 using NHS data. The study found elevated sick note rates in COVID-positive patients compared to matched controls, with highest risk in the first 30 days, providing evidence of long-term COVID-19 impact but did not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Andrea L. Schaffer; Robin Y. Park; John Tazare; Krishnan Bhaskaran; Brian MacKenna; Spiros Denaxas; Iain Dillingham; Sebastian C. J. Bacon; Amir Mehrkar; Christopher Bates; Ben Goldacre; Felix Greaves; John Macleod; Laurie A. Tomlinson; Alex Walker
paper_title: Changes in sick notes associated with COVID-19 from 2020 to 2022: a cohort study in 24 million primary care patients in OpenSAFELY-TPP

summary: An 18-month prospective follow-up survey of 5,464 Swedish COVID-19 patients examining how changes in physical activity relate to daily life functioning. Found that physical activity levels decreased post-infection and decreased PA was strongly associated with difficulties in daily activities, but this is a passive observational study without any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Annie Palstam; Johanna Seljelid; Hanna Charlotte Persson; Katharina S. Sunnerhagen
paper_title: Physical activity, acute severity and long-term consequences of COVID-19: an 18-month follow-up survey based on a Swedish national cohort

summary: Prospective cohort study tracking 1,478 COVID RADAR app users from 40 days before to 100 days after positive SARS-CoV-2 test to describe incidence and symptom clusters of post-acute COVID. Found 8% with persistent symptoms at 100 days, identifying three symptom clusters (non-respiratory, olfactory, respiratory) and associations with vaccination and acute disease severity.
paper_authors: van Dijk WJ; Haaksma ML; Mook-Kanamori DO; Visser LG; Numans ME; van Hylckama Vlieg A.; Rosendaal FR; Kiefte-de Jong JC
paper_title: Incidence, symptom clusters and determinants of post-acute COVID symptoms: a population-based surveillance in community-dwelling users of the COVID RADAR app

summary: Population-based cohort study using administrative health data from Manitoba to identify post-COVID condition cases and their prevalence (23% of 66,365 COVID-positive individuals). Reports predictive factors for PCC including female sex, older age, hospitalization, and comorbidities, while vaccination was protective.
paper_authors: Alan Katz; Okechukwu Ekuma; Jennifer E. Enns; Teresa Cavett; Alexander Singer; Diana C. Sanchez-Ramirez; Yoav Keynan; Lisa Lix; Randy Walld; Marina Yogendran; Nathan C. Nickel; Marcelo Urquia; Leona Star; Kendiss Olafson; Sarvesh Logsetty; Rae Spiwak; Jillian Waruk; Surani Matharaarachichi
paper_title: Identifying people with post-COVID condition using linked, population-based administrative health data from Manitoba, Canada: prevalence and predictors in a cohort of COVID-positive individuals

summary: A population-based longitudinal cohort study of 4,087 long COVID patients enrolled in UK rehabilitation clinics, tracking functional limitations, fatigue, quality of life, and societal costs over 6 months. Participants showed small improvements in functional limitations and fatigue, with mean WSAS score declining by 0.86 points, though significant societal costs (£931/month) were driven primarily by productivity losses.
paper_authors: Jiunn Wang; Henry Goodfellow; Sarah Walker; Ann Blandford; Paul Pfeffer; John R. Hurst; David Sunkersing; Katherine Bradbury; Chris Robson; William Henley; Manuel Gomes
paper_title: Trajectories of functional limitations, health-related quality of life and societal costs in individuals with long COVID: a population-based longitudinal cohort study

summary: Prospective cohort study of 210 acute COVID-19 patients followed 3-6 months post-infection to characterize post-COVID-19 condition phenotypes using cluster analysis. Identified four distinct clinical clusters (paucisymptomatic, physical sequelae, pulmonary comorbidities, functional somatic/mental symptoms) with differing demographics, comorbidities, and disease severity associations.
paper_authors: Thomas Escoda; Laurent Chiche; Hervé Faralli; Frédéric Cohen; Philippe Halfon; Hervé Pegliasco; Stanislas Rebaudet
paper_title: Cluster analysis of post-COVID-19 physical and mental health outcomes 3–6 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection: results of the French Prospective ALCOVID Cohort Study

summary: A prospective observational study following 166 COVID-19 hospitalized patients to identify early predictors of long COVID persistence at 12 months. Develops machine learning models to predict symptom persistence using baseline clinical, imaging, and laboratory data.
paper_authors: Oleksii Honchar; Tetiana Ashcheulova; Tetyana Chumachenko; Dmytro Chumachenko
paper_title: Early prediction of long COVID-19 syndrome persistence at 12 months after hospitalisation: a prospective observational study from Ukraine

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining determinants of post-COVID-19 clinic attendance among SARS-CoV-2-infected individuals in Stockholm, Sweden from 2020-2023. Found that mental health disorders and asthma were strongest predictors of clinic attendance in non-hospitalized patients, while prior sick leave was strongest predictor in hospitalized patients.
paper_authors: Pontus Hedberg; Peder af Geijerstam; John Karlsson Valik; Christer Almgren-Lidman; Anders Ternhag; Pontus Naucler
paper_title: Determinants of post COVID-19 clinic attendance among SARS-CoV-2-infected individuals in Stockholm, Sweden: a population-based cohort study

summary: Prospective cohort study of 1,276 children in a Rio de Janeiro favela tracking symptom duration following acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. Median recovery was 11 days, with 9.5% experiencing symptoms beyond 33 days, but the study focuses on acute COVID-19 recovery in children, not persistent long COVID symptoms or interventions.

paper_title: Duration of COVID-19 symptoms in children: a longitudinal study in a Rio de Janeiro favela, Brazil

summary: The CORFU study is a prospective longitudinal cohort study tracking post-COVID symptoms and health-related quality of life in 901 former COVID-19 patients across four severity groups (non-hospitalized, ward, ICU, and controls) over 24 months. While about long COVID, this is excluded because it is purely observational without any treatment intervention—patients are followed passively to assess symptom prevalence and QOL changes, not to evaluate the effectiveness of any therapeutic intervention.

paper_title: Two years and counting: a prospective cohort study on the scope and severity of post-COVID symptoms across diverse patient groups in the Netherlands—insights from the CORFU study

summary: This cross-sectional and longitudinal observational study from the PERCEIVE cohort examines depression as a moderator and mediator of functional status in 1,794 long COVID patients. The study demonstrates that depression mediates 36-51% of the association between post-COVID symptom severity and reduced functional capacity, but does not test or evaluate a specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Binyam Tariku Seboka; Joel Smith; Kristyn Whitmore; Brodie Baranow; Erin Howden; Jayashri Kulkarni; Quan L. Huynh; Thomas H. Marwick
paper_title: Depression as a moderator and mediator of functional status in patients with Long COVID: a cross-sectional and longitudinal observational study from the PERCEIVE cohort in Australia

summary: This nationwide retrospective cohort study examines how recurrent COVID-19 infections affect clinical outcomes in 313,760 COPD patients, finding progressive increases in exacerbation risk and mortality with repeated infections. Long COVID was more common after initial infection but diminished with subsequent reinfections, highlighting the importance of preventing initial COVID-19 exposure in COPD populations.
paper_authors: Hyun Woo Lee; Kwang Yong Choi; Jung-Kyu Lee; Won Seo Yoon; Youlim Kim; Kwang-Ha Yoo; Yong Il Hwang
paper_title: Recurrent COVID-19 infection and the risk of exacerbation, mortality and long covid in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a nationwide retrospective cohort study

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining the incidence of new-onset conjunctivitis 3.5 years post-SARS-CoV-2 infection in 67,702 COVID-positive patients compared to 1,391,135 COVID-negative controls. Found COVID-positive patients had significantly higher risk of developing new incident conjunctivitis (adjusted HR 1.10-1.11) compared to controls.
paper_authors: Tanya Mahesh; Sagar Changela; Katie S. Duong; Sonya Henry; Stephen H. Wang; Tim Q. Duong
paper_title: New-onset conjunctivitis 3.5 years post SARS-CoV-2 infection in an inner-city population in the Bronx

summary: A prospective cohort study following 3,590 long COVID patients from a specialist post-COVID service over 4 years to characterize recovery trajectory, symptom burden, and healthcare utilization. Only one-third of patients achieved satisfactory recovery (>75% of baseline health), with fatigue severity and vaccination status as key predictors of outcome.
paper_authors: Jai Prashar; Toby Hillman; Emma C. Wall; Amanpreet Sarna; Emma Mi; Robert Bell; Jagdeep Sahota; Michael Zandi; Patricia McNamara; Rebecca Livingston; Rebecca Gore; Catherine Lunken; Elena Bax; Rachel Nyam; Amir Masood Rafie Manzelat; Lyth Hishmeh; Emily Attree; Stephen Cone; Amitava Banerjee; Melissa Heightman
paper_title: Trajectory, healthcare utilisation and recovery in 3590 individuals with long covid: a 4-year prospective cohort analysis

summary: Prospective observational cohort study comparing ongoing symptoms and functional impairment at 12 weeks post-infection between COVID-19 and influenza patients in a vaccinated Australian population. Found no significant difference in symptom prevalence or moderate-to-severe functional impairment between the two groups, suggesting long COVID manifests as a postviral syndrome of similar severity to seasonal influenza.
paper_authors: Matthew Brown; John Gerrard; Lynne McKinlay; John Marquess; Teneika Sparrow; Ross Andrews
paper_title: Ongoing symptoms and functional impairment 12 weeks after testing positive for SARS-CoV-2 or influenza in Australia: an observational cohort study

summary: Serial cross-sectional study comparing well-being measures in 217 Australian participants with long COVID (symptoms >1 month) versus short COVID (symptoms ≤1 month) from a longitudinal cohort. Found lower well-being in the long COVID group before, during, and after infection, with persistent functional impairment.
paper_authors: Aimée Altermatt; Anna L. Wilkinson; Katherine Heath; Defeng Jin; Thi Nguyen; Alexander J. Thomas; Tianhui Ke; Yanqin Zhang; Rebecca E. Ryan; Lisa Gibbs; Alisa Pedrana; Dean Lusher; Stephanie Fletcher-Lartey; Mark Stoové; Katherine B. Gibney; Margaret Hellard
paper_title: Well-being among people with long and short COVID: a serial cross-sectional study in Victoria, Australia

summary: This Swedish national observational cohort study analyzed clinical features and demographic characteristics associated with post-COVID syndrome diagnosis in 6,389 patients identified through multiregistry data from 2020-2021. The study compares PCS patients with matched COVID-negative and severity-matched COVID-positive controls but does not test any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Hanna M. Ollila; Osvaldo Fonseca-Rodríguez; Ida Henriette Caspersen; Sebastian Kalucza; Johan Normark; Lill Trogstad; Per Minor Magnus; Naja Hulvej Rod; Andrea Ganna; Marie Eriksson; Anne-Marie Fors Connolly
paper_title: How do clinicians use post-COVID syndrome diagnosis? Analysis of clinical features in a Swedish COVID-19 cohort with 18 months’ follow-up: a national observational cohort and matched cohort study

summary: Prospective cohort study examining how social factors (education, deprivation, employment) affect recovery from ongoing COVID-19 symptoms in two UK community cohorts. Found that individuals with greater pre-pandemic social disadvantage had lower likelihood of recovery from long COVID.

paper_title: Social determinants of recovery from ongoing symptoms following COVID-19 in two UK longitudinal studies: a prospective cohort study

summary: Ambispective study of 712 Tanzanian patients hospitalized with COVID-19, followed up 2 years later to assess residual cardiopulmonary complications. Found 44.5% had cardiopulmonary sequelae, with BMI ≥25, smoking, and non-steroid use as independent predictors.
paper_authors: Elisha Fred Otieno Osati; Tumaini Joseph Nagu; Raphael Z. Sangeda; Grace Ambrose Shayo
paper_title: Residual cardiopulmonary manifestations following COVID-19: a Tanzanian ambispective study

summary: Prospective observational cohort study of 93 severe COVID-19 survivors followed 3-7 months post-discharge to assess long-term psychosocial and physical consequences. Found high rates of anxiety (46.2%) and depression (34.4%), with employment return dependent on socio-economic status, but no significant differences vs matched non-COVID controls.
paper_authors: Joanne McPeake; Martin Shaw; Pamela MacTavish; Kevin G. Blyth; Helen Devine; Gillian Fleming; Justine Griffin; Lisa Gemmell; Pauline Grose; Mark Henderson; Philip Henderson; Lucy Hogg; Kirstin King; Iain McInnes; Peter O'Brien; Kathryn Puxty; Callum Rainey; Varun Sharma; Malcolm Sim; Laura Strachan; Stefan Siebert; Tara Quasim
paper_title: Long-term outcomes following severe COVID-19 infection: a propensity matched cohort study

summary: This retrospective cohort study compares post-acute outcomes in hospitalized COVID-19 re-infection patients versus first-time infection patients in Hong Kong using propensity-score-weighted analysis. It found that re-infection was associated with significantly higher risk of mortality, hospital readmission, and emergency department attendance during the post-acute period.

paper_title: Post-acute sequelae of hospitalised COVID-19 re-infection compared with hospitalised first-time infection: a population-based retrospective cohort study in Hong Kong

summary: Retrospective cohort analysis of 1,946 COVID-19 patients hospitalized during the first UK wave, examining clinical characteristics, outcomes, and short-term sequelae. While 70% of survivors reported ongoing symptoms including fatigue and breathlessness, the study is primarily focused on acute hospitalization and early post-discharge outcomes rather than long COVID as a chronic condition, and does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Daryl Cheng; Claire Calderwood; Erik Skyllberg; Adam Ainley
paper_title: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of adult patients admitted with COVID-19 in East London: a retrospective cohort analysis

summary: This observational study evaluates the Your COVID Recovery® digital programme, a staged online intervention for long COVID patients, in 110 individuals from primary and secondary care in England. Participants showed statistically significant improvements in quality of life (EQ-5D-5L VAS) and breathing-related symptoms (CAT score) after an average of 8.6 weeks on the programme.
paper_authors: Phoebe H. I. Lloyd-Evans; Molly M. Baldwin; Enya Daynes; Annabel Hong; George Mills; Amye C. N. Goddard; Emma Chaplin; Nikki Gardiner; Sally J. Singh
paper_title: Early experiences of the Your COVID Recovery<sup>®</sup> digital programme for individuals with long COVID

summary: Prospective cohort study comparing breakthrough infection outcomes and post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) in immune-disordered persons (n=219) versus healthy volunteers (n=63) from April 2021 to July 2023. Study found that immune-disordered individuals experienced higher rates of PASC, persistent infections, and reinfections compared to healthy controls, though breakthrough infection rates were largely equivalent between groups.
paper_authors: Mackenzie Zendt; Fausto Andres Bustos Carrillo; Viviane Callier; Maureen DeGrange; Anita Ginigeme; Lurline Wu; Bevin Manuelpillai; Ana Ortega-Villa; Emily E. Ricotta
paper_title: Breakthrough SARS-CoV-2 outcomes in immune-disordered people during the Omicron era: a prospective cohort study

summary: Prospective cohort study examining the bidirectional relationship between sleep problems and long COVID using monthly data from 3,994 UK participants. Poor pre-infection sleep quality and high sleep efficiency variability were associated with increased long COVID risk, while post-infection sleep duration changes were modest and largely resolved within months.
paper_authors: Giulia Vivaldi; Mohammad Talaei; John Blaikley; Callum Jackson; Paul E. Pfeffer; Seif O. Shaheen; Adrian R. Martineau
paper_title: Bidirectional relationship between sleep problems and long COVID: a longitudinal analysis of data from the COVIDENCE UK study

summary: Prospective observational cohort study of 159 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors examined at 28-60 days post-discharge using CT imaging to characterize persistent pulmonary abnormalities and their relationship to patient outcomes. Persistent radiological abnormalities were common (56% of patients) and correlated with impaired quality of life, but no intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Robert Sykes; Andrew J. Morrow; Kenneth Mangion; Alex McConnachie; Alasdair McIntosh; Giles Roditi; Liam Peng; Claire Rooney; Kathryn Scott; David Barrie Stobo; Colin Berry; Colin Church; Hannah Bayes
paper_title: Radiological abnormalities persist following COVID-19 and correlate with impaired health-related quality of life: a prospective cohort study of hospitalised patients

summary: Multicentre prospective cohort study that performed cluster analysis on 935 long COVID patients to identify five distinct symptom phenotypes and their association with quality of life over 1 year. The study identified diverse patient clusters but is registered as a protocol study and does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Fumimaro Ito; Hideki Terai; Masahiro Kondo; Ryo Takemura; Ho Namkoong; Takanori Asakura; Shotaro Chubachi; Keita Masuzawa; Sohei Nakayama; Yusuke Suzuki; Mizuha Hashiguchi; Junko Kagyo; Tetsuya Shiomi; Naoto Minematsu; Tadashi Manabe; Takahiro Fukui; Yohei Funatsu; Hidefumi Koh; Katsunori Masaki; Keiko Ohgino; Jun Miyata; Ichiro Kawada; Makoto Ishii; Yasunori Sato; Koichi Fukunaga
paper_title: Cluster analysis of long COVID in Japan and association of its trajectory of symptoms and quality of life

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing mortality rates in COPD patients who recovered from COVID-19 versus matched controls in South Korea. Finds elevated mortality risk in the post-recovery period, particularly after severe COVID-19, but does not address long COVID or any specific treatment interventions.
paper_authors: Hyun Lee; Sang Hyuk Kim; Cho Yun Jeong; Jee-Eun Chung; Youlim Kim; Kyung Hoon Min; Kwang Ha Yoo; Jong Seung Kim; Ji-Yong Moon
paper_title: COVID-19 and risk of long-term mortality in COPD: a nationwide population-based cohort study

summary: A multicentre prospective cohort study of 1066 hospitalized COVID-19 patients in Japan assessed long COVID prevalence at 3, 6, and 12 months post-infection across three pandemic waves. The study found that patients hospitalized during the first wave had significantly higher rates of long COVID, particularly dyspnoea, compared to later waves, but did not test any specific treatment or intervention.

paper_title: Long COVID among the first three waves of COVID-19 in Japan: a multicentre cohort study

summary: Multicentre prospective cohort study of 777 COVID-19 hospitalised patients followed for up to 12 months post-discharge to assess long-term multidimensional patient-centred outcomes including quality of life, symptoms, and recovery. Found that disease severity during hospitalisation was not associated with long-term HRQoL but was associated with self-perceived recovery, with age, sex, and pulmonary history identified as stronger independent risk factors.

Study found persistent pulmonary changes (reticulation, fibrosis), decreased cardiac abnormalities, significant improvements in inflammatory markers, but lingering symptoms like myalgia and taste loss.

paper_title: Evaluation of Blood Biochemistry and Cardiopulmonary status of Hospitalized Covid-19 Patients in 3 Months  Post Discharged Follow up Survey

summary: Prospective cohort study evaluating functional impairments and limitations in 53 long COVID patients across three time points over 12 months using the ICF framework. Found significant increases in disabilities (mental, sensory, pain, movement, cardiovascular, immunological, respiratory functions) and activity limitations from baseline to 6-12 months, with specific symptom-disability associations identified.

paper_title: Post-coronavirus disease 2019 functional impairments, limitations, and restrictions: A prospective cohort study based on the international classification of functioning, disability, and health
paper_journal: Journal of Central Nervous System Disease

summary: Retrospective multicenter observational study of COVID-19 ICU survivors examining new medical conditions and medication changes at hospital discharge. While focused on post-acute outcomes in ICU survivors, the paper does not specifically address long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months post-infection) and does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

summary: Cross-sectional survey of MS patients examining overlap between PASC symptoms and MS manifestations using the NIH RECOVER PASC score. Found lower than expected PASC prevalence (1.5%) in MS patients and similar symptom proportions across infection groups, complicating PASC assessment in this population.
paper_authors: Amber Salter; Samantha Lancia; Gary R. Cutter; Robert J. Fox; Ruth Ann Marrie
paper_title: Post-acute sequela of COVID-19 infection in individuals with multiple sclerosis

summary: This pilot study investigated interferon-gamma-mediated metabolic pathways (tryptophan catabolism, neopterin, tyrosine, nitrite) in 31 hospitalized COVID-19 patients during acute infection and 60-day follow-up. While it documents persistent symptoms (neurological: 17.2%, fatigue: 51.7%, sleep disturbance: 34.5%) in long COVID reconvalescence, it is a mechanistic biomarker study with no treatment intervention tested.

paper_title: Interferon-gamma Mediated Metabolic Pathways in Hospitalized Patients During Acute and Reconvalescent COVID-19

summary: Retrospective single-center study of 42 post-COVID-19 patients examining the clinical features and prevalence of fatigue and associated comorbidities. Found that fatigue (90.5% prevalence) was the most prominent symptom and was associated with daytime sleepiness and depressed mood, but not with COVID-19 severity or demographic factors.

paper_title: Fatigue in Post-COVID-19 Syndrome: Clinical Phenomenology, Comorbidities and Association With Initial Course of COVID-19
paper_journal: Journal of Central Nervous System Disease

summary: This study uses data from a population-based birth cohort to examine whether confirming COVID-19 infection status influences Long COVID symptom reporting, testing for a potential nocebo effect. The analysis found no evidence of a nocebo effect or moderation by sex or anxiety in Long COVID symptom reporting.

paper_title: Confirmation of COVID-19 infection status and reporting of Long COVID symptoms in a population-based birth cohort: No evidence of a nocebo effect

summary: This retrospective cohort study compared long-term health outcomes in dementia patients with and without prior COVID-19 infection using electronic health records from a large health system. COVID-19 survivors with dementia had significantly higher risks of mortality, cardiovascular events, dysphagia, dyspnea, fatigue, sleep disturbances, and falls compared to non-infected controls.

paper_title: Long COVID-19 outcomes of patients with pre-existing dementia

summary: A cross-sectional study of 2,646 randomly selected COVID-19 patients assessed symptom persistence and health-related quality of life at median 142 days follow-up. Found 22% felt worse than pre-COVID, with hospitalized patients showing more biochemical/haematological abnormalities and higher symptom burden.

paper_title: Clinical outcomes at medium-term follow-up of COVID-19
paper_journal: Journal of the Royal College of Physicians of Edinburgh

summary: This 12-month prospective cohort study examined nonlinear EEG parameters in 83 long COVID patients during rest and cognitive/motor tasks to characterize brain electrical activity patterns. The study found task-dependent changes in EEG activity and complexity over time but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Nonlinear EEG Analysis During Motor and Cognitive Tasks in Patients With Long COVID: A Dynamic Systems Approach

summary: Prospective observational study comparing vascular parameters (intima-media thickness, arterial velocities, inflammatory markers) in 72 post-COVID-19 patients versus 11 controls over 12 months. Found increased IMT and altered arterial velocities in post-COVID patients with no DVT instances, suggesting potential atherosclerotic changes warranting further investigation.

paper_title: Long-term Effects of COVID-19 on Vascular Parameters—A Prospective Longitudinal Ultrasound Clinical Study

summary: Prospective observational study comparing brain activity via EEG and cognitive function in 53 COVID-19 patients and 30 controls over one year post-infection. Found reduced brain activity at rest and during cognitive tasks in COVID-19 group at 6-12 months, with long-term changes in cognitive function, but no treatment intervention was tested.

paper_title: Changes in Electrical Brain Activity and Cognitive Functions Following Mild to Moderate COVID-19: A one-Year Prospective Study After Acute Infection

summary: Retrospective analysis of 205 medical records from Vietnamese inpatients with long COVID, describing the prevalence and characteristics of clinical and subclinical manifestations. Most common symptoms were fatigue (59%), dyspnea (53%), and cough (43%), with 80% experiencing respiratory symptoms and 42% reporting neurological symptoms including sleep disturbance.
paper_authors: Dieu Hien T. Huynh; Dat T. Nguyen; Thu Suong T. Nguyen; Bao An H. Nguyen; Anh T. T. Huynh; Vy N. N. Nguyen; Dat Q. Tran; Thi N. N. Hoang; Huy Dung Tran; Dao Thanh Liem; Giau V. Vo; Minh Nam Nguyen
paper_title: Insights into the epidemiology and clinical aspects of post-COVID-19 conditions in adult

summary: A prospective cohort study following 756 hospitalized COVID-19 patients over 2-3 years to identify risk factors for chronic pain and fibromyalgia-like symptoms in post-COVID syndrome. Key predictors included anxiety/depression severity, sleep disruption, and reduced handgrip strength, highlighting modifiable targets for early intervention.
paper_authors: Linamara Rizzo Battistella; Marta Imamura; Xinyi Christine Zhang; Kevin Pacheco-Barrios; Felipe Fregni
paper_title: Risk factors associated with chronic pain and fibromyalgia-like symptoms post-COVID hospitalization

summary: Prospective cohort study of 317 COVID-19 pneumonia survivors (hospitalized and non-hospitalized) assessing pulmonary function (DLCO) and quality of life (SF-36) at 3 and 6 months post-discharge. While physical functioning improved by 6 months, non-physical QoL domains declined across all severity groups, and diffusion capacity remained decreased in severely affected patients.
paper_authors: Marlise P. de Roos; Sebastiaan Siegerink; Nynke G. Dijkstra; Birit FP Broekman; Kees Brinkman; Nini H. Jonkman; Paul Bresser
paper_title: Pulmonary function and Quality of Life in a prospective cohort of (non-) hospitalized COVID-19 pneumonia survivors up to six months

summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 410 hospitalized Omicron patients at 6 months and 1 year post-discharge to identify mortality predictors and symptom trends. The study found that 86% experienced persistent symptoms at 6 months, with elevated CRP (≥15.38 mg/L) as a predictor of symptom persistence, but no intervention was tested or evaluated.
paper_authors: Jiankang Wu; Naishu Xie; Weiwei Meng; Yiming Ma; Zhuo Li; Huihui Zeng; Yan Chen
paper_title: Long COVID and symptom persistence in post-discharge omicron patients: Insights into C-reactive protein

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluates clinical and imaging findings in 110 patients with post-COVID olfactory dysfunction compared to 50 COVID-negative controls using endoscopy, smell testing, and MRI. The study identifies increased olfactory bulb dimensions and edema as key mechanisms of COVID-related olfactory dysfunction, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Clinical and Imaging Evaluation of COVID-19-Related Olfactory Dysfunction

summary: This retrospective follow-up study examined the prevalence of PTSD symptoms among 903 COVID-19 patients 3 months after discharge from hospitalization. The study found that 23.5% of patients screened positive for clinically significant PTSD, with key risk factors including multiple clinical symptoms at disease onset and residual respiratory symptoms post-discharge.
paper_authors: Zhilei Shang; Xiao Pan; Suhui Cheng; Yuchen Yang; Wenjie Yan; LiangLiang Sun; Hai Huang; Yonghai Bai; Weifen Xie; Shu Xu
paper_title: Prevalence and risk factors of PTSD symptoms: a 3-month follow-up study

summary: This retrospective cohort study uses linked patient data from UK primary and secondary care to compare healthcare utilization in the 3 months before and after COVID-19 diagnosis across 7,791 individuals. The study documents increased non-elective admissions, GP attendances, and mental health contacts post-COVID, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Ben J. Murch; Sarah E. Hollier; Charlie Kenward; Richard M. Wood
paper_title: Use of linked patient data to assess the effect of Long-COVID on system-wide healthcare utilisation

summary: This prospective cohort study compared cytokine (IL-1β, IL-6, TNFα) and cortisol serum levels across four groups: never infected, infected without PASC, resolved PASC, and ongoing PASC patients. The study found no significant differences in these biomarker levels between groups, suggesting they may not be reliable markers for PASC identification.

paper_title: Cytokines (IL1β, IL6, TNFα) and serum cortisol levels may not constitute reliable biomarkers to identify individuals with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19

summary: Retrospective follow-up study of 565 severe/critical COVID-19 patients evaluating post-acute symptoms persisting 4+ weeks after symptom onset. Found 62.6% had persistent symptoms (pulmonary and neuropsychiatric most common), with obesity, ICU admission, and mechanical ventilation as risk factors.

Found that neurological, dermatological, and mood disorder symptoms persisted in >30% of patients, with women and those requiring mechanical ventilation at higher risk.

summary: Prospective cohort study following 112 severe/critical COVID-19 survivors for 6 and 12 months post-discharge to assess pulmonary function, chest imaging, and quality of life outcomes. paper_title: Six and twelve-month respiratory outcomes in a cohort of severe and critical COVID-19 survivors: A prospective monocentric study in Latin America

Most patients showed persistent olfactory dysfunction despite treatment, with 91.2% reporting subjective improvement at 10 months follow-up, though objective testing showed continued hyposmia in 71-77% of patients.

paper_title: Effect of oral zinc and steroids on long COVID hyposmia and hypogeusia

summary: This prospective longitudinal study followed COVID-19 patients over 12 months to identify predictors of clinically meaningful declines in health-related quality of life. The study found that shortness of breath, lower BMI, and history of anxiety were significant predictors of worsening HRQoL, but did not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

paper_title: Predicting Long-Term Health-Related Quality of Life in Individuals With Prior SARS-CoV-2 Infection: A 12-Month Prospective Study
paper_journal: Journal of Primary Care & Community Health

summary: A retrospective observational study characterizing persistent COVID-19 symptoms in 1,542 primary care patients in Spain between December 2020 and May 2022. The study documents symptom prevalence (12.39% at 90 days), affected systems (cardiovascular, respiratory, psychoneurological), and average symptom duration (178 days), but does not test any intervention or treatment.

paper_title: Clinical Characterization of the Persistent COVID-19 Symptoms: A Descriptive Observational Study in Primary Care
paper_journal: Journal of Primary Care & Community Health

summary: A prospective observational feasibility study of Chinese herbal medicine (CHM) delivered via telehealth to 61 patients with COVID-19-related symptoms, documenting clinical encounters, symptom outcomes, and treatment patterns. paper_journal: Global Advances in Health and Medicine

summary: Follow-up study of 329 vaccinated individuals tracking late disorders 6 months post-booster vaccination, identifying conditions possibly linked to vaccination (73.1%), long COVID (0.8%), or both (26.8%). paper_journal: Journal of Primary Care & Community Health

summary: This cross-sectional study analyzes cytokine profiles in 390 long COVID patients stratified by SARS-CoV-2 variant epoch, comparing pro-inflammatory markers (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β) across early versus later variant periods. paper_title: Pro Inflammatory Cytokines Profiles of Patients With Long COVID Differ Between Variant Epochs
paper_journal: Journal of Primary Care & Community Health

summary: Retrospective longitudinal study comparing functional outcomes (ADLs, cognitive function, clinical care needs) in 1,310 LTC home residents with COVID-19 versus 2,301 without COVID-19 over seven months post-infection. Found initially greater deterioration in ADLs and clinical care needs in COVID-positive residents, but trajectories converged over time with similar overall outcomes.

paper_title: Exploring Post-COVID-19 Functional Outcomes in Residents in Long-Term Care Homes in British Columbia, Canada

summary: Describes a novel three-tier integrated multidisciplinary NHS rehabilitation pathway in Leeds for managing long COVID in the community, comprising specialist MDT assessment, community therapy teams, and self-management support. paper_journal: Journal of Primary Care & Community Health

summary: Community-based prospective cohort study investigating short-term impacts of COVID-19 on depressive symptoms and cognitive decline in the BRAVE cohort (n=1,012). Found no significant associations between COVID-19 infection and depressive symptoms or cognitive decline at 3-4 months post-infection.
paper_authors: Mengmeng Ji; Darui Gao; Jie Liang; Yanyu Zhang; Yang Pan; Wenya Zhang; Yanjun Ma; Yongqian Wang; Chenglong Li; Yidan Zhu; Fanfan Zheng; Wuxiang Xie

paper_title: Clinico-epidemiological profile and outcome of infected health care workers during the three consecutive waves of COVID-19 pandemic: a longitudinal cohort study

paper_title: Chronic Neurocognitive, Neuropsychological, and Pulmonary Symptoms in Outpatient and Inpatient Cohorts After COVID-19 Infection

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines characteristics and healthcare utilization patterns among 10,265 U.S. primary care patients with an ICD-10-CM diagnosis code for Post-COVID-19 Condition between 2021-2023. summary: Prospective observational follow-up study tracking 83 Indian patients with moderate-to-severe COVID-19 at 2, 6, and 12 weeks post-acute infection to characterize recovery trajectories and post-COVID syndrome incidence. summary: This prospective cohort study examined how COVID-19 infection affects seminal fluid analysis parameters in 44 male participants followed over 6 months. summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing standard of care alone versus standard of care plus antivirals in 142 Vietnamese patients with mild-to-moderate COVID-19 breakthrough infection. Antivirals were not significantly associated with lower risk of residual respiratory symptoms or long COVID-19 diagnosis.
paper_authors: Hong Tham Pham; Tuong-Anh Mai-Phan; Kim-Huong Truong-Nguyen; Minh-Hoang Tran

summary: Prospective cohort study of 1,451 COVID-19 patients in Tunisia followed for 3 months to estimate post-COVID syndrome (PCS) incidence and identify risk factors. summary: This study assessed long-term cardiovascular effects of COVID-19 in 37 college students >2 months post-infection, measuring endothelial function and arterial stiffness using non-invasive vascular assessment. Results showed significantly impaired flow-mediated dilation (endothelial dysfunction) but improvement in arterial stiffness over time, with increasing blood pressure trends.

summary: Longitudinal investigation of 134 adults and children infected with SARS-CoV-2 B.1.1.7 in Norway, with follow-up at 2 and 7 months post-infection. Study documents symptom persistence rates and identifies fatigue and insomnia as common long-term complications, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Longitudinal investigation of a single variant SARS-CoV-2-outbreak in the immunologically naïve population of Ulvik, Norway

summary: This study examines erectile dysfunction in male kidney transplant recipients across four time periods, including pre- and post-COVID-19. summary: Retrospective cohort study of 2,524 Malaysian adults examining whether nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treatment reduces post-COVID condition (PCC) and improves health-related quality of life over 180 days during the Omicron wave. The study found no significant difference in PCC symptoms between treated and control groups at 3 and 6 months, though nirmatrelvir/ritonavir was associated with reduced negative emotions at 3 months but increased walking limitations.

The study found restrictive respiratory patterns in 35.5% of recovered patients and identified an association between higher viral loads (CT ≤20) and these abnormal patterns, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining 30-month longitudinal changes in glucose metabolism, endocrine, and renal functions in COVID-19 survivors stratified by vaccination status. While the study shows improved metabolic outcomes in fully vaccinated individuals, it is a passive observational analysis of vaccination records rather than an intervention trial, and does not test or evaluate a specific treatment given to long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Ceren Gür; Sezen Kumaş Solak
paper_title: Evaluation of glucose metabolism, endocrine, and renal functions following vaccination in post-COVID-19 individuals: a longitudinal retrospective single-center cohort study

summary: This retrospective cohort study compared serum RAAS component levels (ACE, ACE2, Ang1-7, AngII) between healthcare workers with and without long COVID at 3-6 months and 12 months post-infection. No statistically significant differences in RAAS markers were found between LC cases and controls, suggesting RAAS disruption is not a significant contributor to LC pathophysiology.
paper_authors: Tali Lange-Tal; Neta Tuvia; Sophie Lazar; Yarra Farajh; Tomer Bernstine; Zaid Abassi; Michael Edelstein; Kamal Abu Jabal
paper_title: Is long-term disruption of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system associated with long COVID? A retrospective cohort study among healthcare workers

summary: A four-year prospective cohort study in Saudi Arabia following 816 COVID-19 patients to identify risk factors and predictors of long COVID-19 and recovery patterns. Female sex and diabetes were strong predictors of long COVID development and delayed recovery, with persistent fatigue, post-exertional malaise, and cognitive dysfunction being most common.
paper_authors: Sanaa M. Kamal; Mohammed S. Al Qahtani; Ali Al Aseeri; Mohey El Deen Mohamed Naghib; Adul Majeed Mazroua Al Mazroua; Abdulaziz M. M. Alshamrani; Mohamed Mazroua Al Mazroua; Faisal S. F. AlHarbi
paper_title: Long COVID-19: a Four-Year prospective cohort study of risk factors, recovery, and quality of life

summary: A retrospective study of 24 long COVID patients that used 3D voxel-based morphometry brain imaging to measure cortical grey matter volume depletion at median 85 days post-infection. The study found statistically significant CGM volume reduction but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention—it is a descriptive neuroimaging study of disease correlates.
paper_authors: Ted L. Rothstein
paper_title: Cortical Grey matter volume depletion links to neurological sequelae in post COVID-19 “long haulers”

summary: Prospective cohort study characterizing sleep disorders in 189 long COVID patients, finding insomnia in 22.2% and excessive sleepiness in 3.17%. The study documents the prevalence and types of sleep symptoms as part of the long COVID clinical spectrum but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Alissa Elen Formiga Moura; Danilo Nunes Oliveira; Danielle Mesquista Torres; José Wagner Leonel Tavares-Júnior; Paulo Ribeiro Nóbrega; Pedro Braga-Neto; Manoel Alves Sobreira-Neto
paper_title: Central hypersomnia and chronic insomnia: expanding the spectrum of sleep disorders in long COVID syndrome - a prospective cohort study

summary: Prospective case-control study examining macular vessel density and foveal avascular zone (FAZ) enlargement in recovered COVID-19 patients with and without fatigue using optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA). Found significantly enlarged FAZ in non-ICU patients and fatigue groups compared to controls, suggesting retinal microvascular alterations may be associated with long COVID fatigue.
paper_authors: Spielmann J.; Pink I.; Framme C.; Tode J.; Volkmann I.
paper_title: Association of foveal avascular zone (FAZ) enlargement with SARS-CoV-2 infection and long COVID-19

summary: A patient-engaged cohort survey study of 11,328 COVID-19 hospitalized patients in Rio de Janeiro assessing long COVID prevalence 6-24 months post-discharge. The study found 71.3% reported persistent symptoms and 39.3% self-reported long COVID, with fatigue, post-exertional malaise, and cognitive impairment being most common.
paper_authors: Margareth Crisóstomo Portela; Sheyla Maria Lemos Lima; Claudia Caminha Escosteguy; Mônica Martins; Maurício Teixeira Leite de Vasconcellos; Bárbara do Nascimento Caldas; Michelle Bernardino; Natalie Perez Baginski; Gabriela Góes; Brenda Sabaine; Danielle Furtado; Marta Cavalcanti; Letícia Soares; Elisabeth Stelson; Sara Singer; Flora Cornish; Emma-Louise Aveling
paper_title: Long COVID in the population of COVID-19 hospitalized patients discharged from SUS’ hospitals in Rio de Janeiro City, Brazil: a patient-engaged cohort survey study

summary: Retrospective cohort study estimating long COVID prevalence and symptoms among 6,846 quarantined adults in Germany, finding 14.6% prevalence with fatigue, cognitive impairment, and dyspnoea as most common symptoms. Identifies chronic diseases and acute infection severity as significant risk factors but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Kira Engl; Sven Feddern; Barbara Grüne; Luis Haberstock; Annelene Kossow; Johannes Nießen; Susanne Rost; Gerhard A. Wiesmüller; Nikola Schmidt; Christine Joisten
paper_title: Prevalence, symptoms, and associated factors of long COVID: a retrospective cohort study based on data from two major German health authorities

summary: Prospective cohort study of 105 children with confirmed COVID-19 followed for 24 weeks to characterize acute disease course and long COVID outcomes. Found 15.2% developed long COVID symptoms (fatigue, hair loss, concentration issues, abdominal pain), with older children (11-16 years) and those with ongoing symptoms at 4-6 weeks at higher risk.
paper_authors: Rozhan Nabaz Mohammed Sedik
paper_title: The clinical course and outcomes of SARS-CoV-2 virus infection in children: a 24-week follow-up study in Sulaimaniyah, Iraq

summary: This study used a mobile application (NCRCC) to track daily symptom evolution in 63 Neuro-PASC patients over 12+ months post-COVID onset, classifying them as Improvers or Non-Improvers based on subjective recovery trajectories. Key findings include that women and patients with anosmia/dysgeusia were less likely to improve, and Improvers showed greater fluctuations in recovery perception with modest improvements in processing speed and sleep disturbance at 3-month follow-up.
paper_authors: Lank GK; Budhiraja S.; Gaelen JI; Mukherjee S.; Singer T.; Venkatesh A.; Jimenez M.; Miller J.; Lopez M.; Duax CJ; Blahnik D.; King D.; Hanson BA; Bawa AP; Bharadwaj S.; Batra A.; Liotta EM; Koralnik IJ
paper_title: Characterizing Neuro-PASC outcome with the mobile Neuro-COVID recovery care companion application

summary: This study examined long COVID symptoms in an Italian pediatric cohort of Tourette Syndrome patients with and without SARS-CoV-2 infection via questionnaire and clinical assessments at baseline and 3-month follow-up. While it documents the prevalence of long COVID symptoms (38.5%) and their association with worsening tics and behavioral/mood symptoms, it is observational without any intervention or treatment being tested.
paper_authors: Adriana Prato; Angela Maria Salerno; Federica Saia; Nicoletta Maugeri; Alice Zanini; Miriam Scerbo; Rita Barone; Renata Rizzo
paper_title: Symptoms compatible with long COVID in an Italian pediatric cohort of Tourette patients with and without SARS‑CoV‑2 infection: a short-term follow-up assessment

summary: A prospective longitudinal observational study assessing retinal structure and microvasculature changes in long COVID patients using swept-source OCT imaging at baseline, 1 month, and 1 year post-infection. The study documents retinal alterations but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Kefan Mou; Yuzhu Gao; Yifan Zhang; Shulei Man; Qing Chen; Hanyue Xu; Yi Chen; Ming Zhang
paper_title: Long-term retinal dysfunction following COVID-19 infection: a one-year prospective observational study

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 1,038 medical staff examining how acute-phase COVID-19 symptom trajectories predict anxiety and depression 2 years post-infection. Found that moderate and severe acute symptom trajectories were associated with significantly higher anxiety and depression risk at 2-year follow-up.
paper_authors: Jingli Wen; Lin Zhang; Ling Yuan; Kai Li; Zuoling Tang; Zhenjiang Zhang; Youde Yan
paper_title: Trajectories of symptoms in the acute phase of COVID-19 infection and their association with anxiety and depression 2 years after infection

summary: This multicenter cohort study assessed the prevalence of anxiety and depression symptoms one year after ICU admission for COVID-19 in Swedish patients during the first pandemic wave. The study found high rates of anxiety (38.1%) and depression (35.2%), with female sex identified as a predictor of depression, highlighting the need for long-term mental health support in COVID-19 ICU survivors.
paper_authors: Netha Hussain; Carina M. Samuelsson; Avril Drummond; Carina U. Persson
paper_title: Prevalence of symptoms of anxiety and depression one year after intensive care unit admission for COVID-19

summary: Longitudinal study of 1,581 UK adults examining whether pre-infection health behaviours (exercise, sleep, smoking) are risk factors for developing long COVID. Found that poor sleep quality and smoking increased odds of long COVID, while meeting physical activity guidelines reduced difficulty with self-care.
paper_authors: Elise Paul; Daisy Fancourt
paper_title: Health behaviours the month prior to COVID-19 infection and the development of self-reported long COVID and specific long COVID symptoms: a longitudinal analysis of 1581 UK adults

summary: Registry-based cohort study analyzing sick leave patterns in 11,955 Swedish COVID-19 patients over 4 months, examining predictors of prolonged sick leave and long COVID occurrence. Findings show 13.3% experienced long COVID-related sick leave, with inpatient care, prior sick leave, and older age as key predictive factors.
paper_authors: Emma Westerlind; Annie Palstam; Katharina S. Sunnerhagen; Hanna C. Persson
paper_title: Patterns and predictors of sick leave after Covid-19 and long Covid in a national Swedish cohort

summary: This retrospective cohort study analyzed medical claims data from over 1.37 million COVID-19 survivors to identify long-term health effects and their associations with social determinants of health. The study identified 36 ICD-10 codes significantly increased in the post-COVID period and found age and gender were commonly associated with long-term effects, but it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Sumit Mukherjee; Meghana Kshirsagar; Nicholas Becker; Yixi Xu; William B. Weeks; Shwetak Patel; Juan Lavista Ferres; Michael L. Jackson
paper_title: Identifying long-term effects of SARS-CoV-2 and their association with social determinants of health in a cohort of over one million COVID-19 survivors

summary: This retrospective cohort study analyzed 130,010 pediatric COVID-19 cases from a database to compare Emergency Department utilization between children with and without long COVID symptoms (defined as symptoms occurring 30-180 days post-infection). Children with long COVID symptoms had significantly higher odds of ED visits (OR: 2.52), with chest pain and electrolyte disturbances showing the strongest associations.
paper_authors: Pranav Bhimani; Adina Scheinfeld; Mangala Rajan
paper_title: Emergency department utilization among children with Long COVID symptoms: a COVID-19 research consortium study

summary: Registry-based cohort study examining recurrent sick leave patterns in 11,955 Swedish COVID-19 patients during the first pandemic wave (March–August 2020). Found that 2.0% experienced recurrent sick leave, with older age and female sex as risk factors, but no intervention or treatment was tested.
paper_authors: Annie Palstam; Emma Westerlind; Katharina S. Sunnerhagen; Hanna C. Persson
paper_title: Recurrent sick leave after COVID-19: investigating the first wave of the pandemic in a comprehensive Swedish registry-based study

summary: A longitudinal cohort study of 5,727 Belgian adults followed from SARS-CoV-2 infection to three months post-infection, assessing health-related quality of life (HRQoL) using the EQ-5D-5L questionnaire. The study found significant HRQoL decline during acute infection and persistent decline at three months specifically among those reporting post-COVID-19 condition (PCC), with fatigue, headache, and memory problems as the main symptom drivers.
paper_authors: Pierre Smith; Robby De Pauw; Dieter Van Cauteren; Stefaan Demarest; Sabine Drieskens; Laura Cornelissen; Brecht Devleesschauwer; Karin De Ridder; Rana Charafeddine
paper_title: Post COVID-19 condition and health-related quality of life: a longitudinal cohort study in the Belgian adult population

summary: Prospective matched cohort study examining the prevalence and burden of long COVID among sheltered people experiencing homelessness in Seattle between September 2020–April 2022. Found that 77% of COVID-19-positive cases reported symptoms 30–59 days post-infection, with fatigue and rhinorrhea most common, though few accessed medical care; risk of symptoms was 5.4 times higher in COVID-19 cases versus controls.
paper_authors: Sarah N. Cox; Emily M. Scott; Julia H. Rogers; Eric J. Chow; Jessica K. Wasse; Marco Carone; James P. Hughes; Helen Y. Chu
paper_title: Burden of long COVID among adults experiencing sheltered homelessness: a longitudinal cohort study in King County, WA between September 2020—April 2022

summary: Population-based cohort study comparing health outcomes in 350 individuals with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection to 4467 uninfected controls at ~1.5 years follow-up. Infected individuals showed significantly higher rates of persistent symptoms (smell/taste disorders, shortness of breath, fatigue, myalgia), incident diseases (liver, lung, cardiovascular), and worse quality of life measures.
paper_authors: Christin Heidemann; Giselle Sarganas; Yong Du; Beate Gaertner; Christina Poethko-Müller; Caroline Cohrdes; Sein Schmidt; Martin Schlaud; Christa Scheidt-Nave
paper_title: Long-term health consequences among individuals with SARS-CoV-2 infection compared to individuals without infection: results of the population-based cohort study CoMoLo Follow-up

summary: This study examined immune and endothelial biomarkers in 112 participants from Riverside County across healthy controls, moderate infection, severe infection, and recovery groups to identify factors associated with COVID-19 severity and long-term outcomes. Results showed infection-related changes in immune cells, cytokines, and endothelial markers, with long COVID symptoms persisting up to 11 months post-infection, though pulmonary function recovered.

paper_title: Health disparities in COVID-19: immune and vascular changes are linked to disease severity and persist in a high-risk population in Riverside County, California

summary: This retrospective cohort study evaluated the frequency and patient-reported effectiveness of symptomatic therapies in 200 post-COVID patients at a German specialty center, with 82.5% follow-up response rate. Beta-blockers showed highest effectiveness (31.5% strong improvement), followed by antibiotics (29.6%), while plasmapheresis was perceived as strongly effective by 33.0% of users.

paper_title: Utilization frequency and patient-reported effectiveness of symptomatic therapies in post-COVID syndrome

summary: A 2.5-year prospective cohort study of 130 non-hospitalised adults with post-COVID-19 condition assessing physical function, activity levels, and mental health outcomes. summary: Retrospective cohort study examining the association between Post-COVID Syndrome (PCS) and self-stigma among 759 Israeli adults who tested positive for COVID-19. Found that 25.2% met PCS criteria and individuals with PCS reported significantly higher levels of COVID-19-related self-stigma (p < 0.001), with OR = 2.5.

summary: Population-based surveillance study in Kenya evaluating the burden and risk factors for long COVID among 832 previously SARS-CoV-2 infected participants. summary: This study follows 257 convalescent COVID-19 patients from acute infection through post-discharge recovery, characterizing four distinct trajectory subgroups based on pneumonia lesion progression and lymphocyte counts. summary: Retrospective observational study examining the utility and safety of bronchoscopy as a diagnostic procedure in 45 patients with suspected post-acute COVID-19 sequelae in Italy. Bronchoscopy was used diagnostically to evaluate tracheal complications and persistent parenchymal infiltrates, not as a treatment intervention.

paper_title: Health-related quality of life and radiological and functional lung changes of patients with COVID-19 Pneumonia 3 and 10 months after discharge

summary: A prospective cohort study following 94 COVID-19 patients with severe pneumonia for 12 months post-discharge to characterize respiratory sequelae and functional recovery. Most patients showed improvement in dyspnea, quality of life, and exercise capacity by 12 months, though pulmonary fibrotic-like changes persisted in some patients.

COVID-19 survivors showed similar recovery in lung function and exercise capacity to SARS survivors but exhibited different patterns of psychological recovery over time.

Found clinically meaningful dyspnea in ~46-49% at 12 months, associated with worse sleep, mood, and quality of life, with early dyspnea and depression predicting persistent symptoms.

paper_title: Post-COVID dyspnea: prevalence, predictors, and outcomes in a longitudinal, prospective cohort

Corticosteroid treatment was associated with lower diffusion capacity for carbon monoxide but no difference in health-related quality of life.
paper_authors: Mari Roël; Anna Schandl; Sandra Jonmarker; Anders Hedman; Gisela Vogel; Eva Joelsson-Alm; Maria Cronhjort; Pernilla Darlington
paper_title: Corticosteroids and long-term pulmonary function after critical illness due to COVID-19– a single-center cohort study

Found impaired lung function in 50% of adults and 85% of children, with most recovering by 5 months, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

Found that a significant subset exhibited persistent EVin correlated with unfavorable cardiovascular responses, suggesting prognostic value for long-term post-COVID monitoring.

paper_title: The impact of SARS-COV-2 infection on menstruation

summary: Follow-up study comparing asthma control in Hong Kong patients with and without COVID-19 history across different viral variants (BA.2 to XBB). paper_title: Asthma control after recovery from mild to moderate COVID-19: from Omicron BA.2 to XBB– from a cohort in a university hospital in Hong Kong

summary: This retrospective cohort study examined healthcare utilization and medical expenditures for 250,514 COVID-19 patients over 6 months post-diagnosis using claims data. It found that COVID-19 diagnosis was associated with significantly increased healthcare visits and monthly costs, with effects persisting longer in older age groups, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Antonios M. Koumpias; David Schwartzman; Owen Fleming

summary: This retrospective cohort study used German health insurance claims data to compare healthcare costs and mortality between COVID-19 patients and matched controls from 2020-2021. summary: This retrospective cohort study uses Ontario health administrative data to estimate incidence of post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) following introduction of a diagnostic code in January 2023, and compares demographic characteristics and healthcare utilization between individuals with and without the PCC code. The study found 7,343 individuals received a PCC code, with substantially increased healthcare utilization post-diagnosis (100.61 vs 14.59 encounters per person-year pre-pandemic), but identifies underrepresentation of PCC cases in the coding system.

summary: Prospective cohort study examining financial hardship outcomes 18 months after COVID-19 infection among US Veterans, comparing those with and without COVID-19 history. summary: This prospective cohort study tracked 4,721 NHS healthcare workers at 12 and 32 months post-baseline to examine COVID-19-related sickness absence and predictors of long-term absence among those with long COVID symptoms. summary: Retrospective observational study following 797 COVID-19 hospitalized patients for 6 months after discharge to identify and quantify long-term sequelae.
