paper_authors: Joan Carles Domingo; Federica Battistini; Begoña Cordobilla; Maria Cleofé Zaragozá; Ramón Sanmartin-Sentañes; Jose Alegre-Martin; Trinitat Cambras; Jesus Castro-Marrero
paper_title: Association of circulating biomarkers with illness severity measures differentiates myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome and post-COVID-19 condition: a prospective pilot cohort study

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining the incidence of new-onset chronic fatigue syndrome/myalgic encephalomyelitis (CFS/ME) up to 4 years following SARS-CoV-2 infection in 147,377 patients. COVID-19 infection was associated with significantly elevated risk of developing CFS/ME (HR 1.46–1.56 vs. non-COVID controls), with higher risk among females and patients with autoimmune or anxiety disorders.
paper_authors: Roham Hadidchi; Bhakti Patel; Japji Madan; Alex Liu; Sonya Henry; Tim Q. Duong
paper_title: Elevated risk of new-onset chronic fatigue syndrome/myalgic encephalomyelitis up to four years after SARS-CoV-2 infection

summary: A prospective cohort study of 29 healthcare workers with post-COVID fatigue comparing brain activation and motor cortex excitability to 24 healthy controls over 6 months. The study found that fatigue correlates with reduced prefrontal and motor cortex activation, with recovery in motor cortex excitability linked to fatigue improvement.
paper_authors: Tao Han; Chunqiu Dai; Ying Liang; Xiaodong Lin; Ming Gao; Xinyu Liu; Xiangbo Wu; Yuheng Lu; Xiao Xi; Fei Tian; Chenguang Zhao; Xiaolong Sun; Hua Yuan
paper_title: PFC/M1 activation and excitability: a longitudinal cohort study on fatigue symptoms in healthcare workers post-COVID-19

summary: This retrospective cohort study examined 5,162 matched pairs of type 2 diabetes patients to evaluate whether SGLT2 inhibitor use reduces long COVID risk. SGLT2 inhibitor users showed significantly lower risk of long COVID and associated symptoms including cognitive impairment, pain, headache, and anxiety/depression.
paper_authors: Han-Wei Yeh; Chung-Hsien Chaou; Shun-Fa Yang; Yu-Hsun Wang; Yu-Hsiang Kuan; Chao-Bin Yeh
paper_title: SGLT2 inhibitors prevent long-COVID-associated cognitive and pain symptoms in type 2 diabetes patients

summary: This study develops and validates a prognostic nomogram model to predict long COVID risk in hospitalized COVID-19 patients using clinical variables and biomarkers. It is an observational cohort study focused on risk prediction rather than testing a treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Lu-Cheng Fang; Xiao-Ping Ming; Wan-Yue Cai; Yi-Fan Hu; Bin Hao; Jiang-Hao Wu; Aikebaier Tuohuti; Xiong Chen
paper_title: Development and validation of a prognostic model for assessing long COVID risk following Omicron wave—a large population-based cohort study

summary: This study investigates the prevalence and persistence of autoantibodies (ANA and aPL) in 248 COVID-19 patients with oxygen demand admitted to a South Korean hospital. While the authors note that autoantibody persistence may be related to long-term sequelae, the paper does not study long COVID patients or interventions—it is a cross-sectional serological study of acute COVID-19 patients.
paper_authors: Se Ju Lee; Taejun Yoon; Jang Woo Ha; Jinnam Kim; Ki Hyun Lee; Jung Ah Lee; Chang Hyup Kim; Sang-Won Lee; Jung Ho Kim; Jin Young Ahn; Nam Su Ku; Jun Yong Choi; Joon-Sup Yeom; Su Jin Jeong
paper_title: Prevalence, clinical significance, and persistence of autoantibodies in COVID-19

summary: Prospective study from Czechia that stratifies post-COVID patients into clinical groups based on respiratory symptoms and objective signs of pulmonary involvement at three months post-infection. Found that nearly half of outpatients and one-third of hospitalized patients had objective pulmonary signs without subjective respiratory symptoms, highlighting heterogeneity in post-COVID presentation.
paper_authors: Mikulas Skala; Michal Svoboda; Michal Kopecky; Eva Kocova; Martin Hyrsl; Michal Homolac; Viktor Chrobok; Pavel Bostik; Miroslav Fajfr; Petr Prasil; Stanislav Plisek; Radek Sleha; Vladimir Koblizek
paper_title: Heterogeneity of post-COVID impairment: interim analysis of a prospective study from Czechia

summary: This longitudinal observational study examined how pre-existing medical conditions impact the severity of post-COVID syndrome among healthcare and social services workers in Germany. The analysis identified respiratory, cardiovascular, and urogenital diseases as significant risk factors for severe PCS, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Tiana Barnekow; Claudia Peters; Madeleine Dulon; Albert Nienhaus
paper_title: Impact of pre-existing conditions on the severity of post-COVID syndrome among workers in healthcare and social services in Germany
paper_journal: Journal of Occupational Medicine and Toxicology

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines changes in pulmonary function (spirometry) in 321 healthcare workers before and after COVID-19 infection between 2020-2022, stratified by vaccination status. While the paper confirms that SARS-CoV-2 infection causes measurable respiratory decline (especially in FVC and FEV1) and that vaccination provides protection against these effects, it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention—it is purely an observational assessment of infection-related changes and vaccination's protective effects.
paper_authors: Lorenzo Ippoliti; Luca Coppeta; Giuseppina Somma; Giuseppe Bizzarro; Francesco Borelli; Teresa Crispino; Cristiana Ferrari; Ilaria Iannuzzi; Andrea Mazza; Agostino Paolino; Andrea Magrini; Antonio Pietroiusti
paper_title: Pulmonary function assessment after COVID-19 in vaccinated healthcare workers
paper_journal: Journal of Occupational Medicine and Toxicology

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines the incidence and risk factors of acute transverse myelitis (ATM) in SARS-CoV-2 infected patients versus non-infected controls using TriNetX database records from 2020-2023. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 infection complications and vaccine safety, not long COVID sequelae or treatment interventions.
paper_authors: Jack Yu-Shuo Lu; Shun-Fa Yang; Shu-Ling Tzeng; Yuan-Ti Lee; Yu-Hsun Wang; Chao-Bin Yeh
paper_title: Acute transverse myelitis and associate vaccine complication in SARS-CoV-2 patients: a retrospective cohort analysis in real-world database

summary: Prospective matched household cohort study comparing persistent symptoms in children 6-12 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection versus uninfected controls. Found no significant differences in post-acute sequelae between groups, suggesting PASC is uncommon in previously healthy children after mild infection.
paper_authors: Judith G. C. Sluiter-Post; Elandri Fourie; Joanne G. Wildenbeest; Steven F. L. van Lelyveld; Patricia C. J. L. Bruijning-Verhagen; Marianne A. van Houten
paper_title: Long term sequelae after SARS-CoV-2 infection in children: a household study

summary: Longitudinal observational study of 114 post-COVID patients who underwent inpatient rehabilitation, assessing work ability and return to work before rehabilitation and 12 months after. Fatigue was identified as the main predictor of reduced work ability, with 48.6% of patients returning to work 12 months post-rehabilitation.
paper_authors: Katrin Müller; Iris Poppele; Marcel Ottiger; Alois Wastlhuber; Rainer-Christian Weber; Michael Stegbauer; Torsten Schlesinger
paper_title: Long-term course and factors influencing work ability and return to work in post-COVID patients 12 months after inpatient rehabilitation
paper_journal: Journal of Occupational Medicine and Toxicology

summary: Retrospective comparative analysis of 84 post-COVID-19 patients with osteonecrosis of the femoral head, examining COVID-19 factors and corticosteroid regimens associated with disease severity. The study found that cumulative steroid dose was the primary predictor of ONFH severity, with combined corticosteroid use accelerating symptom onset.
paper_authors: Jichang Seong; Abduaziz Babakulov; Saodat Asilova; Babamukhamedova Shakhnoza; Makhmudova Nodira; Akbarjon Mirzayev
paper_title: Osteonecrosis of the femoral head in post-COVID-19 patients: a retrospective comparative study
paper_journal: Journal of Orthopaedic Surgery and Research

summary: A multicenter observational study evaluating Chinese Medicine (CM) treatment effects in 150 post-COVID-19 patients discharged from Hong Kong hospitals over 3-6 months. Results showed improvements in clinical symptoms, lung function (6MWT and LFQ scores), and body constitution balance, particularly in patients without specific CM syndromes.
paper_authors: Linda Li-Dan Zhong; Yi-Ping Wong; Chor-Yin Leung; Bo Peng; Zhi-Xiu Lin; Vivian Chi-Woon Wong Taam; Yi Luo; Hai-Yong Chen; Chao-Dong Chao; Chor-Fung Wong; Freddie Shung-Chi Tam; Kui Chan; Kwan-Yiu Lee; Lai-Fun Ho; Alan Yat-Lun Wong; Chi-Fung Choy; Bacon Fung-Leung Ng; Rowena How-Wan Wong; Yi-Bin Feng; Ching Liong; Zhao-Xiang Bian
paper_title: Effects of Chinese medicine for COVID-19 rehabilitation: a multicenter observational study

summary: This longitudinal case-control study compared COVID-19 outcomes and long-term consequences in 15 patients with hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia (HED) versus 149 age-matched controls. HED patients with complete ectodysplasin A pathway disruption showed higher rates of chronic fatigue (83% vs 21%) and hair loss (64% vs 13%) following COVID-19, suggesting genetic factors influence post-COVID syndrome risk.
paper_authors: Verena Hennig; Wolfgang Schuh; Antje Neubert; Dirk Mielenz; Hans-Martin Jäck; Holm Schneider
paper_title: Increased risk of chronic fatigue and hair loss following COVID-19 in individuals with hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia

summary: Retrospective descriptive cohort study of 92 children evaluated 1-3 months after COVID-19 onset to characterize long COVID symptoms. Found that 51% of children had persistent symptoms (tiredness, anosmia, headaches), with higher prevalence in ages 10-18.
paper_authors: Liene Smane; Ieva Roge; Zanda Pucuka; Jana Pavare
paper_title: Clinical features of pediatric post-acute COVID-19: a descriptive retrospective follow-up study

summary: An Italian cohort study assessing the prevalence of Long COVID-19 in 629 primary care pediatric patients and 60 hospitalized patients 8-36 weeks post-infection. Found cumulative incidence of 24.3% in primary care and 58% in hospitalized patients, with symptom patterns varying by age group.
paper_authors: Gianfranco Trapani; Giuseppe Verlato; Enrico Bertino; Giulia Maiocco; Roberta Vesentini; Alessia Spadavecchia; Angelica Dessì; Vassilios Fanos
paper_title: Long COVID-19 in children: an Italian cohort study

summary: Prospective controlled cohort study of 213 COVID-19 patients (ICU-treated, ward-treated, home-isolated) and 48 controls assessed cognitive functioning 6 months post-acute phase using comprehensive neuropsychological testing. ICU-treated and ward-treated patients showed significantly worse cognitive performance in attention, executive functions, and memory domains compared to home-isolated patients and non-COVID controls.
paper_authors: Henriikka Ollila; Riikka Pihlaja; Sanna Koskinen; Annamari Tuulio-Henriksson; Viljami Salmela; Marjaana Tiainen; Laura Hokkanen; Johanna Hästbacka
paper_title: Long-term cognitive functioning is impaired in ICU-treated COVID-19 patients: a comprehensive controlled neuropsychological study

summary: Multicenter cohort study examining the relationship between dehydration during acute COVID-19 infection and long-term physical symptoms in 374 ICU patients, with validation in 1,052 additional patients. Findings show dehydration triggers an aestivation response associated with protein degradation and is more strongly linked to physical long-COVID symptoms than mental symptoms.
paper_authors: Hultström M.; Lipcsey M.; Morrison DR; Nakanishi T.; Butler-Laporte G.; Chen Y.; Yoshiji S.; Forgetta V.; Farjoun Y.; Wallin E.; Larsson IM; Larsson A.; Marton A.; Titze JM; Nihlén S.; Richards JB; Frithiof R.
paper_title: Dehydration is associated with production of organic osmolytes and predicts physical long-term symptoms after COVID-19: a multicenter cohort study

summary: Retrospective study of 1,243 children post-SARS-CoV-2 infection examining the effect of nutritional supplements (lactoferrin and multi-element products) on long COVID symptom persistence. Multi-element products alone or combined with lactoferrin were associated with lower risk of persistent long COVID at 6-month follow-up compared to lactoferrin alone.
paper_authors: Rosa Morello; Cristina De Rose; Laura Martino; Francesca Raffaelli; Giuseppe Zampino; Piero Valentini; Danilo Buonsenso
paper_title: Role of nutrient supplements in children with post-COVID condition: a retrospective preliminary observation and narrative review

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing antidepressant initiation rates in children/adolescents with long COVID versus those with COVID only using administrative health claims data. Found that long COVID cases had significantly higher risk of antidepressant initiation (adjusted-RR: 1.40), but this is an observational study of treatment patterns rather than a trial evaluating a specific intervention.
paper_authors: Phuong TM Tran; Alejandro Amill-Rosario; Susan dosReis
paper_title: Antidepressant treatment initiation among children and adolescents with acute versus long COVID: a large retrospective cohort study
paper_journal: Child and Adolescent Psychiatry and Mental Health

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing polysomnographic findings in 92 Prader-Willi syndrome patients before and after COVID-19 infection (57 infected, 35 controls). Study documents persistent pulmonary impairment three months post-infection, including lower oxygen saturation and increased hypopnea, without testing any interventions or treatments.
paper_authors: Sina Braun; Constanze Laemmer; Sandra Schulte; Bettina Gohlke
paper_title: Retrospective longitudinal study on the long-term impact of COVID-19 infection on polysomnographic evaluation in patients with Prader-Willi syndrome

summary: This study characterizes neuropsychological dysfunction in COVID-19 ICU survivors 12 months after discharge, finding objective cognitive impairment in 30% and common emotional disturbances. It is an observational assessment study without any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for a treatment trials meta-analysis.

paper_title: Objective and subjective cognition in survivors of COVID-19 one year after ICU discharge: the role of demographic, clinical, and emotional factors

summary: Retrospective analysis of acute kidney injury (AKI) in 42 children with multisystem inflammatory syndrome post-COVID (MIS-C), examining prevalence, severity, and management outcomes. While post-COVID related, this paper studies acute complications during the immediate post-infection period rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-months later), and does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Hanan El-Halaby; Riham Eid; Ahmed Elagamy; Ahmed El-Hussiny; Fatma Moustafa; Ayman Hammad; Mayada Zeid
paper_title: A retrospective analysis of acute kidney injury in children with post-COVID-19 multisystem inflammatory syndrome: insights into promising outcomes

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing healthcare service utilization between 65,548 COVID-19-positive children aged 1-16 years and matched controls during the 3-6 months post-infection. Found statistically significant increases in mental health referrals and medication prescriptions, though the absolute risk differences were small.
paper_authors: Ziv Hersh; Yiska Loewenberg Weisband; Ariel Bogan; Adir Leibovich; Uri Obolski; Daniel Nevo; Ran Gilad-Bachrach
paper_title: Impact of Long-COVID in children: a large cohort study
paper_journal: Child and Adolescent Psychiatry and Mental Health

summary: Prospective observational cohort study following 167 children hospitalized with acute SARS-CoV-2 infection for up to 12 months post-discharge to characterize long COVID manifestations. Found 16.5% reported long COVID symptoms including weight loss, fatigue, cough, and sleep disturbances, with higher frequency in Omicron-infected children.
paper_authors: Valeria Calcaterra; Veronica Maria Tagi; Enza D’Auria; Alessia Lai; Sara Zanelli; Chiara Montanari; Elia Maria Biganzoli; Giuseppe Marano; Elisa Borghi; Valentina Massa; Agostino Riva; Gianvincenzo Zuccotti
paper_title: Long-term effects of SARS-CoV-2 infection in hospitalized children: findings from an Italian single-center study

summary: This cross-sectional survey of 2,919 adults infected with SARS-CoV-2 investigates the relationship between physical activity status (before and after infection) and long COVID symptom prevalence. The study finds that maintaining physical activity is associated with reduced odds of long COVID symptoms across musculoskeletal, neurological, and respiratory domains (7% overall reduction in symptom likelihood).

paper_title: Physical activity status prevents symptoms of long covid: Sulcovid-19 survey
paper_journal: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation

summary: Longitudinal observational study measuring telomere length in 49 COVID-19 ICU survivors at baseline and 1 year post-discharge. Patients with longer ICU stays or requiring mechanical ventilation showed greater telomere shortening and increased risk of cellular senescence and lung complications.
paper_authors: Ana Virseda-Berdices; Raquel Behar-Lagares; Oscar Martínez-González; Rafael Blancas; Soraya Bueno-Bustos; Oscar Brochado-Kith; Eva Manteiga; María J. Mallol Poyato; Blanca López Matamala; Carmen Martín Parra; Salvador Resino; María Á. Jiménez-Sousa; Amanda Fernández-Rodríguez
paper_title: Longer ICU stay and invasive mechanical ventilation accelerate telomere shortening in COVID-19 patients 1 year after recovery

summary: This nationwide Swedish cohort study followed ICU patients admitted with acute COVID-19 during the first wave, tracking outcomes through October 2020 with a median follow-up of 183 days. The study found that men had higher mortality risk than women in the 90+ days post-ICU period, but focuses on acute disease severity and mortality rather than long COVID symptoms or interventions.
paper_authors: Erik Zettersten; Lars Engerström; Max Bell; Gabriella Jäderling; Johan Mårtensson; Linda Block; Emma Larsson
paper_title: Long-term outcome after intensive care for COVID-19: differences between men and women—a nationwide cohort study

summary: This observational study examines associations between sedentary behavior and physical activity levels with perceived physical capacity, quality of life, and fatigue in 15 people with post-COVID condition. The study found that greater time in moderate/vigorous physical activity was moderately associated with better perceived physical capacity and lower fatigue, but does not evaluate an active treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Elin Östlind; Åsa B. Tornberg; Elisabeth Ekstrand; Iben Axén; Christina Brogårdh; Agneta Malmgren Fänge; Kjerstin Stigmar; Eva Ekvall Hansson
paper_title: Sedentary behaviour and level of physical activity among people with post COVID-19 condition: associated factors and changes over time

summary: This cross-sectional study compared 34 long COVID patients (9 months to 5 years post-infection) with 26 recovered controls, assessing clinical symptoms and immune profiles in a sex-disaggregated manner. Females showed higher symptom burden (fatigue, neurocognitive complaints) with reduced CD8+ T cell cytotoxicity, while males displayed elevated TNF-α, suggesting sex-specific immune pathways underlying long COVID persistence.
paper_authors: José Feliz; Juliana Gonçalves; Carolina Cabedo; José Brito; Maria Gamas; Maria Inês Neves; Helena Soares
paper_title: Long-term sex differences in symptoms and immune profile in long COVID

summary: Population-level study comparing medically certified sick leave and primary healthcare consultations in Norway in 2023 against pre-pandemic trends using Bayesian regression. Found significant excess sick leave associated with general weakness/tiredness and respiratory symptoms consistent with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19, but does not study any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Richard Aubrey White; Chi Zhang; Beatriz Valcarcel Salamanca; Aslaug Angelsen; Dinastry Pramadita Zakiudin; Aristomo Andries; Saranda Kabashi; Lene Lehmann Moberg
paper_title: Aberrations in medically certified sick leave and primary healthcare consultations in Norway in 2023 compared to pre-COVID-19-pandemic trends

summary: A prospective observational cohort study of 263 long COVID patients (54.4% female) undergoing outpatient pulmonary rehabilitation, assessing sex-specific differences in response to treatment. Women showed greater symptom burden (dyspnea, lower lung function) and lower remission rates (19.4% vs 38.5% in men) despite significant improvements in all outcomes across both sexes.
paper_authors: Alexander Kautzky; Stephan Nopp; Dietlinde Gattinger; Milos Petrovic; Martin Antlinger; Dustin Schomacker; Alexandra Kautzky-Willer; Ralf Harun Zwick
paper_title: Sex differences of post-Covid patients undergoing outpatient pulmonary rehabilitation

summary: Single-center prospective cohort study following 32 COVID-19 ICU survivors at 3 months post-discharge to assess physical, cognitive, psychological, and biological outcomes. paper_authors: Rousseau AF; Minguet P.; Colson C.; Kellens I.; Chaabane S.; Delanaye P.; Cavalier E.; Chase JG; Lambermont B.; Misset B.
paper_title: Post-intensive care syndrome after a critical COVID-19: cohort study from a Belgian follow-up clinic

summary: Prospective cohort study following 230 COVID-19 recovered patients for 1 year post-discharge to assess clinical status and identify recovery-related risk factors. Found persistent pulmonary dysfunction (35.4% diffusion impairment), extrapulmonary manifestations (fatigue, sleep disorders, anxiety, depression), and abnormal imaging in 63.5%, with disease severity and demographics predicting outcomes.

Researchers compared biomarkers (oxidative stress markers, fibrosis indicators) between COVID-19 ARDS and non-ARDS patients, finding that redox imbalance correlates with early fibroproliferation and predicts mortality and post-discharge lung impairment.

paper_title: Pulmonary redox imbalance drives early fibroproliferative response in moderate/severe coronavirus disease-19 acute respiratory distress syndrome and impacts long-term lung abnormalities

summary: Population-based cross-sectional study examining the relationship between county-level social vulnerability (using the Minority Health Social Vulnerability Index) and long COVID prevalence among Michigan adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. Finds that medical vulnerability is associated with higher long COVID diagnosis rates, but overall social vulnerability is not significantly associated with long COVID after adjustment for covariates.

paper_title: Minority health social vulnerability index and long COVID illness among a statewide, population-based study of adults with polymerase chain reaction-confirmed SARS-CoV-2

summary: Population-based cohort study tracking 12,925 SARS-CoV-2 positive individuals in Bangladesh over two years to determine incidence, characteristics, and recovery of post-COVID-19 conditions. Reports 3.6% PCC incidence, 1.92% case-fatality rate, and identifies geographical distribution, vaccination, and comorbidities as significant predictors of morbidity.

paper_title: Two-year epidemiology of post-COVID-19 conditions in Bangladesh: a cohort study of post-COVID-19 from 12,925 SARS-CoV-2 cases between July and December 2021–2023 in Bangladesh

summary: This nationwide cohort study investigates the association between weight gain during the pandemic and cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk in COVID-19 patients versus controls. The study found that COVID-19 patients who gained weight had significantly higher CVD risk compared to those who maintained stable weight, but does not evaluate any active treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Su Kyoung Lee; Yohwan Lim; Seogsong Jeong; Hyun Wook Han
paper_title: COVID-19-related cardiovascular disease risk due to weight gain: a nationwide cohort study

summary: Prospective cohort study comparing long-term health-related quality of life and persistent symptoms between COVID-19 patients and test-negative controls during the Omicron period in Japan using EQ-5D-5L questionnaires. paper_title: Comparison of long-term health-related quality of life and symptoms between COVID-19 patients and test-negative controls during the Omicron-predominant period in Japan

summary: Population-level analysis of Norwegian primary healthcare consultations in 2024 compared to pre-pandemic trends, examining whether excess consultations for fatigue, psychological symptoms, and other conditions align with post-acute COVID-19 sequelae. Found 7.1% relative excess in consultations, with fatigue and psychological complaints showing the largest increases, though the study observes patterns rather than evaluating any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Excess primary healthcare consultations in Norway in 2024 compared to pre-COVID-19-pandemic baseline trends

summary: This study follows mechanically ventilated COVID-19 survivors over 2 years to track post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) trajectories and functional recovery. Glucocorticoid-treated patients showed significantly better improvement in pulmonary function (static lung volumes, DLCO) and radiological findings compared to controls.

paper_title: The effectiveness of glucocorticoid treatment in post-COVID-19 pulmonary involvement

summary: A longitudinal cohort study of COVID-19 survivors from the first domestic outbreak in Da Nang, Vietnam, following 362 hospitalized cases at 6 and 16 months post-infection. The study characterized clinical features and long-term health outcomes including long COVID symptoms, which persisted in 72% at 6 months and 63.5% at 16 months, with higher prevalence in females and adults.

paper_title: Characteristics and long-term health outcomes of the first domestic COVID-19 outbreak cases in Da Nang, Vietnam: a longitudinal cohort study

summary: Registry study of 999 COVID-19 positive patients documenting daily symptom severity and progression over 28 days during acute infection. While 60% reported symptoms at day 28, this is acute COVID-19 follow-up, not post-COVID/long COVID treatment or intervention research.
paper_authors: Emma Brinkley; Kendall Knuth; Tom Kwon; Christina Mack; Heidi Leister-Tebbe; Weihand Bao; Matthew W. Reynolds; Nancy Dreyer
paper_title: Daily COVID-19 symptom assessment over 28 days – findings from a daily direct-to-patient registry of COVID-19 positive patients

summary: Prospective study of 2,899 hospital staff in China documenting epidemiological characteristics of Omicron infection and associated long COVID symptoms (4.27% experienced fatigue, brain fog, or both). No treatment intervention tested; paper is observational epidemiology focused on infection rates and symptom prevalence in healthcare workers.
paper_authors: Li Tang; Yeyuan Wang; Xue Li; Liu Yang; Yingjuan Luo; Chunrong Li; Yulei He
paper_title: Epidemiological characteristics of first-time SARS-CoV-2 Omicron infection among hospital staff in Chengdu, China
paper_journal: Journal of Health, Population and Nutrition

summary: This prospective longitudinal study follows 328 COVID-19 patients over 6 months, identifying three symptom-based clusters of long COVID and assessing their associations with health-related quality of life and work productivity outcomes. The study observes natural symptom patterns and vaccination status without assigning any treatment intervention to participants.

paper_title: Associations between symptom-based long COVID clusters and long-term quality of life, work and daily activities among individuals testing positive for SARS-CoV-2 at a national retail pharmacy

summary: Prospective cohort study following 41 COVID-19 ICU survivors for 12 months post-discharge to assess health-related quality of life and post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) outcomes. Found persistent severe fatigue, respiratory impairment, and 60% reduction in overall HRQoL at follow-up, with 93% of patients meeting PICS criteria.

paper_title: Health-related quality of life, physical and mental capacity at one year follow up of COVID-19 ICU patients: A prospective cohort study

summary: Longitudinal observational study of 328 outpatients with COVID-19 during Omicron, tracking long COVID symptoms, quality of life, and work productivity over 6 months in relation to vaccination status. Boosted participants showed fewer and less durable symptoms at month 6 compared to unvaccinated and primed groups, with better quality of life outcomes.

paper_title: Impact of COVID-19 and effects of booster vaccination with BNT162b2 on six-month long COVID symptoms, quality of life, work productivity and activity impairment during Omicron

summary: This study compares clinical characteristics and outcomes of Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) cases triggered by COVID-19 versus other origins in 29 patients. While it includes post-COVID patients, the focus is on a specific neurological complication (GBS) rather than long COVID as a primary syndrome, and it is observational without treatment intervention.

paper_title: Is there a difference between GBS triggered by COVID-19 and those of other origins?

The study found comparable frequencies of post-acute COVID-19 between ARD and non-ARD groups with similar symptom patterns, concluding that immune disturbances from ARD do not significantly influence post-acute COVID-19 development.

paper_title: Post-acute COVID-19 in three doses vaccinated autoimmune rheumatic diseases patients: frequency and pattern of this condition

paper_journal: Egyptian Journal of Radiology and Nuclear Medicine

summary: Retrospective study of 80 COVID-19 survivors examining early detection of post-COVID lung fibrosis via CT imaging and identifying risk factors (age, smoking, mechanical ventilation). No treatment intervention was tested; the study proposes early detection as a prevention strategy but does not evaluate any therapeutic intervention.
paper_authors: Rasha Mostafa Mohamed Ali; Mai Bahgat Ibrahim Ghonimy
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 pneumonia lung fibrosis: a worrisome sequelae in surviving patients
paper_journal: Egyptian Journal of Radiology and Nuclear Medicine

summary: A retrospective study of 192 post-COVID-19 patients assessing CT imaging abnormalities in the lungs at least 4 weeks after infection, using qualitative and semiquantitative scoring methods. The study documents the prevalence and severity of pulmonary sequelae (ground glass opacities, reticulations, consolidations) and correlates imaging findings with spirometric measurements, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Kurian C. Eapen; Leena Robinson Vimala; Barney Isaac; Aparna Irodi
paper_title: Surveying the aftermath: a qualitative and semiquantitative study of post-COVID-19 sequelae in the lungs
paper_journal: Egyptian Journal of Radiology and Nuclear Medicine

summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 81 COVID-19 pneumonia survivors with chest CT imaging at medium-term follow-up (≥3 months) to assess lung abnormality resolution rates and predictors of persistent changes. Nearly half (43.2%) had residual lung opacities, with ground glass opacity and parenchymal bands being most common; older age, higher BMI, comorbidities, and ICU admission predicted persistent abnormalities.

paper_title: Medium-term chest computed tomography (CT) follow-up of COVID-19 pneumonia patients after recovery to assess the rate of resolution and determine the potential predictors of persistent lung changes
paper_journal: Egyptian Journal of Radiology and Nuclear Medicine

summary: This cross-sectional study compared 120 COVID-19 survivors (>3 months post-infection) to controls, measuring clinical signs and biochemical markers. The study found persistent elevations in inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP, D-dimer), lipase, and other biochemical parameters in survivors, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Mohammed Ali Gameil; Rehab Elsayed Marzouk; Ahmed Hassan Elsebaie; Salah Eldeen Rozaik
paper_title: Long-term clinical and biochemical residue after COVID-19 recovery

summary: Study of smell and taste dysfunction in acute COVID-19 patients, evaluating prevalence and recovery patterns over 2 months in a cohort of 105 patients. Does not address long COVID or post-acute sequelae; focuses on acute infection only.
paper_authors: Asuman Feda Bayrak; Banu Karaca; Yılmaz Özkul
paper_title: Could smell and taste dysfunction in COVID-19 patients be a sign of the clinical course of the disease?

summary: Prospective cohort study of 170 Egyptian COVID-19 patients assessing post-COVID-19 syndrome symptoms, incidence, and risk factors at medium-term follow-up. Found 38.82% reported post-COVID symptoms with fatigue and musculoskeletal pain most common; age, disease severity, and comorbidities were significant risk factors associated with functional impairment.
paper_authors: Dalia Mohamed Gamal; Rehab Ali Ibrahim; Sara Farid Samaan
paper_title: Post COVID-19 syndrome in a prospective cohort study of Egyptian patients

summary: A prospective single-center study evaluating the efficacy of a comprehensive multidisciplinary rehabilitation program in 39 post-COVID-19 patients. The program significantly improved quality of life, fatigue, anxiety, depression, and functional status across multiple outcome measures.

paper_title: The effect of comprehensive rehabilitation on post-COVID-19 syndrome

summary: A prospective cohort study following 71 COVID-19 patients at 3, 6, and 12 months to assess persistent respiratory symptoms and identify risk factors. Found that dyspnea, fatigue, and cough persisted in significant proportions, with older age, smoking, diabetes, disease severity, and hypoxemia as associated risk factors.
paper_authors: Eman M. Emad Eldin; Randa S. Mohammed; Mahmoud M. E. L. Batanony; Laila A. Al-Sharawy
paper_title: 12-month risk factor evaluation for persistent pulmonary symptoms in long COVID-19 patients

summary: This case-control study compares post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) symptom prevalence and severity in rheumatic disease patients versus healthy controls, finding significantly higher rates of fatigue, myalgia, cognitive deficits, and functional disability in the patient group. The paper identifies risk factors (smoking, steroid use) and protective factors (biologics use, COVID-19 vaccination) associated with PCS severity in rheumatic patients, but does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Zahraa Nour Eldine Ismail; Mohamed Ahmed Hefny; Ahmed Elarabi Hendi; Marwa Gamal Tawfik
paper_title: Assessment of symptoms of the post-COVID-19 syndrome in patients with different rheumatic diseases

summary: This observational prospective study examined thyroid gland dysfunction in 136 hospitalized patients with moderate to severe acute COVID-19 pneumonia during active infection. The study found that sick euthyroid syndrome was the most common thyroid dysfunction pattern, with 61% of cases showing recovery 90 days post-infection.
paper_authors: Fatima Al Taher Taha Morsi; Marwan Elgohary; Ahmed A. Abdelmoaty; Maha E. Alsadik; Samah M. Shehata; Mohamed Ahmed EL Maghawry
paper_title: Patterns of thyroid gland dysfunction among hospitalized patients with COVID-19 pneumonia

summary: This UK Household Longitudinal Study examined psychological distress in people with probable COVID-19 infection at multiple timepoints up to 7 months post-infection. The study found elevated psychological distress persisted up to 7 months after probable COVID-19 compared to uninfected controls, with stronger associations in younger age groups and men.

paper_title: Psychological distress among people with probable COVID-19 infection: analysis of the UK Household Longitudinal Study

summary: This study uses national COVID-19 databases and healthcare claims to compare post-acute sequelae risks across SARS-CoV-2 reinfected, infected, and uninfected populations in Singapore (2021-2023). It found reinfection associated with increased risk of multi-systemic post-acute sequelae (21% overall), but is a secondary analysis of existing administrative data without treatment evaluation.

paper_title: Multi-systemic risk of post-acute sequelae associated with SARS-CoV-2 reinfection

summary: Longitudinal observational study comparing depressive and anxiety symptom trajectories in long COVID vs short COVID groups using propensity score matching from the UCL COVID-19 Social Study. Finds long COVID patients have greater initial increases and sustained elevations in depressive symptoms over 22 months, with widening divergence in anxiety symptoms compared to short COVID controls.
paper_authors: Daisy Fancourt; Andrew Steptoe; Feifei Bu
paper_title: Psychological consequences of long COVID: comparing trajectories of depressive and anxiety symptoms before and after contracting SARS-CoV-2 between matched long- and short-COVID groups

summary: A case-control study comparing neurocognitive and psychiatric outcomes in 300 COVID-19 recovered patients versus matched controls using standardized assessment scales. The study found no statistically significant differences in depression, anxiety, psychopathology, or quality of life between groups, concluding COVID-19 does not have significant psychological or neurocognitive impact.
paper_authors: Baidyanath Ghosh Dastidar
paper_title: An Explorative Study to Assess the Neuropsychiatric Impact of COVID-19

topics: post-intensive care syndrome|quality of life|ICU outcomes
summary: This 1-year follow-up study evaluates post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) in 60 ICU patients (30 COVID, 30 non-COVID), assessing physical, cognitive, and mental health outcomes using standardized questionnaires. paper_title: Quality of life after ICU: 1-year follow-up in patients with and without COVID

paper_title: Depression and health-related quality of life in critical COVID-19 survivors

paper_title: LONG TERM IMPACT OF COVID-19 ON MENTAL HEALTH: A TUNISIAN STUDY

summary: This study compares cognitive function (processing speed, attention, working memory, executive function, memory) between COVID-19 survivors and non-COVID controls using objective neuropsychological tests. paper_title: Psychiatric consequences in hospitalized patients affected by COVID-19 (RECOVER-PSY)

paper_title: Anxiety and depressive disorders in patients with Covid-19

summary: This prospective cohort study of 121 Tunisian COVID-19 survivors assessed the prevalence and severity of insomnia and pain 6-9 months post-discharge. summary: Retrospective analysis of 65 long COVID patients from a specialized aftercare clinic examining symptom progression over 3 months and the relationship between serum COVID-19 antibody titers and sequelae. This is a study protocol or very early-stage presentation with no results reported.

summary: Retrospective chart review of 39 male post-COVID patients at a specialized outpatient clinic investigating late-onset hypogonadism (LOH) syndrome, finding 48.7% met LOH criteria with higher rates in younger males. Study characterizes the clinical and laboratory features of LOH in post-COVID patients but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

summary: Prospective follow-up study of thyroid function and autoimmunity in 122 COVID-19 survivors at baseline and 3 months post-infection. Majority of baseline thyroid dysfunction recovered; study observed increases in anti-thyroid antibody titers post-COVID-19 but no specific treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: David T. W. Lui; Chi Ho Lee; Wing Sun Chow; Alan C. H. Lee; Anthony Raymond Tam; Carol H. Y. Fong; Chun Yiu Law; Eunice K. H. Leung; Kelvin K. W. To; Kathryn C. B. Tan; Yu Cho Woo; Ching Wan Lam; Ivan F. N. Hung; Karen S. L. Lam

summary: This retrospective observational study examined clinical characteristics of long COVID patients who developed ME/CFS, comparing three groups (ME/CFS, non-ME/CFS, and no-fatigue) from a specialized COVID aftercare clinic. The study identified serum ferritin levels and insulin-like growth factor-I as potential biomarkers for ME/CFS development, with higher ferritin correlating with symptom severity.

paper_title: THU581 Possible Markers For Myalgic Encephalomyelitis / Chronic Fatigue Syndrome Developed In Long Covid: Utility Of Serum Ferritin And Insulin-like Growth Factor-I

summary: Retrospective observational study comparing long COVID patients with sleep disturbance (n=60) to those without (n=303), examining clinical characteristics and endocrine markers. Found sleep disturbance in 16.5% of long COVID patients, with elevated ACTH and reduced GH levels suggestive of hypothalamo-pituitary stress, but no intervention was tested.

paper_title: THU116 Characteristics Of Sleep Disturbance And The Related Hormonal Changes In Patients With Long COVID

summary: Retrospective study evaluating menstrual symptoms in 223 female long COVID patients attending a specialized clinic in Japan between 2021-2023. Found that 19.7% experienced menstrual symptoms (cycle irregularity, pain, heavy bleeding), with elevated cortisol levels and worse fatigue/QOL scores in symptomatic patients.
paper_authors: Fumio Otsuka; Yasue Sakurada; Yui Matsuda; Toru Hasegawa; Yuki Otsuka; Yasuhiro Nakano; Kazuki Tokumasu; Koichiro Yamamoto; Naruhiko Sunada; Hiroyuki Honda; Hideharu Hagiya; Keigo Ueda
paper_title: 5164 Long COVID patients with menstrual symptoms: a retrospective study in Japan

summary: A multicenter cross-sectional observational study examining pituitary hormone dysregulation in 246 symptomatic long COVID patients, with a longitudinal follow-up component for those with abnormalities. The study found frequent hormone abnormalities including hyperprolactinemia (12.7%), low IGF-1 (9.0%), and other endocrine disturbances, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

summary: A retrospective cohort study examining post-COVID complications in 188 patients with pre-existing type 2 diabetes mellitus over 24 months post-infection. The study documents increased incidence of thrombotic complications, hypertension, polyneuropathy progression, vasculitis, and inflammatory markers at various timepoints post-infection, highlighting elevated risk in diabetic patients.
paper_authors: Anna Alieva
paper_title: 8241 Post-Covid complications in patients with diabetes mellitus are high during 24 month after acute infection

summary: Prospective cohort study of 171 hospitalized COVID-19 patients followed for 3 months post-discharge examining endocrine dysfunction and its association with long COVID onset. Found that non-thyroidal illness syndrome during hospitalization and pituitary dysfunctions (hypogonadism, central hypoadrenalism) were associated with long COVID symptom development, with female patients more likely to report long COVID symptoms including fatigue.
paper_authors: Irene Campi; Samuele Minari; Marina Lugaresi; Eva Balla; Gerardina Fratianni; Davide Soranna; Antonella Zambon; Laura Fugazzola; Luca Persani
paper_title: SAT-814 Endocrine Dysfunctions and Onset of Long Covid Syndrome in Hospitalized SARS-Cov-2 Patients.

summary: Retrospective observational study examining plasma brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) as a biomarker in 428 long COVID patients stratified by BNP levels. BNP elevation was associated with female sex, older age, dyspnea, and memory impairment, suggesting potential clinical utility for assessing long COVID severity.

paper_title: SUN-254 Clinical utility of plasma brain natriuretic peptide for evaluation of prolonged symptoms of long COVID

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines the association between morphometric vertebral fractures detected at hospital admission and the subsequent development of long COVID 6 months post-discharge in 162 COVID-19 hospitalized patients. The study finds that vertebral fractures are independently associated with long COVID occurrence (OR 3.41), suggesting skeletal fragility as a potential risk factor rather than testing any treatment intervention.

paper_title: SAT-789 Morphometric vertebral fractures at hospitalization associate with Long COVID occurrence

summary: This prospective cohort study from the UK MS Register followed 599 MS patients who had COVID-19 to track their recovery patterns and identify predictors of long-standing symptoms (≥4 weeks). The study found that ~30% experienced prolonged symptoms, with pre-existing severe neurologic impairment, anxiety/depression, and female sex associated with slower recovery.
paper_authors: Afagh Garjani; Rodden M. Middleton; Richard Nicholas; Nikos Evangelou
paper_title: Recovery From COVID-19 in Multiple Sclerosis

summary: This prospective cohort study examines insulin resistance and inflammatory markers as predictors of new-onset diabetes mellitus in patients hospitalized with acute COVID-19. The study develops predictive models using the TyG index and other biomarkers but does not address long COVID or test any interventions for post-acute sequelae.
paper_authors: Farzahna Mohamed; Sulé Gunter; Bezalem E. Yirdaw; Frederick Johan Raal; Aletta M. E. Millen; Ismail S. Kalla
paper_title: MON-581 Predictive Models For New-onset Diabetes Mellitus In Covid-19: Evaluating Insulin Resistance And Inflammation

summary: Retrospective analysis of 639 long-COVID patients at a post-COVID clinic examining demographic distribution and risk factors for new-onset or progressing peripheral neuropathy. Found older age, male sex, and prior COVID hospitalization associated with new-onset PN, and diabetes/hypertension comorbidities associated with progressing PN.
paper_authors: Jason Li; Camden Bohn; Noah Todd; Jessica Pater; Jeanne Carroll; Brian Henriksen; Fen-Lei Chang
paper_title: Peripheral Neuropathy in Long-COVID Patients: Demographic Distribution and Risk Factors (P6-10.001)

summary: This study measured plasma markers of neurologic injury (GFAP, NfL) and inflammation in 121 people with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection, comparing those with and without self-reported CNS PASC symptoms at early and late recovery timepoints. Participants with CNS PASC symptoms showed elevated neurologic injury and inflammatory markers during early recovery, suggesting these biomarkers are associated with neurologic long COVID symptoms.

paper_title: Plasma Markers of Neurologic Injury and Inflammation in People With Self-Reported Neurologic Postacute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: Prospective study examining whether coated-platelet levels measured during acute COVID-19 infection predict cognitive impairment 14 months later in long COVID patients. This is a secondary analysis of baseline biomarker data without any intervention administered, so it does not qualify as a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Claire Delpirou Nouh; Calin Prodan; Chao Xu; Andrea Vincent; Eleanor Mathews; Leslie Guthery; Jason Sharps; Jim Scott; George Dale; Angelia Kirkpatrick
paper_title: Higher Initial Platelet Procoagulant Potential is Associated with Lower Cognitive Scores at 14 Months after COVID-19 (P2-12.004)

summary: A retrospective chart review investigating whether elevated creatine kinase (CK) levels are a prognostic factor for post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) in 43 encephalopathic COVID-19 patients. The study found no significant difference in PASC symptom development between patients with elevated vs. non-elevated CK levels (RR=0.73, p=0.47).

Critically elevated IL-6 group had 90% PASC symptom development versus 22% in non-critically elevated group (RR=4.05), with tocilizumab treatment attenuating PASC development in 58.3% of treated patients.

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing neurological PASC symptoms between HIV-positive and HIV-negative COVID-19 patients at 4 weeks to 1 year post-infection. Found no significant differences in symptom prevalence between groups, though HIV patients showed slightly higher rates of most neurological symptoms.
paper_authors: Mustafa Jaffry; Kranthi Mandava; Kazim Jaffry; Muhammed Ors; Anam Shaikh; Ronak Trivedi; Iqra Faiz; Firas Gerges; Michel Boufadel; Nizar Souayah
paper_title: Effect of Human Immunodeficiency Virus Infection on the Incidence and Severity of Neurological Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19 (S21.009)

summary: Retrospective analysis of 75 COVID-19 patients with HbA1c measurements to investigate whether diabetic control is associated with neurological PASC symptoms. Found no significant difference in neurological PASC symptom incidence across HbA1c groups, though the analysis is preliminary with work ongoing to expand sample size and follow-up duration.
paper_authors: Muhammed Ors; Anam Shaikh; Mustafa Jaffry; Kranthi Mandava; Kazim Jaffry; Ronak Trivedi; Iqra Faiz; Firas Gerges; Michel Boufadel; Nizar Souayah
paper_title: Association between Diabetic Control (HbA1C) and the Risk of Developing Neurological Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) (P14-4.002)

summary: Retrospective follow-up study comparing neurological post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) symptoms in 57 stroke patients versus 418 non-stroke patients at 4 weeks to 1 year post-infection. Found no significant differences in PASC symptom incidence between groups, though stroke patients had higher mean age and some symptom variations.
paper_authors: Anam Shaikh; Mustafa Jaffry; Ronak Trivedi; Kranthi Mandava; Kazim Jaffry; Muhammed Ors; Iqra Faiz; Firas Gerges; Michel Boufadel; Nizar Souayah
paper_title: Long Term Follow Up of Patients with Stroke after SARS-CoV-2 infection and Incidence of Neurological Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19 (P14-5.006)

summary: This prospective cohort study evaluated cognitive function in 60 COVID-19 survivors at 12 weeks post-discharge, using neuropsychological testing and MRI imaging. The study found persistent cognitive impairments in executive function, attention, and memory that correlated with frontal and frontotemporal brain atrophy, independent of initial disease severity.

summary: Retrospective chart review of 56 long COVID patients comparing those with headache-predominant symptoms to those without, examining demographic risk factors and brain MRI findings. No treatment intervention is evaluated; this is a characterization study of symptom phenotypes and associated imaging findings.
paper_authors: Tyler Kuhns; Jaime Imitola; Shivam Patel

summary: Retrospective study examining the association between interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels and outcomes in post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) using electronic medical records. summary: This observational cohort study evaluated insomnia prevalence and associations in 93 PASC patients from an outpatient neurology clinic, with 42 completing 1-year follow-up assessments using the Insomnia Severity Index. The study found that post-COVID symptoms increased with age and were linked to vaccination coverage, but it is a secondary analysis of existing medical database records with no intervention tested.

summary: A Japanese nationwide retrospective cohort study tracking 515 long COVID patients over 36 months to characterize symptom trajectories and symptom clusters. Patients with continuous and multiple symptoms experienced persistently lower quality of life and greater economic burden, with fatigue and dyspnea persisting while other symptoms declined.

summary: Prospective observational study of 93 patients examined at 12 weeks post-COVID-19 hospitalization to evaluate whether KL-6 (a pulmonary epithelial injury marker) correlates with acute severity or persistent symptoms/radiological abnormalities. Found KL-6 levels at 12 weeks were associated with abnormal CT findings but not with acute severity or subjective breathlessness.
paper_authors: David T. Arnold; Charmaine Donald; Max Lyon; Fergus W. Hamilton; Anna J. Morley; Marie Attwood; Alexandra Dipper; Shaney L. Barratt
paper_title: Krebs von den Lungen 6 (KL-6) as a marker for disease severity and persistent radiological abnormalities following COVID-19 infection at 12 weeks

summary: Retrospective observational cohort study of 256 COVID-19 patients aged 70+ in a German district during the first wave, examining risk factors, mortality, and functional outcomes. Found 18% mortality and identified newly emerged care needs as a significant complication, with 27% of previously self-sufficient survivors unable to return home after discharge.
paper_authors: Matthias L. Herrmann; Johannes-Martin Hahn; Birgit Walter-Frank; Desiree M. Bollinger; Kristina Schmauder; Günter Schnauder; Michael Bitzer; Nisar P. Malek; Gerhard W. Eschweiler; Siri Göpel
paper_title: COVID-19 in persons aged 70+ in an early affected German district: Risk factors, mortality and post-COVID care needs—A retrospective observational study of hospitalized and non-hospitalized patients

summary: Population-based prospective cohort study assessing prevalence of impaired health status and symptoms at 6-8 months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection in 431 Swiss adults. Found 26% reported not fully recovered, 55% reported fatigue, and 25% had dyspnea, with significant healthcare utilization burden.
paper_authors: Dominik Menges; Tala Ballouz; Alexia Anagnostopoulos; Hélène E. Aschmann; Anja Domenghino; Jan S. Fehr; Milo A. Puhan
paper_title: Burden of post-COVID-19 syndrome and implications for healthcare service planning: A population-based cohort study

summary: Population-based cohort study of 303 non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients followed for a median of 61 days to estimate PASC prevalence and symptom patterns. Found 68.7% prevalence at 30 days, with fatigue, shortness of breath, and brain fog as most common symptoms.
paper_authors: Melanie L. Bell; Collin J. Catalfamo; Leslie V. Farland; Kacey C. Ernst; Elizabeth T. Jacobs; Yann C. Klimentidis; Megan Jehn; Kristen Pogreba-Brown
paper_title: Post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 in a non-hospitalized cohort: Results from the Arizona CoVHORT

summary: Prospective cohort study following 8,786 non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients (794 positive, 7,229 negative controls) for 3-8 months post-infection via online surveys assessing self-rated health and symptom persistence. Found 36% of COVID-19 positive patients reported worsening health compared to one year prior, versus 18% of negative controls, identifying age, fitness, and healthcare profession as factors associated with health deterioration.
paper_authors: Arne Søraas; Karl Trygve Kalleberg; John Arne Dahl; Camilla Lund Søraas; Tor Åge Myklebust; Eyvind Axelsen; Andreas Lind; Roar Bævre-Jensen; Silje Bakken Jørgensen; Mette S. Istre; Eyrun F. Kjetland; Giske Ursin
paper_title: Persisting symptoms three to eight months after non-hospitalized COVID-19, a prospective cohort study

summary: A prospective cohort study of 355 COVID-19 patients followed for one month after clinical improvement to determine incidence and risk factors for post-COVID-19 syndrome. Found that 46% developed post-COVID symptoms (primarily fatigue), with female gender, respiratory distress, lethargy, and prolonged disease duration as key risk factors.
paper_authors: Mahmud R.; Rahman MM; Rassel MA; Monayem FB; Sayeed SKJB; Islam MS; Islam MM
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 syndrome among symptomatic COVID-19 patients: A prospective cohort study in a tertiary care center of Bangladesh

summary: Prospective follow-up study of 75 COVID-19 hospitalized patients with interstitial pneumonia tracked for 3-12 months to assess radiological sequelae and immunological patterns (IgG/IgM). Found that 62.7% had persistent radiological findings at 3 months, with baseline IL-6 levels predictive of long-term sequelae, but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Domenico Maurizio Toraldo; Francesco Satriano; Rodolfo Rollo; Gabriella Verdastro; Giovanni Imbriani; Emanuele Rizzo; Alberto Argentiero; Andrea Falco; Paolo Ambrosino; Alessandro Miani; Prisco Piscitelli
paper_title: COVID-19 IgG/IgM patterns, early IL-6 elevation and long-term radiological sequelae in 75 patients hospitalized due to interstitial pneumonia followed up from 3 to 12 months

summary: This prospective cohort study followed 222 COVID-19 patients for up to 6 months post-discharge to identify prevalence and predictors of persistent symptoms (PACS). Key finding: 56.3% experienced persistent symptoms; interferon β-1b triple antiviral therapy during acute infection was associated with reduced symptom persistence and better recovery to baseline health.
paper_authors: Imad M. Tleyjeh; Basema Saddik; Nourah AlSwaidan; Ahmed AlAnazi; Rakhee K. Ramakrishnan; Deema Alhazmi; Ahmad Aloufi; Fahad AlSumait; Elie Berbari; Rabih Halwani
paper_title: Prevalence and predictors of Post-Acute COVID-19 Syndrome (PACS) after hospital discharge: A cohort study with 4 months median follow-up

summary: Retrospective observational study of 155 primary care patients with SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia followed for median 54 days to characterize symptom duration and define long COVID cutoff points. Found 28.3% had persistent symptoms >4 weeks, with longer-lasting cough, dyspnea, and asthenia in that group; proposes 4-12 week window as threshold for long COVID definition.
paper_authors: Sara Ares-Blanco; Marta Pérez Álvarez; Ileana Gefaell Larrondo; Cristina Muñoz; Vanesa Aguilar Ruiz; Marta Castelo Jurado; Marina Guisado-Clavero
paper_title: SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia follow-up and long COVID in primary care: A retrospective observational study in Madrid city

summary: This observational study examined the occurrence and predictors of post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) in a community-based cohort of 390 US adults. Results identified fatigue, anosmia, and myalgia as the most common chronic COVID-19 symptoms, with female sex, severe acute infection, and higher anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG levels as significant predictors.
paper_authors: Silverberg JI; Zyskind I.; Naiditch H.; Zimmerman J.; Glatt AE; Pinter A.; Theel ES; Joyner MJ; Hill DA; Lieberman MR; Bigajer E.; Stok D.; Frank E.; Rosenberg AZ
paper_title: Predictors of chronic COVID-19 symptoms in a community-based cohort of adults

summary: This prospective cohort study followed 300 COVID-19 patients at a tertiary hospital in Nepal for three months to assess the prevalence of post-COVID syndrome and identify risk factors. Fatigue was the most common persistent symptom (34% at 60 days, 28.3% at 90 days), and multiple acute symptoms including anosmia, ageusia, and shortness of breath were significant predictors of post-COVID syndrome development.
paper_authors: Sangam Shah; Shreeyash Raj Bhattarai; Kriti Basnet; Yagya Raj Adhikari; Tara Ballav Adhikari; Nikita Bhatta; Rajan Chamlagain; Susan Aryal; Sanjit Kumar Sah; Govinda Bhandari; Bibek Bhandari; Sujan Poudel; Pankaj Pant; Santa Kumar Das
paper_title: Post-COVID syndrome: A prospective study in a tertiary hospital of Nepal

summary: This prospective observational cohort study of 920 critically ill COVID-19 patients examines risk factors for post-intubation dysphagia (swallowing dysfunction) during hospitalization. The study identifies age, severity, BMI, neuromuscular blockers, neurologic diseases, and diabetes as predictive factors for non-resolved dysphagia but does not test any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Fernanda Chiarion Sassi; Ana Paula Ritto; Maíra Santilli de Lima; Cirley Novais Valente Junior; Paulo Francisco Guerreiro Cardoso; Bruno Zilberstein; Paulo Hilário Nascimento Saldiva; Claudia Regina Furquim de Andrade
paper_title: Characteristics of postintubation dysphagia in ICU patients in the context of the COVID-19 outbreak: A report of 920 cases from a Brazilian reference center

summary: This retrospective cohort study evaluates pulmonary emphysematous changes in COVID-19 patients using follow-up low-dose CT scans. The study found significant emphysema development in patients with >30 days follow-up, suggesting long-term pulmonary sequelae of COVID-19.
paper_authors: Erkan Celik; Christian Nelles; Jonathan Kottlors; Philipp Fervers; Lukas Goertz; Daniel Pinto dos Santos; Tobias Achenbach; David Maintz; Thorsten Persigehl
paper_title: Quantitative determination of pulmonary emphysema in follow-up LD-CTs of patients with COVID-19 infection

summary: Observational chart review comparing post-COVID-19 symptoms between 280 patients who did and did not require invasive mechanical ventilation during acute hospitalization. Found that intubated patients had significantly higher rates of neuropsychiatric (67.3% vs 55.4%) and musculoskeletal (38.7% vs 25.9%) involvement, with 98% reporting persistent symptoms.
paper_authors: Irene Irisson-Mora; Angélica M. Salgado-Cordero; Estefanía Reyes-Varón; Daniela J. Cataneo-Piña; Mónica Fernández-Sánchez; Ivette Buendía-Roldán; Miguel A. Salazar-Lezama
paper_title: Comparison between the persistence of post COVID-19 symptoms on critical patients requiring invasive mechanical ventilation and non-critical patients

summary: Population-based observational study examining the incidence and characteristics of patients starting long-term oxygen therapy (LTOT) in Sweden during the COVID-19 pandemic (2020) compared to pre-pandemic years (2015-2019). Finds that COVID-19 accounted for 20.5% of new LTOT cases in 2020, but overall LTOT incidence did not significantly increase.
paper_authors: Josefin Sundh; Andreas Palm; Josefin Wahlberg; Michael Runold; Magnus Ekström
paper_title: Impact of covid-19 on long-term oxygen therapy 2020: A nationwide study in Sweden

summary: Prospective follow-up study of 153 male COVID-19 patients examining erectile dysfunction and mental health outcomes at three months post-discharge. Found 50.3% ED prevalence at follow-up (down from 64.7% at baseline), with age >40 and major depression as significant risk factors for persistent ED.
paper_authors: Kawintharat Harirugsakul; Sorawit Wainipitapong; Jeerath Phannajit; Leilani Paitoonpong; Kavirach Tantiwongse
paper_title: Erectile dysfunction after COVID-19 recovery: A follow-up study

summary: This retrospective cohort study compared post-COVID symptoms across 178 patients stratified by acute COVID-19 severity (ICU, ward, or no hospitalization) at a rehabilitation unit. Findings showed ICU patients had lower muscle strength and effort capacity, while non-hospitalized patients had worse anxiety and quality-of-life scores, with respiratory muscle weakness common across groups despite varying mechanical ventilation exposure.
paper_authors: Jean Claude Perrot; Macarena Segura; Marta Beranuy; Ignasi Gich; Mª Josepa Nadal; Alberto Pintor; Jimena Terra; Eliot Ramirez; Luis Daniel Paz; Helena Bascuñana; Vicente Plaza; Mª Rosa Güell-Rous
paper_title: Comparison of post-COVID symptoms in patients with different severity profiles of the acute disease visited at a rehabilitation unit

summary: A prospective cohort study of 242 COVID-19 hospitalized patients identified three distinct long COVID symptom phenotypes and their associated therapeutic interventions at 12 months post-infection. Patients receiving psychiatric therapies (for the anxiety/depression phenotype) showed the highest symptom improvement rates (100%), followed by those receiving physical/occupational therapy (97%) and those receiving minimal interventions (83%).
paper_authors: Jennifer A. Frontera; Lorna E. Thorpe; Naomi M. Simon; Adam de Havenon; Shadi Yaghi; Sakinah B. Sabadia; Dixon Yang; Ariane Lewis; Kara Melmed; Laura J. Balcer; Thomas Wisniewski; Steven L. Galetta
paper_title: Post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 symptom phenotypes and therapeutic strategies: A prospective, observational study

summary: Longitudinal observational study examining hospital readmission and mortality outcomes in 17,652 COVID-19 patients, comparing 1,131 mechanically ventilated to non-ventilated patients through propensity score matching. While the paper addresses long-term health implications post-discharge, it does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention for long COVID but rather documents complications following acute COVID-19 hospitalization.
paper_authors: Mark J. Butler; Jennie H. Best; Shalini V. Mohan; Jennifer A. Jonas; Lindsay Arader; Jackson Yeh
paper_title: Mechanical ventilation for COVID-19: Outcomes following discharge from inpatient treatment

summary: This cross-sectional study examined olfactory and gustatory dysfunction in 58 COVID-19 outpatients and 56 negative controls using psychophysical tests and subjective questionnaires at baseline and up to 6 months post-infection. Most individuals recovered normal function by 30 days, but approximately 20% reported persistent sensory dysfunction at 6 months, highlighting long-term sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
paper_authors: Mads Mose Jensen; Kasper Daugaard Larsen; Anne-Sophie Homøe; Anders Lykkemark Simonsen; Elisabeth Arndal; Anders Koch; Grethe Badsberg Samuelsen; Xiaohui Chen Nielsen; Tobias Todsen; Preben Homøe
paper_title: Subjective and psychophysical olfactory and gustatory dysfunction among COVID-19 outpatients; short- and long-term results

summary: Prospective matched cohort study following 3,395 children and young people (1,658 SARS-CoV-2 positive, 1,737 negative controls) for 6 months post-infection to characterize symptom trajectories and prevalence. Found that most common acute symptoms declined over 6 months in both groups, with similar symptom patterns observed in test-negatives, suggesting many symptoms may not be specific to SARS-CoV-2 infection.
paper_authors: Terence Stephenson; Snehal M. Pinto Pereira; Manjula D. Nugawela; Kelsey McOwat; Ruth Simmons; Trudie Chalder; Tamsin Ford; Isobel Heyman; Olivia V. Swann; Lana Fox-Smith; Natalia K. Rojas; Emma Dalrymple; Shamez N. Ladhani; Roz Shafran
paper_title: Long COVID—six months of prospective follow-up of changes in symptom profiles of non-hospitalised children and young people after SARS-CoV-2 testing: A national matched cohort study (The CLoCk) study

summary: Retrospective nationwide matched cohort study comparing long COVID sequelae in 3,949 hospitalized COVID-19 patients versus 15,511 matched controls over 12 months. Documents high incidence of post-acute complications (40.3% vs 20% in controls) including dementia, respiratory disease, and cardiac outcomes, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Anna Tisler; Oliver Stirrup; Heti Pisarev; Ruth Kalda; Tatjana Meister; Kadri Suija; Raivo Kolde; Marko Piirsoo; Anneli Uusküla
paper_title: Post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 among hospitalized patients in Estonia: Nationwide matched cohort study

summary: Prospective cohort study following 487 COVID-19 patients at 4 weeks and 371 at 6 months to identify characteristics and predictors of long COVID. Found 29.2% reported long COVID at 4 weeks declining to 9.4% at 6 months, with fatigue as most common symptom; key predictors included pre-existing conditions, acute symptom severity, and hospitalization.
paper_authors: C., Arjun M.; Das, Kajal; G., Alekhya; Mishra, Baijayantimala; Mohapatra, Prasanta R; Pal, Debkumar; Patro, Binod Kumar; Singh, Arvind Kumar; Subba, Sonu Hangma; Venkateshan, Mahalingam
paper_title: Characteristics and predictors of Long COVID among diagnosed cases of COVID-19

summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 4,427 COVID-19 patients and controls for one year to assess cardiovascular outcomes during the post-acute phase. The study found higher rates of arterial thrombotic events, venous thromboembolism, and arrhythmias in the COVID-19 cohort, but did not test any specific intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Luis Ortega-Paz; Victor Arévalos; Diego Fernández-Rodríguez; Víctor Jiménez-Díaz; Jordi Bañeras; Gianluca Campo; Miguel Rodríguez-Santamarta; José Francisco Díaz; Claudia Scardino; Zaira Gómez-Álvarez; Alberto Pernigotti; Fernando Alfonso; Ignacio J. Angiolillo; Josep Rodés-Cabau; Manel Sabaté; Salvatore Brugaletta
paper_title: One-year cardiovascular outcomes after coronavirus disease 2019: The cardiovascular COVID-19 registry

summary: This longitudinal cohort study examined post-COVID depression in 712 Indonesian COVID-19 survivors over 60 days, comparing outcomes between patients who received favipiravir and non-recipients using propensity score matching. Favipiravir was associated with lower depression rates (aOR 0.488, 95% CI 0.339-0.701) and protective effects against depressive mood and loss of interest.
paper_authors: Bumi Herman; Andrea Bruni; Ekachaeryanti Zain; Azhar Dzulhadj; Aye Chan Oo
paper_title: Post-COVID depression and its multiple factors, does Favipiravir have a protective effect? A longitudinal study of indonesia COVID-19 patients

summary: This study uses machine learning to identify three distinct early-symptom clusters in SARS-CoV-2 infected military beneficiaries and correlates these phenotypes with hospitalization, activity return, and long COVID risk. It is an observational analysis of an existing cohort dataset (EPICC COVID-19) with no intervention given to participants.
paper_authors: Nusrat J. Epsi; John H. Powers; David A. Lindholm; Katrin Mende; Allison Malloy; Anuradha Ganesan; Nikhil Huprikar; Tahaniyat Lalani; Alfred Smith; Rupal M. Mody; Milissa U. paper_title: A machine learning approach identifies distinct early-symptom cluster phenotypes which correlate with hospitalization, failure to return to activities, and prolonged COVID-19 symptoms

summary: Prospective cohort study following 326 ICU-hospitalized COVID-19 patients 6-12 months post-discharge to assess long-term respiratory consequences via CT imaging and pulmonary function tests. Found CT lesions in 81.8% of patients with mild restrictive impairment and diffusion capacity impairment; male sex, longer ICU/mechanical ventilation duration, and vasoactive drug use were predictors of severe lesions.
paper_authors: Carlos Roberto Ribeiro Carvalho; Celina Almeida Lamas; Rodrigo Caruso Chate; João Marcos Salge; Marcio Valente Yamada Sawamura; André L. P. de Albuquerque; Carlos Toufen Junior; Daniel Mario Lima; Michelle Louvaes Garcia; Paula Gobi Scudeller; Cesar Higa Nomura; Marco Antonio Gutierrez; Bruno Guedes Baldi
paper_title: Long-term respiratory follow-up of ICU hospitalized COVID-19 patients: Prospective cohort study

summary: This observational study examines laryngeal electromyography findings in 38 post-COVID patients with chronic cough to assess vagus nerve neuropathy involvement. While it provides clinical insights into post-COVID pathophysiology, it is an observational characterization study without any treatment intervention or outcome evaluation.
paper_authors: Patricia García-Vicente; Antonio Rodríguez-Valiente; Carmen Górriz Gil; Reyes Márquez Altemir; Francisco Martínez-Pérez; Luis Fernando López-Pajaro; Jose Ramón García-Berrocal
paper_title: Chronic cough in post-COVID syndrome: Laryngeal electromyography findings in vagus nerve neuropathy

summary: Retrospective cohort study using electronic health records from 13,033 adults to compare symptom and diagnosis rates before and after COVID-19 infection, with follow-up through November 2021. Found significantly increased odds of multiple diagnoses post-COVID including dyspnea, pulmonary fibrosis, and loss of smell/taste, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Mark J. Butler; Codruta Chiuzan; Heejoon Ahn; Michael Gao; Stefani D’Angelo; Jackson Yeh; Karina Davidson
paper_title: Before and after COVID-19: Changes in symptoms and diagnoses in 13,033 adults

summary: Pooled analysis of two Swiss population-based cohorts examining PCC prevalence and severity across SARS-CoV-2 variants (Wildtype, Delta, Omicron) and vaccination status in 1,350 infected individuals. Found that vaccinated individuals infected with Omicron had significantly reduced odds of developing PCC, with four distinct symptom clusters identified across variants.
paper_authors: Tala Ballouz; Dominik Menges; Marco Kaufmann; Rebecca Amati; Anja Frei; Viktor von Wyl; Jan S. Fehr; Emiliano Albanese; Milo A. Puhan
paper_title: Post COVID-19 condition after Wildtype, Delta, and Omicron SARS-CoV-2 infection and prior vaccination: Pooled analysis of two population-based cohorts

summary: Retrospective cohort study analyzing EHR data from ~27 million patients to characterize post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) following ancestral and Delta variant infections. Study documents excess burden of pulmonary and abdominal conditions post-COVID but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Jay K. Varma; Chengxi Zang; Thomas W. Carton; Jason P. Block; Dhruv J. Khullar; Yongkang Zhang; Mark G. Weiner; Russell L. Rothman; Edward J. Schenck; Zhenxing Xu; Kristin Lyman; Jiang Bian; Jie Xu; Elizabeth A. Shenkman; Christine Maughan; Leah Castro-Baucom; Lisa O’Brien; Fei Wang; Rainu Kaushal
paper_title: Excess burden of respiratory and abdominal conditions following COVID-19 infections during the ancestral and Delta variant periods in the United States: An EHR-based cohort study from the RECOVER program

summary: Prospective cohort study of 42 critical COVID-19 survivors who received inpatient physical and rehabilitation medicine (PRM) during ICU stay, evaluated at 6 and 12 months post-discharge. While the paper describes outcomes in physical, mental, and cognitive domains, it is a passive observational follow-up study of patients who received standard inpatient rehabilitation as part of routine ICU care, not a controlled evaluation of a specific experimental intervention or treatment program.
paper_authors: Ana Teixeira-Vaz; José Afonso Rocha; Mafalda Oliveira; Tiago Simões-Moreira; David Almeida e. Reis; Ana Isabel Silva; José Artur Paiva
paper_title: Surviving critical COVID-19: How functionality, physical, mental and cognitive outcomes evolve?

summary: A longitudinal cohort study of 1,344 long COVID patients that used latent class analysis to identify three distinct phenotypes based on symptom profiles (fatigue/dyspnea, anxiety/depression, or combined). The study examined associations between phenotypes and quality of life outcomes over 6 months but did not test any specific intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Alyson W. Wong; Karen C. Tran; Mawuena Binka; Naveed Z. Janjua; Hind Sbihi; James A. Russell; Christopher Carlsten; Adeera Levin; Christopher J. Ryerson
paper_title: Use of latent class analysis and patient reported outcome measures to identify distinct long COVID phenotypes: A longitudinal cohort study

summary: Intensive longitudinal study of 82 long COVID patients using smartphone app (5 daily entries over 14 days) and wearable accelerometers to examine within-person symptom variation and associations with physical activity. Found substantial within-individual symptom variation, weak correlations between symptoms and activity, and heterogeneous patterns suggesting altered central symptom processing rather than distinct phenotypes.
paper_authors: Christopher Burton; Helen Dawes; Simon Goodwill; Michael Thelwell; Caroline Dalton
paper_title: Within and between-day variation and associations of symptoms in Long Covid: Intensive longitudinal study

summary: This observational study examined whether ABO blood group distribution differs between acute COVID-19 hospitalization patients and long COVID patients, comparing frequencies and calculating adjusted odds ratios. The analysis found no significant association between any ABO blood subgroup or Rh factor and either COVID-19 or long COVID development.
paper_authors: Joan B. Soriano; Adrián Peláez; Xavier Busquets; María Rodrigo-García; Elena Ávalos Pérez-Urría; Tamara Alonso; Rosa Girón; Claudia Valenzuela; Celeste Marcos; Elena García-Castillo; Julio Ancochea
paper_title: ABO blood group as a determinant of COVID-19 and Long COVID: An observational, longitudinal, large study

summary: Ambidirectional cohort study of 332 long COVID patients comparing symptom profiles by antecedent COVID-19 severity and treatment exposure. Mild antecedent COVID-19 was associated with greater odds of fatigue, cognitive impairment, headaches, and dizziness; remdesivir treatment was associated with reduced fatigue and cognitive impairment.
paper_authors: Walker TA; Truong AD; Summers A.; Dixit AN; Goldstein FC; Hajjar I.; Echols MR; Woodruff MC; Lee ED; Tekwani S.; Carroll K.; Sanz I.; Lee FE; Han JE
paper_title: Mild antecedent COVID-19 associated with symptom-specific post-acute sequelae

summary: Prospective observational cohort study evaluating pulmonary function and CT findings in dialysis patients 3+ months after COVID-19 recovery. Found high prevalence of radiological abnormalities (reticulation 64%, ground glass opacities 32%, bronchiectasis 28%) and restrictive lung patterns (41%), though few patients had ongoing symptoms and abnormalities were comparable to the general population.
paper_authors: Solos Jaturapisanukul; Nadwipa Yuangtrakul; Dearada Wangcharoenrung; Krongkan Kanchanarat; Kan Radeesri; Jakravoot Maneerit; Anan Manomaipiboon; Khemika Rojtangkom; Chompoonuth Ananthanalapa; Siwaporn Rungrojthanakit; Peerawit Thinpangnga; Joshua Alvior; Thananda Trakarnvanich
paper_title: Follow-up evaluation of pulmonary function and computed tomography findings in chronic kidney disease patients after COVID-19 infection

summary: Prospective observational study examining cardiac magnetic resonance imaging findings in 95 hospitalized COVID-19 patients at 9-month follow-up compared to controls. Found myocardial scar in 66% of COVID-19 patients but found no association between myocardial injury and long-term symptoms, dyspnea, chest pain, or arrhythmias.
paper_authors: Aria Yar; Valtteri Uusitalo; Satu M. Vaara; Miia Holmström; Aino-Maija Vuorinen; Tiina Heliö; Riitta Paakkanen; Sari Kivistö; Suvi Syväranta; Johanna Hästbacka
paper_title: Cardiac magnetic resonance -detected myocardial injury is not associated with long-term symptoms in patients hospitalized due to COVID-19

summary: The Nivel Corona Cohort is a population-based study combining general practice electronic health records with patient-reported outcomes to investigate short- and long-term effects of COVID-19 in the Netherlands. The cohort of 442 participants documents acute-phase symptoms (fatigue, reduced condition, cough, headache, myalgia) and plans longitudinal follow-up over one year.
paper_authors: Renee Veldkamp; Karin Hek; Rinske van den Hoek; Laura Schackmann; Eugène van Puijenbroek; Liset van Dijk
paper_title: Nivel Corona Cohort: A description of the cohort and methodology used for combining general practice electronic records with patient reported outcomes to study impact of a COVID-19 infection

summary: This paper describes the implementation and outcomes of a post-COVID clinic at an Irish tertiary centre, analyzing patient characteristics and clinic operations for 311 post-COVID patients. The study found that 70% had persistent symptoms and identifies risk factors for ongoing symptoms, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Aoife Heeney; Stephen P. Connolly; Rachel Dillon; Aisling O’Donnell; Tara McSweeney; Brendan O’Kelly; Aoife G. Cotter; Gerard Sheehan; John S. Lambert; Eavan G. Muldoon; Tara McGinty
paper_title: Post-COVID care delivery: The experience from an Irish tertiary centre’s post-COVID clinic
