summary: Community-based case-control study comparing long COVID symptom prevalence and antibody responses in 1,150 COVID-19 cases versus 1,110 matched controls in the Dallas Fort-Worth area. Found that 21.1% of cases reported persistent PASC symptoms including shortness of breath, fatigue, and loss of taste/smell, with decreasing antibody levels over 8.6 months of follow-up.
paper_authors: Noa Kopplin; Angie Garcia; Annika Reczek; Kate Wilkinson; Sruthi Yekkaluri; Caitlin C. Murphy; Jasmin Tiro; Alagar R. Muthukumar; Andrew Masica; Amit G. Singal
paper_title: Post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 and longitudinal antibody levels in a community-based cohort

summary: Prospective observational study following 86 ICU patients who required invasive ventilation for acute COVID-19 pneumonia, assessing radiological lung appearance and pulmonary function at 6 months post-discharge. Found persistent CT abnormalities and reduced lung function in most patients, but no intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Ylva Konsberg; Pawel Szaro; Anders Aneman; Sanna Kjellberg; Nektarios Solidakis; Sara Svedlund; Bengt Nellgård; Keti Dalla
paper_title: Radiological appearance and lung function six months after invasive ventilation in ICU for COVID-19 pneumonia: An observational follow-up study

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining long-term renal outcomes in 451 patients with biopsy-proven kidney disease who experienced COVID-19 infection. Finds COVID-19 patients had worse renal function decline and higher rates of eGFR decline >30% or ESRD, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Bogdan Obrișcă; Valentin Mocanu; Alexandra Vornicu; Roxana Jurubiță; Bogdan Sorohan; George Dimofte; Camelia Achim; Andreea Andronesi; Georgia Micu; Raluca Bobeică; Nicu Caceaune; Alexandru Procop; Vlad Herlea; Mihaela Gherghiceanu; Gener Ismail
paper_title: The impact of SARS-CoV-2 infection on renal function in patients with biopsy-proven kidney diseases

summary: Retrospective follow-up study examining the association between COVID-19 vaccination and prolonged long-COVID symptoms in 1,236 adults with long-COVID syndrome. Found that vaccination status was significantly associated with persistent long-COVID symptoms (44.6% in vaccinated vs 29.4% in unvaccinated), though authors note vaccines reduce severe COVID-19 risk.
paper_authors: Ali A. Asadi-Pooya; Meshkat Nemati; Mina Shahisavandi; Hamid Nemati; Afrooz Karimi; Anahita Jafari; Sara Nasiri; Seyyed Saeed Mohammadi; Zahra Rahimian; Hossein Bayat; Ali Akbari; Amir Emami; Owrang Eilami
paper_title: How does COVID-19 vaccination affect long-COVID symptoms?

summary: This study uses primary care electronic health records to compare symptoms in 11,015 COVID-19 patients versus 18,098 unexposed controls, identifying symptoms most strongly associated with long COVID at 12+ weeks post-infection (fatigue, shortness of breath, palpitations). It does not evaluate any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: Anoop D. Shah; Anuradhaa Subramanian; Jadene Lewis; Samir Dhalla; Elizabeth Ford; Shamil Haroon; Valerie Kuan; Krishnarajah Nirantharakumar
paper_title: Long Covid symptoms and diagnosis in primary care: A cohort study using structured and unstructured data in The Health Improvement Network primary care database

summary: This infodemiology study analyzed online search trends for long-COVID and related symptoms in Japan from 2020-2022 using Yahoo! JAPAN search data. It found that interest in long-COVID increased with COVID-19 case peaks, with hair loss, cough, smell/taste disturbance, and headache as the most frequently searched symptoms.
paper_authors: Kosuke Ishizuka; Taiju Miyagami; Tomoya Tsuchida; Mizue Saita; Yoshiyuki Ohira; Toshio Naito
paper_title: Online search interest in long-term symptoms of coronavirus disease 2019 during the COVID-19 pandemic in Japan: Infodemiology study using the most visited search engine in Japan

summary: A prospective cohort study of 44,386 individuals in Malaysia following SARS-CoV-2 infection during the Omicron wave, assessing the prevalence and associated factors of post COVID-19 condition at 3 months. Found that 3.4% met post COVID-19 criteria, with fatigue, cough, and cognitive impairment as the most common symptoms, and identified female sex, comorbidities, and severe acute illness as risk factors.
paper_authors: Peter Seah Keng Tok; Kong Yeow Kang; Sock Wen Ng; Norazida Ab Rahman; Muhammad Aminul Syahmi; Mohan Dass Pathmanathan; Maheshwara Rao Appannan; Kalaiarasu M. Peariasamy; Sheamini Sivasampu
paper_title: Post COVID-19 condition among adults in Malaysia following the Omicron wave: A prospective cohort study

summary: This study uses the N3C Data Enclave to analyze the association between SARS-CoV-2 infection and new-onset schizophrenia spectrum and psychotic disorders across three time intervals post-infection. It is a secondary analysis of an existing cohort database rather than a primary trial, and does not study a treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Asif Rahman; Michael Russell; Wanhong Zheng; Daniel Eckrich; Imtiaz Ahmed
paper_title: SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with an increase in new diagnoses of schizophrenia spectrum and psychotic disorder: A study using the US national COVID cohort collaborative (N3C)

summary: Prospective cohort study of 481 COVID-19 patients in Pakistan followed for 12 months to assess long COVID prevalence and its association with vaccination status and disease severity. Found 29.9% developed long COVID symptoms, with unvaccinated patients having 2.42× higher odds of developing long COVID compared to vaccinated patients.
paper_authors: Samar Fatima; Madiha Ismail; Taymmia Ejaz; Zarnain Shah; Summaya Fatima; Mohammad Shahzaib; Hassan Masood Jafri
paper_title: Association between long COVID and vaccination: A 12-month follow-up study in a low- to middle-income country

summary: The EPICC study assessed the frequency of post-acute neuropsychological symptoms (depression, anxiety, fatigue, cognitive impairment) in 2,383 U.S. Military Healthcare System beneficiaries 1-6 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection. SARS-CoV-2 positive participants were significantly more likely to report depression, fatigue, and cognitive impairment compared to uninfected controls, with risk ratios up to 2.07 for fatigue.
paper_authors: Liana R. Andronescu; Stephanie A. Richard; Ann I. Scher; David A. Lindholm; Katrin Mende; Anuradha Ganesan; Nikhil Huprikar; Tahaniyat Lalani; Alfred Smith; Rupal M. Mody; Milissa U. Jones; Samantha E. Bazan; Rhonda E. Colombo; Christopher J. Colombo; Evan Ewers; Derek T. Larson; Ryan C. Maves; Catherine M. Berjohn; Carlos J. Maldonado; Caroline English; Margaret Sanchez Edwards; Julia S. Rozman; Jennifer Rusiecki; Celia Byrne; Mark P. Simons; David Tribble; Timothy H. Burgess; Simon D. Pollett; Brian K. Agan
paper_title: SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with self-reported post-acute neuropsychological symptoms within six months of follow-up

summary: This retrospective cohort study uses electronic health record data from 588,611 US patients to create a data-driven definition of post-COVID conditions by measuring symptom changes before and after COVID infection. The study found 20% of COVID patients developed PCC, with prevalence increasing with age, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Kathleen M. Andersen; Farid L. Khan; Peter W. Park; Timothy L. Wiemken; Birol Emir; Deepa Malhotra; Tuka Alhanai; Mohammad M. Ghassemi; Leah J. McGrath
paper_title: Using a data-driven approach to define post-COVID conditions in US electronic health record data

summary: This retrospective cohort study describes long COVID symptom frequency and associated risk factors in 6,142 Nepali women at 6 months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection. It found 16.9% of PCR-positive women reported non-recovery with prominent fatigue, pain, cognitive impairment, dyspnea, and temperature intolerance, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Deepak S. Shrestha; Sajani Manandhar; Bimal Sharma Chalise; Sagar Kumar Rajbhandari; Anup Bastola; Parmananda Bhandari; Santa Kumar Das; Pankaj Pant; Sangita Sharma; Hari Prasad Kattel; Roshan Kumar Jha; Mahendra Raj Shrestha; Anil Shrestha; Richard R. Love
paper_title: Symptoms 6 months following SARS-CoV-2 infection in Nepali women

summary: Retrospective observational study of 100 COVID-19 patients in Colombia who underwent a 12-week pulmonary rehabilitation program, evaluating changes in lung function (spirometry) and dyspnea perception (mMRC scale). Results showed that pulmonary rehabilitation had positive effects on respiratory function and dyspnea regardless of patient gender, with FVC, FEV1, and mMRC as robust indicators of recovery.
paper_authors: Carlos D. Páez-Mora; Diana Carolina Zona; Teddy Angarita-Sierra; Matilde E. Rojas-Paredes; Daniela Cano-Trejos
paper_title: Changes in lung function and dyspnea perception in Colombian Covid-19 patients after a 12-week pulmonary rehabilitation program

summary: Prospective cohort study analyzing self-reported data from 2,939 adults in the INSPIRE registry to examine the association between prolonged SARS-CoV-2 symptoms at 3 months post-infection and employment outcomes. Found that 40.8% reported persistent symptoms and those with ≥5 symptoms had significantly higher odds of missing ≥10 workdays and not returning to work.
paper_authors: Arjun K. Venkatesh; Huihui Yu; Caitlin Malicki; Michael Gottlieb; Joann G. Elmore; Mandy J. Hill; Ahamed H. Idris; Juan Carlos C. Montoy; Kelli N. O’Laughlin; Kristin L. Rising; Kari A. Stephens; Erica S. Spatz; Robert A. Weinstein
paper_title: The association between prolonged SARS-CoV-2 symptoms and work outcomes

summary: A longitudinal observational study following 57 individuals with post-COVID cognitive complaints at baseline (~6 months post-infection) and follow-up (~15 months later) to assess trends in cognitive performance and related fatigue/mood outcomes. Findings show cognitive difficulties persist at both test and domain levels, with some improvement in attention/executive functioning and self-rated health, and greater cognitive impairment in those hospitalized during acute infection.
paper_authors: Nicholas Grunden; Marco Calabria; Carmen García-Sánchez; Catalina Pons; Juan Antonio Arroyo; Beatriz Gómez-Ansón; Marina del Carmen Estévez-García; Roberto Belvís; Noemí Morollón; Mónica Cordero-Carcedo; Isabel Mur; Virginia Pomar; Pere Domingo
paper_title: Evolving trends in neuropsychological profiles of post COVID-19 condition: A 1-year follow-up in individuals with cognitive complaints

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines the incidence of newly diagnosed liver disorders up to 3.5 years post-COVID-19 in 54,699 COVID-19 patients versus 1.4 million non-COVID controls. The study found no significant difference in liver disorder incidence between groups, with older age, Hispanic ethnicity, and obesity—rather than COVID-19 status—being key risk factors.
paper_authors: Thomas Peng; Katie S. Duong; Justin Y. Lu; Kristina R. Chacko; Sonya Henry; Wei Hou; Kevin P. Fiori; Stephen H. Wang; Tim Q. Duong
paper_title: Incidence, characteristics, and risk factors of new liver disorders 3.5 years post COVID-19 pandemic in the Montefiore Health System in Bronx

summary: This cross-sectional and longitudinal study examined clinical characteristics and factors associated with long COVID among 1,359 patients attending a post-acute COVID-19 clinic in Zambia from August 2020 to January 2023. The study identified hospitalization duration, severe acute COVID-19, and comorbidities as significant risk factors for long COVID, but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Warren Malambo; Duncan Chanda; Lily Besa; Daniella Engamba; Linos Mwiinga; Mundia Mwitumwa; Peter Matibula; Neil Naik; Suilanji Sivile; Simon Agolory; Andrew Auld; Lloyd Mulenga; Jonas Z. Hines; Sombo Fwoloshi
paper_title: Clinical characteristics and factors associated with long COVID among post-acute COVID-19 clinic patients in Zambia, August 2020 to January 2023: A cross-sectional and longitudinal study design

summary: This retrospective matched cohort study examined long-term cardiovascular disease outcomes in 944,371 non-hospitalized Medicare beneficiaries diagnosed with COVID-19, comparing them to propensity score-matched controls without COVID-19 with median follow-up of 18.5 months. While the study documents persistent CVD risks in the early post-COVID period, it does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention for long COVID.
paper_authors: Quanhe Yang; Anping Chang; Xin Tong; Sandra L. Jackson; Robert K. Merritt
paper_title: Long-term cardiovascular disease outcomes in non-hospitalized medicare beneficiaries diagnosed with COVID-19: Population-based matched cohort study

summary: Longitudinal panel study examining the effects of Long COVID on UK workers' employment status, work hours, and mental health from 2020-2021. Finds that those with Long COVID symptoms lasting 29+ weeks have higher employment exit risk and worse mental health outcomes, primarily driven by sickness leave rather than reduced hours.
paper_authors: Darja Reuschke; Donald Houston; Paul Sissons
paper_title: Impacts of Long COVID on workers: A longitudinal study of employment exit, work hours and mental health in the UK

summary: This retrospective cohort study uses insurance claims data to compare healthcare utilization 9 months before and after COVID-19 hospitalization among 63,161 patients discharged alive. While it documents increased healthcare utilization post-hospitalization (ED, rehabilitation, office, and telemedicine visits), it is an observational analysis of existing claims data without any treatment intervention being tested or evaluated.
paper_authors: Mohammed Zaidan; Daniel Puebla Neira; Efstathia Polychronopoulou; Kuo Yong-Fang; Gulshan Sharma
paper_title: Healthcare utilization 9 months pre- and post- COVID-19 hospitalization among patients discharged alive

summary: This retrospective cohort study used claims data from 413,958 adults to examine the association between COVID-19 infection in 2020 and sleep disorder diagnoses in 2021, after balancing baseline characteristics. Subjects with prior COVID-19 infection were 53% more likely to develop sleep disorders in the following year (OR=1.53).
paper_authors: Jaewhan Kim; Kenechukwu C. Ben-Umeh; Rachel Weir; Karen Manotas; Kristi Kleinschmit; Aaron Fischer; Peter Weir; Fernando Wilson
paper_title: Evaluating the risk of sleep disorders in subjects with a prior COVID-19 infection

summary: Population-based study examining the association between SARS-CoV-2 antibody status and long COVID symptoms among 3,946 Kaiser Permanente members. Found no association between seropositivity and long COVID symptoms among people with confirmed prior COVID-19, suggesting limited utility of serology testing for long COVID diagnosis.
paper_authors: Ingrid A. Binswanger; Darryl E. Palmer-Toy; Jennifer C. Barrow; Komal J. Narwaney; Katia J. Bruxvoort; Courtney R. Kraus; Jason A. Lyons; Jessica A. Lam; Jason M. Glanz
paper_title: Assessing the association between antibody status and symptoms of long COVID: A multisite study

summary: Retrospective chart review of 459 long-term care home residents examining symptom trajectories over 24 weeks following COVID-19 infection. While the study found that most residents returned to pre-COVID symptom levels within two months, approximately 25% did not recover, with greater symptom burden during acute infection predicting non-recovery.
paper_authors: Gordana Rajlic; Janice M. Sorensen; Benajir Shams; Armin Mardani; Ketki Merchant; Akber Mithani
paper_title: Post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 in residents in long-term care homes: Examining symptoms and recovery over time

summary: This retrospective cohort study compares post-acute symptom risk among adults with severe COVID-19, influenza, and pneumonia using administrative health claims data from 2020 onwards. The findings show COVID-19 produces unique post-acute symptom patterns distinguished by initial disease severity and comorbidities, with outcomes differing from influenza and pneumonia cohorts over six months of follow-up.
paper_authors: Caroline M. Schaefer; Trudy Millard Krause; George L. Delclos; Raymond S. Greenberg
paper_title: Risk of post-acute symptoms among adults: A comparison study of severe COVID-19, pneumonia, and influenza

summary: This retrospective cohort study examined the prevalence and risk factors for long COVID in 247 patients hospitalized for acute COVID-19 in Ethiopia, finding that 72.1% had persistent symptoms at median 35-day follow-up. The study identified longer pre-admission symptom duration and longer hospital stay as significant risk factors for long COVID development, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Bethlehem Berhanu Minassie; Wondwossen Amogne Degu; Eyob Kebede Etissa; Natnael Fitsum Asfeha; Salem Taye Alemayehu; Dawit Kebede Huluka
paper_title: Attributes and factors associated with long covid in patients hospitalized for acute COVID-19: A retrospective cohort study

summary: A prospective cohort study following 165 COVID-19 patients via telemedicine from 2020 to 2-year follow-up to assess Long-COVID symptom persistence and risk factors. Found symptom prevalence decreased from 84% at 1-year to 61% at 2-year follow-up, with prior Long-COVID and reinfection as significant risk factors for persistent symptoms.
paper_authors: Andrea Foppiani; Chiara Montanari; Sara Zanelli; Michele Davide Maria Lombardo; Valeria Calcaterra; Gianvincenzo Zuccotti
paper_title: Long-COVID symptom monitoring: Insights from a two-year telemedicine study

summary: A prospective cohort study (RECoVERED) following 186 COVID-19 survivors for 6 months to characterize longitudinal trajectories of inflammatory cytokines and identify early predictors of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC). Found that elevated CRP, IL-10, IL-17, IL-6, IP10 and TNFα at 24 weeks were associated with PASC, and early IL-1β emerged as a promising predictor of long COVID development.
paper_authors: Elke Wynberg; Alvin X. Han; Hugo D. G. van Willigen; Anouk Verveen; Lisa van Pul; Irma Maurer; Ester M. van Leeuwen; Joost G. van den Aardweg; Menno D. de Jong; Pythia Nieuwkerk; Maria Prins; Neeltje A. Kootstra; Godelieve J. de Bree
paper_title: Inflammatory profiles are associated with long COVID up to 6 months after COVID-19 onset: A prospective cohort study of individuals with mild to critical COVID-19

summary: This retrospective study examines the prevalence and clinical characteristics of ME/CFS in 739 long COVID patients visiting a Japanese university clinic from 2021-2023, stratified by COVID-19 variant phase. The study finds ME/CFS prevalence decreased from 23.9% in the pre-Delta period to 3.3% in the Omicron period, while brain fog complaints inversely increased.
paper_authors: Satoru Morita; Kazuki Tokumasu; Yuki Otsuka; Hiroyuki Honda; Yasuhiro Nakano; Naruhiko Sunada; Yasue Sakurada; Yui Matsuda; Yoshiaki Soejima; Keigo Ueda; Fumio Otsuka
paper_title: Phase-dependent trends in the prevalence of myalgic encephalomyelitis / chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) related to long COVID: A criteria-based retrospective study in Japan

summary: This study compared observational methods (electronic health records and questionnaires) to identify and characterize post-COVID syndrome in the Netherlands, analyzing prevalence rates and clinical subtypes across different classification approaches. While relevant to long COVID, it is excluded because it does not study a treatment or intervention—it is purely observational and descriptive in nature.
paper_authors: Isabelle Bos; Lisa Bosman; Rinske van den Hoek; Willemijn van Waarden; Matthijs S. Berends; Maarten S. Homburg; Tim Olde Hartman; Jean Muris; Lilian S. Peters; Bart Knottnerus; Karin S. Hek; Robert A. Verheij
paper_title: Comparison of observational methods to identify and characterize post-COVID syndrome in the Netherlands using electronic health records and questionnaires

summary: Prospective household cohort study tracking symptom burden, viral loads, and antibody responses during acute COVID-19 infection in 143 outpatients (April-November 2020, pre-vaccine era). Found that higher day 28 antibody levels were associated with later development of long COVID symptoms at 8-10 month follow-up, but the study focuses on acute infection characteristics and PASC risk factors rather than testing any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Mehal Churiwal; Kathleen Tompkins; Gabrielle Streeter; Christy Litel; Sydney Mason; Kelly Lin; Meredith Muller; Srijana Chhetri; Tia Belvin; Feng-Chang Lin; Christopher Basham; Maureen Whittelsey; Tyler Rapp; Lakshmanane Premkumar; Carla Cerami; Jessica T. Lin
paper_title: Symptom burden, viral load, and antibody response to ancestral SARS-CoV-2 strain [D614G] in an outpatient household cohort

summary: Retrospective cohort study using Veterans Health Administration records examining associations between long COVID documentation and clinical outcomes in diabetic veterans (n=1,896,080). Long COVID was associated with increased primary care visits, medication use, dialysis initiation, and hospitalization, but lower mortality.
paper_authors: Pandora L. Wander; Elliott Lowy; Anna Korpak; Lauren A. Beste; Edward J. Boyko
paper_title: Association of long COVID documentation with clinical outcomes among Veterans with diabetes

summary: This cross-sectional analysis examined work absenteeism in adults with long-COVID using the 2022 Medical Expenditure Panel Survey. The study found that individuals with long-COVID missed significantly more workdays (8 days on average) compared to those without long-COVID (4 days), highlighting substantial productivity losses.
paper_authors: Jaewhan Kim; Sanghoon Lee; Peter Weir
paper_title: Long-COVID is associated with increased absenteeism from work

summary: Prospective follow-up study of 37 COVID-19 patients examining associations between convalescent immune responses and long-term pulmonary sequelae at ~27 months post-hospitalization using chest CT imaging. Found pulmonary sequelae in 59.5% of patients, associated with older age, but no significant differences in convalescent cytokines or antibodies predictive of complications.
paper_authors: Minkyeong Lee; Byoung Kwon Park; Dong Hoon Shin; Hong Sang Oh; Chae-Hong Jeong; So-Young Lee; Jungyeon Kim; Sang-Won Park
paper_title: Long-term pulmonary sequelae and convalescent immune reactions in mild to moderate COVID-19 patients during the active treatment era

summary: Retrospective cohort study identifying clinical and sociodemographic predictors of healthcare seeking in post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) patients in a California health system. The study analyzes patterns of care seeking rather than testing a specific intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Durant EJ; Warton EM; Skarbinski J.; Siqueiros MH; Cholleti SM; Vinson DR; Mark DG; DiLena DD; Rauchwerger AS; Reed ME; Ballard DW
paper_title: Predictors of health care utilization in patients with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC)

summary: A 3.5-year prospective cohort study tracking 149 long COVID patients' physical and mental health outcomes at 3 months, 1 year, and 3.5 years post-infection using validated questionnaires (SF-12, PHQ-9, GAD-7, IES-R). While patients showed overall improvement over time, those with persistent long COVID symptoms continued to have significantly worse physical and mental health scores compared to those without long COVID, with ongoing fatigue, sleep difficulties, and post-exertional malaise being most common.
paper_authors: Gregory Vallée; David Xi; Gordana Avramovic; Brendan O’Kelly; John S. Lambert
paper_title: Evaluating the longitudinal physical and psychological health effects of persistent long Covid 3.5 years after infection

summary: Secondary analysis of a prospective multicenter study comparing healthcare utilization patterns between long COVID and non-long COVID patients over 180 days post-infection. Found that long COVID patients had higher rates of additional hospitalization and longer office visit durations compared to those without long COVID.
paper_authors: Michael Gottlieb; Erica S. Spatz; Huihui Yu; Imtiaz Ebna Mannan; Michelle Santangelo; Caitlin Malicki; Nicole L. Gentile; Rachel E. Geyer; Alex Charlton; Jonathan W. Dyal; Joann G. Elmore; Kristyn Gatling; Mandy J. Hill; Juan Carlos C. Montoy; Kelli N. O’Laughlin; Kristin L. Rising; Sharon Saydah; Kari A. Stephens; Ralph C. Wang; Lauren E. Wisk; Arjun K. Venkatesh; Robert A. Weinstein
paper_title: Effects of long COVID on healthcare utilization

summary: A case series of 140 post-COVID patients receiving inpatient pulmonary rehabilitation treatment over an average of 27 days, assessing mental and physical health outcomes at admission and discharge. Both mental (anxiety, depression, PTSD) and physical symptoms showed partial improvement following specialized rehabilitation treatment.
paper_authors: Adrian Meule; Daniela Kroll; Martina Bönsch; Tessa Schneeberger; Inga Jarosch; Rainer Gloeckl; Ulrich Voderholzer; Andreas R. Koczulla
paper_title: Mental and physical health in persons receiving inpatient pulmonary rehabilitation treatment for post-COVID condition

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing clinical characteristics of long COVID patients (n=580) to recovered COVID and non-COVID post-acute infection syndrome patients using EHR data. Found long COVID patients had higher comorbidity burden and greater prevalence of cardiac, cognitive, and fatigue symptoms in post-acute phase.
paper_authors: Caleb R. Carr; Nicole L. Gentile; Jeanne Bertolli; Warren Szewczyk; Jin-Mann S. Lin; Elizabeth R. Unger; Quan M. Vu; Nona Sotoodehnia; Annette L. Fitzpatrick
paper_title: Comparison of long COVID, recovered COVID, and non-COVID Post-Acute Infection Syndromes over three years

summary: A retrospective cohort study of 604 hospitalized COVID-19 patients in Thailand during the Delta variant period, following them for one year post-discharge to assess long COVID prevalence and quality of life. The study found very low long COVID symptom prevalence (4.2% shortness of breath, 1.5% cough) at one-year follow-up, with most patients reporting good physical and mental health outcomes.
paper_authors: Pimpinan Khammawan; Aksara Thongprachum; Kannikar Intawong; Suwat Chariyalertsak
paper_title: Severity, mortality, long COVID-19, and quality of life: Insights from a cohort study of hospitalized COVID-19 patients during the delta variant predominance period in Thailand

summary: COREG-FR is a 24-month prospective cohort study of COVID-19 hospitalized patients assessing mobility and cognitive deficits using standardized instruments. While the study documents persistent functional impairment in long COVID patients, it is observational without any treatment intervention and therefore does not meet inclusion criteria for a treatment trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: Marla Beauchamp; Christopher Farley; Renata Kirkwood; Aaron Jones; Terence Ho; MyLinh Duong; Parminder Raina; Jinhui Ma
paper_title: Functional recovery 2-years after hospitalization for COVID-19: Insights from the COREG-FR extension study

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 38,327 COVID-19 patients examining associations between autoimmune diseases and post-COVID condition (PCC) diagnosis using electronic health records. Found that pre-existing autoimmune diseases (psoriasis, rheumatoid arthritis) and post-infection autoimmune diseases (Sjögren's syndrome) are more prevalent in PCC patients, and medical utilization is significantly higher among those with PCC.
paper_authors: Susan R. Sama; Rebecca Gore; Ann Z. Bauer; Lawrence Garber; Richard Rosiello; Meagan Fair; David Kriebel
paper_title: Autoimmune diseases as pre-existing conditions and sequelae of post COVID-19 condition in a Massachusetts community based observational study of COVID-19 patients

summary: A one-year prospective observational cohort study comparing neuromuscular function, fatigue, and muscle architecture in long COVID patients (moderate and severe cases) versus healthy controls. The study found that severe COVID patients exhibited persistent fatigue, reduced torque, and impaired neuromuscular function even one year post-infection, highlighting the need for targeted rehabilitation strategies.
paper_authors: Isabella da Silva Almeida; Leandro Gomes de Jesus Ferreira; Marco Aurélio Vaz; Gerson Cipriano Junior; Monique Alves de Resende; Denis Cesar Leite Vieira; Rochelle Rocha Costa; Nicolas Babault; Rita de Cássia Marqueti; João Luiz Quagliotti Durigan
paper_title: Fatigue and neuromuscular function in long COVID: A one-year follow-up study

summary: Retrospective study comparing autonomic testing results in 143 Long COVID and 170 ME/CFS patients versus healthy controls and hEDS patients. Found extensive similarities between Long COVID and ME/CFS including reduced cerebral blood flow, autonomic failure, small fiber neuropathy, and POTS, suggesting shared pathophysiological mechanisms.
paper_authors: Peter Novak; David M. Systrom; Alexandra Witte; Sadie P. Marciano; Donna Felsenstein; Jeff M. Milunsky; Aubrey Milunsky; Joel Krier; Mark C. Fishman
paper_title: Shared autonomic phenotype of long COVID and myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome

summary: This retrospective cohort study examined demographic and clinical risk factors associated with long COVID using a nationwide sample of 8,329 narrow-definition and 207,537 broad-definition long haulers from the OptumLabs Data Warehouse. Key findings identified hypertension, chronic lung disease, obesity, diabetes, and depression as leading risk factors, with long haulers being older, more female, and having more comorbidities than non-long haulers.
paper_authors: Zirui Song; Mia Giuriato
paper_title: Demographic And Clinical Factors Associated With Long COVID

summary: This prospective observational study compared cerebral blood flow (CBF) patterns in 55 post-COVID condition (PCC) patients versus 36 COVID-recovered controls using MRI arterial spin labeling. Fatigue in PCC patients was associated with reduced perfusion in right occipital regions, suggesting a potential imaging biomarker for the condition.
paper_authors: Jonas A. Hosp; Nils Schröter; Marco Reisert; Sibylle Frase; Elias Kellner; Hansjörg Mast; Cornelius Weiller; Horst Urbach; Alexander Rau
paper_title: Fatigue in Post-COVID-Condition is accompanied by hypoperfusion of right-occipital areas

summary: Prospective observational study of 100 COVID-19 recovered healthcare workers followed for 3 months to assess lung function recovery via spirometry. Found statistically significant improvements in FEV1 and FEV1/FVC% at 1 and 3 months post-discharge, indicating partial lung function recovery in the post-COVID phase.
paper_authors: Mekala Kamala Priyadarshini; Moravineni Usha Rani
paper_title: Study of Lung Function in COVID-19 Pneumonia Recovered Individuals
paper_journal: Journal of Evolution of Medical and Dental Sciences

summary: Prospective case-control study comparing long-term symptoms in 112 COVID-19 positive patients versus 109 COVID-19 negative controls at 10-month follow-up. Found persistent shortness of breath and cough in COVID cases (36% with at least one symptom) versus controls (6%), with significant functional impairment and financial impact in cases.
paper_authors: Mahak Chauhan, presenter; Ihechiluru Nzeako; Feng Li; Paul Thuluvath
paper_title: S505 Long-term Symptoms After COVID-19 Compared to a Control Group

summary: Large-scale UK Biobank cohort study comparing digestive disease risks in 112,311 COVID-19 patients versus contemporary and historical controls over 2.6 years follow-up. Study found significantly elevated risks of multiple gastrointestinal disorders (GERD, FGID, peptic ulcer, liver disease) in long COVID patients, with risks persisting beyond one year post-infection.
paper_authors: Yuying Ma; Lijun Zhang; Rui Wei; Weiyu Dai; Felix W. Leung; Chongyang Duan; Weihong Sha; Hao Chen
paper_title: S137 Risks of Digestive Diseases in Long COVID: Evidence From a Large-Scale Cohort Study

summary: This propensity-matched cohort study investigates the temporal risk of new-onset gastroparesis following SARS-CoV-2 infection using a large database, comparing rates in infected vs. uninfected populations. It is an observational epidemiological study documenting a long COVID sequela rather than evaluating a treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Thabet Qapaja; Motasem Alkhayyat; Khaled Alsabbagh Alchirazi; Osama Abu-Shawer; Serge Baroud; Almaza Albakri; Prashanthi N. Thota
paper_title: S1854 Temporal Trends in the Risk of New-Onset Gastroparesis Following SARS-CoV-2 Infection: A Propensity Matched Cohort Study

summary: This observational case series of 46 long COVID patients describes the endoscopic features of post-COVID-19 cholangiopathy and the role of ERCP in its management. ERCP with interventional cast removal demonstrated therapeutic benefit, improving cholestasis parameters in approximately 60% of treated patients, though overall prognosis remained poor with 44% 1-year liver transplantation-free survival.
paper_authors: Silke Leonhardt; Donata Grajecki; Dominik Geisel; Uli Fehrenbach; Andreas Adler; Julia Leonhardt; David Horst; Florian Kurth; Charlotte Thibeault; Hans-Joachim Janssen; Thomas Kaul; Siegbert Faiss; Frank Tacke; Christian Jürgensen
paper_title: Endoscopic Features of Post–COVID-19 Cholangiopathy and Its Management Using ERCP

summary: This study analyzed COVID-19 infection rates and outcomes in 379 patients with pre-existing gastroparesis enrolled in the NIH Gastroparesis Registry. While it documents that 20% of gastroparesis patients contracted COVID-19 and experienced transient GI symptom worsening, it is a secondary analysis of registry data without testing any active intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Henry Parkman; Katherine Yates; Richard McCallum; Kenneth Koch; Irene Sarosiek; Robert S. Bulat; Thomas Abell; Braden Kuo; Zubair Malik; Gianrico Farrugia; Bruno Chumpitazi; Robert Shulman; Laura Miriel; James Tonascia; Frank Hamilton; Pankaj Pasricha; Madhusudan Grover
paper_title: S650 Effects of COVID-19 in Patients With Gastroparesis: An Analysis of Patients in the NIH Gastroparesis Registry

summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 1,212 COVID-19 survivors aged 60+ from two Wuhan hospitals over 2 years post-discharge to assess long-term symptom burden and identify risk factors. At follow-up, 21.4% reported persistent symptoms, with fatigue, anxiety, and dyspnea being most common; older age and previous oxygen therapy were significant risk factors for severe fatigue and depression.
paper_authors: Ying Zhang; Zhaojie Han; Yang Dai; Yuhui Liu; Qinghua Wang; Lixia Cheng; Chuyue Xiong; Chao Hou; Xinyue Yang; Yidan Ye; Qian Zhao; Naifu Nie; Xiangyu Ma; Huan Tang; Anqiang Zhang; Zhenhong Hu; Guoqiang Cao; Paul Jones; Jianxin Jiang; Ling Zeng; Yong He; Li Li
paper_title: Symptom Burden among Older COVID-19 Survivors Two Years after Hospital Discharge

summary: Post hoc analysis of the PREDIMED-Plus trial examining cognitive outcomes in 5,179 older adults with high cardiovascular risk before and after COVID-19 infection. Found no significant association between COVID-19 and cognitive impairment at 50-week follow-up, suggesting acute cognitive changes may revert over time.
paper_authors: Shyam S.; Gómez-Martínez C.; Ni J.; Gaforio JJ; Martínez-González MÁ; Corella D.; Martínez JA; Alonso-Gómez ÁM; Wärnberg J.; Vioque J.; Romaguera D.; López-Miranda J.; Estruch R.; Tinahones FJ; Lapetra J.; Serra-Majem L.; Bueno-Cavanillas A.; Tur JA; Martín-Sánchez V.; Pintó X.; Delgado-Rodríguez M.; Matía-Martín P.; Vidal J.; Vázquez C.; Daimiel L.; Ros E.; Fernandez-Aranda F.; Hernández-Cacho A.; Buil-Cosiales P.; Sorli JV; Castañer O.; Garcia-Rios A.; Oncina-Canovas A.; Pérez-Farinós N.; Nafria M.; Casas R.; Martínez-Diz S.; Tojal-Sierra L.; Am GP; Toledo E.; Fernández-Carrión R.; Bayón ÁM; Torres-Peña JD; Compañ-Gabucio L.; Vázquez-Ruiz Z.; Babio N.; Fitó M.; Salas-Salvadó J.
paper_title: COVID-19 and Cognitive Decline in Older Adults with High-Cardiovascular Risk: A Post Hoc Analysis

summary: This propensity-matched cohort study compares 1-year risk of cardiovascular, thrombotic, and renal complications after acute COVID-19 in IBD patients versus non-IBD patients. It found no significant differences in complication rates between IBD patients on various medications and control groups, focusing on acute post-infection complications rather than long COVID sequelae.
paper_authors: Aakash Desai; Raymond Cross; Francis A. Farraye; Gursimran S. Kochhar
paper_title: S770 Risk of Cardiovascular, Thrombotic and Renal Complications After COVID-19 in Patients With Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Propensity-Matched Cohort Study

summary: This study examines carbohydrate metabolism disorders in hospitalized COVID-19 patients during acute infection and 6 months post-discharge, stratifying by DM status, steroid-induced hyperglycemia, and stress-induced hyperglycemia. While it does examine a post-COVID period, the focus is on acute COVID-19 outcomes and metabolic complications during hospitalization, not on long COVID syndrome or treatments for persistent symptoms.
paper_authors: © В.В. Салухов; А. А. Минаков; Т.Г. Шарыпова; А.А. Кононова; В.А. Сурхаева; V. Salukhov; Alexey A. Minakov; Tatyana G. Sharypova; Alena A. Kononova; Victoria A. Surkhaeva
paper_title: Сarbohydrate metabolism disorders and their outcomes in the long-term period in hospitalized patients with COVID-19

summary: Retrospective analysis of 134 type 2 diabetes patients comparing post-COVID clinical and laboratory features across three COVID-19 variant periods (Alpha, Delta, Omicron). Omicron period showed fewer comorbidities, hospitalizations, and new diagnoses; differences were also found in platelet counts and coagulation markers between variants.
paper_authors: Saule Altynbekova; В. В. Фадеев; Zhangentkhan Abilayuly; Svetlana Bolshakova
paper_title: Retrospective Analysis of the Characteristics of the Post-COVID Period in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes, Infected During Different Variant-Associated Periods of COVID-19

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines cardiorenal complications in diabetic patients before and after COVID-19 using data from a mobile diagnostic center. It documents increased frequency of kidney dysfunction and cardiovascular complications in the post-COVID period but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Vikulova OК; Zheleznyakova AV; Serkov AA; Isakov MA; Vagapova GR; Valeeva FV; Trubicina NP; Melnikova OG; Aleksandrova VK; Smirnova NB; Egorova DN; Artemova EV; Sorokina KV; Shestakova MV; Mokrysheva NG; Dedov II
paper_title: Multiplex analysis of post-Covid cardiorenal complications in patients with type 1 and type 2 diabetes mellitus according to the mobile diagnostic and treatment center (Diamobil)

summary: This retrospective registry analysis examines carbohydrate metabolism disorders (hyperglycemia and type 2 diabetes) in COVID-19 patients using the AKTIV and AKTIV 2 registries, comparing outcomes including mortality and 12-month post-COVID symptoms across patient groups. While the paper does assess long-term post-COVID consequences, it is a secondary analysis of existing registry data without any intervention being administered—patients are passively stratified by their pre-existing metabolic status rather than being assigned to treatment groups.
paper_authors: Salukhov VV; Arutyunov GP; Tarlovskaya EI; Batluk TI; Bashkinov RA; Samus IV; Melnikov ES; Trubnikova MA; Arutyunov AG
paper_title: The impact of carbohydrate metabolism disorders on the early and long-term clinical outcomes of patients with COVID-19 according to the AKTIV and AKTIV 2 registries

summary: This cross-sectional study examined the course of COVID-19 and post-COVID syndrome (PCS) in 32 patients with rheumatoid arthritis, finding that 47.8% developed PCS with higher rates of hospitalization and severe disease course. The study identifies risk factors for PCS development in rheumatic disease patients but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Аронова Е.С; Белов Б.С; Гриднева Г.И; Фгбну «Научно-исследовательский; шоссе; 34А
paper_title: COVID-19 and post-covid syndrome in patients with rheumatoid arthritis

summary: This study evaluated Actovegin efficacy in treating chronic cerebral ischemia in 440 patients with recent COVID-19 experience, comparing treatment (n=220) vs control (n=220) groups over 90 days. Actovegin-treated patients showed significantly greater improvements in cognitive function, fatigue, sleep, dizziness, emotional state, and quality of life compared to controls.
paper_authors: V. V. Kovalchuk
paper_title: The role of the new coronavirus infection (COVID-19) in the progression and development of cerebrovascular diseases. A competent choice of pathogenic treatment is the key to success in treatment and prevention. An expert’s view from the ‘red zone’

summary: This retrospective-prospective cohort study examined disease activity dynamics in 100 patients with immune-mediated inflammatory rheumatic diseases (RA, SLE, systemic sclerosis, ankylosing spondylitis) following COVID-19 infection, assessed at 3, 6, and 12 months. While the paper documents increased IMIRD flare frequency post-COVID and identifies risk factors, it does not study a treatment intervention for long COVID itself—it only tracks the natural disease course of pre-existing rheumatic conditions.
paper_authors: Saule Abisheva; А. М. Лила; Kristina Rutskaya-Moroshan
paper_title: Analysis of the course of immune-mediated inflammatory rheumatic diseases after COVID-19: flare frequency and prognostic determinants

summary: Retrospective analysis of 46 children (26 post-COVID symptom-free, 20 with post-COVID symptoms) comparing leukocyte and lymphocyte dynamics one week after acute COVID-19. Findings suggest persistent lymphopenia during acute infection is a risk factor for developing post-COVID syndrome, with lymphocyte normalization acting as a protective factor.
paper_authors: O.L. Lychkovska; Kvit Di; I.Yu. Kulachkovska; О. M. Sadova; L. Ya. Zhyvko; Marta Dats-Opoka; N.S. Kosmynina
paper_title: Post-COVID syndrome in children: whether a change in lymphocyte count is a risk factor for its development?

summary: This observational study followed 62 outpatient pneumonia patients over 16 months to document post-COVID syndrome frequency and symptoms. The analysis is descriptive/epidemiological rather than evaluating a specific treatment intervention—it compares symptom prevalence across age groups and vaccination status but does not test or assign any treatment.
paper_authors: Vasyl Melnyk; О. V. Panasiuk; H. V. Sadomova-Andrianova; Yu. B. Zahuta; I. V. Antoniuk; I. O. Sliusarchuk; I. V. Melnyk
paper_title: Post-COVID syndrome

summary: This retrospective cohort study compares cardiac surgery outcomes in 100 patients with prior COVID-19 infection versus 100 pre-pandemic controls. While it examines post-COVID sequelae affecting surgery, it is not a long COVID treatment trial but rather a surgical outcomes study assessing timing and risk factors for cardiac procedures.
paper_authors: Dmytro M. Kosovan
paper_title: Impact of prior COVID-19 infection on cardiac surgery outcomes: optimal timing for valvular heart disease surgery

summary: This case-control study compares hormonal and metabolic markers (vasopressin, ghrelin, insulin) in 31 long COVID patients with coronary artery disease versus 40 coronary patients without COVID history and 15 healthy controls. The study found significant elevations in vasopressin, insulin, and glucose in long COVID patients, establishing correlations with neurovegetative disorders but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: S. M. Manuilov; N. S. Mykhailovska
paper_title: Hormonal-metabolic markers and their relationships in patients with coronary heart disease after suffering from the COVID-19 coronavirus disease

summary: Retrospective observational study of 1,425 COVID-19 patients examining the prevalence and clinical associations of post-COVID-19 tachycardia (PCT) in the post-acute phase. Found PCT prevalence of 28.18% with stronger association in patients <65 years and certain comorbidity profiles, but the study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Jifeng Wang; Dhaval Patel; Shane Robinson; Ania Rynarzewska; Oluseyi Abidoye
paper_title: Evaluation of the Existence of Post-COVID-19 Tachycardia in a Community Healthcare System

summary: This retrospective cohort study compares cardiac structure and function in 71 CHD patients with and without prior COVID-19 history, finding significantly worse cardiac remodeling, increased myocardial hypertrophy, and higher energy expenditure in the long COVID group. The study demonstrates that COVID-19 history is associated with increased risk of cardiac complications in CHD patients but does not test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: S. M. Manuilov; N. S. Mykhailovska
paper_title: Structural and functional changes of the heart in patients with coronary heart disease who have had coronavirus disease COVID-19

summary: Retrospective study comparing cognitive fatigue and neuropsychological test performance in 35 long COVID and 50 MS patients. Found fatigue correlates with monotonous attention tasks in MS but not long COVID, suggesting different cognitive fatigue mechanisms between conditions.
paper_authors: Helmut Hildebrandt; Katrin Hanken; Thomas Duning; Heiner Stuke; Paul Eling
paper_title: Fatigue acts as a distractor in monotonous and dual attention tasks in patients with multiple sclerosis but not with long COVID

summary: A prospective cross-sectional study of 152 severe COVID-19 survivors in Latin America evaluated long-term mental health and cognitive outcomes at an average of 24.5 months post-illness using validated psychiatric and cognitive assessment instruments. The study found high prevalence of anxiety (33%), depression (49%), and cognitive dysfunction (11%), with worse outcomes in women and ICU-admitted patients, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Juan Carlos Rivas Nieto; Brayan Daniel Cordoba-Melo; Juan Pablo Arango-Ibanez; Sebastian Seni-Molina; Mario Miguel Barbosa Rengifo; Carlos Alberto Miranda-Bastidas; Andres Felipe Casanova Rojas; Andres Fernando Mina Sanchez; Cesar J. Herrera; Miguel Angel Quintana Da Silva; Andres Felipe Buitrago; Maria Lorena Coronel Gilio; Freddy Pow-Chon-Long; Juan Esteban Gomez-Mesa
paper_title: Long-Term Mental Health Evaluation After COVID-19: Insights From the CARDIO COVID 20–21 Registry

summary: This observational study assessed functional capacity, fatigue, and dyspnea in 92 COVID-19 patients (moderate, severe, critical) during the first month post-discharge using standardized instruments (6MWT, FSS, FIS, mMRC). Results showed that critical disease severity was associated with lower functional capacity and higher fatigue and dyspnea severity, but no treatment intervention was evaluated.
paper_authors: Akdeniz Leblebicier, Merve; Kavuncu, Vural; Marım, Feride; Yaman, Fatıma
paper_title: Do functional capacity, fatigue and dyspnea change in the post-acute period according to severity of COVID-19?

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 57 hospitalized COVID-19 patients contacted 6 months post-discharge to assess multi-system symptom burden using standardized questionnaires. Found high rates of fatigue (60%), dyspnea (57%), and neuropsychiatric symptoms (56%), with females and younger patients reporting greater functional impairment.
paper_authors: Ashish Bhargava; Wei Zhao; Mamta Sharma; Susanna M. Szpunar; Louis Saravolatz
paper_title: Six-Month Post-Acute COVID-19: High Self-Reported Morbidity Among Adults Younger Than Sixty Years and Females

summary: Prospective cohort study of 471 university employees followed at 3 and 6 months post-COVID to assess symptom persistence and anxiety. Found that 32.1% had persistent symptoms at 3 months and 13.0% at 6 months, with shortness of breath and fatigue being most common.
paper_authors: Muz FNÖ; Metintaş S.; Önsüz MF; Ünsal A.; Arslantaş D.; Kılınç A.; Koç SDG; Sungur S.
paper_title: Prevalence of Post-COVID-19 Syndrome and Related Factors in University Employees: A Prospective Cohort Study

summary: This prospective study evaluates pulmonary function in 34 pediatric COVID-19 patients compared to 33 controls after hospital discharge, finding reduced FVC, FEV1, and FEV1/FVC values in the patient group. The study does not examine long COVID as a syndrome of persistent symptoms weeks/months post-infection, but rather acute post-discharge respiratory outcomes in recently hospitalized children.
paper_authors: Ipek S.; Gungor S.; Gullu UU; Kizildag B.; Ozkars MY; Yurttutan S.; Kutukcu MK; Demiray S.
paper_title: Evaluation of Pulmonary Functions after Discharge in Pediatric Patients with COVID-19: A Prospective Study
paper_journal: SiSli Etfal Hastanesi Tip Bulteni / The Medical Bulletin of Sisli Hospital

summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 77 COVID-19 patients with olfactory and taste loss for 12-14 months to determine the prevalence, severity, and long-term course of these symptoms. Most patients showed recovery, with only 15.6% experiencing persistent smell loss and 8% persistent taste loss at follow-up; notably, the study did not test any treatment intervention but rather passively observed symptom progression.
paper_authors: Turk B.; Aybal A.; Salepci E.; Dizdar SK; Turgut S.
paper_title: What is the long term findings of olfactory and taste loss due to COVID-19?
paper_journal: SiSli Etfal Hastanesi Tip Bulteni / The Medical Bulletin of Sisli Hospital

summary: Prospective follow-up study of 26 severe COVID-19 patients (~20 months post-hospitalization) assessing late symptoms and pulmonary function via spirometry and diffusion capacity testing. Found high prevalence of fatigue (65.4%), brain fog (50%), and weight gain (46.2%), with 61.5% showing reduced diffusion capacity, though no correlation between symptom burden and functional abnormalities.
paper_authors: Darina Miteva; Sibel Ispir; Vanya Kostadinova
paper_title: Late symptoms and lung function tests  after severe COVID-19

summary: Longitudinal study tracking muscle sympathetic nerve activity and hemodynamic responses over 6 months in young adults recovering from SARS-CoV-2 infection. Found improvements in blood pressure over recovery period but no direct changes in sympathetic activity, suggesting cardiovascular impairments may improve independent of sympathetic changes.
paper_authors: Nina L. Stute; Rachel E. Szeghy; Jonathon L. Stickford; Valesha P. Province; Marc A. Augenreich; Stephen M. Ratchford; Abigail S. L. Stickford
paper_title:
Longitudinal observations of sympathetic neural activity and hemodynamics during 6 months recovery from
            <scp>SARS‐CoV</scp>
            ‐2 infection

summary: This observational study followed 13 professional football players to assess COVID-19 symptom persistence and physiological recovery, comparing pulmonary function and metabolic power before and after infection. The study found that general and muscle fatigue persisted for weeks in most players and metabolic capacity was significantly reduced post-COVID, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Chiara Gattoni; Emanuele Conti; Andrea Casolo; Stefano Nuccio; Carmine Baglieri; Carlo Capelli; Michele Girardi
paper_title: COVID‐19 disease in professional football players: symptoms and impact on pulmonary function and metabolic power during matches

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining the one-minute sit-to-stand test (1MSTST) as a monitoring tool in 97 patients recovering from COVID-19 pneumonia one year post-infection. The study validates 1MSTST as a feasible alternative to pulmonary function tests and identifies correlations with age and inflammatory markers, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Çağla Koç
paper_title: The role of one-minute sit-to-stand test in monitoring patients with COVID-19 pneumonia

summary: Longitudinal observational study of 487 post-acute COVID-19 syndrome patients followed over one year with symptom assessments via questionnaire. Documents persistent symptoms (dyspnea, weakness, fatigue, arthralgia) with higher prevalence in females and non-hospitalized patients, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Emiroglu C.; Dicle M.; Ozagar SD; Gorpelioglu S.; Aypak C.
paper_title: Evaluation of post-acute-COVID-19, and long-COVID symptoms with a questionnaire: Within one year, a longitudinal study

summary: A retrospective proof-of-concept study evaluating a 3-month personalized pulmonary rehabilitation program (endurance and resistance training) in 17 long-COVID patients. The program significantly improved quality of life, physical fitness (6MWT increased from 329 to 365 m), and chest CT parameters including reduced air trapping and increased airway volume.
paper_authors: Wendel Dierckx; Wilfried De Backer; Yinka De Meyer; Eline Lauwers; Erik Franck; Jan De Backer; Kris Ides
paper_title: Personalized pulmonary rehabilitation program for patients with post‐acute sequelae of COVID‐19: A proof‐of‐concept retrospective study

summary: Prospective observational study of young adults undergoing monthly transthoracic echocardiography for 6 months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection to assess cardiac structure and function changes. Found preserved left heart structure but subclinical improvements in some cardiac function parameters and reduced troponin-I over the 6-month recovery period.
paper_authors: Sophie S. Osada; Rachel E. Szeghy; Nina L. Stute; Valesha M. Province; Marc A. Augenreich; Andrew Putnam; Jonathon L. Stickford; Abigail S. L. Stickford; Gregory J. Grosicki; Stephen M. Ratchford
paper_title: Monthly transthoracic echocardiography in young adults for 6 months following <scp>SARS‐CoV</scp>‐2 infection

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing healthcare utilization between 531,702 SARS-CoV-2 test-positive and test-negative adults in Ontario, followed for 56+ days post-infection. Found significantly higher rates of healthcare encounters, hospital admissions, and long-term care use in test-positive individuals, particularly among females.
paper_authors: Candace D. McNaughton; Peter C. Austin; Atul Sivaswamy; Jiming Fang; Husam Abdel-Qadir; Nick Daneman; Jacob A. Udell; Walter P. Wodchis; Ivona Mostarac; Douglas S. Lee; Clare L. Atzema
paper_title: Post-acute health care burden after SARS-CoV-2 infection: a retrospective cohort study

summary: A prospective cohort study measuring maximal inspiratory and expiratory pressure in 145 COVID-19 patients at 5 and 12 months post-infection, comparing to healthy controls. Found reduced respiratory pressures in only 16% of participants with little improvement over time.
paper_authors: Thora Wesenberg Helt; Jan Christensen; Ronan M. G. Berg; Thomas Kromann Lund; Anna Kalhauge; Frederikke Rönsholt; Daria Podlekareva; Elisabeth Arndal; Flemming Madsen; Mathias Munkholm; Birgitte Hanel; Anne‐Mette Lebech; Terese Lea Katzenstein; Jann Mortensen
paper_title: Maximal respiratory pressure after <scp>COVID</scp>‐19 compared with reference material in healthy adults: A prospective cohort study (The <scp>SECURe</scp> study)

summary: A retrospective study of 21 PASC patients examining relationships between symptoms, blood volume distribution, exercise tolerance, lung volumes, and functional status using pulmonary function tests, 6-minute walk tests, and cardiopulmonary exercise testing. The study found significant differences in exercise capacity and lung function between patients with minor vs severe functional limitations, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Wendel Dierckx; Wilfried De Backer; Kris Ides; Yinka De Meyer; Eline Lauwers; Erik Franck; Jan De Backer
paper_title: Unraveling pathophysiologic mechanisms contributing to symptoms in patients with post‐acute sequelae of <scp>COVID</scp>‐19 (<scp>PASC</scp>): A retrospective study

summary: Retrospective analysis of laboratory data from 186 long COVID patients evaluated at Okayama University Hospital to characterize hormonal abnormalities associated with symptom severity. Found correlations between fatigue and elevated cortisol/FT4, thyroid dysfunction, and altered adrenal-pituitary ratios, suggesting endocrine dysfunction contributes to persistent long COVID symptoms.
paper_authors: Naruhiko Sunada; Hiroyuki Honda; Yasuhiro Nakano; Koichiro Yamamoto; Kazuki Tokumasu; Yasue Sakurada; Yui Matsuda; Toru Hasegawa; Yuki Otsuka; Mikako Obika; Yoshihisa Hanayama; Hideharu Hagiya; Keigo Ueda; Hitomi Kataoka; Fumio Otsuka
paper_title: Hormonal trends in patients suffering from long COVID symptoms

summary: Investigates pituitary and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis function in 43 patients 3-7 months after acute COVID-19 infection using hormone stimulation tests. Found abnormalities in GH and cortisol responses in some patients, suggesting COVID-19 may affect pituitary function, but this is a cross-sectional observational study with no intervention or treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Emre Urhan; Zuleyha Karaca; Gamze Kalin Unuvar; Kursat Gundogan; Kursad Unluhizarci
paper_title: Investigation of pituitary functions after acute coronavirus disease 2019

summary: This cross-sectional study measures lung diffusion capacity (DLCO and DLNO) in 49 patients recovering from severe COVID-19 pneumonitis at ~2 months post-discharge, with repeat testing in 17 patients at ~4 months. The findings show that alveolar membrane dysfunction improves over time while vascular injury effects (reduced capillary blood volume) persist, but no specific treatment intervention is evaluated or tested.
paper_authors: Leigh M. Seccombe; David Heath; Claude S. Farah; James R. Di Michiel; Elizabeth M. Veitch; Matthew J. Peters
paper_title: Mechanisms of gas transfer impairment utilizing nitric oxide following severe <scp>COVID</scp>‐19 pneumonitis

summary: Longitudinal observational cohort study of 102 severe COVID-19 survivors followed 3 years post-hospitalization, characterizing radiologic abnormalities, pulmonary function, and histopathologic findings. Study documents persistent fibrotic-like changes in 61% of survivors with modest improvement over time but no active treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Scarlett O. Murphy; Claire F. McGroder; Mary M. Salvatore; Belinda M. D’Souza; Kathleen M. Capaccione; Anjali Saqi; Faisal Shaikh; Shannon Benesh; David Zhang; Matthew R. Baldwin; Christine Kim Garcia
paper_title: Imaging, Pulmonary Function, and Histopathologic Findings of Persistent Fibrosis in a Longitudinal Cohort 3 Years after COVID-19
paper_journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society

summary: A prospective cohort study of 428 COVID-19 ICU survivors followed for 12 months to assess disabilities, frailty, cognitive impairment, and clinical events. While disabilities and cognitive symptoms peaked at 3 months post-discharge, significant improvement occurred over the year, though one-third of patients remained worse than pre-COVID status.
paper_authors: Leandro U. Taniguchi; Márlon J. R. Aliberti; Murilo B. Dias; Wilson Jacob-Filho; Thiago J. Avelino-Silva
paper_title: Twelve Months and Counting: Following Clinical Outcomes in Critical COVID-19 Survivors
paper_journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society

summary: This study measures inflammatory biomarkers and vitamins in hospitalized COVID-19 patients and compares them to post-COVID syndrome patients to identify prognostic markers. It is an observational biomarker study without any treatment intervention, focusing on diagnostic assessment rather than evaluating a therapeutic approach.
paper_authors: Lenka Kujovská Krčmová; Lenka Javorská; Kateřina Matoušová; Petr Šmahel; Mikuláš Skála; Michal Kopecký; Chaweewan Suwanvecho; Nikola Přívratská; Dorota Turoňová; Bohuslav Melichar
paper_title: Evaluation of inflammatory biomarkers and vitamins in hospitalized patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection and post-COVID syndrome

summary: This prospective study compares fetal thymus size in pregnant women who recovered from COVID-19 (4+ weeks post-infection) versus age-matched controls. The study found significantly lower fetal thymic-thoracic ratio in COVID-19 recovered pregnant women but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention for long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Sule Goncu Ayhan; Ezgi Turgut; Deniz Oluklu; Eda Ozden Tokalioglu; Dilek Menekse Beser; Ozlem Moraloglu Tekin; Dilek Sahin
paper_title: Influence of Covid-19 infection on fetal thymus size after recovery

summary: This cross-sectional study compared brain white matter integrity and cognitive/psychiatric outcomes between 23 post-COVID participants and 24 healthy controls using diffusion tensor imaging. While it identified microstructural brain abnormalities in post-COVID patients, it is excluded because it is an observational case-control study with no treatment intervention tested.
paper_authors: Huajun Liang; Thomas Ernst; Kenichi Oishi; Meghann C. Ryan; Edward Herskovits; Eric Cunningham; Eleanor Wilson; Shyamasundaran Kottilil; Linda Chang
paper_title: Abnormal brain diffusivity in participants with persistent neuropsychiatric symptoms after COVID-19

summary: Cross-sectional and longitudinal study comparing brain morphometry and neuropsychiatric symptoms between 29 post-COVID patients and 25 healthy controls using MRI and standardized neurobehavioral assessments. Found larger putamen and amygdala volumes in post-COVID patients at baseline, with abnormalities associated with anxiety, depression, and pain, though morphometric differences diminished at 3-year follow-up.
paper_authors: Meghann Ryan; Jared Thomas; Jeremy Wang; Huajun Liang; Eric Cunningham; Thomas Ernst; Linda Chang
paper_title: Structural brain abnormalities and neuropsychiatric symptoms in post-COVID condition

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines high sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) as a prognostic indicator for cardiovascular disease in 26 non-diabetic COVID-19 ICU survivors with one-year follow-up. The findings show elevated hs-CRP in 23% of patients at high cardiovascular risk, suggesting hs-CRP may serve as an early warning marker for post-COVID cardiovascular complications.
paper_authors: Mugundhan Kandhasami; Subash Panchanathan; Jayanthi Rajendran; Karthik Balajee Laksham
paper_title: High Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein as a Prognostic Indicator of Cardiovascular Disease in Severe Non-Diabetic COVID-19 Patients

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 246 long COVID patients with cardiopulmonary symptoms identified 8-12 weeks post-infection to characterize risk factors for developing long COVID. Found that prior oxygen support during acute COVID-19 combined with pre-existing OSA or COPD significantly increased odds of developing cardiopulmonary long COVID symptoms (OR 3.6-12.19).
paper_authors: Jenna Mahoney; Genti Shatri; Patricia E. Simmer; Daniel Doherty; Vamsi Matta; Dominic J. Valentino
paper_title: Retrospective analysis of patients with cardiopulmonary symptoms in the setting of Long COVID syndrome: investigating risk factors

summary: A cross-sectional study of 217 COVID-19 convalescent patients in Wuhan 30 months post-infection, assessing long COVID symptoms, functional status, and risk factors through questionnaire, laboratory testing, and physical assessments. Found 62.2% had long COVID symptoms; older age, female gender, and lack of vaccination were risk factors, while vaccination and exercise were protective.
paper_authors: Yu Yin; Yi Guo; Mingzhong Xiao; Qinlin Chen; Pinpin Long; Xi Wang; Jingzhi Wang; Zuoyu Shao; Yutong Qiu; Yixuan Lu; Yuchan Yang; Xueqin Shi; Wei Ni; Shanshan Cheng; Qi Wang; Li Liu; Tangchun Wu; Xiaodong Li; Hao Wang; Yu Yuan
paper_title: Health Consequences Among COVID-19 Convalescent Patients 30 Months Post-Infection in China

summary: Cross-sectional assessment of 153 long COVID patients at median 75 days post-infection, evaluating respiratory recovery, fatigue, and health status across initial disease severity groups. Study found persistent subjective health complaints and fatigue in >60% of patients, but these were not associated with initial disease severity or objective respiratory findings.
paper_authors: Liam Townsend; Joanne Dowds; Kate O’Brien; Grainne Sheill; Adam H. Dyer; Brendan O’Kelly; John P. Hynes; Aoife Mooney; Jean Dunne; Cliona Ni Cheallaigh; Cliona O’Farrelly; Nollaig M. Bourke; Niall Conlon; Ignacio Martin-Loeches; Colm Bergin; Parthiban Nadarajan; Ciaran Bannan
paper_title: Persistent Poor Health after COVID-19 Is Not Associated with Respiratory Complications or Initial Disease Severity
paper_journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society

summary: This cross-sectional study examines cardiovascular symptoms in 452 recovered COVID-19 patients at a Chinese hospital, identifying risk factors (female sex, younger age, pre-existing cardiovascular disease) associated with post-COVID cardiovascular sequelae. No treatment intervention is tested; the study is observational and descriptive, characterizing symptom prevalence and risk factors rather than evaluating a therapeutic intervention.
paper_authors: Xiaoyu Zhao; Dongli Wang; Yongzhi Chen; Na Zhang; Tianshu Li; Ruixia Fan; Lei Yang; Chuanhua Yang; Jie Yang
paper_title: Factors influencing cardiovascular system-related post-COVID-19 sequelae: A single-center cohort study

summary: This cross-sectional study compares sST2 biomarker levels and left ventricular morphology in CAD/CHF patients with and without prior COVID-19 infection. While it examines post-COVID cardiac sequelae, it is not a long COVID study as it focuses on established heart disease patients rather than long COVID syndrome, and does not test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Sergey S. Fateev; Ivan M. Ryzhkov; Vladimir K. Fedulov; Elena V. Kovalenko; Ludmila I. Markova; Olga L. Belaya
paper_title: sST2 and morphofunctional parameters of the left ventricle in patients with coronary artery disease and chronic heart failure after COVID-19

summary: This case-control study compares biomarker levels (sFlt-1 and AECA) in ACS patients with and without prior COVID-19 infection history. While it examines post-COVID ACS outcomes, it focuses on acute cardiac events rather than long COVID as a persistent condition and does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Valentina A. Kozik; Lyubov A. Shpagina; Ilya S. Shpagin; Evgeny M. Loktin
paper_title: Evaluation of soluble fms-like thyrosine kinase-1 and anti-endothelial cell antibodies in patients with acute coronary syndrome after COVID-19 infection

summary: This study compares echocardiographic parameters in 118 patients with acute coronary syndrome combined with post-COVID syndrome versus 121 ACS patients without PCS. Patients with ACS+PCS showed significantly more pronounced cardiac changes including increased pulmonary artery pressure, mitral regurgitation, and complications like left ventricular thrombus and aneurysms.
paper_authors: Valentina A. Kozik; Lyubov A. Shpagina; Ilya S. Shpagin; Evgeny M. Loktin
paper_title: Features of echocardiography parameters in acute coronary syndrome in combination with post COVID-19 syndrome

summary: Prospective study of 114 COVID-19 patients followed for ~1 year to evaluate biomarkers predicting major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in post-COVID patients. Found that elevated pentraxin 3 (PTX3) and other inflammatory biomarkers predict MACE development, but this is a biomarker prognostic study, not a treatment intervention trial.
paper_authors: Tatyana V. Kanaeva; Nina A. Karoli
paper_title: Pentraxin 3: possibilities and prospects for using a biomarker in patients with COVID-19

summary: Prospective study of 114 COVID-19 patients followed for ~1 year to assess whether serum biomarkers (PTX3, IL-6, D-dimer, LDH, CK-MB) predict major adverse cardiovascular events post-COVID. PTX3 >3.1 ng/ml showed 94% sensitivity and 82% specificity for MACE prediction, but this is an observational cohort study without any intervention or treatment being tested.
paper_authors: Tatyana V. Kanaeva; Nina A. Karoli
paper_title: Pentraxin-3: Possibilities and perspectives for using the biomarker in patients with previous COVID-19
paper_journal: Saratov Journal of Medical Scientific Research

summary: This retrospective cohort study examined sodium alterations in COVID-19 pneumonia patients and their association with long-term outcomes including hospital readmissions and mortality over 18 months of follow-up. The study identifies abnormal sodium levels as a prognostic factor for poor long-term recovery in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.
paper_authors: Marianna Martino; Nairus Aboud; Michele Perrone; Paolo Falcioni; Giulia Giancola; Alessandro Ciarloni; Gianmaria Salvio; Francesca Silvetti; Augusto Taccaliti; Giorgio Arnaldi
paper_title: Sodium alterations impair the long-term prognosis of hospitalized patients with COVID-19 pneumonia: hospital readmissions and mortality rates after a 18-month follow-up

summary: A 6-month prospective follow-up study of liver function recovery in 78 patients hospitalized for SARS-CoV-2 infection without pre-existing liver disease. The study documents the natural history of liver injury and recovery post-hospitalization but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Adina Roman; Septimiu Moldovan; Mircea Stoian; Brindusa Tilea; Daniela Dobru
paper_title: SARS-CoV-2 associated liver injury: a six-month follow-up analysis of liver function recovery

summary: This study compares echocardiographic parameters in 118 ACS patients with post-COVID syndrome versus 121 ACS patients without post-COVID syndrome. It is observational (no treatment intervention) and does not qualify as a treatment trial, though it does characterize post-COVID cardiac complications.
paper_authors: Valentina A. Kozik; Lyubov A. Shpagina; Ilya S. Shpagin; Evgeny M. Loktin
paper_title: Features of echocardiography parameters in acute coronary syndrome combined with post-COVID syndrome
paper_journal: Saratov Journal of Medical Scientific Research

summary: Longitudinal observational study of 62 type 2 diabetes patients examining mental health and metabolic markers at two timepoints (2023-2024) stratified by COVID-19 severity and infection year. Findings show improved psychological well-being and reduced diabetes-related distress over time, with potential associations between mental health and cholesterol levels.

paper_title: Post-COVID-19: effects on mental health and metabolic markers in type 2 diabetes

summary: This study examines thyroid dysfunction in 183 patients hospitalized with severe acute COVID-19, with 12-month follow-up of 75 survivors. It documents transient thyroid changes during acute infection that largely normalize over time, but does not focus on long COVID or test any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Long-term outcome of thyroid abnormalities in patients with severe Covid-19

summary: This study compares myocardial revascularization outcomes in acute coronary syndrome patients with and without prior COVID-19 infection history. While it examines post-COVID complications, it focuses on acute cardiac events rather than long COVID syndrome, which is characterized by persistent symptoms weeks to months after infection.
paper_authors: Valentina A. Kozik; Lyubov A. Shpagina; Ilya S. Shpagin
paper_title: Characteristics of myocardial revascularization in patients with acute coronary syndrome in the post-COVID period
paper_journal: Saratov Journal of Medical Scientific Research

summary: This cross-sectional study examines clinical features of post-COVID syndrome in 72 patients with carbohydrate metabolism disorders (impaired glucose tolerance or diabetes). The paper describes symptom prevalence and risk factors but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Ksenia S. Savchuk
paper_title: Clinical features of post-COVID syndrome in patients with carbohydrate metabolism disorders
paper_journal: Saratov Journal of Medical Scientific Research

summary: This study examined ECG patterns and arrhythmias in 758 post-COVID-19 patients during a 2-month recovery period, analyzing associations with age, sex, comorbidities, and disease severity. The findings demonstrate that arrhythmias in post-COVID patients are primarily associated with disease severity and comorbidities such as diabetes mellitus, with relationships to hypoxia, inflammation, and metabolic disturbances.

The research identifies elevated inflammatory markers (lactate, glucose, CRP, LDH) in individuals with persistent post-COVID symptoms, suggesting chronic inflammatory processes regardless of vaccination status.

summary: Population-based prospective cohort study of 1,026 Canadian children aged 8–13 followed for 76 weeks to determine the incidence of post-COVID-19 condition (PCC). Found a very low incidence of PCC (0.4%, only 1 child) with most children recovering within 6 weeks; pre-existing comorbidities (asthma, allergies, anxiety, ADHD) were not associated with increased PCC risk.

paper_title: Post–COVID-19 Condition in Children

summary: Prospective observational study of 103 patients with mild to moderate COVID-19 that assessed cardiovascular changes via echocardiography and arterial stiffness measurements at baseline and 6 months. Found persistent diastolic dysfunction, global longitudinal strain alterations, and ventricular-arterial coupling changes, particularly in moderate COVID-19 patients and men, documenting cardiovascular sequelae of COVID-19.

paper_title: Cardiac Dysfunction and Subclinical Atherosclerosis in Post-COVID-19 Patients

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluates associations between long-COVID symptoms and psychological factors (depression, anxiety, life satisfaction, social support) in 166 non-hospitalized patients at a post-COVID clinic. The study found that depression and anxiety correlate positively with symptom count, while life satisfaction and social support correlate negatively, but no treatment intervention was tested.

summary: Prospective observational cohort study following 282 COVID-19 patients for 15-42 weeks to monitor post-COVID symptoms and their duration. Found that 67% developed symptoms lasting >1 month, with fatigue (29%) and hyposmia (27%) being most common; fatigue spontaneously resolved after ~19 weeks in most cases.

paper_title: Poszt-COVID–19-szindrómás esetek kialakulásának követése

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining the incidence of myocarditis in COVID-19 recovered patients using cardiac magnetic resonance imaging over a 2-year period. Found that 54% of patients showed evidence of myocarditis with myocardial oedema and fibrosis, identifying cardiac involvement as a lasting consequence of COVID-19.

summary: Retrospective chart review of 79 long COVID patients presenting with gastrointestinal symptoms to a university hospital, characterizing common GI manifestations, laboratory abnormalities, and demographic/clinical risk factors. Study identifies female gender, obesity, cardiovascular disease, and cancer as major risk factors; does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

summary: Longitudinal observational study of 441 COVID-19 patients from long-term care facilities followed for 6 months post-discharge to identify factors associated with mortality and sequelae. Found high frequency of post-discharge sequelae (59%) and identified advanced age, male sex, ICU admission, and baseline vulnerability as risk factors for mortality.
paper_authors: Rivera Izquierdo; R. Duarte; Cárdenas Cruz; Mario Rivera
paper_title: Factors associated with mortality and sequelae in patients living in long-term facilities hospitalized for COVID-19: a longitudinal 6-month follow-up study

summary: This study examines neurovegetative and psychological characteristics in 80 infertile women with long COVID compared to 40 controls without COVID history, assessing their association with assisted reproductive technology (ART) outcomes. Women with long COVID and infertility showed higher levels of autonomic dysfunction, anxiety, depression, and stress factors, with these being significant risk factors for ART failure.

paper_title: The influence of neurovegetative and psychological characteristics of infertile patients with long-term COVID-19 on the effectiveness of assisted reproductive technologies

summary: Retrospective analysis of post-COVID-19 symptoms and sleep-wake disturbances across three SARS-CoV-2 variant waves (Alpha, Delta, Omicron) in Hungarian patients presenting >4 weeks post-infection. summary: A prospective cohort study of 127 children with COVID-19 examined whether zinc deficiency (hypozincemia) correlates with long COVID development over 12 months. While zinc deficiency was present in 25.2% of children and long COVID occurred in 42.5%, no statistically significant correlation was found between zinc levels and long COVID development, though fatigue and neurological symptoms were numerically more frequent in zinc-deficient children.

paper_title: Hypozincemia and Long COVID symptoms in children

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining the relationship between dialysis adequacy (spKt/V) and long-term COVID-19 outcomes in 195 hemodialysis patients. Finds that suboptimal dialysis dose is associated with significantly increased risk of COVID-19 sequelae, hospitalization, and mortality at one year, but does not test an intervention or treatment—it is purely observational.

paper_title: Hemodialysis dose and long-term COVID-19 outcomes – a retrospective cohort study
paper_journal: European Journal of Clinical and Experimental Medicine

summary: This case-control study compares reproductive function outcomes between 80 infertile women with long COVID history and 40 without COVID history. While it documents associations between long COVID and reproductive dysfunction (reduced ovarian reserve, menstrual disorders, lower IVF success rates), it is not a treatment trial—it is a comparative observational study examining disease consequences rather than evaluating any therapeutic intervention.
paper_authors: I.S. Golovchak
paper_title: The reproductive function of women with infertility after suffering COVID-19 infection

summary: Observational cross-sectional survey of 68 healthcare workers at a Moscow clinic assessing long COVID symptoms and their impact on working capacity.
