paper_title: Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio (NLR) to Monitor Neuroinflammation Status During Long COVID

summary: Retrospective chart review of 543 long-COVID patients examining the relationship between peripheral neuropathy and demographic/comorbidity factors. Study reports incidence and risk factors for new-onset and progressing neuropathy but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Nagata T.; Ochiai N.; Kondo H.; Oku K.; Tsurusaki M.; Futami T.; Watanabe A.; Matsushita I.
paper_title: Peripheral Neuropathy in Long-COVID Patients: Demographic Distribution and Medical Risk Factors

summary: This retrospective study examined cardiac function changes in 54 chronic heart failure patients 5-6 months after COVID-19 infection, finding decreased left ventricular ejection fraction and increased pulmonary artery systolic pressure. While it studies long-term COVID effects, it does not focus on long COVID as a distinct condition and does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention for long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Ageev AA; Kozhevnikova MV; Emelyanov AV; Krivova AV; Shumskaya YF; Musaeva LM; Popova LV; Naymann YI; Abdullaeva GB; Privalova EV; Belenkov YN
paper_title: The Effect of COVID-19 on Long-Term Cardiac Function in Patients With Chronic Heart Failure

summary: This prospective cohort study of 15 post-COVID myocarditis patients describes clinical presentations, cardiac imaging findings, and evidence of SARS-CoV-2 persistence in myocardial biopsies up to 9 months post-infection. The study is primarily descriptive and mechanistic (documenting disease features and autoimmune/viral mechanisms) rather than evaluating a treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the trials dataset.
paper_authors: Blagova OV; Kogan EA; Lutokhina YA; Kukleva AD; Ainetdinova DH; Novosadov VM; Rud RS; Zaitsev AY; Zaidenov VA; Kupriyanova AG; Alexandrova SА; Fomin VV
paper_title: Subacute and chronic post-covid myoendocarditis: clinical presentation, role of coronavirus persistence and autoimmune mechanisms

summary: This retrospective cohort study used multislice CT scans to monitor lung macrostructure changes in 146 COVID-19 pneumonia patients over 2 years post-infection. The study found that residual lung changes (fibrosis, ground glass, bronchiectasis) persisted in older patients and those with severe initial pneumonia, with complete resolution in only 90% of the mildest cases by year 2.
paper_authors: P. M. Kotlyarov; D. G. Soldatov; I. D. Lagkueva; Z. S. Tsallagova; V. A. Solodkiy
paper_title: The macrostructure of lungs on multislice computed tomography scans in the long-term period after COVID-19 pneumonia

summary: This retrospective cohort study evaluates respiratory function dynamics in 60 patients with COVID-19-associated lung injury at two timepoints (1-6 months and 12-24 months post-discharge) using spirometry and diffusion capacity testing. The study documents improvement in restrictive ventilation disorders and lung diffusion capacity over one year, but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: A. V. Chernyak; M. Kh. Mustafina; Zh. K. Naumenko; E. N. Kalmanova; K. A. Zykov
paper_title: Dynamics of functional changes in the respiratory system after COVID-19-associated lung injury at one year after hospital discharge

summary: This prospective cohort study followed 196 COVID-19 hospital survivors at 3, 6, and 12 months post-discharge to assess long-term sequelae and functional recovery. While most patients showed good overall recovery, 51% still had persistent symptoms at 12 months, with breathlessness and fatigue being the most common long COVID manifestations.
paper_authors: Raghavendra B. M.; Chandrashekar Matad
paper_title: Comprehensive assessment of short- and long-term clinical outcomes of COVID-19 patients post discharge from a tertiary care designated COVID-19 hospital in South India
paper_journal: International Journal of Research in Medical Sciences

summary: This prospective study investigated the incidence and factors associated with insomnia in COVID-19 survivors over a one-year period. The study found approximately 7% insomnia prevalence among recovered patients, with no significant correlation to infection severity, demographics, or comorbidities.
paper_authors: Nidhi Bharat Phal; Akshatha Savith; Ameena Meah
paper_title: Exploring the long-term impact of COVID-19: incidence and factors associated with insomnia in recovered patients
paper_journal: International Journal of Research in Medical Sciences

summary: This retrospective observational study examines pathomorphological changes in the iliac artery of cyclists who recovered from COVID-19, comparing recreational and amateur cyclists over 3 years. The study investigates potential associations between post-COVID vascular changes and doping use, finding minimal progression in recreational cyclists but significant intima-media thickness changes in amateur cyclists potentially related to doping.
paper_authors: Sid Solakovic; Haris Serhatlic; Dejan Stojanovic; Mirela Stojanovic; Sara Stojanovic; Nina Solakovic; Fedja Hajrulahovic; Ratko Pavlović; Mensur Vrcić; Dan Alexe; Zhanneta Kozina; Nevzat Demirci
paper_title: Possible interconnection between irational doping, veterinary medication, and pathomorphological changes in the iliac artery segment in population of cyclists who have infected and recovered from Covid-19 disease

summary: Prospective observational study of 40 post-COVID patients presenting with coronary artery disease symptoms, using coronary angiography to assess stenosis severity. Found high prevalence of coronary abnormalities including slow flow, stenosis with thrombosis, and total occlusion in this symptomatic cohort.
paper_authors: Abhinav Chhabra; Vinod Shisode; Richa Rajput
paper_title: Coronary artery disease in post-COVID patients: a prospective study
paper_journal: International Journal of Research in Medical Sciences

summary: Retrospective study of 272 children (182 COVID-19, 90 MIS-C) examining D-dimer levels as a biomarker for disease severity and mortality prediction. D-dimer showed significant elevation in severe cases and non-survivors, with ROC-derived cutoff values of ≥4.58 µg/ml for COVID-19 and ≥4.73 µg/ml for MIS-C predicting mortality.
paper_authors: Nazish Saqlain; Attia Bari; Aimen C.; Masood Sadiq
paper_title: D-dimer: a biomarker for predicting disease severity and outcome in hospitalized children with COVID-19 and post COVID multisystem inflammatory syndrome

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed residual pulmonary dysfunction in 50 post-COVID patients at 12 weeks post-discharge by correlating CT severity scores with pulmonary function tests and exercise capacity. Patients with significant lung involvement showed reduced FVC and breath holding time, suggesting impaired recovery despite clinical discharge.
paper_authors: Rishab Rampradeep; Prasanth G.; Gangadharan V.
paper_title: Correlation between pulmonary function and six minutes walk test with computed tomography severity score in post COVID patients
paper_journal: International Journal of Advances in Medicine

summary: A prospective cohort study of 230 COVID-19 patients in Kerala followed for 6 months to determine the incidence and risk factors for post-COVID syndrome. The study found a 42.2% incidence of post-COVID syndrome and identified age >60 years, female sex, comorbidities, unvaccinated status, and severe initial COVID-19 as significant risk factors.
paper_authors: Deepa K. R.; Bindu Mohandas; Jayakrishnan Thayyil; Meera S. Nair; Rosh P.; Durgesh Kumar
paper_title: Incidence and probable risk factors of post COVID syndrome among COVID-19 patients in urban population of North Kerala: a 6 months cohort study
paper_journal: International Journal Of Community Medicine And Public Health

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining serum albumin levels as a prognostic marker in 52 post-COVID-19 patients admitted to an ICU. Patients with hypoalbuminemia had higher mortality (11.11%) compared to those with normal albumin (2.94%), but the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Akshaya N. Shetti; Jay Manojkumar Bhensdadia; M.K. Chaitanya Krishna; Bhavika Singla; Rachita G. Mustilwar
paper_title: Serum albumin level as a marker to predict morbidity in post COVID-19 patients admitted in a rural critical care unit
paper_journal: International Journal of Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Analysis

summary: A retrospective cohort study examining the relationship between COVID-19 infection and achalasia (esophageal motor disorder) in a patient cohort from 2015-2021. The study found increased achalasia frequency in 2020-2021 and a higher COVID-19 prevalence in type II achalasia patients, suggesting achalasia may be a COVID-19 sequela, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Raúl Aponte; Nefertiti Daulabani; Rosargelis Parra; Luis Pérez-Ybarra
paper_title: Long COVID-19 and achalasia: a possible relationship?
paper_journal: International Journal Of Community Medicine And Public Health

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing incidence of cardiovascular disease and diabetes mellitus in COVID-19 patients versus controls across different post-infection phases. Finds elevated CVD risk in acute and post-acute phases (up to 3 months) but no long-term elevation in CVD or DM prevalence.
paper_authors: Amrendra Kumar Singh; Rajkamal Choudhary; Kumari Ragini; Anjum Perwez
paper_title: Incidence of diabetes and ischemic heart disease in COVID-19 post pandemic
paper_journal: International Journal of Research in Medical Sciences

summary: This prospective observational study followed 25 COVID-19 patients for 2 months post-discharge to track symptom persistence and radiological changes. Two-thirds of patients still had symptoms at day 30, declining to half at day 60, with 18% showing chest X-ray abnormalities at 2 months, suggesting post-COVID sequelae warrant clinical attention and future intervention studies.
paper_authors: Chinmai Sowmya Penmetsa; Vijay Krishna Yalamanchili; Raja Sekhar Yendapu; Pratti Venkata Sai Susmitha Pratti
paper_title: Clinical and radiological follow up of post-COVID patients in tertiary care centre
paper_journal: International Journal Of Community Medicine And Public Health

summary: A prospective observational study of 119 post-COVID patients assessing the prevalence and characteristics of pulmonary fibrosis in the post-acute phase. Post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis was observed in 56.3% of cases, though only 3 patients showed residual lung fibrosis; elderly patients with comorbidities, longer hospital stay, and severity of initial infection were risk factors.
paper_authors: Harshit Jain; Mustafa Singapurwala; Shivmohan Sarraf; Arti Julka
paper_title: Pulmonary Fibrosis in post COVID-19 follow up cases
paper_journal: Journal of Preventive Medicine and Holistic Health

summary: Retrospective cohort study documenting long COVID frequency (64.7%) and associated risk factors in 133 hospitalized COVID-19 patients from Turkey, with follow-up at 4 months post-diagnosis. Identifies female gender, severe COVID-19, comorbidities, diabetes, and depression as significant risk factors, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Nese Yaksi; Ayse Gulsen Teker; Ayfer Imre
paper_title: Long COVID in Hospitalized COVID-19 Patients:  A Retrospective Cohort Study

summary: A prospective cohort study of 300 young COVID-19 patients followed for 3 months to characterize auditory and vestibular symptoms. Auditory and vestibular complaints (vertigo, tinnitus, hearing problems, aural fullness) occurred in only 2-5% of patients during acute phase and resolved or nearly resolved by 3-month follow-up, suggesting these are not persistent long COVID sequelae.
paper_authors: Zahra Shahidipour; Nematollah Rouhbakhsh; Elham Tavanai
paper_title: Auditory and Vestibular Complaints Among COVID-19 Patients: A Descriptive Survey of 300 Young Patients Over a 3-Month Follow-up Period

summary: Prospective cohort study tracking olfactory dysfunction recovery in 138 COVID-19 patients over 16 months using standardized smell testing (UPSIT). Found that 90.6% of patients achieved full recovery, with sudden-onset dysfunction showing better recovery rates than gradual-onset.
paper_authors: Krishna Jadvani; Siddharth Badola
paper_title: Olfactory dysfunction in COVID-19 pandemic and its long-term outcome
paper_journal: International Journal of Otorhinolaryngology and Head and Neck Surgery

summary: Prospective observational study following 199 COVID-19 patients with chemosensory deficits (anosmia and dysgeusia) over 8 weeks to assess persistence of these post-COVID symptoms. Found that residual chemosensory dysfunction persisted in most patients, with male predominance, raising concerns about long-term quality of life impact.
paper_authors: Vivek K. Pathak; Pradeepti Nayak; Rohit Saxena; Rishita Kalra
paper_title: Persistence of chemosensory deficiencies in patients of COVID-19: our experience
paper_journal: International Journal of Otorhinolaryngology and Head and Neck Surgery

summary: This prospective cohort study examines long-term cardiovascular outcomes in 858 hospitalized COVID-19 patients with 13-month follow-up, evaluating the association between early statin use and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). While it studies post-COVID cardiovascular complications, it does not focus on long COVID syndrome (persistent multi-system symptoms weeks-to-months post-infection) and is excluded because it is an observational cohort study without an assigned intervention—patients' statin use was not randomized or controlled.
paper_authors: Arezoo Khosravi; Saeed Ghodsi; Mohammadreza Memarjafari; Alireza Nematollahi; Reza Sheikh-Sharbafan; Seyed-Ali Sadre-Bafghi; Seyed-Vahid Moosavi; Mansour Abdollahzadeh; Arash Jalali; Maryam Moshkani Farahani
paper_title: Long-Term Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events in Patients with Moderate and Severe COVID-19: A Focus on Early Statin Use and Previous CVD
paper_journal: The Journal of Tehran University Heart Center

summary: This observational study compared demographic, clinical, and immunological characteristics between 90 long COVID patients and 116 controls, finding distinct immune profiles including elevated CD8+ T cells and altered B cell counts in long COVID patients. While the study evaluates QazVac vaccination effects, it is primarily descriptive and comparative rather than testing a treatment intervention in long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Saulesh S. Kurmangaliyeva; Akzhan M. Madenbayeva; Saltanat T. Urazayeva; Kairat B. Kurmangaliyev; Yerlan Sh. Bazargaliyev; Khatimya I. Kudabayeva; Aisha B. Urazayeva; Gaukhar B. Kumar
paper_title: Effects of QazVac Vaccination on Immune and Clinical Characteristics in Patients With and Without Long COVID-19

summary: This retrospective matched cohort study compares health care resource use and direct costs between COVID-19 patients and matched controls over 6 months using administrative claims data. While it documents long-term COVID-related complications and economic burden, it is a secondary analysis of existing claims data rather than an intervention trial, making it ineligible for the meta-analysis.
paper_authors: Jessica K. DeMartino; Elyse Swallow; Debbie Goldschmidt; Karen Yang; Marta Viola; Tyler Radtke; Noam Kirson
paper_title: Direct health care costs associated with COVID-19 in the United States
paper_journal: Journal of Managed Care & Specialty Pharmacy

summary: This retrospective cohort study evaluated persistent symptoms in COVID-19 patients following hospital discharge from intensive care. The study found that fatigue was the most common long-term symptom, with symptom incidence increasing with patient age.
paper_authors: Yücel GÜLTEKİN; Zerrin ÖZÇELİK
paper_title: Long-Term Consequences Of Intensive Care Patients Diagnosed With COVID-19 Infection After Hospital Discharge
paper_journal: Turkish Journal of Clinics and Laboratory

summary: This retrospective cohort study compared post-COVID pulmonary complications between individuals vaccinated with BioNTech mRNA vaccine versus Sinovac inactivated vaccine. The study found higher rates of lung sequelae and elevated inflammatory markers in the Sinovac-vaccinated group, suggesting inferior protection from inactivated vaccines in severe COVID cases.
paper_authors: Hasibe Gokce Cinar; Kemal Buğra Memiş
paper_title: Does the incidence of post-COVID pulmonary complications in vaccinated individuals correlate with the types of vaccines they received?
paper_journal: Turkish Journal of Clinics and Laboratory

summary: This study compared structural and functional vascular parameters and exercise tolerance in 31 patients at long-term follow-up (570±179 days) after COVID-19 hospitalization versus 31 non-hospitalized controls from the ESSE-RF epidemiological study. No significant differences were found between groups in vascular biomarkers (von Willebrand factor, IL-6, TMAO), arterial stiffness measures, or cardiopulmonary exercise test parameters.
paper_authors: S. A. Bondar; O. P. Rotar; M. A. Boyarinova; E. V. Moguchaya; E. P. Kolesova; A. M. Erina; E. Yu. Vasilyeva; A. V. Berezina; T. L. Karonova; A. O. Konradi
paper_title: Structural and functional vascular changes and exercise tolerance at the long-term follow-up after COVID‑19

summary: This retrospective cohort study assessed pain, fatigue severity, and quality of life in 392 COVID-19 survivors at admission and 3 months post-discharge. While the paper documents natural recovery of symptoms over time, it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Esma DEMİRHAN; Sevgi ATAR; Günay ER; İpek OKUTAN; Ömer KURU
paper_title: Postdischarge pain, fatigue severity and quality of life in COVID-19 survivors

summary: Observational cross-sectional study examining ophthalmological abnormalities in 23 patients 44-85 days after acute COVID-19 infection. Found persistent dry eyes, abnormal color perception, and retinal layer abnormalities during late convalescence, with no active treatment intervention tested.
paper_authors: A. A. Ryabtseva; E. E. Grishina; O. M. Andryukhina; A. A. Kovrizhkina; A. S. Andryukhina
paper_title: The eye status in patients after new coronavirus infection

summary: This study evaluates early stage I rehabilitation methods for COVID-19 patients with moderate-to-severe lung damage during acute hospitalization. While it does test a rehabilitation intervention, the paper focuses on acute COVID-19 recovery in the ICU rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-to-months post-infection), making it outside scope for this long COVID trials database.
paper_authors: Shpagina, L. A.; Drobyshev, Viktor A.; Karmanovskaya, S. A.; Loktin, Evgenij M.; Shpagin, I. S.; Kotova, O. S.; Panacheva, L. A.; Musienko, T. V.; Zaikina, E. A.
paper_title: Efficacy of stage I rehabilitation of medical workers with moderate course of interstitial lung damage associated with COVID-19

summary: Prospective observational cohort study of 72 post-COVID-19 patients with intestinal symptoms, documenting clinical presentations, endoscopic findings, and histological changes including diarrhea, inflammatory changes, and in some cases pseudomembranous or ulcerative colitis. Treatment was symptom-oriented and 56.9% showed improvement during hospitalization with complete recovery in 27.8% within 4-8 weeks.
paper_authors: Efim S. Korsunskiy; Elena A. Belousova; Anastasiya A. Budzinskaya
paper_title: The post-COVID-19 intestinal damages: clinical, endoscopic and morphological features. The results of a single-center prospective observational cohort study

summary: Retrospective analysis of 785 COVID-19 patients examining prevalence and types of gastrointestinal symptoms during acute COVID and post-COVID syndrome, with follow-up assessments up to 2 years post-discharge. Found that GI symptoms persist in post-COVID patients (20% prevalence), with dyspeptic symptoms (heartburn, bloating) more common in long-term period compared to acute phase.
paper_authors: Lidiya D. Sadretdinova; Khalida Kh. Gantseva; Ilmira I. Galina; Anton V. Tyurin
paper_title: The duration of gastrointestinal symptom persistence at various periods of coronavirus infection

summary: This study examines trends in sick sinus syndrome (SSS) incidence and pacemaker implantation rates before and after the COVID-19 pandemic using interrupted time series analysis. While it finds increased SSS incidence post-COVID-19, it does not study treatments for long COVID patients and focuses on a cardiac conduction disorder as a potential COVID-19 sequela rather than on long COVID itself.
paper_authors: Dulal D.; Maraey A.; Grubb B.
paper_title: Impact of Coronavirus Disease 2019 on Sick Sinus Syndrome: Trends in Incidence and Pacemaker Implantation.
paper_journal: The Journal of innovations in cardiac rhythm management

summary: A retrospective cohort study of 205 long COVID patients with dyspnea (3+ months post-infection) that identifies clinical and biomarker predictors of post-COVID syndrome, comparing those with prior severe vs mild acute COVID. Key predictors include anxiety/depression (OR 12.14), cognitive impairment (OR 6.12), reduced oxygen saturation on exertion, elevated NT-proBNP, and caspase-6 levels.
paper_authors: Olga V. Masalkina; Anna I. Chernyavina; Natalia A. Koziolova; Elena A. Polyanskaya
paper_title: Predictors of the formation of long-term post-COVID syndrome with the main symptom of dyspnea in patients with a severe course of a new coronavirus infection
paper_journal: Journal of Volgograd State Medical University

summary: Observational cross-sectional study comparing post-COVID respiratory and neuromuscular sequelae in patients with and without type 2 diabetes at a primary care unit in Mexico. Found that respiratory sequelae (particularly cough) were more prevalent than neuromuscular sequelae, and patients with diabetes were more exposed to post-COVID effects.
paper_authors: Lalané Lira Tania; Ericka Esther Cadena Moreno; Leticia Blanco Castillo; Ma. Azucena Bello Sánchez
paper_title: Secuelas Pulmonares y Neuromusculares Posterior a Infección Por Covid-19 en Población con y sin Diabetes Tipo 2

summary: Retrospective analysis of 152 long COVID patients examining the relationship between autonomic nervous system dysfunction (parasympathetic and sympathetic imbalance) and long COVID symptoms, with investigation of neuro-modulation as a potential therapeutic approach. The study proposes that oxidative stress and autonomic dysfunction explain the severity and prevalence of long COVID manifestations.
paper_authors: J. Colombo
paper_title: Long-COVID and the Autonomic Nervous System: The journey from Dysautonomia to Therapeutic Neuro-Modulation, Analysis of 152 Patient Retrospectives

summary: Cross-sectional study characterizing cardiac manifestations of post-COVID syndrome in 30 children and adolescents with a comparison group of 32 controls. Found 11.5% incidence of PCS with cardiac manifestations, including arrhythmic syndrome in 67%, asthenic syndrome in 70%, and persistent chest pain, palpitations, and fatigue at 3 and 6 months post-infection.
paper_authors: D.A. Ponomareva; T.A. Nagaeva; V.A. Zhelev; N.I. Basareva; L.A. Mochalina; A.S. Reim; J.A. Ermolaeva
paper_title: Cardiac manifestations of post-COVID syndrome in children and adolescents

summary: A prospective cohort study investigating the relationship between minute ventilation and metabolic contribution in long COVID patients using cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET). Analysis is ongoing with no results reported yet; this is a study protocol without completed findings.
paper_authors: Ellie Tennant; Mark Faghy
paper_title: Investigating the relationship between minute ventilation and metabolic contribution in long COVID: A retrospective cohort study utilizing cardiopulmonary exercise testing
paper_journal: Graduate Journal of Sports Science, Coaching, Management, & Rehabilitation

summary: This prospective comparative study evaluated the long-term effects of favipiravir (Areplivir) treatment during acute COVID-19 infection in 190 patients with metabolic syndrome, following them for 1 year into the post-COVID period. Favipiravir-treated patients showed significantly lower inflammatory markers (IL-6/sIL6r and LIF/sLIFr) and reduced risk of cardiovascular complications including a 2.66-fold decrease in stroke and acute coronary syndrome incidence compared to untreated controls.
paper_authors: Balykova, Larisa A.; Zaslavskaya, Kira Y.; Taganov, Aleхey V.; Bely, P. A.; Radaeva, Oa; Negodnova, E. V.; Mashnina, S. V.; Bessheinov, D. D.; Iskandyarova, M. S.; Eremeev, V. V.; Chumakov, N. M.
paper_title: STUDY OF LONG-TERM CLINICAL AND PATHOGENETIC EFFECTS OF FAVIPIRAVIR-BASED ANTI-VIRAL DRUG IN PATIENTS WITH METABOLIC SYNDROME IN POST-COVID PERIOD

summary: Prospective study of 74 long COVID patients referred to physical medicine and rehabilitation, evaluating persistent symptoms and impact on physical function and quality of life. Home exercise program resulted in significant improvements in physical function (1-MSTS), activity limitations, and quality of life measures.
paper_authors: Joana Romano; Pedro Ribeiro; Joana Alberto; Paula Almeida; Duarte Dantas
paper_title: A Prospective Study of Patients with Persistent Symptoms after SARS-CoV-2 Infection Referred to Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 284 non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients examining long COVID sequelae and associations between acute symptoms and long-term symptoms. Found that specific acute symptoms (anosmia, tiredness, fever, dyspnea) were significantly associated with long COVID outcomes, and symptom burden negatively impacted quality of life.
paper_authors: Andreia M. Oliveira; Catarina Ferreira Coelho; Filipa Lourenço; Inês Campos Pinto; Joana Atabão; Raquel Cabrita; Rita Paraíso; Edgar Mesquita; Dyna Torrado; Pilar Marquez; Vanessa Z. Guerreiro
paper_title: Long COVID Symptoms in Non-Hospitalised Patients: A Retrospective Study

summary: This study measured IgG antibody levels to toxoid vaccines and SARS-CoV-2 in COVID-19 patients over 17 months, including assessment for prolonged olfaction impairment as a proxy for long COVID symptoms. The researchers found no significant decline in vaccine-induced antibodies during or after COVID-19 infection, though temporary total IgG decline occurred in severe cases.
paper_authors: Jokiranta ST; Miettinen S.; Salonen S.; Kareinen L.; Uusitalo R.; Korhonen EM; Virtanen J.; Kivistö I.; Aaltonen K.; Mosselhy DA; Lääveri T.; Kantele A.; Arstila TP; Jarva H.; Vapalahti O.; Heinonen S.; Kekäläinen E.
paper_title: Stable Levels of Antibodies Against Unrelated Toxoid Vaccines After COVID-19: COVID-19 Infection Does Not Affect Toxoid Vaccine Antibody Levels

summary: This cross-sectional study examined the relationship between endothelial dysfunction, arterial stiffness, and post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC) in a prospectively enrolled cohort of 379 COVID-negative and COVID-positive participants. The study found that arterial stiffness (measured by augmentation index) and oxidized LDL were independently associated with PASC, particularly in patients with neurological and/or cardiopulmonary phenotypes, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Sokratis Zisis; Jared Durieux; Christian Mouchati; Nicholas Funderburg; Kate Ailstock; Mary Chong; Danielle Labbato; Grace McComsey
paper_title: Arterial Stiffness and Oxidized LDL Independently Associated With Post-Acute Sequalae of SARS-CoV-2

summary: Retrospective study of 199 COVID-19 patients examining the frequency and characteristics of newly verified or worsened arterial hypertension following infection. Found that 16% of patients developed hypertension post-COVID, typically 3 months after infection, with younger patients affected and significantly elevated blood pressure readings compared to controls.
paper_authors: Delalić Đ.; Jug J.; Prkačin I.
paper_title: Arterial hypertension following COVID-19: A retrospective study of patients in a Central European tertiary care center

summary: A 12-month prospective follow-up study of 643 Polish COVID-19 patients assessing the prevalence and characteristics of post-COVID syndrome symptoms. The study identifies female sex and severe acute COVID-19 as risk factors for persistent symptoms but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Mateusz Babicki; Damian Kołat; Joanna Kapusta; Żaneta Kałuzińska-Kołat; Piotr Jankowski; Agnieszka Mastalerz-Migas; Maciej Banach; Robert Mordaka; Michał Chudzik
paper_title: Prevalence and assessment of risk factors among Polish adults with post-COVID syndrome: 12-month follow-up study

summary: Longitudinal observational study following 152 COVID-19 patients at 3, 6, and 9 months post-discharge to assess long-COVID prevalence, risk factors, and impact on health-related quality of life. Found persistent long-COVID symptoms in 53-67% of patients with significant impairment in multiple QoL domains, particularly anxiety/depression, though this is a natural history study without any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Pedro Gaspar; Mariana Dias; Inês Parreira; Hélder Diogo Gonçalves; Federica Parlato; Valeria Maione; Henrique Atalaia Barbacena; Carolina Carreiro; Leila Duarte
paper_title: Predictors of Long-COVID-19 and its Impact on Quality of Life: Longitudinal Analysis at 3, 6 and 9 Months after Discharge from a Portuguese Centre

summary: Retrospective cohort study documenting post-discharge clinical, laboratory, and radiographic features in 126 COVID-19 patients (88 mild-moderate, 38 severe-critical) at two Japanese university hospitals. Found persistent symptoms (36.5%), abnormal imaging (83.3%), and lab abnormalities in substantial proportions at a median 46 days post-discharge.
paper_authors: Sasaki T.; Toyama Y.; Horiguchi T.; Hibino M.; Tsuzuki SI; Hayashi M.; Doi Y.; Iwata M.; Imaizumi K.; Inaba M.
paper_title: Post-discharge clinical, laboratory and radiographic features of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) patients at university hospitals in Japan.

summary: This study analyzes 87 patients presenting with audiovestibular symptoms (hearing loss, tinnitus, vertigo) persisting more than 3 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection, confirming the existence of audiovestibular post-COVID syndrome. The paper describes symptom prevalence and characteristics but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Klančnik M.; Ivanišević P.; Golec N.; Vučemilović MZ
paper_title: Does Audiovestibular Post-COVID Syndrome Exist?

summary: A prospective cohort study comparing forced expiratory flow (FEF 25-75%) values between mild-moderate and severe-critical post-COVID-19 patients to assess small airway disease. Found no statistically significant differences in small airway function between severity groups, with only a small proportion of patients showing abnormal values.
paper_authors: Muhammad Khidir; Siswanto Siswanto; Henda Ageng Rasena; Roihan Mohamad Iqbal; Rahmaningsih Mara Sabirin; Rakhmat Ari Wibowo; Sani Hadiyan Rasyid
paper_title: Comparison of Forced Expiratory Flow (FEF) 25-75% between Post-COVID-19 Patients with Different Severity at Universitas Gadjah Mada Academic Hospital

summary: Prospective cohort study examining the association between comorbidity status and emotional/behavioral disorder risk in 29 children following COVID-19 infection using the SDQ questionnaire. Findings show 48.3% prevalence of emotional and behavioral difficulties, with comorbidity status significantly associated with emotional problems (p=0.028).
paper_authors: Winengku Basuki Adi; Ronny Tri Wirasto; P. Sumarni; Carla R. Marchira
paper_title: Exploring the Association Between Comorbidity Status and Emotional and Behavioral Disorder Risk in Children Following COVID-19 Infection

summary: Retrospective cohort follow-up study of 195 COVID-19 convalescents at ~4.7 months and 183 at ~11 months post-infection, assessing prevalence and severity of residual symptoms. Found that 63-75% experienced persistent symptoms (fatigue, joint pain, dyspnea most common) but severity remained low; no intervention tested.
paper_authors: A. V. Melekhov; A. I. Agaeva; I. G. Nikitin
paper_title: Symptoms in the Long Period after the Coronavirus Infection: Results of Long-Term Follow-Up
paper_journal: The Russian Archives of Internal Medicine

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining long COVID symptoms in 44 vaccinated women with PCOS, finding that 70% reported persistent symptoms (fatigue, hair loss). The study found no significant difference in PCOS symptoms before/after COVID-19 vaccination or infection, emphasizing vaccination importance for symptom mitigation.
paper_authors: R. Muharam; Aswan Bagastoro; Anindita Abigail Faradina; Edward Christopher Yo; Alisha Nurdya Irzanti; Kanadi Sumapraja; Achmad Kemal Harzif; Gita Pratama; Mila Maidarti; Vita Silvana; Budi Wiweko; Andon Hestiantoro
paper_title: Long COVID in vaccinated women with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome:  A retrospective cohort pilot study

summary: This retrospective cohort study from the ACTIV registry analyzed 9,364 COVID-19 patients to examine how pre-existing chronic kidney disease (CKD) and acute kidney injury (AKI) impact disease course and long-term prognosis during acute infection and at 3, 6, and 12 months post-hospitalization. Findings show CKD and AKI significantly increased hospital mortality (3.94-fold and 4.88-fold higher at 3 months) and continued to elevate mortality risk in the post-COVID period.
paper_authors: M. M. Batiushin; M. A. Trubnikova; E. I. Tarlovskaya; G. P. Arutyunov; T. I. Batluk; R. A. Bashkinov; E. S. Melnikov; A. G. Arutyunov
paper_title: Impact of Kidney Damage on the Course and Prognosis of COVID-19 Infection According to the International Registry «Analysis of Chronic Non-Infectious Diseases Dynamics After Covid-19 Infection in Adult Patients»
paper_journal: The Russian Archives of Internal Medicine

summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 1,438 COVID-19 survivors one year post-discharge to assess long-term neurological sequelae through self-reported symptoms. The study found that neurological symptoms were common (53.46% of severe cases, 27.84% of non-severe cases), with memory and attention deficits being most frequent, but did not evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Li Jiang; Xiao-Yu Liu; Xiao-Qin Yan; Yu-Hui Liu; Yan-Jiang Wang; Ying Yang; Ling-Ru Wang
paper_title: One-year self-reported neurological sequelae in older COVID-19 survivors

summary: This longitudinal observational cohort study tracked post-COVID syndrome symptom dynamics over 2 years in 225 patients (138 with prior positive PCR, 87 negative control), comparing symptom prevalence and associations with clinical/laboratory factors. Key findings: post-COVID severity is independent of PCR results; cardiac and respiratory syndromes decline 2-3 fold by year 2; asthenia persists as the longest-lasting symptom; risk factors shift from COVID severity and D-dimer in year 1 to age in year 2.
paper_authors: T. Yu. Agafonova; N. N. Elovikova; O. V. Bronnikova; D. A. Golyadinets
paper_title: Post-COVID Syndrome: Persistence of Symptoms and Risk Factors (Longitudinal Observational Study)
paper_journal: The Russian Archives of Internal Medicine

summary: This cross-sectional study compared hemostasis and catecholamine metabolism markers in 60 long COVID patients versus 30 controls without post-COVID syndrome, examining associations with cognitive impairment. While the study confirms elevated catecholamines and cognitive dysfunction in long COVID patients, it is purely observational without any treatment intervention or control group comparison of therapeutic outcomes.
paper_authors: Kh.G. Omarova; A.R. Marzhokhova; A.D. Muzyka; N.T. Shapieva; M.P. Provotorova
paper_title: Features of the course of postcovid syndrome, its effect on quality of life and some indicators of hemostasis and catecholamine metabolism

summary: A prospective cohort study examining immunological and coagulation parameters in 34 children with COVID-19, measured during acute infection and 8 months post-disease. The study documents persistent immune and hemostasis abnormalities at 8 months follow-up but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: O.M. Olenkova; O.P. Kovtun
paper_title: Dynamics of changes in immunological and coagulation parameters in children with novel coronavirus infection

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing immunological markers (IL-18, IL-6, rheumatoid factor) in 247 COVID-19 survivors stratified by gastrointestinal symptom duration: ongoing symptomatic (4-12 weeks), post-COVID syndrome (>12 weeks), and asymptomatic controls. Elevated IL-18 and IL-6 levels were significantly higher in both symptomatic groups, identifying IL-18 as a potential diagnostic marker for post-COVID gastroenterological manifestations.
paper_authors: L. D. Sadretdinova; Halida Gantseva; A. F. Itkulov; Anton Tyurin
paper_title: Immunological Markers in Patients with Gastroenterological Manifestations During Different Periods of COVID-19
paper_journal: The Russian Archives of Internal Medicine

summary: This study examined clinical and microbiological features in 61 children with post-COVID-19 syndrome undergoing sanatorium-based rehabilitation. The findings showed that standard recreational and health-improving sanatorium activities promoted clinical and laboratory recovery, with improvements in fatigue, appetite, and microbiota composition.
paper_authors: L.V. Feklisova; A.M. Zatevalov; E.I. Likhanskaya; L.I. Elezova; E.R. Mekhtiev; M.K. Khadisova; N.A. Shmakov; E.N. Guseva; S.V. Nikolaeva; A.V. Gorelov
paper_title: Clinical and microbiological features and metabolic activity of fecal microorganisms in the rehabilitation of children with post-COVID-19 syndrome

summary: This retrospective cohort study investigates the CONUT (Controlling Nutritional Status) score as a predictor of hospital stay length and long COVID risk in 151 COVID-19 patients followed for two years. The study finds that higher CONUT scores correlate with longer hospitalization and increased long COVID incidence, but does not test or evaluate any intervention.
paper_authors: Zi-Wen Zhao; Qin Chen; Xin-Tao Zhang; Yu-Kun Luo
paper_title: The CONUT score predicts the length of hospital stay and the risk of long COVID

summary: Retrospective observational study examining how COVID-19 infection affects the course of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) in 28 children, comparing clinical and laboratory markers before and after infection. The study documents increased symptoms (fatigue, joint pain) and intestinal inflammation markers post-COVID, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: O.A. Savvateeva; A.V. Gorelov; D.V. Pechkurov; A.M. Savvateev; V.S. Krikun
paper_title: Does COVID-19 infection affect the course of inflammatory bowel disease in children

summary: This study examines post-COVID conditions in 78 children (43 with post-COVID syndrome, 35 controls) and reports that 55% of children developed post-COVID symptoms, with herpesvirus reactivation occurring in 51.2% of affected children. Treatment with meglumine acridone acetate (Cycloferon®) achieved clinical improvement in 80% (20/25) of children with herpesvirus reactivation.
paper_authors: Т.S. Sabinina; А.D. Muzyka; Т.V. Shalbarova; Е.V. Melekhina; А.V. Gorelov
paper_title: Post-COVID conditions in children

summary: This study evaluated the effect of three hepatoprotectors (ursodeoxycholic acid, glycyrrhizic acid with phospholipids, and ademeteonin) versus no hepatoprotective treatment on liver function in 243 post-COVID-19 patients during early rehabilitation. Ursodeoxycholic acid showed the most pronounced effect on normalizing liver enzyme markers and bilirubin levels.
paper_authors: LOLA T. DAMINOVA
paper_title: THE EFFECT OF HEPATOPROTECTORS ON THE STATE OF THE LIVER IN POST COVID-19 PATIENTS
paper_journal: The Bulletin of Contemporary Clinical Medicine

topics: liver damage|hepatic dysfunction|clinical characteristics|laboratory markers|post-COVID syndrome
summary: This cross-sectional study assessed clinical and laboratory indicators of liver damage in 243 COVID-19 patients during early rehabilitation (10+ days post-infection, PCR-negative). The study found elevated liver enzymes, anemia, thrombocytopenia, and multiple clinical syndromes but did not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: LOLA T. DAMINOVA
paper_title: CLINICAL AND LABORATORY CHARACTERISTICS OF PATIENTS WITH LIVER DAMAGE IN THE COVID-19 EARLY REHABILITATION PERIOD
paper_journal: The Bulletin of Contemporary Clinical Medicine

summary: Prospective cohort study of 5,446 COVID-19 patients followed for 6 months post-diagnosis to assess prevalence and risk factors for anxiety and depression using EQ-5D-3L scale. Found anxiety/depression prevalence ranged from 18.5% at 1 month to 15.4% at 6 months, with female gender, poor economic status, higher symptom burden, and ICU admission as significant risk factors.
paper_authors: Neslişah ŞİYVE; Ahmet Naci EMECEN; Salih KESKİN; Ecem BAŞOĞLU ŞENSOY; Öykü TURUNÇ; Ahmet Furkan SÜNER; Can CİMİLLİ; Belgin ÜNAL
paper_title: Self-reported anxiety and depression among COVID-19 patients within six months of follow-up: A prospective cohort study

summary: A prospective follow-up study of 90 COVID-19 patients examining the relationship between annexin A5 (ANXA5) levels and regression of pulmonary complications 6 months post-infection. The study is a secondary biomarker analysis without a specific treatment intervention being tested.
paper_authors: ASIA SH. KURMAEVA; OLGA A. BASHKINA; TATIANA V. PROKOFYEVA; OLGA S. POLUNINA; EKATERINA A. POLUNINA
paper_title: RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN THE ANNEXIN A5 LEVEL AND THE REGRESSION OF PULMONARY COMPLICATIONS IN PATIENTS WITH SARS-COV-2- ASSOCIATED PNEUMONIA AT THE OUTPATIENT STAGE
paper_journal: The Bulletin of Contemporary Clinical Medicine

summary: A prospective follow-up study of 700 hospitalized COVID-19 patients assessed long-term sequelae at 3-7 months post-discharge through telephone contact and outpatient clinical evaluations. The study found that over half of patients experienced persistent symptoms including dyspnea, fatigue, and chest pain, with CT imaging revealing persistent lung changes in patients with severe acute infection.

paper_title: Sequelae of COVID-19 at long-term follow-up after hospitalization

summary: This cross-sectional study characterizes clinical recovery in 43 elderly post-COVID patients stratified by recovery duration (≤3 months vs >3 months) and lung parenchymal abnormality severity. Persistent fatigue (75%), dyspnea (59%), and joint pain were common, with respiratory functional impairment correlating with greater lung lesion volume (>25%).
paper_authors: EVGENII A. PRASKURNICHY; SVETLANA I. ZENKOVA; IRINA V. TRIGOLOSOVA; OLGA S. ORLOVA; LYUBOV I. ELEZOVA; NIKOLAI A. SHMAKOV
paper_title: THE CLINICAL FEATURES OF RECOVERY IN PATIENTS WHO HAD CORONAVIRUS INFECTION COVID-19 BASED ON THE DURATION OF POST-COVID PERIOD AND SEVERITY OF LUNG PARENCHYMAL ABNORMALITIES
paper_journal: The Bulletin of Contemporary Clinical Medicine

summary: This paper retrospectively analyzes 154 COVID-19 patients with prolonged anosmia, tracking their symptoms and neuropsychiatric manifestations over 9 months post-infection. It identifies anosmia as a predictor of anxiety, depression, and sleep disorders but does not test or evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Iryna Kravchenko; Olga Morozova; Oleksandr Yaroshevskyi; Inna Reminiak
paper_title: OLFACTORY DYSFUNCTION IN COVID-19: FEATURES OF THE COURSE IN THE ACUTE AND POST-COVID PERIOD
paper_journal: Bulletin of medicine, psychology and pharmacy

summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 337 COVID-19 survivors with chest CT scans performed 102-361 days after disease onset to evaluate long-term pulmonary changes and their correlation with post-discharge dyspnea. While it documents natural disease progression and identifies imaging predictors of dyspnea, it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Xi Yin; Xiaoqing Xi; Xiangde Min; Zhaoyan Feng; Basen Li; Wei Cai; Chanyuan Fan; Liang Wang; Liming Xia
paper_title: Long-term chest CT follow-up in COVID-19 Survivors: 102–361 days after onset

summary: Retrospective study evaluating whether chest CT findings influence pneumologist decision-making for diagnosis and management of pulmonary long COVID in 41 patients. CT did not influence diagnostic or management decisions, only modestly improved diagnostic confidence, and is not routinely necessary when pulmonary function tests and auscultation are normal.
paper_authors: Stefanie Meiler; Daniel Schmalenberger; Maximilian Malfertheiner; Iris Dvorak; Quirin Strotzer; Christian Stroszczynski; Okka Wilkea Hamer
paper_title: Chest computed tomography findings do not influence the decision of pneumologists regarding the diagnosis and management of pulmonary long coronavirus disease: a single center retrospective study

summary: Prospective hospital registry study examining clinical characteristics, cardiovascular pharmacotherapy, and long-term outcomes in post-COVID-19 patients with cardiovascular multimorbidity over 13 months of follow-up. Patients with CVMM were older, had higher all-cause mortality and hospitalization rates, and showed declining adherence to anticoagulant therapy, suggesting inadequate management of post-COVID cardiovascular complications.

paper_title: Clinical and Anamnestic Characteristics, Cardiovascular Pharmacotherapy and Long-term Outcomes in Multimorbid Patients after COVID-19

summary: A prospective cohort study following 306 COVID-19 hospitalized patients for 2 years post-discharge to assess the prevalence and characteristics of post-COVID syndrome. The study found 43.8% prevalence of PCS with fatigue, brain fog, and anxiety as most common symptoms, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Lucio Boglione; Federica Poletti; Roberto Rostagno; Roberta Moglia; Marco Cantone; Maria Esposito; Cristina Scianguetta; Beatrice Domenicale; Fortunata Di Pasquale; Silvio Borrè
paper_title: Long-COVID syndrome in hospitalized patients after 2 years of follow-up

summary: Prospective study of cardiac tissue from 9 patients undergoing heart surgery ~6 months post-COVID, examining SARS-CoV-2 persistence and inflammatory markers. Found viral RNA in 4/9 patients with elevated IL-6 and IL-1β in some cases, but this is observational tissue sampling with no intervention—a mechanistic investigation rather than a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Sanjiu Yu; Jiao Xu; Chuang Yu; Xianpu Zhang; Yongbo Cheng; Deqing Lin; Chaojun Yan; Mei Guo; Jun Li; Ping He; Wei Cheng
paper_title: Persistence of SARS-CoV-2 colonization and high expression of inflammatory factors in cardiac tissue 6 months after COVID-19 recovery: a prospective cohort study

summary: A longitudinal observational study following 25 COVID-19 patients 8-16 weeks after discharge to assess radiological recovery, lymphocyte dynamics, and antibody levels. While it documents post-acute sequelae, it is a passive observational follow-up study without any intervention or treatment being administered to patients.
paper_authors: Ziqi Wang; Li Yang; Yi Chen; Zhiwei Xu; Hui Wang; Xiaoju Zhang
paper_title: A longitudinal follow-up of COVID-19 patients in the convalescent phase showed recovery in radiological results, the dynamics of lymphocytes, and a decrease in the level of IgG antibody: a single-centre, observational study

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines the association between electrolyte supplementation and cardiac injury in 144 long COVID patients with cardiac complications, comparing supplementation (n=72) versus control (n=72) groups. Results show that electrolyte supplementation was associated with improved heart rate variability parameters, reduced premature contractions, and better quality of life scores.
paper_authors: Xida Li; Yonghua Chen; Shuo Sun; Haojian Dong; Jianfang Luo
paper_title: Association between electrolyte supplementation and cardiac injury in long COVID-19

summary: Retrospective follow-up study of 129 COVID-19 patients examining prevalence and risk factors for persistent postinfectious cough at median 8.1 months post-discharge. Found 20.9% developed postinfectious cough, with smoking and digestive symptoms during hospitalization as significant risk factors.
paper_authors: Yuehan Chen; Xu Zhang; Xiansheng Zeng; Tingting Xu; Wei Xiao; Xuejiao Yang; Wenzhi Zhan; Chen Zhan; Kefang Lai
paper_title: Prevalence and risk factors for postinfectious cough in discharged patients with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19)

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing long COVID sequelae symptoms in Omicron-infected patients versus never-infected controls from a Japanese fever clinic. Found loss of taste/smell, hair loss, neurocognitive symptoms, and respiratory symptoms as specific long COVID sequelae, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Takahiro Omori; Mariko Hanafusa; Nobuyuki Kondo; Yasunari Miyazaki; Shusho Okada; Takeo Fujiwara; Jin Kuramochi
paper_title: Specific sequelae symptoms of COVID-19 of Omicron variant in comparison with non-COVID-19 patients: a retrospective cohort study in Japan

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 405 post-COVID patients comparing pulmonary function recovery in those who received corticosteroids during acute COVID-19 infection versus those who did not. Corticosteroid treatment was associated with faster recovery of FEV1 and FVC over long-term follow-up, even in higher-risk subgroups.
paper_authors: Liora Boehm Cohen; Yael Raviv; Walid Shalata; Michael Kasirer; Anat Reiner Benaim
paper_title: Long-term effect of corticosteroid treatment during acute COVID-19 infection on pulmonary function test results

summary: Prospective observational study tracking pulmonary function and exercise capacity in 38 post-COVID-19 pneumonia patients over 12 months compared to 25 healthy controls. Findings show significant impairments in FVC/FEV1 and 6-minute walk distance at baseline, with gradual improvement over time, but persistent deficits throughout follow-up.

paper_title: The long-term impact of COVID-19 pneumonia on pulmonary function and exercise capacity

The study found significant impairments in white matter integrity and negative correlations between psychological scores and fractional anisotropy, but involved no intervention or treatment—only assessment of existing neurobiological changes.

paper_title: Long-term white matter changes in patients who develop severe depression after multiple COVID-19 infections: a 3–6-month study

summary: This study evaluates semen parameters in 36 male COVID-19 recovered patients versus 45 controls at median 177.5 days post-recovery. While the paper mentions long-term follow-up, it is not primarily about long COVID—it focuses on acute COVID-19's impact on male fertility and does not study an intervention or treatment for long COVID symptoms.
paper_authors: Bintao Hu; Kang Liu; Yajun Ruan; Xian Wei; Yue Wu; Huan Feng; Zhiyao Deng; Jihong Liu; Tao Wang
paper_title: Evaluation of mid- and long-term impact of COVID-19 on male fertility through evaluating semen parameters

summary: Retrospective study of 48 patients (88 hips) with post-COVID osteonecrosis of the femoral head treated with bisphosphonate therapy (zoledronic acid and alendronate) over a minimum 6-month follow-up. 95.5% of hips showed good clinical outcomes with improved pain scores and Harris hip scores, with only 4.5% requiring surgical intervention.
paper_authors: Sanjay Agarwala; Mayank Vijayvargiya; Tushar Sawant; Siddhesh Kulkarni
paper_title: Bisphosphonates for Post-COVID Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head

summary: Retrospective cohort study assessing frailty syndrome in older patients who recovered from COVID-19 using the FRAIL screening tool. The study demonstrates that post-COVID patients show asthenic syndrome rather than age-related frailty and require individualized geriatric assessment and long-term rehabilitation.
paper_authors: E. S. Lapteva; A. L. Ariev; O. G. Khurtsilava; N. V. Sovetkina; O. G. Sirotkin; I. P. Fedunyak; K. I. Triputina
paper_title: The impact of the Covid-19 pandemic on the operation of a geriatric center in St. Petersburg. Part 2: screening for frailty syndrome during the peak of the pandemic.

summary: This retrospective cohort study uses VA healthcare databases to characterize 6-month risks of death and post-acute sequelae in people with breakthrough COVID-19 compared to uninfected controls and COVID-19-infected non-vaccinated individuals. The study found elevated risks of multisystem post-acute sequalae (pulmonary, cardiovascular, neurologic, mental health, and others) following breakthrough infection, with risks varying by hospitalization status.

paper_title: Long Covid after Breakthrough COVID-19: the post-acute sequelae of breakthrough COVID-19

summary: Multicentre retrospective study examining the prevalence and characteristics of prolonged symptoms (lasting >12 weeks) in Spanish children with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. Found 14.6% of 451 children experienced long COVID symptoms, with age >5 years, PICU admission, and family history of prolonged symptoms as significant risk factors.

paper_title: Study of Prevalence and Characteristics of Long Covid in Spanish Children

summary: This study uses a representative sample of 308 U.S. COVID-19 infected individuals from the Understanding America Study to characterize long COVID prevalence and symptom trajectories over 12 weeks post-infection. The authors find that 23% experienced persistent new-onset symptoms (long COVID), with headache, fatigue, and GI symptoms most common, and obesity and certain acute symptoms significantly increasing risk.
paper_authors: Qiao Wu; Jennifer Ailshire; Eileen Crimmins
paper_title: Long COVID and Symptom Trajectory in a Representative Sample of Americans

summary: Norwegian prospective cohort study of 312 COVID-19 patients (247 home-isolated, 65 hospitalized) tracking long-term symptoms at 6 months. Found 61% had persistent symptoms including fatigue (37%), impaired concentration (26%), and dyspnea (21%), with young home-isolated adults particularly affected by cognitive and respiratory symptoms.

paper_title: Long COVID affects home-isolated young patients

summary: Prospective observational cohort study of 42 long COVID patients examining clinical parameters and biomarkers associated with persistent fatigue and exertion intolerance 6 months post-infection. Found evidence of low-level inflammation and hypoperfusion as potential pathomechanisms, with hand grip strength diminished in most patients.
paper_authors: Claudia Kedor; Helma Freitag; Lil Meyer-Arndt; Kirsten Wittke; Leif Hanitsch; Thomas Zoller; Fridolin Steinbeis; Haffke Milan; Gordon Rudolf; Bettina Heidecker; Thomas Bobbert; Joachim Spranger; Harald Heidecke; Hans-Dieter Volk; Carsten Skurk; Friedemann Paul; Uta Behrends; Judith Bellmann-Strobl; Carmen Scheibenbogen

paper_title: Risk Factors and Predictive Modeling for Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Infection: Findings from EHR Cohorts of the RECOVER Initiative

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed 229 Slovak young adults to investigate long-term psychological and physical symptoms following COVID-19 recovery. The study found significant effects on cognitive health (memory, concentration, task-handling) particularly in women, along with physiological changes including decreased fitness and headaches, but did not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Darina Falbová; Viktória Kovalčíková; Radoslav Beňuš; Lenka Vorobeľová
paper_title: Long-term consequences of COVID-19  on mental and physical health in young adults
paper_journal: Central European Journal of Public Health

summary: This RECOVER Initiative study estimates long COVID (PASC) incidence across adult and pediatric populations using electronic health records from three nationwide research networks, finding 7% incidence in children and 8.5-26.4% in adults depending on classification algorithm. The paper is an observational epidemiological study examining incidence patterns and risk factors but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

summary: Retrospective observational study comparing clinical outcomes and long COVID occurrence in 100 acute pancreatitis patients with and without COVID-19 infection. Found no significant differences in mortality or severity between groups, though long COVID syndrome (specifically cough) was more common in the COVID-19 positive group.
paper_authors: Jinchang Zhang; De luo; Maoji kang; Bo Li; Song Su
paper_title: Clinical Characteristics and Short-term Outcomes of Acute Pancreatitis with COVID-19

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining racial/ethnic differences in long COVID symptoms among 225,723 pediatric patients with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection compared to 677,448 uninfected controls from the RECOVER Initiative. Findings show significant disparities in symptom prevalence by race/ethnicity and COVID-19 severity, including differential rates of fever, respiratory symptoms, hair loss, dysautonomia, and cognitive symptoms.

summary: This study compared in-hospital rehabilitation outcomes between COVID-19 survivors who received rehabilitation (N=155) and those who did not (N=162), measuring functional status at discharge using Mental Status, ICU Mobility, and modified Barthel Index scores. Rehabilitation patients were older with more comorbidities and worse pre-admission dependency, and the study found that functional scores were impaired at discharge and associated with pre-admission dependency and various comorbidities, warranting follow-up of COVID-19 survivors for post-acute sequelae.

summary: Prospective cohort study tracking symptom prevalence in 837 long COVID patients over 9 months using the ComPaRe e-cohort in France. Describes natural disease course rather than evaluating a treatment intervention, with 88.7% reporting persistent symptoms at 9 months and varying patterns of symptom resolution.
paper_authors: Viet-Thi Tran; Raphael Porcher; Isabelle Pane; Philippe Ravaud
paper_title: Course of long COVID symptoms over time in the ComPaRe long COVID prospective e-cohort

summary: This retrospective cohort study uses VA healthcare databases to characterize cardiovascular complications in COVID-19 survivors at one year post-infection, comparing 151,195 COVID-19 patients to controls. The study identifies increased risks of various cardiovascular diseases in the post-acute phase but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Ziyad Al-Aly; Benjamin Bowe; Yan Xie; Evan Xu
paper_title: One-year Risks and Burdens of Incident Cardiovascular Disease in COVID-19: Cardiovascular Manifestations of Long COVID

summary: This nationwide cohort study compares long COVID symptom prevalence in 37,522 SARS-CoV-2 infected children versus 78,037 uninfected controls using questionnaires. The study documents symptom prevalence and duration in children but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Luise Borch; Mette Holm; Maria Knudsen; Svend Ellermann-Eriksen; Soeren Hagstroem
paper_title: Prevalence, Symptoms and Duration of Post Acute Effects in SARS-CoV-2 Positive Children – a Nationwide Cohort Study

Results showed Paxlovid was associated with a 12% reduction in long COVID risk (HR 0.88) in high-risk patients, but showed no significant benefit in low-risk patients.

summary: Retrospective analysis evaluating the clinical utility of cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) in 12 post-COVID patients with persistent breathlessness. The study found that while CPET identified various physiological limitations, it did not substantially improve clinical management and may not be a cost-effective diagnostic approach for post-COVID assessment.
paper_authors: Edward Parkes; Joanna Shakespeare; Timothy Robbins; Ioannis Kyrou; Harpal Randeva; Asad Ali
paper_title: Utility of Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing (CPET) in the Post-COVID-19 Context: Retrospective Analysis of a Single Centre Experience.

summary: Observational cohort study of 130 hospitalized COVID-19 patients (stratified by ventilation intensity) followed at one year with pulmonary function tests and health status questionnaires. Found lung function in lower normal limits without significant differences by initial disease severity, suggesting broader testing warranted in patients with lingering symptoms.
