summary: This paper describes a hotline consultation service established by the Department of Pulmonology and Respiratory Medicine to provide health advice and triage for COVID-19 survivors with long COVID symptoms in Indonesia. The service reached 60 survivors, most with mild symptoms requiring self-care observation, and identified 42% needing further specialist care, but does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Sabrina Ermayanti; Russilawati Russilawati; Fenty Anggraini; Afriani Afriani; Irvan Madison; Oea Khairsyaf; Masrul Basyar; Deddy Herman; Yessy Susanty Sabri; Dewi Wahyu Fitrina; Dessy Mirzati; Elsa Purnama Sari; Dimas Bayu Firdaus
paper_title: Layanan hotline konsultasi masalah kesehatan pasca Covid-19

summary: Longitudinal study evaluating residual lung parenchymal CT changes in COVID-19 patients at median 137 days post-diagnosis. Found that 69.4% of patients had persistent CT changes, with significant reduction in CT severity scores between scans, but does not test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Rajive Raj Shahi; Bibek Karki; Lee Budhathoki; Shavana RL Rana; Sujata Panta Panta; Bikalp Thapa; Ranju Shrestha Shrestha; Parag Karki
paper_title: Residual Lung Parenchymal CT Changes in COVID-19 Patients and its Association with Common Predictors
paper_journal: Medical Journal of Shree Birendra Hospital

summary: This cross-sectional study examines cardiovascular system impairment and its contribution to dyspnea in 87 post-acute COVID-19 patients stratified by acute illness severity. The authors find that dyspnea severity correlates with acute illness severity and is driven by residual lung changes and cardiovascular involvement, with recommendations for multidisciplinary management.
paper_authors: Lyudmyla Konopkina; Olha Shchudro
paper_title: CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM STATUS IN PATIENTS WITH DYSPNEA AFTER COVID-19-ASSOCIATED PNEUMONIA

summary: A 2-year prospective observational cohort study of 71 vaccinated college students infected with Omicron and 18 uninfected controls, measuring immune and metabolic parameters at multiple timepoints. The study documents persistent immune dysregulation and metabolic alterations for at least 1 year post-infection, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Fengzhi Li; Yijin Zan; Yukun Cao; Fan Liu; Bingxin Si; Qingling Zhang; LeLa Lin; Jing Guo; Dong Wang; Xianrong Xu
paper_title: Analysis of the impact of SARS-CoV-2 infection on immune function and metabolic changes in college students

summary: This retrospective observational study analyzed 53 COVID-19 related interstitial lung disease (ILD) cases at a tertiary hospital in Sri Lanka, examining demographic, clinical, and radiological characteristics. The majority of patients were male with multiple comorbidities, and HRCT findings demonstrated disease progression patterns, but the study does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Dushantha Madegedara; Lihini Basnayake; Damith Nissanka Bandara
paper_title: Descriptive Analysis of the Patients with Post COVID Interstitial Lung Diseases in a Tertiary Care Hospital in Central Sri Lanka: An Observational Study
paper_journal: SAARC Journal of Tuberculosis, Lung Diseases and HIV/AIDS

summary: Prospective cohort study examining the prevalence of post-COVID-19 conditions in Delta variant infections across vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals. The study found similar prevalence of post-COVID conditions in both groups (61.4% vs 51.4%), with acute symptom burden as an independent risk factor, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Maxime Gallant; Christine Rioux-Perreault; Samuel Lemaire-Paquette; Alain Piché
paper_title: SARS-CoV-2 infection outcomes associated with the Delta variant: A prospective cohort study
paper_journal: Journal of the Association of Medical Microbiology and Infectious Disease Canada

summary: A prospective observational study in Quebec examining the prevalence and risk factors of persistent post-COVID-19 symptoms at least 1 month after Omicron infection in PCR-confirmed cases. Found that 47.2% of 290 participants reported persistent symptoms, with fatigue, shortness of breath, and cough being most common; number of acute COVID symptoms was identified as a significant risk factor.
paper_authors: Maxime Gallant; Kassandra Mercier; Christine Rioux-Perreault; Samuel Lemaire-Paquette; Alain Piché
paper_title: Prevalence of persistent symptoms at least 1 month after SARS-CoV-2 Omicron infection in adults
paper_journal: Journal of the Association of Medical Microbiology and Infectious Disease Canada

summary: Retrospective study of 856 long COVID patients treated with ivermectin at a public hospital in Buenos Aires. Treatment with ivermectin reportedly led to faster reduction of long COVID manifestations and symptom duration.
paper_authors: DelFranco Haroldo; Hirsch Roberto; Carvallo Hector
paper_title: Ivermectin IN Long-Covid Patients: A Retrospective Study
paper_journal: Journal of Biomedical Research and Clinical Investigation

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed androgen status in 90 men (60 post-COVID, 30 controls) at 3 months post-infection using hormone measurement and questionnaires. Severe COVID-19 was associated with 61% reduction in total testosterone and elevated FSH, SHBG, and prolactin compared to healthy controls, with mild COVID showing less pronounced hormonal changes and erectile dysfunction.
paper_authors: A.G. Antonov; K.I. Gamylin; V.V. Gordeev
paper_title: ASSESSMENT OF ANDROGEN STATUS IN MEN WITH POST-COVID SYNDROME

summary: This observational cohort study followed 385 COPD patients (55 without MS, 330 with MS) for 12 months to characterize the dynamics of metabolic syndrome features after acute COVID-19 infection. Post-COVID syndrome was diagnosed in 6.7-34.3% depending on MS status, with strong correlations found between post-COVID syndrome and carbohydrate metabolism disorders (VAI and HOMA-IR), though most metabolic parameters improved by 12 months while hypertension complications persisted.
paper_authors: Elena Klester; В. А. Елыкомов; Klester K.V.
paper_title: Comparative analysis of the dynamics of clinical and functional features of the metabolic syndrome in COPD patients who had a novel coronavirus infection

summary: Retrospective observational study examining associations between fatigue syndrome and inflammatory markers/medical interventions in 100 long COVID patients. Study identifies correlations between specific inflammatory markers and fatigue but does not test or evaluate a treatment intervention.
paper_authors: PAVEL E. KOLESNIKOV; А. A. Vizel; A. R. Abashev; A.R. Abashev; Ministry of Health of the Republic of Tatarstan; Kazan, Russian Federation
paper_title: Evaluation of the Association of Fatigue Syndrome with Levels of Key Inflammatory Markers and Various Medical Interventions in Long-COVID and Post-COVID Patients

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines coronary artery disease (CAD) patients at least 12 weeks after mild or moderate COVID-19 infection, comparing clinical, laboratory, and angiographic findings between the two groups. Patients with moderate acute COVID-19 showed worse cardiovascular outcomes including higher blood pressure, greater coronary artery lesions, and lower ejection fraction, indicating that moderate acute COVID increases long-term cardiovascular risk in CAD patients.
paper_authors: Daria A. Derisheva; D. A. Yakhontov; O.V. Dunicheva
paper_title: Features of the course of coronary artery disease in the post-COVID period

summary: Retrospective analysis of 1,329 COVID-19 patients admitted to a rural hospital (March 2020–November 2021) examining baseline pulmonary conditions and changes in lung function. Found significant decrease in DLCO in surviving patients but no clear treatment intervention tested.
paper_authors: Mansur Assaad; Apurwa Karki
paper_title: The Internal COVID-19 Database Registry: A Rural, Community Hospital’s Experience with the Pandemic

summary: A 2-year prospective cohort study comparing health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in 413 post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) patients versus 520 recovered controls using the EQ-5D-5L questionnaire and Clinical Frailty Scale. The study found significant HRQoL decline in PCC patients up to 18 months, with notable impairment in pain/discomfort, anxiety/depression, and usual activities, highlighting the need for continued monitoring and mental health support.
paper_authors: Kassandra Mercier; Jasmine Piché; Christine Rioux-Perreault; Samuel Lemaire-Paquette; Alain Piché
paper_title: A longitudinal prospective cohort study of health-related quality of life assessment in outpatient adults with post-COVID-19 conditions
paper_journal: Journal of the Association of Medical Microbiology and Infectious Disease Canada

summary: A descriptive cross-sectional cohort study examining dermatological manifestations in 120 COVID-19 patients (≥12 weeks post-infection). The study documents acute-period skin lesions (urticaria, erythema) in 9.7% and post-COVID dermatological symptoms in 94.4% of patients (alopecia, xerosis, onychopathy, new-onset dermatoses), but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: О.B. Nemchaninova; Елена Павловна Симонова
paper_title: Dermatological manifestations associated with a novel coronavirus infection in the acute and post-acute period of COVID-19

summary: This multicenter retrospective cohort study examines the association between baseline parathyroid hormone (iPTH) levels and COVID-19 severity and post-acute outcomes in 142 hemodialysis patients followed for 20 months. While the study identifies iPTH as a prognostic biomarker for post-acute hospitalization and mortality in long COVID patients with kidney disease, it is observational without any treatment intervention, thus not eligible for the intervention trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: L. Snisar; Andriy Rysyev; Ihor Poperechnyi; V. Filonov; Tetyana Ostapenko; V. N. Marchenko; Victor Dzhur
paper_title: Association between baseline intact parathyroid hormone levels, COVID-19 severity, and long-term outcomes in patients undergoing hemodialysis: A multicenter retrospective study
paper_journal: Ukrainian Journal of Nephrology and Dialysis

summary: Retrospective observational study comparing lipid profiles and cardiac electrical axis measurements in 30 young patients during acute COVID-19 and post-COVID-19 recovery. Found increases in cholesterol and LDL after recovery, with leftward deviation of the electrical axis detected in 17% of patients post-COVID.
paper_authors: N.T. Mirzoev; G.G. Kutelev; V.V. Ivanov; D.V. Cherkashin; K.S. Shulenin; R.G. Makiev
paper_title: Changes of the Electrical Axis of the Heart and Dyslipidemia as Possible Markers of Cardiovascular Damage in Patients after COVID-19

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 1,969 COVID-19 patients examining the frequency and risk factors for carbohydrate metabolism disorders (type 2 diabetes, prediabetes) during the post-COVID period over 3.5 years. New-onset hyperglycemia during acute COVID-19 was a strong predictor of later carbohydrate metabolism disorders, with age, BMI, and glucose levels identified as independent risk factors.
paper_authors: Z.Z. Khamidullina; D.Sh. Avzaletdinova; I.R. Gorbachev; Ya.R. Timasheva; T.V. Morugova; K.R. Khamidullin
paper_title: New Coronavirus Infection as a Factor in Increasing Carbohydrate Metabolism in the Late Post-COVID Period

summary: Prospective cohort study examining kidney involvement during acute COVID-19 hospitalization as a predictor of cardiovascular complications within one year post-discharge. Finds that kidney dysfunction is independently associated with increased risk of CV events, with persistent inflammation and endothelial dysfunction as potential mechanisms.
paper_authors: Anastasiia Hovornyan; Tetiana Ilashchuk
paper_title: Kidney involvement in acute COVID-19 and long-term cardiovascular outcomes: The role of inflammation and endothelial dysfunction
paper_journal: Ukrainian Journal of Nephrology and Dialysis

summary: This observational study characterizes the endocrine phenotype of post-COVID syndrome in 208 long COVID patients, identifying metabolic and cardiovascular risk factors associated with this phenotype. It is excluded because it is a passive observational study with no intervention or treatment evaluated—patients are merely assessed for existing conditions rather than given any treatment.
paper_authors: V.V. Zorina; Russian Federation Novosibirsk; A.D. Afanaseva; S.V. Mustafina; E.V. Shakhtschneider; I.I. Logvinenko
paper_title: Clinical and laboratory characteristics of the endocrine phenotype of post-COVID syndrome

summary: Prospective study assessing thyroid function and reproductive hormones in 171 women with menstrual disorders after COVID-19, comparing post-acute COVID (1-3 months) versus long COVID (3-6 months) phases. Findings show phase-dependent thyroid dysfunction patterns (transient thyrotoxicosis in post-acute phase, autoimmune hypothyroidism in long COVID) associated with specific menstrual disturbances, but no treatment intervention was administered or evaluated.
paper_authors: Alla O. Petruk; Olena O. Lytvak; Sergii A. Sheptukha
paper_title: ASSESSMENT OF THYROID STATUS IN WOMEN WITH MENSTRUAL FUNCTION DISORDERS AFTER COVID-19

summary: This observational study compares systemic inflammatory markers in 416 patients with stable coronary heart disease stratified by COVID-19 severity (mild vs. moderate) more than 12 weeks post-infection. Patients with moderate COVID-19 showed elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines (MCP-1, TNF-α, IL-1β) and complement component C3, suggesting worse cardiovascular outcomes in the post-acute period.
paper_authors: Davyd A. Yakhontov; Daria A. Derisheva; Vitaly L. Lukinov
paper_title: SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION IN PATIENTS WITH STABLE CORONARY HEART DISEASE IN THE POST-COVID PERIOD DEPENDING ON THE SEVERITY OF COVID-19 TRANSFER

summary: This natural pre-post experiment compared olfactory function and brain imaging in 9 COVID-19 patients and 12 controls, using baseline assessments conducted before the pandemic. Despite subjective olfactory complaints, the study found reduced olfactory bulb volume in most COVID-19 patients but no significant morphologic differences in central olfactory regions compared to controls.
paper_authors: Thunell E.; Peter MG; Lenoir V.; Andersson P.; Landis BN; Becker M.; Lundström JN
paper_title: Effects of COVID-19 on the Human Central Olfactory System: A Natural Pre-Post Experiment

summary: Retrospective observational study of 30 children with asthma who had COVID-19, assessing the course of acute infection and frequency of post-COVID syndrome development. Found that 13.3% of children developed post-COVID syndrome, but no intervention or treatment was tested.
paper_authors: О. О. Rechkina; S. M. Rudenko; V. O. Stryzh
paper_title: COVID-19 and Post-covid syndrome in children with bronchial asthma

summary: This retrospective cohort study analyzed electronic health records from 122,045 COVID-19 patients in Japan to describe the incidence of post-COVID symptoms and nursing care requirements across three periods with different viral strains and vaccination coverage. It found lower post-COVID symptom incidence with increased vaccination and identified depression and disuse syndrome as more prevalent in older patients, but did not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Kinugasa Y.; Llamas-Covarrubias MA; Ozaki K.; Fujimura Y.; Ohashi T.; Fukuda K.; Higashiue S.; Nakamura Y.; Imai Y.
paper_title: Post-Coronavirus Disease 2019 Syndrome in Japan: An Observational Study Using a Medical Database

summary: Cross-sectional study of 53 post-COVID-19 patients using MRI and neuropsychological testing to assess cognitive outcomes and correlate them with structural brain changes at median 1.8 years post-infection. Found significant cognitive impairment in attention, executive function, and memory domains associated with reduced cortical thickness in specific brain regions, but no intervention or treatment was tested.
paper_authors: Rosalia Dacosta-Aguayo; Josep Puig; Noemi Lamonja-Vicente; Meritxell Carmona-Cervelló; Brenda Biaani León-Gómez; Gemma Monté-Rubio; Victor M. López-Linfante; Valeria Zamora-Putin; Pilar Montero-Alia; Carla Chacon; Jofre Bielsa; Eduard Moreno-Gabriel; Rosa Garcia-Sierra; Alba Pachón; Anna Costa; Maria Mataró; Julia G. Prado; Eva Martinez-Cáceres; Lourdes Mateu; Marta Massanella; Concepción Violán; Pere Torán-Monserrat
paper_title: Reduced Cortical Thickness Correlates of Cognitive Dysfunction in Post-COVID-19 Condition: Insights from a Long-Term Follow-up

summary: A retrospective cohort study of 85 patients examining post-COVID-19 pulmonary fibrosis development, identifying risk factors including age, smoking history, and mechanical ventilation. The paper documents prevalence of fibrotic changes but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Allahrasan; Mahnaz Baloch; Muhammad Yousuf; Abdul Waheed; Sara Shahid; Zeeshan Jamal
paper_title: Patients having Lung Fibrosis after Covid-19: A Problematic Sequelae in Surviving Patients
paper_journal: International Journal of Current Research and Review

summary: Prospective observational study of 101 COVID-19 survivors followed at 6 months and 1 year post-discharge to assess pulmonary sequelae using spirometry and imaging. Found that 26.7% had persistent symptoms at 6 months (primarily exertional dyspnea) with correlation between initial disease severity and pulmonary impairment.
paper_authors: Mrinmayee Mayekar; Amreesh Paul
paper_title: Evaluating pulmonary sequelae in patients recovering from COVID-19: Short- and mid term complications and correlations with initial disease severity

summary: Retrospective analysis of Rowan Medicine electronic patient data examining prevalence and characterization of memory dysfunction and 'brain fog' symptoms in long COVID patients. The study found no significant observations due to extremely small dataset size, limiting the ability to provide meaningful analysis.
paper_authors: Chelsea McNamara; Alison Mancuso
paper_title: The Impact of Covid-19 on Post-Recovery Memory

summary: A retrospective cohort study examining central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) as an ocular complication in post-COVID syndrome patients across three Egyptian hospitals. The study documents clinical characteristics and symptoms in CRVO patients post-COVID but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Sanaa Ahmed; Ahmed Elmahdy; Eglal Kenawy; Marwa Abdulrehim; Samar Shoeir; Ghada Elmohaseb; Eman Youssef; Eman Bayoumy; Marwa Byomy
paper_title: The prevalence of central retinal vein occlusion was observed in middle age patients with post-covid syndrome multicenter study
paper_journal: Bioactive Compounds in Health and Disease

summary: Prospective multicentric observational study examining D-Dimer as a biomarker in acute COVID-19 pneumonia to predict severity, mechanical ventilation need, and post-COVID lung fibrosis. While the paper mentions long-term post-COVID effects, it focuses on acute hospitalization outcomes during active infection rather than treating long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Shital Patil; Manojkumar Bhadake; Abhijit Acharya; Ganesh Narwade
paper_title: Role of D-Dimer in Covid-19 pneumonia: sensitive marker of inflammation, predictor of mechanical ventilation, thromboembolic events and early marker of post covid-lung fibrosis; Prospective Multicentric, Observational, Interventional study in tertiary care setting in India

summary: Multicenter prospective study examining the relationship between nutrition therapy in the acute phase of severe COVID-19 (requiring mechanical ventilation) and post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) outcomes at 10-month follow-up. Found that supplemental parenteral nutrition >400 kcal/day independently correlated with lower occurrence of physical PICS, but does not study long COVID specifically—focuses on acute ICU survivors and general post-ICU outcomes.
paper_authors: Kensuke Nakamura; Junji Hatakeyama; Keibun Liu; Kazuma Yamakawa; Takeshi Nishida; Shinichiro Ohshimo; Shigeaki Inoue; Satoru Hashimoto; Shuhei Maruyama; Daisuke Kawakami; Yoshitaka Ogata; Katsura Hayakawa; Hiroaki Shimizu; Taku Oshima; Tatsuya Fuchigami; Osamu Nishida
paper_title: Relationship between critical care nutrition and post-intensive care syndrome in surviving ventilated patients with COVID-19: a multicenter prospective observational study
paper_journal: Journal of Clinical Biochemistry and Nutrition

summary: A prospective cohort study of 51 cancer survivors hospitalized for COVID-19, assessing post-acute symptoms including fatigue, nutritional status, anxiety, depression, and voice/swallowing impairments at discharge and 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. By one year, 66% of patients retained at least one impairment, with fatigue and psychological symptoms persisting despite improvements in nutritional status and overall daily functioning.
paper_authors: Victor Figueiredo Leite; Maria Teresa Duarte Pereira da Cruz Lourenço; Christina Haas Tarabay; Agnes Ayumi Sewo Mori; Giseli Maria; Thais Manfrinato Miola; Luciana da Costa; Celena Freire Friedrich; Telma Ribeiro Rodrigues; Jordana Balbinot; Elisabete Carrara-Angelis
paper_title: A prospective and longitudinal cohort study assessing postacute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection in patients with cancer

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines chest CT findings and pulmonary function test results in COVID-19 survivors during post-recovery phase (median 95 days post-symptom onset). The study correlates imaging abnormalities with lung function impairment but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Gustavo Borges da Silva Teles; Eduardo Kaiser Uruhary Nunes Fonseca; Julia Capobianco; Patricia Yokoo; Marcela Emer Egypto Rosa; Telma Antunes; Carolina Silva Bernardes; Tatiane Cristina Marques; Rodrigo Caruso Chate; Gilberto Szarf
paper_title: Correlation between chest computed tomography findings and pulmonary function test results in the post-recovery phase of COVID-19

summary: Observational study examining structural and functional cardiac changes in 221 COVID-19 patients at hospital discharge and 1-month follow-up using echocardiography, comparing hypertensive and normotensive subgroups. Found persistent left ventricular concentric geometry and diastolic dysfunction without improvement in the early post-discharge period, particularly in hypertensive patients.
paper_authors: Oleksii Honchar
paper_title: Структурно-функціональне ремоделювання серця у хворих на гіпертонічну хворобу та COVID-19: оцінка змін наприкінці періоду госпіталізації та упродовж 1 місяця спостереження

summary: This study examined 100 post-COVID patients admitted for stage 3 medical rehabilitation, assessing autonomic nervous system dysfunction using vegetative status assessment methods. After comprehensive rehabilitation, positive dynamics were observed in most patients, though residual symptoms persisted in those with autonomic dysfunction.
paper_authors: K. V. Petrov; Е. Yu. Mozheyko; Elena Shanina; Andrey V. Petrov
paper_title: Autonomic dysfunction syndrome in patients who underwent COVID-19, at stage 3 of medical rehabilitation

summary: Prospective cohort study of 175 Brazilian COVID-19 survivors assessing long-term symptoms over >120 days post-infection. Study documents prevalence of persistent fatigue, dyspnea, cough, headache, and muscle weakness but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Lívia P. Bonifácio; Viviane N.F. Csizmar; Francisco Barbosa-Júnior; Ana P.S. Pereira; Marcel Koenigkam-Santos; Danilo T. Wada; Gilberto G. Gaspar; Felipe S. Carvalho; Valdes R. Bollela; Rodrigo C. Santana; João P. Souza; Fernando Bellissimo-Rodrigues
paper_title: Long-Term Symptoms among COVID-19 Survivors in Prospective Cohort Study, Brazil

summary: Observational study of 36 IBD patients with prior COVID-19 assessing post-COVID syndrome prevalence and severity at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months via questionnaire and functional assessments (respiratory function, echocardiography, CT imaging). Found that post-COVID syndrome was more severe and prolonged in patients with respiratory distress during acute COVID-19, with minimal radiological changes in the non-RD group.
paper_authors: L. M. KUPKENOVA; D. I. ABDULGANIEVA; N. G. SHAMSUTDINOVA; А. Х. Одинцова; Dilyara G. Iskhakova; Maria Ilyinichna Cherkashina; Н. А. Черемина
paper_title: Long-term consequences of COVID-19 in patients with inflammatory intestine diseases (by the data of functional-radiology examinations of lungs and EchoKG)

summary: This study uses electronic health records to compare pre- and post-COVID-19 diagnostic codes to identify symptoms with higher incidence in the post-COVID period as potential long COVID sequelae. The work serves as a hypothesis-generation and monitoring method for long COVID symptoms in the population.
paper_authors: Eleanor S. Click; Donald Malec; Jennifer Chevinsky; Guoyu Tao; Michael Melgar; Jennifer Giovanni; Adi Gundlapalli; Deblina Datta; Karen K. Wong
paper_title: Longitudinal Analysis of Electronic Health Information to Identify Possible COVID-19 Sequelae

summary: This retrospective cohort study compared the frequency and course of post-COVID syndrome in 140 patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) versus spondyloarthritis (SpA), assessing disease activity and exacerbation risk factors over 12 months post-infection. RA patients had significantly higher post-COVID syndrome incidence (73.7% vs 61.3%) with more frequent fatigue, pain, and cognitive symptoms; disease exacerbations peaked at 3 months, with cardiovascular disease and female gender identified as key risk factors.
paper_authors: V. N. MUKHAMADIEVA; N. G. SHAMSUTDINOVA; T. YU. NURIAKHMETOVA; D. I. ABDULGANIEVA
paper_title: Frequency and course of post-COVID syndrome in patients with rheumatoid arthritis and spondyloarthritis

summary: Population-based cross-sectional study comparing prevalence of post-COVID-19 condition in 25,911 SARS-CoV-2 infected persons versus matched uninfected controls in Japan during the Omicron-dominant wave. Found 11.8% prevalence of post-COVID-19 condition (≥2 months persistent symptoms), with female sex, comorbidities, and mild-to-moderate acute infection as risk factors.
paper_authors: Arisa Iba; Mariko Hosozawa; Miyuki Hori; Yoko Muto; Isao Muraki; Rie Masuda; Nanako Tamiya; Hiroyasu Iso
paper_title: Prevalence of and Risk Factors for Post–COVID-19 Condition during Omicron BA.5–Dominant Wave, Japan

summary: This retrospective cohort study compared fatigue incidence rates between 4,589 COVID-19 patients and 9,022 propensity score-matched controls over a median 11.4-month follow-up period. The study found COVID-19 patients had significantly higher incidence rates of fatigue (10.2/100 person-years) and chronic fatigue (1.8/100 person-years) compared to controls, with hazard ratios of 1.68 and 4.32 respectively.
paper_authors: Vu QM; Fitzpatrick AL; Cope JR; Bertolli J.; Sotoodehnia N.; West TE; Gentile N.; Unger ER
paper_title: Estimates of Incidence and Predictors of Fatiguing Illness after SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: A 12-month observational follow-up study of 134 adults previously hospitalized for severe COVID-19 pneumonia, characterizing long-term sequelae including persistent cough, dyspnea, lung texture abnormalities, cognitive impairment, and fatigue. The study identifies risk factors (age, disease severity, comorbidities) associated with worse long-term outcomes but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Ivan O. Rosas; Alejandra Benitez; James A. McKinnell; Reena Shah; Michael Waters; Bradley D. Hunter; Robert Jeanfreau; Larry Tsai; Margaret Neighbors; Ben Trzaskoma; Rita de Cassia Castro; Fang Cai
paper_title: Long-Term Clinical Outcomes of Adults Hospitalized for COVID-19 Pneumonia

summary: Retrospective comparison of electrodiagnostic findings in patients with post-COVID-19 Guillain-Barré syndrome versus non-COVID-19 GBS. The study analyzes electromyography results but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Recep YEVGİ; Nuray BİLGE
paper_title: Comparison of electrodiagnostic findings in patients with  post-COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 Guillain-Barre syndrome
paper_journal: Journal of Health Sciences and Medicine

summary: This population-based study compares the prevalence of post-acute COVID-19 symptom clusters between individuals infected with Omicron versus wild-type SARS-CoV-2 variants. The research examines whether long COVID manifestations and symptom patterns differ depending on which variant caused the initial infection.
paper_authors: Rothenbacher, Dietrich
paper_title: Population-based comparison of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 and symptom clusters following Omicron versus wild-type infection
paper_journal: 70. Jahrestagung der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Medizinische Informatik, Biometrie und Epidemiologie e. V. (GMDS)

summary: This retrospective cohort study compared thrombotic event incidence in the year after COVID-19 versus other acute respiratory infections using PCORnet data from 2022-2023. It found a 63% increased risk for any thrombotic event and 73% increased risk in nonhospitalized patients with COVID-19, but does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Caroline Q. Pratt; Alexandra F. Dalton; Emily H. Koumans; Abraham Agedew; Fatima Coronado; Elizabeth A. Lundeen; Rebecca C. Woodruff; Jason P. Block; Mark Weiner; Lindsay Cowell; Jonathan D. Arnold; Sharon Saydah
paper_title: Thrombotic Events and Stroke in the Year After COVID-19 or Other Acute Respiratory Infection

summary: A prospective cohort study following 1,809 health and welfare workers with work-related COVID-19 infections over 26-32 months to identify predictors of persistent post-COVID symptoms. The study found that female gender, older age, pre-existing conditions, and severe acute symptoms were significant risk factors for prolonged recovery, with 60% still experiencing symptoms at 32 months.
paper_authors: Koch, Peter; Steinke, Lara; Peters, Claudia; Nienhaus, Albert
paper_title: Prevalence and predictors of post-COVID-19-related symptoms: an extended follow-up among employees in health and welfare services in Germany: a short report

summary: A prospective cohort study tracking 1,810 German healthcare workers with post-COVID symptoms over 18 months to identify factors influencing symptom persistence and recovery. Found that 67% reported ongoing symptoms at 18 months, with female sex, age >50, pre-existing conditions, and severe acute symptoms as risk factors for prolonged recovery.
paper_authors: Steinke, Lara; Peters, Claudia; Nienhaus, Albert; Bethge, Matthias; Koch, Peter
paper_title: Factors influencing the course of post-COVID-19-related symptoms: A bidirectional cohort study among employees in health and welfare services in Germany

summary: Cross-sectional study of 367 COVID-19 survivors examining the prevalence and intensity of musculoskeletal symptoms (fatigue, myalgia, arthralgia, muscle weakness) during the 6-month recovery period. Found high rates of musculoskeletal complications but no association with acute infection severity; does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Rukhsana Gulzar; Taifo Mahmud; A. Rasheed; Saima Riaz; W. Akhtar Adnan; Uzair Hafeez; Abdul Malik
paper_title: Musculoskeletal Symptoms in Patients Recovering from COVID-19

summary: Retrospective and prospective study examining factors associated with prolonged oxygen therapy need in COVID-19 patients discharged from hospital, with one-year mortality follow-up. While the study addresses post-discharge outcomes in COVID-19 survivors, it does not evaluate a specific treatment or intervention—it is a descriptive observational study of oxygen therapy use and outcomes, not a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Sibel Doğru; Meral Uyar; Sema Aytaç; Özlem Ovayolu
paper_title: The relationship between the need for prolonged oxygen therapy after discharge in COVID-19 patients and mortality
paper_journal: Journal of Health Sciences and Medicine

summary: This study compared neuropsychological and cognitive outcomes before and after COVID-19 infection in older adults from two ongoing longitudinal cohorts (Arizona APOE and ADRC). The authors found no significant differences in cognitive decline between pre- and post-COVID assessments, with members of both cohorts recovering well despite their age-related vulnerability.
paper_authors: Richard J. Caselli; Yinghua Chen; Kewei Chen; Robert J. Bauer; Dona E.C. Locke; Bryan K. Woodruff
paper_title: Cognition Before and After COVID-19 Disease in Older Adults: An Exploratory Study

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 67,000 German primary care patients comparing incidence of mild cognitive disorder (MCD) in COVID-19 patients versus acute upper respiratory infection controls. Found significantly higher MCD incidence in COVID-19 patients (7.6 vs 5.1 per 1,000 person-years), particularly in women and younger patients, but no treatment intervention was studied.
paper_authors: Jens Bohlken; Kerstin Weber; Steffi Riedel Heller; Bernhard Michalowsky; Karel Kostev
paper_title: Mild Cognitive Disorder in Post-COVID-19 Syndrome: A Retrospective Cohort Study of 67,000 Primary Care Post-COVID Patients

summary: Prospective descriptive study of 97 post-COVID-19 patients examining musculoskeletal symptoms and pain using VAS, DN-4, and SF-36 assessments. Found that arthralgia, myalgia, and neuropathic pain are common in post-COVID patients and negatively correlate with quality of life, but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Ender Erden; Ayla Cagliyan Turk; Ebru Erden; Zuhal Dag
paper_title: Musculoskeletal system symptoms in patients with COVID-19 and the impact of these symptoms on quality of life
paper_journal: Journal of Back and Musculoskeletal Rehabilitation

summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 1,546 COVID-19 survivors from Wuhan for two years post-discharge to assess long-term neurological symptoms. The study found that 44.24% reported at least one neurological symptom, with fatigue (28.33%) and memory deficit (13.26%) most common, and severe cases experiencing higher incidence of neurological sequelae.
paper_authors: Jing-Juan Wang; Qiao-Feng Zhang; Di Liu; Qing Du; Cheng Xu; Quan-Xin Wu; Yi Tang; Wang-Sheng Jin
paper_title: Self-Reported Neurological Symptoms Two Years After Hospital Discharge Among COVID-19 Survivors

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing dementia incidence in 8,129 matched pairs of COVID-19 patients versus acute upper respiratory infection controls over 12 months. Found no significant association between COVID-19 and dementia risk (IRR 1.05, 95% CI 0.85-1.29).
paper_authors: Celina Gollop; Rebecca Zingel; Louis Jacob; Lee Smith; Ai Koyanagi; Karel Kostev
paper_title: Incidence of Newly-Diagnosed Dementia After COVID-19 Infection versus Acute Upper Respiratory Infection: A Retrospective Cohort Study

summary: Observational longitudinal study following 350 post-acute COVID-19 patients over 12 months, assessing muscle function, quality of life, fatigue, and lung function at multiple timepoints. Results show progressive improvement in quality of life, fatigue, and pulmonary function, with greater gains in the first 6 months.
paper_authors: João Eduardo de Azevedo Vieira; Thiago Thomaz Mafort; Laura Braga Monnerat; Mariana Soares da Cal; Angelo Thomaz Abalada Ghetti; Agnaldo José Lopes
paper_title: Assessment of short- and long-term functionality and quality of life in patients with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome
paper_journal: Journal of Back and Musculoskeletal Rehabilitation

summary: This prospective cohort study assessed cognitive and neuropsychiatric outcomes in 208 long COVID patients 25 months post-infection and 17 months after initial evaluation, with some patients participating in neuropsychological rehabilitation. Results showed persistent cognitive deficits despite discrete improvement, with better outcomes in patients who completed rehabilitation, had higher education, and lower depression scores.
paper_authors: Lucia Willadino Braga; Sandro Barbosa Oliveira; Andrea Suhet Moreira; Maria Eloá Moreira da Silva Martins Pereira; Andrea Simoes Serra Serio; Virgínia da Silva Carneiro; Luciana de Figueiredo Pereira Freitas; Lígia Maria do Nascimento Souza
paper_title: Long COVID neuropsychological follow-up: Is cognitive rehabilitation relevant?

summary: This paper conducted an exploratory factor analysis of self-reported symptoms in long COVID patients collected at two time points (mean 21.7 weeks apart) to identify which acute-phase factors predict long-term impairment. Early autonomic and gastrointestinal dysfunction emerged as significant predictors of later functional impairment and ME/CFS-like symptoms.
paper_authors: Leonard A. Jason; Joseph A. Dorri
paper_title: Predictors of impaired functioning among long COVID patients

summary: This study compares cognitive functioning and brain connectivity at 6-12 months post-discharge in COVID-19 patients with multiple organ failure versus non-COVID MOF patients and healthy controls. While it documents neurological deficits in long COVID, it is an observational cross-sectional assessment without any intervention or treatment being tested.
paper_authors: Daniela Ramos-Usuga; Antonio Jimenez-Marin; Alberto Cabrera-Zubizarreta; Itziar Benito-Sanchez; Diego Rivera; Endika Martínez-Gutiérrez; Elena Panera; Victoria Boado; Fermín Labayen; Jesus M. Cortes; Juan C. Arango-Lasprilla
paper_title: Cognitive and brain connectivity trajectories in critically ill COVID-19 patients

summary: This paper analyzes thin-section CT imaging in 59 COVID-19 patients 24-39 days post-hospital discharge to assess pulmonary fibrosis development. While it follows patients after acute infection, it is primarily an acute COVID-19 imaging study conducted during early recovery without testing any treatment intervention, making it outside the scope of long COVID treatment trials.
paper_authors: Jiangping Wei; Hong Yang; Pinggui Lei; Bing Fan; Yingying Qiu; Bingliang Zeng; Peng Yu; Jian Lv; Yinchao Jian; Chengfeng Wan
paper_title: Analysis of thin-section CT in patients with coronavirus disease (COVID-19) after hospital discharge
paper_journal: Journal of X-Ray Science and Technology: Clinical Applications of Diagnosis and Therapeutics

summary: This cross-sectional study compares post-COVID-19 symptoms in 120 children (stratified by acute COVID severity) and 35 healthy controls, finding post-COVID condition in 38.3% overall with higher prevalence (71%) in those with severe acute COVID. The study documents symptom frequency, duration, and Chalder fatigue scale scores but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Olha Dmytryshyn; Yurii Marushko
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 and other changes in the health status of children and adolescents associated with the transmission of COVID-19
paper_journal: The Ukrainian Scientific Medical Youth Journal

summary: This cross-sectional study examined 221 hospitalized COVID-19 patients 1-2 days before discharge to assess associations between hypertension and clinical features during acute infection and residual functional disorders. While the paper mentions long COVID syndrome in the introduction, it does not study an intervention or treatment—it only characterizes acute-phase clinical features and discharge-status outcomes in hypertensive vs normotensive patients, making it a baseline/prognostic study rather than a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Oleksii Honchar; Tetiana Ashcheulova
paper_title: Associations of hypertension with clinical and instrumental characteristics in the ukrainian cohort of patients hospitalized for COVID-19
paper_journal: The Ukrainian Scientific Medical Youth Journal

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of clinical manifestations in 253 COVID-19 survivors at different time points (within 3 months and 3-12 months post-infection), stratified by acute illness severity. The study found that persistent symptoms were common (58-82% of patients), with fatigue, shortness of breath, and cough being most prevalent, though no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: N.S. Asfandiyarova; E. V. Filippov; В. Г. Демихов; O. V. Dashkevich; AlinA G. YAkubovskAYA; K.A. Moseychuk; N Zhuravleva; S.A. Kulikov
paper_title: Clinical manifestations of post-COVID-19 syndrome

summary: Comparative study of 37 post-COVID patients with joint hypermobility syndrome versus 21 controls without COVID-19, examining clinical manifestations and treatment response over 2 months. Treatment with NSAIDs, tofisopam (anxiolytic), and sulbutiamine significantly reduced pain, anxiety, and improved quality of life in the post-COVID group.
paper_authors: И. А. Викторова; Daria Ivanova; М.В. Моисеева; R.Sh. Kochimov; A.M. Adyrbayev
paper_title: Course patterns and patient management with joint hypermobility syndrome in the post-COVID-19 period

summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 268 COVID-19 pneumonia patients discharged from hospital with longitudinal laboratory measurements over five follow-up visits to characterize residual effects and recovery patterns. The study identified persistent abnormalities in hematologic parameters, immune cell function, and lung imaging up to 75 days post-discharge, with sex and age-based differences in recovery trajectories.
paper_authors: Deyang Huang; Hengyuan Miao; Ziqi Zhang; Yanhong Yang; Lieguang Zhang; Fleming Y.M. Lure; Zixian Wang; Stefan Jaeger; Lin Guo; Tao Xu; Jinxin Liu
paper_title: Longitudinal changes of laboratory measurements after discharged from hospital in 268 COVID-19 pneumonia patients
paper_journal: Journal of X-Ray Science and Technology

summary: Open observational study evaluating whether Maxilac® Baby synbiotic improves gastrointestinal symptoms, gut microbiota composition, and intestinal permeability in 16 children (ages 3-14) with mild-to-moderate post-COVID-19 syndrome, compared to 16 untreated controls. Synbiotic treatment was associated with reduced recurrence of GI symptoms 30 days post-recovery compared to control group.
paper_authors: В.П. Новикова; A. V. Polunina; С. L. Bannova; Алексей Львович Балашов; V. V. Dudurich; Л. Г. Данилов; A. E. Blinov; О. Н. Варламова
paper_title: Gastrointestinal tract in children with novel coronavirus infection and post-COVID-19 syndrome. The role of synbiotics for improving clinical symptoms, gut microbiota, and intestinal permeability
paper_journal: Russian Journal of Woman and Child Health

summary: This retrospective study assessed long-term pulmonary changes in 68 COVID-19 patients 1–2 years post-infection using CT, SPECT, spirometry, and DLCO measurements. The paper documents imaging and functional findings associated with persistent respiratory symptoms but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: V.P. Zolotnitskaya; Alexandra A Speranskaya; Н. А. Кузубова; О. Н. Титова; O. V. Amosova
paper_title: Long-term effects of COVID-19 in patients according to the functional lung imaging in radiation therapy

summary: This study examines microvascular abnormalities in 78 children 3-12 months post-COVID-19 using slit lamp biomicroscopy to assess bulbar conjunctival microvasculature, comparing them to 30 healthy controls. While microcirculatory disorders were identified and the authors mention designing rehabilitation measures, the paper is a descriptive observational study without testing or evaluating any specific intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: И Г Михеева; О. Б. Курасова; M.Yu. Milekhina; А.Б. Моисеев; Н. И. Кузнецова; I.I. Kalinovskaya; N.A. Zimina; T.G. Vereshchagina; Children Bronchopulmonary Sanitarium, Moscow, Russian Federation; T.G. Vereshchagina
paper_title: Study of microcirculation and the scheduling of rehabilitation measures in children who have recovered from coronavirus disease 2019
paper_journal: Russian Journal of Woman and Child Health

summary: This study compares clinical and laboratory characteristics in 62 hemodialysis patients with chronic kidney disease stage 5, stratified by prior COVID-19 infection history. The authors report significantly higher mortality (35%) in COVID-19-infected dialysis patients versus uninfected controls (4.7%), attributed to protein-energy deficiency.
paper_authors: Kulibaba, T. G.; Мусаева, Д.Т.; Pchelin, Ivan Y.; Rumyantsev, A. Sh; Slepyh, L. A.; Соловьева, О.М.; Тертышная, А.С.; Hudiakova, Natalia V.
paper_title: Clinical and Laboratory Characteristics of Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease 5D Depending on the Episode of SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: Prospective cohort study following mild-moderate COVID-19 patients at 6 weeks, 12 weeks, and 12 months post-infection to identify persistent symptoms and health status impact. Found that asthenia, anosmia, dysgeusia, and cognitive problems were most common, with several patients not recovering to baseline health status one year later, particularly those over 40, female, or with comorbidities.
paper_authors: Margarida Cepa; Rosário Raimundo; Fernando Fernando Sebastião
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 condition in patients with mild-moderate infection

summary: A cross-sectional study comparing olfactory and trigeminal event-related potentials in 77 long COVID patients (≥1 year post-infection) versus 21 healthy controls. The study identifies electrophysiological biomarkers of post-COVID olfactory dysfunction but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Richard Holý; David Kalfeřt; Libor Vašina; Oleksii Vorobiov; Petra Dytrych; Karla Janoušková; Eva Augste; Shahriar Kashiri; Nikola Pastorková; Kristýna Mamiňák; Jiří Hložek; Daniel Kovář; Jan Vodička; Jaromír Astl
paper_title: Olfactory event-related potentials (OERPs) and trigeminal event-related potentials (TERPs) in subjects after Covid-19 infection: single-center prospective study

summary: This RCT evaluated four rehabilitation regimens in 195 post-COVID patients, comparing standard care alone versus standard care with vitamin, mineral, or combined vitamin-mineral supplementation over 6 months. Combined vitamin-mineral supplementation showed the greatest improvement in quality of life (measured by SF-36), with all intervention groups showing 10-20% improvement over the study period.
paper_authors: Алексей Олегович Романов; Анна Николаевна Архангельская; Майсият Магомедовна Шарипова; Константин Георгиевич Гуревич; A. O. Romanov; A. N. Arkhangelskaya; M. M. Sharipova; K.G. Gurevich; A. I. Y. Moscow
paper_title: Quality of life in patients with novel coronavirus infection: association with disease severity and change depending on rehabilitation regimens after inpatient treatment

summary: Prospective study comparing lung CT scan findings in 60 COVID-19 patients at hospital admission and 3 months post-discharge. Found that 53.3% of patients had persistent abnormal lung findings at follow-up, with more severe initial involvement predicting worse outcomes, but this is a descriptive follow-up study without treatment intervention.
paper_title: Comparison of Lung CT Scan Findings upon Admission and Three Months after the Discharge of Patients with COVID-19

summary: This retrospective cohort study evaluates the frequency and nature of cardiovascular and other complications during long-term follow-up after COVID-19 in patients with and without pre-existing cardiovascular disease. The study identifies cardiovascular risk factors and outcomes in long COVID patients to inform clinical management.
paper_authors: Nana Pogosova; D. T. Kuchiev; A.B. Popova; A. K. Ausheva; Ashot Avagimyan; R. Zhetisheva
paper_title: Impact of cardiovascular diseases on the risk of adverse long-term outcomes after COVID-19

summary: This prospective cohort study measured endothelial function markers (endothelin-1 and thrombomodulin) in 16 patients who experienced non-hospitalized COVID-19 pneumonia, assessed at 60 days and one year post-onset, with 10 healthy controls. Most patients showed clinical improvement and recovered lung function by one year, but elevated thrombomodulin levels persisted in some patients, suggesting ongoing endothelial dysfunction.
paper_authors: Tetyana Pertseva; Nataliia Habshydze
paper_title: Endothelial function in patients after severe or critical acute phase of COVID-19 one year after the disease onset

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing electrophysiological changes (EEG) in Chornobyl clean-up workers and Ukrainian military personnel who recovered from COVID-19 versus control groups. Study documents persistent cerebral dysfunction (delta and theta power abnormalities) in COVID-19 recuperates but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Bazyka DA; Kuts KV; Perchuk IV; Kreinis GY; Antipchuk KY; Vasylenko ZL; Hryhorenko MS
paper_title: ELECTROPHYSIOLOGICAL CHANGES IN THE PARTICIPANTS OF THE LIQUIDATION OF THE CONSEQUENCES OF THE CHORNOBYL ACCIDENT AND THE MILITARY PERSONNEL OF THE UKRAINIAN DEFENSE FORCES RECOVERING FROM CORONAVIRUS DISEASE (COVID-19)
paper_journal: Проблеми радіаційної медицини та радіобіології = Problems of Radiation Medicine and Radiobiology

summary: This cross-sectional study examines surfactant protein A (SP-A) levels in 77 patients with dyspnea during the subacute post-COVID period (day 47 post-infection) to assess lung surfactant system dysfunction. The study finds that elevated SP-A levels (>59 ng/ml) are associated with severe/critical acute COVID-19 disease and predict dyspnea severity, but it is an observational biomarker study without any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Lyudmyla Konopkina; O.O. Shchudro
paper_title: The role of surfactant system dysfunction in the formation of dyspnea in patients with COVID-19-associated pneumonia

summary: A retrospective study of 85 long COVID patients in eastern Canada who received weekly acupuncture for 8-12 weeks. Results showed 85% clinical effectiveness with reduction in shortness of breath, fatigue, body pain, and brain fog.
paper_title: The Effectiveness of Acupuncture in The Treatment of Post COVID-19 Condition: A Retrospective Study

summary: Retrospective analysis of 90 post-COVID syndrome patients hospitalized for respiratory and lung complications, documenting the frequency and types of secondary infectious complications including fungal and bacterial infections. Study identifies infectious complications in 53.3% of patients, with Epstein-Barr virus reactivation (30%), bacterial infections (15.6%), and opportunistic fungi as primary causes, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: О.К. Yakovenko; М.І. Lynnyk; V.І. Іgnatieva; G.L. Gumeniuk; S.G. Opimakh; M.A. Polianska; I.V. Zvol; S.M. Moskalenko
paper_title: Infectious complications of the respiratory tract and lungs in patients with post-COVID syndrome

summary: This cohort study assessed cardiovascular function and imaging findings in 30 COVID-19 recovered healthcare workers 3-12 months post-infection. Despite preserved exercise tolerance, subclinical cardiac abnormalities including myocardial edema and reduced right ventricular function were detected in nearly half the participants.
paper_authors: Mir Jamal Uddin; A. K. M. Monwarul Islam; Kaniz Fatema Ananya; Shovan Rahman; Nusrat Ghafoor; Saqif Shahriar; Mizanur Rahman Majumder; Mahmudul Hasan; AKS Zahid Mahmud Khan
paper_title: Long-term impact of COVID-19 on cardiovascular health of healthcare workers of a tertiary care hospital of Bangladesh

summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 332 COVID-19 survivors for two months post-discharge to assess persistence and risk factors for fatigue using the Chalder fatigue scale. The study found that 62.9% of participants still experienced fatigue two months after hospital discharge, with significant associations between fatigue and age, comorbidities, and baseline biomarkers.
paper_authors: Md Khairul Islam; Mohammad Murad Hossain; Md Monowar Hossain; Md Mohiuddin Sharif; Fahima Sharmin Hossain; Md Robed Amin; Md Ridwanur Rahman
paper_title: Persistence of Fatigue among COVID-19 Survivors in Bangladesh: A Two-month after Follow-up Study

summary: A cross-sectional study of 261 long COVID patients in Croatia examining symptoms, functional status (PCFS scale), and risk factors for severe impairment. Found that female sex, oxygen therapy during acute disease, malignant disease, and hypertension were associated with greater functional impairment, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Marko Banić; Mateja Janković Makek; Miroslav Samaržija; Davorka Muršić; Zagorka Boras; Vesna Trkeš; Denis Baričević; Marta Koršić; Latinka Basara; Tajana Jalušić; Glunčić; Andrea Vukić Dugac
paper_title: Risk factors and severity of functional impairment in long COVID: a single-center experience in Croatia

summary: Descriptive observational study analyzing chest X-ray findings in 277 RT-PCR confirmed COVID-19 patients during acute infection, correlating radiological findings with clinical severity and short-term outcomes. While it documents post-COVID complications (fatigue, SOB on exertion) observed after discharge, it does not study or test any treatment intervention for long COVID.
paper_authors: Nirmol Kumar Biswas; Juli Chowdhury; Rita Majumder; Mahmuda Yesmin; Pijous Biswas; Ahmad Monjurul Aziz; Tapan Chandra Shil
paper_title: Pattern of Chest X-rays findings and clinical correlation with the severity in COVID-19 (RT-PCR positive) infected patients admitted in a COVID-19 dedicated hospital in Bangladesh

summary: This retrospective epidemiological study examines the incidence of ixodid tick-borne borreliosis and tick-borne encephalitis in Krasnoyarsk residents, hypothesizing that increased susceptibility among post-COVID-19 individuals may be due to immune dysregulation. The study found higher proportions of women with prior COVID-19 among borreliosis and encephalitis cases, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: O.V. Sorokina; A.Ya. Nikitin; N.Yu. Kharlamp'eva
paper_title: THE INCIDENCE OF IXODID TICK-BORNE BORRELIOSIS IN RESIDENTS OF THE KRASNOYARSK TERRITORY WHO SUFFERED COVID-19

summary: A prospective observational study that assessed hormonal changes (thyroid, adrenal, and sex-steroid axes) in 15 long COVID patients at baseline and 3-6 months post-infection. The study found high prevalence of endocrine dysfunctions at follow-up but did not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Shohael Mahmud Arafat; Hurjahan Banu; Md Shahed Morshed; Nusrat Sultana; Muhammad Abul Hasanat
paper_title: A Short-Term Follow-up Study on Hormonal Changes after Three to Six Months of SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: Prospective observational cohort study examining the frequency and pattern of chest pain in long COVID patients over 3 months of follow-up at a cardiology center. Found that 59% of patients developed cardiac symptoms at 3 months, with chest pain due to coronary artery disease being a common manifestation, but no intervention or treatment was tested.
paper_authors: AFM Azim Anwar; Tania Sharmeen; Md Al Amin; Md Masud Rana; Harisul Hoque; Noor Mohammed; Md Nazmul Hashan; Abul Fazal Md Helal Uddin; Srizon Roy Tirtho
paper_title: Pattern of Chest Pain in Long COVID Syndrome

summary: A prospective cohort study of 98 older adults with post-COVID syndrome in Kazakhstan investigating the effectiveness and safety of transitioning from multiple antihypertensive medications to a single-tablet strategy over 8 weeks. The intervention led to significant reduction in hypertensive crises and adverse events, with improved initial therapy adherence that declined by 10% by week 8.
paper_authors: Kudabaeva Venera; Mansharipova Almagul; Bolsyn Assel
paper_title: Initial expierence with Deprescribing in physically active older adults with post-COVID syndrome in Kazakhstan: A Cohort Study Investigating Transition to Simplified Treatment Regimen

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed thyroid functional status in 58 COVID-19 survivors (>6 months post-infection) compared to 27 healthy controls, measuring thyroid hormones and autoantibodies. While most survivors showed normal thyroid function, female survivors had significantly lower FT3 and FT4 levels, and 17% showed abnormalities including thyroid toxicity or elevated autoantibodies.
paper_authors: Mahjabin Nobi Khan; Pabitra Kumar Bhattacharjee; Md Farhan Muhtasim; Abdullah Al Persi; Noor E. Amrin Alim; Md Sazzad Hossain
paper_title: Analysis of Thyroid Functional Status of the Covid-19 Survivors: A Single Center Study

summary: Observational study of 56 RT-PCR confirmed COVID-19 patients in Bangladesh documenting long-term sequelae at follow-up. Found high rates of fatigue (44.6%), memory impairment (39.3%), joint pain (39.6%), and psychiatric symptoms (28.6%) among survivors.
paper_authors: Neena Islam; Mohammed Abdur Rahim; Prabir Kumar Das; Golam Mostafa; A. K. M. Manzurul Alam
paper_title: Long Term Effects of COVID-19 among RT-PCR Positive Bangladeshi Patients
paper_journal: Journal of Chittagong Medical College Teachers' Association

summary: Prospective observational study of 3,000 COVID-19 patients evaluating the role of CT severity phenotypes (mild/moderate/severe) in predicting disease outcomes and post-COVID lung fibrosis. While CT severity correlated with interventions needed and long-term sequelae, it showed inconsistency in predicting individual disease severity and early outcomes.
paper_authors: Shital Patil; Uttareshvar Dhumal; Laxman Kasture; Gajanan Gondhali
paper_title: CT severity Radiological phenotypes (CTS) assessment in COVID-19 pneumonia as ‘inconsistent predictor of disease severity’: A large tertiary care center study in India

summary: Retro-prospective observational study of 606 COVID-19 patients in Bangladesh documenting post-COVID symptoms at 3-10 months follow-up. Describes symptom prevalence (33.8% with symptoms) and phenotypes (fatigue, palpitations, muscle pain, neurological) but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Al Amin Amin; Najnin Jahan Hafsa; Roksana Akter; Pinki Shaha; Utshab Roy; Nazmul Hasan; Abu Mohammad Saem; Mohammad Izazul Hoque
paper_title: Post COVID symptoms in Patients of Cumilla District, Bangladesh
paper_journal: Journal of Comilla Medical College Teachers' Association

summary: Retrospective analysis of 670 archival patient records from a rheumatology department examining the relationship between COVID-19 infection and rheumatic disease exacerbation, identifying three patient groups including those with post-COVID syndrome. The study documents post-COVID symptomatology (asthenia, arthropathy, connective tissue features) but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Elena Rechkina; N.I. Korshunov; А. А. Баранов; K. M. Konovalov; E. A. Malygina
paper_title: New coronavirus infection (COVID-19) and the nosological structure of patients of the rheumatological department. A glance look from the region
paper_journal: Public health of the Far East Peer-reviewed scientific and practical journal

summary: This nationwide cohort study examined the incidence of unspecified and idiopathic pain in COVID-19 patients versus matched controls during the 90 days following COVID-19 diagnosis. The findings show elevated risk of unspecified pain post-COVID, though results vary by control group selection, and it is an observational study with no treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Namwoo Kim; Jeewuan Kim; Bo Ram Yang; Bong-Jin Hahm
paper_title: Associations of unspecified pain, idiopathic pain and COVID-19 in South Korea: a nationwide cohort study

summary: A prospective cohort study examining the incidence and characteristics of chronic daily headache (CDH) after COVID-19 in 199 patients with persistent headaches followed for at least one year post-infection. The study found that 20.3% developed CDH, with prior headache history and acute-phase headache intensity identified as risk factors.
paper_authors: Larissa Clementino Leite Sá Carvalho; Priscila Aparecida da Silva; Pedro Augusto Sampaio Rocha-Filho
paper_title: Persistent headache and chronic daily headache after COVID-19: a prospective cohort study

summary: This observational cohort study followed 177 COVID-19 patients over 12 months to assess dynamics of respiratory function and exercise tolerance, comparing those who developed post-COVID syndrome with those who did not. While the paper demonstrates that post-COVID syndrome is associated with persistent respiratory impairment requiring long-term rehabilitation, it is observational in design with no intervention tested and therefore excluded from the treatment trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: O. A. Abuldinova; Olga Prikhodko; Anton S. Abuldinov
paper_title: Dynamics of Functional Parameters of the Respiratory System in Patients with Various Forms of COVID-19
paper_journal: Public health of the Far East Peer-reviewed scientific and practical journal

summary: This cross-sectional study examines cardiovascular manifestations in 175 children aged 8-17 years with post-COVID autonomic dysfunction syndrome, comparing them to 42 controls without SARS-CoV-2 exposure. The study identified cardiac arrhythmias, hypertension, ECG changes, and lipid profile alterations associated with IgG antibodies to SARS-CoV-2.
paper_authors: M.A. Lazareva; S.V. Suprun; G.P. Evseeva; S.V. Anureyev; G.I. Zolotareva; E.V. Rakitskaya; O.A. Lebedko
paper_title: Cardiovascular Manifestations in Children with Autonomic Dysfunction Syndrome Associated with Coronavirus Infection
paper_journal: Public health of the Far East Peer-reviewed scientific and practical journal

summary: A prospective 3-month follow-up study of 76 COVID-19 survivors evaluating symptom persistence, antibody dynamics, and pulmonary function after hospital discharge. While documenting post-acute symptoms like fatigue, dyspnea, and chest tightness, the study is purely observational monitoring without any intervention or treatment evaluation, making it ineligible as a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Limei Liang; Bohan Yang; Nanchuan Jiang; Wei Fu; Xinliang He; Yaya Zhou; Wan-Li Ma; Xiaorong Wang
paper_title: Three-Month Follow-Up Study of Survivors of Coronavirus Disease 2019 after Discharge

summary: This cross-sectional study compared clinical characteristics and persistent symptoms in 1,122 patients who visited a post-COVID clinic, categorizing symptoms into three groups based on prevalence patterns across acute and post-acute phases. While it documents the multi-organ nature of long COVID symptoms and identifies anxiety, depression, and fatigue as key factors, it is a descriptive epidemiological study without any treatment intervention or control group.
paper_authors: Young Hee Jung; Eun-Hye Ha; Kang Won Choe; Seungbok Lee; Dong Ho Jo; Wang Jun Lee
paper_title: Persistent Symptoms After Acute COVID-19 Infection in Omicron Era

summary: Prospective follow-up study of 147 mild COVID-19 patients from a South Korean community treatment center assessing persistent symptoms and health-related quality of life 3 months after discharge. Found that 55.8% remained symptomatic with neuropsychiatric, neurological, and constitutional symptoms, with female sex, metabolic disease, and anxiety associated with long COVID persistence and diminished HRQoL.
paper_authors: Hi Sun Soh; BeLong Cho
paper_title: Long COVID-19 and Health-Related Quality of Life of Mild Cases in Korea: 3-Months Follow-up of a Single Community Treatment Center

summary: This study evaluates comprehensive rehabilitation management (exercise, nutrition, psychology) in severe-to-critical COVID-19 inpatients during acute hospitalization and early recovery. While it shows rehabilitation improves functional outcomes, it focuses on acute COVID-19 recovery rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-months after infection) and therefore does not meet inclusion criteria.
paper_authors: Hyeonseong Woo; Sanghee Lee; Hyun Sung Lee; Hyun Jun Chae; Jongtak Jung; Myung Jin Song; Sung Yoon Lim; Yeon Joo Lee; Young-Jae Cho; Eu Suk Kim; Hong Bin Kim; Jae-Young Lim; Kyoung-Ho Song; Jaewon Beom
paper_title: Comprehensive Rehabilitation in Severely Ill Inpatients With COVID-19: A Cohort Study in a Tertiary Hospital

summary: Prospective follow-up study of 187 COVID-19 recovered patients assessing long COVID symptoms and gut microbiota composition at one year post-discharge. Found that 44.9% reported long COVID symptoms with significantly altered gut microbiota profiles compared to healthy controls, suggesting a potential mechanistic link between dysbiosis and persistent symptoms.
paper_authors: Dongmei Zhang; Yaya Zhou; Yanling Ma; Ping Chen; Jian Tang; Bohan Yang; Hui Li; Mengyuan Liang; YuE Xue; Yao Liu; Jianchu Zhang; Xiaorong Wang
paper_title: Gut Microbiota Dysbiosis Correlates With Long COVID-19 at One-Year After Discharge

summary: Retrospective analysis of 440 post-COVID patients at a clinic examining prevalence and associations of neurological symptoms (brain fog, memory impairment, headache, dizziness). Found brain fog most common (38.6%), with associations to sleep problems, fatigue, depression, and olfactory/gustatory dysfunction.
paper_authors: Young Hee Jung; Eun-Hye Ha; Junli Park; Kang Won Choe; Wang Jun Lee; Dong Ho Jo
paper_title: Neurological and Psychiatric Manifestations of Post-COVID-19 Conditions

summary: This prospective longitudinal study followed 82 COVID-19 patients for 12 weeks post-discharge to characterize persistent symptoms and their impact on quality of life, frailty, and employment. The study found that 75.6% of patients reported at least one symptom at 12 weeks (fatigue being most common), with significant declines in functional status and 6 patients losing employment.
paper_authors: Sung-Geun Kim; Hyeok Choon Kwon; Tae Kyoung Kang; Mi Young Kwak; Seungmin Lee; Kyungmee Lee; Kilkon Ko
paper_title: COVID-19 Sequelae and Their Implications on Social Services

summary: This prospective study compared viral, immunologic, and laboratory parameters in 57 COVID-19 patients (29 with PASC, 28 without) at three timepoints over 3 months. PASC patients showed significantly elevated nucleocapsid antigen and multiple cytokines (IL-2, IL-17A, VEGF, RANTES, etc.), suggesting prolonged immune dysregulation rather than autoimmune or hormonal abnormalities.

summary: Prospective cohort study following 170 adult COVID-19 patients at 6 and 12 months post-infection to assess persistent symptoms and quality of life. paper_title: Risk and protective factors for Long COVID in Brazilian adults (CUME Study)

paper_title: A prospective cohort study on cognitive and psychological outcomes in COVID-19 ICU survivors at 3 months of follow up

paper_title: Spontaneous physical functional recovery after hospitalization for COVID-19: insights from a 1 month follow-up and a model to predict poor trajectory

summary: Prospective observational study examining retinal microvascular changes in 25 patients 1 and 12 months after severe COVID-19 hospitalization using optical coherence tomography angiography. paper_title: Long-term COVID-19 sequelae by Theta and SARS-CoV-2 variants in a Philippine cohort

summary: Retrospective observational study examining the relationship between smoking, obesity, and post-COVID-19 sequelae in Spanish COVID-19 patients. paper_title: Influence of smoking and obesity on post-COVID-19 sequelae and risk of hospitalization

paper_title: Accumulated subcutaneous fat in abdomen is associated with long COVID-19 symptoms among non-hospitalized patients: a prospective observational study

summary: A prospective cohort study of 88 long COVID patients examining the association between fatigue and systemic biomarkers, pulmonary/cardiac function, and diaphragm morphology. paper_title: Elevated adipokines and myokines are associated with fatigue in long COVID patients

paper_title: Post-COVID-19 condition: a sex-based analysis of clinical and laboratory trends

summary: A retrospective observational study of 31 severe COVID-19 survivors evaluating functional capacity decline using the Duke Activity Status Index (DASI) before and after ICU hospitalization. paper_title: Functional decline after severe COVID-19: duke activity status index for preoperative risk assessment

summary: This observational cross-sectional study assessed pulmonary function, structural lung changes, and functional capacity in 210 COVID-19 patients (mild/moderate, severe, critical) evaluated at least 3 months post-infection. paper_title: Efficacy of major ozone autohemotherapy in patients with post-COVID syndrome

paper_title: Risk of hematologic malignancies following herpes zoster after COVID-19: a global cohort study

paper_title: Post-COVID-19 condition after SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy: a population-based questionnaire cohort study

summary: This prospective feasibility study evaluated a virtual in-home cardiac monitoring system in 16 COVID-19 survivors using pulse oximeters and ECG patches over 3 months. paper_title: Remote, smart telemonitoring of COVID-19 survivors for early detection of deterioration in cardiac health (the PARTMO study)

summary: The COVID and Cognition Study is a cross-sectional/longitudinal observational study examining predictive factors for physical, neurological, and cognitive symptoms in 181 long COVID patients versus 185 uninfected controls. summary: This real-world retrospective cohort study evaluated 372 post-COVID-19 pulmonary fibrosis (PCPF) patients, comparing one-year readmission and mortality rates between those treated with small-molecule antiviral drugs (SMADs, n=293) during acute hospitalization versus those who were not (n=79). paper_title: Clinical and prognostic implications of hyaluronic acid in patients with COVID-19 reinfection and first infection

paper_title: COVCOG 2: Cognitive and Memory Deficits in Long COVID: A Second Publication From the COVID and Cognition Study

paper_title: Long term follow-up of heart rate variability in healthcare workers with mild COVID-19

paper_title: Long COVID-19–related and non-COVID-19 postviral olfactory dysfunction a comparative MRI study focusing on the olfactory cleft and bulbs

Findings show MG patients experience higher rates of post-COVID sequelae (insomnia, myalgia, dizziness, cough) compared to normal patients, with severity associated with daily corticosteroid dose and pre-COVID myasthenia crises frequency.

paper_title: The clinical risk and post-COVID-19 sequelae in patients with myasthenia gravis: a retrospective observational study

paper_title: Neurologic symptoms following COVID-19 in Lima, Peru: a prospective longitudinal observational study

Found high burden of cognitive impairment (79%), headache (74%), and insomnia (58%), with symptom severity correlating with depression but not PTSD scores.

paper_title: Neuropsychiatric symptoms cluster as primary drivers of Long COVID complexity: a South Texas retrospective cohort study

paper_title: Prevalence and severity of neurologic symptoms in Long-COVID and the role of pre-existing conditions, hospitalization, and mental health

Found white matter hyperintensities comparable to controls, occasional signs of inflammation/demyelination (4%), and cranial nerve enhancement (7%), suggesting MRI's role is primarily to exclude alternative diagnoses rather than guide treatment.

paper_title: Trajectory of post-COVID brain fog, memory loss, and concentration loss in previously hospitalized COVID-19 survivors: the LONG-COVID-EXP multicenter study

Although post-COVID patients showed cognitive deficits and differences in brain connectivity in attention-related regions, the study was observational without any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Serena Fineschi; Markus Fahlström; David Fällmar; Sven Haller; Johan Wikström
paper_title: Comprehensive MRI assessment reveals subtle brain findings in non-hospitalized post-COVID patients with cognitive impairment

summary: This prospective observational cohort study investigates whether orthostatic hemodynamic changes mediate cognitive impairment in PASC and ME/CFS patients compared to healthy controls. The study finds that PASC and ME/CFS patients show significantly lower cognitive efficiency after orthostatic challenge, with abnormal hemodynamic responses (narrow pulse pressure, elevated heart rate) associated with impaired information processing.

summary: Prospective cohort study examining associations between COVID-19 vaccination, food consumption patterns, and risk of post-acute COVID-19 syndrome in Brazilian adults. Finds that adequate intake of vitamin C, vitamin D, zinc, and white meat, along with pre-infection vaccination, are protective against PACS development.

paper_title: Vaccination and food consumption: association with Post-Acute COVID-19 Syndrome in Brazilian adults (CUME Study)

summary: This prospective registry study assessed pain and neurological symptoms in hospitalized COVID-19 patients at 3 months post-infection. While it documents high rates of persistent pain (60%), fatigue (42%), and PTSD (25%), it is an observational follow-up study with no intervention or treatment being tested.

paper_title: Pain and Other Neurological Symptoms Are Present at 3 Months After Hospitalization in COVID-19 Patients

summary: This retrospective cohort study examined 84 pediatric long COVID patients to investigate whether smell and taste dysfunction following SARS-CoV-2 infection was associated with subsequent development of eating disorders. The study observed that 6 out of 24 children with post-COVID anosmia/ageusia developed anorexia nervosa, suggesting a possible link between persistent chemosensory dysfunction and restrictive eating behaviors.

paper_title: Development of restrictive eating disorders in children and adolescents with long-COVID-associated smell and taste dysfunction

summary: Longitudinal online survey tracking COVID-19 infection patterns and persistent symptoms in 1,415–2,224 cancer patients across four pandemic waves over 16 months. paper_title: Modulating Role of Breastfeeding Toward Long COVID Occurrence in Children: A Preliminary Study

paper_title: Pulmonary Function and Long-Term Respiratory Symptoms in Children and Adolescents After COVID-19

summary: A prospective cohort study characterizing post-COVID symptoms in adults and children living in the same household in Italy, followed for up to 12 months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study found that adults experienced persistent symptoms more frequently and severely than children, with no correlation between symptoms in co-habitant household members.

Found 70% of COVID-19 survivors reported persistent symptoms (fatigue, cognitive sequelae, headaches most common), with significantly higher symptom persistence in COVID-19 vs control group, but no treatment intervention was tested.

The study found that persistent symptoms (dyspnea, fatigue, cough) declined from 32.6% at 2 months to 2.3% at 6 months, with most children showing clinical improvement and experiencing sequalae including alopecia, radiculopathy, and psychiatric symptoms.

paper_title: Vitamin D status in children with COVID-19: does it affect the development of long COVID and its symptoms?

Found persistent symptoms in 85.8% at 3 months declining to 32.5% at 12 months, with older age associated with most symptom types and fatigue being the most common persistent symptom.
