summary: This cross-sectional observational study examined the relationship between post-COVID-19 symptoms and daily physical activity in 18 PCS patients using smartwatch tracking and daily symptom surveys. The study found that dizziness was negatively associated with physical activity, while lower fatigue and chest pain were linked to higher daily step counts, but no intervention was administered to participants.
paper_authors: Antonio Sarmento; Sandra Webber; Shelley Sargent; Brenda Tittlemier; Diana C. Sanchez-Ramirez
paper_title: Relationship between post-COVID-19 symptoms and daily physical activity

summary: A prospective multicenter study of 272 severe COVID-19 survivors examining the prevalence and factors associated with xerostomia (dry mouth). Found xerostomia in 20.6% of patients, with asthma/COPD, palpitations, and chest pain as independent risk factors.
paper_authors: Paola Andrea Escobar Villegas; Brayan Daniel Cordoba-Melo; Juan Pablo Arango-Ibanez; Maria Camila Naranjo-Ramirez; Mario Miguel Barbosa; Andrés Felipe Casanova Rojas; Andrés Fernando Mina Sánchez; Cesar José Herrera; Miguel Ángel Quintana Da Silva; Andrés Felipe Buitrago Sandoval; María Lorena Coronel Gilio; Freddy Pow Chon Long; Liliana Cárdenas Aldaz; Juan Esteban Gomez-Mesa
paper_title: Xerostomia in survivors of severe COVID-19: findings from a Latin American cohort

summary: This prospective observational study tracked 166 COVID-19 hospitalization survivors over 12 months to evaluate symptom dynamics and predict long COVID persistence using survey-based assessments and machine learning. While it demonstrates that symptom scales at 3 months can predict 12-month long COVID persistence with 91% accuracy, it is a purely observational natural history study with no treatment or intervention provided to participants.
paper_authors: Oleksii Honchar; Tetiana Ashcheulova; Alla Bobeiko; Viktor Blazhko; Eduard Khodosh; Nataliia Matiash; Vladyslav Syrota
paper_title: 12-Month trajectories of physical and mental symptom scores after COVID-19 hospitalization and their role in predicting “very long” COVID

summary: A 4-month prospective cohort study of 2,471 Chinese participants examining changes in frailty after COVID-19 infection using interrupted time series and Cox regression analysis. The study found increased frailty post-pandemic and identified lifestyle factors (mood, physical activity, diet) associated with frailty reduction, but does not test a specific intervention—it is an observational study of natural health trajectories and associations with behavioral factors rather than a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Guihua Li; Yue Zhao; Wenhui Gu; Qianqian Wang; Xinyi Lu; Xinlei Miao
paper_title: The problem of frailty caused by acute infection and future health management strategies to improve frailty

summary: This prospective cohort study assessed physical activity levels and their association with persistent COVID-19 symptoms in 64 non-hospitalized survivors at 8.5 months and 43 participants at 4.25 years post-infection. COVID-19 survivors with persistent symptoms showed significantly lower physical activity levels and daily steps compared to those without symptoms, though activity rebounded to pre-pandemic levels by 4 years.
paper_authors: Lauren E. Opielinski; Toni D. Uhrich; Michael H. Haischer; Rachel N. Beilfuss; Lindsey M. Mirkes Clark; Kamryn M. Kroner; Rachel E. Bollaert; Michael J. Danduran; Linda B. Piacentine; Marie Hoeger Bement; Paula E. Papanek; Sandra K. Hunter
paper_title: COVID-19 and the impact of physical activity on persistent symptoms
paper_journal: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living

summary: This cross-sectional study compared physical capacities and health outcomes in 120 individuals with Long COVID, 120 with short COVID, and 120 controls without COVID history. While the study provides valuable descriptive data on physical impairments, pain, fatigue, and quality of life in Long COVID patients, it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention and therefore does not meet criteria as a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Imane Salmam; Kadija Perreault; Krista L. Best; Imane Zahouani; Gilles Drouin; Jean Tittley; François Desmeules; Alexandre Campeau-Lecours; Simon Beaulieu-Bonneau; Jean-Sébastien Paquette; Simon Deslauriers; Sarah-Maude Brouillard; Katherine Lepage; Jean-Sébastien Roy
paper_title: Physical impairments in individuals with Long COVID
paper_journal: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living

summary: This prospective cohort study examines COVID-19's short- and long-term effects on male reproductive hormones and semen parameters in 48 patients (30 asymptomatic, 18 symptomatic) followed for 6 months post-infection. While the paper documents temporary testosterone changes during acute infection recovery, it does not focus on long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-to-months post-infection) and is primarily about acute reproductive effects rather than treating long COVID complications.
paper_authors: Ahmad Majzoub; Kareim Khalafalla; Mohamed Arafa; Walid El Ansari; Arun Nair; Ahmad Al Bishawi; Mulham Saleh; Mohamed Khair Ella; Haitham ElBardisi; Muhammad Abu Khattab; Khalid AlRumaihi
paper_title: COVID-19 and male fertility: short- and long-term impacts of asymptomatic vs. symptomatic infection on male reproductive potential

summary: Cross-sectional study examining cardiac abnormalities in 150 previously healthy outpatients with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome 4-12 weeks after mild/moderate infection using echocardiography. Found cardiac abnormalities in 25.33% of patients, with significant correlations between symptom severity and cardiac dysfunction metrics.
paper_authors: Cristina Tudoran; Mariana Tudoran; Gheorghe Nicusor Pop; Catalina Giurgi-Oncu; Talida Georgiana Cut; Voichita Elena Lazureanu; Cristian Oancea; Florina Parv; Tudor Ciocarlie; Felix Bende
paper_title: Associations between the Severity of the Post-Acute COVID-19 Syndrome and Echocardiographic Abnormalities in Previously Healthy Outpatients Following Infection with SARS-CoV-2

summary: This study examines the relationship between Mediterranean diet adherence and inflammatory/oxidative stress markers in long-COVID patients, comparing low and high adherence groups (n=188 total). High MD adherence was associated with reduced LDH, LDL-cholesterol, and glucose levels, with gut microbiota composition (specifically Oscillibacter abundance) mediating these effects.
paper_authors: Cuevas-Sierra A.; de la O. V.; Higuera-Gómez A.; Chero-Sandoval L.; de Cuevillas B.; Martínez-Urbistondo M.; Moreno-Torres V.; Pintos-Pascual I.; Castejón R.; Martínez JA
paper_title: Mediterranean Diet and Olive Oil Redox Interactions on Lactate Dehydrogenase Mediated by Gut Oscillibacter in Patients with Long-COVID-19 Syndrome

summary: This paper uses National COVID Cohort Collaborative (N3C) EHR data to create a balanced cohort of long COVID and non-long COVID patients and analyzes whether documented long COVID is associated with decreased survival length using Bayesian survival analysis. It is a secondary analysis of existing EHR data rather than an original treatment intervention study.
paper_authors: Sihang Jiang; Johanna Loomba; Andrea Zhou; Suchetha Sharma; Saurav Sengupta; Jiebei Liu; Donald Brown
paper_title: A Bayesian Survival Analysis on Long COVID and Non-Long COVID Patients: A Cohort Study Using National COVID Cohort Collaborative (N3C) Data

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining long COVID risk factors and outcomes among solid organ transplant recipients, comparing graft failure and mortality rates between those with and without long COVID diagnosis. Found that long COVID was not significantly associated with death or graft failure in this transplant population, though relationships varied by transplant type.
paper_authors: Micaela N. Sandoval; Linda W. Moore; Howard J. Huang; Edward A. Graviss
paper_title: Long COVID risk factors and outcomes among solid organ transplant recipients: a retrospective cohort study

summary: This retrospective cohort study evaluated the effects of a multicomponent exercise program (Vivifrail) on frailty and physical function in older adults with post-COVID-19 syndrome who had been admitted to intensive care units. The intervention produced statistically significant improvements across multiple measures of frailty, muscle strength, balance, gait, and functional independence.
paper_authors: Juan Nicolás Cuenca-Zaldivar; Álvaro Monroy Acevedo; Josué Fernández-Carnero; Eleuterio A. Sánchez-Romero; Jorge Hugo Villafañe; Carlos Barragán Carballar
paper_title: Effects of a Multicomponent Exercise Program on Improving Frailty in Post-COVID-19 Older Adults after Intensive Care Units: A Single-Group Retrospective Cohort Study

summary: This cross-sectional study compared cardiac function via echocardiography in 112 long COVID patients with diabetes/metabolic syndrome versus 91 controls without metabolic dysfunction. Patients with metabolic disorders showed significantly higher rates of left/right ventricular dysfunction and diastolic dysfunction, with predictive associations between inflammatory markers and cardiac abnormalities at 6-month follow-up.
paper_authors: Cristina Tudoran; Renata Bende; Felix Bende; Catalina Giurgi-Oncu; Alexandra Enache; Raluca Dumache; Mariana Tudoran
paper_title: Connections between Diabetes Mellitus and Metabolic Syndrome and the Outcome of Cardiac Dysfunctions Diagnosed during the Recovery from COVID-19 in Patients without a Previous History of Cardiovascular Diseases

summary: This cohort study describes COVID-19 patients hospitalized during acute infection in France, examining referral patterns to rehabilitation units post-hospitalization. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 hospitalization and post-acute rehabilitation needs, not on long COVID as a distinct chronic condition months after infection.
paper_authors: Amandine Rapin; Peter-Joe Noujaim; Redha Taiar; Sandy Carazo-Mendez; Gaetan Deslee; Damien Jolly; François Constant Boyer
paper_title: Characteristics of COVID-19 Inpatients in Rehabilitation Units during the First Pandemic Wave: A Cohort Study from a Large Hospital in Champagne Region

summary: This cross-sectional study compared left and right ventricular strain using echocardiography in 184 post-COVID patients versus 106 matched controls without COVID-19 history. The study found significantly reduced ventricular strain in recovered COVID-19 patients correlating with reduced exercise capacity, but did not test any specific treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Or Shimoni; Roman Korenfeld; Sorel Goland; Valery Meledin; Dan Haberman; Jacob George; Sara Shimoni
paper_title: Subclinical Myocardial Dysfunction in Patients Recovered from COVID-19 Disease: Correlation with Exercise Capacity

summary: This CT imaging study compared thymic appearance in 102 COVID-19 patients with and without pulmonary sequelae at 3-month follow-up. Thymic involution was associated with a 9.3-fold increased odds of pulmonary sequelae, suggesting thymic reactivation may protect against long-term COVID outcomes.
paper_authors: Michaela Cellina; Maurizio Cè; Andrea Cozzi; Simone Schiaffino; Deborah Fazzini; Enzo Grossi; Giancarlo Oliva; Sergio Papa; Marco Alì
paper_title: Thymic Hyperplasia and COVID-19 Pulmonary Sequelae: A Bicentric CT-Based Follow-Up Study

summary: This study evaluates plasma levels of matrix metalloproteinases (MMP-2, MMP-9) and TIMP-1 in acute COVID-19 patients at hospital admission and 3 months post-discharge, stratified by ARDS severity. It does not study long COVID patients or any treatment interventions, focusing instead on biomarkers of acute-phase disease and recovery.
paper_authors: Maria Antonella Zingaropoli; Tiziana Latronico; Patrizia Pasculli; Giorgio Maria Masci; Roberta Merz; Federica Ciccone; Federica Dominelli; Cosmo Del Borgo; Miriam Lichtner; Franco Iafrate; Gioacchino Galardo; Francesco Pugliese; Valeria Panebianco; Paolo Ricci; Carlo Catalano; Maria Rosa Ciardi; Grazia Maria Liuzzi; Claudio Maria Mastroianni
paper_title: Tissue Inhibitor of Matrix Metalloproteinases-1 (TIMP-1) and Pulmonary Involvement in COVID-19 Pneumonia

summary: This retrospective cohort study evaluates hs-TnI and sST-2 biomarkers as predictors of major cardiovascular events (MACE) in 251 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors during ~415-day follow-up. While relevant to long COVID sequelae, it is a secondary analysis of existing biomarker data rather than an intervention trial.
paper_authors: Lukas Fiedler; Lukas J. Motloch; Peter Jirak; Ruslan Gumerov; Paruir Davtyan; Diana Gareeva; Irina Lakman; Alexandr Tataurov; Gulnaz Lasinova; Valentin Pavlov; Laurenz Hauptmann; Kristen Kopp; Uta C. Hoppe; Michael Lichtenauer; Rudin Pistulli; Anna-Maria Dieplinger; Naufal Zagidullin
paper_title: Investigation of hs-TnI and sST-2 as Potential Predictors of Long-Term Cardiovascular Risk in Patients with Survived Hospitalization for COVID-19 Pneumonia

summary: This retrospective observational study compared neuropsychological performance in 226 younger and older COVID-19 survivors at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months post-infection using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment. The findings suggest COVID-19 survivors experience cognitive deficits characterized by attention/concentration difficulties affecting memory retrieval processes, consistent with post-COVID 'brain fog' symptoms.
paper_authors: Maria Devita; Adele Ravelli; Anna Panzeri; Elisa Di Rosa; Pamela Iannizzi; Gioia Bottesi; Chiara Ceolin; Marina De Rui; Annamaria Cattelan; Silvia Cavinato; Chiara Begliomini; Biancarosa Volpe; Rossana Schiavo; Marta Ghisi; Daniela Mapelli
paper_title: Deep into Cognition: The Neuropsychological Identikit of Younger and Older Individuals after COVID-19 Infection

summary: This cross-sectional study examines factors contributing to persistent exercise intolerance in 120 long COVID patients 3-6 months post-infection with normal left ventricular function. The authors identify that male gender and specific cardiac/hydration parameters (late diastolic filling velocity, TAPSE, global peak systolic strain) are independently associated with reduced oxygen uptake at peak exercise.
paper_authors: Katarzyna Gryglewska-Wawrzak; Agata Sakowicz; Maciej Banach; Marek Maciejewski; Agata Bielecka-Dabrowa
paper_title: Factors of Persistent Limited Exercise Tolerance in Patients after COVID-19 with Normal Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction

summary: This observational study examined the prevalence and evolution of diastolic dysfunction in 203 post-COVID-19 patients with and without obesity/metabolic syndrome, using transthoracic echocardiography at baseline and 6-month follow-up. While it demonstrates cardiovascular complications in long COVID, it is observational and descriptive with no intervention tested or evaluated.
paper_authors: Cristina Tudoran; Mariana Tudoran; Talida Georgiana Cut; Voichita Elena Lazureanu; Felix Bende; Renata Fofiu; Alexandra Enache; Silvius Alexandru Pescariu; Dorin Novacescu
paper_title: The Impact of Metabolic Syndrome and Obesity on the Evolution of Diastolic Dysfunction in Apparently Healthy Patients Suffering from Post-COVID-19 Syndrome

summary: Retrospective cohort and cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of long COVID-19 symptoms (34% at 2 years post-infection) and their association with anxiety and depression among 1,038 healthcare workers. The study found significant associations between acute-phase and long COVID symptoms and mental health outcomes, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Jingli Wen; Ling Yuan; Lin Zhang; Liang Li; Junyi Chen; Zhenjiang Zhang; Youde Yan
paper_title: Distribution of acute symptoms and long COVID-19 and their association with anxiety and depression 2 years after infection

summary: Multicenter prospective cohort study following 1,266 previously hospitalized COVID-19 survivors at four timepoints (8-18 months post-discharge) to track the trajectory of self-reported fatigue and dyspnoea symptoms. Found that fatigue prevalence decreased from 56.94% to 42.66% and dyspnoea from 28.71% to 12.04% over follow-up, with female sex identified as a risk factor for persistent symptoms.
paper_authors: César Fernández-de-las-Peñas; Ignacio Cancela-Cilleruelo; Jorge Rodríguez-Jiménez; Stella Fuensalida-Novo; José D. Martín-Guerrero; Oscar J. Pellicer-Valero; Ana I. de-la-Llave-Rincón
paper_title: Trajectory of Post-COVID Self-Reported Fatigue and Dyspnoea in Individuals Who Had Been Hospitalized by COVID-19: The LONG-COVID-EXP Multicenter Study

summary: A prospective longitudinal study of 106 older patients (≥65 years) who recovered from COVID-19, assessing body composition, muscle strength, and sarcopenia prevalence at 3 and 12 months post-infection. The study found high sarcopenia at 3 months that improved by 12 months alongside functional and symptomatic recovery, without significant changes in lean mass.
paper_authors: Almudena López-Sampalo; Lidia Cobos-Palacios; Alberto Vilches-Pérez; Jaime Sanz-Cánovas; Antonio Vargas-Candela; Juan José Mancebo-Sevilla; Halbert Hernández-Negrín; Ricardo Gómez-Huelgas; María Rosa Bernal-López
paper_title: COVID-19 in Older Patients: Assessment of Post-COVID-19 Sarcopenia

summary: This cross-sectional study examined arterial and aortic stiffness and diastolic dysfunction in 121 women with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (with and without metabolic syndrome) compared to 40 healthy controls using echocardiography and pulse-wave velocity measurements. Patients with concurrent metabolic syndrome showed worse cardiovascular parameters, with aortic stiffness, C-reactive protein, and triglyceride-glucose index identified as independent predictors of diastolic dysfunction.
paper_authors: Cristina Tudoran; Felix Bende; Renata Bende; Catalina Giurgi-Oncu; Raluca Dumache; Mariana Tudoran
paper_title: Correspondence between Aortic and Arterial Stiffness, and Diastolic Dysfunction in Apparently Healthy Female Patients with Post-Acute COVID-19 Syndrome

summary: This prospective study examined radiological pulmonary changes in 54 critically ill COVID-19 patients treated with mechanical ventilation, comparing intubation methods at 6-month follow-up. The paper focuses on acute respiratory failure during active infection rather than long COVID sequelae, and does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Mircea Stoian; Adina Roman; Alina Boeriu; Danusia Onișor; Sergio Rareș Bandila; Dragoș Florin Babă; Iuliu Cocuz; Raluca Niculescu; Anamaria Costan; Sergiu Ștefan Laszlo; Dragoș Corău; Adina Stoian
paper_title: Long-Term Radiological Pulmonary Changes in Mechanically Ventilated Patients with Respiratory Failure due to SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: Prospective case series of 278 PASC-CVS patients receiving guideline-oriented medical therapy (NSAIDs for pericardial effusion, heart failure medications for cardiac dysfunction). Three-month follow-up imaging in 82 patients showed significant improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction and reduction in pericardial effusion, with clinical symptom improvement.
paper_authors: Mariann Gyöngyösi; Ena Hasimbegovic; Emilie Han; Katrin Zlabinger; Andreas Spannbauer; Martin Riesenhuber; Kevin Hamzaraj; Jutta Bergler-Klein; Christian Hengstenberg; Andreas Kammerlander; Stefan Kastl; Christian Loewe; Dietrich Beitzke
paper_title: Improvement of Symptoms and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Abnormalities in Patients with Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Cardiovascular Syndrome (PASC-CVS) after Guideline-Oriented Therapy

summary: This retrospective cohort study compares hospitalized COVID-19 patients with and without type 2 diabetes, analyzing in-hospital mortality and cardiovascular endpoints at 10-month follow-up. The study focuses on acute COVID-19 outcomes and comorbidity effects rather than long COVID symptoms or treatments.
paper_authors: Zemfira Khamidullina; Diana Avzaletdinova; Diana Gareeva; Tatyana Morugova; Irina Lakman; Kristen Kopp; Lukas Fiedler; Lukas J. Motloch; Naufal Zagidullin
paper_title: Long-Term Outcomes of COVID-19 in Hospitalized Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Patients

summary: This cross-sectional study compares clinical features and pulmonary involvement in 282 post-COVID patients assessed up to 12 weeks after acute COVID-19 recovery. Patients with pulmonary involvement showed distinct characteristics including older age, higher hospitalization rates, and significantly impaired pulmonary function, suggesting pulmonary involvement represents a distinct phenotype requiring individualized clinical approaches.
paper_authors: Krystian T. Bartczak; Joanna Miłkowska-Dymanowska; Małgorzata Pietrusińska; Anna Kumor-Kisielewska; Adam Stańczyk; Sebastian Majewski; Wojciech J. Piotrowski; Cezary Lipiński; Sebastian Wawrocki; Adam J. Białas
paper_title: Is Pulmonary Involvement a Distinct Phenotype of Post-COVID-19?

summary: This observational cohort study evaluated muscle loss and functional status in 16 COVID-19 pneumonia patients during hospitalization and at follow-up points up to 6 months post-discharge. The study found significant reductions in muscle mass, handgrip strength, and quality of life that persisted 6 months after discharge, but did not test any specific intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Otakar Psenicka; Tomas Brutvan; Jan Kratky; Jarmila Krizova
paper_title: Muscle Dysfunction and Functional Status in COVID-19 Patients during Illness and after Hospital Discharge

summary: This prospective cross-sectional study compared immune cell profiles and pituitary-adrenal axis function in 29 long COVID patients versus 13 recovered controls at 6+ months post-infection. The study found dysregulation in certain immune cells and immune activation but no significant adrenal dysfunction or association between cortisol levels and clinical symptoms.
paper_authors: Jaume Alijotas-Reig; Ariadna Anunciacion-Llunell; Enrique Esteve-Valverde; Stephanie Morales-Pérez; Sergio Rivero-Santana; Jaume Trapé; Laura González-García; Domingo Ruiz; Joana Marques-Soares; Francesc Miro-Mur
paper_title: Pituitary–Adrenal Axis and Peripheral Immune Cell Profile in Long COVID

summary: This cross-sectional study compared kidney function tests six months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection between patients with Post-COVID Syndrome (n=92) and controls (n=114). Post-COVID patients showed significantly elevated serum creatinine, reduced eGFR, and higher albuminuria, indicating persistent renal impairment that the authors argue requires ongoing monitoring and intervention strategies.
paper_authors: Madalina Boruga; Susa Septimiu-Radu; Prashant Sunil Nandarge; Ahmed Elagez; Gabriela Doros; Voichita Elena Lazureanu; Emil Robert Stoicescu; Elena Tanase; Roxana Iacob; Andreea Dumitrescu; Adrian Vasile Bota; Coralia Cotoraci; Melania Lavinia Bratu
paper_title: Kidney Function Tests and Continuous eGFR Decrease at Six Months after SARS-CoV-2 Infection in Patients Clinically Diagnosed with Post-COVID Syndrome

summary: Prospective single-center study following 46 COVID-19 hospitalization survivors at 3 and 9 months post-discharge to assess persistent symptoms and health-related quality of life using the EQ-5D-5L questionnaire. Identified fatigue as the most common persistent symptom, with 80-82% of patients reporting impaired HRQoL in at least one domain, particularly pain/discomfort.
paper_authors: Ewa Pietruszka-Wałęka; Michał Rząd; Renata Rożyńska; Piotr Miklusz; Emilia Zieniuk-Lesiak; Magdalena Żabicka; Karina Jahnz-Różyk
paper_title: Quality of Life in Follow-Up up to 9 Months after COVID-19 Hospitalization among the Polish Population—A Prospective Single Center Study

summary: A 12-month longitudinal study of 47 COVID-19 patients examining body composition changes and cytokine production in relation to insulin resistance (HOMA-IR). Patients with elevated HOMA-IR showed increased body fat, decreased lean mass, and altered cytokine profiles suggesting immune dysfunction and chronic inflammation.
paper_authors: Rona Kartika; Imam Subekti; Farid Kurniawan; Syahidatul Wafa; Tika Pradnjaparamita; Dicky L. Tahapary; Heri Wibowo
paper_title: Altered Body Composition and Cytokine Production in Patients with Elevated HOMA-IR after SARS-CoV-2 Infection: A 12-Month Longitudinal Study

summary: A prospective cohort study examining hemoglobin levels and their relationship with fatigue in 95 long-COVID patients 3-6 months post-infection. While the study finds hemoglobin increase associated with lower fatigue odds, it is observational without any intervention or treatment—patients are followed passively without receiving a specific therapy.
paper_authors: Somayeh Bazdar; Lizan D. Bloemsma; Nadia Baalbaki; Jelle M. Blankestijn; Merel E. B. Cornelissen; Rosanne J. H. C. G. Beijers; Brigitte M. Sondermeijer; Yolanda van Wijck; George S. Downward; Anke H. Maitland-van der Zee
paper_title: Hemoglobin and Its Relationship with Fatigue in Long-COVID Patients Three to Six Months after SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: Prospective cohort study following CKD and non-CKD patients for three years post-COVID-19 infection to examine long-term PASC outcomes and the impact of RAAS-blocker therapy. Results showed no permanent renal function changes and most patients recovered from PASC symptoms within a short period, though some required prolonged management.
paper_authors: Rumen Filev; Mila Lyubomirova; Boris Bogov; Krassimir Kalinov; Julieta Hristova; Dobrin Svinarov; Alexander Garev; Lionel Rostaing
paper_title: Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Infection (PASC) for Patients—3-Year Follow-Up of Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease

summary: Longitudinal descriptive study analyzing pharmacotherapy patterns in 95 long COVID patients across pre-COVID, acute, and post-COVID phases. Pre-COVID medication history is explored as a potential health status indicator for characterizing patients, but no treatment intervention is tested or evaluated.
paper_authors: Nadia Baalbaki; Sien T. Verbeek; Harm Jan Bogaard; Jelle M. Blankestijn; Vera C. van den Brink; Merel E. B. Cornelissen; Jos W. R. Twisk; Korneliusz Golebski; Anke H. Maitland-van der Zee
paper_title: Pharmacotherapy from Pre-COVID to Post-COVID: Longitudinal Trends and Predictive Indicators for Long COVID Symptoms

summary: Prospective observational cohort study of 88 long COVID patients (aged 40-65) followed monthly over 12-18 months to identify symptom progression trajectories for fatigue and dyspnea. Identified three distinct trajectories (decreasing, high persistent, low persistent) and found that lifestyle intervention participation, smoking status, sex, age, and COVID-19 severity were associated with symptom progression patterns.
paper_authors: Merel E. B. Cornelissen; Myrthe M. Haarman; Jos W. R. Twisk; Laura Houweling; Nadia Baalbaki; Brigitte Sondermeijer; Rosanne J. H. C. G. Beijers; Debbie Gach; Lizan D. Bloemsma; Anke H. Maitland-van der Zee
paper_title: The Progression of Symptoms in Post COVID-19 Patients: A Multicentre, Prospective, Observational Cohort Study

summary: This study implements a novel remote patient monitoring system to track symptom intensity changes over 15 days in 133 COVID-19 survivors and post-COVID syndrome patients across four recovery groups. The analysis reveals distinct symptom profiles among groups, with shortness of breath, fatigue, cough, headache, and body pain being most prevalent, providing insights for personalized care strategies.
paper_authors: Eduarda Martins de Faria; Cíntia Moraes de Sá Sousa; Caroline de Oliveira Ribeiro; Márcio Neves Bóia; Agnaldo José Lopes; Pedro Lopes de Melo
paper_title: Longitudinal Symptom Analysis of COVID-19 Survivors and Post-COVID Syndrome Patients

summary: This multinational retrospective cohort study investigates mortality risk in 651 acute COVID-19 survivors followed until December 2023, with comparison to age- and sex-matched COVID-negative controls. The authors identify 201 urinary peptides associated with post-acute mortality and develop a peptide-based classifier (DP201) that predicts death risk in post-acute COVID-19 patients, demonstrating that SARS-CoV-2 infection significantly increases mortality risk for approximately one year post-infection.
paper_authors: Justyna Siwy; Felix Keller; Mirosław Banasik; Björn Peters; Emmanuel Dudoignon; Alexandre Mebazaa; Dilara Gülmez; Goce Spasovski; Mercedes Salgueira Lazo; Marek W. Rajzer; Łukasz Fuławka; Magdalena Dzitkowska-Zabielska; Harald Mischak; Manfred Hecking; Joachim Beige; Ralph Wendt
paper_title: Mortality Risk and Urinary Proteome Changes in Acute COVID-19 Survivors in the Multinational CRIT-COV-U Study

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 244 COVID-19 hospitalized patients followed at a post-COVID clinic, comparing 110 patients who developed PASC with 134 who did not. Identifies female gender, type 2 diabetes, and acute COVID symptoms as risk factors for PASC development and prognostic markers for symptom evolution.
paper_authors: Mariantonietta Pisaturo; Antonio Russo; Pierantonio Grimaldi; Caterina Monari; Simona Imbriani; Klodian Gjeloshi; Carmen Ricozzi; Roberta Astorri; Caterina Curatolo; Roberta Palladino; Francesco Caruso; Francesca Ambrisi; Lorenzo Onorato; Nicola Coppola
paper_title: Prevalence, Evolution and Prognostic Factors of PASC in a Cohort of Patients Discharged from a COVID Unit

summary: This retrospective observational study compared vitamin D and electrolyte levels in 406 hospitalized children with post-COVID-19 status versus SARS-CoV-2/EBV coinfection. While it examines post-COVID children, it is primarily an observational descriptive study of biochemical markers in acute/recent infection rather than a long COVID intervention trial.
paper_authors: Carmen Loredana Petrea (Cliveți); Diana-Andreea Ciortea; Gabriela Gurău; Nicoleta Mădălina Matei; Ciprian Adrian Dinu; Simona-Elena Bergheș (Oprea); Gabriela Isabela Verga (Răuță); Sorin Ion Berbece
paper_title: Vitamin D Imbalance and Hydro-Electrolyte Disturbances in Hospitalized Children: A Comparation Between Post-COVID-19 Status and SARS-CoV-2/EBV Coinfection

summary: This three-year follow-up study assessed 192 post-COVID patients using fatigue questionnaires and cardiopulmonary exercise testing to evaluate physical capacity and aerobic fitness. The study found that 24% of the population still exhibited persistent long-COVID syndrome with reduced cardiorespiratory fitness and increased symptom burden, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Radostina Cherneva; Zheyna Cherneva; Vania Youroukova; Tanya Kadiyska; Dinko Valev; Ebru Myuyun Hayrula-Manaf; Vanyo Mitev
paper_title: Cardio-Respiratory Fitness and Fatigue in Post-COVID-19 Syndrome—A Three-Year Update

summary: This study investigated the occurrence of antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) in 100 severe COVID-19 patients with pneumonia and thrombosis, testing for aPLs at multiple time points during hospitalization and 3-month follow-up. While the paper connects APS findings to post-COVID syndrome pathophysiology, it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention—it is purely a diagnostic/observational study examining aPLs prevalence and patterns.
paper_authors: Mirjana Zlatković-Švenda; Melanija Rašić; Milica Ovuka; Slavica Pavlov-Dolijanović; Marija Atanasković Popović; Manca Ogrič; Polona Žigon; Snežna Sodin-Šemrl; Marija Zdravković; Goran Radunović
paper_title: The New Occurrence of Antiphospholipid Syndrome in Severe COVID-19 Cases with Pneumonia and Vascular Thrombosis Could Explain the Post-COVID Syndrome

summary: Retrospective cohort study using TriNetX data examining herpes zoster reactivation following COVID-19 and its association with renal, infectious, and autoimmune complications. Propensity-matched analysis found HZ after COVID-19 significantly increased risks of MAKE, sepsis, SLE, and RA over three-year follow-up.
paper_authors: Ming-Hung Chien; Joshua Wang; Kuo-Cheng Lu; Chien-Lin Lu
paper_title: Herpes Zoster Reactivation Following COVID-19 and the Risk of Renal, Infectious, and Autoimmune Complications: A Global Propensity-Matched Cohort Study

summary: This repeated cross-sectional study examined long-term health and cognitive effects of COVID-19 in 584 university students up to four years post-infection, assessing how variants, vaccination status, and illness severity impact outcomes. Results showed persistent fatigue and memory impairments, particularly in women and men respectively, with the ancestral variant having the greatest long-term impact and Omicron the least.

summary: Observational comparison study examining the prevalence and characteristics of persistent symptoms one year after hospitalization in children with acute COVID-19 versus non-COVID-19 conditions. Found no significant difference in persistent symptom rates between groups (34% vs 37%), classifying this as a descriptive epidemiological study rather than a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Marta Conde; Irati Gastesi; Lucía de Pablo; Sara Villanueva-Medina; David Aguilera-Alonso; Ana Esteban; Cristina Epalza; María López; Sara Domínguez-Rodríguez; Pablo Gómez; Álvaro Ballesteros; Carlota Pinto; Marisa Navarro; Carlo Giaquinto; Cinta Moraleda; Alfredo Tagarro
paper_title: Persistent Symptoms (Lasting Longer than 1 Year) in Children Hospitalized with Acute COVID-19 Versus Other Conditions

summary: This retrospective cohort study compares echocardiographic findings in 22 children with MIS-C and 22 healthy controls at baseline and 1-year follow-up. While the paper studies post-COVID cardiac sequelae, it focuses on MIS-C (multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children) rather than long COVID as defined in the screening criteria, and contains no intervention/treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Jihye You
paper_title: Echocardiographic Strain Evaluation Shows Persistent Echocardiographic Changes at 1 Year after Diagnosis of Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children

summary: Prospective cohort study of 97 adolescents with long-COVID, evaluating symptom prevalence, clustering, and persistence over a mean 340-day follow-up. Found that fatigue (62.9%) and dyspnea (43.3%) were most common, with 45.3% still symptomatic at final follow-up, and polisymptomaticity predicting longer persistence.
paper_authors: Marco Floridia; Danilo Buonsenso; Laura Macculi; Liliana Elena Weimer; Marina Giuliano; Flavia Pricci; Leila Bianchi; Domenico Maurizio Toraldo; Graziano Onder
paper_title: Adolescents with Persistent Symptoms Following Acute SARS-CoV-2 Infection (Long-COVID): Symptom Profile, Clustering and Follow-Up Symptom Evaluation

summary: This longitudinal study followed 168 COVID-19 hospitalized patients for 6 months post-discharge to assess the onset of mental disorders using standardized questionnaires. While it documents a high incidence (57.34%) of common mental disorders in post-COVID patients, it is an observational study without any treatment or intervention being tested.
paper_authors: Jaime Chamorro-Delmo; Pablo Portillo De-Antonio; Alejandro Porras-Segovia; Santiago de León-Martínez; Marta Figuero Oltra; Pablo del Pozo-Herce; Adela Sánchez-Escribano Martínez; Irene Abejón Pérez; Constanza Vera-Varela; Teodor T. Postolache; Olatz Lopez-Fernandez; Enrique Baca-Garcia
paper_title: Onset of Mental Disorders Following Hospitalization for COVID-19: A 6-Month Follow-Up Study

summary: This cross-sectional study compared peripheral and central auditory function in 23 children/adolescents who had recovered from COVID-19 versus 23 pre-pandemic controls with normal hearing. The COVID-19 group showed significant auditory impairments including worse hearing thresholds at standard and high frequencies, absent otoacoustic emissions, longer brainstem auditory evoked potential latencies, and poorer central auditory processing performance.
paper_authors: Julia Siqueira; Milaine Dominici Sanfins; Piotr Henryk Skarzynski; Magdalena Beata Skarzynska; Maria Francisca Colella-Santos
paper_title: Evaluation of the Peripheral and Central Auditory Systems in Children and Adolescents Before and After COVID-19 Infection

summary: Prospective observational study evaluating pulmonary function in children aged 6-18 years at ~10 months after asymptomatic or mild COVID-19 infection. Found no respiratory symptoms, abnormal lung function, or need for therapy in any of the 61 participants, indicating that mild infection in children does not lead to chronic respiratory impairment.
paper_authors: Costanza Di Chiara; Silvia Carraro; Stefania Zanconato; Sandra Cozzani; Eugenio Baraldi; Carlo Giaquinto; Valentina Agnese Ferraro; Daniele Donà
paper_title: Preliminary Evidence on Pulmonary Function after Asymptomatic and Mild COVID-19 in Children

summary: This retrospective cohort study of 17 ICU survivors evaluated psychosomatic, respiratory, and neurocognitive outcomes 12 months after discharge, identifying clinical and laboratory predictors of PASC symptoms. The study is primarily observational and prognostic, not an intervention trial, and focuses on identifying risk factors rather than testing a treatment.
paper_authors: Nicolas Germann; Daria Amozova; Kristina Göhl-Freyn; Tim Fischer; Manuel Frischknecht; Gian-Reto Kleger; Urs Pietsch; Miodrag Filipovic; Martin H. Brutsche; Thomas Frauenfelder; Christian R. Kahlert; Dagmar A. Schmid; Werner C. Albrich
paper_title: Evaluation of Psychosomatic, Respiratory, and Neurocognitive Health in COVID-19 Survivors 12 Months after ICU Discharge

summary: This epidemiological study analyzes mortality attributed to post-COVID-19 condition using US National Center for Health Statistics data from 2018–2024. The paper reports 2,653 deaths classified under ICD-10 code U09.9, with higher mortality rates in males, older adults, and individuals who died at home.
paper_authors: Giuseppe Lippi; Fabian Sanchis-Gomar
paper_title: Mortality of Post-COVID-19 Condition: 2025 Update

summary: This epidemiological analysis examines trends in suicide mortality across India from 2019-2022 and explores whether long COVID may have contributed to increases in suicide rates. The study found increased suicide rates post-COVID but found no association with COVID deaths and suggests long COVID may play a potential role.
paper_authors: Karan Varshney; Mansoor Ahmed Panhwar
paper_title: Long COVID as a Possible Contributor to Rising Suicide Mortality in Bharat (India): An Analysis of Suicide Trends Since the Emergence of COVID-19

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining whether antipsychotic and SSRI use in veterans reduces the risk of developing long COVID. Antipsychotics showed 11-43% reduction in long COVID risk depending on age and COVID wave, while SSRIs showed no benefit.
paper_authors: Jerry Bradley; Fei Tang; Dominique Tosi; Natasha Resendes; Iriana S. Hammel
paper_title: The Effects of SSRIs and Antipsychotics on Long COVID Development in a Large Veteran Population

summary: Retrospective chart review of 155 long COVID patients from UConn Health's Long COVID Clinic examining the incidence and impact of neuropsychological symptoms. Study found high prevalence of neuropsychiatric symptoms that did not correlate with brain imaging findings, highlighting symptom burden but not evaluating any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Alexandria N. Plant; Ameer Z. Rasheed; Mira Hasan
paper_title: Long COVID and the Brain: A Retrospective Study of the Neuropsychological Manifestations of Long COVID

summary: Prospective cohort study following 117 hospitalized COVID-19 patients over 18 months post-discharge to assess evolution of mental health, sleep quality, and quality of life. Participants showed gradual recovery over time with substantial improvement by month 6, though complete return to pre-disease baseline was not achieved.
paper_authors: Eleni Tsimitrea; Maria Chatzi; Maria Saridi; Aikaterini Toska; Konstantinos I. Gourgoulianis; Ioanna V. Papathanasiou; Stylianos Boutlas; Evangelos C. Fradelos
paper_title: Variation in Mental Health, Sleep Quality and Quality of Life Following COVID-19 Hospitalization

summary: This prospective follow-up study evaluated the type, frequency, onset, and recovery duration of neurological symptoms in 110 COVID-19 patients at 1, 3, and 6 months post-discharge. Fatigue was the most common symptom (75.5%, lasting 10.43 weeks), followed by myalgia and headache, with forgetfulness persisting longest (22.03 weeks), highlighting the need for systematic neurological monitoring in long COVID.
paper_authors: Mirkan Bulğak; Tuna Demirdal
paper_title: Prospective Follow-Up of Neurological Findings and Recovery Tımes in COVID-19 Patients

summary: This retrospective cohort study compares frailty characteristics between 106 long COVID patients and 97 geriatric patients at a VA Medical Center using the Fried phenotype. Long COVID patients were significantly younger but experienced higher rates of exhaustion and low activity, suggesting long COVID may predispose patients to develop frailty with distinct phenotypic features.
paper_authors: Jerry Bradley; Elizabeth Bast; Natasha M. Resendes; Fei Tang; Victor D. Cevallos; Dominique M. Tosi; Leonardo Tamariz; Ana Palacio; Iriana S. Hammel
paper_title: Long COVID Frailty: A Comparative Analysis in a Veteran Population

summary: This study evaluates temporal changes in sperm parameters and inflammasome markers in men during the first three months following acute COVID-19 infection. Results show gradual recovery in sperm function and decreased TNF-α levels over time, but this is a post-acute observation study focused on male fertility recovery, not long COVID sequelae or treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Bahareh Ghazavi; Bahare Nikoozar; Marziyeh Tavalaee; Mohammad Shojaei; Ensiyeh Kheirollahi Hosseinabadi; Mohammad J. Hayati; Negin Tavakoli; Ali Ajami; Mohammad H. Nasr-Esfahani
paper_title: Temporal Changes in Sperm Function and Inflammasome Activity Following COVID-19: Evidence for Recovery

summary: This cross-sectional study examines myocardial abnormalities using cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging in 94 post-COVID-19 patients with persistent cardiac symptoms (≥3 months post-infection) compared to 100 controls. The study found subclinical myocardial dysfunction (reduced strain parameters) and higher major adverse cardiac event rates in post-COVID patients, but this is an observational characterization study without any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Miltiadis Georgiadis; Nuriye Akyol; Lars Kamper; Nima Nadem-Boueini; Athanasios Ziakos; Patrick Haage; Melchior Seyfarth; Nadine Abanador-Kamper
paper_title: Long-Term Myocardial Involvement and Outcome in the Post-COVID-19 Condition

summary: Comparative study of immunometabolic profiles in 78 patients: 35 with newly diagnosed carbohydrate disorders after COVID-19 (Post-COVID group) and 33 COVID-negative controls with metabolic syndrome. Post-COVID patients showed significantly elevated inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL-17A, IL-10) and worse metabolic control (higher fasting glucose, HbA1c, lipids, uric acid) independent of traditional risk factors, indicating inflammation-driven metabolic dysfunction distinct from classical metabolic syndrome.
paper_authors: Victoria Tsvetkova; Malvina Todorova; Milena Atanasova; Irena Gencheva; Katya Todorova
paper_title: Comparative Characteristics of the Immunometabolic Profile of Individuals with Newly Developed Metabolic Disorders and Classic Metabolic Syndrome

summary: An observational case-control study identifying risk factors associated with post-COVID syndrome in older adults with hypertension. Found that female sex, younger age, lower systolic blood pressure, and rhythm disturbances were independently associated with PCS presence.
paper_authors: Venera Kudabaeva; Timur Tastaibek; Almagul Mansharipova; Arystan Seidalin; Nargiza Nassyrova
paper_title: Factors Associated with the Presence of Post-COVID Syndrome in Older Patients with Arterial Hypertension

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed cognitive function in 297 adults three years post-COVID-19 infection, stratified by disease severity. Findings showed persistent cognitive deficits (attention, memory, executive function) correlated with initial COVID-19 severity and age, but the study does not test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Antonio de Pádua Serafim; Victor Linking Magalhães Campos; Fabiana Saffi; Cristiana Castanho de Almeida Rocca; Ricardo Silva dos Santos Durães
paper_title: Persistence of Cognitive Difficulties in Adults Three Years After COVID-19 Infection

summary: A disease-wide association study using the FinnGen registry to map risk factors and long-term sequelae following influenza and COVID-19, comparing 9,204 influenza and 4,258 COVID-19 patients against 420,005 unexposed controls. The study identifies broad multi-system morbidity signatures extending beyond respiratory tract including cardiovascular, neurological, metabolic, and mental health complications, reframing influenza as a systemic post-viral event analogous to long COVID.
paper_authors: Ming Zheng
paper_title: Longitudinal Landscape of Long Flu and Long COVID

summary: This observational cohort study examined inflammatory and cardiac biomarkers in 978 COVID-19 patients to predict post-acute COVID-19 and 30-day mortality. The study identified NT-pro BNP and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio as predictive biomarkers but did not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Catalina Lionte; Victorita Sorodoc; Raluca Ecaterina Haliga; Cristina Bologa; Alexandr Ceasovschih; Ovidiu Rusalim Petris; Adorata Elena Coman; Alexandra Stoica; Oana Sirbu; Gabriela Puha; Mihai Constantin; Gabriela Dumitrescu; Victoria Gorciac; Andrei-Costin Chelariu; Andreea Nicoleta Catana; Elisabeta Jaba; Laurentiu Sorodoc
paper_title: Inflammatory and Cardiac Biomarkers in Relation with Post-Acute COVID-19 and Mortality: What We Know after Successive Pandemic Waves

summary: This prospective study assessed subclinical cardiac dysfunction in 66 COVID-19 patients at one-year follow-up, comparing those with and without persistent dyspnea using echocardiography. While it identified reduced myocardial performance (GCW and GWI) in dyspneic patients, it is an observational study without any treatment intervention or control group comparison.
paper_authors: Maria-Luiza Luchian; Andreea Motoc; Stijn Lochy; Julien Magne; Dries Belsack; Johan De Mey; Bram Roosens; Karen Van den Bussche; Sven Boeckstaens; Hadischat Chameleva; Jolien Geers; Laura Houard; Tom De Potter; Sabine Allard; Caroline Weytjens; Steven Droogmans; Bernard Cosyns
paper_title: Subclinical Myocardial Dysfunction in Patients with Persistent Dyspnea One Year after COVID-19

summary: This prospective/retrospective cohort study followed 160 COVID-19 patients at 5-month post-discharge to characterize cardiac sequelae, finding RV dilation, pulmonary hypertension, and bi-ventricular dysfunction. RV changes were associated with pneumonia severity and hemodynamic instability, while LV dysfunction correlated with inflammatory markers.
paper_authors: Giovanna Pelà; Matteo Goldoni; Chiara Cavalli; Felice Perrino; Sara Tagliaferri; Annalisa Frizzelli; Pier Anselmo Mori; Maria Majori; Marina Aiello; Nicola Sverzellati; Massimo Corradi; Alfredo Chetta
paper_title: Long-Term Cardiac Sequelae in Patients Referred into a Diagnostic Post-COVID-19 Pathway: The Different Impacts on the Right and Left Ventricles

summary: A case series of 98 COVID-19 patients admitted to inpatient cardiopulmonary rehabilitation, with functional assessments at admission, discharge, and 6-month follow-up. Inpatient rehabilitation resulted in significant improvements in mobility and quality of life, with 86% of patients exhibiting post-COVID-19 symptoms at follow-up, and vaccinated individuals showing fewer symptoms than unvaccinated counterparts.
paper_authors: Amy Comley Steele; Heather McKenna; Amy Teale
paper_title: Functional Recovery of COVID-19 Patients Admitted to a Cardiopulmonary Inpatient Rehabilitation Unit

summary: This retrospective longitudinal study evaluated endocrine disturbances in 96 COVID-19 hospitalized patients at 4-year follow-up, assessing dysglycemia and thyroid autoimmunity prevalence. While it is a long COVID observational study, it lacks a control/comparison group and does not evaluate any intervention or treatment, making it a secondary analysis of existing cohort data rather than a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Ligia Rodina; Vlad Monescu; Lavinia Georgeta Caplan; Maria Elena Cocuz; Victoria Bîrluțiu
paper_title: Long COVID Endocrine and Metabolic Sequelae: Thyroid Autoimmunity and Dysglycemia Four Years After SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: A retrospective study of 16 post-COVID patients who underwent lung ultrasound (LUS) examinations at baseline and follow-up to assess lung residuals. LUS scores showed significant improvement over time, demonstrating reverberation artifacts decreased during rehabilitation, but this is an observational follow-up study with no treatment intervention being tested.
paper_authors: Martin Altersberger; Anna Grafeneder; Yerin Cho; Roland Winkler; Ralf Zwick; Gebhard Mathis; Martin Genger
paper_title: One-Year Follow-Up Lung Ultrasound of Post-COVID Syndrome—A Pilot Study

summary: Retrospective analysis of 764 COVID-19 hospitalized patients from October-December 2020, examining disease severity, hospitalization duration, and post-discharge residual symptoms including fatigue (36%). Study characterizes long COVID symptomatology but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Ramona Cioboata; Dragos Nicolosu; Costin Teodor Streba; Corina Maria Vasile; Madalina Olteanu; Alexandra Nemes; Andreea Gheorghe; Cristina Calarasu; Adina Andreea Turcu
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 Syndrome Based on Disease Form and Associated Comorbidities

summary: This observational study compares long COVID patients who are physically active versus sedentary to examine effects on fatigue, muscle power output, sleep quality, and cognitive function. Active subjects showed 50% greater fatigue reduction at 1 year and less muscle force decline compared to sedentary subjects, suggesting physical activity may mitigate certain long COVID functional impairments.
paper_authors: Francesco Coscia; Rosa Mancinelli; Paola Virginia Gigliotti; Franco Checcaglini; Giorgio Fanò-Illic
paper_title: Physical Activity Effects on Muscle Fatigue in Sport in Active Adults with Long COVID-19: An Observational Study

summary: This observational cross-sectional study assessed 146 COVID-19 survivors with post-COVID pain to identify variables associated with kinesiophobia. The study found that kinesiophobia levels were significantly associated with anxiety, catastrophism, and sensitization-associated symptoms, but did not evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Manuel Herrero-Montes; César Fernández-de-las-Peñas; Diego Ferrer-Pargada; Sheila Izquierdo-Cuervo; Beatriz Abascal-Bolado; Juan Antonio Valera-Calero; Paula Paras-Bravo
paper_title: Association of Kinesiophobia with Catastrophism and Sensitization-Associated Symptoms in COVID-19 Survivors with Post-COVID Pain

summary: Retrospective chart review examining the association between prior SARS-CoV-2 infection or vaccination and acute appendicitis presentation in pediatric patients from January–June 2022. Found a potential positive relationship between COVID-19 infection and subsequent appendicitis, but does not study long COVID or any long COVID treatment.
paper_authors: Christos Kaselas; Maria Florou; Maria Tsopozidi; Ioannis Spyridakis
paper_title: Acute Appendicitis Following COVID-19 Infection in Pediatric Patients: A Single Center’s Study in Greece

summary: This study describes clinical findings from COVID-19 Recovery and Engagement (CORE) Clinics in the Bronx, where COVID-19 survivors underwent comprehensive assessment of physical, emotional, cognitive, and pulmonary function at 5 months post-infection. The authors found dyspnea, fatigue, and brain fog were common, with abnormal lung imaging and moderately restrictive pulmonary function in hospitalized patients, but rare neurological imaging abnormalities.
paper_authors: Anna Eligulashvili; Megan Darrell; Carolyn Miller; Jeylin Lee; Seth Congdon; Jimmy S. Lee; Kevin Hsu; Judy Yee; Wei Hou; Marjan Islam; Tim Q. Duong
paper_title: COVID-19 Patients in the COVID-19 Recovery and Engagement (CORE) Clinics in the Bronx

summary: A prospective cohort study of 635 post-COVID patients that assessed complete radiological remission of COVID-19 pneumonia using HRCT imaging at 90 days post-infection. Found that 25.8% achieved complete radiological remission, with older age and persistent imaging features (ground glass, reticulations, pleural thickening) associated with worse outcomes.
paper_authors: Diana Manolescu; Bogdan Timar; Felix Bratosin; Ovidiu Rosca; Cosmin Citu; Cristian Oancea
paper_title: Predictors for COVID-19 Complete Remission with HRCT Pattern Evolution: A Monocentric, Prospective Study

summary: A longitudinal case series of 17 long COVID patients examining the Adaptive Force (AF) parameter of elbow and hip flexors across three timepoints: pre-treatment, immediately post-treatment, and recovery. The study found that AFisomax increased significantly from ~50% of maximum at baseline to ~99-100% at recovery, correlating with substantial symptom improvement and improved maximal holding capacity.
paper_authors: Laura V. Schaefer; Frank N. Bittmann
paper_title: The Adaptive Force as a Potential Biomechanical Parameter in the Recovery Process of Patients with Long COVID

summary: Prospective observational study of 100 COVID-19 pneumonia patients and 61 controls examining persistent interstitial lung fibrosis after hospital discharge. Identifies risk factors (ESR, CRP, LDH, hospitalization duration) associated with post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Mihai Lazar; Ecaterina Constanta Barbu; Cristina Emilia Chitu; Catalin Tiliscan; Laurentiu Stratan; Sorin Stefan Arama; Victoria Arama; Daniela Adriana Ion
paper_title: Interstitial Lung Fibrosis Following COVID-19 Pneumonia

summary: This case-control study compared dry eye parameters in 44 patients (22 post-COVID, 22 controls) to investigate whether COVID-19 infection worsens dry eye disease. Results show post-COVID patients had significantly reduced lipid layer thickness, worse meibomian gland dysfunction, and shorter tear break-up time, suggesting COVID-19 may exacerbate dry eye as a long-term sequela.
paper_authors: Xulin Liao; Arthur Chun Chi Wong; June Oi Yau Wong; Ruofan Jia; Wanxue Chen; Hanson Yiu Man Wong; Fatema Mohamed Ali Abdulla Aljufairi; Kenneth Ka Hei Lai; Zhichao Hu; Yingying Wei; Clement Chee Yung Tham; Chi Pui Pang; Kelvin Kam Lung Chong
paper_title: Investigating the Impact of COVID-19 Infection on Dry Eye Parameters

summary: Retrospective single-center analysis of 64 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors from the first wave to determine incidence of secondary sclerosing cholangitis (SSC-COVID) and its risk factors. Found 7.8% incidence of SSC-COVID in follow-up patients, all with prolonged ICU stays requiring mechanical ventilation, but no specific treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Christoph R. Werner; Stefano Fusco; Katharina Kienzle; Stefanie Döbele; Kerstin Artzner; Nisar P. Malek; Dörte Wichmann; Siri Göpel
paper_title: Incidence of Secondary Sclerosing Cholangitis in Hospitalized Long COVID-19 Patients: A Retrospective Single Center Study

summary: Retrospective analysis of flow cytometric data comparing lymphocyte populations in 106 post-COVID-19 patients (56 with PCC) versus healthy controls. Found significant reductions in B cell subsets and T helper cells in PCC patients compared to controls, but no specific immune cellular changes unique to PCC versus non-PCC COVID-19 patients.
paper_authors: Luisa Berger; Johannes Wolf; Sven Kalbitz; Nils Kellner; Christoph Lübbert; Stephan Borte
paper_title: Comparative Analysis of Lymphocyte Populations in Post-COVID-19 Condition and COVID-19 Convalescent Individuals

summary: This retrospective cohort study examined cardiac MRI findings in 129 patients referred for evaluation of post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC). The majority (57%) had normal cardiac results, but 30% showed non-ischemic myocardial fibrosis, suggesting a possible history of myocarditis as an explanation for persistent cardiovascular symptoms in PASC patients.
paper_authors: Moritz Halfmann; Julian Luetkens; Isabel Langenbach; Dmitrij Kravchenko; Philip Wenzel; Tilman Emrich; Alexander Isaak
paper_title: Cardiac MRI Findings in Patients Clinically Referred for Evaluation of Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: This study examines the relationship between quantitative CT imaging parameters and pulmonary function tests in COVID-19 patients at 6+ months follow-up. It is an observational study with no treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the clinical trials pipeline despite being long COVID-related research.
paper_authors: Davide Colombi; Marcello Petrini; Camilla Risoli; Angelo Mangia; Gianluca Milanese; Mario Silva; Cosimo Franco; Nicola Sverzellati; Emanuele Michieletti
paper_title: Quantitative CT at Follow-Up of COVID-19 Pneumonia: Relationship with Pulmonary Function Tests

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing long-term health outcomes in 1,074 essential tremor patients with and without prior COVID-19 infection. COVID-19 was associated with increased risk of cardiovascular events, sleep disturbances, fatigue, dyspnea, falls, anxiety, and depression, but not mortality.
paper_authors: Rachel Pakan; Roham Hadidchi; Yousef Al-Ani; Hannah Piskun; Katie S. Duong; Sonya Henry; Stephen Wang; Carine W. Maurer; Tim Q. Duong
paper_title: Long-Term Outcomes of Patients with Pre-Existing Essential Tremor After SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: This prospective population-based study measured serum brain injury biomarkers (sNfL and sGFAP) in 146 individuals before, during, and after SARS-CoV-2 infection to assess association with neurological symptoms and long COVID status. While sGFAP significantly increased in long COVID patients, neither biomarker was associated with specific neurological symptoms, suggesting astroglial activation may occur in long COVID without symptom correlation.
paper_authors: Julia Telser; Kirsten Grossmann; Ornella C. Weideli; Dorothea Hillmann; Stefanie Aeschbacher; Niklas Wohlwend; Laura Velez; Jens Kuhle; Aleksandra Maleska; Pascal Benkert; Corina Risch; David Conen; Martin Risch; Lorenz Risch
paper_title: Concentrations of Serum Brain Injury Biomarkers Following SARS-CoV-2 Infection in Individuals with and without Long-COVID—Results from the Prospective Population-Based COVI-GAPP Study

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 420 patients with severe COVID-19 pneumonia tracking pulmonary fibrosis development at 3 months and 2 years post-hospitalization using CT scans and biomarkers. Found fibrosis in 68% at 3 months declining to 42% at 2 years, identifying risk factors including age, inflammatory markers, and pulmonary involvement patterns.
paper_authors: Mihai Lazar; Ecaterina Constanta Barbu; Cristina Emilia Chitu; Mihaela Buzoianu; Andreea Catalina Petre; Catalin Tiliscan; Stefan Sorin Arama; Victoria Arama; Daniela Adriana Ion; Mihaela Cristina Olariu
paper_title: Surviving COVID-19 and Battling Fibrosis: A Retrospective Cohort Study Across Three Pandemic Waves

summary: This cross-sectional study compared optic disc and retinal microvasculature changes in 40 post-COVID-19 patients versus 40 healthy controls using optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) at baseline, 4 months, and 12 months. The COVID-19 group showed reduced vessel density in multiple retinal regions and increased foveal avascular zone measurements, suggesting ischemic changes, but the study is observational without any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Mine Ozturk; Deniz Kumova Guler; Ekin Ece Oskan; Feyza Onder
paper_title: Long-Term Effects of COVID-19 on Optic Disc and Retinal Microvasculature Assessed by Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography

summary: This prospective cohort study examines the association between prior COVID-19 infection and long-term mortality in chronic kidney disease patients over 24 months, using echocardiographic parameters and survival analysis. While the study involves COVID-19 patients, it focuses on acute complications and mortality in CKD patients rather than long COVID syndrome (persistent post-COVID symptoms), and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Laura Vasiliu; Gianina Dodi; Mihai Onofriescu; Anca Diaconu; Luminita Voroneanu; Radu A. Sascau; Cristian Statescu; Adrian C. Covic
paper_title: The Impact of Prior COVID-19 on Long-Term Mortality and Echocardiographic Predictors in Chronic Kidney Disease Patients

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing incidence of new-onset diabetic retinopathy in type 2 diabetic patients with and without prior COVID-19 infection over 3 years. While the paper studies a post-COVID complication, it does not study a treatment intervention and focuses on acute/short-term disease sequelae in diabetic patients rather than long COVID syndrome itself.
paper_authors: Jai Mehrotra-Varma; Sonya Henry; Diane Chernoff; Andre Galenchik-Chan; Katie S. Duong; Shiv Mehrotra-Varma; Stephen H. Wang; Tim Q. Duong
paper_title: Increased Incidence of New-Onset Diabetic Retinopathy in Individuals with COVID-19 in an Underserved Urban Population in the Bronx

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing long-term kidney outcomes in transplant recipients with and without prior SARS-CoV-2 infection over four years post-infection. Found accelerated eGFR decline in infected patients (males primarily) but this is an observational study documenting sequelae, not evaluating any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Shawn Qiu; Roham Hadidchi; Aditi Vichare; Justin Y. Lu; Wei Hou; Sonya Henry; Enver Akalin; Tim Q. Duong
paper_title: SARS-CoV-2 Infection Is Associated with an Accelerated eGFR Decline in Kidney Transplant Recipients up to Four Years Post Infection

summary: This retrospective cohort study compares pregnancy and childbirth outcomes in 133 women with a history of COVID-19 versus 96 unexposed women, finding significant associations between past COVID-19 infection and adverse outcomes including oligohydramnios and low birth weight. While the study examines long-term consequences of COVID-19 infection, it does not focus on long COVID syndrome (persistent symptoms weeks to months post-infection) but rather on specific perinatal complications in pregnant women with prior infection.
paper_authors: Gaukhar Kurmanova; Ardak Ayazbekov; Almagul Kurmanova; Madina Rakhimbayeva; Gulzhan Trimova; Anarkul Kulembayeva
paper_title: PostCOVID-19 Impact on Perinatal Outcomes

summary: This cross-sectional study examines cardiovascular manifestations in 176 long COVID patients using echocardiography and cardiac MRI, finding significant structural and functional cardiac changes. The study is observational and descriptive in nature, assessing disease characteristics rather than evaluating any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Gordana Krljanac; Milika Asanin; Mihajlo Viduljevic; Stefan Stankovic; Kristina Simatovic; Ratko Lasica; Olga Nedeljkovic-Arsenovic; Ruzica Maksimovic; Slavisa Zagorac; Ana Savic-Radojevic; Tatjana Djukic; Goran Stevanovic; Vedrana Pavlovic; Tatjana Simic
paper_title: Cardiovascular Manifestations of Patients with Long COVID

summary: Observational cohort study examining long-term risks of ischemic stroke and transient cerebral ischemia (TCI) in COVID-19 survivors versus uninfected controls over 4 years. Finds elevated stroke and TCI risk in COVID+ patients, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Sagar Changela; Roham Hadidchi; Aditi Vichare; Liora Rahmani; Sonya Henry; Tim Q. Duong
paper_title: Risks of Stroke and Transient Cerebral Ischemia up to 4 Years Post-SARS-CoV-2 Infection in Large Diverse Urban Population in the Bronx

summary: This longitudinal cohort study examined brain volume changes 12 months after baseline MRI in 112 COVID-19 recovered patients (mild and severe) compared to controls. The study found severity-dependent right hippocampal atrophy in COVID-19 patients but no widespread progressive atrophy in other regions, highlighting long-term neurological vulnerability.
paper_authors: Zeynep Bendella; Catherine Nichols Widmann; Christine Kindler; Robert Haase; Malte Sauer; Michael T. Heneka; Alexander Radbruch; Frederic Carsten Schmeel
paper_title: Longitudinal Monitoring of Brain Volume Changes After COVID-19 Infection Using Artificial Intelligence-Based MRI Volumetry

summary: This longitudinal cohort study compares psychosocial outcomes, quality of life, coping strategies, and mental health between long COVID patients (n=86) and asymptomatic COVID-19 survivors (n=432) at 6 months post-infection. Long COVID patients showed significantly worse outcomes across depression, anxiety, quality of life domains, and greater use of disengagement and emotion-focused coping strategies.
paper_authors: Adrian Vasile Bota; Felix Bratosin; Iulia Bogdan; Susa Septimiu-Radu; Adrian Cosmin Ilie; Sonia-Roxana Burtic; David Vladut Razvan; Raluca Tudor; Mirela Florica Indries; Andrei Nicolae Csep; Ariadna Petronela Fildan; Camelia Melania Budea; Iosif Marincu
paper_title: Assessing the Quality of Life, Coping Strategies, Anxiety and Depression Levels in Patients with Long-COVID-19 Syndrome: A Six-Month Follow-Up Study

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining long-term cardiovascular and mortality outcomes in patients with pre-existing arrhythmia stratified by COVID-19 hospitalization status. While the paper studies post-COVID complications, it focuses on acute-infection sequelae in a pre-existing arrhythmia population rather than long COVID syndrome as defined by persistent symptoms weeks/months post-infection, and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Suhani Pahuja; Roham Hadidchi; Janhavi Tonge; Sonya Henry; Tim Q. Duong

The authors found reduced FMD in COVID-19 survivors but found no association between FMD impairment and acute infection severity, and did not test any intervention.

Left ventricular subclinical myocardial injury was found in 36% of patients and was associated with male gender and cardiovascular risk factors, with no significant improvement by 12 months.

summary: This retrospective cohort study investigated long COVID characteristics and risk factors in 5,750 healthcare workers at a university hospital, comparing BMI and comorbidities between those who developed 35-day long COVID and those who did not. summary: Retrospective cohort study following 587 COVID-19 hospital survivors for one year post-discharge, assessing clinical outcomes, mortality, and post-COVID-19 syndrome prevalence. 90% of hospitalized patients reported ongoing symptoms at one year, including breathlessness, tiredness, anosmia, and ageusia, with 7.5% mortality rate.

paper_title: Long-Term Outcomes of Patients with Coronavirus Disease 2019 at One Year after Hospital Discharge

summary: A longitudinal cohort study of 67 kidney transplant recipients assessed the presence of post-COVID-19 syndrome 6 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection using standardized questionnaires. The study found that 70.1% of recipients had post-COVID-19 syndrome with persistent symptoms including fatigue, hair loss, and dyspnea, and demonstrated significant reductions in health-related quality of life compared to baseline.

paper_title: Post-COVID-19 Sydrome and Decrease in Health-Related Quality of Life in Kidney Transplant Recipients after SARS-COV-2 Infection—A Cohort Longitudinal Study from the North of Poland

summary: A longitudinal cohort study of 79 hemodialyzed patients followed at 3 and 6 months post-COVID-19 to assess persistent symptoms and health-related quality of life. The study found that 93.7% and 81% of patients reported at least one persistent symptom at 3 and 6 months respectively, with fatigue, muscle weakness, and palpitations being most common, and significant declines across all EQ-5D-5L domains.

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 111 COVID-19 patients evaluated at a post-acute COVID clinic ~12 weeks after pneumonia diagnosis, tracking radiological and pulmonary function changes. paper_title: Coronavirus Pneumonia: Outcomes and Characteristics of Patients in an Inner-City Area after 3 Months of Infection

summary: Observational study examining residual symptoms after SARS-CoV-2 infection in Polish MS patients treated with various disease-modifying therapies. summary: Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of long COVID in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) patients at a tertiary referral center. Found 40% of 53 COVID-infected IBD patients developed long COVID (primarily asthenia), with no significant impact on IBD disease course.

summary: A prospective follow-up study of 218 patients hospitalized with COVID-19, assessing symptoms and pulmonary function 3 months after discharge. Fatigue was highly prevalent (65% with any fatigue, 18% severe), and ICU treatment was associated with significantly reduced diffusion capacity (DLCO < 80%).

paper_title: Fatigue Is a Major Symptom at COVID-19 Hospitalization Follow-Up

summary: Prospective cohort study of 248 COVID-19 patients followed for ~1 year post-discharge examining long COVID symptoms and associated risk factors. summary: Retrospective cohort study examining the incidence of myocarditis and pericarditis in 196,992 adults after COVID-19 infection in Israel, compared to 590,976 matched controls. The research identified BMI, severe acute COVID course, and joint pain during acute infection as independent predictors of long COVID development, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

summary: This cross-sectional study examined sociodemographic and clinical characteristics of 1,891 long COVID patients presenting to an outpatient clinic in Tokyo between January 2020 and October 2021. The study found associations between female sex, employment changes, and specific symptoms (fatigue, depression, brain fog, dyspnea) with lower performance status, but did not evaluate any treatment intervention.

summary: Prospective cohort study following 29 patients with post-COVID olfactory and gustatory disorders for 3-6 and 12 months post-hospitalization, using standardized smell and taste tests. Study documents persistent sensory dysfunction and its negative impact on health-related quality of life, but is observational with no treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Elisabeth Arndal; Anne-Mette Lebech; Daria Podlekarava; Jann Mortensen; Jan Christensen; Frederikke F. Rönsholt; Thomas Kromann Lund; Terese L. Katzenstein; Christian von Buchwald
paper_title: Olfactory and Gustatory Outcomes Including Health-Related Quality of Life 3–6 and 12 Months after Severe-to-Critical COVID-19: A SECURe Prospective Cohort Study

summary: Retrospective observational study comparing clinical and endocrinological features of 60 long COVID patients with sleep disturbance versus 303 without sleep symptoms at a Japanese COVID-19 aftercare clinic. Found increased sleep disturbance prevalence in Omicron-infected patients with elevated ACTH and reduced growth hormone, suggesting hypothalamic-pituitary stress.
paper_authors: Naruhiko Sunada; Yasuhiro Nakano; Yuki Otsuka; Kazuki Tokumasu; Hiroyuki Honda; Yasue Sakurada; Yui Matsuda; Toru Hasegawa; Daisuke Omura; Kanako Ochi; Hideharu Hagiya; Keigo Ueda; Hitomi Kataoka; Fumio Otsuka
paper_title: Characteristics of Sleep Disturbance in Patients with Long COVID: A Retrospective Observational Study in Japan

summary: Prospective cohort study following 166 COVID-19 survivors for 18 months post-discharge to characterize symptom prevalence and persistence. Findings show variable symptom trajectories: while overall symptom burden decreased over time, dyspnea, weakness, and brain fog remained elevated at 18 months, suggesting heterogeneous long-term recovery patterns.
paper_authors: George Kalak; Amir Jarjou’i; Abraham Bohadana; Pascal Wild; Ariel Rokach; Noa Amiad; Nader Abdelrahman; Nissim Arish; Chen Chen-Shuali; Gabriel Izbicki
paper_title: Prevalence and Persistence of Symptoms in Adult COVID-19 Survivors 3 and 18 Months after Discharge from Hospital or Corona Hotels

summary: This study characterizes a Danish post-COVID clinic cohort of 447 patients referred for persistent symptoms 6+ months after mild COVID-19, evaluating symptom prevalence and validating a post-COVID symptom questionnaire (PCQ). The work is descriptive and does not test any treatment or intervention, making it ineligible as a treatment trial despite being about long COVID.
paper_authors: Jane Agergaard; William M. Ullahammer; Jesper D. Gunst; Lars Østergaard; Berit Schiøttz-Christensen
paper_title: Characteristics of a Danish Post-COVID Cohort Referred for Examination due to Persistent Symptoms Six Months after Mild Acute COVID-19

summary: This study evaluates cardiac mechanics in 157 children who recovered from COVID-19 infection using speckle-tracking echocardiography at an average of 148 days post-infection, comparing them to 107 healthy controls. The study found persistent left ventricular myocardial deformation abnormalities in post-COVID children, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

summary: Prospective registry study examining outcomes and prognostic factors in COVID-19 survivors with underlying heart disease, following patients post-hospitalization. Vaccination was found to reduce all-cause mortality risk, while cardiovascular disease predicted worse outcomes including increased mortality during follow-up.

paper_title: Post-COVID-19 Symptoms and Heart Disease: Incidence, Prognostic Factors, Outcomes and Vaccination: Results from a Multi-Center International Prospective Registry (HOPE 2)

summary: Two-year follow-up study of 45 complex post-COVID patients receiving coordinated multidisciplinary care including exercise, respiratory, olfactory, cognitive/speech therapy and psychological support. Results show significant reductions in dyspnea, anxiety and chest pain, with 2/3 of patients reporting improvement and partial/full return to work, though persistent fatigue and neurocognitive symptoms remained in many.

paper_title: Two-Years Follow-Up of Symptoms and Return to Work in Complex Post-COVID-19 Patients

summary: Retrospective study comparing autonomic nerve function testing results in PASC patients versus POTS patients and healthy controls. Findings suggest significant PASC patients have abnormal autonomic function tests with clinical features similar to POTS.
paper_authors: Tae Hwan Chung; Antoine Azar
paper_title: Autonomic Nerve Involvement in Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Syndrome (PASC)

summary: This observational cohort study followed 167 COVID-19 patients at 3 and 18 months post-infection to assess vascular function, inflammation, and coagulation markers. The study found persistent endothelial activation, systemic inflammation, and coagulation abnormalities 18 months after infection, but no increased macrovascular dysfunction.

paper_title: Vascular Function, Systemic Inflammation, and Coagulation Activation 18 Months after COVID-19 Infection: An Observational Cohort Study

summary: This cross-sectional study compares erectile function in 95 male healthcare workers with prior COVID-19 infection (at different time points post-infection) versus 30 controls without COVID history using the IIEF-5 questionnaire. The study found erectile dysfunction was elevated early after COVID-19 but improved over time, particularly by 12 months post-infection, suggesting the condition may be temporary.
paper_authors: Alper Gök; Mehmet Altan; Ahmet Emin Doğan; Aşır Eraslan; Fahrettin Şamil Uysal; Ufuk Öztürk; Ardan Muammer Saguner; Muhammet Abdurrahim İmamoğlu
paper_title: Does Post-COVID-19 Erectile Dysfunction Improve over Time?

summary: This retrospective observational study compared serum zinc levels in 194 long COVID patients, finding hypozincemia (low zinc) in 22.2% of cases, with higher prevalence in older patients and males. The study identified associations between zinc deficiency and symptoms like fatigue, dysosmia, and dysgeusia, but did not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Yui Matsuda; Kazuki Tokumasu; Yuki Otsuka; Naruhiko Sunada; Hiroyuki Honda; Yasue Sakurada; Yasuhiro Nakano; Toru Hasegawa; Mikako Obika; Keigo Ueda; Fumio Otsuka
paper_title: Symptomatic Characteristics of Hypozincemia Detected in Long COVID Patients

summary: Prospective cohort study of 121 COVID-19 hospitalized patients followed for a mean of 17 months to assess persistence of long COVID symptoms and their associations with acute-phase factors. Finds that 60% of patients have persistent symptoms at follow-up, primarily fatigue and dyspnea, with vaccination and baseline neuropsychological symptoms being independent predictors of symptom persistence.
paper_authors: Marco Ranucci; Ekaterina Baryshnikova; Martina Anguissola; Sara Pugliese; Luca Ranucci; Mara Falco; Lorenzo Menicanti
paper_title: The Very Long COVID: Persistence of Symptoms after 12–18 Months from the Onset of Infection and Hospitalization

summary: This pre-post observational study measured arterial stiffness and hemodynamic parameters in 32 patients with mild COVID-19 at baseline (up to 2 years pre-infection) and follow-up (2-3 months post-infection). The study found significant increases in arterial stiffness and alterations in central hemodynamics parameters, suggesting long-lasting vascular impairment following mild COVID-19.

paper_title: Long-Term Adverse Effects of Mild COVID-19 Disease on Arterial Stiffness, and Systemic and Central Hemodynamics: A Pre-Post Study

summary: A prospective observational study of 474 COVID-19 patients (252 ambulatory, 222 hospitalized) followed for 1 year post-infection to characterize long COVID symptoms and identify risk factors. The study found high prevalence of fatigue (87.5%), neurological symptoms, and psychiatric comorbidity, and identified two distinct patient phenotypes prone to long COVID.

paper_title: Long-Term Consequences of COVID-19: A 1-Year Analysis

summary: Prospective registry study following 150 hospitalized COVID-19 patients at 6 months post-discharge to identify cardiopulmonary long-term effects and predictors of long COVID. Found 75% met long COVID criteria; exertional dyspnea correlated with impaired pulmonary function and cardiac abnormalities, while hospitalization duration and ICU admission predicted long COVID development.

paper_title: Cardiopulmonary Long-Term Sequelae in Patients after Severe COVID-19 Disease

summary: This cross-sectional study examines associations between physical activity levels and physical function in 1,846 COVID-19 survivors with post-acute symptoms. While it documents that reduced physical activity is associated with worse physical outcomes (lower handgrip strength, shorter 6MWT distance, higher fatigue), it is an observational study without any intervention assignment and therefore does not qualify as a treatment trial.
