paper_title: Inadequate Physical Activity Is Associated with Worse Physical Function in a Sample of COVID-19 Survivors with Post-Acute Symptoms

summary: Prospective cohort study analyzing sex and age interactions as risk factors for post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 in 452 adults and 925 children followed for median 7.8 months. Found statistically significant interaction between sex and age, with higher risk in males aged 0-5 and females aged 12-50, particularly for cardiovascular, neurological, gastrointestinal, and sleep symptoms.
paper_authors: Matteo Puntoni; Susanna Esposito; Laura Patrizi; Chiara Maria Palo; Michela Deolmi; Giovanni Autore; Valentina Fainardi; Caterina Caminiti
paper_title: Impact of Age and Sex Interaction on Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19: An Italian Cohort Study on Adults and Children

summary: Prospective case-control study comparing lung ultrasound (LUS) findings in children with persistent symptoms post-SARS-CoV-2 infection versus fully recovered children. LUS showed minimal differences between groups, with mostly normal findings in all children at median 2-month follow-up.
paper_authors: Danilo Buonsenso; Rosa Morello; Francesco Mariani; Cristina De Rose; Rossella Cortese; Luigi Vetrugno; Piero Valentini
paper_title: Role of Lung Ultrasound in the Follow-Up of Children with Previous SARS-CoV-2 Infection: A Case-Control Assessment of Children with Long COVID or Fully Recovered

summary: A prospective observational study examining ICU memories and their association with six-month psychological outcomes in COVID-19 critical illness survivors. The study found that lack of pre-ICU memories independently predicted worse psychological outcomes (anxiety, depression, PTSD), but focuses on acute COVID-19 ICU recovery rather than long COVID.

paper_title: Hospital Memories and Six-Month Psychological Outcome: A Prospective Study in Critical Ill Patients with COVID-19 Respiratory Failure

summary: This retrospective cohort study examined 204 COVID-19 hospitalized patients to investigate associations between acute-phase electrolyte imbalances and persistent mental fatigue after recovery. Females with mild COVID-19 showed higher odds of post-COVID mental fatigue, particularly when dysnatremia occurred during hospitalization.

paper_title: The Association between Dysnatraemia during Hospitalisation and Post-COVID-19 Mental Fatigue

summary: A retrospective observational study comparing long COVID patients with and without headaches, examining symptom prevalence, demographics, and quality of life impacts. Headache was found to significantly affect depression, QOL scores, and general fatigue in long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Kana Fujita; Yuki Otsuka; Naruhiko Sunada; Hiroyuki Honda; Kazuki Tokumasu; Yasuhiro Nakano; Yasue Sakurada; Mikako Obika; Hideharu Hagiya; Fumio Otsuka
paper_title: Manifestation of Headache Affecting Quality of Life in Long COVID Patients

summary: This study evaluates pulmonary functional outcomes, quality of life, and chest CT patterns in ICU survivors of acute COVID-19 ARDS at 3 months post-discharge across three pandemic waves. It is a retrospective comparison of acute COVID-19 survivors without a specific treatment intervention, focusing on acute-phase disease severity rather than long COVID sequelae.

summary: This study assessed neuropsychiatric outcomes in 50 children 1-18 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection using standardized clinical rating scales. Results showed elevated rates of internalizing symptoms (40%), anxiety (48%), sleep disturbance (28%), and cognitive/executive function impairment (52%), suggesting long-term mental health sequelae of COVID-19 in children.

summary: A prospective cohort study of 184 post-COVID patients followed at 3 and 6 months in a rehabilitation clinic, documenting symptom burden, fatigue, cognition, and physiological abnormalities. paper_title: Longitudinal Clinical Features of Post-COVID-19 Patients—Symptoms, Fatigue and Physical Function at 3- and 6-Month Follow-Up

summary: Prospective observational study of 1,966 patients following acute COVID-19 examining risk factors for PASC and outcomes based on acute-phase treatments. Patients treated with dexamethasone and/or remdesivir during acute illness showed lower median symptom duration, with female gender, obesity, asthma, and disease severity identified as PASC risk factors.

summary: This prospective study evaluated cardiopulmonary rehabilitation in 84 severe COVID-19 patients stratified into low- and high-intensity exercise groups over 3 months. Both groups showed significant improvements in lung function, ejection fraction, and exercise capacity, demonstrating that personalized rehabilitation strategies improve long-term cardiopulmonary outcomes in post-COVID patients.

Higher BMI, elevated C-reactive protein at admission, longer hospitalization duration, and right ventricular dysfunction were independently associated with persistent dyspnea.

paper_title: Utility of Serum Ferritin for Predicting Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome in Patients with Long COVID

summary: A prospective cohort study of 1,266 previously hospitalized COVID-19 survivors followed for up to 18.3 months post-discharge to assess prevalence of self-reported anosmia and ageusia. The study found that both anosmia and ageusia prevalence decreased over time, with female sex and asthma history associated with anosmia development.

paper_title: Prevalence of Self-Reported Anosmia and Ageusia in Elderly Patients Who Had Been Previously Hospitalized by SARS-CoV-2: The LONG-COVID-EXP Multicenter Study

summary: A retrospective imaging study assessing lung CT abnormalities in 39 long COVID patients 4-7 months after moderate-to-severe COVID-19 pneumonia. Found persistent radiological changes (ground-glass opacities, fibrotic changes) in 94.9% of patients with no significant differences by initial severity or sex.
paper_authors: Ewa Kurys-Denis; Anna Grzywa-Celińska; Katarzyna Podgórska; Miłosz Piotr Kawa
paper_title: What Remains up to 7 Months after Severe and Moderate Pneumonia in Non-Vaccinated Patients with Long COVID? Results of a CT Study

summary: Prospective cohort study examining the prevalence and incidence of fatigue in 1,417 participants at baseline and 9-month follow-up during the initial COVID-19 pandemic wave. Found that COVID-19 positivity, symptom severity, and symptom duration were significantly associated with higher fatigue at follow-up, suggesting acute illness characteristics predict longer-term fatigue outcomes.
paper_authors: Alexandria Muench; Elizabeth W. Lampe; Julia T. Boyle; Mark Seewald; Michelle G. Thompson; Michael L. Perlis; Ivan Vargas
paper_title: The Assessment of Post-COVID Fatigue and Its Relationship to the Severity and Duration of Acute COVID Illness

summary: Prospective population-based cohort study in Canada tracking COVID-19 symptom evolution for up to 9 months in 1,349 participants, predominantly unvaccinated. Found 48% exhibited persistent symptoms ≥3 months post-infection, with female sex, symptom severity, and prior mental health conditions as key risk factors; no treatment intervention studied.

summary: This retrospective cohort study compares KL-6 biomarker levels in post-COVID patients stratified by acute COVID-19 severity across three groups (critical, non-critical, and home-hospitalized). KL-6 levels were found to be less elevated in mild COVID-19 patients compared to those with moderate or severe disease, with KL-6 associated with inflammatory, hepatic, and thrombosis markers.

paper_title: Krebs von den Lungen-6 (KL-6) Levels in Post-COVID Follow-Up: Differences According to the Severity of COVID-19

summary: Retrospective longitudinal study of 436 COVID-19 patients in Southeastern Italy assessing predictive factors for long COVID development at 12 weeks post-infection. Identified female sex and corticosteroid therapy during acute infection as independent predictive factors, with 71.8% of patients developing long COVID.

paper_title: The Predictors of Long COVID in Southeastern Italy

summary: Prospective cohort study evaluating sleep and circadian rhythm disturbances in COVID-19 survivors with and without acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) at 4 and 12 months post-discharge. Found persistent sleep dysfunction (91.3% poor sleep quality, 58.7% insomnia) with no significant improvement between timepoints.

summary: This retrospective cohort study assessed cardiovascular risk factors in 70 post-COVID patients at a rehabilitation clinic in Romania between September-December 2022. The study found increased hypertension risk (69.57% to 90%) and dyslipidemia after COVID-19, but does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

paper_title: Evolution of Cardiovascular Risk Factors in Post-COVID Patients

summary: Longitudinal cohort study comparing incidence, severity, and duration of smell and taste loss between COVID-19 positive and negative participants from the Dutch Lifelines biobank. Finds higher incidence and severity in COVID-19 cases but longer duration in non-COVID cases, with no intervention or treatment being evaluated.

paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of the Incidence, Severity and Duration of Smell and Taste Loss in COVID-19 Cases Versus Non-COVID-19 Cases: A Longitudinal Cohort Study

summary: Prospective cohort study of 184 children with post-COVID-19 condition and respiratory symptoms, characterizing pulmonary function tests (PFTs) and changes over time from November 2020 to December 2022. Most common finding was mild obstructive pattern (11%); diffusion limitation was rare unlike in adults; most children showed improvement on repeat testing, with older age and specific imaging findings predicting obstructive patterns.

paper_title: Pulmonary Evaluation in Children with Post-COVID-19 Condition Respiratory Symptoms: A Prospective Cohort Study

summary: An uncontrolled prospective observational pilot study examining sleep disturbances in 61 long COVID patients using self-reported scales and actigraphy. The study documents high prevalence of moderate daytime sleepiness and insomnia persisting beyond one month post-infection, with female gender and younger age associated with greater severity.

paper_title: Sleep Disturbances as a Consequence of Long COVID-19: Insights from Actigraphy and Clinimetric Examinations—An Uncontrolled Prospective Observational Pilot Study

summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 46 COVID-19 survivors who experienced respiratory failure, assessing pulmonary function and functional capacity at 3 and 9 months post-discharge. The findings show that severe respiratory impairment gradually improves spontaneously over time, though recovery is slower in patients who required intensive oxygenation support.

summary: This observational study follows 122 previously hospitalized COVID-19 patients (4-84 weeks post-symptom onset) to investigate the association between plasma osteopontin levels and post-acute COVID-19 symptoms. Elevated osteopontin was independently associated with severe dyspnea and impaired quality of life, but was not related to imaging or functional lung abnormalities.

paper_title: 24 h Holter Monitoring and 14-Day Intermittent Patient-Activated Heart Rhythm Recording to Detect Arrhythmias in Symptomatic Patients After Severe COVID-19—A Prospective Observation

summary: This cross-sectional study examined 252 post-COVID patients at a Hungarian tertiary hospital over a 19-month period, characterizing cardiopulmonary outcomes and identifying a 10× higher prevalence of lupus anticoagulant positivity compared to the general population. The findings suggest autoimmunity may play a role in post-COVID syndrome pathomechanism, with worse cardiopulmonary outcomes associated with severe acute infections.
paper_authors: Krisztina Fekete; Barbara Sándor; Anita Kacsó; Anita Pálfi; Szilard Tóth; László Deres; Eszter Szabados; László Czopf; Miklós Rábai; Roland Gál; Tamas Alexy; Tamás Habon; Kálmán Tóth; Hussain Alizadeh; Szilvia Soós; Róbert Halmosi
paper_title: Prevalence and Cardiopulmonary Characteristics of Post-COVID Syndrome at a Hungarian Tertiary Referral Hospital

summary: This retrospective case-control study compared long-COVID prevalence in 247 women with and without endometriosis/adenomyosis, finding significantly higher rates of persistent COVID-19 symptoms in those with gynecological conditions. The study identifies a risk factor association but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Anjeza Xholli; Isabella Perugi; Francesca Cremonini; Ambrogio Pietro Londero; Angelo Cagnacci
paper_title: Evaluation of Long-COVID Syndrome in a Cohort of Patients with Endometriosis or Adenomyosis

summary: This study evaluates quality of life and mental health outcomes in survivors of acute COVID-19-related ARDS who received venovenous ECMO support, with follow-up at 1.7 years post-discharge. While it reports persistent mental health issues in ECMO survivors, it focuses on acute respiratory failure outcomes rather than long COVID-specific symptoms or post-COVID syndrome.
paper_authors: Dawid L. Staudacher; Meret Felder; Markus Jäckel; Felix A. Rottmann; Alexander Supady; Xavier Bemtgen; Philipp Diehl; Tobias Wengenmayer; Viviane Zotzmann
paper_title: Quality of Life and Mental Health in COVID-ARDS Survivors After V-V ECMO Support: Results from the Freiburg ECMO Outcome Study (FEOS)

summary: This retrospective cohort study compared 216 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors who received intravenous remdesivir during acute infection with 216 matched controls who received no antivirals, following them for ~18 months to assess post-COVID-19 pain development. Remdesivir treatment was protective against overall post-COVID pain (OR 0.444) and lumbar spine pain (OR 0.347), suggesting early antiviral administration may prevent long-term pain sequelae.
paper_authors: César Fernández-de-las-Peñas; Anabel Franco-Moreno; María Ruiz-Ruigómez; Estibaliz Arrieta-Ortubay; Pablo Ryan-Murua; Carlos Lumbreras-Bermejo; Pablo del-Valle-Loarte; Oscar J. Pellicer-Valero; Juan Torres-Macho; Rocco Giordano; Lars Arendt-Nielsen
paper_title: Intravenous Administration of Remdesivir at the Acute Phase of SARS-CoV-2 Infection Is Associated with a Lower Prevalence of Post-COVID-19 Pain

summary: Retrospective observational study examining brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) levels in 428 long COVID patients to assess its usefulness as a biomarker for severity evaluation. Finds that elevated BNP is more common in female patients and associated with respiratory symptoms and memory impairment, suggesting BNP measurement may help evaluate long COVID severity.
paper_authors: Yohei Masuda; Yuki Otsuka; Kazuki Tokumasu; Hiroyuki Honda; Yasue Sakurada; Yui Matsuda; Yasuhiro Nakano; Ryosuke Takase; Daisuke Omura; Toru Hasegawa; Keigo Ueda; Fumio Otsuka
paper_title: Interrelationships Between Plasma Levels of Brain Natriuretic Peptide and Prolonged Symptoms Due to Long COVID

summary: Retrospective study of 382 severely ill COVID-19 patients followed at 3 months using unsupervised machine learning to identify symptom phenotypes and patient clusters. The analysis found extreme heterogeneity with no identifiable distinct symptom clusters, preventing the generation of common diagnostic-therapeutic pathways.
paper_authors: Eleonora Fresi; Elisabetta Pagani; Federica Pezzetti; Cristina Montomoli; Cristina Monti; Monia Betti; Annalisa De Silvestri; Orlando Sagliocco; Valentina Zuccaro; Raffaele Bruno; Catherine Klersy
paper_title: Long COVID’s Hidden Complexity: Machine Learning Reveals Why Personalized Care Remains Essential

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 893 older adults (≥60 years) in Brazil examining the spatial distribution and incidence of post-COVID-19 health complications 12 months after acute infection. Found cardiovascular (39.5%) and metabolic diseases (27.3%) most frequent, with medication use and age associated with increased risk of complications.
paper_authors: Franciele Aline Machado de Brito; Carlos Laranjeira; Stéfane Lele Rossoni; Amira Mohammed Ali; Maria Aparecida Salci; Lígia Carreira
paper_title: Spatial Distribution and Post-COVID-19 Health Complications in Older People: A Brazilian Cohort Study

summary: Prospective cohort study assessing health-related quality of life in COVID-19 survivors >18 months after ICU discharge following ARDS and ECMO therapy. Found significant impairments in physical, mental, and cognitive health compared to non-COVID ARDS survivors, with longer ECMO duration associated with improved vitality and emotional well-being.
paper_authors: Martina Hermann; Rebecca Filipsky; Nils Bukowski; Gernot Gerger; Alexander Hermann; Katharina Krenn; Anna Teufel; Oliver Kimberger; Daniel Laxar; Mathias Maleczek; Eva Schaden; Marion Wiegele; Harald Willschke; Akos Tiboldi
paper_title: Long-Term Health-Related Quality of Life Following Survival of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome and Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Due to COVID-19

summary: This study compared cognitive and emotional outcomes in 92 healthcare workers one year after mild COVID-19 infection (50 infected, 42 uninfected controls). While no significant cognitive differences were found between groups, the COVID-19 group showed higher trait anxiety and emotional distress, with burnout correlating with slower neuropsychological performance.
paper_authors: Irene Peláez; David Martínez-Íñigo; Roberto Fernandes-Magalhaes; María E. De Lahoz; Ana Belén del Pino; Sonia Pérez-Aranda; Alejandro García-Romero; Dino Soldic; Francisco Mercado
paper_title: One Year After Mild COVID-19: Emotional Distress but Preserved Cognition in Healthcare Workers

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing 774 long COVID patients with early recovery (<180 days) versus persistent symptoms (>180 days) during the Omicron period. Found female gender, higher symptom burden, and psychological symptoms associated with longer symptom persistence, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Hiroshi Akiyama; Yasue Sakurada; Hiroyuki Honda; Yui Matsuda; Yuki Otsuka; Kazuki Tokumasu; Yasuhiro Nakano; Ryosuke Takase; Daisuke Omura; Keigo Ueda; Fumio Otsuka
paper_title: Symptomatic Trends and Time to Recovery for Long COVID Patients Infected During the Omicron Phase

summary: A prospective cohort study examining the prevalence, severity, and trajectory of insomnia in 172 long COVID patients over 9 months using the Insomnia Severity Index and neuropsychological assessments. Found that 78% of patients experienced insomnia symptoms at baseline, with strong correlations between insomnia and cognitive dysfunction, mood symptoms, and fatigue; symptoms did not improve significantly over the follow-up period.
paper_authors: Jamie Hansel Robinson; Halle Bakir; Alicia Shanti James; Marquita S. Brooks; Stephen J. Thomas; Kristine L. Lokken
paper_title: Prevalence, Severity, Concomitant Factors, and Natural Trajectory of Insomnia in Patients with Long COVID

summary: Prospective cohort study comparing objectively measured physical activity and physical function 12 months after hospital discharge in COVID-19 patients versus healthy controls. Patients had significantly lower daily step counts and movement intensity than controls, but outcomes were comparable between ICU and non-ICU admission groups.
paper_authors: Eva Arents; Fien Hermans; Lies Glorie; Bihiyga Salhi; Cedric Bosteels; Eric Derom; Wim Janssens; Eva Van Braeckel; Natalie Lorent; Yannick Vande Weygaerde; Thierry Troosters; Heleen Demeyer
paper_title: Physical Activity and Physical Function One Year After Hospital Discharge for COVID-19

summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 93 COVID-19 pneumonia patients with CT imaging over 10 months to characterize persistent pulmonary imaging abnormalities and their clinical correlates. The study found that fibrotic-like changes persisted in 75% of patients and were associated with fatigue and chest pain, but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Gorkem Durak; Kaan Akin; Okan Cetin; Emre Uysal; Halil Ertugrul Aktas; Ulku Durak; Ahmet Yasin Karkas; Naci Senkal; Hatice Savas; Atadan Tunaci; Alpay Medetalibeyoglu; Ulas Bagci; Sukru Mehmet Erturk
paper_title: Radiologic and Clinical Correlates of Long-Term Post-COVID-19 Pulmonary Sequelae

summary: A retrospective pre-post study of 14 post-COVID-19 patients with isolated dysphonia who received multimodal treatment including corticosteroids, inhalations, and voice therapy. High-speed videoendoscopy and patient-reported outcomes showed improvements in vocal fold oscillation, amplitude, regularity, and voice-related quality of life at 1-month follow-up.
paper_authors: Joanna Jeleniewska; Jakub Malinowski; Ewa Niebudek-Bogusz; Wioletta Pietruszewska
paper_title: Objective and Subjective Voice Outcomes in Post-COVID-19 Dysphonia: A High-Speed Videoendoscopy Pre–Post Study

summary: Retrospective cohort study evaluating non-invasive ventilatory strategies (CPAP and HFNC) in long COVID patients with severe ARDS, comparing outcomes and sequelae before endotracheal intubation. CPAP showed a trend toward improved survival, though the data are hypothesis-generating and highlight the need for larger multicenter studies in this underrepresented population.
paper_authors: Diana-Alexandra Mîțu; Florina Buleu; Daian-Ionel Popa; Cosmin Trebuian; Dumitru Sutoi; Adina Coman; Daniel Florin Lighezan; Tiberiu Buleu; Natheer Sliman; Oana Raluca Radbea; Ovidiu Alexandru Mederle
paper_title: Outcomes, Sequelae, and Ventilatory Strategies in Long COVID Patients with Severe ARDS: A Retrospective Cohort Study

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing acute ischemic stroke presentation and outcomes in 26 long COVID patients versus 106 controls presenting to the emergency department. Long COVID patients showed higher rates of headache and facial drooping but similar stroke severity, ED time targets, and short-term outcomes.
paper_authors: Daian-Ionel Popa; Florina Buleu; Aida Iancu; Anca Tudor; Carmen Gabriela Williams; Marius Militaru; Codrina Mihaela Levai; Tiberiu Buleu; Livia Ciolac; Anda Gabriela Militaru; Ovidiu Alexandru Mederle
paper_title: Long COVID and Acute Stroke in the Emergency Department: An Analysis of Presentation, Reperfusion Treatment, and Early Outcomes

summary: A prospective observational study of 146 post-COVID-19 patients examining how metabolic syndrome affects rehabilitation outcomes, using functional tests (6MWT, spirometry) to measure recovery. The study found that comprehensive rehabilitation benefits all patients regardless of metabolic syndrome status, though age and comorbidities significantly predict rehabilitation effectiveness.
paper_authors: Alicja Mińko; Agnieszka Turoń-Skrzypińska; Aleksandra Rył; Iwona Rotter
paper_title: The Impact of Metabolic Syndrome on the Outcomes of Rehabilitation in Post-COVID-19 Patients

summary: A prospective cohort study following 148 COVID-19 survivors (101 with Long COVID) from 12-18 months post-infection to assess changes in physical activity, sedentary behaviour, and associated functional outcomes. People with Long COVID showed increased light PA but decreased MVPA and sedentarism, with higher proportions experiencing functional impairment, dyspnoea, fatigue, and poor quality of life compared to controls, suggesting physical limitations drive activity behaviour changes.
paper_authors: Nicola S. Diciolla; Ana Ampuero-López; Alda Marques; Ana Jiménez-Martín; Sara García-De Villa; María Torres-Lacomba; María José Yuste-Sánchez
paper_title: Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour in People with Long COVID: A Follow-Up from 12 to 18 Months After Discharge

summary: This prospective longitudinal cohort study (12 months) compared health-related quality of life and biomarkers (inflammation, bone turnover, vitamin D) in 45 long COVID patients vs 40 well-recovered controls. Long COVID patients showed significantly lower HRQoL and more hand pain, but no differences in inflammatory markers or bone turnover markers were observed between groups.
paper_authors: Fahad Alghamdi; Robert Meertens; Abasiama Dick Obotiba; Lorna W. Harries; Sarah Appleby; Kinan Mokbel; Karen M. Knapp; William David Strain
paper_title: Assessment of Health-Related Quality of Life and Biomarkers in Long COVID: A 12-Month Longitudinal Feasibility Cohort

summary: This observational study examined late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) patterns on cardiac MRI in 50 COVID-19 ICU patients with severe acute respiratory distress syndrome to assess associations with cardiac dysfunction. LGE was present in 33.3% of patients and correlated with prolonged hospitalization duration but not with left ventricular dysfunction or remodeling.
paper_authors: Alessandro Pingitore; Filippo Figini; Laura Pederzoli; Patrizia Landi; Luca Bastiani; Claudio Marabotti; Filippo Leonardo
paper_title: Non-Ischemic Pattern of LGE After COVID-19 Correlates More with Severity of Acute Illness than with Long-Term Myocardial Dysfunction

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 150 pregnant individuals with acute SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy, examining long COVID symptomatology and adverse outcomes in a predominantly Black and Latina population. Study characterizes symptom prevalence (26.7% with long COVID symptoms) and outcome patterns but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Clementine Adeyemi; Leticia Breuer; Raghad Kodvawala; Delia Miller; Margaret V. Powers-Fletcher
paper_title: A Cohort Study Characterizing the Outcomes Following an Acute SARS-CoV-2 Infection in Pregnancy

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining acute pulmonary edema in hospitalized COVID-19 patients and its long-term pulmonary sequelae at three-month follow-up. The study identifies predictors of APE and documents fibrotic changes and restrictive ventilatory defects in survivors, but does not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Diana-Maria Mateescu; Dragos-Mihai Gavrilescu; Andrei Marginean; Ioana-Georgiana Cotet; Elena-Cristina Guse; Camelia-Oana Muresan; Ana-Olivia Toma; Stela Iurciuc; Adrian-Cosmin Ilie; Alexandra Enache
paper_title: Acute Pulmonary Edema in COVID-19: Clinical Predictors, Long-Term Pulmonary Sequelae, and Mortality in a Romanian Cohort Study

summary: Retrospective study of asthmatic children who contracted SARS-CoV-2, examining changes in lung function and persistent respiratory symptoms months after infection. The study documents symptom persistence and treatment modifications but does not evaluate or test any specific intervention or treatment for long COVID.
paper_authors: Jaqueline Abdul-Razzak; Mihaela Ionescu; Radu Diaconu; Alexandru Dan Popescu; Elena Carmen Niculescu; Mihai Gafencu; Ileana Octavia Petrescu; Cristina Elena Singer; Liliana Anghelina; Cristian Gheonea
paper_title: Retrospective Study of the Impact of SARS-CoV-2 Infection on Asthma Control in Children

summary: Population-based retrospective cohort study of 1,034,093 Danish adults over 40 examining prevalence and risk factors for COVID-19 sequelae diagnoses and their long-term health outcomes over two years. Study found 0.55% prevalence of sequelae, with higher comorbidity burden increasing risk of severe sequelae and complications including thromboembolic events, chronic lung disease, and infections.
paper_authors: Simon Kjeldsen; Jan Nielsen; Bente Mertz Nørgård; Ken Lund; Pedro Póvoa; Torben Knudsen; Jens Kjeldsen
paper_title: Risk of Sequelae Following COVID-19 Infection: A Nationwide Study Focusing on Risk Factors and Long-Term Impacts

summary: A 12-month longitudinal feasibility cohort study comparing bone mineral density, body composition, and joint integrity in 45 long COVID patients versus 40 well-recovered controls. The study found no evidence of rapid bone loss but identified increased adiposity and joint symptoms, suggesting a need for ongoing monitoring of musculoskeletal health in long COVID.
paper_authors: Fahad Alghamdi; Abasiama Dick Obotiba; Robert Meertens; Omar Alshalawi; Kinan Mokbel; William David Strain; Karen M. Knapp
paper_title: Assessment of Bone Mineral Density, Total Body Composition and Joint Integrity in Long COVID: A 12-Month Longitudinal Feasibility Study

summary: This cross-sectional study examined 61 long COVID patients 16.5 months post-infection to explore associations between type I interferon gene expression, hematologic markers during acute infection, and long COVID symptom severity. The study found that elevated WBC/neutrophil counts, reduced monocyte counts, elevated LDH/SGOT, intubation history, and reduced MX-1 transcript levels during acute infection were associated with high long COVID symptom burden, but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Mary Emmanouil; Vasiliki E. Georgakopoulou; Konstantinos Drougkas; Panagiotis Lembessis; Charalampos Skarlis; Aikaterini Gkoufa; Nikolaos V. Sipsas; Clio P. Mavragani
paper_title: Type I Interferon-Related Gene Expression and Laboratory Abnormalities in Acute Infection Are Associated with Long COVID Symptom Burden

summary: Secondary analysis of COVID-19 ICU survivors examining associations between mechanical ventilation duration and cognitive outcomes one year post-discharge. Findings suggest tracheostomy-based ventilation may be associated with better cognitive outcomes compared to endotracheal intubation, but this is a secondary analysis of published data rather than a primary treatment trial.
paper_authors: Clementina M. van Rijn; Marta Godoy-González; Sol Fernández-Gonzalo; Pierre Souren; Malcolm G. Coulthard; David J. Howard; Marijtje L. A. Jongsma
paper_title: Rethinking Mechanical Ventilation: Can Ventilation Mode Influence Long-Term Cognitive Outcomes in ICU Patients with COVID-19?

summary: This observational study followed 233 oldest-old adults (≥80 years) for 18 months after COVID-19 hospitalization to assess transitions in physical function and frailty. While it documents post-hospitalization recovery patterns in elderly survivors, it does not focus on long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months post-infection) and involves no intervention or treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Rafael Saavedra-Palacios; Alejandro Álvarez-Bustos; Lucía Furones-Fernández; Ángel Chen-Chim; María Teresa Boimorto-Medina; Rebeca Martiño-Córdoba; Pedro Gil-Gregorio; Walter Sepúlveda-Loyola; Isabel Rodríguez-Sánchez
paper_title: Transitions in Functional Status and Frailty Among Post-Hospitalized COVID-19 Oldest-Old Adults: An 18-Month Follow-Up Study

summary: This prospective observational study examines MMP-2 and MMP-9 dysregulation in post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis patients at 6 and 12 months post-infection, comparing those with and without fibrotic changes. The study identifies biomarker patterns and inflammatory pathways but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Olga V. Balan; Irina E. Malysheva; Ella L. Tikhonovich; Liudmila A. Lysenko
paper_title: Dysregulation of MMP-2 and MMP-9 in Post-COVID-19 and IPF: Correlations with Systemic Inflammation and Endothelial Dysfunction

summary: A 32-month prospective cohort study of 94 ICU survivors with COVID-19 that documents the prevalence and persistence of post-COVID condition manifestations across five organ system domains. The study shows high initial prevalence (96.8% at discharge) declining over time, with respiratory symptoms resolving by 32 months while musculoskeletal/neuromuscular involvement persisted, and 36.5% of survivors developing new chronic conditions by 32 months.
paper_authors: Alicia Ávila Nieto; Paulo Infante; Francisco Javier Barca Durán
paper_title: Prevalence and Persistence of Post-COVID-19 Condition After Critical Care: 32-Month Follow-Up

summary: Retrospective observational study of 97 post-COVID syndrome patients assessing longitudinal changes in pulmonary function over 22 months post-infection. Found progressive improvements in airflow measures up to 9-18 months but persistent diffusion abnormalities beyond 12 months, with greater impairment in patients with moderate acute COVID-19.
paper_authors: Daniela Robu Popa; Corina Marginean; Mona Elisabeta Dobrin; Radu Adrian Crisan Dabija; Oana-Elena Melinte; Stefan Dumitrache-Rujinski; Ioan Emanuel Stavarache; Ionel-Bogdan Cioroiu; Antigona Carmen Trofor
paper_title: Impact of COVID-19 on Respiratory Function: A Post-Recovery Comparative Assessment

summary: This cross-sectional study examines the association between obesity (measured by BMI and waist-to-height ratio) and post-COVID-19 condition in 376 male military conscripts with prior COVID-19 infection. Both BMI-defined and central obesity were significantly associated with increased odds of experiencing persistent post-COVID symptoms.
paper_authors: Reinhard Domanyi; Emanuel Maitz; Alexandros Andrianakis
paper_title: Association Between Obesity and Post-COVID-19 Condition in Military Conscripts

summary: Cross-sectional observational study comparing retinal vascular perfusion (RPCP) between 80 post-COVID-19 patients and 30 healthy controls using OCT angiography. Found significantly lower retinal capillary perfusion density in post-COVID patients, particularly those with hypertension or prior antiviral/antiplatelet treatment, suggesting potential microvascular impairment.
paper_authors: Alfonso Savastano; Emanuele Crincoli; Maria Savastano; Saad Younis; Gloria Gambini; Umberto De Vico; Grazia Cozzupoli; Carola Culiersi; Stanislao Rizzo
paper_title: Peripapillary Retinal Vascular Involvement in Early Post-COVID-19 Patients

summary: This observational cohort study assessed left ventricular function in 125 COVID-19 patients without prior cardiovascular disease at 6-10 weeks post-discharge. The study found persistent systolic and diastolic dysfunction in a subset of patients, correlated with myocardial injury markers, but did not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Mariana Tudoran; Cristina Tudoran; Voichita Lazureanu; Adelina Marinescu; Gheorghe Pop; Alexandru Pescariu; Alexandra Enache; Talida Cut
paper_title: Alterations of Left Ventricular Function Persisting during Post-Acute COVID-19 in Subjects without Previously Diagnosed Cardiovascular Pathology

summary: Retrospective observational study examining MRI imaging patterns in a cardiovascular center before and during the COVID-19 pandemic, analyzing 8,137 MRI studies from 2019-2022. Found that patients with COVID-19 history showed persistent cardiac symptoms and myocardial damage consistent with long COVID, but the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Tatiana A. Shelkovnikova; Aleksandra S. Maksimova; Nadezhda I. Ryumshina; Olga V. Mochula; Valery K. Vaizov; Wladimir Y. Ussov; Nina D. Anfinogenova
paper_title: Transformative Effect of COVID-19 Pandemic on Magnetic Resonance Imaging Services in One Tertiary Cardiovascular Center

summary: This prospective observational cohort study assessed echocardiographic abnormalities in 102 previously healthy individuals recovering from COVID-19, monitoring cardiac patterns (LV dysfunction, pulmonary hypertension, diastolic dysfunction, pericardial effusion) at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months. Most cardiac abnormalities improved over time, though diastolic dysfunction showed persistent changes, suggesting potential chronic cardiac sequelae in post-acute COVID-19 syndrome.
paper_authors: Cristina Tudoran; Mariana Tudoran; Talida Georgiana Cut; Voichita Elena Lazureanu; Cristian Oancea; Adelina Raluca Marinescu; Silvius Alexandru Pescariu; Gheorghe Nicusor Pop; Felix Bende
paper_title: Evolution of Echocardiographic Abnormalities Identified in Previously Healthy Individuals Recovering from COVID-19

summary: This study prospectively measured pulmonary function tests and exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO and CaNO) in 169 post-COVID patients 6 weeks to 1 year after acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, stratified by initial severity. Elevated distal lung inflammation (CaNO) was found in severe/critical COVID-19 patients and inversely correlated with lung gas transfer, suggesting persistent alveolar inflammation may contribute to long-term pulmonary complications.
paper_authors: Thông Hua-Huy; Sven Günther; Christine Lorut; Marielle Subileau; Frédérique Aubourg; Caroline Morbieu; Jonathan Marey; Joëlle Texereau; Isabelle Fajac; Luc Mouthon; Nicolas Roche; Anh Tuan Dinh-Xuan
paper_title: Distal Lung Inflammation Assessed by Alveolar Concentration of Nitric Oxide Is an Individualised Biomarker of Severe COVID-19 Pneumonia

summary: This prospective cohort study used optical coherence tomography angiography (OCT-A) to compare retinal capillary perfusion parameters between non-hospitalized neuro-PASC patients and healthy controls. The study found statistically significant reduction in deep capillary plexus vessel length density in neuro-PASC patients, suggesting preferential involvement of the smallest blood vessels as a potential mechanism.
paper_authors: Clayton E. Lyons; Jonathan Alhalel; Anna Busza; Emily Suen; Nathan Gill; Nicole Decker; Stephen Suchy; Zachary Orban; Millenia Jimenez; Gina Perez Giraldo; Igor J. Koralnik; Manjot K. Gill
paper_title: Non-Hospitalized Long COVID Patients Exhibit Reduced Retinal Capillary Perfusion: A Prospective Cohort Study

summary: Observational cohort study of 114 long COVID patients investigating associations between serum biomarkers (cystatin-c, orosomucoid, arginine derivatives) and long COVID symptoms. Found that cystatin-c may indicate subclinical renal impairment and orosomucoid is associated with fatigue, but this is a cross-sectional biomarker analysis without treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Laszlo Zavori; Tihamer Molnar; Reka Varnai; Andrea Kanizsai; Lajos Nagy; Bence Vadkerti; Balazs Szirmay; Attila Schwarcz; Peter Csecsei
paper_title: Cystatin-c May Indicate Subclinical Renal Involvement, While Orosomucoid Is Associated with Fatigue in Patients with Long-COVID Syndrome

summary: A cross-sectional study of 142 long COVID patients examining immune activation and amino acid metabolism changes associated with persistent symptoms. The study found that women report persistent symptoms more frequently and that alterations in tryptophan and phenylalanine metabolism correlate with symptom severity and recovery, but no treatment or intervention was evaluated.
paper_authors: Talia Piater; Mario Gietl; Stefanie Hofer; Johanna M. Gostner; Sabina Sahanic; Ivan Tancevski; Thomas Sonnweber; Alex Pizzini; Alexander Egger; Harald Schennach; Judith Loeffler-Ragg; Guenter Weiss; Katharina Kurz
paper_title: Persistent Symptoms and IFN-γ-Mediated Pathways after COVID-19

summary: The P4O2 COVID-19 extension is a prospective multicenter cohort study of 95 long COVID patients that includes a nested personalized counseling intervention trial to identify treatable traits and develop tailored therapeutic strategies. Results show persistence of respiratory (78.9%), neurological (68.4%), and fatigue symptoms (67.4%) at 3-6 months post-infection, with female sex and Delta variant infection associated with more persisting symptom categories.
paper_authors: Baalbaki N.; Blankestijn JM; Abdel-Aziz MI; de Backer J.; Bazdar S.; Beekers I.; Beijers RJHCG; van den Bergh JP; Bloemsma LD; Bogaard HJ; van Bragt JJMH; van den Brink V.; Charbonnier JP; Cornelissen MEB; Dagelet Y.; Davies EH; van der Does AM; Downward GS; van Drunen CM; Gach D.; Geelhoed JJM; Glastra J.; Golebski K.; Heijink IH; Holtjer JCS; Holverda S.; Houweling L.; Jacobs JJL; Jonker R.; Kos R.; Langen RCJ; van der Lee I.; Leliveld A.; Mohamed Hoesein FAA; Neerincx AH; Noij L.; Olsson J.; van de Pol M.; Pouwels SD; Rolink E.; Rutgers M.; Șahin H.; Schaminee D.; Schols AMWJ; Schuurman L.; Slingers G.; Smeenk O.; Sondermeijer B.; Skipp PJ; Tamarit M.; Verkouter I.; Vermeulen R.; de Vries R.; Weersink EJM; van de Werken M.; de Wit-van Wijck Y.; Young S.; Nossent EJ; Maitland-van der Zee AH
paper_title: Precision Medicine for More Oxygen (P4O2)—Study Design and First Results of the Long COVID-19 Extension

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluated psychological outcomes (depression, anxiety, PTSD, insomnia) and quality of life in 143 COVID-19 survivors 1-2 months after hospital discharge using standardized screening tools. Mental health symptoms were common (depression 19%, anxiety 27%, PTSD 39%, insomnia 33%) and more frequent in females; worse outcomes were associated with ICU admission and longer hospital stays.
paper_authors: Sofia Pappa; Zafeiria Barmparessou; Nikolaos Athanasiou; Elpitha Sakka; Kostas Eleftheriou; Stavros Patrinos; Nikolaos Sakkas; Apostolis Pappas; Ioannis Kalomenidis; Paraskevi Katsaounou
paper_title: Depression, Insomnia and Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder in COVID-19 Survivors: Role of Gender and Impact on Quality of Life

summary: Retrospective analysis of 2,007 long COVID patients comparing medication use before and after SARS-CoV-2 infection, finding significant increases in chronic medications across multiple drug categories. COVID-19 severity and age >65 were predictors of increased polypharmacy, while vaccination showed protective effects against medication burden.
paper_authors: Antonella Gallo; Marcello Covino; Alice Lipari; Simona Pellegrino; Francesca Ibba; Maria Chiara Agnitelli; Matteo Tosato; Francesco Landi; Massimo Montalto
paper_title: Increase in Chronic Medications and Polypharmacy—The Multifaceted Burden of COVID-19 Disease on Public Health Care

summary: This observational cross-sectional study measured 13 endothelial biomarkers in 68 long COVID patients and matched controls, finding elevated markers of endothelial activation/dysfunction in patients. The study correlates these biomarkers with fatigue, dyspnea, lung diffusion capacity, and functional capacity but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Andreas T. Asimakos; Alice G. Vassiliou; Chrysi Keskinidou; Stavroula Spetsioti; Archontoula Antonoglou; Charikleia S. Vrettou; Panagiotis Mourelatos; Aristidis Diamantopoulos; Maria Pratikaki; Nikolaos Athanasiou; Edison Jahaj; Parisis Gallos; Anastasia Kotanidou; Ioanna Dimopoulou; Stylianos E. Orfanos; Paraskevi Katsaounou
paper_title: Persistent Endothelial Lung Damage and Impaired Diffusion Capacity in Long COVID

summary: Retrospective observational study examining echocardiographic abnormalities in 203 long COVID patients, comparing those with and without dysautonomia. Found that most long COVID patients did not demonstrate cardiac dysfunction on echocardiography, and dysautonomia was not accompanied by structural or functional cardiac alterations.
paper_authors: Laura Tabacof; Jamie Wood; Erica Breyman; Jenna Tosto-Mancuso; Amanda Kelly; Kaitlyn Wilkey; Chi Zhang; David Putrino; Amy Kontorovich
paper_title: Dysautonomia, but Not Cardiac Dysfunction, Is Common in a Cohort of Individuals with Long COVID

summary: This single-center observational study longitudinally evaluated pulmonary function in 140 COVID-19 survivors one year post-infection using spirometry and DLCO testing, stratified by disease severity. While significant improvements in DLCO and TLC were observed over one year, particularly in severe disease patients, this is a passive follow-up study without any treatment intervention and therefore does not meet inclusion criteria for treatment trials.

paper_title: Longitudinal Analysis of Pulmonary Function Impairment One Year Post-COVID-19: A Single-Center Study

summary: This study compared treatment outcomes for post-COVID olfactory dysfunction in 45 long COVID patients treated with anti-neuroinflammatory therapy (um-PEA-LUT plus olfactory training) versus 40 MS patients treated with disease-modifying therapies (DMTs). summary: A prospective cohort study evaluating cardiopulmonary fitness in 2,732 post-COVID patients from a specialized clinic over 26 months, with 97 undergoing exercise testing compared to pre-pandemic controls. Found no significant relationship between VO2 max and post-COVID disability or COVID-19 severity, with cardiac symptoms occurring in only a small percentage of patients.

The study focuses on acute post-intubation sequelae (dysphonia, dyspnea, dysphagia, laryngeal mobility alterations) rather than long COVID syndrome, and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Laryngotracheal Complications after Intubation for COVID-19: A Multicenter Study

summary: Observational multicenter study comparing long COVID symptom prevalence and persistence across different SARS-CoV-2 strains in 308 Italian patients. Found substantial improvements in dyspnea and fatigue at 6-month follow-up, but minimal improvement in mental health and daily functioning domains.

paper_title: Prevalence of Long COVID Symptoms Related to SARS-CoV-2 Strains

summary: This study follows 17 COVID-19 survivors who required ECMO support during acute infection for over one year post-discharge. summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 247 long COVID patients over 15 months to characterize symptom persistence, risk factors, and work ability. At 15-month follow-up, 75% of patients had returned to baseline health status; females had lower work ability and higher psychiatric symptoms, while pre-existing depression was associated with persistent symptoms.

summary: This retrospective cohort study investigates the relationship between malnutrition and adverse clinical outcomes, including post-COVID-19 condition, within 90-180 days after acute COVID-19 infection using propensity score matching. The study finds that patients with malnutrition have significantly higher incidence of hospitalization, mortality, and post-COVID-19 condition compared to those without malnutrition.

The HILT plus kinesiotherapy group showed greater functional improvements than kinesiotherapy alone, with 96.96% of patients completing the 6MWT and performance improvements ranging from 3% to 60%.

paper_title: Follow-Up Analysis of Pulmonary Function, Exercise Capacity, Radiological Changes, and Quality of Life Two Months after Recovery from SARS-CoV-2 Pneumonia

summary: Single-centre observational study assessing respiratory muscle function (MIP/MEP) in 223 COVID-19 survivors at 3-6 months post-discharge. Found 54.3% exhibited respiratory muscle dysfunction associated with prior non-invasive ventilation use and female gender, but this is a descriptive observational study without any treatment intervention.

summary: Retrospective analysis of 152 long COVID patients with pre- and post-COVID autonomic nervous system testing, comparing sympathetic/parasympathetic function before and after infection, with autonomic therapy intervention. The study identifies risk factors for developing post-acute COVID-19 (female sex, older age, sleep apnea, asthma, elevated glucose/cholesterol) but does not test any interventions or treatments.

summary: COVEVOL is a retrospective observational study of 74 COVID-19 patients describing the natural course of symptoms at 6 months post-infection, identifying predictors of symptom persistence. The study found 71.6% experienced persistent symptoms, with older age, higher BMI, and prior hospitalization as risk factors, but no intervention was tested.

paper_title: COVEVOL: Natural Evolution at 6 Months of COVID-19

summary: Retrospective analysis of 428 long COVID patients from a post-COVID outpatient service examining symptom patterns and risk factors. Found that SARS-CoV-2 variants (wild-type vs Alpha B.1.1.7) were associated with different long COVID symptom phenotypes, with female sex and severe COVID-19 course as main risk factors.

paper_title: Infection with SARS-CoV-2 Variants Is Associated with Different Long COVID Phenotypes

summary: Prospective cohort study of 55 long COVID patients followed in family practice (May 2021–July 2022), with SPECT-CT brain imaging in 32 patients showing vascular encephalopathy. No treatment was tested; the study documents clinical phenotypes and natural recovery patterns over 18 months, with no intervention arm.
paper_authors: Marc Jamoulle; Gisele Kazeneza-Mugisha; Ayoub Zayane
paper_title: Follow-Up of a Cohort of Patients with Post-Acute COVID-19 Syndrome in a Belgian Family Practice

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining the prevalence of alternative diagnoses in 110 pediatric patients with suspected long COVID. Found that 47% had alternative somatic/mental diseases, 29% had LC, and 23% remained unclarified; neurological and respiratory symptom clusters were effective at identifying LC cases.

paper_title: High Prevalence of Alternative Diagnoses in Children and Adolescents with Suspected Long COVID—A Single Center Cohort Study

summary: Retrospective analysis of 2,218 patients from the STOP-COVID registry examining long-COVID clinical features and risk factors at three-month follow-up. Identifies chronic fatigue, cough, and brain fog as most common symptoms, with female gender, severe acute COVID-19, dyspnea, and chest pain as significant risk factors.

paper_title: Long-COVID Clinical Features and Risk Factors: A Retrospective Analysis of Patients from the STOP-COVID Registry of the PoLoCOV Study

summary: This retrospective cohort study assessed outcomes of SARS-CoV-2 breakthrough infections in 98 fully vaccinated liver transplant recipients during the Omicron wave. While most had mild disease, 37.5% reported long-lasting symptoms for ≥4 weeks, with older age and female sex identified as risk factors.

paper_title: Clinical Outcomes of SARS-CoV-2 Breakthrough Infections in Liver Transplant Recipients during the Omicron Wave

summary: This cross-sectional study measured SARS-CoV-2-specific antibody levels in COVID-19 convalescents at 5-6 weeks and 5-6 months post-infection, comparing those with and without post-COVID symptoms. The findings show that patients reporting multiple post-infectious symptoms had significantly higher anti-spike and anti-nucleocapsid antibody levels, suggesting dysregulated immune response as a potential mechanism underlying post-COVID syndrome.
paper_authors: Christopher Hackenbruch; Yacine Maringer; Christian M. Tegeler; Juliane S. Walz; Annika Nelde; Jonas S. Heitmann
paper_title: Elevated SARS-CoV-2-Specific Antibody Levels in Patients with Post-COVID Syndrome

summary: This multicenter cohort study tracked gastrointestinal symptoms in 1,266 previously hospitalized COVID-19 survivors over 18 months post-infection using Sankey plots and exponential regression modeling. The study documents the natural recovery trajectory of gastrointestinal symptoms and diarrhea without any intervention, showing declining prevalence over time.
paper_authors: César Fernández-de-las-Peñas; Juan Torres-Macho; Carlos Guijarro; José D. Martín-Guerrero; Oscar J. Pellicer-Valero; Gustavo Plaza-Manzano
paper_title: Trajectory of Gastrointestinal Symptoms in Previously Hospitalized COVID-19 Survivors: The Long COVID Experience Multicenter Study

summary: This study examined anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibody dynamics and cell-free DNA as potential biomarkers for post-COVID syndrome over 12 months in 49 recovered individuals. The paper is primarily an observational immunological characterization study with no treatment intervention evaluated, and functions as a secondary analysis examining biomarkers in an existing cohort rather than testing a therapeutic intervention.

summary: The GENCOV study characterizes risk factors associated with severe COVID-19 and persistent symptoms in 966 Canadian participants. summary: This study performed a 2.5-year follow-up analysis of 110 COVID-19 convalescents to examine the relationship between early immune response (antibodies and T-cells), vaccination status, reinfection rate, and long-term post-COVID symptoms. While the paper is about long COVID, it is an observational cohort study without any intervention—it passively follows patients and measures immune markers associated with symptoms, rather than testing a treatment.
paper_authors: Anna Seller; Christopher Hackenbruch; Juliane S. Walz; Annika Nelde; Jonas S. Heitmann
paper_title: Long-Term Follow-Up of COVID-19 Convalescents—Immune Response Associated with Reinfection Rate and Symptoms

summary: This prospective study evaluates lung ultrasonography (LUS) as a diagnostic tool for assessing lung involvement in 72 patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome, comparing LUS findings with chest CT scans. The study finds strong correlation between LUS and CT findings but does not test any treatment intervention.

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining PASC development rates in patients with hereditary connective tissue diseases using JH-CROWN consortium data. Found that connective tissue disease patients had elevated rates of PASC (9.52%) compared to the overall cohort (2.54%), suggesting a potential risk association.
paper_authors: Maggie L. Bartlett; Daniel Sova; Mahim Jain
paper_title: Hereditary Connective Tissue Diseases and Risk of Post-Acute SARS-CoV-2

summary: A prospective cohort study of 199 long COVID patients followed 26 months post-infection that identified three distinct symptom clusters using cluster analysis. The study demonstrates that symptom clusters persist beyond two years but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

paper_authors: Jared C. Durieux; Sokratis N. Zisis; Christian Mouchati; Danielle Labbato; Marc Abboud; Grace A. McComsey

paper_title: COVID-19 and Cardiovascular Complications: A Follow-Up Study from Tertiary Center

summary: This multi-center cross-sectional survey investigated long COVID prevalence and risk factors in 5,432 healthcare workers from north-eastern Italy during June-August 2022. summary: A 1-year follow-up observational cohort study of 22 COVID-19 survivors compared with 29 healthy controls using resting-state fMRI to examine brain function changes. The study found altered amplitudes of low-frequency fluctuation in multiple brain regions related to mood and sleep regulation, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

paper_title: The predictors of long–COVID in the cohort of Turkish Thoracic Society– TURCOVID multicenter registry

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining glycaemic control changes in type 2 diabetic patients over 6 months following COVID-19 infection. Found persistent impairment of glycaemic control post-infection despite drug titration, with severity correlating to infection severity.
paper_authors: Alekya Vulpala; Prasun Deb; Smitha Nalla
paper_title: Abstract 5
paper_journal: Indian Journal of Endocrinology and Metabolism

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed endocrine dysfunction in 83 COVID-19 recovered individuals 8-20 weeks post-infection, stratified by disease severity. The study found that 44.6% had endocrine dysfunction, most commonly thyroid abnormalities (21.6%) and secondary adrenal insufficiency (18.1%), with no association between COVID severity and dysfunction type.
paper_authors: Phibakordor L. Nonglait; Sv Madhu; Nishant Raizada
paper_title: Abstract 148
paper_journal: Indian Journal of Endocrinology and Metabolism

summary: This retrospective and prospective observational study examines new-onset hyperglycemia in 302 COVID-19 patients during acute hospitalization and at 1-year follow-up. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 complications and metabolic outcomes during active infection, not on long COVID syndrome or post-acute interventions.
paper_authors: Juhi Jamwal; Ashraf Ganaie; Sonaullah Shah; Syed Mudasir Qadri
paper_title: Abstract 107
paper_journal: Indian Journal of Endocrinology and Metabolism

summary: A prospective observational study following 150 COVID-19 patients for 1 year post-discharge to estimate the prevalence of post-COVID symptoms at 1, 3, and 12 months and correlate symptoms with infection severity and inflammatory markers. The study found that 67% had symptoms at 1 month declining to 31% at 1 year, with fatigue, breathlessness, and insomnia being most common, with no significant correlation to initial infection severity.
paper_authors: Akshatha Savith; Ameena Meah; Ramya Shapur Sridhar Murthy; Nidhi Bharat Phal
paper_title: Long-term Health Implications of Coronavirus Disease 2019: A Prospective Study on Post-coronavirus Disease 2019 Symptoms

summary: Prospective observational study of 238 post-COVID patients with rhino-orbital cerebral mucormycosis undergoing surgical treatment (functional endoscopic sinus surgery, craniotomies, maxillofacial surgeries, orbital exenteration). Study describes perioperative challenges, clinical characteristics, and outcomes including 3% 15-day mortality rate, with most patients presenting with difficult airways and poor preoperative general condition.
paper_authors: Pradnya Milind Bhalerao; Shital Mahendra Kuttarmare; Shweta Joshi; Sanyogita Vijay Naik
paper_title: Perioperative Challenges in the Management of Rhino-Orbital Cerebral Mucormycosis

summary: Prospective observational cohort study of 800 COVID-19 patients followed for 6 months post-discharge examining blood sugar abnormalities and diabetes outcomes. Study documents prevalence of transient hyperglycemia (43.75%), new-onset diabetes (8.59%), and aggravation of preexisting diabetes (12.75%), finding associations with inflammatory markers and disease severity, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Shital Patil; Devang Kulkarni; Gajanan Gondhali
paper_title: Does Ongoing Inflammation in Recovered COVID-19 Disease Aggravates Preexistent Diabetes Mellitus or Unmasks New-onset Diabetes Mellitus? A Single-center Experience of 800 Cases at 6-month Follow-up

summary: A prospective cohort study of 60 COVID-19-positive individuals followed for 6 months, stratified by presence or absence of loss of smell/taste, to assess incidence of new-onset psychiatric illness. Found psychiatric illness in 26.7% of those with smell/taste loss versus 6.7% without, with a relative risk of 4, suggesting olfactory/gustatory symptoms may be an early marker for neuropsychiatric sequelae.
paper_authors: MMohamed Ilyas Rahamathulla; S. Shankar
paper_title: Incidence of Psychiatric Illness Among COVID-19-Positive Individuals with and Without Loss of Smell or Taste Symptoms in a Tertiary Care Hospital in South India – A Prospective Cohort Study

summary: Prospective observational study following 1,000 COVID-19 patients with lung involvement to assess radiological outcomes at 1-year post-discharge. Of 209 cases with residual lung abnormalities (RLAs), 72.24% showed resolving findings, 19.61% persistent, and 8.13% progressive, with significant associations between RLA severity and baseline clinical parameters.
paper_authors: Shital Patil; Devang Kulkarni; Abhishek Vairagade; Gajanan Gondhali
paper_title: Radiological Outcomes in Recovered COVID-19 Pneumonia Cases at 1-year Follow-up: The “Post-COVID-19 Lung Study” in Dedicated COVID-19 Care Setting in India

summary: Descriptive cross-sectional study of 72 long COVID patients at a rural tertiary care center documenting clinical manifestations and symptom burden. No active treatment or intervention was tested; the study passively records existing symptoms and outcomes in a patient cohort without assigning any intervention.
paper_authors: Satish Reddy; Vasantha Kamath; Josna Ganesh Teli; Nisha Davy Olakkengil; Buvana Radhakrishnan; Kushal Markanday
paper_title: Study of Post COVID-19 Sequelae at a Tertiary Rural Health Care Center

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 131 COVID-19 survivors assessed at 6+ months post-infection to determine incidence of glucose intolerance and new-onset diabetes and identify risk factors. Found 39% had dysglycemia, with age, BMI, and comorbidities as significant predictors, but this is an observational study with no treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Jonita Fernandes; Alphonsa Mary; Aanchal Sebastian; Franciosalgeo George; Jyothi Idiculla
paper_title: Predictors of New Onset Dysglycemia Post COVID-19

summary: Longitudinal follow-up study assessing persistent symptoms in healthcare workers who recovered from COVID-19, evaluating symptom prevalence and quality of life impact. Found respiratory and cardiovascular systems most affected, with fatigue and weakness being common manifestations.
paper_authors: Sreelatha, P; Suresh, Roopa; Reddy, Ac Sanjay; Reddy, Yj Visweswara; Dhananjaya, Pe; Hashmath, ArshiyaSehar
paper_title: Long COVID 19 – Persistent and Longitudinal Symptoms in Covid Infected Health Care Personnel

summary: Prospective cohort study of 152 COVID-19 patients followed for 6 months to characterize long COVID symptoms and identify risk factors. Found neurological, respiratory, and musculoskeletal symptoms most common, with female sex, sedentary lifestyle, high BMI, and comorbidities as significant risk factors.
paper_authors: Sudha Bala; Surendra Babu Darivemula; Venkatesham Animalla; Rajiv Kumar Bandaru
paper_title: Long Coronavirus Disease 2019 Sequel among Cohorts Admitted to a Tertiary Care Hospital, Hyderabad

summary: A retrospective case series evaluating the impact of 6-8 week outpatient pulmonary rehabilitation on 30 moderate-to-severe COVID-19 survivors with long COVID symptoms. The program showed significant improvements in subjective quality of life scores and objective measures including 6-minute walk distance, dyspnea scales, oxygenation, and muscle strength (p<0.001), though spirometry improvements were not statistically significant.
paper_authors: Manoj Kumar Singh; Kavithakani Annamalai
paper_title: Impact of Pulmonary Rehabilitation on Recuperation of Moderate-to-Severe Coronavirus Disease 2019 Patients in Western India

summary: A prospective observational cohort study evaluating pulmonary function, exercise capacity, and health-related quality of life in 85 COVID-19 survivors at 3 and 6 months post-infection. The study found significant reductions in diffusing capacity and exercise capacity at 6 months compared to healthy controls, with substantial impairment in health-related quality of life.
paper_authors: Doaa M. Magdy; Ahmed Metwally; Doaa Abdel Tawab; Shimaa Abaas Hassan; Marwa Makboul; Shimaa Farghaly
paper_title: Long-term COVID-19 effects on pulmonary function, exercise capacity, and health status

summary: Cross-sectional study evaluating neuropsychiatric manifestations in 106 post-COVID patients presenting to psychiatric and medicine outpatient clinics. Found anxiety disorders, depression, adjustment disorders, fatigue, and myalgia as prevalent late sequelae of COVID infection, with neurological symptoms more common in older patients with comorbidities.
paper_authors: Pasupuleti, Sreelatha; Suresh, Roopa; Reddy, Sanjay; Reddy, Yj Visweswara
paper_title: Neuropsychiatric manifestations in post-COVID patients in second wave of pandemic

summary: This prospective study assessed the prevalence of major depressive disorder (MDD) among COVID-19 survivors at hospital discharge and 1 month post-discharge using the PHQ-9 questionnaire. While the paper does study mental health outcomes in COVID survivors, it focuses on acute COVID hospitalization effects rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-months post-infection), and it is an observational study without any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Kajalpreet Kaur; Vishal Kanaiyalal Patel; Parveen Kumar; Disha Alkeshbhai Vasavada; Lubna Mohammedrafik Nerli; Deepak Sachidanand Tiwari
paper_title: A prospective study of major depressive disorder among COVID 19 survivors at a tertiary care hospital

summary: A prospective observational study following 106 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors for up to 2 years to assess long-term radiological and pulmonary function outcomes. The study found that 22.6% of patients had residual radiological abnormalities including fibrosis, with significant improvements in lung function parameters by 2 years except for exercise tolerance.
paper_authors: Sadia Imtiaz; Enas M. Batubara; Mohammed H. Abuelgasim; Mahdi M. Alabad; Lujain Mahmoud Alyousef; Nayef H. Alqahtani; Alaa Y. Sabbagh; Fawaz A. Alharbi; Ahmed S. Ibrahim
paper_title: Long-term outcome of pulmonary involvement in patients with coronavirus disease 2019: The role of high-resolution computed tomography and functional status – A prospective single-center observational study

summary: This prospective study compared gastrointestinal manifestations in 100 children with confirmed COVID-19 versus 98 with suspected but negative COVID-19 infections, collected from June 2020 to April 2021 with follow-up in August 2024. At 3.9-year median follow-up, the study found no higher incidence of chronic GI symptoms in the post-COVID extended phase, though diarrhea was more common during acute infection in COVID-positive children.
paper_authors: Chinta Annie Jyothirmayi; Leenath Thomas; Jayendra Seetharaman; Mahesh Moorthy; Arul Premanand Lionel
paper_title: Gastrointestinal Manifestations and Long-term Outcomes of Symptomatic COVID-19 Infection in Children: A Prospective Study from a Tertiary Center in Southern India

summary: A prospective cohort study evaluating post-COVID sequelae on male reproductive function in 57 male COVID-19 patients, measuring semen parameters and hormone levels at 1 and 3 months post-discharge. The study found significant changes in sperm concentration, motility, and hormone levels correlated with disease severity, but this is an observational study with no intervention or treatment being tested.
paper_authors: Mohamed S. Mousa; Mostafa Elshazly; Mohamed A. Abd El Salam; Salwa H. Ahmed
paper_title: Post-coronavirus disease 2019 sequelae on male-reproductive functions
paper_journal: The Egyptian Journal of Chest Diseases and Tuberculosis

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed clinical patterns and quality of life impacts in 115 post-COVID patients at 3 months post-infection. The study found dyspnea, fatigue, and muscle/joint pain as most prevalent post-COVID manifestations, with significant quality of life impairment particularly in severe cases.
paper_authors: Ashraf Zin EL-Abdeen Mohamed; Lamiaa Hassan Shaaban; Mostafa Mahmoud Attia; Waleed Gamal Elddin Khaleel
paper_title: Post-COVID syndrome: Clinical pattern and impact on health related quality of life
paper_journal: The Egyptian Journal of Chest Diseases and Tuberculosis

summary: This case-control study of 669 COVID-19 survivors compared 169 patients with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PACS) to 500 without PACS to identify risk factors and predictive biomarkers. Older age, male sex, smoking, diabetes, and elevated inflammatory markers (CRP, D-dimer, ferritin, LDH) were associated with higher PACS risk, but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Wafaa Abdelwahab; Manal M.R. Algharbawy; Lucy A. Suliman; Magdy Emara; Mohammed A. Ibrahim
paper_title: Predictors of postacute coronavirus disease 2019 syndrome an experience of 669 patients
paper_journal: The Egyptian Journal of Chest Diseases and Tuberculosis

summary: This observational cohort study followed 100 COVID-19 patients for 3 months post-discharge, assessing pulmonary function via spirometry and DLCO testing, along with chest HRCT imaging. The study found significant long-term pulmonary sequelae including restrictive patterns (14.9%), obstructive patterns (17.8%), and combined defects (5.9%), with DLCO abnormalities being the strongest predictor of severe respiratory impairment during recovery.
paper_authors: Yasser Mostafa; Mahmoud M.M. Khalil; Sherif N.A. Hegazy; Marwa S. Daif
paper_title: The outcome of pulmonary function tests and high-resolution computed tomography of chest in post-coronavirus disease 2019-confirmed cases after 3 months of recovery
paper_journal: The Egyptian Journal of Chest Diseases and Tuberculosis

summary: Prospective cohort study following 137 COVID-19 survivors for 6 months to assess immune responses, laboratory markers, and CT imaging changes. Found gradual improvement in inflammatory markers and CT abnormalities over follow-up but no intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Shereen Bahgat; Aya M. Abdelhamid; Osama A. Gaber; Noha M. Abdelsalam; Rasha M. B. Eldin
paper_title: Comprehensive evaluations of coronavirus disease 2019 survivors regarding immunity, laboratory and computed tomography change
paper_journal: The Egyptian Journal of Chest Diseases and Tuberculosis

summary: This prospective cohort study followed 35 ESRD patients on maintenance hemodialysis for 12 months after COVID-19 infection to assess long-term thrombotic and neuropsychiatric complications. The study found elevated D-dimer levels, high vascular access thrombosis incidence (25.7%), and very high prevalence of depression (94.3%) and anxiety (85.7%) symptoms in post-COVID ESRD patients.

paper_title: The effect of coronavirus disease 2019 severity on male sexual functions among patients on follow-up after hospital discharge

summary: This prospective cross-sectional study examined 146 post-COVID patients 30 days after acute infection to investigate associations between inflammatory markers (D-dimer, CRP) and pericardial effusion. summary: Retrospective analysis of foetomaternal outcomes in pregnant women with acute COVID-19 who underwent caesarean section between April-June 2021. While some patients experienced post-discharge fatigue and myalgia, the study focuses on acute COVID-19 complications during pregnancy and does not address long COVID or test any treatments.
paper_authors: Sandeep K. Yadav; Soumya S. Nath; Neetu Singh; Samiksha Parashar; Smarika Mishra; Deepak Malviya
paper_title: Study of foetomaternal outcomes in COVID-19 afflicted parturients who underwent operative delivery - A retrospective analysis

summary: Single-center prospective observational study of 1,954 COVID-19 survivors followed up at 1 year post-recovery to assess musculoskeletal symptoms and functional status. Found 55.6% had MSK symptoms (most commonly fatigue, myalgia, backache, joint pain), with symptomatic COVID-19 patients showing higher incidence and greater functional limitations than non-MSK group.

paper_title: Musculoskeletal Symptoms and Post-COVID Functional Status among COVID-19 Survivors: A Single-Center Prospective Observational Study

summary: This retrospective cohort study identifies risk factors for persistent diffuse parenchymal lung abnormalities in patients recovering from severe COVID-19 pneumonia. The study found that longer hospital stay was the only independent predictor of lung abnormalities at 6 months, and elevated baseline TGF-β levels were associated with persistent disease.

summary: Retrospective cross-sectional study following 132 hospitalized mild-to-moderate COVID-19 patients to characterize post-COVID symptoms and recovery times. Found that 80.35% experienced post-acute symptoms (cough, breathlessness, fatigue predominant), with delayed recovery associated with older age, female gender, and moderate disease severity.

paper_title: Post-COVID symptoms and recovery times in hospitalized mild and moderate COVID-19 patients

summary: Prospective observational study of 1,000 acute COVID-19 pneumonia patients examining ferritin as a biomarker for disease severity and lung fibrosis prediction during hospitalization. While the abstract mentions "long-term effects on lung functions" and post-COVID lung fibrosis, the study focuses on acute COVID-19 pneumonia management and severity assessment, not on long COVID patients or interventions.

summary: A retrospective cohort study analyzing risk factors for development of pulmonary fibrosis in post-COVID-19 patients using baseline and follow-up CT imaging over 3-6 months. The study identified old age, smoking, comorbidities, low oxygen saturation, prolonged hospitalization, lymphopenia, and disease severity as independent risk factors for fibrosis development, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Shruti Thakur; Anupam Jhobta; Sai Kalyani; Sunil Sharma; Charu S. Thakur
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 pulmonary fibrosis with prognostic risk factors: A study in the hilly state of North India
paper_journal: The Journal of Association of Chest Physicians

summary: Prospective observational study assessing pulmonary function tests (spirometry and DLco) in 96 COVID-19 survivors at 6-month follow-up. Most survivors had normal lung function, but 33.3% showed reduced DLco and restrictive patterns correlated with initial disease severity.
paper_authors: Jimit Mistry; Ankita Kumari; Sunil Kumar; Manish Advani; Chandra Shekhar Purohit; Harsh Vyas
paper_title: Assessment of Pulmonary Functions in COVID-19 Survivors and their Clinical Correlation at 6-month Follow-up

summary: This prospective observational study of 1000 acute COVID-19 patients monitors serial IL-6 levels during hospitalization to predict disease severity and lung fibrosis outcomes. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 pneumonia and IL-6 monitoring during active infection, not on long COVID or post-acute sequelae.
paper_authors: Shital Patil; Abhijit Acharya; Gajanan Gondhali; Ganesh Narwade
paper_title: Serial Interleukin-6 Titer Monitoring in COVID-19 Pneumonia
paper_journal: Journal of Association of Pulmonologist of Tamil Nadu

summary: This prospective observational study compared chronic airway obstruction profiles in 164 patients with and without prior COVID-19 history. While radiological findings differed significantly between groups, the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention and primarily characterizes airway disease rather than long COVID-specific sequelae.
paper_authors: Unnati Desai; Ketaki Utpat; Sharad Sable
paper_title: Chronic Airway Obstruction in the Post-COVID-19 Era: Is There a Cause or Effect?

summary: Prospective observational study of 493 post-COVID-19 patients followed between August 2022 and February 2024 to investigate cardiopulmonary complications. Found respiratory complications in 58.42% of patients (mainly ground-glass appearance and interstitial thickening), pulmonary fibrosis in 52.56%, and cardiovascular complications in 32%, with prolonged hospitalization and elevated inflammatory markers as key risk factors.
paper_authors: Sarvesh Satish Bhala; Gajanan Vaijnath Halkanche; Neelima Sreenivas Deshpande
paper_title: Study of Cardiopulmonary Complications in Post-COVID-19 Patients at Tertiary Care Hospitals

summary: Prospective observational cohort study following 322 COVID-19 patients for 6 months to characterize long COVID pulmonary complications. Found that severe/critical cases developed restrictive lung impairment, lung fibrosis (22%), and secondary infections, while mild/moderate cases showed recovery.
paper_authors: Yellapu G. Devi; Pudi D. Rao; Kanaka L. Kotana; Preethi Koyyana
paper_title: Pulmonary sequel of covid-19 infection – 6 month follow-up observational cohort study
paper_journal: Journal of Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluates pulmonary pulse transit time (pPTT) as a diagnostic tool for detecting long-term pulmonary dysfunction in COVID-19 survivors by comparing 102 post-COVID patients (≥1 year post-hospitalization) with 100 healthy controls. The study finds correlations between pPTT and various pulmonary and cardiac measures, suggesting pPTT may be useful for early prediction of pulmonary dysfunction in COVID-19 survivors, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Mustafa Duran; Turgut Uygun; Ercan Kurtipek
paper_title: Assessment of Long-Term Sequelae of Pulmonary Dysfunction Associated with COVID-19 Using Pulmonary Pulse Transit Time

summary: This prospective cohort study followed 349 COVID-19 survivors hospitalized in 2022-2023, assessing musculoskeletal symptoms (myalgia, arthralgia, back pain, fatigue) at 1 and 3 months post-discharge. While 20.1% experienced musculoskeletal pain or fatigue during follow-up with symptoms gradually decreasing over time, no specific treatment intervention was tested; the paper recommends physiotherapy and patient education as potential improvements.
paper_authors: Mohammad Reza Vafaei Nasab; Behnaz Tirandazi; Amin BaradaranFar; Farimah Shamsi
paper_title: Musculoskeletal symptoms in COVID-19 survivors: A brief report on outcomes after 1 and 3 months of hospitalization
paper_journal: Journal of Education and Health Promotion

summary: A follow-up comparative study evaluating the effect of an 8-week selective yoga regime on pulmonary function recovery in 82 COVID-19 survivors with deranged lung function. The intervention showed significant improvements in most spirometry parameters after the yoga rehabilitation program.
