paper_title: A collaborative study on rehabilitating altered pulmonary functions of COVID-19 survivors with selective yoga regime
paper_journal: Journal of Family Medicine and Primary Care

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluated endocrine function abnormalities in 83 COVID-19-recovered individuals (8-20 weeks post-recovery) across hypothalamic-pituitary axes. Fifty-three percent had endocrine dysfunction, with pituitary axis dysfunction (33.7%), thyroid abnormalities (30.1%), and gonadal dysfunction being most common.
paper_authors: Phibakordor L. Nonglait; Srivenkata Madhu; Nishant Raizada; Amitesh Aggarwal; Rafat Ahmed; Mohammad Aslam
paper_title: Abnormalities of Endocrine Function Tests in COVID-19-Recovered Individuals
paper_journal: Indian Journal of Endocrinology and Metabolism

summary: Prospective multicentric study of 600 post-COVID-19 pneumonia patients assessing pulmonary function at 12 weeks post-discharge via spirometry. Found 77.5% had abnormal lung function with restrictive pattern predominant; CT severity, age, gender, and timing of ventilatory support were significant factors.
paper_authors: Shital Patil; Rajesh Patil; Gajanan Gondhali
paper_title: Pulmonary Functions Assessment in Post-COVID-19 Pneumonia Cases by Spirometry
paper_journal: Journal of Applied Sciences and Clinical Practice

summary: Observational study assessing clinical symptoms, pulmonary function, and radiological changes in 75 post-COVID-19 patients with respiratory symptoms 4 weeks to 2 years after acute infection. Study documents high prevalence of restrictive lung patterns, abnormal DLCO, and CT findings but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Nilakantha Behera; Jeetendra Kumar Patra; Bijay Kumar Dash; Manoranjan Pattnaik; Deepak Sahu; Bayyaram Rambhoopal Reddy
paper_title: Clinico-radiological and pulmonary function assessment of post-COVID-19 patients with respiratory symptoms
paper_journal: Journal of Family Medicine and Primary Care

summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 86 patients with diabetic-range hyperglycemia first detected during acute COVID-19 hospitalization to determine if they developed persistent diabetes. Most patients (73.3%) returned to normoglycemic state post-discharge, but 11.6% developed new-onset diabetes and 15.1% developed pre-diabetes.
paper_authors: Ketan Agarwal; Ravi Kirti; Shyama Shyama; Pragya Kumar; Ratnadeep Biswas; Vishnu S. Ojha
paper_title: Long-term outcome of patients with diabetic-range hyperglycemia first detected during admission for COVID-19: A single-center observational study
paper_journal: Journal of Family Medicine and Primary Care

summary: This prospective study compared breakthrough COVID-19 infections in vaccinated healthcare workers (n=401) with unvaccinated cases (n=390) over 78 weeks, finding 5.62% breakthrough incidence with 43.3% asymptomatic cases. The study demonstrates that vaccination reduced post-COVID-19 syndrome incidence from 57.2% in unvaccinated to 17.45% in vaccinated individuals, but does not evaluate any active treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Rajasi RS; Chandran P.; Sivakumar CP; George B.; Amrutha D.; Elizabeth M.; George AM
paper_title: Profile of COVID-19 breakthrough cases and its comparison with unvaccinated COVID-19 cases among healthcare workers in a tertiary care centre in North Kerala
paper_journal: Journal of Family Medicine and Primary Care

summary: This prospective observational study assessed sleep patterns and quality of life in 212 non-hospitalized adults 24 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study found that 17% experienced sleep impairment and all dimensions of quality of life were adversely affected, with demographic and clinical factors influencing outcomes.
paper_authors: Shiv K. Mudgal; Vipin Patidar; Sanjay Kumar; Suman Kumar; Rakhi Gaur; Rajat Agarwal; Seshadri Reddy Varikasuvu; Pratima Gupta; Saurabh Varshney
paper_title: Long-COVID-19 Impact in non-hospitalized patients: Sleep and quality of life 24 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection
paper_journal: Journal of Family Medicine and Primary Care

summary: Retrospective study analyzing clinical, biochemical, and radiological profiles of 514 COVID-19 patients admitted across three pandemic waves at a dedicated COVID hospital in India, examining mortality predictors and outcomes in relation to COVAXIN vaccination status. While long COVID is mentioned as a clinical entity observed during the study period, this is primarily an analysis of acute COVID-19 hospitalization data and vaccination outcomes rather than a treatment intervention study for long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Rao CM; Mohapatra AK; Patnaik AK; Panda PS; Behera PR

paper_title: Manifestations and risk factors of post COVID syndrome among COVID-19 patients presented with minimal symptoms – A study from Kerala, India

paper_title: Supervised hospital based pulmonary rehabilitation outcome in long COVID–experience from a tertiary care hospital

paper_title: Orthopedic Manifestations in Patients of Long COVID-19 Syndrome
paper_journal: Journal of Orthopaedic Diseases and Traumatology

summary: Prospective observational cohort study of 152 COVID-19 patients followed for 6 months to identify new-onset diabetes mellitus and associated risk factors. Found 25% developed new-onset diabetes with significant associations to comorbidities, sedentary lifestyle, tobacco use, and symptomatic COVID presentation.

paper_title: Long COVID-19 “A Metabolic Sequela,” the New-Onset Diabetes among Cohorts Admitted at Tertiary Care Hospital, Hyderabad

paper_title: Profile of Cardiopulmonary Fitness Across Pre- and Post-COVID-19 Confinement in a Cohort of Young Adults
paper_journal: Journal of Pharmacy and Bioallied Sciences

summary: Prospective observational study evaluating cognitive impairment in 120 post-COVID-19 patients using standardized neuropsychological tests (MoCA, TMT, Digit Span) compared to 60 matched controls. paper_title: Cognitive Impairment in Post-COVID-19 Patients: A Prospective Neuropsychological Evaluation Study
paper_journal: Journal of Pharmacy and Bioallied Sciences

summary: This retrospective cohort study examined the frequency of musculoskeletal complications in 100 COVID-19 patients, finding that 27% experienced orthopedic impairments. The analysis identified obesity and diabetes as significant risk factors for musculoskeletal symptoms in patients with chronic COVID-19 syndrome.
paper_authors: Priti R. Sinha; Nitin Mallick; Ramjee L. Sahu
paper_title: Orthopedic Manifestations and Post-COVID-19 Infection
paper_journal: Journal of Pharmacy and Bioallied Sciences

summary: This cross-sectional study of 85 post-COVID patients examined persistent respiratory symptoms and lung function abnormalities using spirometry and clinical assessment. paper_title: Persistent respiratory symptoms and lung function abnormalities in recovered patients of COVID-19

Persistent dyspnea and impaired lung function were common at 2 years, particularly in females and those infected during the delta wave, but no intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Suri TM; Srivastava G.; Kumar S.; Surendranath A.; Shaji S.; Mittal S.; Tiwari P.; Hadda V.; Madan K.; Chauhan A.; Mohan A.
paper_title: Persistent pulmonary impairment after 2 years of COVID-19 infection: An observational study

summary: Prospective follow-up study of 200 COVID-19 patients in India assessing long-term health effects at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months post-recovery. paper_title: Follow-up study of COVID-19 sequelae (FOSCO study)

paper_authors: Nikita Jagtap; Aafia A. Shaikh; Bela Agarwal
paper_title: Association between computed tomography scan findings, lung function, and functional capacity in patients with COVID-19

summary: Prospective descriptive study of 72 COVID-19 patients treated with topical intranasal corticosteroids and olfactory training for post-COVID olfactory dysfunction. Most patients (47.22%) recovered within 3 weeks, with intranasal mometasone spray and olfactory training identified as useful treatment options.
paper_authors: Santosh Kumar Swain; Swaha Panda; Ansuman Sahu; Somya Ranjan Pani
paper_title: Role of Topical Intranasal Corticosteroid for Treatment of Post-COVID Olfactory Dysfunction – Our Experiences

summary: A cross-sectional study that followed 1,902-1,464 COVID-19 patients at 3, 6, and 9 months post-infection to assess the prevalence and types of long COVID sequelae. Found post-COVID sequelae in 5.59%-8.81% of patients, with diabetes being the most common persistent condition.
paper_authors: Sunila Sanjeev Ernam; Daniel Matthews; Runika Gade; Keertana Prabhakar
paper_title: A descriptive study of post-COVID sequelae in mild to severe cases in western India

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing quality of life measures (SF-36) in 125 long COVID patients at two time intervals (3 months and 3-6 months post-infection) from a single COVID-19 follow-up center. The study documents changes in symptoms and QoL but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

paper_title: Investigation of Long-Term COVID-19 Patients’ Quality of Life and Affecting Factors: Data from Single COVID-19 Follow-Up Center

summary: Longitudinal neuroimaging study comparing brain structural changes in COVID-19 patients with and without sleep disturbances versus healthy controls at baseline and 3-month follow-up. paper_title: Persistent alterations in gray matter in COVID-19 patients experiencing sleep disturbances: a 3-month longitudinal study

paper_authors: Kemec Z.; Akgul F.
paper_title: Are Patients with Covid-19 at Risk of Long-Term Chronic Kidney Disease?

summary: This prospective observational study compares perioperative outcomes in neurosurgery patients with prior symptomatic versus asymptomatic COVID-19 infection, conducted 7 months post-infection. While it uses long-COVID terminology, it is fundamentally a surgery outcomes study examining acute perioperative complications rather than long COVID treatments or long-term sequelae management.

paper_title: Perioperative outcomes in patients with symptomatic versus asymptomatic previous COVID-19 infection undergoing neurosurgical treatment (post–COVID-19 study)

summary: Descriptive observational study of 165 post-COVID patients at 3 months post-acute infection, characterizing pulmonary and clinical features including dyspnea, fatigue, and radiological abnormalities. paper_authors: Sheraf, Shahina; Sulaiman, ShajahanP; Bindu, Cg
paper_title: Clinicoradiological profile and predictors of postcoronavirus disease syndrome – Lessons learned and the way forward

paper_title: Long-term recovery from COVID-19 olfactory and gustatory dysfunction: a longitudinal study

paper_title: A Retrospective Observational Study of Neurological Manifestations in COVID-19 (SON-CoV)

summary: Longitudinal cohort study following 42 low-income adults hospitalized for moderate-severe COVID-19, assessing cognitive and behavioral outcomes at 12-18 and 24-30 months post-discharge. Found significant cognitive improvement over two years but persistent neuropsychiatric symptoms including increased anxiety and depression.
paper_authors: Danielle Calil Sousa; Arnaldo Santos Leite; Luiz Gustavo Guimarães Sacramento; Bruna Achtschin Fernandes; Bárbara Caroline Dias Faria; Vinicius Ribeiro Jeunon; Carolina Coimbra Marinho; Paulo Caramelli
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 cognitive changes in low-income and low-educated adults: a longitudinal study

summary: Prospective cohort study following 123 COVID-19 patients for ~2 years to evaluate the incidence and characteristics of chronic daily headache (CDH) as a long COVID symptom. Found 52% experienced persistent headache post-COVID, with 20.3% developing CDH; previous headache and acute-phase severity were risk factors.
paper_authors: Larissa Clementino Leite de Sá Carvalho; Priscila Aparecida da Silva; Pedro Augusto Sampaio Rocha Filho
paper_title: Chronic daily headache after COVID-19: a prospective cohort study

summary: A retrospective cohort study of 174 COVID-19 patients from a Taipei hospital integrated clinic followed for 6 months post-isolation, characterizing symptoms and risk factors of post-COVID condition (PCC). The study documents symptom prevalence (39.7% with PCC) and associations with gender, comorbidities, and acute-phase hospitalization, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: 莊美幸 莊美幸; 侯君穎 Mei-Hsing Chuang
paper_title: 新冠後症候群病人症狀與相關因素 —台北市某醫院新冠肺炎整合門診回溯性研究

summary: Longitudinal follow-up study of 173 long COVID patients assessed at ~6 months and 20 months post-infection using validated questionnaires for fatigue, sleepiness, anxiety, depression, and work capacity. Found worsening of neuropsychiatric symptoms and significant reduction in work ability over time, but this is an observational study with no treatment intervention tested.
paper_authors: Gabriel Monteiro Salvador; Ana Paula Beppler Lazaro Lino; Fernando Cendes; Guilherme Vieira Nunes Ludwig; Hildete Prisco Pinheiro; Marcia Bandini; Clarissa Lin Yasuda
paper_title: Longitudinal analysis of 173 long-COVID subjects reveals worsening of work capacity and neuropsychiatric symptoms 20 months after diagnosis

summary: This longitudinal observational study follows 602 long COVID survivors at three timepoints (7, 20, and 25 months post-infection) to assess neuropsychiatric symptoms and work capacity using standardized questionnaires. The study found persistent fatigue, sleepiness, anxiety, and depression symptoms, with reduced work capacity remaining consistent across all timepoints, but represents a secondary analysis from an existing database rather than a primary treatment intervention trial.
paper_authors: Gabriel Monteiro Salvador; Ana Paula Beppler Lazaro Lino; Fernando Cendes; Márcia Bandini; Clarissa Lin Yasuda
paper_title: Longitudinal analysis reveals the persistence of reduced work capacity and neuropsychiatric symptoms 25 months after infection in post-survivors

summary: A prospective cohort study of 2,535 COVID-19 hospitalized patients followed for one year post-discharge across 16 countries, tracking long COVID symptoms, quality of life, and clinical outcomes. While comprehensive in documenting long COVID burden (56% reported major symptoms at 1 month, 25% at 9-12 months), the study is purely observational with no intervention or treatment evaluation, and therefore does not meet the criteria for inclusion in a treatment trials meta-analysis.

paper_title: Long COVID Syndrome, Mortality and Morbidity in Patients Hospitalized with COVID-19 From 16 Countries: The World Heart Federation Global COVID-19 Study

summary: This retrospective cohort study examined biochemical anomalies (electrolytes, enzymes, kidney/liver markers) in 150 acute COVID-19 patients over 44 weeks. While the paper describes long-term biochemical changes, it focuses on acute infection and post-acute sequelae monitoring rather than evaluating a specific treatment intervention for long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Zarrin Khaliq Chaudari; Muhammad Yaseen; Maria Sarfraz; Maleeha Tahir Butt; Madeeha Jadoon; Sofia Shoukat
paper_title: Spectrum of Biochemical Alterations in Patients with Covid-19
paper_journal: Pakistan Journal of Medical and Health Sciences

summary: A longitudinal prospective study evaluating cognitive and neuropsychiatric changes in 58 long COVID patients at baseline and 6-month follow-up using cognitive testing and psychiatric inventories. Cognitive complaints were associated with depression and anxiety but were not predictive of actual cognitive decline, with improvement observed at 6 months.
paper_authors: Flávia Esper Dahy; Aline de Moura Brasil Matos; Thais Malta Romano; Rosa Maria Nascimento Marcusso; Tatiane Assone; Jorge Casseb; Camila Malta Romano; Augusto César Penalva de Oliveira; Jerusa Smid
paper_title: Cognitive and neuropsychiatric changes related to covid-19 in patients evaluated at a referral center in São Paulo, Brazil.

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 243 patients admitted to Qatar Rehabilitation Institute for inpatient rehabilitation post-COVID-19, assessing functional outcomes using validated instruments (FIM, BBS, DGI, mMRC) at baseline and discharge. IPR resulted in statistically significant improvements across all functional outcome scales, with 98% reduction in respiratory support need and 95% reduction in tracheostomy dependence.
paper_authors: Sami Ullah; Zahra Noureddine; Brijesh Sathian; Krishnaprasad Narayanankutty; Thajus Asirvatham; Muhaiadeen Abubacker; Moustafa Omar; Mohammed Nassir Awadh; Fatima Al-Kuwari; Rafat Saad
paper_title: Rehabilitation and functional outcomes of COVID-19 patients in a rehabilitation hospital in Qatar

summary: Descriptive cohort study following 500 discharged COVID-19 patients in Sri Lanka to document persistent symptoms at one month post-discharge. Found high prevalence of fatigue (63.6%), breathlessness (32.6%), and musculoskeletal pain, highlighting the need for systematic follow-up care but making no treatment interventions.
paper_authors: Wanigasuriya RS; De Silva KR; Dissanayake R.; Indrakumar J.; Matthias AT
paper_title: Unresolved Post-COVID Symptomatology: An Experience from a Tertiary Care Hospital in Sri Lanka

summary: Retrospective cross-sectional study examining the incidence of avascular necrosis (AVN) of the femoral head in 86 patients with COVID-19 history, identifying significant associations with steroid use and specific comorbidities. The study documents a post-COVID complication but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention for long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Saurabh Sharma; Akhil Bhansal; Rehan Khan; Suresh Uikey; Jonsi Tavethia; Anshul Bhadania; Shubh Mehta; Kinjal Solanki; Prahar Darji; Kavya Darji; Kamal Sharma
paper_title: The association of COVID-19 with the development of acute avascular necrosis of the head of the femur, apart from steroid usage

summary: This pilot study compared functional rehabilitation outcomes in 20 post-COVID-19 stroke patients versus 20 non-COVID stroke patients using a mixed prospective/retrospective design with measures including FIM, ARAT, NIHSS, and PCFS. Both groups showed significant functional improvements with rehabilitation, though non-COVID stroke patients demonstrated larger gains, suggesting that additional COVID-19 complications may impair recovery potential in post-COVID stroke.

paper_title: A pilot study comparing the rehabilitation functional outcomes of post-COVID-19 stroke and non-COVID stroke patients: An occupational therapy perspective

summary: A retrospective cohort study of 30 post-COVID-19 patients with persistent dyspnea investigating the relationship between cardiac dysfunction and respiratory symptoms. The study found left ventricular dysfunction in 63.3% of patients and myocardial perfusion defects in 33.3%, suggesting cardiac involvement as a cause of persistent dyspnea in the absence of pulmonary sequelae.
paper_authors: Tuğçe ÇÖLLÜOĞLU; Murat ACAT; Ömer ÖZSARAÇ; Yeşim AKIN; Orhan ÖNALAN
paper_title: Cardiac Involvement is the Reason for Persistent Dyspnea in Post COVID-19 Patients without Pulmonary Sequelae: A Retrospective Study

summary: This study compared neurological symptoms and immune parameters in 95 long COVID patients divided by Gam-COVID-Vac vaccination status. Vaccination was associated with statistically significant reductions in headaches, sleep disturbances, and dizziness (p=0.035) and increased B-lymphocyte counts, suggesting immunization may help mitigate CNS symptoms in post-COVID-19 syndrome.
paper_authors: Saulesh Kurmangaliyeva; Akzhan Madenbayeva; Saltanat Urazayeva; Kristina Baktikulova; Kairat Kurmangaliyev
paper_title: A comparison of Gam-COVID-Vac vaccination and non-vaccination on neurological symptoms and immune response in post-COVID-19 syndrome

summary: This retrospective cohort study examined the incidence of neurological and psychiatric disorders following COVID-19 diagnosis using electronic health records data from June 2021 to December 2021. The study found that 82% of 200 COVID-19 patients received a neurological or psychiatric diagnosis within six months post-infection.
paper_authors: Anand Bakre; Anil Wanjari; Parag Rameshrao Aradhey
paper_title: Neurological complications in COVID 19

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) in 78 mild COVID-19 patients 1-6 months post-recovery. Found that increased urinary urgency and frequency were common post-COVID sequelae, particularly among diabetic patients, but no intervention or treatment was tested.
paper_authors: N. Sudhakar; S. Sree Ranjini; Srilakshmi Giridharan; P. Padmapriya
paper_title: LUTS in COVID-19 sequelae

summary: This follow-up study compares semen parameters in 14 COVID-19 survivors between baseline (6+ months post-infection) and follow-up timepoints to assess long-term effects on male fertility. Results show a significant decrease in semen pH at follow-up (7.9 vs 7.4), but the study is observational without intervention and does not test any treatment.
paper_authors: Christian Christopher Sunnu; Jefry Albari Tribowo; Widya Juwita; Andri Rezano; Reny I’tishom; Supardi Supardi; Ria Margiana
paper_title: long-term impact of COVID-19 infection on semen quality of the COVID-19 survivors

summary: This prospective cohort study followed 321 kidney transplant recipients for 6 months after COVID-19 infection to assess late renal effects. The study found stable glomerular filtration rates but increased proteinuria prevalence post-infection, with no specific treatment intervention tested.
paper_authors: Bruno Teixeira Gomes; Marcos Vinicius de Sousa; Fernanda Garcia Bressanin; Matheus Rizzato Rossi; Marilda Mazzali
paper_title: Late Renal Effects of COVID-19 in Kidney Transplant Recipients: A Single-Center Study

summary: This retrospective cross-sectional study evaluated long-term quality of life and respiratory function in patients with severe COVID-19 at ICU discharge and 12 months post-discharge using the Nottingham Health Profile and Modified Medical Research Council Scale. Although statistically significant improvements were detected at 12 months, patients remained substantially impaired across multiple domains including pain, emotional well-being, sleep, social isolation, and physical activity.
paper_authors: Sinem Berik Safçi; Gülşah Yaşa Öztürk; Tarık Salcan
paper_title: A New Beginning After Severe COVID-19: Long-Term Quality of Life Study

summary: Retrospective observational study comparing healthcare utilization in 132 COVID-19 patients from Brunei's first wave before and after infection, with 12 months of follow-up. Found significantly increased healthcare visits post-COVID (mean 5.0 visits) compared to pre-COVID, but attributed primarily to scheduled post-COVID follow-up visits rather than disease-related complications.
paper_authors: Muhammad Syafiq Abdullah; Rosmonaliza Asli; Pui Lin Chong; Babu Ivan Mani; Natalie Riamiza Momin; Noor Affizan Rahman; Chee Fui Chong; Vui Heng Chong
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 health-care utilization: one year after the 2020 first wave in Brunei Darussalam
paper_journal: Western Pacific Surveillance and Response Journal

summary: Prospective observational study following 995 hospitalized COVID-19 patients at 6, 12, and 18 months post-discharge to estimate long COVID prevalence and identify risk factors. Found >40% had at least one symptom at 18 months, with remdesivir treatment and complete vaccination associated with lower long COVID rates.
paper_authors: Petrakis V.; Rafailidis P.; Terzi I.; Dragoumani I.; Markatou F.; Papanas N.; Vradelis S.; Gouveri E.; Panopoulou M.; Papazoglou D.; Periklis P.
paper_title: The prevalence of long COVID-19 syndrome in hospitalized patients with COVID-19 pneumonia

summary: This retrospective cohort study evaluated cognitive functions and dementia in 64 COVID-19 survivors two years after hospitalization, finding cognitive impairment in 25% of patients and new-onset dementia in 12.5%. The study identified age, pre-existing neurological comorbidity, and anxiety as independent risk factors for cognitive impairment but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Hatice Yuksel; Ebru Bilge Dirik; Gorkem Tutal Gursoy; Hesna Bektas; Levent Yamanel; Rahmet Guner
paper_title: Evaluation of cognitive functions and dementia two years after COVID-19 infection

summary: This study evaluates the effects of a 3-month supervised physical rehabilitation program (PRP) on muscle strength and exercise capacity in 28 post-COVID-19 patients. Results show significant improvements in peripheral and respiratory muscle strength, cardiorespiratory fitness, and exercise tolerance following the intervention.
paper_authors: Luana dos Passos Vieira; Elisabete Antunes San Martin; Sophia Luiza Eich; Cecilia Vieira Prestes; Luiza Scheffer Dias; Grenita Hall; Andrea Lucia Gonçalves da Silva
paper_title: Exercise capacity in COVID-19 surviving patients: impact of physical rehabilitation

summary: Post hoc analysis of 1,500 medical records from a Russian hospital examining neurological manifestations of post-COVID syndrome from July 2020 to February 2022. Identified 455 patients with post-COVID neurological disorders, primarily affecting the central nervous system (91.6%), but this is a passive retrospective chart review with no intervention or treatment being tested.
paper_authors: Larisa A. Shchepankevitch; Ivan E. Arkhipov; Veronika V. Polyanskaya; Ivan A. Veretelnikov; Elena V. Taneeva; Ksenya V. Rerikh
paper_title: Post-Covid disorders of nervous system: personal experience
paper_journal: Annals of Clinical and Experimental Neurology

summary: This prospective observational study assessed the prevalence and types of chronic neuropathic pain in 150 post-COVID patients, comparing mild/moderate versus severe disease groups. The study found that 53.3% of patients experienced neuropathic pain, with significantly higher prevalence (65%) and severity in those who had severe initial COVID-19 infection.

paper_title: CHRONIC NEUROPATHIC PAIN IN POST COVID PATIENTS RELATION WITH DISEASE SEVERITY
paper_journal: Biological and Clinical Sciences Research Journal

summary: This multi-center retrospective study analyzes cardiovascular sequelae in COVID-19 survivors using electronic health records, echocardiography, electrocardiography, and biomarker analysis across diverse demographics. Findings reveal significant long-term cardiovascular complications including myocardial injury, arrhythmias, and thrombotic events, with greater risk in older adults and those with pre-existing cardiovascular conditions.
paper_authors: Ayesha Imtiaz; AA KHAN; SA RAJA; SF KHAN; ASM Nawshad Uddin Ahmed; Rizwana Raheel
paper_title: LONG-TERM CARDIOVASCULAR EFFECTS OF COVID-19: A COMPARATIVE STUDY
paper_journal: Biological and Clinical Sciences Research Journal

summary: This study examines the relationship between lymphocytopenia (low lymphocyte count) and the persistence of long COVID symptoms in recovered COVID-19 patients over a 3-8 month period. paper_authors: Yifei Li
paper_title: The effects of lymphocytopenia over the next three to eight months in patients who experience COVID-19 persistent symptoms

summary: A 1-year retrospective cohort study of 66 post-COVID-19 patients with persistent cough who received systematic investigation and treatment at a specialist cough clinic. One-third of patients had persistent cough at 12 months, with airway eosinophilia and abnormal laryngeal sensation identified as key factors associated with cough persistence.
paper_authors: Sang Pyo Lee; Sung-Yoon Kang
paper_title: Clinical outcomes of persistent cough following coronavirus disease 2019 infection: A 1-year retrospective cohort study

summary: Prospective observational study comparing high-resolution CT chest findings in severe COVID-19 patients from admission to 5-week follow-up, stratified by steroid exposure. While it documents radiological changes in the recovery phase (including persistent bronchiectasis and fibrosis), it is an observational imaging assessment without any intervention or treatment being tested.
paper_authors: Niraj Puri; Shital Adhikari; Madhur Dev Bhattarai; Basanta Gauli; Sailesh Gurung; Sunil Patel; Pratik Wagley; Deepak Adhikari; Bigyan Paudel
paper_title: HIGH RESOLUTION COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY CHEST FINDINGS DURING ADMISSION AND FOLLOW-UP IN SEVERE COVID-19 INFECTION

summary: Prospective observational study evaluating lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) in 85 COVID-19 patients across infection severity groups at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months post-infection. paper_title: Longitudinal Evaluation of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms up to Six Months after COVID-19 Infection in a Jordanian Cohort

summary: This cross-sectional study compared reaction time, psychomotor speed, and concentration in 56 individuals with prior COVID-19 infection versus 56 healthy controls. The COVID-19 group showed significantly longer reaction times and reduced psychomotor speed, but this is an observational assessment study without any intervention or treatment provided.
paper_authors: Furkan Bodur; Deniz Senol; Demet Senol; Cenk Ozer
paper_title: Analysis of reaction time, psychomotor speed and concentration levels in individuals who had COVID-19 infection

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines acute kidney injury (AKI) in COVID-19 patients during acute infection, identifying hypoalbuminemia as a risk factor for non-recovery. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 complications rather than long COVID sequelae.
paper_authors: enver ksel; derya nta
paper_title: Acute Kidney Injury Following COVID-19 and Risk factors for Progression to Chronic Kidney Disease

summary: A retrospective cohort study of 1,534 long COVID patients examining whether antivirals, IL-6 inhibitors, monoclonal antibodies, and corticosteroids given during acute COVID-19 reduce subsequent long COVID symptoms. paper_title: Administration of antivirals, IL-6 inhibitors, monoclonal neutralizing antibodies and systemic corticosteroids in acute SARS-CoV-2 infection do not reduce the subsequent burden of Long-COVID symptoms

summary: This cross-sectional study examines the correlation between spirometry measurements and CT imaging findings in post-COVID-19 patients hospitalized during 2020-2021, assessed one year after infection. paper_authors: Vázquez Pérez M.; Torres San Miguel GP; Torres San Miguel CR; Sevilla González M. L.

summary: This retrospective cohort study compared dermatological conditions between COVID-19 patients and non-COVID controls from 2020-2022, finding mostly reduced risk for common skin conditions but increased pallor in COVID-19 patients. summary: Prospective cohort study comparing COVID-19 outcomes, vaccine response, and long COVID incidence between IMID patients and healthy controls during the pandemic. While the paper includes long COVID analysis, it is primarily a secondary analysis of a larger vaccination/immunosuppression study rather than a treatment intervention trial.
paper_authors: Laura Boekel
paper_title: COVID-19 in patients with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases

summary: This study followed 100 acute COVID-19 patients for 12 months to assess ECG changes during acute infection and arrhythmia incidence in the post-COVID period. paper_authors: Zekeriya Doğan; Çiğdem İleri
paper_title: Acute ECG changes and post-COVID arrhythmia incidence in patients with acute COVID-19 infection

summary: This retrospective cohort study uses electronic health records from 4,437 COVID-19 patients matched with 4,437 controls to examine the incidence of neurological and psychiatric diagnoses over 4 years post-infection. The study is excluded because it is an observational epidemiological study documenting disease prevalence in COVID-19 survivors, not a treatment intervention trial.
paper_authors: Majed Ramadan; Lara Malaka; Remaz Ghabrah; Aljodi Sulimani; Farah Aljadani; Lama Al Dosari; Rawiah Alsiary
paper_title: Risk of neurological and psychiatric diagnoses in COVID-19 survivors: A multicenter retrospective cohort study using electronic health records

summary: Retrospective analysis of 262 emergency department presentations >14 days post-COVID-19 infection, documenting symptom patterns and hospitalization outcomes. Study describes disease burden and clinical evolution rather than evaluating any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Silvia Nica; Adriana Albu; Remus Nica; Catalina Ciornei; Florina Cofaru; Irina Eremia; Danut Cimponeriu
paper_title: Addressability to the Emergency Department of patients with acute post-COVID 19 clinical symptoms

Found that electrophysiological severity correlated with functional outcomes (muscle strength and daily living scores) at baseline, 1 month, and 6 months, suggesting early electrophysiological assessment can predict short- to medium-term recovery.

summary: Prospective observational study of 785 post-acute COVID-19 patients examined 4-12 weeks after infection, assessing pulmonary function tests and symptom persistence across disease severity groups. Found dyspnoea, anosmia, and PFT decline correlated with acute disease severity, with females experiencing more persistent symptoms.
paper_authors: Samuel Genzor; Petr Jakubec; Milan Sova; Jan Mizera; Pavol Joppa; Radim Burget; Pavol Pobeha
paper_title: Clinical presentation and pulmonary function tests in post-acute COVID-19 patients

summary: This retrospective-prospective study examined thyroid function in 160 post-COVID-19 patients at two, four, and eight weeks post-infection. While the paper documents thyroid dysfunction as a post-COVID complication, it is observational without any intervention or treatment being tested.
paper_authors: Abid Ali Khawaj; Sabahat Asghar; Samman Khurshid; Noreen Taj; Rubina Faisal Paul; Fozia Jehangir

summary: An observational cross-sectional study assessing the status of ojus (Ayurvedic concept of vital essence) and prakriti (constitutional type) in 71 post-COVID subjects. The study documents radiological sequelae (35% developed fibrotic-like changes) but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

paper_title: Pulmonary fibrotic-like changes on follow-up chest CT exam in patients recovering from COVID-19 pneumonia

summary: This cross-sectional study describes neurological sequelae in 50 mild COVID-19 patients at a mean of 99 days post-infection, finding headache and cognitive dysfunction as the most frequent complaints. The study is observational/descriptive with no intervention or treatment evaluation, making it ineligible for a treatment trials meta-analysis.

paper_title: Subacute neurological sequelae in mild COVID-19 outpatients

Found abnormal EMG findings in 75% of patients, including sensorimotor axonal polyneuropathy, acute polyneuropathy, myopathy, and entrapment neuropathy; critical illness neuropathy and myopathy were most common in mechanically ventilated patients.

This observational study surveyed 256 COVID-19 hospitalized patients with persistent symptoms to identify risk factors for long COVID development. summary: This cross-sectional study assessed quality of life and its determinants in 173 long COVID patients referred to a pulmonary rehabilitation center, using SF-36 questionnaire and physical/psychological evaluations. The study identified predictors of impaired QoL (low exercise capacity, poor psychosocial status, fatigue, young age, male sex) but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Seher Satar; Mustafa Engin Şahin; Pınar Ergün
paper_title: Health related quality of life and its determinants in COVID-19 patients

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed clinical, functional, and radiological outcomes in 126 COVID-19 survivors at three months post-discharge, examining persisting symptoms and imaging changes. It found that 64.6% of patients had persistent pulmonary pathologies, primarily fibrotic-like changes (44.2%) and ground-glass opacities, with dyspnea being the most common symptom, but no treatment intervention was tested.

paper_title: Clinical and radiological outcomes of long-COVID: Is the post-COVID fibrosis common?

summary: This prospective study evaluated 30 long COVID patients undergoing pulmonary rehabilitation, measuring changes in dyspnea (MRC scale) and functional independence (FIM). Patients showed positive functional outcomes post-rehabilitation, though some symptoms persisted, suggesting need for continuous monitoring.

paper_title: Long-COVID: symptomatic and functional analysis post pulmonary rehabilitation

summary: Prospective observational study following 1,234 COVID-19 patients in Northern India for a median of 91 days to describe clinical features and risk factors of post-COVID sequelae. Found that 40.1% had persistent symptoms, with myalgia, fatigue, and dyspnea most common; hospitalization, hypothyroidism, and hypoxia during acute illness were identified as risk factors.

paper_title: Post COVID-19 sequelae: A prospective observational study from Northern India

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 53 mild COVID-19 patients followed up at 30 days post-discharge to identify clinical predictors of persistent symptoms and symptom phenotypes. Found diarrhea at presentation and longer gap between symptom onset and admission were associated with persistence of symptoms (mainly fatigue, cough, myalgias), but this is a passive observational follow-up without any intervention given.
paper_authors: Neha Chopra; Mohit Chowdhury; Anupam K. Singh; Khan MA; Arvind Kumar; Piyush Ranjan; Devashish Desai; Naveet Wig
paper_title: Clinical predictors of long COVID-19 and phenotypes of mild COVID-19 at a tertiary care centre in India

summary: Observational study comparing respiratory and physical function outcomes 14 days post-discharge between patients with delta VOC versus ancestral SARS-CoV-2 infection. Found residual imaging abnormalities in 56.5% of patients but no significant differences between variant groups.

paper_title: Post-hospitalisation respiratory and physical functions in patients with SARS-CoV-2 delta
paper_journal: The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease

summary: A retrospective study of 30 sailors with persistent haematological changes after COVID-19, examining WBC count and differential patterns at long-term follow-up. The study documents typical laboratory changes (neutrophilia, lymphopenia, leukopenia patterns) in post-COVID syndrome but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Oleksandr Ignatyev; Oleksii Panyita; Tetiana Prutiian; Pavel Kostromin
paper_title: Haematological changes in sailors who had COVID-19

summary: This retrospective cohort study examined 162 COVID-19 patients 6 months post-infection to assess associations between continued angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor (ACEI) or angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) use and long-term clinical outcomes. ARB users showed significantly lower fatality rates and lower prevalence of in-hospital adverse outcomes, though no intervention was administered—the study passively observed outcomes by medication use status.

paper_title: COVID-19 clinical outcomes in patients with and without ongoing therapy with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors or angiotensin II receptor blockers

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluated 172 patients with mild-to-moderate COVID-19 at a neurology clinic to assess post-COVID neurological symptoms during the post-infectious phase. Results showed 51.7% reported at least one persistent neurological symptom, with hyposmia/anosmia, chronic fatigue, and dysgeusia being most frequent.

summary: A single-center cross-sectional study of 914 outpatients evaluated cardiovascular symptoms and abnormalities at median 126 days post-COVID-19, comparing patients with different severity of acute infection. The study found associations between initial COVID-19 severity and persistent cardiovascular symptoms (dyspnea, chest pain, fatigue) plus subtle cardiac alterations on follow-up testing.

paper_title: Study on the utility and efficacy of clinical and instrumental tests in the follow-up of COVID-19 patients

Results show significant improvement in olfactory VAS scores over time, with 50% achieving full recovery and only 1 patient showing no recovery.
paper_authors: Sümeyra Doluoğlu
paper_title: Evaluation of long-term results of olfactory training for persistent olfactory dysfunction after COVID-19 infection

summary: This retrospective cohort study tracked the course of fatigue symptoms in 204 previously hospitalized COVID-19 patients at multiple timepoints (0-4 weeks, 4-12 weeks, >12 weeks post-infection). summary: Retrospective observational study examining temporal patterns of neurological manifestations in 905 COVID-19 patients with 6-month follow-up across Pakistani centers. Study describes symptom evolution over time but does not test or evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Sajid Hameed; Bashir Soomro; Samar Iltaf; Abdul Malik; Anjum Farooq; Alam Ibrahim Siddiqui; Safia Awan; Mohammad Wasay
paper_title: Short, medium and long term neurological manifestations and outcome in Covid-19 Patients

summary: A prospective longitudinal study characterizing ophthalmological manifestations in 90 COVID-19 recovered patients followed at a national convalescent care clinic from February 2021 to June 2023. The study found that 25.5% of patients presented ocular diseases, with conjunctivitis and dry eye being most common, and noted that some conditions improved over time while others persisted.

Found that 63.2% of patients experienced CPD exacerbations in the first 6 months post-COVID, with most occurring in the first 3 months; most frequent complaints were weakness, cough, and dyspnea during the post-COVID period.

summary: This retrospective cohort study compares postoperative complications in 30 CABG patients with prior COVID-19 infection versus 30 without COVID history. Patients with prior COVID-19 experienced higher rates of bleeding, prolonged extracorporeal circulation, and late complications including cardiac arrhythmias and CHF, suggesting elevated perioperative risk.

paper_title: Mid- to long-term cardiac magnetic resonance findings in elite athletes recovered from COVID-19: results from an ongoing observational COVID-19 study at a German Olympic medical centre

summary: Observational analytical cohort study comparing psychocognitive status in 223 elderly patients with atrial fibrillation and comorbidities, stratified by presence/absence of post-COVID syndrome. Found higher rates of cognitive dysfunction and anxiety-depressive syndrome in patients with post-COVID syndrome compared to controls without prior SARS-CoV-2 infection.
paper_title: PSYCHOCOGNITIVE STATUS OF COMORBID ELDERLY PATIENTS IN THE POST-COVID PERIOD

summary: This retrospective cohort study examined neuropsychiatric symptoms and psychotropic medication use among nursing home residents with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection (73.9% of 111 participants) compared to uninfected residents at 3-month follow-up. No significant changes in neuropsychiatric symptoms were observed during follow-up, though infected residents had higher psychotropic medication prescriptions, particularly antidepressants and antipsychotics.

summary: Retrospective study examining echocardiographic parameters in COVID-19 patients over a two-year follow-up period, assessing cardiac function recovery. While documenting natural recovery of cardiac measures post-infection, the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Abdolhamid Bagheri; Mohammad Khani; Parisa Atarodian
paper_title: Long-Term Echocardiographic Findings in COVID-19 Patients: Insights from a Two-Year Follow-up Study

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in 194 Iranian COVID-19 patients at six months post-infection using the EQ-5D-3L questionnaire. While it documents significant impairment in HRQoL after acute COVID-19 recovery, it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Dena Firouzabadi; Laleh Mahmoudi; Maryam Kadkhodamohammadi; Ramin Niknam; Ali Amanati
paper_title: Health-Related Quality of Life (HRQoL) in COVID-19 Patients After Recovering from the Acute Infection

summary: This retrospective and prospective cohort study examines cardiovascular changes in 400 children 24-36 months after COVID-19 infection, identifying persistent ECG abnormalities, rhythm disorders, and BP dysregulation in school-age children. While it demonstrates long-term post-COVID cardiovascular effects, it is an observational study with no treatment intervention tested.
paper_authors: Svetlana Kim; Zhamilya Issanguzhina; Gulzhan Tulegenova; Arystan Dossimov; Gulmira Kuldeyeva; Natalya Puxovikova; Natalya Chagay

summary: Prospective observational study measuring sexual function in 96 COVID-19 patients using the IIEF questionnaire at 0, 1, 3, and 6 months post-infection. Found temporary sexual dysfunction in the first month that gradually resolved by 6 months, with age and education as confounding factors.

paper_title: Short and Long-Term Effects of COVID-19 on Male Sexual Function

summary: A longitudinal follow-up study of 260 COVID-19 patients assessing cognitive function at 3 months and 1 year post-hospitalization using the blind Montreal Cognitive Assessment. The study found cognitive scores significantly declined over time and identified risk factors including older age, elevated inflammatory markers (CRP), hypertension, and severe pulmonary involvement.

paper_title: Prevalence of Cognitive Impairment and Its Risk Factors in Patients with COVID-19: A Follow-up Study
paper_journal: Iranian Journal of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences

summary: A retrospective study of 400 Iranian COVID-19 recovered patients examining chronic dyspnea prevalence and associated factors. Found 61.8% experienced dyspnea with higher likelihood associated with increased BMI and age, while exercise was protective.
paper_authors: Raheleh Shirazi; Ali Darvishpoor Kakhki; Sara Salarian
paper_title: Chronic Dyspnea in Iranian COVID-19 Recovered Patients: A Retrospective Study
paper_journal: Middle East Journal of Rehabilitation and Health Studies

summary: This cross-sectional survey study examined short-term menstrual cycle changes in 268 women following acute COVID-19 infection, comparing outcomes by vaccine type received prior to infection. Found 87.8% experienced at least one long COVID symptom, with depression (69.1%) and hair loss (23.9%) most common, and identified risk factors including anemia, diabetes, and prior acute infection severity.

paper_journal: BULLETIN OF STOMATOLOGY AND MAXILLOFACIAL SURGERY

summary: This retrospective cross-sectional study examines short- and long-term manifestations of COVID-19 in 295 hospitalized pediatric patients, following them for up to 12 weeks post-infection. Disease severity correlated with pulmonary manifestations and fatigue persisting at long-term follow-up, highlighting the need for targeted monitoring of post-COVID sequelae in high-risk children.

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluated pulmonary gas exchange abnormalities in 33 long COVID patients one year post-severe COVID-19, using combined DLNO and DLCO measurements. The findings demonstrate that gas exchange impairment is primarily driven by vascular component dysfunction rather than alveolar membrane diffusion defects.
paper_authors: Gianluca Imeri; Caterina Conti; Anna Caroli; Alberto Arrigoni; Pietro Bonaffini; Sandro Sironi; Luca Novelli; Federico Raimondi; Greta Chiodini; Simone Vargiu; Fabiano Di Marco
paper_title: Gas exchange abnormalities in Long COVID are driven by the alteration of the vascular component

summary: This study compares lung microvascular injury (capillary blood volume loss) between vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals following paucisymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection using lung function measurements. While it addresses long COVID pathophysiology and vaccine protection, it is observational without treatment assignment and should be excluded as it does not test an intervention given to long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Roberto W. Dal Negro; Paola Turco; Massimiliano Povero
paper_title: mRNA vaccines protect from the lung microvasculature injury and the capillary blood volume loss occurring in SARS-CoV-2 paucisymptomatic infections

summary: This study compares brain imaging parameters (BOLD and DTI) in long COVID patients with mild vs severe emotional symptoms after multiple infections, assessed 3-6 months post-infection. Results show decreased FA and increased ALFF in specific brain areas associated with transformation from mild to severe emotional problems.
paper_authors: Jiao H.; Wu S.; Wang L.; Meng C.; Zhou G.; Guo J.; Cao L.; Zhao Y.; Song Z.; Wen J.
paper_title: The long-term cerebral change of patient transformed from mildly into severely emotional problem after multiple COVID-19 infections: 3-6 months

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining factors associated with depression in 510 post-COVID-19 patients using PHQ-9 assessment. Found that female gender, increased symptom count, and specific symptoms like ageusia/anosmia were significantly associated with higher depression risk, but this is an observational study analyzing associations rather than evaluating a treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Tischer KM; Yadav S.; Bell D.; Hansen K.; Veres LN; Maddy B.; Bakkum-Gamez JN
paper_title: Factors Associated with Depression in Post-Covid-19 Patients: A Tool for Prediction of Depression in Neurotropic Viral Infections
paper_journal: Journal of Adolescent and Addiction Research

summary: Retrospective descriptive study of persistent COVID-19 symptoms in older adults attending Peruvian senior centers, with telephone follow-up up to four months. Found that only 4.4% of COVID-19 cases in this population had symptoms persisting over three weeks.
paper_authors: Pavel J. Contreras; Zoila Romero-Albino; María Sofía Cuba-Fuentes
paper_title: Description of frequent and persistent symptoms of COVID-19 among older adults who attend senior centers

summary: This longitudinal study uses pre- and post-pandemic MRI and NIH Toolbox cognitive data from the ABCD Study to compare brain morphometry and cognitive performance in adolescents with and without COVID-19 history. The study observes morphometric abnormalities in COVID-infected youth but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Cui P.; Zou P.; Kang Y.; Yan X.; Zhou X.; Wang B.; Wu F.; Pan S.; Ma J.; Huang W.
paper_title: Longitudinal Brain Morphometry and NIH Toolbox Performance in Adolescents Before and After COVID-19

summary: This study examined dyssomnia (sleep disorders) in 126 patients across three groups: post-COVID syndrome patients (28), anxious patients with coronaphobia (48), and pre-pandemic neuropsychiatric disorder controls (50). The authors identified high prevalence of dyssomnia in post-COVID patients (88%) and evaluated psychopharmacotherapy approaches to treat sleep disturbances and associated anxiety in the post-COVID population.
paper_authors: Kim JH; Park SJ; Chung DJ; Hong HP; Lee JK; Yoon CJ; Lee JM
paper_title: Dyssomnia in the structure of post-covid syndrome
paper_journal: Medical and Biological Problems of Life Activity

summary: Retrospective chart review comparing pneumonia presentations in 141 patients with and without prior COVID-19 history between December 2021 and January 2023. Found no significant differences in clinical, radiologic, or prognostic parameters except elevated LDH in post-COVID group; does not focus on long COVID sequelae or test any intervention.
paper_authors: Coşkun Doğan; Hatice İrem Uzun; Esra Gür; Deniz Bilici; Sacit İçten
paper_title: Clinical-radiologic Features of Pneumonia in Patients who had Recovered from COVID-19 Pneumonia
paper_journal: ANNALS OF ABBASI SHAHEED HOSPITAL AND KARACHI MEDICAL & DENTAL COLLEGE

summary: This paper analyzes hospital discharge data from Chile in 2021 to characterize long COVID patients requiring hospitalization, examining demographics, duration of stay, and regional variation. It is a descriptive epidemiological analysis of secondary administrative data (ICD-10 coded hospital records) with no intervention or treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Xaviera Molina Avendaño; Camila Awad Avendaño; Florencia Antonia Rojas Espejo; María Fernanda Vidal Ruiz; Iris Delgado Becerra
paper_title: EGRESOS HOSPITALARIOS POR LONG COVID-19 EN CHILE DURANTE EL AÑO 2021

summary: This study uses 129Xe MRI imaging to monitor longitudinal pulmonary recovery in 13 long-COVID patients over >1 year following infection, measuring ventilation, gas-exchange, exercise tolerance, and quality of life. The paper reports imaging findings and physiological improvements but presents no intervention or treatment—it is a natural history/observational study without a therapeutic component.
paper_authors: Natally AlArab; Marrissa McIntosh; Andrew Hahn; Nicholas Feeley; Keegan Staab; Jonathan Percy; Conner Wharff; Jessica Sieren; Alejandro Comellas; Eric Hoffman; Sean Fain
paper_title: Longitudinal 129Xe MRI Gas-exchange and Exercise Intolerance in Long-COVID

summary: Prospective observational study of 300 COVID-19 patients followed for 4 months to identify risk factors for symptom persistence, examining the impact of age, sex, comorbidities, and infection severity. Findings show that severity of acute illness was the most important predictor of symptom persistence, but the study does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Mansi Shah; Atul Kakar; Atul Gogia; Shrishti Byotra; Vinus Taneja
paper_title: Persistence of Coronavirus Disease 2019 Symptoms in Postacute Phase: Does Age, Sex, Comorbidities, and Severity of Infection Have an Impact?
paper_journal: Journal of the Association of Physicians of India

summary: Prospective cohort study of 72 pregnant women with mild COVID-19 infection during pregnancy, followed through delivery and 3 months postpartum. Study focuses on acute COVID-19 outcomes during pregnancy and neonatal outcomes, with long COVID mentioned only as an incidental finding (47.2% frequency) but not as the primary research focus.
paper_title: Mild COVID-19 among pregnant women managed with home self-isolation in Lebanon: A prospective cohort study

summary: Observational cross-sectional survey of 70 hospital workers diagnosed with COVID-19 between March 2020 and March 2023 to determine long COVID incidence and characterize persistent symptoms. Found 9.8% incidence of long COVID with predominantly musculoskeletal (51%), mental health (50%), and otorhinolaryngological (42%) symptoms, but the study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Nelly Baeza Tapia; Ninoshka Vicencio Fredes; Carolina Rivacoba Rojas
paper_title: LONG COVID19 EN FUNCIONARIAS DE UN HOSPITAL CHILENO

summary: Prospective cohort study of 81 hospitalized COVID-19 patients with post-acute syndrome examining cardiac dysfunction via echocardiography at 2 months post-discharge and following cardiovascular adverse events at 3 and 6 months. Found longitudinal strain abnormalities in 22% of patients (LV-GLS 9.87%, RV-FWLS 14.8%) with no major adverse events during follow-up.

summary: A prospective hospital-based cohort study following 264 COVID-19 patients hospitalized during the delta wave for 12-18 months post-discharge to determine long COVID incidence and symptom burden. Found 17% incidence of long COVID, with higher prevalence in women and older individuals, but no interventions were tested.
paper_authors: Mittal K.; Khedar RS; Gupta R.; Bharati S.; Sharma KK; Gupta JB; Mathur A.
paper_title: Incidence of Long COVID-19 at 12–18 Months Following Delta Wave of Coronavirus Disease 2019: Hospital-based Prospective Registry
paper_journal: Journal of The Association of Physicians of India

summary: This prospective case series of 183 COVID-19 patients evaluated a dietary supplement and nutrition protocol designed to boost immune function and prevent long-term post-COVID complications. The protocol resulted in significant reductions in COVID severity scores and reportedly achieved complete recovery within 10-13 days, preventing long-term symptoms.
paper_authors: Hadi Mohammad; Tariq Sadeq; Media Ismail; Swar O. Ahmed; Zana Ameen
paper_title: The Healing Power Of Dietary Supplements To Prevent Long-Term Covid-19; A Prospective Observation Study

summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 398 adults in Iraq two years post-COVID-19 to assess long COVID prevalence and risk factors. The study found 85.9% had persistent symptoms, with hospitalization and reinfection increasing risk and vaccination showing no protective effect.
paper_authors: Rahim, Hawbash M.; Ahmed, Gasha S.; Hama, Salih A.
paper_title: Prevalence and predictors of Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19 two years after SARS-CoV-2 infection: the role of vaccination, hospitalization, reinfection, and peripheral blood immunological profile in an ambidirectional cohort study

summary: Retrospective study analyzing EMR data from 2017-2023 to compare cough prevalence and types before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic across age groups. Findings show a significant increase in acute cough incidence post-COVID-19, particularly unspecified cough, highlighting long-term respiratory consequences.
paper_authors: Agam Vora; Surinder Kumar Jindal; Priti Thakor; Harshad Malve; Roshni Panchal
paper_title: Impact of COVID-19 Pandemic on Incidence and Prevalence of Cough and its Types: A Real-world Study
paper_journal: Journal of The Association of Physicians of India

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines the relationship between lung damage severity during acute COVID-19 and metabolic biomarkers (tryptophan and TMAO levels) in 30 long COVID patients. The authors find significant associations between severe acute COVID-19 and reduced tryptophan/elevated TMAO in long COVID patients, contributing to understanding of pathogenic mechanisms.
paper_authors: Irina Kadyrova; D. M. Turebekova; A. B. Marchenko; D. A. Solyanov
paper_title: CONTRIBUTION OF TRYPTOPHAN AND TRIMETHYLAMINE N-OXIDE DYSREGULATION TO THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF LONG COVID-19 DEVELOPMENT DEPENDING ON THE CT STAGE OF LUNG INVOLVEMENT

summary: This study compares lung function parameters, specifically diffusion capacity (DLCO), between 99 athletes with post-COVID-19 sequelae and 36 uninfected control athletes. The authors found that 30% of post-COVID athletes had reduced DLCO and significantly lower forced vital capacity and FEV1 compared to controls, with dyspnea during infection associated with lower DLCO values.

paper_title: Changes in lung diffusion capacity after SARS-CoV-2 infections in highly trained athletes
paper_journal: Deutsche Zeitschrift für Sportmedizin/German Journal of Sports Medicine

summary: A prospective observational study following 60 children after acute COVID-19 to investigate the prevalence, symptoms, duration, and risk factors of long COVID. Found that 31% developed long COVID symptoms (mostly respiratory and neuropsychiatric), which typically resolved within 3 months.
paper_authors: Manoj Chaudhary; Hem Sagar Rimal; Love Kumar Sah; Pankaj Chaudhary
paper_title: Long COVID Among the Children Admitted to the Department of Pediatrics in a Tertiary Care Centre

The study found 75.8% had persistent symptoms at 1 month and 65% had PCA at 4 months, with older age, longer hospital stay, and dyspnea as independent predictive factors for PCA.

Found 20.3% had at least one PCS symptom, with shortness of breath and psychological effects like nightmares and PTSD being most common.
paper_authors: Dyah Wulan Sumekar Rengganis Wardani; Bayu Anggileo Pramesona; Yuni Nirmala
paper_title: Physical and psychological effects of post-COVID-19 syndrome on patients in Bandar Lampung, Indonesia: a descriptive prospective study
paper_journal: Journal of Current Science and Technology

summary: Retrospective observational study comparing long COVID patterns between vaccinated (n=913) and unvaccinated (n=4616) hospitalized COVID patients in India across three pandemic waves. Found no significant difference in long COVID incidence or duration between groups, though some symptom type differences existed and comorbidities (diabetes, hypertension) increased symptom risk.

paper_title: Effect of COVID Vaccine on Long COVID: An Observational Study on Hospitalised Patients in North India
paper_journal: Effect of COVID Vaccine on Long COVID: An Observational Study on Hospitalised Patients in North India

summary: A retrospective and prospective cohort study of 233 Thai children followed for 9 months post-COVID-19 infection to determine long COVID incidence and risk factors. The study found that 35.6% had persistent symptoms at 3 months, decreasing to 10.3% at 6 months, with moderate-severity acute infection identified as an independent risk factor for persistent symptoms.
paper_authors: Sunsanee Chatpornvorarux; Wiriya Nilprapa; Montira Sintara; Prakasit Wannapaschaiyong
paper_title: Incidence and Risk Factors of Long COVID in Children and Adolescents: A Single-Center Cohort Study in Thailand

While 11% of long COVID patients exhibited FSD-like symptom profiles and fatigue/muscle pain were common, the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Symptom profiles in long COVID compared to functional somatic disorder and the general population

summary: A 9-month prospective follow-up study of 48 hospitalized COVID-19 patients in Iran documenting the prevalence of persistent symptoms post-discharge. Findings show 10.4% experienced dyspnea, 6.2% olfactory complications and fatigue, and 10.4% reported new-onset symptoms, predominantly neurological.
paper_authors: Parmida shahbazi; Mahshid Talebi-Taher; Behrooz Banivaheb; Zeynab Yassin; Ashkan Yahyavi; Nima Hemmati
paper_title: Long-Term Symptoms in Hospitalized COVID-19 Patients: A Prospective 9-Month Follow-up Study

summary: A prospective cohort study of 173 kidney transplant recipients who survived acute COVID-19, followed for 24 months to assess long-term effects on graft function and survival. Severe COVID-19 cases showed significant declines in glomerular filtration rate and increased graft loss and mortality compared to mild/moderate cases.
paper_authors: Manfro AG; Schneider ET; Backes LLA; Petrolli G.; Franco RF; Cezar CEO; Bauer AC; Manfro RC
paper_title: Late Effect of Early Phase COVID-19 on Outcomes of Kidney Transplant Recipients Who Survived the Acute Infection.

summary: This retrospective study examines pulmonary fibrosis development in 49 hospitalized COVID-19 patients during acute infection (March-September 2020) and explores how environmental factors in Lahore affect post-infection recovery. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 hospitalization outcomes rather than long COVID sequelae, and does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Zaibunnisa; Syeda Neelam Fatima Ali Gilani; Wajeeha Khursheed
paper_title: Pulmonary Fibrosis Progression in Hospitalized COVID-19 Patients: The Role of Environmental and Climatic Stressors in Post-Infection Recovery in Lahore, Pakistan
paper_journal: Physical Education, Health and Social Sciences

summary: This study monitored cardiac haemodynamics in COVID-19 patients with coronary heart disease over 12 months post-hospitalization, measuring ejection fraction, ventricular volume, and inflammatory markers. While demonstrating partial cardiac recovery, the study was observational with no intervention applied, making it ineligible for a treatment trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: Serhii Mostovyi
paper_title: Coronary heart disease and dynamics of intracardiac haemodynamics after hospitalisation for COVID-19: Results of a 12-month follow-up study
paper_journal: Bulletin of Medical and Biological Research

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluated 2,252 post-COVID-19 patients in Argentina to characterize persistent symptoms and their impact on cardiovascular, respiratory, and neurocognitive function. Fatigue (28.2%), dyspnea (21.8%), and cognitive symptoms (10.2%) were common; however, no significant differences in cardiovascular or respiratory function were found between those with and without post-COVID syndrome, though older patients (>50 years) showed worse neurocognitive performance.

summary: Population-based cohort study of 24 million English adults examining the relationship between COVID-19 and gastrointestinal diseases up to two years post-infection, stratified by vaccination status and severity. summary: Multicenter Canadian cohort study examining factors associated with post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) symptom deterioration following SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in 476 patients. Found that 28.8% experienced symptom deterioration after vaccination, with Moderna vaccine and persistent cough as significant risk factors.
paper_authors: Malika Seydou Beidari; Martyne Audet; Stéphane Turcotte; Raoul Daoust; Corinne M. Hohl; Patrick M. Archambault
paper_title: Factors Associated with the Deterioration of Post-COVID-19 Condition Symptoms Following a Dose of SARS-CoV-2 Vaccine

summary: An observational cohort study of 33 participants tracked from 2019 to 2023 to investigate the relationship between post-COVID syndrome and small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO), examining melatonin dysregulation, inflammatory cytokines, and dysbiosis. The study found that SIBO-positive participants had significantly reduced melatonin levels, elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α, IL-12, IL-17), severe dysbiosis, and elevated tumor markers (CEA, CA19.9), suggesting SIBO may represent a pre-cancerous condition in post-COVID patients.

Found persistent lung injuries in 32% of cases with elevated biomarkers (KL-6, D-dimer) and decreased lung function, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Correlations Between COVID-19 Pneumonia and Long-Term Lung Injuries
paper_journal: MedEpicent: Journal of Medical Education and Clinical Research

summary: This is a prospective cohort study examining neurophysiologic changes in 145 people with post-COVID fatigue over 12-45 months post-infection, measuring cortical excitability, muscle fatigue, and autonomic function. paper_title: Risk Factors for Severe Post-COVID Condition in Children, Adolescents, and Young Adults

summary: Prospective cohort study following 545 PCS patients over 15 months to identify patterns of fatigue change using trajectory analysis. Found six distinct fatigue trajectories, with severe fatigue persisting and moderate fatigue showing improvement over time.
paper_authors: Nancy Mayo; Stanley Hum; Lyne Nadeau; Marie-Josée Brouillette; Lesley K. Fellows
paper_title: Change in Fatigue over 15 months in people the Post-Covid Syndrome

summary: This case-control study compares cellular and humoral immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 and EBV between 27 neuropsychiatric long COVID patients and 27 matched recovered controls at 3-6 months post-symptom onset. The study found no differences in virus-specific T-cell responses but identified diminished EBV-specific humoral immunity as a potential prognostic marker for neuropsychiatric long COVID development, particularly associated with fatigue persistence at 12 months.

summary: All Eyes on PCS is a prospective observational study comparing retinal microvascular structure and function between post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) patients, ME/CFS patients, and healthy controls using retinal vessel analysis. The study found persistent endothelial dysfunction and retinal microvascular alterations in PCS patients that correlate with symptom severity and inflammatory markers, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Microvascular Remodeling and Endothelial Dysfunction Across Post-COVID-19 and ME/CFS: Insights from the All Eyes on PCS Study

summary: This observational cohort study examines associations between oropharyngeal and gut microbiota composition with lung function recovery in 83 ICU patients with severe COVID-19 at 3, 6, and 12 months post-hospitalization. The study identifies distinct microbiota patterns in patients who recovered lung function versus those with persistent impairment, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

paper_title: Respiratory and Gut Microbiota Correlate with Lung Function Recovery after Severe COVID-19

summary: Retrospective cohort study using TriNetX EHR data comparing cardiovascular, renal, and pulmonary outcomes in 315,612 adults with vs without long COVID, stratified by age and sex. summary: Population-based cohort study examining healthcare resource use and costs attributable to COVID-19 in Ontario, Canada, stratified by social determinants of health. Study documents post-acute phase costs and identifies disparities in burden across marginalized communities, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Adeteju Ogunbameru; Sarah Swayze; Kuan Liu; Rob Lorway; Beate Sander
paper_title: Long-term healthcare resource use and cost associated with COVID-19 disease from a health system perspective. An equity-focused population-based cohort study

summary: Retrospective cohort study using EHR data from 910,393 patients to evaluate whether SARS-CoV-2 infection increases risk of new-onset obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) up to 4.5 years post-infection. Found that both hospitalized and non-hospitalized COVID+ patients had significantly higher adjusted risk of OSA compared to COVID− controls, with downstream cardiovascular complications in hospitalized patients.
paper_authors: Sagar Changela; Rachel Katz; Jainam Shah; Sonya S. Henry; Tim Q. Duong
paper_title: Risk of new-onset obstructive sleep apnea up to 4.5 years after COVID-19 in the urban population

summary: This observational cohort study followed 360 critically ill COVID-19 patients with acute kidney injury in ICU, analyzing AKI stages, kidney replacement therapy, and outcomes at 90 and 365 days. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 in hospitalized/ICU patients during active infection, not on long COVID or post-acute sequelae.

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed sleep quality in 82 post-COVID-19 patients using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index questionnaire, with data collected three years after hospitalization. summary: A prospective longitudinal cohort study following 326 COVID-19 survivors (hospitalised and non-hospitalised) over two years in Bangladesh to assess the burden and evolution of long COVID symptoms and complications. Findings show hospitalised survivors experienced higher rates of persistent symptoms at two years, while vaccination significantly reduced respiratory and psychiatric sequelae in both groups.
