paper_title: Evolution of long COVID over two years in hospitalised and non-hospitalised survivors in Bangladesh: a longitudinal cohort study

summary: This binational cohort study investigates the long-term risk of autoimmune inflammatory rheumatic diseases (AIRDs) following COVID-19 infection in Korean and Japanese populations. The study found that COVID-19 patients had increased risk for incident AIRD compared to uninfected controls, with risk increasing alongside acute COVID-19 severity.
paper_authors: Min Seo Kim; Hayeon Lee; Seung Won Lee; Rosie Kwon; Sang Youl Rhee; Jin A. Lee; Ai Koyanagi; Lee Smith; Guillaume Fond; Laurent Boyer; Jinseok Lee; Masoud Rahmati; Ju-Young Shin; Chanyang Min; Jae Il Shin; Dong Keon Yon
paper_title: Long-Term Autoimmune Inflammatory Rheumatic Outcomes of COVID-19

summary: A prospective cohort study characterizing persistent symptoms and medical sequelae in 189 COVID-19 survivors versus 120 controls at the NIH Clinical Center. Extensive diagnostic evaluation revealed no specific pathophysiologic cause of reported PASC symptoms in most participants, with findings limited to symptom burden and quality-of-life measures.
paper_authors: Sneller MC; Liang CJ; Marques AR; Chung JY; Shanbhag SM; Fontana JR; Raza H.; Okeke O.; Dewar RL; Higgins BP; Tolstenko K.; Kwan RW; Gittens KR; Seamon CA; McCormack G.; Shaw JS; Okpali GM; Law M.; Trihemasava K.; Kennedy BD; Shi V.; Justement JS; Buckner CM; Blazkova J.; Moir S.; Chun TW; Lane HC
paper_title: A Longitudinal Study of COVID-19 Sequelae and Immunity: Baseline Findings

summary: Prospective observational study comparing psychological outcomes and quality of life between COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 ICU survivors at 6 and 12 months post-discharge. While the study includes COVID-19 patients, it focuses on acute critical illness sequelae rather than long COVID specifically, with COVID-19 patients showing better outcomes than non-COVID ICU survivors.
paper_authors: Damico V.; Margosio V.; Nattino G.; Crimella F.
paper_title: Long-term consequences in Covid-19 and Non-Covid-19 patients survivors of critical illness. A descriptive study.
paper_journal: Annali di igiene : medicina preventiva e di comunita

summary: Prospective observational cohort study of 187 long COVID patients with persistent dyspnoea who received low-intensity spa-based rehabilitation treatment. 88.2% reported improvement in dyspnoea and 80.6% in both dyspnoea and fatigue, with older age, obesity, and comorbidities predicting poorer treatment response.
paper_authors: Resta E.; Quarato CMI; Scioscia G.; Cuscianna E.; Tondo P.; Mansueto G.; Lulaj E.; Sorangelo S.; Resta O.; Foschino Barbaro MP; Tafuri S.; Lacedonia D.
paper_title: Low-intensity rehabilitation in persistent post COVID-19 dyspnoea: the value of Spa health resort as appropriate setting.
paper_journal: Annali di igiene : medicina preventiva e di comunita

summary: Prospective cohort study of 250 COVID-19 patients examining post-COVID cardiovascular manifestations, with detailed follow-up at 60 and 90 days post-infection. Observational study with no treatment intervention; documents persistence of symptoms including palpitations, dyspnea, and other sequelae rather than evaluating a specific therapy.
paper_authors: Osadchuk M.; Kolesnikova I.; Zakharova L.; Nagibina J.; Kubareva M.
paper_title: Post-Covid Conditions and their Effects on the Cardiovascular System.

summary: This cross-sectional study examined the occurrence of long COVID in 3,127 healthcare workers at a university hospital, finding that 10 workers developed moderate long COVID with symptoms including asthenia, anosmia, and neuromuscular disorders. The paper focuses on epidemiological characterization and insurance/compensation challenges rather than testing any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Giorgianni C.; Cianci V.; Pitrone C.; Burrascano G.; Mondello C.; Gullì N.; Gualniera P.; Asmundo A.; Sapienza D.
paper_title: Occurrence Of Long COVID In Healthcare Workers At A University Hospital And Challenges In Insurance And Compensation Evaluation.

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining risk factors for long COVID among 256 hospitalized COVID-19 patients in Indonesia. Identified fatigue during admission, chronic kidney disease, thrombocytosis, and positive RT-PCR at discharge as risk factors, while vaccination was protective—but this is observational epidemiology, not a treatment trial.
paper_title: Risk Factors Associated with Long COVID Among Hospitalized Adults in Several Hospitals in Palembang City, Indonesia
paper_journal: Kesmas Jurnal Kesehatan Masyarakat Nasional (National Public Health Journal)

summary: This observational cohort study followed 312 cancer patients after acute COVID-19 to assess the prevalence and persistence of post-acute sequelae (PASC). 60% of patients reported long COVID symptoms persisting up to 14 months, with fatigue, sleep disturbance, and myalgia being the most common, with higher prevalence in females.
paper_authors: Hiba Dagher; Anne-Marie Chaftari; Ishwaria M. Subbiah; Alexandre E. Malek; Ying Jiang; Peter Lamie; Bruno Granwehr; Teny John; Eduardo Yepez; Jovan Borjan; Cielito Reyes-Gibby; Mary Flores; Fareed Khawaja; Mala Pande; Noman Ali; Raniv Rojo; Daniel D. Karp; Patrick Chaftari; Ray Hachem; Issam I. Raad
paper_title: Long COVID in cancer patients: preponderance of symptoms in majority of patients over long time period

summary: Prospective cohort study of 388 long COVID patients in Malaysia followed for 6 months to identify symptom patterns and risk factors. The study is observational without intervention assignment—it documents natural disease progression and medications patients happened to take, not a treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Ahtheemathurra Ballasingam; Farida Islahudin; Siti Azdiah; Abdul Aziz
paper_title: Factors Associated with Postacute COVID-19 Syndrome Among Patients in Malaysia

summary: Retrospective cross-sectional study of 452 COVID-19 patients in Malaysia assessing long COVID prevalence (27.4%) and associated risk factors at 4-5 weeks post-infection. Identifies fatigue, cough, and myalgia as common symptoms and female sex, cardiovascular disease, and asthma as risk factors, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Kim Sui Wan; Esther Rishma Sundram; Ammar Amsyar Abdul Haddi; Abdul Rahman Dashuki; Azainorsuzila Ahad; Rowena John; MuhammadKhairul Ridhuan Abdul Wahid; Ungku Izmin Farah Ungku Halmie; Farah Edura Ibrahim; Nachia Banu Abdul Rahim
paper_title: Long COVID active case detection initiative among COVID-19 patients in Port Dickson, Malaysia: a retrospective study on the positive outcomes, the proportion of patients with long COVID and its associated factors

summary: This study tracked 230 professional athletes over ~1 month after returning to training following Omicron infection, measuring changes in fatigue, sleep quality, and mood using standardized scales. While it documents psychological recovery in acute post-infection period, it does not study persistent long COVID symptoms or test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Chenhao Tan; Jinhao Wang; Guohuan Cao; Yelei He; Jun Yin; Yudan Chu; Zhizhong Geng; Longji Li; Jun Qiu
paper_title: Psychological changes in athletes infected with Omicron after return to training: fatigue, sleep, and mood

summary: This cross-sectional study examined the relationship between CRP/albumin ratio and pulmonary function parameters in 157 patients at 12 weeks post-acute COVID-19, stratified by pneumonia severity during acute infection. The study found that CRP/albumin ratio was negatively correlated with respiratory function measures, suggesting potential prognostic value, but it does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Dursun Afsin; Bugra Kerget
paper_title: Evaluation of the Relationship between CRP/Albumin Ratio and Pulmonary Function Parameters in Patients with Post-Acute COVID-19

summary: Prospective observational study of 93 hospitalized COVID-19 patients requiring prolonged oxygen therapy after testing negative for SARS-CoV-2, examining factors associated with failure to wean and mortality. Identifies age ≥50 years with multiple comorbidities as a risk factor for prolonged hospitalization and poor outcomes, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Alokananda Ray; Rajan Chaudhry; Sudhir Rai; Sujata Mitra; Sridhar Pradhan; Ashok Sunder; Deb Sanjay Nag
paper_title: Prolonged Oxygen Therapy Post COVID-19 Infection: Factors Leading to the Risk of Poor Outcome

summary: A prospective cohort study comparing post-COVID syndrome incidence and outcomes over 12 months between 298 individuals with prior COVID-19 infection and 298 unexposed controls in rural Kerala. The study found higher PCS incidence in the exposure group (91.9%) versus controls (83.2%), with persistent functional impairments and overlapping symptom burden between groups.
paper_authors: Veena K. Puthenveedu; Sreelal T. Prabhakaran; Aneesh Basheer
paper_title: Clinical Spectrum and Outcomes of Post-COVID Syndrome Among Adults in Rural Kerala: A Cohort Study

summary: This case-control study compared pulmonary function, exercise capacity, and quality of life between post-COVID-19 subjects (1 year post-recovery) and healthy controls. While lung function was relatively preserved, the post-COVID group showed reduced diffusion capacity (DLCO), reduced exercise capacity, and impaired quality of life scores in energy/fatigue and physical function domains.
paper_authors: Ayedh Alahmari; Gokul Krishna; Ann Mary Jose; Rowaida Qoutah; Aya Hejazi; Hadeel Abumossabeh; Fatima Atef; Alhanouf Almutiri; Mazen Homoud; Saleh Algarni; Mohammed AlAhmari; Saeed Alghamdi; Tareq Alotaibi; Khalid Alwadeai; Saad Alhammad; Mushabbab Alahmari
paper_title: The long-term effects of COVID-19 on pulmonary status and quality of life

summary: Longitudinal observational study of 145 COVID-19 patients followed over 6 months to characterize pulmonary recovery trajectories using CT imaging, lung function tests, and clinical parameters. Study identified phenotypes of recovery and developed machine learning classifiers to predict incomplete pulmonary recovery from non-imaging biomarkers.
paper_authors: Thomas Sonnweber; Piotr Tymoszuk; Sabina Sahanic; Anna Boehm; Alex Pizzini; Anna Luger; Christoph Schwabl; Manfred Nairz; Philipp Grubwieser; Katharina Kurz; Sabine Koppelstätter; Magdalena Aichner; Bernhard Puchner; Alexander Egger; Gregor Hoermann; Ewald Wöll; Günter Weiss; Gerlig Widmann; Ivan Tancevski; Judith Löffler-Ragg
paper_title: Investigating phenotypes of pulmonary COVID-19 recovery: A longitudinal observational prospective multicenter trial

summary: This real-world study characterized 141 outpatients with subacute or chronic post-COVID cough, collecting clinical data, prescriptions, and cough severity over follow-up visits. The authors evaluated treatment effectiveness and found ICS/LABA to be the most effective option for post-COVID cough, with a higher prevalence in females.
paper_authors: Chun Yao; Dongliang Cheng; Wenhong Yang; Yun Guo; Tong Zhou
paper_title: Characterization and clinical outcomes of outpatients with subacute or chronic post COVID-19 cough: a real-world study

summary: A cross-sectional study of 186 COVID-19 recovered medical doctors in Bangladesh examining post-COVID symptom prevalence, duration, and associated risk factors through telephone interviews. Female sex and comorbid conditions were identified as significant risk factors for long-lasting post-COVID symptoms.
paper_authors: Sultana S.; Islam MT; Salwa M.; Zakir Hossain SM; Hasan MN; Masum AA; Khan AH; Khan MMH; Haque MA
paper_title: Duration and Risk Factors of Post-COVID Symptoms Following Recovery Among the Medical Doctors in Bangladesh

summary: This observational study tracked chest X-ray findings in 429 COVID-19 patients at hospital discharge and 30-day follow-up. While it documents long-term radiological sequelae (consolidation, reticular thickening) and symptoms like fatigue post-COVID, it is an observational monitoring study without any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Aarzoo Gupta; Ishan Garg; Abbas Iqbal; Abdul Subhan Talpur; Alyanna Marie B. Mañego; Rama Kalyani Kavuri; Parkash Bachani; Sidra Naz; Zoya Qamar Iqbal
paper_title: Long-Term X-ray Findings in Patients With Coronavirus Disease-2019

summary: A prospective cohort study of 279 older adults hospitalized with COVID-19, followed for 90 days post-discharge to assess post-COVID syndrome prevalence, symptom patterns, and functional outcomes. The study found 23.6% of patients reported at least one clinical feature at 90 days, with fatigue being the most common symptom (8.9%), while functional status (ADL/IADL) largely returned to baseline.
paper_authors: Sathyamurthy P.; Sudha Madhavan; Viswanathan Pandurangan
paper_title: Prevalence, Pattern and Functional Outcome of Post COVID-19 Syndrome in Older Adults

summary: A prospective cohort study following 1,000 COVID-19 patients at 30 and 90 days post-discharge to assess long-term neurological sequelae. Found that headache and insomnia were the most common neurological symptoms, with prevalence declining over time but highlighting the persistent neurological complications of COVID-19.
paper_authors: Kumar J.; Makheja K.; Rahul F.; Kumar S.; Kumar M.; Chand M.; Kammawal Y.; Khalid D.; Jahangir M.; Bachani P.
paper_title: Long-Term Neurological Impact of COVID-19

summary: Longitudinal study measuring sleep quality changes in 500 COVID-19 patients from ICU/isolation discharge to 30-day follow-up using PSQI scores. Found significant increase in insomnia prevalence post-COVID (45.1% vs 12.1% pre-COVID), but no intervention was tested or evaluated.
paper_authors: Ayesha A. Choudhry; Fnu Shahzeen; Sara A. Choudhry; Narjis Batool; Fatir Murtaza; Anum Dilip; Murk Rani; Aakash Chandnani
paper_title: Impact of COVID-19 Infection on Quality of Sleep

summary: Multicentric retrospective cohort study in Iraq comparing inflammatory polyneuropathy rates in 1,344 COVID-19 patients versus 896 controls over six months. Found 1.14% of COVID-19 patients developed inflammatory polyneuropathy (vs 0.29% in controls, RR=6), with 44.4% of cases occurring 4-12 weeks post-infection and GBS as the most common type (72.2%).
paper_authors: Nareen H. Hasrat; Haithem J. Kadhum; Ali R. Hashim; Zaineb A. Yakob; Lana A. Kadhim; Hassan A. Farid
paper_title: Neurographic Evidence of Inflammatory Polyneuropathies in Peri-COVID-19 Circumstances and Their Relationship With Acute Disease Severity and Inflammatory Storm

summary: Retrospective observational study of 84 long COVID patients with pneumonia admitted to a tertiary care hospital, analyzing microbial isolates and antibiotic resistance patterns. Treatment with targeted antimicrobial therapy based on culture and sensitivity results achieved 91% survival and discharge rate, with resistance patterns (MDR/XDR strains) correlating with mortality outcomes.
paper_authors: Rao CM; Rout P.; Pattnaik AP; Singh N.; Rajendran A.; Patro S.
paper_title: The Microbial Profile and Resistance Pattern of Pathogens Isolated From Long COVID Pneumonia Patients and Their Correlation to Clinical Outcome: Our Experience From a Tertiary Care Hospital

summary: Longitudinal study measuring sexual function in 300 female COVID-19 survivors using the FSFI scale at discharge and 60 days post-discharge. Found significant decline in sexual function scores post-infection (28.16 vs 24.43, p<0.0001), but this is a natural history/observational study without any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Muhammad Umair Nawaz; Edgar Rivera; Sagar Vinayak; Kanwal Elahi; Manoj Kumar; Momal Chand; Sana Ezae; Dua Khalid; Sidra Naz; Faizan Shaukat
paper_title: Comparison of Sexual Function Before and After COVID-19 Infection in Female Patients

summary: Prospective follow-up study comparing pulmonary function, mental health, and quality of life outcomes 3+ months post-ICU discharge in COVID-19 ARDS survivors who received non-invasive versus invasive mechanical ventilation. Patients requiring mechanical ventilation showed greater impairment in pulmonary function and reduced physical quality of life, suggesting need for enhanced rehabilitation.
paper_authors: Amarjyoti Hazarika; Varun Mahajan; Kamal Kajal; Ananya Ray; Karan Singla; Inderpaul S. Sehgal; Ashish Bhalla; Shubh M. Singh; Naveen B. Naik; Narender Kaloria; Kulbhushan Saini; Ajay Singh; Ganesh Kumar; Indranil Biswas; Shiv L. Soni; Hemant Bhagat; Yadvender Singh; Goverdhan D. Puri
paper_title: Pulmonary Function, Mental and Physical Health in Recovered COVID-19 Patients Requiring Invasive Versus Non-invasive Oxygen Therapy: A Prospective Follow-Up Study Post-ICU Discharge

summary: A prospective observational study of 48 COVID-19 patients with dyspnea assessed factors associated with persistence of dyspnea and health-related quality of life at discharge and 60 days post-discharge. Early pulmonary rehabilitation resulted in significant improvements in dyspnea and quality of life scores, with age and BMI identified as significant predictive factors.
paper_authors: Anurug Biswas; Sanjay Pandey; Srutarshi Ghosh; Jyoti Pandey; Niraj Kumar; Subha Das; Renu A. Johnson; Ranjeet Kumar; Anjusha E. V.; Anoop P.
paper_title: Factors Associated With Persistence of Dyspnea and Change in Health-Related Quality of Life in Patients With COVID-19 After Discharge

summary: Observational cross-sectional study identifying risk factors for severe long COVID-19 using questionnaire data from 220 respondents. Found that age >45 years, ≥15 COVID-19 symptoms, and obesity were significant predictors of severe long COVID-19.
paper_authors: Antonio S. Menezes; Silvia M. Botelho; Luciana R. Santos; Aline L. Rezende
paper_title: Acute COVID-19 Syndrome Predicts Severe Long COVID-19: An Observational Study

summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 2,000 COVID-19 patients discharged from a Pakistani hospital, documenting persistent symptoms at discharge and 12-month follow-up. The study found fatigue as the most common long-term symptom (6.78% at follow-up) but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Shivani F.; Kumari N.; Bai P.; Rakesh F.; Haseeb M.; Kumar S.; Jamil A.; Zaidi M.; Shaukat F.; Rizwan A.
paper_title: Long-Term Symptoms of COVID-19: One-Year Follow-Up Study

summary: Prospective case series of 36 post-ICU COVID-19 survivors evaluated at admission, discharge, and 3-month follow-up after an inpatient multimodal rehabilitation program. Study found significant improvements in respiratory muscle strength, cough effectiveness, and functional capacity between discharge and 3-month follow-up, though fatigue levels worsened despite overall functional recovery.
paper_authors: Ana Costa; Ana F. Gonçalves; Margarida Rodrigues; Rui Santos; Miguel P. Almeida; Ana Lima
paper_title: Post-intensive Care Unit COVID-19 Survivors: Functional Status and Respiratory Function Three Months After an Inpatient Rehabilitation Program

summary: A follow-up observational study examining body composition and metabolic changes (fat distribution, insulin, HOMA-IR) in 441 individuals before and after mild-to-moderate COVID-19 infection. The study documents acute post-infection metabolic dysregulation but does not address long COVID or test any intervention.
paper_authors: Mohammad Hosein Yazdanpanah; Maryam Mardani; Saeed Osati; Elham Ehrampoush; Seyed Hossein Davoodi; Reza Homayounfar
paper_title: COVID-19 Induces Body Composition and Metabolic Alterations

summary: This cross-sectional study compares health-related quality of life (HRQL) in hospitalized COVID-19 patients six months post-discharge versus non-hospitalized patients and healthy controls using multiple validated questionnaires (EQ5D5L, SF36v2, FACIT-F, PCFSS). While the paper documents significant HRQL impairment in hospitalized patients and suggests potential for rehabilitation programs, it is excluded because it does not evaluate or test any specific intervention or treatment—it is purely observational and descriptive in nature.
paper_authors: Emmanouil Koullias; Georgios Fragkiadakis; Maria Papavdi; Georgia Manousopoulou; Triantafyllia Karamani; Helena Avgoustou; Evangelia Kotsi; Dimitris Niakas; Dimitrios Vassilopoulos
paper_title: Long-Term Effect on Health-Related Quality of Life in Patients With COVID-19 Requiring Hospitalization Compared to Non-hospitalized COVID-19 Patients and Healthy Controls

summary: Prospective observational study of 476 hospitalized COVID-19 patients in South India followed at 1, 2, and 4 weeks post-discharge to assess persistence of symptoms and quality of life using the 15D questionnaire. Most symptoms resolved by 4 weeks with improved health-related quality of life and physical performance, contrasting with findings from other global regions.
paper_authors: Lakshmanan S.; Mv B.; Dharmalingam A.; Bhaskar E.; Anil AA; Senthil N.
paper_title: Post-acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Infection: Do Indians Fare Better?

summary: This retrospective pathology study analyzes tissue specimens from COVID-associated mucormycosis cases to characterize histomorphological patterns and fungal characteristics. While the cases occur post-COVID, the paper is a descriptive pathology analysis of acute fungal complications during active infection sequelae, not a treatment trial for long COVID.
paper_authors: Walke V.; Jayashankar E.; Khurana U.; Panwar H.; Karuna T.; Gupta V.; Kapoor N.
paper_title: Preliminary Experience in Post-COVID-19 Mycoses: A Pathologist’s Perspective

summary: A retrospective cohort study of 42 hospitalized COVID-19 patients with organizing pneumonia comparing glucocorticoid treatment (dexamethasone vs prednisone vs none) and their impact on oxygen requirements and outcomes over 12 months post-discharge. Steroids were associated with improved oxygen weaning, though incidence of post-COVID organizing pneumonia was lower than expected at 0.05% with 14% mortality.
paper_authors: Fereshteh Yazdi; Uzoamaka Ogbonnah; Cesar Davila-Chapa; Prathik Krishnan
paper_title: Glucocorticoid Therapy in COVID-19-Induced Organizing Pneumonia: A Rare Occurrence

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluates autonomic dysfunction and silent ischemia in 128 post-COVID-19 outpatients (55 asymptomatic, 73 symptomatic) using 24-hour ambulatory ECG and heart rate variability analysis. The study found that symptomatic patients had significantly higher ST depression burden and were at greater risk of silent ischemic attacks, but no treatment or intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Muammer Karakayalı; Inanc Artac; Dogan Ilis; Timor Omar; Ibrahim Rencuzogullari; Yavuz Karabag; Mehmet Altunova; Ayça Arslan; Ezgi Guzel
paper_title: Evaluation of Outpatients in the Post-COVID-19 Period in Terms of Autonomic Dysfunction and Silent Ischemia

summary: Descriptive cross-sectional study assessing post-acute COVID-19 complications in 100+ patients at a teaching hospital in North India through clinical examination, echocardiography, and pulmonary function testing. Found fatigue as the most common persistent symptom and cardiac/pulmonary changes on imaging even in asymptomatic patients.
paper_authors: Vikas Chandra Vidyarthi; Harish Gupta; Ajay Verma; Abhishek Singh; Satish Kumar; Prem Singh
paper_title: Descriptive Study to Assess Post-acute COVID-19 Complications in Patients Presenting at a Teaching Hospital in North India

summary: This longitudinal observational cohort study followed 146 COVID-19 recovered patients for up to 12 months with monthly assessments to identify persistent sequelae and associated risk predictors. Key findings include pulmonary (40%), psychiatric (25%), and neurological (21.7%) sequelae, with comorbidities, older age, higher BMI, and severe disease identified as significant risk factors.
paper_authors: Gujral HS Jr; Sahasrabudhe TR; Nirmala MA
paper_title: A Systematic Evaluation of Risk Predictors for COVID-19 Sequelae

summary: Retrospective analysis of post-COVID-19 patients with pulmonary embolism who received anticoagulant therapy, assessing predisposing factors and vascular reperfusion outcomes over six months. Study found high rates of complete reperfusion with anticoagulation alone and identified hypertension, diabetes, and obesity as prevalent risk factors, but did not evaluate or compare treatment interventions.
paper_authors: Margarida Agudo; Pedro Moura; Francisca Santos; Carolina Robalo; Adriano Carvalho; Sónia Serra
paper_title: Pulmonary Embolism of COVID-19: A Year of Reflection

summary: Retrospective cohort study of 504 COVID-19 patients from a Saudi Arabian hospital examining the incidence and risk factors for post-COVID-19 syndrome. Found 45% incidence with fatigue, joint pain, and decreased exercise tolerance as most common persistent symptoms; female gender, multiple comorbidities, steroid use, and acute infection complications were significant risk factors.
paper_authors: Saad A. Alghamdi; Mona A. Alfares; Raeid A. Alsulami; Abdullah F. Alghamdi; Asim M. Almalawi; Mohammed S. Alghamdi; Hassan A. Hazazi
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 Syndrome: Incidence, Risk Factor, and the Most Common Persisting Symptoms

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) severity before and after COVID-19 infection in 33 patients, with 17 having COVID-19 history and 16 as controls. Found no significant differences in SNOT-22 scores between groups, and no significant association between intranasal corticosteroid use and COVID-19 infection status (except in asthma patients).
paper_authors: Ahmad Alroqi; Mashal B. Abaalkhail; Nawaf Albuhayjan; Jehad Alorainy; Mohammed Jomah; Saud Alromaih; Khalifa Binkhamis
paper_title: Evaluation of Chronic Rhinosinusitis Symptoms' Severity Following COVID-19 Infection: A Retrospective Analysis

summary: A retrospective cohort study of 41 long COVID patients treated with stellate ganglion block (SGB) to manage persistent symptoms. Results showed 86% of patients experienced symptom reduction following SGB treatment.
paper_authors: Lisa Pearson; Alfred Maina; Taylor Compratt; Sherri Harden; Abbey Aaroe; Whitney Copas; Leah Thompson
paper_title: Stellate Ganglion Block Relieves Long COVID-19 Symptoms in 86% of Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study

summary: Retrospective observational study of 617 laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 cases in India comparing post-COVID-19 condition prevalence and characteristics between Delta and Omicron variants. Found 6.48% reported persistent symptoms, with Delta cases showing higher prevalence (12.38%) than Omicron (5.27%), but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Rajesh P. Karyakarte; Rashmita Das; Mansi V. Rajmane; Sonali Dudhate; Jeanne Agarasen; Praveena Pillai; Priyanka M. Chandankhede; Rutika S. Labhshetwar; Yogita Gadiyal; Preeti P. Kulkarni; Safanah Nizarudeen; Savita Mukade; Suvarna Joshi
paper_title: The Burden and Characteristics of Post-COVID-19 Conditions Among Laboratory-Confirmed Delta and Omicron COVID-19 Cases: A Preliminary Study From Maharashtra, India

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines post-discharge healthcare usage and costs for 200 patients hospitalized with COVID-19 across four pandemic surges. The study compares utilization patterns and identifies high-cost patient groups, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention for long COVID.
paper_authors: Jasmine Leahy; Rebecca Bajracharya; Brian Altonen; Maria Ferreira-Ortiz; Leopolda Silvera; Alfred J. Astua
paper_title: Post-discharge Healthcare Usage and Costs From March 2020 Through the Omicron Surge for Individuals Hospitalized With COVID-19

summary: A retrospective analysis of 289 COVID-19 patients examining the relationship between demographic factors (age, gender, smoking), clinical variables (vaccination, disease severity), and post-COVID symptoms. Female gender, higher BMI, and smoking were identified as risk factors for symptom prevalence, while booster vaccination showed promise in reducing symptoms.
paper_authors: Saad Tariq Khan; Khalid Rashid; Farrukh Ansar; Muhammad Y. Khan; Fahd Ali Khan; Rawan Ebrahim Husain Ahmed Ali Ismaeel; Raheem Hanif Mohammed; Rehan Mustafa; Bisma Tariq Khan; Behram Tariq; Mubbashar Husssain; Aamir Waheed
paper_title: Long COVID-19 Syndrome: Insights From a Major Tertiary Center in the UK on Who Is at Greater Risk

summary: A 12-month observational pilot study evaluating a combination treatment (systemic corticosteroids, mesoglycan, diuretic, and vitamin complex) in 87 patients with persistent post-COVID hyposmia and dysgeusia. Both olfactory and gustatory functions improved significantly from baseline to 12 months, with earlier treatment initiation associated with better recovery.
paper_authors: Maurizio G. Vento; Caterina Marinelli; Luciano Ferrari; Giuseppe Pedrazzi
paper_title: Recovery of Smell and Taste in Patients With Persistent COVID-19-Related Hyposmia and Dysgeusia by Targeting Also Inflammation and Endothelial Dysfunction

summary: Retrospective study comparing patients with chronic epipharyngitis who have or lack previous COVID-19 infection, evaluating differences in symptoms and endoscopic findings. Long COVID patients showed higher severity scores and different symptom profiles (fatigue, brain fog), with epipharyngeal abrasive therapy recommended as treatment.
paper_authors: Manabu Mogitate
paper_title: Differences Between Patients With Chronic Epipharyngitis With and Without Previous COVID-19 Infection

summary: This observational cohort study followed 100 hospitalized COVID-19 patients over 24 weeks to evaluate pulmonary function, dyspnea scores, and antibody levels in long COVID. Results showed slower improvement in lung function parameters in patients with severe acute COVID-19 compared to moderate cases, with no difference in neutralizing antibody levels between groups.
paper_authors: Kadir Özmen; Mehmet Meral; Bugra Kerget; Elif Yılmazel Uçar; Leyla Sağlam; Murat Özmen
paper_title: Evaluation of Pulmonary Function Tests, Dyspnea Scores, and Antibody Levels at the Six-Month Follow-Up of Patients Hospitalized for COVID-19 Pneumonia

summary: This retrospective cohort study examines the prevalence and outcomes of persistent sinus tachycardia 12-16 weeks post-SARS-CoV-2 infection in 1.36 million patients from the TriNetX network. Patients with post-COVID tachycardia showed significantly higher mortality, critical care utilization, and ventilator use compared to matched controls, with worse outcomes in unvaccinated individuals.
paper_authors: Borna Amir-Kabirian; Frank H. Annie; Morgan Koontz; Rayan Ihle
paper_title: Sinus Tachycardia Following COVID-19 and Its Implications

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed cognitive performance and sleep quality in 138 long COVID patients at 11 months post-infection using standardized cognitive tests (MMSE, MOCA) and sleep assessment. The study found cognitive deficits in 15-79% of participants but did not evaluate any treatment intervention, making it ineligible as a treatment trial.

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 238,828 American Red Cross blood donors examining the prevalence of long-term symptoms (>4 weeks) associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection using self-report and serologic testing. paper_authors: Nasim Raad; Jahangir Ghorbani; Ali Safavi Naeini; Neda Tajik; Mahboobeh Karimi‐Galougahi
paper_title: Parosmia in patients with COVID‐19 and olfactory dysfunction

summary: Cross-sectional survey using 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System data to estimate prevalence of COVID-19 and long COVID across U.S. industries and occupations. Identifies healthcare, protective services, and specific occupations (bartenders, farmworkers, personal care workers) with elevated long COVID prevalence, but does not test or evaluate any interventions or treatments.
paper_authors: Silver SR; Li J.; Ford ND; Shi D.; Saydah SH
paper_title: Prevalence of COVID‐19 and Long COVID by Industry and Occupation: Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System 2022

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing cognitive dysfunction in Chinese older adults post-COVID-19 using the SCD-18 questionnaire. Found that COVID-infected participants, particularly females and rural residents, showed significantly higher cognitive impairment scores within 1-6 months of infection, with gradual recovery after 6 months.
paper_authors: Qing Huang; Jingnan Wu; Liming Li; Shi Yao; Yan Wang; Yatian Li; Lili Cui
paper_title: Long‐term impact of COVID‐19 infection on cognitive dysfunction among Chinese older adults: a national cross‐sectional online study

summary: Cross-sectional cognitive assessment of 187 COVID-19 survivors one year after hospitalization in Brazil, with detailed neuropsychiatric testing on a subset of 26 participants. Found impairments in global cognition, attention, orientation, and episodic memory in those with abnormal TICS-M screening scores.
paper_authors: Danielle Calil Sousa; Arnaldo Santos Leite; Barbara Caroline Dias Faria; Luiz Gustavo Guimarães Sacramento; Carolina Coimbra Marinho; Paulo Caramelli
paper_title: Cognitive impairment one year after hospitalization due to COVID‐19 infection in Brazil: preliminary results.

summary: This retrospective cross-sectional study examines malnutrition risk and nutritional indicators in 174 COVID-19 patients during the rehabilitation phase in Hong Kong. While the paper studies patients in rehabilitation post-COVID, it focuses on acute/post-acute hospitalization outcomes rather than long COVID sequelae, and does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Terry Ho Yan Ting; Tiffany Hoi Man Lo; Winnie Wing Tung Lo; Qi Ding; Daniel Ka Lok Yuk; Elsie Hui; Maria Wing Sze Tang
paper_title: Inadequate energy and protein intake, underweight and malnutrition are associated with in‐hospital mortality among <scp>COVID</scp>‐19 rehabilitation patients during the omicron outbreak in Hong Kong

summary: Cross-sectional study nested within a prospective cohort examining caregiver burden in 52 older adults with post-COVID syndrome and their caregivers. Found 54.2% prevalence of caregiver burden, significantly associated with caregiver depressive symptoms, highlighting the need for long-term psychosocial support.
paper_authors: Fabiana Carla Matos da Cunha Cintra; Marco Túlio Cintra; Estevão Alves Vallle; Vitória Lanza Lommez; Júlia Monção Dias Carvalho; Antônio Augusto De Carvalho Duarte; Gerson Santos Azevedo; Iza de Faria Fortini; Bernardo De Mattos Viana; Maria Aparecida Camargos Bicalho
paper_title: Prevalence and factors associated with the burden of caregivers of older adults with post‐COVID syndrome

summary: This cross-sectional study uses 2022 BRFSS data to assess the prevalence of functional disabilities and adverse well-being among workers by employment status and COVID-19/Long COVID history. It finds that long COVID is associated with substantially elevated prevalence of cognitive disability and depression compared to 2019 pre-pandemic levels, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Sharon R. Silver; Jia Li; Nicole D. Ford; Sharon H. Saydah
paper_title: Functional disabilities and adverse well‐being by COVID‐19 and Long COVID history and employment status: 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing post-COVID patients (n=26) and healthy controls (n=57) to examine neuropsychiatric symptoms, inflammatory markers, and gut microbiome alterations. Found elevated depression, increased CCL23 levels, and dysbiosis in post-COVID patients but no differences in Alzheimer's disease markers.
paper_authors: Vijayasree V. Giridharan; Celso Catumbela; Bruno Kluwe‐Schiavon; Camila O. Arent; Laura A. Borba; Margarete D. Bagatini; Zuleide M. Ignácio; Lucas C. Pedro; Luciane B. Ceretta; João Quevedo; Rodrigo Morales; Gislaine Z. Reus; Tatiana Barichello
paper_title: Increased Myeloid Progenitor Inhibitory Factor 1 and Dysbiosis in Mild COVID‐19 Patients With No Change in Alzheimer's Disease Markers

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of the 2022 National Health Interview Survey examining employment status, work limitations, and sickness absenteeism among US adults with and without long COVID (n=26,270). Long COVID was associated with higher odds of work limitations, cognitive dysfunction, and sickness absenteeism, but the study does not evaluate any treatment interventions.
paper_authors: Nicole D. Ford; Alexandra F. Dalton; Deja Edwards; Hope King; Sara E. Luckhaupt; Kevin C. Ma; Douglas Slaughter; Sharon R. Silver; Sharon Saydah
paper_title: Employment Status, Work Limitations, Cognitive Dysfunction, and Sickness Absenteeism Among US Adults With and Without Long COVID

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing cognitive assessment tools (MoCA vs PROMIS) in long COVID patients. Finds that self-rated PROMIS cognitive function scores are better predictors of functional impairment than traditional neuropsychological testing in long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Kristen E. Kehl‐Floberg; Aurora Pop‐Vicas; Dorothy F. Edwards
paper_title: Self‐rated PROMIS cognitive function is a better predictor of long COVID related functional impairment than the Montreal Cognitive Assessment

summary: A cross-sectional study nested in a prospective cohort examining cognitive, clinical, and functional outcomes in 80 elderly Brazilian patients with post-COVID syndrome (mean 10 months post-infection). The study found high prevalence of cognitive impairment (77.5%), functional disability (73.33%), frailty (37.50%), and dyspnea (88.75%), with implications for early identification and management in aging populations.
paper_authors: Fabiana Carla Matos da Cunha Cintra; Marco Túlio Cintra; Henrique Dias Furtado De Souza; Luciano Pimenta Júnior; Gabriel de Faria Chaimowicz; Marcus Vinicius Miranda Macedo; Iza de Faria Fortini; Bernardo de Mattos Viana; Maria Aparecida Camargos Bicalho
paper_title: Cognitive and Clinical‐Functional Outcomes in Elderly People with Post‐COVID Syndrome: Data from a Brazilian Cohort

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing neuropsychiatric testing outcomes in 279 patients with and without long COVID, finding that long-COVID patients had significantly worse cognitive test results and higher rates of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) diagnoses. The study includes COVID-negative controls and COVID-positive patients both with and without long-COVID symptoms, using standardized UDS3 cognitive testing and NACC diagnostic criteria.
paper_authors: Jennifer A. Frontera; Arjun V. Masurkar; Alok Vedvyas; Rebecca A. Betensky; Allal Boutajangout; Manisha Bohara; Joshua Chodosh; Salma Hammam; Li Jiang; Jon Links; Karyn Marsh; Sujata Thawani; Daria Vasilchenko; Amin Yakubov; Yulin Ge; Thomas Wisniewski
paper_title: Long‐COVID‐19 Symptoms are associated with Abnormal Cognitive Testing and Mild Cognitive Impairment Compared to Controls

summary: This cross-sectional study examines the occurrence and risk factors of PTSD among 144 discharged COVID-19 patients in China, finding a 16% PTSD occurrence rate. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 recovery and psychological outcomes, not long COVID or treatment interventions.
paper_authors: Zaoxian Mei; Xiaohui Wu; Xueli Zhang; Xingjie Zheng; Wenxin Li; Rui Fan; Hongwei Yu; Shunming Zhang; Yeqing Gu; Xuena Wang; Yang Xia; Ge Meng; Jun Shen; Kaijun Niu
paper_title: The occurrence and risk factors associated with post‐traumatic stress disorder among discharged COVID‐19 patients in Tianjin, China

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the correlation between cognitive impairment and functional disability in 80 elderly people 2-24 months after COVID-19 infection. Found significant correlations between cognitive impairment and functional disability across multiple domains, but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Fabiana Carla Matos da Cunha Cintra; Marco Túlio Cintra; Gerson Santos Azevedo; João Vitor de Queiroz Campos; Gabriel Brant Moreira Ferreira; Júlia Dias; Iza de Faria Fortini; Bernardo de Mattos Viana; Maria Aparecida Camargos Bicalho
paper_title: Correlation between Cognitive Impairment and Functional Disability in Elderly People After COVID‐19

summary: Cross-sectional study of 844 COVID-19 recovered patients examining associations between self-stigma, PTSD, mental health, quality of life, and insomnia using structural equation modeling. Found that mental health mediates relationships between COVID-related self-stigma and PTSD with quality of life and insomnia outcomes, but no intervention or treatment was tested.
paper_authors: Hosein Mahmoudi; Mohsen Saffari; Mahmoud Movahedi; Hormoz Sanaeinasab; Hojat Rashidi‐Jahan; Morteza Pourgholami; Ali Poorebrahim; Jalal Barshan; Milad Ghiami; Saman Khoshmanesh; Marc N. Potenza; Chung‐Ying Lin; Amir H. Pakpour
paper_title: A mediating role for mental health in associations between COVID‐19‐related self‐stigma, PTSD, quality of life, and insomnia among patients recovered from COVID‐19

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing neurologic manifestations of long COVID across age groups in 200 hospitalized and 1,100 non-hospitalized patients. Found that younger and middle-aged adults experience higher symptom burden and cognitive dysfunction despite lower rates of abnormal neurologic findings compared to older patients.
paper_authors: Natasha A. Choudhury; Shreya Mukherjee; Tracey Singer; Aditi Venkatesh; Gina S. Perez Giraldo; Millenia Jimenez; Janet Miller; Melissa Lopez; Barbara A. Hanson; Aasheeta P. Bawa; Ayush Batra; Eric M. Liotta; Igor J. Koralnik
paper_title: Neurologic Manifestations of Long <scp>COVID</scp> Disproportionately Affect Young and Middle‐Age Adults

summary: Prospective cross-sectional study of 226 post-COVID-19 patients examining new-onset chronic pain, neuropathic pain, and their clinical associations. The study characterizes pain trajectories and phenotypes but does not evaluate any treatment intervention or outcome.
paper_authors: Gabriel T. Kubota; Felipe H. C. Soares; Alessandra S. da Fonseca; Talita dos Santos Rosa; Valquiria A. da Silva; Gisele R. Gouveia; Viviane G. Faria; Pedro H. M. da Cunha; André R. Brunoni; Manoel J. Teixeira; Daniel C. de Andrade
paper_title: Pain paths among post‐COVID‐19 condition subjects: A prospective cross‐sectional study with in‐person evaluation

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 29,079 Norwegian type 2 diabetes patients examining gender differences in COVID-19 experiences and long COVID symptom reporting. Finds that 27.3% of infected patients reported long COVID symptoms, with women significantly more likely to experience prolonged illness compared to men.
paper_authors: Grethe Åstrøm Ueland; Tony Ernes; Tone Vonheim Madsen; Sverre Sandberg; Bjørn Olav Åsvold; Karianne Fjeld Løvaas; John Graham Cooper
paper_title: Women Suffered More Than Men Both During and After the COVID‐19 Pandemic—A Cross‐Sectional Study Among 29,079 Patients With Type 2 Diabetes

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 410 post-COVID patients assessing depression prevalence using PHQ-9 and identifying associated factors. Found 23.7% prevalence of depression with multiple demographic and clinical correlates, but is an observational assessment study without any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Nguyen Thanh Binh; Tran Thien Thuan; Nguyen Hoang Tan Luc; Ho Tat Bang; Le Thi Diem Trinh
paper_title: Depression and related factors among patients with post‐COVID‐19 conditions: Cross‐sectional, hospital‐based study

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing long COVID symptom prevalence in 99 pregnant women who had COVID-19 during pregnancy versus 99 uninfected controls. Finds 74.7% of infected women had at least one long COVID symptom (fatigue, myalgia, anosmia most common), with prevalence correlating to acute disease severity.
paper_authors: Hülya Kandemir; Gül Alkan Bülbül; Emine Kirtiş; Selin Güney; Cem Yaşar Sanhal; İbrahim İnanç Mendilcioğlu
paper_title: Evaluation of <scp>long‐COVID</scp> symptoms in women infected with <scp>SARS‐CoV</scp>‐2 during pregnancy

summary: Cross-sectional observational study examining resting-state fMRI brain dynamics in post-COVID patients with and without persistent headache, using Hurst exponent as a measure of functional brain scaling. Finds that patients with ongoing post-COVID headache show suppressed brain dynamics compared to those without headache, suggesting a potential neurophysiological biomarker for this symptom.
paper_authors: Churchill NW; Roudaia E.; Jean Chen J.; Gilboa A.; Sekuler A.; Ji X.; Gao F.; Lin Z.; Masellis M.; Goubran M.; Rabin JS; Lam B.; Cheng I.; Fowler R.; Heyn C.; Black SE; MacIntosh BJ; Graham SJ; Schweizer TA
paper_title: Persistent post‐COVID headache is associated with suppression of scale‐free functional brain dynamics in non‐hospitalized individuals

summary: A cross-sectional study of 370 long COVID patients from a community rehabilitation service that characterizes symptom severity and functional disability using the COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale. The study identifies three distinct severity phenotypes (mild, moderate, severe) and explores correlations between symptom severity, functional disability, and overall health, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Manoj Sivan; Amy Parkin; Sophie Makower; Darren C. Greenwood
paper_title: Post‐COVID syndrome symptoms, functional disability, and clinical severity phenotypes in hospitalized and nonhospitalized individuals: A cross‐sectional evaluation from a community COVID rehabilitation service

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 1,062 healthcare workers assessing the prevalence (10%), determinants, and consequences of post-COVID including workplace contamination and return-to-work outcomes. Study documents symptoms and risk factors but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention for post-COVID.
paper_authors: Anastasia Saade; Quentin Didier; Léo Cha; Ronan Garlantezec; Christophe Paris; Pierre Tattevin
paper_title: The prevalence, determinants, and consequences of post‐COVID in healthcare workers: A cross‐sectional survey

summary: Retrospective cohort study comparing lung water density (LWD) measured by MRI in 185 COVID-19 survivors versus 109 healthy controls. Findings show elevated LWD in survivors, associated with hospitalization, comorbidities, elevated inflammatory biomarkers, and higher BMI.
paper_authors: Keen C.; Grenier J.; Šereš P.; Stobbe R.; White J.; Beaulieu C.; Sherrington R.; Kirkham A.; Paterson DI; Thompson R.
paper_title: <scp>MRI</scp> Assessment of Lung Water Density in Individuals Previously Infected With <scp>COVID</scp>‐19: A Cross‐Sectional Study

summary: A cross-sectional study of 48 patients hospitalized with COVID-19 in the first wave, interviewed ~553 days post-discharge to assess persistent symptoms and quality of life. Found 77.1% had ≥5 persistent symptoms (fatigue 79.2%, dyspnea 68.8%, weakness 60.4%), with 81.3% reporting poor quality of life and persistent fatigue significantly associated with symptom burden and reduced QoL.
paper_authors: Joseph P. Skinner; Lauren V. Moran
paper_title: Persistent effects of COVID‐19 in patients hospitalized during the first wave of the pandemic: The impact of persistent fatigue on quality of life in a cross‐sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing ventilation and perfusion scintigraphy findings in 33 post-COVID-19 individuals (23 symptomatic, 10 asymptomatic). Symptomatic patients showed significantly reduced radiopharmaceutical activity and pulmonary function compared to asymptomatic individuals, with up to 50% reduction in severe cases.

paper_title: Long COVID: Ventilation and Perfusion Are Reduced in Symptomatic Individuals Compared to Asymptomatic Patients—A V/Q Scintigraphy Study
paper_journal: International Journal of Imaging Systems and Technology

summary: Retrospective cohort study examining the prevalence and risk factors of memory impairment among 1,157 recovered COVID-19 patients in Iraq using the MAC-Q test. Found 34.49% with memory impairment and identified female gender, older age, repeated infections, severe disease, and multiple variant exposure as independent risk factors.
paper_authors: Muayad A. Merza; Hind B. Almufty; Heewa A. Younis; Suzan O. Rasool; Shinah A. Mohammed
paper_title: Memory impairment among recovered COVID‐19 patients: The prevalence and risk factors, a retrospective cohort study

summary: Cross-sectional study of 128 Brazilian adults examining associations between COVID-19 sequelae and periodontal disease/obesity. Found that individuals with both obesity and generalized periodontitis had 86% higher probability of reporting COVID-19 sequelae, but no significant associations in the overall sample.
paper_authors: Maísa Casarin; Francisco Hecktheuer Silva; Ana Flávia Leite Pontes; Betina Dutra Lima; Flavia Q. Pirih; Francisco Wilker Mustafa Gomes Muniz
paper_title: Association between sequelae of COVID‐19 with periodontal disease and obesity: A cross‐sectional study

summary: This prospective cross-sectional study compares health utility values and olfactory-specific quality of life between patients with COVID-19-related olfactory dysfunction and those with chronic rhinosinusitis/rhinitis-related olfactory dysfunction. While it includes COVID-19 patients, the study is primarily about comparing two etiologies of olfactory dysfunction rather than investigating long COVID or testing any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Thanh Luong; Sophie S. Jang; Mena Said; Adam S. DeConde; Carol H. Yan
paper_title: Impact of <scp>COVID</scp>‐19 versus chronic rhinosinusitis/rhinitis associated olfactory dysfunction on health utility and quality of life

summary: This cross-sectional study profiled 332 long COVID patients in the Brazilian Amazon region, examining hematological, coagulation, immunological, metabolic, hepatic, renal, and muscular biomarkers. The study identified associations between acute phase hospitalization and persistent laboratory abnormalities, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Vanessa Costa Alves Galúcio; Daniel Carvalho de Menezes; Elem Cristina Rodrigues Chaves; Ana Virgínia Soares van den Berg; Patrícia Danielle Lima de Lima; Pedro Fernando da Costa Vasconcelos; Juarez Antônio Simões Quaresma; Luiz Fábio Magno Falcão
paper_title: Laboratory profiling of patients with long COVID in the Brazilian Amazon region: A cross‐sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing patient-reported functional outcomes and fatigue 30 days after COVID-19 hospitalization in 55 survivors. Found high rates of new ADL difficulty/dependence and clinically significant fatigue worsening, but this is observational follow-up without intervention—not a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Evelyn S. Qin; Laura S. Gold; Catherine L. Hough; Patricia P. Katz; Aaron E. Bunnell; Katherine D. Wysham; James S. Andrews
paper_title: <scp>Patient‐reported</scp> functional outcomes 30 days after hospitalization for <scp>COVID</scp>‐19

summary: This retrospective cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence and risk factors for persistent symptoms (Long COVID) in 226 adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection presenting to primary care in Brazil. Key risk factors identified include ≥5 symptoms, female sex, and ages 40-49 and 70+ years, with cognitive symptoms (memory loss, attention loss) and anxiety showing the strongest associations.

paper_title: Symptoms and Risk Factors for Long COVID: A Cross‐Sectional Study in Primary Care

summary: This case-control study compares health-related quality of life (HRQOL) outcomes in COVID-19-recovered patients with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARD) versus matched controls without SARD. While it confirms post-COVID syndrome prevalence and documents HRQOL impairment, it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Pamela Munguía‐Realpozo; Claudia Mendoza‐Pinto; Sandra Ibañez‐Ovando; Ana Luisa Roco‐Zúñiga; Jesús Texis‐Ramírez; Juan Serrano‐Ramírez; Ivet Etchegaray‐Morales
paper_title: Health‐Related Quality of Life in Patients With Systemic Autoimmune Rheumatic Diseases (SARD) and Post‐COVID Syndrome: A Case‐Control Study

summary: This cross-sectional study examined electromyography (EMG) findings in 29 non-hospitalized long COVID patients and compared symptom severity, quality of life, and physical function between those with and without myopathic EMG changes. Myopathic EMG findings were present in 62% of patients, but no significant differences in clinical outcomes were observed between groups, suggesting myopathic EMG changes in long COVID should be interpreted cautiously within clinical context.
paper_authors: Atif Sepic; Andrea Tryfonos; Helene Rundqvist; Tommy R. Lundberg; Thomas Gustafsson; Kaveh Pourhamidi
paper_title: Non‐Hospitalized Patients With Post‐<scp>COVID</scp> Condition and Myopathic Electromyography Findings Show no Difference in Symptom Severity and Clinical Manifestations Compared to Those Without Myopathic Findings

summary: Cross-sectional observational study of 200 post-COVID-19 patients assessing fatigue and anhedonia using self-assessment scales. Found high prevalence of both symptoms with positive correlation between them, and negative correlation with time since recovery, but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Samir El Sayed; Doaa Shokry; Sarah Mohamed Gomaa
paper_title: Post‐COVID‐19 fatigue and anhedonia: A cross‐sectional study and their correlation to post‐recovery period

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 48 COVID-19 patients >1 year post-inpatient rehabilitation to examine how social determinants of health factors relate to long-term functional status and quality of life outcomes. Found that male gender, higher income, and urban residence were associated with better functional recovery and quality of life measures after rehabilitation.
paper_authors: Hannah Martin; Christopher Lewis; Sean Dreyer; Juliana Couri; Sanchita Sen; Prakash Jayabalan
paper_title: Social determinants of health and <scp>COVID</scp>‐19 recovery after inpatient rehabilitation

summary: Cross-sectional survey measuring compassion fatigue, work engagement, and psychological distress in 116 healthcare workers caring for long COVID patients. Finds that HCWs with personal history of long COVID and those in early career stages report significantly worse outcomes across all measures.
paper_authors: Hannah Uhlig‐Reche; Summer Rolin; Rasika Karnik; Maureen Lyons; Monica Verduzco‐Gutierrez
paper_title:
Compassion fatigue, work engagement, and psychological distress in health care workers treating patients with long
                    <scp>COVID</scp>

summary: This retrospective cross-sectional analysis of 1,237 long COVID patients at a post-COVID recovery clinic in British Columbia characterizes rehabilitation needs using objective tests and patient-reported outcomes. The study identifies high prevalence of rehabilitation needs across pulmonary, mental health, and neurological domains but does not test or evaluate any intervention.
paper_authors: Débora M. Petry Moecke; Evan H. Kwong; Sonya Cressman; Jennifer Yao; Chiara Singh; Carolyn Taylor; Pat G. Camp
paper_title:
Rehabilitation needs of long
                    <scp>COVID</scp>
                    patients in
                    <scp>British Columbia</scp>

summary: This cross-sectional study compared postural balance, fatigue, muscle strength, and quality of life between 40 post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) patients and 40 controls. PCS patients showed significantly worse postural balance and fatigue, with balance deficits correlating with reduced quality of life, but no intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Kennedy Cristian Alves de Sousa; Damara Guedes Gardel; Agnaldo José Lopes
paper_title: Postural balance and its association with functionality and quality of life in non‐hospitalized patients with post‐acute COVID‐19 syndrome

summary: This cross-sectional survey study compared mental and physical health outcomes between adults with diagnosed long COVID, self-reported long COVID, and no long COVID in California. While it documents significant differences in anxiety, depression, fatigue, and physical function across groups, it is observational without any intervention or treatment being tested.
paper_authors: Tyler B. Mason; Tara K. Knight; Ryan Lee; Shirin E. Herzig; Daniella Meeker; Jason N. Doctor
paper_title: Long covid and mental and physical health: A cross‐sectional study of adults in California

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing personality traits and psychological characteristics between 26 healthcare workers with long COVID and 141 without long COVID. Found that long COVID group had higher neuroticism scores and poorer mental health, suggesting neurotic tendency and high symptom burden may be risk factors for long COVID.
paper_authors: Keiko Sakai; Seiichiro Tarutani; Takehiko Okamura; Hiroshi Yoneda; Tatsuhito Kawasaki; Masatoshi Takeda
paper_title: Comparing personality traits of healthcare workers with and without long COVID: Cross‐sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional observational study comparing functional capacity in 159 adults and older people 1 month after COVID-19 hospitalization using the Barthel Index. Found that hospitalization impairs functional status, with older people showing greater functional decline; age, sarcopenia, and frailty were associated factors.
paper_authors: Gabriela Sayuri Ochiai; Caroline Gil de Godoy; Érika Christina Gouveia e. Silva; Danielle Brancolini de Oliveira; Elizabeth Mendes da Silva; Bianca de Oliveira Candido Viana; Juliana Magalhães da Silva; Roberta Oliveira Bueno de Souza; Michelle Didone dos Santos; Camila Machado de Campos; Ana Carolina Basso Schmitt; Celso Ricardo Fernandes de Carvalho; Carolina Fu; Clarice Tanaka; Carlos Toufen; Carlos Roberto Ribeiro de Carvalho; José Eduardo Pompeu
paper_title: Functional impact on adults and older people after hospitalization by Covid‐19

summary: Cross-sectional study examining ECG abnormalities in 244 Ugandan long COVID patients at least 2 months post-infection. Found 18.9% had abnormal ECG findings, with non-specific T-wave inversion being most common; no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Andrew Weil Semulimi; Charles Batte; Daniel Iraguha; Pamela Apio Okwir; Hope Atuhaire; Chelsea Lipoto; Tonny Muwonge; Norah Namirembe; Grace Biyinzika Lubega; Provia Ainembabazi; John Mukisa; Felix Bongomin; Isaac Ssinabulya; Emmy Okello
paper_title: Long COVID in Uganda: Electrographic findings among patients at risk

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 765 young Australians (aged 15-29) assessing the prevalence and impact of long COVID. Found 11.2% reported long COVID with significant impacts on work and daily functioning, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Robin Engelberts; Caitlin H. Douglass; Ana Orozco; Sarah Eddy; Anna Lee Wilkinson; Aimée Altermatt; Suzanne van den Toren; Megan S. C. Lim
paper_title: Understanding Long COVID Among Young People in Victoria, Australia: Prevalence, Impact, and Associated Factors

summary: This cross-sectional survey of 4,315 healthcare workers in Germany examined the prevalence and risk factors for post-COVID fatigue symptoms in spring 2021, using the Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory. Severe fatigue occurred in 10.7% of respondents and was associated with preexisting mental/respiratory conditions, acute infection severity, psychological distress, lower quality of life, and work incapacity.
paper_authors: Julia Haller; Rüya-Daniela Kocalevent; Albert Nienhaus; Claudia Peters; Corinna Bergelt; Uwe Koch-Gromus
paper_title: Anhaltende Fatigue als Folge einer COVID-19-Infektion bei Beschäftigten im Gesundheitswesen: Risikofaktoren und Auswirkungen auf die Lebensqualität

summary: Cross-sectional comparison of health-related quality of life (SF-12) in 192 severe vs 192 non-severe COVID-19 patients at 6 months post-discharge. Severe COVID-19 patients had significantly lower HRQOL scores (34.45 vs 39.64), suggesting long-term quality of life impairment correlates with acute infection severity.
