paper_title: The impact of long COVID on health-related quality of life in patients 6 months after discharge with severe COVID-19

summary: Cross-sectional study examining brain metabolic connectivity using FDG-PET in 44 long COVID patients across acute, subacute, and chronic phases compared to healthy controls. Found hyperconnectivity in executive and attention networks in acute/subacute phase that becomes hypoconnectivity in chronic phase, suggesting connectivity dysfunction may underlie persistent neurological symptoms.
paper_authors: Anna Lisa Martini; Giulia Carli; Silvia Paola Caminiti; Lorenzo Kiferle; Andrea Leo; Daniela Perani; Stelvio Sestini
paper_title: Persistent dysfunctions of brain metabolic connectivity in long-covid with cognitive symptoms
paper_journal: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

summary: Population-based survey of 1,087 Michigan adults diagnosed with COVID-19 examining predictors of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Study found that long COVID (symptom duration >60 days), pandemic-related economic disruption, and worse acute symptom severity were associated with poor mental health outcomes, but did not test or evaluate any intervention.
paper_authors: Andrea R. Titus; Briana Mezuk; Jana L. Hirschtick; Patricia McKane; Michael R. Elliott; Nancy L. Fleischer
paper_title: Patterns and predictors of depressive and anxiety symptoms within a population-based sample of adults diagnosed with COVID-19 in Michigan

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed olfactory recovery patterns in 200 recovered COVID-19 patients using subjective and objective measures (Sniffin' Sticks test) over three months. While 55% of patients reported subjective smell recovery at 3 months, objective testing revealed only 1% had normal olfactory function, indicating persistent objective deficits despite perceived recovery.
paper_authors: Ehab Abou Zaid; Ahmad Mohamed Eltelety; Khaled Omar Azooz; Gouda Ragab; Ahmed Amin Nassar
paper_title: Assessment of olfactory recovery after COVID-19: cross-sectional study

summary: This online survey of 3,472 COVID-19 patients across France and Mexico explores associations between self-reported olfactory loss and cognitive/affective complaints. While it documents symptom associations relevant to long COVID, it is an observational cross-sectional survey that does not evaluate any treatment or intervention, and therefore does not meet criteria for inclusion in a clinical trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: Christophe Bousquet; Veronica Pereda-Loth; Denis Pierron; Mauricio Gonzalez-Navarro; Santiago Avila-Ríos; Nathalie Mandairon; Camille Ferdenzi; Moustafa Bensafi
paper_title: Self-reported cognitive and affective complaints associated with olfactory loss in an online survey of individuals with COVID-19

summary: This case-control study compared neuropsychological performance between 20 long COVID patients with fatigue and 20 SARS-CoV-2 negative controls via telephone-based testing. Results show that post-COVID fatigue is significantly associated with decreased cognitive performance on standardized neuropsychological measures.
paper_authors: Cristian O. Mancilla-Corona; Manuel Sanchez-Alavez; Gisela Pineda-García; Julieta Y. Islas-Limon; Oscar E. Zazueta; Jonathan V. Lopez-Baena; Jesús I. Rodríguez-Vásquez; Idanya R. Serafin-Higuera
paper_title: The influence of physical fatigue on telephone-based neuropsychological test performance in COVID-19 survivors
paper_journal: European Archives of Psychiatry and Clinical Neuroscience

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 535 COVID-19 survivors 1 year post-discharge assessed mental health outcomes including anxiety, depression, PTSD, fatigue, and sleep quality using standardized scales. Chronic disease history, smoking, and low education were identified as risk factors for poor psychological and physical outcomes in survivors.
paper_authors: Zhuqing Li; Jiangming He; Yaqi Wang; Minghua Bai; Ying Zhang; Hongshu Chen; Wenle Li; Yuyang Cai; Shunqi Chen; Miao Qu; Ji Wang
paper_title: A cross-sectional study on the mental health of patients with COVID-19 1 year after discharge in Huanggang, China
paper_journal: European Archives of Psychiatry and Clinical Neuroscience

summary: Cross-sectional clinical phenotyping study of 157 post-COVID patients evaluating applicability of proposed subtypes (postintensive care syndrome, secondary diseases, fatigue, exacerbation, minimal complaints) using standardized neurological and psychological assessments. While the paper discusses treatment recommendations (SSRIs, psychotherapy, monitoring), it is a descriptive phenotyping study without an active intervention trial or treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Karen Humkamp; Ana Sofia Costa; Kathrin Reetz; Julia Walders
paper_title: Post-COVID-19-Zustand – klinische Phänotypisierung in der Praxis

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the correlation between persistent olfactory dysfunction and cognitive impairment in 241 long COVID patients in Brazil using standardized assessments (CCCRC and MoCA). Found a weak but significant association between olfactory severity and cognitive impairment (OR=2.87), suggesting olfactory dysfunction as a potential marker for cognitive monitoring.
paper_authors: Alna Carolina Mendes Paranhos; Apio Ricardo Nazareth Dias; Erick Antonio Rodrigues Mendes; Emily Vitória Almeida Paixão; Samuel Franco Viana Santos Silva; Lidiane Palheta Miranda dos Santos; Gisele Vieira Hennemann Koury; Mariângela Moreno Domingues; Juarez Antônio Simões Quaresma; Givago da Silva Souza; Luiz Fábio Magno Falcão
paper_title: Persistent olfactory dysfunction as an indicator of cognitive impairment in long COVID-19 syndrome: implications for monitoring and rehabilitation
paper_journal: European Archives of Psychiatry and Clinical Neuroscience

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed episodic memory function in 157 post-COVID condition patients versus 74 healthy controls using comprehensive neuropsychological testing. Patients with PCC showed significant impairment in memory encoding, learning, and retrieval processes, with findings relevant for characterizing cognitive deficits but no intervention or treatment evaluated.
paper_authors: Silvia Oliver-Mas; Jordi A. Matias-Guiu; Cristina Delgado-Alonso; María Valles-Salgado; María José Gil-Moreno; Juan I. López-Carbonero; Lucía Fernández-Romero; Constanza Cuevas; Alfonso Delgado-Álvarez; Jorge Matias-Guiu; Maria Diez-Cirarda
paper_title: Episodic memory deficits and processes in post-COVID condition
paper_journal: European Archives of Psychiatry and Clinical Neuroscience

summary: A large-scale cross-sectional study of 793 patients (723 PASC, 70 PVS) assessing cognitive function, depression, and fatigue using standardized neuropsychological tests and inflammatory markers. Cognitive impairment was highly prevalent (61.7% working speed deficits, 54.7% attention deficits), associated with older age, lower education, depression, and elevated CRP, with similar patterns observed in post-vaccination syndrome.
paper_authors: Evelyne Hanc; Katharina Koller; Regina Herold; Yesim Erim; Eva Morawa
paper_title: Cognitive impairment, depression, and fatigue in post-COVID and post-vaccination syndrome: a large-scale cross-sectional study
paper_journal: European Archives of Psychiatry and Clinical Neuroscience

summary: Multicenter retrospective cohort study assessing prevalence of post-COVID-19 respiratory symptoms at 11.2 months after hospital discharge in 1,950 COVID-19 survivors. Found 2.5% prevalence of long-term cough with no clear associated risk factors.
paper_authors: César Fernández-de-las-Peñas; Carlos Guijarro; Susana Plaza-Canteli; Valentín Hernández-Barrera; Juan Torres-Macho
paper_title: Prevalence of Post-COVID-19 Cough One Year After SARS-CoV-2 Infection: A Multicenter Study

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing cognitive and neuropsychological outcomes in 62 COVID-19 patients stratified by disease severity (outpatients vs. inpatients with hypoxemic pneumonia). Found that inpatients with hypoxia had greater impairments in attention and memory, while fatigue, depression, and anxiety were similarly high in both groups.
paper_authors: Thibaut Dondaine; Florine Ruthmann; Fanny Vuotto; Louise Carton; Patrick Gelé; Karine Faure; Dominique Deplanque; Régis Bordet
paper_title: Long-term cognitive impairments following COVID-19: a possible impact of hypoxia

summary: A cross-sectional study comparing cardiopulmonary function in 20 children with post-COVID-19 and 28 matched controls using exercise testing. Found significantly lower peak oxygen uptake in the post-COVID group, attributed to deconditioning rather than cardiac or pulmonary dysfunction.
paper_authors: Isabelle Schoeffl; Roman Raming; Jan-Philipp Tratzky; Adrian P. Regensburger; Calvin Kraus; Wolfgang Waellisch; Regina Trollmann; Joachim Woelfle; Sven Dittrich; Rafael Heiss; Ferdinand Knieling; Annika Weigelt
paper_title: Cardiopulmonary function in paediatric post-COVID-19: a controlled clinical trial

summary: A cross-sectional study examining brainstem raphe alterations in 70 long-COVID patients using transcranial sonography and their association with depressive and anxiety symptoms. Hypoechogenic brainstem raphe was found in 28.6% of patients and independently associated with higher depressive symptoms, but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Daniel Richter; Hannah Schulze; Jeyanthan Charles James; Nadine Siems; Nadine Trampe; Ralf Gold; Christos Krogias; Simon Faissner
paper_title: Hypoechogenicity of brainstem raphe in long-COVID syndrome–less common but independently associated with depressive symptoms: a cross-sectional study

summary: A multicentre cross-sectional cohort study comparing long COVID symptoms in children and adolescents infected with SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant versus uninfected controls. Most PCS-associated symptoms were comparable between groups, though concentration disorders and impaired physical performance were more frequent in the COVID-19 group.
paper_authors: Anne Schlegtendal; Christoph Maier; Julien Stein; Jakob Höpner; Astrid Petersmann; Denisa Drinka; Reinhard Berner; Thomas Lücke; Nicole Toepfner; Folke Brinkmann
paper_title: Post-coronavirus disease 2019–associated symptoms among children and adolescents in the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron era

summary: A cross-sectional study comparing long-COVID prevalence and clinical characteristics in 147 children with and without immunodeficiency using a parent-completed questionnaire. Immunocompetent children showed higher long-COVID prevalence (60% at 12 weeks vs 35.7% in immunocompromised) and greater impact on daily functioning, with immunocompromised children experiencing milder symptoms overall.
paper_authors: Karolina Kuczborska; Piotr Buda; Janusz Książyk
paper_title: Long-COVID in immunocompromised children

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluates lung ultrasound and diaphragm excursion in 45 COVID-19 ARDS survivors to assess their relationship with dyspnea and exercise tolerance. While the study assesses long COVID sequelae (persistent dyspnea in post-ICU survivors), it is a diagnostic/observational study without any intervention, making it ineligible for a treatment trials analysis.
paper_authors: Gerardo Eman; Shwe Synn; Benjamin Galen; Roshni Shah; Peter Nauka; Aluko A. Hope; Seth Congdon; Marjan Islam
paper_title: Thoracic Ultrasound in COVID-19: Use of Lung and Diaphragm Ultrasound in Evaluating Dyspnea in Survivors of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome from COVID-19 Pneumonia in a Post-ICU Clinic

summary: This cross-sectional study surveyed 366 UK long COVID patients to quantify productivity losses and informal care burden since infection. While directly relevant to long COVID, the paper is an observational survey without any treatment intervention—it measures economic impact rather than testing a therapy or intervention.
paper_authors: Joseph Kwon; Ruairidh Milne; Clare Rayner; Román Rocha Lawrence; Jordan Mullard; Ghazala Mir; Brendan Delaney; Manoj Sivan; Stavros Petrou
paper_title: Impact of Long COVID on productivity and informal caregiving
paper_journal: The European Journal of Health Economics

summary: A cross-sectional study of 520 Arabic COVID-19 patients examining the prevalence and characteristics of post-COVID-19 syndrome, finding 25% developed persistent symptoms lasting ≥28 days. The study identified female sex, hospitalization during acute infection, and chronic diseases as significant risk factors, but did not evaluate any interventions or treatments.
paper_authors: Nagla Mahmoud; Nashwa Radwan; Abdullah Alkattan; Mustafa Hassanien; Elfadil Elkajam; Sara Alqahtani; Alhan Haji; Amal Alfaifi; Amjad Alfaleh; Khaled Alabdulkareem
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 syndrome: nature of symptoms and associated factors

summary: Cross-sectional study of 2023 that classifies long COVID patients into five symptom clusters based on subjective symptoms at first outpatient visit and evaluates their background characteristics including autonomic dysfunction and work status. Study provides descriptive classification but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Tomoya Tsuchida; Naohito Yoshimura; Kosuke Ishizuka; Kohta Katayama; Yoko Inoue; Masanori Hirose; Yu Nakagama; Yasutoshi Kido; Hiroki Sugimori; Takahide Matsuda; Yoshiyuki Ohira
paper_title: Five cluster classifications of long COVID and their background factors: A cross-sectional study in Japan

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing physical activity levels, respiratory and peripheral muscle strength, and pulmonary function in 54 young post-COVID-19 patients versus 46 controls at least 6 months after mild COVID-19 infection. Found that respiratory and peripheral muscle strength and physical activity levels were significantly reduced in COVID-19 patients compared to controls, with persistent dyspnea and fatigue.
paper_authors: Musa Güneş; Metehan Yana; Meral Boşnak Güçlü
paper_title: Physical activity levels respiratory and peripheral muscle strength and pulmonary function in young post-COVID-19 patients

summary: This cross-sectional study examines the financial burden of post-acute COVID-19 syndrome in German patients, including employment status changes, income loss, and out-of-pocket payments for diagnostics and therapies. While it is about long COVID, it does not study or evaluate any treatment intervention—it only documents patients' financial experiences and their use of various paid services.
paper_authors: Jennifer Scheel-Barteit; Caroline Floto; Henrike Höpfner; Thomas Kühlein; Bettina Hohberger; Maria Sebastião
paper_title: Financial burden of patients with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome

summary: Cross-sectional study of 25,389 US adults examining family history of cancer as a risk factor for Long COVID using National Health Interview Survey data. Found that adults with family history of cancer were 1.26 times more likely to have Long COVID, with 30% of the association mediated through underlying health conditions.
paper_authors: Hannah L. Wilkey; Biplab Kumar Datta
paper_title: Family history of cancer as a risk factor for Long COVID among United States adults

summary: This cross-sectional study compared left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LV-GLS) in 70 asymptomatic outpatients who recently recovered from COVID-19 versus 70 matched healthy controls using echocardiography. The COVID-19 group showed significantly impaired LV-GLS, suggesting subclinical myocardial dysfunction during early recovery, but no intervention or treatment was tested.
paper_authors: Turhan Turan; Ahmet Özderya; Sinan Şahin; Ali Hakan Konuş; Selim Kul; Ali Rıza Akyüz; Ezgi Kalaycıoğlu; Muhammet Raşit Sayın
paper_title: Left ventricular global longitudinal strain in low cardiac risk outpatients who recently recovered from coronavirus disease 2019
paper_journal: The International Journal of Cardiovascular Imaging

summary: Cross-sectional study measuring flow-mediated dilation (FMD) to assess endothelial dysfunction in 59 COVID-19 patients and 33 controls two months post-infection. Found COVID-19 independently predicted endothelial dysfunction, but the study is observational without treatment intervention and therefore excluded from the treatment trial pipeline.
paper_authors: Elif Ergül; Ahmet Seyda Yılmaz; Muhammet Mürsel Öğütveren; Nadir Emlek; Uğur Kostakoğlu; Mustafa Çetin
paper_title: COVID 19 disease independently predicted endothelial dysfunction measured by flow-mediated dilatation
paper_journal: The International Journal of Cardiovascular Imaging

summary: Secondary analysis of National Health Interview Survey data (2022-2023) examining cognitive difficulties in individuals with ME/CFS and long COVID. Found ME/CFS and long COVID significantly associated with reported cognitive impairments, with comorbid cases showing greatest risk.
paper_authors: Zoe Sirotiak; Jenna L. Adamowicz; Emily B. K. Thomas
paper_title: Cognitive Impairments in Two Samples of Individuals with ME/CFS and Long COVID: A Comparative Analysis
paper_journal: Journal of Clinical Psychology in Medical Settings

summary: A cross-sectional study of 318 long COVID patients assessing health-related quality of life using SF-36 and RehabNeQ instruments, stratified by symptom duration and symptom count. Finds that both mental and physical quality of life are significantly reduced compared to general population, with symptom burden and work ability as key drivers of these deficits.
paper_authors: Christina Lemhöfer; Christian Sturm; Dana Loudovici-Krug; Christoph Guntenbrunner; Marcus Bülow; Philipp Reuken; Stefanie Quickert; Norman Best
paper_title: Quality of life and ability to work of patients with Post-COVID syndrome in relation to the number of existing symptoms and the duration since infection up to 12 months: a cross-sectional study

summary: This study analyzes the 100 most-viewed YouTube videos about long COVID, examining their sources, engagement metrics, and content. The paper is a descriptive analysis of media content rather than a clinical study or intervention trial, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: Erin T. Jacques; Corey H. Basch; Eunsun Park; Betty Kollia; Emma Barry
paper_title: Long Haul COVID-19 Videos on YouTube: Implications for Health Communication

summary: A cross-sectional study comparing symptom presentation and quality of life between people with ME/CFS, post-COVID condition, and healthy controls in Australia. The study found both patient cohorts experienced similar debilitating symptoms and significantly lower quality-of-life scores compared to controls, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Breanna Weigel; Natalie Eaton-Fitch; Kiran Thapaliya; Sonya Marshall-Gradisnik
paper_title: Illness presentation and quality of life in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome and post COVID-19 condition: a pilot Australian cross-sectional study

summary: A retrospective cross-sectional study assessing myocardial function and exercise capacity in 56 symptomatic long COVID patients, stratified by prior COVID-19 severity. Found subclinical left ventricular dysfunction (increased global wasted work, decreased work efficiency) and substantially reduced peak oxygen uptake, with severity being an independent predictor of myocardial dysfunction.
paper_authors: Luciana Bartolomei Orru D’Ávila; Mauricio Milani; David C. S. Le Bihan; Alexandra Correa Gervazoni Balbuena de Lima; Juliana Goulart Prata Oliveira Milani; Graziella França Bernardelli Cipriano; Vinicius Zacarias Maldaner da Silva; Gerson Cipriano Jr
paper_title: Longitudinal strain and myocardial work in symptomatic patients having recovered from COVID-19 and possible associations with the severity of the disease
paper_journal: The International Journal of Cardiovascular Imaging

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing pupillary light responses in 35 post-COVID subjects (71% with long COVID) versus 30 healthy controls using infrared pupillometry. Found significant alterations in pupillary contractile responses indicative of parasympathetic dysfunction, with correlations between symptom severity and pupil metrics, but no treatment intervention tested.
paper_authors: Gulfidan Bitirgen; Celalettin Korkmaz; Adil Zamani; Mehmet Sinan Iyisoy; Hurkan Kerimoglu; Rayaz A. Malik
paper_title: Abnormal quantitative pupillary light responses following COVID-19

summary: This epidemiological study analyzes long COVID prevalence and disability across demographic groups in the US using national survey data, finding higher rates among women, Hispanic people, sexual/gender minorities, and those without college degrees. The paper does not evaluate any treatment or intervention, focusing instead on prevalence patterns and workplace accommodation disparities.
paper_authors: Jennifer Cohen; Yana van der Meulen Rodgers
paper_title: Long COVID Prevalence, Disability, and Accommodations: Analysis Across Demographic Groups

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of 414 long COVID patients identifying mental health symptoms through patient-generated text data, using BERTopic analysis to categorize anxiety (35%), depression (29%), cognitive impairment (22%), and mood disturbances. Study develops understanding of mental health impact but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Nancy E. Mayo; Stanley Hum; Mohamad Matout; Lesley K. Fellows; Marie-Josée Brouillette
paper_title: Portrait of mental health identified by people with the post-covid syndrome

summary: A cross-sectional investigation comparing symptom clusters and patient-reported outcomes between people with ME/CFS and post-COVID condition (PCC). The study identifies associations between autonomic symptoms and functional impairment but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Breanna Weigel; Natalie Eaton-Fitch; Kiran Thapaliya; Sonya Marshall-Gradisnik
paper_title: A pilot cross-sectional investigation of symptom clusters and associations with patient-reported outcomes in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome and Post COVID-19 Condition

summary: This cross-sectional study examined multidimensional correlates of long COVID symptom burden in 656 participants, using latent profile analysis to categorize participants into low, medium, and high symptom-burden groups. While the study identifies important social, behavioral, and healthcare factors associated with symptom severity, it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Carolyn E. Schwartz; Katrina Borowiec; Bruce D. Rapkin
paper_title: The faces of Long-COVID: interplay of symptom burden with socioeconomic, behavioral and healthcare factors

summary: Cross-sectional structural equation model analysis of 535 adults from the Quebec Action for Post-COVID cohort examining interrelationships among fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, activity/role functioning, and mental health in post-COVID-19 syndrome. Study identifies fatigue and self-reported cognitive concerns as key factors associated with mental health symptoms but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Henry Ukachukwu Michael; Fernando Gonzales Aste; Marie-Josée Brouillette; Lesley K. Fellows; Nancy E. Mayo
paper_title: How do fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, activity and role functioning, and mental health inter-relate in adults with post-COVID-19 syndrome? A structural equation model analysis

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence of post-COVID-19 syndrome and its impact on health-related quality of life among 249 healthcare workers at a Tunisian university hospital. Found that 65% experienced post-COVID syndrome with 28.6% reporting low overall quality of life, with gender, post-COVID status, and time off work significantly associated with QoL scores.
paper_authors: Amene Fki; Imène Kacem; Chaima Sridi; Farah Chelly; Rania Bouchech; Nabil Ben Gadha; Mohamed Kahloul; Sonia Ksibi
paper_title: Post COVID-19 infection and quality of life of healthcare workers at Sahloul University Hospital of Sousse in Tunisia

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 350 COVID-19 recovered patients identifying new or worsening overactive bladder symptoms 10-14 weeks post-hospitalization, with median OAB symptom and quality-of-life scores reported by sex. The study documents the prevalence and burden of post-COVID genitourinary symptoms but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Laura E. Lamb; Ryan Timar; Melissa Wills; Sorabh Dhar; Steve M. Lucas; Dragana Komnenov; Michael B. Chancellor; Nivedita Dhar
paper_title: Long COVID and COVID-19-associated cystitis (CAC)

summary: This prospective follow-up study of individuals tested for SARS-CoV-2 at Geneva University Hospitals assessed the prevalence, severity, and impact of post-COVID fatigue and post-exertional malaise at 6+ months post-infection using standardized scales (ECOG, Chalder, DePaul). The study characterizes symptom burden and functional impairment in long COVID patients but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Mayssam Nehme; Francois Chappuis; Laurent Kaiser; Frederic Assal; Idris Guessous
paper_title: The Prevalence, Severity, and Impact of Post-COVID Persistent Fatigue, Post-Exertional Malaise, and Chronic Fatigue Syndrome

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of the 2022 National Health Interview Survey examining health service utilization patterns and barriers to care among US adults with post-COVID-19 condition (PCC). Finds that individuals with PCC history were significantly more likely to use various health services and report both financial and nonfinancial barriers to care compared to other US adults.
paper_authors: Hiten Naik; Roy H. Perlis; Karen C. Tran; John A. Staples
paper_title: Self-reported Health Service Utilization and Barriers to Care Among US Adults with a History of Post COVID-19 Condition

summary: This national survey study examines self-reported long COVID symptoms among 409,087 working-age U.S. adults and their associations with demographic and socioeconomic characteristics. The paper documents that long COVID is disproportionately reported among Hispanic individuals and economically disadvantaged populations, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Nicolo A. Villasis; Jasmeen J. Santos; Susan L. Ettner; Haiyong Xu; José J. Escarce; Lucinda B. Leung
paper_title: Long COVID Disproportionately Reported by Disadvantaged Individuals: A National Survey of U.S. Working-Age Adults

summary: This cross-sectional study validates the RECOVER PASC diagnostic scoring tool in 130 long COVID patients and 60 recovered controls to assess its sensitivity and specificity for LC diagnosis. The PASC score showed 100% specificity but limited 80% sensitivity, and the authors identified symptom combinations (loss of smell/taste, post-exertional malaise, sexual dysfunction) with superior diagnostic accuracy.
paper_authors: Alba Azola; Raha M. Dastgheyb; Rebecca Easter; Hannah Parker; Christina Della Penna; Isabel Santiuste; Holly Schultz; Ana Ehrenspeck; Rebecca Veenhuis; Leah H. Rubin
paper_title: Putting the PASC Score to the Test: Clinical vs. Statistical Accuracy in Long COVID Diagnosis

summary: An observational cross-sectional study evaluating the Alcohol Sniff Test (AST) as a screening tool for post-viral olfactory dysfunction (PVOD) in patients with flu-like syndrome. While the paper mentions COVID-19 as one cause of PVOD, it is primarily focused on diagnostic tool validation rather than studying a treatment for long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Domenico Seabra Modesto; Hugo Machado Silva Neto; Felipe Carvalho Leão; José Arruda Mendes Neto; Fábio Akira Suzuki
paper_title: Alcohol Sniff Test (AST): An Important Tool for Screening Post-Viral Olfactory Loss in Acute Flu-Like Dysfunction
paper_journal: Indian Journal of Otolaryngology and Head & Neck Surgery

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 114 Irish senior physicians assessing burnout and long COVID prevalence during the pandemic. While the paper includes long COVID prevalence data (25% reported personal or colleague experience), it does not study or evaluate any treatment or intervention for long COVID.
paper_authors: Anne M. Doherty; Gabrielle C. Colleran; Laura Durcan; Alan D. Irvine; Elizabeth Barrett
paper_title: A pilot study of burnout and long covid in senior specialist doctors

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing caspase 3, caspase 8, and BDNF levels in individuals with and without COVID-19 to assess associations with psychiatric symptoms. Found elevated biomarkers in COVID-19 patients but no significant associations with symptom severity or psychiatric conditions.
paper_authors: Lia D. R. Broseghini; Camila O. Arent; Lucas C. Pedro; Laísa N. dos Santos; Flávia S. Niero; Gabriel S. Mondo; Amanda G. Bertollo; Maiqueli Eduarda D. Mingoti; Khyani Mathias; Lucineia G. Danielski; Tatiana Barichello; João Quevedo; Luciane B. Ceretta; Zuleide Maria Ignácio; Fabricia Petronilho; Gislaine Z. Réus
paper_title: Caspases and brain-derived Neurotrophic Factor Levels and their Correlations with Psychiatric Symptoms in post-COVID-19

summary: This cross-sectional study compares gut microbiome composition and inflammatory markers between post-COVID-19 individuals and healthy controls. While it identifies significant alterations in microbiome diversity and inflammatory profiles in long COVID patients, it is observational without any intervention or treatment being tested.
paper_authors: Tatiana Barichello; Bruno Kluwe-Schiavon; Laura A. Borba; Lucas C. Pedro; Flávia S. Niero; Laísa N. dos Santos; Letícia M. Leonardo; Zuleide M. Ignácio; Rodrigo Morales; Luciane B. Ceretta; Gislaine Z. Reus
paper_title: Alterations in Gut Microbiome Composition and Increased Inflammatory Markers in Post-COVID-19 Individuals

summary: This prospective cross-sectional study evaluates olfactory and gustatory symptoms in 76 patients with mild acute COVID-19 during a 2-week follow-up period. The study documents prevalence and time course of smell/taste loss during acute infection, not post-acute sequelae or long COVID.
paper_authors: Mahboobeh Karimi-Galougahi; Ali Safavi Naini; Jahangir Ghorbani; Nasim Raad; Negar Raygani
paper_title: Emergence and Evolution of Olfactory and Gustatory Symptoms in Patients with COVID-19 in the Outpatient Setting
paper_journal: Indian Journal of Otolaryngology and Head & Neck Surgery

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing neurologic manifestations and cognitive profiles between post-hospitalization and non-hospitalized long COVID patients in Nigeria. Findings show high prevalence of brain fog, fatigue, and sleep problems, with some evidence of mild cognitive impairment on standardized assessments.
paper_authors: Iorhen Ephraim Akase; Osigwe Paul Agabi; Oluwadamilola Omolara Ojo; Roosevelt Amaobichukwu Anyanwu; Samuel Awodumila; Sodiq Ayilara; Obiamaka Jane Ede; Pheekanmilla Ghajiga; Olufunto Kalejaiye; Chibueze Nwanmah; Francisca Nwaokorie; Ann Ogbenna; Moyinoluwa Olajide; Gina S. Perez-Giraldo; Zachary Steven Orban; Millenia Jimenez; Igor Jerome Koralnik; Njideka Ulunma Okubadejo
paper_title: A systematic analysis of neurologic manifestations of Long COVID in Nigeria

summary: Cross-sectional study examining longer-term mental health consequences of COVID-19 infection (≥6 months post-infection) in 277 Black and White adults, with analysis of moderation by race and socioeconomic status. COVID-19 history was associated with significantly greater depressive, anxiety, PTSD, and insomnia symptoms, with education level moderating these relationships.
paper_authors: Michelle K. Williams; Christopher A. Crawford; Tamika C. Zapolski; Adam T. Hirsh; Jesse C. Stewart
paper_title: Longer-Term Mental Health Consequences of COVID-19 Infection: Moderation by Race and Socioeconomic Status

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of chronic fatigue syndrome and post-traumatic stress disorder among 120 COVID-19 survivors 6 months post-infection using validated questionnaires. The study found low prevalence rates (CFS 2.5%, PTSD 5.8%) with no significant association between the two conditions, but did not test or evaluate any interventions.
paper_authors: Leila Simani; Mahtab Ramezani; Ilad Alavi Darazam; Mastooreh Sagharichi; Mohammad Amin Aalipour; Fatemeh Ghorbani; Hossein Pakdaman
paper_title: Prevalence and correlates of chronic fatigue syndrome and post-traumatic stress disorder after the outbreak of the COVID-19

summary: A cross-sectional study assessing long-term persistent symptoms in 112 COVID-19 patients with and without diabetes mellitus at 9 months post-infection. Patients with diabetes reported significantly higher rates of fatigue, shortness of breath, and chest pain compared to non-diabetic patients.
paper_authors: Ahmed Mechi; Alhan Al-Khalidi; Rasha AL-Darraji; Mohammed Noori Al-Dujaili; Karrar Al-Buthabhak; Mohammed Alareedh; Foaad Shaghee; Hussein Nafakhi
paper_title: Long-term persistent symptoms of COVID-19 infection in patients with diabetes mellitus
paper_journal: International Journal of Diabetes in Developing Countries

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of 50,402 COVID-19 patients in Germany identifying risk factors for long COVID syndrome development. Lipid metabolism disorders and obesity are identified as strong independent risk factors, along with age, female sex, and pre-existing conditions like asthma and depression.
paper_authors: Sven H. Loosen; Björn-Erik Ole Jensen; Christian Tanislav; Tom Luedde; Christoph Roderburg; Karel Kostev
paper_title: Obesity and lipid metabolism disorders determine the risk for development of long COVID syndrome: a cross-sectional study from 50,402 COVID-19 patients

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 744 Saudi Arabian COVID-19 recovered patients assessing the prevalence and severity of persistent post-COVID symptoms. Found that 47.5% experienced ongoing symptoms, most commonly fatigue (25.4%), headache (15.9%), and myalgia (8.5%), with notable anxiety and depression rates.
paper_authors: Mohammed A. Garout; Saleh A. K. Saleh; Heba M. Adly; Altaf A. Abdulkhaliq; Abdullah A. Khafagy; Magda R. Abdeltawab; Ali A. Rabaan; Alfonso J. Rodriguez-Morales; Jaffar A. Al-Tawfiq; Maher N. Alandiyjany
paper_title: Post‐COVID-19 syndrome: assessment of short- and long-term post-recovery symptoms in recovered cases in Saudi Arabia

summary: Cross-sectional pilot study (n=67) measuring respiratory muscle function in long COVID patients ~5 months post-infection, comparing hospitalized vs non-hospitalized groups. Found respiratory muscle dysfunction in 88% of symptomatic patients, with pathological P0.1/PImax ratio associated with exercise intolerance and reduced functional status.
paper_authors: Jan K. Hennigs; Marie Huwe; Annette Hennigs; Tim Oqueka; Marcel Simon; Lars Harbaum; Jakob Körbelin; Stefan Schmiedel; Julian Schulze zur Wiesch; Marylyn M. Addo; Stefan Kluge; Hans Klose
paper_title: Respiratory muscle dysfunction in long-COVID patients

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 909 post-COVID patients in Jena, Germany using cluster analysis of quality-of-life measures to identify post-COVID subgroups. Study found two distinct clusters: 29.4% with markedly diminished QoL (post-COVID disease) and 70.6% with near-normal QoL (post-COVID condition), suggesting heterogeneous disease impact.
paper_authors: Benjamin Giszas; Sabine Trommer; Nane Schüßler; Andrea Rodewald; Bianca Besteher; Jutta Bleidorn; Petra Dickmann; Kathrin Finke; Katrin Katzer; Katja Lehmann-Pohl; Christina Lemhöfer; Mathias W. Pletz; Christian Puta; Stefanie Quickert; Martin Walter; Andreas Stallmach; Philipp Alexander Reuken
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 condition is not only a question of persistent symptoms: structured screening including health-related quality of life reveals two separate clusters of post-COVID

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of 2023 National Health Interview Survey data examining the association between asthma and long COVID prevalence in U.S. adults. Found that adults with asthma had significantly higher odds of long COVID (OR 1.58) and poor asthma control was associated with increased long COVID risk, but this is an observational study with no intervention or treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Chun-Tse Hung; Yu-Chien Hung; Chi-Won Suk; Chung-Hsuen Wu
paper_title: Evaluating the associations among asthma, asthma control and long COVID in U.S. adults

summary: This cross-sectional study from the German Ageing Survey examines associations between physician-diagnosed long COVID and psychosocial outcomes (depression, loneliness, social isolation, life satisfaction) in 4,017 middle-aged and older adults. While long COVID was associated with perceived social isolation (particularly in women), the study is observational without any treatment intervention and does not evaluate treatment outcomes.
paper_authors: André Hajek; Christine Blome; Dong Keon Yon; Pinar Soysal; Razak M. Gyasi; Karl Peltzer; Supa Pengpid; Hans-Helmut König
paper_title: Long COVID and psychosocial factors among middle-aged and older adults. Results of the nationally representative German Ageing Survey

summary: Community-based cross-sectional survey of 562 adults in a Tribal community examining associations between nicotine use and COVID-19 health outcomes, including recovery time and disease severity. The study is excluded because it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention—it observationally examines nicotine exposure as a risk factor, not a therapeutic intervention.
paper_authors: Anna Tillery; Rae O’Leary; Angela Aherrera; Jaylynn Farlee; Brittany Youpee; Erena S. Hovhannisyan Romero; Miranda Cajero; Jacob Duran; Esther Erdei; Ana M. Rule
paper_title: COVID-19 Disease and Chronic Health Outcomes Associated with Nicotine Use in a Great Plains Tribal Community: A Community-Based Study
paper_journal: Journal of Racial and Ethnic Health Disparities

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed health-related quality of life in 200 Indonesian individuals with long COVID at four recovery timepoints (< 6 months to > 24 months) using the SF-36 survey. The study found that mental health challenges were prevalent (56.1%) and persisted even after 24+ months of recovery, with fatigue, concentration difficulties, sleep disorders, and anxiety being common symptoms.
paper_authors: Irma Hidayana; Zahira Rahvenia; Dicky C. Pelupessy; Milya Urfa Ahmad
paper_title: Quality of life among individuals with long COVID symptoms in Indonesia at four points of recovery

summary: A mixed-methods cross-sectional survey examining long COVID symptoms and health outcomes in Black Americans, comparing qualitative and quantitative descriptions. The study found that Black adults with long COVID reported significantly worse mental health outcomes including anxiety, depression, and suicidal ideation, despite similar qualitative reporting of physical symptoms.
paper_authors: Janelle R. Goodwill; Tiwaloluwa A. Ajibewa
paper_title: A Mixed Methods Analysis of Long COVID Symptoms in Black Americans: Examining Physical and Mental Health Outcomes
paper_journal: Journal of Racial and Ethnic Health Disparities

summary: This case-control study compared cognitive function, sleep quality, depression, and fatigue between 45 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients and 60 healthy controls from April-December 2021. The PCS group showed significantly higher rates of cognitive impairment (13.3% vs 1.6%), depression (53.9% vs 25.9%), and sleep disturbances (53.9% vs 18.6%), though working memory performance did not differ between groups.
paper_authors: Armin Adibi; Ali Motahharynia; Iman Adibi; Mehdi Sanayei
paper_title: Long-term consequences of COVID-19 on sleep, mental health, fatigue, and cognition: a preliminary study

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 843 members from three American Indian Reservation communities exploring attitudes and experiences of long COVID. The study found that 40% of COVID-19 survivors reported ongoing symptoms, with distinct symptom clusters associated with different sociodemographic factors, highlighting health and workforce sequelae in these communities.
paper_authors: Tobey M.; Purvis SJ; Daubman BR; Isaacson MJ; Duran T.; Johnson G.; LaPlante JR; Armstrong K.
paper_title: The Experience of Long COVID Among American Indian Individuals in Three Great Plains Communities
paper_journal: Journal of Racial and Ethnic Health Disparities

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence of post-COVID-19 fatigue and depression among 361 confirmed COVID-19 cases in Saudi Arabia. Found 22.7% reported fatigue and identified COVID-19 severity and depression as significant predictors of post-COVID fatigue.
paper_authors: Abdulrahman Alharbi; Faisal Almogbel; Unaib Rabbani; Ziad A. Memish
paper_title: Long COVID-19 and Coexistence of Fatigue and Depression: A Cross-sectional Study from Saudi Arabia
paper_journal: Journal of Epidemiology and Global Health

summary: This cross-sectional study analyzes 2022-2023 BRFSS data to examine racial/ethnic, metropolitan, and healthcare access disparities in long COVID prevalence among U.S. adults. The study finds higher odds of long COVID among American Indian/Alaskan Native and Other/Multiracial respondents, and among non-metropolitan and uninsured populations, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Camilo Vargas; Rebeka Moges; Grace Caltabellotta; Lulu David; Nicola Manalili; Marilyn Tseng; Emily C. Marlow; Adrienne B. Lent
paper_title: Exploring the Role of Race/Ethnicity, Metropolitan Status, and Health Insurance in Long COVID Among U.S. Adults
paper_journal: Journal of Racial and Ethnic Health Disparities

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 369 vaccinated individuals in Saudi Arabia examining the persistence of post-COVID-19 symptoms. Found that 54.8% experienced persistent symptoms 3-6 months after recovery and 29.1% reported symptoms lasting >6 months, with symptom duration varying by age group and vaccination timing.
paper_authors: Heba M. Adly; Saleh A. K. Saleh; Mohammed A. Garout; Altaf A. Abdulkhaliq; Abdullah A. Khafagy; Abdullah A. Saati; Imad A. AlJahdali; Maher N. Alandiyjany; Jaffar A. Al-Tawfiq
paper_title: Post COVID-19 Symptoms Among Infected Vaccinated Individuals: A Cross-Sectional Study in Saudi Arabia
paper_journal: Journal of Epidemiology and Global Health

summary: Cross-sectional study of 105 long COVID patients examining how self-compassion and psychological flexibility moderate the relationship between physical symptoms and psychosocial impact. Found that both constructs significantly buffer the effect of symptom burden on daily life, suggesting they are important therapeutic targets for multidisciplinary rehabilitation.
paper_authors: Lewis Tudor; Sari Harenwall; Rebecca Henderson; Amy R. Bland
paper_title: Post-covid-19 syndrome: Self-compassion and psychological flexibility moderate the relationship between physical symptom load and psychosocial impact

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in 143 patients after mild COVID-19 infection using standardized instruments (SF-36, FSS, HADS, MMSE-2, SDMT). The study found that fatigue, depression, anxiety, and cognitive complaints were negatively correlated with all HRQoL domains, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

paper_title: Assessment of health-related quality of life after mild COVID-19 infection

summary: Cross-sectional study describing chronic pain characteristics in 143 COVID-19 ICU survivors nine months post-discharge, finding that 54% developed new-onset chronic pain predominantly from secondary causes (musculoskeletal, post-traumatic, neuropathic). The study characterizes pain patterns and their associations with psychological symptoms but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Valéria Martinez; Mikhail Dziadzko; Juan Tamayo; Sébastien Schitter; Leah Guichard; Florine Richeux; Stephanie Roggerone; Patricia Branche; Leo Schlaefflin; Youri Nacto; Tiago Antunes; Isabelle Negre; Djillali Annane; Frederic Aubrun
paper_title: Chronic pain characteristics in COVID-19 survivors after an ICU stay. A cross-sectional study

summary: This cross-sectional study develops a machine learning model to identify post-COVID condition cases from administrative health data in Alberta, Canada, achieving 96% accuracy in detecting PCC from healthcare utilization patterns. The study estimates PCC period prevalence at 9.3% in the general population but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Tkt Lo; Gary F. Teare; Jeffrey A. Bakal; Gavin Y. Oudit; Kyle A. Kemp; Hussain Usman; Khokan C. Sikdar
paper_title: Identification of post-COVID condition in a large population: a machine learning approach

summary: This paper analyzes data from the 2022 National Health Interview Survey to quantify the relationship between COVID-19 (including symptoms lasting 3+ months) and health care-related financial toxicity in the US adult population. It finds that individuals with severe or prolonged COVID-19 symptoms are significantly more likely to experience financial hardship, delayed/forgone care, and medication nonadherence, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Biplab Kumar Datta; Steven S. Coughlin; Ishtiaque Fazlul; Ajay Pandey
paper_title: COVID-19 and health care–related financial toxicity in the United States: Evidence from the 2022 National Health Interview Survey

summary: Cross-sectional study of 254 healthcare workers at a Tunisian university hospital investigating the persistence of COVID-19 symptoms at 1-6 months post-infection. Found that >70% retained symptoms (dyspnea, fatigue, anosmia, headache, memory problems), with persistence significantly associated with female gender, older age, non-smoking status, and asymptomatic initial presentation.
paper_authors: Asma Chouchane; Maher Maoua; Imène Kacem; Manel Makhloufi; Marwa Bouhoula; Asma Aloui; Aicha Brahem; Houda Kalboussi; Olfa El Maalel; Souheil Chatti; Nejib Mrizak
paper_title: Le syndrome post-COVID chez le personnel de santé dans un centre hospitalo-universitaire dans la région du centre tunisien
paper_journal: Archives des Maladies Professionnelles et de l'Environnement

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of 27,651 survey respondents comparing symptom profiles between long COVID, ME/CFS, and combined presentations. Found subjects with both conditions report higher rates of memory issues, anxiety, depression, fatigue, and reduced physical activity, suggesting potential overlap in pathophysiological mechanisms.
paper_authors: Nikitha Garapaty; Kristina M. Reyes; Lily Tehrani; Maximiliano Barbosa Mendoza; Patrick Hardigan
paper_title: Assessing the Relationship in Symptomology of Myalgic Encephalitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome and Long COVID

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 253 long COVID patients in Scotland examining symptom prevalence, frequency, and severity. Found post-exertional malaise (95%), fatigue (85%), and cognitive impairment (68%) as most prevalent, with no treatment intervention evaluated.
paper_authors: Marie Mclaughlin; Luke Cerexhe; Eilidh Macdonald; Joanne Ingram; Nilihan E.M. Sanal-Hayes; Rachel Meach; David Carless; Nicholas Sculthorpe
paper_title: A Cross-Sectional Study of Symptom Prevalence, Frequency, Severity, and Impact of Long COVID in Scotland: Part I

summary: A nationwide cross-sectional survey of 19,784 Japanese respondents assessing prolonged symptoms after COVID-19 and their impact on quality of life. The study identifies headache, chest discomfort, dysgeusia, and dysosmia as independently associated with long COVID and documents reduced health-related QOL, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Hitoshi Honda; Akane Takamatsu; Toshiki Miwa; Takahiro Tabuchi; Kiyosu Taniguchi; Kenji Shibuya; Yasuharu Tokuda
paper_title: Prolonged Symptoms after COVID-19 in Japan: A Nationwide Survey of the Symptoms and Their Impact on Patients’ Quality of Life

summary: Cross-sectional observational study characterizing fatigue severity and laboratory markers (cortisol, cytokines) in 100 long COVID patients with fatigue-dominant symptoms. Findings show severe fatigue correlated with lower plasma cortisol levels, particularly for mental fatigue components, providing reference data for understanding postviral fatigue.
paper_authors: Jin-Seok Lee; Yujin Choi; Jin-Yong Joung; Chang-Gue Son
paper_title: Clinical and Laboratory Characteristics of Fatigue-Dominant Long-COVID Subjects: A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 2022 examining symptom prevalence, frequency, severity, and functional impact of long COVID in Scottish patients (n unclear from abstract). Study documents significant work disability, study impairment, and caregiving burden associated with fatigue, pain, and cognitive impairment, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Marie Mclaughlin; Luke Cerexhe; Eilidh Macdonald; Joanne Ingram; Nilihan E.M. Sanal-Hayes; Lawrence D. Hayes; Rachel Meach; David Carless; Nicholas Sculthorpe
paper_title: A Cross-Sectional Study of Symptom Prevalence, Frequency, Severity, and Impact of Long COVID in Scotland: Part II

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of 2022 BRFSS data examining prevalence and determinants of long-term post-COVID conditions in US COVID survivors. Found 21.7% prevalence with associations to female sex, BMI, comorbidities, and lifestyle factors, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Seyyed Sina Hejazian; Alireza Vafaei Sadr; Shima Shahjouei; Ajith Vemuri; Vida Abedi; Ramin Zand
paper_title: Prevalence and Determinants of Long-Term Post-COVID Conditions in the United States: 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 24,803 US adults examining the association between obstructive sleep apnea and post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC). The study found obstructive sleep apnea was associated with increased odds of PASC-related symptoms, with this risk mitigated in patients receiving sleep apnea treatment.
paper_authors: Stuart F. Quan; Matthew D. Weaver; Mark É. Czeisler; Laura K. Barger; Lauren A. Booker; Mark E. Howard; Melinda L. Jackson; Rashon I. Lane; Christine F. McDonald; Anna Ridgers; Rebecca Robbins; Prerna Varma; Joshua F. Wiley; Shantha M.W. Rajaratnam; Charles A. Czeisler
paper_title: Association of Obstructive Sleep Apnea with Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: This cross-sectional study analyzes health insurance coverage and healthcare access among U.S. working-age adults with long COVID using 2022 National Health Interview Survey data (n=18,117). While it documents that long COVID patients use healthcare services more frequently but face greater cost-related barriers to care, it does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Nicole D. Ford; Douglas Slaughter; Alexandra F. Dalton; Deja Edwards; Kevin Ma; Hope King; Sharon Saydah
paper_title: Health Insurance and Access to Care in U.S. Working-Age Adults Experiencing Long COVID

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of two nationwide surveys (BRFSS and NHIS) identifying demographic and clinical factors associated with long COVID prevalence. Finds that middle age, female sex, lack of college degree, and severe acute COVID-19 infection are associated with increased long COVID risk.
paper_authors: Yixuan Wu; Mitsuaki Sawano; Yilun Wu; Rishi M. Shah; Pamela Bishop; Akiko Iwasaki; Harlan M. Krumholz
paper_title: Factors Associated With Long COVID: Insights From Two Nationwide Surveys

summary: Cross-sectional survey study of 423 long COVID patients examining internal tremors and vibrations as a symptom phenotype. Participants with internal tremors/vibrations had worse quality of life and higher rates of new-onset mast cell and neurologic conditions compared to those without these symptoms.

paper_title: Internal Tremors and Vibrations in Long COVID: A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: Descriptive study of 441 long COVID patients from the Yale LISTEN cohort characterizing symptoms, treatments tried, and psychological/social/financial impacts. Does not evaluate efficacy of any specific treatment—participants self-reported prior treatment attempts without outcome assessment.
paper_authors: Mitsuaki Sawano; Yilun Wu; Rishi M. Shah; Tianna Zhou; Adith S. paper_title: Long COVID Characteristics and Experience: A Descriptive Study From the Yale LISTEN Research Cohort

summary: This study uses 2022 National Health Interview Survey data to identify factors associated with recovery from long COVID in US adults. It finds that 48.5% of those with long COVID reported recovery, with significant variations by age, sex, race/ethnicity, education, and initial COVID-19 severity, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Kavya M. Shah; Rishi M. Shah; Mitsuaki Sawano; Yixuan Wu; Pamela Bishop; Akiko Iwasaki; Harlan M. Krumholz
paper_title: Factors Associated with Long COVID Recovery among US Adults

summary: Cross-sectional study of 1,135 working-age COVID-19 survivors in British Columbia assessing health-related quality of life >2 years post-infection using the EQ-5D-5L instrument. Found that 19.2% with current post-COVID condition had significantly lower health utility and functional deficits compared to those without symptoms or who had recovered.
paper_authors: Hiten Naik; James Wilton; Karen C. Tran; Naveed Zafar Janjua; Adeera Levin; Wei Zhang
paper_title: Long-Term Health-Related Quality of Life in Working-Age COVID-19 Survivors: A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 253 long COVID patients in Scotland documenting symptom prevalence, frequency, severity, and duration. The study found post-exertional malaise (95%), fatigue (85%), and cognitive impairment (68%) as the most prevalent symptoms, with socioeconomic deprivation associated with symptom burden.

paper_title: Erratum to A Cross-Sectional Study of Symptom Prevalence, Frequency, Severity, and Impact of Long-COVID in Scotland: Part I

summary: Secondary analysis of the 2022 National Health Interview Survey examining prevalence and types of complementary medicine use among US adults with post-COVID-19 symptoms. Finds 46.2% of post-COVID respondents used complementary medicine in the past 12 months, with higher use of mind-body medicine and massage.

paper_title: Use of Complementary Medicine Among US Adults with Post-COVID-19: Results from the 2022 National Health Interview Survey

summary: Prospective survey of 437 COVID-19 patients assessing prevalence and predictors of post-acute sequelae (PASC). Found 34.9% had persistent symptoms, with fatigue, sleep issues, and anosmia most common; female sex and psychological impact were key predictive factors.
paper_authors: Dacre R.T. Knight; Bala Munipalli; Ilana I. Logvinov; Meghana G. Halkar; Ghada Mitri; Abd Moain Abu Dabrh; Stephanie L. Hines
paper_title: Perception, Prevalence, and Prediction of Severe Infection and Post-acute Sequelae of COVID-19
paper_journal: The American Journal of the Medical Sciences

summary: Cross-sectional study examining echocardiographic changes in 100 COVID-19 patients within 3 months of infection, stratified by disease severity and symptom persistence. Found high prevalence of right and left ventricular dysfunction, with worse cardiac function associated with moderate-to-severe disease and persistent symptoms.

paper_title: Echocardiographic manifestations during the first 3 months after an episode of COVID-19 and their relationship with disease severity and persistence of symptoms
paper_journal: The American Journal of the Medical Sciences

summary: This cross-sectional study examined peripheral microvascular endothelial dysfunction in 92 symptomatic long COVID patients using peripheral arterial tonometry and measured NT-proBNP levels over time. While 41% of patients showed microvascular endothelial dysfunction with associations to NT-proBNP increases, this is an observational study without treatment intervention—it only characterizes disease pathophysiology without testing any therapeutic intervention.

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 30,130 Japanese individuals assessing health-related quality of life and somatic symptoms in post-COVID patients versus controls using EQ-5D-5L and SSS-8 scales. Found that COVID-19 survivors, especially those with severe disease, had significantly lower quality of life and higher somatic symptom burden, with vaccination associated with better outcomes.

paper_title: Post-COVID health-related quality of life and somatic symptoms: A national survey in Japan
paper_journal: The American Journal of the Medical Sciences

summary: This cross-sectional study examined metabolic profiles in 39 diabetic patients post-COVID-19 at a Tunisian nutrition institute. The study found that COVID-19 infection disrupted metabolic control in diabetic patients, including worsening glycemic control, lipid abnormalities, and increased cardiovascular risk, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

paper_title: Le profil métabolique des patients diabétiques en post-COVID-19

The study found that 92.3% of diabetic patients experienced post-COVID symptoms, predominantly fatigue and psychomotor slowing (79.5%), with dyspnea, dry cough, anosmia, chronic headaches, and memory disorders also commonly reported.
paper_authors: I. Bani; Z. Hadjali; A. Bouzid; Y. Htira; C. Jemai; I. Hedfi; F. Ben Mami
paper_title: Les patients diabétiques en post-COVID-19

summary: A prospective cross-sectional study comparing smell and taste function in 35 COVID-19 recovered patients versus 35 COVID-naïve controls using standardized testing (UPSIT and Burghart tests). Results showed no significant difference in chemosensory recovery between groups, suggesting patients who experience COVID-related smell/taste disturbance regain sensory ability similar to pre-COVID baseline.

paper_title: Chemosensory function recovery in COVID-19 patients: A cross-sectional study

The study found high prevalence of long COVID symptoms (33.2% with >1 month, 20.3% with >3 months) but limited awareness and understanding, particularly among African American and Latino/a patients, with significant gaps in care access.

summary: Cross-sectional study of 264 long COVID patients examining associations between physical activity levels and cardiorespiratory fitness, sleep quality, and quality of life. paper_title: Association Between Physical Activity Amount and Cardiorespiratory Fitness, Sleep Quality, and Health-Related Quality of Life in Patients With Long COVID: A Cross-sectional Study

summary: Cross-sectional study measuring prevalence of depression (27.9%) and anxiety (43.6%) among COVID-19 survivors in Malaysia using DASS-21 and Brief-COPE scales. paper_authors: Thinesh Kumar Karadapanddy; Anne Yee; Thian Chee Loh; Ong Hui Koh; Nur 'Aqilah Mohd Hodori
paper_title: Prevalence of depression, anxiety and the coping strategies of patients recovered from COVID-19 infection in a Malaysian tertiary hospital

summary: Population-based telephone survey of 121 adults hospitalized for COVID-19 in Quebec assessing long-term functional deficits at ≥2 months post-infection using the COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Screen. Found 94% reported increased fatigue, 90% deteriorated global health, with significant reductions in mobility, employment, and daily activities; time since diagnosis was associated with functional outcomes.
paper_authors: Barbara Mazer; Debbie Ehrmann Feldman
paper_title: Functional Limitations in Individuals With Long COVID
paper_journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 491 long COVID patients examining symptom profiles and their association with self-efficacy for symptom management using latent profile analysis. The study identified four distinct symptom burden profiles and found that higher self-efficacy was associated with lower symptom burden, but does not test an intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Weijiao Zhou; Janet L. Larson; Philip T. Veliz; Kanchani Kitto; Sheree Smith

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the association between PTSD symptoms and health-related quality of life in 636 post-COVID-19 patients in primary care settings. Found that 21.4% had PTSD symptoms and over half had affected quality of life, with PTSD significantly associated with worse HRQoL outcomes.

paper_title: Trastorno de estrés postraumático y calidad de vida del paciente post-COVID-19 en Atención Primaria

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of 1,913 European adults ≥50 years examining the association between COVID-19 vaccination status and long COVID prevalence, stratified by chronic multimorbidity. Finds that vaccination is associated with lower long COVID rates only among those with chronic multimorbidity, not in those without.

paper_title: COVID-19 vaccination and long COVID among 50 years older and above European: The role of chronic multimorbidity

Found significantly elevated autoantibody levels in long-COVID patients that correlate with neurological symptom severity including fatigue and cognitive impairment.

paper_title: Severity of neurological Long-COVID symptoms correlates with increased level of autoantibodies targeting vasoregulatory and autonomic nervous system receptors

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 96 convalescent COVID-19 patients examining correlation between immune markers and self-reported depression during early recovery phase. paper_title: Characterisation of Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS): Findings from a physician chart-audit pre- and post-COVID-19

summary: This cross-sectional MRI study examines blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability in 97 long COVID patients with neuropsychiatric symptoms compared to 31 recovered controls. paper_title: Blood-Brain barrier disruption in long COVID and cognitive correlates: A cross-sectional MRI study
