paper_title: Executive deficits after SARS-CoV-2 infection: A cross-sectional population study

summary: A cross-sectional study investigating whether fatigue and depressive symptoms are associated with altered reward and effort processing in decision-making at different timepoints after COVID-19 infection. The study found that greater fatigue in the long-term phase (beyond 12 weeks) is more strongly associated with reduced reward sensitivity compared to the early phase, suggesting potential neural dysregulation in post-COVID-19 fatigue.
paper_authors: Judith M. Scholing; Britt I.H.M. Lambregts; Ruben van den Bosch; Esther Aarts; Marieke E. van der Schaaf
paper_title: Greater fatigue is more strongly associated with reduced reward sensitivity in the long-term phase of coronavirus disease (COVID-19) than in the early phase

summary: Cross-sectional study of 500 participants in Jordan assessing prevalence of post-COVID-19 syndrome symptoms and treatment approaches. Found high burden of sensory, psychiatric, and other complications, with distinct symptom patterns associated with different vaccine types; primarily a descriptive epidemiological survey rather than a treatment intervention study.
paper_authors: Deema Jaber; Alaa Alhusban
paper_title: Long-term complications of COVID-19 in Jordan: A study on persisting symptoms and management

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the Glittre-ADL test as a functional assessment tool in 37 post-COVID-19 patients, correlating performance with pulmonary function and muscle strength measures. The study finds that lung function and quadriceps strength are strong predictors of functional performance but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Tatiana Conceição Pereira de Oliveira; Damara Guedes Gardel; Angelo Thomaz Abalada Ghetti; Agnaldo José Lopes
paper_title: The Glittre-ADL test in non-hospitalized patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome and its relationship with muscle strength and lung function

summary: This cross-sectional study examines the association between childhood trauma and mental health outcomes in 641 participants (487 with post-COVID syndrome, 154 controls) recruited through the DEFEAT platform. The study finds that childhood trauma, particularly emotional abuse, is significantly associated with higher rates of depression and anxiety in PCS patients, with lower health-related quality of life, suggesting the need for trauma-informed care approaches.
paper_authors: Andrea Stölting; Dominik Schröder; Tim Schmachtenberg; Inga Schimansky; Massa Yaqubi-Naqizadah; Christian Klemann; Franziska Rebmann; Marie Mikuteit; Sandra Steffens; Georg M.N. Behrens; Frank Klawonn; Alexandra Dopfer-Jablonka; Frank Müller; Christine Happle
paper_title: Childhood trauma and mental health outcomes in Post-COVID Syndrome: Results from a cross-sectional study in Germany

summary: Population-based cross-sectional survey comparing prevalence of disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBI) before and after the COVID-19 pandemic across UK and US populations. Study found increased DGBI prevalence post-pandemic and identified long COVID as a significant associated factor, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Olafur Palsson; Magnus Simren; Ami D. Sperber; Shrikant Bangdiwala; Jóhann P. Hreinsson; Imran Aziz
paper_title: The Prevalence and Burden of Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction (DGBI) Before vs After the COVID-19 Pandemic

summary: Cross-sectional observational study examining chronic pain prevalence in 242 patients at least 3 months after hospitalization for COVID-19. Found 31.8% reported chronic pain, with female sex and obesity identified as risk factors, but this is a prevalence survey with no intervention or treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Guilherme Antonio Moreira de Barros; Douglas Inomata Cardoso da Silva; Mariana Lopes Amaral Barbosa; Rafael Abbud Soares; Rodrigo Leal Alves; Claudio Lucas Miranda; Paula Danieli Lopes da Costa; Paulo do Nascimento Júnior; Norma Sueli Pinheiro Módolo
paper_title: Chronic pain after hospital discharge on patients hospitalized for COVID-19: an observational study

summary: This cross-sectional study examined associations between fatigue, dysautonomia, depression, and cognitive impairment in 141 long-COVID patients referred to a neuro-long-COVID service. The study used self-reporting questionnaires to compare fatigued and non-fatigued patients and identified significant associations between fatigue and autonomic dysfunction, cognitive impairment, and depression.
paper_authors: Giovanni Furlanis; Alex Buoite Stella; Giovanna Torresin; Marco Michelutti; Miloš Ajčević; Paolo Manganotti
paper_title: Neurological long-COVID: Associations among fatigue, dysautonomia, depression, and subjective memory complaints

summary: Retrospective cross-sectional study evaluating the clinical significance of low-field MRI lung opacity in 62 post-acute COVID-19 patients. Found that lung opacity severity correlated with decreased DLCO on pulmonary function tests but was not associated with patient-reported outcomes.
paper_authors: Lea Azour; Leopoldo N. Segal; Rany Condos; William H. Moore; Nicholas Landini; Destiny Collazo; Daniel H. Sterman; Isabel Young; Jane Ko; Shari Brosnahan; James Babb; Hersh Chandarana
paper_title: Low-field MRI lung opacity severity associated with decreased DLCO in post-acute Covid-19 patients

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing skeletal muscle energy metabolism and oxidative capacity during exercise in 71 long COVID patients versus 63 healthy controls. Found reduced peak fat oxidation and impaired mitochondrial bioenergetics in long COVID patients, with muscle power output mediating this relationship.
paper_authors: Robinson Ramírez-Vélez; Sergio Oscoz-Ochandorena; Yesenia García-Alonso; Nora García-Alonso; Gaizka Legarra-Gorgoñon; Julio Oteiza; Ander Ernaga Lorea; Mikel Izquierdo; María Correa-Rodríguez
paper_title: Maximal oxidative capacity during exercise is associated with muscle power output in patients with long coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) syndrome. A moderation analysis

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of 2023 BRFSS survey data examining prevalence and sociodemographic/health factors associated with long COVID among cancer survivors. Found 15.2% of COVID-positive cancer survivors reported long COVID, with associations to age, sex, vaccination status, and comorbid conditions.
paper_authors: Stuart J. Case; Lindsay Sabik; Haley Grant
paper_title: Factors associated with long COVID among cancer survivors: A population-based analysis

summary: A nationwide random sampling cross-sectional survey in France (August-November 2022) estimated long COVID prevalence in the adult population using multiple definitions, finding 4.0% prevalence using WHO-PCC criteria. The study examined variations by sociodemographic and infection characteristics but did not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Joël Coste; Cyrille Delpierre; Jean-Baptiste Richard; Caroline Alleaume; Anne Gallay; Sarah Tebeka; Cédric Lemogne; Olivier Robineau; Olivier Steichen; Tatjana T. Makovski
paper_title: Prevalence of long COVID in the general adult population according to different definitions and sociodemographic and infection characteristics. A nationwide random sampling survey in France in autumn 2022

summary: A cross-sectional pilot study examining vagus and phrenic nerve dysfunction in 30 post-COVID-19 patients compared to 14 COVID-recovered and 16 uninfected controls using ultrasound and respiratory testing. The study found structural and functional nerve abnormalities in PCC patients but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Gemma Lladós; Marta Massanella; Roser Coll-Fernández; Raúl Rodríguez; Electra Hernández; Giuseppe Lucente; Cristina López; Cora Loste; José Ramón Santos; Sergio España-Cueto; Maria Nevot; Francisco Muñoz-López; Sandra Silva-Arrieta; Christian Brander; Maria José Durà; Patricia Cuadras; Jordi Bechini; Montserrat Tenesa; Alicia Martinez-Piñeiro; Cristina Herrero; Anna Chamorro; Anna Garcia; Eulalia Grau; Bonaventura Clotet; Roger Paredes; Lourdes Mateu; Muñoz-Moreno José; Rodríguez-Fumaz Carmina; Prats Anna; Estany Carla; Vallejo Nuria; Villuendas Roger; Aranyó Julia; Marín Toni; Mitjans Julia; Casafont Ivette
paper_title: Vagus nerve dysfunction in the post–COVID-19 condition: a pilot cross-sectional study

summary: This cross-sectional study compared cognitive performance between college students who had COVID-19 and uninfected controls using data from 24 cognitive psychology experiments. The findings indicate that COVID-19 infection has minimal impact on cognition in university students, contradicting concerns about long-term cognitive impairment from long COVID.
paper_authors: Gregory Francis; Evelina Thunell
paper_title: COVID-19 infection does not seem to affect cognition in college students

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 3,251 U.S. adults examining the frequency and duration of long-term symptoms (>4 weeks) and healthcare utilization among adults with and without disabilities following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Found that those who tested positive had significantly higher odds of reporting long-term symptoms, with healthcare utilization approximately twofold higher among adults with disabilities.
paper_authors: Maureen J. Miller; Leora R. Feldstein; Joseph Holbrook; Ian D. Plumb; Emma K. Accorsi; Qing C. Zhang; Qi Cheng; Jean Y. Ko; Valentine Wanga; Stacey Konkle; Lina V. Dimitrov; Jeanne Bertolli; Sharon Saydah
paper_title: Post-COVID conditions and healthcare utilization among adults with and without disabilities—2021 Porter Novelli FallStyles survey

summary: Cross-sectional study examining associations between Long COVID and housing stability/accessibility among 1533 people with disabilities (514 with Long COVID, 1019 without). Finds Long COVID associated with higher rates of housing instability, financial concerns, and home maintenance issues, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Kelsey Goddard; Andrew Myers; Catherine Ipsen
paper_title: The hidden crisis: Long COVID's association with housing stability and home accessibility among people with disabilities

summary: This cross-sectional study analyzed how vaccination status and SARS-CoV-2 re-infections influenced changes in sports-related physical activity one month after infection in 5,829 adults. The study documents a decline in physical activity post-infection but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Dimitrios I. Bourdas; Panteleimon Bakirtzoglou; Antonios K. Travlos; Vasileios Andrianopoulos; Emmanouil Zacharakis
paper_title: Analysis of a comprehensive dataset: Influence of vaccination profile, types, and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 re-infections on changes in sports-related physical activity one month after infection

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing cognitive performance in 81,337 participants using the Great British Intelligence Test, examining associations between COVID-19 infection history and cognitive deficits. Found significant cognitive deficits in COVID-19 survivors including non-hospitalized cases, suggesting multi-domain cognitive impact from SARS-CoV-2 infection.
paper_authors: Adam Hampshire; William Trender; Samuel R. Chamberlain; Amy E. Jolly; Jon E. Grant; Fiona Patrick; Ndaba Mazibuko; Steve CR Williams; Joseph M. Barnby; Peter Hellyer; Mitul A. Mehta
paper_title: Cognitive deficits in people who have recovered from COVID-19

summary: Cross-sectional survey study (N=212) investigating life satisfaction among long COVID patients and predictors using mixture model analysis. Found heterogeneous patterns: social support significantly predicted life satisfaction in one cluster but not the other, suggesting tailored psychosocial interventions may improve quality of life.
paper_authors: Jina Chun; Joonbum Lee; Katelyn Matkin; Constance Richard; Uzma Khan; Susan Smedema
paper_title: Bimodality in life satisfaction: The role of social support in individuals with long COVID

summary: A multicenter cross-sectional study assessing long-term quality of life, sleep patterns, psychological health, and work ability in 491 severe COVID-19 survivors 18+ months post-discharge. The study found persistent psychological disorders, sleep disturbances, and poor work ability despite overall physiological improvement.
paper_authors: Anshul Jain; Prashant Gupta; Apurva Abhinandan Mittal; Narendra Singh Sengar; Rachna Chaurasia; Neeraj Banoria; Arvind Kankane; Arpita Saxena; Brijendra; Mrinal Sharma
paper_title: Long-term quality of life and work ability among severe COVID-19 survivors: A multicenter study

summary: This cross-sectional pilot study assessed long COVID prevalence and characteristics 7-12 months post-hospitalization among 145 patients from a safety-net hospital serving predominantly Black and Hispanic populations in Chicago. The study found 34% reported persistent symptoms, with acute COVID-19 severity being a significant risk factor for long COVID.
paper_authors: Miao Jenny Hua; Sriram Gonakoti; Ruhi Shariff; Carlos Corpuz; Hernandez Acosta RA; Hillary Chang; Iriagbonse Asemota; Elizabeth Gobbi; Katayoun Rezai
paper_title: Prevalence and Characteristics of Long COVID 7–12 Months After Hospitalization Among Patients From an Urban Safety-Net Hospital: A Pilot Study

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing neurocognitive function and brain structure in 75 participants: healthy controls, COVID-19 survivors without brain fog, and COVID-19 survivors with brain fog. Found persistent cognitive deficits and structural brain alterations (reduced gray matter, altered network connectivity) even after mild infection, particularly in those with brain fog.
paper_authors: Bedia Samanci; Ulaş Ay; Haşim Gezegen; Sanem Sultan Yörük; Alpay Medetalibeyoğlu; Elif Kurt; Erdi Şahin; Faruk Uğur Doğan; Mehmet Barbüroğlu; Başar Bilgiç; Haşmet Hanağası; Hakan Gürvit
paper_title: Persistent neurocognitive deficits in long COVID: Evidence of structural changes and network abnormalities following mild infection

summary: Cross-sectional descriptive study of 1,047 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients in Colombia documenting symptom prevalence and demographics. Reports high rates of fatigue (53.3%), dyspnea (40.3%), arthralgia (43%), and sleep disorders (35.7%), with 72% experiencing four or more symptoms, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Martin Romero; Martha Caicedo; Andrea Díaz; Delia Ortega; Claudia Llanos; Alejandro Concha; Andrés Vallejo; Fernando Valdés; César González
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 syndrome: Descriptive analysis based on a survivors' cohort in Colombia

summary: Cross-sectional study of 288 elderly adults with post-COVID condition in the Brazilian Amazon examining disability and self-care capacity using the WHODAS 2.0 assessment. Found that older age (≥70 years) and shortness of breath are associated with increased disability scores.
paper_authors: Ana Rosa Tavares da Paixão; Amanda Loyse da Costa Miranda; Wenderson Melo Martins; Vanessa Ladyanne da Silva Costa; Maurício das Neves Pereira; Marília de Fátima Vieira de Oliveira; Andressa Tavares Parente; Eliã Pinheiro Botelho; Renata Karina Reis; Glenda Roberta Oliveira Naiff Ferreira; Sandra Helena Isse Polaro
paper_title: Disability and associated factors among elderly people with post-COVID condition, in a metropolitan region in the Brazilian amazon: A cross-sectional using the World Health Organization disability assessment schedule (WHODAS) 2.0

summary: This multicentre cross-sectional study compared cognitive function in 270 long COVID patients versus two control groups using web-based reaction time and vigilance tasks. The study identified pronounced cognitive slowing in long COVID patients that was not explained by comorbidities, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Sijia Zhao; Eva Maria Martin; Philipp A. Reuken; Anna Scholcz; Akke Ganse-Dumrath; Annie Srowig; Isabelle Utech; Valeska Kozik; Monique Radscheidt; Stefan Brodoehl; Andreas Stallmach; Matthias Schwab; Emily Fraser; Kathrin Finke; Masud Husain
paper_title: Long COVID is associated with severe cognitive slowing: a multicentre cross-sectional study

summary: This study assessed the frequency and characteristics of long COVID-19 in 30 heart transplant recipients through telephone surveys and chart reviews. While it confirms long COVID occurs in this population with significant morbidity, it is an observational descriptive study without any intervention or treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Rachel Sigler; B. Chen; Ajay Bharti; Saima Aslam
paper_title: Long COVID-19 in Heart Transplant Recipients
paper_journal: The Journal of Heart and Lung Transplantation

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing prevalence of fibromyalgia syndrome and anxiety in rheumatic disease patients versus controls who recovered from COVID-19. Finds significantly higher rates of fibromyalgia (22.5% vs 12%) and anxiety (27% vs 16%) in RD patients post-COVID, with severity, diabetes, and anxiety as predictors.
paper_authors: Soha Senara; Hisham Salah; Wafaa Abdel Wahed; Ahmed Yehia
paper_title: Frequency of fibromyalgia syndrome and anxiety post-corona virus disease-2019 (COVID-19) in patients attending the rheumatology clinic

summary: This cross-sectional study surveyed 239 Iranian COVID-19 survivors to assess the prevalence of musculoskeletal symptoms in the post-acute phase. The study found that 98.74% of patients experienced persistent musculoskeletal symptoms, with fatigue being the most common (91.2%), but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Mohaddeseh Azadvari; Afarin Haghparast; Amin Nakhostin-Ansari; Seyede Zahra Emami Razavi; Maryam Hosseini
paper_title: Musculoskeletal symptoms in patients with long COVID: A cross-sectional study on Iranian patients

summary: Cross-sectional cohort study comparing COVID-19 and long COVID outcomes in 732 Chinese psoriasis patients treated with IL-23 inhibitor versus other therapies. IL-23 inhibitor treatment was associated with decreased risk of COVID-19 and long COVID, with treated patients more likely to be asymptomatic after recovery.
paper_authors: Yifan Hu; Dawei Huang; Yuxiong Jiang; Qian Yu; Jiajing Lu; Yangfeng Ding; Yuling Shi
paper_title: Decreased risk of COVID-19 and long COVID in patients with psoriasis receiving IL-23 inhibitor: A cross-sectional cohort study from China

summary: Cross-sectional online survey comparing health-related quality of life and social participation across 3,188 German participants with long COVID, recovered from COVID-19, and never infected. Long COVID participants showed significantly lower quality of life and social participation scores compared to both comparison groups.
paper_authors: Dominik Schröder; Stephanie Heinemann; Gloria Heesen; Eva Hummers; Tim Schmachtenberg; Alexandra Dopfer-Jablonka; Kai Vahldiek; Frank Klawonn; Sandra Klawitter; Sandra Steffens; Marie Mikuteit; Jacqueline Niewolik; Frank Müller
paper_title: Association of long COVID with health-related Quality of Life and Social Participation in Germany: Finding from an online-based cross-sectional survey

summary: A cross-sectional study of 100 adults (ages 18-70) examining the effects of long COVID on memory and cognitive function. The study documents memory impairment and cognitive issues as part of the broader long-term health sequelae following COVID-19 infection.
paper_authors: Mario Alberto Garcia-Ramirez; Estela Adriana Castellanos-Alvarado; Wendy Liliana Martinez-Angeles; Claudia Margarita Ascencio-Tene; Orfil Gonzalez-Reynoso; Itzel Alondra Castillo-Garcia
paper_title: STUDY ON LONG COVID—19 EFFECTS ON MEMORY

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing myocardial work and exercise capacity in 52 severe COVID-19 survivors versus 31 controls using echocardiography and cardiopulmonary exercise testing. Findings show significantly reduced aerobic capacity, lower myocardial efficiency, and abnormal heart rate response in COVID-19 survivors, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

paper_title: Evaluation of myocardial work and exercise capacity in patients recovered from the severe form of COVID-19
paper_journal: International Journal of Cardiology Cardiovascular Risk and Prevention

summary: Cross-sectional study evaluating sexual dysfunction prevalence and risk factors among 391 long COVID patients at a multidisciplinary COVID clinic. Sexual dysfunction was reported by 36% of men and 28% of women, significantly associated with age, long COVID symptoms (cough, chest pain, paresthesia), and emotional distress.
paper_authors: Yelin D.; Daitch V.; Kalfon T.; Mor M.; Buchrits S.; Shafir Y.; Awwad M.; Ghantous N.; Shapira-Lichter I.; Leibovici L.; Yahav D.; Margalit I.
paper_title: Long COVID sexual dysfunction among both genders: Evaluation of a cohort of COVID-19 recoverees

summary: Observational cross-sectional study evaluating associations between lung function and endothelial dysfunction in 32 long COVID patients (mean 32 months post-infection). Found impaired endothelial function and significant correlation between KCO (lung diffusion) and vascular response, suggesting persistent cardiovascular complications in long COVID recovery.
paper_authors: Lêda Leonôr Mendonça Carvalho; Cássia da Luz Goulart; Gabriele Da Dalto Pierazzo; Ester Laura Cordeiro-Costa; Audrey Borghi-Silva; Adriana Sanches Garcia-Araújo
paper_title: Associations between lung and endothelial function in long COVID: Two years after acute infection

summary: Cross-sectional study of 439 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors in Brazil assessing long COVID symptoms, risk factors, and quality of life 2-12 months post-infection. Found 84% reported persistent symptoms (fatigue, dyspnea, arthralgia, depression/anxiety), with ICU admission and dysgeusia as independent risk factors.
paper_authors: Jacqueline Ferreira de Oliveira; Renata Eliane de Ávila; Neimy Ramos de Oliveira; Natália da Cunha Severino Sampaio; Maiara Botelho; Fabíola Araújo Gonçalves; Cirilo José Ferreira Neto; Ana Carolina de Almeida Milagres; Tatiane Cristina Caldeira Gomes; Tássia Lopardi Pereira; Renan Pedra de Souza; Israel Molina
paper_title: Persistent symptoms, quality of life, and risk factors in long COVID: a cross-sectional study of hospitalized patients in Brazil

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 460 long COVID patients examining the relationship between social support and psychological resilience, mediated by personal mastery and self-esteem. Study found that instrumental social support protects long haulers by promoting resilience through self-esteem and personal mastery.
paper_authors: Atefeh Aghaei; Shan Qiao; Cheuk Chi Tam; Guangzhe Yuan; Xiaoming Li
paper_title: Role of self-esteem and personal mastery on the association between social support and resilience among COVID-19 long haulers

summary: Cross-sectional study investigating the relationship between TFPI gene polymorphisms, D-dimer levels, and post-COVID-19 condition in 144 patients. Found no significant associations between TFPI polymorphisms and PCC development, though TFPI -33T>C homozygosity may predict lower hospitalization risk during acute COVID-19.
paper_authors: GO Paschoal; Marcílio Figueiredo Lemos; Thalia Medeiros; Natalia Fonseca do Rosário; Catarina Nascimento; Jocemir Ronaldo Lugon; GW Gomes
paper_title: RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN TFPI GENE POLYMORPHISMS, POST-COVID-19 CONDITION AND D-DIMER LEVELS IN PATIENTS WITH HISTORY OF COVID-19

summary: A cross-sectional study examining the relationship between HLA alleles, KIR receptors, and long COVID development in 153 COVID-19 patients from Spain. Findings show HLA-A*03 is less frequent in long COVID patients and is associated with enhanced CD8+ T cell and NK cell responses.
paper_authors: Pons-Fuster E.; Martinez-Rodriguez R.; Gimeno-Arias L.; Alcaraz MJ; Moreno M.; Gómez JM; Pelaez A.; García E.; Tomás C.; Muñoz A.; Martínez-Sánchez MV; Ruiz-Lorente I.; Ceballos D.; Minguela A.; Bernal E.
paper_title: HLA-A*03 may confer protection against long COVID through an enhanced immune response

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 136 long-COVID patients recruited from online support groups to assess prevalence and severity of mast cell activation (MCA) symptoms compared to general population controls and MCAS patients. Found that post-COVID long-COVID subjects had MCA symptom profiles identical to untreated MCAS patients, suggesting mast cell dysfunction may underlie part of long-COVID pathophysiology.
paper_authors: Leonard B. Weinstock; Jill B. Brook; Arthur S. Walters; Ashleigh Goris; Lawrence B. Afrin; Gerhard J. Molderings
paper_title: Mast cell activation symptoms are prevalent in Long-COVID

summary: Cross-sectional study estimating PCC prevalence among 1,546 COVID-19 patients in Alexandria, Egypt (June 2022–February 2023) and investigating associated risk factors. Found 49.2% reported PCC symptoms; primary manifestations were shortness of breath (94.2%), mood changes (13.9%), and fatigue (8.8%), with older age, hospitalization, and comorbidities (asthma, hypertension, diabetes) as significant risk factors.
paper_authors: Rasha Ashmawy; Yousra A. El-Maradny; Amira Tahio; Salma Afifi; Sahar Samy; Hala BahaaEldin; Nahla Gaber; Ibrahim A. Abdelwahab
paper_title: Prevalence, duration, and factors influencing post-COVID conditions among patients at several public hospitals, Alexandria governorate, Egypt 2022–2023

summary: Population-based cross-sectional study of 9,752 German employees assessing work ability 6-12 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Identifies post-COVID symptom clusters (neurocognitive impairment, fatigue, mental disorders) associated with reduced work ability but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Post-COVID syndrome and work ability 9-12 months after a SARS-CoV-2 infection among over 9000 employees from the general population

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence and characteristics of long COVID among 486 COVID-19 survivors in Saudi Arabia, finding that 61% reported persistent symptoms including fatigue, breathlessness, and loss of smell. The study identifies demographic patterns and symptom burden but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Haya M. Almalag; Njoud Altuwaijri; Lamya S. Alnaim; Dareen Alassiri; Ghaida Alsolaimi; Sarah Aldakhil; Noha Al Aloola; Jawza F. Alsabhan; Ghada A. Bawazeer; Lobna Al Juffali; Hadeel Alkofide; Rihaf Alfaraj; Nora Alkhudair; Raniah Aljadeed; Rana Aljadeed
paper_title: Prevalence and characteristics of long COVID among COVID-19 survivors in Saudi Arabia: A cross-sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 164 healthcare workers who recovered from COVID-19, assessing post-COVID-19 syndrome symptoms months after infection. Found 48% of participants reported persistent symptoms, with fatigue being the most common (71%), but no treatment intervention was evaluated.
paper_authors: Nezar Ahmed Salim; Bella Stevanny; Annisya Ayu Putri; M. Khoirudin; Aufa Muhammad Nadhif; Harmiziana Hamzah; Rini Andriani; Maulidya Permata; H. Hudari; Zarak Hussain Ahmad
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 Syndrome in Healthcare Personnel in Dr. Mohammad Hoesin General Hospital Palembang Indonesia

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of menopause symptom prevalence in 122 women attending post-COVID syndrome clinics in England. Study found high prevalence of menopause symptoms in women aged 40-54, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Stuart Stewart; Adrian Heald; Yvette Pyne; Nawar Diar Bakerly
paper_title: Menopause symptom prevalence in three post–COVID-19 syndrome clinics in England: A cross-sectional analysis

summary: A multicenter cross-sectional study of 1,011 Greek patients with long COVID documenting clinical presentation and symptom burden across multiple organ systems. The study is descriptive/observational with no intervention tested, making it ineligible for a treatment trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: Garyphallia Poulakou; Vasileios Michailidis; Athina Gogali; Stylianos Boutlas; Melina Kavousanaki; Paschalina Giouleka; Alexandros Stefanidis; Panagiota Styliara; Paschalis Steiropoulos; Argyris Tzouvelekis
paper_title: Real-world evidence on long COVID-19 in Greece: A multicenter, cross-sectional study (LONCOV2)

summary: Cross-sectional study investigating circulating and urinary inflammatory mediators and extracellular vesicles in post-COVID condition patients stratified by hospitalization status during acute infection. Found higher urinary extracellular vesicles and specific immune mediators in hospitalized post-COVID patients, suggesting remnant renal inflammatory processes.

paper_title: Higher levels of urinary extracellular vesicles and immune mediators are related to acute infection severity during the post-COVID period

summary: Cross-sectional study examining psychological distress and its predictive factors (cognitive failures, avoidance, rumination, injustice perception) in long COVID patients recruited from a hospital clinic and online. Found that these factors significantly predicted psychological distress but did not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Sinead A. Brown; Jessica Holland; Keith Gaynor; Jessica Bramham; Fiadhnait O'Keeffe; Susan O'Flanagan; Stefano Savinelli; Patrick Mallon; Eoin Feeney; Grace Kenny; Kathleen McCann; Christine Boyd
paper_title: A psychological model of predictive factors of distress following long COVID

summary: Cross-sectional study of 44,652 young adults examining the association between post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) and serious psychological distress, with prior mental health diagnosis as a moderator. Finds PASC associated with 53% increased odds of psychological distress, with stronger association in those without prior mental health diagnosis.
paper_authors: Ritika Rastogi; Ivo H. Cerda; Abdelrahman Ibrahim; Justin A. Chen; Courtney Stevens; Cindy H. Liu
paper_title: Long COVID and psychological distress in young adults: Potential protective effect of a prior mental health diagnosis

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing cognitive impairments in 194 long-COVID patients at a clinic, comparing their performance to age/sex/education-matched controls. Finds 44-53% of patients have clinically relevant cognitive impairments, particularly in global cognition, working memory, and executive function, with associations to poorer work function and quality of life.
paper_authors: Miskowiak KW; Pedersen JK; Gunnarsson DV; Roikjer TK; Podlekareva D.; Hansen H.; Dall CH; Johnsen S.
paper_title: Cognitive impairments among patients in a long-COVID clinic: Prevalence, pattern and relation to illness severity, work function and quality of life

summary: Secondary analysis of Census Bureau Household Pulse Survey data examining associations between anxiety/depression symptoms and social vulnerabilities (expenses, employment, food, housing, insurance) among long COVID patients across racial/ethnic groups. Found that social vulnerabilities partially mediated racial disparities in anxiety and depression outcomes.
paper_authors: Victoria Menzies; Fern Webb; Debra E. Lyon; Lisiane Pruinelli; Debra Lynch Kelly; Molly Jacobs
paper_title: Anxiety and depression among individuals with long COVID: Associations with social vulnerabilities

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between social network characteristics and depressive/anxiety symptoms in 410 long COVID patients from Germany. Found that larger social networks and living with others were associated with fewer depressive and anxiety symptoms, but this is an observational study without treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Gerhards SK; Luppa M.; Zülke A.; Sander C.; Schomerus G.; Buechner R.; Wirkner K.; Reusche M.; Zeynalova S.; Lehmann J.; Baber R.; Obrig H.; Herzig S.; Thöne-Otto A.; Witte AV; Villringer A.; Fricke C.; Bergh FT; Saur D.; Schroeter ML; Löffler M.; Engel C.; Riedel-Heller SG
paper_title: Depressive and anxiety symptoms in individuals with Long-COVID: Does social network matter? – Results of a German Long-COVID study

summary: A cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence of probable post-COVID cardiac sequelae (PCCS) among 336 healthcare workers in India, finding 11.9% prevalence with higher risk in females, hypertensive individuals, and those with moderate-severe acute COVID. The study also examined health-seeking behavior, finding that 55% of those with PCCS did not seek further evaluation.

summary: Cross-sectional study analyzing the association between long COVID and food insecurity among low-income US adults using 2022 National Health Interview Survey data. Found that individuals with long COVID had significantly higher risk of marginal and low/very low food insecurity, particularly among non-participants in food assistance programs.
paper_authors: Biplab Kumar Datta; Serena Phillips
paper_title: Long COVID and the Higher Risk of Food Insecurity Among Participants and Nonparticipants of Food Assistance Programs in the United States

paper_title: A Cross-Sectional Study of the Health of Emerging Young Adults in England Following a COVID-19 Infection

The study identified Borg Dyspnoea Scale, maximum oxygen uptake, and resting oxygen saturation as key predictors of physical activity in long COVID patients, but did not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

paper_title: Clinical indicators for predicting physical activity levels in long-term COVID-19: Insights from physical exertion and oxygen saturation
paper_journal: Journal of Bodywork and Movement Therapies

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing health-related quality of life in COVID-19 survivors 10 months after acute infection using the EQ-5D instrument. Found that anxiety/depression and mobility were most affected, with worse outcomes in females, older patients, and those with comorbidities or prior hospitalization.

paper_title: Calidad de vida relacionada con la salud en pacientes recuperados de COVID-19

summary: This cross-sectional survey describes acute and long COVID-19 symptoms among 80- and 90-year-old Swedish adults, identifying predictive factors for symptom development. paper_title: Individuals with a COVID-19 history exhibit asymmetric gait patterns despite full recovery

summary: Cross-sectional online survey of 1,046 Australian adults with type 2 diabetes assessing long COVID prevalence and its impact on diabetes management and physical activity. summary: This study evaluates the frequency and clinical relevance of post-COVID-19 condition in childcare facility employees using both prospective and retrospective questionnaire data. paper_title: The frequency of post-COVID-19 condition and its clinical relevance after COVID-19 disease of employees in facilities of preschool childcare

summary: Cross-sectional study evaluating functional capacity (Glittre-ADL test) in 42 men with long COVID 3 years post-infection, alongside measures of lung function, muscle strength, and quality of life. paper_title: Evaluating performance on the Glittre-ADL test in men with long COVID 3 years after a SARS-CoV-2 infection

The study found significantly lower prevalence of post-COVID conditions in the Omicron group (5.6%) compared to the control group (55.6%).

paper_title: Prevalence and trends in persistent symptoms following COVID-19 in Japan: A nationwide cross-sectional survey

summary: This cross-sectional study measures serum concentrations of 14 metals in 25 recovered COVID-19 patients versus 38 healthy controls at 6+ months post-discharge. The findings show persistent abnormal metal homeostasis and disrupted metabolic processes in recovered patients, suggesting long-term biochemical sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
paper_authors: Luyao Zhang; Fang Li; Xiaoxiong Liu; Xin-An Liu; Dawei Lu; Qian Luo; Qian Liu; Guibin Jiang
paper_title: Long-term effects of SARS-CoV-2 infection on metal homeostasis
paper_journal: Journal of Trace Elements in Medicine and Biology

summary: This cross-sectional survey study examines how vicarious experience with long COVID (knowing someone who suffered from it) influences vaccination intentions through protection motivation theory dimensions. The study finds that knowing long COVID patients increases perceived risk and vaccine efficacy but decreases self-efficacy, ultimately associating with higher vaccination intentions—but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Sarah Eitze; Philipp Sprengholz; Lars Korn; Parichehr Shamsrizi; Lisa Felgendreff; Cornelia Betsch
paper_title: Vicarious experiences of long COVID: A protection motivation theory analysis for vaccination intentions

summary: Cross-sectional study evaluating whether maximum phonation time tests can predict forced vital capacity impairment in post-COVID-19 patients. Findings show MPT has only moderate discriminatory power and is not a reliable indicator of pulmonary function in this population.
paper_authors: Juliana Alves Souza; Adriane Schmidt Pasqualoto; Carla Aparecida Cielo; Débora Bonesso Andriollo; Denis Altieri Oliveira Moraes
paper_title: Can We Use the Maximum Phonation Time as a Screening of Pulmonary Forced Vital Capacity in Post-COVID-19 Syndrome Patients?

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of employed US respondents from the 2022 National Health and Wellness Survey examining work productivity losses (absenteeism and presenteeism) among adults with physician-identified long COVID. The study found substantial heterogeneity in activity limitations, with presenteeism ranging from 24.2% to 92.8% across tertiles and strong associations between activity limitations and depression/anxiety, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Ashley Martin; Katharine Thomson; A. LePrade; Jeanne Bertolli; Scott D. Grosse
paper_title: PCR61 Persistent Work Limitations in Long COVID: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of Employed US Respondents to the 2022 National Health and Wellness Survey

summary: Cross-sectional study examining prevalence of dysphonia and voice disorders in 160 non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients during acute infection in Lombardy. While dysphonia was common (43.7%), this study focuses on acute COVID-19 symptoms during active infection, not long COVID sequelae, and includes no treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Giovanna Cantarella; Mirko Aldè; Dario Consonni; Gianvincenzo Zuccotti; Federica Di Berardino; Stefania Barozzi; Simona Bertoli; Alberto Battezzati; Diego Zanetti; Lorenzo Pignataro
paper_title: Prevalence of Dysphonia in Non hospitalized Patients with COVID-19 in Lombardy, the Italian Epicenter of the Pandemic

summary: An observational cross-sectional study of 1,366 Ecuadorian outpatients examining post-COVID-19 symptoms and their severity across different initial infection levels. The study found that 64.3% had symptoms 4-6 weeks post-infection, with fatigue (67.3%) and headache (45.2%) being most common, and identified risk factors including sedentary lifestyle and pre-existing comorbidities.
paper_authors: Fabricio González-Andrade
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 conditions in Ecuadorian patients: an observational study

summary: This study analyzes nationally representative data from Mexico's 2022 Health and Nutrition Survey to characterize the epidemiology of long COVID and identify determinants of PASC prevalence. It is a secondary analysis of survey data without any intervention or treatment component, making it ineligible for the treatment trials pipeline.
paper_authors: Omar Yaxmehen Bello-Chavolla; Carlos A. Fermín-Martínez; Daniel Ramírez-García; Arsenio Vargas-Vázquez; Luisa Fernández-Chirino; Martín Roberto Basile-Alvarez; Paulina Sánchez-Castro; Alejandra Núñez-Luna; Neftali Eduardo Antonio-Villa
paper_title: Prevalence and determinants of post-acute sequelae after SARS-CoV-2 infection (Long COVID) among adults in Mexico during 2022: a retrospective analysis of nationally representative data

summary: Observational multi-center cross-sectional study assessing prevalence and risk factors for post-COVID sequelae among 679 healthcare workers 12-52 weeks post-infection. Found 30.34% prevalence of COVID sequelae (fatigue, insomnia, dyspnea, arthralgia), with severity of acute illness, female gender, advanced age, and comorbidities as significant risk factors.

Chatterjee; Jerin Jose Cherian; Ved Prakash Kamboj; Nilima Kshirsagar
paper_title: An observational multi-centric COVID-19 sequelae study among health care workers
paper_journal: The Lancet Regional Health - Southeast Asia

summary: Population-based cross-sectional survey assessing the burden of long COVID symptoms in three districts of Haryana, India by linking to a prior seroprevalence study. Found cough as the only statistically significant persistent symptom after adjustment, with higher physical morbidity in women, but did not evaluate any treatment interventions.
paper_authors: Dhruva Chaudhry; Shweta Khandelwal; Chandrika Bahadur; Benjamin Daniels; Malay Bhattacharyya; Raman Gangakhedkar; Sapna Desai; Jishnu Das; Usha Gupta; Veena Singh; Shalu Garg; Liza Bhardwaj; Vinod Chayal; Varun Arora; Pawan Kumar Singh; Nizamuddin Khan; Suneela Garg; Sheela Godbole
paper_title: Prevalence of long COVID symptoms in Haryana, India: a cross-sectional follow-up study
paper_journal: The Lancet Regional Health - Southeast Asia

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) results in 200 patients with and without post-COVID-19 syndrome, conducted 45-120 days post-infection. Patients with post-COVID syndrome showed significantly lower peak VO2 and higher symptom occurrence during exercise, but no intervention or treatment was tested.
paper_authors: Leandro Barbagelata; Walter Masson; Diego Iglesias; Ezequiel Lillo; Juan Francisco Migone; Maria Laura Orazi; Joaquin Maritano Furcada
paper_title: Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing in Patients with Post-COVID-19 Syndrome

summary: Cross-sectional study of 384 recovered COVID-19 patients in Dhaka examining prevalence of long-term physical and psychological complications at 6 months post-discharge. Found high rates of general weakness (58.5%), insomnia (82.0%), and age-related differences in dementia prevalence and hospital stay duration, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Md. Monir Hossain Shimul; Salamat Khandker; Salim Khan
paper_title: Long-term health and psychological complications in recovered COVID-19 patients: A study in Dhaka city

summary: Community-based cross-sectional study of 12,789 adults infected with Omicron in December 2022–January 2023, assessed one year later for long COVID prevalence and health outcomes. Found 7.8% experienced long COVID (5.1% persistent), with fatigue and post-exertional malaise most common; no intervention was tested or evaluated.
paper_authors: Hui Zhang; Peng Yang; Xiaoying Gu; Ying Sun; Rongling Zhang; Daitao Zhang; Jiaojiao Zhang; Yeming Wang; Chunna Ma; Min Liu; Jiaxin Ma; Aili Li; Yingying Wang; Xiao Ma; Xiaojing Cui; Yimin Wang; Zhibo Liu; Wei Wang; Zhi Zheng; Yong Li; Jin Wu; Quanyi Wang; Bin Cao
paper_title: Health outcomes one year after Omicron infection among 12,789 adults: a community-based cross-sectional study
paper_journal: The Lancet Regional Health - Western Pacific

summary: This cross-sectional survey assessed the prevalence of functional, psychological, and social complaints in 200-300 patients 2-3 months after hospitalization for severe SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study describes persistent symptoms, identifies risk factors, and characterizes healthcare and psychosocial support needs in this emerging long COVID population.
paper_authors: Hikombo Hitoto; N. Crochette; Pierre Ménager; Sophie Blanchi; Jennifer Laine; L. Grandière-Pérez; Audrey Paris; Anna Berréhare; F. Scholastique; François Goupil
paper_title: REPERCOV : repérage des plaintes fonctionnelles et psychosociales après une hospitalisation pour infection sévère à SARS-CoV-2

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 107 people with multiple sclerosis assessing post-COVID-19 syndrome prevalence and risk factors, stratified by vaccination, infection frequency, and disease-modifying therapy categories. Found 6.5% PCS prevalence associated with category I DMTs and repeated infections, but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Deepak Sharma; Christian P. Kamm; Robert Hoepner; Iris-Katharina Penner; Thomas Nyffeler; Lara Diem
paper_title: Characterizing post-COVID-19 syndrome in multiple sclerosis: Vaccine status, infection burden, and therapy categories as predictors

summary: Cross-sectional study using nailfold capillaroscopy to evaluate microvascular changes in 97 participants (52 acute COVID-19, 45 convalescent including long COVID). Found increased capillary hemorrhages in convalescent group (40%) vs acute (17%), but no clinically significant structural differences in capillary width or density.
paper_authors: Wilkinson S.; Wilkinson J.; Grace A.; Lyon D.; Mellor M.; Yunus T.; Manning J.; Dinsdale G.; Berks M.; Knight S.; Bakerly N.; Gebril A.; Dark P.; Herrick A.; Taylor C.; Dickinson M.; Murray A.
paper_title: Imaging the microvasculature using nailfold capillaroscopy in patients with coronavirus disease-2019; A cross-sectional study

summary: Survey of 1,000 dialysis patients at 6 months post-COVID-19 infection to characterize long COVID sequelae prevalence and associated risk factors. Found 17.9% (179/1000) experienced at least one sequela, with muscle loss/weight loss (53%), fatigue (29%), and depression/anxiety (16%) most common; severe acute COVID, older age, overweight, and comorbidities associated with sequelae presence.
paper_authors: Malika Belkacemi; H. Baouche; Sébastien Gomis; Mathilde Lassalle; Cécile Couchoud
paper_title: Séquelles à 6 mois après une infection à SARS-CoV2 chez les patients dialysés

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 201 workers in tertiary sector (banking, telecommunications) examining prevalence of post-COVID-19 syndrome symptoms including sleep disorders. Found 17.9% of workers reported one or more post-COVID symptoms at time of study, with fatigue, exhaustion on effort, anxiety, and memory problems being most common; sleep disturbances were rare.
paper_authors: Mohamed Hamadouche; Nadia Zouda; Naziha Abed
paper_title: Étude du syndrome post-COVID-19 chez les travailleurs du secteur tertiaire

summary: Cross-sectional study of 694 COVID-19 patients in Spain assessing long-term symptoms and quality of life 4.7-24 months post-infection. Found 16.57% reported not fully recovering, with fatigue, anosmia, and cognitive dysfunction most prevalent; female gender and older age were independent risk factors.
paper_authors: Oscar Perez; Miguel Santibañez; Laura Rasines; Jose Maria Castillo; Adrian Hugo Aginagalde-Llorente
paper_title: Long-Term Patient Symptoms and Quality of Life in Adults After COVID-19: A Real Life Study

summary: This cross-sectional study compares the prevalence of post-acute COVID-19 symptoms and functional impairment in healthcare workers versus the general population in Switzerland (April-July 2021). Healthcare workers showed significantly higher rates of fatigue, headache, concentration difficulty, and functional impairment both overall and specifically associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection.
paper_authors: Mayssam Nehme; Laure Vieux; Delphine S. Courvoisier; Olivia Braillard; Hervé Spechbach; Frederique Jacquerioz; Julien Salamun; Frederic Assal; Frederic Lador; Matteo Coen; Thomas Agoritsas; Jean-Luc Reny; Christophe Graf; Lamyae Benzakour; Riccardo Favale; Paola M. paper_title: The pandemic toll and post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 in healthcare workers at a Swiss University Hospital

summary: This cross-sectional study compared retinal and choroidal parameters between post-COVID-19 patients with neurologic symptoms and healthy controls using spectral-domain OCT imaging. The study found thinning of the ganglion cell layer and inner plexiform layer in post-COVID patients, suggesting direct or indirect effects of SARS-CoV-2 on retinal structure, but concludes these are not indicative of long-term neurodegeneration.
paper_authors: Ayşe Yağmur Kanra; Meltem Güzin Altınel; Funda Alparslan
paper_title: Evaluation of retinal and choroidal parameters as neurodegeneration biomarkers in patients with post-covid-19 syndrome

summary: This cross-sectional study compared the clinical and psychosocial profiles of 55 post-COVID syndrome patients with healthy controls and recovered COVID-19 patients. Post-COVID patients showed significantly worse outcomes across pain intensity/interference, central sensitization, insomnia, kinesiophobia, catastrophizing, depression, anxiety, and stress.
paper_authors: Andrés Calvache-Mateo; Alba Navas-Otero; Alejandro Heredia-Ciuró; Javier Matín-Núñez; Irene Torres-Sánchez; Laura López-López; Marie Carmen Valenza
paper_title: Post-COVID Patients With New-Onset Chronic Pain 2 Years After Infection: Cross-Sectional Study

summary: A cross-sectional telephone survey study of 2,070 patients assessing the prevalence, clinical characteristics, and predictive factors of long COVID. The study found a 41.6% prevalence of long COVID with ageusia, cognitive problems, and fatigue as the most common symptoms, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: N. Ketata; J. Jedidi; H. Maamri; M. Baklouti; Fadhila Issaoui; Olfa Chakroun; J. Damak; M. Ben Yahya; Y. Mejdoub; Rania Hammami
paper_title: Profil épidémiologique et aspects cliniques du COVID long

summary: This population-based longitudinal survey study compares different survey-based definitions of long COVID to understand variation in prevalence estimates across a Michigan cohort. The paper documents that prevalence rates range from 10.8% to 24.5% depending on the survey question used, with disparities by race/ethnicity and income, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Jana L. Hirschtick; Elizabeth Slocum; Blair Whittington; Michael R. Elliott; Sameera Ahmed; Nancy L. Fleischer
paper_title: Comparison of survey questions to define long COVID: Implications for prevalence and disparities

summary: Cross-sectional study of 182 participants 6 months post-COVID-19 assessing sleep quality and mental health outcomes using standardized instruments (PSQI, PTSD Checklist, SCL-90). Found that 91.2% had psychiatric symptoms including poor sleep (64.8%), PTSD (28.6%), and anxiety (28%), with risk factors including female sex, diabetes, oxygen support, and elevated neutrophil/lymphocyte ratio.
paper_authors: Gellan K. Ahmed; Eman M. Khedr; Dina A. Hamad; Taghreed S. Meshref; Mustafa M. Hashem; Mai M. Aly
paper_title: Long term impact of Covid-19 infection on sleep and mental health: A cross-sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the association between underlying health conditions and long COVID among 4,507 Vietnamese COVID-19 survivors, stratified by hospitalization status. Found that health literacy moderates the negative impact of underlying conditions on long COVID in non-hospitalized individuals but not in hospitalized survivors.
paper_authors: Han T. Vo; Thang V. Dao; Tinh X. Do; Binh N. Do; Tan T. Nguyen; Khue M. Pham; Vinh H. Vu; Linh V. Pham; Lien T.H. Nguyen; Lan T.H. Le; Hoang C. Nguyen; Tuan V. Tran; Trung H. Nguyen; Anh T. Nguyen; Hoan V. Nguyen; Phuoc B. Nguyen; Thu T.M. Pham; Tien D. Dao; Thuy T. Le; Thao T.P. Nguyen; Cuong Q. Tran; Kien T. Nguyen; Tuyen V. Duong
paper_title: Association between underlying health conditions and long COVID among non-hospitalized and hospitalized individuals as modified by health literacy: A multi-center study

summary: Cross-sectional survey of CUNY students examining associations between long-COVID, COVID-related stress, and comorbid depression/anxiety outcomes in Winter 2021-2022. Found that women, lower-SES participants, those with high stress, and those with long-COVID had significantly higher odds of probable comorbid depression and anxiety.
paper_authors: Sasha Rudenstine; Talia Schulder; Krish J. Bhatt; Kat McNeal; Catherine K. Ettman; Sandro Galea
paper_title: Long-COVID and comorbid depression and anxiety two years into the COVID-19 pandemic

summary: Cross-sectional cohort study of 7,601 German participants examining associations between SARS-CoV-2 infection, pandemic burden, and mental health outcomes measured via online surveys. Found that past infection, particularly with persistent symptoms 12 weeks post-infection, was associated with mental health deterioration (exhaustion, fatigue, concentration deficits, memory problems), independent of pandemic burden.
paper_authors: Lavinia A. Steinmann; Luise V. Claaß; Moritz Rau; Janka Massag; Sophie Diexer; Bianca Klee; Cornelia Gottschick; Mascha Binder; Daniel Sedding; Thomas Frese; Matthias Girndt; Jessica Hoell; Irene Moor; Jonas Rosendahl; Michael Gekle; Rafael Mikolajczyk; Nils Opel
paper_title: Differential associations between SARS-CoV-2 infection, perceived burden of the pandemic and mental health in the German population-based cohort for digital health research

summary: Cross-sectional study developing prediction models to identify individuals at risk of long COVID based on pre- and post-infection factors in a Chinese community population of 420 COVID-19 patients. The study identifies age, psychological factors, and acute-phase symptoms as key predictors but does not test any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Meng Zhou; Qicheng Zhu; Yucheng Xu; Zhifeng Zhou; Congrui Guo; Zhiping Lin; Xinyi Zhang; Zhipeng Yang; Xueyun Li; Wei Lin
paper_title: A nomogram to predict long COVID risk based on pre- and post-infection factors: Results from a cross-sectional study in South China

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of PTSD symptoms and associated risk factors among COVID-19 survivors from the first pandemic wave, including 1,108 participants after propensity score matching. Identified four key risk factors: higher COVID-19 severity, fatigue, COVID-related stigma, and poor sleep quality.
paper_authors: Weijun Xiao; Xiaoyang Liu; Hao Wang; Yiman Huang; Zhenwei Dai; Mingyu Si; Jiaqi Fu; Xu Chen; Mengmeng Jia; Zhiwei Leng; Dan Cui; Winnie W.S. Mak; Xiaoyou Su
paper_title: Prevalence and risk for symptoms of PTSD among survivors of a COVID-19 infection

summary: Cross-sectional study of 1,354 adults aged ≥50 in Europe investigating risk factors for post-COVID-19 conditions using logistic regression. Found that older age, lower education, and COVID-19 hospitalization significantly increase risk of persistent post-COVID symptoms.
paper_authors: Bovil T.; Wester CT; Scheel-Hincke LL; Andersen-Ranberg K.
paper_title: Risk factors of post-COVID-19 conditions attributed to COVID-19 disease in people aged ≥50 years in Europe and Israel

summary: This cross-sectional study examines the association between multimorbidity and anxiety symptomatology in 389 post-COVID patients using the HAD anxiety scale and linear regression analysis. The findings show that each additional chronic condition is associated with a mean increase of 0.11 in anxiety scores, suggesting that comorbidity management is important for mental health outcomes in post-COVID care.
paper_authors: Milena Nogueira Azevedo; Elisângela da Silva Rodrigues; Emília Augusta Franz Vieira Passos; Márcio Andrade Barreto Filho; Ana Paula Andrade Barreto; Marcelo Chalhoub Coelho Lima; Mauricio Lima Barreto; Luis Fernando Silva Castro-de-Araujo
paper_title: Multimorbidity associated with anxiety symptomatology in post-COVID patients

summary: Cross-sectional study examining post-traumatic stress disorder risk in COVID-19 survivors in Colombia, finding 13.3% PTSD-R prevalence. Study identifies depression, insomnia, low income, and marital status as associated factors but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Edwin Herazo; John Carlos Pedrozo-Pupo; Adalberto Campo-Arias
paper_title: Post-Traumatic Stress Risk Among COVID-19 Survivors in Colombia

summary: Cross-sectional questionnaire survey of 502 COVID-19 recovered patients assessing the prevalence and persistence of post-COVID symptoms beyond 12 months. Found that ~25-33% of patients reported at least one symptom at 6-24 months post-infection, with fatigue, dyspnea, and olfactory dysfunction being most common, particularly in those with moderate/severe acute infection.
paper_authors: Morioka S.; Tsuzuki S.; Maruki T.; Terada M.; Miyazato Y.; Kutsuna S.; Saito S.; Shimanishi Y.; Takahashi K.; Sanada M.; Ashida S.; Akashi M.; Kuge C.; Osanai Y.; Tanaka K.; Suzuki M.; Hayakawa K.; Ohmagari N.
paper_title: Epidemiology of post-COVID conditions beyond 1 year: a cross-sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional questionnaire survey of 749 respondents examining the association between marital status and post-COVID-19 symptom development. Found that single patients, particularly those aged 40+ with mild COVID-19, experienced higher rates of depression and memory impairment, suggesting a need for targeted psychological support.
paper_authors: Ryohei Kudoh; Kosaku Komiya; Aya Shinohara; Takaaki Kageyama; Kazufumi Hiramatsu; Jun-ichi Kadota
paper_title: Marital status and post-COVID-19 conditions

summary: This study validates the concordance between evaluator-administered and self-assessed versions of the Post-COVID-19 Functional Status Scale (PCFS) in 97 post-COVID patients. While the study is about long COVID, it does not test a treatment intervention—it only evaluates agreement between two assessment methods.
paper_authors: Betancourt-Peña J.; Rodriguez-Castro J.; Perez-Hortua V.; Ávila-Valencia JC; Benavides-Córdoba V.
paper_title: Escala de estado funcional post-COVID-19: concordancia entre la versión administrada por evaluador versus autoevaluada en pacientes con síndrome post-COVID-19

summary: A nationally representative survey study examining Americans' knowledge about Long COVID and the relationship between meta-ignorance (overconfidence in knowledge) and public health outcomes. The study found that over one-fifth of Americans express high confidence in their Long COVID knowledge despite having lower objective knowledge, and this meta-ignorance is associated with vaccine hesitancy and increased Long COVID risk.
paper_authors: Matt Motta; Timothy Callaghan; Medini Padmanabhan; Jennifer Cornacchione Ross; Lisa M. Gargano; Sarah Bowman; David Yokum
paper_title: Identifying and mitigating the public health consequences of meta-ignorance about "Long COVID" risks

summary: A prospective descriptive cross-sectional survey of 206 post-COVID-19 patients documenting symptom prevalence and impact on quality of life. The study characterizes long COVID symptoms (fatigue, anxiety, joint pain, dyspnea, cognitive impairment) and notes greater quality-of-life impairment in women and older adults, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: K. Abbaci Daghor; N. Mellas; I. Haraoubia; A. Berrah; N. Laraba
paper_title: Le syndrome post COVID-19 : un mythe ou une réalité ?

summary: This national cross-sectional survey assessed long COVID symptom prevalence and risk factors among 2,665 COVID-19 patients in Malta 3-6 months post-infection. Female sex, hospitalization, and initial acute symptoms were associated with higher odds of persistent fatigue, shortness of breath, anxiety, and other long COVID symptoms.
paper_authors: Baruch J.; Zahra C.; Cardona T.; Melillo T.
paper_title: National long COVID impact and risk factors

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluates fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) as a potential biomarker in 68 post-COVID patients compared to 29 healthy controls. The findings suggest FeNO is not useful as a biomarker for post-COVID-19, though sex-based differences were observed.
paper_authors: Mauro Maniscalco; Pasquale Ambrosino; Remo Poto; Salvatore Fuschillo; Sergio Poto; Maria Gabriella Matera; Mario Cazzola
paper_title: Can FeNO be a biomarker in the post-COVID-19 patients monitoring?

summary: A cross-sectional study of 142 patients hospitalized with moderate-to-severe COVID-19 pneumonia examining the prevalence and predictive factors of post-COVID syndrome at 12 weeks. The study found a 26.1% prevalence of post-COVID syndrome with dyslipidemia as an independent risk factor, but it is an observational cohort study with no treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Tasnim Znegui; I. Moussa; I. Sahnoun; H. Mrassi; A. Allouche; C. Ksouri; L. Douik El Gharbi
paper_title: Profil des patients ayant le syndrome post-COVID-19

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing diabetogenic risk markers (insulin resistance, beta-cell function, glucose tolerance) between recovered COVID-19 patients and unexposed controls in Ghana. Recovered COVID-19 respondents showed higher insulin resistance and beta-cell dysfunction, indicating elevated type 2 diabetes risk, but no intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Jeffrey Amankona Obeng; Richard Kujo Adatsi; Leonard Derkyi-Kwarteng; Ansumana Sandy Bockarie; Samuel Victor Nuvor; Ebenezer Aniakwaa-Bonsu; Paul Nsiah; Samuel Acquah
paper_title: Increased diabetogenic risk of recovered COVID-19 infection and unexposed respondents in the Central Region of Ghana

summary: A cross-sectional descriptive study of 372 long COVID patients (>12 weeks post-infection) hospitalized or followed in ambulatory care at a military hospital in Morocco, assessing symptom prevalence and quality of life using the EQ-5D instrument. The study found that 20-25% of patients reported difficulties with mobility, activities of daily living, pain/discomfort, and anxiety/depression, with neuropsychiatric manifestations being prominent in this population.
paper_authors: Silvia Sassi; J. Oujaber; I. Ouande; R. Benchanna; R. Bouchentouf; A. Benjelloun; H. Janah
paper_title: COVID long : expérience de l’hôpital militaire Avicenne de Marrakech

summary: International cross-sectional study examining the bidirectional relationship between insomnia and long COVID across 16 countries using web-based surveys. Finds that pre-pandemic insomnia increases long COVID risk (RR 1.33) and that long COVID is associated with higher incident insomnia rates (RR 2.00), highlighting sleep as an important management factor.
paper_authors: Si-Jing Chen; Charles M. Morin; Hans Ivers; Yun Kwok Wing; Markku Partinen; Ilona Merikanto; Brigitte Holzinger; Colin A. Espie; Luigi De Gennaro; Yves Dauvilliers; Frances Chung; Juliana Yordanova; Domagoj Vidović; Catia Reis; Giuseppe Plazzi; Thomas Penzel; Michael R. paper_title: The association of insomnia with long COVID: An international collaborative study (ICOSS-II)

summary: This international cross-sectional survey examines changes in excessive daytime sleepiness, excessive sleep quantity, and fatigue during the COVID-19 pandemic across 18,785 participants in 15 countries. While COVID-19 is mentioned and associated with increased sleepiness and fatigue, the study focuses on pandemic-related sleep changes in the general population rather than long COVID sequelae, and does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

paper_title: Association between hypersomnolence and the COVID-19 pandemic: The International COVID-19 Sleep Study (ICOSS)

summary: Cross-sectional study of 170 healthcare workers at a Tunisian hospital with prior COVID-19 infection, assessing the frequency and evolution of respiratory symptoms in long COVID. Among 90 patients (52.9%) reporting persistent symptoms, 32 had respiratory manifestations (dyspnea, chest tightness, cough) with mean duration of 13±7 weeks; 26 were followed up 14 months later, with 10 still reporting exertional dyspnea despite inhaled corticosteroid treatment.
paper_authors: A. Dallagi; J. Hsinet; Nihel Khouja; S. Ismail; Asma Koubaa; T. Yahyaoui; Emna Bechrifa; Emna Baraketi; A. Benzarti; A. Ben Jemâa
paper_title: La symptomatologie respiratoire du COVID long chez le personnel de santé de l’hôpital la Rabta

summary: International cross-sectional survey of 1,001 COVID-19 survivors examining self-reported sleep health across 6 dimensions (regularity, satisfaction, alertness, timing, efficiency, duration) compared to pre-infection baseline. Finds worse current sleep health associated with greater COVID-19 symptom severity and poorer quality of life, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Elisabet Alzueta; Paul B. Perrin; Dilara Yuksel; Daniela Ramos-Usuga; Orsolya Kiss; Stella Iacovides; Massimiliano de Zambotti; Mar Cortes; Laiene Olabarrieta-Landa; Juan Carlos Arango-Lasprilla; Fiona C. Baker
paper_title: An international study of post-COVID sleep health

summary: Cross-sectional study evaluating the prevalence of sleep disorders 3 months after hospitalization for SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia in 50 patients using the Insomnia Severity Index and HADS scales. Found sleep disturbances in 68% of patients (predominantly insomnia at 80%), associated with obesity, ICU admission history, longer hospitalization duration, and depression scores.
paper_authors: N. Boubaker; S. Mhamdi; Selsabil Daboussi; N. Guediri; I. Mejri; Z. Moatemri; C. Aïchaouia; M. Khadhraoui
paper_title: Évaluation des troubles de sommeil à long terme chez les patients hospitalisés pour pneumopathie à SARS-CoV-2

summary: Cross-sectional study using electronic nose technology and chemometric analysis to discriminate volatile organic compounds in exhaled breath samples between COVID-19 patients, post-COVID syndrome patients, and healthy controls. The study demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy (97.6-100%) for identifying post-COVID patients but is a diagnostic proof-of-concept study without treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Blanca Nohemí Zamora-Mendoza; Lorena Díaz de León-Martínez; Maribel Rodríguez-Aguilar; Boris Mizaikoff; Rogelio Flores-Ramírez
paper_title: Chemometric analysis of the global pattern of volatile organic compounds in the exhaled breath of patients with COVID-19, post-COVID and healthy subjects. Proof of concept for post-COVID assessment

summary: This cross-sectional study examined how socioeconomic position (SEP) influences the relationship between post-COVID-19 condition and health-related quality of life in a representative sample of 1,448 French adults surveyed in autumn 2022. The study found that PCC, low education, and low household income negatively impact HRQoL, with greater PCC-induced impairment among people without tertiary education, unemployed individuals, and business owners.
paper_authors: Cyrille Delpierre; Cédric Lemogne; Olivier Steichen; Sarah Tebeka; Tatjana T. Makovski; Joël Coste
paper_title: Influence of socioeconomic position on the relationship between long COVID and health-related quality of life: A nationwide random sampling survey in France in autumn 2022

summary: A national online survey of 1,507 Czech adults assessing the frequency and types of sleep disorders occurring after COVID-19 infection. The study found that 81.3% reported at least one sleep difficulty post-infection, with insomnia (59.4%), night sweats (38.4%), and hypersomnolence (33.3%) being most common; sleep symptoms persisted in over 62% even 9+ months after infection.
paper_authors: Tereza Dvořáková; Radana Měrková; Jitka Bušková
paper_title: Sleep disorders after COVID-19 in Czech population: Post-lockdown national online survey

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of 206,969 US household survey responses (Sept 2022-Apr 2023) examining the association between long COVID and housing insecurity. Found that people with long COVID were 1.5-2x more likely to experience housing difficulties, with highest risk among low-income adults and those with functional limitations.
paper_authors: Samuel E. Packard; Ezra Susser
paper_title: Association of long COVID with housing insecurity in the United States, 2022–2023

summary: This cross-sectional study compared respiratory and metabolic profiles between 20 post-COVID-19 soccer players and 20 healthy controls during cardiopulmonary exercise testing. Post-COVID athletes showed increased respiratory work and hyperventilation during exercise with elevated resting and maximal lactate levels, but no difference in maximal oxygen uptake.

paper_title: Athletes with mild post-COVID-19 symptoms experience increased respiratory and metabolic demands: Α cross-sectional study

summary: This multicenter cross-sectional study evaluates the impact of pulmonary embolism (PE) on health outcomes in COVID-19 patients at 3 months after hospitalization. Patients with PE showed reduced quality of life and greater pulmonary impairment, suggesting PE is a marker of COVID-19 severity with potential long-term health implications.

paper_title: The impact of pulmonary embolism on health outcomes of COVID-19 at 3 months after hospitalization
paper_journal: Research and Practice in Thrombosis and Haemostasis

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 2,883 California residents to assess long COVID prevalence using five different definitions. Found prevalence ranged from 4.9% (severe long COVID) to 20.9% (incomplete recovery), with vaccination status inversely associated with long COVID risk.
paper_authors: Jake M. Pry; Kalyani McCullough; Kristina Wen-Jeh Lai; Esther Lim; Megha L. Mehrotra; Katherine Lamba; Seema Jain
paper_title: Defining long COVID using a population-based SARS-CoV-2 survey in California

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of 8,757 U.S. adults examining associations between COVID-19 booster vaccination status and long-COVID prevalence using 2022 National Health Interview Survey data. Booster-vaccinated individuals had significantly lower adjusted odds of long-COVID (OR 0.75, 95% CI 0.61-0.93) compared to unvaccinated individuals.
paper_authors: Zhigang Xie; Sericea Stallings-Smith; Shraddha Patel; Stuart Case; Young-Rock Hong
paper_title: COVID-19 booster vaccine uptake and reduced risks for long-COVID: A cross-sectional study of a U.S. adult population

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 3,042 U.S. adults during June-July 2022 estimating SARS-CoV-2 prevalence (17.3%) and long COVID prevalence among those infected >4 weeks prior (21.5%). Study documents inequitable distribution of infection and long COVID burden across demographic groups and socioeconomic strata.
paper_authors: Saba A. Qasmieh; McKaylee M. Robertson; Chloe A. Teasdale; Sarah G. Kulkarni; Heidi E. Jones; Margaret McNairy; Luisa N. Borrell; Denis Nash
paper_title: The prevalence of SARS-CoV-2 infection and long COVID in U.S. adults during the BA.4/BA.5 surge, June–July 2022

topics: post-intensive care syndrome|prolonged COVID|mortality|quality of life|cognitive impairment
summary: A cross-sectional study describing mortality, rehospitalization, quality of life, and post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) symptoms in 124 COVID-19 patients discharged from ICUs in Argentina, assessed 6-18 months post-discharge via telephone interview. The study documents outcomes including 7.3% mortality, cognitive impairment in 54.4%, PICS in 66.7%, and reduced quality of life, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Fernando Argento; Manuel Donato; Dario Villalba; Marisol García Sarubbio; Anabella Giménez; Agustin Ciapponi; Federico Augustovski
paper_title: Mortalidad, Secuelas Clínicas y Calidad de Vida Luego del Alta de Unidades de Cuidados Intensivos en Pacientes con COVID-19: Estudio Multicéntrico Descriptivo en Argentina

summary: Cross-sectional study of 179 long COVID patients in Mexico assessing physical and psychosomatic manifestations and their association with decreased quality of life. Found that pain/discomfort, anxiety/depression, and persistence of ≥3 symptoms were independently associated with decreased QOL, with authors suggesting neuropsychological rehabilitation might benefit patients but noting that such interventions require evaluation.
paper_authors: Jonnathan O. Cázares-Lara; Alberto Ordinola-Navarro; Zully Carmona-Aguilera; Gustavo M. Benitez-Altamirano; Luis D. Beltran-Ontiveros; Juan P. Ramirez-Hinojosa; Cesar Lopez-Vejar; Bruno A. Lopez-Luis
paper_title: Main Predictors of Decreasing in Quality of Life in Patients With Post-COVID-19: A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: Population-based cross-sectional study of 121,379 US adults examining associations between Long COVID prevalence and risk factors including COPD, smoking status, and COVID-19 vaccination. Finds 21.8% Long COVID prevalence, with protective effect of 3-4 vaccine doses and increased risk with COPD and current smoking.
paper_authors: Olufemi Erinoso; Olatokunbo Osibogun; Siva Balakrishnan; Wei Yang
paper_title: Long COVID among US adults from a population-based study: Association with vaccination, cigarette smoking, and the modifying effect of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)

summary: Cross-sectional study of 478 COVID-19 survivors (mean 30 days post-infection) assessing cognitive performance and symptom clusters. Finds domain-specific cognitive deficits in processing speed and reasoning, with cognitive impairment correlating to physical symptoms rather than mental health symptoms.
paper_authors: Conor J. Wild; Loretta Norton; David K. Menon; David A. Ripsman; Richard H. Swartz; Adrian M. Owen
paper_title: Disentangling the cognitive, physical, and mental health sequelae of COVID-19

summary: Population-based cross-sectional survey of 2,533 Michigan residents with confirmed prior SARS-CoV-2 infection examining prevalence and predictors of eight Long COVID symptom clusters. Found neuropsychiatric symptoms (23.7%) most prevalent, with female sex, pre-existing psychological conditions, and ICU admission as strong predictors; notably, age and pre-existing conditions showed differential associations across symptom clusters.
paper_authors: Jana L. Hirschtick; Yanmei Xie; Elizabeth Slocum; Robert E. Hirschtick; Laura E. Power; Michael R. Elliott; Robert C. Orellana; Nancy L. Fleischer
paper_title: A statewide population-based approach to examining Long COVID symptom prevalence and predictors in Michigan

summary: This is a cross-sectional analysis from the EPICOVID 2.0 Brazilian survey examining associations between self-reported changes in physical activity during the pandemic and post-COVID symptoms in 33,250 participants. The study found that participants who maintained physical activity had lower odds of tiredness and joint pain, but it is an observational study of associations without testing an intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Deanivea Mendes Felix; Vishnu Jaisree Mohandas; Otávio Amaral de Andrade Leão; Fernando Vinholes Siqueira; Pedro Curi Hallal
paper_title: Physical activity and post-COVID symptoms: Findings from the EPICOVID 2.0 survey in Brazil

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 214 children in Indonesia assessing prevalence of long COVID symptoms more than four weeks after positive COVID-19 test. Found 28.5% with respiratory disorders, 26.2% with sleep disorders, 23.4% with fatigue, and other symptoms, demonstrating long COVID occurs in children though less frequently than adults.
paper_authors: Yann-Mickael Dalmat
paper_title: Covid long ou syndrome post-guérison

summary: This cross-sectional study examines whether EEG-based frontal aperiodic exponent values can serve as an objective biomarker for cognitive fatigue in Long COVID and multiple sclerosis patients. While it identifies a promising diagnostic biomarker, it does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Stefanie Linnhoff; Roi Cohen Kadosh; Tino Zaehle
paper_title: EEG-based frontal excitation/inhibition balance as an objective biomarker for cognitive fatigue across multiple sclerosis and Long COVID

summary: This international cross-sectional survey examined the prevalence and predictors of post-COVID-19 condition in patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases versus healthy controls, analyzing data from 1,677 respondents surveyed >90 days post-infection. Post-COVID-19 condition was reported in 10.7% of autoimmune rheumatic disease patients versus 5.3% of controls, with female sex, disease duration, comorbidities, and severe acute COVID-19 identified as significant risk factors.

paper_title: Post-COVID-19 condition in patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases: the COVID-19 Vaccination in Autoimmune Diseases (COVAD) study

summary: A national cross-sectional study comparing long COVID symptom prevalence in Danish children aged 0-14 years with matched uninfected controls. Children with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection reported significantly higher rates of long-lasting symptoms, though quality-of-life differences were minimal and not clinically meaningful.
paper_authors: Selina Kikkenborg Berg; Pernille Palm; Ulrikka Nygaard; Henning Bundgaard; Maria Nivi Schmidt Petersen; Siri Rosenkilde; Anne Bonde Thorsted; Annette Kjær Ersbøll; Lau Casper Thygesen; Susanne Dam Nielsen; Anne Vinggaard Christensen
paper_title: Long COVID symptoms in SARS-CoV-2-positive children aged 0–14 years and matched controls in Denmark (LongCOVIDKidsDK): a national, cross-sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional cohort study investigating the persistence of SARS-CoV-2 RNA in diverse tissues at 1, 2, and 4 months post-infection and its association with long COVID symptoms. Found viral RNA in 30% of tissues at 1 month declining to 11% at 4 months, with significant association between viral persistence and long COVID development (OR 5.17), but this is an observational study examining correlation with disease mechanisms rather than testing a treatment intervention.

summary: This cross-sectional study identified three distinct long COVID phenotypes based on symptom burden using cluster analysis of 8,630 survey respondents. The analysis found that symptom count (rather than type) predicts healthcare use and quality of life, with higher-burden patients consulting significantly more providers.
paper_authors: Iris Gerritzen; Iris M. Brus; Inge Spronk; Sara Biere-Rafi; Suzanne Polinder; Juanita A. Haagsma
paper_title: Identification of post-COVID-19 condition phenotypes, and differences in health-related quality of life and healthcare use: a cluster analysis

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 1,331 post-COVID patients examining the prevalence and severity of tinnitus and its association with other long COVID symptoms. The study found that 27.9% of patients reported post-COVID tinnitus, with severity strongly associated with poor recovery outcomes, hearing loss, and anxiety.
paper_authors: Shihang Mao; Dantong Gu; Di Wang; Peifan Li; Xiaoling Huang; Haoning Yin; Shan Sun
paper_title: Prevalence and prognosis of tinnitus in post-COVID-19 patients: a cross-sectional survey

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing psychiatric symptoms and diagnoses in 101 long COVID patients with cognitive complaints using standardized psychometric scales and psychiatric interviews. Found that 47.4% of referred patients had psychiatric diagnoses (adjustment disorder, anxiety, depression, PTSD), but the study is observational without intervention or treatment evaluation.

paper_title: Post-COVID condition: a focus on psychiatric symptoms and diagnoses in patients with cognitive complaints

While the paper demonstrates that COVID-19 patients report greater depression and cognitive decline, it does not evaluate any treatment intervention and is observational in nature.
