paper_title: 52 Depressive Symptoms and Subjective Cognitive Decline in Individuals with COVID-19
paper_journal: Journal of the International Neuropsychological Society

summary: This study is a secondary analysis of a cross-sectional survey investigating associations between COVID-19 vaccination (≥3 doses) and self-reported long COVID symptoms in Hong Kong residents with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection. While about long COVID, it does not study an intervention/treatment given to patients—it only observes existing vaccination status as a passive exposure variable without administering or testing any treatment for long COVID.

paper_title: Receiving three doses of inactivated or mRNA COVID-19 vaccines was associated with lower odds of long COVID symptoms among people with a history of SARS-CoV-2 infection in Hong Kong, China: a cross-sectional survey study

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing cognitive performance fatigability, perceived fatigability, and trait fatigue between 34 post-COVID-19 patients and 36 recovered controls. Found performance fatigability in processing speed tasks in the PCC group but no correlations between fatigue domains.
paper_authors: Agnes Andersson; Josefine Andin; Richard Levi; Ulrika Birberg Thornberg
paper_title: Cognitive performance fatigability, perceived fatigability, and trait fatigue in post-COVID-19 condition: A cross-sectional study.

summary: Cross-sectional study examining long-term psychological effects (anxiety, depression, PTSD, sleep disorders) in children and adolescents 6+ months after COVID-19 infection. paper_authors: Arif Önder; Aslı Sürer Adanır; Zehra İşleyen; Özge Gizli Çoban; Yasemin Merve Ayrancı; Tuğçe Tural Kara; Serhat Nasıroğlu

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing cognitive performance between COVID-19 survivors and controls using smartphone-based cognitive tests. Found no significant differences in cognitive performance between groups at baseline, highlighting the need for longitudinal follow-up.

paper_title: 67 COVID-19 Mobile Brain Health
paper_journal: Journal of the International Neuropsychological Society

summary: Cross-sectional study examining how anxiety and depression symptoms moderate the association between COVID-19 infection and memory performance in 84 Canadian adults. Found that anxiety symptom severity had a significant moderating effect on delayed verbal and visual memory retrieval in COVID-19 positive participants, but this is an observational study with no treatment intervention.

summary: Cross-sectional observational study assessing cognitive and psychiatric disturbances in 101 post-COVID patients using neurological screening (MoCA) and psychiatric questionnaires. Found cognitive deficits in 34% and psychiatric symptoms in ~60%, but no intervention was tested or evaluated—this is a descriptive assessment study, not a treatment trial.

paper_authors: Elem Cristina Rodrigues Chaves; Juarez Antônio Simões Quaresma; Maria Helena Cruz Rodrigues; Daniel Carvalho de Menezes; Igor Costa de Lima; Jorge Rodrigues de Sousa; Vanessa Costa Alves Galúcio; Maria Alice Freitas Queiroz; Igor Brasil-Costa; Maria Clara Barros; Ândrea Ribeiro-dos-Santos; Antonio Carlos Rosário Vallinoto; Luiz Fábio Magno Falcão; Patrícia Danielle Lima de Lima
paper_title: Altered leukocyte pattern and inflammatory markers in unvaccinated long covid patients: a cross-sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 2,134 transgender and nonbinary people in the US examining the prevalence of long COVID (≥3 months symptom duration) and its association with gender identity and hormone therapy. Found 10% of participants with COVID-19 history reported long COVID symptoms, with higher prevalence in transmasculine and nonbinary individuals assigned female sex at birth, with no evidence of association with hormone therapy use.
paper_authors: Wirtz AL; Reisner SL; Cole SW; Adams D.; Davids JD; Cohen AK; Brown C.; Miller M.; Poteat TC
paper_title: Long COVID in transgender and gender nonbinary people in the United States

summary: This multicentric, community-based cross-sectional study assessed long-term health-related quality of life (HRQoL) among COVID-19 recovered patients in two Indian cities using the EQ-5D-5L instrument. The study found regional variation in HRQoL scores (Delhi mean 0.89 vs Bhubaneswar mean 0.66) and identified age as a significant correlate, but did not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Shubhanjali Roy; Alveena Malik; Alka Singh; Shomik Ray
paper_title: Long term health related quality of life among individuals after COVID 19 recovery in a multicentric community based study

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing COVID-19 symptoms at 12 months post-hospitalization in 486 Spanish patients, identifying neurological (46.3%) and respiratory (41.4%) symptoms as most frequent. Female sex, obesity, anxiety history, and fibromyalgia/chronic fatigue were independent risk factors for symptom presentation.
paper_authors: Ignacio Pérez Catalán; Celia Roig Martí; Sofía Folgado Escudero; Ana Segura Fábrega; María Varea Villanueva; Sergio Fabra Juana; Elena Domínguez Bajo; Germán Herrero Rodríguez; María José Esteve Gimeno; Daniela Palomo de la Sota; Alejandro Cardenal Álvarez; María Lidón Mateu Campos; Jorge Usó Blasco; Jose Manuel Ramos Rincón
paper_title: Presence of COVID-19 self-reported symptoms at 12 months in patients discharged from hospital in 2020–2021: a Spanish cross-sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the association between smoking status (combustible cigarettes, heated tobacco products, and dual use) and persistent symptoms in 5,068 participants with a history of COVID-19. Finds that smoking, particularly dual use of combustible and heated tobacco products, is associated with significantly elevated odds of arthralgia, chest pain, dyspnea, dysgeusia, and dysosmia.
paper_authors: Erika Toyokura; Kazuhiro Yamada; Kazuhisa Asai; Masaya Tsutsumi; Takahiro Ueda; Kaho Hirai; Yuichiro Furukawa; Atsushi Miyamoto; Misako Nishimura; Kanako Sato; Tetsuya Watanabe; Takahiro Tabuchi; Tomoya Kawaguchi
paper_title: Dual use of combustible and heated tobacco products associates persistent symptoms with a history of COVID-19: a JASTIS 2023 cross‑sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing the relationship between somatic symptom disorder, anxiety, depression, and daily life impairment across 371 patients with post-COVID syndrome, asthma, and COPD. Finds that SSD has greater impact on impairment in post-COVID patients than in asthma or COPD patients, with implications for rehabilitation approaches.
paper_authors: Antonius Schneider; Alexander Hapfelmeier; Anna Greißel; Matthias Limbach; Gabriele Schwarzl; Franziska Ebert; Veronika Huber; Markus C. Hayden
paper_title: The implications of somatic symptom disorder on the impairment of daily life are greater in post-COVID syndrome than in asthma or COPD - results of a cross-sectional study in a rehabilitation clinic

summary: A nationwide cross-sectional study analyzing risk factors for long COVID and its economic and mental health consequences using data from over 375,000 U.S. adults from the Household Pulse Survey. The study identifies sociodemographic predictors of long COVID and quantifies associations with unemployment, financial hardship, anxiety, and depression, estimating $211-218 billion in lost earnings.
paper_authors: Daniel Kim
paper_title: A nationwide study of risk factors for long COVID and its economic and mental health consequences in the United States

summary: A nationwide French cross-sectional survey of 1,813 adults assessing factors associated with long COVID using multiple case definitions. The study identifies demographic, medical, psychological, and social risk factors but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Joël Coste; Cyrille Delpierre; Olivier Robineau; Melissa Rushyizekera; Jean-Baptiste Richard; Caroline Alleaume; Anne Gallay; Sarah Tebeka; Olivier Steichen; Cédric Lemogne; Tatjana T. Makovski
paper_title: A multidimensional network of factors associated with long COVID in the French population

summary: This cross-sectional study compared the prevalence of post-COVID-19 conditions in 1,410 non-hospitalized COVID-19 positive patients versus 1,129 negative controls from primary care. PCC symptoms (fatigue, sleep difficulty, concentration problems) were significantly more prevalent in COVID-positive patients, though substantial symptom overlap exists with common primary care complaints.
paper_authors: Dominik J. Ose; Elena Gardner; Morgan Millar; Andrew Curtin; Jiqiang Wu; Mingyuan Zhang; Camie Schaefer; Jing Wang; Jennifer Leiser; Kirsten Stoesser; Bernadette Kiraly
paper_title: A cross-sectional and population-based study from primary care on post-COVID-19 conditions in non-hospitalized patients

summary: Cross-sectional observational study of 931 individuals (hospitalized and non-hospitalized) assessing symptoms, physical function, and mental health outcomes after COVID-19. Identifies clusters of physical and mental impairments but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Malin Nygren-Bonnier; Anna Svensson-Raskh; Linda Holmström; Anna Törnberg; Annie Svensson; Daniel Loewenstein; Malin Regardt; Mikael Björnson; Carl Hallberg; Mike Kemani; Anita Mc Allister; Joakim Körner Gustafsson; Alexandra Halvarsson; Urban Ekman; Linda Nordstrand; Susanne Guidetti; Lena Anmyr; Maria Bragesjö; Jenny Åström Reitan; Farzaneh Badinlou; Oili Dahl; Eva Åkerman; Pär Villner; Petter Brodin; Kenneth Caidahl; Marcus Ståhlberg; Artur Fedorowski; Magnus Sköld; Michael Runold; Judith Bruchfeld; Elisabeth Rydwik
paper_title: Health outcomes in hospitalised and non-hospitalised individuals after COVID-19, an observational, cross-sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of 107,249 US adults from the 2022 BRFSS examining associations between e-cigarette use and post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PCS). E-cigarette use was not significantly associated with PCS, though female gender, obesity, current smoking, and history of depression, asthma, and COPD were significant risk factors.
paper_authors: Shahryar Rajai Firouzabadi; Ida Mohammadi; Mohammadreza Alinejadfard; Arman Shafiee
paper_title: E-cigarettes are not associated with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome among US adults

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed anxiety and depression levels among healthcare workers two years post-COVID-19 infection using PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scales. While the paper includes long COVID patients (50.8% prevalence), it is a descriptive/validation study of mental health outcomes rather than a treatment intervention trial.
paper_authors: Lin Zhang; Jingli Wen; Ling Yuan; Youde Yan; Zhenjiang Zhang; Kai Li; Zuoling Tang
paper_title: Anxiety and depression in healthcare workers 2 years after COVID-19 infection and scale validation

summary: This cross-sectional survey study evaluates psychiatric symptoms and coping mechanisms in long COVID patients compared to recovered COVID-19 controls from a large international cohort. While the paper identifies associations between psychiatric outcomes and various factors, it is an observational study without any treatment or intervention tested, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: Yochai Re’em; Elisabeth A. Stelson; Hannah E. Davis; Lisa McCorkell; Hannah Wei; Gina Assaf; Athena Akrami
paper_title: Factors associated with psychiatric outcomes and coping in Long COVID

summary: This retrospective cohort study analyzes 9,666 medical rehabilitation cases for post-COVID syndrome covered by German Pension Insurance in 2021. The analysis finds that 80.7% of patients showed improvement in symptoms through rehabilitation, with 88% maintaining employment and over 90% deemed capable of working 6+ hours on the general labor market.
paper_authors: Tanja Trefzer; Silke Brüggemann; Susanne Weinbrenner; Axel Schlitt
paper_title:
Rehabilitationen bei Post-COVID-Syndrom der Deutschen
                    Rentenversicherung 2021

summary: This cross-sectional study investigates the prevalence of chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) in patients with long COVID, examining the relationship between persistent smell disorders and CRS in post-COVID populations. The paper addresses controversial findings in the literature regarding CRS prevalence among COVID-19 patients experiencing long-term sequelae.
paper_authors: Detlef Kleemann; Jörg Menschikowski; Elisabeth Wellhausen; Anselm Prechtl; Alexander Fritz; Silke Jablowski; Jördis Frommhold
paper_title: Prevalence of chronic rhinosinusitis in patients with a Long Covid course

summary: Retrospective cross-sectional analysis examining olfactory dysfunction prevalence, severity, and duration in long COVID patients across different SARS-CoV-2 variants. The study compares symptom manifestation between variants and investigates associations between risk factors and symptom presentation.
paper_authors: S Heinig; Thomas Lemcke; J Huntemann; Claus Steppert
paper_title: Retrospektive Analyse von hospitalisierten Patienten und Vergleich verschiedener SARS-CoV-2 Varianten hinsichtlich Anosmie

summary: This paper analyzes work disability claims data from German AOK insurance records to assess the prevalence and duration of Long COVID-related absences from work between 2021-2022. It is a secondary analysis of administrative claims data rather than a primary treatment trial or intervention study.
paper_title:
Lange Arbeitsunfähigkeitszeiten
                    wegen Long/Post
                    COVID

summary: This retrospective cross-sectional survey assessed the experience and satisfaction of 211 healthcare workers with post-COVID syndrome who underwent rehabilitation measures (inpatient, outpatient, or both). 65.9% of participants reported subjective symptom improvement following rehabilitation, with similar outcomes between outpatient and inpatient settings.
paper_authors: Svenja Mertens; Albert Nienhaus; Matthias Morfeld; Claudia Westermann; Uwe Koch-Gromus
paper_title:
Rehabilitationsmaßnahmen nach einer COVID-19-Erkrankung bei
                    Versicherten der Berufsgenossenschaft für Gesundheitsdienst und
                    Wohlfahrtspflege: Ergebnisse einer retrospektiven
                    Querschnittserhebung

summary: Population-based cross-sectional survey of 619 former SARS-CoV-2 infected persons in Lübeck assessing Post-COVID syndrome prevalence, symptoms, quality of life, and healthcare utilization. Found 54% self-reported PCS with significantly higher symptom burden and unmet care needs, but no intervention was tested or evaluated.
paper_authors: Mercedes Rutsch; Alexander Mischnik; Alexander Katalinic; Ruth Deck
paper_title:
Regionale Versorgungssituation und -bedarfe von ehemals
                    SARS-CoV-2-Infizierten am Beispiel der Hansestadt Lübeck – Ergebnisse einer
                    Bevölkerungsbefragung

summary: Population-based cross-sectional study of 667 participants with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection examined between November 2020 and June 2021, assessing smell dysfunction using questionnaires, visual analog scales, and objective testing with extended Sniffin' Sticks Test. The study characterizes chemosensory impairment as a persistent symptom of long COVID but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Sanja Winkelmann; Alia Korth; Bettina Voss; Nasr Maher Abou; Naomi Behrend; Annett Pudszuhn; Veit Maria Hofmann; Philipp Schendzielorz; Martin Witzenrath; Lilian Krist; Julia Fricke; Thomas Bahmer; Stefan Schreiber; Thomas Keil; Wolfgang Lieb; Jens-Peter Reese; Peter Heuschmann; Thomas Hummel; Christoph Borzikowsky; Martin Laudien
paper_title: Geruchsstörungen bei Long-COVID

summary: School health examination survey in Jena, Germany (2014/15–2022/23) assessing obesity, behavioral problems, and health behaviors in children and adolescents, including prevalence of long COVID in this population. This is an epidemiological survey with no intervention or treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: H. Beyermann; D Freesmeyer; Olivia Pfeiffer; C. Suck; A Wilberg; Volker Holzendorf
paper_title: Schuluntersuchungen in Jena – Darstellung ausgewählter Befunde und Ergebnisse von Befragungen, unter anderem zur Häufigkeit von Long COVID

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the association between body composition (fat, muscle, bone) and vertigo in 105 post-COVID-19 patients using bioimpedance analysis. Found significant associations between body composition metrics and self-reported vertigo, but did not evaluate or test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Luciana Lozza de Moraes Marchiori; Glória de Moraes Marchiori; Licia Sayuri Tanaka Okamura; Daiane Soares de Almeida Ciquinato; Braulio Henrique Magnani Branco
paper_title: An Analysis Between Body Composition and Vertigo Post-Coronavirus Disease 2019 Patients

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed health literacy and care experiences among 407 long COVID patients with neuropsychiatric symptoms using the HLS-EU-Q16 and RehaQ-N1 questionnaires. The findings show that 53.7% of patients had problematic or inadequate health literacy, with the majority having unmet care needs and 47.7% expressing dissatisfaction with their treatment.
paper_authors: Franziska Jung; Andrea Zülke; Kerstin Wirkner; Matthias Reusche; Christoph Engel; Christian Sander; Veronica Witte; Samira Zeynalova; Markus Loeffler; Arno Villringer; Dorothee Saur; Georg Schomerus; Melanie Luppa; Steffi G. Riedel-Heller
paper_title:
Gesundheitskompetenz, Anlaufstellen, ungedeckte subjektive Bedarfe und
                Behandlungszufriedenheit von Long-COVID-Betroffenen mit langanhaltender
                neuropsychiatrischer Symptomatik

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 121 Australian adults with long COVID assessing disability, function, and quality of life using standardized instruments (WHODAS 2.0 and SF-36). Study found significant functional impairment and reduced quality of life compared to population norms, with 86% reporting clinically significant disability.
paper_authors: Danielle Hitch; Tanita Botha; Fisaha Tesfay; Sara Holton; Catherine M. Said; Martin Hensher; Kieva Richards; Mary Rose Angeles; Catherine M. Bennett; Genevieve Pepin; Bodil Rasmussen; Kelli Nicola-Richmond
paper_title: Impacts of long COVID on disability, function and quality of life for adults living in Australia

summary: This case-control study compared olfactory bulb volume and olfactory sulcus depth between 41 long COVID patients (10-12 months post-infection) and 42 healthy controls, finding significantly reduced measurements in the COVID-19 group. The study is an observational comparison study without any intervention or treatment component.
paper_authors: Bünyamin Güney; Ferda Bacaksızlar Sarı; Murat Yunus Özdemir; Neşat Çullu; Emrah Doğan; Turhan Togan
paper_title: Changes in olfactory bulbus volume and olfactory sulcus depth in the chronic period after COVID-19 infection

summary: This cross-sectional study investigates correlations between post-COVID symptoms and RT-PCR cycle threshold (Ct) values, age, and hospitalization status using questionnaire data. The analysis found no significant correlations between viral load and post-COVID symptom occurrence, though there was a positive trend with advancing age.
paper_authors: Alexander Rempen; Christoph Pfeiffer; Conrad Riemann; Holger Sudhoff; Lars-Uwe Scholtz; Ingo Todt; Matthias Schürmann; Leonie Hose
paper_title: Investigation of correlations between the occurrence of symptoms of the Post-COVID syndrome after SARS-CoV-2 infection, the cycle threshold in RT-PCR, age and hospitalisation

summary: This cross-sectional study estimates the prevalence of post-COVID syndrome and its clinical spectrum among 2,070 non-severe COVID-19 patients in southern Tunisia, finding a 41.6% prevalence with ageusia, cognitive difficulties, and fatigue as most common symptoms. The paper identifies demographic and clinical factors associated with post-COVID syndrome but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Nouha Ketata; Jihen Jdidi; Hanen Maamri; Mouna Baklouti; Fadhila Issaoui; Chakroun Olfa; Jamel Damak; Sourour Yaich; Yosra Mejdoub; Rania Hammami
paper_title: Post-COVID Syndrome in Southern Tunisia: Prevalence, Clinical Spectrum, and Associated Factors Among Non-Severe Patients

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 958 Chinese college students examining the prevalence of long COVID symptoms and their association with anxiety and depression ~2-3 months post-infection. Study identifies long COVID somatic symptoms, insomnia, and fatigue as mediators between COVID-19 infection and mental health outcomes, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Yuanyuan Deng; Yifan Tong; Yao Zhang; Mingfan Liu
paper_title: The Effects of COVID-19 on Anxiety and Depressive Symptoms Among Chinese College Students: Chain Mediation of Three Long COVID-19 Symptoms

summary: This cross-sectional study of 53 long-COVID patients at a neurology clinic identifies symptom patterns using cluster analysis and examines associations with psychological health, sleep quality, and well-being. Patients with higher symptom burden (>17 symptoms) showed significantly worse depression, anxiety, sleep quality, and overall well-being outcomes.
paper_authors: Artemios Artemiadis; Andreas G. Tofarides; Andreas Liampas; Christiana Ioannou; Katerina Christodoulou; Rafaela Louka; George Vavougios; Panagiotis Zis; Panagiotis Bargiotas; Georgios Hadjigeorgiou
paper_title: Long-COVID from the perspective of neurologists at the outpatient clinic: A cross-sectional field study

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing functioning and disability in 442 post-COVID-19 patients versus 198 controls using WHODAS 2.0, 6-minute walk test, and hand grip strength assessments. Found significantly reduced functioning in PCC patients, with comorbidities, anxiety, depression, and smoking predicting worse outcomes.
paper_authors: Sanna Stålnacke; Helena Liira; Velina Vangelova-Korpinen; Hélène Virrantaus; Mari Kanerva; Kirsi Kvarnström; Markku Sainio; Antti Malmivaara; Aki Vuokko; Mikko Varonen; Mikko Venäläinen; Jari Arokoski
paper_title: Functioning of post-COVID-19 patients: a cross-sectional study at the outpatient clinic for long-term effects
paper_journal: Scandinavian Journal of Primary Health Care

summary: Cross-sectional study examining inflammatory markers (CRP, neutrophil count, fibrinogen) in 121 patients with post-COVID syndrome versus recovered controls. Found elevated biomarkers associated with PCS symptoms, particularly fatigue and sensory loss, with notable sex differences in risk profiles.
paper_authors: Meryam Maamar; Arancha Artime; Emilio Pariente; Patricia Fierro; Yolanda Ruiz; Silvia Gutiérrez; Marian Tobalina; Sara Díaz-Salazar; Carmen Ramos; José M. Olmos; José L. Hernández
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 syndrome, low-grade inflammation and inflammatory markers: a cross-sectional study

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) in 437 post-COVID-19 patients using IOM diagnostic criteria. The study found 8.1% of participants met ME/CFS criteria, with 2.8% having COVID-19-related ME/CFS and 3.7% having long COVID, demonstrating a connection between ME/CFS and post-COVID symptoms.
paper_authors: Suha AlMuhaissen; Amal Abu Libdeh; Yara ElKhatib; Rund Alshayeb; Areej Jaara; Sanaa K. Bardaweel
paper_title: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) and COVID-19: is there a connection?

summary: This cross-sectional study analyzed 2022 National Health Interview Survey data to assess long COVID prevalence and characteristics among U.S. adults with asthma. The study found that long COVID prevalence was 13.9% among adults with asthma versus 6.2% without asthma, with older age, female sex, obesity, and asthma attack history as risk factors.
paper_authors: Chun-Tse Hung; Yu-Chien Hung; Chi-Won Suk
paper_title: Prevalence and characteristics in long COVID among adults with asthma in the United States

summary: Cross-sectional community survey of 1,564 individuals examining symptoms and predictors of deteriorated quality of life associated with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC). Found that fatigue, anxiety, depression, activity intolerance, and work/school difficulties significantly predict reduced QOL in long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Judith M. Burnfield; Natalie A. Williams; Fang Yu; Jihyun Ma
paper_title: Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) Symptoms Associated with Deteriorated Quality of Life in a Community Sample of Individuals Reporting Previous SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 424 college students examining sensory and cognitive processing after COVID-19 infection. Study found associations between lingering symptoms, perceived severity, and difficulties with sleep quality, sensory processing, and cognitive function, but does not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Paige E. Hemming; Lyric S. Arvizu; Carly A. Yadon
paper_title: Sensory and cognitive experiences after COVID-19 infection in college students

summary: This cross-sectional study examines the prevalence and patterns of abnormal menstruation in women with a history of COVID-19 infection, comparing pre- and post-infection rates. While the study identifies menstrual dysfunction as a long COVID symptom, it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: Siriwan Tangjitgamol; Rapeephan R. Maude; Natapon Ativanichayapong; Rebecca Walsh; Ellen Beer; Kamonwan Kaprakhon; Chayanan Chaowanklang
paper_title: Prevalence and pattern of abnormal menstruation after COVID-19 infection

summary: This study validates a Spanish translation of the PAC-19QoL, a disease-specific quality of life questionnaire for long COVID patients, using a cross-sectional design with 206 participants. The translated instrument demonstrates high internal consistency and validity but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Irene Marcilla-Toribio; Maria Martinez-Andres; Maria Leopolda Moratalla-Cebrian; Ravi Jandhyala; Omolade Femi-Ajao; Eva Maria Galan-Moya
paper_title: Adaptation and validation of the PAC-19QoL-specific quality of life questionnaire for the Spanish population with long COVID

summary: Cross-sectional case-control study comparing cognitive and autonomic function in young adults 28 months post-COVID-19 (n=34) versus matched controls (n=34). Found subtle cognitive inefficiencies in working memory and executive function tasks but minimal overall long-term impact on cognition or autonomic regulation.
paper_authors: Gopika Gopinath; Chinmay A. Suryavanshi; Pallavi L. C.
paper_title: Long-term cognitive and autonomic effects of COVID-19 in young adults: a cross-sectional study at 28 months

summary: This cross-sectional study characterizes the epidemiology and organ-specific sequelae in 200 adult long COVID patients referred to a COVID recovery clinic in Texas. The study documents symptom burden (dyspnea, fatigue, cognitive dysfunction) and functional impairment (13% using home oxygen, 10% unable to return to work), with median time to clinic presentation of 37 days and follow-up extending to 10 months post-infection.
paper_authors: Valerie Danesh; Alejandro C. Arroliga; James A. Bourgeois; Andrew J. Widmer; Michael J. McNeal; Tresa M. McNeal
paper_title: Post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 in adults referred to COVID recovery clinic services in an integrated health system in Texas

summary: Retrospective cross-sectional study identifying risk factors for post-COVID-19 cardiovascular symptoms in 204 patients. Found anxiety, depression, elevated C-reactive protein, D-dimer, and LDL-C as independent risk factors.
paper_authors: Tingting Liu; Haofei Kang
paper_title: The risk factors for long term cardiovascular symptoms in patients after coronavirus disease 2019 infection

summary: Cross-sectional questionnaire study (N=220) comparing fatigue levels and quality-of-life between COVID-19 patients and controls using FSS and WHOQoL instruments. Found that severe subjective fatigue is associated with lower quality-of-life and occurs even in mild disease courses, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Chiara Biserni; Bob O. De Groot; Anselm B. M. Fuermaier; Dick de Waard; Stefanie Enriquez-Geppert
paper_title: Post-COVID fatigue: Reduced quality-of-life associated with clinically relevant fatigue in mild disease courses

summary: Questionnaire survey of 3,000+ Bremen residents with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, assessing post-COVID-19 condition presence at least 3 months post-infection. Found that mild COVID-19 poses risk for developing post-COVID condition, with females and those reporting fatigue, breathing difficulties, and cognitive symptoms at infection showing higher odds of later post-COVID symptoms.
paper_authors: Stefan Rach; Lisa Kühne; Hajo Zeeb; Wolfgang Ahrens; Ulrike Haug; Hermann Pohlabeln
paper_title: Mild COVID-19 infection associated with post-COVID-19 condition after 3 months – a questionnaire survey

summary: A cross-sectional study of 439 UAE women examining menstrual symptom changes after COVID-19, using online questionnaires and standardized psychological scales. Findings show increased menstrual symptoms, pad usage, bleeding days, and pain medication use in the post-COVID period, along with higher stress levels.
paper_authors: Huda Ahmad; Ahmad El Oweini; Souheil Hallit; Diana Malaeb
paper_title: Assessment of COVID-19 impact on menstrual symptom variation among women in the United Arab Emirates
paper_journal: International Journal of Environmental Health Research

summary: This cross-sectional study proposes a standardized method for using the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) to describe health status in post-acute COVID-19 syndrome patients. The study validates interrater agreement for linking ICF codes to clinical instruments and exams measuring quality of life, anxiety, depression, fatigue, and exercise capacity.
paper_authors: Ana Clara Gonçalves da Costa; Taís Ferreira Martins; Vinicius Zacarias Maldaner da Silva; Camila Ferreira Leite; Shamyr Sulyvan de Castro; Gerson Cipriano; Graziella França Bernardelli Cipriano
paper_title: Standardization use of the international classification of functioning, disability and health in the determination of health status in patients with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome

summary: This cross-sectional study compared cognitive performance and psychological symptoms in 120 long COVID patients versus recovered and never-infected controls using neuropsychological tests and self-report questionnaires. Long COVID patients showed poorer attention/working memory and higher cognitive, anxiety, and depression symptoms, but the study did not evaluate or test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Maxime Boutet; Imane Salmam; Jean-Sébastien Roy; Krista Best; Kadija Perreault; François Desmeules; Alexandre Campeau-Lecours; Simon Beaulieu-Bonneau
paper_title: Cognitive and psychological functioning in individuals with long COVID: a comparative cross-sectional study

summary: This cross-sectional survey of 1,031 adults with long COVID in Laval, Canada examined rehabilitation service utilization (PT, OT, SLP, Psychology) and identified barriers to care. Only 3-8% of participants accessed rehabilitation services, with unmet needs attributed to lack of referrals, financial barriers, and not knowing who to contact.
paper_authors: Barbara Mazer; Stephanie Haynes; Venezia Ficara; Anna Streib; Daria St-Jean; Anne-Marie Spiridigliozzi; Rosa Minichiello; Debbie Ehrmann Feldman
paper_title: Rehabilitation service utilization among individuals with long COVID in Laval, Canada

summary: Cross-sectional study of 300 participants in Pakistan examining health and psychosocial outcomes in long COVID patients (n=54). Found fatigue and muscle problems most common (14.7%), with moderate-to-severe perceived stress in most participants.
paper_authors: Madeeha Khan; Sadaf Majeed; Quratul Ain; Amjad Nawaz; Khadija Awais Sumra; Vilma Lammi; Faizan Nihal; Aleena Afrah; Ejaz Ahmed Khan; Mohammad Iqbal Khan; Fouzia Sadiq
paper_title: Long COVID in Pakistan: a cross-sectional analysis of health and psychosocial outcomes

summary: Cross-sectional survey study investigating demographic, chronic illness, and psychiatric correlates of long-COVID-19 in an urban sample of CUNY students. Found that Latinx participants, those with prior chronic illness, and those meeting criteria for probable psychiatric diagnoses had higher odds of long-COVID-19.
paper_authors: Talia Schulder; Sasha Rudenstine; Catherine K. Ettman; Sandro Galea
paper_title: Correlates of long-COVID-19: the role of demographics, chronic illness, and psychiatric diagnosis in an urban sample

summary: This cross-sectional study examined how long COVID affects performance of activities of daily living (ADL) in 30 participants in a municipality-based rehabilitation program. Participants reported decreased quality of performance in both personal and instrumental ADL tasks, with fatigue showing a moderate correlation with ADL ability.
paper_authors: Rina Juel Kaptain; Karina Ethelberg Bach Jensen; Kristina Tomra Nielsen; Eva Ejlersen Wæhrens
paper_title: Activities of daily living following Long COVID: An exploratory cross-sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional survey of U.S. adults examining self-management practices for persistent COVID-19 symptoms using alcohol, marijuana, and prescription medications. Found that adults with symptoms persisting 13+ weeks had significantly higher rates of substance use for symptom management compared to those with shorter symptom duration.
paper_authors: Philip T. Veliz; Weijiao Zhou; Sheree Smith; Janet L. Larson
paper_title: Substance Use and the Self-Management of Persistent Symptoms of COVID-19

summary: Cross-sectional study measuring depression prevalence in COVID-19 survivors in Colombia using PHQ-9 screening. Nearly 50% of survivors scored above depression cut-off, with associations to female gender, younger age, and severity of acute infection.
paper_authors: Carmen Cecilia Caballero-Domínguez; John Carlos Pedrozo-Pupo; Adalberto Campo-Arias
paper_title: Depression among COVID-19 survivors in Colombia

summary: A cross-national survey of 34 European countries examining Long COVID definitions and diagnostic criteria used in clinical practice. Unresolved long COVID patients reported significantly greater impairment across all four health domains, while short COVID patients reported the least challenges.
paper_authors: Christopher Kricorian
paper_title: P-1910. Long COVID Resolution Status and Health Impacts

summary: This cross-sectional analysis of the US Census Bureau's Household Pulse Survey (N=68,544) examines the relationship between long COVID and mental health outcomes as measured by the PHQ-4. The study found that long COVID patients report significantly higher rates of anxiety, depression, anhedonia, and hopelessness compared to those with short COVID or no COVID history.
paper_authors: Christopher Kricorian
paper_title: P-1908. The Relationship Between Long COVID and PHQ-4 Measures of Emotional Health

summary: Cross-sectional study of 203 Mexican patients with persistent COVID assessing cardiovascular manifestations using PASC score ≥12 as diagnostic criterion. Found high prevalence of cardiovascular symptoms (82.8%), with palpitations, tachycardia, and chest pain most common; symptoms more frequent in women and associated with multiple COVID-19 infections and severe initial disease.
paper_authors: Luis Del Carpio-Orantes; Daniela Trelles-Hernández; Sergio García-Méndez; Mayra Evelyn Quiñones-Martínez
paper_title: P-1643. Cardiovascular Manifestations of Persistent COVID in Mexico

summary: Cross-sectional pilot study comparing cognitive performance and quality-of-life outcomes in 132 long COVID patients (mean 2.4 years post-infection) versus 42 controls. While long COVID participants reported significantly worse self-perceived cognitive function and quality of life, objective neurocognitive testing showed no significant differences between groups.
paper_authors: Kristen Kehl-Floberg; Fauzia Hollnagel; Emily Danzl; Dorothy Farrar-Edwards; Aurora Pop-Vicas
paper_title: P-1652. Cognitive performance long after COVID infection: results of a cross-sectional pilot study

summary: This cross-sectional study compared immunologic biomarker patterns across 78 participants with PASC (with and without MECFS) and post-COVID-19 vaccination syndrome, analyzing abnormalities in cytokines, T cells, and autoantibodies. The study found high anti-HSP-70 antibody positivity in all groups and elevated autoimmunity markers in the PVS group, but is limited by small sample size and lack of control group.

paper_title: P-1662. Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19 and Post-COVID-19 Vaccination Syndrome: A Comparison of Clinical Immune Biomarkers

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System data examining long COVID prevalence and associated factors among US adults. Finds 7.2% overall prevalence with higher rates in women, middle-aged individuals, those with lower socioeconomic status, and various comorbidities; vaccination associated with lower rates.
paper_authors: Juanjuan Shi; Rui Lu; Yan Tian; Fengping Wu; Xiaozhen Geng; Song Zhai; Xiaoli Jia; Shuangsuo Dang; Wenjun Wang
paper_title: P-1669. Prevalence of and Factors Associated with Long COVID among US Adults: A Nationwide Survey

summary: A cross-sectional study comparing mast cell activation patterns in blood and terminal ileum tissue of 21 long COVID patients versus 11 controls at 2 years post-infection. Findings show elevated mast cell activation, tryptase, zonulin, and tissue-resident spike protein in long COVID patients, suggesting ongoing immune activation and intestinal damage.

paper_title: P-1978. Long-Term Mast Cell Activation Patterns in Systemic and Tissue-Resident Compartments Following COVID-19: Insights from a 2-Year Post-Infection Study

summary: This cross-sectional analysis of US Census Bureau Household Pulse Survey data (N=68,544) compares social connectedness metrics between long COVID, resolved COVID, and non-COVID populations. While confirming that long COVID patients report significantly lower social connectedness and emotional support than comparison groups, the study does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Christopher Kricorian
paper_title: P-1909. Social Connectedness in the COVID-19 Pandemic’s Aftermath: The Influence of Disease Status

summary: An observational cross-sectional study measuring fatigue severity and postexertional malaise in 213 long COVID patients using validated questionnaires. The study found that 71.4% experienced chronic fatigue and 58.7% met PEM thresholds, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Twomey R.; DeMars J.; Franklin K.; Culos-Reed SN; Weatherald J.; Wrightson JG
paper_title: Chronic Fatigue and Postexertional Malaise in People Living With Long COVID: An Observational Study

summary: Cross-sectional study of 1,031 post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) patients examining prevalence and associations of mobility and balance decline. Found 44.9% had reduced mobility and 37.1% had balance deterioration, associated with older age, hospitalization, comorbidities, and obesity, which correlated with functional impairment in daily activities.
paper_authors: Debbie Ehrmann Feldman; Albert Guillemette; Juliana Sanzari; Stéphane Youkheang; Barbara Mazer
paper_title: Decline in Mobility and Balance in Persons With Post–COVID-19 Condition

summary: This is a retrospective cross-sectional analysis from the RECOVER cohort characterizing physical function impairment (30-second sit-to-stand test) in adults with and without prior SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study found minimal clinically meaningful differences in physical function between groups, suggesting individual responses to interventions may be more relevant than group-level comparisons.

paper_title: Physical Function Differences by COVID-19 Status: A Cross-sectional Analysis From the RECOVER Adult Cohort

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing prevalence and risk factors of suicidal ideation among 1,297 COVID-19 survivors in Wuhan, China. Found 6.7% reported suicidal ideation, with fatigue, stigma, and sleep disorder as positive risk factors, while marriage and peace of mind were protective.

paper_title: Suicidal ideation and associated risk factors among COVID-19 patients who recovered from the first wave of the pandemic in Wuhan, China

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the association between food insecurity and long COVID prevalence in 956 Brazilian adults from the PAMPA cohort. Found that food insecurity was associated with increased probability of long COVID and specific symptom domains (neurological, pulmonary, gastrointestinal).

paper_title: Association between food insecurity and long COVID in adults from southern Brazil: findings of the PAMPA cohort

summary: This cross-sectional study examined the prevalence of cardiac arrhythmias in 100 patients 1-6 months post-COVID-19 recovery. Findings showed 17% developed arrhythmias, with inappropriate sinus tachycardia most common (7%), and associations between absolute lymphopenia during acute infection and arrhythmia prevalence.
paper_authors: Ahmed Mahmoud; Mohamed Amin; Emad Effat; Lamyaa Allam
paper_title: Prevalence of cardiac ARRHYTHMIAs in patients recovering from COVID-19
paper_journal: QJM: An International Journal of Medicine

summary: This case-control study assessed conjunctival surface changes in post-COVID patients using impression cytology, comparing 32 post-COVID cases with 32 controls. The study found no statistically significant inflammatory or neoplastic changes in the conjunctiva between groups, except for lymphocyte infiltration.
paper_authors: Marwa Mohamed Asaad; Momen Mahmoud Hamdi; Fatma S. Hafez; Radwa Mohamed Nabil
paper_title: Assessment of Conjunctival Surface Changes in Post COVID Patients by Impression Cytology
paper_journal: QJM: An International Journal of Medicine

summary: Retrospective survey of 139 COVID-19 patients at 3 months post-infection assessing prevalence of pulmonary and extrapulmonary long COVID symptoms. Study documents symptom frequencies across multiple organ systems (respiratory, cardiac, neurological, psychological, gastrointestinal) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Hazem Hosni Elsayed Hammam; Yasser Moustafa Mohamed; Mahmoud Mokhtar Mohamed
paper_title: Pulmonary and Extra-Pulmonary Persistent COVID-19 sequalae
paper_journal: QJM: An International Journal of Medicine

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 400+ New Giza University staff assessing long COVID prevalence and identifying predictors of post-COVID symptoms. Found higher BMI, middle age, and male gender (for sleep disturbance) associated with increased long COVID symptom occurrence, but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Habiba Mahmoud AboAmra; Yasser Mostafa; Ahmed Mohamed AbdElSamad
paper_title: Predictors of Long COVID Syndrome: A Self-Reported Survey in New Giza University Staff
paper_journal: QJM: An International Journal of Medicine

summary: Cross-sectional study examining sleep disturbances and associated PASC symptoms in 494 patients from the ReCOVER cohort using sleep studies and PROMIS-Sleep Disturbance assessments. Found that lower REM sleep percentage and specific PASC symptoms (dyspnea, joint pain, headaches) are associated with greater sleep disruption, but no treatment intervention was evaluated.
paper_authors: Zahra Zia; Yadi Li; Brittany Lapin; Reena Mehra
paper_title: 1134 Post-acute Sequelae SARS CoV-2 Related Sleep Study and Symptom-based Factors Associated with Sleep Disturbances

summary: This cross-sectional study compared physical function outcomes in 10 idiopathic inflammatory myopathy (IIM) patients versus 40 healthy controls at 30 days post-COVID-19 infection. While IIM patients showed greater deterioration in physical function and higher fatigue compared to controls, this is an observational study without treatment intervention and should be excluded as it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention for long COVID.
paper_authors: Rajat Kharbanda; Keya Ganatra; Vikas Agarwal; Latika Gupta
paper_title: P070 Patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathies suffer from poor self-reported PROMIS physical function after COVID-19 infection: an interview-based study from the MyoCite cohort

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 90 COVID-19 patients (assessed 308+ days post-infection) examining sleep characteristics and their association with acute COVID-19 severity. Found that COVID-19 severity (hospitalization, oxygen therapy, ventilation) significantly predicted poor sleep quality and daytime sleepiness, though effect sizes were small.
paper_authors: An-Yun Yeh; Ying-Yu Chao; Shiela Strauss
paper_title: 1139 The Association Between Sleep and Coronavirus disease-19 Severity

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of 26,260 US adults from the 2022 National Health Interview Survey examining the relationship between COVID-19 status and sleep outcomes. Long COVID was associated with significantly shorter sleep duration (0.3 hours less per night) and poorer sleep quality compared to those without COVID-19.
paper_authors: Ali Aalam; Xiaobei Chen; Hannah Jury; Muhammad Ali Syed; Catalina Quintero
paper_title: 1404 Examining the Relationship Between Sleep and COVID-19 Status in a US National Sample

summary: Cross-sectional study examining B-cell subpopulations in 30 pediatric patients 6 months after COVID-19 recovery, including 6 MIS-C cases. Found normal CD19 and B-cell counts post-recovery with no significant variations between different COVID-19 presentations.
paper_authors: Hanan M. Ibrahim; Dalia H. ElGhoneimy; Nesrine Radwan; Shereen M. Reda; Mohamed T. Hamza; Suzan H. Refaey
paper_title: Evaluation of B-Cell Repertoire Among Recovered COVID-19 Pediatric Patients
paper_journal: QJM: An International Journal of Medicine

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing nitric oxide-dependent cutaneous vasodilation in adults recovered from COVID-19 versus healthy controls, with assessment of physical activity status. Found no significant differences in NO-mediated vasodilation or microvascular function between groups, and no correlation with symptom severity or physical activity levels.
paper_authors: Gabrielle A. Dillon; Faith A. Swanger; S. T. Wolf; Lacy M. Alexander
paper_title: Nitric Oxide‐dependent Cutaneous Vasodilation is not Altered in Adults Following SARS‐CoV‐2 Infection

summary: The COVAD study surveyed 1,677 respondents (45% with autoimmune rheumatic diseases, 12.5% with non-rheumatic autoimmune diseases, 42.5% healthy controls) >90 days post-COVID to assess long COVID prevalence and risk factors. Individuals with autoimmune rheumatic diseases had higher long COVID prevalence (10.8% vs 5.3% in controls), with comorbidities, advanced treatment, and ICU admission emerging as significant risk factors.

paper_title: P065 Post COVID-19 Syndrome in patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases: Results from the COVID-19 Vaccination in Autoimmune Diseases (COVAD) study

summary: Retrospective cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of sleep disorders in 250 pediatric long COVID patients and their association with comorbid conditions and symptoms. Finds that 26% of youth with long COVID have sleep disturbances, which correlate with worse well-being, fatigue, anxiety, and depression.
paper_authors: Shikha Mistry; Samuel Rodgers-Melnick; Jennifer Murphy; David Miller; Amy Edwards; Sally Ibrahim
paper_title: 1136 Sleep Disorders in Children and Adolescents with Long COVID

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between low HDL levels and inflammatory markers in long COVID patients undergoing hemodialysis one year post-infection. Found that long COVID patients had significantly lower HDL and elevated inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-17, CRP), with pronounced inflammation in those with concurrent low HDL.

summary: Cross-sectional study of 80 long COVID patients examining GPCR autoantibodies and their relationship to vascular dysfunction, endothelial function, and inflammation. Found that GPCR antibodies are present in 65% of long COVID patients and correlate with vascular parameters like blood pressure and FMD, but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Felix Seibert; Lea Wiemers; Ulrik Stervbo; Oliver Sander; Maximilian Seidel; Sebastian Bertram; Nina Babel; Timm Westhoff
paper_title: G-PROTEIN-COUPLED RECEPTORS ANTIBODIES HAVE SUBSTANTIAL VASOREGULATIVE IMPLICATIONS IN LONG-COVID

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the association between pre-infection blood pressure control, serum IL-17 levels, and long-COVID sequelae in hemodialysis patients. While the paper studies long COVID outcomes, it is an observational analysis of existing patient cohorts without any intervention or treatment being tested, making it ineligible for a treatment trials meta-analysis.

paper_title: UNCONTROLLED BLOOD PRESSURE BEFORE COVID-19 IS ASSOCIATED WITH ELEVATED SERUM IL-17 AND LONG-COVID SEQUELAE IN HEMODIALYSIS PATIENTS

summary: This cross-sectional survey describes the structure, operations, and assessment practices of 39 post-ICU and post-COVID recovery clinics across 29 U.S. health systems. summary: This large-scale Japanese internet survey (n=32,000) examined the overlap between chronic pain and long COVID-like symptoms, finding that chronic pain is independently associated with symptom burden regardless of COVID-19 history. The study found that long COVID affects work attendance and disability risk, particularly in patients with comorbid mental health, cardiovascular, malignancy, metabolic, and musculoskeletal conditions, but does not evaluate any treatment interventions.

summary: Secondary analysis comparing self-reported functional disability in people with long COVID and myalgic encephalomyelitis, both characterized by post-exertional neuroimmune exhaustion (PENE). Found few significant differences between groups in functional burden, suggesting similar impacts across conditions regardless of precipitating event.
paper_authors: Katie Graves; Todd E. Davenport; Staci Stevens; Jared Stevens; J. Mark Van Ness
paper_title: Self-Reported Disablement in People Living With Long Covid and Myalgic Encephalomyelitis: A Cross-Sectional Comparative Study

summary: Self-reported survey of 420 COVID-19 patients examining prevalence and severity of hair loss after infection, finding that 77.6% reported hair loss with onset typically within 3 weeks and resolution within 1 year. paper_title: Psychological General Well-being, Cognitive Failure, and Inflammation Biomarkers Among Workers 4 Months After a Mild/Asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: A cross-sectional study comparing clinical characteristics in 150 pediatric post-COVID-19 patients versus 55 noninfected controls. paper_title: Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes of Long COVID-19 Hospitalized Children in Vietnam

summary: Cross-sectional survey of employed COVID-19 survivors in British Columbia assessing work productivity loss using the Valuation of Lost Productivity questionnaire. paper_title: Association Between Postacute Sequelae of COVID-19 Infection and Work Environment in a Semiconductor Packaging Plant in Taiwan

summary: Secondary data analysis examining correlates of mental health and employment in individuals with long COVID using cross-sectional data from 1901 participants. paper_authors: Kenneth O. Anujuo; Peter O. Ikuabe; Ikenna D. Ebuenyi
paper_title: Exploring Correlates of Mental Health and Employment in Individuals With Long COVID

summary: This cross-sectional study characterized cognitive and psychosocial symptoms in 52 COVID-19 survivors 4 months post-illness using cognitive testing batteries and surveys. The study is excluded because it is purely observational without any treatment intervention—it only describes symptom prevalence and correlations, not treatment outcomes.
paper_authors: Ashley M. Henneghan; Kimberly A. Lewis; Eliana Gill; Oscar Y. Franco-Rocha; Ruben D. Vela; Sarah Medick; Shelli R. Kesler
paper_title: Describing cognitive function and psychosocial outcomes of COVID-19 survivors: A cross-sectional analysis

summary: International cross-sectional study using questionnaires to assess long-term symptoms of COVID-19 and prevalence of myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome in recovered patients. Examines persistent symptoms occurring weeks to months post-infection across a large global cohort.

paper_title: Long-term sequelae of COVID-19 (myalgic encephalomyelitis): An international cross-sectional study
