summary: Cross-sectional study of 457 long COVID patients examining prevalence of neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disturbances, and sexual dysfunction in a psychiatry unit. Found females 4.8× more likely to experience neuropsychiatric symptoms than males, with age inversely associated with symptom likelihood.
paper_authors: Sana A. Khan; Rabeeah Ashkar; Sona Kumari; Raja R. Khenhrani; Shafqat Ullah; Rahimeen Rajpar; Hareem Arshad; Johum Aziz Haque; Kiran Abbas; Javeria Khan; Bipin Poudel; Sushmita Bhandari; Moiz Ahmed; Jawed A. Dars
paper_title: Long COVID syndrome: psychological and sexual dysfunction among survivors of COVID-19 infection

summary: Cross-sectional study of 285 COVID-19 survivors examining long-term cognitive impairment ('brain fog') and associated psychosocial factors. Found 6.3% prevalence of moderate/severe cognitive impairment, with associations to sex, sleep quality, perceived severity, mental distress, and social discrimination.
paper_authors: Wen Dang; Wenjing Li; Haotian Liu; Chunyang Li; Tingxi Zhu; Lin Bai; Runnan Yang; Jingyi Wang; Xiao Liao; Bo Liu; Simai Zhang; Minlan Yuan; Wei Zhang
paper_title: Psychosocial Factors Associated With Long-Term Cognitive Impairment Among COVID-19 Survivors

summary: Cross-sectional observational study documenting persistent symptoms in 156 long COVID patients at a median of 351 days post-infection, measuring impacts on physical function, cognition, and quality of life. Study characterizes symptom prevalence and triggers but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Laura Tabacof; Jenna Tosto-Mancuso; Jamie Wood; Mar Cortes; Amy Kontorovich; Dayna McCarthy; Dahlia Rizk; Gabriela Rozanski; Erica Breyman; Leila Nasr; Christopher Kellner; Joseph E. Herrera; David Putrino
paper_title: Post-acute COVID-19 Syndrome Negatively Impacts Physical Function, Cognitive Function, Health-Related Quality of Life, and Participation
paper_journal: American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation

summary: This cross-sectional study describes a clinical evaluation protocol (combining clinical assessment, ultrasound, and robotic testing) in 74 post-COVID patients with fatigue and neurological deficits. The paper reports the protocol and diagnostic findings (41% sarcopenia prevalence, multisensory integration deficits) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Antonella LoMauro; Fabrizio Gervasoni; Vincenzo Ricci; Gregorio Salce; Arnaldo Andreoli; Leonardo Pantoni; Levent Özçakar
paper_title: Sarcopenia and Multisensory Integration Deficit in Post-COVID Syndrome Patients
paper_journal: American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing COVID-19 symptoms and post-COVID conditions between vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals in Pakistan (n=250). Finds that vaccination reduces symptom duration, symptom variety, and post-COVID condition prevalence, but does not test any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Asad Rahman; Muhammad T. Ikram; Amina Arif; Bakht D. Khan; Kamal U. Azam; Muhammad Sanaan Fida; Adam K. Rahim; Muhammad S. Khan; Muhammad H. Mushtaq; Raiyan Fida; Hamza Yunus; Mohammad D. Khan
paper_title: Prevalence and difference of COVID-19 symptoms, post-COVID conditions and duration of illness among the vaccinated and unvaccinated population: a cross-sectional study in Peshawar

summary: This study examines fibrinolytic system parameters in donor groups stratified by anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG titers to investigate potential mechanisms of post-COVID-19 coagulopathy. The authors found significant changes in fibrinolytic parameters (plasminogen, tPA, PAI-1, inhibitory factors) across different IgG titer groups, suggesting anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG may influence coagulation dysfunction in long COVID.
paper_authors: Antonina Rachkovska; Daryna Krenytska; Vitalii Karbovskyy; Nataliia Raksha; Tetiana Halenova; Tetiana Vovk; Olexii Savchuk; Liudmyla Ostapchenko
paper_title: A study of fibrinolytic system components in donor groups depending on various titers of circulating anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG in the bloodstream

summary: Cross-sectional study of 69 hospitalized post-COVID-19 patients examining predictors of functional status using muscle strength, functional capacity, and quality-of-life assessments. Found that functional mobility, muscle quality, length of stay, and female sex are independent predictors of post-COVID functional status, but no intervention or treatment was provided.
paper_authors: Tamires Daros dos Santos; Juliana Alves Souza; Dannuey Machado Cardoso; Viviane Bohrer Berni; Adriane Schmidt Pasqualoto; Isabella Martins de Albuquerque
paper_title: Predictors of Post–COVID-19 Functional Status Scale in Hospitalized Patients Recovering From SARS-CoV-2 Infection
paper_journal: American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation

summary: Observational cross-sectional study comparing sleep quality, fatigue, and pain between post-COVID-19 patients (n=201) and controls (n=206) using validated questionnaires. Found significantly worse sleep quality and higher fatigue in long COVID patients, with strong positive correlations between sleep quality and fatigue severity.
paper_authors: Srutarshi Ghosh; Anjani Kumar; Sanjay Kumar Pandey; Sanyal Kumar
paper_title: Association of Sleep Quality With Fatigue in Post–COVID-19 Patients in an Indian Population
paper_journal: American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluated post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) symptoms among 93 solid organ transplant recipients who had COVID-19 during the Omicron period. Female sex, longer time since transplantation, and receipt of tixagevimab-cilgavimab prophylaxis were associated with lower odds of developing PASC symptoms.
paper_authors: Leela Morená; Ayman Al Jurdi; Christopher El Mouhayyar; Rucháma Verhoeff; Nora Alzahrani; Camille N. Kotton; Leonardo V. Riella
paper_title: Post–acute Sequelae of COVID-19 Among Solid Organ Transplant Recipients: Insights From the Omicron Period

summary: This cross-sectional study surveyed 2,764 adults ≥12 weeks post-COVID to identify demographic and clinical factors associated with functional changes in long COVID. The analysis found that prior hospitalization, longer time since infection, comorbidities, and obesity were significantly associated with functional decline including fatigue, reduced mobility, and decreased participation in daily activities.
paper_authors: Barbara Mazer; Debbie Ehrmann Feldman
paper_title: Demographic and Clinical Factors Associated With Functional Changes in Long-Covid
paper_journal: American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation

summary: This cross-sectional study of 1,218 long COVID patients identified four distinct psychological symptom clusters using cluster analysis, finding that anxiety, depression, and somatoform symptoms significantly impact mental health outcomes. The authors conclude that tailored psychological interventions targeting specific symptom clusters may improve both mental and physical outcomes in long COVID.
paper_authors: Raquel Gómez Bravo; Alexandre Infanti; Joël Billieux; Mark Ritzen; Sandra Nischwitz; Angelika Erhardt; Thérèse Staub; Christian G. Huber; Undine Lang; Steffi Weidt; Kira Wolff; Juliane Müller; Claus Vögele; Charles Benoy
paper_title: Unmasking the Psychological Landscape of Long COVID: A Cluster-analytical Approach

summary: This study analyzed self-reported long COVID symptoms from Twitter users, identifying 89 individuals who shared data about their experiences. The most common symptoms reported were fatigue, shortness of breath, pain, and brain fog, typically occurring in an episodic pattern.
paper_authors: Shubh Mohan Singh; Chaitanya Reddy
paper_title: An Analysis of Self-reported Longcovid Symptoms on Twitter

summary: This cross-sectional study uses quantitative chest CT and machine learning to identify imaging phenotypes in 257 long COVID survivors 6-12 months post-hospitalization. The analysis identified four distinct clusters including a small airways disease phenotype with characteristic pulmonary function abnormalities, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Rodrigo Caruso Chate; Carlos Roberto Ribeiro Carvalho; Marcio Valente Yamada Sawamura; João Marcos Salge; Eduardo Kaiser Ururahy Nunes Fonseca; Paula Terra Martins Almeida Amaral; Celina de Almeida Lamas; Luis Augusto Visani de Luna; Fernando Uliana Kay; Antonildes Nascimento Assunção Junior; Cesar Higa Nomura
paper_title: Quantitative Chest Computed Tomography and Machine Learning for Subphenotyping Small Airways Disease in Long COVID

summary: This retrospective cross-sectional study characterizes post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PACS) in 84 patients from Mount Sinai's recovery program, documenting persistent symptoms at mean 151 days post-infection including fatigue (92%), cognitive impairment (74%), and weakness (68%). The study is descriptive and does not evaluate any treatment intervention, focusing instead on symptom prevalence and impact on quality of life.
paper_authors: Laura Tabacof; Jenna Tosto-Mancuso; Jamie Wood; Mar Cortes; Amy Kontorovich; Dayna McCarthy; Dahlia Rizk; Nicki Mohammadi; Erica Breyman; Leila Nasr; Christopher Kellner; David Putrino
paper_title: Post-acute COVID-19 syndrome negatively impacts health and wellbeing despite less severe acute infection

summary: This cross-sectional study rapidly enrolled 246 racially and ethnically diverse individuals at least 3 months post-COVID to characterize the prevalence and patterns of persistent symptoms (PASC). The study found that 26% had not recovered to baseline health, with fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, and sensory disturbances being most common; older age and hospitalization were protective factors for recovery.
paper_authors: Robin J. Mermelstein; Meenakshy Aiyer; Christine Canfield; David Chestek; Judith A. Cook; Marina Del Rios; Kathleen R. Diviak; Angela M. Ellison; Howard S. Gordon; Sai Dheeraj Illendula; Manasa Kandula; Jonathan D. Klein; Karen Larimer; James Lash; Janet Lin; Jeffrey A. Loeb; Teresa J. Lynch; Hugh Musick; Richard M. Novak; Heather M. Prendergast; Jerry A. Krishnan
paper_title: Rapid implementation of cross-sectional study: Post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC) in a racially and ethnically diverse sample in Illinois

summary: Cross-sectional study using PROMIS surveys to characterize persistent symptoms in post-COVID syndrome patients, measuring fatigue, sleep, pain, physical functioning, and social roles. Findings show significant deficits in social roles and elevated fatigue and pain scores in a predominantly female cohort.
paper_authors: Ravindra Ganesh; Aditya K. Ghosh; Mark A. Nyman; Ivana T. Croghan; Stephanie L. Grach; Christopher V. Anstine; Ryan T. Hurt
paper_title: PROMIS scales for assessment of the impact of post-COVID syndrome: A Cross Sectional Study

summary: Retrospective questionnaire study of COVID-19 infection and post-COVID complications among 271 healthcare workers at a cancer centre. Documents that 51.8% experienced post-COVID syndrome with effects on QOL and productivity, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Atika Dogra; Anuj Parkash; Anurag Mehta; Meenu Bhatia
paper_title: Impact of COVID-19 on healthcare workers at a cancer care centre

summary: A cross-sectional study analyzing cell-mediated immune responses in 74 long COVID patients, measuring T cell and NK cell responses to SARS-CoV-2 via flow cytometry. The study found that 96% of patients showed specific cellular immunity despite negative serology, with abnormal immune cell populations suggesting immune dysregulation as a potential mechanism in long COVID pathogenesis.
paper_authors: Nerea Montes; Èlia Domènech; Sílvia Guerrero; Bárbara Oliván-Blázquez; Rosa Magallón-Botaya
paper_title: Analysis of cell-mediated immunity in people with long COVID

summary: Observational cross-sectional online survey measuring chronic fatigue and post-exertional malaise severity in 213 long COVID patients using validated questionnaires (FACIT-F, DePaul). Found 71.4% experienced clinically relevant chronic fatigue and 58.7% met myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome thresholds for PEM, with significant impacts on physical activity and social functioning.
paper_authors: Rosie Twomey; Jessica DeMars; Kelli Franklin; S. Nicole Culos-Reed; Jason Weatherald; James G. Wrightson
paper_title: Chronic fatigue and post-exertional malaise in people living with long COVID

summary: Community-based cross-sectional survey of 508,707 people in England examining the prevalence and characteristics of persistent symptoms 12+ weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Study identifies risk factors (age, sex, obesity, hospitalization, deprivation) and symptom clusters but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Matthew Whitaker; Joshua Elliott; Marc Chadeau-Hyam; Steven Riley; Ara Darzi; Graham Cooke; Helen Ward; Paul Elliott
paper_title: Persistent symptoms following SARS-CoV-2 infection in a random community sample of 508,707 people

summary: Cross-sectional questionnaire survey of 457 COVID-19 patients identifying risk factors for long COVID development and persistence. Finds that women, younger age, and low BMI are risk factors for symptom development, with 26.3% reporting symptoms at 6 months and 8.8% at 12 months.
paper_authors: Yusuke Miyazato; Shinya Tsuzuki; Shinichiro Morioka; Mari Terda; Satoshi Kutsuna; Sho Saito; Yumiko Shimanishi; Kozue Takahashi; Mio Sanada; Masako Akashi; Chika Kuge; Yasuyo Osanai; Keiko Tanaka; Michiyo Suzuki; Kayoko Hayakawa; Norio Ohmagari
paper_title: Risk factors associated with development and persistence of long COVID

summary: Secondary analysis of the Covid Infection Survey estimating the prevalence of disabling long COVID (symptoms >12 weeks with activity limitation) in UK population aged <35 years. Reports approximately 39,000 cases of disabling long COVID seeded by confirmed infections through July 2021, highlighting the burden in younger populations.
paper_authors: Nicola Spiers
paper_title: Quantifying the ongoing epidemic of disability after covid-19 in the UK population aged under 35 years; secondary analysis of the Covid Infection Survey

summary: Cross-sectional study describing persistent symptoms (dyspnea, fatigue, chest pain) in 602 long COVID patients from a Brazilian post-COVID health center, stratified by acute disease severity. Documents symptom burden, quality-of-life impacts, and laboratory abnormalities (elevated HbA1c, CRP, anemia) with higher symptom prevalence in women.
paper_authors: Ana Paula Andrade Barreto; Lucimeire Cardoso Duarte; Thiago Cerqueira-Silva; Marcio Andrade Barreto Filho; Aquiles Camelier; Natalia Machado Tavares; Manoel Barral-Netto; Viviane Boaventura; Marcelo Chalhoub Coelho Lima
paper_title: Post-Acute COVID Syndrome, the Aftermath of Mild to Severe COVID-19 in Brazilian Patients

summary: Cross-sectional study examining associations between cardiopulmonary symptoms in post-acute phase SARS-CoV-2 infection and echocardiographic findings, cardiac biomarkers, and inflammatory markers in 102 participants. Found female sex, prior hospitalization, SARS-CoV-2 antibodies, and C-reactive protein associated with cardiopulmonary symptoms, with pericardial effusions noted in symptomatic cases.
paper_authors: Matthew S. Durstenfeld; Michael J. Peluso; J. Daniel Kelly; Sithu Win; Shreya Swaminathan; Danny Li; Victor M. Arechiga; Victor Zepeda; Kaiwen Sun; Shirley Shao; Christopher Hill; Mireya I. Arreguin; Scott Lu; Rebecca Hoh; Viva Tai; Ahmed Chenna; Brandon C. Yee; John W. Winslow; Christos J. Petropoulos; John Kornak; Timothy J. Henrich; Jeffrey N. Martin; Steven G. Deeks; Priscilla Y. Hsue
paper_title: Role of antibodies, inflammatory markers, and echocardiographic findings in post-acute cardiopulmonary symptoms after SARS-CoV-2 infection

summary: This cross-sectional observational study investigates orthostatic intolerance in 85 adults with long COVID using active stand and tilt testing. The study characterizes the relationship between orthostatic symptoms and hemodynamic responses, finding that POTS is infrequent despite initial orthostatic heart rate differences.
paper_authors: Ann Monaghan; Glenn Jennings; Feng Xue; Lisa Byrne; Eoin Duggan; Roman Romero-Ortuno
paper_title: Orthostatic intolerance in adults with long COVID was not associated with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing cognitive performance on standardized tests between 282 post-COVID patients and 52 healthy controls, finding significant deficits in delayed memory, attention, and executive function. No treatment or intervention is tested; this is a descriptive/observational assessment of cognitive dysfunction and its relationships with clinical variables.
paper_authors: Valeska Kozik; Philipp A. Reuken; Isabelle Utech; Judith Gramlich; Zoe Stallmach; Nele Demeyere; Florian Rakers; M. Schwab; Andreas Stallmach; Kathrin Finke
paper_title: Subtle cognitive impairments in memory, attention, and executive functioning in patients with post-COVID syndrome and their relationships with clinical variables and subjective complaints

summary: Cross-sectional study examining cardiac-related post-acute sequelae symptoms in 442 community-dwelling adults after COVID-19 infection. Found 43% reported persistent cardiac symptoms and identified cardiovascular risk factors, pre-existing conditions, and hospitalization as key risk factors for cardiac PASC.
paper_authors: Oluwabunmi Ogungbe; Nisha A. Gilotra; Patricia M. Davidson; Jason E. Farley; Cheryl R. Dennison Himmelfarb; Wendy S. Post; Yvonne Commodore-Mensah
paper_title: Cardiac Post-acute Sequelae symptoms of SARS-CoV-2 in Community-Dwelling Adults: Cross-sectional Study

summary: Secondary analysis of the SAPRIS-SERO cohort examining persistent symptoms in relation to SARS-CoV-2 seropositivity and self-reported COVID-19 infection in 26,823 French individuals. Identifies three potential long COVID sub-syndromes (anosmia, respiratory symptoms, and fatigue-related symptoms) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Nicola Spiers
paper_title: Reassessment of persistent symptoms, self-reported COVID-19 infection and SARS-CoV-2 serology in the SAPRIS-SERO cohort: identifying possible sub-syndromes of Long Covid

summary: Population-representative survey of 3,042 US adults estimating long COVID prevalence at 7.3% (~18.5 million adults) and characterizing impact by demographics, comorbidities, and vaccination status. Findings show higher prevalence among females, those with comorbidities, and unvaccinated individuals, with 25% reporting substantial impact on daily activities.
paper_authors: McKaylee M. Robertson; Saba A. Qasmieh; Sarah G. Kulkarni; Chloe A. Teasdale; Heidi Jones; Margaret McNairy; Luisa N. Borrell; Denis Nash
paper_title: The epidemiology of long COVID in US adults two years after the start of the US SARS-CoV-2 pandemic

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing long COVID symptom reporting between vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals infected with SARS-CoV-2 between March 2020 and November 2021. Finds that vaccination with two doses was associated with substantially reduced reporting of common post-acute symptoms.
paper_authors: Paul Kuodi; Yanay Gorelik; Hiba Zayyad; Ofir Wertheim; Karine Beiruti Wiegler; Kamal Abu Jabal; Amiel A. Dror; Saleh Nazzal; Daniel Glikman; Michael Edelstein
paper_title: Association between vaccination status and reported incidence of post-acute COVID-19 symptoms in Israel: a cross-sectional study of patients tested between March 2020 and November 2021

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of 15,307 survey respondents examining associations between long COVID symptoms and employment status. Long COVID was associated with higher unemployment rates and lower likelihood of full-time work, with cognitive symptoms showing stronger associations with reduced employment.
paper_authors: Roy H. Perlis; Kristin Lunz Trujillo; Alauna Safarpour; Mauricio Santillana; Katherine Ognyanova; James Druckman; David Lazer
paper_title: Research Letter: Association between long COVID symptoms and employment status
paper_journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

summary: Cross-sectional baseline analysis of a US cohort study examining physical and mental disability in long-COVID patients (n=7,926) compared to recovered and never-infected controls. Finds 65% of long-COVID participants have at least one disability, with dizziness, heavy limbs, and dyspnea strongly associated with disability burden.
paper_authors: Bryan Lau; Eryka Wentz; Zhanmo Ni; Karine Yenokyan; Candelaria Coggiano; Shruti H. Mehta; Priya Duggal
paper_title: Physical and mental health disability associated with long-COVID: Baseline results from a US nationwide cohort
paper_journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

summary: Population-based cross-sectional analysis of 201,799 UK participants examining socioeconomic inequalities in Long COVID prevalence. Found that participants in the most deprived areas had higher Long COVID risk (11.4% vs 8.2%), with larger disparities in females and healthcare/education workers.
paper_authors: Sharmin Shabnam; Cameron Razieh; Hajira Dambha-Miller; Tom Yates; Clare Gillies; Yogini V. Chudasama; Manish Pareek; Amitava Banerjee; Ichiro Kawachi; Ben Lacey; Eva JA Morris; Martin White; Francesco Zaccardi; Kamlesh Khunti; Nazrul Islam
paper_title: Socioeconomic inequalities of Long COVID: findings from a population-based survey in the United Kingdom

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 231 long COVID patients at 12-month follow-up describing symptom course, daily life impact, and factors associated with symptom relief. Found that most symptoms persisted (83% asthenia, 92% neurocognitive/neurological), only 8.7% achieved complete remission, and pre-vaccination SARS-CoV-2 antibodies were associated with better improvement while persistent ageusia predicted worse outcomes.
paper_authors: Dominique Salmon; Dorsaf Slama; Françoise Linard; Nicolas Dumesges; Valérie Lebaut; Florence Hakim; Pauline Oustric; Emilie Seyrat; Patricia Thoreux; Esaie Marshall
paper_title: Factors associated with release relief of Long COVID symptoms at 12-Months and their impact on daily life

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 732 COVID-19 survivors in Malaysia examining depression prevalence and associated factors using the PHQ-9 instrument. Found 47.3% had mild to severe depression, with female sex, younger age, overweight/obesity, having long COVID, and poor self-perceived health as significant associated factors.
paper_authors: Foong Ming Moy; Eugene Ri Jian Lim; Noran Naqiah Hairi; Awang Bulgiba
paper_title: Depression and its associated factors among COVID-19 survivors in a middle income country

summary: This is a large US population-based cross-sectional analysis of 153,543 adults examining sociodemographic predictors and socioeconomic/mental health consequences of long COVID. While the paper provides important epidemiological data on long COVID burden and risk factors, it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention—it is purely observational and descriptive.
paper_authors: Daniel Kim
paper_title: Who Gets Long COVID and Suffers its Mental Health and Socioeconomic Consequences in the United States? Preliminary Findings from a Large Nationwide Study

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 108 Greek workers with post-COVID-19 syndrome examining impacts on daily life and work productivity, with analysis of resilience and social support as protective factors. Finds that 68.5% report great impact on daily life and 56.5% report great impact on work productivity, with dysautonomia and symptom duration as key predictive factors.
paper_authors: Petros Galanis; Aglaia Katsiroumpa; Irene Vraka; Katerina Kosiara; Olga Siskou; Olympia Konstantakopoulou; Theodoros Katsoulas; Parisis Gallos; Daphne Kaitelidou
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 syndrome and related dysautonomia affect patients’ life and work productivity

summary: A cross-sectional study assessing the psychosocial and health impacts of long COVID in 300 Pakistani participants, of whom 54 had persistent symptoms beyond 12 weeks. The study found high rates of fatigue, breathing problems, and cognitive issues, with moderate to severe stress levels in a majority of participants.
paper_authors: Madeeha Khan; Sadaf Majeed; Qura Tul Ain; Amjad Nawaz; Khadija Awais Sumra; Vilma Lammi; Faizan Nihal; Aleena Afrah; Ejaz Ahmed Khan; Mohammad Iqbal Khan; Fouzia Sadiq
paper_title: Analysing the psychosocial and health impacts of Long COVID in Pakistan: A cross sectional study

summary: A cross-sectional pilot study examining serum biomarkers in long COVID patients with neuro-cognitive symptoms to identify clinically meaningful subgroups for precision medicine. The study identified three major PASC subgroups based on biomarker profiles (HERV-W ENV, neurofilaments, IL-6) but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Benjamin Charvet; Alexandre Lucas; Justine Pierquin; Joanna Brunel; Steven Fried; Corinne Bernis; Zachary S. Orban; Millenia Jimenez; Barbara A. Hanson; Lavanya Visvabharathy; Igor J. Koralnik; Hervé Perron
paper_title: Blood biomarkers-defined subgroups show heterogeneity in post-acute COVID-19 syndrome: a rationale for precision medicine

summary: This nationally representative survey of 24,434 Mexican adults characterizes the prevalence and determinants of long COVID (PASC) in 2022, finding 21.21% prevalence among previously diagnosed COVID-19 cases with musculoskeletal pain, headache, and brain fog as most common symptoms. The study identifies reinfections, depressive symptoms, and social lag as risk factors, while vaccination and Omicron variant infections were associated with lower prevalence.
paper_authors: Omar Yaxmehen Bello-Chavolla; Carlos A. Fermín-Martínez; Luisa Fernández-Chirino; Daniel Ramírez-García; Arsenio Vargas-Vázquez; Martín Roberto Basile-Alvarez; Paulina Sánchez Castro; Alejandra Núñez-Luna; Neftali Eduardo Antonio-Villa
paper_title: Nationally representative prevalence and determinants of post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (Long COVID) amongst Mexican adults in 2022

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 24,803 U.S. adults examining the association between obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC). OSA was associated with increased odds of PASC-related symptoms, with the association mitigated in those with treated OSA.
paper_authors: Stuart F. Quan; Matthew D. Weaver; Mark É. Czeisler; Laura K. Barger; Lauren A. Booker; Mark E. Howard; Melinda L. Jackson; Rashon I. Lane; Christine F. McDonald; Anna Ridgers; Rebecca Robbins; Prerna Varma; Joshua F. Wiley; Shantha M.W. Rajaratnam; Charles A. Czeisler
paper_title: Association of Obstructive Sleep Apnea with Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC)
paper_journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

summary: The PRIME post-COVID study assessed the prevalence of long-term symptoms in COVID-19 tested adults using six different case definitions, comparing positively and negatively tested individuals. Prevalence ranged from 26.9-64.1% in positive cases and 11.4-32.5% in negative controls, highlighting significant variation depending on which definition is applied.
paper_authors: Demi ME Pagen; Céline JA van Bilsen; Stephanie Brinkhues; Maarten Van Herck; Kevin Konings; Casper DJ den Heijer; Henriëtte LG ter Waarbeek; Martijn A. Spruit; Christian JPA Hoebe; Nicole HTM Dukers-Muijrers
paper_title: Prevalence of long-term symptoms varies by using different post-COVID-19 definitions in positively and negatively tested adults: the PRIME post-COVID study

summary: Population-based cross-sectional survey of 385,617 US adults using the 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System to estimate COVID-19 and long COVID prevalence by state and demographic characteristics. Found 7.4% of all adults reported long COVID (21.9% of those with prior COVID), with fatigue, shortness of breath, and taste/smell loss being most common reported symptoms.
paper_authors: Mary L. Adams; Joseph Grandpre
paper_title: Prevalence of COVID-19 and long COVID - Results from the 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System, 50 states

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence of long COVID symptoms among 330 children aged 5-12 in Duhok, Iraq, using IgG serology and symptom interviews. Found 4.6% (14 children) reported long COVID symptoms lasting >4 weeks, with fatigue, cough, and post-exertional malaise most common.
paper_authors: Rojeen Chalabi Khalid; Tamara Bassam Jamal; Sara Ardalan Mahdi; Abdullah Saeed Mustafa
paper_title: Prevalence of long covid-19 among pediatric age group in Duhok city, Kurdistan region, Iraq

summary: This case-control study compares serum levels of galanin, its receptor (GalR1), electrolytes, and inflammatory markers in 90 long-COVID patients versus 60 recovered controls. The study identifies galanin and GalR1 as potential biomarkers for long-COVID disease but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Wasim Talib Mahdi Al Masoodi; Sami Waheed Radhi; Habiba Khdair Abdalsada; Hussein Kadhem Al-Hakeim
paper_title: Correlation between Galanin and its receptor with the serum electrolytes in Long-COVID patients

summary: This study estimates the disability burden of Long COVID in US adults using cross-sectional survey data from 2022-2023, calculating Years of Life with Disability (YLDs) and comparing NIH funding allocation relative to disease burden. It finds that Long COVID affects ~1.5% of respondents with substantial disability impact, particularly in women, but receives disproportionately low NIH research funding relative to its burden.
paper_authors: Karen Bonuck; Qi Gao; Seth Congdon; Ryung Kim
paper_title: Long COVID Disability Burden in US Adults: YLDs and NIH Funding Relative to Other Conditions

summary: This study analyzes data from two nationally representative U.S. surveys (BRFSS and NHIS) to identify demographic and clinical risk factors associated with long COVID. The analysis finds that middle age, female gender, Hispanic ethnicity, lower education, and initial infection severity are associated with higher long COVID risk.
paper_authors: Yixuan Wu; Mitsuaki Sawano; Yilun Wu; Rishi M. Shah; Pamela Bishop; Akiko Iwasaki; Harlan M. Krumholz
paper_title: Risk factors for experiencing Long-COVID symptoms: Insights from two nationally representative surveys

summary: Cross-sectional immune-endocrine profiling study of 165 individuals with and without long COVID comparing sex differences in symptom manifestations and immune characteristics. Found distinct immunological patterns and symptom burdens between males and females with long COVID, with testosterone levels inversely associated with symptom severity.
paper_authors: Julio Silva; Takehiro Takahashi; Jamie Wood; Peiwen Lu; Alexandra Tabachnikova; Jeff R. Gehlhausen; Kerrie Greene; Bornali Bhattacharjee; Valter Silva Monteiro; Carolina Lucas; Rahul M. Dhodapkar; Laura Tabacof; Mario Peña-Hernandez; Kathy Kamath; Tianyang Mao; Dayna Mccarthy; Ruslan Medzhitov; David van Dijk; Harlan M. Krumholz; Leying Guan; David Putrino; Akiko Iwasaki
paper_title: Sex differences in symptomatology and immune profiles of Long COVID
paper_journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

summary: This paper uses 2022 BRFSS survey data to compare the prevalence and correlates of cognitive impairment and long COVID across 50 US states. It is a secondary analysis of existing survey data without testing any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Mary Adams; Joseph Grandpre
paper_title: Similarities between long COVID and cognitive impairment and potential implications; Results from the 2022 BRFSS

summary: This cross-sectional study of 24,803 U.S. adults examines associations between pre-existing sleep issues (insomnia, poor sleep quality, short sleep duration) and the prevalence of post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) using three different case definitions. The study finds that insomnia, poor sleep quality, and short sleep duration are associated with increased PASC prevalence, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment—only identifies sleep problems as potential risk factors for PASC development.
paper_authors: Stuart F. Quan; Matthew D. Weaver; Mark É. Czeisler; Laura K. Barger; Lauren A. Booker; Mark E. Howard; Melinda L. Jackson; Rashon I. Lane; Christine F. McDonald; Anna Ridgers; Rebecca Robbins; Prerna Varma; Joshua F. Wiley; Shantha M.W. Rajaratnam; Charles A. Czeisler
paper_title: Sleep and long COVID: Preexisting sleep issues and the risk of PASC in a large general population using 3 different model definitions
paper_journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

summary: This cross-sectional analysis compares health outcomes and risk factors among 385,617 adults from the 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System, stratifying by long COVID status, positive COVID test only, and no prior infection. The study found that 48.3% had long COVID, sleep problems were reported by 41.2%, and individuals with sleep problems had significantly higher prevalence of altered sensitivity, nasal congestion, musculoskeletal symptoms, respiratory issues, and overall long COVID symptoms.

paper_title: Assessment of Level of Depression and Associated Factors among COVID-19-Recovered Patients: a Cross-Sectional Study

summary: This cross-sectional survey assessed Long COVID prevalence among healthcare workers in two Singapore tertiary hospitals and its impact on work-role functioning using the WRFQv2.0 instrument. While the study found 47.5% Long COVID prevalence with significant work functioning impairment, it is excluded because it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment or intervention—it is purely observational/epidemiological.
paper_authors: Zeenathnisa Mougammadou Aribou; Alvin Kian Wei Tan; See Ming Lim; John Wah Lim; Wee Hoe Gan; Wee Tong Ng; David Soo Quee Koh
paper_title: Assessing the impact of Long COVID on healthcare workers’ work – role functioning in tertiary hospitals in Singapore
paper_journal: WORK: A Journal of Prevention, Assessment & Rehabilitation

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 2,764 COVID-19 positive residents in Quebec comparing employment status changes between those with long COVID and those who recovered, identifying clinical and demographic factors associated with decreased employment. Finds that long COVID patients are significantly more likely to experience employment decrease (15.6% vs 5.4%), particularly those with moderate-to-severe health decline, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Farah Jaber; Marie-An Hoang; Debbie Ehrmann Feldman; Sara Saunders; Barbara Mazer
paper_title: Factors associated with changes in employment in individuals with long COVID
paper_journal: WORK: A Journal of Prevention, Assessment & Rehabilitation

summary: A cross-sectional study examining the relationship between resilience and health-related quality of life in 97 post-COVID-19 patients, with and without lingering symptoms. The study found that approximately 35% of post-COVID patients had low resilience levels, and that age and depression significantly impacted resilience, but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Víctor Fernández-Alonso; Sara Rodríguez-Fernández; Laura Secadas-Rincón; Manuela Pérez-Gómez; María Nieves Moro-Tejedor; Magdalena Salcedo
paper_title: Resilience After COVID-19: A Descriptive, Cross-Sectional Study

summary: A cross-sectional survey study of 3,094 adults from a virtual COVID-19 clinic identifying risk factors for post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC). The study found that severe acute COVID-19 symptoms, female gender, hospitalization, psychological repercussions, and prolonged recovery time were associated with PASC development, but conducted no intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Bala Munipalli; Yaohua Ma; Zhuo Li; Ravindra Ganesh; Dacre Knight; Ilana I. Logvinov; Stefan N. Paul; Troy R. Delaney; Abd Moain Abu Dabrh
paper_title: Risk factors for post-acute sequelae of COVID-19: Survey results from a tertiary care hospital

summary: This cross-sectional survey (N=605) uses the Health Belief Model to examine how awareness and understanding of long COVID shape COVID-19 preventive behavior intentions among U.S. adults. The study finds that perceived susceptibility to long COVID and self-efficacy predict intent to adopt preventive behaviors like masking and booster vaccination, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention for long COVID.
paper_authors: Jeanine P.D. Guidry; Linnea I. Laestadius; Candace W. Burton; Paul B. Perrin; Carrie A. Miller; Melissa D. Pinto; Michael P. Stevens; Thomas Chelimsky; Raouf Gharbo; Gary S. Cuddeback; Kellie E. Carlyle
paper_title: Staying Safe for the Long Haul: A Health Belief Model Analysis of COVID-19 Preventive Behaviors Through the Lens of Long COVID

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 308 COVID-19 infected individuals in Iran examining associations between clinical/sociodemographic factors and long COVID symptoms. Identifies females, educated persons, reinfection history, underlying diseases, and COVID severity as risk factors for long COVID but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Zohreh Mahmoodi; Giti Bahrami; Ehsan Shahrestanaki; Hamed Seddighi; Nooshin Ghavidel
paper_title: Clinical and Socio-Demographic Variables Associated With Long COVID-19: A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: A cross-sectional study of 490 long COVID patients examining the relationship between long COVID symptoms and mental health outcomes (anxiety, depression, suicidal ideation). Finds that 30% screened positive for depression, 46% for anxiety, and that female sex and symptom burden are associated with increased psychiatric risk.
paper_authors: Neslihan Özçelik; Songül Özyurt; Elvan Şentürk Topaloğlu; Aziz Gümüş; Çiçek Hocaoğlu; Ünal Şahin
paper_title: Long COVID: A risk factor for anxiety, depression, and suicidality?

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 491 adults with post-COVID-19 symptoms that uses exploratory factor analysis to identify symptom clusters across different timeframes (5-8 weeks vs 9+ weeks). The study identifies six coherent symptom clusters including respiratory, cognitive, cardiac, and mental health domains, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Janet L. Larson; Weijiao Zhou; Philip T. Veliz; Sheree Smith
paper_title: Symptom Clusters in Adults with Post-COVID-19: A Cross-Sectional Survey

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluated perception of verticality in 60 post-COVID-19 patients (24 hospitalized, 36 non-hospitalized) using subjective visual vertical and subjective haptic vertical tests. The study found that hospitalized patients with post-COVID-19 showed significantly less accurate visual and haptic verticality perception compared to non-hospitalized patients, correlating with infection severity.
paper_authors: Bruno Henrique de Souza Fonseca; Pedro Henrique Sousa de Andrade; Maria Eduarda Salum Aveiro Henrique; Jussara Almeida de Oliveira Baggio; Rodrigo Bazan; Luciane Aparecida Pascucci Sande de Souza; Gustavo José Luvizutto
paper_title: Perception of verticality in the post-COVID-19 condition correlates to infection severity
paper_journal: Journal of Central Nervous System Disease

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 1,644 Swedish young adults examining the prevalence and characteristics of long-term COVID-19 symptoms (≥4 weeks) from August-November 2020. Long-term symptoms occurred in 10.8% of those with suspected COVID-19 and were associated with pre-existing conditions like rhinitis, migraine, and lower self-rated health.
paper_authors: Sandra Ekström; Niklas Andersson; Alexandra Lövquist; André Lauber; Antonios Georgelis; Inger Kull; Erik Melén; Anna Bergström
paper_title: COVID-19 among young adults in Sweden: self-reported long-term symptoms and associated factors

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 1,912 Chinese college students assessing physical and mental health symptoms 3 months after COVID-19 recovery. Identifies three clusters of symptom severity through latent class analysis but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Yue-yang Wu; Na Wang; Qian Tang; Wen-bin Shen; Wei Xiao; Jian-wei Li; Fen Huang
paper_title: The Physical Condition and Mental Health of Chinese College Students 3 Months After COVID-19 Recovery

summary: This cross-sectional survey of 201 German adults with long COVID examined how self-compassion and self-coldness mediate the effects of stigma on well-being and flourishing. While the study identifies psychological mechanisms and suggests interventions, it is observational without any treatment intervention being tested or evaluated.
paper_authors: Maor Shani; Kilian Wübbelt
paper_title: Coping with long-COVID stigma: The role of self-compassion and self-coldness

summary: This cross-sectional study examines associations between lifestyle factors (physical activity, substance use, diet) and psychiatric symptoms (depression, anxiety, PTSD) in 730 COVID-19 survivors at 6-11 months post-hospitalization. While the paper addresses long COVID sequelae, it is observational and does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Borges, Sophia Aguiar Monteiro; Roncete, Guilherme Pimenta; Amendola, Felipe Couto; Zanetti, Marcus Vinicius; Miguel, Euripedes Constantino; Filho, Geraldo Busatto; Forlenza, Orestes V.; Damiano, Rodolfo Furlan; Hcfmusp Covid-19 Study Group
paper_title: Exploring the Relationship Between Lifestyle and Post-COVID Psychiatric Symptoms: Findings from a Brazilian Cohort

summary: This cross-sectional study compares psychological distress (anxiety and depression) in 220 long COVID patients with persistent olfactory dysfunction (>6 months duration) versus 102 asymptomatic controls. The study found significantly higher rates of depression and anxiety in the OD group, with severity correlating with olfactory and nasal symptom severity, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Manon Louvrier; Sven Saussez; Jerome R. Lechien
paper_title: Psychological Distress in Patients with Long-lasting COVID-19 Olfactory Dysfunction
paper_journal: Journal of Otolaryngology - Head & Neck Surgery

summary: This cross-sectional study surveyed 342 post-COVID-19 patients to evaluate acceptance of eHealth interventions for symptom management using the UTAUT model. Findings showed moderate-to-high acceptance, with higher acceptance in patients with lower education, moderate-to-severe initial infection, ongoing impairment, and comorbid mental illness.
paper_authors: Julia Schröder; Alexander Bäuerle; Lisa Maria Jahre; Eva-Maria Skoda; Mark Stettner; Christoph Kleinschnitz; Martin Teufel; Hannah Dinse
paper_title: Acceptance, drivers, and barriers to use eHealth interventions in patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome for management of post-COVID-19 symptoms: a cross-sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 213 COVID-19 survivors in Saudi Arabia conducted ≥3 months post-infection to characterize persistent symptoms and risk factors for delayed return to baseline health. Found 51.2% had residual symptoms (fatigue, anosmia, muscle aches most common) and 71.4% reported return to baseline, with chronic comorbidities as a significant predictor of delayed recovery.
paper_authors: Hend M. Alkwai; Amany M. Khalifa; Ahmed M. Ahmed; Alfatih M. Alnajib; Khaznah A. Alshammari; Muslima M. Alrashidi; Hussain G. Ahmed
paper_title: Persistence of COVID-19 symptoms beyond 3 months and the delayed return to the usual state of health in Saudi Arabia: A cross-sectional study

summary: A cross-sectional survey assessing sleep disturbance prevalence among 312 PASC clinic patients using the PROMIS-Sleep Disturbance framework. Found 41% with no sleep disturbance, 51.3% with mild-to-moderate disturbance, and 7.7% with severe disturbance, with modest negative correlation to time since initial COVID infection.
paper_authors: Mantavya Punj; Michael Schwartz; Anjali Morris; Joseph Cheung; Bala Munipalli
paper_title: A Survey of Sleep Quality From a Post-COVID Clinic
paper_journal: Journal of Primary Care & Community Health

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 1,108 primary care patients assessing prevalence and predictors of post-acute COVID-19 symptoms in an Italian population. Found 29% prevalence with fatigue, memory, and concentration impairment as most common symptoms; identified female sex, age >50, BMI >25, and autoimmune disease as significant risk factors.
paper_authors: Andreana Foresta; Luisa Ojeda-Fernández; Claudia Augurio; Cecilia Guanziroli; Mauro Tettamanti; Giulia Macaluso; Paolo Lauriola; Alessandro Nobili; Maria Carla Roncaglioni; Marta Baviera
paper_title: Prevalence and Predictors of Post-Acute COVID-19 Symptoms in Italian Primary Care Patients
paper_journal: Journal of Primary Care & Community Health

summary: This cross-sectional study examined functional cognition and health in 118 community-dwelling adults, comparing 25 with prior COVID-19 infection to uninfected controls. No significant differences were found between infected and uninfected groups, though men showed better functional cognition and health measures than women overall.
paper_authors: Naomi Josman; Yael Atiya; Tal Dagan; Elizabeth Issa; Naor Demeter
paper_title: Assessing Functional Cognition and Health During COVID-19 Pandemic: Gender Differences Among Community-Dwelling Adults
paper_journal: Journal of Primary Care & Community Health

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 536 long COVID clinic patients assessing symptom improvement and perceived helpfulness of various interventions including medications, supplements, and neuromodulation. Patients reported significant symptom improvement from baseline, with low-dose naltrexone (58%), vagal nerve stimulation (53%), and fisetin (64%) rated as most helpful, though complete recovery remained low at 23 months post-infection.
paper_authors: Ryan T. Hurt; Siddhant Yadav; Darrell R. Schroeder; Ivana T. Croghan; Michael R. Mueller; Stephanie L. Grach; Christopher A. Aakre; Elizabeth A. Gilman; Christopher R. Stephenson; Joshua Overgaard; Nerissa M. Collins; Donna K. Lawson; Ann M. Thompson; Lasonya T. Natividad; Osman Mohamed Elfadil; Ravindra Ganesh
paper_title: Longitudinal Progression of Patients with Long COVID Treated in a Post-COVID Clinic: A Cross-Sectional Survey
paper_journal: Journal of Primary Care & Community Health

summary: A cross-sectional study assessing health-related quality of life among 271 COVID-19 survivors in Nepal using the WHOQOL-BREF questionnaire. The study identifies employment, exercise, and family structure as positive factors for QoL, while chronic disease is a significant barrier to well-being.
paper_authors: Bhawana Dhakal; Dhurba Khatri; Shishir Paudel; Dipendra Kumar Yadav; Yamuna Chhetri; Shushil Tripathee; Bhakta Bahadur KC
paper_title: Health-related quality of life among COVID-19 survivors in Pokhara Metropolitan, Nepal: A cross-sectional study

summary: This cross-sectional analysis uses Household Pulse Survey data to examine associations between race, socioeconomic status, and long COVID prevalence in the U.S. The study finds that socioeconomic status buffers racial disparities in long COVID risk, with larger protective effects among White individuals than racial/ethnic minorities.
paper_authors: Patricia Louie; Cary Wu
paper_title: Race, Socioeconomic Status, and Long COVID

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 167 airline crew members examining factors affecting quality of life, including post-COVID-19 syndrome prevalence (4.2%) and its impact across physical, psychological, social, and environmental domains. Found significant differences in QoL scores based on age, job role, years of service, and post-COVID-19 syndrome status, but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Jung-Ha Kim; Seunghye Choi
paper_title: Effects of Post-COVID-19 Syndrome on Quality of Life Among Airline Crew

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 845 COVID-19 survivors examining predictors of persistent long COVID symptoms at 1 year post-infection. Identifies female sex, higher income, and greater acute symptom burden as risk factors for symptom persistence.
paper_authors: Adam F. Aldhawyan; Mohammed A. BuSaad; Bothayna A. Alamri; Mohammed I. Alsaihati; Bader S. Alanazi; Rawan A. alanazi; Ahmed S. Bahamdan
paper_title: Evaluating the Predictors of Persistent Long COVID Symptoms and Their Severity in COVID-19 Survivors 1 Year After Infection
paper_journal: Journal of Primary Care & Community Health

summary: This retrospective cross-sectional study assessed symptom experiences and perceived health status in 86 individuals with long COVID in Thailand using telephone interviews and standardized screening. The study found that 75.6% of participants experienced long COVID with multiple symptoms lasting a median of 5.6 months, with significant correlations between symptom severity and negative health perception, but it does not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Bangern Pumipak; Sirinapha Jittimanee; Sirima Thananun; Kaewjai Mathong; Jomtien Poungdok; Manthana Sinsap; Thatsanee Sueathong; Oranong Kongruang; Sujitraporn Faungprachakorn; Thunyarut Thunyaphun; Poramate Insook; Kaewalee Soontornmon
paper_title: Symptom Experience and Perceived Health Status of People With Long COVID in Thailand

summary: Cross-sectional study of 251 mild COVID-19 patients assessing the prevalence and symptom spectrum of long COVID-19 (defined as symptoms persisting >28 days) and its impact on quality of life. Found 28.2% prevalence of long COVID-19 with musculoskeletal and respiratory symptoms most common, and significantly worse fatigue and quality of life scores compared to patients without long COVID-19.
paper_authors: Radhika Sarda; Arvind Kumar; Ankit Chandra; Megha Bir; Sanchit Kumar; Manish Soneja; Sanjeev Sinha; Naveet Wig
paper_title: Prevalence of Long COVID-19 and its Impact on Quality of Life Among Outpatients With Mild COVID-19 Disease at Tertiary Care Center in North India

summary: A cross-sectional study assessing the correlation between vitamin D levels and anosmia (loss of smell) in 143 patients attending a post-acute COVID syndrome clinic. The study found an association between anosmia and vitamin D deficiency in patients under 65 years, but this pattern did not hold in older age groups.
paper_authors: Andrew O’Connor; Carol Buckley; M Griffin; A Basirat; J Olaniyi; M Monaghan; S Donnelly; P Mitchell
paper_title: Correlation between vitamin D and anosmia in post acute Covid syndrome clinic
paper_journal: 01.01 - Clinical problems - no related to asthma or COPD

summary: This cross-sectional study compared carotid intima-media thickness between 47 recovered severe COVID-19 patients (3-6 months post-hospitalization) and 42 healthy controls using Doppler sonography. The study found significantly lower cIMT in recovered COVID-19 patients compared to controls, suggesting endothelial dysfunction may not be the primary driver of post-COVID vascular complications.
paper_authors: Hosna Yahyaei Ferizhendi; Hamid Dahmardeh; Abolfazl Parsi-Moud
paper_title: The Status of Intima-Media Thickness of Bilateral Carotid Arteries in the Postinfection Phase of SARS-CoV-2

summary: An exploratory cross-sectional study evaluating long-term home oxygen therapy (LTOT) as a strategy to reduce hospitalization time in COVID-19 patients with persistent hypoxemia. Most patients did not need to maintain LTOT beyond 15 days post-discharge, suggesting it is effective as a temporary intervention for both ICU and ward patients.
paper_authors: Davi Barbosa Pereira da Silva; R Prudente; E Franco; V Marcondes; Késsila Pietrzack de Oliveira; L Machado; Luis Fernando Pereira Brizola; M Santos; E Savadkouhi; C Colombo; Angélica María Moreno Peralta; S Tanni
paper_title: Long-term home oxygen therapy as a strategy to reduce hospitalization time in patients affected by COVID-19 with persistent hypoxemia
paper_journal: 01.01 - Clinical problems - no related to asthma or COPD

summary: A cross-sectional study of 1,124 non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients describing the clinical profile and prevalence of persistent symptoms >4 weeks post-infection. Found that 76.6% reported persistent symptoms, with cognitive disorders and asthenia being the most common complaints, showing gradual improvement over 12+ months.
paper_authors: Amany Touil; E Nemsi; S Maazaoui; T Znegui; M Chaabane; S Maddeh; S Habibech; H Racil; N Chaouch
paper_title: Lingering COVID-19 symptoms in non-hospitalized (NH) patients: Results from a Tunisian prospective cohort

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 90 patients in Agadir describing taste and smell disorders during and after acute COVID-19, documenting prevalence and recovery patterns. While the study addresses post-acute COVID symptoms, it is descriptive/observational without testing any specific intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: A. Khannous; F. Bounoua; H. Moubachir; H. Serhane
paper_title: Taste and smell disorders during and post-acute Covid-19 in the population of Agadir

summary: This cross-sectional observational study examines the relationship between prior traumatic stress history and autonomic symptom burden in 404 US adults with and without COVID-19 infection. The study finds that prior traumatic stress positively moderates the association between COVID-19 history and autonomic dysregulation, but is a passive observational survey without any intervention or treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Rebecca C. Hendrickson; Christine S. Cheah; Marlene L. Tai; Kathleen F. Pagulayan; Katharine J. Liang; Catherine A. McCall; Abigail G. Schindler; Kimberly L. Hart; Aaron F. Rosser; John C. Oakley
paper_title: Impact of Prior History of Traumatic Stress on Autonomic and Multi-System Symptoms Following COVID-19 Infection

summary: Cross-sectional study of 121 long COVID patients examining headache characteristics pre- and post-infection, comparing changes in frequency, severity, and analgesic use. Found that pre-existing headaches worsened significantly post-COVID while new-onset headaches were common and typically resolved within one month.
paper_authors: Jasem Youssef Al-Hashel; Fathi Abokalawa; Maram Alenzi; Raed Alroughani; Samar Farouk Ahmed
paper_title: Coronavirus disease-19 and headache; impact on pre-existing and characteristics of de novo: a cross-sectional study
paper_journal: The Journal of Headache and Pain

summary: This paper maps rehabilitation provision for UK patients after COVID-19 hospitalization as part of the PHOSP-COVID study. It is a survey/mapping study of existing rehabilitation services rather than a treatment trial, and does not evaluate outcomes of a specific intervention.
paper_authors: Sarah Ward; C Overton; Archie Walters; A Ibbetson; S Singh; R Evans; A Briggs; L Houchen-Wolloff
paper_title: Mapping UK rehabilitation provision for adults after hospital admission with COVID-19

summary: Observational cross-sectional study characterizing clinical profile and symptoms in 89 long-COVID patients via internet survey using the C19-YRS screening tool. Found significant impairments in dyspnea, fatigue, pain, psychological distress, and quality of life, plus additional sequelae including throat sensitivity, swallowing problems, and cognitive issues.
paper_authors: L Lopez Lopez; Irene Cabrera‐Martos; I Torres Sánchez; J Martín Núñez; Alejandro Heredia‐Ciuró; M C Valenza
paper_title: Clinical profile, symptomatology and sequelae of long-COVID patients

summary: Cross-sectional study of 276 long COVID patients in Indonesia treated with inhaled long-acting bronchodilators and corticosteroids (LABACS) over 3 months, assessing symptoms, respiratory function, and imaging. Treatment with all three LABACS regimens showed significant improvements in lung obstruction, spirometry measurements, mMRC scores, and chest X-ray findings.
paper_authors: Retno Ariza Soemarwoto; Pralia Winda Sari; J Oktabiannobel; Dian Ekawati; ANSE DIANA MESSAH; Arif Setyo Wibowo; I Darmajati
paper_title: The Role of Labacs in Long COVID-19 Patients in Pringsewu, Indonesia

summary: This cross-sectional study examined dyspnoea quality, mental health symptoms, and exercise responses in 49 COVID-19 survivors 4 months post-illness, comparing those with and without persistent dyspnoea. The dyspnoea group showed greater anxiety, depression, post-traumatic stress symptoms, ventilatory inefficiency, and deconditioning, suggesting persistent dyspnoea post-COVID-19 is linked to abnormal pulmonary gas exchange and psychological burden.
paper_authors: Kathryn M. Milne; Juthaporn Cowan; Michele R. Schaeffer; Nha Voduc; Vicente Corrales-Medina; Kim L. Lavoie; Julio A. Chirinos; Joseph H. Puyat; Sara J. Abdallah; Jordan A. Guenette
paper_title: Exercise responses and mental health symptoms in COVID-19 survivors with dyspnoea

summary: A cross-sectional study examining associations between long COVID, physical activity level, functional decline, and health-related quality of life in 121 older adults (age 60-90) at 6 months post-infection. Found that fatigue, pain, low physical activity, and cognitive-communication problems were significant predictors of reduced physical and mental health-related quality of life.
paper_authors: Sanaz Shanbehzadeh; Nasibeh Zanjari; Marzieh Yassin; Zeynab Yassin; Mahnaz Tavahomi
paper_title: Association between long COVID, functional activity, and health-related quality of life in older adults

summary: Cross-sectional study of 421 Latin American participants characterizing new daily persistent headache (NDPH) after SARS-CoV-2 infection and identifying associated risk factors. Finds 25% of persistent headache cases meet NDPH criteria, with occipital location, burning character, and palpebral edema during acute infection as significant risk factors.

paper_title: New daily persistent headache after SARS-CoV-2 infection in Latin America: a cross-sectional study

summary: This cross-sectional study followed 1,806 COVID-19 patients infected with omicron variant three months post-discharge to identify factors associated with long COVID development. The analysis found female sex, allergy history, and higher vaccination doses as risk factors, with persistent fatigue, amnesia, and insomnia being the most common long COVID symptoms.
