paper_title: Analysis of influencing factors on long COVID in COVID-19 patients infected with omicron variant three months after discharge: a cross-sectional study

summary: This study uses repeated surveys from the COVID-19 Schools Infection Survey to describe the weighted prevalence of post-COVID-19 condition and persisting symptoms among English schoolchildren aged 4-18 years during 2021/22. It found that 1.8-6.9% of children met the definition of post-COVID-19 condition depending on age group, with specific symptoms like loss of smell and taste more prevalent in those with previous positive COVID-19 tests.
paper_authors: Charlotte Warren-Gash; Andrea Lacey; Sarah Cook; Dylan Stocker; Samantha Toon; Ffion Lelii; Ben Ford; Georgina Ireland; Shamez N. Ladhani; Terence Stephenson; Patrick Nguipdop-Djomo; Punam Mangtani; Elliot McClenahan; Gillian McKay; Jody Phelan; Liang-Yu Lin; Alex Lewin; Alison Judd; Byron Davies; Anisah Saib; James McCrae; Joe Kelly; Ian Diamond; Emma Rourke; Fiona Dawe; Pete Jones
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 condition and persisting symptoms in English schoolchildren: repeated surveys to March 2022

summary: A cross-sectional household survey of 12,925 SARS-CoV-2 cases in Bangladesh examining the prevalence and clinical presentation of pain symptoms in long COVID patients. The study found pain affects 1-3.1% of the population and significantly reduces quality of life, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Kabir MF; Yin KN; Jeffree MS; Ahmedy FB; Zainudin MF; Htwe O.; Jahan S.; Hossain MZ; Hossain KMA; Hossain T.; Jahid IK; Chakrovorty SK
paper_title: Clinical presentation of post-COVID pain and its impact on quality of life in long COVID patients: a cross-sectional household survey of SARS-CoV-2 cases in Bangladesh

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 150 general practitioners (GPs) in Belgium and Malta examining their knowledge, perceptions, and experience caring for long COVID patients. The study found that GPs frequently encounter long COVID patients but report insufficient knowledge and lack of multidisciplinary coordination, with most providing care independently rather than through coordinated multidisciplinary teams.
paper_authors: Sarah Moreels; Sherihane Bensemmane; Robrecht De Schreye; Sarah Cuschieri
paper_title: Caring for Long Covid patients in primary healthcare: a cross-sectional study on general practitioners’ knowledge, perception and experience in Belgium and Malta

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 12.61% long COVID prevalence among primary healthcare workers in Jiangsu, China, identifying age, sex, work stress, and vaccination as risk/protective factors. Study is observational without intervention and does not evaluate any treatment or therapeutic outcome.
paper_authors: Hualing Chen; Yongkang Qian; Beier Lu; Rongji Ma; Pengcheng Miao; Mingwang Fu; Haijian Guo; Ya Shen; Zhengkai Shen; Yan Li; Biyun Xu; Yongjie Zhang; Jinshui Xu; Bingwei Chen
paper_title: Prevalence and factors influencing long COVID among primary healthcare workers after epidemic control policy adjustment in Jiangsu, China

summary: This cross-sectional study investigated associations between clinical symptoms, vaccination status, antibody responses, and post-COVID-19 sequelae in 110 Thai COVID-19 patients infected with Delta or Omicron variants during a 1-year follow-up period. Key findings showed Delta infections were associated with pneumonia and post-infection symptoms like forgetfulness and hair loss, while Omicron was linked to upper respiratory symptoms, with vaccination and antibody responses showing differential patterns between variants.
paper_authors: Wathusiri Khongsiri; Prapassorn Poolchanuan; Adul Dulsuk; Narin Thippornchai; Rungnapa Phunpang; Chakkaphan Runcharoen; Thitiya Boonprakob; Onura Hemtong; Suchada Chowplijit; Vachara Chuapaknam; Tanaya Siripoon; Watcharapong Piyaphanee; Viravarn Luvira; Chawarat Rotejanaprasert; Pornsawan Leaungwutiwong; Wasun Chantratita; Narisara Chantratita; Nathamon Kosoltanapiwat
paper_title: Associations between clinical data, vaccination status, antibody responses, and post-COVID-19 symptoms in Thais infected with SARS-CoV-2 Delta and Omicron variants: a 1-year follow-up study

summary: This cross-sectional study identifies symptom clusters in long COVID patients 9 and 12 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection using hierarchical cluster analysis on 552 individuals from a Portuguese surveillance database. Four clusters were identified (no/minor symptoms, multi-symptoms, joint pain, and neurocognitive-related), with clusters remaining stable over time except for increased memory loss and concentration issues in the neurocognitive cluster at 12 months.
paper_authors: Marta Moniz; Carolina Ruivinho; Ana Rita Goes; Patrícia Soares; Andreia Leite
paper_title: Long COVID is not the same for everyone: a hierarchical cluster analysis of Long COVID symptoms 9 and 12 months after SARS-CoV-2 test

summary: This cross-sectional survey assessed quality of life, functional impairment, and cognitive decline in 435 long COVID patients compared to those who recovered or never had long COVID symptoms, measured at a median of 23.3 months post-infection. The study found that long COVID patients experienced significantly greater impairment across all health domains, with persistent cognitive complaints and fatigue even among those who reported recovery.
paper_authors: Szewczyk W.; Fitzpatrick AL; Fossou H.; Gentile NL; Sotoodehnia N.; Vora SB; West TE; Bertolli J.; Cope JR; Lin JS; Unger ER; Vu QM
paper_title: Long COVID and recovery from Long COVID: quality of life impairments and subjective cognitive decline at a median of 2 years after initial infection

summary: This cross-sectional study surveyed 114 long COVID patients to assess neuropsychiatric symptoms and explore how personality traits and social support relate to psychological distress and cognitive decline through mediation analysis. While the paper is about long COVID, it is an observational survey without any treatment intervention—participants were not given or evaluated for any specific therapy.
paper_authors: Asia Avinir; Aviv Kupershmidt; Dana Amsterdam; Guy Choshen; Jacob Nadav Ablin; Odelia Elkana
paper_title: Personality and neuropsychiatric symptoms in individuals diagnosed with long COVID

summary: Cross-sectional observational study examining renal function in 246 long COVID patients from a clinical care program in the Amazon region. Found renal function decline in 33.7% of patients, with older age and glycaemic alterations as risk factors, but this is a descriptive epidemiological study without intervention or treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Gabriela Maria Coimbra Coelho de Assis; Ian Gonçalves da Veiga; Rita de Nazaré Rayol Reis; Daniel Carvalho de Menezes; Stanley Soares Xavier; Elem Cristina Rodrigues Chaves; Jorge Rodrigues de Sousa; Juarez Antônio Simões Quaresma; Luiz Fábio Magno Falcão; Patrícia Danielle Lima de Lima
paper_title: Investigation of renal function in patients with long COVID in the Amazon region: a cross-sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing post-COVID functional status and associated sociodemographic factors among 3,067 residents of vulnerable neighborhoods in two Brazilian cities. Found 34.6% prevalence of post-COVID functional limitations, with increased risk in those with comorbidities, reinfection, and healthcare access barriers.
paper_authors: Danielle Souto de Medeiros; Gabriele Amorim; Fabiane Soares; Laio Magno; Thaís Regis Aranha Rossi; Thiago Silva Torres; Valdiléa Gonçalves Veloso; Débora Castanheira; Inês Dourado
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 functional status in socioeconomically vulnerable neighborhoods attended in primary health care in two Brazilian cities: a cross-sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional study measuring heart rate variability (HRV) as a marker of autonomic nervous system function in 173 COVID-19 patients with and without long COVID symptoms. Found that young to middle-aged patients with LC showed lower HRV in the very-low-frequency domain and higher rates of autonomic dysfunction compared to those without LC.
paper_authors: Minyu Qin; Kwan Lee; Seok-Ju Yoo
paper_title: The impact of long COVID on heart rate variability: a cross-sectional study

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed the impact of post-COVID-19 syndrome on quality of life, mental health, and functional capacity in 25 ethnically diverse and socioeconomically vulnerable individuals from the Brazilian Amazon. The study found high rates of fatigue (88%) and psychological symptoms, with worse outcomes associated with older age, lower education, and lower income, but did not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Marcelo Silva de Paula; Sheyla Mara Silva de Oliveira; Tatiane Costa Quaresma; Guilherme Augusto Barros Conde; Laura Maria Vidal Nogueira; Valney Mara Gomes Conde; Adjanny Estela Santos de Souza; Waldiney Pires Moraes; Camila Castilho Moraes; Marcos Manoel Honorato; Daliane Ferreira Marinho; Franciane de Paula Fernandes; Lívia de Aguiar Valentim
paper_title: Impact of post-COVID-19 syndrome on quality of life and functionality in ethnically diverse and vulnerable populations in the Amazon

summary: This cross-sectional study examines coagulation abnormalities in 1,473 COVID-19 patients compared to 2,310 controls, tracking multiple time points from acute phase to 12 months post-infection. The findings document persistent coagulation dysfunction in long COVID patients, including abnormal D-dimer (66.96% at 12 months) and prolonged PT/INR, but no intervention or treatment is tested.
paper_authors: Yucan Li; Zhengqi Jiang; Fengjiao Han; Qiuyu Guo; Qi Feng; Tichao Shan; Jun Peng; Miao Xu
paper_title: Coagulation Abnormalities in Post-Acute COVID-19 Syndrome: A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 535 long COVID patients in Quebec assessing symptom profiles, functional impact, and quality of life priorities. Study identifies fatigue and post-exercise malaise as primary concerns but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Nancy E. Mayo; Marie-Josée Brouillette; Emilia Liana Falcone; Lesley K. Fellows
paper_title: A patient-centered view of symptoms, functional impact, and priorities in post-COVID-19 syndrome: cross-sectional results from the Québec Action Post-COVID cohort

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 6,572 Chinese participants examining the relationship between vaccination status and COVID-19 infection outcomes and long COVID symptoms. Study found that booster shots reduced risk of specific symptoms, but vaccination timing was associated with persistence of symptoms like fatigue and headache beyond one month.
paper_authors: Xiaolong Yan; Xin Zhao; Hao Wang; Yin Du; Li Liu; Jianhua Liu; Qi Wang; Sheng Wei
paper_title: Impact of vaccination on SARS-CoV-2 infections and long COVID symptoms: a cross-sectional study in China

summary: Cross-sectional observational study examining mental health symptoms (depression, anxiety, insomnia) in 228 long COVID patients and their association with autoimmune markers. Found high prevalence of mental health symptoms in long COVID with association to autoantibody positivity, particularly ANA and anti-TPO antibodies.
paper_authors: Hernan F. Guillen-Burgos; Mauricio Sarmiento; Juan F. Gálvez-Flórez; Catalina Rojas; Yaneth Beatriz Lora; Ivan David Lozada-Martinez; María C. Diazgranados-Garcia; GIBACUS; Manuel Rojas; Juan Carlos Salazar-Uribe; Juan-Manuel Anaya
paper_title: Association between mental health symptoms and autoimmunity in patients with long COVID

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluates neurocognitive screening tools and cognitive impairment rates in 102 COVID-19 patients (ambulatory vs hospitalized) 24 days post-infection. While highly relevant to long COVID, it is excluded because it is a descriptive assessment study without any treatment intervention—patients are only evaluated, not treated.
paper_authors: Karen Blackmon; Gregory S. Day; Harry Ross Powers; Wendelyn Bosch; Divya Prabhakaran; Dixie Woolston; Otto Pedraza
paper_title: Neurocognitive screening in patients following SARS-CoV-2 infection: tools for triage

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 783 healthcare workers in Qatar examining prevalence and profile of long COVID symptoms and associated risk factors. Three-quarters reported long-term symptoms post-infection, with fatigue most common and significant gender disparities observed; no interventions or treatments were tested.
paper_authors: Shuja Reagu; Majid Alabdulla; Nisha Kalariparambil Abdul Kader; Nighat Ara Ajmal; Sara Kamal Hassan Abdelgafar; Ovais Wadoo
paper_title: Long-term symptoms after SARS-CoV-2 infection in a cohort of healthcare workers in Qatar

summary: Cross-sectional study of 699 patients from a COVID-19 telehealth service examining the prevalence and associated factors of long COVID symptoms. Found 26.8% prevalence of long COVID with cognitive symptoms, chronic diarrhea, and cough being most common; female sex, lower education, lower income, and anosmia during acute COVID were significant risk factors.
paper_authors: Ana Flávia Avelar Maia Seixas; Milena Soriano Marcolino; Felipe Souza Guimarães; Gustavo Machado Rocha; Aline Carrilho Menezes; Hygor Kleber Cabral Silva; Clareci Silva Cardoso
paper_title: Exploring the landscape of long COVID: prevalence and associated factors in patients assisted by a telehealth service

summary: This cross-sectional study used comet assay to measure DNA damage in 29 post-COVID-19 patients stratified by initial COVID-19 severity, compared to 10 healthy controls. The study found significantly elevated DNA damage in long COVID patients correlated with COVID-19 severity, but did not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Elaheh Abiri; Ali Abiri; Salman Daneshi; Rasoul Raesi
paper_title: The silent legacy of COVID-19: exploring genomic instability in long-term COVID-19 survivors

summary: Cross-sectional study of 93 COVID-19 survivors evaluated ~20 weeks post-discharge to identify risk factors and radiological/functional sequelae of long COVID. Found obesity, ICU admission, and NIV requirement associated with long COVID; 45% of patients had long COVID with fatigue and dyspnea as most common symptoms.
paper_authors: Marhia Eduarda Vilela de Araújo; Sophia Garcia de Oliveira Dias; J Lourenço; A L Fernandes; B Cabrita; J Amado; A P Vaz; I Neves; P Simão; Brunna Ferrari Seabra
paper_title: Long COVID risk factors in a Portuguese cohort

summary: This multicentre cross-sectional study investigates the prevalence of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) and thrombus resolution in COVID-19 survivors who experienced acute pulmonary embolism. The findings indicate that CTEPH is not more common after COVID-19-associated PE than after non-COVID PE, and thrombus resolution patterns are similar between groups.
paper_authors: de Jong CMM; Visser C.; Bemelmans RHH; Boersma WG; van den Borst B.; Burggraaf JLI; Cannegieter SC; Ten Cate-Hoek AJ; Croles FN; Faber HJ; Faber LM; Hellemons ME; Hessels LM; Huisman MV; Kamphuisen PW; Koster SCE; Kroft LJM; van der Lee I.; Leentjens J.; Meijer K.; Ninaber MK; Sondermeijer BM; Stads S.; Vonk Noordegraaf A.; Winckers K.; Kruip MJHA; Klok FA
paper_title: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension and clot resolution after COVID-19-associated pulmonary embolism

summary: A psychological needs analysis of 47 long COVID clinic patients assessing anxiety, depression, and PTSD using validated instruments (GAD-7, PHQ-9, PCL-5, b-IPQ). The analysis identifies depression as a key intervention target but presents only baseline assessment data without testing or evaluating any actual treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Amy Barradell; C Bourne; Sonal Kristin Singh; N Robertson
paper_title: A psychological needs analysis of individuals with Long-Covid

summary: Cross-sectional study examining cognitive symptoms and brain structural changes in 109 long COVID patients versus 28 healthy controls approximately two years post-infection in Argentina. Found persistent cognitive complaints, brain atrophy in cerebellum and parietal regions, and reduced cortical thickness despite no significant objective cognitive impairment on testing.
paper_authors: Sol A. Cataldo; Andrea Micciulli; Laura Margulis; Melina Cibeyra; Sabrina Defeo; Silvina G. Horovitz; Analía Martino; Raul Melano; Milagros Mena; Francisco Parisi; Diego Santoro; Florencia Sarmiento; Martin A. Belzunce
paper_title: Cognitive impact and brain structural changes in long COVID patients: a cross-sectional MRI study two years post infection in a cohort from Argentina

summary: This study assessed long-term self-reported disability in public employees after COVID-19 compared to controls with negative PCR tests using the WHO Disability Assessment Schedule. It found higher disability rates in the post-COVID phase (64%) versus controls (52%), with more severe disability among women, but does not test or evaluate any intervention.
paper_authors: Linda Ashman Kröönström; Johanna Krause; Simon B. Larsson; Robert Sigström; Katharina Stibrant Sunnerhagen
paper_title: Long-term self-reported health and disability after COVID-19 in public employees

summary: Cross-sectional study examining Alice in Wonderland syndrome (AIWS) symptoms in 421 adults with persistent headache after COVID-19 across Latin America. Found that 25.2% reported AIWS symptoms, with younger age and pre-existing migraine as risk factors, but this is an observational characterization study without any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Fhabián S. Carrión-Nessi; Luis C. Ascanio; Óscar D. Omaña-Ávila; Oriana A. Regalado-Gutiérrez; Daniela L. Mendoza-Millán; Natasha A. Camejo-Ávila; David A. Forero-Peña; Alberto E. Paniz-Mondolfi
paper_title: Exploring Alice in Wonderland syndrome in adults with persistent headache after COVID-19: a cross-sectional study in Latin America

summary: Cross-sectional study of 936 school-aged children in China examining COVID-19 symptoms and long COVID (LC 28) prevalence following infection in early 2023. Found LC 28 in 3.4% of children, with alopecia, cognitive dysfunction, and emotional problems being the most common persistent symptoms.
paper_authors: Honglin Wang; Fangfang Lu; Xiuxian Ni; Rijing Luo; Linxiang Chen; Jing Yuan; Zhen Zhang; Qiuying Lv
paper_title: Acute and persistent symptoms of COVID-19 infection in school-aged children: a retrospective study from China

summary: Cross-sectional study developing a prediction model for depressive symptoms among middle-aged/elderly CVD patients who recovered from SARS-CoV-2 infection in Wuhan, China. While it identifies long COVID-related predictors (fatigue, insomnia, PTSD, anxiety), it is a secondary analysis of baseline depression prevalence rather than a treatment evaluation study.
paper_authors: Zhenwei Dai; Xin Liu; Shu Jing; Hao Wang; Yiman Huang; Jiaqi Fu; Yijin Wu; Ling Zhang; Bicheng Han; Xiaoyou Su
paper_title: Development and internal validation of a depressive symptoms prediction model among the patients with cardiovascular disease who have recovered from SARS-CoV-2 infection in Wuhan, China: a cross-sectional study

summary: This study validates a Thai translation of the COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale (C19-YRS) for assessing long COVID symptom severity in community members. While focused on long COVID, it is a validation study of a measurement tool, not a treatment intervention study, and therefore does not meet criteria for the clinical trials pipeline.
paper_authors: Suphamas Partiprajak; Suphanna Krongthaeo; Noppawan Piaseu; Jatuporn Wongsathikun; Anon Kongsuwan
paper_title: The Thai version of the COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale: a valid instrument for the psychometric assessment of the community members in Bangkok, Thailand

summary: A nationwide cross-sectional survey in China examining acute and long COVID-19 symptoms and associated risk factors during the omicron-dominant period in 32,528 COVID-19 patients. The study reports a 19.68% long COVID rate at 3+ months post-infection, with muscle weakness, headache, and smell/taste disorders as primary symptoms, identifying age, smoking, gender, and vaccination as risk factors.
paper_authors: Zheng Su; Yinghua Li; Ying Xie; Zhenxiao Huang; Anqi Cheng; Xinmei Zhou; Jinxuan Li; Rui Qin; Xiaowen Wei; Yi Liu; Xin Xia; Qingqing Song; Liang Zhao; Zhao Liu; Dan Xiao; Chen Wang
paper_title: Acute and long COVID-19 symptoms and associated factors in the omicron-dominant period: a nationwide survey via the online platform Wenjuanxing in China

summary: Population-based cross-sectional survey in Iran examining the prevalence and patterns of long COVID symptoms among 1,561 individuals with prior COVID-19 infection and a control group. Found 36.4% experienced persistent symptoms post-recovery, with older age, prior hospitalization, cardiovascular disease, and steroid/chemotherapy use associated with long COVID development.
paper_authors: Mehrdad Askarian; Erfan Taherifard; Fatemeh Jazzabi; Zahra Shayan; Ojan Assadian; Gary Groot; Nahid Hatam; Ardalan Askarian; Seyed Mohammadebrahim Faghihi; Ehsan Taherifard
paper_title: Epidemiological and clinical characteristics of long COVID-19 among Iranians: A community-based study in southern Iran

summary: This international survey study (ICOSS-II) examined associations between changes in sleep duration and self-rated health among 1,509 COVID-19 survivors across 16 countries. It found that both decreased and increased habitual sleep duration after infection were associated with lower self-rated health and post-COVID symptoms like fatigue and shortness of breath, but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Kentaro Matsui; Frances Chung; Adrijana Koscec Bjelajac; Ilona Merikanto; Maria Korman; Sérgio Mota-Rolim; Ana Suely Cunha; Bjørn Bjorvatn; Pei Xue; Christian Benedict; Charles M. Morin; Colin A. Espie; Anne-Marie Landtblom; Thomas Penzel; Luigi De Gennaro; Brigitte Holzinger; Harald Hrubos-Strøm; Damien Leger; Courtney J. Bolstad; Michael R. paper_title: Associations between changes in habitual sleep duration and lower self-rated health among COVID-19 survivors: findings from a survey across 16 countries/regions

summary: This cross-sectional survey assessed post-COVID-19 manifestations in 428 Saudi Arabian college students, categorizing them by symptom duration (recovered, prolonged, or persistent). Young adults showed mild overall symptom severity with persistent symptoms including loss of smell/taste and shortness of breath, and a significant association with depression.
paper_authors: Areej Abed Alkhormani; Reema Abdullah Alghamdi; Yara Abdulaziz Damdam; Maria Eissa Almaghrabi; Faisal F. Alamri; Muhammad Anwar Khan; Alqassem Y. Hakami
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 manifestations among college students: shedding the light on young adults’ health

summary: This cross-sectional study investigated the prevalence of long COVID and characterized symptom clusters among 337 previously infected individuals in Bangkok, Thailand. The analysis identified three symptom clusters (common symptoms/communication, fatigue/functioning/nutrition, psychosocial impacts) and found a significant relationship between symptom severity and functional disability, with no intervention or treatment tested.
paper_authors: Suphanna Krongthaeo; Suphamas Partiprajak; Noppawan Piaseu; Sineenuch Ckumdee; Chonthicha Taaon; Anon Kongsuwan
paper_title: Prevalence and exploratory factor analysis of long COVID-19 symptoms among experienced infected population in Bangkok, Thailand

summary: This cross-sectional study analyzes the association between long COVID symptoms and functional disability (BADL/IADL) in Brazilian adults and seniors using data from the SulCovid-19 study. The findings show that specific symptoms like dyspnea, joint pain, and muscle pain are associated with limitations in daily functioning, but the study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Yohana Pereira Vieira; Luan Nascimento da Silva; Bruno Pereira Nunes; Tatiane Nogueira Gonzalez; Suele Manjourany Silva Duro; Mirelle de Oliveira Saes
paper_title: Relationship between long covid and functional disability in adults and the seniors in the south of Brazil

summary: A nationally representative cross-sectional survey of Mexican COVID-19 survivors estimating the prevalence of post-COVID conditions (37.0%) and characterizing common persistent symptoms including fatigue, myalgia, and respiratory distress. This is an observational prevalence study with no treatment intervention, so it does not meet inclusion criteria for the intervention trial pipeline.
paper_authors: Ramírez-Toscano Y.; Torres-Ibarra L.; Carnalla M.; Basto-Abreu A.; Vidaña-Perez D.; Colchero MA; Bautista-Arredondo S.; Saydah S.; Barrientos-Gutiérrez T.
paper_title: Prevalence of Post-COVID conditions among Mexican COVID-19 survivors: a nationwide cross-sectional study

summary: A prospective cross-sectional study examining potential long-term ocular complications in 21 COVID-19 patients at 3 months post-recovery using ophthalmological exams and imaging. Found no evidence of retinal damage or vascular complications, concluding ocular complications are unlikely at 3 months without prior eye involvement.
paper_authors: Victor Brantl; Benedikt Schworm; Gregor Weber; Johannes Schiefelbein; Thomas C. Kreutzer; Stylianos Michalakis; Jakob Siedlecki; Siegfried G. Priglinger
paper_title: Long-term ocular damage after recovery from COVID-19: lack of evidence at three months

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing prevalence of post-COVID-19 condition among young adults (n=2,098) and its associations with general health, stress, and lifestyle factors three years post-pandemic onset. Found 10.5% with previous and 3.9% with ongoing PCC symptoms, with reduced physical activity and worsened dietary habits in the ongoing PCC group, but no intervention or treatment was tested.
paper_authors: Sandra Ekström; Ida Mogensen; Maria Ödling; Antonios Georgelis; Anne-Sophie Merritt; Sophia Björkander; Erik Melén; Anna Bergström; Inger Kull
paper_title: Post COVID-19 among young adults– prevalence and associations with general health, stress, and lifestyle factors

summary: This cross-sectional study assesses the prevalence and distribution of persistent symptoms in young adults (aged 18-25) with long COVID using the Symptom Burden Questionnaire, evaluating 123 symptoms across 17 health domains. The research finds high rates of mental health issues, sleep disturbances, and cognitive dysfunction, with female participants reporting greater symptom severity.
paper_authors: Rupal Dhariwal; Krishna Thakkar; Kritagnasinh Vaghela; Mukul Jain
paper_title: Evaluating post-acute COVID-19 sequelae in younger population using symptom burden questionnaire (SQL)

summary: This is a cross-sectional analysis of the 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System survey examining the prevalence of long COVID among US adults and factors associated with it. The study reports 7.2% prevalence of long COVID and identifies higher risk among women, middle-aged individuals, and those with chronic conditions or socioeconomic disadvantage, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Juanjuan Shi; Rui Lu; Yan Tian; Fengping Wu; Xiaozhen Geng; Song Zhai; Xiaoli Jia; Shuangsuo Dang; Wenjun Wang
paper_title: Prevalence of and factors associated with long COVID among US adults: a nationwide survey

summary: This cross-sectional study examined the association between adverse childhood events (ACEs) and long-term COVID-19 symptoms using 2022 BRFSS data from 14,560 participants. The study found that exposure to ACEs, particularly sexual abuse, household substance abuse, and household mental illness, was positively associated with increased risk of long-term COVID symptoms, with no intervention tested.
paper_authors: Safa Elkefi; Alana Steffen; Alicia K. Matthews
paper_title: Association between Adverse Childhood Events (ACEs) and long-term COVID-19 symptoms: evidence from the 2022 behavioral risk factor surveillance system

summary: This cross-sectional study examines associations between physical activity levels and various outcomes (symptoms, cardiovascular fitness, sleep quality, QoL) in 219 long COVID patients. The results show that moderate-to-high PA is associated with better cardiorespiratory fitness, heart rate recovery, sleep quality, and QoL domains, but this is an observational study without intervention assignment—patients self-selected into PA groups rather than being assigned a treatment.
paper_authors: Yi-Pang Lo; Shang-Lin Chiang; Chieh-Yi Song; Wen-Chii Tzeng; Cheng-Chiang Chang; Chia-Huei Lin
paper_title: Associations between moderate-to-high physical activity levels and long COVID symptoms, heart rate recovery, cardiorespiratory fitness, sleep quality, and quality of life in patients with long COVID: a cross-sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional study of 780 long COVID patients examining gender differences in disability, employment, sick leave, and activities of daily living. Finds women report significantly higher mental fatigue than men, but ADL challenges are largely similar between genders.
paper_authors: Cecilia Hee Laursen; Trine Brøns Nielsen; Steffen Leth; Berit Schiøttz-Christensen; Claus Vinther Nielsen; Vivian Langagergaard; Lotte Sørensen; Dorthe Sørensen; Lisa Gregersen Oestergaard
paper_title: Characterising disability in patients with long COVID–does gender matter? an analytic cross-sectional study

summary: This cross-sectional study compared accelerometer-measured physical activity and sleep quality between 65 COVID-19 recovered individuals (including 3 with post-COVID syndrome) and 65 healthy controls in the UAE. The study found no significant differences in physical activity or most sleep parameters, except longer sleep latency in recovered individuals, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Ashokan Arumugam; Monica Raja Kumari Raghunathan; Mohammad Fawzi Safarini; Sangeetha Narasimhan; Sivapriya Ramakrishnan; Raneen Mohammed Qadah; Reime Jamal Shalash; Fatma Hegazy; Tamer Mohamed Shousha; George P. Nassis; Wael Daab; Sana Mehek; Yunus Nadeemulla Beig Khader; Nadia Rashed Al Mazrouei; Vennila J.; Arto J. Pesola; Senthil D. Kumaran
paper_title: Do COVID-19 recovered individuals differ from healthy controls in accelerometer-measured physical activity and self-reported sleep? a UAE-based study

summary: This cross-sectional study examined associations between long COVID symptoms and loneliness among 5,692 World Trade Center Health Registry enrollees who reported acute COVID-19 infection in 2022-23. The study found that enrollees with long COVID symptoms had significantly higher prevalence of loneliness (PR=1.19) compared to those without symptoms, with stronger associations for emotional loneliness.
paper_authors: Julia S. Sisti; Samuel E. Packard; Janna Metzler
paper_title: Long COVID symptoms and loneliness: findings from the World Trade Center Health Registry

summary: Population-based cross-sectional survey of 3,048 Slovenian adults examining relationships between pre-pandemic lifestyle patterns and mental health outcomes in people with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC). Found 29.5% of infected individuals met PASC criteria with elevated stress, anxiety, and depression alongside reduced well-being, though this is an observational study without treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Gaja Zager Kocjan; Jana Verdnik; Jure Manfreda; Luka Komidar; Žan Lep; Darja Kobal Grum; Kaja Hacin Beyazoglu; Anja Podlesek; Katarina Babnik
paper_title: Pre-pandemic lifestyle patterns and mental health outcomes among people reporting post-acute sequelae of COVID-19: evidence from a Slovenian population-based sample

summary: Cross-sectional study of 530 post-COVID patients assessing body composition and risk factors for sarcopenia 3 months after moderate-to-severe COVID-19. Found that age >60, obesity, and prolonged hospitalization with mechanical ventilation were associated with higher sarcopenia risk, but no treatment intervention was evaluated.
paper_authors: Dulce González-Islas; Carlos Sánchez-Moreno; Arturo Orea-Tejeda; Samantha Hernández-López; Fernanda Salgado-Fernández; Candace Keirns-Davis; Susana Galicia-Amor; Esperanza Trejo-Mellado; Laura Gochicoa-Rangel; Armando Castorena-Maldonado
paper_title: Body composition and risk factors associated with sarcopenia in post-COVID patients after moderate or severe COVID-19 infections

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the association between obesity and long COVID prevalence, as well as obesity's impact on physical and mental health outcomes in 3,663 SARS-CoV-2 infected participants. While about long COVID, this is an observational epidemiologic study that does not test or evaluate a treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Michael Gottlieb; Huihui Yu; Ji Chen; Erica S. Spatz; Nicole L. Gentile; Rachel E. Geyer; Michelle Santangelo; Caitlin Malicki; Kristyn Gatling; Kelli N. O’Laughlin; Kari A. Stephens; Joann G. Elmore; Lauren E. Wisk; Michelle L’Hommedieu; Robert M. Rodriguez; Juan Carlos C. Montoy; Ralph C. Wang; Kristin L. Rising; Efrat Kean; Jonathan W. Dyal; Mandy J. Hill; Arjun K. Venkatesh; Robert A. Weinstein
paper_title: Obesity and Long COVID: intersecting epidemics?

summary: A multi-centre cross-sectional study of 3,693 Chinese individuals examining long COVID prevalence, symptom patterns, and risk factors using a WHO-based definition. Older age, female sex, and reinfection increased long COVID risk, while vaccination and traditional Chinese medicine use were protective factors.
paper_authors: Danying Yan; Ying Liu; Ran Chen; Lei Zhou; Chuwen Wang; Ada Hoi Yan Ma; Xueqin Chen; Qifa Song; Guoqing Qian
paper_title: Follow-up of long COVID based on the definition of WHO: a multi-centre cross-sectional questionnaire-based study

summary: Cross-sectional study of 997 Thai university students assessing the prevalence of long COVID symptoms and identifying risk factors. Found 21.9% prevalence with respiratory, neurological, and psychological symptoms as common manifestations, and identified severe initial infection, illness duration, and poor sleep quality as significant predictors.
paper_authors: Pheerasak Assavanopakun; Suphapich Wangkawong; Wuttipat Kiratipaisarl; Wachiranun Sirikul; Tharntip Promkutkao; Suchat Promkutkeo; Amornphat Kitro
paper_title: The hidden burden: prevalence and risk factors of long COVID among university students in Chiang Mai, Thailand

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the association between muscle quality index (MQI) and pulmonary function in 748 post-COVID-19 patients with severe-to-critical disease history. Found that low MQI is independently associated with reduced respiratory function, suggesting musculoskeletal weakness as a marker of post-COVID pulmonary impairment.
paper_authors: Dulce González-Islas; Robinson Robles-Hernández; Laura Flores-Cisneros; Arturo Orea-Tejeda; Susana Galicia-Amor; Nadia Hernández-López; Mariana I. Valdés-Moreno; Rocío Sánchez-Santillán; Juan Carlos García-Hernández; Armando Castorena-Maldonado
paper_title: Association between muscle quality index and pulmonary function in post-COVID-19 subjects

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence and risk factors for post-COVID-19 pulmonary complications in 405 recovered COVID-19 patients from Ethiopia. Found 14.1% prevalence of pulmonary complications associated with older age and lung consolidation on imaging.
paper_authors: Abebaw Bekele Seyoum; Sisay Shine Tegegnework; Mahider Molla Mengistu; Tenbite Daniel Mekonnen; Abdurahman Mohammedamin Asabel; Alazar Gizate Dagnaw; Abenet Girma Deribe; Tadios Niguss Derese; Tsegaye Gebreyes Hundie; Bisrat Kassa Getahun; Dawit Kebede Huluka
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 pulmonary complications among recovered COVID-19 patients: a cross-sectional study from Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

summary: Cross-sectional study of 52 patients with respiratory symptoms 4 months after COVID-19 hospitalization, measuring lung function, muscle strength, and physical capacity. Finds 90% had objective respiratory abnormalities, but this is a descriptive assessment study without treatment intervention—it measures existing dysfunction rather than testing a treatment.
paper_authors: Monika Fagevik Olsén; Louise Lannefors; Ewa-Lena Johansson; Hanna C. Persson
paper_title: Variations in respiratory and functional symptoms at four months after hospitalisation due to COVID-19: a cross-sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 1,170 nurses in Slovakia examining the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on their health, wellbeing, and working conditions from January to November 2021. About two-thirds reported long COVID symptoms, but the study does not evaluate any treatment or intervention—it is purely observational and descriptive of prevalence and burden.
paper_authors: Silvia Putekova; Jana Martinkova; Alena Urickova; Lukas Kober; Stanislava Reichertova; Dominika Plancikova; Marek Majdan
paper_title: The impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the health and working conditions of nurses and its implications for policies: a cross-sectional study in Slovakia

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 350 healthcare workers in Iran assessing prevalence and characteristics of long COVID-19 symptoms. Found 75.7% experienced long COVID symptoms, with fatigue, cough, and muscle weakness being most common, and identified several clinical risk factors.
paper_authors: Hamidreza Zeraatkhah; Negin Masoudi Alavi; Hanieh Ziabakhsh; Zahra Mahdaviasl
paper_title: Prevalence and characters of post-acute COVID-19 syndrome in healthcare workers in Kashan/Iran 2023: a cross-sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional study of 1,911 Tunisian COVID-19 survivors examining long COVID prevalence (46.5%) and risk factors. Identifies female gender and age ≥60 as risk factors, with complete vaccination as protective, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Souhir Chelly; Sourour Rouis; Olfa Ezzi; Asma Ammar; Sami Fitouri; Asma Soua; Ines Fathallah; Mansour Njah; Mohamed Mahjoub
paper_title: Symptoms and risk factors for long COVID in Tunisian population

summary: This cross-sectional study surveyed 362 French nurses about their roles in Long COVID care, finding that nurses informally delegate tasks including psychological support, screening, and therapeutic education. The study identifies implications for formalizing nursing responsibilities in emerging chronic disease management but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Odette Linda Kamdem; Caroline Dupre; Jessica Guyot; Louise Ruiz; Mabrouk Nekaa; Elisabeth Botelho-Nevers; Bienvenu Bongue
paper_title: Task delegation in emerging chronic diseases: Long COVID care as a paradigm - a cross-sectional study

summary: This cross-sectional study compared thyroid function (TT3, TT4, TSH) in COVID-19-positive unvaccinated patients, COVID-19-negative vaccinated individuals, and healthy controls. While it documents thyroid hormone abnormalities in post-COVID patients that gradually recover over time, it is a passive observational study without any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Mamudul Hasan Razu; Md. Iqbal Hossain; Zabed Bin Ahmed; Mousumi Bhowmik; Md. Kazy Ebnul Hasan; Md. Kaderi Kibria; Dil Afroj Moni; Mala Khan

summary: Cross-sectional population survey of 1,813 French adults examining associations between multimorbidity and post-COVID condition (PCC). paper_title: Relationship between multimorbidity, SARS-COV-2 infection and long COVID: a cross-sectional population-based French survey

paper_journal: Health and Quality of Life Outcomes

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 457 Japanese COVID-19 patients assessing health-related quality of life differences between those with and without persistent symptoms lasting >4 weeks. paper_title: Impact of long-COVID on health-related quality of life in Japanese COVID-19 patients
paper_journal: Health and Quality of Life Outcomes

paper_title: Investigating the impact of the number of COVID-19 reinfections, vaccination status, risk factors, and reinfection interval on long COVID symptomatology

paper_title: Long COVID: risk factors, mental health and quality of life among Malaysian population

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of long COVID symptoms in 300 rural Indian participants who had recovered from COVID-19, measuring both physical symptoms (cough, fatigue, dyspnea) and psychological symptoms (fear, anxiety, sleep problems). paper_title: The impact of Post-COVID-Syndrome on functioning – results from a community survey in patients after mild and moderate SARS-CoV-2-infections in Germany

summary: This nationwide French survey examines the association between anxiety/depression symptoms and post-COVID-19 condition in 1,095 PCC patients and 1,021 infected controls without PCC. The study finds that anxiety and depression are highly prevalent in PCC but challenges their inclusion in the PCC definition, suggesting pre-COVID chronic anxiety/depression may share vulnerability factors with PCC rather than defining it.
paper_authors: Sarah Tebeka; Laure Carcaillon-Bentata; Valentina Decio; Caroline Alleaume; Nathalie Beltzer; Anne Gallay; Cédric Lemogne; Baptiste Pignon; Tatjana T. Makovski; Joël Coste
paper_title: Complex association between post-COVID-19 condition and anxiety and depression symptoms

summary: Cross-sectional study of 137 long COVID patients in Tunisia examining associations between post-COVID symptoms and anxio-depressive disorders using the HAD scale. Found that arthralgia (but not other post-COVID symptoms) was independently associated with anxiety/depression in this observational cohort.
paper_authors: F. Zaouali; A. Chaouch; F. Boubaker; S. Bouchareb; H. E. Mrabet; A. Ben Mabrouk; I. Touil; L. Boussoffara; J. Knani; N. Boudawara; W. Alaya; M. H. Sfar
paper_title: Arthralgia is the main associated symptom to anxio-depressive disorders during the “Long COVID” among Tunisian patients

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed the frequency of psychiatric disorders (anxiety, depression, PTSD, sleep disorders) in 104 patients 3 months after COVID-19 hospitalization. The study identified risk factors for psychological distress but did not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Nadia Sghaier; H. Ben Garouia; H. Khiari; W. Belaguide; J. Mannai; Hédia Bellali
paper_title: Psychiatric disorders in patients after hospitalization for COVID-19: Frequency, coping behaviours and associated factors

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing mental health and quality of life in 276 COVID-19 survivors one year post-hospitalization at Tehran hospitals. Found impaired mental health in 83.7% of survivors with inverse relationship between mental health status and all quality-of-life dimensions.
paper_authors: Hasan Khosravi; Leila Sayadi; Esmaeil Mohammadnejad
paper_title: Assessment of relationship of mental health and quality of life of COVID-19 Survivors in selected hospitals of Tehran University of Medical Sciences, 2021

summary: Cross-sectional study of 137 long COVID patients in Tunisia assessing physical symptoms and anxio-depressive disorders using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression scale. Found high prevalence of anxiety (28% severe) and depression (24% severe), with dyspnea, mood disorders, and myalgia being the most common symptoms.
paper_authors: F. Zaouali; Aziz Chaouch; F. Boubaker; S. Bouchareb; H. Mrabet; A. Ben Mabouk; I. Touil; L. Boussofara; Jalel Knani; N. Boudawara; W. Alaya; M.H. Sfar
paper_title: Organic and psychiatric symptoms of “Long COVID” among Tunisian patients: a cross sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing corticotroph and somatotroph functions between recovered COVID-19 patients and those with long COVID. Found that long COVID patients were more likely to have anterior pituitary deficiencies, supporting an endocrine hypothesis for long COVID pathogenesis.
paper_authors: Taieb Ach; Nassim Ben Haj Slama; Asma Gorchane; Asma Ben Abdelkrim; Meriem Garma; Nadia Ben Lasfar; Foued Bellazreg; Widéd Debbabi; Wissem Hachfi; Molka Chadli Chaieb; Monia Zaouali; Amel Letaief; Koussay Ach
paper_title: Explaining Long COVID: A Pioneer Cross-Sectional Study Supporting the Endocrine Hypothesis

summary: This cross-sectional survey examined medical diagnoses and treatment outcomes in 57 ultra-endurance athletes with and without prior COVID-19 infection during a 2022 triathlon championship. The study found no significant associations between recent COVID-19 infection and medical care outcomes, though COVID-19 symptom severity was associated with muscle cramping during competition.
paper_authors: Alicja B. Stannard; Christopher P. Connolly; W. D. B. Hiller
paper_title: COVID-19 INFECTION AND MEDICAL CARE DURING ULTRA-ENDURANCE COMPETITION: A PRELIMINARY INVESTIGATION

summary: This cross-sectional study examined physical activity levels and symptoms in 22 adults during acute COVID-19 infection, finding reduced weekly physical activity post-diagnosis and an association between inactivity and difficulty breathing. The paper focuses on acute infection phase rather than long COVID sequelae occurring weeks to months after infection.
paper_authors: Ana Beatriz Minelli Ramos; Euripedes Barsanulfo Gonçalves Gomide; Thiago Cândido Alves; Natália Drieli Miguel; Átila Alexandre Trapé; Emerson Sebastião; André Pereira dos Santos
paper_title: Physical activity and sitting time in adults after positive diagnosis for COVID-19: a cross-sectional study
paper_journal: Revista Brasileira de Atividade Física & Saúde

summary: This cross-sectional study compares cardiovascular parameters (pulse rate, central aortic systolic pressure, systolic and diastolic blood pressure) in 79 university teachers who had COVID-19 versus 116 teachers without COVID-19 history. The findings show that post-COVID cardiovascular changes depend on age and pre-existing hypertension status, with non-hypertensive individuals showing decreased heart rate and blood pressure while those with prior hypertension showed increases.
paper_authors: Marina A. Popova; Viktoriya V. Chistova; Alexandra E. Scherbakova
paper_title: INDICATORS OF PULSE, CENTRAL AND PERIPHERAL BLOOD PRESSURE OF NORTHERN UNIVERSITY TEACHERS WHO UNDERWENT COVID-19 WHILE WORKING REMOTELY
paper_journal: Siberian Journal of Life Sciences and Agriculture

summary: Cross-sectional study using BOLD-fMRI to assess brain activation patterns during working memory tasks in 29 people with post-COVID condition versus 21 healthy controls. Participants with PCC showed greater brain activation and compensatory neural processes but similar cognitive performance, with greater activation predicting worse neuropsychiatric symptoms.
paper_authors: Linda Chang; Meghann C. Ryan; Huajun Liang; Xin Zhang; Eric Cunningham; Justin Wang; Eleanor Wilson; Edward H. Herskovits; Shyamasundaran Kottilil; Thomas M. Ernst
paper_title: Changes in Brain Activation Patterns During Working Memory Tasks in People With Post-COVID Condition and Persistent Neuropsychiatric Symptoms

summary: This cross-sectional study using the 2022 National Survey on Health and Disability examines unmet healthcare needs among people with pre-existing disabilities who have long COVID, finding that 73% reported unmet needs compared to 62.6% without long COVID. The paper identifies themes including healthcare system navigation challenges, provider gaslighting, and financial burdens, but does not study or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Darcy L. Sullivan; Kelsey Goddard; Noelle K. Kurth; Jean P. Hall
paper_title: "I'm in Hell …": Experiences of Unmet Health Care Needs Among People with Pre-Existing Disability and Long COVID
paper_journal: Journal of Health Care for the Poor and Underserved

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed life quality and health perception among 337 recovered COVID-19 patients using a 26-item questionnaire. Results show that 46% of respondents reported COVID-19 negatively affected their quality of life and health, with risk increasing with symptom count, duration, and severity.
paper_authors: Natalia Zięba; Grażyna Stryjewska-Makuch; Karolina Goroszkiewicz; Maciej Zieliński; Adam Dadok; Barbara Pietrzyk; Julia Gajewska; Katarzyna Miśkiewicz-Orczyk; Grażyna Lisowska
paper_title: Assessment of life quality and health perception among recovered COVID-19 patients: multivariate analysis – own material and a review of previous reports on life quality assessment among convalescents

summary: Cross-sectional study of 953 healthcare workers with COVID-19 assessing prevalence and risk factors for neuropsychological manifestations including both acute and long COVID symptoms. Found 72.6% had neuropsychological manifestations acutely, with memory impairment, anosmia, and headache being common long COVID symptoms; associations identified with age, gender, smoking, and comorbidities.
paper_authors: Amal Ghenim; Imène Kacem; A. Chouchane; Asma Aloui; Sridi Chaima; A. Fekih; M. Hafsia; Maher Maoua; Mohamed Kahloul; N. Mrizak
paper_title: The neuro-psychological manifestations of COVID-19 in healthcareworkers

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of the 2022 National Health Interview Survey examining associations between medical history, COVID vaccination, and long COVID development in US adults. Found that chronic conditions (obesity, hypertension, asthma, anxiety, depression) and older age were associated with higher long COVID risk, while prior COVID vaccination was associated with lower risk.
paper_authors: Robert Post
paper_title: The association of medical and vaccination history with the development of long COVID

summary: This cross-sectional study compared insulin resistance prevalence and determinants in 510 Ghanaian adults with and without prior COVID-19 infection. It found higher insulin resistance prevalence in those with past COVID-19, but made no treatment assessments.
paper_authors: Ansumana Sandy Bockarie; Leonard Derkyi-Kwarteng; Jeffrey Amankona Obeng; Richard Kujo Adatsi; Ebenezer Aniakwaa-Bonsu; Charles Apprey; Jerry Ampofo-Asiama; Samuel Acquah
paper_title: Prevalence and determinants of insulin resistance in recovered COVID-19 and uninfected residents of two regional capitals in Ghana: An observational study

summary: This cross-sectional study compares the prevalence of long-COVID symptoms in non-hospitalized COVID-19 positive patients (n=1,410) versus negative patients (n=1,129) in primary care using electronic health records and questionnaires. The study found long-COVID symptoms significantly more prevalent in COVID-positive patients, with fatigue (59.5% vs 41.3%), difficulty sleeping (52.1% vs 41.9%), and concentration problems (50.6% vs 28.5%) being most common.
paper_authors: Dominik Ose; Elena Gardner; Andrew Curtin; Kirsten Stoesser; Mingyuan Zhang; Jennifer Leiser; Bernadette Kiraly
paper_title: Prevalence of long-COVID symptoms among non-hospitalized patients in primary care – Part 1 of 3

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed pulmonary function, exercise tolerance, and quality of life in 207 Indian subjects who recovered from COVID-19, comparing those with prior pneumonia to those with mild disease. The study found significant impairment in lung function (restrictive defects, reduced DLCO) and exercise capacity in the COVID-19 pneumonia group, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Devasahayam Jesudas Christopher; Barney T. J. Isaac; Flavita Benna John; Deepa Shankar; Prasanna Samuel; Richa Gupta; Balamugesh Thangakunam
paper_title: Impact of post-COVID-19 lung damage on pulmonary function, exercise tolerance and quality of life in Indian subjects

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 483 women from Jordan and Iraq examining menstrual cycle changes following COVID-19 infection. Found that 47.2% reported changes in cycle length or blood loss, with perceptions of COVID-19 impact varying by education level, location, marital status, and smoking status.
paper_authors: Mohammad A. A. Al-Najjar; Ruaa R. Al-alwany; Firas M. Al-Rshoud; Rana K. Abu-Farha; Mohammed Zawiah
paper_title: Menstrual changes following COVID-19 infection: A cross-sectional study from Jordan and Iraq

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 396 Egyptian patients examining prevalence and predictors of post-COVID symptoms. Found 87.63% prevalence with fatigue as most common symptom; identified severe disease, antibiotics, and corticosteroids as predictors but did not evaluate any intervention.
paper_authors: Ahmed Samir Abdelhafiz; Asmaa Ali; Ayman Mohamed Maaly; Mohamed Anwar Mahgoub; Hany Hassan Ziady; Eman Anwar Sultan
paper_title: Predictors of post-COVID symptoms in Egyptian patients: Drugs used in COVID-19 treatment are incriminated

summary: This cross-sectional survey of 979 Saudi Arabian COVID-19 patients describes the prevalence and severity of long-term post-recovery symptoms across multiple body systems, including fatigue, neurological symptoms, sensory loss, and gastrointestinal effects. The study proposes a classification system for post-COVID symptoms but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Mostafa M. Khodeir; Hassan A. Shabana; Zafar Rasheed; Abdullah S. Alkhamiss; Mohamed Khodeir; Mohammad S. Alkhowailed; Sami Alharbi; Mansour Alsoghair; Suliman A. Alsagaby; Waleed Al Abdulmonem
paper_title: COVID-19: Post-recovery long-term symptoms among patients in Saudi Arabia

summary: Online cross-sectional survey of 732 COVID-19 survivors in Malaysia examining prevalence and associations of long COVID symptoms. Found 20% reported long COVID with fatigue, brain fog, depression, anxiety and insomnia as common symptoms; females and those with moderate/severe acute COVID had higher odds of long COVID.
paper_authors: Foong Ming Moy; Noran Naqiah Hairi; Eugene Ri Jian Lim; Awang Bulgiba
paper_title: Long COVID and its associated factors among COVID survivors in the community from a middle-income country—An online cross-sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional study of 1,164 long COVID patients in Brazil evaluating symptomatology, complications, and quality of life 2-3 months post-acute infection. Found high prevalence of dyspnea, fatigue, and chest pain, with newly diagnosed metabolic disorders and post-acute hospitalization in a majority black/mixed-race population.
paper_authors: Ana Paula Andrade Barreto; Marcio Andrade Barreto Filho; Lucimeire Cardoso Duarte; Thiago Cerqueira-Silva; Aquiles Camelier; Natalia Machado Tavares; Manoel Barral-Netto; Viviane Boaventura; Marcelo Chalhoub Coelho Lima
paper_title: Metabolic disorders and post-acute hospitalization in black/mixed-race patients with long COVID in Brazil: A cross-sectional analysis

summary: Cross-sectional study examining menstrual cycle changes in 956 Saudi females following SARS-CoV-2 infection, stratified by vaccination status and COVID-19 severity. Found 26.1% of unvaccinated and 15.3-26.4% of vaccinated individuals reported menstrual changes, with 6.4% experiencing persistence beyond six months, correlating with infection severity.
paper_authors: Youssef A. S. Abdel-Moneim; Hussam Y. Alghamdi; Abdulaziz M. Alrashed; Amjad M. Jawhari; Suhaib M. M. Bukhari; Nirmeen M. M. Bukhari; Ahmed S. Abdel-Moneim
paper_title: Menstrual cycle changes: A cross-sectional study of Saudi females following SARS-CoV-2 infection

summary: Cross-sectional study of 198 COVID-19 convalescent patients examining the incidence and predictors of fibromyalgia syndrome post-infection. Found 15% incidence of post-COVID fibromyalgia, associated with female gender, high traumatic stress, and low resilience, but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Einat Savin; Gali Rosenn; Avishai M. Tsur; Or Hen; Scott Ehrenberg; Omer Gendelman; Dan Buskila; Gilad Halpert; Daniela Amital; Howard Amital
paper_title: The possible onset of fibromyalgia following acute COVID-19 infection

summary: This cross-sectional study uses National Health Interview Survey data to examine whether COVID-19 severity is a risk factor for chronic pain, comparing pain prevalence across infection severity groups. It finds that moderate/severe COVID-19 infection is associated with higher odds of chronic pain, but does not test or evaluate any intervention.
paper_authors: Jamie L. Romeiser; Christopher P. Morley; Sunitha M. Singh
paper_title: COVID-19 symptom load as a risk factor for chronic pain: A national cross-sectional study

summary: Secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial examining loss of socioemotional and occupational roles in 100 long COVID patients in primary care. Study found median loss of 3 roles, with cognitive impairment and lack of active work role as predictors, but does not test or evaluate a specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Sandra León-Herrera; Mario Samper-Pardo; Bárbara Oliván-Blázquez; Raquel Sánchez-Recio; Rosa Magallón-Botaya; Rafael Sánchez-Arizcuren
paper_title: Loss of socioemotional and occupational roles in individuals with Long COVID according to sociodemographic and clinical factors: Secondary data from a randomized clinical trial

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 990 Jordanian respondents assessing long COVID prevalence, symptoms, and associated risk factors. Found significant associations between long COVID and age, obesity, chronic illness, vitamin D intake, and infection history, with tinnitus, concentration problems, and musculoskeletal pain as most common symptoms.
paper_authors: Marya Obeidat; Abdulmalek Abu Zahra; Farah Alsattari
paper_title: Prevalence and characteristics of long COVID-19 in Jordan: A cross sectional survey

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing pro-inflammatory SARS-CoV-2-specific cytokine levels in recovered COVID-19 and long-COVID patients versus unexposed controls. Found elevated IL-1β and IL-6 in long-COVID group but no interventions or treatments were tested.
paper_authors: Shayane Martins Rodrigues Gomes; Andréia Carolinne de Souza Brito; Wânia Ferraz Pereira Manfro; Marcelo Ribeiro-Alves; Roberto Stefan de Almeida Ribeiro; Mariana Soares da Cal; Vinicius da Cunha Lisboa; Daniel Paiva Barros de Abreu; Leda dos Reis Castilho; Luís Cristóvão de Moares Sobrino Porto; Thiago Thomáz Mafort; Agnaldo José Lopes; Silvia Amaral Gonçalves da Silva; Patrícia Maria Lourenço Dutra; Luciana Silva Rodrigues
paper_title: High levels of pro-inflammatory SARS-CoV-2-specific biomarkers revealed by in vitro whole blood cytokine release assay (CRA) in recovered and long-COVID-19 patients

summary: A cross-sectional study documenting the incidence, characteristics, and risk factors of post-COVID chronic pain in Thailand from 1,019 participants assessed 3-6 months post-infection. Female sex and greater COVID-19 severity were identified as significant risk factors, with overall chronic pain incidence of 3.2%.
paper_authors: Suratsawadee Wangnamthip; Nantthasorn Zinboonyahgoon; Pranee Rushatamukayanunt; Patcha Papaisarn; Burapa Pajina; Thanawut Jitsinthunun; Panuwat Promsin; Rujipas Sirijatuphat; César Fernández-de-las-Peñas; Lars Arendt-Nielsen; Daniel Ciampi de Andrade
paper_title: The incidence, characteristics, impact and risk factors of post-COVID chronic pain in Thailand: A single-center cross-sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional study of 939 recovered COVID-19 patients in Thailand examining prevalence of long COVID symptoms (79.3%) and mental health status (depression 11.1%, anxiety 19.1%, stress 4.8%). Found significant associations between long COVID symptoms (especially fatigue, shortness of breath, chest tightness) and mental health disorders, with female sex, medical history, and low income as risk factors.
paper_authors: Doan Hoang Phu; Sarunya Maneerattanasak; Shamarina Shohaimi; Le Thanh Thao Trang; Truong Thanh Nam; Muminah Kuning; Aunchalee Like; Hameedah Torpor; Charuai Suwanbamrung
paper_title: Prevalence and factors associated with long COVID and mental health status among recovered COVID-19 patients in southern Thailand

summary: Population-based cross-sectional study using US Census Bureau Household Pulse Survey data (June-December 2022) to characterize long COVID prevalence, demographic patterns, and associations with mental health and functional impairment. While descriptive of long COVID burden, this observational epidemiological study does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: David G. Blanchflower; Alex Bryson
paper_title: Long COVID in the United States

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 460 long COVID patients examining associations between substance use, psychiatric symptoms, and psychosocial factors. Found high rates of substance use (tobacco 82%, opioids 67%, cocaine 53%) positively associated with depression, anxiety, and PTSD, while personal mastery and social support were protective factors.
paper_authors: Cheuk Chi Tam; Shan Qiao; Camryn Garrett; Ran Zhang; Atefeh Aghaei; Abhishek Aggarwal; Alain H. Litwin; Xiaoming Li
paper_title: Substance use, psychiatric symptoms, personal mastery, and social support among COVID-19 long haulers: A compensatory model

summary: This cross-sectional observational study compared 33 long COVID patients who underwent pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) with 32 who did not, evaluating respiratory function and exercise capacity using the 6-minute walk test. Patients receiving PR showed significantly better walking distance, less dynamic hyperinflation, and improved impulse oscillometry findings compared to controls, suggesting PR provides measurable pulmonary benefits in post-acute COVID-19 syndrome.
paper_authors: Renan Pereira Campos; Jéssica Gabriela Messias Oliveira; Iasmim de Oliveira Farias; Viviane Cristina Viana de Souza; Samantha Gomes de Alegria; Rosemere Saldanha Xavier; Agnaldo José Lopes
paper_title: Effects of pulmonary rehabilitation on ventilation dynamics measured during exertion in patients with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome: A cross-sectional observational study

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 416 long COVID patients examining symptom prevalence, disease burden, and impact on work/quality of life across demographics and vaccination status. Study characterizes long COVID as a heterogeneous condition affecting multiple life domains but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Manuel Leitner; Gloria Pötz; Martin Berger; Maria Fellner; Stephan Spat; Marisa Koini
paper_title: Characteristics and burden of acute COVID-19 and long-COVID: Demographic, physical, mental health, and economic perspectives

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 609 healthcare workers assessing prevalence and predictors of post-acute COVID syndrome (PACS). Found 50.7% prevalence with fatigue, cough, and musculoskeletal pain as most common symptoms; female sex, asthma, and COVID severity were risk factors while booster vaccination was protective.
paper_authors: Say Hiang Lim; Yin Cheng Lim; Rafdzah Ahmad Zaki; Bushra Megat Johari; Chung Yuan Chang; Sharifah Faridah Syed Omar; Amirah Azzeri; Maznah Dahlui; Adeeba Kamarulzaman
paper_title: Prevalence and predictors of post-acute COVID syndrome among infected healthcare workers at University Malaya Medical Centre

summary: This cross-sectional survey of 468 COVID-19 survivors examines the prevalence and risk factors for otological symptoms (tinnitus, hearing loss, aural fullness, dizziness) weeks to months after infection. Sex, age, initial symptom duration, and vaccination status were identified as risk factors for various otological manifestations of long COVID.
paper_authors: Qiang Wang; Hailing Gu; Jianjun Ren; Yu Zhao; Zhaoli Meng
paper_title: Analysis of characteristics of and risk factors for otological symptoms after COVID-19 infection

summary: Cross-sectional characterization of 267 long COVID patients enrolled in the MedStar COVID Recovery Program, assessing clinical symptoms, quality-of-life, fatigue, and work productivity. Participants showed significant impairment across all domains, with 63% reporting activity impairment and 61% experiencing work productivity loss.
paper_authors: Suzanne M. Simkovich; Naheed Ahmed; Jiling Chou; Asli McCullers; Eric M. Wisotzky; Jennifer Semel; Kathryn Pellegrino; Derek DeLia; William S. Weintraub
paper_title: Health, social, and economic characteristics of patients enrolled in a COVID-19 recovery program

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing quality of life in 150 COVID-19 recovered patients in Ghana using EQ-5D-5L and EQ-VAS instruments. Found relatively good QoL overall, with symptom persistence and rehabilitation access as significant predictors, but this is an observational assessment study without any intervention or treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Esinam Aku Amedewonu; Genevieve Cecilia Aryeetey; Anthony Godi; Josephine Sackeyfio; Alfred Dickson Dai-Kosi
paper_title: Assessment of the quality of life of COVID-19 recovered patients at the Ghana Infectious Disease Centre

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence and determinants of post-acute COVID-19 syndrome among 340 severe COVID-19 survivors at 2-year follow-up in Ethiopia. It identified risk factors including older age, female sex, comorbidities, and alcohol use as predictors of PACS, with fatigue and cough being the most common persistent symptoms (38.1% prevalence overall).
paper_authors: Tamrat Petros Elias; Tsegaye Wesenseged Gebreamlak; Tigist Tesfaye Gebremeskel; Binyam Lukas Adde; Abraham Sisay Abie; Bitaniya Petros Elias; Abel Mureja Argaw; Addis Aschenek Tenaw; Biruk Mulugeta Belay
paper_title: Determinants of post-acute COVID-19 syndrome among hospitalized severe COVID-19 patients: A 2-year follow-up study

summary: Cross-sectional web survey of 138 Medicaid enrollees assessing PASC symptom prevalence and associations with sociodemographic characteristics and comorbidities, stratified by HIV status. Found no significant difference in PASC symptoms between individuals with and without HIV, but identified inadequate income and comorbidities (cardiac, cancer, fibromyalgia) as independent predictors of higher symptom burden.
paper_authors: Yiyi Wu; Eleni Mattas; Carey Brandenburg; Ethan Fusaris; Richard Overbey; Jerome Ernst; Mark Brennan-Ing
paper_title: The association of sociodemographic characteristics and comorbidities with post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 in a Medicaid managed care population with and without HIV

summary: Cross-sectional study of 41 hospitalized COVID-19 patients assessed ~2 years post-discharge using comprehensive neuropsychological testing. Found that greater COVID-19 severity was associated with more brain fog symptoms, worse global cognitive functioning, and reduced attention/working memory performance.
paper_authors: Barbara Junco; Daniel Samano Martin Del Campo; Vela Karakeshishyan; Danielle Bass; Evie Sobczak; Emily Swafford; Ana Bolanos; Joshua Rooks; Bernard S. Baumel; Alberto R. Ramos; Tatjana Rundek; Ayham Alkhachroum
paper_title: Long-term brain fog and cognitive impairment in previously hospitalized COVID-19 patients

summary: This study analyzes Reddit communication patterns of 6,107 users before and after COVID-19 to identify psychological and linguistic traits associated with Long COVID development. The research is observational and does not involve any treatment intervention, focusing instead on identifying pre-existing risk factors through social media text analysis.
paper_authors: Ludovica Segneri; Nandor Babina; Teresa Hammerschmidt; Andrea Fronzetti Colladon; Peter A. Gloor
paper_title: Too much focus on your health might be bad for your health: Reddit user’s communication style predicts their Long COVID likelihood

summary: Cross-sectional analysis using 2022 National Health Interview Survey data examining financial toxicity in Long COVID patients compared to other comorbidities. Finds that adults with Long COVID experience significantly higher financial hardship than those with epilepsy, dementia, cancer, or cardiovascular/respiratory conditions, with vulnerable populations at greatest risk.
paper_authors: Han Su; Hilaire J. Thompson; Karl Cristie Figuracion; Mayur Bipin Patel; Dale M. Needham
paper_title: Comparative analysis of financial toxicity between SARS-CoV-2 infection and common comorbidities

summary: Cross-sectional study using 2022 BRFSS data examining health-related quality of life (HRQL) among 108,237 US COVID survivors, comparing those with post-COVID conditions (PCCs) to those without. Finds that PCC-positive survivors report significantly worse HRQL across general health, mental health, physical health, and daily functioning, with dizziness on standing, mood changes, and musculoskeletal pain most strongly associated with poor HRQL.
paper_authors: Seyyed Sina Hejazian; Ajith Vemuri; Alireza Vafaei Sadr; Shima Shahjouei; Sasan Bahrami; Zhou Shouhao; Vida Abedi; Ramin Zand
paper_title: The health-related quality of life among survivors with post-COVID conditions in the United States

summary: Cross-sectional study of 249 long COVID patients at a dedicated clinic identifying factors associated with symptom presence and intensity. Found anxiety symptoms, longer COVID-19 duration, and hypercholesterolemia correlated with greater symptom burden, but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Brinkman N.; Teunis T.; Choi S.; Ring D.; Brode WM
paper_title: Factors associated with the presence and intensity of ongoing symptoms in Long COVID

summary: Population-based cross-sectional survey of 9,825 adults assessing ME/CFS-like illness prevalence in a large integrated health system. Found 1.67% prevalence overall, with 14.12% of ME/CFS cases developing after COVID-19, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Mariah S. Wood; Nicole Halmer; Jeanne Bertolli; Laura B. Amsden; Joshua R. Nugent; Jin-Mann S. Lin; Gretchen Rothrock; Joelle Nadle; Shua J. Chai; Jennifer R. Cope; Jamila H. Champsi; James Yang; Elizabeth R. Unger; Jacek Skarbinski
paper_title: Impact of COVID-19 on myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome-like illness prevalence: A cross-sectional survey

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 209 Indiana residents examining the association between self-reported periodontal disease and long COVID symptoms, with attention to socioeconomic disparities. Found significant associations between periodontal disease markers (bleeding gums, tooth loss, gum disease) and reduced sense of taste/smell in long COVID patients, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Sara Alhaffar; Sriha Yalamanchi; Anubhuti Shukla
paper_title: Association of self-reported periodontal disease and inequities with long haul COVID-19

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing health symptoms across post-COVID-19, ex-COVID, and non-infected individuals using merged survey and primary care data from 315,586 respondents. Post-COVID-19 individuals reported significantly more frequent, longer-lasting, and more severe symptoms compared to both ex-COVID and non-infected groups.
paper_authors: Gerbecks J.; Yzermans CJ; Dückers MLA; Bosmans M.; Baliatsas C.
paper_title: Health symptoms and post-COVID-19: Comparing symptomatic groups based on self-reported and primary care data

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 374 Spanish long-COVID patients examining relationships between fatigue severity, mood disturbances, and other clinical manifestations using validated scales (FSS and EVEA). The study found significant correlations between fatigue, anxiety/depression, and neurological, psychological, locomotive, and pain symptoms, but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Esther Bahillo Ruiz; Lucía Pérez-Pérez; Rosa M. Cárdaba-García; Carlos Durantez-Fernández; Lourdes Jiménez-Navascués; Veronica Velasco-Gonzalez; Alba Muñoz-del Caz; Miguel Madrigal; Elena Olea
paper_title: Relationships between fatigue severity scale (FSS)/ scale for mood assessment (EVEA) and clinical manifestations in spanish long-COVID patients

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 4,231 Brazilians examining the prevalence of long COVID (56.4%) and identifying associated factors including sex, vaccination status, comorbidities, hospitalization, and health-related behaviors. This is an observational study of disease prevalence and risk factors, not a treatment trial, so it does not meet inclusion criteria for the clinical trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: José Francisco Martoreli Júnior; Andrey O. Pedroso; Laís do E. S. Lima; Cristine Maria P. Gusmão; Mayra G. Menegueti; Hemílio F. C. Coêlho; Cristina Mara Zamarioli; Ana Cristina de O. e. Silva; Glenda R. O. Naiff; Elucir Gir; Renata K. Reis
paper_title: Prevalence and associated factors with long COVID in the Brazilian population: The role of health-related behaviors and sociodemographic characteristics

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of 734 COVID-19 survivors examining associations between skeletal muscle parameters and kidney function 7 months post-discharge. Found skeletal muscle mass associated with eGFR but sarcopenia not independently associated with poor kidney function outcomes.
paper_authors: Heitor S. Ribeiro; Dário R. Mondini; Guilherme P. Santa-Catharina; Lia Marçal; Leila Antonângelo; Luis Yu; Dirce M. T. Zanetta; Linamara R. Battistella; Geraldo F. Busatto; Carlos R. R. Carvalho; Emmanuel A. Burdmann
paper_title: Skeletal muscle-kidney crosstalk in a cohort of critical illness survivors

summary: Cross-sectional study of 1,587 long COVID patients from British Columbia clinics examining associations between COVID-19 vaccination status, SARS-CoV-2 variants, and symptom severity using patient-reported outcome measures. Found that full vaccination was associated with reduced PTSD likelihood in non-hospitalized patients, and infection with alpha/delta variants was associated with increased dyspnea reporting.
paper_authors: Saif-El-Din El-Akkad; Selena Shao; Karen C. Tran; Hiten Naik; Naveed Janjua; Hind Sbihi; Christopher Carlsten; James A. Russell; Adeera Levin; Alyson W. Wong
