paper_journal: Revista do Instituto de Medicina Tropical de São Paulo

summary: Cross-sectional observational study assessing the prevalence of neurological complications in 385 post-COVID-19 patients using the Edinburgh Questionnaire. Found high prevalence of fatigue (73.5%), muscle weakness (66.2%), and chronic pain (64.1%), but no intervention or treatment was tested.
paper_authors: Garvisha Sudhir Janorkar; Quazi Ibtesaam Huma
paper_title: Prevalence of Neurological Complications amongst Post-COVID-19 Patients Using the Edinburgh Questionnaire: A Cross-Sectional Study in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra
paper_journal: International Journal of Physiotherapy and Research

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluates the effect of oxygen concentrators on oxygen saturation in 108 patients (42 using concentrators, 66 not) presenting to a pulmonology clinic after COVID-19 infection. Patients using oxygen concentrators were older, had longer hospital stays, higher rates of pulmonary involvement, and lower oxygen saturation levels, suggesting that dyspnea during acute infection predicts later need for supplemental oxygen.
paper_authors: Zuhal Yavuz Dağlı; Duygu Yengil Taci; İzzet Fidancı
paper_title: Effect of Using Oxygen Concentrators on Oxygen Saturation after COVID-19 Infection

summary: Cross-sectional study examining burnout among nursing home care providers and its association with work stress, fatigue, and coping during the COVID-19 pandemic. While 85.7% of care providers reported long COVID symptoms, the study does not evaluate any treatment or intervention for long COVID patients—it studies occupational health outcomes in healthcare workers.
paper_authors: Hyunju Lee; Youngja Seo; Jihye Kim; Hye Young Song; Jinhee Park; Youngran Yang
paper_title: The impact of Long COVID, work stress related to infectious diseases, fatigue, and coping on burnout among care providers in nursing home: A cross-sectional correlation study

summary: This cross-sectional study examined the association between post-COVID sleep disturbance (PCSD) and neurocognitive function in 8,692 COVID-19 survivors using propensity score matching. The study found that nearly half of survivors reported sleep disturbance, which was significantly associated with impaired cognitive performance on standardized tests.
paper_authors: Shixu Du; Leqin Fang; Yuanhui Li; Shuai Liu; Xue Luo; Shufei Zeng; Shuqiong Zheng; Hangyi Yang; Yan Xu; Dai Li; Bin Zhang
paper_title: Association between post-COVID-19 sleep disturbance and neurocognitive function: a comparative study based on propensity score matching

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing quality of life outcomes in 60 patients with neurological post-COVID syndrome manifestations (headaches, pain, fatigue, cognitive/mood symptoms) versus 20 controls with only the underlying neurological disease. Found that age >40, high anxiety, depressive and asthenic syndromes negatively affect QOL in post-COVID patients.
paper_authors: Peretechikova AV; Voskresenskaya ON
paper_title: Factors affecting the quality of life of patients with neurological manifestations of post-COVID syndrome
paper_journal: S.S. Korsakov Journal of Neurology and Psychiatry

summary: Cross-sectional online survey of 101 long COVID patients assessing fatigue and functional status one year post-infection using the Chalder Fatigue Scale and post-COVID functional status scale. Found that 38.61% reported fatigue and most participants had minimal to no functional limitations.
paper_authors: Tanvi Kelkar; Mandar Malawade
paper_title: Prevalence of Fatigue and Reduced Functional Status One Year Post-COVID 19 Infection
paper_journal: International Journal of Physiotherapy and Research

summary: Retrospective cross-sectional study of 265 military sailors in the Arctic examining risk factors for COVID-19 severity during the first and second waves. Found that 88.7% of those who recovered showed post-COVID syndrome symptoms (asthenia, dyspnea, dyssomnia, arthralgia), with age >35 and lower education as risk factors for more severe disease.
paper_authors: A.S. Dybin; P.Yu. Shapovalov; Sergey P. Yanborisov; Oleg A. Tumilovich; E.A. Mordovskiy
paper_title: Risk factors for the development of the disease and predictors of the severity of the course of COVID-19 of the first and second waves in military sailors serving in the Arctic zone of Russia

summary: Cross-sectional study of 665 long COVID patients identifying 7 main clinical phenotypes and their associations with demographic factors, acute COVID severity, and comorbidities. Observational study with no treatment intervention—patients were surveyed about symptoms and disease course rather than receiving or being evaluated for any treatment.
paper_authors: A.V. Isaeva; M.V. Vetluzhskaya; A.N. Korobeynikova; A.V. Vlasova
paper_title: Clinical phenotypes and features of the post-COVID syndrome course

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing hemodynamics, autonomic regulation, and psychological stress resistance in 69 university students with and without prior COVID-19 infection (1.5-2.5 years post-infection). Students with prior COVID-19 showed persistent differences in cardiovascular function, sympathetic nervous system predominance, and elevated stress markers compared to unaffected peers.
paper_authors: M.V. Kuropatenko; T.V. Novikova; E.A. Agapova; A.S. Anisimova; T.V. Sergeev
paper_title: Impact of the COVID-19 epidemic on students’ health. Part II. Features of hemodynamics, vegetative regulation, results of psychological and stress resistance testing among students depending on the COVID-19 presence in their medical history

summary: Population-based telephone survey of 398 adults discharged from hospital post-COVID-19 assessing prevalence and types of long COVID symptoms. Found 31.5% reported persistent symptoms, with female sex, higher education, and obesity as associated factors, but no intervention or treatment was tested.
paper_authors: Debbie Ehrmann Feldman; Marie-Hélène Boudrias; Barbara Mazer
paper_title: Long COVID symptoms in a population-based sample of persons discharged home from hospital

summary: Population-based cross-sectional survey of Canadian adults conducted April-August 2022 investigating factors associated with post COVID-19 condition occurrence, severity, and resolution. Found 17.2% of confirmed infection cases experienced PCC, with female sex, comorbidities, and severe initial infection as major risk factors; no treatment intervention was studied.
paper_authors: Dianne Zakaria; Alain Demers; Nicholas Cheta; Samina Aziz; Peri Abdullah
paper_title: Factors associated with the development, severity, and resolution of post COVID-19 condition in adults living in Canada, January 2020 to August 2022

summary: This cross-sectional study examines factors influencing long COVID patients' willingness to pay for digital medical platforms using structural equation modeling and stress-coping theory on 371 patients. The research shows that role stress and coping strategies significantly predict patients' behavioral intentions toward digital health platform adoption, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Jing Yao Han; Kyong Jin Park
paper_title: A Composite Study on Influence Factors of the “Long Covid” Patients’ Willingness to Pay of Digital Medical Platforms
paper_journal: The Korean Society of Science & Art

summary: This cross-sectional observational study examines autonomic nervous system function in young adults with a history of mild-to-moderate COVID-19 compared to healthy controls. The research investigates whether body mass index and physical activity levels modulate autonomic function differences between COVID-19-infected and uninfected participants.
paper_authors: Ana Paula Freire
paper_title: BODY MASS AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY IN AUTONOMIC FUNCTION MODULATION ON POST-COVID-19 CONDITION: AN OBSERVATIONAL SUBANALYSIS OF FIT-COVID STUDY

summary: This cross-sectional study examined electrocardiographic abnormalities in 225 COVID-19 convalescents and their association with cardiometabolic parameters and inflammatory markers. ECG abnormalities were found in 29.3% of convalescents and were associated with male sex and elevated IL-6 levels.
paper_authors: Alexandra A. Karaseva; Alena D. Afanaseva; Evgeniia V. Garbuzova; Alexandr A. Kuznetsov; Victoria S. Shramko
paper_title: Electrocardiographic abnormalities in COVID-19 convalescents: a cross-sectional study

summary: This cross-sectional study examined lipid profile parameters (cholesterol, HDL, LDL, VLDL, triglycerides) in COVID-19 donors with varying anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG titers to investigate biochemical changes in the post-COVID period. The study found significant variations in lipid concentrations across different antibody titer groups, suggesting potential cardiovascular disease risk in long COVID patients, but did not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Antonina Rachkovska; Kuntsova Margaryta; Daryna Krenytska; Olexiy Savchuk; Vitaliy Karbovskiy
paper_title: PARAMETERS OF THE LIPID PROFILE IN DONORS WHO HAD SUFFERED FROM COVID-19 AND HAD VARIOUS TITERS OF ANTI-SARS-CoV-2 IgG IN BLOOD PLASMA
paper_journal: Bulletin of Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv. Series: Biology

summary: A cross-sectional observational study evaluating clinical manifestations and functional impacts in 137 long COVID patients 3-12 months post-infection, stratified by presence/absence of prior comorbidities. Patients with comorbidities showed significantly greater impairments in mobility, work productivity, physical functionality, and cognitive function compared to those without comorbidities.
paper_authors: Thalyta Cibele P. Santos; Pammela Weryka S. Santos; Samara A. Souza; Pedro Henrique L. S. Santos; Hevan S. Torres; Maria Eduarda C. B. Nascimento; Abrahão F. Baptista; Fuad A. Hazime
paper_title: Clinical manifestations in POST-COVID-19 patients

summary: A cross-sectional observational study examining caspase-6 levels and inflammatory markers in 186 long COVID patients with dyspnea compared to controls. The study identifies associations between severe acute COVID-19 pneumonia and reduced caspase-6 levels, arterial stiffness, and elevated inflammatory markers in the post-COVID period.
paper_authors: Olga V. Masalkina; Anna I. Chernyavina; Natalya A. Koziolova; Elena A. Polyanskaya
paper_title: Factors influencing caspase-6 levels in patients with dyspnea associated with long COVID

summary: Cross-sectional observational study of 103 post-COVID-19 patients examining the relationship between pain and functional capacity using VAS, dynamometry, and functional status assessments. Found significant correlations between pain severity and reduced muscle strength/functionality, with age associated with worse performance in mobility tasks.
paper_authors: Leticia Emilly Mesquita de Sousa; Larisse Da Silva Gomes; Wysllana Marinho Machado; Thalyta Cibele Passos dos Santos; Pammela Weryka da Silva Santos; Fuad Ahmad Hazime; Baldomero Antonio Kato da Silva
paper_title: Analysis of functionality in patients with post-COVID-19 pain

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing cognitive impairment in COVID-19 patients and developing a prognostic scale for psychopharmacotherapy selection. Identified risk factors (lower education, older age, endocrine disorders, elevated respiratory rate) but did not test or evaluate a specific intervention.
paper_authors: Mikhail Y. Sorokin; Ekaterina S. Gerasimchuk; Natalia B. Lutova; Elena Y. Zubova
paper_title: Cross-sectional study of the risk of cognitive impairment associated with COVID-19 and a prognostic scale for psychopharmacotherapy selection in outpatient settings

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluates detailed screening procedures for detecting post-COVID-19 consequences in 970 patients, assessing physical function, pulmonary status, and comorbidities. While the paper identifies high prevalence of respiratory impairment and multimorbidity in post-COVID patients, it does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention, only screening protocols.
paper_authors: D.A. Anikin; I.V. Demko; A.E. Cupinin; A.E. Kudro; I.V. Nazhivin
paper_title: Results of detailed screening of patients who have undergone a novel coronavirus infection COVID-19

summary: A cross-sectional study describing the most frequent symptoms in post-COVID-19 patients in Paraguay during 2021. The study documents persistent symptoms including fatigue, dyspnea, anosmia, and neurological manifestations following acute SARS-CoV-2 infection.
paper_authors: Manuel Esteban Codas; Karem Alejandra Torres Villagra; Cesar Adrian Barrios Gayoso
paper_title: LONG COVID, most frequent symptoms in post-COVID-19 patients, Paraguay, 2021
paper_journal: Revista Virtual de la Sociedad Paraguaya de Medicina Interna

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed working capacity and mental state in 62 young COVID-19 convalescents at 90 days post-discharge using psychological questionnaires. The majority showed reduced working capacity and asthenic syndrome, attributed to post-illness fatigue and post-traumatic stress disorder symptoms.
paper_authors: Igor M. Uliukin; Aleksey A. Sechin; Vadim V. Rassokhin; Elena S. Orlova; Alyona A. Shuklina
paper_title: Differential diagnosis of states of operability in young people who have had COVID-19 infection

summary: This cross-sectional screening study identified predictors of newly diagnosed chronic heart failure in 878 long COVID patients with shortness of breath. While about long COVID and using a valid study design, it does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment—it is purely observational/epidemiological in nature.
paper_authors: Masalkina OV; Chernyavina AI; Koziolova NA; Polyanskaya EA; Mironova SV; Ulybina EV
paper_title: Predictors of the Development of Newly Diagnosed Chronic Heart Failure in Patients with Shortness of Breath in Long-Term Post-COVID Syndrome

summary: This OECD PaRIS survey assessed Long COVID prevalence and impact in 107,011 primary care patients aged 45+ across 19 countries (2023-2024), finding ~7% reported ever having Long COVID and ~5% reported current symptoms. The study documents worse self-rated health and healthcare experiences in Long COVID patients but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Nicolas Larrain; K. D. Bienassis; Federico Pratellesi; Elina Suzuki; Michael Berg; Frederico Guanais; Francesca Colombo; M. Pearson; S. Scarpetta; D. Kelly
paper_title: The prevalence and impact of Long COVID in the primary care population

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluated long-term persistent symptoms and quality of life in 231 mild COVID-19 outpatients using adapted questionnaires. The findings show that non-hospitalized patients experience persistent symptoms (dyspnea, fatigue, cognitive impairment, headache), with higher symptom frequency in younger patients and women, but no treatment or intervention is tested.
paper_authors: Patrícia Candido; Luís Mendonça; Paulo Pereira; Elisa Valente; Camila Morais; Michael Miranda; Samuel Câmara; Poliana Romão; Eunice Higuchi; João Manzano; Katia Leite; Ruan Pimenta; Victor Srougi; Sabrina Reis
paper_title: Long-Term Effects of COVID-19 and Health-Related Quality of Life of Mild Cases an outpatient clinic

summary: This cross-sectional study surveyed 105 people living with HIV to examine associations between long COVID (PASC) symptoms and health-related quality of life using the EQ-5D instrument. The study found that PASC symptoms were significantly associated with poorer quality of life outcomes, but it is observational only with no treatment intervention tested.
paper_authors: Yiyi Wu; Carey Brandenburg; Luis Scaccbarrozzi; Richard Overbey; Jerome Ernst; Mark Ing
paper_title: Associations Between Long COVID Symptoms and Health-related Quality of Life among a Medicaid Managed Care Population Living with HIV

summary: Cross-sectional study surveying 5,770 family caregivers of COVID-19 survivors in Punjab, Pakistan to quantify economic burden using structural equation modeling. Identified that female caregivers over 45, unemployed, with low income, and those performing household/medical/personal care tasks faced higher financial strain.
paper_authors: Shumaila Abbas; Jamal Abdul Nasir
paper_title: Estimating the Economic Burden of Family Caregivers of COVID-19 Survivors in Punjab-Pakistan
paper_journal: Pakistan Journal of Statistics and Operation Research

summary: A cross-sectional comparative study assessing blood sugar levels (HbA1c) among post-COVID patients stratified by diabetes status versus non-diabetic controls. The study found significantly elevated HbA1c levels in post-COVID diabetic patients (9.82±3.22) compared to non-diabetic post-COVID patients (5.83±3.32), indicating differential glycemic effects post-infection.
paper_authors: L. Parimala; Vimal Kishore
paper_title: A comparative study to assess the blood sugar level of post Covid patients with diabetes patients and non diabetic clients

summary: This case-control study compared mental fatigue and cognitive flexibility in 102 young adults with post-acute COVID-19 sequelae versus 111 controls using the Mental Fatigue Scale and Cognitive Flexibility Inventory. The study found significantly higher mental fatigue and lower cognitive flexibility in the long COVID group, identifying COVID-19 infection as a risk factor (OR: 2.74), but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Sedat Yasin; Erman Altunisik; Yasemin Ekmekyapar Firat
paper_title: Post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 in young adults: Mental fatigue and decreased cognitive flexibility

summary: Cross-sectional study of 31 long COVID patients examining the association between neurological symptoms (myalgia, anosmia, headache) and D-dimer levels as a potential biomarker of hypercoagulability. Found significant correlation between D-dimer levels and number of neurological symptoms (OR=1.05, p=0.020), suggesting hypercoagulable conditions may contribute to long COVID neurological manifestations.
paper_authors: Diah Kurnia Mirawati; Pepi Budianto; Rivan Danuaji; Subandi Subandi; Ira Ristinawati; Hanindia Riani Prabaningtyas
paper_title: Long-COVID neurological symptoms are associated with D-dimer levels in COVID-19 patients

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing post-COVID health effects and psychological impact in 153 patients discharged from a tertiary COVID care hospital in southern India. Found high prevalence of physical symptoms (fever, breathing difficulty) and psychiatric sequelae, with significant associations between psychological impact and demographic/lifestyle factors.
paper_authors: Subhashree Das; Lakhan Singh; Sharique Nadeem; Deepak Kumar Dubey
paper_title: Post COVID health effects on patients discharged from tertiary COVID care hospital of Southern Rajasthan, India: a cross-sectional study
paper_journal: International Journal Of Community Medicine And Public Health

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 150 COVID-19 survivors assessing the prevalence and symptom patterns of post-COVID-19 syndrome in the Indian population. The study found 39.33% prevalence with fatigue, myalgia, and cognitive symptoms being most common, but did not evaluate any treatment interventions.
paper_authors: Riddhi S. Shroff; Jaspreet Kaur Talwar; Manish M. Ray
paper_title: Prevalence of post COVID-19 syndrome
paper_journal: International Journal Of Community Medicine And Public Health

summary: Cross-sectional survey assessing psychological distress in 167 COVID-19 survivors, finding high prevalence of depression, anxiety, sleep disturbances, and cognitive impairment. No treatment or intervention was tested; this is a descriptive epidemiological study of post-COVID psychological symptoms without an experimental or therapeutic component.
paper_authors: Riddhi Nilesh Shah; Raziya Nagarwala; Rachana Dabadghav
paper_title: Psychological distress in post COVID-19 patients
paper_journal: International Journal Of Community Medicine And Public Health

summary: A cross-sectional study of 128 healthcare workers in India assessed long COVID symptomatology at 4 weeks post-infection, documenting the prevalence of constitutional, respiratory, neurological, and musculoskeletal symptoms. The paper describes symptom patterns and functional impact but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Poonam Joshi; Zichen Sherpa; Farhad Ahamed; Smita Das; Mugunthan M.
paper_title: The long-term adverse events and persisting clinical symptomatology post COVID-19 infection among the healthcare workers of a tertiary care hospital in West Bengal
paper_journal: International Journal Of Community Medicine And Public Health

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed quality of life in 1,162 COVID-19 recovered patients in South India using the WHOQOL-BREF questionnaire, comparing those with moderate/severe versus mild disease. While it documents long-term effects on QOL, it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention—it is purely observational/descriptive and therefore not eligible for the trials database.
paper_authors: Vanessa Ravel; Venkatachalam Jayaseelan; Vignesh Rajan S.; Renjana Sivaji; Arul Prasad R.; Mahadevan D.; Sitanshu Sekhar Kar
paper_title: Quality of life and its associated factors among COVID-19 recovered patients in South India: a cross-sectional analytical study
paper_journal: International Journal Of Community Medicine And Public Health

summary: This multicenter cross-sectional study describes the sociodemographic and clinical profile of 611 long COVID patients attending Brazilian rehabilitation hospitals, documenting prevalence of neuropsychiatric symptoms (65%), memory/attention impairment (55.6%), pain (53.7%), and fatigue (51.6%). The study reports functional status and mobility outcomes but does not evaluate or test a specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Valéria B. Muniz; Roberta C. Macedo; Ana Karla M. Vasconcelos; Thayse Nayara F. V. Sant'anna; Ana Claudia P. F. Maranhao; Fernando S. Ida; Elaine C. Netto; Alfredo C. Da Silva; Cruiff Emerson P. Da Silva; Márcio R. Venturini; Matheus F. Barros
paper_title: Sociodemographic and clinical profile of patients attending a post-COVID-19 rehabilitation program: a multicenter cross-sectional study

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 100 COVID-19 recovered patients assessing quality of life using the SF-36 questionnaire. Found mild-to-moderate impairment in quality of life domains, with general health and emotional well-being most affected, and persistent breathlessness and fatigue post-recovery.
paper_authors: Jigna Chaudhary; Sarfraznawaz F. Shah
paper_title: Impact of covid-19 on quality of life in COVID recovered patients: A cross-sectional survey
paper_journal: The Journal of Community Health Management

summary: Cross-sectional survey of general practitioners in Belgium and Malta examining their knowledge, perception, experience, and definitions of Long COVID care in primary health care settings. This observational study does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention, making it ineligible as a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Sarah Moreels; Sarah Cuschieri; Sherihane Bensemmane; Robrecht Schreye
paper_title: Caring for Long Covid patients in primary health care: a cross-sectional study among general practitioners in Belgium and Malta

summary: Comparative cross-sectional study comparing symptom presentation and quality of life between post COVID-19 condition patients (n=31), ME/CFS patients (n=61), and healthy controls (n=54) using validated instruments. Found that both patient groups had comparable symptom profiles and significantly impaired QoL compared to controls, with ME/CFS showing higher rates of specific symptoms like muscle weakness and memory loss.
paper_authors: Breanna Weigel; Natalie Eaton-Fitch; Kiran Thapaliya; Sonya Marshall-Gradisnik
paper_title: Symptom presentation and quality of life are comparable in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome and post COVID-19 condition

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing the incidence of breakthrough COVID-19 infections and prevalence of post-COVID syndrome symptoms (fatigue, dyspnea, mood changes, concentration difficulty) among medical staff and students at a tertiary care hospital in Telangana. Found 9.40% breakthrough infection incidence and 21.16% post-COVID syndrome prevalence, with fatigue as the most common symptom.
paper_authors: Mohammed Faraaz Khan; Sai Ajay Bompalli; Roopa C.; Panthagani Narasimhulu Shilpa
paper_title: Incidence of breakthrough infection after COVID vaccination and effect of post-covid-19 syndrome on medical students in a tertiary care hospital in Telangana
paper_journal: IP International Journal of Medical Microbiology and Tropical Diseases

summary: This cross-sectional study examines how social networking sites (YouTube, Facebook, Twitter, TikTok, LINE) influence self-protective behaviors and attitudes to prevent long COVID among 400 working-aged Thai participants. While the paper addresses long COVID prevention, it does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention—it only measures correlations between SNS exposure and self-reported behavioral intentions.
paper_authors: Nottakrit Vantamay
paper_title: Effects of social networking sites on strengthening self-protective behaviors after COVID-19 recovery among the working-aged population

summary: A cross-sectional study of 1,500 Iranian women examining menstrual cycle changes during the COVID-19 pandemic, comparing women with and without COVID-19 infection and vaccination status. The study found higher rates of menstrual changes in infected and vaccinated women but does not address long COVID or any treatment interventions.
paper_authors: Fahimeh Ranjbar; Shima Haghani; Motahareh Aghashahi; Maryam Gharacheh
paper_title: Changes in menstrual cycles among Iranian women during the COVID-19 pandemic: A cross-sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 956 long COVID patients from a Twitter community assessing symptom prevalence and incidence at 60+ days post-infection. Identifies smoking and female gender as risk factors for cutaneous signs and smoking as a correlate of tachycardia/hypertension incidence, but does not test or evaluate any intervention.
paper_authors: Hugues Barthélémy; Emmanuelle Mougenot; Martin Duracinsky; Dominique Salmon-Ceron; Jennifer Bonini; Fabienne Péretz; Olivier Chassany; Patrizia Carrieri
paper_title:
Smoking increases the risk of post-acute COVID-19
syndrome: Results from a French community-based survey

summary: Cross-sectional study of 400 COVID-19 recoverees in Iran measuring prevalence of depressive symptoms, anxiety, and stress using validated screening instruments (PHQ-9, DASS-21), and examining self-medication behaviors. Finds 35.1% with moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms and 32.8% reporting self-medication, with depression significantly associated with self-medication behavior.
paper_authors: Sarah Mousavi; Mohammadreza Razmi Afshar
paper_title: Psychological Symptoms and Self-Medication Behavior among COVID-19 Recoverees

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed long-term complications in 105 children hospitalized with COVID-19, evaluating outcomes 3 months after discharge through family questionnaires and medical records. The most common complications were mood disorders (35.2%), loss of appetite (22.9%), and fatigue (20%), with higher incidence in older children; however, this is an observational study with no intervention or treatment being tested.
paper_authors: Meysam Yazdian; Farzad Ferdosian; Zahra Nafei; Mohamad Naghibi; Elahe Akbarian
paper_title: Evaluation of Complications of Covid-19 in Children Admitted to Shahid Sadoughi Hospital in Yazd (March 2020 - March 2021)
paper_journal: Journal of Shahid Sadoughi University of Medical Sciences

summary: A cross-sectional study describing cardiac and autonomic findings (24-hour Holter monitoring and tilt table testing) in 83 post-COVID-19 patients. The study documents prevalence of abnormal findings but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Juan David Jiménez-Gómez; Laura Duque-González; Melisa Zuluaga-Martínez; Wilmer Borja-Gómez; Elsa María Vásquez-Trespalacios
paper_title: Hallazgos en el Holter 24 horas (H24H) y la prueba de mesa basculante (PMB) de pacientes con situación pos-COVID-19

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the association between persistent COVID-19 symptoms, vaccination status, and somatization disorders in Lebanese adults. Found that persistent COVID symptoms were associated with increased somatization, while vaccination was associated with decreased somatization.
paper_authors: Antonio Nehme; Muna Barakat; Diana Malaeb; Sahar Obeid; Souheil Hallit; Georges Haddad
paper_title: Association Between COVID-19 Symptoms, COVID-19 Vaccine, and Somatization Among A Sample of the Lebanese Adults

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed sleep quality in 56 COVID-19 patients with severe pulmonary involvement six months after ICU discharge using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. The findings show that 80.4% of participants exhibited sleep disorders post-discharge, with gender differences noted, but this is an observational prevalence study without any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Nima Mohamadi Afrakoti; Aylin Hefzollesan; Mohammadsadegh Talebi Kahdouei; Seyyed Mojtaba Marashi; Samaneh Hajy Mola Rabi; Fatemeh Aghaei
paper_title: Evaluation of Sleep Disturbances Prevalence in a Period of 6 Months after Recovery Post Covid-19 Patients Admitted to the Intensive Care Unit with Pulmonary Involvement of more than 20%
paper_journal: Archives of Anesthesia and Critical Care

summary: A cross-sectional study of 1,005 long COVID patients presenting to an internal medicine clinic ≥120 days post-infection, documenting the prevalence and frequency of persistent symptoms. The most common symptoms were fatigue (11.2%), shortness of breath (6.1%), and back/low back pain (4.6%), with mean 1.38 persistent symptoms per patient.
paper_authors: Zeynep KOÇ; Seydahmet AKIN
paper_title: The most common persistent symptoms in patients with COVID-19 who were evaluated in the Internal Medicine polyclinic

summary: This cross-sectional study surveyed 385 recovered COVID-19 patients in Indonesia to determine the prevalence of persistent COVID-19 syndrome and associated risk factors. Among respondents, 66.5% experienced persistent symptoms with fatigue, cough, and muscle pain being most common, and pneumonia was identified as the strongest predictor of developing persistent COVID-19 syndrome.
paper_authors: Agus Dwi Susanto; Fathiyah Isbaniah; Irandi Putra Pratomo; Budhi Antariksa; Erlang Samoedro; Muhammad Taufik; Fadlika Harinda; Fariz Nurwidya
paper_title: Clinical characteristics and quality of life of persistent symptoms of COVID-19 syndrome in Indonesia

summary: This case-control study compares lipid metabolism and hemostasis parameters in 104 hypertensive patients >2 months post-COVID-19 against 117 hypertensive controls without COVID history. Results show elevated cholesterol, LDL, triglycerides, D-dimers, and platelets, plus altered coagulation in the post-COVID group, indicating atherogenic and prothrombotic changes in the long-term period after COVID-19.
paper_authors: E. V. Sevostyanova; Yu. A. Nikolaev; V. Ya. Polyakov; I. L. Emelyanova
paper_title: Features of lipid metabolism and hemostasis in patients with arterial hypertension underwent a new coronavirus infection COVID-19

summary: This cross-sectional analysis of the 2022 National Health Interview Survey examined multilevel determinants of long COVID prevalence, including social factors and internet access as a proxy for telehealth viability. The study found long COVID more prevalent among older adults, Black individuals, and low-income households, but identified no disparities in internet access that would prevent telehealth implementation.
paper_authors: Molly Jacobs; Charles Ellis; Irene Estores
paper_title: Multilevel Determinants of Long COVID and Potential for Telehealth Intervention

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 133 medical professionals and students assessing health-promoting behaviors and anxiety about long-term COVID-19 complications during the pandemic. While nearly half of participants expressed concerns about long-term effects, the study does not investigate long COVID itself or test any treatment interventions.
paper_authors: Barbara Pietrzyk; Tomasz Maciejczyk; Stanisław Kulejewski
paper_title: Health-promoting strategies and anxiety about long COVID in medical professionals: A cross-sectional survey during the pandemic

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between long COVID symptoms and quality of life in 50 rural COVID-19 survivors using WHO questionnaires. Found that symptom count was weakly associated with lower physical quality of life (p=0.009) but not with overall QoL.
paper_authors: Eva Rahayu; Ridlwan Kamaluddin
paper_title: Exploring The Quality Of Life Phenomenon Among Patients With Long Covid Syndrome

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluated anxiety and depression in 51 healthcare workers with post-COVID-19 condition using Hamilton scales and assessed associations with inflammatory markers (NLR, PLR, MLR, SII). The study found high frequencies of anxiety (72.5%) and depression (51%) but found no significant association between inflammatory markers and these psychiatric symptoms.
paper_authors: David Ruiz-Ramos; Cecilia Yazmin Alonso-García; Roberto Esteban Salazar-Rifka; José Jaime Martínez-Magaña; Germán Alberto Nolasco-Rosales; Mario Villar-Soto
paper_title: Neuropsychiatric symptoms of post-COVID-19 condition in Mexican healthcare personnel.

summary: This prospective cross-sectional study evaluated lung ultrasonography findings in 54 patients with prior COVID-19 pneumonia to explore relationships between lung changes and prolonged COVID-19 symptoms. The study found that B lines detected by lung ultrasound are significantly associated with dyspnea in long COVID, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Ultrasonographic evaluation of post-COVID long-term lung changes and relation to prolonged COVID symptoms: a prospective cross-sectional study

paper_authors: Omar Althomali; Junaid Amin; Daria Shaik; Wael Alghamdi; Ahmed Ibrahim; Hisham Hussein; Raheela Kanwal
paper_title: Short-Term and Long-Term Impact of COVID-19 on Quality of Life and Psychological Outcomes in Saudi Arabia: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study

summary: Community-based cross-sectional study examining the association between COVID-19 infection and new-onset hypertension among 333 residents in Saudi Arabia. Found that 8.1% of infected individuals without prior hypertension developed new-onset hypertension, with age and dyslipidemia as significant risk factors.
paper_authors: Ayoub Ali Alshaikh; Hatim M. Alyazidi; Ali Mushabbab Mohammad Al Nuwayhidh; Ayman Mohammed Madkhali; Abdullatif Saleh S. Alshehri; Saad Ali Alshahrani; Mohammed Alqarni; Hussien Alslatin; Mohammed Hassan Alshehri; Omar Alsultan; Hassan Aladhadhi; Ayedh Al-Ayedh; Razan Alhumayed; Ramy Ghazy
paper_title: New-Onset Hypertension Following COVID-19 Among Aseer Residents, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia; Community-Based Screening

summary: Cross-sectional national survey examining the prevalence and predictors of viral arthropathy and myalgia following COVID-19 in 1,065 participants. Found that 26.5% reported arthralgia and 53.2% reported myalgia, with 9.9% and 6.0% respectively reporting new-onset symptoms after acute COVID-19 resolution.
paper_authors: Christopher M. Herndon; Van Nguyen
paper_title: Patterns of Viral Arthropathy and Myalgia Following COVID-19: A Cross-Sectional National Survey

summary: Cross-sectional study characterizing new-onset chronic musculoskeletal pain in 30 long COVID patients, examining clinical features, sensory abnormalities, and functional/psychological impacts. Findings reveal widespread pain with central sensitization markers, pro-inflammatory profiles, reduced mobility and strength, and moderate depression/anxiety with severely compromised quality of life.

paper_title: Clinical Characterization of New-Onset Chronic Musculoskeletal Pain in Long COVID: A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 757 Indonesian post-COVID-19 patients examining sleep disturbances and their impact on quality of life using standardized questionnaires (PSQI, ISI, ESS, STOP-BANG, SF-36). The study found that sleep quality and insomnia significantly affected patients' physical, emotional, and social functioning, but no intervention or treatment was tested.
paper_authors: Astri Budikayanti; Manfaluthy Hakim; Faradillah Mutiani; Sri Handayani; Nushrotul Lailiyya; Herlyani Khosama; Seilly Jehosua; Vivien Puspitasari; Pricilla Gunawan; Yetty Hambarsari; Wardah Islamiyah; Abdul Gofir; Amelia Vidyanti; Asnelia Devicaesaria; Rizka Ibonita; Herlina Suryawati; Rimawati Tedjasukmana
paper_title: The Impact of Post-COVID-19 Conditions on Sleep and Quality of Life in Indonesia: A Nationwide Cross-Sectional Study

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing insomnia prevalence and associated factors among 325 COVID-19 recovered patients in Vietnam, finding 34.5% had insomnia. Identifies age, social support, anxiety, depression, and stress as significant factors associated with insomnia in post-COVID patients, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Giao Huynh; Hau Viet Nguyen; Lan Y. Vo; Ngoc Thi Le; Han Thi Ngoc Nguyen
paper_title: Assessment of Insomnia and Associated Factors Among Patients Who Have Recovered from COVID-19 in Vietnam

summary: Cross-sectional study examining ocular manifestations in 200 COVID-19 and post-COVID patients at a teaching hospital in India. Found ocular abnormalities in 18% of patients including conjunctivitis, dry eyes, and glaucoma, with most cases resolving within 1-4 weeks.
paper_authors: K. Ravi Naini; V.V.L. Narasimha Rao M.S.D.O; K. Sai Sushma; Professor and HOD.; K. Sai Sushma M.D; Assistant Professor.
paper_title: A STUDY OF OCULAR MANIFESTATIONS AMONG COVID-19 AND POST COVID PATIENTS ATTENDING A TEACHING HOSPITAL, VISHAKAPATNAM

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 3,165 COVID-19 patients in China assessing long COVID prevalence (9.73%) and health status differences using propensity score matching. Study found long COVID cases had significantly lower health scores and identified healthy lifestyles and mental decompression as protective factors, but did not test any intervention.
paper_authors: Yudong Miao; Ruizhe Ren; Zhanlei Shen; Yi Li; Wanliang Zhang; Junwen Bai; Dongfang Zhu; Jingbao Zhang; Dan Guo; Clifford Tarimo; Rongmei Liu; Qiuping Zhao; Jianping Hu; Xue Zhou; Wenyong Dong
paper_title: Quantifying the Adverse Effects of Long COVID on Individuals’ Health After Infection: A Propensity Score Matching Design Study

summary: A cross-sectional study of 180 post-COVID patients in India assessing the prevalence, profile, and determinants of post-COVID syndrome ≥12 weeks after recovery from acute COVID-19. Found 72.8% prevalence with fatigue (62%), hair fall (45%), and sleep disturbance (24%) as common symptoms, with significant associations to age, gender, comorbidity, hospitalization duration, and anticoagulant use.
paper_authors: Preetham M.S; Ashwini G.S; Mohan M.E; Jayashree S. Seeri
paper_title: PREVALENCE, PROFILE AND DETERMINANTS OF POST-COVID SYNDROME AMONG PATIENTS RECOVERED FROM COVID-19 IN BANGALORE, SOUTH INDIA

summary: This study assessed quality of life in 62 children aged 5-17 years with post-COVID syndrome compared to 30 children with other respiratory infections using the PedsQL 4.0 questionnaire. Children with COVID-19 history showed significantly reduced quality of life across all age groups at 6-month follow-up, with differences noted between child and parental assessments.
paper_authors: Elena P. Isaeva; О. V. Zaytseva; Э. Э. Локшина; Olga A. Murtazaeva; Svetlana V. Zaytseva; Н. А. Сирота; Denis A. Ponkratov; I. V. Zyabkin
paper_title: Quality of life in children after a new coronavirus infection

summary: This cross-sectional study examined the relationship between self-efficacy and adherence to therapeutic regimen among 133 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients at a chest outpatient clinic. The study found a positive correlation between self-efficacy levels and therapeutic regimen adherence, but does not evaluate the effectiveness of any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Heba Ahmed Soliman Mohamed; Kamelia Fouad Abdalla; Arzak Mohamed Khalifa
paper_title: Relation between Self- Efficacy and Adherence to Therapeutic Regimen among Patients with Post COVID-19 Syndrome

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed sleep disorders, cardiovascular symptoms, and body weight dynamics in 253 women with post-COVID-19 syndrome using questionnaires and vital sign measurements. The paper documents symptom prevalence and correlations but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: В. А. Сергеева; Lipatova Te
paper_title: Sleep disorders, cardiovascular symptoms and body weight dynamics in women with post-COVID-19 syndrome

summary: A cross-sectional study assessing women's knowledge, practices, and attitudes toward post-COVID-19 syndrome in Fayoum governorate, Egypt. The study found 80% had unsatisfactory knowledge about post-COVID syndrome, though 90.4% reported satisfactory practices and attitudes were mixed (43.5% positive, 56.5% negative).
paper_authors: Asmaa Abdel Halim Mosaad; Hanan Ibrahim Ahmed; Walaa Abdel Kader Mohamed
paper_title: Women's Awareness about Post Covid-19 Syndrome

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the effect of COVID-19 infection on ovarian reserve in 120 infertile women using assisted reproductive technology. Found no statistically significant differences in AMH, AFC, FSH, and LH levels before and after COVID-19 infection across disease severity groups.
paper_authors: Abd El-Samie Abd El-Samie; Mohamed Etman
paper_title: Post COVID-19 effect of ovarian reserve

summary: Cross-sectional screening study of 88 nurses with COVID-19 history using the MINIDEP tool to assess post-COVID depression prevalence. Found 13.6% had post-COVID depression, with female sex, illness duration, and sleep disturbance as significant correlates, but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Afnan Radi; Rania Mohammed; Gihan Omar
paper_title: Depression and COVID 19

summary: This cross-sectional study describes delayed effects of COVID-19 in 137 hospitalized children in Iran from 2021-2023, using medical records and parental interviews. Fatigue was the most common complication (21.1%), with other effects including cough, rhinorrhea, and nausea; the study calls for personalized follow-up care but does not test any intervention.
paper_authors: Shima Groohi-Sardou; Mohammad Mahdi Dehghani; Rasoul Raesi; Kiavash Hushmandi; Salman Daneshi
paper_title: Determining the Delayed Effects of COVID-19 in Children Hospitalized in Southeastern Iran from 2021 to 2023

summary: This cross-sectional study compared pain, fall frequency, fear of falling, and physical activity levels in 48 older people who had recovered from COVID-19 versus 66 healthy controls. The COVID-19 group showed significantly higher pain, fatigue, cognitive impairment, fall frequency, and fear of falling, but this is an observational comparison study without any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Ozan Gür; Selda Başar
paper_title: EFFECT OF COVID-19 ON PAIN, FALL FREQUENCY, FEAR OF FALLING, AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY LEVEL IN OLDER PEOPLE: A CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY

summary: This cross-sectional study examines clinical characteristics and risk factors for prolonged hospital stays in 52 post-COVID-19 patients readmitted 30-90 days after acute infection. The study identifies severe COVID-19 history and lung consolidation as independent risk factors for extended hospitalization, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Doan Le Minh Hanh; Nguyen Hoang Minh Thao
paper_title: Risk Factors Associated with Re-Hospitalization Duration in Post-COVID-19 Patients

summary: This cross-sectional study compared sexual activity in 110 women before and after acute COVID-19 infection, measured at baseline and one month post-infection. The study found significant decreases in sexual activity scores following infection, with greater severity correlating to larger declines.
paper_authors: Zohreh Keshavarz; Naeimeh Shariatifar; Maliheh Nasiri; Zahra Kiani
paper_title:
Comparison of Women's Sexual Activity Before and After being Infected
with COVID-19

summary: Cross-sectional study of 382 Iraqi medical students assessing the frequency of persistent respiratory symptoms 60+ days after COVID-19 infection. Found that intermittent cough (47.4%), dry cough (46.6%), and chronic cough (40.6%) were the most common persistent symptoms.
paper_authors: Batool Mutar Mahdi; Zainab Muthanna Akbar; Dima Ali Mohammed; Rafal Qassim Amer; Aya Haider Fareed
paper_title: Persistent Respiratory Symptoms Post-COVID Virus Infection in a Sample of Iraqi Medical Students

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed vitamin D levels in 82 long COVID patients with fatigue or neuropsychiatric symptoms and examined correlations with symptom severity using standardized scales. While 73.2% of participants had vitamin D deficiency, the analysis found no association between vitamin D levels and any clinical outcomes including fatigue, depression, anxiety, sleep quality, or cognitive function.
paper_authors: Veevarin Charoenporn; Thammanard Charernboon
paper_title: Prevalence of Vitamin D Deficiency in Patients with Fatigue and Neuropsychiatric Symptoms of Long COVID and its Correlation with Symptom Severity

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 160 Egyptian children assessed 12 weeks post-COVID-19 infection to determine prevalence and nature of persistent symptoms. Found 36.25% exhibited post-COVID symptoms including fatigue, sleep disturbances, and neuropsychiatric issues, but this is an observational prevalence study with no treatment intervention tested.
paper_authors: Nagwa Mohamed Sabry Mahmoud; Ahmed Maher Taha Abdelrasoul; Gamal Baheeg
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 Health Outcomes in Pediatric Patients: A Survey Study

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed cardiovascular disease risk and fitness levels (via VO2 max) in 150 post-COVID middle-aged industrial workers, finding that 34% had moderate-to-high cardiovascular risk and reduced cardiorespiratory fitness particularly in the 45–55 age group. The study is observational without any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the clinical trials pipeline.
paper_authors: Kaushik Raman; Ramachandran Sivagnanam
paper_title: Descriptive Analysis of Cardiovascular Fitness and Cardiovascular Disease Susceptibility Profiling in Post-COVID Middle-aged Industrial Workers

summary: Cross-sectional questionnaire study examining correlations between medications used during acute COVID-19 infection and post-recovery symptoms in recovered patients. The study found differential symptom persistence associated with various medications (vitamin D, ACE inhibitors, azithromycin, H2 antagonists) but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment given to long COVID patients—it only retrospectively associates prior acute-phase medications with symptom outcomes.

paper_title: Correlation between Medications Used During Covid Infection and Post-Conditions after the Acute Phase of Infection: A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 657 COVID-19 recovered patients in Jordan assessing post-COVID syndrome prevalence and risk factors. Study identifies 71.9% PCS prevalence and six significant risk factors (female sex, age ≥30, diabetes, hypertension, respiratory disease, neuropsychological disturbance) but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Risk Factors and Characterization of Post-COVID-19 Syndrome in Jordan

summary: A hospital-based cross-sectional questionnaire study of 385 COVID-19 patients in Hiroshima investigating persistent symptoms at median 23.5 days post-infection across different viral variants (Wild-type, Alpha, Delta, Omicron). The study identifies symptom clusters and examines risk factors but does not test any intervention or treatment.

summary: Cross-sectional study examining depression, anxiety, and suicidal thoughts/behaviors in COVID-19 survivors versus non-infected controls using standardized mental health questionnaires. Found significantly higher depression and anxiety scores in those with COVID-19 history, with symptoms overlapping post-COVID syndrome presentation.
paper_authors: Sean F. Woodward; Sumra Bari; Nicole Vike; Shamal Lalvani; Khrystyna Stetsiv; Byoung Woo Kim; Leandros Stefanopoulos; Nicos Maglaveras; Hans Breiter; Aggelos K. Katsaggelos
paper_title: Anxiety, Post–COVID-19 Syndrome-Related Depression, and Suicidal Thoughts and Behaviors in COVID-19 Survivors: Cross-sectional Study

summary: Online cross-sectional survey of 1,262 Chinese participants investigating the prevalence of tinnitus and ear-related symptoms following COVID-19 infection. summary: Cross-sectional study examining depression, anxiety, and suicidal thinking/behavior in COVID-19 survivors versus non-infected controls using questionnaire responses from 506 U.S. adults. Found significantly elevated PHQ-9 and STAI scores in those with COVID-19 history, with symptom overlap to Post-COVID Syndrome, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

paper_title: Anxiety, Post-COVID-Syndrome-related depression, and suicidal thinking and behavior in COVID-19 survivors: a preliminary study (Preprint)

summary: This retrospective cohort study assessed cardiovascular manifestations in 650 post-COVID patients attending a dedicated outpatient department, using echocardiography and standardized cardiac classifications. Among the cohort, 22.5% of patients had cardiac manifestations including angina, arrhythmia, and NSTEMI, with higher prevalence in those with multiple comorbidities.

summary: Observational cross-sectional study of 101 COVID-19 survivors in Indonesia examining factors associated with long-term COVID-19 occurrence. Study found good knowledge (72.94%) and positive attitudes (88.82%) toward nutrition, but no correlation between dietary knowledge/attitudes and nutritional status.

summary: This cross-sectional study surveyed 1,000 post-COVID patients (4 weeks to 12 months post-infection) to characterize the prevalence and nature of neurological, somatic, and mental health complaints. The study found high rates of fatigue (77.5%), cognitive impairment (69.5%), hair loss (49.5%), and gender-specific differences in symptom severity, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Delayed mental, neurological and somatic disorders associated with COVID-19

Found that 47.3% had mild to severe depression, with female gender, younger age, overweight/obesity, presence of long COVID, and perceived poor health as significant risk factors.

paper_title: DEPRESSION AND ITS ASSOCIATED FACTORS AMONG COVID-19 SURVIVORS IN MALAYSIA – AN ONLINE CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY
paper_journal: Journal of Health and Translational Medicine

summary: A cross-sectional study examining the relationship between social determinants of health and chronic diseases in two parishes in Ecuador during 2022-2023. paper_title: SOCIAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH AND CHRONIC DISEASES POST COVID-19. SALINAS. ECUADOR, 2023

summary: This cross-sectional survey of 194 COVID-19 recovered individuals identified predictors of taste and smell loss (profession, smoking status, allergies, respiratory infection frequency) and examined associations with post-COVID symptoms. paper_authors: Milana Bojinovic; Tijana Lainovic; Milica Jeremic-Knezevic; Daniela Djurovic-Koprivica; Aleksandra Maletin; Milos Cankovic
paper_title: Predictor analysis of smell and taste loss onset and its significance in COVID-19 disease

summary: Retrospective quality-improvement analysis characterizing baseline symptoms and functional impairments in 422 long COVID patients attending outpatient rehabilitation in the UK. Found high prevalence of fatigue (76%), breathlessness (69%), depression (55%), and work/social dysfunction (57%), but this is a descriptive baseline assessment, not a treatment trial.

paper_title: Characterization of baseline symptoms and functional impairments in a large cohort of outpatients attending a long covid rehabilitation clinic in the United Kingdom
paper_journal: Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine - Clinical Communications

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 1,044 COVID-19 patients conducted 4+ weeks post-infection to assess long COVID symptom prevalence and impact on quality of life. Found 65.6% reported persistent symptoms, with myalgia, fatigue, joint pain, and anosmia most common; no intervention tested.

paper_authors: Jan-Rickard Norrefalk; Kristian Borg; Indre Bileviciute-Ljungar
paper_title: Self-scored impairments in functioning and disability in post-COVID syndrome following mild COVID-19 infection

summary: Cross-sectional survey assessing how persistent olfactory dysfunction after COVID-19 impacts quality of life in 1,072 participants using the QOD-NS questionnaire. Study documents that olfactory impairment significantly affects QOL but does not evaluate or test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Karimi-Galougahi, Mahboobeh; Raad, Nasim; Haseli, Sara; Ghorbani, Jahangir; Seyed-Mohammadi, Behnaz
paper_title: Evaluating Patients with Olfactory Dysfunction after COVID-19 Infection by Questionnaire of Olfactory Disorders-Negative Statements
paper_journal: Journal of Otorhinolaryngology and Facial Plastic Surgery

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 614 post-COVID-19 patients examining the impact of self-reported fatigue on daily functioning and its associations with sociodemographics, physical capacity, and work ability. The study found fatigue is common and negatively impacts functioning, suggesting rehabilitation interventions may be beneficial, but does not test any specific treatment.
paper_authors: Christina Brogårdh; Elisabeth Ekstrand; Agneta Malmgren Fänge; Iben Axen; Kerstin Stigmar; Eva Ekvall Hansson
paper_title: Self-reported fatigue in people with post COVID-19: impact on functioning in daily life, and associated factors – a cross-sectional study

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed cardiovascular autonomic function in 47 long COVID patients (with and without type 2 diabetes) compared to 45 diabetic controls without COVID-19, using autonomic reflex tests and heart rate variability measures. The study found that COVID-19 exacerbates autonomic dysfunction in diabetic patients and impairs autonomic function in non-diabetic long COVID patients to a similar degree as diabetes alone.

paper_title: 487-P: Cardiovascular Autonomic Function in Long COVID-19 Individuals With and Without Diabetes

summary: Cross-sectional observational study measuring physical activity and sedentary time in 159 adults with post-COVID-19 condition using activity monitors. Study identifies associations between symptoms (POTS, palpitations, paraesthesia) and activity levels, but does not test or evaluate any intervention—it is purely descriptive/observational.
paper_authors: Anna Törnberg; Anna Svensson-Raskh; Lucian Bezuidenhout; David Moulaee Conradsson; Annie Svensson; Judith Bruchfeld; Elisabeth Rydwik; Malin Nygren-Bonnier
paper_title: Physical activity, sedentary time, and associated factors in post-COVID-19 condition: a cross-sectional study

summary: This cross-sectional study characterizes pulmonary function and disability in 32 post-acute COVID-19 patients admitted to an Italian rehabilitation unit and proposes an early rehabilitation protocol. However, the paper focuses on acute post-hospitalization recovery during active disease sequelae in the immediate post-ICU period, not long COVID as persistent symptoms weeks-to-months after infection.
paper_authors: Claudio Curci; Fabrizio Pisano; Eleonora Bonacci; Danila M. Camozzi; Claudia Ceravolo; Roberto Bergonzi; Silvia De Franceschi; Paolo Moro; Rodolfo Guarnieri; Martina Ferrillo; Francesco Negrini; Alessandro de Sire
paper_title: Early rehabilitation in post-acute COVID-19 patients: data from an Italian COVID-19 Rehabilitation Unit and proposal of a treatment protocol
paper_journal: European Journal of Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing chronic pain prevalence in 52 COVID-19 patients (evaluated 4.2 months post-infection) versus 52 matched healthy controls using painDETECT and DN4 questionnaires. Found 70% chronic pain prevalence in COVID-19 group (similar to controls), with 10% of COVID patients reporting new-onset or worsened pain post-infection, particularly neuropathic pain.
paper_title: Chronic pain in patients with COVID-19: Cross sectional study

summary: This descriptive cross-sectional study compares referral patterns for COVID-19 recovered participants versus a general population control group using Qatar Biobank data. It identifies that diabetes is the most common reason for healthcare referral in COVID-recovered patients, in contrast to osteopenia in the general population, suggesting increased post-COVID metabolic complications.
paper_authors: Eldeeb M.; Fthenou E.; Elkousy N.; Sheikh N.; Nasr M.; Afifi N.; Al Thani A.; Frenneaux M.
paper_title: Common Indications for Referral to the Healthcare system for COVID-19 recovered patients versus Qatar Biobank study population: A descriptive analysis.

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing nutrition status and quality of life in 40 post-COVID-19 patients using dietary frequency analysis and SF-36 questionnaire. Found nutritional deficiencies (vitamin D, B vitamins, iron, selenium), excess fat and calories, and impaired quality of life scores, particularly in emotional and mental health domains.
paper_authors: Ol’ga V. Kozubenko; Anna V. Erina
paper_title: Hygienic Assessment of Nutrition and Quality of Life of Patients with Post-COVID-19 Syndrome

summary: Online survey of medical workers assessing residual clinical manifestations of COVID-19 during early (0-6 months) and late recovery periods (6-15 months), including fatigue, cognitive impairment, alopecia, and affective disorders. Study is descriptive/observational with no treatment intervention tested.
paper_authors: Т. А. Платонова; А. А. Голубкова; M.S. Sklyar; Mikhail S. Rozhkov; Т. R. Tomenko; С. С. Смирнова; ERIVI of the FBRI SRC VB «Vector», Rospotrebnadzor
paper_title: Clinical Manifestations of COVID-19 in Employees of Medical Organizations in the Early and Late Recovery Periods and Issues of Their Rehabilitation

summary: A cross-sectional study examining the relationship between D-dimer levels and post-COVID neurological syndrome (PCNS) in 100 COVID-19 patients 3-6 months after hospitalization. Found a statistically significant positive correlation between elevated D-dimer and PCNS symptoms (p=0.003), suggesting hypercoagulability in post-COVID neurological manifestations.
paper_authors: Rita Mulyana; Dessy R. Emril; Endang Mutiawati; Nurrahmah Yusuf; Fauzul Husna
paper_title: Hubungan Kadar D-dimer dengan Kejadian Post-COVID Neurological Syndrome pada Pasien COVID-19

summary: Retrospective analysis of 2020 CDC National Health Interview Survey data comparing functional and behavioral limitations associated with frailty risk in older adults (65+) stratified by COVID-19 infection status and symptom severity. Older adults with moderate-to-severe COVID-19 demonstrated significantly greater frailty-related limitations including tiredness, self-care deficits, and anxiety/depression compared to COVID-negative controls.
paper_authors: Kume June; Jumbo Adiebonye; Voltmer Christopher; Luo Fang
paper_title: Functional Limitations Associated with Frailty Risk in Older Adults Increased after COVID-19 Infection in 2020 CDC NHIS Data
paper_journal: Journal of Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology

summary: This observational cross-sectional study examines the association between long COVID-19 symptoms and posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in 4,463 Vietnamese COVID-19 survivors, investigating health literacy as a protective modifier. The findings show that long COVID-19 symptoms are associated with higher PTSD likelihood, and higher health literacy is protective against PTSD.

paper_title: Impact of long COVID-19 on posttraumatic stress disorder as modified by health literacy: an observational study in Vietnam
paper_journal: Osong Public Health and Research Perspectives

summary: A cross-sectional study assessing subjective quality of life and health outcomes in 64 COVID-19 survivors (mean ~1 year post-infection) in Kazakhstan using the SF-36 instrument. Most participants reported stable or slightly worse health compared to pre-COVID baseline, with women reporting lower quality of life than men.
paper_authors: Elmira Kaidar; Asiya Turgambayeva; Saule Kassymova
paper_title: Assessment of quality of life one year after in COVID-19 cases using the SF-36
paper_journal: Journal of Clinical Medicine of Kazakhstan

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 94 COVID-19 survivors presenting with unresolved respiratory symptoms at a pulmonology clinic in Lagos, Nigeria. Study documents prevalence of respiratory morbidity (fatigue 85.1%, dyspnea 56.4%, cough 62.8%) and functional impairment but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Oluwafemi Tunde Ojo; Olufunke Olayinka Adeyeye; Adeola Ajibare; Temitope Fapohunda
paper_title: Burden of respiratory morbidity amongst survivors of COVID-19 infection in Lagos, Southwest Nigeria
paper_journal: Journal of Clinical Medicine of Kazakhstan

summary: A cross-sectional study assessing objective and subjective olfactory dysfunction in 147 post-COVID-19 patients in Saudi Arabia. Findings showed persistent anosmia/hyposmia was significantly associated with delayed onset, longer duration of symptoms, and longer overall COVID-19 symptom duration.
paper_authors: Mohamed R.; Alsuhibani R.; Almasaoud H.; Alsubhi S.; Alabdulazeem L.; Alzahrani N.; Alsaif S.; Al Ghamdi K.; Al-Asoom L.
paper_title: Assessment of anosmia/hyposmia in post-COVID-19 patients: a cross-sectional study in an eastern province of Saudi Arabia.

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 381 adults assessing persistent COVID-19 symptoms and socioeconomic correlates one year post-infection. Identifies fatigue, memory deficit, headache, hair loss, and cough as most common symptoms, with higher prevalence in females, unvaccinated individuals, and lower-income groups.
paper_authors: Daniel Prestes de Barros Patara; Carlos Eduardo Fontana
paper_title: Perfil sintomático e socioeconômico de adultos um ano após COVID-19
paper_journal: Revista Remecs - Revista Multidisciplinar de Estudos Cientí­ficos em Saúde

summary: This cross-sectional survey of 168 Pakistani participants assessed the prevalence and symptom profile of long COVID syndrome, finding that 78.6% experienced persistent symptoms beyond 4 weeks post-infection, with fatigue, fever, and loss of taste being most common. The study identified risk factors including male gender, existing chronic illnesses, and hospital isolation, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Sana Abbas; Beenish Abbas; Haifsa Rafique; Aisha Rafique; Saima Zafar; Ramesha Azam
paper_title: Deciphering Long Covid: Next Emergent Healthcare Dilemma
paper_journal: European Journal of Medical and Health Sciences

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence and patterns of antinuclear antibodies (ANA) in 108 post-COVID patients with articular and musculoskeletal symptoms between August-October 2021. The study found that 29% tested positive for ANA, with higher prevalence in patients >6 months post-infection, suggesting COVID-19 may trigger autoantibody development but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Koyamangalath Krishnan; Therese Mary Dhason; Ananthakrishnan Parthasarathy; Thyagarajan Ravinder
paper_title: Evaluation of Antinuclear Antibodies of SLE Panel in COVID-19 Patients: A Cross-Sectional study in a Tertiary Care Hospital
paper_journal: Journal of Clinical and Health Sciences

summary: This cross-sectional study compared metacognitive beliefs and mental health in 122 post-COVID-19 patients and quarantined individuals using questionnaires (MCQ and GHQ-12). While the paper identifies psychological sequelae in long COVID patients, it is excluded because it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention—it is a descriptive/observational assessment only.
paper_authors: Sylwia Krasowska; Marzena Samardakiewicz; Jacek Kurzepa
paper_title: Late mental sequelae in post-COVID-19 individuals
paper_journal: Pielegniarstwo XXI wieku / Nursing in the 21st Century

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 220 pediatric patients in Latvia that characterized the prevalence and types of long COVID symptoms across age groups (< 1.5 years to 11-18 years). The study identified fatigue, persistent cough, mood swings, and impaired physical activity as the most common symptoms but did not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Anija Meiere; Liene Smane; Anda Ķīvīte-Urtāne; Lizete Kļaviņa; Iveta Račko; Ieva Roģe; Zanda Pučuka; Jana Pavāre
paper_title: Long COVID-19 Symptom Profile in Children and Adolescents Tested for SARS-CoV-2
paper_journal: Proceedings of the Latvian Academy of Sciences. Section B. Natural, Exact, and Applied Sciences.

summary: This cross-sectional survey assessed knowledge and anxiety levels regarding long COVID-19 among 50 respondents in Semarang Regency, Indonesia. The study found that 74% had low knowledge and 54% experienced mild anxiety, but it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention—only measures baseline knowledge and psychological status.
paper_authors: Widha Nur Rafika; Puji Purwaningsih; Abdul Wakhid
paper_title: STUDI DESKRIPTIF PENGETAHUAN DAN KECEMASAN MENGENAI  LONG COVID-19 PADA MASYARAKAT DI KABUPATEN SEMARANG
paper_journal: Coping: Community of Publishing in Nursing

summary: This cross-sectional study examines how sociodemographic and clinical characteristics correlate with BMI and recovery time in individuals with long COVID-19 from Bangladesh. The research focuses on understanding how persistent COVID-19 symptoms affect age, gender, education, and occupational functioning.
paper_authors: Md. Faruk Hasan
paper_title: A Comprehensive Analysis of Sociodemographic Factors on Recovery Time in Individuals Diagnosed with COVID-19 from Chittagong Division, Bangladesh
paper_journal: Community Medicine and Public Health Care

summary: Cross-sectional observational study examining the relationship between PTSD and psychosomatic symptoms in long COVID patients at a regional hospital in Indonesia (n=73). Found significant correlation between PTSD factors and long-lasting psychosomatic symptoms (P=0.001), but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: I. Made; Krishna Putra Pramanda; S. Purnawati; Nila Wahyuni; I. Dewa; Ayu Inten; Dwi Primayani; Jurnal Medika; Udayana Jurnal; Medika Udayana
paper_title: THE RELATIONSHIP OF POST TRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER FACTORS WITH PSYCHOSOMATIC SYMPTOMS TO LONG COVID PATIENTS AT RSUD TABANAN

summary: Cross-sectional comparative study examining attention and memory deficits in adults with central auditory processing disorder (CAPD), comparing those with and without prior COVID-19 infection. Found no significant differences on the Neuropsi test between groups overall, though differences emerged in specific attention and memory domains when stratified by age, education, and time since COVID infection.
paper_authors: Aline I. Ayala-Carrillo; Ma. del Consuelo Martínez-Wbaldo; Sergio Díaz-Leines
paper_title: Atención y memoria en sujetos con trastorno en el procesamiento auditivo central con y sin antecedente de infección por SARS-CoV-2
paper_journal: Anales Médicos de la Asociación Médica del Centro Médico ABC

summary: This descriptive cross-sectional study examined post-acute COVID-19 syndrome symptoms in 30 recovered patients, finding that fatigue, persistent cough, and loss of taste/smell were the most commonly reported symptoms 1-2 weeks after infection. The study describes symptom prevalence and severity but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: I. Gusti Ayu Julia Arsita Devie; Ni Kadek Ayu Suarningsih; Indah Mei Rahajeng; Desak Made Widyanthari
paper_title: GAMBARAN POST-ACUTE COVID-19 SYNDROME PADA PASIEN PASCA TERINFEKSI CORONAVIRUS DISEASE 2019
paper_journal: Coping: Community of Publishing in Nursing

summary: Cross-sectional study examining associations between social support, socioeconomic status, age, and psychological well-being in 255 post-COVID-19 patients in Indonesia. Found significant positive relationships between these factors and psychological well-being, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Arief Budiman; Jidan Ramadhan; Nanda Nur Hidayah; Putri Dwi Hasmi; Rafika Sandra
paper_title: Hubungan Dukungan Sosial, Status Sosial Ekonomi dan Usia dengan Kesejahteraan Psikologis  Pasien Pasca Covid-19

summary: This cross-sectional descriptive study estimated the prevalence of persistent symptoms in 114 individuals who had recovered from COVID-19 infection in Kerala, India. The findings showed that 57.9% of participants reported persistent symptoms, with fatigue (39.5%) and joint pain (20.2%) being the most common, but no specific treatment or intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Sreelakshmi PR; Siji VS; Gopan K.; Gopinath S.; Nair AS
paper_title: Persistence of symptoms after Covid-19 infection in Kerala
paper_journal: The National Medical Journal of India

summary: A cross-sectional study of 52 COVID-19 pneumonia survivors in Brazzaville assessed long-term radiographic and spirometric outcomes at least 6 months post-infection. The study found abnormal chest imaging in 42.3% of patients and ventilatory disorders in 71.1%, with advanced age, comorbidities, and mechanical ventilation associated with worse outcomes.

paper_title: Post-COVID-19 pneumonia: Long-term radiographic and spirometric outcomes

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of vitamin D deficiency in 219 post-COVID-19 patients and its association with symptom severity. Found 84% had deficient vitamin D levels but detected no significant link between vitamin D status and post-COVID symptoms.
paper_authors: Mohamed Hussein AAR; Galal I.; Amin MT; Moshnib AA; Makhlouf NA; Makhlouf HA; Abd-Elaal HK; Kholief KMS; Abdel Tawab DA; Kamal Eldin KA; Attia AM; Othman AEA; Shah J.; Aiash H.
paper_title: Prevalence of vitamin D deficiency among patients attending Post COVID-19 follow-up clinic: a cross-sectional study.

summary: This paper assesses the population's need for post-COVID rehabilitation services in Primorsky Krai, Russia, and evaluates the capacity of sanatorium-resort facilities to meet that demand. It is a descriptive needs assessment study without any intervention, treatment evaluation, or patient outcomes data.

summary: This cross-sectional study tested whether SARS-CoV-2 induces persistent genome instability in endothelial cells of long COVID patients by examining micronuclei and chromosomal bridges in 51 COVID-recovered and 43 COVID-naive individuals. The hypothesis was not confirmed; no cases of genome instability were detected in either group, suggesting that any systemic endothelial effects from COVID-19 may be reversible.
paper_authors: Natalia Lubinets; Alexey V. Yusupov; Viacheslav Kravtsov
paper_title: «COVID endothelioteca» in testing the hypothesis of induction of genome instability by the SARS-CoV-2 virus in the endothelium of patients who have recovered from COVID-19

summary: This study analyzes the relationship between COVID-19 severity and cognitive impairment in students during the post-acute phase, and examines associations with chronic diseases. It is a cross-sectional assessment of post-COVID symptoms but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: В.А. Шалабодина
paper_title: Cognitive impairment in Post-COVID-19 Syndrome: analysis of students’ health status

summary: Retrospective cross-sectional study of 4,450 SARS-CoV-2-positive individuals in Missouri that developed machine learning models to predict clinical outcomes including hospitalization, ICU admission, and long COVID using viral sequences, host genetics, and environmental factors. The study identified risk factors for long COVID including prior hospitalization, ventilation, and female sex, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Edmonds, Keith Morgan
paper_title: Supersymmetry searches in the single lepton final state with the ATLAS detector

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing quality of life, cognitive, and psycho-emotional status in post-COVID patients with and without metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD). Patients with MAFLD showed significantly impaired quality of life, increased anxiety/depression, and worse cognitive function compared to controls.
paper_authors: Taisiia A. Turankova; Eva A. Verdiyan; Marina V. Novikova; Alexey Iu. Brazhnikov; Chavdar S. Pavlov
paper_title: Impact of MAFLD on quality of life and neuropsychological status in post-COVID patients: a cross-sectional analysis

summary: Cross-sectional study of 90 COVID-19 patients discharged from a medical college in Bangalore, India, assessing symptom persistence post-discharge and associated risk factors. Found 41.1% had persistent symptoms (mostly fatigue), with age, hospitalization, obesity, and smoking as risk factors.

paper_title: Persistence of Symptoms in Post-Discharge COVID 19 Patients in the Urban Field Practice Area of Bangalore Medical College and Research Institute - A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: Retrospective multicenter cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence and characteristics of post-COVID syndrome in 435 Russian children at 7.6 months post-infection. summary: A cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence of post-COVID syndrome in an urban community in Bangalore, India, recruiting 82 participants aged 18+ years. The study found that 85% experienced fatigue, 84% malaise/discomfort, and 82% mood disturbance, with multiple organ systems affected, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

paper_title: A Cross-sectional study assessing the Prevalence of Post Covid Syndrome in Urban Field Practice Area of Bangalore Medical College and Research Institute, Bangalore
paper_journal: RGUHS National Journal of Public Health

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 294 long COVID patients in Bangladesh examining symptom characteristics and associations with demographics and comorbidities. The study describes prevalence (15.6%), symptom severity using pain and fatigue scales, and demographic patterns but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Tamzid Hossain; Mohammad Anwar Hossain*; Farjana Sharmin; Md Ershad Ali; Md. Shafiqul Islam; Kulsum Akter; Shahid Afridi; Amina Akter; Luthfor Rahman; Rubaya Sultana
paper_title: Characteristics of Long COVID Symptoms of People Affected by COVID-19 living at Dhaka Division, Bangladesh

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 60 residents of Kharkiv assessing prevalence of post-COVID symptoms and their impact on daily functioning. Primary findings: fatigue (61.7%), brain fog (58.3%), exercise intolerance (56.7%), muscle pain (45%), sleep disorders and joint pain (43.3%). Paper recommends comprehensive rehabilitation but does not test or evaluate any intervention.
paper_authors: Evgene Nikolenko; Iryna Adamovych; Kira Vovk
paper_title: Prevalence of post-covid syndrome among inhabitants of Kharkiv
paper_journal: The Journal of V. N. Karazin Kharkiv National University, Series "Medicine"

summary: A cross-sectional study evaluating inflammatory biomarkers (LDH, RF, CRP, ferritin, uric acid) in 139 long COVID patients with arthritis symptoms in India. The study found that inflammatory markers decreased over six months of follow-up, but this is an observational characterization study without testing any active intervention or treatment.

paper_title: Evaluation of Inflammatory Biomarkers in Post-COVID-19 Arthritis: a Cross-Sectional Study from Telangana, South India

summary: Observational cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence of ongoing symptoms and laboratory abnormalities in 42 COVID-19 cases at least 12 months post-infection in Wellington, New Zealand.
