paper_authors: Annette Nesdale; Nethmi Kearns; Neakiry Kivi; Emily Dickinson; Emma Mayo; Allie Eathorne; Augustus Anderson; Richard Beasley; Craig Thornley
paper_title: The long-term impacts of COVID-19 on confirmed cases at least 12 months post-infection in Wellington, New Zealand: an observational, cross-sectional study

summary: This is a secondary analysis of 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System data examining the relationship between long COVID, cognitive impairment, and Alzheimer's Disease risk factors across 29 states. The study is observational/descriptive (no intervention tested) and uses existing survey data rather than conducting a primary research study.
paper_authors: Mary L. Adams; Joseph Grandpre
paper_title: Long COVID and Cognitive Impairment: 2022 survey results from 29 states with relevance to Alzheimer’s Disease

summary: Cross-sectional study examining associations between metabolic risk factors (BMI, blood pressure, diabetes, heart disease, stroke) and long COVID risk in 990 New Zealand survey respondents. Found high BMI strongly associated with long COVID (aOR 2.35) but no intervention or treatment was tested.
paper_authors: Bailey Yee; Fiona McKenzie; Lis Ellison-Loschmann; Lynne Russell; Mona Jeffreys
paper_title: Metabolic risk factors and long COVID: a cross-sectional study in Aotearoa New Zealand

summary: A cross-sectional study of 27 post-COVID patients with hypertension examining transforming growth factor β1 as a potential biomarker for cardiovascular complications. The study found elevated TGF-β1 levels associated with worse glucose control and uncontrolled hypertension in post-COVID patients.
paper_authors: O.V. Kuryata; O.S. Mytrokhina; O.I. Stadnyk
paper_title: Transforming growth factor beta-1 in patients with hypertension who had COVID-19

summary: Cross-sectional study of 83 long COVID patients in Aragon examining employment status and associated sociodemographic and clinical factors. Finds 44.6% on temporary work disability, with greater symptom burden and male gender predicting work incapacity.
paper_authors: Sandra León Herrera; Mario Samper-Pardo; Angela Asensio-Martínez
paper_title: Situación laboral en personas con Long-COVID: Análisis de factores sociodemográficos y clínicos asociados.

summary: Retrospective analysis comparing physical development and fitness indicators between freshmen who had COVID-19 and those who did not in 2022. No treatment intervention was administered; this is an observational study examining differences in physical fitness outcomes stratified by BMI.
paper_authors: Kotova N.V.; Klochkova S.V.; Kolupaev V.A.
paper_title: COMPARISON OF PHYSICAL DEVELOPMENT AND FITNESS INDICATORS OF FRESHMEN WITH DIFFERENT HEALTH CONDITIONS WHO HAVE UNDERGONE COVID-19

summary: Cross-sectional web-survey analyzing factors associated with long COVID in 228 Brazilian adults who tested positive for COVID-19. Found associations between long COVID persistence and age, lower family income, lack of physical activity, hypertension, and specific acute symptoms (chills, headache, cough, anosmia, ageusia, dyspnea, diarrhea), with fatigue being the most prevalent long COVID symptom.
paper_authors: Aélya Drisana Dias Gomes de Araújo; Jéssica Maria Silva de Carvalho; Francisca Tereza de Galiza; Fernando José Guedes da Silva Júnior; Chrystiany Plácido de Brito Vieira; Emanoelle Fernandes Silva
paper_title: Factors related to long COVID in the adult population of Brazil

summary: Descriptive cross-sectional study comparing physical development and functional indicators (endurance, strength, fitness) in first-year university students who recovered from COVID-19 versus those who never had the infection. The study documents persistent post-COVID effects on motor function and exercise tolerance but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Kotova N.V.; Klochkova S.V.; Kolupaev V.A.
paper_title: INDICATORS OF PHYSICAL STATE AND PHYSICAL DEVELOPMENT OF FRESHMEN WHO HAVE UNDERGONE COVID-19

summary: A cross-sectional study of 115 post-COVID patients examining the frequency and characteristics of sleep disorders after COVID-19 infection. The study found restless leg syndrome was the most common sleep disorder, and moderate-to-severe COVID-19 infection was associated with 11.6-fold higher risk of reduced sleep quality in younger patients (26-59 years).

paper_title: Patterns of sleep disorders after a new coronavirus infection COVID-19

summary: Cross-sectional study examining factors affecting quality of life, physical activity, cognitive function, and dyspnea in 176 long COVID patients (12+ weeks post-infection). paper_title: Examination of factors affecting quality of life, physical activity level, cognitive impairment, and dyspnea level in individuals with long COVID: A cross-sectional study

paper_authors: Mona Jeffreys; Fiona McKenzie; Maite Irurzun Lopez; Lynne Russell; Lis Ellison-Loschmann
paper_title: Long COVID impacts people’s ability to work: cross-sectional study in Aotearoa New Zealand

paper_authors: Arantxa Cabañas-Martínez; María Desamparados Bernat‐Adell; Ana Folch Ayora; Eladio Collado‐Boira; Pablo Salas‐Medina
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 Syndrome: Quality of Life One Year after ICU Discharge
paper_journal: Journal of Community Medicine & Public Health

summary: This cross-sectional study examined oral health complaints and dental pathology in post-COVID patients using the OHIP-14 questionnaire and clinical examination. While it documents elevated rates of dry mouth (30.04%), taste loss (24.90%), and oral mucosal lesions in COVID-19 survivors, it is a descriptive epidemiological study with no intervention or treatment component.
paper_authors: O. E. Bekjanova; S. P. Rubnikovich; V. R. Kayumova; Yu. L. Denisova; K. Y. Egorova
paper_title: Symptoms of post-COVID oral health conditions and their influence on the risk of developing dental pathology
paper_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus, Medical series

summary: This cross-sectional study compares ocular blood flow parameters in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) who recently had COVID-19 versus those without prior COVID-19 infection using laser speckle flowgraphy. The study identifies significant changes in microvascular hemodynamics in the optic nerve head and peripapillary retina in POAG patients with moderate post-COVID-19 syndrome, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: S. Yu. Petrov; T. D. Okhotsimskaya; O. I. Markelova
paper_title: Analysis of Blood Circulation Parameters of the Optic Nerve Head and Peripapillary Region of the Retina in Patients with Poag Against the Background of Post-COVID-19 Syndrome

summary: This prospective cross-sectional study assessed sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL) in 100 post-COVID-19 patients using pure tone audiometry. The study documents that SNHL is a common extrapulmonary complication of COVID-19, with 45% of patients experiencing bilateral moderate hearing loss, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Shaimaa E. Kabil; Reda Behairy; Mohammad Sayed; Mohamed El Sharkawy; Houssam Eldin Hassanin; Mahmoud Elsaeed; Ibrahim H. Yousef; Ahmed M. Ewis; Ahmed H. Wahba; Fawzy Omar; Ahmed Beshir; Mohamed S. H. Zaki; Ashraf Moursi; Khaled Makboul; Ahmed Kabil
paper_title: Sensorineural hearing loss in post-COVID-19 patients

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 197 individuals assessing persistent symptoms in those partially or fully recovered from COVID-19. Found post-COVID syndrome present in 52.3% of respondents, with women showing higher risk for depression, anosmia, dysgeusia, and alopecia, while obese participants reported more arthralgia, dyspnea, cough, and odynophagia.
paper_authors: María Isabel Rojo-Gutiérrez
paper_title: Frequency of signs and symptoms in the Post-COVID Syndrome of subjects partially or fully recovered from COVID-19

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed the frequency of depression and anxiety in 450 COVID-19-positive patients using PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scales during April-May 2021. The study found depression more prevalent in older age groups and anxiety in younger age groups, but it is a descriptive epidemiological study that does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Muhammad Imran Javid; Hanan Alressi
paper_title: Frequency of depression among mental health patients in the POST-COVID-19 ERA.

summary: Descriptive cross-sectional study of 88 COVID-19 patients with cardiovascular disease history, examining patient demographics and long COVID prevalence. Findings show majority were aged 60-75 years, female, with hospitalization <14 days, but no treatment intervention was studied.
paper_authors: Mochammad Rachmat Deriansyah; Poernomo; Titik Respati
paper_title: Gambaran Karakteristik Pasien Covid-19 dengan Riwayat Penyakit Kardiovaskular di Sebuah Rumah Sakit di Provinsi Jawa Barat

summary: Cross-sectional observational study assessing respiratory muscle strength, lung function, and exercise capacity in 49 post-COVID-19 patients two years after recovery. Found diffusion impairment (32%), reduced exercise capacity (44%), and respiratory muscle weakness (41%), but provides no intervention or treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Ayad Mohammed Salem; Noor Al Khathlan; Majid Alogily; Mohammed Alharbi; Naser Alsubaei; Hisham AlOuhali; Abdullah AlOtaibi; Abdulaziz Al Hamam; Kholoud Al Ghamdi; Lubna Al-Asoom; Talay Yar
paper_title: Respiratory muscle weakness, reduced exercise capacity, and impaired lung functions in long-term post-COVID-19 patients

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 2,055 COVID-19 recovered individuals in Jordan assessing mental health outcomes using the MHI-38 inventory. Found high prevalence of depression (46.3%), anxiety (45.8%), and loss of control (47.2%), with employment status, tobacco use, and COVID-19 severity as risk factors.
paper_authors: Sawsan Abuhammad; Omar F. Khabour; Karem H. Alzoubi; Shaher Hamaideh; Basheer Y. Khassawneh; Baha F. Alsmadi; Abdelrahman M. Ababneh; Safa Alqudah
paper_title: Mental health of COVID-19 recovered individuals: A national study from Jordan

summary: Observational cross-sectional study of 457 elderly Turkish patients (≥65 years) with persistent musculoskeletal complaints after COVID-19 infection. Found widespread pain (81%), myalgia (63.7%), and arthralgia (44.4%) significantly associated with comorbidities, hospitalization, and pulmonary involvement.
paper_authors: Yesim GOKCE-KUTSAL; Nilufer Kutay ORDU-GÖKKAYA; Sevilay KARAHAN; Fatma Jale IRDESEL; Nurdan PAKER; Saime AY; Vildan BİNAY-SAFER; Dilek KESKİN; İlke COSKUN BENLİDAYİ; Aylin SARİ; Filiz SERTPOYRAZ; Ozlem ALTİNDAG; Pinar BORMAN
paper_title: WHAT AWAITS US AFTER COVID-19? MUSCULOSKELETAL SYSTEM INVOLVEMENT IN THE ELDERLY POPULATION IN TÜRKİYE AND ITS AFTERMATH

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed the clinical and psychological consequences of COVID-19 in 96 Russian adolescents (48 with prior COVID-19, 48 controls) at various time points post-infection. The study found post-COVID syndrome characterized by asthenia, impaired attention/taste/smell, high anxiety, and depressive symptoms, with the most severe emotional symptoms occurring around the second month post-infection.
paper_authors: I. A. Cherevikova; E. A. Tkachuk; V. M. Polyakov; N. S. Vasileva; Zh. V. Prokhorova; A. S. Votineva; N. A. Myasishchev
paper_title: Assessment of consequences of COVID-19 in adolescents by the method of questionnaire

summary: Cross-sectional study examining insomnia, dysfunctional beliefs about sleep, and depression in COVID-19-infected individuals. While the paper addresses post-infection sleep disorders, it focuses on acute COVID-19 infection outcomes rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months post-infection).
paper_authors: Jaeeun Song; Seockhoon Chung
paper_title: Post-Infection Insomnia, Dysfunctional Beliefs About Sleep, and Depression in the COVID-19-Infected General Population

summary: Cross-sectional study of 447 COVID-19 patients in Tehran examining the prevalence and types of persistent/late-onset complications at least 4 weeks after symptom onset. Found 77.2% experienced complications (cardiopulmonary and skin-related most common), with associations to older age, female sex, psychological stress, and inadequate rest.
paper_authors: Saberian P.; Pazooki B.; Hasani-Sharamin P.; Garjani K.; Ahmadi Hatam Z.; Dadashi F.; Baratloo A.
paper_title: Persistent/Late-Onset Complications of COVID-19 in General Population: A Cross-Sectional Study in Tehran, Iran.
paper_journal: International journal of community based nursing and midwifery

summary: This study analyzes serological testing for SARS-CoV-2-specific antibodies (IgM and IgG) in 12,860 urological hospital patients from 2021-2025, monitoring immune response patterns over time. It is an observational study characterizing immune markers in post-COVID syndrome rather than evaluating a treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Sergiy Vozianov; Tetyana Poroshina; Victoria Driyanska; Alina Romanenko; Oleksandr Vozianov; Oleksandr Shevchuk; Maryna Kosiukhno; Viktoriya Savchenko; Nataliya Kalinina; Olena Petryna; Nina Malashevska; Olena Yanishevska; Halyna Hrymova; Volodymyr Savchuk; Rostyslav Ladniuk; Maryna Akimova; Kamil Nurimanov
paper_title: Serological Testing for Specific Antibodies to SARS-CoV-2 in Patients in a Urological Hospital

summary: Cross-sectional study of 188 COVID-19 survivors 1-6 months post-infection examining sleep disturbances (poor sleep quality and insomnia) and associated factors including anxiety and depression. Found 43.6% reported poor sleep quality and 41% reported insomnia, with higher anxiety and depression scores associated with worse sleep outcomes.
paper_authors: Selvi Ceran; Gonca Aşut; Bilge Ağar; Güler Almıla Güllü; Dilan Değer; Selin Saka; Yağmur Azra Bilçen; Umut Barış Çalışkan
paper_title: Post-Acute Sleep Disturbances Following COVID-19 and Associated Factors: A Single-Center Study

summary: Cross-sectional study of 85 COVID-19 patients evaluated >3 weeks after acute infection to assess symptom persistence and associated factors. Found 52% had persistent symptoms (fatigue 49%, cough 33%), associated with female sex, obesity, age 35-55, and initial hospitalization, with symptoms generally resolving over time.
paper_authors: Manuel Antonio Prieto; Omar Prieto; Horacio Matias Castro
paper_title: Covid prolongado: estudio de corte transversal
paper_journal: Revista de la Facultad de Ciencias Médicas de Córdoba

summary: This comparative cross-sectional study compared physical manifestations in COVID-19 recovered individuals versus uninfected controls, finding significantly elevated risks of fatigue, anosmia, ageusia, irregular heartbeat, and dyspnea in the recovered group. The study is descriptive/observational and does not evaluate any treatment intervention, so it does not meet inclusion criteria for a treatment trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: Lana Alzamil; Lolwah Almotairy; Reem Alghamdi; Layan Alkhoriji; Lamiaa Fiala; Samira Mahboub
paper_title: Long-Term Physical Manifestations among Patients Recovered From COVID-19 Infection

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 635 mild COVID-19 patients in Turkey assessed the presence and frequency of persisting symptoms at 6+ months post-infection. The study identified fatigue, muscle pain, memory problems, joint pain, and smell disorders as the most common long COVID symptoms, with significant associations between symptom persistence and factors like initial lung involvement and anticoagulant use.
paper_authors: Adem DURMAZ; Muammer YILMAZ
paper_title: Long-Covid: What Awaits Us After Corona Infection?
paper_journal: Journal of Basic and Clinical Health Sciences

summary: This cross-sectional study compared cognitive function and ammonia levels in 41 post-COVID patients versus 19 controls, finding cognitive impairment in 45% of COVID survivors (more pronounced in those with post-COVID syndrome) and hyperammonemia in 54% of survivors. No significant correlation was found between hyperammonemia and cognitive impairment.
paper_authors: D. D. Mukhametova; E. N. Belousova; Z. I. Fashieva; M. G. Nazarova; M. V. Knyazeva; D. I. Abdulganieva
paper_title: Evaluation of Hyperammonemia and Cognitive Impairment in post-COVID patients

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 556 workers with intensive computer workload examining the timing and frequency of post-COVID syndrome manifestations occurring 1-4 weeks after hospital discharge. Study ranked occupational risk factors and symptom patterns but did not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Nina P. Golovkova; Lyudmila P. Kuzmina; Yulia F. Afanasyeva; Lyudmila M. Bezrukavnikova
paper_title: Risk factors, timing and frequency of occurrence of post-COVID syndrome in workers with intensive computer workload
paper_journal: Russian Journal of Occupational Health and Industrial Ecology

summary: This cross-sectional study examines the prevalence and persistence of post-COVID symptoms among medical workers employed in COVID clinics and laboratories in Russia. While it documents long-term sequelae including chest pain, joint pain, shortness of breath, and cognitive impairment, it is a passive epidemiological survey with no intervention or treatment evaluation, making it ineligible for the treatment trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: Amanbekova Au; Olga Grebeneva; А.Ж. Шадетова
paper_title: PREVALENCE OF LONG-TERM EFFECTS OF COVID‑19 AMONG MEDICAL WORKERS EMPLOYED IN COVID CLINICS AND LABORATORIES
paper_journal: Proceedings of The 17th Russian National Congress with International Participation «OCCUPATION and HEALTH», 26-29 September 2023, Nizhny Novgorod

summary: Cross-sectional survey of French general practitioners documenting the prevalence of long COVID patients in primary care and their most common symptoms. This is an epidemiological survey of GP experience, not a treatment intervention study.
paper_authors: Bérengère Davin-Casalena; Romain Lutaud; Dimitri Scronias; Valérie Guagliardo; Pierre Verger
paper_title: French General Practitioners Frequently See Patients with Long-COVID
paper_journal: The Journal of the American Board of Family Medicine

summary: This cross-sectional study examined the prevalence and patterns of long COVID symptoms in 3, 6, 9, and 18 months post-hospitalization among COVID-19 survivors in Aruba. The study identified female sex and respiratory comorbidity as risk factors for persistent symptoms, but did not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Veronika Duwel; Jaclyn M.L. de Kort; Caroline M. Becker; Selène M. Kock; Garreth G. Tromp; Jamiu O. Busari
paper_title: A Cross-Sectional Study of the Physical and Mental Well-Being of Long COVID Patients in Aruba

summary: This observational cross-sectional study assessed long COVID symptoms in 45 children aged 5-17 years with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection at a tertiary hospital in 2021. Two-thirds of children developed long COVID symptoms, most commonly fatigue (45.2%), decreased appetite (38.7%), and muscle aches (32.3%), with symptoms occurring across all initial COVID severity levels.
paper_authors: Djatnika Setiabudi; Buti Azfiani Azhali; Muhammad Akbar Tirtosudiro; Monika Hasna Ramadhan; Muhamad Rinaldhi; Heda Melinda Nataprawira
paper_title: Long COVID or Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) in Children and Adolescents

summary: Cross-sectional study examining new symptoms reported at primary care visits among 3,154 NYC patients during three post-acute COVID-19 follow-up intervals (0.5-9 months post-infection). Found that 16% of patients had new diagnoses, with respiratory complaints and fatigue being most common, but this is an observational epidemiological study with no treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Kelly Terlizzi; Eric Kutscher; Yuliya Yoncheva
paper_title: Monitoring New Symptoms After COVID-19 Infection Among Primary Care Patients in New York City
paper_journal: The Journal of the American Board of Family Medicine

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of the 2022 MEPS dataset examining work absenteeism in US adults with long COVID, comparing missed workdays across three groups: never had COVID, COVID-19 without long COVID, and long COVID. Finds that long COVID patients miss 171% more workdays annually than those without COVID infection.
paper_authors: Rachel Liu-Galvin; Frank A. Orlando; Tamkeen Khan; Gregory D. Wozniak; Arch G. Mainous
paper_title: Long COVID and Days of Work Missed Due to Illness or Injury by Adults in the United States, 2022
paper_journal:
The Journal of the American Board of Family
                Medicine

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 488 university students measuring prior SARS-CoV-2 infection prevalence (41%) via antibody testing and assessing persistent symptoms post-infection. Found 11.4% of symptomatic students reported persistent symptoms consistent with post-acute COVID-19 a median of 132 days after infection, but this is a descriptive epidemiological study without treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Mark H. Ebell; David Forgacs; Ye Shen; Ted M. Ross; Cassie Hulme; Michelle Bentivegna; Hannah B. Hanley; Alexandria M. Jefferson; Lauren Hainess
paper_title: High Prevalence of Both Previous Infection with SARS-CoV-2 and Persistent Symptoms
paper_journal:
The Journal of the American Board of Family
                Medicine

summary: This paper analyzes the economic burden of long COVID by estimating lost labor costs among US adults using the 2022 Medical Expenditure Panel Survey. It found that individuals with long COVID had more than twice the lost labor costs compared to those without COVID, totaling approximately $12.8 billion in population-level lost labor costs.
paper_authors: Rachel Liu-Galvin; Frank A. Orlando; Arch G. Mainous
paper_title: Economic Burden of Long COVID: Lost Labor Costs in US Adults
paper_journal:
The Journal of the American Board of Family
                Medicine

summary: This cross-sectional study compared choroidal thickness measurements using OCT imaging between 40 post-COVID-19 patients and 40 age-matched controls. Post-COVID patients showed significantly increased choroidal thickness across all measured regions, suggesting vascular involvement in post-COVID syndrome pathogenesis.
paper_authors: Jeniffer Domingues de Jesus; Raquel J. Soares; Libania M. Dias; Suzana M. Ventura; Joao C. Pedro
paper_title: Analysis of Choroidal Macular Thickness in Early Post-Covid-19 Patients

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 183 long COVID patients investigating associations between fatigue, autonomic symptoms, interoceptive sensibility, illness perceptions, and distress. Findings show fatigue is severe and multifaceted, with autonomic symptoms and illness perceptions explaining 21-54% of variance, but no intervention or treatment is evaluated.
paper_authors: Bethan Thomas; rachael pattinson; Christine Bundy; Jennifer Davies
paper_title: Interactions between autonomic symptoms, interoception, illness perceptions and distress in Long COVID fatigue: An integrative model

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 250 COVID-19 recovered patients assessing sleep disturbances and sleep quality using standardized questionnaires. Found high prevalence of sleep problems (77.6% poor sleep quality, 53.6% subthreshold insomnia) and identified associations with reinfection and daytime tiredness, but did not test or evaluate any intervention.
paper_authors: Jyotirbina Karmakar; Amar Kumar Misra; Parnava Das; Joydeep Mukherjee; Jasodhara Chaudhuri; Praveen Kumar Yadav; Milan Chakraborty; Dibakar Haldar; Manamita Mandal
paper_title: A cross-sectional survey on sleep disturbances with special reference to sleep quality among COVID-19-recovered patients attending outpatient department of a medical college hospital in Eastern India

summary: Cross-sectional survey of healthcare workers at a Nepalese medical academy assessing the prevalence and symptom profile of long COVID-19 using the COVID Yorkshire Rehabilitation Screening Tool. Study found 68.1% prevalence with fatigue, anxiety, and dyspnea as the most common symptoms, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Bimal Pandey; Sanjeev Gautam; Sanjit Karki; Mipsang Lama; Keshav Raj Sigdel; Niroj Hirachan
paper_title: Prevalence of long COVID-19 syndrome among health care workers of Patan Academy of Health Sciences
paper_journal: Journal of Patan Academy of Health Sciences

summary: A descriptive cross-sectional study of 108 healthcare professionals who recovered from COVID-19, assessing the prevalence and types of post-COVID health problems they experienced. Found that 42.6% experienced various symptoms including fatigue, persistent cough, headache, and malaise, with no significant association with age, sex, or vaccination status.
paper_authors: Babita Sapkota; Gita Dhakal Chalise; Sarala Shrestha
paper_title: Post COVID Health Problems faced by COVID-19 Infected Healthcare Professionals of a Tertiary Level Hospital
paper_journal: Medical Journal of Shree Birendra Hospital

summary: Community-based observational study documenting the prevalence and clinical presentation of post-COVID syndrome in 265 patients recovered from acute COVID-19 in North Kerala, India. Found 9.81% had post-COVID symptoms beyond 3 months, with female gender, comorbidities, and treatment severity as significant risk factors.
paper_authors: Sarin SM; Surag MK; Rijit Kannan; Mukundan PK; Ranjit Kumar KC; Aishwarya Sureshbabu K.
paper_title: Prevalence and clinical presentation of Post-COVID syndrome in patients recovered from acute COVID infections in North Kerala

summary: This cross-sectional study examines the association between COVID-19 infection and new-onset diabetes in 38 patients at a tertiary care hospital in Nepal. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 complications (hyperglycemia and diabetes onset during active infection) rather than long COVID sequelae, and does not test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Prabin Adhikari; Krishna Chandra Devkota
paper_title: Association Between COVID-19 Infection and New-Onset Diabetes in a Tertiary Care Hospital in Kathmandu

summary: This study develops and validates the PCS Fatigue Severity Measure V1, a 10-item instrument for quantifying fatigue in post-COVID-19 syndrome, using Rasch analysis on 414 participants from the Quebec Action for Post-COVID cohort. The measure showed strong correlations with criterion measures and distinguished between working individuals and those on sick leave, providing initial evidence for measuring PCS fatigue at a single time point.
paper_authors: Nancy Mayo; Marie-Josée Brouillette; Lesley K. Fellows; Stanley Hum
paper_title: Quantifying the Degree of Fatigue in People Reporting Symptoms of Post-COVID-19 Syndrome: Results from a Rasch Analysis

summary: This cross-sectional study compared oxidative stress markers in hemodialysis patients with and without long-COVID sequelae 3.5 months post-infection. Long-COVID patients showed significantly elevated malondialdehyde and reduced antioxidant levels, suggesting oxidative stress may contribute to persistent symptoms, but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Belousova, O.; Kolesnyk, Mykola; Korol, Lesya; Malashevska, N.; Marchenko, V.; Ostapenko, T.; Popova, O.; Rysyev, A.; Snisar, Lyudmyla; Stepanova, Natalia
paper_title: Long-COVID sequelae are associated with oxidative stress in hemodialysis patients
paper_journal: Ukrainian Journal of Nephrology and Dialysis

summary: This cross-sectional cohort study examines oxidative stress markers in hemodialysis patients with and without post-COVID syndrome, measuring blood levels of malondialdehyde, paraoxonase-1, myeloperoxidase, and other biomarkers. The study identifies an elevated MPO/PON-1 ratio as a potential predictive biomarker for post-COVID syndrome in HD patients, with 88.5% sensitivity and 68.4% specificity.
paper_authors: L. Korol; Natalia Stepanova; O. Popova; N. Malashevska; V. Vasylchenko; Tetyana Ostapenko; A. Rysyev; М. Kolesnyk
paper_title: Myeloperoxidase/paraoxonase ratio as a prognostic marker for post-COVID syndrome in patients undergoing hemodialysis: A cross-sectional cohort study
paper_journal: Ukrainian Journal of Nephrology and Dialysis

summary: This cross-sectional survey of 215 Malaysian COVID-19 survivors documents the prevalence and types of prolonged symptoms (lethargy, concentration difficulty, cough) at 1-3 months post-infection, and identifies female sex, chronic lung disease, and hypertension as risk factors. The study is descriptive and observational with no intervention tested, making it ineligible for a clinical trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: Hana Maizuliana Solehan; Nurul Azmawati Mohamed; Mohd Dzulkhairi Mohd Rani; Muslimah Ithnin
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 Symptoms, an Online Survey in Malaysia

summary: Three-centre cross-sectional study examining COPD course in 46 patients with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection stratified by extent of viral pulmonary involvement. Found high rates of COPD exacerbation (69.6%) and new-onset COPD (26.1%) in post-COVID period, with worse outcomes in those with severe pulmonary involvement, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Р.И. Алекперов; Natalia Makaryants; Mikhail Chushkin; А.Ф. Абубикиров; E.Z. Kudryavtseva; Rashad Abdullayev; R.Yu. Abdullayev
paper_title: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease in Post-COVID-19 Patients

summary: This cross-sectional study examines kidney pathology (glomerulonephritis) occurring 8-12 months after moderate COVID-19 by measuring TGF-β1 and VEGF levels in blood and urine across three groups: GN patients with prior COVID-19, COVID-19 patients without GN, and healthy controls. While the paper confirms an association between moderate COVID-19 and delayed GN manifestation, it is excluded because it does not test or evaluate any treatment or intervention—it is purely a biomarker study of disease pathology.
paper_authors: Л.О. Зуб; B.V. Horban; Вероника Кулачек
paper_title: The link between moderate COVID-19 and delayed manifestation of glomerulonephritis: Insights from cluster analysis of TGF-β1 and VEGF levels
paper_journal: Ukrainian Journal of Nephrology and Dialysis

summary: This cross-sectional study examines the psycho-emotional state of 80 women with infertility after COVID-19 infection, comparing them to a control group. The authors found significantly higher rates of anxiety (91.2% vs 30%) and depression (13.8% vs 2.5%) in the long COVID group, with strong correlations between psycho-emotional severity and personality traits.
paper_authors: Igor S. Golovchak; Oleksandra H. Boichuk; Iryna M. Kupchak; Yuliya B. Motsyuk
paper_title: THE INFLUENCE OF THE PSYCHO-EMOTIONAL STATE ON THE REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH OF WOMEN AFTER THE EXPERIENCED DISEASE OF COVID-19

summary: This cross-sectional study examined the association between vitamin D levels and inflammatory markers (CRP and D-dimer) in 70 post-COVID recovery patients. The study found that vitamin D deficiency was associated with significantly higher CRP and D-dimer levels, but it is an observational assessment without any intervention or treatment being tested.
paper_authors: Sisir Chakraborty; Sanchayan Sinha; Soumita Ghosh Sengupta; Satwika Sinha; Indranil Chakraborty
paper_title: Association between vitamin D and C-reactive protein level in post-COVID recovery period

summary: Cross-sectional study examining risk factors for post-COVID-19 syndrome in 65 children with recurrent/chronic lung diseases. Found no statistically significant associations with demographic or acute-phase clinical variables, but identified increased airway hyperreactivity in children with asthma as a potential long-term risk factor.
paper_authors: O. O. Rechkina; V. O. Stryzh; S. M. Rudenko
paper_title: Analysis of the Risk Factors of Post-COVID-19 Syndrome in Children with Recurrent and Chronic Lung Diseases

summary: Cross-sectional study examining quality of life in 132 post-COVID syndrome patients, comparing those with newly diagnosed carbohydrate metabolism disorders (impaired glucose tolerance or type 2 diabetes) to those without. Finds that post-COVID patients with carbohydrate metabolism disorders have significantly reduced quality of life on physical and role functioning scales.
paper_authors: K.S. Savchuk; Saint Petersburg, Russian Federation; A.S. Simbirtsev; L.V. Ryabova
paper_title: Disturbances in Carbohydrate Metabolism as a Predictor of Decreased Quality of Life in Patients with Post-COVID Syndrome

summary: This Ukrainian study examines post-COVID syndrome (PCS) prevalence and its association with cognitive dysfunction and quality of life in 200 hemodialysis patients (118 with PCS, 82 without). While the paper documents worse cognitive function and quality of life in hemodialysis patients with long COVID, it is a passive observational cross-sectional study with no intervention or treatment being tested.
paper_authors: І. Dudar; O. Loboda; І. Shifris; Yuliia Honchar
paper_title: Post-COVID syndrome and cognitive dysfunction in patients treated with hemodialysis
paper_journal: Ukrainian Journal of Nephrology and Dialysis

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing functional status and long COVID-related limitations in 142 nurses at a Ecuadorian hospital during 2022. 45.1% experienced minimal to severe functional limitations, with significant associations found between functional status and age/infection count.
paper_authors: Teresa Daniela Cuenca Jumbo; Dylan Javier Loachamin Quinatoa; Rosa Pastuña Doicela; Paulina Isabel Armas Freire
paper_title: Functional status related to post-COVID 19 Syndrome in the nursing staff of a Second Level Hospital in Quito-Ecuador

summary: Cross-sectional survey comparing post-COVID syndrome prevalence and symptoms among senior students at two Ukrainian universities, finding high rates of neurological and psychological symptoms affecting academic performance. The paper identifies symptoms and their impact but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: T.I. Yarmola; O. V. Vlasova; Lidiia Tkachenko; N.V. Moisieieva; A.V. Vakhnenko
paper_title: STRATEGIES TO MITIGATE THE IMPACT OF POST-COVID-19 SYNDROME ON HIGHER EDUCATION QUALITY
paper_journal: Актуальні проблеми сучасної медицини: Вісник Української медичної стоматологічної академії

summary: Cross-sectional study of 201 post-COVID-19 discharged patients assessing health problems and persistent symptoms during recovery. Found high prevalence of weakness (71.64%), fatigue (60.69%), and cough (39.80%) in the post-recovery period, with recommendations for follow-up care and lifestyle modifications.
paper_authors: Pandya Vijay; Dave Bhargav; Patel Nikhil; Prajapati Manisha
paper_title: Evaluation of Health Problems of Post COVID-19 Discharged Patients from Dedicated COVID Health Centre (DCHC), (Nootan General Hospital, Visnagar)
paper_journal: International Journal of Current Research and Review

summary: This descriptive-quantitative study investigates factors influencing cycling as physical activity in elderly post-COVID-19 patients using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire. Results show 88.6% of elderly participants cycle due to awareness of exercise benefits, with higher participation among females aged 55-60.
paper_authors: Cahyo Setiawan; Suci Muqodimatul Jannah
paper_title: THE INFLUENCE-FACTOR OF CYCLING AS PHYSICAL ACTIVITY IN ELDERLY POST COVID-19

summary: This cross-sectional study examined determinants of support systems and quality of life in 110 post-COVID-19 patients in Indonesia. The study found significant relationships between quality of life and factors like family attitudes/behavior, age, and comorbid conditions, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Irfan Irfan; Syaputra Artama; Aris Wawomeo
paper_title: Determinants of the Support System and Quality of Life for Post-COVID-19 Patients

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing white matter macro- and microstructure in 31 neurologic long COVID (NeuroPASC) patients versus 41 asymptomatic controls using brain MRI and cognitive testing. Found larger cerebral white matter volume, higher white matter mean kurtosis, and lower cognitive performance (attention, processing speed, verbal learning) in NeuroPASC patients, along with elevated interferon levels suggesting immune dysregulation.
paper_authors: Erin E. O’Connor; Rosangela Salerno-Goncalves; Nikita Rednam; Rory O’Brien; Peter Rock; Andrea R. Levine; Thomas A. Zeffiro
paper_title: Macro- and Microstructural White Matter Differences in Neurologic Postacute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: A cross-sectional study comparing 120 COVID-19 survivors with 120 healthy controls on cognitive, somatic, and psychiatric measures using standardized questionnaires. Findings show survivors have significantly higher cognitive difficulties, body sensations, and anxiety, but not depression.
paper_authors: Uğur ERAY; Başar AYRIBAŞ; Ömer Furkan ÇAĞLAR; Turgut HACIOĞLU; Fatih ALİBEYOĞLU
paper_title: Post-COVID syndrome? COVID-19 survivors suffer from cognitive difficulties, somatic complaints and anxiety
paper_journal: Journal of Health Sciences and Medicine

summary: This cross-sectional study examined the prevalence and predictors of long COVID among 1,338 COVID-19 cases at a university in Washington, DC, finding 36% prevalence and identifying risk factors including underlying conditions, female sex, smoking, and acute symptom severity. The study does not evaluate any treatment or intervention, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis despite being relevant long COVID research.
paper_authors: Megan Landry; Sydney Bornstein; Nitasha Nagaraj; Gary A. Sardon; Amanda Castel; Amita Vyas; Karen McDonnell; Mira Agneshwar; Alyson Wilkinson; Lynn Goldman
paper_title: Postacute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 in University Setting

summary: Cross-sectional study of 11,057 US school-aged children examining functional limitations and illness-related absenteeism in children with and without long COVID. Found that children with long COVID had higher rates of functional limitations (18.3% vs 8.6% memory difficulty) and chronic absenteeism, but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Nicole D. Ford; Regina M. Simeone; Caroline Pratt; Sharon Saydah
paper_title: Functional Limitations and Illness-Related Absenteeism among School-Aged Children with and without Long COVID, United States, 2022–2023

summary: This cross-sectional study examines the relationship between antibody levels (IgM and IgG) and ongoing symptoms in 105 COVID-19 survivors who donated plasma. The findings show that IgM and IgG levels vary with time elapsed, prior medications (favipiravir, hydroxychloroquine), and demographic factors, contributing to understanding of post-COVID symptom persistence.
paper_authors: Aşkı Vural; Erdoğan Öz; Osman Küçükkelepçe; Bilengül Aslan Vural; Hakan Sezgin Sayiner
paper_title: Correlation between antibody levels and long-term symptoms in survivors of COVID-19: health outcomes and societal implications
paper_journal: Journal of Health Sciences and Medicine

summary: Cross-sectional study of 524 post-COVID patients with dizziness, measuring dizziness-related disability using the Dizziness Handicap Inventory. Finds that 51.8% have moderate/severe dizziness disability, particularly during head movements and strenuous activities, suggesting vestibular impairment.
paper_authors: Elin Östlind; Elisabeth Ekstrand; Iben Axén; Christina Brogårdh; Agneta Malmgren Fänge; Kjerstin Stigmar; Eva Ekvall Hansson
paper_title: Dizziness-related disability in persons with post-COVID condition: A cross sectional study

summary: This cross-sectional study compares post-exertional malaise (PEM) experiences between 80 long COVID patients and 151 ME/CFS patients using questionnaires about PEM triggers, symptoms, recovery, and prevention. While it finds that long COVID patients experience PEM similarly to ME/CFS patients in some ways, it is a purely observational comparison study with no treatment intervention or control group assignment.
paper_authors: Suzanne D. Vernon; Megan Hartle; Karen Sullivan; Jennifer Bell; Saeed Abbaszadeh; Derya Unutmaz; Lucinda Bateman
paper_title: Post-exertional malaise among people with long COVID compared to myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS)

summary: Cross-sectional comparative study examining cardiometabolic characteristics in elderly patients (aged 60-89) with comorbidities who experienced mild-to-moderate COVID-19 versus controls. Found that post-COVID patients had significantly worse lipid profiles, elevated fasting glucose, reduced renal function, elevated heart rate, and higher NT-proBNP levels, suggesting persistent cardiometabolic sequelae of COVID-19.
paper_authors: A.A. Starichkova; O.V. Tsygankova; L.D. Khidirova; V.L. Lukinov; P.I. Litvinenko; A.A. Starichkov
paper_title: Cardiometabolic characteristics of post-COVID-19 syndrome in elderly and senile patients with comorbidities

summary: Cross-sectional study of 30 long COVID patients (>3 months post-infection) undergoing outpatient neurorehabilitation, characterizing physical and neuropsychological sequelae. Fatigue (86.6%), dyspnea (66.7%), cognitive impairment (63.3%), and neurological sequelae were prevalent, with rehabilitation addressing these persistent symptoms regardless of acute COVID severity.
paper_authors: Sergiu Albu; Nicolás Rivas Zozaya; Narda Murillo; Alberto García-Molina; Cristian Andrés Figueroa Chacón; Hatice Kumru
paper_title: What’s going on following acute COVID-19? Clinical characteristics of patients in an out-patient rehabilitation program

summary: Population-based cross-sectional study of 1,459 COVID-19 patients in Germany examining long-term symptoms ≥12 weeks post-infection. Found 72.6% prevalence in hospitalized patients and 46.2% in non-hospitalized patients, with fatigue, exhaustion, and cognitive difficulties as most common symptoms; identified female sex and comorbidity severity as key risk factors.
paper_authors: Christian Förster; Miriam Giovanna Colombo; Anna-Jasmin Wetzel; Peter Martus; Stefanie Joos
paper_title: Persisting symptoms after COVID-19

summary: Cross-sectional study of 135 type 2 diabetes patients 3-24 months post-COVID-19 examining endothelial dysfunction and thrombotic markers. Found elevated D-dimer, von Willebrand factor, and cell adhesion molecules in many patients despite normal coagulation parameters, but this is a descriptive observational study without treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Anna Alieva
paper_title: Indicators of endothelial dysfunction and the rate of thrombotic complications in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus at different periods after COVID-19

summary: Cross-sectional study of 497 Portuguese COVID-19 patients assessed 12-16 weeks after disease onset to estimate prevalence of post-COVID conditions and describe baseline characteristics. Found 47.5% cumulative incidence with fatigue (30.4%) and dyspnea (26.4%) as most frequent symptoms; male gender and certain BMI ranges were associated with lower odds of post-COVID conditions.
paper_authors: Tiago Gomes de Oliveira; Hugo Silva Almeida; Inês Baptista Pereira; Maria João Fernandes; Mariana Dias Almeida; Carlos Carvalho; Ana Bessa Monteiro; Ana Filipa Belo
paper_title: Post-COVID conditions: a Portuguese primary care study

summary: A cross-sectional study of 150 patients with prior COVID-19 infection presenting to an otolaryngology department, identifying otorhinolaryngologic symptoms in 84.67% and finding a 16% prevalence of long COVID syndrome (>12 weeks). The study describes symptom patterns including rhinorrhea, hyposmia, dysgeusia, and anosmia, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Ma. Nina Kristine Sison; Emmanuel Tadeus Cruz
paper_title: Otorhinolaryngologic Manifestations  of Long COVID-19 Infection Among Patients  at the Quezon City General Hospital
paper_journal: Philippine Journal of Otolaryngology Head and Neck Surgery

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing quality of life in acute COVID-19 patients with anosmia using a translated questionnaire. Focuses on acute infection symptom burden rather than long COVID or any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Anjenneth Mallari-Bernarte; Emmanuel Tadeus Cruz
paper_title: Quality of Life Among SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) Positive Patients with Anosmia Using the Short Version Questionnaire of Olfactory Disorders - Negative Statements Translated in Filipino (sQOD-NS Ph)
paper_journal: Philippine Journal of Otolaryngology Head and Neck Surgery

summary: This cross-sectional survey study (n=1,482) examines the prevalence of persistent post-COVID symptoms and their associations with depression, anxiety, and insomnia in Sweden at 18 months post-pandemic. The paper reports high prevalence of persistent symptoms (84.5%) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention, making it an epidemiological/observational study rather than a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Karin C. Brocki; Monica Buhrman; Farzaneh Badinlou; Lance M. McCracken
paper_title: The context of COVID-19 at 18 months in relation to depression, anxiety, insomnia: The emerging role of post COVID-19 symptoms

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 98 patients recovering from moderate-severe COVID-19 in Vietnam examining prevalence of post-COVID health issues. Found 73.5% experienced persistent symptoms at ≥12 weeks, most commonly hair loss, fatigue, dyspnea, and sleep difficulties, but no intervention or treatment was tested.
paper_authors: Nguyen Ngoc Tran; Khoa Quy; Huy Ngoc Pham; Khanh Trinh Ngoc Van; Hoang Nguyen Vu Ung; Tung Huy Pham; Viet Quoc Cao; Lan Ngoc Vuong
paper_title: Cross-sectional study of self-report of health issues in patients who had recovered from moderate-severe COVID-19 in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 384 post-COVID-19 recovering patients examining the relationship between cold-heat patterns in Traditional Chinese Medicine and post-COVID-19 symptoms. The study found significant associations between gender, cold-heat patterns, and post-COVID-19 status, providing TCM characterization of post-COVID syndrome.
paper_authors: An Nguyen Thanh Do; Minh Thi Binh Pham; Oanh Thi Kim Ngo
paper_title: A cross-sectional survey-based study of the cold and heat pattern of recovering patients after COVID-19 at the University medical center at Ho Chi Minh City branch 3 and students of the faculty of Traditional medicine, University of Medicine and Pharmacy at Ho Chi Minh City.

summary: Compares static balance, dynamic balance, and knee joint position sense between 15 women with acute/recent COVID-19 and 15 healthy controls. Finds significant differences in balance metrics and proprioception, but does not study long COVID (persistent post-acute sequelae) or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Salehe Negarestani; Mohammadreza Amirseyfaddini; Abdolhamid Daneshjoo; Masoud Karimzadeh; Sheida Shourabadi
paper_title: Comparison of Static, Dynamic Balance, Knee Joint Position Among Healthy Women and Those Infected with COVID-19
paper_journal: The Scientific Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine

summary: A cross-sectional descriptive study assessing psychosocial distress in 101 post-COVID-19 survivors using the Self-Reporting Questionnaire 29 (SRQ-29). Found that 82.17% of survivors experienced psychosocial problems including PTSD (43%), anxiety/depression (20%), and psychosis disorders (20%), but no treatment intervention was tested or evaluated.
paper_authors: Adinda Putri Lestari; Aat Sriati; Henny Yulianita
paper_title: Screening for psychosocial distress of post‐Covid‐19 among survivors using the self-reporting questionnaire 29 (SRQ-29)
paper_journal: Malahayati International Journal of Nursing and Health Science

summary: Cross-sectional study of 220 diabetic and non-diabetic COVID-19 patients assessing health-related quality of life (HRQoL) after hospitalization using the EQ-5D-5L questionnaire. Found that diabetic patients had significantly lower HRQoL scores than non-diabetic patients, with education and diabetes being independent predictors of quality of life outcomes.
paper_authors: Atashbahar, Omolbanin; Moqaddasi Amiri, Mohammad; Heidari Jamebozorgi, Majid; Sadat Razavi Nasab, Moazame; Nosratabadi, Iman; Sadeghi, Reza
paper_title: Factors Associated with Health-related Quality of Life after Hospitalization for COVID-19 in Diabetic and Non-diabetic Patients: A Cross-sectional Study

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between academic stress and quality of life among 106 nursing students who are COVID-19 survivors using standardized instruments (ASS and WHOQoL-BREF). Found no significant association between academic stress and quality of life domains, though authors recommend further research on factors affecting quality of life in COVID-19 survivors.
paper_authors: Butsainah Jihan; Chiyar Edison
paper_title: TINGKAT STRES AKADEMIK DAN KUALITAS HIDUP PADA MAHASISWA PENYINTAS COVID-19
paper_journal: Jurnal Ilmiah Keperawatan (Scientific Journal of Nursing)

summary: This retrospective observational study examines the relationship between COVID-19 reinfection and menstrual pattern changes in 155 women at a health polytechnic in Indonesia. While it documents menstrual changes associated with COVID-19 infection, it does not study long COVID specifically (persistent symptoms weeks-to-months post-infection) and contains no treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Suci Sholihat; Diah Eka Nugraheni; Susilo Damarini; Wewet Savitri; Septiyana Septiyana
paper_title: THE RELATIONS OF RE-INFECTION OF COVID-19 WITH CHANGES IN MENSTRUAL PATTERNS IN WOMEN OF CHILDBEARING AGE AT THE HEALTH POLYTECHNIC OF THE BENGKULU MINISTRY OF HEALTH IN 2022

summary: A cross-sectional descriptive study of 181 COVID-19 recovered patients in Bangladesh examining long-term health problems and their associations with demographic and clinical factors. The study found post-viral fatigue (85%), shortness of breath (74%), and cognitive symptoms as the most common long-term sequelae, with significant associations between symptom severity and comorbidities.
paper_authors: Abu Kawser Sarker; Kazi Shafiul Alam; Fateha Akter Ema; Md Yunus Ali
paper_title: Long Term Health Problems and Associated Factors among COVID-19 Recovered Patients

summary: Cross-sectional study measuring thyroid hormone levels (TSH, FT4) in 100 post-COVID patients with fatigue, comparing home-treated (n=50) vs hospital-treated (n=50) patients. Found significantly higher TSH and FT4 levels in home-treated patients, but this is a descriptive observational study with no intervention or treatment being tested.
paper_authors: Mohammad Masum Alam; Mohammad Matiur Rahman; Forhadul Hoque Mollah; Indira Chowdhury
paper_title: Post-COVID fatigue: a new era of complication by altered thyroid function

summary: Cross-sectional study of 236 post-COVID patients examining metabolic parameters including glucose, lipids, ferritin, and renal function. Found significant metabolic abnormalities including elevated blood glucose, HbA1c, serum ferritin, and dyslipidemia, suggesting increased risk of diabetes and systemic complications.
paper_authors: Mohammed Atiqur Rahman; Shamim Ahmed; Rajashish Chakrabortty; Shahjada Selim; Samprity Islam; Md. Tanvir Rahman; Shah Ashiqur Rahman Ashiq Choudhury; Kazi Rahila Ferdousi; Shahabul Huda Chowdhury
paper_title: Metabolic Parameters of Post-COVID Patients in a Tertiary Care Hospital in Bangladesh

summary: Cross-sectional descriptive study measuring fatigue levels in 40 elderly long COVID survivors in Pekanbaru, Indonesia at least 14 days post-infection. Found that 55% experienced mild fatigue, 25% moderate fatigue, 5% severe fatigue, and 15% no fatigue, with recommendations for post-isolation nursing assessment and intervention.
paper_authors: Abdurrahman Hamid; Eka Wisanti; Awaliyah Ulfah Ayudytha Ezdha
paper_title: Analisa Tingkat Kelelahan Lansia Post Covid-19 di Kota Pekanbaru

summary: Cross-sectional study investigating histopathological changes in lung tissue of long COVID patients through transbronchial biopsies. Findings show patterns of diffuse alveolar damage, vascular abnormalities, inflammation, and fibrosis over weeks to months post-infection, providing mechanistic insight but not evaluating any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Grgur Salai; Jasna Tekavec-Trkanjec; Ivona Kovačević; Čedna Tomasović-Lončarić; Arijana Pačić; Mirna Vergles; Divo Ljubičić; Daria Cvetković-Kučić; Ivica Lukšić; Bruno Baršić
paper_title: Lung long distance: histopathological changes in lung tissue after COVID-19 pneumonia

summary: Cross-sectional study examining associations between body composition, muscle mass, strength, and physical function with Long COVID symptom severity in 17 adults. Found that higher muscle mass and strength are associated with lower Long COVID symptom scores, while greater body fat and BMI correlate with higher symptom severity.
paper_authors: Markus Filardi Moura Olinto; Victor César Dias Lins; Maurílio Tiradentes Dutra
paper_title: Muscle mass and strength are associated with lower scores of Long COVID symptoms

summary: This cross-sectional diagnostic validation study evaluated the KINDL questionnaire and CSSI-24 inventory for measuring quality of life and symptom burden in 84 children and adolescents with pediatric long COVID. The study established screening thresholds and found that these tools can help clinicians identify high-risk pediatric PASC cases, but did not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Lawrence Shih-Hsin Wu; Pei-Chi Chen; Xiao-Ling Liu; Shu-Tsen Liu; Chi-Hung Wei; Yu-Lung Hsu; Kai-Sheng Hsieh; Huan-Cheng Lai; Chien-Heng Lin; Chieh-Ho Chen; An-Chyi Chen; I-Ching Chou; Wen-Jue Soong; Hui-Ju Tsai; Chung-Ying Lin; Jiu-Yao Wang
paper_title: Effectiveness of Kinder Lebensqualität Fragebogen (KINDL) and Children’s Somatic Symptom Inventory-24 (CSSI-24) for measuring postacute sequelae of COVID-19 in children: a diagnostic validation study

summary: This study investigates olfactory and gustatory dysfunction in 228 mild COVID-19 patients during acute infection (March-April 2020), finding high prevalence of these symptoms with mostly spontaneous improvement within months. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 symptoms during active infection, not long COVID or post-acute sequelae, and does not test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Sung Jae Heo; Tae Hoon Kim; Seung-Heon Shin; Mi-Kyung Ye
paper_title: Characteristics and Prognosis of COVID-19 Induced Olfactory and Gustatory Dysfunction in Daegu
paper_journal: Korean Journal of Otorhinolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery

summary: This cross-sectional study surveyed COVID-19 survivors about persistent symptoms four weeks post-infection using online questionnaires. While documenting the prevalence and impact of long COVID symptoms on daily activities, it does not evaluate or test any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Sianty Dewi; Bernadette Dian Novita Dewi; Niluh Suwasanti; Paul L. Tahalele
paper_title: POST COVID-19 SYNDROME EFFECT ON DAILY LIFE ACTIVITIES

summary: This cross-sectional study investigated cellular stress responses, immune dysregulation, and biochemical signatures in 120 post-acute COVID-19 patients ≥30 days post-infection. The authors found persistent elevations in ER stress markers, inflammatory cytokines, and oxidative biomarkers that correlated with fatigue and dyspnea symptoms, suggesting quantifiable molecular disturbances underlying long COVID pathophysiology.
paper_title: Post-Acute COVID-19 Pathophysiology: Cellular Stress Responses, Immune Dysregulation, and Biochemical Signatures in Recovery Phase

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing lung function abnormalities using spirometry in 100 symptomatic post-COVID-19 patients 6-8 weeks post-discharge at a tertiary hospital in Bangladesh. Found 66% had restrictive changes in spirometry, significantly associated with disease severity and comorbidities like hypertension and diabetes.
paper_authors: Sharmin Sultana; Md Mohiuddin Ahmad; Hena Kamal; Md Bellal Hossain; Nirmal Kanti Sarkar; Goutom Sen; Sharmin Afroze; Md Miraz Mahmud
paper_title: Pulmonary Function Assessment with Spirometry in Symptomatic Post-COVID-19 Patients: A Cross-Sectional study at Dhaka Medical College Hospital
paper_journal: Journal of Bangladesh College of Physicians and Surgeons

summary: A retrospective cross-sectional analysis of 281 women comparing post-COVID syndrome manifestations between those with laboratory-confirmed vs non-confirmed COVID-19, stratified by age groups. Women with confirmed COVID-19 experienced 1.5–2.0 times higher rates of symptom burden including decreased quality of life, cardiac symptoms, hair loss, and arthralgia, with age-dependent patterns in laboratory abnormalities (ESR, D-dimer, platelet counts).
paper_authors: T. Yu. Agafonova; N. N. Elovikova; A. N. Fadeeva; D. A. Igisheva; V. O. Reshetnyak; A. A. Yudina
paper_title: Post-covid syndrome in women of different ages with laboratory-proven and non-confirmed COVID-19

summary: A cross-sectional study of 145 long COVID patients at a Turkish hospital assessing 77 symptoms and quality of life using standardized instruments. The study found fatigue (53.1%), forgetfulness (40%), and dyspnea (26.9%) as most common symptoms, with sleep disorders and muscle pain most affecting quality of life.
paper_authors: Ersan Gursoy; Salih Eren
paper_title: The Burden of Post-COVID-19 Syndrome: A Cross-Sectional Study of Symptoms and Quality of Life in a Turkish Sample

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 100 COVID-19 survivors in Padang, Indonesia examining factors associated with long COVID occurrence. Found 53% experienced long COVID, with comorbidities and smoking habits as significant risk factors, but the study is observational without intervention or treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Gusni Rahma; Yulia Yulia
paper_title: Faktor yang Mempengaruhi Kejadian Long COVID Pada Penyintas COVID-19  di Kota Padang

summary: Cross-sectional observational study of 200 COVID-19 survivors assessing prevalence of depression, anxiety, and stress using the DASS-21 scale and correlating mental health outcomes with severity of acute COVID-19 infection. Found high prevalence of psychological morbidity (38.5% depression, 38.5% anxiety, 11% stress) with significant correlations between acute infection severity and psychological distress.
paper_authors: Priyanka Meena; Kuldeep Deopujari; Jyotsna Agrawal; Simmi Dube
paper_title: Study for Assessment of Mental Health in Survivors of COVID-19

summary: This cross-sectional observational study of 798 patients examined the association between endothelial dysfunction (measured by endothelial quality index via thermal monitoring) and long COVID-19 symptoms. The study found that fatigue, chest pain, and neuro-cognitive difficulties were significantly associated with impaired endothelium function, but no treatment intervention was tested or evaluated.
paper_authors: Salma Charfeddine; Hassen Ibn Hadj Amor; Jihen Jdidi; Slim Torjmen; Salma Kraiem; Rania Hammami; Amine Bahloul; Nesrine Kallel; Nedia Moussa; Imen Touil; Aiman Ghrab; Jamel Elghoul; Zineb Meddeb; Yamina Thabet; Samir Kammoun; Kamel Bouslama; Sami Milouchi; Salem Abdessalem; Leila Abid
paper_title: Long COVID 19 Syndrome: Is It Related to Microcirculation and Endothelial Dysfunction? Insights From TUN-EndCOV Study

summary: This cross-sectional study compares plasma cytokine and monocyte levels in COVID-19 convalescents with pulmonary long COVID (PASC) versus recovered controls. The findings demonstrate elevated CD169+ monocyte counts and increased monocyte activation in long COVID patients, with correlations to reduced pulmonary function and inflammatory cytokines.
paper_authors: Juwon Park; Logan S. Dean; Boonyanudh Jiyarom; Louie Mar Gangcuangco; Parthav Shah; Thomas Awamura; Lauren L. Ching; Vivek R. Nerurkar; Dominic C. Chow; Fritzie Igno; Cecilia M. Shikuma; Gehan Devendra
paper_title: Elevated circulating monocytes and monocyte activation in COVID-19 convalescent individuals

summary: Cross-sectional study evaluating the prevalence of hypocortisolism in 41 patients with a history of COVID-19 pneumonia using corticotropin stimulation testing. Found 27% had hypocortisolism (predominantly secondary), with over half reporting persistent fatigue and some requiring glucocorticoid replacement.
paper_authors: Thachanun Porntharukchareon; Bothamai Dechates; Supamas Sirisreetreerux; Phonthip Therawit; Kriangkrai Tawinprai
paper_title: The existence of adrenal insufficiency in patients with COVID-19 pneumonia

summary: This cross-sectional study surveyed 10,194 adults with post-COVID-19 condition to compare symptoms, health-related quality of life, fatigue, and mental well-being across different time periods since acute infection (3-6 months to >24 months). The study found that fatigue and concentration problems were the most debilitating symptoms throughout, with worst outcomes at 3-6 months post-infection and slight improvement by 13-18 months, though health-related quality of life remained low even beyond 24 months.
paper_authors: Iris M. Brus; Inge Spronk; Juanita A. Haagsma; Annemieke de Groot; Peter Tieleman; Sara Biere-Rafi; Suzanne Polinder
paper_title: The prolonged impact of COVID-19 on symptoms, health-related quality of life, fatigue and mental well-being: a cross-sectional study

summary: This cross-sectional study analyzes the correlation between heart rate variability (HRV) and palpitation symptoms in 272 female healthcare workers with long COVID, comparing HRV parameters across three groups (with palpitations, other symptoms, asymptomatic). The study finds that reduced HRV parameters (SDNN, HRVIndex, LF, TP) are significantly associated with palpitations, suggesting autonomic dysfunction underlies palpitation symptoms in female long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Yu Jiang; Yan Cheng; Jingwen Xiao; Yicheng Wang; Geng Chen; Yan Zhang
paper_title: Analysis of the correlation between heart rate variability and palpitation symptoms in female patients with long COVID

summary: Cross-sectional study examining gut integrity and oxidized lipid markers in 415 participants (85 with PASC, 72 without PASC, COVID-negative controls). Found significantly elevated zonulin and oxidized LDL in PASC patients, with strong associations between these biomarkers and PASC diagnosis.
paper_authors: Christian Mouchati; Jared C. Durieux; Sokratis N. Zisis; Danielle Labbato; Michael A. Rodgers; Kate Ailstock; Brian L. Reinert; Nicholas T. Funderburg; Grace A. McComsey
paper_title: Increase in gut permeability and oxidized ldl is associated with post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing SARS-CoV-2-specific T cell responses, antibody levels, and autoantibodies in 51 healthcare workers with and without long COVID symptoms at 18-23 months post-infection. Found significant associations between elevated anti-TPO antibodies and long COVID incidence, but this is an observational characterization study with no intervention tested.
paper_authors: Zsolt Matula; Viktória Király; Gabriella Bekő; Márton Gönczi; András Zóka; Róbert Steinhauser; Ferenc Uher; István Vályi-Nagy
paper_title: High prevalence of long COVID in anti-TPO positive euthyroid individuals with strongly elevated SARS-CoV-2-specific T cell responses and moderately raised anti-spike IgG levels 23 months post-infection

summary: A prospective multicenter cross-sectional study evaluating clinical characteristics and post-COVID-19 persisting symptoms in 20-week follow-up after acute infection, including hematological and radiological findings. Found that 21.4% of symptomatic patients had persisting symptoms lasting ≥20 weeks, with significant associations to COVID-19 illness duration and comorbidities.
paper_authors: Abu Taiub Mohammed Mohiuddin Chowdhury; Md Rezaul Karim; Md. Ahasan Ali; Jahirul Islam; Yarui Li; Shuixiang He
paper_title: Clinical Characteristics and the Long-Term Post-recovery Manifestations of the COVID-19 Patients—A Prospective Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study

summary: Cross-sectional ultrasound study of 312 long COVID patients assessing rectus femoris and vastus intermedius muscle thickness and echo intensity 3-11 months post-hospitalization. Muscle characteristics were significantly associated with demographic, clinical, and functional parameters including age, handgrip strength, sleepiness, and inflammatory markers.
paper_authors: Abicalaf, Cláudia Andréia Rabay Pimentel; Battistella, Linamara Rizzo; Hcfmusp Covid-19 Study Group; Imamura, Marta; Mirisola, Aline Rossetti; Naves, Gabriella Souza; Santos, Artur César Aquino Dos; Uchyiama, Sabrina Saemy Tome
paper_title: Ultrasonographic findings in long COVID: A cross-sectional study of 312 patients

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 2,466 long COVID patients across 16 Latin American countries assessing symptom burden, activity limitations, and healthcare utilization patterns. While highly relevant to long COVID epidemiology, this is a descriptive observational study without any intervention or treatment evaluation, and therefore does not meet criteria for the trials pipeline.
paper_authors: Adriana Angarita-Fonseca; Rodrigo Torres-Castro; Vicente Benavides-Cordoba; Santos Chero; Mauricio Morales-Satán; Bricia Hernández-López; Rafael Salazar-Pérez; Santiago Larrateguy; Diana C. Sanchez-Ramirez
paper_title: Exploring long COVID condition in Latin America: Its impact on patients’ activities and associated healthcare use

summary: This cross-sectional study examines the prevalence and patterns of benzodiazepine and Z-hypnotic consumption among Spanish adults with long COVID, stratified by gender. While the paper is about long COVID, it does not study a treatment intervention but rather observes existing medication use patterns in the population, making it observational epidemiology rather than a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Pilar Carrasco-Garrido; Cesar Fernández-de-Las-Peñas; Valentín Hernández-Barrera; Domingo Palacios-Ceña; Isabel Jiménez-Trujillo; Carmen Gallardo-Pino
paper_title: Benzodiazepines and Z-hypnotics consumption in long-COVID-19 patients: Gender differences and associated factors

summary: Cross-sectional study investigating hyposmia (reduced smell) incidence and recovery in 349 hospitalized non-severe COVID-19 patients infected with Omicron variant in Shanghai. Finds 6.3% had hyposmia with higher rates of respiratory and gastrointestinal symptoms, with 72.7% recovering within 1 month.
paper_authors: Jun Shen; Li Wu; Ping Wang; Xiaolei Shen; Yuhan Jiang; Jianren Liu; Wei Chen
paper_title: Clinical characteristics and short-term recovery of hyposmia in hospitalized non-severe COVID-19 patients with Omicron variant in Shanghai, China

summary: Cross-sectional study measuring cognitive function, balance, and retinal changes in 166 long COVID patients with cognitive complaints in Barcelona. Found cognitive impairment in 68.67%, balance dysfunction in 51.52%, and retinal alterations in 9.2%, with no significant association between symptom duration and cognitive impairment.
paper_authors: Meritxell Carmona-Cervelló; Brenda Biaani León-Gómez; Rosalía Dacosta‐Aguayo; Noemí Lamonja-Vicente; Pilar Montero-Alía; Gemma Molist; Aitana Ayet; Carla Chacón; Anna Costa-Garrido; Victor M. López-Lifante; Valeria Zamora-Putin; Liudmila Liutsko; Rosa García‐Sierra; Antònia Fornés; Eduard Moreno‐Gabriel; Marta Massanella; José A. Muñoz-Moreno; Manuel Rodríguez-Pérez; Lourdes Mateu; Anna Prats; María Mataró; Marc Boigués; Bibiana Quirant‐Sánchez; Júlia G. Prado; Eva Martínez‐Cáceres; Concepción Violán; Pere Torán‐Monserrat; the APC Collaborative Group
paper_title: Long COVID: cognitive, balance, and retina manifestations

summary: The PRIME post-COVID study assessed the prevalence of post-exertional malaise (PEM) and orthostatic intolerance (OI) in 3,783 people living with post-COVID-19 condition compared to uninfected controls. The study found that PEM and OI are highly prevalent in post-COVID patients (48.1% and 29.3% in women, respectively) and significantly more common than in controls, with age ≤60 years, comorbidities, and living alone as associated factors.
paper_authors: Demi M. E. Pagen; Maarten Van Herck; Céline J. A. van Bilsen; Stephanie Brinkhues; Kevin Konings; Casper D. J. den Heijer; Martijn A. Spruit; Christian J. P. A. Hoebe; Nicole H. T. M. Dukers-Muijrers
paper_title: High proportions of post-exertional malaise and orthostatic intolerance in people living with post-COVID-19 condition: the PRIME post-COVID study

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 1,355 COVID-19 recovered patients in Saudi Arabia examining long COVID prevalence and associated sociodemographic and clinical risk factors. Women reported 17.4% more LC symptoms than men, and acute-phase symptom severity correlated with long COVID symptom count.
paper_authors: Adam F. Aldhawyan; Mohammed A. BuSaad; Nawaf E. Almaghlouth; Abdullah H. Alnasser; Jomana A. Alnasser; Abdulelah H. Almansour; Khalid S. AlHarkan
paper_title: Understanding long COVID: prevalence, characteristics, and risk factors in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed patient satisfaction among COVID-19 survivors in Northeast India using the Patient Satisfaction Questionnaire-18 (PSQ-18) administered via telephone interviews. While the study addresses long COVID survivors' healthcare experiences, it is not a treatment trial—it merely surveys satisfaction with existing healthcare services without testing or evaluating any specific intervention.

paper_title: What is the quality of life in patients with long COVID compared to a healthy control group?

paper_title: Post-COVID-19 syndrome and quality of life impairment in severe COVID-19 Mexican patients

paper_title: Prevalence and impact of long COVID-19 among patients with diabetes and cardiovascular diseases in Bangladesh

paper_title: Evidence of mental health-related morbidities and its association with socio-economic status among previously hospitalized patients with symptoms of COVID-19 in Bangladesh

summary: Cross-sectional population survey of 2,063 Saudi Arabians assessing prevalence of post-COVID fatigue and health-related quality of life. Found 52% prevalence of fatigue and identified female gender, higher education, pre-existing chronic disease, and acute respiratory symptoms as independent predictors, but did not test or evaluate any intervention.
paper_authors: Moath S. Al-Johani; Rehana Khalil; Yazeed A. Al-Mohaimeed; Omar M. Al-Mundarij; Abdulmajeed S. Al-Samani; Osama S. Al-saqry; Alwaleed A. Al-saawi; Ibrahim K. Al-dhali; Waleed A. Al-Essa
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 fatigue and health-related quality of life in Saudi Arabia: a population-based study

Results showed COVID-19 survivors had significantly elevated rates of depression (91% increased risk), anxiety (68%), and insomnia (140%), with depression and anxiety strongly associated with cognitive decline and mild cognitive impairment.
paper_authors: Madhushree Chakrabarty; Piali Chatterjee; Adreesh Mukherjee; Gautam Das; Rafikul Islam Mollah; Banshidhar Mondal; Swarup Sardar; Ayanendranath Basu; Mrinalkanti Ghosh; Amitabha Sengupta; Sankar K. Pal; Atanu Biswas
paper_title: Mental health problems raise the odds of cognitive impairment in COVID-19 survivors

summary: This cross-sectional study measured health-related quality of life in 547 post-COVID-19 patients using the EQ5D-3L questionnaire at a mean of 287 days post-infection, comparing results to normative population data and chronic pain patients. The study found that post-COVID patients reported significantly impaired quality of life (mean EQ5D-3L index: 0.57), with 89.6% experiencing pain/discomfort and 82.5% reporting activity limitations, though quality of life appeared better than in chronic pain surgery patients.
paper_authors: Maarten Moens; Rui V. Duarte; Ann De Smedt; Koen Putman; Jonas Callens; Maxime Billot; Manuel Roulaud; Philippe Rigoard; Lisa Goudman
paper_title: Health-related quality of life in persons post-COVID-19 infection in comparison to normative controls and chronic pain patients

paper_title: Sleep quality among non-hospitalized COVID-19 survivors: a national cross-sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional survey examining prevalence of depression symptoms among individuals with self-reported SARS-CoV-2 infection in China (n=2,726). While the study mentions COVID-19 symptoms lasting >13 days, it does not focus on long COVID specifically and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Liangjia Wei; Jiao Qin; Zhifeng Lin; Xinju Huang; Jinfeng He; Dee Yu; Fei Zhang; Sisi Li; Ping Cen; Mu Li; Tong Luo; Rongjing Zhang; Shanmei Zhong; Cai Qin; Zeyu Li; Yuan Yang; Huiqi Pan; Mengdi Zhao; Xiaoqiong Wu; Junjun Jiang; Hao Liang; Li Ye; Bingyu Liang
paper_title: Prevalence of depressive symptoms and correlates among individuals who self-reported SARS-CoV-2 infection after optimizing the COVID-19 response in China

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 172 recovered COVID-19 inpatients from Jakarta examining the prevalence and impact of long COVID symptoms on health-related quality of life domains using WHOQOL-BREF. Found 30.2% had long COVID symptoms with significant negative effects on most quality-of-life domains, but no intervention or treatment was tested.
paper_authors: Indang Trihandini; Manendra Muhtar; Dea Allan Karunia Sakti; Chintya Putri Erlianti
paper_title: The effect of long-haul COVID-19 toward domains of the health-related quality of life among recovered hospitalized patients

summary: This cross-sectional survey of 184 post-COVID patients examines personal resources, organizational support, and care pathways that facilitate return to work. The study finds that coping ability and workplace structural modifications are the strongest predictors of successful work reintegration, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Claudia Straßburger; Daniel Hieber; Maximilian Karthan; Markus Jüster; Johannes Schobel
paper_title: Return to work after Post-COVID: describing affected employees' perceptions of personal resources, organizational offerings and care pathways

summary: This cross-sectional study examines gender differences in symptomatology and quality of life among 206 Spanish long COVID patients using an online questionnaire. While the study confirms long COVID affects both genders with similar symptom profiles, it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

paper_title: Gender differences in symptomatology, socio-demographic information and quality of life in Spanish population with long COVID condition: a cross-sectional study

summary: This retrospective cross-sectional study evaluated long-term gastrointestinal symptoms and sleep quality in Chinese adolescents following COVID-19 infection using standardized questionnaires (GSRS and PSQI). The study found that GI symptoms increased by 11.86% and sleep quality decreased by 10.9% post-infection, with female sex, older age, and higher education identified as risk factors, though symptoms gradually improved over time.
paper_authors: Wei-Lin Yang; Qi Wang; Ying Wang; Shaopeng Sun; Yan Shen; Lei-Min Yu
paper_title: Long-term gastrointestinal symptoms and sleep quality sequelae in adolescents after COVID-19: a retrospective study

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 2,828 US adults examining awareness of long COVID and receipt of medical care across racial and ethnic groups. Found that 62.5% had heard of long COVID, with significantly lower awareness among Black and Hispanic respondents, and only 26.8% of those with long COVID symptoms received medical care.
paper_authors: Kimberly A. Fisher; Kathleen M. Mazor; Mara M. Epstein; Lydia Goldthwait; Hiba Abu Ghazaleh; Yanhua Zhou; Sybil Crawford; Jai Marathe; Benjamin P. Linas
paper_title: Long COVID awareness and receipt of medical care: a survey among populations at risk for disparities

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 1,510 participants examining the prevalence of musculoskeletal pain after COVID-19 infection and associated factors. Found 42.6% exhibited musculoskeletal pain post-COVID, with education level and concomitant symptoms as risk factors, while exercise duration and stress scores were protective.

paper_title: The impact of COVID-19 infection on musculoskeletal pain and its associating factors: a cross-sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between spiritual health and quality of life in 475 COVID-19 patients with long-term complications in Iran. Found that patients with complications had significantly lower spiritual well-being and quality of life scores, with positive correlation between spiritual health and quality of life outcomes.
paper_authors: Mehdi Safarabadi; Vahid Yousofvand; Ali Jadidi; Seyed Mohammad Taghi Dehghani; Kazem Ghaffari
paper_title: The relationship between spiritual health and quality of life among COVID-19 patients with long-term complications in the post-coronavirus era

summary: This cross-sectional study surveyed 368 COVID-19 confirmed cases in Qatar during 2022 to determine the prevalence and predictors of post-COVID-19 syndrome. Female gender, lack of social support, and obesity were significant predictors of PCS, with fatigue, anxiety, and cognitive symptoms being most commonly reported; however, this is an observational epidemiological study with no treatment intervention.

paper_title: Post-COVID-19 syndrome, who at risk and why: an insight from Qatar 2022

summary: Community-based cross-sectional survey of 1,485 Chinese residents examining the prevalence of post-COVID persistent symptoms and associations with reinfection. Found that 89.1% of previously infected participants reported ongoing symptoms, with reinfection associated with higher odds of headaches, smell/taste changes, sleep impairment, and brain fog.

summary: This cross-sectional study examined cognitive performance and psychological factors (anxiety, social support) in 227 Peruvian adults with varying COVID-19 symptom histories. paper_title: Anxiety and perceived social support as moderators of cognitive and emotional well-being in populations affected by COVID-19

summary: This cross-sectional survey of 364 long COVID patients in the Brazilian Amazon examines factors associated with access to healthcare services, finding that only 45.88% received treatment. The study identifies symptom severity and pre-existing chronic disease as key factors determining healthcare access, rather than demographic or socioeconomic variables.

paper_title: Factors associated with access to health services among people with long COVID in the Brazilian Amazon

summary: This paper describes a national virtual clinic project in Saudi Arabia that assessed the frequency and types of post-COVID conditions in 5,913 recovered COVID-19 patients at least 4 weeks after infection. paper_title: Virtual post-COVID-19 clinics in Saudi Arabia: navigating the effect of the pandemic with a national project

summary: Cross-sectional study of 5,735 adults in rural Indonesia examining the association between COVID-19 vaccination status, vaccine type, and long COVID prevalence. While the paper addresses long COVID, it is observational without testing or evaluating any treatment intervention—vaccination status is assessed as a risk factor rather than an assigned treatment.
