paper_title: Association between vaccination uptake, vaccine type, and long COVID in rural Indonesia

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 1,511 individuals with tinnitus examining associations between tinnitus onset and COVID-19 infection, long COVID, or vaccination. Findings show tinnitus severity is higher in COVID-associated groups compared to pre-existing tinnitus, with depression/anxiety as key predictors, but no intervention or treatment is tested.
paper_authors: Yihsin Tai; Namitha Jain; Gibbeum Kim; Fatima T. Husain
paper_title: Tinnitus and COVID-19: effect of infection, vaccination, and the pandemic

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the association between long COVID and burnout, anxiety, and depression among US healthcare workers using survey data from 1,678 respondents. Found that long COVID was significantly associated with higher burnout, anxiety, and depression scores compared to those without long COVID.
paper_authors: Thanh-Huyen T. Vu; Miao Jenny Hua; Cerina Dubois; Judith T. Moskowitz; Amisha Wallia; Lisa R. Hirschhorn; John T. Wilkins; Charlesnika T. Evans
paper_title: Long COVID and its associations with burnout, anxiety, and depression among U. S. healthcare workers in the United States

summary: Secondary analysis of a cross-sectional community survey examining prevalence and risk factors for long COVID in 168 households (14,769 weighted total) in Houston, Texas. Identifies symptom severity, comorbidities (heart disease, asthma), and acute symptoms (anxiety, chest pain, palpitations) as significant risk factors for long COVID development, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Zuri Dale; Sherrie Flynt Wallington; Michelle Penn-Marshall
paper_title: Prevalence and characteristics of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 in recovered patients

summary: This cross-sectional analysis of the 2023 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System examined associations between post-COVID-19 condition and risk factors (physical inactivity, vaccination status, non-communicable diseases) among 27,074 U.S. adults reporting long COVID symptoms. The study found that adults with low physical activity, incomplete vaccination, and chronic conditions had significantly higher odds of reporting post-COVID-19 condition, but did not test or evaluate any treatment interventions.
paper_authors: Gregory W. Heath; David Levine; Gloria Oppong; Majdi Alghader
paper_title: Prevalence of post COVID-19 condition and associations with risk factors among U.S. adults: 2023 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System

summary: A cross-sectional survey examining post-COVID-19 complications and management patterns among 659 participants treated in hospitals versus home settings in Bangladesh. The study documents differences in recovery time and complication rates (fatigue, chest pain, digestive disorders) between treatment settings but does not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

paper_title: Post-COVID-19 complications in home and hospital-based care: A study from Dhaka city, Bangladesh

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing prevalence and severity of PTSD, anxiety, depression, and fear in 227 COVID-19 survivors 3 months post-hospitalization. paper_title: Changes in Quality of Life Following SARS-CoV-2 Infection Among Jewish and Arab Populations in Israel: A Cross-Sectional Study

paper_title: Long COVID Patients with Orthostatic Intolerance Have Reduced Heart Rate Variability and Preserved Physiological Response to Active Standing

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 2,246 Israeli respondents examining socioeconomic and demographic factors associated with self-reported long-COVID symptom prevalence. summary: Cross-sectional study of long COVID prevalence and symptoms among 903 healthcare workers at a Romanian pediatric hospital in 2024. Describes long COVID epidemiology and symptom burden in this occupational population, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Maria Valentina Popa; Irina Luciana Gurzu; Claudia Mariana Handra; Cristina Mandanach; Bogdan Gurzu; Dana Elena Mîndru; Mădălina Duceac (Covrig); Mădălina Irina Ciuhodaru; Letiția Doina Duceac
paper_title: Long COVID in Healthcare Workers from a Pediatric Hospital in Romania: A Cross-Sectional Study of Prevalence, Symptom Burden, and the Role of Vaccination and Reinfection

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 895 Lithuanian participants investigating new comorbidities and medications after mild SARS-CoV-2 infection. While focused on long COVID sequelae, this is an observational study that does not evaluate any treatment intervention—it only documents symptom patterns and medication use in uncontrolled fashion.
paper_authors: Dovilė Važgėlienė; Raimondas Kubilius; Indre Bileviciute-Ljungar
paper_title: The Impact of Previous Comorbidities on New Comorbidities and Medications after a Mild SARS-CoV-2 Infection in a Lithuanian Cohort

summary: This cross-sectional study compared postural balance assessments between 30 post-COVID-19 patients and 30 controls, evaluating five different balance tests (Tinetti, FRT, BBS, TUG, MBESTest). The Tinetti Balance Test was identified as the most effective predictor of functional decline in post-COVID-19 individuals, but the study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Janice R. M. Bastos; Arthur S. Ferreira; Agnaldo J. Lopes; Talita P. Pinto; Erika Rodrigues; Fabio V. dos Anjos
paper_title: The Tinetti Balance Test Is an Effective Predictor of Functional Decline in Non-Hospitalized Post-COVID-19 Individuals: A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: This observational cross-sectional study examined retinal microvascular changes in 104 post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) patients using optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) and their relationship to cognitive performance. The findings showed that severe PCC cases had reduced retinal vascular density and larger foveal avascular zones, which were associated with cognitive impairment, particularly in executive function and speed processing.
paper_authors: Mar Ariza; Barbara Delas; Beatriz Rodriguez; Beatriz De Frutos; Neus Cano; Bàrbara Segura; Cristian Barrué; Javier Bejar; Mouafk Asaad; Claudio Ulises Cortés; Carme Junqué; Maite Garolera
paper_title: Retinal Microvasculature Changes Linked to Executive Function Impairment after COVID-19

summary: This cross-sectional study examines CT imaging metrics and their association with reduced lung diffusion capacity in 45 post-COVID patients with minimal residual lung lesions. The findings suggest that diffuse vascular and parenchymal changes, beyond alveolar volume reduction, may contribute to persistent diffusion impairment after COVID-19.
paper_authors: Han Wen; Julio A. Huapaya; Shreya M. Kanth; Junfeng Sun; Brianna P. Matthew; Simone C. Lee; Michael Do; Marcus Y. Chen; Ashkan A. Malayeri; Anthony F. Suffredini
paper_title: Quantitative CT Metrics Associated with Variability in the Diffusion Capacity of the Lung of Post-COVID-19 Patients with Minimal Residual Lung Lesions

summary: This cross-sectional study examines the relationship between anthropometric measurements and retinal vascular caliber in 284 persistent COVID-19 patients. The study found that obesity is associated with increased venous caliber and decreased arterio-venous index, but this is observational research without an intervention—it passively characterizes patients rather than testing a treatment.
paper_authors: Rosario Alonso-Domínguez; Teresa Vicente-García; Silvia Arroyo-Romero; Nuria Suárez-Moreno; Alicia Navarro-Cáceres; Andrea Domínguez-Martín; Leticia Gómez-Sánchez; Cristina Lugones-Sánchez; Luis García-Ortiz; Alicia Ortega; Marta Gómez-Sánchez; Elena Navarro-Matias; Manuel A. Gómez-Marcos
paper_title: Relationship Between Retinal Vascular Measurements and Anthropometric Indices in Patients Diagnosed with Persistent COVID-19

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence and characteristics of post-COVID-19 syndrome among 265 COVID-19 patients in Oman, finding a 48.5% prevalence with fatigue and joint pain as the most common symptoms. Female gender was identified as a significant independent predictor of post-COVID-19 syndrome development.
paper_authors: Reem Ali Alhabsi; Amani Abdullah Almukhladi; Rania Ali Mahdi Kadhim; Reham Ali Alhabsi; Maisa Hamed Al Kiyumi; Abdulaziz Al Mahrezi
paper_title: The Prevalence and Characteristics of Post-COVID-19 Syndrome Among Patients Attending the University Health Center in Muscat, Oman
paper_journal: Journal of the Oman Medical Association

summary: Cross-sectional study of 145 COVID-19 survivors assessing quality of life and psychological distress using SF-36 and SCL-90-R questionnaires alongside clinical data. Found that 67.6% reported fatigue and 44.8% reported pain, with physical pain, loss of smell, and female gender associated with poor quality of life.
paper_authors: Evangelos C. Fradelos; Stylianos Boutlas; Eleni Tsimitrea; Alexandra Sistou; Konstantinos Tourlakopoulos; Ioanna V. Papathanasiou; Konstantinos I. Gourgoulianis
paper_title: Perceived Symptoms, Mental Health and Quality of Life after Hospitalization in COVID-19 Patients

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing retinal microvasculature imaging (OCT-A) and retinal layer thickness in 40 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients versus 40 healthy controls at ~15 months post-infection. Found no significant differences in vascular or retinal parameters between groups, suggesting absence of long-term retinal damage.
paper_authors: Maha Noor; Orlaith McGrath; Ines Drira; Tariq Aslam
paper_title: Retinal Microvasculature Image Analysis Using Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography in Patients with Post-COVID-19 Syndrome

summary: This cross-sectional study compared homocysteine levels, depression, and cognitive function in 62 long COVID patients (≥3 months post-infection) versus 64 controls. Long COVID patients had significantly higher homocysteine levels and lower cognitive scores (MoCA), with a strong negative correlation between homocysteine and cognitive performance.
paper_authors: Pinar Oner; Seda Yilmaz; Serpil Doğan
paper_title: High Homocysteine Levels Are Associated with Cognitive Impairment in Patients Who Recovered from COVID-19 in the Long Term

summary: This cross-sectional survey study examined the prevalence and impact of persistent olfactory and gustatory dysfunctions on quality of life in 431 long COVID patients. While the paper confirms that POD and PGD are frequent long COVID symptoms that significantly reduce mental health-related quality of life, it is an observational characterization study without any treatment intervention or control group.
paper_authors: Luigi Angelo Vaira; Claudia Gessa; Giovanna Deiana; Giovanni Salzano; Fabio Maglitto; Jerome R. Lechien; Sven Saussez; Pasquale Piombino; Andrea Biglio; Federico Biglioli; Paolo Boscolo-Rizzo; Claire Hopkins; Valentina Parma; Giacomo De Riu
paper_title: The Effects of Persistent Olfactory and Gustatory Dysfunctions on Quality of Life in Long-COVID-19 Patients

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 1,649 adults in Norway, UK, USA, and Australia examining sociodemographic predictors and health correlates of self-reported long COVID. Found long COVID associated with higher psychological distress, fatigue, and perceived stress, with greater effects in men than women.
paper_authors: Tore Bonsaksen; Janni Leung; Daicia Price; Mary Ruffolo; Gary Lamph; Isaac Kabelenga; Hilde Thygesen; Amy Østertun Geirdal
paper_title: Self-Reported Long COVID in the General Population: Sociodemographic and Health Correlates in a Cross-National Sample

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing chemosensory dysfunction (smell, taste, chemesthesis) in 133 long COVID patients vs 75 controls using self-reported and direct psychophysical testing methods. Found significant impairment of all three chemical senses in long COVID patients with moderate to large agreement between assessment methods.
paper_authors: Javier Albayay; Lara Fontana; Valentina Parma; Massimiliano Zampini
paper_title: Chemosensory Dysfunction in Long-Term COVID-19 Assessed by Self-Reported and Direct Psychophysical Methods

summary: Cross-sectional study of 471 long COVID patients in a rehabilitation program assessing symptom frequency and correlations with sex, disease severity, time since onset, and exercise capacity. Found fatigue and dyspnea are highly prevalent (99.57% and 99.36%), more common in women, do not resolve by 6 months post-onset, and correlate with impaired lung function and reduced exercise tolerance.
paper_authors: Elżbieta Paradowska-Nowakowska; Danuta Łoboda; Krzysztof S. Gołba; Beata Sarecka-Hujar
paper_title: Long COVID-19 Syndrome Severity According to Sex, Time from the Onset of the Disease, and Exercise Capacity—The Results of a Cross-Sectional Study

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluated 53 long COVID patients previously hospitalized with severe COVID-19 to assess the prevalence and types of cardiac arrhythmias, finding arrhythmias in 41.5% with atrial fibrillation most common. Metformin therapy was inversely associated with arrhythmia occurrence, suggesting a potential protective effect.
paper_authors: Haydee Ninette Morales-Vazquez; David Cardona-Müller; Fernando Grover-Paez; Carlos Gerardo Ramos-Becerra; Ernesto Germán Cardona-Muñoz; Maria Guadalupe Ramos-Zavala; Jaime Carmona-Huerta; Jorge Eduardo Hernandez-del-Rio; Tomas Miranda-Aquino; Christian Gonzalez-Padilla; Christopher Josue Lopez-Gradilla
paper_title: Arrhythmias as Part of Long COVID Syndrome in Hospitalized Patients That Survived a Severe COVID-19 Infection and the Potential Protective Role of Metformin in These Patients

summary: A cross-sectional study surveying 549 previously COVID-19 infected individuals in Romania to assess post-COVID-19 syndrome outcomes, risk factors, and symptom prevalence at 3, 6, and 12 months post-infection. While the study documents the epidemiology and burden of long COVID, it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the trial extraction pipeline.
paper_authors: Ioana Bejan; Corneliu Petru Popescu; Simona Maria Ruta
paper_title: Insights into the Risk Factors and Outcomes of Post-COVID-19 Syndrome—Results from a Retrospective, Cross-Sectional Study in Romania

summary: This cross-sectional study compared hemodynamic, vascular, and autonomic responses to maximal exercise in 38 young adults with and without long COVID, stratified by sex. The authors found that young physically active adults with long COVID showed preserved cardiovascular and autonomic responses during and after exercise, with no clinically relevant impairments compared to controls.
paper_authors: Carla Nascimento dos Santos Rodrigues; Fernanda Rico Angelotto; Vitória Luiz Diotto; Daniel da Motta Cristofoletti; Tatiana Oliveira Passos de Araújo; Marco Antonio de Lima; José Campanholi Neto; Jonato Prestes; James Navalta; Guilherme Borges Pereira
paper_title: Long COVID Does Not Impair Hemodynamic, Vascular, or Autonomic Responses to Maximal Exercise: Sex-Stratified Study in Young Adults

summary: Cross-sectional study of 215 post-COVID-19 patients in Indonesia characterizing headache phenotypes using ICHD-3 criteria and assessing impact on quality of life via SF-36. Found 21.4% had poor QoL related to headache, with unemployed status, early headache onset, and high severity predicting worse outcomes—but this is a descriptive epidemiological study, not a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Endang Mutiawati; Hendrix Indra Kusuma; Marhami Fahriani; Harapan Harapan; Syahrul Syahrul; Nasrul Musadir
paper_title: Headache in Post-COVID-19 Patients: Its Characteristics and Relationship with the Quality of Life

summary: Cross-sectional study examining relationships between brain fog symptoms and diet, sleep quality, mood, and gastrointestinal health in long COVID patients. Found mood and gastrointestinal symptoms were significant predictors of brain fog, while MIND diet adherence showed no significant relationship.
paper_authors: Canan Altinsoy; Derya Dikmen
paper_title: How Are Brain Fog Symptoms Related to Diet, Sleep, Mood and Gastrointestinal Health? A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: Observational cross-sectional study of 206 outpatients assessing persistence of COVID-19 symptoms and quality of life using SF-36. Finds 73.3% experienced persistent symptoms (fatigue, anxiety, headache), with female gender and comorbidities associated with reduced QoL, but no intervention/treatment is evaluated.
paper_authors: Lizeth Guadalupe Gutiérrez-Canales; Carolina Muñoz-Corona; Isaac Barrera-Chávez; Carlos Viloria-Álvarez; Alejandro E. Macías; Eduardo Guaní-Guerra
paper_title: Quality of Life and Persistence of Symptoms in Outpatients after Recovery from COVID-19

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 235 participants examining factors associated with prolonged COVID-19-induced smell loss (>28 days). Found older age and increased illness severity were associated with prolonged recovery, while flossing was associated with rapid recovery.
paper_authors: Georgia Catton; Alexander Gardner
paper_title: Relationship between Recovery from COVID-19-Induced Smell Loss and General and Oral Health Factors

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 406 long COVID patients comparing quality of life and functional status between those who reported completing rehabilitation (44.8%) and those who did not (55.2%). Rehabilitation status was associated with significantly better outcomes on most SF-36 domains and PCFS scales, though the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.
paper_authors: Michal Macej; Cyril Grus; Jakub Čuj; Lucia Demjanovič Kendrová; Wioletta Bronislawa Mikuľaková; Anna Kubincová; Peter Takáč
paper_title: Quality of Life and Functional Status in Individuals with Persistent Post-COVID Symptoms: A Cross-Sectional Comparison by Reported Rehabilitation

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence of ME/CFS and post-exertional malaise among 465 long COVID patients using validated questionnaires. Found 58% of participants met ME/CFS case definition, with evidence of both over- and under-diagnosis on self-report.
paper_authors: Leonard A. Jason; Joseph A. Dorri
paper_title: ME/CFS and Post-Exertional Malaise among Patients with Long COVID

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluates sarcopenia prevalence and risk factors in 30 post-critical COVID-19 outpatients using ultrasound, bioimpedance analysis, and functional tests. The study identifies ICU stay, mechanical ventilation, and age as predictors of sarcopenia but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Isabel Cornejo-Pareja; Ana Gloria Soler-Beunza; Isabel María Vegas-Aguilar; Rocío Fernández-Jiménez; Francisco J. Tinahones; Jose Manuel García-Almeida
paper_title: Predictors of Sarcopenia in Outpatients with Post-Critical SARS-CoV2 Disease. Nutritional Ultrasound of Rectus Femoris Muscle, a Potential Tool

summary: Cross-sectional study examining metabolic and laboratory markers in 215 long COVID patients from an Amazon region clinical program. Finds that abnormal metabolic profiles (elevated BMI, triglycerides, HbA1c, ferritin) are more prevalent in patients with worse long COVID presentations and prior hospitalization.
paper_authors: Daniel Carvalho de Menezes; Patrícia Danielle Lima de Lima; Igor Costa de Lima; Juliana Hiromi Emin Uesugi; Pedro Fernando da Costa Vasconcelos; Juarez Antônio Simões Quaresma; Luiz Fábio Magno Falcão
paper_title: Metabolic Profile of Patients with Long COVID: A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing muscle strength and fatigue characteristics in 45 post-COVID survivors versus 49 healthy controls using dynamometry. Post-COVID participants showed significantly higher fatigue in extensors/flexors and reduced power output, highlighting the need for rehabilitation considerations.
paper_authors: Mateusz Kowal; Ewa Morgiel; Sławomir Winiarski; Robert Dymarek; Weronika Bajer; Marta Madej; Agata Sebastian; Marcin Madziarski; Nicole Wedel; Krzysztof Proc; Katarzyna Madziarska; Piotr Wiland; Małgorzata Paprocka-Borowicz
paper_title: Ebbing Strength, Fading Power: Unveiling the Impact of Persistent Fatigue on Muscle Performance in COVID-19 Survivors

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between Mediterranean Diet adherence and vascular structure/function in 304 long COVID patients. Found that Mediterranean Diet components (olive oil, pulses, fewer pastries) were associated with better vascular outcomes and lower vascular aging measures.
paper_authors: Alicia Navarro-Cáceres; Leticia Gómez-Sánchez; Silvia Arroyo-Romero; Nuria Suárez-Moreno; Andrea Domínguez-Martín; Cristina Lugones-Sánchez; Susana González-Sánchez; Emiliano Rodríguez-Sánchez; Luis García-Ortiz; Marta Gómez-Sánchez; Elena Navarro-Matias; Manuel A. Gómez-Marcos
paper_title: Relationship of Mediterranean Diet and Its Components with Parameters of Structure, Vascular Function, and Vascular Aging in Subjects Diagnosed with Long COVID: BioICOPER Study

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the association between Mediterranean diet adherence and cardiovascular risk factors/metabolic syndrome in 305 long COVID patients. Higher Mediterranean diet scores were associated with lower uric acid, fewer metabolic syndrome components, smaller waist circumference, and higher HDL cholesterol.
paper_authors: Nuria Suárez-Moreno; Leticia Gómez-Sánchez; Alicia Navarro-Caceres; Silvia Arroyo-Romero; Andrea Domínguez-Martín; Cristina Lugones-Sánchez; Olaya Tamayo-Morales; Susana González-Sánchez; Ana Castro-Rivero; Emiliano Rodríguez-Sánchez; Luis García-Ortiz; Elena Navarro-Matias; Manuel Gómez-Marcos
paper_title: Association of Mediterranean Diet with Cardiovascular Risk Factors and with Metabolic Syndrome in Subjects with Long COVID: BioICOPER Study

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the association between body composition phenotypes and insulin resistance in 483 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients without diabetes. Found that obesity and dynapenic obesity are significantly associated with insulin resistance, but the study is observational without treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Dulce González-Islas; Laura Flores-Cisneros; Arturo Orea-Tejeda; Candace Keirns-Davis; Nadia Hernández-López; Laura Patricia Arcos-Pacheco; Andrea Zurita-Sandoval; Frida Albarran-López; Luis García-Castañeda; Fernanda Salgado-Fernández; Samantha Hernández-López; Angelia Jiménez-Valentín; Ilse Pérez-García
paper_title: The Association between Body Composition Phenotype and Insulin Resistance in Post-COVID-19 Syndrome Patients without Diabetes: A Cross-Sectional, Single-Center Study

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed subjective and objective cognitive impairments in 372 non-hospitalized persons 9 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection using standardized neuropsychological tests. The study found high prevalence of cognitive complaints and test abnormalities but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Inge Kirchberger; Daniela Peilstöcker; Tobias D. Warm; Jakob Linseisen; Alexander Hyhlik-Dürr; Christine Meisinger; Yvonne Goßlau
paper_title: Subjective and Objective Cognitive Impairments in Non-Hospitalized Persons 9 Months after SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: Cross-sectional case-control study examining associations between serum calprotectin, arterial stiffness, and long COVID symptoms in kidney transplant recipients. The study characterizes long COVID manifestations and identifies calprotectin as a potential biomarker but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Tina Đogaš; Ivana Novak; Marija Babić; Marijana Vučković; Leida Tandara; Josipa Radić
paper_title: Associations of Serum Calprotectin, Arterial Stiffness and Long COVID Symptoms in Dalmatian Kidney Transplant Recipients

summary: This cross-sectional study examined symptom burden, healthcare utilization, and healthcare experiences in 304 non-hospitalized Germans 2 years after SARS-CoV-2 infection, finding that 69.1% had post-COVID-19 syndrome with significant functional limitations. The study identifies gaps in patient information and access to specialized care, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Inge Kirchberger; Christine Meisinger; Tobias D. Warm; Alexander Hyhlik-Dürr; Jakob Linseisen; Yvonne Goßlau
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 Syndrome in Non-Hospitalized Individuals: Healthcare Situation 2 Years after SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: Cross-sectional study of 307 healthy volunteers examining cardiac function and biomarkers in those with prior COVID-19 infection (IgG-SARS positive, n=70) versus negative controls. Found decreased left ventricular filling, increased inflammation markers, and decreased hemoglobin in previously infected participants, but does not study long COVID patients or any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Nadezhda G. Gumanova; Alexander U. Gorshkov; Natalya L. Bogdanova; Andrei I. Korolev
paper_title: Effects of COVID-19 Infection in Healthy Subjects on Cardiac Function and Biomarkers of Oxygen Transport, Blood Coagulation and Inflammation

summary: This cross-sectional study examines the relationship between alcohol consumption and vascular structure/arterial stiffness in 305 adults with persistent COVID. The results show that heavy alcohol use is associated with higher carotid intima-media thickness and carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity, suggesting increased cardiovascular risk in this population.
paper_authors: Silvia Arroyo-Romero; Leticia Gómez-Sánchez; Nuria Suárez-Moreno; Alicia Navarro-Cáceres; Andrea Domínguez-Martín; Cristina Lugones-Sánchez; Olaya Tamayo-Morales; Susana González-Sánchez; Ana B. Castro-Rivero; Marta Gómez-Sánchez; Emiliano Rodríguez-Sánchez; Luis García-Ortiz; Elena Navarro-Matías; Manuel A. Gómez-Marcos
paper_title: Relationship Between Alcohol Consumption and Vascular Structure and Arterial Stiffness in Adults Diagnosed with Persistent COVID: BioICOPER Study

summary: This cross-sectional study evaluated hematological laboratory markers in long COVID patients from a clinical care program in the Amazon region, examining associations with clinical findings and long-term outcomes. The study found persistent changes in blood cell parameters and coagulation markers up to 985 days post-infection, with differences based on symptom severity and disease duration.
paper_authors: Vanessa Costa Alves Galúcio; Daniel Carvalho de Menezes; Patrícia Danielle Lima de Lima; Vera Regina da Cunha Menezes Palácios; Pedro Fernando da Costa Vasconcelos; Juarez Antônio Simões Quaresma; Luiz Fábio Magno Falcão
paper_title: Evaluation of the Hematological Patterns from Up to 985 Days of Long COVID: A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: Cross-sectional study of 322 COVID-19 hospitalized patients at 2-year follow-up examining prevalence and predictors of long-term working ability impairment (41.6% reported impaired ability). Female sex, diabetes, oxygen during hospitalization, and age were independent predictors of impaired working ability, but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Luisa Frallonardo; Annunziata Ilenia Ritacco; Angela Amendolara; Domenica Cassano; Giorgia Manco Cesari; Alessia Lugli; Mariangela Cormio; Michele De Filippis; Greta Romita; Giacomo Guido; Luigi Piccolomo; Vincenzo Giliberti; Francesco Cavallin; Francesco Vladimiro Segala; Francesco Di Gennaro; Annalisa Saracino
paper_title: Long-Term Impairment of Working Ability in Subjects under 60 Years of Age Hospitalised for COVID-19 at 2 Years of Follow-Up: A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 2,226 Vietnamese schoolchildren estimating long COVID prevalence (5.6%) and symptom profile, including cognitive symptoms (memory loss, poor concentration) and fatigue. Study documents impacts on schooling, daily activities, and health service utilization but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Trang Thu Vu; Khanh Cong Nguyen; Hieu Thi Nguyen; Anh Hoang; Nghia Duy Ngu; Duong Nhu Tran; Hoa Bich Phan; Ha Thi Thu Nguyen; Thai Quang Pham; Florian Vogt
paper_title: Prevalence and Symptom Profile of Long COVID among Schoolchildren in Vietnam

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing eating behavior, sleep quality, and anxiety levels between 756 adults who had COVID-19 infection versus those who did not during the final phase of social isolation. The COVID-infected group showed higher weight, BMI, anxiety, sleep disorders, and worse sleep quality, with associations between ultra-processed food consumption and worse mental health outcomes.
paper_authors: Simone Gonzaga do Carmo; Júlia Paulino Teixeira Oliveira; Bruna de Almeida Aragão; Patrícia Borges Botelho
paper_title: Impact of Final Phase Social Isolation and the COVID-19 Pandemic on Eating Behavior, Sleep Quality, and Anxiety Level

summary: This case-control study investigates genetic susceptibility to long COVID by comparing 199 long COVID patients with 79 COVID-19 patients without long COVID symptoms to detect associations between ten functional polymorphisms in thrombophilia and immune response genes. The study found that IFNG genotype AA and MTHFR genotype CC were more frequently present in long COVID patients, suggesting a genetic component to long COVID development.
paper_authors: Rosilene da Silva; Kevin Matheus Lima de Sarges; Marcos Henrique Damasceno Cantanhede; Flávia Póvoa da Costa; Erika Ferreira dos Santos; Fabíola Brasil Barbosa Rodrigues; Maria de Nazaré do Socorro de Almeida Viana; Mauro de Meira Leite; Andréa Luciana Soares da Silva; Mioni Thieli Magalhães de Brito; Maria Karoliny da Silva Torres; Maria Alice Freitas Queiroz; Izaura Maria Vieira Cayres Vallinoto; Daniele Freitas Henriques; Carla Pinheiro dos Santos; Giselle Maria Rachid Viana; Juarez Antônio Simões Quaresma; Luiz Fábio Magno Falcão; Antonio Carlos Rosário Vallinoto; Eduardo José Melo dos Santos
paper_title: Thrombophilia and Immune-Related Genetic Markers in Long COVID

summary: The VAXILONG study surveyed 567 long COVID patients to assess the effect of SARS-CoV-2 vaccination on persistent symptoms. Among 380 vaccinated patients with ongoing symptoms, 52.8% reported a global effect (21.8% improvement, 31% worsening), with no differences by vaccine type and good immunogenicity in seronegative patients.
paper_authors: Marc Scherlinger; Luc Pijnenburg; Emmanuel Chatelus; Laurent Arnaud; Jacques-Eric Gottenberg; Jean Sibilia; Renaud Felten
paper_title: Effect of SARS-CoV-2 Vaccination on Symptoms from Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19: Results from the Nationwide VAXILONG Study

summary: This cross-sectional online survey of 235 long COVID patients in Bavaria examined the relationship between vaccination status, timing, and symptom severity/functional outcomes assessed at three timepoints. The study found that vaccination prior to infection was associated with lower symptom severity, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention for long COVID.
paper_authors: Sonia Lippke; Robin Rinn; Christina Derksen; Alina Dahmen
paper_title: Patients’ Post-/Long-COVID Symptoms, Vaccination and Functional Status—Findings from a State-Wide Online Screening Study

summary: This cross-sectional study of 1,036 patients examines the relationship between autonomic nervous system dysfunction (measured via head-up tilt testing) and serological markers of past/persistent infections in post-COVID syndrome, chronic fatigue syndrome, and Lyme disease. Findings show that antibody status—particularly to HSV-1, HHV-6, Coxiella burnetii, Toxoplasma gondii, and Borrelia—significantly predicts tilt test outcomes and orthostatic intolerance in these post-infectious conditions.
paper_authors: Branislav Milovanovic; Nikola Markovic; Masa Petrovic; Smiljana Stojanovic; Vasko Zugic; Milijana Ostojic; Milovan Bojic
paper_title: The Relationship Between Hemodynamic Responses During Head-Up Tilt Testing and Parameters of Infection in Post-COVID Syndrome, Chronic Fatigue Syndrome, and Late-Stage Lyme Disease

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing cognitive impairment, anxiety, and depression in university students with and without prior COVID-19 infection using standardized assessment scales (MoCA, PHQ-9, GAD-7). Found that 32.4% of students with COVID-19 history had cognitive impairment compared to 16.8% without COVID-19, with affective symptoms negatively affecting cognitive function.

paper_journal: Vestnik nevrologii, psihiatrii i nejrohirurgii (Bulletin of Neurology, Psychiatry and Neurosurgery)

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed long-term sequelae of COVID-19 in 141 Brazilian patients, identifying symptom patterns across cardiovascular, respiratory, and neurological systems. No intervention or treatment was tested; it is an observational epidemiological study examining symptom prevalence and risk factors.
paper_authors: Antonio da Silva Menezes Junior; Aline Andressa Schroeder; Aline Lazara Rezende; Luciana da Ressureição Santos; Silvia Marçal Botelho; Antonio Marcio Cordeiro Teodoro Filho
paper_title: Systemic impact of the post-Coronavirus disease syndrome in Brazil

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of 2022 US National Health Interview Survey data examining the association between COVID-19 booster vaccination status and long COVID prevalence among previously infected individuals. Found that booster vaccination was associated with lower odds of moderate/severe symptoms and long COVID, though primary series alone was not protective.
paper_authors: Jamie L. Romeiser; Kelsey Schoeneck
paper_title: COVID-19 Booster Vaccination Status and Long COVID in the United States: A Nationally Representative Cross-Sectional Study

summary: This cross-sectional study examined changes in physical activity levels in 5,829 respondents at one month post-SARS-CoV-2 infection, analyzing determinants including vaccination status, re-infection, and disease severity. While it documents significant PA declines post-infection, it is an observational survey without any treatment intervention and thus excluded from the treatment trial analysis.
paper_authors: Dimitrios I. Bourdas; Panteleimon Bakirtzoglou; Antonios K. Travlos; Vasileios Andrianopoulos; Emmanouil Zacharakis
paper_title: Exploring the Impact of COVID-19 on Physical Activity One Month after Infection and Its Potential Determinants: Re-Infections, Pre-Illness Vaccination Profiles/Types, and Beyond

summary: Cross-sectional study of 155 long COVID patients in Barcelona assessing prevalence of anxiety, depression, and stress using the DASS-21 scale. Found high rates of severe stress and extremely severe anxiety, with significant differences by age and job role.

summary: This cross-sectional study established peak expiratory flow (PEF) reference values in a Peruvian population of 316 healthy adults aged 20-60 years without cardiac or pulmonary pathologies. paper_authors: Santos Lucio Chero-Pisfil; Aimeé Yajaira Díaz-Mau; Jhosely Quispe-Nina; Gustavo Raymundo Infantes-Bracamonte; Clelia Patricia Suaña-Apaza; Milagros Nohely Rosas-Sudario
paper_title: Establishing Reference Values for Peak Expiratory Flow in the Peruvian Population from Primary Care: Contributing to SDG 3
paper_journal: Journal of Lifestyle and SDGs Review

summary: Cross-sectional study of 445 healthcare workers assessing the prevalence and characteristics of long COVID symptoms at a 6-month follow-up in Iran. The study identified a 9.44% prevalence of long COVID, with anxiety and mood disturbances as the most common persistent mental symptoms, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Nazanin Izadi; Arezu Najafi; Khosro Sadeghniiat-Haghigh; Hosein Mohammadi
paper_title: Characterization of Long COVID and Its Contributing Factors among a Population of Health Care Workers in a 6-Month Follow-up
paper_journal: Medical Journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran

summary: Cross-sectional observational study surveying 1,000+ Jordanian COVID-19 survivors about persistent and new symptoms at ≥90 days post-infection. Found high prevalence of smell loss (34.7%), fatigue (34.6%), and taste loss (29.5%), with greater symptom persistence in females and those requiring oxygen therapy, but no intervention or treatment was tested.
paper_authors: Hatem M.Jaber; Mohammad Abusamak; Sajedah N.Obeid; Nizar Heissat; Razan Qashou'; Mohammad AB Shtaiyat; Ibrahim Alasad; Dana Aldaghlise
paper_title: Prevalence of Persisting and New Symptoms Following Recovery from COVID-19 in the Jordanian Population
paper_journal: Medical Journal of The Islamic Republic of Iran

summary: A cross-sectional study examining the prevalence and determinants of long COVID among COVID-19 survivors in a rural area of Maharashtra, India. Found a 17.5% prevalence of long COVID, with risk factors including elderly age, male sex, severe acute COVID presentation, and history of intubation.
paper_authors: Mohini Sopanrao Jogdand; Meghraj Ranchandra Bhondwe; Keerti Sopanrao Jogdand; Pravin Nathuji Yerpude; Ganesh Rameshrao Tathe; Shweta Subhashrao Wadiyar
paper_title: Prevalence and Determinants of Long COVID among the COVID-19 Survivors: A Cross-sectional Study from A Rural Area of Maharashtra

summary: Cross-sectional study of 400 home-treated COVID-19 patients in Baghdad examining prevalence and risk factors for persistent symptoms beyond 4 weeks. Found 30.25% had long-lasting symptoms, with fatigue (23.5%), smell/taste loss (14.75%), and cough (2%) most common; age, smoking, comorbidities, and initial symptom burden significantly associated with symptom duration.
paper_authors: Mazin Ghazi Al-Rubaey; Ahmed Abdul-Sattar Salman
paper_title: Factors affecting symptom duration and recovery among home-treated COVID-19 patients in Baghdad-Iraq: a cross-sectional study
paper_journal: Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association

summary: Cross-sectional study evaluating symptom persistence and health-related quality of life in 225 COVID-19 patients at 6 months post-discharge using the EuroQol scale. Most patients (76.9%) showed no symptoms or significant deterioration in quality of life at follow-up.
paper_authors: Gulsah Gunluoglu; Mustafa Cortuk; Nurdan Simsek Veske; Halit Cinarka; Furkan Atasever; Melih Akay Arslan; Admin
paper_title: Long-term follow-up and health-related quality of life in COVID-19 patients treated in hospital
paper_journal: Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association

summary: This cross-sectional survey assessed insomnia and sleep disturbances in medical students who recovered from acute COVID-19, using standardized insomnia severity (ISI) and sleep quality (PSQI) indices. The study found 65% of 117 students had some degree of insomnia and 78.6% reported sleep difficulty, with significant correlations between sleep measures and emotional health.
paper_authors: Presley Gruezo-Realpe; Alejandro Benavides-López; Romina Cedeño-Morejon; Alexander Noritz-Mero; Linker Viñan-Paucar; Israel Rosero-Basurto; Monica Jaramillo-Castro; Arianna Chango-Pinargote; Joyce Jiménez-Zambrano
paper_title: Insomnio y factores asociados entre los estudiantes de medicina que se recuperaron de la infección aguda por COVID-19.

summary: Cross-sectional study of 160 COVID-19 patients investigating the frequency and severity of telogen effluvium (hair loss) as a post-COVID consequence. Found telogen effluvium in 28.8% of patients with higher frequency in females, but this is a descriptive epidemiological study without any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Faisal Ahmad; Fatima Sajid; Afnan Bin Haq; Shayan Rizwan; Ayesha Siraj; Muneeza Rizwan
paper_title: Telogen effluvium in covid-19 patients: a cross-sectional survey
paper_journal: Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing endocrine disease prevalence in 724 athletes with prior COVID-19 versus 390 uninfected controls examined in 2021-2022. Found significantly higher rates of hypothyroidism, autoimmune thyroiditis, thyrotoxicosis, and type 1 diabetes in the COVID-19 group, suggesting post-COVID autoimmune endocrine sequelae.
paper_authors: E. A. Tenyaeva; E. A. Turova; V. A. Badtieva; E. O. Okonkwo
paper_title: Influence of the transferred coronavirus infection on diseases of the endocrine system in athletes

summary: This cross-sectional survey of 121 COVID-19 survivors examined the relationship between taste/smell alterations and post-COVID syndrome, finding 12.4% with persistent olfactory symptoms and 9.1% with persistent gustatory symptoms at 12 months. The study is descriptive epidemiology documenting symptom prevalence and recovery patterns, not a treatment intervention study.
paper_authors: Elías Eduardo Celi Yépez; Javier Alejandro Astudillo Mayorga; Christopher Sebastián López Rodríguez; Aarón Alberto Guzmán Tello; Jessica Nicole Ordóñez Reyna; Juan Carlos Padilla Espín
paper_title: Relación entre las alteraciones del sentido del gusto y/o el olfato y el síndrome post-covid

summary: A cross-sectional study assessing quality of life and functional status in 100 post-COVID-19 patients within 6 months of infection using EQ-5D-5L and PCFS scales. The study found high prevalence of mobility limitations (43%), pain/discomfort (65%), and functional impairment (65%), but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Pavithra A.; Nalini Sofia H.; Vetha Merlin Kumari H.; Lakshmikantham T.; Meenakumari R.
paper_title: A cross-sectional study on quality of life and the functional status in post covid-19 patients

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed clinical manifestations of post-COVID-19 syndrome in 80 patients using questionnaires and standardized scales for fatigue, dyspnea, and cognitive dysfunction. The study found gender differences in symptom presentation, with men reporting more severe fatigue and women more frequently experiencing headaches, but it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Victoriya A. Sergeeva; Tatiana E. Lipatova
paper_title: Clinical manifestations of post-COVID-19 syndrome in men and women

summary: Retrospective cross-sectional study characterizing COVID-19 prevalence and clinical profile among 107 Brazilian farmworkers, with 52% reporting long COVID symptoms (predominantly fatigue and breathlessness). This is an observational epidemiological survey with no treatment intervention tested.
paper_authors: Carlos Henrique de Lemos Muller; Hildegard Hedwig Poh; Miriam Beatrís Reckziegel
paper_title: Prevalence and clinical profile of COVID-19 among farmworkers from the interior of the state of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
paper_journal: Revista Brasileira de Medicina do Trabalho

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 539 long COVID patients examining the physical and psychosocial symptom profile to determine if symptoms constitute a defined syndrome. Found high prevalence of persistent symptoms (fatigue 52%, cognitive dysfunction 42%, dyspnea 39%) at 3 and 6 months post-infection, but analyses did not identify a distinct post-COVID syndrome.
paper_authors: J. Domen; Ipek Guler; L. Swartenbroekx Janssens; Birgitte Schoenmakers
paper_title: Vormen de fysieke en psychosociale symptomen van long-Covid een syndroom? Een cross-sectioneel patiëntenonderzoek

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing knowledge, awareness, and attitudes toward post-COVID-19 syndrome among 355 medical students across four Malaysian universities. Study found significant associations between age and knowledge, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention for long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Hao Ze Lee; Adam Amirudin Mohammad Tony; Nurul Asyikin Ismanizan; Nurul Hayati Mohamad Zainal; Norsuhana Omar; Ku Mastura Ku Mohd Noor; Hanan Hamimi Wahid; Nurul Huda Mohd Nor
paper_title: Association Between the Level of Knowledge, Awareness and Attitude on Post-COVID-19 Syndrome Amongst Medical Students in Four Malaysian Universities
paper_journal: Malaysian Journal of Medicine and Health Sciences

summary: A retrospective cross-sectional study examining the prevalence and clinical outcomes of long COVID in 1,600 patients from a large municipality in northeast Brazil. The paper highlights the burden of long COVID on an already overwhelmed healthcare system and provides real-world data on disease prevalence in a low-to-middle-income country context.
paper_authors: Phiri P.; Cavalini HFS; Delanerolle G.; Shi JQ; Shetty A.; Magalhães PF; Fernanda E.; Padovez RDFC; Neves VR
paper_title: The Long Covid abyss in Brazil; Is this another concern for an overwhelmed healthcare system?
paper_journal: Annals of Public Health and Research

summary: This cross-sectional study surveyed 510 residents of Mosul, Iraq to document the prevalence and types of long-term health effects following COVID-19 infection. The study found that COVID-19 caused persistent complications across multiple organ systems, with the highest rates in cardiovascular (67.1% tachycardia), neurological (60.6% chronic headache), and ophthalmological (69.9% blurred vision) domains.
paper_authors: Arwa Adress ALNUIMY
paper_title: LONG-TERM PATHOLOGICAL SIDE EFFECTS OF INFECTION WITH THE COVID-19 VIRUS IN THE MOSUL CITY
paper_journal: Full Text Book of Minar Congress4

summary: A cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence of post-COVID-19 syndrome among 300 recovered COVID-19 patients in Erbil, Iraq, finding 54.67% experienced persistent symptoms. The study examines associations between symptom persistence and factors like disease severity, chronic disease comorbidities, and disease duration, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Hawar AS; Dauod AS
paper_title: Long COVID19 prevalence among in Long COVID19 prevalence among a sample of infected people in Erbil City
paper_journal: Journal of Population Therapeutics and Clinical Pharmacology

summary: This cross-sectional survey of 306 people (98 with COVID-19 history) assessed whether post-COVID-19 syndrome (PPCS) symptoms correlate with signs of aging using a 17-item questionnaire. The study found significantly higher frequency of aging signs in post-COVID individuals and developed diagnostic procedures using Bayesian and neural network methods, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Anatoly Pisaruk; Natalya Koshel; Ludmila Pisaruk; Valeri Shatilo
paper_title: Impact of COVID-19 on the signs of human ageing

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing serum IL-6, IL-10, and vitamin D levels in 252 asthmatic and non-asthmatic subjects with and without post-COVID condition. Findings show elevated IL-6 and vitamin D in asthmatics with PCC, with complex correlations between inflammatory markers and vitamin D status.
paper_authors: Jaleel A.
paper_title: Interplay of interleukins (IL6, IL10) and 25 hydroxycholecalciferol in asthmatic subjects with chronic post-COVID condition (PCC)

summary: A cross-sectional study comparing cardiovascular risk factors and metabolic markers in 10 post-COVID patients (1-3 months post-infection) versus 21 controls, all with obesity or metabolic syndrome. The study finds higher cardiovascular risk indicators in the post-COVID group and suggests obesity may accelerate aging post-COVID, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Oleg Korkushko; Valentyna Chyzhova; Valeri Shatilo; Iryna Samots; Tetiana Kovtonyuk; Anna Gavalko
paper_title: Cardiovascular risk among people of all ages during the recovery period after COVID-19 (1-3 months) in the background of morbid obesity of the first stage

summary: This paper analyzes self-reported long COVID symptoms from 165 Twitter posts to characterize symptom prevalence and patterns in patient-reported experiences. It is a descriptive analysis of social media content rather than a treatment trial or clinical study.
paper_authors: Shubh M. Singh; Sai C. Reddy; Sanjana Kathiravan
paper_title: An Analysis of Self-reported Long COVID-19 Symptoms on Twitter
paper_journal: Journal of Postgraduate Medicine, Education and Research

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing quality of life in 44 children with long COVID versus 49 recovered controls using the PedsQL 4.0 questionnaire. Children with long COVID showed significantly lower quality of life scores across physical, emotional, and educational domains compared to fully recovered peers.
paper_authors: Oksana Boyarchuk; Vita Perestiuk; Tetiana Kovalchuk; Tetiana Kosovska; Liubov Volianska
paper_title: ASSESSMENT OF THE QUALITY OF LIFE IN CHILDREN WITH LONG COVID BASED ON THE STANDARDIZED PEDSQL 4.0 QUESTIONNAIRE

summary: Cross-sectional follow-up study of healthcare workers at least 12 weeks post-COVID-19 recovery describing clinical profiles and health outcomes. Found persistent physical symptoms (fatigue 25%, breathlessness 23%, muscle weakness 16%) and mental health issues (depressive symptoms 45%, anxiety 18%) in recovered workers.
paper_authors: Laviña SMS; Meija-Samonte MD; Isidro-Lapeña JS; Lacambra BCO; Hipol IGG; Anuran GO
paper_title: Outcomes and Clinical Profiles of Health Care Workers who Recovered from COVID-19: A Cross-sectional Study on Follow-up and Post-COVID-19 Syndrome

summary: A cross-sectional study of 228 COVID-19 recovered individuals identifying post-COVID syndrome symptoms using structured questionnaires. Found that 60.5% experienced moderate symptoms and 28.5% severe symptoms, with fatigue, shortness of breath, cough, and joint pain being most common, persisting for an average of 12 months.
paper_authors: Shreyas S. Walvekar; Vaishali R. Mohite
paper_title: Tracking Health Beyond Recovery: A Study on Identifying Post-COVID Syndrome Symptoms
paper_journal: Indian Journal of Critical Care Medicine

summary: Cross-sectional web-based survey of 1,172 Indian adults comparing neuropsychiatric symptoms (depression, anxiety, PTSD-like symptoms) in COVID-19 survivors versus controls. Found significantly higher rates of depression, anxiety, and cognitive symptoms in post-COVID patients, highlighting the need for mental health interventions in long COVID care.
paper_authors: Ajit Avasthi; Sandeep Grover; Gautam Saha; Mrugesh Vaishnav; Parth Vaishnav; Gundugurti Prasad Rao
paper_title: Neuropsychiatric Issues in Persons with COVID-19 Infection: An Online Survey from India

summary: Cross-sectional study of 125 COVID-19 survivors in Lahore assessing the prevalence and characteristics of chronic fatigue and related symptoms post-COVID. Found 55% experienced chronic fatigue, with strong associations between fatigue and body aches, low energy, and other post-COVID symptoms.
paper_authors: Hassan Sarwar; Anna Zaheer; Sahar Fatima
paper_title: TENDENCY AND ASSOCIATION OF DEVELOPING RELATED SYMPTOMS WITH CHRONIC FATIGUE AMONG COVID-19 SURVIVORS FROM LAHORE; CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY.
paper_journal: Journal of Akhtar Saeed Medical & Dental College

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing right ventricular function via echocardiography in COVID-19 survivors with lung involvement. Found statistically significant differences in RV functional parameters between severe and mild lung involvement groups, but this is a passive observational assessment without any treatment intervention or long COVID focus.
paper_authors: Nayab Balqees; Sajjad Hussain; Rizwan Yusuf; Mir Jalal Ud Din; Hafsa Khalil; Jahanzab Ali; Ayesha Sana; Rehana Javaid
paper_title: Echocardiographic Assessment of Right Ventricular Function in COVID-19 Recovered Patients at a Tertiary Care Hospital

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 341 recovered COVID-19 patients in Baghdad assessed the prevalence and duration of post-COVID-19 symptoms at various timepoints after acute infection. The study found that fatigue (12.3%), cognitive impairment (11.7%), and taste/smell loss (11.4%) were the most common persistent symptoms, with some lasting beyond 12 weeks.
paper_authors: Hasanain Faisal Ghazi; Taqi Mohammed Jwad Taher; Sumayah Al-Mahmood; Shaimaa Ahmad Hassan; Rana Talib Al-Nafakh; Shaymaa Abdul Lateef Alfadhul; Tamathir Abbas Hamoudi; Tiba Nezar Hasan; Ahmed Alaa Al-Temimi
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 among Iraqi Population: Symptoms and Duration

summary: Descriptive cross-sectional analysis of post-COVID-19 syndrome incidence in South Korean Army personnel using a self-completed survey. Study reports 32.9% overall incidence rate with symptom variation by dominant variant, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Taejae Kim; Beomman Ha; Ji-in Yang; Mi-Jung Kim; Kyung-Wan Seo
paper_title: Descriptive analysis of the incidence rate of post-acute COVID-19 syndrome in the Republic of Korea Army
paper_journal: Journal of the Korean Medical Association

summary: Cross-sectional study of 218 Italian adolescents examining the relationship between post-pandemic psychological distress (anxiety, depression, stress) and perceived decline in physical activity. Stress, anxiety, and depression were significant predictors of reduced physical activity, with depression showing the strongest effect and notable gender differences favoring greater psychological distress in females.
paper_authors: Gilles M. Costa; Andrea De Giorgio; Nicola L. Bragazzi; Goran Kuvacic; Sonia Angilletta; Irene Pivetta; Marco Alessandria
paper_title: Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19 in Adolescents: A Cross-Sectional Study on Perceived Physical Activity Decline and Mental Health

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing symptom intensity between 59 post-COVID patients entering rehabilitation and 57 non-COVID controls using a 31-item questionnaire. Found post-COVID patients reported significantly higher intensity for fatigue, dyspnea on exertion, cognitive dysfunction, and musculoskeletal pain, though some symptoms overlapped with the non-COVID cohort.
paper_authors: Jan Ceklarz
paper_title:
Symptom intensity of post-COVID and long COVID syndromes 
in patients entering rehabilitation treatment

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing quality of life and functional capacity between 33 symptomatic long COVID patients and 37 asymptomatic individuals 6-18 months post-infection using standardized outcome measures. Symptomatic patients showed significantly lower functional capacity (6MWT, 30s-STS) and worse quality of life scores across multiple SF-36 domains.
paper_authors: Ziya Yildiz; Süleyman Gürsoy; Ayşegül Yıldız; Feray Soyupek
paper_title: Comparison of Quality of Life and Functional Capacity of Long COVID-19 Patients and Asymptomatic Individuals: A Cross-sectional Study

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the frequency and characteristics of long COVID in 131 healthcare workers, finding that 48.1% had long COVID symptoms with fatigue, myalgia, and arthralgia being most common. The study identifies associations between hospitalization/oxygen need during acute infection and long COVID development, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Hazal Cansu Çulpan; Sümeyye Nur Aydın; Günay Can; Ayşen Kutan Fenercioğlu; Ethem Erginöz
paper_title: Long Coronavirus Disease and Chronic Coronavirus Disease in  Health-Care Workers: A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: This cross-sectional descriptive study surveyed 390 post-COVID-19 patients with insomnia at two traditional Chinese medicine hospitals in Vietnam (Dec 2022–Jun 2023) to characterize traditional medicine clinical patterns and their associations with comorbidities. The study identified common traditional medicine syndromes (Heart-Spleen deficiency 31.28%, Heart-Kidney discord 17.44%, Heart-blood deficiency 11.79%, Heart-yin deficiency 11.28%) and found significant associations between these patterns and comorbidities like hypertension, diabetes, and dyslipidemia.
paper_authors: Ngọc Xuân Nhi Phạm; Thị Bay Nguyễn; Ngô Lê Minh Anh Nguyễn
paper_title: KHẢO SÁT CÁC BỆNH CẢNH LÂM SÀNG Y HỌC CỔ TRUYỀN TRÊN NGƯỜI BỆNH MẤT NGỦ KHÔNG THỰC TỔN HẬU COVID-19
paper_journal: Tạp chí Y học Việt Nam

summary: Retrospective cross-sectional study describing the clinical and sociodemographic profile of 193 adults with long COVID in Costa Rica, comparing them to 198 controls without persistent symptoms. Identifies female sex, age ≥40 years, severe acute symptoms, and mental health disorders as significant risk factors for long COVID development.
paper_authors: Fabiana Rey-Cuadra; Adriana Rojas-Bermúdez; Sofía Solano-Pérez; Karla Sofía Gutiérrez-González; Gabriela Chavarría-Soley; Henriette Raventos
paper_title: Caracterización clínica y sociodemográfica delCOVID-19 persistente en Costa Rica

summary: Observational cross-sectional study of 396 post-COVID patients documenting persistent symptoms and their demographic/clinical correlates. Found that 87.9% experienced at least one persistent symptom, with fatigue, cough, and dyspnea being most common; no intervention or treatment was evaluated.
paper_authors: Barış Çil; Mehmet Kabak
paper_title: Persistent Post-COVID Symptoms and the Related Factors

summary: Cross-sectional observational study examining clinical features and symptom severity stratification in 101 post-COVID patients using standardized cognitive and psychological assessments. Identified three patient subgroups based on symptom severity scores, but did not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: N. V. Halinouskaya; E. V. Voropaev; A. A. Barbarovich; N. V. Bobovich; O. V. Osipkina; E. V. Boeva; I. O. Stoma
paper_title: Stratification of clinical groups in patients with post-COVID syndrome

summary: Cross-sectional observational study examining the relationship between sleep quality and learning concentration in 49 post-COVID-19 patients in Malang Raya using PSQI and concentration questionnaires. Found a statistically significant but weak association (p=0.029, r=0.312) between sleep quality and concentration.
paper_authors: Ali Multazam; Muhammad Hafiz; Bayu Prastowo
paper_title: Relationship between sleep quality and study concentration in Post-COVID-19 patients in Malang Raya

summary: Characterization study of clinical symptoms in young adults (18-44 years) with post-COVID syndrome using a validated self-assessment questionnaire. Findings show high multisystem manifestation (86.3% neurological, 61.2% cardiovascular) with women reporting significantly higher symptom burden than men.
paper_authors: Yu. V. Repina; E. A. Dotsenko; M. V. Sholkava
paper_title: Characterization of clinical set of symptoms in young adults (18–44 years old) with post-COVID syndrome

summary: This cross-sectional survey of 264 youth in Bengaluru assessed the prevalence of long COVID symptoms and quality of life using demographic questionnaires and the SF-36 instrument. The study found 43.2% had long COVID symptoms with significant gender differences in symptom patterns and mental health as the most affected quality-of-life domain.
paper_authors: Mohammed Wasim; Sheethal Kuriakose
paper_title: Assessment of long COVID symptoms and post-COVID quality of life in youth
paper_journal: International Journal of Epidemiology and Health Sciences

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between fatigue and dyspnea in 56 post-COVID-19 patients in Indonesia using the Fatigue Severity Scale and Borg Scale. Found a moderate positive correlation (r=0.498) between fatigue level and dyspnea, but this is an observational study with no intervention tested.
paper_authors: Ali Multazam; Herlianti; Nurul Aini Rahmawati
paper_title: The relationship between fatigue level and dyspnea in post-COVID-19 patients

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 275 nursing students assessing sleep pattern disturbances post-COVID-19 using insomnia severity index and Epworth sleepiness scale. Found 83.64% had mild sleep disturbances, 76.4% reported insomnia, and 57.1% experienced daytime sleepiness, with women showing higher sleepiness tendencies.
paper_authors: Joselyn Patricia Cruz-Romero; Fabiola Beatriz Chasillacta-Amores
paper_title: Prevalence of sleep pattern impairment post Covid-19
paper_journal: Sapienza: International Journal of Interdisciplinary Studies

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between anxiety levels and dyspnea in 56 post-COVID-19 patients in Malang, Indonesia using standardized anxiety and dyspnea scales. Found a statistically significant moderate correlation (r=0.503, p<0.001) between anxiety and dyspnea severity.
paper_authors: Ali Multazam; Diah Nur Pratiwi; Nurul Aini Rahmawati
paper_title: Relationship between anxiety levels and dyspnea among post-COVID-19 patients

summary: This cross-sectional study compared functional features (lung capacity, exercise tolerance, cardiac rhythm) in 101 adolescent students who had COVID-19 versus 25 controls without prior infection. While it documents post-COVID sequelae including asthenia and reduced exercise capacity, it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention—it is purely descriptive and observational.
paper_authors: Alexander Eduardovich Stradze; Anna Nikolaevna Nalobina; Ekaterina Sergeevna Kachenkova; Ilya Nikolaevich Medvedev; Sofia Niazovna Bobkova; Marina Valentinovna Zvereva
paper_title: Functional Features of Adolescent Students Who Underwent COVID-19

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing factors associated with quality of life and persistent dyspnea in 100 COVID-19 survivor healthcare workers using EQ-5D-5L, EQ-VAS, and mMRC scales. Found that post-COVID syndrome symptoms including activity limitation, cough, and fatigue were significantly associated with lower quality of life and persistent dyspnea.
paper_authors: Joshua P. Sinaga; Bintang YM. Sinaga; Parluhutan Siagian; Putri C. Eyanoer; Iduh M. Unata
paper_title: Factors associated with the quality of life and persistent dyspnea severity in COVID-19 survivors: A cross-sectional study among healthcare workers

summary: This cross-sectional follow-up survey assessed long-COVID outcomes in 219 participants from two prior RCTs comparing individualized homoeopathy as adjunct therapy versus placebo alongside conventional treatment for moderate-to-severe COVID-19. The homoeopathy group showed significantly better functional status scores (0.83 vs 1.33, p=0.04) and lower rates of post-COVID complications including diabetes, hypertension, and exertional breathlessness.
paper_authors: Harleen Kaur; Ramesh Bawaskar; Tania Chatterjee; Gurpreet Singh; Anurag Bajpai; Shweta Singh; Twinkle Kaur Bhogal; Mohammad Yamin Khan; Sunil S. Ramteke; Subhash Kaushik
paper_title: Prevalence of Post-Covid Complications in a Follow-Up Survey of Participants of Two Randomized Controlled Trials of Individualised Homoeopathy on Moderate and Severe Cases of COVID-19: A Cross-Sectional, Telephonic Survey
paper_journal: International Journal of High Dilution Research - ISSN 1982-6206

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing small airway obstruction and associated factors in 89 COVID-19 survivors under 50 years old at a hospital in Indonesia (2020-2022). Found a 19.1% incidence of small airway obstruction but no significant associations with age, gender, comorbidities, disease severity, or post-COVID symptoms.
paper_authors: Minarni ES. Aritonang; Pandiaman Pandia; Andika Pradana; Taufik Ashar
paper_title: Factors associated with small airway obstruction in COVID-19 survivors: A cross-sectional study among health-care providers

summary: Hospital-based descriptive cross-sectional study documenting the sociodemographic and clinical profile of 261 post-COVID patients with neurological manifestations. Study identifies tremor (50.6%), sleep disturbance (39.5%), neurocognitive decline (30.3%), and anosmia (29.9%) as the most common neurological presenting complaints but does not evaluate any treatment interventions.
paper_authors: Ibrahim Ali Saleem; Udayamma K. P.
paper_title: The Sociodemographic and Clinical Profile of Post COVID Patients with Neurological Manifestations Attending a Tertiary Care Centre
paper_journal: Galore International Journal of Health Sciences and Research

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 203 people assessing attitudes toward physiotherapy and psychotherapy for post-COVID recovery. Finds that 80.3% of respondents had COVID-19 infection, but only 25-30% sought physiotherapy or psychotherapy despite reported physical and mental sequelae.
paper_authors: Iuliu MOLDOVAN; Călina-Maria MUNTEANU; Septimiu VOIDAZAN
paper_title: Importanta procesului de reabilitare medicala în cazul pacientilor infectati cu virusul SARS COV2

summary: This cross-sectional study examined fatigue and associated risk factors among 100 mild COVID-19 survivors working in an Indonesian hospital from September to December 2022. The study found significant associations between post-COVID syndrome symptoms (particularly confusion, insomnia, myalgia, arthralgia, throat pain, headache, and chest pain) and fatigue incidence, but did not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Bintang YM. Sinaga; Parluhutan Siagian; Joshua P. Sinaga; Yoseph L. Samodra
paper_title: Fatigue in healthcare workers with mild COVID-19 survivors in Indonesia

summary: Cross-sectional study of 720 post-COVID individuals examining immediate and long-term neurological complications and their association with comorbidities. Found neurological complications in 6.38% (immediate) and 3.34% (long-term) of participants, with significant associations between diabetes/hypertension and neurological symptoms.
paper_authors: Joshi Snehal; Kunte Arya P.
paper_title: Immediate and Long-Term Neurological Complications Post COVID-19 Infection and Their Association with Co-Morbidities: A Cross-Sectional Study
paper_journal: International Journal of Health Sciences and Research

summary: Cross-sectional observational study examining the relationship between baseline neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and spirometry results in 80 severe COVID-19 survivors. Found no significant correlation between elevated NLR and lung function parameters (FVC, FEV1, FEV1/FVC, FEF 25-75%).
paper_authors: Ida Bagus Janantara Wirakusuma; I. Ketut Agus Somia; Ni Luh Eka Arisanti
paper_title: Correlation Between Neutrophil to Lymphocyte Ratio Baseline with Spirometry Test in Severe Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19)
paper_journal: International Journal of Research and Review

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of psychiatric disorders (insomnia, anxiety, depression, PTSD) among 100 post-COVID patients in an outpatient psychiatry clinic. Finds high rates of psychiatric complications but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Mala Bharti; Rakesh Banal; Rameshwar Singh Manhas
paper_title: Presentations of Psychiatric Disorders Among Post COVID Patients
paper_journal: International Journal of Research and Review

summary: A cross-sectional prevalence study of 750 individuals (aged 44-64) infected with COVID-19 during India's second wave, assessing chronic fatigue syndrome using the Fatigue Assessment Scale 1 year post-infection. The study found mild to moderate CFS prevalence in both hospitalized and home-quarantined individuals, with females more affected and significant correlations with age and smoking status.
paper_authors: Daxesh Sonara; Bosky Mehta
paper_title: Prevalence of Chronic Fatigue Syndrome in Individuals with Long COVID
paper_journal: International Journal of Health Sciences and Research

summary: Cross-sectional observational study comparing functional capacity and quality of life between COVID-19 survivors (second wave) and healthy controls in Ahmedabad, using 6-minute walk test and WHO-BREF questionnaire. summary: Cross-sectional study of 100 Iraqi participants examining changes in food preferences and taste-related characteristics following COVID-19 infection or vaccination. summary: This cross-sectional study compared sleep quality between medical students with and without a history of COVID-19 infection in Northern Vietnam using the Sleep Quality Scale. paper_authors: Thao Thi Thu Nguyen; Thinh Cuong Dao; Binh Thi Thanh Nguyen; Duc Cap Minh
paper_title: Sleep quality in non-hospitalized medical students after COVID-19 infection in Northern Vietnam
paper_journal: Journal of Public Health and Development

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between quality of life and echocardiographic findings in 31 healthcare workers with long COVID. paper_title: Hubungan Kualitas Hidup dengan Gambaran Ekokardiografi Tenaga Kesehatan dengan Long COVID

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the correlation between sleep quality and cognitive function in healthcare workers with post-COVID-19 symptoms at a hospital in Banda Aceh. Found no statistically significant correlation between sleep quality (PSQI) and cognitive function (MoCA-Ina) in the 54 healthcare worker participants.
paper_authors: Ika Marlia; Suherman Suherman; Cut Sri Rachmawati
paper_title: Korelasi Kualitas Tidur Dengan Fungsi Kognitif pada Tenaga Kesehatan Post Covid-19 di RSUDZA

paper_authors: Ahmed Mahdi Dawah; Meriam Ghardallou; Buthaina A. Rashid
paper_title: Receiving The COVID-19 Vaccine and Its Correlation with Post COVID-19 Long Term Morbidity

summary: Cross-sectional study of 266 COVID-19 patients assessing frequency, severity, and impact of fatigue on quality of life during the prolonged post-COVID period. Found that 33.6% experienced persistent fatigue beyond acute illness, which significantly impaired quality of life, particularly in energy and physical activity domains.
paper_authors: Özgül Ocak; Erkan Melih Şahin
paper_title: Fatigue in long-COVID; frequency, severity and impact on  quality of life

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing psychiatric illness and quality of life in 200 COVID-19 patients three months post-hospitalization. paper_authors: Preetika Baghel; Pradeep Kumar P. C.; Kishor M.
paper_title: Long Term Impact of Covid 19 On Psychiatric Health and Quality of Life in Recovered Patients
paper_journal: International Journal of Health and Allied Sciences

summary: This is a cross-sectional survey of 248 post-COVID patients in Panama examining long-term symptom prevalence and associated risk factors. The study documents symptoms persisting after acute infection (headaches, dyspnea, fatigue) and identifies risk factors like female gender and multiple acute-phase symptoms, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Manifestaciones clínicas en post COVID en adultos en la República de Panamá

summary: This cross-sectional study of 254 COVID-19 patients identified post-COVID symptoms and risk factors for chronic post-COVID syndrome at 5 and 12 weeks post-infection. Female sex and specific radiological findings were significant risk factors for chronic symptoms, while long-term ARB use was associated with lower symptom burden.
paper_authors: Hülya ABALI; Dilara DEMİR; Şule GÜL; Nurdan ŞİMŞEK VESKE; Seda TURAL ONUR
paper_title: Analysis of post-COVID symptoms and predisposing factors for chronic post-COVID syndrome

summary: Cross-sectional study examining correlations between complete blood count (CBC) inflammatory markers measured at hospital admission and long COVID symptoms reported at 6-month follow-up in 167 patients. Found that neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and lymphopenia correlated with specific symptoms like decreased libido and poor concentration, suggesting CBC markers may predict long COVID symptom development.

paper_title: Correlations of Long COVID Symptoms and Inflammatory Markers of Complete Blood Count (CBC): A cross-sectional study.

summary: A cross-sectional study of 329 COVID-19 patients in Turkey assessed symptom persistence nine months after infection, finding that 79.3% still had at least one symptom with fatigue, cognitive impairment, and effort loss being most common. paper_authors: Tahmaz A.; Çetin E.; Balcı U.; Sarıgül Yıldırım F.; Seyman D.; Gürgen A.
paper_title: [The Evaluation of Long Coronavirus Disease Symptoms at Ninth Month from a Hospital in Türkiye].

summary: Cross-sectional survey comparing long COVID symptom prevalence between 167 non-hospitalised and 95 hospitalised COVID-19 patients. Found long COVID in 59.9% overall, more frequent in non-hospitalised patients (68.3% vs 45.3%), with neuropsychiatric manifestations being most common.

summary: Cross-sectional study of 183 COVID-19 patients examining relationships between smoking status, physical activity, and COVID-19 outcomes including sequelae. Active and former smokers reported higher rates of sequelae (memory issues, fatigue) compared to non-smokers, but the study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Impact of smoking and physical activity on COVID-19 infection and vaccination rates

paper_authors: Diana Paskaleva
paper_title: Differences in treatment and post-COVID symptoms in elderly and young patients: a cross-sectional study

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed brain fog symptoms in 303 non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients retrospectively across four time periods post-infection, comparing symptom prevalence between women and men. paper_authors: Luciana Tati Suparti; Maria Yunita Indriarini; Yosi Maria Wijaya
paper_title: KARAKTERISTIK PENDERITA LONG COVID

summary: This cross-sectional study applies the WHO ICF framework to characterize functional limitations, disabilities, and health-related conditions in 213 long COVID patients with persistent respiratory symptoms in Turkey. paper_title: An Overview of Clinical Features, and Medical Access Among Patients with Post-Acute COVID-19 Syndromes: Analysis of a Nationwide Survey in Korea

summary: This cross-sectional study examined the prevalence and clinical predictors of post COVID-19 condition in 186 pediatric patients (aged 0-18) compared to matched controls. The study found a 15% prevalence of post COVID-19 symptoms, with hospitalization and age 5-11 years identified as significant predictors of persistent symptoms including cough, rhinorrhea, and taste loss.

paper_title: Impact of physical activity and body composition on cardio-vascular health post-COVID-19 in Guayaquil

paper_title: Neuropathology of Severe Depression in Long COVID-19 Infection; Possible Roles for Astrocytes, Creatine Kinase and Lactate Dehydrogenase Activity

paper_title: Long COVID Effects on Level of Physical Activity and Health-Related Quality of Life in the Post-infection Period: A Cross-sectional Study
paper_journal: Middle East Journal of Rehabilitation and Health Studies

summary: Cross-sectional study examining bone mineral density (BMD) in 164 post-COVID-19 patients and its associations with demographic and clinical characteristics. Found that older age and lower BMI were associated with higher osteoporosis risk, but the study is observational without testing any intervention.

paper_title: Post-COVID-19 Bone Mineral Density and Its Association with Demographic and Clinical Characteristics: A Cross-sectional Study

summary: A retrospective cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of post-COVID hair loss (alopecia) in Indian patients and its association with COVID-19 severity and stress levels. paper_title: Post COVID Alopecia in the Indian Subcontinent - A Harbinger of Disease Severity

summary: Cross-sectional survey assessing knowledge, attitudes, and experiences of physiotherapists in the UAE regarding long COVID management and rehabilitation. summary: This cross-sectional study evaluated the frequency and risk factors for functional gastrointestinal disorders (FGIDs) one year after COVID-19 recovery in 357 patients. paper_title: Frequency and Risk Factors for Post-COVID-19 Functional Gastrointestinal Disorders After One Year

summary: Cross-sectional descriptive study of 667 COVID-19 patients in Long Ho district, Vietnam (2022-2023) assessing post-COVID prevalence and associated factors. Found 60.9% post-COVID prevalence, with psychiatric symptoms most common (50.8%) and gastrointestinal symptoms least common (7.9%); hospitalization and comorbidities were associated factors.

paper_journal: Tạp chí Y Dược học Cần Thơ

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed cognitive and neuropsychiatric disorders in 20 Tunisian patients one month after COVID-19 hospitalization, using standardized cognitive tests (MMS, FAB, TMT, maze task). summary: Cross-sectional study of 500 Egyptian women examining the prevalence of telogen effluvium (hair loss) as a post-COVID-19 dermatological manifestation. paper_authors: Abo Bakr Helal El Asmar; Khaled Mohammed Ibrahim Halema; Alaa Adel Ibrahim Hammad

paper_title: Measurement of the Body Physical Parameters by Bioelectrical Impedance Method in Individuals Survived after Covid-19

summary: This paper analyzes serum samples from 99 post-COVID patients to test for antibodies to three tick-borne bacteria (Borrelia burgdorferi, Coxiella burnetii, Bartonella henselae), finding that 74% had antibodies to one or more bacteria.
