summary: A cross-sectional study of 312 Iraqi long COVID patients characterizing hematological abnormalities and coagulopathy patterns, finding high prevalence of elevated D-dimer (62.5%), lymphopenia (43.6%), fibrinogen elevation (38.1%), and thrombocytopenia (28.2%). The study documents disease pathophysiology and identifies hematological markers associated with symptom severity but does not evaluate or test any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Nuha Abd Ali Muhsin Al-Sarai; Abbas Abd Ali Muhsin Al-Sarai; Hussain Abd Ali Muhsin Al-Sarai
paper_title: Characterization of Hematological Changes and Coagulopathy Patterns in Iraqi Patients with Post-COVID-19 Syndrome
paper_journal: European Journal of Medical and Health Research

summary: Cross-sectional study examining secondary chronic musculoskeletal pain development in COVID-19 patients with and without lung involvement over a 3-month period. Findings indicate that patients with lung involvement had lower pain intensity, potentially due to stress-induced analgesia rather than long-term COVID-19 sequelae.
paper_authors: İbrahim BAŞHAN; Gülşah YAŞA ÖZTÜRK
paper_title: The Relationship Between COVID-19 and Secondary Chronic Musculoskeletal Pain
paper_journal: Journal of Immunology and Clinical Microbiology

summary: This cross-sectional study examined the frequency and correlates of subjective fatigue in 110 COVID-19 patients at 3 months post-infection. Key risk factors for fatigue included older age, chronic disease, severe acute infection (fever, pneumonia), and longer hospitalization duration.
paper_authors: Dejan Mihajlović; Mirjana Virijević; Ana Radovanović
paper_title: Factors associated with the subjective feeling of fatigue three months after COVID-19

summary: Cross-sectional study of 62 patients with chronic neuropathic pain after COVID-19 examining lifestyle factors using questionnaires and pain scales. Found that activity levels and alcohol use were negatively associated with lifestyle quality in this population.
paper_authors: Weltton Augusto da Silva Barbosa; Lilian Chessa Dias; Ana Marcia Rodrigues Cunha; Marcos D’all Aglio Foss; Paulo Rafael Condi; Marielza Regina Ismael Martins
paper_title: Lifestyle factors in patients with chronic neuropathic pain after COVID-19: a cross-sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 90 post-COVID patients examining symptom prevalence and associations with demographic factors and comorbidities. Found 24.4% experienced symptoms >6 months, with fatigue and concentration difficulty most common, but no treatment intervention was evaluated.
paper_authors: Irena Pušica; Ana Lončar
paper_title: Post-COVID syndrome: Current challenge in the work of the general practitioner

summary: This cross-sectional study examined anxiety-depressive disorders in 90 post-COVID patients using standardized scales (HADS, Beck depression scale). The study found no clear association between viral presence and anxiety-depressive manifestations, suggesting psychosocial factors may be the primary driver rather than direct pathophysiology.
paper_authors: Z. D. Kulbayeva; Sh. S. Kaliyeva; Dmitriy Klyuyev; Svetlana Tuleutayeva
paper_title: Anxiety-depressive disorders after COVID-19

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 1,300+ COVID survivors in Karachi (Oct 2021–Apr 2022) examining the prevalence and factors associated with long COVID symptoms and impact on work performance. Over 35% reported symptoms lasting ≥6 weeks, with frequent coughing and appetite loss; the study emphasizes the need for awareness and prevention strategies but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Sobia Majeed; Imran Ahmed Khan; Tahira Tariq
paper_title: Exploring the Prevalence of Long-Covid and its Factors among Post-Covid Survivors of Karachi

summary: This cross-sectional study examines associations between physical activity, mental health, and quality of life in 193 women with prior COVID-19 using questionnaires (IPAQ, DASS, WHOQOL). The study found partial associations between physical activity and mental health parameters, but no correlation with quality of life, and calls for longitudinal research with objective activity measurement.
paper_authors: Miloš Stamenković
paper_title: Physical activity, mental health and quality of life of women who have experienced COVID-19
paper_journal: Physical education and sport through the centuries

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 189 Korean nurses assessing long COVID symptoms and associated risk factors using the COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale. The study found 94.7% of nurses experienced long COVID symptoms, with fatigue, weakness, and breathlessness most prevalent, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Ga Eun Park; Yeon-Hwan Park
paper_title: Long COVID symptoms and associated factors in registered nurses with COVID-19
paper_journal: The Journal of Korean Academic Society of Nursing Education

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 134 elderly Vietnamese patients with hypertension and diabetes examining their knowledge and behavior regarding post-COVID health care. While 89% understood post-COVID self-care recommendations (nutrition, exercise, continuous treatment), only 48% actually followed them, and 36% required hospitalization due to unstable blood pressure and glucose levels.
paper_authors: Gắt Lê Văn; Liễu Lê Thị Hoàng; Phẩm Lê Bá
paper_title: Kiến thức chăm sóc sức khỏe sau nhiễm Covid-19 của bệnh nhân cao tuổi bệnh tăng huyết áp & đái tháo đường (Nghiên cứu tại Tp.HCM năm 2022)
paper_journal: Pham Ngoc Thach Journal of Medicine and Pharmacy

summary: This cross-sectional study of 150 Thai patients with post-COVID respiratory symptoms investigates Traditional Chinese Medicine syndrome patterns and their correlation with spirometry and fatigue severity. While it identifies TCM syndromes in post-COVID patients, it is a descriptive/diagnostic study without treatment evaluation and therefore excluded from the intervention trials pipeline.
paper_authors: Wachiraporn Padungkiettiwong; Watjanarat Panwong; Siraprapa Veerapattananon; Peeradone Srichan; Chatchada Sutalangka; Wilawan Chaiut; Ekalak Sitthipornvorakul; Raksuda Taniguchi
paper_title: Study of Traditional Chinese Medicine Syndrome Differentiation in post-COVID patients  with Respiratory Symptoms in Thailand
paper_journal: Journal of Current Science and Technology

summary: Cross-sectional survey study of 263 Brazilian residents examining the prevalence and correlates of self-reported post-COVID-19 fatigue between March 2023 and March 2024. Found 90.5% fatigue prevalence, associated with symptom persistence >4 weeks and alcohol consumption, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Vanigleidson Silva do Nascimento; Maria Hellena Ferreira Brasil; Viviane Cordeiro de Queiroz; Oriana Deyze Correia Paiva Leadebal; Juliana Raquel Silva Souza; Renata Karina Reis; Ana Cristina De Oliveira e. Silva
paper_title: Condiciones post COVID-19: un análisis de la fatiga y factores asociados

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 308 COVID-19 survivors in Indonesia examining factors associated with long COVID occurrence. Found 80.2% prevalence of long COVID with fatigue, brain fog, and cough as most common symptoms; gender and comorbidities were significantly associated with long COVID, but age and healthcare worker status were not.
paper_authors: Yudha Asy'ari
paper_title: FAKTOR-FAKTOR YANG BERHUBUNGAN DENGAN KEJADIAN LONG COVID PADA PENINTAS COVID-19

summary: This cross-sectional case-control study examines oxidative stress markers in post-COVID-19 survivors compared to controls in Central India. The findings show that superoxide dismutase levels were lower and serum malondialdehyde levels were altered in post-COVID cases relative to controls, suggesting a role for oxidative stress in long COVID pathophysiology.

paper_title: Oxidative stress markers among post-Covid-19 survivors in Central India

summary: Cross-sectional study of 30 long COVID patients examining the prevalence of depression, anxiety, and fatigue in those with olfactory dysfunction. Finds high prevalence of neuropsychiatric symptoms (66.7% depression, 53.3% anxiety and fatigue) with significant negative impact on quality of life dimensions.
paper_authors: Déborah Santos Sales; Mariana Beiral Hammerle; Rayanne da Silva Souza; Patricia Gomes Pinheiro; Débora Viana Freitas; Ana Carolina F. Herzog; Daniel Lucas de L. S. Santos; Nathalie Souza de Andrade; Hannah de Souza Resende; Carolina Garcia Nunez Carrijo; Luiz Claudio Thuler; Claudia C. F. Vasconcelos
paper_title: Long Covid-19 Syndrome: the Prevalence of Neuropsychiatric Symptoms in Patients with Olfactory Disorders

summary: This cross-sectional survey assessed the prevalence of insomnia among 300 post-COVID-19 elderly patients using the Insomnia Severity Index scale. The study found significant insomnia prevalence, with different gender distributions across the first and second COVID-19 waves.
paper_authors: Annie Jerin Retna Raj; Kumaresan Abathsagayam; Surya Vishnuram; Prathap Suganthirababu; Vignesh Srinivasan; Vinodhkumar Ramalingam; Preethi Gokulan
paper_title: Prevalence of Insomnia among Post Covid 19 Elderly Population

summary: Observational cross-sectional study assessing pulmonary function tests (PFT) in 50 Indian adults recovered from COVID-19, finding restrictive lung patterns in 56% of subjects. Study documents post-COVID respiratory sequelae but does not evaluate or test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Chaithanya K. S.; Anahita R. Shenoy Basti; Srilakshmi M. Prabhu
paper_title: Pattern of pulmonary function tests in subjects recovered from COVID 19 infection
paper_journal: NATIONAL BOARD OF EXAMINATIONS JOURNAL OF MEDICAL SCIENCES

summary: A prospective cross-sectional study examining chest CT findings six months after COVID-19 pneumonia in 43 patients. The study documents residual radiological manifestations (ground glass opacities, subpleural lines) in approximately half of patients but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Ezat Hesni; Aydin Pourkazemi; Sima Fallah Arzpeyma; Seyedeh Nazanin Seyed Saadat; Ali Alavi Foumani; Tofigh Yaghubi Kalurazi; Sonbol Taramian; Lida Mahfoozi; Hamed Akbari Koushkjeh
paper_title: Chest CT scan findings six months after COVID-19 pneumonia: A prospective cross-sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional study of 150 participants investigating the prevalence and factors associated with telogen effluvium (temporary hair loss) in individuals recovering from COVID-19 in Pakistan. Found that 73.3% of participants reported post-COVID hair loss, with significantly higher rates in females (68.2%), but this is a passive observational survey with no intervention or treatment tested.
paper_authors: Seemab Safdar; Iqra Jamshaid; Kanwal Noman; Nishwah Khan; Sajjad Butt
paper_title: Correlation of COVID-19 and Hairfall – A Cross-Sectional Study
paper_journal: Journal of Health and Rehabilitation Research

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of Hyperventilation Syndrome among 377 COVID-19 recovered patients using the Nijmegen Questionnaire, finding that 63.66% exhibited HVS with common symptoms including anxiety, palpitations, and blurred vision. The study is a descriptive prevalence survey with no intervention or treatment being tested, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: Aneeqa Sultan; Sumat Tariq; Usama Jamil; Fatima Choudhury; Muhammad Rehan Amjad; Salman Akram; Sania Maqbool; Amna Maqsood
paper_title: Prevalence of Hyperventilation Syndrome among Covid-19 Recovered Patients
paper_journal: Journal of Health and Rehabilitation Research

summary: A cross-sectional study of 225 COVID-19 survivors in Pakistan assessing the prevalence and severity of long-term respiratory symptoms including dyspnea, chronic cough, and pleuritic pain. Demographic factors such as older age, lower education, and female gender were associated with higher symptom severity, highlighting the need for targeted screening and rehabilitation.
paper_authors: Matiullah Hashimi; Muhammad Zafar Majeed Babar; Maria Noori; Areej Bilal; Hassnian Khan; Sana Sajjid; Muhammad Abdur Rehman
paper_title: <b>Long term Respiratory complications of Covid-19 patients admitted in Sheikh Zayed Hospital Rahim Yar Khan</b>
paper_journal: Journal of Health, Wellness and Community Research

summary: A cross-sectional descriptive study examining post-COVID-19 sequelae and biochemical parameters in vulnerable populations aged 50-65 years. The study found high prevalence of hypertension (42%), normal glucose and creatinine levels in most participants, and significant comorbidity burden, but describes monitoring and characterization rather than testing a specific intervention.
paper_authors: Jandry Josue Pisco-La Rochelle; Roberto Raul Piguave-Cacao; Alexander Dario Castro-Jalca
paper_title: Identificación y seguimiento de secuelas post-COVID-19 e intervención bioquímica en poblaciones vulnerables de 50 a 65 años

summary: Cross-sectional observational study assessing the impact of post-COVID-19 syndrome on health-related quality of life in 53 individuals from Santa Cruz, Brazil using the SF-36 questionnaire. Found no significant relationship between quality of life and long COVID, with time since acute infection not affecting health-related quality of life outcomes.
paper_authors: João Victor de Araujo Feitosa; Sarah Gabriele Dias Silva; Maria do Socorro Luna Cruz; Catharinne Angélica Carvalho de Farias
paper_title: Impacto da síndrome pós-covid-19 na qualidade de vida relacionada à saúde de indivíduos do município de Santa Cruz – RN

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 307 COVID-19 survivors assessing long COVID prevalence, symptom types, and associated factors. Found 40.1% prevalence with cardiopulmonary and general symptoms most common, but no significant associations with demographic or clinical characteristics.

paper_title: Prevalence, Symptoms, and Associated Factors of Long COVID-19: A Cross-Sectional Survey Study
paper_journal: Vajira Medical Journal :  Journal of Urban Medicine

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing pulmonary function (FEV1, FVC, FEV1/FVC ratio) in 43 COVID-19 survivors and 53 non-COVID-19 controls among medical students and laboratory volunteers at Andalas University. All participants had normal average pulmonary function, with no intervention or treatment evaluated.
paper_authors: Zalva Indira Dhiaulhaq; Afriwardi Afriwardi; Sabrina Ermayanti; Lili Irawati; Russilawati Russilawati; Biomechy Oktomalio Putri
paper_title: GAMBARAN FUNGSI PARU PADA MAHASISWA DAN RELAWAN LABORATORIUM DENGAN DAN TANPA RIWAYAT COVID-19 DI FAKULTAS KEDOKTERAN UNIVERSITAS ANDALAS TAHUN 2021

summary: Cross-sectional observational study assessing pain prevalence and characteristics in 76 patients recovered from COVID-19 using the Brief Pain Inventory questionnaire. Found 33.78% prevalence of post-COVID pain, with chest pain, neck pain, headache, and low back pain being most common, and pain severity higher in older patients, females, and those with comorbidities.
paper_authors: Md Mosharaf Hossain; Md Mostafa Kamal; Shahara Afroz; Easmin Akter; Sakera Sultana; Dilip Kumar Bhowmick; A. K. M. Akhtaruzzaman
paper_title: Assessment of Pain among Patients Recovered from COVID-19: A Cross-sectional Observational Study

summary: Cross-sectional study measuring functional limitation in 76 patients recovered from COVID-19 using the Post-COVID-19 Functional Status scale. Found that 39.5% had negligible functional limitation, 34.2% slight, 14.5% moderate, and 9.2% severe limitation, but the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Md. Mosharaf Hossain; Md. Mostafa Kamal; Md. Amirul Islam; Easmin Akter; Md. Bablu Hossain; Md. Abdullah Tareq Bhuiyan; Miftahul Jannat Khan; Saroar Jahan Rajib; A. K. M. Akhtaruzzaman
paper_title: Limitation of Functional Status after COVID 19 Infection: A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: Cross-sectional study examining demographics, risk factors, and post-COVID-19 syndrome manifestations among 410 patients in Iraq. Describes prevalence of symptoms (fatigue, cognitive impairment, joint pain, respiratory issues) across age groups but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Maitham G. Yousif; Luma S. Zeiny; Fadhil G. Al-Amran; Alaa M. Sadeq; Salman Rawaf; Dhiya Al-Jumeily
paper_title: Demographics, Risk Factors, and Post-COVID-19 Syndrome Among Patients in the Middle Euphrates Region of Iraq

summary: Cross-sectional study of 247 long COVID patients examining chronic musculoskeletal pain prevalence and associated factors after hospital discharge. Found 87% pain occurrence rate, with female sex, low income, recent discharge, and mechanical ventilation as significant risk factors for pain presence and intensity.
paper_authors: Igor da Silva Bonfim; Leandro Alberto Calazans Nogueira; Ney Armando Meziat-Filho; Arthur de Sá Ferreira; Renato Santos de-Almeida
paper_title: Factors associated with chronic musculoskeletal pain in individuals with long-COVID after hospital discharge: cross-sectional study

summary: A retrospective cross-sectional study of 536 COVID-19 patients in Nigeria that describes the clinical spectrum and predictors of post-COVID syndrome, finding 18.3% prevalence with fatigue and headache as common symptoms. Pre-COVID vaccination was associated with reduced PCS risk, and affected patients had lower quality of life scores across multiple domains.
paper_authors: Ilori Temitope; Odekunle Temitope. O.; Adebiyi Akindele. O.; Ajayi Ikeoluwapo. O.
paper_title: PREDICTORS OF POST-COVID SYNDROME AMONG ADULT PATIENTS WITH COVID -19 INFECTION IN IBADAN, NIGERIA

summary: Cross-sectional analysis of 653 COVID-19 hospitalization survivors examining the association between physical activity levels and lung/kidney abnormalities 8 months post-discharge. Physically active survivors showed significantly lower prevalence of lung (28% vs 40%), kidney (14% vs 23%), and combined lung-kidney abnormalities (4% vs 9%) compared to inactive survivors.
paper_authors: Heitor S. Ribeiro; Dário R. Mondini; Francisco Z. Mattedi; Lia Marçal; Leila Antonângelo; Guilherme S. Catharina; Luis Yu; Geraldo F. Busatto; Carlos R. R. Carvalho; Emmanuel A. Burdmann
paper_title: BEING PHYSICALLY ACTIVE IS ASSOCIATED WITH BETTER LUNG AND KIDNEY FUNCTIONS IN A COHORT OF COVID-19 SURVIVORS

summary: Cross-sectional observational study of 515 COVID-19 survivors in western Libya examining prevalence and duration of post-COVID-19 symptoms. Study found 72% reported persistent symptoms with recovery occurring within 3 months in 75.5% of cases, identifying fatigue, cough, anosmia, and anxiety as most common sequelae.
paper_authors: Ali Madour; Rahmah Aboulqasim; Alaa Alghanoudi; Safiyah Ikreedeegh; Shadi Aboulqasim; Khawlah Alghanoudi
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 Syndrome: Assessment of Short  and Long-Term Post-Recovery Symptoms In Recovered Cases In  Western Libya

summary: A cross-sectional study examining the prevalence and factors associated with acute telogen effluvium (hair loss) in 100 COVID-19 PCR-positive patients in Pakistan. paper_authors: Faryal Nawab; Farina Zameer; Salman Ahmed; Tooba Hanif; Nimrah Sarwar Awan; Shahwaiz Aman
paper_title: Factors Associated with Acute Telogen Effluvium and COVID-19 Infection

summary: This cross-sectional survey compares COVID-19 recovery outcomes between 53 physically active and 47 inactive subjects (ages 30-44), finding that regular exercise was associated with fewer symptoms and faster recovery. The study does not focus on long COVID specifically, but rather on general COVID-19 recovery in younger adults without chronic diseases.
paper_authors: Lejla Šebić; Alma Suhonić; Erol Kovačević; Nedim Čović; Izet Bajramović
paper_title: Influence of the Level of Physical Activity on Symptoms and Duration of Recovery From Covid-19

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in 60 individuals who were hospitalized for COVID-19 and investigating relationships with sociodemographic variables, quality of life, muscle strength, and functional capacity. Found 48.3% had PTSD with significant associations to sedentary behavior, reduced functional capacity (TUG, 6MWT), and impaired quality of life domains.
paper_authors: Tatyane Gomes de Oliveira; Arméle Dornelas de Andrade; Elaine Cristina Santa Cruz de Moura; Natalia Tarcila Santos Amorim; Patrícia Érika de Melo Marinho
paper_title: Post-traumatic stress disorder in individuals who required hospitalization for  COVID-19: A cross-sectional study

summary: Cross-sectional study evaluating kidney injury prevalence in 75 long COVID patients at 6, 12, and 24 months post-infection. Found progressive glomerular injury over time (50.7% with reduced eGFR) and tubular injury in 50.6% of patients, suggesting decoupling between glomerular and tubular mechanisms.

paper_title: KIDNEY DAMAGE IN PATIENTS WITH LONG COVID: CROSS-SECTIONAL CLINICAL STUDY

summary: This cross-sectional study characterized post-COVID-19 condition in Kenya by measuring clinical symptoms, anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibodies, and inflammatory markers (IL-6, CRP) in 189 participants. The study found post-COVID-19 in 30% of previously infected individuals but found no significant differences in antibody or inflammatory marker levels between symptomatic and asymptomatic groups.
paper_authors: Martin Theuri; Eric M. Ndombi; Peris Thamaini; James Opiyo Ogutu; Lister Onsongo; June K. Madete; Victor Ofula; Samuel Gitau; Gladys Mwangi; Paul Okemo

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 348 Portuguese healthcare workers examining the prevalence of long COVID and its impact on quality of life and work performance. Found 64.1% reported long COVID history with significant associations between extreme fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, and reduced work performance and life satisfaction.
paper_authors: Filipe Prazeres; Ana Paula Romualdo; Inês Campos Pinto; Joana Silva; Andreia M. Oliveira
paper_title: The impact of long COVID on quality of life and work performance among healthcare workers in Portugal

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed clinical long-term complications in 100 COVID-19 patients within 3 months of hospital discharge in Pakistan. The most frequent symptoms were fatigue (59%), dyspnea (47%), and loss of taste/smell (41%), reflecting respiratory, musculoskeletal, and neurological complications of post-COVID syndrome.
paper_authors: Javaria Mehtab; Asif Niaz; Nabeeha Azhar; Mahnoor Khawaja
paper_title: Clinical Long-Term Complications of Post Covid Time in Patients Reporting at PAF Hospital Within 3 Months After Discharge

summary: This study evaluates the readability, reliability, and quality of 100 websites providing patient education materials about post-COVID-19 pain. It finds that most materials are too difficult to read, lack credibility, and are of poor quality, with only a small percentage meeting recommended standards.
paper_authors: Erkan Ozduran; Sibel Büyükçoban
paper_title: Evaluating the readability, quality and reliability of online patient education materials on post-covid pain

summary: A retrospective cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of long COVID in Thailand during Delta and Omicron epidemic periods, analyzing associated biological factors through logistic regression and comparing spike protein mutations. The study found higher long COVID prevalence during Omicron (74.5% vs 66.0%) and identified epidemic variant, age, symptomatic medication use, and vaccination status as associated factors, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Supanchita Kiatratdasakul; Pirom Noisumdaeng; Nattamon Niyomdecha
paper_title: Biological factors associated with long COVID and comparative analysis of SARS-CoV-2 spike protein variants: a retrospective study in Thailand

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 52 COVID-19 patients in Bahrain assessing persistent symptoms 3 months post-infection using a symptom intensity scale. Found emotional stress, anosmia, and neurological symptoms were most common persistent symptoms, with associations between symptom intensities (e.g., dyspnea linked to pulmonary dysfunction).
paper_authors: Perna S.; Abdulsattar S.; Alalwan TA; Zahid MN; Gasparri C.; Peroni G.; Faragli A.; La Porta E.; Ali Redha A.; Janahi EM; Rondanelli M.
paper_title: A cross-sectional analysis of post-acute COVID-19 symptoms.
paper_journal: Annali di igiene : medicina preventiva e di comunita

summary: This cross-sectional online survey examined symptom clusters and their relationship to quality of life in 220 people with long COVID, identifying five distinct symptom clusters (digestive-cognitive, respiratory-fatigue, pain-dermatological, sensory, and emotional). While it provides valuable epidemiological data on symptom patterns, it does not evaluate or test any specific treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Yu Kyeong Jeong; Hye Young Kim
paper_title: Symptom Clusters and Quality of Life in People with Long COVID: A Cross-Sectional Online Survey
paper_journal: Journal of Korean Academy of Fundamentals of Nursing

summary: This cross-sectional survey assessed post-COVID-19 symptoms and quality of life in 158 recovered COVID-19 patients in Pakistan, finding that 94.9% experienced at least one post-discharge symptom with fatigue being most prevalent (82.9%). paper_title: The COVID-19 Sequelae: A Cross-Sectional Evaluation of Post-recovery Symptoms and the Need for Rehabilitation of COVID-19 Survivors

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing disability in COVID-19 survivors at three months post-infection using WHODAS 2.0. Found fatigue and dyspnea most common, with females and symptomatic patients showing significantly greater disability.
paper_authors: Ravi Gaur; Satyasheel Asthana; Rajkumar Yadav; Rambeer Ghuleliya; Deepak Kumar; Minhaj Akhtar; Nitesh Gonnade; Arun Choudhary; Merrin M. Mathew; Neeru Gaur
paper_title: Assessment of Physical Disability After Three Months in Patients Recovered From COVID-19: A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 85.3% of post-COVID-19 patients in Saudi Arabia identifying manifestations including fatigue, musculoskeletal complaints, neuropsychiatric symptoms, and gastrointestinal issues. Study identifies risk factors (gender, age, smoking, BMI, comorbidities, severity) associated with post-COVID-19 syndrome but does not evaluate any interventions or treatments.
paper_authors: Manal H. Mahmoud; Fahad A. Alghamdi; Ghaida A. Alghamdi; Loai A. Alkhotani; Mohammad A. Alrehaili; Dalia K. El-Deeb
paper_title: Study of Post-COVID-19 Syndrome in Saudi Arabia

summary: Cross-sectional study characterizing the clinical and laboratory profile of 259 patients visiting a post-COVID clinic in India, with 168 (64.9%) meeting PASC criteria. Identifies fatigue, breathlessness, and cough as common symptoms and hypertension, obesity, and persistent chest X-ray abnormalities as potential risk factors, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Vijayashree Thyagaraj; Akshay Rao; Ashwin Kulkarni; Tharanath Shankar; Nithin R.; Hridya Unnikrishnan; Keerthi Kalaiah; Iniya E.; Sundar K. Veluswamy; Nanda Kumar B. S.; Savita Ravindra; Naresh Shetty
paper_title: Clinical and Laboratory Profile of Patients Visiting the Post-COVID-19 Clinic at a Tertiary Care Hospital: A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: A retrospective chart review and survey study of 72 COVID-19 patients from a primary care clinic in Alabama, assessing prevalence of lingering symptoms at 3+ months post-infection. Found that 50.9% reported long COVID symptoms (fatigue, brain fog, shortness of breath), with women more affected than men, but no association with comorbidities.
paper_authors: Durgamani Kishore Yellumahanthi; Bethany Barnett; Sarabeth Barnett; Shushruth Yellumahanthi
paper_title: COVID-19 Infection: Its Lingering Symptoms in Adults

summary: Cross-sectional survey study evaluating the prevalence of post-COVID symptoms in a tertiary care center in northern India at 3, 6, and 12 weeks post-infection. Found that disease severity, BMI, and comorbidities significantly affected persistence of post-COVID symptoms, but this is an observational epidemiological study with no treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Nidhi Uniyal; Yashendra Sethi; Pradeep C. Sharma; Ashutosh Sayana; Narayan Jeet; Anurag Agarwal; Vijay Rawat
paper_title: Post-COVID Syndrome and Severity of COVID-19: A Cross-Sectional Epidemiological Evaluation From North India

summary: This cross-sectional observational study examined the prevalence of hair loss among COVID-19 recovered patients in Saudi Arabia and its impact on quality of life using questionnaires. The study found that 52.7% of 806 participants experienced post-COVID hair loss associated with high temperature during infection, female gender, and prior hair loss history, with 8.6% reporting severe quality of life impact.

paper_title: The Association Between Hair Loss and COVID-19: The Impact of Hair Loss After COVID-19 Infection on the Quality of Life Among Residents in Saudi Arabia

The study describes the manifestation and types of hair loss but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention for long COVID.
paper_authors: Rahaf A. Abdulwahab; Bushra M. Aldajani; Nujood K. Natto; Azad M. Janabi; Orjuwan I. Alhijaili; Norah T. Faqih; Aymen Alharbi
paper_title: Prevalence of Hair Loss After COVID-19 Infection in Makkah Region, Saudi Arabia

summary: A descriptive cross-sectional study of 227 post-COVID patients attending a tertiary care clinic in India, characterizing the prevalence and types of persistent symptoms including dyspnea (72%), cough (48%), and fatigue (42%). The study documents symptom patterns but is purely observational without any intervention or treatment component.
paper_authors: Sivaselvi C.; Manju Rajaram; Jayalakshmi Ramakrishnan; Vishnukanth Govindaraj; Vemuri Mahesh Babu; Subathra Adithan; Mukta Wyawahare
paper_title: Characterization of Post-COVID-19 Clinical Manifestations Among Patients Visiting a Post-COVID-19 Clinic in a Tertiary Care Center: A Descriptive Study

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 13,530 COVID-19 patients in Saudi Arabia documenting long-term otolaryngology manifestations, with vertigo being the most common long-term symptom (43.3%), followed by persistent fever and ear blockage. This is an observational prevalence study with no intervention or treatment component.
paper_authors: Musaed Alzahrani; Almaha H. Alshathri; Khalil Alduraibi; Aljohara H. Alshathri; Tahani F. Alanazi; Hamza Alandijani; Jumana a. Almajed; Khloud A. Wajdi
paper_title: Long-Term Outcomes of COVID-19 Otolaryngology Symptoms in Saudi Arabia

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing depression and anxiety symptoms in COVID-19 survivors at six months post-recovery versus matched controls using standardized rating scales. Found significantly elevated anxiety and depression scores in survivors, with severity correlating to initial disease severity.
paper_authors: Vijaya Chandra R. Avula; Sridhar Amalakanti; Shashidhara M.; Afreen Fasiha
paper_title: Anxiety and Depression in COVID Survivors - A Cross-Sectional Study Six Months Past the Acute Illness

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 54 adolescents examining the impact of post-COVID-19 syndrome on school and physical performance. Study found that prolonged symptoms (fatigue, cough) were associated with decline in sports participation but not academic performance, with multiple infections and incomplete vaccination increasing symptom persistence.
paper_authors: Jane El Khoury; May Skoury; Marc Y. El Khoury
paper_title: The Impact of Post-COVID-19 Syndrome in Adolescents: A Pilot Study

summary: Cross-sectional study of 286 COVID-19 patients in Bangladesh assessing post-COVID-19 symptom prevalence and characteristics. Found 18.5% reported post-COVID symptoms (fatigue, myalgia, anorexia, palpitations), with higher rates in older patients and those with severe initial disease.
paper_authors: Md Fahad Hossain; Syed Nurul Aziz; Mahfuza Akter; Manish Kharel; Nitesh Mandal; Indresh Yadav; Anjali Mandal; Roshan Rajbanshi
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 Illness Trend in a Local Community in Bangladesh

summary: Cross-sectional study of 194 COVID-19 patients examining prevalence and patterns of olfactory and gustative dysfunctions, with assessment of psychosocial impact. While the study documents that sensory symptoms persisted beyond acute infection (meeting long COVID criteria), it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Mohammad H. Shaheen; Abdullah Alghamdi; Abdullah Alrajhi; Meshal F. Khan; Alaa Babkour
paper_title: Prevalence, Patterns, Prognosis, and Psychosocial Impact of Olfactory and Gustative Dysfunctions Among Saudi COVID-19 Patients

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing the incidence of long-term fatigue in 343 Saudi COVID-19 survivors using the Chalder fatigue scale. Found 55.7% prevalence of long-term fatigue, with higher rates in females and those with longer post-infection duration.
paper_authors: Waleed M. Alotibi; Zaid Alzeer; Ibrahim F. Alfarhan; Abdulrahman D. Alharbi; Faris A. Alhaqbani; Ahmed S. Almutairi; Taghreed M. Alhazmi
paper_title: The Incidence of Long-Term Fatigue in Patients Who Achieved Remission From COVID-19 at King Abdulaziz Medical City

summary: Cross-sectional web survey of 404 fibromyalgia patients examining the relationship between fibromyalgia and post-acute COVID-19 syndrome. Found that 19.8% met ACR fibromyalgia criteria, with female gender and dyspnea as significant predictors.
paper_authors: Alaa Akel; Bilal Almanasyeh; Abdulrahman Abo Kobaa; Ahmed Aljabali; Ahmed Al-Abadleh; Asem Alkhalaileh; Abdel Rahman Alwardat; Mohammed Y. Sarhan; Mohammad Abu-Jeyyab
paper_title: A Cross-Sectional Study of Fibromyalgia and Post-acute COVID-19 Syndrome (PACS): Could There Be a Relationship?

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 346 women in Saudi Arabia examining the effect of COVID-19 on menstrual cycle regularity, duration, frequency, and pain severity. Found significant increases in menstrual irregularities during and after COVID-19 infection compared to pre-infection baseline.
paper_authors: Uma H. Chourasia; Ali H. Khormi; Hanan A. Jawkhab; Shahad I. Zoli; Kholoud A. Assiri; Shaden A. Thurwi; Saleha H. Alhazmi; Altaf A. Alhazmi; Jawahir M. Homadi; Raneem K. Zakri; Nada Y. Kenani; Ibrahim M. Dighriri
paper_title: Determining the Effect of COVID-19 on the Menstrual Cycle Among Women of Reproductive Age Group in the Jazan Region: A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: This hospital-based cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence and determinants of long COVID among 212 outpatients with confirmed COVID-19 history in India, using symptom checklists, PHQ-9 depression screening, and diagnostic tests. The study found a 37.3% prevalence of long COVID, with depression and COVID-19 severity identified as significant determinants, but did not test any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Harshal R. Salve; Roy A. Daniel; Alok Kumar; Rakesh Kumar; Puneet Misra
paper_title: Prevalence and Determinants of Long COVID Among Patients Attending the Outpatient Department of a Subdistrict Hospital in Haryana

summary: A cross-sectional study comparing auditory and visual working memory capacity in 17 medical students recovering from mild COVID-19 versus 18 healthy controls. The study found selective impairment of auditory working memory in long COVID cases but no overall differences in visual working memory or attention span.
paper_authors: Soumen Manna; Shaon Ghosh Dastidar; Ramkumar S.; Himani Ahluwalia; Manpreet Kaur
paper_title: Preferential Impairment of Auditory Working Memory in Long COVID: An Observational Study of Undergraduate Medical Students

summary: Prospective longitudinal study of COVID-19 survivors in India assessing long COVID symptoms and pulmonary function abnormalities. Found that breathlessness and restrictive lung patterns were prevalent in long COVID patients, particularly those with severe initial infection and female participants.
paper_authors: Nitish M. S.; Revadi G.; Ananyan Sampath; Ramesh Gadwala; Charan G. V.; Abhijit P. Pakhare; Rajnish Joshi; Abhishek Singhai; V. N. Mishra; Sagar Khadanga
paper_title: The Post-COVID-19 Haul on Pulmonary Function: A Prospective Cross-Sectional Study

summary: A cross-sectional study of 196 COVID-19 patients in Islamabad examining the prevalence of long COVID symptoms and their association with blood group and demographic factors. The study found no association between long COVID and ABO blood groups, but identified females as more likely to experience long COVID symptoms, particularly in those with perceived severe acute infection.
paper_authors: Muhammad Abdurrahman Butt; Muhammad Areeb Abdullah; Mustafa Waseem; Hamna Ahmed; Amna Aamir; Rafia Asif; Hameed M. Durrani
paper_title: Prevalence of Long COVID Syndrome and its Association With Blood Group: A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 482 Saudi adults examining the association between COVID-19 infection and back pain prevalence in the Eastern Province. The study found that 10.1% of participants reported back pain with varied durations, and among those with back pain, 24.7% attributed it to COVID-19, highlighting back pain as a potential post-COVID symptom.
paper_authors: Bushra M. Alsayari; Shahad M. Alshehri; Abdullatif Y. Almulhim; Leena M. Alzakry; Abdullatif A. Alzuraiq; Fahad H. Binshalhoub; Hanin M. Banjer; Lama Mohammed A. Alkhediwi; Kholood M. Rasdwi; Abdul Sattar Khan
paper_title: COVID-19 and Its Impact on Back Pain in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing asthma-like symptoms and clinical parameters between 39 post-COVID patients and 37 asthmatic controls in Dubai. Post-COVID patients showed improvement with bronchodilator therapy (inhaled corticosteroids and long-acting beta-agonists), suggesting potential efficacy of anti-asthma treatment for managing post-COVID respiratory symptoms.
paper_authors: Syed Arshad Husain; Amirarshia Rategh; Muhammad Omar Larik; Leon G. D'Cruz; Jean Mary John; Bassam Mahboub
paper_title: Development of Asthma-Like Symptoms After COVID-19: A Cross-Sectional Study in Dubai, United Arab Emirates

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing pulmonary function tests (PFTs) in post-convalescent COVID-19 patients versus controls and smokers. Found minimal differences in most PFT parameters between groups, with only FEV1/FVC% and PEFR showing statistically significant increases in smoking patients.
paper_authors: Ghada E. Elgarawany; Sapna Shevade; Shahad Aldebi; Bader Ahmed; Fagr Omer; Raghad Adel
paper_title: Evaluation of Pulmonary Function in Post-convalescent COVID-19 Adults: A Comparative Insight

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the association between acute COVID-19 severity and persistent dyspnea in 385 recovered adults, stratified by infection severity (mild to critical). Found a strong correlation between initial COVID-19 severity and both persistence and severity of dyspnea symptoms, with oxygen therapy recipients showing higher clinical scores.
paper_authors: Atif Saeed; Marium Nadeem Khan; Momina Kamran; Shivam Singla; Sri Teja Chikkala; Moeed Akbar Malik; Joseph Benjamin Baidoo; Farhan Ullah; Bhavna Singla; Sara Ali; Fatima Alam
paper_title: Association Between Severity of COVID-19 Infection and Persistent Dyspnea in Recovered Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: Cross-sectional study of 100 Pakistani patients examining neurocognitive and emotional outcomes of long COVID, using standardized assessments including MMSE and ADHD screening. Found significant correlations between COVID-19 symptoms and depression, anxiety, and ADHD, with females reporting higher psychological burden.
paper_authors: Muddsar Hameed; Mahrukh Anwar Abbasi; Fatima Noor; Ayesha Fatima; Muhammad Ibrahim; Shah Bano; Ali Hamza; Ali Afaq Rasool Malik; Muhammad Ahsan Saeed; Saman Iqbal
paper_title: Exploring Neurocognitive and Emotional Outcomes of Long COVID: A Study Among Pakistani Patients

summary: A cross-sectional survey of 2,153 Saudi Arabian residents assessing public awareness of post-COVID-19 syndrome symptoms and risk factors between June-August 2023. The study found low overall awareness (64.09% had low awareness) with significant knowledge gaps regarding PC19S symptoms and risk factors.
paper_authors: Mushabab Alghamdi; Sami Mohammed A. Alaklabi; Saud G. Alshmrani; Yaser Mohammed D. Alamri; Turki A. Alamri; Turki M. Alaklabi; Sultan Saber Z. Alharethi; Salem Mohammed K. Alalyani; Masoud I. E. Adam
paper_title: Awareness of Post-COVID-19 Syndrome Among the General Population of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia

summary: Cross-sectional study of 335 COVID-19 patients discharged from a tertiary care hospital in India, assessing persistent symptoms at 28 days post-symptom onset via telephonic interview. Found 66% had persistent symptoms, with fatigue (32.5%), dyspnea (23%), and cough (13.4%) being most common; higher persistence in severe cases and those with comorbidities.
paper_authors: Binu Areekal; Sudhiraj Thiruthara Sukumaran; Andrews Mekkattukunnel Andrews; Sreejith Parayil Nanu; Indira Madhavan; Pranav Veepanattu; idhin Raj Parambath; Jobin Palluruthil Solomon
paper_title: Persistence of Symptoms after Acute COVID-19 Infection- An Experience from a Tertiary Care Centre in South India
paper_journal: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH

summary: Cross-sectional survey of 735 nurses assessing anxiety and depression levels two years after COVID-19 infection, comparing long COVID (n=263) vs non-long COVID (n=472) groups. Found that nurses with long COVID had significantly higher depression and anxiety scores, with older age and depression severity as independent risk factors.
paper_authors: Lin Zhang; Liang Li; Junyi Chen; Suhua Pang; Zhenjiang Zhang; Youde Yan
paper_title: Psychological Burden of Long COVID and Associated Factors Among Nurses Two Years Post-infection: A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: Cross-sectional study of 287 post-COVID-19 patients with rhino-orbital fungal infections in India, identifying Fusarium, Aspergillus, and Mucor as causative organisms. Study evaluates epidemiology and risk factors (diabetes, steroids, immunosuppression) but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: BM Shanker Venkatesh; P. Ganga Bhavani; K. Manjusha; Sania Sultana
paper_title: Rhino-orbital Fungal Invasion in Post COVID-19 Cases at a Tertiary Eye Care Centre in Hyderabad- A Cross-sectional Study
paper_journal: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH

summary: A descriptive cross-sectional study assessing pulmonary function tests in 155 COVID-19 recovered health science students six weeks post-infection at a medical college in India. The study found altered respiratory function patterns (primarily restrictive disease) in recovered subjects compared to predicted values, with female participants showing significantly reduced FEV and FEF values.
paper_authors: Sudha Patil; Anita Teli; Rekha Nayaka; Parwati Patil
paper_title: Assessment of Pulmonary Function in COVID-19 Recovered Health Science Students: A Descriptiv Cross-sectional Study
paper_journal: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing cognitive function between 29 young adults with mild COVID-19 infection (≥2 years post-infection) and 29 matched controls using NIH Toolbox cognitive assessments. Found no statistically significant differences in cognitive domains (executive function, flexibility, attention, memory, processing speed) between cases and controls.
paper_authors: Vatsal A. Batra; Kairavi B. Unarkat; Manpreet Kaur; Himani Ahluwalia; Soumen Manna
paper_title: Post-COVID Condition Does Not Alter Cognitive Functions in Young Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study in North India

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing mental health outcomes (anxiety, depression, sleep quality) in 240 healthcare workers with and without post-acute COVID-19 syndrome. Found significantly higher anxiety and poorer sleep quality in the post-acute COVID-19 group, but no significant difference in depression.
paper_authors: Priyanka Gulati; Dimple Choudhry; Nitish Sharma; Poonam Dhankher; Manshi .; Anshu Kumari
paper_title: Impact of Post-acute COVID-19 Syndrome on Mental Health of Healthcare Professionals: A Cross-sectional Study
paper_journal: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing autonomic nervous system dysfunction and inflammatory markers in 150 COVID-recovered patients three months post-infection. Found that 36 patients had autonomic dysfunction with significantly elevated inflammatory biomarkers (IL-6, CRP) and correlations between inflammation and autonomic function parameters.
paper_authors: Lakshmi Jatiya; Jothi Marie Feula; Latha R.; Vidhyalakshmi R.; James Rajesh
paper_title: Autonomic Imbalance and Elevated Inflammatory Cytokines in Long COVID: A Cross-Sectional Study

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of post-COVID pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) among 854 COVID-19 pneumonia survivors and its association with CT severity scores. Found 12.1% prevalence of PAH with significant association between chest CT severity during acute infection and PAH development.
paper_authors: Panda Sibaram; Panda Mayadhar; Sanju Nanda; Subodha Kumar
paper_title: Prevalence of Post COVID-19 Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension and Its Clinical Association with CT Severity Score among COVID-19 Pneumonia Survivors in a Tertiary Care Hospital of Western Odisha, India
paper_journal: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of cognitive impairments including memory loss, attention deficits, and executive function disorders in 539 post-COVID-19 recovered individuals in Saudi Arabia. While it documents significant cognitive symptoms (39.15% with memory changes), it is observational without any intervention or treatment arm, making it ineligible for a clinical trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: Ahmad Hamad Zaila; Megren S. Alqarni; Abdulmlk A. Alqasem; Yazeed Yahya H. Alasmari; Alwaleed K. Almouzan; Rayan Ahmed N. Alghamdi; Ahmed Rajab A. Alzahrani; Huda Ibrahim Alhelais; Batool Shaker J. Alsaad; Mohammed H. Karrar Alsharif
paper_title: Memory Impairment and its Impact on Post-COVID-19 Patients among Saudi Population: An Exploratory Study
paper_journal: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of cognitive impairment in 204 long COVID patients with psychiatric sequelae at a specialized mental health clinic in India. The study found that 86.8% of patients had cognitive impairment, which was significantly correlated with depression but not associated with socio-demographic factors; however, this is an observational study with no intervention or treatment being tested.
paper_authors: Riyal Das; Aniket Mukherjee; Sujit Sarkhel; Mayank Kumar
paper_title: Cognitive Impairment in Long COVID Patients Presenting with Psychiatric Sequelae: A Cross-sectional Study
paper_journal: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing post-COVID-19 menstrual abnormalities in 204 medical students treated at home vs. hospital during acute infection. Menstrual cycle abnormalities were more prevalent in the hospital group (61.9%) than home treatment group (46.9%), with premenstrual syndrome being the most common abnormality; most irregularities resolved within six months.
paper_authors: Aliya Jabeen Syed; Badusha Mohammad; Praveen Kumar Lakinena; Venkata Vedantam; Shashi Prakash
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 Menstrual Abnormalities among Medical Students at a Tertiary Care Medical College in Southern India: A Cross-sectional Study
paper_journal: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH

summary: Cross-sectional study comparing heart rate variability (HRV) and autonomic nervous system function between young adults with bronchial asthma who have and have not had prior COVID-19 infection. Asthma patients with prior COVID-19 showed significantly lower parasympathetic markers and elevated sympathetic activity, indicating post-COVID autonomic dysfunction.
paper_authors: Gunaseelan Deivendran; Thamarai Selvi Kanagaraj; Bhavisha Sreenivasan Leelabai; Nalini Jayanthi; Saravanan Ayyavoo
paper_title: Heart Rate Variability in Young Adults with Bronchial Asthma with and without Previous COVID-19 Infection: A Cross-sectional Study
paper_journal: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH

summary: Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between long COVID syndrome severity and quality of life in 67 COVID-19 survivors aged 15-64 years. Found significant negative correlations between severity and quality of life across physical, mental, and social domains.
paper_authors: Eric Fernandez; Paulus Alexander Supit; Niluh Suwasanti
paper_title: The Effect of Long COVID Syndrome Degree Severity on the Quality of Life of COVID-19 Survivors Aged 15-64 Years Old at Gotong Royong  Hospital, Surabaya
paper_journal: Asian Journal of Medicine and Health

summary: Cross-sectional study assessing taste and smell impairment in university students with and without COVID-19 history using standardized flavor recognition tests. Found that COVID-19 infection moderately impaired ability to identify salty and bitter tastes, with 63.3% reporting taste loss and 69.4% reporting smell loss.
paper_authors: Krzysztof TERESZKIEWICZ; Piotr ANTOS; Paulina OSTYŃSKA; Karolina KOWALCZYK; Anna GŁADYSZ
paper_title: ASSESSMENT OF LONG-TERM TASTE AND SMELL COLOR BLINDNESS AS A RESULT OF COVID-19 DISEASE

summary: This cross-sectional study describes the clinico-epidemiological profile of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) as a post-COVID complication in a North Indian tertiary care hospital. While MIS-C is temporally related to COVID infection, the paper focuses on acute inflammatory complications rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-to-months post-infection) and does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Fazil M. Izhar; Ayisha A. Haque; Zulquar Nain; Shaad Abqari; Iraj Alam Khan
paper_title: Clinico-epidemiological Profile of Multisystem Inflammatory  Syndrome in Children

summary: Comparative cross-sectional study assessing cognitive impairment in severe post-COVID-19 patients admitted for rehabilitation versus ICU controls. Found no significant difference in cognitive impairment between post-COVID and control groups across multiple cognitive domains.
paper_authors: Florencia Deschle; Maria Eugenia Tabernero; Jorge Jose Cancino
paper_title: Cognitive impairment after ICU: Comparative study of severe post‐COVID19 patients with other causes of ICU admission

summary: Cross-sectional study of 312 adolescents examining the association between physical activity time and chronic post-COVID syndrome. Finds that female sex, post-pubertal status, and insufficient physical activity are significant predictors of developing post-COVID syndrome.
paper_authors: Gustavo Baroni Araujo; Michelle Moreira Abujamra Fillis; Helio Serassuelo Junior
paper_title: Is chronic post-covid syndrome associated with physical activity time in adolescence?             /               A síndrome pós-covid crônica está associada ao tempo de atividade física na adolescência?
paper_journal: Revista de Pesquisa Cuidado é Fundamental Online

summary: This nested case-control study examines the association between SARS-CoV-2 infection and dementia risk in 1.1 million Israeli adults aged ≥50, matching 27,280 dementia cases to 272,800 controls. The study finds that hospitalized COVID-19 patients had 75-93% increased dementia risk, but this is an epidemiological association study with no treatment intervention, and long COVID is not the primary focus.
paper_authors: Nika Zur; Nili Stein; Walid Saliba; Galit Weinstein
paper_title: Sars‐Cov‐2 infection and dementia risk: a nationwide, nested case‐control study

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed quality of life and fatigue symptoms in 38 post-COVID-19 patients in Brazil using the EQ-5D-5L and CFQ-11 scales. Results show 60.53% exhibited fatigue symptoms and 26-29% reported moderate problems with pain/discomfort and anxiety/depression, with median health quality-of-life scores of 70-80.

paper_title: Quality of Life and Fatigue Symptoms of Post-Covid-19 Patients in  Paraíso do Tocantins
paper_journal: Journal of Advances in Medicine and Medical Research

summary: Cross-sectional observational study examining post-COVID symptom prevalence across vaccination types and booster dose effects in 110 Bangladeshi participants. Study reports symptom patterns by vaccine type but lacks a treatment intervention—booster status is an observational variable, not an assigned treatment, making this an epidemiological assessment rather than a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Mahbuba Khatun; Shohal Hossain; Shahnaz Rahman; Md. Abu Rayhan; Md. Nafij Mashrur; Md. Fuad Hossain; Asma Farid; Nahin Islam Lammi; Mostafa Tanvir Tusar; Md. Kamrul Hasan Jabed Chowdhury; Mst. Sumi Islam
paper_title: The Silent Struggle: Addressing Post-COVID Health Challenges with Booster Doses

summary: A retrospective cross-sectional study characterizing long COVID sequelae in 138 patients attending primary care in Mexico from 2023-2025. The study identified respiratory symptoms (cough, odynophagia) as most common sequelae and found vaccination offered protection against dyspnea but was associated with increased cough.
paper_authors: Sandy Andrea Saavedra- Contreras; Daniel Lopez- Hernandez; Nallely Blanco- Osorio; Leticia Brito- Aranda; Daniel Cannan- Perez; Karina Ayala- Lopez; Guadalupe Jacqueline Flores- Morales; Liliana Garcia- Montiel; Liliana Grisel Liceaga- Perez; Tania Castillo- Cruz; María del Rocío Thompson- Bonilla; Saul Odin Rodriguez- Ramirez; Edgar Cruz- Aviles; Rocio Liliana Jimenez- Hernandez; Emmanuel Melgarejo- Estefan; Abraham Espinoza- Perdomo; Luis Beltran- Lagunes
paper_title: Characterisation of Post-COVID-19 Sequelae in a Primary Care Setting:  A Cross-sectional Study
