summary: Case-control study examining racial and ethnic disparities in outpatient rehabilitation utilization among post-COVID-19 patients using the TriNetX database. Finds that African American/Black individuals received rehabilitation services at lower rates despite similar symptom incidence, highlighting healthcare access inequities.
paper_authors: Claudia B. Hentschel; Benjamin A. Abramoff; Timothy R. Dillingham; Liliana E. Pezzin
paper_title: Race, ethnicity, and utilization of outpatient rehabilitation for treatment of post <scp>COVID</scp>‐19 condition

summary: A case-control study developing a urinary peptidomic diagnostic model (PASC195) to distinguish long COVID patients from controls using 195 differentially abundant peptides. While the study suggests potential therapeutic interventions (exercise, GLP-1RAs, MRAs) based on in silico analysis, it does not test or evaluate any actual treatment interventions in patients.
paper_authors: Dilara Gülmez; Justyna Siwy; Katharina Kurz; Ralph Wendt; Miroslaw Banasik; Björn Peters; Emmanuel Dudoignon; Francois Depret; Mercedes Salgueira; Elena Nowacki; Amelie Kurnikowski; Sebastian Mussnig; Simon Krenn; Samuel Gonos; Judith Löffler‐Ragg; Günter Weiss; Harald Mischak; Manfred Hecking; Eva Schernhammer; Joachim Beige
paper_title: Urinary Peptidomic Profiling In Post‐Acute Sequelae of SARS‐CoV‐2 Infection: A Case‐Control Study

summary: Case-control study comparing cognitive performance and brain network organization in 42 long COVID patients with cognitive complaints versus 43 healthy controls using MRI and neuropsychological testing. Found long COVID patients had significantly impaired memory, attention, and executive function with reduced efficiency in salience/ventral attention and global networks.
paper_authors: Micaela A. Hernández; Fermin Travi; Juan Kamienkowski; Bruno Bianchi; Agostina Carello; Belén Helou; Lucia Crivelli; Diego Fernández Slezak; Gustavo Sevlever; Ricardo Allegri; Ismael Luis Calandri
paper_title: Cognitive impairment, brain connectivity, and long‐Covid: understanding the complex interplay

summary: A case-control study comparing whole-body [18F]FDG-PET/CT imaging between 13 long COVID patients and 26 matched melanoma-free controls to investigate systemic inflammation and brain metabolism patterns in long COVID. The study found characteristic brain hypometabolism in long COVID patients and multi-organ inflammatory changes on PET imaging, suggesting distinct temporal inflammatory sequences between brain and systemic involvement.
paper_authors: Martina Sollini; Silvia Morbelli; Michele Ciccarelli; Maurizio Cecconi; Alessio Aghemo; Paola Morelli; Silvia Chiola; Fabrizia Gelardi; Arturo Chiti
paper_title: Long COVID hallmarks on [18F]FDG-PET/CT: a case-control study
paper_journal: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

summary: This cross-sectional study compares semen quality (sperm concentration, motility, morphology) between 100 men who recovered from acute COVID-19 and 100 men who never had COVID-19. The study found decreased sperm concentration in the COVID-19 recovered group but no significant differences in motility or morphology, focusing on acute post-infection effects rather than long COVID sequelae.
paper_authors: Tiinçe Aksak; Deniz A. Satar; Rıdvan Bağci; Efdal O. Gülteki̇n; Arzu Coşkun; Umut Demi̇rdelen
paper_title: Investigation of the effect of COVID‐19 on sperm count, motility, and morphology

summary: A 6-month prospective case-control study of 320 health workers examining the incidence, evolution, and recovery of COVID-related olfactory and gustatory dysfunction. The study found that 64% of COVID cases experienced olfactory dysfunction and 61% experienced gustatory dysfunction, with 89% showing total or partial recovery by 6 months, though 11% showed no recovery.
paper_authors: Juan Riestra-Ayora; Joaquin Yanes-Diaz; Jonathan Esteban-Sanchez; Cristina Vaduva; Cristina Molina-Quiros; Alba Larran-Jimenez; Eduardo Martin-Sanz
paper_title: Long-term follow-up of olfactory and gustatory dysfunction in COVID-19: 6 months case–control study of health workers

summary: Case-control study examining the association between previous SARS-CoV-2 infection and new antidepressant prescription in an Italian region from 2020-2022. Finds that COVID-19, especially severe infection, is associated with increased antidepressant treatment, with vaccination appearing protective.
paper_authors: Valentina Rosolen; Luigi Castriotta; Marco Driutti; Umberto Albert; Fabio Barbone; Giulio Castelpietra
paper_title: Association between previous SARs-CoV-2 infection and new prescription of antidepressant drugs: a case-control study in Friuli Venezia Giulia region, Italy
paper_journal: European Archives of Psychiatry and Clinical Neuroscience

summary: A case-control study evaluating serum ferritin as a biomarker in post-COVID telogen effluvium (hair loss), comparing 100 COVID-19 convalescents with controls. The study reports that dietary supplements (vitamin C, D, lactoferrin, zinc) used during acute infection showed preventive value against post-COVID hair loss, while certain medications (azithromycin, ivermectin) were associated with increased telogen effluvium.
paper_authors: Nermeen Ibrahim Bedair; Alaa Safwat Abdelaziz; Fatemaalzahraa Saad Abdelrazik; Mohamed El-kassas; Mohamed Hussein AbouHadeed
paper_title: Post Covid telogen effluvium: the diagnostic value of serum ferritin biomarker and the preventive value of dietary supplements. a case control study

summary: This case-control study compared cognitive function and serum BDNF levels between 54 COVID-19 patients and 36 healthy controls, finding significant cognitive decline and lower BDNF levels in the COVID-19 group. The study is observational/pathophysiological in nature and does not evaluate any treatment intervention for long COVID.
paper_authors: Biçem Demir; Elmas Beyazyüz; Murat Beyazyüz; Aliye Çelikkol; Yakup Albayrak
paper_title: Long-lasting cognitive effects of COVID-19: is there a role of BDNF?
paper_journal: European Archives of Psychiatry and Clinical Neuroscience

summary: Case-control study investigating autonomic nervous system dysfunction in long COVID patients compared to healthy controls using sympathetic skin response and vagus nerve ultrasound measurements. Found differences in ANS function between long COVID patients and controls, suggesting ANS maladaptation as a potential pathogenic mechanism.
paper_authors: Marianna Papadopoulou; Eleni Bakola; Apostolos Papapostolou; Maria-Ioanna Stefanou; Mina Gaga; Vasiliki Zouvelou; Ioannis Michopoulos; Georgios Tsivgoulis
paper_title: Autonomic dysfunction in long-COVID syndrome: a neurophysiological and neurosonology study

summary: This case-control study compared autonomic cardiac function in 56 pediatric long COVID patients versus 27 healthy controls using ECG, Holter monitoring, and echocardiography. The study found significant abnormalities in heart rate variability parameters in long COVID patients, suggesting an imbalance toward parasympathetic predominance, but no significant structural cardiac differences.
paper_authors: Delogu AB; Aliberti C.; Birritella L.; De Rosa G.; De Rose C.; Morello R.; Cambise N.; Marino AG; Belmusto A.; Tinti L.; Di Renzo A.; Lanza GA; Buonsenso D.
paper_title: Autonomic cardiac function in children and adolescents with long COVID: a case-controlled study

summary: Case-control study comparing nasal cytological alterations in 36 patients with persistent post-viral olfactory dysfunction versus two control groups (recovered from COVID-19 without olfactory loss, and non-COVID controls). Found increased lymphocytes, neutrophils, and ciliocytophthoria in olfactory dysfunction patients, indicating chronic local inflammation in the olfactory cleft.
paper_authors: Gianluca Velletrani; Denise Fiorelli; Beatrice Francavilla; Marzia Nuccetelli; Sergio Bernardini; Simonetta Masieri; Stefano Di Girolamo
paper_title: Nasal cytological evidence of chronic inflammation in the olfactory cleft in post-viral olfactory dysfunction

summary: Case-control study comparing headache prevalence and severity in 188 post-COVID patients versus 27 controls with prior COVID or other infectious disease history. Found significantly higher headache prevalence, worse quality of life, and higher depression/fatigue in PCC patients, emphasizing the need for multi-professional symptom assessment.
paper_authors: Mike Rueb; Michael Ruzicka; Gerardo Jesus Ibarra Fonseca; Elisabeth Valdinoci; Christopher Benesch; Anna Pernpruner; Max von Baum; Jan Remi; Tarek Jebrini; Florian Schöberl; Andreas Straube; Hans Christian Stubbe; Kristina Adorjan
paper_title: Headache severity in patients with post COVID-19 condition: a case-control study
paper_journal: European Archives of Psychiatry and Clinical Neuroscience

summary: Prospective cross-sectional study comparing qualitative and quantitative smell/taste dysfunction in 17 COVID-19 patients versus 21 healthy controls using standardized testing and questionnaires. Finds persistent qualitative disorders (phantosmia, parosmia, phantogeusia, parageusia) in ~35% of recovering patients, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Tommaso Ercoli; Carla Masala; Ilenia Pinna; Gianni Orofino; Paolo Solla; Lorenzo Rocchi; Giovanni Defazio
paper_title: Qualitative smell/taste disorders as sequelae of acute COVID-19

summary: Case-control study comparing mental health outcomes in 103 children with long COVID versus 113 uninfected controls. Found that long COVID was associated with memory difficulties but not with higher rates of emotional-behavioral problems; parental economic stress and worries were stronger predictors of children's distress than LC diagnosis itself.
paper_authors: Iris Shachar-Lavie; Maayan Shorer; Hila Segal; Silvana Fennig; Liat Ashkenazi-Hoffnung
paper_title: Mental health among children with long COVID during the COVID-19 pandemic

summary: This case-control study assessed olfactory and gustatory function in 93 post-COVID-19 patients compared to matched controls at 1-year and 2-year follow-up using standardized psychophysical testing. While chemosensory dysfunction improved over time, COVID-19 cases still showed significantly higher rates of olfactory dysfunction at 2 years compared to controls.
paper_authors: Paolo Boscolo‐Rizzo; Thomas Hummel; Sara Invitto; Giacomo Spinato; Michele Tomasoni; Enzo Emanuelli; Margherita Tofanelli; Angelo Cavicchia; Vittorio Grill; Luigi Angelo Vaira; Jerome R. Lechien; Daniele Borsetto; Jerry Polesel; Michele Dibattista; Anna Menini; Claire Hopkins; Giancarlo Tirelli
paper_title: Psychophysical assessment of olfactory and gustatory function in post‐mild COVID‐19 patients: A matched case‐control study with 2‐year follow‐up

summary: A case-control study comparing echocardiographic findings in 270 children with PASC and 400 age-matched controls using deep learning to detect cardiac abnormalities. Standard echocardiographic parameters showed no differences, but a ResNet-50 model achieved 96.6% accuracy in distinguishing subtle image-based differences between groups, though clinical significance remains unclear.
paper_authors: Yi-Chin Peng; Yi-Jen Huang; Xiao-Ling Liu; Jacky Chung-Hao Wu; Pang-Yan Liu; Yu-Lung Hsu; Pei-Chi Chen; Lawrence Shih-Hsin Wu; Hui-Ju Tsai; Wei-Wen Chen; Kai-Sheng Hsieh; Henry Horng-Shing Lu; Jiu-Yao Wang
paper_title: Echocardiographic Evaluation in Children with Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Infection Using Deep Learning
paper_journal: Journal of Imaging Informatics in Medicine

summary: Case-control study comparing 88 long COVID patients with 96 controls to identify demographic, laboratory, and genetic factors associated with long COVID syndrome. Found that severe acute COVID-19, elevated BMI, CRP, IL-6, and specific HLA alleles (A*11, C*07) were significantly associated with long COVID development.
paper_authors: Ensiye Torki; Fahimeh Hoseininasab; Marjan Moradi; Ramin Sami; Mark J. M. Sullman; Hamed Fouladseresht
paper_title: The demographic, laboratory and genetic factors associated with long Covid-19 syndrome: a case–control study

summary: Prospective case-control study comparing gene expression levels (ALOX12, ITGA2B, F13A1, PF4) in pregnant women who recovered from COVID-19 versus uninfected controls. Finds significantly elevated expression of three candidate genes in post-COVID-19 survivors, suggesting potential association with placenta-mediated pregnancy complications.
paper_authors: Mai M. Shaker; Asia E. Abdelghany; Nesma M. Elaraby
paper_title: Expression Levels of PF4, ALOX12, ITGA2B, F131A in Pregnant COVID-19 Survivors

summary: This case-control study compared pulmonary function, respiratory endurance, and cardiovascular responses between 45 COVID-19 convalescent patients and 45 healthy controls. COVID-19 convalescent patients showed significant declines in multiple pulmonary function measures (FVC, FEV1, FEF metrics) and increased lung age, indicating long-term respiratory impacts of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
paper_authors: Manohara H. G.; Megha Bhat Agni; Damodara Gowda K. M.
paper_title: Long-term health consequences of COVID-19 in young adults: a focus on respiratory and cardiovascular endurance

summary: This case-control study examines hearing loss patterns in acute COVID-19 infected adults and children born to COVID-19 infected mothers. The paper focuses on acute infection effects (transient hearing loss detected at day 7), not long COVID or any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Balaji Swaminathan; Jhansirani Vidyasagar; Shanmugam Vellavedu Umapathy; Ruta Shanmugam; Prakash Paramasivam Gunasekaran; Lavanya Varadhan Mani; Sangeetha Murugan
paper_title: Impact on Hearing Among SARS COV-2 Infected Adults and Children Born to Gestational COVID-19 Infected Mothers: A Prospective Case Control Study
paper_journal: Indian Journal of Otolaryngology and Head & Neck Surgery

summary: A pilot case-control study investigating blood-brain barrier permeability in 14 long COVID patients with cognitive complaints compared to 10 controls using SPECT imaging and cognitive testing. Found no significant differences in blood-brain barrier permeability or cognitive function between groups, suggesting disruption of the blood-brain barrier is unlikely the primary mechanism of COVID-related brain fog.
paper_authors: Aditi Gupta; Branden Comfort; Kate Young; Robert Montgomery
paper_title: A pilot study to assess blood-brain barrier permeability in long COVID

summary: A retrospective case-control study comparing serum serotonin levels between 34 PASC patients and 14 healthy controls. The study found no significant differences in serotonin levels and concluded that peripheral serotonin is not a reliable biomarker for PASC.
paper_authors: Philipp Mathé; Veronika Götz; Katarina Stete; Dietrich Walzer; Hanna Hilger; Stefanie Pfau; Maike Hofmann; Siegbert Rieg; Winfried V. Kern
paper_title: No reduced serum serotonin levels in patients with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19

summary: Case-control study comparing 174 COVID-19 patients at 6-month follow-up with 75 matched controls to assess persistent symptoms, quality of life, and markers of inflammation and cardiac injury. Found persistent shortness of breath, fatigue, and elevated inflammatory markers in post-COVID patients, but this is an observational study without any intervention or treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Rachel-Anne Xuereb; Marica Borg; Kevin Vella; Alex Gatt; Robert G. Xuereb; Christopher Barbara; Stephen Fava; Caroline J. Magri
paper_title: Long COVID Syndrome: A Case-Control Study

summary: This case-control study compares postural sway and physical capacity between people with long COVID (~16 months duration), ME/CFS (~16 years duration), and age-matched healthy controls. Both long COVID and ME/CFS groups showed similarly impaired balance and physical capacity compared to controls, with no significant differences between the two patient groups.
paper_authors: Lawrence D. Hayes; Nilihan E.M. Sanal-Hayes; Marie Mclaughlin; Ethan C.J. Berry; Nicholas F. Sculthorpe
paper_title: People with Long Covid and ME/CFS Exhibit Similarly Impaired Balance and Physical Capacity: A Case-Case-Control Study

summary: This prospective multicenter case-control study evaluated sulodexide treatment in 79 long COVID patients with endothelial dysfunction compared to 131 untreated controls, followed for 21 days. Sulodexide treatment was associated with significant improvements in endothelial function and reduction in long COVID symptoms including chest pain, palpitations, fatigue, and neuro-cognitive difficulties.
paper_authors: S. Charfeddine; H. Ibn Hadjamor; Slim Torjmen; S. Kraïem; Rania Hammami; Amine Bahloul; N. Kallel; N. Moussa; I. Touil; Jihen Jdidi; Salem Abdesselem; Leïla Abid
paper_title: Sulodexide in the treatment of patients with long COVID 19 symptoms and endothelial dysfunction: The results of TUN-EndCOV study

summary: This case-control study compared the prevalence of PTSD and complex PTSD (CPTSD) among 21 individuals with long COVID, 20 with ME/CFS, and 20 healthy controls using the International Trauma Questionnaire. Long COVID participants had significantly higher PTSD and CPTSD prevalence (5% and 33% respectively) compared to ME/CFS and controls, with greater symptom scores across all PTSD and DSO domains.
paper_authors: Nilihan E.M. Sanal-Hayes; Lawrence D. Hayes; Marie Mclaughlin; Ethan C.J. Berry; Nicholas F. Sculthorpe
paper_title: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder and Complex Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder in People with Long COVID, ME/CFS, and Controls

summary: This case-control study compared flow-mediated dilation (endothelial function) in 17 long COVID patients, 17 ME/CFS patients, and 17 healthy controls. Both long COVID and ME/CFS groups showed significantly impaired endothelial function compared to controls, with no difference between the two patient groups.
paper_authors: Marie Mclaughlin; Nilihan E.M. Sanal-Hayes; Lawrence D. Hayes; Ethan C. Berry; Nicholas F. Sculthorpe
paper_title: People with Long COVID and Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome Exhibit Similarly Impaired Vascular Function

summary: This case-control study compares well-being and cognitive function between people with long COVID (~16 months duration), ME/CFS (~16 years duration), and age-matched healthy controls. While both patient groups show similar impairment on well-being measures compared to controls, this is an observational comparison study that does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Nilihan E.M. Sanal-Hayes; Marie Mclaughlin; Lawrence D. Hayes; Ethan C.J. Berry; Nicholas F. Sculthorpe
paper_title: Examining Well-Being and Cognitive Function in People With Long COVID and ME/CFS, and Age-Matched Healthy Controls: A Case-Case-Control Study

summary: Nested case-control study comparing oral microbiota differences between long COVID patients and controls using 16S rRNA sequencing. Identifies distinct microbial dysbiosis and marker bacteria associated with long COVID, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Jianchao Xu; Di Wu; Jie Yang; Yinuo Zhao; Xuzhao Liu; Yingying Chang; Yao Tang; Feng Sun; Yubin Zhao
paper_title: Adult Outpatients with Long COVID Infected with SARS-CoV-2 Omicron Variant. Part 1: Oral Microbiota Alterations

summary: This case-control study compared dexterity and bimanual coordination between people with long COVID (~16 months), ME/CFS (~16 years), and healthy controls using the Purdue pegboard test. The study found that both long COVID and ME/CFS patients showed similarly impaired dexterity and bimanual coordination compared to controls, but did not evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Nilihan E.M. Sanal-Hayes; Lawrence D. Hayes; Marie Mclaughlin; Ethan C.J. Berry; Nicholas F. Sculthorpe
paper_title: People with Long COVID and ME/CFS Exhibit Similarly Impaired Dexterity and Bimanual Coordination: A Case-Case-Control Study

summary: Case-control study comparing 37 post-COVID patients with 30 healthy controls using objective balance assessments (CDP, VEMP, v-HIT). Found significant impairments in balance-related systems in COVID-19 survivors, including decreased visual scores, altered vestibular responses, and persistent dizziness persisting after clinical recovery.
paper_authors: Oğuz Yılmaz; Berna Özge Mutlu; Handan Yaman; Dilara Bayazıt; Hasan Demirhan; Yıldırım Ahmet Bayazıt
paper_title: Assessment of balance after recovery from Covid-19 disease

summary: This case-control study compared 140 long COVID patients with persistent fatigue and post-exertional malaise to 80 recovered controls, finding that EBV reactivation occurred in 28.6% of patients versus 11.3% of controls (p=0.003). The study identifies EBV reactivation as a potential mechanism in long COVID syndrome, though it does not test an intervention.
paper_authors: Eslam Farid Abu Shady; Abdelhakim Fouad Ghallab; Doaa Abdullah Shaker; Rasha Abd Elhamid Elsayed
paper_title: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) reactivation in post COVID-19

summary: Case-control study comparing cognitive functioning between older adults with serologically confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and seronegative controls. Found that infected individuals had significantly lower scores in memory, attention, and executive functions, supporting the 'Cognitive COVID' construct.
paper_authors: Greta Rizzi; Deborah Pacifico; Serena Sabatini; Anna Maria Annoni; Federico Mele; Sandra Jovic; Luca Piccoli; Laurie Corna; Rebecca Amati; William Pertoldi; Maddalena Fiordelli; Federica Sallusto; Emiliano Albanese
paper_title: SARS-CoV-2 infection and cognition in community-dwelling and nursing home residents in southern Switzerland

summary: This case-control study compares post-COVID-19 fatigue prevalence in 52 type 2 diabetes patients who had COVID-19 versus 56 matched controls without COVID-19. Findings show T2D patients post-COVID had significantly higher fatigue scores, increased inflammation markers, and reduced physical activity, but no treatment intervention was tested.
paper_authors: Juhi Mittal; Amerta Ghosh; Surya Prakash Bhatt; Shajith Anoop; Irshad Ahmad Ansari; Anoop Misra
paper_title: High prevalence of post COVID-19 fatigue in patients with type 2 diabetes: A case-control study
paper_journal: Diabetes & Metabolic Syndrome: Clinical Research & Reviews

summary: A case-control study examining the role of galanin system and insulin resistance parameters as diagnostic biomarkers in long COVID patients compared to healthy controls. The study identifies altered biomarkers and develops a neural network model for LC prediction, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Wasim Talib Al Masoodi; Sami Waheed Radhi; Habiba Khdair Abdalsada; Hussein Kadhem Al-Hakeim
paper_title: Role of Galanin system and insulin resistance parameters as predictive tools for diagnosis of Long-COVID patients

summary: Case-control study comparing oral microbiota composition, salivary cytokines, and short-chain fatty acids between long COVID patients and healthy controls. Found no significant differences in microbiota diversity or cytokines, with only weak uncorrected signal for valeric acid; study is mechanistic rather than a treatment intervention trial.
paper_authors: Laura Pérez-Martínez; Lourdes Romero; Esther Palacios; Raquel Barbero; Ana Moreno-Blanco; Rosa del Campo; José Ramón Blanco
paper_title: Oral microbiota in patients with long COVID: A pilot study
paper_journal: Enfermedades infecciosas y microbiologia clinica (English ed.)

summary: This case-control study examines the association between pre-infection BMI and long COVID development in 315 Spanish COVID-19 patients. It finds that overweight/obesity significantly increases the risk of developing long COVID and moderate-to-severe functional limitations, but does not test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: María Gabriela Torres-Romero; Nicolás Escrivá; Elena Barado; Laura Moreno-Galarraga; Alejandro Fernandez-Montero
paper_title: Association of body mass index on long COVID: Predisposing factors, symptom severity, and functional status in a Spanish cohort of COVID-19 patients

summary: Case-control study examining central and peripheral autonomic nervous system dysfunction in post-COVID-19 syndrome patients (n=7) versus matched healthy controls (n=7) using sympathetic skin response and fNIRS imaging. Found prolonged SSR latencies and altered fronto-parietal network connectivity in PCS patients, but this is a mechanistic/biomarker study without any treatment intervention or evaluation.
paper_authors: Jia-Yin Ma; Jia-Jia Wu; Yi Zhu; Mou-Xiong Zheng; Xu-Yun Hua; Jian-Guang Xu
paper_title: Investigating autonomic dysfunction in post-COVID-19 syndrome from skin to brain: A case-control study using EMG-SSR and fNIRS

topics: cardiovascular|autonomic nervous system|breathing exercises|heart rate variability
summary: A case-control study of 126 healthcare workers examining cardiovascular autonomic function in 58 long COVID patients versus 53 never-infected and 14 recovered controls, testing the effect of slow-paced breathing on heart rate variability. Long COVID patients showed reduced resting vascular modulation but improved baroreflex sensitivity during slow-paced breathing, suggesting breathing exercises may help restore vascular reactivity.
paper_authors: Marcella Mauro; Luca Cegolon; Nicoletta Bestiaco; Elisa Zulian; Francesca Larese Filon
paper_title: Heart Rate Variability Modulation Through Slow-Paced Breathing in Health Care Workers with Long COVID: A Case-Control Study

summary: This retrospective case-crossover study analyzes associations between ambient temperature, air pollution, and SARS-CoV-2 infection risk in individuals who later developed post-COVID condition (PCC) versus those who did not. The study identifies cold exposure and air pollution as risk factors for infection severity and PCC development, but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Huyen Nguyen Thi Khanh; Katrien De Troeyer; Pierre Smith; Claire Demoury; Lidia Casas
paper_title: The impact of ambient temperature and air pollution on SARS-CoV2 infection and Post COVID-19 condition in Belgium (2021–2022)

summary: This case-control study examined the association between SARS-CoV-2 infection and low back pain (LBP) in 878 Bangladeshi participants, finding significantly higher LBP prevalence among post-acute COVID-19 patients (24.4% vs 15.7%). The study identified SARS-CoV-2 infection as an independent risk factor for LBP, with moderate COVID-19 symptom severity as a significant predictor among long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Mohammad Ali; Atia Sharmin Bonna; Abu-sufian Sarkar; Md. Ariful Islam; Nur-A-Safrina Rahman
paper_title: SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with low back pain: findings from a community-based case-control study

summary: This nested case-control study examines the burden of post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) in patients with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD), dialysis patients, and kidney transplant recipients. It documents the prevalence and symptom burden of PCC in these high-risk populations but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Bouwmans P.; Malahe SRK; Messchendorp AL; Vart P.; Imhof C.; Sanders JF; Gansevoort RT; de Vries APJ; Abrahams AC; Bemelman FJ; Vervoort JPM; Hilbrands LB; Ten Dam MAGJ; van den Dorpel RMA; Rispens T.; Steenhuis M.; Reinders MEJ; Hemmelder MH
paper_title: Post COVID-19 condition imposes significant burden in patients with advanced chronic kidney disease: A nested case-control study

summary: This cross-sectional case-control study compared exercise capacity in 20 ACS patients with concurrent COVID-19 infection to 20 controls without COVID-19, assessed 6-12 months post-revascularization via cardiopulmonary exercise testing. The COVID-19 group showed significantly reduced oxygen consumption (74% vs 86.7% predicted) and ventilatory inefficiency, with 50% meeting long COVID symptom criteria and demonstrating the most compromised exercise capacity.
paper_authors: Giovanni Provenzale; Lucia Barbieri; Gabriele Tumminello; Stefano Carugo; Marco Guazzi
paper_title: Exercise response in post-acute coronary syndrome patients survived to COVID-19 infection

summary: This prospective case-control study compared cardiac function and long-COVID symptoms in children 1 year post-COVID-19 (n=Group 1) versus healthy controls without SARS-CoV-2 exposure. While conventional echocardiography was normal, Group 1 showed persistent reduction in left ventricular GLS (subclinical myocardial dysfunction) and 23.6% reported long-COVID symptoms (fatigue 16.6%, palpitations 2.0%).
paper_authors: Dareilena Karaviti; Marietta Charakida; Dimitra Dimopoulou; Antonios Marmarinos; Maria Papadaki; Despoina Maritsi; Nikos Spyridis; Margaritis Avgeris; Dimitrios Gourgiotis; Aggeliki Syggelou; Maria Tsolia
paper_title: Long term cardiovascular effects on COVID-19 infection in children. The need for monitoring

summary: A matched case-control study examining prevalence and risk factors for post-COVID-19 condition in Japanese children aged 5-17 years. The study found that SARS-CoV-2 infected children had significantly higher odds of persistent symptoms than uninfected controls, with older age, low household income, and pre-existing conditions increasing risk, while vaccination reduced risk.
paper_authors: Mariko Hosozawa; Miyuki Hori; Mina Hayama-Terada; Iba Arisa; Yoko Muto; Akihiko Kitamura; Yoshihiro Takayama; Hiroyasu Iso
paper_title: Prevalence and risk factors of post-coronavirus disease 2019 condition among children and adolescents in Japan: A matched case-control study in the general population

summary: Case-control study investigating complement system activation in post-COVID-19 condition by comparing protein levels (C3, C4, C5, C7) and hemolytic activity between 57 long COVID survivors and 27 matched controls. Found no overall complement pathway differences between groups, though specific complement proteins were lower in patients with post-COVID fatigue or dyspnea.
paper_authors: César Fernández-de-las-Peñas; Maria Ruiz-Ruigómez; Laura Esparcia-Pinedo; Beatriz Colom-Fernández; Fernando Cava-Valenciano; Juan Torres-Macho; Estibaliz Arrieta-Ortubay; Míriam Akasbi-Moltalvo; Carlos Lumbreras-Bermejo; Lars Arendt-Nielsen; Anabel Franco-Moreno
paper_title: Classic pathway persistent complement activation is associated with specific symptoms in individuals with post–COVID-19 condition: A case-control study

summary: Retrospective case-control study analyzing 1,086 long COVID patients and matched controls from a US health system to identify risk factors for developing long COVID. Findings show chronic pulmonary disease, migraine, and fibromyalgia as significant risk factors, with severe acute infection markers associated with long COVID development.
paper_authors: Ghosh P.; Niesen MJM; Pawlowski C.; Bandi H.; Yoo U.; Lenehan PJ; Kumar-M P.; Nadig M.; Ross J.; Ardhanari S.; O'Horo JC; Venkatakrishnan AJ; Rosen CJ; Telenti A.; Hurt RT; Soundararajan V.
paper_title: Case-control study on post-COVID-19 conditions reveals severe acute infection and chronic pulmonary disease as potential risk factors

summary: This retrospective cohort and case-control study using Japanese health insurance data examined risk factors for COVID-19 infection and post-infection sequelae in patients aged ≥60 years hospitalized by December 2020. The study identified mental/behavioral disorders and pulmonary conditions as major risk factors for developing sequelae, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Takuya Uematsu; Shuko Nojiri; Masashi Nagao; Muneaki Ishijima; Yuji Nishizaki
paper_title: Comprehensive analysis of risk factors for coronavirus disease 2019 infection and post-infection sequelae based on real-world data from a health insurance database in Japan

summary: This case-control study compared 31 long COVID patients with 27 healthy controls using oxygenation-sensitive cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) to assess vascular function during breathing exercises. The study found that long COVID patients had blunted hemodynamic and myocardial oxygenation responses compared to controls, suggesting endothelial dysfunction contributes to long COVID pathophysiology.
paper_authors: Lukas D. Weberling; Elizabeth Hillier; Matthias G. Friedrich; Marc Zahlten; Norbert Frey; Florian André; Henning Steen
paper_title: Abnormal coronary vascular response in patients with long COVID syndrome – a case‐control study using oxygenation‐sensitive cardiovascular magnetic resonance

summary: This case-control study compared 167 biomarkers between long COVID patients and COVID-recovered controls 12-24 months post-infection, identifying a panel of 4 markers (αGAD, IL-10, potassium, CD16brightCD56- cells) that distinguished the two groups with >88% accuracy. The study characterizes the immunological and biochemical profile of post-COVID condition but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Bárbara Oliván-Blázquez; Marta Bona-Otal; Fátima Méndez-López; David Lerma-Irureta; Paula García-Izuel; Jesús Ibáñez-Ruiz; Alberto Montolío; María Ruiz-Herreros; Javier Godino; Beatriz Jimeno-Beltran; María del Mar Encabo-Berzosa; Izaskun Arenaz; Ana Medel-Martínez; Verónica Casado-Vicente; Mayte Coiras; Carlos Tellería-Orriols; Jon Schoorlemmer; Rosa Magallón-Botaya
paper_title: Characterization model of the post COVID-19 condition based on immunological, biochemical, and cytokine markers

summary: This case-control study compared static and dynamic balance and fall risk between 30 individuals with mild to moderate COVID-19 and 30 healthy controls 3-6 months post-infection. Significant differences were found in most balance measures including mCTSIB, Fall Risk Test, and Unipedal Stance Test, demonstrating persistent balance disorders even in mild to moderate COVID-19 cases.
paper_authors: Fatemeh Eskandari; Leila Abbasi; Narges Meftahi
paper_title: Long-term effects of mild and moderate COVID-19 on static and dynamic balance
paper_journal: Journal of Bodywork and Movement Therapies

summary: A nested case-control study of 55 long COVID patients with fatigue who were taking Macaranga sinensis, comparing treatment responders (n=27) to non-responders (n=28) using OLink proteomic analysis. The study identified CX3CL1 as a candidate biomarker for predicting treatment efficacy of the herbal intervention.
paper_authors: Guang Chen; Shichen Zhou; Yuanyuan Chen; Jiayan Zhou; Ning Wang; Yibin Feng
paper_title: OLink proteomic biomarker to predict clinical efficacy of Macaranga sinensis Müll.Arg: A nested case-control study

summary: This case-control study recruited 163 long-COVID patients with new-onset chronic pain and 151 controls to identify factors associated with quality of life. Key findings show that anxiety and symptom complexity negatively impact QoL, while aerobic capacity and employment status positively influence it, though this is an observational characterization study without any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Laura Barrero-Santiago; Pablo Bellosta-López; Víctor Doménech-García; Lucía Pérez-Pérez; Juan J. Tellería; Raquel Almansa; Federico Montero-Cuadrado
paper_title: Determinants of quality of life in long-COVID patients with new-onset chronic pain

summary: This German case-control study compared cognitive performance in 410 adults with post-COVID syndrome, 87 recovered controls, and 64 healthy controls. Adults with PCS showed worse episodic memory and visuospatial abilities but no impairments in executive function or global cognition.
paper_authors: Zülke AE; Luppa M.; Wirkner K.; Reusche M.; Sander C.; Büchner R.; Schomerus G.; Then Bergh F.; Lehmann J.; Witte AV; Villringer A.; Zeynalova S.; Löffler M.; Engel C.; Riedel-Heller SG
paper_title: Cognitive performance in adults with post-COVID syndrome: Results from a German case-control study

summary: This case-control study compared psychosocial dimensions between Italian children with long COVID, children who had COVID-19 without long COVID, and children without prior COVID-19 infection. While it confirms a link between maternal health anxiety and child long COVID, it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Cédric Lemogne; Clément Gouraud; Victor Pitron; Brigitte Ranque
paper_title: Why the hypothesis of psychological mechanisms in long COVID is worth considering

summary: Case-control study evaluating the impact of early post-COVID clinic attendance on downstream healthcare utilization, costs, and mortality in 2,814 matched long COVID patients over 6 months. Early clinic usage was associated with reduced inpatient stays, ED visits, costs, and mortality, with increased outpatient utilization suggesting successful care shift to outpatient settings.
paper_authors: Kirby D. Gong; Ali S. Afshar; Fred Brown; Reza Alavi; Ravindra Ganesh; Hadi Kharrazi
paper_title: Assessing the Impact of Post-COVID Clinics on 6-Month Health Care Utilization for Patients With Long COVID: A Single-Center Experience
paper_journal: Mayo Clinic Proceedings: Innovations, Quality & Outcomes

summary: This case-control pilot study compares growth hormone secretion and metabolic markers between long COVID patients (n=10) with neurologic symptoms and recovered controls (n=13). The study finds reduced GH secretion associated with fatigue and brain fog in PASC patients, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Traver J. Wright; Richard B. Pyles; Melinda Sheffield-Moore; Rachel R. Deer; Kathleen M. Randolph; Kristen A. McGovern; Christopher P. Danesi; Charles R. Gilkison; Weston W. Ward; Jayson A. Vargas; Peyton A. Armstrong; Sarah E. Lindsay; Mohammed F. Zaidan; Justin Seashore; Tamara L. Wexler; Brent E. Masel; Randall J. Urban
paper_title: Low growth hormone secretion associated with post-acute sequelae SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) neurologic symptoms: A case-control pilot study

summary: This cross-sectional case-control study compared psychosocial characteristics of 29 Italian children with long COVID (15% of 198 children exposed to SARS-CoV-2) against two control groups (never infected and COVID-recovered without LCS). The study found that maternal health anxiety and child deprivation were elevated in long COVID cases, predominantly presenting with neurological/neuropsychiatric symptoms, highlighting the need for integrated psychosocial care.
paper_authors: Maria Francesca Freda; Cristiano Scandurra; Ersilia Auriemma; Alfredo Guarino; Daniela Lemmo; Maria Luisa Martino; Francesco Nunziata; Nelson Mauro Maldonato; Grazia Isabella Continisio
paper_title: Long-COVID in children: An exploratory case-control study from a bio-psycho-social perspective

summary: A case-control study comparing tissue oxygenation responses in 30 long COVID patients versus 16 cardiovascular disease patients and 11 healthy controls using near-infrared spectroscopy during an arterial occlusion protocol. Findings show that long COVID patients have altered tissue oxygen consumption rates, with slower desaturation during ischemia and slower reoxygenation after cuff release compared to controls, potentially explaining fatigue and physical impairment symptoms.
paper_authors: Hendrik Schäfer; Marc Teschler; Frank C. Mooren; Boris Schmitz
paper_title: Altered tissue oxygenation in patients with post COVID-19 syndrome

summary: Retrospective case-control study examining the association between COVID vaccinations and antiviral treatments (nirmatrelvir/ritonavir, remdesivir) with long COVID outcomes beyond 6 months in a large US healthcare system. Study found inverse associations between vaccination doses and antiviral treatments with long COVID diagnosis, suggesting protective effects of vaccination and early antiviral therapy.
paper_authors: Curtis Liu; Celina Liu; Rui Yan; Davida Becker; Jia Xiao Shi; Jeffrey Slezak; Diane Jerng
paper_title: Association of COVID vaccinations and treatments with long COVID beyond 6 months: a case-control study on the adult population in a large integrated healthcare system in the United States from 2020 to 2023

summary: Case-control study comparing cardiopulmonary function, muscle strength, and quality of life in 50 COVID-19 recovered patients (3-6 months post-recovery) versus 50 matched healthy controls. Found significant reductions in the COVID-19 group across all measured domains, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

paper_authors: Elena Enax‐Krumova; Johannes Forsting; Marlena Rohm; Peter Schwenkreis; Martin Tegenthoff; Christine H. Meyer‐Frießem; Lara Schlaffke
paper_title: Quantitative muscle magnetic resonance imaging depicts microstructural abnormalities but no signs of inflammation or dystrophy in post‐<scp>COVID</scp>‐19 condition

summary: This multicentre case-control study compares long COVID symptom prevalence and severity between obese and non-obese hospitalised COVID-19 survivors at 7.2 months post-discharge. Obesity was associated with a greater number of post-COVID symptoms and poor sleep quality, but no significant differences in individual symptom prevalence were found.
paper_authors: César Fernández‐de‐las‐Peñas; Juan Torres‐Macho; Carlos M. Elvira‐Martínez; Luis J. Molina‐Trigueros; Tomas Sebastián‐Viana; Valentín Hernández‐Barrera
paper_title: Obesity is associated with a greater number of long‐term post‐COVID symptoms and poor sleep quality: A multicentre case‐control study

summary: A case-control study evaluating intravenous immunoglobulins (IVIg) as an immunomodulatory treatment for severe post-COVID syndrome in patients unresponsive to supportive care. The study compares outcomes between post-COVID patients treated with IVIg and appropriate controls, testing whether autoimmune mechanisms can be therapeutically targeted.
paper_authors: Maximilian Hogeweg; Adrian Doevelaar; Sonja Rieckmann; Felix Seibert; David Scholten; Monika Segelmacher; Ulrik Stervbo; Nina Babel; Timm H. Westhoff
paper_title: Intravenous immunoglobulins in the treatment of post‐COVID: A case–control study

summary: This case-control study prospectively compared 280 COVID-19 patients with 264 healthy controls to assess the development of post-infection functional gastrointestinal disorders at 1, 3, and 6 months follow-up. The study found significantly higher rates of IBS, uninvestigated dyspepsia, and chronic bowel dysfunction in COVID-19 patients compared to controls, but it is an observational study documenting disease outcomes rather than evaluating any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Ghoshal UC; Ghoshal U.; Rahman MM; Mathur A.; Rai S.; Akhter M.; Mostafa T.; Islam MS; Haque SA; Pandey A.; Kibria MG; Ahmed F.
paper_title: Post‐infection functional gastrointestinal disorders following coronavirus disease‐19: A case–control study

summary: This case-control study compares coronary microvascular function between patients with chest pain 30-60 days post-COVID-19 and controls without COVID history, measuring angio-derived microcirculatory resistance via angiography. Patients with prior COVID-19 showed significantly elevated microcirculatory resistance, suggesting coronary microvascular dysfunction may contribute to post-COVID chest pain.
paper_authors: Lei Dong; Ritai Na; Lang Peng; Xinye Xu
paper_title: Increased Angio‐Derived Index of Microcirculatory Resistance Within a Timeframe of 30–60 days After COVID‐19 Infection

summary: This case-control study compared objective and subjective olfactory and gustatory function in 42 post-COVID-19 patients versus 41 matched controls with no COVID history. While it documents significant dysfunction in taste and smell (hyposmia in 73.8% of post-COVID patients), it is a descriptive cross-sectional assessment study, not a treatment/intervention trial, and therefore does not meet criteria for inclusion.
paper_authors: Dror Livni; Osnat Grinstein‐Koren; Ayelet Zlotogorski‐Hurvitz; Shoshana Reiter; Orit Winocour‐Arias; Jeremy Edel; Yuli Goldman; Marilena Vered; Guy Choshen; Daniella Rahamim‐Cohen; Shirley Shapiro‐Ben David; Ilana Kaplan
paper_title: The effect of post‐COVID‐19 on gustatory and olfactory function: A preliminary case‐controlled study

summary: A case-control study comparing serum mast cell activation markers (TPSB2 and CPA3) between 24 long-COVID patients and 24 matched healthy controls with prior COVID-19 infection. The study found no significant differences in mast cell markers between groups and no correlation with exercise intolerance, concluding mast cell activation is not a key pathogenic mechanism in long-COVID.
paper_authors: Ole Bernt Lenning; Grete Jonsson; Tore Grimstad; Emiel A. M. Janssen; Geir Sverre Braut; Frode Berven; Roald Omdal
paper_title: No signs of mast cell involvement in long‐COVID: A case–control study

summary: This case-control study examines asthma control, mental health, and exhaled nitric oxide levels in asthmatic children 1 month after COVID-19 infection. While it measures outcomes post-infection, it does not study long COVID (persistent sequelae weeks-to-months later) or any treatment intervention—it is a cross-sectional assessment of correlations between asthma control and anxiety/depression in the acute post-infection period.
paper_authors: Tung‐Ming Chang; Yun Chen; Kuender D. Yang; Jiu‐Yao Wang; Ching‐Yuang Lin; Yu‐Jun Chang; Chang‐Hua Chen; Yi‐Giien Tsai
paper_title: Asthma control associated with anxiety and depression in asthmatic children following post‐acute COVID‐19

summary: This case-control study compares long COVID incidence and clinical features in rheumatoid arthritis and psoriatic arthritis patients versus healthy controls at 12 weeks post-infection. It documents higher symptom burden and disease activity worsening in rheumatic disease patients, particularly females, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Mario Ferraioli; Loredana De Marco; L. Fiannacca; M. Iacovantuono; B. Monosi; Paola Triggianese; Paola Conigliaro; Alberto Bergamini; Maria Sole Chimenti
paper_title: POS0556 LONG COVID IN RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS AND IN PSORIATIC ARTHRITIS: CLINICAL PATTERN AND GENDER-BASED DIFFERENCES FROM A SINGLE-CENTRE CASE-CONTROL STUDY

summary: A case-control study comparing 352 long COVID patients with 1,464 non-long-COVID controls from a retrospective online survey to identify whether joint hypermobility is a risk factor for long COVID. Found that both generalized joint hypermobility and extreme hypermobility significantly predict long COVID risk, operating through increased severity of initial COVID-19 symptoms and direct pathophysiological pathways.
paper_authors: Regina A. Torok; Jeffrey Lubell; Rena M. Rudy; Jessica Eccles; Lisa Quadt
paper_title: Variant connective tissue as a risk factor for long COVID: a case-control study of data from a retrospective online survey of adults in the USA and UK

summary: This case-control study from the British COVID Symptom Study Biobank examines whether joint hypermobility is a risk factor for non-recovery from COVID-19 in 3,064 participants surveyed in August 2022. While it finds a significant association between hypermobility and self-reported non-recovery (OR 1.33), this is an observational analysis of biobank data without any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the clinical trials pipeline.
paper_authors: Jessica A. Eccles; Dorina Cadar; Lisa Quadt; Alan J. Hakim; Nicholas Gall; Vicky Bowyer; Nathan Cheetham; Claire J. Steves; Hugo D. Critchley; Kevin A. Davies
paper_title: Is joint hypermobility linked to self-reported non-recovery from COVID-19? Case–control evidence from the British COVID Symptom Study Biobank

summary: Retrospective case-control study comparing post-COVID symptoms in IBD patients versus infected household members without IBD and IBD patients without infection. Study is observational/descriptive with no treatment intervention—it characterizes disease prevalence and associations rather than testing a therapeutic intervention.
paper_authors: Benedikt Bierbaum; Ulrike von Arnim; Renate Schmelz; Rosa Rosania; Jens Walldorf; Michael Bierbaum; Sven Geißler; Markus Hänßchen; Andreas Stallmach; Philipp Reuken; Niels Teich
paper_title: Long-Term Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Infection in Patients with Inflammatory Bowel Diseases Compared to Relatives with SARS-CoV-2 Infection without Inflammatory Bowel Disease and Inflammatory Bowel Disease Patients without SARS-CoV-2: Results of a Retrospective Case-Control Study

summary: Retrospective case-control study comparing luminal areas of large conducting airways between PASC patients, acute COVID-19 patients, and healthy controls using 3D CT reconstruction. Found PASC and COVID-19 patients have significantly enlarged airways compared to controls, but no differences between PASC and acute COVID groups.
paper_authors: Solomiia Zaremba; Alex J. Miller; Erik A. Ovrom; Jonathon W. Senefeld; Chad C. Wiggins; Paolo B. Dominelli; Ravindra Ganesh; Ryan T. Hurt; Brian J. Bartholmai; Brian T. Welch; Juan G. Ripoll; Michael J. Joyner; Andrew H. Ramsook
paper_title: Increased luminal area of large conducting airways in patients with COVID-19 and post-acute sequelae of COVID-19: a retrospective case-control study

summary: This case-control study compares cardiac autonomic function in 14 long-COVID POTS patients versus 15 healthy controls, measuring heart rate variability and hemodynamic responses to head-up tilt. Findings show long-COVID POTS patients have impaired parasympathetic (vagal) modulation with reduced high-frequency heart rate variability, suggesting parasympathetic dysfunction contributes to disease pathophysiology.
paper_authors: Stefano Rigo; Vasile Urechie; Andre Diedrich; Luis E. Okamoto; Italo Biaggioni; Cyndya A. Shibao
paper_title: Abstract 022: Impaired Parasympathetic Cardiac Modulation In Long-COVID Postural Tachycardia Syndrome

summary: This pilot case-control study compared 15 athletes with cardiovascular post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (CV-PASC) to 7 control athletes without prior COVID-19 using stress cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. CV-PASC athletes showed reduced coronary flow reserve and impaired myocardial strain, suggesting coronary microvascular dysfunction related to endothelial injury as a mechanism underlying cardiovascular symptoms in long COVID.
paper_authors: Daniel E. Clark; Sean G. Hughes; Jeffrey M. M. Dendy; Kimberly Crum; Debra Dixon; Kristen George-Durrett; Justin M. Gregory; Neil J. Phillips; Elliot J. Stein; Lena E. Tran; Jean W. Wassenaar; Eric D. Austin; Jonathan Soslow
paper_title: Abstract 12603: Impaired Coronary Flow Reserve in Athletes With Long-Term Cardiovascular Symptoms After COVID-19

summary: Case-control study comparing 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure profiles in 100 post-COVID POTS patients versus 100 population-based controls. Finds that post-COVID POTS patients show higher mean systolic BP and disrupted circadian BP rhythm, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Madeleine Johansson; Marcus Ståhlberg; Fabrizio Ricci; Christian Lewinter; Viktor Hamrefors; Peter M. Nilsson; Richard Sutton; Artur Fedorowski
paper_title: Blood Pressure Regulation in Post–COVID POTS: Beyond Sinus Tachycardia

summary: This case-control study compares blood pressure regulation in 100 COVID-19 patients with new-onset POTS to 100 healthy controls using 24-hour ambulatory monitoring. Post-COVID POTS patients showed significantly higher nighttime systolic BP, more daytime hypotensive episodes, and disrupted BP regulation patterns (non-dipper and reverse-dipper), suggesting altered hemodynamic mechanisms beyond sinus tachycardia.
paper_authors: Madeleine Johansson; Marcus Stahlberg; Fabrizio Ricci; Christian Lewinter; Viktor Hamrefors; Peter Nilsson; Richard Sutton; Artur Fedorowski
paper_title: Abstract 4125636: Impaired blood pressure regulation in post-COVID-19 postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome: novel disease mechanisms beyond sinus tachycardia

summary: Case-control study nested within a cohort examining the association between pro-inflammatory cytokines during acute COVID-19 infection and subsequent major depressive disorder, treatment-resistant depression, and suicidal ideation in long COVID patients. The study identifies elevated cytokine levels as a risk factor for psychiatric outcomes in long COVID but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Major Depressive Disorder in Long COVID and Exposure to Pro‐Inflammatory Cytokines During Infection by SARS‐CoV‐2

summary: This case-control study compares functional autoantibody levels in 4 PASC patients with POTS versus 4 age/gender-matched healthy controls. The study demonstrates elevated autoantibodies to G-protein coupled receptors in POTS patients but is a secondary analysis of previously identified subjects and is too small for statistical testing.
paper_authors: Sameer M. Jamal; William T. Gunning; John W. Spatafore; Zoltan Turi; David Landers; Steven Hollenberg; Taya Glotzer; Jana Tancredi; Blair P. Grubb; Joseph E. Parrillo
paper_title: Abstract 16323: Functional Autoantibody Analysis in Post-Acute Sequela of COVID-19 Patients With and Without Pots: A Case Control Study

summary: A prospective case-control study comparing long COVID patients with fatigue to COVID-19 recovered controls without fatigue, measuring fatigue severity, sleep, cognition, mood, and inflammatory markers at baseline and 6 months. Physical fatigue improved over time but psychological fatigue persisted, with significant differences in sleep quality, cognitive impairment, anxiety, and TNF-α levels between groups.
paper_authors: Gómez-Eguílaz M.; López-Alava S.; Ramón-Trapero JL; Castillo-Álvarez F.; Gómez Loizaga N.; García-Penco C.; Boukichou-Abdelkader N.; Pérez-Martínez L.
paper_title: Focusing on post-COVID syndrome fatigue

summary: A case-control study comparing oculomotor behavior in 75 long COVID patients versus 42 healthy controls using eye-tracking and reading tests. Long COVID patients showed significantly impaired eye movement performance, suggesting cognitive rather than muscular dysfunction, but this is a diagnostic/observational study with no treatment intervention.
paper_authors: González-Vides L.; Hernández-Verdejo JL; Gómez-Pedrero JA; Ruiz-Pomeda A.; Cañadas-Suárez P.
paper_title: Oculomotor Behaviour in Individuals with Long COVID-19

summary: This case-control study compared the prevalence of PTSD and Complex PTSD (CPTSD) in individuals with long COVID (n=21) and ME/CFS (n=20) versus healthy controls (n=20) using the International Trauma Questionnaire. Long COVID patients showed significantly higher rates of PTSD (5%) and CPTSD (33%) compared to ME/CFS and controls, with greater symptom scores across all PTSD and DSO (Disturbances in Self-Organization) domains.
paper_authors: Vicky McQuillan
paper_title: Book Review: Social Participation in Occupational Contexts, in Schools, Clinics and Communities

summary: Case-control study of 205 hospitalized COVID-19 patients with acute headache versus 410 without acute headache, followed 7.3 months post-discharge. Found that acute-phase headache was associated with higher prevalence of long-term post-COVID headache and fatigue, but the study is observational without any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: César Fernández-de-las-Peñas; Víctor Gómez-Mayordomo; María L. Cuadrado; Domingo Palacios-Ceña; Lidiane L. Florencio; Angel L. Guerrero; David García-Azorín; Valentín Hernández-Barrera; Lars Arendt-Nielsen
paper_title: The presence of headache at onset in SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with long-term post-COVID headache and fatigue: A case-control study

summary: Case-control study comparing long COVID incidence in SLE patients versus healthy matched controls after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Found higher long COVID prevalence in SLE patients (54.5% vs 34.6%) with certain symptoms more common, but this is an epidemiological comparison study, not a treatment intervention trial.
paper_authors: Chris Ching Lam Cheung; Chi Chiu Mok
paper_title: Long COVID in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus: A case-control study

summary: This case-control study compares blood biomarkers of vascular transformation between long COVID patients and controls to identify diagnostic signatures. While it identifies elevated angiogenesis markers, it is a diagnostic/mechanistic study without testing any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Elevated vascular transformation blood biomarkers in Long-COVID indicate angiogenesis as a key pathophysiological mechanism

summary: Retrospective case-control study examining uveitis relapse rates in patients with versus without COVID-19 infection in China during late 2022-early 2023. Finds COVID-19 increases relapse risk, but focuses on pre-existing uveitis complications rather than long COVID syndrome or post-acute sequelae.
paper_authors: Kaixuan Wang; Jiawen Li; Kailei Guo; Xiaomin Zhang
paper_title: New-onset or relapse of uveitis after rapid spreading of COVID-19 infection in China and risk factor analysis for relapse

summary: Case-control study comparing post-COVID-19 neuropsychiatric symptoms in 204 migraine patients versus 204 non-migraine controls 3 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Migraine patients showed significantly higher rates of fatigue, anosmia, depression, anxiety, insomnia, and chronic headache transformation, but no treatment intervention was tested.

paper_title: Post-COVID-19 neuropsychiatric manifestations among COVID-19 survivors suffering from migraine: a case–control study

summary: This case-control study compared the prevalence of musculoskeletal health complaints (MHC) between post-acute COVID-19 patients and matched controls who never tested positive, conducted in Bangladesh in 2022. While it found a robust association between SARS-CoV-2 infection and MHC, it is a purely observational epidemiological study with no intervention or treatment evaluation and thus does not qualify as a treatment trial.

paper_title: Is Coronavirus Infection Associated With Musculoskeletal Health Complaints? Results From a Comprehensive Case-Control Study

summary: This case-control study compares macular thickness between post-COVID-19 patients and healthy controls using optical coherence tomography. While it found subtle retinal thinning in older post-COVID patients, it is not a treatment/intervention trial and does not qualify as a long COVID study (no documentation of persistent symptoms weeks/months post-infection, measuring structural changes in acute/early post-infection phase).

summary: This retrospective case-control study from N3C identifies risk factors associated with PASC/long-COVID diagnosis by comparing 8,325 cases to 41,625 matched controls across US health systems. summary: This case-control study uses machine learning on Swedish primary care data to identify diagnostic predictors of PASC, including prior COVID-19 hospitalization, fatigue, and post-viral syndromes. summary: Prospective case-control study comparing cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging and spectroscopy findings in 20 long COVID patients versus 10 healthy controls. Six patients with persistent dyspnea on exertion showed impaired diaphragm function and voluntary activation, suggesting diaphragm dysfunction may contribute to post-COVID exertional dyspnea.

paper_title: Diaphragm dysfunction as a potential determinant of dyspnea on exertion in patients 1 year after COVID-19-related ARDS

summary: Case-control study comparing prevalence of depression, anxiety, fatigue, and headache in 5,589 long COVID patients versus 47,561 matched controls from Stockholm regional health records. Findings show long COVID patients had higher pre-pandemic and post-diagnosis frequencies of these conditions, suggesting an association between mental health vulnerabilities and long COVID.

The study found cardiovascular pathology in 12% of symptomatic soldiers and CV PASC in 37% at follow-up, but does not test any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance evaluation of soldiers after recovery from symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection: a case–control study of cardiovascular post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (CV PASC)

Follow-up over 12 months found progressive radiological improvement but persistent fibrotic-like changes in 57% of OP patients, with higher corticosteroid doses not associated with better long-term prognosis.

Post-COVID patients showed significantly impaired auditory cognitive function and prolonged P300 latency, but the study does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Fatigue was moderately correlated with depression but not airway obstruction, suggesting distinct mechanistic pathways.

The study found that long-COVID POTS patients had impaired parasympathetic function (reduced RMSSD and high-frequency heart rate variability) but normal sympathetic function, suggesting parasympathetic dysfunction may contribute to long-COVID POTS pathogenesis.

paper_title: Impaired parasympathetic function in long-COVID postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome – a case-control study

summary: Longitudinal case-control study comparing cognitive performance and mental health in 50 post-COVID-19 patients and 48 matched healthy controls over 10 months, starting 2 years post-infection. Patients showed initial cognitive deficits but improved over time, though fatigue and mental health issues persisted.

summary: Retrospective case-control study comparing vitamin D levels between 50 long COVID patients and 50 matched controls at 6 months post-hospitalization. Found significantly lower vitamin D levels in long COVID patients (20.1 vs 23.2 ng/mL), particularly in those with neurocognitive symptoms, with vitamin D deficiency independently associated with long COVID diagnosis.

Found increased saccade velocity and smooth pursuit phase shift in post-COVID group, with BPPV diagnosed in 20% of cases, suggesting COVID-19 affects the vestibular system.
paper_authors: Mirhan Eldeeb; Mohamed Talaat; Nada Mokhtar; Ahmed Abdelhady; Doaa Elmoazen
paper_title: The hidden impact of COVID-19 on balance: a VNG evaluation

Patients showed comparable early learning but significantly reduced overnight consolidation and slower initial performance, suggesting deficits in procedural memory formation and executive function.

Found significantly higher prevalence of obstructive sleep apnea (97.4% vs 72.5%), worse sleep quality, and greater daytime sleepiness in COVID-19 cases, though AHI differences were not significant after adjusting for age and BMI.

paper_title: The Role of Acetyl-Carnitine and Rehabilitation in the Management of Patients with Post-COVID Syndrome: Case-Control Study

summary: Case-control study comparing endothelial function (flow-mediated dilation) in 133 convalescent COVID-19 patients versus 133 matched controls. paper_title: Persistent Endothelial Dysfunction in Post-Acute COVID-19 Syndrome: A Case-Control Study

summary: A case-control study comparing symptom prevalence between COVID-19-infected and non-infected individuals in Brazil, analyzing 2,886 participants from October 2023 to May 2024. The study found that long COVID significantly impacts cognitive health with memory problems, fatigue, and shortness of breath being most prevalent, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

paper_title: Enhanced External Counterpulsation Improves Dyspnea, Fatigue, and Functional Capacity in Patients with Long COVID

summary: This case-control study assessed functional capacity and cardiopulmonary function in 34 individuals with persistent symptoms 17 months after severe COVID-19 infection using 6-minute walk testing, spirometry, and quality of life measures. paper_title: Functional Capacity Impairment in Long COVID After 17 Months of Severe Acute Disease
paper_journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health

summary: This retrospective case-control study of 1.3 million patients examined anxiety diagnosis incidence up to four years post-SARS-CoV-2 infection, comparing COVID-19 patients to non-COVID-19 controls. paper_title: Incidence of Anxiety Diagnosis up to Four Years Post SARS-CoV-2 Infection in the Montefiore Medical Center in the Bronx and New York

summary: Case-control study comparing 14 long-haul COVID patients with 14 ME/CFS patients (post-EBV and insidious-onset) using tilt testing and Doppler measurements to assess orthostatic intolerance and cerebral blood flow. Found higher POTS prevalence in long-COVID (100%) versus post-EBV (43%) and insidious-onset (50%) groups, but comparable OI symptomatology and objective abnormalities between groups.

summary: A case-control study comparing serum Pentraxin 3 (PTX3) levels and inflammatory markers in 40 previously COVID-19-infected healthcare workers versus 40 never-infected controls. paper_title: Serum Pentraxin 3 as Promising Biomarker for the Long-Lasting Inflammatory Response of COVID-19

summary: Case-control study comparing behavioral and sleep disorders in 107 children/adolescents 1 month to 1 year post-COVID-19 versus pre-pandemic controls. Found significant differences in sleep-related issues and internalizing problems (anxiety/depression) in the post-COVID group, with adolescents most affected.

paper_title: Behavioral and Sleep Disorders in Children and Adolescents following COVID-19 Disease: A Case-Control Study

summary: This nested case-control study investigates circulating noncoding RNA expression in 98 long COVID patients 18 months post-hospitalization, comparing symptomatic and asymptomatic individuals. paper_title: LEF1-AS1 Deregulation in the Peripheral Blood of Patients with Persistent Post-COVID Symptoms

summary: This case-control study investigates circulating autoantibodies against G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) in 11 severe long COVID patients versus 4 asymptomatic post-COVID controls. paper_title: Prevalence of Circulating Autoantibodies Against G-Protein-Coupled Receptors as Potential Biomarkers for Long COVID: Preliminary Investigations

paper_journal: Vestnik nevrologii, psihiatrii i nejrohirurgii (Bulletin of Neurology, Psychiatry and Neurosurgery)

summary: This paper characterizes post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) using electronic health record data from 63,675 COVID-19 survivors and develops risk prediction models to identify patients at high risk for PASC. summary: Case-control study of 10,426 Chinese adults examining factors associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection incidence, symptom persistence, and severity during the Omicron wave. paper_title: Are there any abnormalities in lipid profile of post-COVID patients: A case–control study?

paper_title: Determinants of post discharge mortality among hospitalized COVID-19 patients

summary: This case-control study assessed retinal and choroidal changes in COVID-19 recovered patients using optical coherence tomography angiography, comparing 180 recovered patients to healthy controls three months post-infection. paper_title: Optical coherence tomography-based assessment of macular vessel density, retinal layer metrics and sub-foveal choroidal thickness in COVID-19 recovered patients

summary: This case–control study compared hematological and biochemical parameters in 300 middle-aged individuals 10 months after mild COVID-19, stratifying them into long COVID and control groups. summary: This case-control study investigates the association between fear, loneliness, and mental health outcomes (anxiety, depression, PTSD) in long COVID patients compared to a control group. paper_title: Long COVID: Association of fear and loneliness with anxiety, depression, and post-traumatic stress disorder: A case-control study

paper_title: incidence of myocarditis and pericarditis in post COVID-19 unvaccinated patients

summary: Case-control study comparing semen parameters between 53 recovered COVID-19 patients and 457 healthy controls at an average of 157 days post-infection. Found no statistically significant differences in sperm motility, morphology, or concentration between groups.

paper_title: Analysis of Semen Parameters of Recovered Patients after COVID-19

paper_title: Arterial stiffness and vascular ageing in COVID-19 recovered young patients – A comparative study
