paper_authors: Thitiya Lukkunaprasit; Patompong Satapornpong; Pongsiri Kulchanawichien; Abhisit Prawang; Chaiwat Limprasert; Worawan Saingam; Chatpetch Permsombut; Wongvarit Panidthananon; Arthimond Vutthipong; Yupin Lawanprasert; Parnthep Pourpongpan; Supakit Wongwiwatthananukit; Thanapat Songsak; Nalinee Pradubyat
paper_title: Impact of combined plant extracts on long COVID: An exploratory randomized controlled trial

summary: A pilot study evaluating Biosound Therapy (multimodal treatment combining biofeedback, vibroacoustic therapy, and binaural beats) in 13 long COVID patients (9 intervention, 4 control) over 4 weeks. Intervention group showed significant improvements in anxiety (GAD-7), depression (PHQ-9), cognitive function, fatigue, and concentration/memory with no reported side effects.
paper_authors: Colleenia Korapatti; Lauren Vera; Keith Miller
paper_title: Biosound Therapy as a treatment for long COVID patients: A pre-post pilot study

summary: Open diagnostic study of 30 long COVID patients assessing airflow limitation via methacholine bronchial provocation test and diurnal FEV1 variability, with 3-week asthma treatment intervention. Treatment normalized mean diurnal FEV1 variability from 18.0% to 7.3% and reduced LC symptom burden.
paper_authors: Tonje Reier-Nilsen; Charlotte Grønneberg; Stephanie Røine; Björn Nordlund
paper_title: Assessment of lung function variability documents airflow limitation in many patients with long covid

summary: This RCT evaluated major ozone autohemotherapy (O3-MAH) combined with conventional therapy versus conventional therapy alone in 73 PASC patients. O3-MAH showed greater efficacy with 71% symptom response versus 45% in controls, along with significant improvements in pulmonary function, exercise capacity, and inflammatory markers.
paper_authors: Yang He; Xu Liu; Shiqian Zha; Yixuan Wang; Jingyi Zhang; Qingfeng Zhang; Ke Hu
paper_title: A pilot randomized controlled trial of major ozone autohemotherapy for patients with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19

summary: A prospective pilot study evaluating three traditional East Asian herbal medicines (Bojungikgi-tang, Kyungok-go, and Cheonwangbosim-dan) for treating fatigue and cognitive dysfunction in 45 long COVID patients over 12 weeks. Herbal treatment showed significant fatigue improvement (46-80% success) but more modest cognitive benefits, with high medication adherence and no serious adverse events.
paper_authors: Tae-Hun Kim; Jiwon Yoon; Sanghyun Kim; Byoung-Kab Kang; Jung Won Kang; Sunoh Kwon
paper_title: Herbal medicines for long COVID: A phase 2 pilot clinical study

summary: A randomized controlled trial investigating donepezil hydrochloride as a treatment for post-COVID memory impairment in 25 patients, with assessments at baseline, 4 weeks, and 12 weeks using the Wechsler Memory Scale-Revised. While no significant overall improvement was observed in memory scales compared to controls, the drug group showed improvements in specific memory subtests (visual reproduction and verbal paired associates).
paper_authors: Parham Pooladgar; Mehdi Sakhabakhsh; Saeed Soleiman-Meigooni; Arsia Taghva; Malihe Nasiri; Ilad Alavi Darazam
paper_title: The effect of donepezil hydrochloride on post-COVID memory impairment: A randomized controlled trial

summary: Baseline analysis of a randomized controlled trial testing acupressure and qigong interventions in 235 post-COVID syndrome patients, characterizing their medication use patterns, symptom burden, and demographic profile. The study documents high prevalence of off-label drug use and complementary medicine adoption among PCS patients seeking relief from persistent fatigue and multi-systemic symptoms.
paper_authors: Theresa Bauer; Weronika Grabowska; Miriam Ortiz; Judith Bellmann-Strobl; Ute Engelhardt; Rainer Nögel; Josef Hummelsberger; Andreas Michalsen; Stephanie Roll; Barbara Stöckigt; Hosnya Batram; Anna Mietzner; Carmen Scheibenbogen; Stefan N. Willich; Friedemann Paul; Benno Brinkhaus; Joanna Dietzel
paper_title: Self-medication and off-label prescribing in post COVID-19 syndrome: Baseline data of a randomized acupressure and qigong trial

summary: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial testing celecoxib monotherapy (100 mg twice daily for 6 weeks) versus placebo in 62 patients with moderate depressive symptoms following COVID-19 infection. Celecoxib showed superior improvement in depression scores with 70% response rate and 67% remission rate compared to 9% and 0% in placebo, with no significant difference in adverse events.
paper_authors: Sahar Ansari; Hossein Sanjari Moghaddam; Fatemeh A. Basti; Mohammadreza Salehi; Shahin Akhondzadeh
paper_title: Efficacy and safety of celecoxib monotherapy for treatment of moderate depressive symptoms following COVID-19 infection: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial

summary: This pilot study evaluated intranasal immunotherapy using M2 macrophage conditioned medium for treating post-COVID hyposmia in 7 patients with persistent olfactory dysfunction (7-24 months post-infection). Treatment was well-tolerated and resulted in significant improvements in olfactory perception, odor recognition, and subjective smell at 6-12 month follow-up, with 5/7 patients reporting high satisfaction.
paper_authors: Shevela EY; Davydova MN; Meledina IV; Bogachev SS; Ostanin AA; Kozlov VA; Chernykh ER
paper_title: Intranasal immunotherapy with M2 macrophage soluble factors in post-COVID hyposmia: A pilot study

summary: Randomized controlled trial comparing nintedanib vs pirfenidone for treating post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis in 30 patients followed for 12 weeks. Both treatments improved pulmonary function and exercise capacity, with nintedanib showing greater benefits for exercise and oxygen saturation but more adverse effects than pirfenidone.
paper_authors: Buğra Kerget; Gizem Çil; Ömer Araz; Fatih Alper; Metin Akgün
paper_title: Comparison of two antifibrotic treatments for lung fibrosis in post-COVID-19 syndrome: A randomized, prospective study

summary: Open-label pilot study of oral minocycline (100 mg daily for 42 days) in 55 ME patients including 19 with long COVID, showing 80% favorable response (≥2 point improvement in functional status) among 51 completers, with 89% response in long COVID subgroup. Early treatment (<6 months disease duration) predicted better outcomes, with significant symptom improvements in fatigue, post-exertional malaise, brain fog, and orthostatic intolerance.
paper_authors: Kunihisa Miwa
paper_title: Oral minocycline therapy as first-line treatment in patients with Myalgic encephalomyelitis and long COVID: A pilot study

summary: This interventional cohort study evaluates Psychophysiologic Symptom Relief Therapy (PSRT), a 13-week virtual therapy program, in 23 adults with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC). PSRT significantly reduced somatic symptom burden and secondary outcomes including dyspnea, fatigue, and pain.
paper_authors: Michael Donnino; Patricia Howard; Shivani Mehta; Jeremy Silverman; Maria J. Cabrera; Jolin B. Yamin; Lakshman Balaji; Katherine M. Berg; Stanley Heydrick; Robert Edwards; Anne V. Grossestreuer
paper_title: Psychophysiologic Symptom Relief Therapy for Post-Acute Sequelae of Coronavirus Disease 2019
paper_journal: Mayo Clinic Proceedings: Innovations, Quality & Outcomes

summary: Open trial evaluating a six-week biofeedback intervention (heart rate variability and temperature biofeedback) in 20 long COVID patients for alleviating mood, somatic, and sleep symptoms. Participants showed significant improvements in somatic, anxiety, and depressive symptoms, sleep quality, and quality of life with moderate-to-large effect sizes, though the lack of control group is a major limitation.
paper_authors: Natacha D. Emerson; Helen Lavretsky; William Q. Pittman; Nisha Viswanathan; Prabha Siddarth
paper_title: An open trial of biofeedback for long COVID

summary: Randomized controlled trial evaluating eight weeks of Pilates Method against supervised physical exercise and control in 59 post-COVID-19 patients. Pilates group showed significant improvements in 6-minute walk distance, post-exercise fatigue, and sleep quality compared to controls.
paper_authors: Matheus Santos Gomes Jorge; Patrik Nepomuceno; Rodolfo Herberto Schneider; Lia Mara Wibelinger
paper_title: Eight weeks of Pilates Method improves physical fitness and sleep quality of individuals with post-COVID-19 syndrome: A randomized clinical trial blinded
paper_journal: Journal of Bodywork and Movement Therapies

summary: Prospective cohort study of COVID-19 mRNA revaccination safety in 103 individuals with prior adverse vaccine reactions and/or long COVID. Revaccination was safe and well tolerated, with mild immediate reactions in 4.9% and common post-vaccination symptoms (fatigue, headache, muscle pain) reported at 7-day follow-up.
paper_authors: Ian F. Slack; Kelly M. O’Shea; George E. Freigeh; Lea M. Franco; Sara Jaafar; Charles F. Schuler; James R. Baker
paper_title: COVID-19 mRNA revaccination is safe and well tolerated in individuals with previous adverse reactions to the vaccine and/or long COVID
paper_journal: Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology: Global

summary: Randomized controlled trial evaluating early physiotherapy and health education in hospitalized COVID-19 patients during acute infection. While the study shows benefits for reducing hospitalization duration and improving physical conditioning during acute illness, it does not study long COVID patients or long-term post-COVID sequelae—it focuses on acute COVID-19 hospital care.
paper_authors: M. S. Domínguez; Beatriz González Vallejo; Raquel Hernández; María Nogueira López; Ana Isabel Montejo García; Mª Eugenia Muñoz Bermejo; Beatriz Kindelan Alonso; I. T. Thuissard Vasallo; Cristina Andreu Vázquez; S. A. Rivera
paper_title: Ensayo clínico aleatorizado en pacientes COVID- 19 sobre el efecto de la fisioterapia precoz en su acondicionamiento físico

summary: A pilot study evaluating the feasibility and effectiveness of a two-week audio-guided and mindfulness-based forest bathing intervention in 36 moderately affected long COVID patients using a repeated-measures pre-post design. Results showed significant improvements in overall long COVID symptoms, fatigue, and well-being, with a 22% dropout rate, suggesting forest bathing may be a feasible complementary treatment approach.
paper_authors: Anna J. Torner; Anika Meißner; Alicia Borchert; Gisela Immich; Kristian Folta-Schoofs
paper_title: Audio-guided and mindfulness-based forest bathing in moderately affected Long/Post-COVID patients: A pre-post pilot-study

summary: This randomized controlled trial evaluated a lifestyle adjustment intervention focused on symptom monitoring and functional improvement in 54 long COVID patients (27 intervention, 27 control). The intervention group showed significant improvements in quality of life, disability (self-care subscale), and functional impairment compared to controls receiving standard care plus informational leaflet.
paper_authors: Navas-Otero A.; Calvache-Mateo A.; Calles-Plata I.; Valenza-Peña G.; Hernández-Hernández S.; Ortiz-Rubio A.; Valenza MC
paper_title: A lifestyle adjustments program in long COVID-19 improves symptomatic severity and quality of life. A randomized control trial

summary: A randomized controlled trial evaluating a 12-week telerehabilitation training program in 182 long COVID participants compared to physical activity counseling alone. The intervention significantly improved walking behavior, total physical activity, exercise self-efficacy, and sleep quality, but did not improve cardiorespiratory fitness or health-related quality of life.
paper_authors: Chia-Ying Lai; Chia-Huei Lin; Ta-Chung Chao; Chueh-Ho Lin; Cheng-Chiang Chang; Chien-Yao Huang; Shang-Lin Chiang
paper_title: Effectiveness of a 12-week telerehabilitation training in people with long COVID: A randomized controlled trial
paper_journal: Annals of Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine

summary: This study evaluates a cognitive rehabilitation program (RehaCom) in acute COVID-19 survivors using a quasi-experimental design with pre-test/post-test and control group. However, the paper focuses on acute COVID-19 patients during active infection, not long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks/months after infection), and therefore does not meet inclusion criteria.
paper_authors: García-Molina A.; Espiña-Bou M.; Rodríguez-Rajo P.; Sánchez-Carrión R.; Enseñat-Cantallops A.
paper_title: Neuropsychological rehabilitation program for patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome: a clinical experience

summary: A 10-week randomized controlled multicenter trial evaluated individualized, symptom-titrated resistance and aerobic training in 118 long COVID patients with chronic fatigue. The intervention group showed significant improvements in fatigue (FSS: -1.14), health-related quality of life (SF-12 mental: 5.94, physical: 4.33), functional aerobic capacity (CST: 22.72 steps), and handgrip strength compared to waitlist controls, with no increased risk of symptom exacerbation.
paper_authors: Christian Puta; Simon Haunhorst; Wilhelm Bloch
paper_title: Post-akutes COVID-19 (“long-COVID”): Andauernde Symptome, mögliche Ursachen und symptomgeleitetes post-akut COVID-19 Management zur Wiedererlangung der körperlichen Leistungsfähigkeit (Scoping Review)

summary: Secondary analysis of a randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial examining vortioxetine treatment effects on depressive symptoms in post-COVID-19 condition, with anxiety as a moderator. Found that vortioxetine significantly reduced depressive symptoms in 147 participants, with anxiety symptoms moderating treatment efficacy.
paper_authors: Gia Han Le; Angela T.H. Kwan; Ziji Guo; Kayla M. Teopiz; Sabrina Wong; Shakila Meshkat; Giacomo d'Andrea; Roger Ho; Taeho Greg Rhee; Bing Cao; Sebastian Badulescu; Lee Phan; Joshua D. Rosenblat; Rodrigo B. Mansur; Mehala Subramaniapillai; Roger S. McIntyre
paper_title: Impact of vortioxetine on depressive symptoms moderated by symptoms of anxiety in persons with post-COVID-19 condition: A secondary analysis

summary: The PAIN-COVID randomized controlled trial evaluated a follow-up program combining patient education and psychological intervention (based on Rehm's self-control model) for critical COVID-19 survivors at risk of post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) and chronic pain. The intervention was not superior to standard care in improving quality of life at 6 months, though the data may inform future strategies for managing PICS and pain in this population.
paper_authors: Ojeda A.; Calvo A.; Cuñat T.; Mellado-Artigas R.; Costas-Carrera A.; Sánchez-Rodriguez MM; Comino-Trinidad O.; Aliaga J.; Arias M.; Martínez-Pallí G.; Dürsteler C.; Ferrando C.
paper_title: Effectiveness of a specific follow up program for the management of the mental components of post-intensive care syndrome and chronic pain after COVID-19: results from the PAIN-COVID randomized clinical trial
paper_journal: Revista Española de Anestesiología y Reanimación (English Edition)

summary: A randomized controlled trial (n=42) comparing thoracic spinal manipulation plus pulmonary rehabilitation versus pulmonary rehabilitation alone in long COVID patients. The intervention group showed significant improvements in pulmonary function and thoracic spine mobility, supporting the therapeutic benefit of spinal manipulation for long COVID respiratory symptoms.
paper_authors: Amita Aggarwal; Aas Chanda
paper_title: Effects of thoracic spinal manipulation in long COVID patients: A randomised controlled trial

summary: A bicentric randomized controlled trial evaluating the feasibility and effects of singing-based respiratory training (SBRT) in 45 post-COVID syndrome patients with breathing disorders. SBRT showed high compliance (96%), with medium effect sizes on health-related quality of life, anxiety, and depression, though SBRT aimed at reducing respiratory rate did not outperform regular SBRT.
paper_authors: Anke Steinmetz; Alexander Hönning; Wiebke Käckenmester; Ingo Schmehl; Marc Secara; Sigrid Biffar; Ina Kim; Katja Bahcesular; Bernhard Lehnert; Kristin Lehnert; Marcus Dörr; Kristina Zappel
paper_title: Singing-based respiratory training in people with post-COVID syndrome: a bicentric randomized feasibility study
paper_journal: Annals of Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine

summary: This observational study evaluates immunoadsorption therapy in 12 post-COVID patients with ME/CFS symptoms, finding that the treatment effectively removes autoantibodies and reduces pro-inflammatory cytokines while improving neuropsychological function and grip strength. However, self-reported symptoms and ME/CFS questionnaire scores did not show significant improvement, and removed proteins rebounded within one month.
paper_authors: Moritz Anft; Lea Wiemers; Kamil S. Rosiewicz; Adrian Doevelaar; Sarah Skrzypczyk; Julia Kurek; Sviatlana Kaliszczyk; Maximilian Seidel; Ulrik Stervbo; Felix S. Seibert; Timm H. Westhoff; Nina Babel
paper_title: Effect of immunoadsorption on clinical presentation and immune alterations in COVID-19–induced and/or aggravated ME/CFS

summary: A randomized controlled trial testing intermittent hypoxia exposure (IHE) versus normoxia exposure as a treatment for dyspnea and fatigue in 95 PASC patients. IHE significantly improved 6-minute walk distance, spirometry parameters, and dyspnea/fatigue scales with no severe adverse events.
paper_authors: Shiqian Zha; Xu Liu; Yan Yao; Yang He; Yixuan Wang; Qingfeng Zhang; Jingyi Zhang; Yaohua Yi; Rui Xiao; Ke Hu
paper_title: Short-term intermittent hypoxia exposure for dyspnea and fatigue in post-acute sequelae of COVID-19: A randomized controlled study

summary: Open-label study evaluating safety and efficacy of prolonged-release pirfenidone in 70 patients with post-acute COVID-19 pulmonary fibrosis over 3 months. Treatment was well-tolerated with significant improvements in pulmonary function tests, 6-minute walk test, dyspnea, and symptoms.
paper_authors: Sansores RH; Ramírez-Venegas A.; Montiel-Lopez F.; Domínguez-Arellano S.; Alva-Lopez LF; Falfán-Valencia R.; Pérez-Rubio G.; Olaya-López E.; Zavaleta-Martínez EO; Aguilar-Medina S.; Escobar-Alvarado JC; Poo JL; Matera MG; Cazzola M.
paper_title: Prolonged-release pirfenidone in patients with pulmonary fibrosis as a phenotype of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 pneumonia. Safety and efficacy

summary: A phase 2 double-blind randomized controlled trial testing nirmatrelvir-ritonavir versus placebo for treating long COVID in 100 US participants, with treatment given for 15 days. Nirmatrelvir-ritonavir showed no significant improvement in PROMIS-29 physical health scores compared to placebo at day 28, though the trial demonstrated feasibility of decentralized long COVID trials.

paper_title: Nirmatrelvir–ritonavir versus placebo–ritonavir in individuals with long COVID in the USA (PAX LC): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 2, decentralised trial

summary: A feasibility trial evaluating a specialized 8-session cognitive-behavioral group intervention for inpatients with post-COVID-19 condition in a neurological rehabilitation setting. The program was well-received and showed significant improvements in subjective fatigue and disease coping, though findings are limited by lack of control group, small sample size, and high drop-out rate.
paper_authors: Daniel Huth; Anne-Kathrin Bräscher; Sarah Tholl; Johanna Fiess; Gunnar Birke; Christoph Herrmann; Michael Jöbges; Daniela Mier; Michael Witthöft
paper_title: Cognitive-behavioral therapy for patients with post-COVID-19 condition (CBT-PCC): a feasibility trial

summary: An uncontrolled case series of 95 post-COVID patients treated with SSRIs, finding that two-thirds showed good to strong response with substantial improvements in brain fog, sensory overload, fatigue, and dysautonomia. The authors propose neurobiological mechanisms underlying SSRI efficacy in post-COVID syndrome, particularly involving the kynurenine pathway and immune dysregulation.
paper_authors: Rus CP; de Vries BEK; de Vries IEJ; Nutma I.; Kooij JJS
paper_title: Treatment of 95 post-Covid patients with SSRIs

summary: This pilot study evaluated 8 weeks of inspiratory muscle training (IMT) in healthy controls (n=12), people with PASC (n=9), and people with mild-to-moderate ME/CFS (n=12). All groups improved in inspiratory pressure, 6-minute walk distance, resting heart rate, heart rate variability, and sleep symptoms; ME/CFS participants additionally showed improvements in vascular function, autonomic questionnaire scores, and pain.
paper_authors: Heather Edgell; Tania J. Pereira; Kathleen Kerr; Riina Bray; Farah Tabassum; Lauren Sergio; Smriti Badhwar
paper_title: Inspiratory muscle training improves autonomic function in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome and post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2: A pilot study

summary: A feasibility study evaluating individually tailored exercise (endurance and strength training) in 26 post-COVID-19 patients with POTS over 12 weeks. The intervention showed good adherence (76%), high completion rates (96%), and preliminary improvements in symptom burden, psychological function, and physical outcomes.
paper_authors: Annie Svensson; Anna Svensson-Raskh; Linda Holmström; Carl Hallberg; Lucian Bezuidenhout; David Moulaee Conradsson; Marcus Ståhlberg; Judith Bruchfeld; Artur Fedorowski; Malin Nygren-Bonnier
paper_title: Individually tailored exercise in patients with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome related to post-COVID-19 condition – a feasibility study

summary: A pilot clinical trial of 14 long COVID patients undergoing 10-week aerobic exercise training, analyzing serum extracellular vesicle RNA profiles before and after intervention. Exercise training modulated EV-associated gene expression, suppressing inflammation and metabolism-related genes at peak exertion post-training, suggesting potential molecular mechanisms of symptom improvement.
paper_authors: Asghar Abbasi; Nathaniel Hansen; Joanna Palade; Dorothy Paredes; Bessie Meechoovet; Kendall Van Keuren-Jensen; Patrick Pirrotte; William W. Stringer
paper_title: Serum extracellular vesicle RNA profiles in long COVID: insights from exercise-induced gene modulation

summary: The PsyLoCo project developed a psychotherapeutic treatment manual addressing psychosocial burdens in long COVID patients across four modules: coping/distress management, physical complaints/pain, chronic fatigue/affective symptoms, and social/working life. The manual was tested for feasibility and effectiveness in a multicentre randomized controlled pilot study.
paper_authors: Tamara Frank; Paul Bruckmann; Marius Binneböse; Hannah Wallis; Melanie Elgner; Florian Junne; Janka Massag; Rafael Mikolajczyk; Marisa Schurr; Katrin Giel; Lisa Wedekind; Julia Kuhn; Harald Gündel; Anne-Maria Müller; Pauline Beckmann; Claas Lahmann; Christine Allwang
paper_title:
Psychosoziale Aspekte bei Long COVID – Ein psychotherapeutisches
                    Behandlungsmanual aus dem PsyLoCo-Projekt

summary: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial evaluated the effects of a multispecies probiotic on post-acute COVID-19 symptoms in 21 patients over 6 months. The probiotic group showed significant improvements in respiratory function, immune markers, microbial richness, and serum metabolome compared to placebo.
paper_authors: Angela Horvath; Alexandra Polyák; Hansjörg Habisch; I. Balazs; Nicole Feldbacher; S. Köfler; Kurt Buchegger; Tobias Madl; Vanessa Stadlbauer
paper_title: Effects of a multispecies probiotic intake on the recovery of patients with post-acute COVID-19 symptoms; a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial

summary: A pilot study evaluating high-tone therapy (HTT), a form of electrotherapy, on functional capacity and quality of life in 22 post-COVID-condition patients with fatigue. Patients receiving ten 60-minute HTT sessions showed significant improvements in the one-minute sit-to-stand test (23.5 to 35.5 repetitions, p<0.001), SF-12 quality of life scores (both physical and mental components), post-COVID severity score, and subjective work ability.
paper_authors: Franz Gröner; Dana Loudovici-Krug; Christin Mäurer; Hanna Meinunger; Steffen Derlien; Josephine Kühnemund; Christina Lemhöfer
paper_title:
Positive Wirkung von Hochtontherapie auf die funktionelle Kapazität
                    von Patienten mit Post-COVID-Condition – eine Pilotstudie

summary: This non-randomized controlled study compared neuropsychological rehabilitation (8 participants, 6-month intervention) versus no treatment (7 controls) in post-COVID-19 syndrome patients with similar baseline cognitive profiles. The treatment group showed significant improvements in verbal memory and action naming, while the control group improved only in action fluency, suggesting that cognitive rehabilitation may benefit some post-COVID cognitive impairments.
paper_authors: Elena Herrera; Claudia Blanco; Belén Álvarez-Mundiñano; María González-Nosti
paper_title: Neuropsychological Rehabilitation Improves Memory and Action Naming in Patients With Post–COVID-19 Syndrome

summary: A randomized controlled trial evaluating the acute effects of osteopathic treatment on autonomic nervous system function (measured via heart rate variability) in long COVID patients with fatigue syndrome compared to sham treatment. The study aims to assess whether osteopathy can positively influence post-COVID fatigue by measuring HRV changes.
paper_authors: T Pöhlmann; Daniela Leitl; Tessa Schneeberger; Inga Jarosch; R Glöckl; AR Koczulla
paper_title: Der Effekt einer osteopathischen Behandlung auf das autonome Nervensystem bei Long/Post COVID -19 PatientInnen mit Fatigue Syndrom, verglichen mit einer Scheinbehandlung, wurde gemessen mit der Herzratenvariabilität (HRV) – eine randomisiert, kontrollierte Studie.

summary: This study evaluates diaphragm muscle weakness and exertional dyspnea at 2 years post-COVID-19 hospitalization, and investigates the impact of inspiratory muscle training (IMT) on these outcomes in long COVID patients. The research determines the persistence of diaphragm dysfunction and demonstrates whether targeted respiratory muscle training can improve symptoms in this population.
paper_authors: B Regmi; R Glöckl; Stephan Walterspacher; Michael Dreher; Jens Spießhoefer
paper_title: Diaphragm Muscle Weakness related Dyspnea Persists Two Years After COVID-19 and can be Improved by Inspiratory Muscle Training

summary: A pilot double-blind randomized controlled trial evaluating classical homeopathy as a treatment for post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (long COVID). The study tests whether homeopathy, which has shown benefits for chronic diseases with similar symptom profiles, may be effective for the diverse symptoms associated with long COVID.
paper_authors: Elizabeth Rice; Jennifer Jacobs; Iris Bell; Eleni Krommidas
paper_title: Homeopathic Treatment of Post-acute COVID-19 Syndrome – A Pilot Double-blind Randomized Controlled Trial

summary: Pilot randomized controlled trial evaluating a 12-week cognitive rehabilitation intervention adapted for long COVID patients with objective cognitive impairment. Intervention group showed non-futile trends in processing speed, learning, memory, language, and executive function, with significant self-reported improvements compared to time-matched controls, supporting further evaluation in a larger trial.
paper_authors: Jacqueline H. Becker; Eric Watson; Nadia Zubair; Fernando Carnavali; Emilia Bagiella; David Reich; Juan P. Wisnivesky
paper_title: Preliminary evaluation of a cognitive rehabilitation intervention for post-COVID-19 cognitive impairment: A pilot randomized controlled trial

summary: This non-randomized trial evaluated an 8-week supervised exercise intervention (resistance training plus aerobic exercise) in 32 healthcare workers with post-COVID symptoms, stratified by severity. Physical exercise significantly improved aerobic fitness (VO2peak), functional capacity (6MWT, 30-second sit-to-stand), mental health outcomes, and work ability, with greater benefits observed in those with severe fatigue.
paper_authors: Timothy Hasenoehrl; Stefano Palma; Dominikus F.-X Huber; Stefan Kastl; Margarete Steiner; Galateja Jordakieva; Richard Crevenna
paper_title: Post-COVID: effects of physical exercise on functional status and work ability in health care personnel

summary: A feasibility study of occupational therapy-based energy management education (EME) in 17 post-COVID patients with fatigue using a pre-post design. The intervention showed large effect sizes on fatigue impact, self-efficacy, daily activity competency, and quality of life, with promising results supporting further research.
paper_authors: Ruth Hersche; Andrea Weise; Beate Hummel; Marco Barbero
paper_title: Occupational therapy-based self-management education in persons with post-COVID-19 condition related fatigue: a feasibility study with a pre-post design

summary: A randomized controlled trial evaluating photobiomodulation therapy for treating dysgeusia (taste disturbance) in long COVID patients. The study found variable treatment responses and calls for further research to elucidate optimal outcomes.
paper_authors: Carlos Eduardo Fontana; Letícia Parreira; Sérgio Pinheiro
paper_title: Photobiomodulation in the Treatment of Dysgeusia in Patients with Long COVID: A Single-Blind, Randomized Controlled Trial

summary: An 8-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of vortioxetine (5-20 mg) versus placebo in 149 adults with post-COVID-19 condition. Vortioxetine did not significantly improve primary cognitive outcome (Digit Symbol Substitution Test) in unadjusted analysis but showed cognitive benefit when adjusted for baseline CRP; significant improvements in depressive symptoms and quality of life were observed.
paper_authors: Roger S. McIntyre; Lee Phan; Angela T. H. Kwan; Rodrigo B. Mansur; Joshua D. Rosenblat; Ziji Guo; Gia Han Le; Leanna M. W. Lui; Kayla M. Teopiz; Felicia Ceban; Yena Lee; Julia Bailey; Ranuk Ramachandra; Joshua Di Vincenzo; Sebastian Badulescu; Hartej Gill; Pawel Drzadzewski; Mehala Subramaniapillai
paper_title: Vortioxetine for the treatment of post-COVID-19 condition: a randomized controlled trial

summary: Randomized controlled trial of 44 long COVID patients comparing 4 weeks of supervised strength-endurance training versus usual care. Exercise intervention significantly improved VO2peak and oxygen-pulse compared to control, though fatigue and quality of life improvements were not statistically different between groups.
paper_authors: Alexander Kögel; M. Machatschek; Ronja Scharschmidt; Claudia Wollny; Florian Lordick; Mohamed Ghanem; Ulrich Laufs; Sven Fikenzer
paper_title: Physical exercise as a treatment for persisting symptoms post covid infection

summary: A randomized, sham-controlled, double-blind trial of hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) in 60 post-COVID syndrome patients with symptoms lasting ≥3 months. HBOT significantly improved global longitudinal strain (GLS) compared to sham, suggesting recovery of subclinical left ventricular dysfunction in post-COVID patients.
paper_authors: Marina Leitman; Sandra Cristina Pereira Costa Fuchs; Vladimir Tyomkin; Amir Hadanny; Shani Zilberman-Itskovich; Shai Efrati
paper_title: The effect of hyperbaric oxygen therapy on myocardial function in post- covid syndrome patients: a randomized controlled trial

summary: The PERCEIVE randomised controlled trial evaluated a 6-month multidisciplinary exercise intervention (aerobic and resistance training plus medical management) versus usual care in 133 long COVID patients with exercise intolerance. The intervention significantly improved peak oxygen uptake and cardiorespiratory fitness but had no significant effect on mood or quality of life.
paper_authors: E J Howden; Lauren Burnham; Joel Smith; Kristyn Whitmore; K Morrison; R Hoare; Y Sata; Q. Huynh; T H Marwick
paper_title: Individualised aerobic and resistance exercise training improves exercise tolerance in individuals with Long COVID: findings from the PERCEIVE randomised controlled trial

summary: This cross-sectional study with qualitative interviews examines how gender and parenting responsibilities affect social participation, quality of life, and mental health in 920 long COVID patients. The study documents associations between parenting tasks and impairments in family/domestic responsibilities, and finds higher anxiety in men with long COVID compared to women, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Dominik Schröder; Tim Schmachtenberg; Stephanie Heinemann; Christina Müllenmeister; Sascha Roder; Iman El-Sayed; Gloria Heesen; Gloria Königs; Alexandra Dopfer-Jablonka; Eva Hummers; Marie Mikuteit; Christian Dopfer; Simon Grewendorf; Jacqueline Niewolik; Sandra Steffens; Valerie Doze; Frank Klawonn; Frank Müller
paper_title: Parenting and Gender as Impact Factors for Social Participation, Quality of Life, and Mental Health in Long COVID
paper_journal: Journal of Primary Care & Community Health

summary: A pre-post feasibility study of teleyoga delivered via live-streamed sessions and digital app for 11 people with post-COVID condition over 7-12 weeks. The intervention was safe with low adherence but showed significant improvement in cognitive function (p=0.048) and self-reported benefits in breathing, relaxation, and stress reduction.
paper_authors: Marie Lundberg; Leonie Klompstra; Lotti Orwelius; Mirjam Schimanke; Cecilia Olsson; Anna Strömberg
paper_title: Feasibility of teleyoga for people with post COVID-19 condition– a mixed method design

summary: This study analyzes 1.38 million social media posts about long COVID across three pandemic phases to examine gaps between official health communications and patient narratives online. Rather than testing a treatment, it provides qualitative and quantitative analysis of patient experiences and public discourse, functioning as a secondary literature review of social media data rather than a primary clinical trial.
paper_authors: Esperanza Miyake; Sam Martin
paper_title: Long Covid: Online patient narratives, public health communication and vaccine hesitancy

summary: A qualitative study examining quality standards and variation in long COVID care delivery across 10 UK clinics through interviews, ethnography, and observational data. The study found that variation in services is often justified by patient complexity and comorbidities, and recommends supporting multidisciplinary team case-based learning rather than generic standardization.
paper_authors: Trisha Greenhalgh; Julie L. Darbyshire; Cassie Lee; Emma Ladds; Jenny Ceolta-Smith
paper_title: What is quality in long covid care? Lessons from a national quality improvement collaborative and multi-site ethnography

summary: This cross-sectional survey describes 112 specialized long COVID outpatient clinics in Germany and their diagnostic/treatment approaches, based on responses from 45 clinic directors. Treatment is predominantly personalized and symptom-oriented (respiratory vs neurocognitive) rather than standardized, with high perceived patient distress and clinician confidence in benefits, though greater standardization is recommended.
paper_authors: Lucas C. Adam; Fabian Boesl; Vanessa Raeder; Ameli Breuer; Benno Bremer; Heinrich J. Audebert; Christiana Franke
paper_title: The legacy of the COVID-19 pandemic for the healthcare environment: the establishment of long COVID/ Post-COVID-19 condition follow-up outpatient clinics in Germany

summary: Mixed-methods study examining sleep and alcohol use experiences among Veterans with long COVID through chart reviews (n=57) and interviews (n=12). Finds that pre-existing sleep problems are exacerbated in long COVID, while alcohol use disorder is rare, and explores provider perspectives on delivering evidence-based care for these comorbidities.
paper_authors: Rachel L. Bachrach; Caitlan A. Tighe; Nicole Beyer; Kristina Hruska; Angela Phares; Karley Atchison; Lynn Baniak; Gretchen Haas; Adam D. Bramoweth
paper_title: Sleep and Alcohol Use Among Veterans Living With Long COVID
paper_journal: Journal of Primary Care & Community Health

summary: A mixed-methods RCT protocol evaluating face-to-face rehabilitation (twice-weekly for 6 weeks, combining symptom-titrated exercise with self-management education) versus usual care in non-hospitalised long COVID patients, with embedded qualitative components to explore acceptability and healthcare inequalities. This is a protocol paper with no results yet (trial registered September 2024).
paper_authors: Kate Kontou; Enya Daynes; Sally J. Singh; Rachael A. Evans; Nikki Gardiner; Emma Chaplin; Matthew Richardson; Nicolette Bishop; Jennifer Creese; Nicola Bateman; Adam Wright; Elga Zivtins; Linzy Houchen-Wolloff
paper_title: The effectiveness and acceptability of face-to-face rehabilitation for patients with Long Covid who were not hospitalised with their acute infection: a mixed-methods study comprising a randomised controlled trial (RCT) with embedded qualitative component

summary: Cross-sectional and longitudinal study comparing cognitive function and psychological well-being in 121 adults with and without COVID-19, including 17 with long COVID symptoms. Found that COVID-19 survivors, especially those with long COVID, experience significant cognitive disruption (reduced processing speed, attention, memory) and higher depression/anxiety, but this is an observational assessment study without any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Krupa Vakani; M. Ratto; Anna Sandford-James; E. Antonova; V. Kumari
paper_title: Cognitive Trajectory of COVID-19 and Long COVID in Adult Survivors

summary: This paper reviews the hypothesis that long COVID results from impaired cholinergic neurotransmission and evaluates low-dose transcutaneous nicotine (LDTN) as a treatment. It presents a case report with PET imaging showing improved cholinergic function after LDTN, plus survey data from 231 LDTN users reporting 73.5% symptom improvement.
paper_authors: Marco Leitzke; Donald Troy Roach; Swen Hesse; Peter Schönknecht; Georg-Alexander Becker; Michael Rullmann; Bernhardt Sattler; Osama Sabri
paper_title: Long COVID – a critical disruption of cholinergic neurotransmission?

summary: Mixed-methods study characterizing the burden of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) in 442 community-dwelling individuals through surveys and in-depth interviews. Found 30% experienced severe fatigue, persons with PASC had worse quality of life and mental health, and reported debilitating impacts on daily functioning.
paper_authors: Oluwabunmi Ogungbe; Sarah Slone; Abeer Alharthi; Tosin Tomiwa; Baridosia Kumbe; Alanna Bergman; Katherine McNabb; Rhonda Smith Wright; Jason E. Farley; Cheryl R. Dennison Himmelfarb; Lisa A. Cooper; Wendy S. Post; Patricia M. Davidson; Yvonne Commodore-Mensah
paper_title: “Living like an empty gas tank with a leak”: Mixed methods study on post-acute sequelae of COVID-19

summary: This mixed-methods feasibility study tested a 4-week online mindful-walking intervention delivered via Facebook to 23 long COVID patients, with quantitative data collected via daily surveys and qualitative data from engagement metrics. Participants reported high feasibility scores and those who engaged in mindful walking showed improvements in positive affect, reduced negative affect, better perceived cognitive ability, and increased physical activity.
paper_authors: Abhishek Aggarwal; Shan Qiao; Chih-Hsiang Yang; Slone Taylor; Cheuk Chi Tam; Xiaoming Li
paper_title: Feasibility and preliminary efficacy of an online mindful walking intervention among COVID-19 long haulers: A mixed methods study including daily diary surveys

summary: A mixed-method cross-sectional study assessing physical, mental, and social health status in 552 COVID-19 recovered patients across Nepal. The study documents symptom prevalence and functional impacts but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Sashi Silwal; Kristina Parajuli; Astha Acharya; Ajnish Ghimire; Savita Pandey; Ashok Pandey; Anil Poudyal; Bihungum Bista; Pradip Gyanwali; Meghnath Dhimal
paper_title: Physical, mental and social status after COVID-19 recovery in Nepal: A mixed method study

summary: A multicentric prospective cohort study following 315 hospitalized COVID-19 patients for 1 year to assess long COVID prevalence and identify predictive factors. Found 16.5% prevalence with shortness of breath, cough, fatigue, and weight loss as significant predictors, but this is a passive observational follow-up without any intervention or treatment being tested.
paper_authors: Vignesh Kumar J.; Jency Maria Koshy; Divyashree S.; Suneetha Narreddy; Mahasampath Gowri S.; Priscilla Rupali; Sowmya Sathyendra
paper_title: Prevalence and predictors of long COVID at 1 year in a cohort of hospitalized patients: A multicentric qualitative and quantitative study

summary: A mixed-methods retrospective observational study examining Reddit activity of 7,544 users, finding that pre-pandemic activity on ME/CFS forums is the strongest predictor of participation in long COVID forums. The study explores motives for co-participation including mutual support, dual identification, and the possibility of shared pathophysiology between ME/CFS and long COVID.
paper_authors: William U. Meyerson; Rick H. Hoyle
paper_title: Pre-pandemic activity on a myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome support forum is highly associated with later activity on a long COVID support forum for a variety of reasons: A mixed methods study

summary: A feasibility study of a complementary long COVID support service combining psycho-education and mind-body approaches (physiotherapy, craniosacral therapy) delivered in a UK community setting to 25 participants. The service showed positive changes in mental, physical, emotional, and spiritual wellbeing measured by the Warwick Holistic Health Questionnaire (33.7 to 39.5, n=16), with high participant satisfaction.
paper_authors: Nicola Brough; Sally Abel; Lucy Priddle
paper_title: A Feasibility Study Combining Psycho-Education and Mind-Body Complementary Approaches to Support Those with Post COVID-19 Syndrome ‘Long COVID’ in a UK Based Community Setting

summary: Mixed-methods evaluation of an ECHO tele-mentoring program designed to train medical officers in long COVID management across four Indian states, measuring changes in provider knowledge, competence, and patient satisfaction. Results showed significant improvements in MOs' knowledge and skills, with trained providers demonstrating increased confidence and adopting a comprehensive approach including mental health strategies, leading to high patient satisfaction.
paper_authors: Rajmohan Panda; Ritika Mukherjee; Kalpana Singh; Supriya Lahoti; Apoorva Karan Rai; Amit Verma; Sandeep Bhalla; Haresh Chandwani; Kumud Rai; Archisman Mohapatra
paper_title: Effects of the ECHO tele-mentoring program on Long COVID management in health facilities in India: A mixed-methods evaluation

summary: Mixed-methods study evaluating a mobile app designed to improve self-management skills in 19 older adults with post-acute COVID-19 sequelae (PASC), measuring fatigue, cognitive problems, mood, and health-related quality of life. Findings indicate the app is relevant for PASC patients and support further development for this population.
paper_authors: Kamilah Thomas-Purcell; Rosemary Davenport; Victoria Ayala; Donrie Purcell; Raymond L. Ownby
paper_title: Chronic Disease Self-Management of Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19 Among Older Adults: A Mixed-Methods Analysis

summary: Literature review and case study examining musculoskeletal symptoms in COVID-19 and post-COVID patients, with evaluation of physiotherapy interventions including exercises. Physical therapy, particularly exercise, significantly improved disability and function in a post-ICU long COVID patient.
paper_authors: Adel Zedan
paper_title: Musculoskeletal symptoms in COVID-19 and physiotherapy role: Literature review and case study
paper_journal: Benha International Journal of Physical Therapy

summary: A proof-of-concept study of the Hope Programme for Long COVID, an 8-week digital self-management intervention codesigned with people living with long COVID, combining peer support and positive psychology approaches. The uncontrolled study of 47 participants showed improvements in mental well-being and self-efficacy, with follow-up rates of 59.6%.
paper_authors: Hayley Wright; Andrew Turner; Stuart Ennis; Carol Percy; Garry Loftus; Wendy Clyne; Gabriela Matouskova; Faith Martin
paper_title: Digital Peer-Supported Self-Management Intervention Codesigned by People With Long COVID: Mixed Methods Proof-of-Concept Study

summary: A multimethod study analyzing #longCOVID and #longhaulers conversations on Twitter (2,500 tweets) using text analysis and social network analysis to understand public discourse and lived experiences. Findings show long haulers emphasize symptoms and community-building, while general discussion frames focus on support and research, with networks being highly decentralized.
paper_authors: Sara Santarossa; Ashley Rapp; Saily Sardinas; Janine Hussein; Alex Ramirez; Andrea E. Cassidy-Bushrow; Philip Cheng; Eunice Yu
paper_title: Understanding the #longCOVID and #longhaulers Conversation on Twitter: Multimethod Study

summary: A mixed methods analysis of YouTube content discussing long COVID (post-COVID condition) symptoms, patient experiences, and information shared by medical professionals, news sources, and long haulers themselves. This is a qualitative content analysis study that does not test any treatment interventions.
paper_authors: Alexis Jordan; Albert Park
paper_title: Understanding the Long Haulers of COVID-19: Mixed Methods Analysis of YouTube Content

summary: A mixed-methods Twitter analysis examining healthcare workers' discourse and sentiment regarding post-COVID-19 condition in children and young people in the UK from January 2021-2022. The study analyzes 2,588 tweets to understand HCW perceptions and identifies themes including uncertainty, policies, vaccination, and management strategies, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Macarena Chepo; Sam Martin; Noémie Déom; Ahmad Firas Khalid; Cecilia Vindrola-Padros
paper_title: Twitter Analysis of Health Care Workers’ Sentiment and Discourse Regarding Post–COVID-19 Condition in Children and Young People: Mixed Methods Study

summary: This paper describes a situation analysis assessing post-COVID-19 patient needs and preferences in South Africa, followed by the design and piloting of an 8-week group intervention combining rehabilitation and mental health support. While outcome analysis is pending, the study demonstrates that patients found rehabilitation helpful and the intervention was feasible to deliver.
paper_authors: Nicole Audrey Glover; Farzana Sathar; Pride Mokome; Nkululeko Mathabela; Sipokazi Taleni; Sarah Alexandra van Blydenstein; Anna-Maria Mekota; Salome Charalambous; Andrea Rachow; Olena Ivanova
paper_title: Improving Health and Well-Being of People With Post–COVID-19 Consequences in South Africa: Situation Analysis and Pilot Intervention Design

summary: This mixed methods analysis examines patterns of electronic consultation (eConsult) cases submitted by primary care providers to long COVID specialists in Ontario between 2021-2022. The study documents common symptoms, question types, and response times but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Jatinderpreet Singh; Michael Quon; Danica Goulet; Erin Keely; Clare Liddy
paper_title: The Utilization of Electronic Consultations (eConsults) to Address Emerging Questions Related to Long COVID-19 in Ontario, Canada: Mixed Methods Analysis

summary: A pilot study evaluating the feasibility of inspiratory muscle training as a home-based intervention for 16 patients with persistent dyspnoea after COVID-19. The intervention showed 73.7% adherence with no adverse events, and maximal inspiratory pressure improved from 84.7% to 111.3% of predicted values, though careful supervision and individualized training parameters were recommended.
paper_authors: Romain Collet; Maarten Van Egmond; Marike Van der Schaaf; Mel Major
paper_title: Feasibility of inspiratory muscle training for patients with persistent dyspnoea after COVID-19 infection: A pilot study
paper_journal: Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine - Clinical Communications

summary: Review article assessing mechanisms of CNS damage in HIV infection and examining how SARS-CoV-2 may contribute to neuropsychiatric pathology in HIV-infected patients. A small preliminary study of 146 HIV-infected patients found long-term neuropsychiatric manifestations post-COVID, but no specific intervention was tested.
paper_authors: V. V. Rassokhin; E. I. Svetashova; I. О. Modestova; N. V. Kaplevskaya; N. А. Belyakov
paper_title: Main mechanisms of central nervous system damage with combined infection of HIV and SARS-COV-2: review

summary: This paper combines a literature review of obesity as a COVID-19 risk factor with a cross-sectional survey of COVID-19 patients in Latvia. It does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for a trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: Diāna Arāja; Vita Rovīte; Modra Murovska; Anna Terentjeva; Diāna Vaidere; Katrīne Vecvagare; Ludmila Vīksna
paper_title: Severity of COVID-19: Causes and Consequences — From Obesity to Chronic Fatigue Syndrome
paper_journal: Proceedings of the Latvian Academy of Sciences. Section B. Natural, Exact, and Applied Sciences.

summary: Mixed-methods study examining how post-COVID-19 conditions affected sociocultural activities and quality of life in a Nepal district between 2022-2024. Found reduced motivation, economic disruption, and emotional strain, but identified cultural activities as protective factors for adaptation and recovery.
paper_authors: Prakash Prasad Sapkota
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 Impacts on Sociocultural Practices and Quality of Life in Baglung District, Nepal
paper_journal: Dhaulagiri Journal of Sociology and Anthropology

summary: This study analyzes #longCOVID and #longhaulers conversations on Twitter using text and social network analysis to examine how long COVID is framed by users. It found that support and research frames dominate general discussions, while symptoms and community-building dominate patient perspectives, but no treatment interventions were tested or evaluated.
paper_authors: Sara Santarossa; Ashley Rapp; Saily Sardinas; Janine Hussein; Alex Ramirez; Andrea E. Cassidy-Bushrow; Philip Cheng; Eunice Yu
paper_title: Understanding the #longCOVID and #longhaulers Conversation on Twitter: Multimethod Study (Preprint)

summary: This study analyzes English-language tweets about long COVID from 2021 in Canada, the US, and Europe using topic modeling and sentiment analysis to understand public perceptions. It identifies five main topics including vaccination discussions, symptom duration, persistent symptoms, calls for treatment research, and symptom measurement, with findings showing mixed sentiments fluctuating with COVID-related news events.
paper_authors: Ahmed Ghassan Tawfiq AbuRaed; Emil Azuma Prikryl; Giuseppe Carenini; Naveed Zafar Janjua
paper_title: Long COVID Discourse in Canada, the United States, and Europe: Topic Modeling and Sentiment Analysis of Twitter Data

summary: Literature review combined with a single-center observational study comparing post-COVID syndrome prevalence and features in 203 healthcare workers versus 156 non-occupational controls followed for 60 days. Study documents higher rates of thermoregulation disorders, arrhythmias, and psychiatric symptoms in healthcare workers post-COVID but is primarily descriptive epidemiology without testing any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Lyubov A. Shpagina; Lyudmila P. Kuzmina; Olga S. Kotova; Ilya S. Shpagin; Natalya V. Kamneva; Galina V. Kuznetsova; Kristina V. Likhenko-Logvinenko
paper_title: COVID-19 in healthcare workers (literature review and own data)
paper_journal: Russian Journal of Occupational Health and Industrial Ecology

summary: Mixed methods study examining how PASC status modifies the relationship between physical activity and perceived physical/mental health using an online survey (N=4316) and interviews (N=34). Findings show PASC participants report worse health outcomes with increased PA, with qualitative data highlighting post-exertional malaise and symptom worsening—this is an observational study, not a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Zoe Sirotiak
paper_title: The effects of long COVID (PASC) status on the relationship between physical activity and perceived physical and mental health

summary: Literature review of post-COVID syndrome in children and adolescents with a clinical case report of a 4-year-old boy treated with combination therapy including L-carnitine. The case demonstrates improvement in muscle weakness, fatigue, and overall well-being following L-carnitine treatment.
paper_authors: L.A. Balykova; Marina V. Shirmankina; Д.О. Владимиров; E.I. Naumenko; Е. С. Самошкина; R.A. Chernyshova
paper_title: Post-COVID syndrome in children and adolescents: a literature review and clinical case
paper_journal: Russian Journal of Woman and Child Health

summary: An intervention study evaluating a doctor-led blended therapy (stress-controlled training plus intensive cognitive behavioral therapy) in 46 post-COVID-19 patients with fatigue and sensorimotor instability. The study applied the Health Action Process Approach (HAPA) model to identify factors influencing health behavior and therapeutic outcomes, providing actionable recommendations for clinicians to improve patient engagement and symptom management.
paper_authors: Thomas Urban
paper_title: Influence of Post-COVID-19 and a doctor-led Blended Therapy on health behavior and the health action of patients

summary: This study surveyed 251 people with multiple sclerosis who had COVID-19 infection to identify post-COVID symptoms and test whether physiotherapy could help. Among respondents, 22% (76 people) experienced post-COVID symptoms lasting ≥12 weeks, with fatigue, dyspnea, and neurological deterioration being most common; a small pilot of 6 participants received individual physiotherapy with reported subjective relief.
paper_authors: Klára Novotná; Kristýna Dandová; Ivana Knapová; Dominika Šťastná; Ingrid Menkyová; Eva Kubala Havrdová
paper_title: Post COVID challenges in chronic neurological conditions: exploring perceived symptoms and the potential effect of individual physiotherapy

summary: This mixed-methods usability study evaluated occupational therapy telerehabilitation delivered via the Caspar Health system to 12 long COVID patients over a 6-week program in Hong Kong. Most participants found the system acceptable and reported perceived health benefits, with a median System Usability Scale score of 56.25 and willingness to continue or recommend the intervention.
paper_authors: Lynn H. J. Kok; Jenny T. Gu; Jessica T. Y. Kung; Shera S. Liang; Pablo Cruz Gonzalez; Fong Mei Toh; Emily Sin; Kenneth N. K. Fong
paper_title: User experiences of patients with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome receiving occupational therapy telerehabilitation

summary: This paper reviews clinical trials on long COVID listed in ClinicalTrials.gov and analyzes public sentiment about long COVID through Twitter data using emotion lexicon and regression methods. It does not conduct an original treatment trial but rather surveys existing trials and social media discourse.
paper_authors: Arinjita Bhattacharyya; Anand Seth; Shesh Rai
paper_title: The effects of long COVID-19, its severity, and the need for immediate attention: Analysis of clinical trials and Twitter data

summary: This mixed-methods pilot study evaluated the acceptability and feasibility of an 8-week rehabilitation and self-management program for long COVID in South Africa, recruiting patients and staff from a tertiary hospital. Participants reported positive perceptions of the intervention and improved knowledge/confidence, though barriers included infrastructure, time, and language constraints.
paper_authors: Rupa Ramachandran; Farzana Sathar; Pride Mokome; Nkululeko Mathabela; Ency Mahlase; Salome Charalambous; Andrea Rachow; Nicole Audrey Glover; Olena Ivanova
paper_title: Acceptability and feasibility of a group intervention for long COVID in Johannesburg, South Africa: a mixed-method study

summary: Mixed-methods study examining long COVID symptoms and occupational status among 170 teachers in Israel using surveys and interviews. Found fatigue, weakness, and sleep difficulty as primary symptoms; sense of control and well-being predicted lower symptom levels.
paper_authors: Inbar Levkovich; Ela Kalimi
paper_title: Long COVID-19 Symptoms among Recovered Teachers in Israel: A Mixed-Methods Study

summary: Cross-sectional exploratory study assessing Romanian patients' perceptions of accessibility and quality of post-COVID-19 rehabilitation services, particularly for those with chronic conditions. Identifies barriers including lack of publicly funded services, cost, limited physician referral, and rural service scarcity, but does not evaluate or test any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Adrian Militaru; Petru Armean; Nicolae Ghita; Despina Paula Andrei
paper_title: Perceptions of Rehabilitation Access After SARS-CoV-2 Infection in Romanian Patients with Chronic Diseases: A Mixed-Methods Exploratory Study

summary: This mixed-methods study evaluated a football club community trust exercise rehabilitation programme for post-COVID condition patients (n=7) over 12 weeks with 6-month follow-up using the RE-AIM framework. The programme produced significant improvements in physical function (6MWT distance, grip strength, MEP), quality of life, anxiety, and depression, with strong participant satisfaction.
paper_authors: Steven Rimmer; Adam J. Herbert; Adam L. Kelly; Irfan Khawaja; Sam Lee; Lewis A. Gough
paper_title: A Mixed-Methods Evaluation of a Post-COVID-Condition Rehabilitation and Recovery Intervention Delivered in a Football Club Community Trust
paper_journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health

summary: This paper evaluates a 10-week virtual rehabilitation program (VRP) designed to provide early education and self-management techniques for long COVID patients. Mixed-methods analysis of 38 patient interviews and 17 healthcare professional surveys found the VRP was highly valued, digital delivery enabled self-management, but barriers to attendance included work/life balance and technology use.
paper_authors: Thuvia Flannery; Hannah Brady-Sawant; Rachel Tarrant; Jennifer Davison; Jenna Shardha; Stephen Halpin; Manoj Sivan; Denise Ross
paper_title: A Mixed-Methods Evaluation of a Virtual Rehabilitation Program for Self-Management in Post-COVID-19 Syndrome (Long COVID)
paper_journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health

summary: A mixed methods exploratory study examining functioning and rehabilitation needs in 20 individuals with self-reported disability following COVID-19, using patient-reported outcomes, physical function tests, and focus groups. The study identified persistent symptoms (fatigue, concentration issues, breathing problems) and gaps in rehabilitation services, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Tina Backmann; Thomas Maribo; Ann-Dorthe Zwisler; Jesper Rømhild Davidsen; Nina Rottmann
paper_title: A Mixed Methods Study of Functioning and Rehabilitation Needs Following COVID-19

summary: This paper describes a cross-sectional study of student self-perceptions and learning outcomes from organizing the Third Brazilian Congress on Clinical Evidence in COVID-19. It is an educational assessment, not a treatment trial, and should be excluded as it is primarily about pedagogy and student development rather than long COVID research or intervention testing.
paper_authors: Gabriela Teodora de Souza Sanches; Rafaela Bonfioli Costa; Ana Carolina de Almeida Bastos; Lucas Macedo Pereira Viana; Michelle Ralil da Costa; Victor Schulthais Chagas; Amanda Santos de Jesus; Milena Soriano Marcolino
paper_title: Empowering health sciences students in spreading knowledge: insights from the long COVID Brazilian Congress

summary: This paper investigates the undiagnosed burden of ME/CFS in Latvia and its potential overlap with post-COVID syndrome, comparing self-reported data from ME/CFS patients, undiagnosed symptomatic individuals, and former COVID-19 patients. It is primarily an epidemiological and diagnostic burden assessment rather than an intervention trial, and does not evaluate any treatment.
paper_authors: Diana Araja; Uldis Berkis; Asja Lunga; Modra Murovska
paper_title: Shadow Burden of Undiagnosed Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) on Society: Retrospective and Prospective—In Light of COVID-19

summary: A social network analysis of Twitter discourse on long COVID identifying key themes, influential users, and sentiment from 119,185 tweets collected over three months. The study examines how information about long COVID spreads on social media but does not test or evaluate any treatment interventions.
paper_authors: Ikhwan Yuda Kusuma; Suherman Suherman
paper_title: The Pulse of Long COVID on Twitter: A Social Network Analysis

summary: This study assessed cognitive functions and functional status in 32 COVID-infected individuals 3 months post-recovery, comparing differences by infection severity. While overall cognitive impairment was not significant on MMSE, subgroups differed in recent memory and functional domains, with qualitative follow-up at 6 months indicating subtle cognitive and psychological deficits that may be transient in nature.
paper_authors: Susmita Halder; Akash Kumar Mahato; Shinjini Samajdar
paper_title: Alteration of neurocognitive and functional status related to post-COVID infections

summary: This qualitative study examines the difficulties long COVID patients faced accessing and navigating the Belgian healthcare system through surveys, interviews, and forum discussions. The paper identifies shortcomings in clinical care (lack of empathy, unsystematic diagnosis, poor coordination) and recommends better provider education and interdisciplinary assessment—but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Laurence Kohn; Marie Dauvrin; Jens Detollenaere; Célia Primus-de-Jong; Charline Maertens de Noordhout; Diego Castanares-Zapatero; Irina Cleemput; Koen Van den Heede
paper_title: Difficultés rencontrées par les patients COVID long dans le système de santé belge

summary: This is a narrative review and survey-based analysis describing the characteristics, symptoms, and mechanisms of long COVID in Belgian patients, based on literature review and a 1,320-person online survey. The paper concludes that treatment effectiveness is unknown and recommends a symptom-oriented multidisciplinary rehabilitation approach, but does not test or evaluate any specific intervention.
paper_authors: Klaas Van Den Heede; Diego Castanares‐Zapatero; Laurence Kohn; Marie Dauvrin; Jens Detollenaere; Charline Maertens de Noordhout; C. Primus-de Jong; Irina Cleemput
paper_title: Langdurige Covid: de contouren worden langzaam duidelijk

summary: A cross-sectional study of 98 post-COVID patients in Thailand examining factors associated with post-exertional malaise using questionnaires and interviews. Female sex, BMI, and COVID-19 severity were identified as predictors of PEM, but the study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Nongnaphat Rungnoei; Penkhae Dittabunjong; Siriporn Kruttakart; Nittaya Thongma; Wilaiwan Komkhum; Somporn Pongrod
paper_title: Factors associated with post-exertional malaise in persons living with long COVID: A mixed-methods study
paper_journal: Journal of Public Health and Development

summary: Mixed-method study examining return-to-work experiences and health-related quality of life among Filipino COVID-19 survivors with post-COVID condition through surveys and interviews. While focused on long COVID symptoms and rehabilitation, this is an observational study without any intervention or treatment being tested, making it ineligible as a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Sy MP; Pineda RCS; Yao DPG; Togonon HD; Asaba E.
paper_title: Return-to-Work among COVID-19 Survivors in the Philippines and the Role of Rehabilitation: A Mixed-method Design

summary: This quasi-experimental study developed a decision-making logic model embedded in the iALERTS platform to stratify long COVID patients into risk categories based on demographic and clinical factors. The model identified fatigue, cough, cognitive dysfunction, and myalgia as most common persistent symptoms, with higher risk in females, older adults, those with obesity, unvaccinated individuals, and those with severe acute COVID.
paper_authors: Krishna Mohan Surapaneni; Manmohan Singhal; Ashish Joshi
paper_title: Decision-Making Logic Model for Risk Stratification Using iALERTS (Informatics Analytics for Long-Term Evaluation and Repercussions Tracking Of SARS-Cov-2 Infection)

summary: Mixed-methods study investigating health consequences of long COVID among student teachers at Kasetsart University, with Phase 1 surveying 286 students and Phase 2 conducting interviews. The research identified seven categories of symptoms experienced by student teachers with long COVID but does not evaluate or test any interventions.
paper_authors: Tharisara Chirasatienpon
paper_title: Health Impact of Long Covid among Student Teachers, Kasetsart University

summary: This pilot study evaluates iALERTS, a clinical decision support system designed to assist clinicians in identifying, stratifying, and managing long COVID patients. While the system showed high accuracy and user acceptance in a 120-patient pilot, it is a tool validation study rather than a treatment intervention trial.
paper_authors: Krishna Mohan Surapaneni; Manmohan Singhal; Ashish Joshi
paper_title: iALERTS: A Pragmatic Pilot Study of a Clinical Decision Support System for Long COVID Care

summary: Qualitative analysis of VA electronic health records examining how long COVID is clinically diagnosed and managed in a healthcare system. Identifies two dominant themes: clinical uncertainty in attribution of symptoms and care fragmentation in post-COVID patient management, highlighting the complexity of diagnosing and treating long COVID.
paper_authors: O'Hare AM; Vig EK; Iwashyna TJ; Fox A.; Taylor JS; Viglianti EM; Butler CR; Vranas KC; Helfand M.; Tuepker A.; Nugent SM; Winchell KA; Laundry RJ; Bowling CB; Hynes DM; Maciejewski ML; Bohnert ASB; Locke ER; Boyko EJ; Ioannou GN
paper_title: Complexity and Challenges of the Clinical Diagnosis and Management of Long COVID

summary: A prospective cohort study evaluating a multidisciplinary post-COVID outpatient clinic at a Swiss hospital, following 50 long COVID patients over 6 months with standardized questionnaires and qualitative interviews. Patients showed significant symptom improvement between weeks 4-8 and months 4-6, with most reporting satisfaction with the interprofessional coaching, though cognitive limitations worsened over time.
paper_authors: Markus Wirz; Irina Nast; Anne-Kathrin Rausch; Swantje Beyer; Jürgen Hetzel; Markus Hofer

paper_authors: Adrián Norberto De Paúl
paper_title: Evaluation of the impact of SARS-CoV-2 on licensed nursing professionals in southern Santa Fe

paper_authors: Dan Shan; Carol Holland; Trevor Crawford
paper_title: Treatment Experiences, Preferences, and Expectations for Long COVID Cognitive Impairments: A Constructivist Grounded Theory Study

paper_journal: Proceedings of the Association for Information Science and Technology

paper_title: Treatment Approaches for Long COVID Based on Traditional Medicine  Wisdom: A Case Study of Healer Suphamas Kananurak in Chonburi Province

paper_title: Pulmonary sequelae of COVID-19: An interpretive description study

summary: Qualitative grounded theory study exploring how younger and older UK adults experience and manage long COVID-related cognitive impairment, their coping strategies, and treatment preferences. paper_title: Patient needs and expectations regarding cognitive impairments in long COVID: perspectives of young and older adults in the UK

paper_title: Developing services for long COVID: lessons from a study of wounded healers

summary: This study analyzes 10,670 English-language tweets about long COVID from March-April 2022 to characterize public sentiment and discussion topics. paper_title: Twitter Sentiment Analysis of Long COVID Syndrome

paper_title: Impaired mental health status following intensive care unit admission in a patient with COVID‐19

paper_title: A case of post COVID‐19 subacute thyroiditis

summary: A case report describing a pediatric patient with post-COVID hypertension and hyperreninemic hyperaldosteronism. paper_title: Sarcoidosis following <scp>SARS‐CoV</scp>‐2 infection: Cause or consequence?
