paper_authors: Abdullah Alshablan; Reem Jabbad; Sarah Tayeb; Tariq Albeshri; Suvarna Raju Yelamanchili; Nada Rabie; Fahdah Almutairi; Mohammed Samannodi
paper_title: Diagnosis of Adult Onset Still’s Disease in a Patient Who has recovered from Coronavirus-19

summary: Case report of serpiginous choroiditis (eye inflammation) presenting one month after mild SARS-CoV-2 infection in a previously healthy woman. While the case demonstrates a potential immunological link between COVID-19 and choroidal inflammation, this is a single case report rather than a long COVID study, as it focuses on an acute post-infection complication rather than persistent long COVID syndrome.
paper_authors: Joana Providência; Cristina Fonseca; Filipe Henriques; Rui Proença
paper_title: Serpiginous choroiditis presenting after SARS-CoV-2 infection: A new immunological trigger?

summary: Case report of a 61-year-old patient with post-COVID inattention and fatigue treated with stimulant and antidepressant medications (Methylphenidate, Lisdexamfetamine, and Bupropion). The patient achieved symptom remission, suggesting potential benefit of ADHD-like syndrome treatment approach in post-COVID patients, though the authors acknowledge the need for further research to confirm findings.
paper_authors: Marcelo Moraes Victor; Letícia Müller Haas; Eugenio Horácio Grevet; Luís Augusto Rohde
paper_title: Successful Treatment of Post-COVID-19 ADHD-like Syndrome: A Case Report

summary: Case report of a 23-year-old with long COVID who developed mixed cholestatic-hepatocellular liver injury after recreational kratom use for insomnia. The patient recovered after conservative management and liver function normalized at 3 months, highlighting kratom as a potential cause of acute liver injury in this population.
paper_authors: Yotsapon Thewjitcharoen; Sirinate Krittiyawong; Soontaree Nakasatien; Thep Himathongkam
paper_title: Kratom-Associated Mixed Cholestatic-Hepatocellular Liver Injury in a Patient With Long COVID: A case Report

summary: A case study of patient-led integrated cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) for a 36-year-old male with long COVID and comorbid depression and anxiety, conducted over five months with 12 sessions. The patient showed reliable improvement in somatic symptoms, depression, anxiety, and quality of life.
paper_authors: Lilian Skilbeck
paper_title: Patient-led integrated cognitive behavioural therapy for management of long COVID with comorbid depression and anxiety in primary care - A case study

summary: Case report of a 24-year-old male who developed aquagenic syringeal keratoderma (ASK) 3 months after COVID-19 infection, presenting with palmar edema and white papules triggered by water exposure. Treatment with botulinum toxin injection led to sustained symptom resolution over 7 months, suggesting ASK may be a novel post-acute sequela of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
paper_authors: Bryce W. Polascik; Samantha P. Karklins; Matthew C. Johnson; Warren C. Hammert; Amy J. McMichael
paper_title: Acquired Aquagenic Syringeal Keratoderma Following COVID-19 Infection

summary: Case report of a severely immunized COVID-19 patient who developed progressive lung parenchyma damage over 2.5 months, culminating in massive pneumothorax and respiratory failure. The paper documents acute COVID-19 complications during the active infection phase, not long COVID sequelae.
paper_authors: Maria Iuliana Ghenu; Maria Mirabela Manea; Delia Timofte; Andra-Elena Balcangiu-Stroescu; Dorin Ionescu; Raluca Tulin; Mariana Cătălina Ciornei; Dorin Dragoş
paper_title: Critical Damage of Lung Parenchyma Complicated with Massive Pneumothorax in COVID-19 Pneumonia

summary: Case report of a critically ill patient with acute COVID-19 who developed generalized myoclonus during the recovery phase of active infection. The patient responded to high-dose steroids, but the paper focuses on acute infection complications rather than post-COVID syndrome.
paper_authors: Henly Hewan; Annie Yang; Aparna Vaddiparti; Benison Keung
paper_title: Nonepileptic Myoclonus in COVID-19: Case Report

summary: Case report of a patient with SARS-CoV-2 infection who developed Miller Fisher syndrome with autonomic dysfunction, confirmed anti-ganglioside antibodies, and treated with intravenous immunoglobulin. The paper documents excellent clinical response to IVIG treatment and reviews similar post-COVID Miller Fisher syndrome cases in the literature.
paper_authors: Subhrajyoti Biswas; Ritwik Ghosh; Arpan Mandal; Alak Pandit; Dipayan Roy; Samya Sengupta; Kaustav De; Bikash Chandra Swaika; Julián Benito-León
paper_title: COVID-19 Induced Miller Fisher Syndrome Presenting With Autonomic Dysfunction: A Unique Case Report and Review of Literature

summary: A case report describing a patient with post-COVID acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) affecting the cervicothoracic spinal cord and medulla, presenting with microhemorrhages and hemosiderin deposition. The patient received aggressive immunotherapy to control the inflammatory response.
paper_authors: Spencer Kristian Hutto; Otto Rapalino; Nagagopal Venna
paper_title: Spinomedullary Weston Hurst Syndrome After COVID-19 and Influenza Co-Infection: A Case Report

summary: Case report describing magnetic resonance neurography findings in 2 patients who developed severe peripheral neuropathies during recovery from COVID-19. The paper documents imaging findings and clinical presentation but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Darryl B. Sneag; Christian Geannette; Sophie Queler; Susan Shin; Christopher Winfree; Michael Hausman; Clare Bryce; David Simpson
paper_title: Long-Segment Nonfocal Peripheral Neuropathies After COVID-19 Infection: A Case Report of Magnetic Resonance Neurography Findings
paper_journal: HSS Journal®: The Musculoskeletal Journal of Hospital for Special Surgery

summary: Case report describing a patient who developed psoriatic arthritis following COVID-19 infection, with review of literature on post-COVID rheumatologic manifestations. This is a single case report with no intervention or treatment evaluation, focusing on disease characterization rather than therapeutic outcomes.
paper_authors: Francis Essien; Lisa Chastant; Collen McNulty; Matthew Hubbard; Luria Lynette; Matthew Carroll
paper_title: COVID-19-induced psoriatic arthritis: a case report

summary: Case report of a rheumatoid arthritis patient who developed multiple new-onset autoimmune diseases (autoimmune thyroiditis, LADA, pernicious anemia) following SARS-CoV-2 infection. The paper describes clinical manifestations of post-COVID autoimmune complications but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Gordana Milic; Masa Ristic; Milica Milosevic; Nikola Mitovic; Ljubica Dimitrijevic; Tanja Jesic Petrovic; Bojana Salovic
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 Syndrome Associated With Multiple Autoimmune Diseases (DM I—LADA, Chronic Autoimmune Thyroiditis and Pernicious Anemia): Case Report
paper_journal: Clinical Medicine Insights: Endocrinology and Diabetes

summary: This paper describes a single case of a long COVID patient with SARS-CoV-2 RNA detected in cerebrospinal fluid, suggesting possible viral persistence in the central nervous system. While directly relevant to long COVID pathophysiology, it is a case report without a treatment intervention or control comparison, making it ineligible for the treatment trials analysis.
paper_authors: Daša Viszlayová; Martin Sojka; Silvia Dobrodenková; Szabolcs Szabó; Ondrej Bilec; Mária Turzová; Juraj Ďurina; Barbara Baloghová; Zoltán Borbély; Martin Kršák
paper_title: SARS-CoV-2 RNA in the Cerebrospinal Fluid of a Patient with Long COVID

summary: A case report of a 22-year-old healthcare worker with prolonged multi-systemic long COVID symptoms lasting 18 weeks and persistent SARS-CoV-2 detection for over 110 days. The paper documents clinical presentation and viral shedding duration but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Ayanfe Omololu; Barakah Ojelade; Oluwatomiwa Ajayi; Tolu Adesomi; Oreoluwa Alade; Segun Adebisi; Victor Nwadike
paper_title: “Long COVID”: A case report of persistent symptoms in a patient with prolonged SARS-CoV-2 shedding for over 110 days

summary: Case report of a patient with persistent dyspnea after COVID-19 infection, diagnosed with bilateral diaphragmatic paralysis. The patient was managed with CPAP support and showed symptomatic improvement at 1-year follow-up without specific interventions.
paper_authors: Christine Gill; Alpana Garg; Rami Fakih; Nabeel Y. Hamzeh
paper_title: Bilateral diaphragmatic dysfunction: A cause of persistent dyspnea in patients with post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2

summary: Case report of a 31-year-old woman with incontinentia pigmenti who developed severe COVID-19 and subsequent long COVID symptoms. The paper discusses the potential role of autoimmunity and interferon dysfunction in both conditions but presents only a single patient case without systematic treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Sylvie Rheault
paper_title: Severe COVID-19 and long COVID in a 31-year-old woman with incontinentia pigmenti: A case report

summary: Case report of a 54-year-old man with functional movement disorder (repetitive head flexions) that developed 2 months after acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, accompanied by cognitive impairment, headaches, fatigue, and psychiatric symptoms. Extensive neurological workup was normal, and symptoms persisted at 1-year follow-up, highlighting the neuropsychiatric manifestations and quality-of-life burden of long COVID.
paper_authors: Alpana Garg; Sachin Goyal; Alejandro P. Comellas
paper_title: Post-acute COVID-19 functional movement disorder

summary: Case report of a 51-year-old female with post-COVID-19 acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) presenting with multifocal neurologic symptoms. Early MRI evaluation and glucocorticoid-based treatment led to satisfactory clinical outcomes, demonstrating the importance of timely neurological evaluation and intervention in post-COVID neurological complications.
paper_authors: Aayush Adhikari; Sushil Kumar Yadav; Yashaswi Kafle; Kundan Yadav; Gaurav Nepal; Rajeeb Ojha
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 acute disseminated encephalomyelitis in a 51–year-old female from Nepal: A case report with literature review

summary: A case report describing a woman who developed abnormal uterine bleeding and premature ovarian insufficiency following COVID-19 infection, with suspected autoimmune-mediated mechanisms. The paper highlights post-viral endocrine dysfunction as a long COVID consequence but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Adrianna Clapp; Dani Zapp; Thomas DeLuca; Anjali Morris; Shin jie Yong; Ridwan Ahmad; Bala Munipalli
paper_title: Abnormal uterine bleeding and fertility challenges secondary to long COVID: A case report

summary: Case report of taste impairment in a COVID-19 patient with pre-existing chronic smell loss during acute infection. Does not address long COVID or post-acute sequelae.
paper_authors: Hadar Klein; Noam Karni; Sarah Israel; Menachem Gross; Mordechai Muszkat; Masha Y. Niv
paper_title: Reversible Taste Loss in a COVID-19 Patient With Preexisting Chronic Smell Impairment
paper_journal: Journal of Investigative Medicine High Impact Case Reports

summary: Case report of a young male who developed diabetes insipidus and myocarditis as late sequelae of COVID-19 infection. The patient recovered following treatment with desmopressin, demonstrating successful management of this rare post-COVID endocrine complication.
paper_authors: Abu Baker Sheikh; Nismat Javed; Abdul Ahad Ehsan Sheikh; Shubhra Upadhyay; Rahul Shekhar
paper_title: Diabetes Insipidus and Concomitant Myocarditis: A Late Sequelae of COVID-19 Infection
paper_journal: Journal of Investigative Medicine High Impact Case Reports

summary: Case report of a 65-year-old COVID-19 patient who developed post-infectious encephalitis with delirium one week after discharge from severe pneumonia. Patient was treated with intravenous methylprednisolone and immunoglobulin therapy and recovered, demonstrating immunosuppressive therapy as an intervention for post-COVID neurological complications.
paper_authors: Makoto Hara; Kento Kouda; Tomotaka Mizoguchi; Yuki Yokota; Kentaro Hayashi; Yasuhiro Gon; Hideto Nakajima
paper_title: COVID-19 Post-Infectious Encephalitis Presenting With Delirium as an Initial Manifestation
paper_journal: Journal of Investigative Medicine High Impact Case Reports

summary: Case report of an infant with febrile status epilepticus and MIS-C (Multi-system Inflammatory Syndrome in Children) occurring 2-4 weeks post-COVID, presenting with bilateral brain MRI abnormalities. Patient improved with pulse steroids and IVIg, but this describes acute post-infectious MIS-C, not long COVID (chronic persistent symptoms months later).
paper_authors: Holly C. Appleberry; Alexis Begezda; Helen Cheung; Soriayah Zaghab-Mathews; Gayatra Mainali
paper_title: Report of a Child With Febrile Status Epilepticus and Post-COVID Multi-System Inflammatory Syndrome

summary: Case report of a 12-year-old girl who developed Type 1 Diabetes and morphea (scleroderma) following mild COVID-19 infection, attributed to autoimmune activation during long COVID. The paper documents the clinical presentation and course but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Ievgeniia Burlaka; Inga Mityuryayeva; Olena Sevastiian; Ivanna Kachula
paper_title: Onset of Type I Diabetes Followed by Scleroderma Syndrome in a Child After the COVID-19: A Case Report

summary: A case report describing a single immunocompromised patient with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma who developed post-COVID interstitial lung disease (PC-ILD) with prolonged viral shedding. The paper documents the patient's clinical course and pathophysiology but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention or trial design.
paper_authors: John S. Dayco; Zeinab El-Reda; Nabeel Sumbal; Rashid Alhusain; Shaheena Raheem
paper_title: Perpetually Positive: Post-COVID Interstitial Lung Disease in an Immunocompromised Patient With Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma
paper_journal: Journal of Investigative Medicine High Impact Case Reports

summary: Case report of a 73-year-old male who developed secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (sHLH) 11 months after recovering from COVID-19 infection. The patient was treated with dexamethasone, transfusions, filgrastim, and intravenous immunoglobulin but ultimately deteriorated and died, illustrating the severe complications and high mortality of delayed sHLH in post-acute COVID-19 patients.
paper_authors: Mohamed Zakee Mohamed Jiffry; Mohammad Aimal Ahmed-khan; Jonathan Alejandro Vargas; Teena Thomas; Susanna Josey
paper_title: Hemophagocytic Lymphohystiocytosis in a Patient with Post-Acute COVID-19 Infection

summary: Case report of a 69-year-old woman presenting with life-threatening ventricular tachycardia and aortitis in the weeks following mild COVID-19 infection, treated with radiofrequency ablation and long-term corticosteroids. While the case occurs in the post-COVID period, it focuses on acute multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS-A) rather than long COVID, which is characterized by persistent symptoms weeks to months after infection.
paper_authors: Simon E. Melchior; Mikkel M. Schoos; Uffe Gang; Peter K. Jacobsen; Lothar Wiese; Thomas Maria Melchior
paper_title: Recurring episodes of bundle branch reentry ventricular tachycardia due to aortitis preceded by SARS-CoV-2 infection: a case report

summary: Case report of a patient with MOG antibody-positive optic neuritis that developed post-COVID-19, treated with methylprednisolone and intravenous immunoglobulin. While this describes a complication occurring after acute COVID-19 infection, it does not study long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks/months post-infection) but rather an acute/subacute post-infection neurological condition in a single case.
paper_authors: Ankit Bhardwaj; Hara Prasad Mishra; Ayush Goel; Ashi Gupta
paper_title: COVID-19 – a potential trigger for MOGAD-associated optic neuritis: a case report and literature review

summary: Case report of a non-severe COVID-19 patient who developed persistent thrombocytopenia (low platelet count) for several months after viral clearance, representing a long COVID sequela. The patient was treated with glucocorticoids (prednisone) with eventual improvement, highlighting immune system involvement in post-COVID complications.
paper_authors: Xia Wu; Dongxia Luo; Yaling Liu; Yilan Zeng; Yuping Gong
paper_title: Continuous thrombocytopenia after SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid negative in a non-severe COVID-19 patient for several months

summary: Case report of a 77-year-old male who developed restless anal syndrome (a variant of restless legs syndrome) several weeks after COVID-19 recovery. The patient was successfully treated with clonazepam 1.5 mg per day, with resolution of symptoms.
paper_authors: Itaru Nakamura; Takao Itoi; Takeshi Inoue
paper_title: Case report of restless anal syndrome as restless legs syndrome variant after COVID-19

summary: A case report describing a 27-year-old runner who developed severe dysautonomia five weeks after mild COVID-19 infection, presenting with orthostatic intolerance, tachycardia, and post-exertional fatigue. The patient showed improvement over months with fluid/sodium intake, compression stockings, and a graduated exercise program.
paper_authors: Joan Bosco; Ruwanthi Titano
paper_title: Severe Post-COVID-19 dysautonomia: a case report

summary: A case report of a 62-year-old patient who developed subacute cerebellar ataxia one day after resolution of acute COVID-19 respiratory symptoms, with laboratory findings suggesting post-infectious immune-mediated etiology. The patient showed rapid improvement following high-dose methylprednisolone therapy, suggesting corticosteroids as a potential treatment for post-COVID neurological complications.
paper_authors: Jana Werner; Ina Reichen; Michael Huber; Irene A. Abela; Michael Weller; Ilijas Jelcic
paper_title: Subacute cerebellar ataxia following respiratory symptoms of COVID-19: a case report

summary: This case report describes a single patient with acute COVID-19 presenting with persistent dyspnea caused by an intrapulmonary right-to-left shunt (Acute Vascular Distress Syndrome). The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 pathophysiology and diagnosis during active infection, not long COVID or post-acute sequelae.

summary: Case report of a 73-year-old female with post-COVID-19 encephalopathy presenting with cognitive decline, depression, and oral cenesthopathy 16 months post-infection. Treatment with Aripiprazole and Carbamazepine resulted in partial symptom improvement.
paper_authors: Ju-I Wu; Shwu-Hua Lee; Pei-Jung Chen
paper_title: Case report: post COVID-19 encephalopathy and oral cenesthopathy

summary: A case report of a 62-year-old patient with long COVID presenting with dyspnea and bilateral lung infiltrates who was found to have Tropheryma whipplei infection on lung biopsy. The report documents a serious long-term complication of COVID-19 involving thromboembolism but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Multiple simultaneous embolic cerebral infarctions 11 months after COVID-19

summary: This paper reports a single case of a 21-year-old female with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome presenting with a right atrioventricular thrombus and pulmonary embolism, complicated by an underlying cardiac myxoma. The case illustrates potential thrombotic complications in the post-acute phase of COVID-19 but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Ghaliya Mohamed H. Alrifae; Amel Ahmed Said Almuquddami; Khaled Masaud Etaleb; Mohamed Hadi Mohamed Abdelhamid
paper_title: Post-Acute COVID-19 syndrome (PACS) right atrioventricular and vena cava thrombus on top of a myxoma. A Case report

summary: Case report of a 51-year-old male presenting with persistent dyspnea and widespread pulmonary embolism seven weeks after suspected COVID-19 infection. Documents a single case of long COVID-associated thrombotic complication treated with anticoagulation, highlighting PE as a potential long-term sequela.
paper_authors: Mats Beckman; Sven Nyrén; Anna Kistner
paper_title: A case-report of widespread pulmonary embolism in a middle-aged male seven weeks after asymptomatic suspected COVID 19 infection

summary: Case report of a 9-year-old with bilateral anterior intermediate uveitis occurring 1 month after recovery from MIS-C, treated with topical difluprednate and immunosuppression. While this describes a post-viral complication and treatment, it is a single case report focused on an acute inflammatory syndrome (MIS-C) rather than long COVID, which is characterized by chronic sequelae weeks to months after acute infection.
paper_authors: Jessica Shantha; Amit K. Reddy; Amol Sura; Adrian Tsang; Kareem Moussa; Nisha Acharya; John Gonzales; Thuy Doan
paper_title: Bilateral anterior and intermediate uveitis in SARS-CoV-2 associated multisystem inflammatory syndrome in a pediatric patient

summary: Case report of a 55-year-old woman who developed myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) following SARS-CoV-2 infection and recovered after multimodal treatment including dietary modifications, cognitive-behavioral interventions, conditioning exercises, and pharmacotherapy (amitriptyline and Kampo medicine). The paper presents therapeutic options for managing disabling symptoms in post-COVID ME/CFS patients.
paper_authors: Takakazu Oka
paper_title: A patient who recovered from post-COVID myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome: a case report

summary: Case report of a 34-year-old patient who developed penile Mondor disease (superficial vein thrombophlebitis) one month after COVID-19 infection, suggesting COVID-19 as a prothrombotic risk factor. The patient was treated pharmacologically and achieved complete recovery with clot dissolution confirmed on ultrasound.
paper_authors: Krzysztof Balawender; Anna Pliszka; Agata Surowiec; Sebastian Rajda
paper_title: COVID-19 infection as a new risk factor for penile Mondor disease

summary: Case report of a 9-year-old girl with abducens nerve palsy following COVID-19 infection, with improvement at 2-month follow-up. Discusses possible post-infectious immune-mediated mechanism but presents no treatment intervention or controlled study design.
paper_authors: Martina Capponi; Bianca Laura Cinicola; Giulia Brindisi; Cristiana Alessia Guido; Maria Cristina Torcé; Anna Maria Zicari; Alberto Spalice
paper_title: COVID-19 and abducens nerve palsy in a 9-year-old girl—case report

summary: A case report describing the use of dry and wet needling (trigger point injections) to treat myofascial pain in a long COVID patient. Both interventions showed good short- and long-term therapeutic effects in reducing the patient's myalgia symptoms.
paper_authors: Mengyi Zha; Kristina Chaffee; Jude Alsarraj
paper_title: Trigger point injections and dry needling can be effective in treating long COVID syndrome-related myalgia: a case report

summary: A case report of a patient who developed ventricular tachycardia and cardiac fibrosis 6 months after mild COVID-19 infection. The case illustrates potential long-term cardiac involvement in post-COVID patients but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Jonathan Solaimanzadeh; Aaron Freilich; Michael R. Sood
paper_title: Ventricular tachycardia with epicardial and pericardial fibrosis 6 months after resolution of subclinical COVID-19: a case report

summary: A case report of a 29-year-old male who developed cavitary lung disease as a late complication months after COVID-19 recovery, initially unresponsive to conservative management. The patient ultimately required surgical intervention (lung decortication) with gradual improvement on combined medical and surgical therapy.
paper_authors: Goar Egoryan; Elise Hyser; Ammar H. Mushtaq; Maria Adriana Yanez-Bello; Daniela Patricia Trelles-Garcia; Harvey J. Friedman; Guillermo Rodriguez-Nava
paper_title: Development of cavitary lung disease as a long-term complication of coronavirus disease 2019 in a young previously healthy patient: a case report

summary: A case report of a long COVID patient who developed collagenous gastritis associated with Epstein-Barr virus reactivation following SARS-CoV-2 infection. The patient was treated with corticosteroids, proton pump inhibitors, and iron supplementation with improvement.
paper_authors: Ashten Duncan; Ivonne Veli; Dathan Tsosie; Elizabeth Koffler
paper_title: Probable collagenous gastritis via Epstein–Barr virus reactivation in the setting of coronavirus disease 2019: a case report

summary: A case report of a 27-year-old male presenting with persistent hiccups 35 days post-COVID-19 (a post-acute sequela), successfully treated with chlorpromazine 25 mg. The case documents an atypical and rare manifestation of long COVID and its pharmacological management.
paper_authors: Ireen Chanda Bwalya
paper_title: Persistent hiccups after acute COVID-19 successfully treated with chlorpromazine: a case report

summary: A case report of a 55-year-old long COVID patient treated with 60 sessions of hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT), showing significant improvements in brain perfusion, cognitive function (particularly nonverbal memory and executive function), and cardiopulmonary capacity (34% increase in VO2 max, 44% improvement in forced vital capacity). The authors acknowledge this is a single case and call for prospective randomized controlled trials to validate the findings.
paper_authors: Aisha M. Bhaiyat; Efrat Sasson; Zemer Wang; Sherif Khairy; Mouzayan Ginzarly; Umair Qureshi; Moin Fikree; Shai Efrati
paper_title: Hyperbaric oxygen treatment for long coronavirus disease-19: a case report

summary: A case report of anesthetic management for transurethral prostate resection in a COVID-19 survivor with aortic dissection. The paper describes clinical presentation and surgical management of a single patient rather than a treatment trial or systematic evaluation of an intervention.
paper_authors: Shagun Bhatia Shah; Itee Chowdhury; Venkatesh Pally; Chamound Rai Jain
paper_title: Anesthetic implications for transurethral resection of prostate in a COVID-19 survivor with Stanford-A aortic dissection with acute urinary retention due to metastatic carcinoma prostate: a case report

summary: A case report of rehabilitation therapy in a severe acute COVID-19 patient who regained physical function after discharge. The paper focuses on acute-phase recovery and muscle rehabilitation during the immediate post-infection period, not long COVID or persistent post-acute sequelae.
paper_authors: Toru Takekawa; Kazumi Kashiwabara; Naoki Yamada; Shu Watanabe; Midori Hama; Gentaro Hashimoto; Masahiro Abo; Kyota Shinfuku
paper_title: Rehabilitation therapy for a severe case of coronavirus disease 2019: a case report

summary: Case report of a 73-year-old woman with gastric cancer who developed orthostatic hypotonia as a late sequela of SARS-CoV-2 infection. Treatment with thiethylperazine maleate and nonpharmacological measures (postural changes, dietary modifications, fluid intake) resulted in sustained symptom relief.

It raises CMD as a potential etiologic factor in long COVID syndrome but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Maan Malahfji; Valentina Crudo; Ahmed Ibrahim Ahmed; Mujtaba Saeed; Jean Michel Saad; William A. Zoghbi; Mouaz H. Al-Mallah
paper_title: Coronary microvascular dysfunction and COVID-19: implications for long COVID patients

summary: This observational cohort study identifies persistent neurocognitive deficits in non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients, with 14 of the first 100 enrolled participants reporting cognitive issues lasting a median of 98 days post-infection. The study characterizes the nature and duration of cognitive symptoms but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Hellmuth J.; Barnett TA; Asken BM; Kelly JD; Torres L.; Stephens ML; Greenhouse B.; Martin JN; Chow FC; Deeks SG; Greene M.; Miller BL; Annan W.; Henrich TJ; Peluso MJ
paper_title: Persistent COVID-19-associated neurocognitive symptoms in non-hospitalized patients

summary: Case report of two patients who developed acute transverse myelitis 10 days after acute COVID-19 infection, treated with high-dose corticosteroids. Both patients showed rapid recovery, but this describes acute post-infectious complications during active infection rather than long COVID (weeks-to-months persistent symptoms).
paper_authors: Thaís de Maria Frota Vasconcelos; Danilo Nunes Oliveira; Glauber de Menezes Ferreira; Fabrícia Carneiro Torres; José Daniel Vieira de Castro; Pedro Braga-Neto; Manoel Alves Sobreira-Neto
paper_title: Covid-19 post-infectious acute transverse myelitis responsive to corticosteroid therapy: report of two clinical cases

summary: Case series of five patients with post-COVID-19 myelopathy and myeloradiculopathy following mild-to-moderate acute infection, all with negative MRI findings. The paper documents clinical presentations and raises questions about pathophysiology but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Rory M. C. Abrams; Farinaz Safavi; Stanley Tuhrim; Allison Navis; Jeremy Steinberger; Susan C. Shin
paper_title: MRI negative myelopathy post mild SARS-CoV-2 infection: vasculopathy or inflammatory myelitis?

summary: This paper describes tracheal resection and reconstruction outcomes in 15 patients with post-intubation tracheal stenosis, 7 of whom had COVID-19-related intubation. The study found no significant differences in surgical outcomes between COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 patients, demonstrating that the procedure can be safely performed in both groups.
paper_authors: Muhammet Ali Beyoglu; Mehmet Furkan Sahin; Sinan Turkkan; Alkin Yazicioglu; Erdal Yekeler
paper_title: Complex Post-intubation Tracheal Stenosis in Covid-19 Patients

summary: A case report of a dialysis patient with preexisting adrenal insufficiency who developed post-COVID-19 syndrome with persistent fatigue, requiring significantly increased corticosteroid dosages to manage hypotension and stabilize hemodynamics. The case illustrates the clinical challenge of managing adrenal insufficiency in the context of concomitant long COVID syndrome.
paper_authors: Eriko Eguchi
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 syndrome increased the requirement for corticosteroids in a dialysis patient with preexisting adrenal insufficiency

summary: A case report of a hemodialysis patient who developed hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) during COVID-19 treatment, documented over one month post-infection onset. The patient was treated with methylprednisolone pulse therapy followed by combination immunosuppressive therapy (prednisolone and cyclosporine) and survived, demonstrating HLH as a potential post-acute COVID-19 complication.
paper_authors: Satoru Kaneko; Tsutomu Inoue; Norihito Tarumoto; Yoshiyuki Haga; Kazuhiro Yokota; Hiroshi Yamaguchi; Hirokazu Okada
paper_title: A case of hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis in a hemodialysis patient with coronavirus disease 2019

summary: Case report of a 69-year-old male presenting with systemic and cerebral vasculitis as a post-acute COVID-19 manifestation, diagnosed 6 weeks after mild infection. Patient was treated with high-dose corticosteroids and therapeutic plasma exchange, showing clinical response to intervention.
paper_authors: Jovana Ivanovic; Maja Stojanovic; Aleksandar Ristic; Dragoslav Sokic; Nikola Vojvodic
paper_title: Post-acute COVID-19 syndrome presented as a cerebral and systemic vasculitis: a case report

summary: Case series of three post-COVID patients with neuropsychiatric symptoms (seizures, insomnia, attention difficulties) treated with TNF-α inhibitor (Adalimumab). All patients showed dramatic improvement in symptoms following treatment, suggesting TNF inhibitors may be effective for post-COVID neuropsychiatric complications.
paper_authors: Gita Shafiee; Tohid Arastou; Ramin Heshmat; Ahmad Reza Jamshidi; Bagher Larijani; Seyed Masoud Arzaghi
paper_title: Post COVID-19 neuropsychiatric complications and therapeutic role for TNF-α inhibitors: a case series study

summary: This case series followed 13 COVID-19 pneumonia survivors to assess respiratory function recovery at clinical recovery, 6 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months post-discharge. Patients showed significant improvement in FEV1, FVC, and FEV1/FVC ratios over the 12-month follow-up period, with residual restrictive pattern at 6 weeks resolving substantially by 12 months.
paper_authors: Alessia Fumagalli; Clementina Misuraca; Achille Bianchi; Noemi Borsa; Simone Limonta; Sveva Maggiolini; Daniela Rita Bonardi; Andrea Corsonello; Mirko Di Rosa; Luca Soraci; Fabrizia Lattanzio; Daniele Colombo
paper_title: Long-term changes in pulmonary function among patients surviving to COVID-19 pneumonia

summary: This case study uses electrical impedance tomography (EIT) to visualize lung ventilation patterns in a post-COVID patient with exertional dyspnea compared to a healthy control during treadmill exercise. The authors demonstrate that EIT can detect abnormal ventilation distribution and conclude it may be useful as a diagnostic tool, but this is a descriptive case report with no intervention or treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Yvonne Gremme; Steffen Derlien; Katrin Katzer; Philipp A. Reuken; Andreas Stallmach; Jan-Christoph Lewejohann; Christina Lemhöfer
paper_title: Visualizing exertional dyspnea in a post-COVID patient using electrical impedance tomography

summary: Case report of two patients with LMNA p.R349W mutation who developed severe cardiovascular complications weeks after mild SARS-CoV-2 infection. Highlights elevated cardiac risk in lipodystrophy patients with underlying morbidities post-COVID, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Ceccarini G.; Gilio D.; Magno S.; Pelosini C.; Leverone M.; Miceli C.; Barison A.; Fabiani I.; Emdin M.; Santini F.
paper_title: Post-acute cardiac complications following SARS-CoV-2 infection in partial lipodystrophy due to LMNA gene p.R349W mutation

summary: A case report of a 60-year-old female who developed central diabetes insipidus with infundibuloneurohypophysitis 8 weeks after recovering from COVID-19 infection. The patient was successfully treated with oral desmopressin and showed prompt response with sustained improvement over 5+ months of follow-up.
paper_authors: Misgar RA; Rasool A.; Wani AI; Bashir MI
paper_title: Central diabetes insipidus (Infundibuloneuro hypophysitis): A late complication of COVID-19 infection

summary: A case report of a 44-year-old male with pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP) developing after COVID-19 recovery, initially misdiagnosed as post-COVID syndrome. The patient was successfully treated with left lung lavage in combination with conventional therapy, with significant clinical improvement during follow-up.
paper_authors: Bao Le-Khac; Quoc-Khanh Tran-Le; Lam Nguyen-Ho; Sy Duong-Quy
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis Treated Successfully with Whole Lung Lavage: A Rare Case Report

summary: This is a narrative piece about nurses with long COVID sharing their personal experiences and recovery journeys. It is an editorial/opinion article rather than a research study and does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Edith Tulp; Jeroen Wagenaar
paper_title: Verpleegkundigen met long covid

summary: Case report of a 32-year-old woman with long COVID presenting with persistent cardiac symptoms (chest pain, palpitations, dyspnea on exertion) and fatigue following overexertion during recovery. Treatment with acupuncture is described for managing her long COVID symptoms.
paper_authors: Claudia Lazar
paper_title: Einsatz von Akupunktur bei Long Covid

summary: This paper proposes a 6-week immersive VR-based cognitive intervention for post-COVID-19 condition and presents initial results through a single case report of a 46-year-old female. The patient showed improvements in attention, executive functions, and processing speed, with reductions in perceived cognitive deficits and depression, though the paper is primarily a protocol paper with limited case data.
paper_authors: Kinga Nedda Pete; János Tamás Varga; Zsuzsanna Valachiné Geréb; Orsolya Gőbel; Cecília Sik-Lanyi; Veronika Müller; Renáta Cserjési
paper_title: Immersive virtual reality intervention to enhance cognitive-affective neuropsychological functions in post-COVID-19 condition: Research protocol and a case report

summary: A case series describing eyelid myokymia (involuntary eyelid twitching) in 15 patients during or immediately after COVID-19 recovery. The study found that myokymia resolved within 3 months in most patients, with older age and longer hospitalization associated with slower recovery, but no intervention or treatment was tested.
paper_authors: Hashim Ali Khan; Muhammad Aamir Shahzad; Smaha Jahangir; Junaid Iqbal; Suhail Abbas Juwa; Qaim Ali Khan; Munib-ur-Rehman; Naeemullah Khan; Muhammad Afzal; Fatima Iqbal
paper_title: Eyelid Myokymia—a Presumed Manifestation of Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19)

summary: Case report describing a 38-year-old man who developed long-term neurological symptoms (syncopes, paresis, vision loss, fatigue, dizziness) following BNT162b2 vaccination, with symptom exacerbation after subsequent COVID-19 infection. The paper discusses potential shared pathophysiology between vaccine adverse reactions and post-COVID syndrome but presents only a single clinical case without systematic evaluation of treatment or intervention outcomes.
paper_authors: Tobias Weirauch; Gundolf Schüttfort; Maria J. G. T. Vehreschild
paper_title: Syncopes, paresis and loss of vision after COVID-19 mRNA-based vaccination and SARS-CoV-2 infection

summary: This retrospective study identifies 13 cases of jaw osteonecrosis (post-COVID osteonecrosis of the jaw, PCONJ) occurring up to 21 months after severe COVID-19 in patients who received steroid treatment. The authors propose that a triad of post-COVID coagulopathy, steroid administration, and provocative dental treatment may contribute to this complication.
paper_authors: Mohd Aswad Khan; Tabishur Rahman; Sajjad Abdur Rahman; Ghulam Sarwar Hashmi; Md Kalim Ansari; Mohammad Danish; Mohammad Arman; Rizwan Ahmad; Wasim Ahmad
paper_title: Is post-COVID osteonecrosis of jaw (PCONJ) Masquerading as osteomyelitis ? A largest unicentric report of 13 cases
paper_journal: Advances in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery

summary: Case series of six patients with functional neurological disorders after COVID-19 infection or vaccination, combined with a literature review of reported cases. The paper describes clinical presentations and symptomatology but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Sergiu Albu; Margarita Vallès; Hatice Kumru
paper_title: Diagnostic challenges of functional neurological disorders after covid-19 disease or vaccination: case series and review of the literature

summary: Case series describing four children presenting with prolonged fever and inflammatory shock-like states 1 month after COVID-19 infection, characterized by elevated cytokines (IL-6, IL-8, TNF-α). The condition overlaps with Kawasaki Disease and Toxic Shock Syndrome, representing acute post-infectious inflammation rather than long COVID sequelae.
paper_authors: Temima Waltuch; Prakriti Gill; Lauren E. Zinns; Rachel Whitney; Julia Tokarski; James W. Tsung; Jennifer E. Sanders
paper_title: Features of COVID-19 post-infectious cytokine release syndrome in children presenting to the emergency department
paper_journal: The American Journal of Emergency Medicine

summary: This pilot case series evaluates transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) as a treatment for neuropsychiatric symptoms in 23 long-COVID patients in Japan, primarily targeting chronic fatigue and cognitive dysfunction. Results show improvements in depression, fatigue, and cognitive function scores with no serious adverse events, supporting further investigation in randomized controlled trials.
paper_authors: Yoshihiro Noda; Akiko Sato; Misaki Shichi; Ayano Sato; Kyoshiro Fujii; Mio Iwasa; Yasuhiro Nagano; Ryosuke Kitahata; Ryota Osawa
paper_title: Real world research on transcranial magnetic stimulation treatment strategies for neuropsychiatric symptoms with long-COVID in Japan

summary: Autopsy study of fatal COVID-19 cases (27-51 days post-admission) examining lung tissue remodeling patterns, showing basal epithelial cell hyperplasia and immune activation. This is a post-mortem pathological analysis without any treatment intervention or clinical trial design.
paper_authors: Kangyun Wu; Yong Zhang; Stephen R. Austin; Huiqing Yin-Declue; Derek E. Byers; Erika C. Crouch; Michael J. Holtzman
paper_title: Lung Remodeling Regions in Long-Term Coronavirus Disease 2019 Feature Basal Epithelial Cell Reprogramming

summary: Case report describing two patients who developed avascular necrosis of the hip following COVID-19 treatment with corticosteroids. Discusses the pathological mechanisms and clinical management of this long COVID complication.
paper_authors: Prathiba Annam; Anusha Manda; Uday Krishna Myneni; Aaminah Najmus Sahar; Nagendra Prasad; Kezia K. Sam; Sambit Sahu; Kiran Kumar Reddy
paper_title: Corticosteroids induced avascular necrosis of hip, a “long COVID-19” complication: Case report

summary: A case series documenting two cases of chronic inducible urticaria (CIndU) following COVID-19 infection and mRNA vaccination, with treatment outcomes. Both patients were managed with antihistamines (cetirizine), with one showing symptom improvement and the other experiencing persistent symptoms despite treatment.
paper_authors: T. Hellu; S. Weiss; K. Adams
paper_title: A CASE SERIES: CHRONIC INDUCIBLE URTICARIA FOLLOWING COVID-19 INFECTION AND MRNA VACCINE

summary: Case report of a 3-year-old with Guillain-Barré syndrome occurring two weeks after COVID-19 infection, demonstrating a post-COVID neurological complication. Patient recovered favorably after intravenous immunoglobulin treatment, suggesting a causal link between COVID-19 and GBS development.
paper_authors: Sanae El Mezzeoui; Fatima zahra Aftiss; Mohammed Aabdi; Houssam Bkiyar; Brahim Housni
paper_title: Guillan barre syndrome in post Covid-19 infection in children

summary: Case series reporting that plasma exchange improves cognitive function in long COVID patients with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome and autoimmune neurological dysfunction. Demonstrates potential therapeutic benefit of plasma exchange for a subset of long COVID patients with autoimmune features.
paper_authors: Marie-Claire Seeley; Matthew Hooper; Jason Tan; Rachel Wells; Celine Gallagher; Dennis H. Lau
paper_title: Plasma Exchange Improves Cognitive Function in Long-COVID-Related Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome and Autoimmune Neurological Dysfunction

summary: Monocentric observational study of 33 post-COVID-19 myocarditis patients examining ejection fraction recovery and prognostic factors at 3-month follow-up. While descriptive of disease evolution, this is a secondary analysis of cardiac outcomes in post-COVID patients rather than an evaluation of a specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Zaoui N.; Bachir N.; Terki A.; Boukabous A.
paper_title: Myocardite à COVID-19 : « à propos d'une série monocentrique de 33 cas »

summary: Case report of six COVID-19 patients who developed post-intubation laryngeal injury (PI-LI) presenting with persistent dyspnea after recovery from acute infection. Four patients required surgical intervention; the paper highlights the need for otolaryngologists to assess the larynx in post-COVID patients presenting with dyspnea.
paper_authors: Naoyuki Sakihama; Ryuhei Okada; Naoto Takahashi; Naoki Fushimi; Tomoki Ooka; Hiroaki Kawabe; Yosuke Ariizumi; Kazuchika Ohno; Yutaka Ueki; Niro Tayama; Takeshi Tsutsumi; Takahiro Asakage
paper_title: Post-intubation laryngeal injury after COVID-19 treatment causing dyspnea: A report of six cases

summary: This paper presents a case report of rapidly progressing diabetic retinopathy following severe COVID-19 infection with long-COVID sequelae. It is a descriptive case study without intervention or treatment evaluation, focusing on the potential mechanism of accelerated retinal pathology due to hypoxia.
paper_authors: Clayton E. Lyons; Ivy Zhu; Manjot K. Gill
paper_title: Accelerated progression of diabetic retinopathy following severe COVID-19 infection
paper_journal: American Journal of Ophthalmology Case Reports

summary: This paper describes pseudo-chilblain (pseudo-engelures) and other acute cutaneous manifestations in children during the early SARS-CoV-2 epidemic (April-June 2020). It documents clinical features and inflammatory markers in a case series but does not study long COVID (persistent post-acute sequelae) or test any intervention.
paper_authors: L. Fertitta; Arnaud Welfringer; Laura Polivka; Stéphanie Chhun; Amani Ouedrani; Lucienne Chatenoud; S. Hadj‐Rabia; Isabelle Sermet‐Gaudelus; Christine Bodemer
paper_title: Pseudo-engelures de l’enfant et SARS-CoV-2 : quel lien ?
paper_journal: Annales de Dermatologie et de Vénéréologie

summary: Case series reporting three index cases of severe long COVID patients who experienced complete remission of symptoms within days to a week following monoclonal antibody (casirivimab/imdevimab) infusions. The authors present clinical signals suggesting potential efficacy of MCA treatment for certain long COVID cases and discuss mechanistic implications for post-viral chronic conditions.
paper_authors: Kenneth A. Scheppke; Paul E. Pepe; Jonathan Jui; Remle P. Crowe; Eric K. Scheppke; Nancy G. Klimas; Aileen M. Marty
paper_title: Remission of severe forms of long COVID following monoclonal antibody (MCA) infusions: A report of signal index cases and call for targeted research
paper_journal: The American Journal of Emergency Medicine

summary: Case series of 9 severe COVID-19 patients assessing cognitive functioning 30+ days post-hospitalization for acute respiratory distress syndrome. Found cognitive decline in 33% of patients, with deficits correlated to ICU length of stay, but acknowledges results are preliminary and calls for larger future studies rather than presenting treatment intervention outcomes.
paper_authors: Francesco Negrini; Irene Ferrario; Daniele Mazziotti; Marzia Berchicci; Maurizio Bonazzi; Alessandro de Sire; Stefano Negrini; Laura Zapparoli
paper_title: Neuropsychological Features of Severe Hospitalized Coronavirus Disease 2019 Patients at Clinical Stability and Clues for Postacute Rehabilitation
paper_journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation

summary: This case series reports on 4 patients with persistent post-COVID olfactory dysfunction unresponsive to medical therapy who underwent endoscopic sinus surgery to address olfactory cleft adhesions. All patients showed significant subjective improvement in olfaction within one week and objective test score improvements over subsequent months, suggesting surgical intervention may benefit carefully selected long-COVID patients with prolonged anosmia and CT-confirmed cleft obstruction.
paper_authors: Tanaka H.; Kubota E.; Otori N.; Mori E.
paper_title: Olfactory cleft adhesion in post-COVID-19 olfactory dysfunction
paper_journal: European Annals of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Diseases

summary: Case series of five long COVID patients with visual dysfunction (blurred vision, diplopia, photophobia, near-point focus impairment) treated in acute and outpatient rehabilitation settings. All five patients showed confirmatory findings on comprehensive visual assessment, highlighting visual impairment as an underrecognized sequela of COVID-19 requiring systematic screening.
paper_authors: Jaimee Perea; Min Jeong Graf; John Ross Rizzo
paper_title: Visual dysfunction in survivors of COVID-19: Case series
paper_journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation

summary: Retrospective case series examining autonomic function testing findings in 14 long-COVID patients with orthostatic intolerance using autonomic reflex screening and tilt table testing. Most patients (57%) showed symptoms without demonstrable orthostatic abnormalities, and only 3 met POTS criteria.
paper_authors: Ahmed M. Eldokla; Sara T. Ali
paper_title: Autonomic function testing in long-COVID syndrome patients with orthostatic intolerance

summary: This paper describes the implementation of a multidisciplinary post-COVID clinic in a small rural community, detailing the roles of various healthcare providers (PM&R, physical therapy, speech therapy, respiratory therapy, psychology) in treating long COVID patients. It is a clinical implementation guide rather than a treatment evaluation study, with no comparative data or trial results.
paper_authors: Ellen Price; Nikos Hollis; Joseph Salganik; Megan Lykke; Cheryl Paolinelli; Stuart Chamovitz; Clay King; Richard Ott
paper_title: Implementing a Multidisciplinary Post-COVID Clinic in a Small Community Environment
paper_journal: Archives of Rehabilitation Research and Clinical Translation

summary: A case series of 13 long COVID patients who received individualized multidisciplinary outpatient cognitive rehabilitation at Mayo Clinic, with assessments at admission and discharge using standardized instruments (MPAI-4, SWLS, PHQ-9, NSI-22). The study found no clear benefit in any of the outcome measures after cognitive therapy.
paper_authors: Ellen Farr; Dmitry Esterov; Blake A. Kassmeyer; Ryan J. Lennon; Thomas F. Bergquist
paper_title: Demographics, Clinical Characteristics, and Outcomes of a Post-Coronavirus-19 Sample After Cognitive Rehabilitation: A Case Series
paper_journal: Archives of Rehabilitation Research and Clinical Translation

summary: Retrospective chart review of 6 months of patients treated with bilateral stellate ganglion blockade (SGB) for long COVID symptoms, with self-reported outcomes on a 10-point scale. Patients reported significant reductions in fatigue, cognitive problems, sleep disturbance, anxiety, and depression, though taste and smell loss did not respond to treatment.
paper_authors: Deborah Duricka; Luke Liu
paper_title: Reduction of long COVID symptoms after stellate ganglion block: A retrospective chart review study

summary: This paper presents a case series of 100 post-COVID syndrome patients and includes a systematic review and meta-analysis of 40 articles (11,196 patients) examining symptom prevalence and clinical characteristics. No specific treatment intervention was tested; the study characterizes the disease presentation and confirms long-term antibody responses.
paper_authors: Juan-Manuel Anaya; Manuel Rojas; Martha L. Salinas; Yhojan Rodríguez; Geraldine Roa; Marcela Lozano; Mónica Rodríguez-Jiménez; Norma Montoya; Elizabeth Zapata; Diana M. Monsalve; Yeny Acosta-Ampudia; Carolina Ramírez-Santana
paper_title: Post-COVID syndrome. A case series and comprehensive review

summary: A case series evaluating the feasibility and tolerability of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) using intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) in four patients with post-COVID-19 condition. Active stimulation showed positive trends in cognitive interference, quality of life, and anxiety compared to sham, with no adverse events reported.
paper_authors: Mohammad Nazmus Sakib; Ashish Saragadam; Mariella C. Santagata; Marie Jolicoeur-Becotte; Lena Kozyr; Amer M. Burhan; Peter A. Hall
paper_title: rTMS for post-covid-19 condition: A sham-controlled case series involving iTBS-300 and iTBS-600

summary: This paper reports 3 case histories of arterial thrombotic complications occurring weeks to months after COVID-19 recovery, describing delayed vascular events as long COVID manifestations. It is a descriptive case series without intervention or treatment evaluation, and functions as a clinical observation/review rather than a treatment trial.
paper_authors: Maria Pia Borrelli; Adelaide Buora; Paola Scrivere; Massimo Sponza; Paolo Frigatti
paper_title: Arterial Thrombotic Sequalae After Covid-19: Mind the Gap

summary: A case series describing long-term complications of COVID-19 in 42 patients with rheumatic diseases, with 8 patients developing long-term consequences including lung involvement, neurological symptoms, and dermatitis 40+ days post-infection. The paper is excluded because it is observational documentation of complications without evaluation of any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: TATIANA BEKETOVA; ALEKSANDR KULIKOV; VALERIYA BABAK; MARINA SUPRUN; MARIIA BEKETOVA
paper_title: LONG-TERM CONSEQUENCES OF COVID-19 AMONG PATIENTS WITH RHEUMATIC DISEASES

summary: This retrospective case series examines CD8 T-cell dysfunction in Long COVID and ME/CFS patients and evaluates treatment with a nebulized antioxidant/anti-pathogen agent. The study reports improved CD8 T-cell function and 54% reduction in symptom severity in 8 treated Long COVID/ME/CFS patients over 3-15 months with no serious adverse effects.
paper_authors: Anna Gil; George E. Hoag; John P. Salerno; Mady Hornig; Nancy Klimas; Liisa K. Selin
paper_title: Identification of CD8 T-cell dysfunction associated with symptoms in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) and Long COVID and treatment with a nebulized antioxidant/anti-pathogen agent in a retrospective case series

summary: A pilot case series of 4 long COVID patients receiving transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) combined with online cognitive training over 20 daily sessions. The intervention showed improvements across multiple neuropsychological domains, mood, anxiety, and PASC symptom scores, supporting further evaluation in a planned randomized controlled trial.
paper_authors: Beatriz A. Cavendish; Alisson Lima; Laiss Bertola; Leigh Charvet; Marom Bikson; Andre R. Brunoni; Kallene S. Vidal
paper_title: Combination of transcranial direct current stimulation with online cognitive training improves symptoms of Post-acute Sequelae of COVID-19: A case series

summary: Case report of a 37-year-old man with post-COVID multisystem inflammatory syndrome in adults (MIS-A) presenting one month after initial SARS-CoV-2 infection with cardiogenic shock and multiorgan failure. Treatment included corticosteroids, tocilizumab, plasma exchange, and mechanical circulatory support, though the patient ultimately died despite maximal intervention.
paper_authors: CHRISTIAN VON GIZYCKI; WAHAAJ KHAN; PEDRO MOGROVEJO
paper_title: SYSTEMIC SHOCK: A CASE OF POST-COVID-19 MULTISYSTEM INFLAMMATORY SYNDROME IN ADULTS

summary: A clinical perspective paper presenting case reports to illustrate diagnostic approaches for respiratory symptoms in long COVID patients. Does not present original research, trial data, or treatment evaluation—primarily an educational commentary on diagnosis.
paper_authors: Andrea S. Gershon; Daisy Fung; Grace Y. Lam
paper_title: Diagnosing Respiratory Long COVID

summary: A case report of a 75-year-old severe COVID-19 survivor who developed diffuse pulmonary fibrosis and long-term oxygen dependence. The paper describes clinical presentation and risk factors but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: A. YANAMADALA
paper_title: A CASE REPORT OF COMPLICATIONS IN A SURVIVOR OF SEVERE COVID-19: PULMONARY FIBROSIS AND LONG-TERM SUPPLEMENTAL OXYGEN REQUIREMENT

summary: Retrospective case series examining exercise capacity in 169 long COVID patients using cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) at baseline and 41 patients at 1-year follow-up. Found reduced peak oxygen uptake and abnormal oxygen uptake/workload slopes in subsets of patients, with no improvement at 1-year follow-up.
paper_authors: Lotte Sørensen; Camilla Lundgren Pedersen; Mads Jønsson Andersen; Johannes Martin Schmid; Lisa Gregersen Oestergaard; Berit Schiøttz-Christensen; Søren Sperling
paper_title: Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing in Patients With Long COVID

summary: Case report of a long COVID patient presenting with insulin autoimmune syndrome, including excessive sweating, hypoglycemia, and high insulin levels with anti-insulin antibodies. Patient improved with azathioprine treatment and nutritional recommendations.
paper_authors: Fernanda Isadora Corona-Meraz; Blanca Perla Quintero-Castillo; Luis Alexis Hernández-Palma; Andrea Carolina Machado-Sulbaran
paper_title: Long COVID-19 and Insulin Autoimmune Syndrome: A Case Report

summary: Case report of a lung transplant recipient who developed post-COVID complications including haemophagocytic lymphohistocytosis (HLH) and cholangiopathy following acute COVID-19 and subsequent transplantation. This is a single case describing clinical sequelae rather than a treatment trial or intervention study.
paper_authors: Silvia Roda; Alessandra Ricciardi; Angela Maria Di Matteo; Marco Zecca; Patrizia Morbini; Marco Vecchia; Teresa Chiara Pieri; Paola Giordani; Angelo Tavano; Raffaele Bruno
paper_title: Post-acute coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID 19) syndrome:

summary: Case report of a 41-year-old woman who developed polyphagia and weight gain 6 months after acute COVID-19 infection, representing a rare post-acute COVID-19 syndrome. Patient was treated with psychotherapy and behavioral modifications with good outcomes.
paper_authors: Mark Mohan Kaggwa; Alain Favina; Sarah Maria Najjuka; Zebunnesa Zeba; Mohammed A. Mamun; Felix Bongomin
paper_title: Excessive eating and weight gain:A rare post-acute COVID-19 syndrome
paper_journal: Diabetes & Metabolic Syndrome: Clinical Research & Reviews

summary: Case report of a 28-year-old woman who developed prosopagnosia (face recognition impairment) following COVID-19, with survey data from 54 long COVID patients showing self-reported visual and navigational deficits. This is a descriptive case study without any treatment intervention, making it outside the scope of the intervention trials screening.
paper_authors: Marie-Luise Kieseler; Brad Duchaine
paper_title: Persistent prosopagnosia following COVID-19

summary: Case report of two Egyptian patients who developed optic neuritis 1.5-2 months after severe COVID-19 infection and hospitalization. Both patients presented with visual disturbances (monocular delayed perception and complete unilateral vision loss) with abnormal visual evoked potentials but no other neurological or ophthalmological findings.
paper_authors: Aliaë Mohamed-Hussein; Amira M. El Gohary
paper_title: HP47 : Post covid optic neuritis,Egyptian two case reports

summary: Case report of a 35-year-old patient with post-COVID Guillain-Barré syndrome who experienced treatment-related fluctuation after intravenous immunoglobulin therapy but achieved complete recovery with repeat treatment. The study identifies clinical predictors of treatment-related fluctuation in post-COVID GBS and emphasizes importance of early recognition for proper management.
paper_authors: Subhadeep Gupta; Atanu Chandra; Biman Kanti Ray; Alak Pandit
paper_title: Treatment related fluctuation and response to intravenous immunoglobulin therapy in post COVID-19 Guillain-Barre syndrome
paper_journal: Diabetes & Metabolic Syndrome: Clinical Research & Reviews

summary: This paper describes a case of de novo seronegative inflammatory oligoarthritis occurring at the onset of acute COVID-19 infection in a single patient, with MRI findings of synovitis. The authors compare this presentation with two other similar cases but do not study long COVID (persistent post-acute symptoms weeks to months after infection) or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Lily H. Sung; Natalya Surmachevska; Jose E. Rubio
paper_title: A case of de novo seronegative inflammatory oligoarthritis associated with COVID-19 infection

summary: Three case reports of children aged 4-7 years presenting with seizures 2-4 weeks after COVID-19 recovery, with no prior epilepsy history. The paper describes clinical presentation and characteristics suggesting a predisposition for neurological complications post-COVID, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Tal Bechor Ariel; Ben Ariel; Michael Ben-Acon; Nechama Sharon
paper_title: Focal and generalized onset seizures in children post-COVID (Omicron) recovery: 3 clinical case reports

summary: A case series of three long COVID patients with persistent encephalopathy treated with therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE), showing positive therapeutic effects. The authors propose that TPE warrants further evaluation through a prospective randomized trial.
paper_authors: Chakrapani Ranganathan; Shelley D. Fusinski; Imad M. Obeid; Khaled M. Ismail; Derrick T. Ferguson; Mindy F. Raminick; Sean M. Dawes
paper_title: Therapeutic plasma exchange for persistent encephalopathy associated with Covid-19

paper_title: Post-COVID seizure: A new feature of “long-COVID”

paper_title: Abrupt bilateral blindness as a rare post-acute demyelinating consequence of COVID-19

paper_title: Demonstrating new-onset or worsened sudomotor function post-COVID-19 on comparative analysis of autonomic function pre-and post-SARS-CoV-2 infection

summary: Case report of a 46-year-old woman with chronic COVID-19 pneumonia presenting with bilateral cavitary lung lesions and calcification, requiring bilateral lung transplantation. paper_title: Olfactory training with essential oils for patients with post-COVID-19 smell dysfunction: A case series

paper_authors: Stefania Bellone; Eric R. Siegel; Alessandro D. Santin
paper_title: N-acetylcysteine (NAC) supplementation improves dyspnea and may normalize von Willebrand plasma levels in gynecologic patients with Post-Acute-COVID-Sequela (PASC)/Long COVID

paper_title: Lésions acrales chroniques (« orteils COVID ») : un syndrome post-COVID long ?
paper_journal: Annales de Dermatologie et de Vénéréologie - FMC

summary: Case report of a patient who developed severe pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP) following COVID-19 infection, initially misdiagnosed as post-COVID syndrome. paper_title: COVID-19 and severe pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP): A case report

paper_title: Outpatient management of Post-COVID syndrome – single center experience

paper_title: Long-term rheumatoid manifestations as a consequence of COVID-19 and/or vaccination: A case report after a 2-year follow-up

paper_title: Long-Haul Post–COVID-19 Symptoms Presenting as a Variant of Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome
