summary: Retrospective study of 22 post-COVID-19 patients with acute invasive fungal rhinosinusitis (AIFR) describing clinical presentation and treatment outcomes. All patients received combined surgical debridement and antifungal medications, achieving a 72.7% survival rate, with meningitis as a significant predictor of fatal outcome.
paper_authors: Ly Xuan Quang; Truong Thanh Tam; Luong Huu Dang; Yen-Chun Chen; Shih-Han Hung; Tran Thanh Tai; Nguyen Le Vu Hoang; Nguyen Van Thanh
paper_title: Acute invasive fungal rhinosinusitis in post-COVID-19 patients in Vietnam
paper_journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association

summary: Case series of two long COVID patients who developed de novo autoimmune disorders (Crohn's disease and ankylosing spondylitis) treated with TNF-α inhibitors, followed by subsequent development of post-COVID Parkinson's disease. Both patients showed substantial motor improvement with dopaminergic therapy, suggesting a pathogenic cascade linking viral-induced immune dysregulation to neurodegeneration.
paper_authors: Esra Demir Unal
paper_title: A Neuroimmunological Axis between systemic autoimmunity and Parkinson's disease following long-COVID: A case series

summary: This case series reports treatment of two long COVID patients with stellate ganglion block, a regional anesthetic procedure targeting cervical sympathetic chain activity. The authors propose that dysautonomia underlies long COVID symptoms and suggest stellate ganglion block as a novel therapeutic approach.
paper_authors: Luke D. Liu; Deborah L. Duricka
paper_title: Stellate ganglion block reduces symptoms of Long COVID: A case series

summary: This case series describes six patients who developed endogenous fungal endophthalmitis (Candida or Aspergillus) following COVID-19 hospitalization and corticosteroid/antiviral treatment. While treatment with antivirals and antifungals was provided, the paper focuses on acute post-COVID complications during hospitalization recovery rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months post-infection).
paper_authors: Fekri S.; Khorshidifar M.; Esfahanian F.; Veisi A.; Nouri H.; Abtahi SH
paper_title: Endogenous Fungal Endophthalmitis following COVID-19 Hospitalization: Evidence from a Year-Long Observational Study

summary: Retrospective descriptive case series comparing antibody test results and clinical characteristics between patients with confirmed post-acute COVID-19 sequelae (true-PASC) and those with PASC-like symptoms without COVID-19 history (PASC-mimic). Findings show no significant clinical differences between groups, highlighting the need to exclude PASC-mimic conditions in future research.
paper_authors: Masayuki Ohira; Takashi Osada; Hiroaki Kimura; Terunori Sano; Masaki Takao
paper_title: Post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 mimic: An important neurological condition

summary: Reports five cases of osteonecrosis of the femoral head in long COVID patients who received high-dose corticosteroid treatment during acute COVID-19 hospitalization. This is a case report documenting a potential adverse effect of treatment rather than an intervention trial evaluating a treatment for long COVID.
paper_authors: Shigeo Hagiwara; Satoshi Iida; Junichi Nakamura; Yasushi Wako; Michiru Moriya; Makoto Takazawa; Yuya Kawarai; Seiji Ohtori
paper_title: COVID-19-related osteonecrosis of the femoral head: Case reports of five cases

summary: A case series evaluating Integrative Breathing Therapy (IBT) for post-COVID patients with dysfunctional breathing and associated symptoms like dyspnea, fatigue, and cognitive difficulties. All participants showed improvements in breathing parameters and symptom reduction after 6-12 weekly group telehealth sessions combined with individual sessions.
paper_authors: Hadas Golan; Rosalba Courtney; Jeremy Wolfberg
paper_title: Novel Respiratory Therapy for the Improvement of Post COVID Condition Symptoms: A Case Series

summary: Retrospective case series describing neurological complications following acute COVID-19 infection in 7 patients, including thrombotic events, Guillain-Barré syndrome, and stroke. The paper focuses on acute and early post-infection complications rather than long COVID syndrome.
paper_authors: Emna Fakhfakh; Salma Sakka; Bouattour Nadia; Sawsan Daoud; Khadija Sonda Moalla; Nouha Farhat; Dammak Mariem; Chokri Mhiri
paper_title: Manifestations neurologiques associées à la Covid-19

summary: Describes a multidisciplinary COVID-19 Activity Rehabilitation Program at Mayo Clinic that evaluated and treated 100 patients with post-COVID syndrome, characterizing their symptoms, comorbidities, and functional impairment. Most patients required physical therapy, occupational therapy, or brain rehabilitation, with the majority showing no abnormalities on lab/imaging despite debilitating symptoms affecting return to work and daily activities.
paper_authors: Vanichkachorn G.; Newcomb R.; Cowl CT; Murad MH; Breeher L.; Miller S.; Trenary M.; Neveau D.; Higgins S.
paper_title: Post–COVID-19 Syndrome (Long Haul Syndrome): Description of a Multidisciplinary Clinic at Mayo Clinic and Characteristics of the Initial Patient Cohort

summary: A case series of 26 virologially confirmed long COVID patients presenting with prolonged or recurrent symptoms weeks after initial COVID-19 infection, seen at a post-COVID clinic from May-June 2020. The paper describes symptom patterns (neurological, cardiovascular, fatigue) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Dorsaf Slama; Marina Karmochkine; J. Pavie; Emmanuel Sorbets; T. de Broucker; Gabriela Spiridon; Valérie Lebaut; Mariel Piétri; É. Pichard; Dominique Salmon
paper_title: Symptômes prolongés ou résurgents de COVID-19 : à propos de 26 cas virologiquement confirmés

summary: This case-series study examined neurometabolic and structural brain changes in the hippocampus before and after COVID-19 infection in three elderly patients, two of whom had completed resistance training prior to infection and one in a non-training control condition. Findings suggest mild COVID-19 may be associated with neuroinflammation and altered glutamate levels, potentially explaining chronic neurological complaints in long COVID patients.
paper_authors: Wouter A.J. Vints; Kristina Valatkevičienė; Oron Levin; Akila Weerasekera; Simonas Jesmanas; Simona Kušleikienė; Vida J. Česnaitienė; Uwe Himmelreich; Jeanine A. Verbunt; Eva-Maria Ratai; Rymantė Gleiznienė; Nerijus Masiulis
paper_title: Hippocampal neurometabolic and structural changes from pre-to post-COVID-19: A case-series study

summary: This paper describes neurological manifestations of long COVID, particularly cognitive dysfunction (executive, attentional, and memory impairment) observed in dozens of cases. Brain PET-FDG imaging shows hypometabolic zones in cingulate cortex, precuneus, temporal cortex, and brainstem, with variable patient outcomes dependent on the extent of cerebral hypometabolism.
paper_authors: Jacques Hugon
paper_title: COVID 19 : COVID long et neurologie

summary: Case series of 3 patients (ages 15-64) who developed Guillain-Barré syndrome during or 3 weeks after acute COVID-19 infection, treated with immunoglobulin with favorable outcomes. While it documents treatment of a COVID-related complication, this describes acute post-infection neurological syndrome, not persistent long COVID symptoms weeks-months later.
paper_authors: Ameur Ameny; Hajer Bouguila; Ichrak Ghachem; Brahim Syrine; Younes Samia
paper_title: Syndrome de Guillain–Barré post-COVID-19 : à propos de 3 cas

summary: Retrospective study of 28 patients with ME/CFS following COVID-19 vaccination who received vitamin D replacement therapy, showing increases in serum vitamin D levels associated with symptom improvement. 82% of patients (23/28) no longer met ME/CFS diagnostic criteria after therapy, with sleep problems and autonomic symptoms showing the greatest improvement.
paper_authors: Shinichiro Kodama; Nafuko Konishi; Yuriko Hirai; Akinori Fujisawa; Mitsuko Nakata; Satoshi Teramukai; Masanori Fukushima
paper_title: Efficacy of vitamin D replacement therapy on 28 cases of myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome after COVID-19 vaccination

summary: This case series describes two patients with postacute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC/long COVID) who received over-the-counter antihistamines and showed significant improvement in symptoms and functional ability. The authors propose histamine involvement in PASC pathogenesis and call for future studies to evaluate antihistamine efficacy in long COVID treatment.
paper_authors: Melissa D. Pinto; Natalie Lambert; Charles A. Downs; Heather Abrahim; Thomas D. Hughes; Amir M. Rahmani; Candace W. Burton; Rana Chakraborty
paper_title: Antihistamines for Postacute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: Open-label case series of 12 long COVID patients with cognitive deficits treated with guanfacine (α2A-adrenoceptor agonist) and N-acetylcysteine (NAC). Treatment improved cognitive abilities in 8 of 12 patients, with reported improvements in working memory, concentration, and executive function; 4 patients discontinued due to adverse effects or unspecified reasons.
paper_authors: Arman Fesharaki-Zadeh; Naomi Lowe; Amy F.T. Arnsten
paper_title: Clinical experience with the α2A-adrenoceptor agonist, guanfacine, and N-acetylcysteine for the treatment of cognitive deficits in “Long-COVID19”

summary: Cross-sectional study of 10 patients with demyelinating manifestations of the central and peripheral nervous system occurring after SARS-CoV-2 infection, with mean onset 43 days post-infection. The study characterizes the neurological presentations (myelin, optic neuritis, brainstem syndrome, peripheral neuropathy) but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Syrine Laroussi; Saloua Mrabet; Emna Bouguira; Alya Gharbi; Amira Souissi; Nasri Amina; Amina Gargouri-Berrechid; Kacem Imen; Riadh Gouider
paper_title: Démyélinisation centrale et périphérique post Covid-19 : quels liens ?

summary: This case report describes steroid-induced avascular necrosis of the jaw in patients recovering from COVID-19, a post-COVID complication emerging at a tertiary care center in India. The paper is a descriptive case series without treatment evaluation or intervention testing.
paper_authors: Anubhuti Sood; Vivek Nayyar; Ajoy Roychoudhury; Ashu Seith Bhalla; Deepika Mishra
paper_title: Post-COVID steroid induced avascular necrosis of the jaw: Emerging challenge in India
paper_journal: Oral Surgery, Oral Medicine, Oral Pathology and Oral Radiology

summary: Case series of 11 new pediatric patients with new-onset psychiatric symptoms (including psychosis) after acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, followed for 1 year, combined with a review of 12 previously reported similar cases. Most patients received treatment and had good outcomes, with CSF analysis in some showing central immune responses.
paper_authors: Shivani S. Desai; Ashley L. Nguyen; Gail A. Bernstein
paper_title: Letter to editor: Case report of long COVID-19 with psychosis in a child

summary: This case report describes temporal changes in sputum rheological parameters in two patients with chronic cough following SARS-CoV-2 infection. While it documents post-COVID pathophysiology, it is a descriptive case series without an intervention or treatment being tested, making it unsuitable for a clinical trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: Haruhiko Ogawa; Yuka Uchida
paper_title: Temporal changes over time in sputum rheological parameters after SARS-CoV-2 infection in two patients with chronic cough

summary: A prospective observational study evaluating angina-like chest pain in long COVID patients using adenosine stress perfusion cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. The paper presents preliminary results from the first 10 patients of the ANGI-Covid study, showing that 50% displayed microvascular dysfunction patterns, but the full protocol and broader results are still ongoing.
paper_authors: Nuria Vallejo Camazón; Albert Teis; María José Martínez Membrive; Cinta Llibre; Antoni Bayés-Genís; Lourdes Mateu
paper_title: Long COVID-19 and microvascular disease-related angina

summary: A case series of 15 post-COVID-19 patients with femoral head osteonecrosis treated with autologous bone marrow mononuclear cell transplantation. Treatment with autologous bone marrow progenitor cells reduced pain and improved Harris Hip Score in patients with this complication.
paper_authors: Bruno Adelmo Franco; Saulo Garrido; Thiago Faleiro; Davi Veiga; Paula Daltro; Beatriz Pereira; Gildásio Daltro
paper_title: Autologous bone marrow mononuclear cell transplantation for osteonecrosis of the femoral head in post-covid-19 syndrome: A case series

summary: This is a personal testimony piece from two hospital caregivers describing their experiences with long COVID and its impact on their daily lives. It is an editorial/opinion piece rather than a research study with systematic data collection or treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Claire Trochet
paper_title: Les soignants aussi sont concernés par le Covid long

summary: Retrospective case series of 23 patients with post-COVID reactive arthritis treated at a tertiary care center in India, documenting clinical profiles and treatment outcomes. Most patients responded well to NSAIDs and intra-articular steroids, with no relapses reported, though the study notes COVID-19's definitive role in arthritis etiology remains unproven.
paper_authors: Atanu Pal; Rashmi Roongta; Sumantro Mondal; Debanjali Sinha; Pradyot Sinhamahapatra; Alakendu Ghosh; Arghya Chattopadhyay
paper_title: Does post-COVID reactive arthritis exist? Experience of a tertiary care centre with a review of the literature

summary: This pilot study used whole-exome sequencing to investigate genetic factors in COVID orchitis (testicular pain), a symptom affecting 10-15% of long COVID patients. The authors identified a rare NACAD deletion in 3 brothers with orchitis and found decreased ACE2 levels, generating a hypothesis about genetic susceptibility to this complication.
paper_authors: Rohit Reddy; Iakov Efimenko; Willy Chertman; Taylor Kohn; Parris Diaz; Deepa Seetharam; Kajal Khodamoradi; Eliyahu Kresch; Ranjith Ramasamy
paper_title: Whole Exome Sequencing Identifies a Rare Mutation in NACAD as a Possible Cause of COVID Orchitis in Brothers

summary: This study describes characteristics of 4 long COVID patients listed for heart transplantation compared to 41 patients with other etiologies of advanced heart failure. It is a descriptive case series without any treatment intervention—patients are being evaluated for transplantation as a last-resort treatment for refractory heart failure, not receiving an experimental or evaluable intervention.
paper_authors: Joao Manoel Rossi Neto; Raphael Machado Rossi; Plinio Jose Whitaker Wolf; Victor Bemfica De Mello; Daniel Chagas Dantas; Carolina Casadei Dos Santos; Marco Aurelio Finger
paper_title: Long Covid as an Indication for Heart Transplantation and Its Characteristics

summary: This cross-sectional study describes postacute COVID-19 syndrome (long COVID) symptoms in maxillofacial surgeons in Brazil following their initial SARS-CoV-2 infection. The paper documents the prevalence and nature of persistent symptoms in this healthcare worker population but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Lucas Alves da Mota Santana; Marcos Antônio Lima dos Santos; Hélio Igor Melo de Albuquerque; Eduardo Morato de Oliveira; Lucyene Miguita Luiz; Wilton Mitsunari Takeshita; Liane Maciel de Almeida Souza
paper_title: Postacute coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) syndrome in maxillofacial surgeons after initial infection: A Brazilian experience

summary: A serial single-case observational study evaluating cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) for severe post-COVID-19 fatigue in five adolescents. Three of five patients showed significant fatigue reduction at 12 weeks, with all five patients no longer severely fatigued post-CBT and improvements in physical functioning and school attendance.
paper_authors: Tanja A. Kuut; Fabiola Müller; Annemarie M.J. Braamse; Jan Houtveen; Chantal P. Rovers; Hans Knoop
paper_title: Cognitive behavioural therapy for severe fatigue following COVID-19 in adolescents: a serial single-case observational study of five consecutively referred patients

summary: An exploratory case-series study of 80 COVID-19 survivors in Brazil examined persistent gastrointestinal symptoms two years post-infection through clinical interviews and cytokine analysis. The study found that 30 participants reported ongoing GI symptoms with distinct inflammatory signatures, including elevated TNF-α and delayed IL-6 response, suggesting prolonged inflammatory dysregulation may underlie GI manifestations in long COVID.
paper_authors: Arlene dos Santos Pinto; Victor Irungu Mwangi; Juliana Costa Ferreira Neves; Alex Bezerra Silva Maciel; Alexandre V. Neto; Jefferson da Silva Valente; Gisely Cardoso de Melo; Wuelton Marcelo Monteiro; Vanderson de Souza Sampaio; Allyson Guimarães da Costa; Fernando F. Almeida-Val
paper_title: Clinical features and inflammatory signatures of patients with persistent gastrointestinal long COVID two years after severe SARS-CoV-2 infection

summary: A descriptive case series study of older adults from Peruvian Senior Centers who tested positive for COVID-19, followed up to four months to assess acute and persistent symptoms. Found a low frequency of long COVID (4.4%) in this population, with most experiencing one to three symptoms.
paper_authors: Michael Marshall
paper_title: The four most urgent questions about long COVID

summary: Case series reporting favorable clinical response to azithromycin treatment in three long COVID patients with neurological symptoms and cognitive impairment. Authors propose azithromycin as a potential intervention for post-COVID neuropsychiatric manifestations and recommend formal clinical trials.
paper_authors: Robert A. Schwartz; Robert M. Suskind
paper_title: Post-COVID-19 neuropsychiatric manifestations: a suggested therapeutic approach to ‘long COVID’ with azithromycin

summary: Two case studies describing speech-language pathology treatment of dysfunctional breathing in long COVID patients with dyspnea and upper airway symptoms. Results show positive outcomes after comprehensive breathing retraining addressing multiple dimensions of dysfunctional breathing.
paper_authors: Hadas Golan
paper_title: Addressing Dysfunctional Breathing in Patients With Long COVID-Related Speech and Upper Airway Symptoms: Two Case Studies
paper_journal: Perspectives of the ASHA Special Interest Groups

summary: A case series of 13 long COVID patients who took extended courses (7.5-30 days) of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir (Paxlovid) to evaluate symptom response. Some participants experienced meaningful symptom reduction while others reported no effect, suggesting potential benefits for a subset of long COVID patients but with variable responses.
paper_authors: Cohen AK; Jaudon TW; Schurman EM; Kava L.; Vogel JM; Haas-Godsil J.; Lewis D.; Crausman S.; Leslie K.; Bligh SC; Lizars G.; Davids JD; Sran S.; Peluso M.; McCorkell L.
paper_title: Impact of extended-course oral nirmatrelvir/ritonavir in established Long COVID: a case series

summary: This paper describes homeopathic treatment outcomes for COVID-19 acute symptoms, sequelae, and long COVID through 12 documented case reports. While it addresses long COVID treatment, it is an uncontrolled case series without a control group and lacks quantitative outcome data.
paper_authors: Jens Wurster
paper_title: Covid-19 und die positiven Erfahrungen mit Homöopathie

summary: This case series describes six patients with retinal vascular anomalies (vasculitis, vein/artery occlusions) occurring 0-8 months after COVID-19 infection, suggesting ocular long-term effects of COVID-19. No treatment was administered; the study documents clinical manifestations and diagnostic findings only.
paper_authors: Georgios N. Tsiropoulos; Daniela Gallo Castro; Aude Ambresin
paper_title: Six Cases of Retinal Vascular Anomalies after Coronavirus Disease 2019: A Case Series

summary: Diagnostic case series of 42 long COVID patients evaluated in a dedicated COVID-19 sleep clinic, identifying five sleep disorder syndromes including obstructive sleep apnea, chronic insomnia, hypersomnia, REM behavior disorder, and circadian phase delay. The study recommends comprehensive sleep evaluation for persistent severe sleep symptoms in PASC patients, providing diagnostic characterization and treatment recommendations.
paper_authors: Fernando M.S. Coelho; Richard Czuma; Amberly Ticotsky; Jason Maley; Janet M. Mullington; Robert Joseph Thomas
paper_title: Sleep disorder syndromes of post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC) / Long Covid

summary: Case report of two patients with Parsonage-Turner neuralgia (amyotrophic brachial neuritis) presenting with accessory nerve paralysis following acute COVID-19 infection. The paper documents clinical presentation, imaging, and electromyography findings but does not involve treatment intervention or long COVID sequelae.
paper_authors: Clemence Coll; Muriel Tessier; Christophe Vandendries; Paul Seror
paper_title: Névralgie amyotrophiante et infection à COVID-19 : deux cas de paralysie du nerf spinal accessoire

summary: This paper describes a homeopathic treatment project for long COVID and post-acute COVID patients in Switzerland, presenting 8 case studies (4 vaccinated, 4 unvaccinated) treated with the Jus method and Natrium arsenicosum. All cases reportedly achieved health restoration, though the work lacks rigorous clinical design, control groups, and objective outcome measures.
paper_authors: Andrea Corinna Mayer; Christoph Grabenhofer; Martine Jus; Gabriela Keller
paper_title:
Homöopathische Begleitung von Long Covid und
                    „Postacute“ Covid – ein Forschungsprojekt der Dr. B. K.
                    Bose Stiftung, Zug

summary: This paper reports surgical outcomes for 11 post-COVID patients with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension treated via pulmonary endarterectomy, showing significant improvement in pulmonary vascular resistance and low operative mortality. It presents the first published series of post-COVID CTEPH patients undergoing this curative surgical intervention.
paper_authors: Nezih Onur Ermerak; Sehnaz Olgun Yildizeli; Derya Kocakaya; Bulent Mutlu; Koray Ak; Serpil Tas; Bedrettin Yildizeli
paper_title: Surgical Treatment of Another Sequalae of COVID-19: Post-COVID CTEPH

summary: Two case reports demonstrating homeopathic treatment of COVID-19, long COVID, and vaccine-related symptoms. No quantitative outcomes or control group; editorial/case report format without systematic evaluation.
paper_authors: Bernhard Zauner
paper_title:
Zwei alltägliche Fälle aus der Praxis –
                    Impfnebenwirkung, Long Covid

summary: This paper presents 4 clinical cases of long COVID patients with anxiety and depression treated with herbal remedies (Silexan lavender oil, EGb 761 ginkgo extract, and SHR-5 rhodiola extract). The authors argue that phytotherapy has a clinically relevant role in managing psychiatric manifestations of long COVID, particularly subsyndromal anxiety and depression.
paper_authors: Jan Zourek; Rainer Stange; Siegfried Kasper; Lucie Bartova
paper_title:
Die Rolle von Phytotherapie bei COVID-19-assoziierter Angst und
                Depression

summary: Describes neurological presentations in children with long COVID at Germany's first pediatric long COVID outpatient clinic in Jena, with systematic assessment using questionnaires and tests. Provides descriptive data on neurological symptoms but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Anett Fischer; Heike de Vries; Marius Rasche; Michael Lorenz; James Beck; Peter Huppke; Daniel Vilser
paper_title: Neurological Presentations in Long COVID-19 Syndrome in Childhood: First Data from the Pediatric Long COVID-19 Outpatient Clinic Jena

summary: Case report describing three patients presenting with voice impairment (dysphonia/aphonia) following COVID-19 infection. No treatment intervention is described; this is a descriptive clinical observation of post-COVID symptoms.
paper_authors: Shabnam Shahpasand; Arno Olthoff; Dirk Beutner
paper_title: Dysphonia as post-covid-syndrome ?

summary: Case report of two patients with heterotopic ossification (abnormal bone formation in soft tissues) following severe acute COVID-19 requiring mechanical ventilation. The paper describes radiological and nuclear medicine findings but does not evaluate any treatment intervention and focuses on acute COVID-19 complications rather than long COVID syndrome.
paper_authors: Deepak P. Kalbi; Edgar Zamora; Adithya Hari; Kwang J. Chun
paper_title: Fulminant Heterotopic Ossification following COVID-19 associated Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome: Manifestations in Radiology, Nuclear Medicine, and Clinical Application

summary: This case report describes two patients who developed longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (LETM) following acute COVID-19 infection. The paper documents the clinical presentation and timeline of neurological complications during the acute infection phase, not persistent long COVID sequelae.
paper_authors: Emine Rabia Koc; Ömer Faruk Turan; Bedirhan Mengüç
paper_title: Covid-19 infection as a possible risk factor for longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis!

summary: This case series describes oral cavity manifestations of long COVID in 1,256 patients, including discoloration, ulceration, mycosis, and aphthous lesions occurring weeks to months post-infection. The authors document treatment responses (laser biostimulation, hygiene recommendations, specialist care) and spontaneous resolution patterns, with recommendations for monitoring and management strategies.
paper_authors: Barbara Rafałowicz; Leopold Wagner; Juliusz Rafałowicz
paper_title: Long COVID Oral Cavity Symptoms Based on Selected Clinical Cases

summary: Ultrastructural analysis of quadriceps muscle biopsies from 8 severe COVID-19 patients reveals microangiopathic changes including endothelial damage, pinocytotic vesicles, and lamina thickening. The study documents pathological mechanisms underlying post-COVID muscle weakness but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Josep Lloreta-Trull; Judith Marin-Corral; Nuria Juanpere; Sergi Pascual-Guardia; Javier Gimeno; Dolores Naranjo; Laura Segalés; Silvia Hernández; Mercedes Simón; Laia Serrano; Beatriz Casado; Belén Lloveras; Joaquim Gea
paper_title: Muscle disease in severe COVID-19 patients: a microangiopathic myopathy

summary: A retrospective case series of seven long COVID patients with recurrent fever and autonomic dysfunction, including symptoms of tachycardia, blood pressure abnormalities, and electrolyte imbalances. Physical cooling and electrolyte correction with medication were effective treatments for managing autonomic dysfunction-related fever.
paper_authors: Liu Haihong; Xu Nannan; Meng Xiangzhu; Wang Gang
paper_title: A clinical case study of seven patients of autonomic dysfunction in post COVID-19 conditions with fever as the main clinical symptom: a case series

summary: Retrospective case series describing clinical and OCT imaging features of retinitis in 17 patients with presumed post-COVID infection. The study documents retinal findings and imaging characteristics but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Apoorva Ayachit; Madan Joshi; Guruprasad Ayachit; Shrinivas Joshi; Priya Shah
paper_title: Presumed Post-COVID Infection Retinitis – Clinical and Tomographic Features of Retinitis as a Post-COVID Syndrome

summary: A case series describing neurocognitive deficits in three severe COVID-19 patients during acute rehabilitation, with formal neuropsychological testing showing deficits in encoding and verbal fluency. While it demonstrates cognitive sequelae post-infection, it is a descriptive case series without intervention or treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Douglas M. Whiteside; Victoria Oleynick; Erin Holker; Eric J. Waldron; James Porter; Michael Kasprzak
paper_title: Neurocognitive deficits in severe COVID-19 infection: Case series and proposed model

summary: This retrospective case series evaluated whole-body hyperthermia (WBH) as part of a multimodal inpatient treatment approach for post-COVID syndrome patients. The study found significant improvements in fatigue (FACIT-F) and COVID-associated symptoms at 4-week follow-up, with 63% of patients rating WBH as effective, though the authors note results are preliminary and future RCTs are needed to isolate specific treatment effects.
paper_authors: Jan Vagedes; Thomas Breitkreuz; Victoria Heinrich; Mohsen Sobh; Mohammad Oli Al Islam; Katrin Vagedes; Jan Mergelsberg
paper_title: Whole-body hyperthermia as part of a multimodal treatment for patients with post-covid syndrome – a case series

summary: A case series of two COVID-19 patients describing neuropsychological outcomes at 3–12 months post-illness, with one patient receiving formal cognitive remediation. Both patients showed cognitive recovery over follow-up despite some residual deficits and persistent emotional symptoms.
paper_authors: Elena Ostroy; Irma Campbell
paper_title: A-83 Neuropsychological Outcomes in Two COVID-19 Patients

summary: This case series describes the neuropsychological profile of 54 pediatric long COVID patients referred for testing, finding that approximately one-third showed objective weaknesses in sustained and divided attention. While the study identifies cognitive and emotional concerns in children with long COVID, it does not evaluate or test any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Jessica C. Luedke; Gray Vargas; Dasal Tenzin Jashar; Laura A. Malone; Amanda Morrow; Rowena Ng
paper_title: Neuropsychological functioning of pediatric patients with long COVID

summary: Case series of 5 male patients with subacute thyroiditis presenting 12.8 weeks after COVID-19 infection, characterized by neck pain, fever, thyroid tenderness, and elevated thyroid hormones with suppressed TSH. All patients responded well to oral prednisolone therapy (average 6.8 mg/day for 2 months) and achieved full recovery to euthyroid state.
paper_authors: Paulami Deshmukh; Vaishali Deshmukh
paper_title: Case Series of Subacute Thyroiditis Presenting as a Late Complication of COVID-19

summary: A case series of three older adults with cardiovascular risk factors who presented with cognitive symptoms 6-10 months after severe COVID-19 infection. Neuropsychological evaluations documented deficits in executive function, learning, recall, and mood, with all patients diagnosed with Mild Neurocognitive Disorder.
paper_authors: Jennifer Christopher; Shana Muslin; Erica Hymen; Kate Wyman
paper_title: A-151 Cognitive Sequelae of “Long COVID-19” in Older Adults with Cerebrovascular Risk Factors: A Case Series

summary: Retrospective clinical case series of 18 pediatric patients with long COVID who underwent neuropsychological evaluation at a multidisciplinary post-COVID clinic. Most patients had preexisting attention or mood/anxiety concerns, and over half performed below average on auditory attention measures, though the study cannot determine whether cognitive deficits are directly attributable to COVID-19 or to preexisting conditions.
paper_authors: Rowena Ng; Gray Vargas; Dasal Tenzin Jashar; Amanda Morrow; Laura A. Malone
paper_title: Neurocognitive and Psychosocial Characteristics of Pediatric Patients With Post-Acute/Long-COVID: A Retrospective Clinical Case Series

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed neurocognitive performance in 92 long COVID patients referred to a treatment program, using standardized neuropsychological tests. While patients showed specific cognitive impairments in processing speed and immediate recall, this is a descriptive assessment study without treatment evaluation or control group, functioning as a secondary analysis of an existing cohort.
paper_authors: Kristine Lokken; Melissa J. Greenfield; Jamie Hansel Robinson; Udit Vipul Shah; Ronald M. Lazar; Richard Kennedy; Roy C. Martin; Kristen Triebel Gerstenecker; Adam Gerstenecker; Pariya Fazeli Wheeler; Shruti P. Agnihotri; David E. Vance
paper_title: A-159 Neurocognitive Performance in Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC)

summary: Case report of two COVID-19 patients who developed pulmonary embolism days after discharge from initial hospitalization for non-severe pneumonia. Discusses VTE as a cardiovascular manifestation during acute COVID-19 infection, not long COVID.
paper_authors: Mohamad Kanso; Thomas Cardi; Halim Marzak; Alexandre Schatz; Loïc Faucher; Lélia Grunebaum; Olivier Morel; Laurence Jesel
paper_title: Delayed pulmonary embolism after COVID-19 pneumonia: a case report

summary: A post-COVID-19 smell clinic assessed olfactory dysfunction in 20 long COVID patients using standardized tests (UPSIT, eODQ) and provided 4 months of smell retraining therapy. Initial results showed 40% experienced parosmia and 40% had rhinological symptoms, with outcomes to be evaluated after retraining completion.
paper_authors: D Gopikrishna; John Rocke; Michael Chu; Nirmal Kumar
paper_title: 539 Post-Covid-19 Smell Clinic - Management of Patients With ‘Long Covid’

summary: A single-center registry study of 16 long COVID patients with chest pain who underwent endomyocardial biopsy to investigate histopathological causes of myocardial injury. Findings showed diffuse ischemic necrosis in 75% of patients, with some cases of lymphocytic myocarditis, thrombotic microangiopathy, and amyloidosis, but no active treatment intervention was evaluated.
paper_authors: Omar Gómez-Monterrosas; Daniel Juárez Santos‐García; G Loyola; G J Jimenez Cisneros; Josep M. Miró
paper_title: Long COVID echocardiography, cardiac MRIi, and endomyocardial biopsy findings in previously healthy individuals

summary: This retrospective case series assessed medium-term outcomes in 200 severely ill COVID-19 survivors at 4-7 months post-infection. The study found persistent symptoms (breathlessness, fatigue, reduced mobility, pain) and abnormal lung function tests in a significant proportion of patients, with no sustained systemic inflammation despite ongoing symptoms.

Electron microscopy revealed mitochondrial vacuolations and myofilament degradation in cardiomyocytes, with similar findings reproduced in SARS-CoV-2-infected mice, suggesting a cellular mechanism for long COVID-associated cardiac effects.

paper_title: Male pituitary–gonadal axis dysfunction in post‐acute COVID‐19 syndrome—Prevalence and associated factors: A Mediterranean case series

paper_title: Shoulder palsy following SARS‐CoV‐2 infection: two cases of typical Parsonage–Turner syndrome

paper_title: Telogen effluvium associated with COVID‐19 infection

paper_title: Parkinson disease following <scp>COVID</scp>‐19: Report of six cases

paper_title: Toward a better understanding of persistent headache after mild COVID‐19: Three migraine‐like yet distinct scenarios

paper_title: Protracted headache after COVID‐19: A case series of 31 patients from a tertiary headache center
paper_journal: Headache: The Journal of Head and Face Pain

summary: This case series examines accelerated androgenetic alopecia (pattern hair loss) occurring 220 days post-COVID-19 recovery and evaluates platelet-rich plasma (PRP) treatment in 9 patients. paper_title: Platelet‐Rich Plasma Treatment for Accelerated Androgenetic Alopecia Pattern Hair Loss After COVID‐19 Infection: A Case Series

summary: Retrospective case series of 24 children with post-COVID-19 condition referred to a specialized clinic in Japan, documenting symptom profiles, duration, and treatments. Most patients (83.4%) showed symptom resolution or improvement with pain management and pacing-based counseling over a median 4.5-month follow-up.
paper_authors: Yuho Horikoshi; Meiwa Shibata; Hanako Funakoshi; Shintaro Baba; Sahoko Miyama
paper_title: Post coronavirus disease 2019 condition in children at a children's hospital in Japan

summary: This case series describes sicca symptoms (dry eye and dry mouth) in 22 patients recovering from severe COVID-19 at a Brazilian rehabilitation unit, finding high rates of Schirmer test positivity (72.7%) and reduced salivary flow (54.5%). The paper identifies oral dryness as a previously undescribed manifestation of post-COVID syndrome but does not test any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Sicca symptoms in post‐acute COVID‐19 syndrome

summary: Descriptive study of 16 consecutive patients with post-COVID-19 reactive arthritis presenting to rheumatology clinic, characterizing the clinical pattern of joint and periarticular involvement. Patients responded well to NSAIDs in 68.7% of cases, with corticosteroids and methotrexate used in select cases.
paper_authors: N. Varghese; V. Salaru; V. Sadovici-Bobeica
paper_title: AB1141 THE PATTERN OF POST COVID-19 REACTIVE ARTHRITIS

summary: This cross-sectional study investigates the association between COVID-19 infection and new-onset rheumatoid arthritis (RA), examining ACPA seroprevalence and autoantibody characteristics in post-COVID patients. The findings suggest that RA onset after COVID-19 is likely coincidental rather than causally connected, with post-COVID RA patients resembling regular RA patients clinically and serologically.
paper_authors: V. Derksen; Theresa Kissel; F. Lamers-Karnebeek; AE Van Der Bijl; A. C. Venhuizen; T. Huizinga; René E. M. Toes; Anna H.E. Roukens; Diane van der Woude
paper_title: AB0668 THE ONSET OF RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS AFTER COVID-19 – COINCIDENCE OR CONNECTED?

summary: Case series examining septal panniculitis (erythema nodosum) as a manifestation of COVID-19 in 21 patients, categorized by timing relative to infection (acute, ongoing symptomatic, and post-COVID syndrome). The study describes clinical features, laboratory findings, and imaging results but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: O. Egorova; G. Tarasova; A. Datsina
paper_title: POS1467 SEPTAL PANNICULITIS AS A MANIFESTATION OF COVID-19 INFECTION

summary: Reports three cases of avascular necrosis of the femoral head developing after COVID-19 treatment with corticosteroids, occurring earlier than typical post-steroid AVN presentations. This case series documents a potential long COVID complication but does not evaluate any intervention for treating AVN or long COVID.
paper_authors: Sanjay R. Agarwala; Mayank Vijayvargiya; Prashant Pandey
paper_title: Avascular necrosis as a part of ‘long COVID-19’

summary: Case series reporting two children with vestibular migraine as a post-COVID-19 manifestation and describing their management. Highlights vestibular migraine as a novel symptom of long COVID in pediatric populations requiring prompt evaluation and treatment.
paper_authors: Jeyasakthy Saniasiaya
paper_title: Vestibular migraine: a manifestation of long COVID syndrome in children

summary: A case series describing two patients who developed osteonecrosis of the knee as a long COVID-19 sequela following corticosteroid treatment for acute COVID-19. The authors recommend early MRI diagnosis and bisphosphonate therapy as intervention for this long COVID manifestation.
paper_authors: Sanjay R. Agarwala; Mayank Vijayvargiya; Tushar Sawant
paper_title: Secondary osteonecrosis of the knee as a part of long COVID-19 syndrome: a case series

summary: A family practice case series of 55 long COVID patients characterized by extreme fatigue, brain fog, and multi-systemic symptoms, with 32 undergoing SPECT-CT imaging showing vascular encephalopathy. The study describes patient outcomes and clinical presentation but explicitly states 'there is no known verified treatment' and does not test any intervention.
paper_authors: Jacqui Wise
paper_title: Covid-19: WHO urges action as 17 million long covid cases are estimated in Europe

summary: This paper reports on inpatient rehabilitation for long COVID patients and its effects on exercise performance, lung function, and psychological parameters. However, the abstract presents only conclusions without reporting actual trial results or patient numbers, indicating this is likely a protocol or incomplete abstract rather than a full study with results.
paper_authors: PS Schueller; JF Frommhold
paper_title: P71 Patients with Long Covid benefit from rehabilitation independently of the severity of the acute course of the disease
paper_journal: Breaking barriers in pulmonary rehabilitation and physiotherapy

summary: This prospective case series of 48 long COVID patients with dysfunctional breathing describes symptoms, functional impact, and quality of life using standardized questionnaires and cardiopulmonary exercise testing. Despite preserved pulmonary function, patients showed high symptom burden with dyspnea, hyperventilation, and palpitations being most common, with significantly reduced quality of life scores compared to reference values.
paper_authors: Léon Genecand; Marco Altarelli; Alzbeta Binkova; Selina Loew; Stéphanie Vaudan; Grégoire Gex; Pierre-Olivier Bridevaux; Isabelle Frésard
paper_title: Dysfunctional breathing symptoms, functional impact and quality of life in patients with long COVID-19: a prospective case series

summary: This case series describes six patients who developed or had exacerbated autoimmune phenomena following SARS-CoV-2 infection, discussing possible mechanisms underlying the association between autoimmunity and COVID-19. paper_authors: Yuval Ishay; Ariel Kenig; Limor Rubin; Oded Shamriz; Fadi Kharouf
paper_title: Autoimmune Diseases Induced or Exacerbated by COVID-19: A Single Center Experience

summary: Descriptive case series of three young COVID-19 convalescent patients presenting with long-term neuropsychological symptoms including inattention, executive dysfunction, and memory problems ('brain fog'). Reports neuropsychological test results and brain MRI findings but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Ayumi Nakamura; Thomas J. Farrer; Andy Liu
paper_title: Long-Term Sequelae in Young Convalescent COVID-19 Patients

summary: This case series of 5 long COVID patients uses invasive cardiopulmonary exercise testing to characterize exercise limitation 1 year post-infection. The study finds that reduced aerobic capacity is attributable to impaired systemic oxygen extraction rather than central cardiopulmonary dysfunction.

paper_title: Abstract 6991: Impaired Systemic Oxygen Extraction Relates to Reduced Exercise Capacity in Post-COVID-19 Long Hauler Syndrome

summary: Case series of 14 patients presenting with telogen effluvium (hair loss) occurring 1-3 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study describes clinical patterns and proposes possible pathogenic mechanisms (pro-inflammatory cytokines, viral damage) but is observational without intervention and focuses on characterizing a symptom rather than testing a treatment.

paper_title: Telogen Effluvium after SARS-CoV-2 Infection: A Series of Cases and Possible Pathogenetic Mechanisms

summary: This cross-sectional study describes cardiovascular manifestations in 71 patients referred to a cardiology clinic 4 months post-COVID-19, examining symptom prevalence and imaging abnormalities. The cohort presented with dyspnea, palpitations, and chest pain, with imaging revealing cardiomyopathy, ischemia, myocarditis, and orthostatic intolerance in subsets of patients.
paper_authors: Stephen Y. Wang; Philip Adejumo; Oyere K. Onuma; Edward J. Miller; Erica S. Spatz
paper_title: Abstract 11639: Characteristics of Patients Referred to a Cardiovascular Disease Clinic for Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Infection

summary: Retrospective case series of 5 pediatric patients who developed liver injury following COVID-19 recovery, including 2 infants with acute liver failure requiring transplantation and 3 children with hepatitis responsive to steroid treatment. All patients underwent extensive workup excluding infectious and metabolic etiologies, supporting a potentially immune-mediated post-COVID-19 liver manifestation.
paper_authors: Bertram Bengsch
paper_title: Ungewöhnliche akute Hepatitisfälle bei Kindern 2022 – Evidenz für eine immunvermittelte Erkrankung – ein Fall von Long-COVID?

summary: Case series describing three COVID-19 patients who developed post-ARDS pulmonary fibrosis with persistent dyspnea six months after acute infection. The paper documents clinical outcomes and management but contains no treatment intervention or control group, serving primarily as clinical documentation of a long COVID complication.
paper_authors: Kuldeep Ghosh; Gabriel Lara Ibarra; Maria Rosa Velasquez Espiritu; A. Poor; N. Trenard
paper_title: Development of Pulmonary Fibrosis in Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) Patients: A Case Series
paper_journal: TP47. TP047 COVID AND ARDS CASE REPORTS

summary: A three-year follow-up case study of two patients who developed autoimmune diseases (systemic lupus erythematosus and Hashimoto's thyroiditis) following COVID-19 infection and/or vaccination. The study highlights the connection between autoimmune disease manifestation and a family history of autoimmunity in the context of long-COVID symptoms and post-vaccination effects.

paper_title: Late‐Induced Autoimmune Disorders Post‐COVID‐19 Vaccination/Infection: Case Report From Iran

paper_title: Abstract 14202: Vasospastic Angina as a Potential Cause of Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19

paper_title: A Multidisciplinary Pediatric Neurology Clinic for Systematic Follow-up of Children with Neurologic Sequelae of COVID-19

paper_title: Histopathogical Lung Patterns of SARS CoV2 Infection
paper_journal: TP100. TP100 UNEXPECTED COVID-19 CASE REPORTS

paper_title: Severe Neurocognitive Manifestations in Healthy Young Individuals With COVID-19: A Case Series

paper_title: SARS-CoV-2 Survivors With Chronic Health Conditions: A Pilot Study on “COVID Long-Haulers”

paper_title: The first-year experience of a long covid clinic in a UK district general hospital

paper_title: Long COVID-19 Infections and Organizing Pneumonia in a Series of Patients with Indolent Lymphoma Treated with Rituximab

Vascular redistribution was used to differentiate patient selection: one patient received corticosteroids due to cardiac concerns and improved significantly, while the other enrolled directly in rehabilitation and showed substantial improvement in VO2max.
paper_authors: Kris Ides; W Dierckx; Y De Meyer; E Lauwers; M Lanclus; J De Backer; W De Backer
paper_title: The role of vascular density in pulmonary rehabilitation of PASC patients

summary: Case series describing three cases of membranous nephropathy with double-negative crescentic glomerulonephritis occurring after SARS-CoV-2 infection, treated with anti-CD20 agents. While the cases occurred in the post-COVID era, the paper focuses on rare renal autoimmune complications rather than long COVID syndrome as typically defined (persistent multi-system symptoms weeks to months post-infection).

paper_title: Tender cervical lymphadenitis as a herald of multi-system inflammatory syndrome in COVID-19 infection of children and adolescents: a report of two cases

paper_authors: Zachary Ciochetto; Peter L. Havens; Sol Aldrete
paper_title: Two cases of multi-inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) in adults in 2020

summary: This paper describes clinical, metabolic, and inflammatory features in 13 pediatric patients with neuropsychiatric symptoms occurring within one month of acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study focuses on acute/subacute post-infection neuropsychiatric manifestations rather than long COVID (which requires symptom persistence weeks to months later) and is a retrospective descriptive analysis without treatment intervention.

summary: This case series describes acute macular neuroretinopathy (AMN) occurring within one month of acute COVID-19 infection in 11 patients. paper_title: The characteristics of acute macular neuroretinopathy following COVID-19 infection

summary: This paper describes a distinct long COVID phenotype characterized by exertional intolerance and dyspnea despite preserved lung function. The study appears to be a descriptive characterization of patient symptoms rather than a treatment intervention trial.

paper_title: Exertional intolerance and dyspnea with preserved lung function: an emerging long COVID phenotype?

paper_title: Small airway function in Finnish COVID-19 survivors

paper_authors: Zhikai Chi; Naheed Moghal; Dinesh Rakheja; Lan Peng
paper_title: Histological features of liver biopsy in patients with COVID-19: a single institution experience with long term follow-up outcome

summary: A case series of 6 severe COVID-19 patients followed for 12 months, documenting persistent fatigue, cognitive deficits, and multidomain complaints. The paper describes clinical outcomes and symptom patterns but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

paper_title: Outcome of severe COVID-19: spotlight on fatigue, fatigability, multidomain complaints and pattern of cognitive deficits in a case series without prior brain dysfunction and without COVID-19-related stroke and/or cardiac arrest

paper_title: Characterization of adolescents with functional respiratory disorders and prior history of SARS-CoV-2

Treatment restored sleep and unexpectedly improved depression, anxiety, and cognitive symptoms (brain fog) within 4-5 days, with improvements maintained for weeks to months without relapse.

paper_title: Circadian re-set repairs long-COVID in a prodromal Parkinson’s parallel: a case series

paper_title: Reducing fatigue-related symptoms in Long COVID-19: finding an intervention that works

paper_authors: Margherita Bellucci; Federica Maria Bozzano; Chiara Castellano; Giampaola Pesce; Alessandro Beronio; Alireza Hajabbas Farshchi; Alessandro Limongelli; Antonio Uccelli; Luana Benedetti; Andrea De Maria
paper_title: Post-SARS-CoV-2 infection and post-vaccine-related neurological complications share clinical features and the same positivity to anti-ACE2 antibodies

summary: This early-phase prospective trial evaluated the safety, tolerability, and effects of tolerability-adapted exercise therapy in three patients with severe COVID-19, delivered remotely over 30 weeks with escalated aerobic doses. Exercise therapy was safe and well-tolerated, with improvements in exercise capacity and quality of life, along with marked alterations in immune and protein phenotypes related to post-COVID condition.
paper_authors: Jessica M. Scott; Zhuyu Qiu; Jahan Rahman; Chaya S. Moskowitz; Meghan G. Michalski; Sarah Lehman; Catherine P. Lee; Jenna Harrison; Anthony F. Yu; Amira Marouf; Santosha Vardhana; Paul C. Boutros; Lee W. Jones
paper_title: Case Report: Decentralized trial of tolerability-adapted exercise therapy after severe Covid-19

summary: Case series of 9 long COVID patients treated with high-dose immunoglobulin therapy for 3 months. Six patients completed treatment and all showed significant to remarkable clinical improvement in pulmonary, neurological, and cardiological symptoms.
paper_authors: John S. Thompson; Alice C. Thornton; Timothy Ainger; Beth A. Garvy
paper_title: Long-term high-dose immunoglobulin successfully treats Long COVID patients with pulmonary, neurologic, and cardiologic symptoms

summary: An open-label case series evaluating antiviral therapy (IMC-2 alone or combined with Paxlovid) in 24 long COVID patients over 120 days. Both groups showed fatigue reduction, with the combined antiviral group demonstrating statistically significant improvements in fatigue, brain fog, and dysautonomia that persisted at follow-up.
paper_authors: William L. Pridgen; David Putrino
paper_title: Patient-reported improvements from use of IMC-2 alone and IMC-2 and Paxlovid® in a Long COVID cohort: a case series

summary: Case report describing five patients who developed or experienced worsening of autoimmune thyroid disease (Hashimoto's thyroiditis, Graves disease, thyroiditis) following COVID-19 infection. No treatment intervention was tested; the paper documents disease manifestations and immune responses triggered by SARS-CoV-2 infection.
paper_authors: Si-na Du; Jian-wei Chen; Wei Li; Meng-chuan Wang; Yu-shan Mao
paper_title: Development of autoimmune thyroid disease after COVID-19 infection: case report

summary: A case series of 5 long COVID patients with post-infectious neurological syndromes (PINS) who underwent intensive neurorehabilitation, with clinical and electrophysiological assessments at baseline and 3/6-month follow-ups. Results showed variable functional recovery, with myelitis cases improving more substantially than polyradiculoneuropathy cases.
paper_authors: Micol Avenali; Daniele Martinelli; Massimiliano Todisco; Isabella Canavero; Francesca Valentino; Giuseppe Micieli; Enrico Alfonsi; Cristina Tassorelli; Giuseppe Cosentino
paper_title: Clinical and Electrophysiological Outcome Measures of Patients With Post-Infectious Neurological Syndromes Related to COVID-19 Treated With Intensive Neurorehabilitation

summary: Autopsy study examining microglial and macrophage activation in COVID-19 deceased patients using immunohistochemical analysis. Findings show pronounced activation in white matter, brain stem, and cerebellar areas, with reduced but detectable activation in post-COVID patients, potentially explaining long COVID syndrome mechanisms.
paper_authors: Julian A. Stein; Manuel Kaes; Sigrun Smola; Walter J. Schulz-Schaeffer
paper_title: Neuropathology in COVID-19 autopsies is defined by microglial activation and lesions of the white matter with emphasis in cerebellar and brain stem areas

summary: Case report of two post-COVID patients with olfactory dysfunction treated with traditional acupuncture at the LI20 point. Acupuncture provided short-term symptom relief lasting 2-4 days, with improvement duration increasing with repeated treatments.
paper_authors: Akira Morita; Aya Murakami; Takushu Uchihara; Noriyuki Ohashi; Koichi Ryu; Yuki Watanabe; Sadayuki Ochi; Kazuho Okudaira; Yoshiro Hirasaki; Takao Namiki
paper_title: Case Report: Acupuncture is an effective treatment for olfactory dysfunction in the post COVID-19 condition

summary: This paper reports clinical presentations of 100 patients attending a post-COVID-19 syndrome neurology outpatient clinic, assessing cognitive impairment, fatigue, headache, and other neurological sequelae. While it characterizes long COVID phenotypes, it is a descriptive cross-sectional study with no treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the intervention trials meta-analysis.
paper_authors: Fabian Boesl; Heinrich Audebert; Matthias Endres; Harald Prüss; Christiana Franke
paper_title: A Neurological Outpatient Clinic for Patients With Post-COVID-19 Syndrome — A Report on the Clinical Presentations of the First 100 Patients

summary: Open-label case series of 18 long COVID patients treated with the CCR5 antagonist maraviroc and pravastatin targeting the monocytic-endothelial-platelet axis. Six to twelve weeks of combination therapy produced significant clinical improvements in neurological, autonomic, respiratory, cardiac, and fatigue symptoms with corresponding decreases in vascular markers sCD40L and VEGF.
paper_authors: Bruce K. Patterson; Ram Yogendra; Jose Guevara-Coto; Rodrigo A. Mora-Rodriguez; Eric Osgood; John Bream; Purvi Parikh; Mark Kreimer; Devon Jeffers; Cedric Rutland; Gary Kaplan; Michael Zgoda
paper_title: Case series: Maraviroc and pravastatin as a therapeutic option to treat long COVID/Post-acute sequelae of COVID (PASC)

summary: A retrospective chart review of 16 long COVID patients with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) seen at a tertiary care center, examining clinical presentation, autonomic testing results, and symptom burden. The study documents high prevalence of palpitations and fatigue in post-COVID POTS patients but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.
paper_authors: Christopher Cantrell; Conor Reid; Claudia S. Walker; Samantha J. Stallkamp Tidd; Ryan Zhang; Robert Wilson
paper_title: Post-COVID postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS): a new phenomenon

summary: This paper reports 4 case studies of post-COVID central hypersomnia (excessive daytime sleepiness) identified among 530 long COVID patients, with objective sleep examination data. Three cases showed favorable response to methylphenidate treatment, and one resolved spontaneously, highlighting post-COVID hypersomnia as a treatable manifestation.
paper_authors: Clémence Morelli-Zaher; Andrea Vremaroiu-Coman; Nicolas Coquoz; Léon Genecand; Marco Altarelli; Alzbeta Binkova; Isabelle Frésard; Pierre-Olivier Bridevaux; Grégoire Gex
paper_title: Post-COVID central hypersomnia, a treatable trait in long COVID: 4 case reports

summary: Case report of three long COVID patients with persistent gastrointestinal symptoms (epigastric pain and diarrhea) treated with celiac plexus block, a procedure targeting the autonomic nervous system. The authors report successful symptom improvement, extending previous findings on nerve block interventions for long COVID symptoms.
paper_authors: Luke D. Liu; Deborah L. Duricka
paper_title: Case Report: Celiac plexus block improves gastrointestinal Long COVID symptoms

summary: A case series of 14 long COVID patients who underwent medically supervised long-term fasting (6-16 days) using the Buchinger Wilhelmi protocol. Thirteen patients reported improvement in overall health and multiple symptoms (fatigue, breathlessness, muscle/joint pain, cognitive impairment, smell/taste disorders), with reduced body weight and cardiometabolic risk factors.
paper_authors: Franziska Grundler; Robin Mesnage; Alberto Cerrada; Françoise Wilhelmi de Toledo
paper_title: Improvements during long-term fasting in patients with long COVID – a case series and literature review

summary: Case series describing two CLL patients with persistent SARS-CoV-2 infection and post-COVID-19 condition treated with casirivimab/imdevimab monoclonal antibodies. Both patients experienced rapid viral clearance and resolution of post-COVID symptoms following treatment, suggesting passive anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibody therapy as a potential therapeutic option for persistent infection.

paper_title: Case report: Long-lasting SARS-CoV-2 infection with post-COVID-19 condition in two patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia: The emerging therapeutic role of casirivimab/imdevimab

summary: Case report of two sisters with post-COVID neurocognitive decline and bilateral mesial-temporal hypometabolism documented by brain imaging. This is a descriptive case report with no treatment intervention or control group, focusing on clinical presentation and diagnostic findings rather than treatment evaluation.
paper_authors: Fabrizio Cocciolillo; Daniela Pia Rosaria Chieffo; Alessandro Giordano; Valentina Arcangeli; Ilaria Lazzareschi; Rosa Morello; Giuseppe Zampino; Piero Valentini; Danilo Buonsenso
paper_title: Case report: Post-COVID new-onset neurocognitive decline with bilateral mesial-temporal hypometabolism in two previously healthy sisters

summary: This pharmacovigilance analysis reviews 44 case reports of off-label use of Pelargonium sidoides root extract (EPs 7630) for treatment of COVID-19 and post-COVID-19 syndrome. All 28 cases reporting treatment outcomes showed patient improvement with no unexpected adverse reactions.
paper_authors: Fathi Abdul Malek; Petra Funk
paper_title: Identifying in-market application of Pelargonium root extract EPs 7630 for the treatment of COVID-19: analysis of pharmacovigilance data

summary: This case series of six long COVID patients with persistent dyspnea examines the role of dysfunctional breathing using hyperventilation provocation tests (HVPT). Findings suggest underlying post-COVID respiratory dysregulation but no treatment intervention is tested or evaluated.
paper_authors: Ophélie Ritter; Sofia Noureddine; Lucie Laurent; Pauline Roux; Virginie Westeel; Cindy Barnig
paper_title: Unraveling persistent dyspnea after mild COVID: insights from a case series on hyperventilation provocation tests

summary: Case series of three patients with jaw osteomyelitis during or after COVID-19 infection, including surgical and antibiotic management. While one patient is described as post-COVID, the paper focuses on a specific opportunistic infection complication rather than long COVID syndrome or treatment of long COVID symptoms.
paper_authors: Ana Kvolik Pavić; Vedran Zubčić
paper_title: Osteomyelitis of the Jaw in COVID-19 Patients: A Rare Condition With a High Risk for Severe Complications

summary: This case series describes contactless sensor monitoring of three COVID-19 patients in an assisted living facility over 3 months to track respiratory and behavioral phenotypes during recovery. The study found persistent sleep and motor abnormalities months after viral clearance, demonstrating proof-of-concept for passive monitoring as a research tool, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Guo Zhang; Ipsit V. Vahia; Yingcheng Liu; Yuzhe Yang; Rose May; Hailey V. Cray; William McGrory; Dina Katabi
paper_title: Contactless In-Home Monitoring of the Long-Term Respiratory and Behavioral Phenotypes in Older Adults With COVID-19: A Case Series

summary: A case series of 7 post-COVID patients undergoing a comprehensive rehabilitation program that included whole-body cryostimulation (WBC) as an adjuvant therapy. All patients showed improvements in symptoms including dyspnea, fatigue, pain, and sleep quality, though the isolated contribution of WBC versus other program components (physiotherapy, nutrition, psychology) could not be determined.
paper_authors: Paolo Piterà; Michele Gobbi; Jacopo Maria Fontana; Stefania Cattaldo; Maurizio Massucci; Paolo Capodaglio
paper_title: Whole-Body Cryostimulation: A Rehabilitation Booster in Post-COVID Patients? A Case Series

summary: This paper combines a literature review of 25 studies with a case series examining MRI findings of olfactory bulb reduction in long COVID patients with persistent smell dysfunction. The work presents imaging evidence of structural changes but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Andrea Frosolini; Daniela Parrino; Cristoforo Fabbris; Francesco Fantin; Ingrid Inches; Sara Invitto; Giacomo Spinato; Cosimo Filippis
paper_title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Confirmed Olfactory Bulb Reduction in Long COVID-19: Literature Review and Case Series

summary: Case series of 5 pediatric long COVID patients presenting with neuropsychiatric symptoms (abnormal movements, anxiety, emotional dysregulation) weeks to months post-infection. Patients received pharmacological treatment and cognitive behavioral therapy, with the authors noting a multifactorial etiology involving systemic/brain inflammation and environmental stress.
paper_authors: Rosa Savino; Anna N. Polito; Giulia Arcidiacono; Mariacristina Poliseno; Sergio Lo Caputo
paper_title: Neuropsychiatric Disorders in Pediatric Long COVID-19: A Case Series

summary: A retrospective case series describing three young male patients who developed cardiac arrhythmias (atrial fibrillation, ventricular tachycardia) in the post-acute phase of COVID-19 infection. The paper documents clinical presentations of new-onset rhythm disturbances but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Ciprian Ilie Rosca; Horia Silviu Branea; Abhinav Sharma; Violeta Ariana Nicoras; Claudia Borza; Daniel Florin Lighezan; Stelian I. Morariu; Nilima Rajpal Kundnani
paper_title: Rhythm Disturbances in Post-Acute COVID-19 Syndrome in Young Men without Pre-Existing Known Cardiovascular Disease—A Case Series

summary: Case series describing resolution of chronic gastrointestinal symptoms in two pediatric long COVID patients treated with high-dose oral lactoferrin. The paper reviews lactoferrin's anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory properties and proposes it as a potential treatment strategy for post-COVID gastrointestinal complications.
paper_authors: Rosa Morello; Cristina De Rose; Sara Cardinali; Piero Valentini; Danilo Buonsenso
paper_title: Lactoferrin as Possible Treatment for Chronic Gastrointestinal Symptoms in Children with Long COVID: Case Series and Literature Review

summary: A case series of 23 post-COVID patients with cognitive impairment who received neuroprotective agents (Citicoline, Piracetam, Memantine) and underwent neuropsychological and neuroimaging assessments. After 3 months of treatment, both groups showed positive results on neuropsychological testing, suggesting potential benefit of pro-cognitive agents for cognitive recovery in post-COVID patients.
paper_authors: Milena Dimitrova; Yoanna Marinova; Dancho Dilkov
paper_title: Investigation of Cognitive Impairment in the Course of Post-COVID Syndrome

summary: First study assessing clinical management of severe isolated dysphonia in post-COVID-19 syndrome, examining 6 patients with instrumental laryngeal assessment before and after treatment. Treatment with systemic steroids, hyaluronic acid inhalations, and reflux protective agents resulted in improvement in vocal fold function and patient-reported voice quality.
paper_authors: Joanna Jeleniewska; Ewa Niebudek-Bogusz; Jakub Malinowski; Joanna Morawska; Joanna Miłkowska-Dymanowska; Wioletta Pietruszewska
paper_title: Isolated Severe Dysphonia as a Presentation of Post-COVID-19 Syndrome

summary: Retrospective analysis of 38 critically ill COVID-19 patients admitted to ICU with ARDS, assessing long-term activities of daily living (ADLs) at hospital discharge and one year post-discharge using the Barthel index and Karnofsky Performance Status scales. Patients showed significant functional recovery at one-year follow-up, with complete ADL recovery in most patients, but this is an observational cohort study without an intervention or treatment being tested.
paper_authors: Samuele Ceruti; Andrea Glotta; Maira Biggiogero; Martino Marzano; Giovanni Bona; Marco Previsdomini; Andrea Saporito; Xavier Capdevila
paper_title: Long-Term Evolution of Activities of Daily Life (ADLs) in Critically Ill COVID-19 Patients, a Case Series

summary: This paper describes liver histopathology findings in 10 severe COVID-19 survivors with persistent cholestasis, examining bile duct anomalies and fibrosis patterns. It is a descriptive case series without any treatment intervention or control group, documenting the natural disease course rather than testing a therapeutic approach.
paper_authors: Valéria Borges; Helma Cotrim; Antônio Andrade; Liliana Mendes; Francisco Penna; Marcelo Silva; Frederico Salomão; Luiz Freitas
paper_title: COVID-19-Related Cholangiopathy: Histological Findings

summary: Two case reports of long COVID patients with persistent cough, breathlessness, and fatigue treated with manual lymph drainage (MLD) using the Dr Vodder method over six weekly 45-minute sessions. Both patients showed improvement in respiratory function, oxygen saturation, dyspnea, and fatigue measures by the third treatment, with further gains at three-month follow-up.
paper_authors: Bronwyn Overall; Kaori Langley; Janet Douglass
paper_title: Manual Lymph Drainage for Post-COVID-19 Related Cough, Breathlessness, and Fatigue; Two Case Reports

summary: A case series of 16 post-COVID patients (8 with PCS, 8 with PVS) treated with statins plus ARBs for 6 weeks, with HDL proteome analysis via mass spectrometry and inflammatory markers assessed in endothelial cells. Treatment improved clinical symptoms and reduced inflammatory potential of the HDL proteome, identifying specific protein alterations and metabolic pathways involved in disease pathogenesis.
paper_authors: Karsten Grote; Ann-Christin Schaefer; Muhidien Soufi; Volker Ruppert; Uwe Linne; Aditya Mukund Bhagwat; Witold Szymanski; Johannes Graumann; Yana Gercke; Sümeya Aldudak; Denise Hilfiker-Kleiner; Elisabeth Schieffer; Bernhard Schieffer
paper_title: Targeting the High-Density Lipoprotein Proteome for the Treatment of Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2

summary: This case series presents two patients with long COVID-related vertebral algic syndrome and radiculopathy that worsened after SARS-CoV-2 infection and were resistant to conservative treatment. Both patients underwent spinal surgery with radicular decompression, resulting in significant pain relief and neurological improvement.
paper_authors: Andrej Džubera; Juraj Chochol; Róbert Illéš; Alica Chocholová; Erika Zemková
paper_title: Vertebral Algic Syndrome Treatment in Long COVID—Cases Reports
paper_journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health

summary: This case series describes histopathological and immunohistochemical findings in six long COVID patients with cutaneous neuropathic symptoms, revealing hypertrophy of nerve endings and disturbances in dermal neuronal fibers. While it provides pathological evidence of nerve involvement, it is a descriptive case series without any treatment intervention or comparison group.
paper_authors: Teresa Grieco; Vito Gomes; Alfredo Rossi; Carmen Cantisani; Maria Elisabetta Greco; Giovanni Rossi; Alvise Sernicola; Giovanni Pellacani
paper_title: The Pathological Culprit of Neuropathic Skin Pain in Long COVID-19 Patients: A Case Series

summary: This case series describes clinical management outcomes of new-onset atrial fibrillation in 23 COVID-19 patients evaluated at a tertiary cardiac center after hospital discharge. The focus is on acute COVID-related cardiac complications rather than long COVID, and management did not differ from standard arrhythmia practice.
paper_authors: Marco Schiavone; Fabiola B. Sozzi; Alessio Gasperetti; Cecilia Gobbi; Elisa Gherbesi; Lucia Barbieri; Roberto Arosio; Gianfranco Mitacchione; Filippo Toriello; Andrea Faggiano; Maurizio Viecca; Giovanni B. Forleo; Stefano Carugo
paper_title: Clinical Management of New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation in COVID-19 Patients Referred to a Tertiary Cardiac Arrhythmia Center after Hospital Discharge

summary: Preliminary case study of 3 long-COVID patients using telemonitoring devices to track vital signs (respiratory rate, heart rate, oxygen saturation, temperature) over 10-day periods. The study presents initial findings of detected cardiorespiratory abnormalities but lacks a complete trial design with structured outcomes and control group.

paper_title: Telemonitoring in Long-COVID Patients—Preliminary Findings
paper_journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health

summary: This retrospective case series describes clinicopathologic features of Acute Fibrinous and Organizing Pneumonia (AFOP) nodules in post-COVID-19 patients, finding a 55% association with prior COVID-19 infection. The study focuses on diagnostic imaging and histopathological characterization to distinguish these nodules from malignancy, not on testing or evaluating any treatment intervention.

paper_title: Clinicopathologic Features of Isolated AFOP Nodules Radiologically Mimicking Malignancy in Post COVID-19 Patients: A Case Series Study

summary: A retrospective case series of three long COVID patients presenting with myocarditis-related heart failure of varying severity. All three patients showed cardiac function improvement with optimal medical treatment, demonstrating that myocarditis is a treatable but serious complication of long COVID.
paper_authors: Justyna Rohun; Karolina Dorniak; Anna Faran; Anna Kochańska; Dariusz Zacharek; Ludmiła Daniłowicz-Szymanowicz
paper_title: Long COVID-19 Myocarditis and Various Heart Failure Presentations: A Case Series
paper_journal: Journal of Cardiovascular Development and Disease

summary: This case series evaluates cardiac and pulmonary involvement in 29 patients recovered from COVID-19 pneumonia using echocardiography, lung ultrasound, and ECG. The study documents persistent cardiopulmonary abnormalities but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
paper_authors: Jacopo Marazzato; Roberto De Ponti; Paolo Verdecchia; Sergio Masnaghetti; Dina Visca; Antonio Spanevello; Monica Trapasso; Martina Zappa; Antonella Mancinelli; Fabio Angeli
paper_title: Combined Use of Electrocardiography and Ultrasound to Detect Cardiac and Pulmonary Involvement after Recovery from COVID-19 Pneumonia: A Case Series
paper_journal: Journal of Cardiovascular Development and Disease

summary: Retrospective analysis of 12 post-acute COVID-19 patients in a rehabilitation unit evaluating neuropsychological patterns and their correlation with functional outcomes. Study found subclinical cognitive alterations (dysexecutive disorders) in 4% of recovering patients, with correlations between verbal memory/frontal functions and degree of functional impairment.
paper_authors: Davide Antonio Di Pietro; Laura Comini; Lidia Gazzi; Alberto Luisa; Michele Vitacca
paper_title: Neuropsychological Pattern in a Series of Post-Acute COVID-19 Patients in a Rehabilitation Unit: Retrospective Analysis and Correlation with Functional Outcomes
paper_journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health

summary: Case report of two relatives (age 14 and mother) presenting with spontaneous pneumomediastinum, thymic hyperplasia, myasthenic-like symptoms, and long COVID features following COVID-19 infection/vaccination. No treatment intervention evaluated; primarily a clinical observation with literature review.
paper_authors: Barbara Brogna; Mariagrazia Nunziata; Luigi Urciuoli; Annamaria Romano; Antonietta Laporta; Claudia Brogna
paper_title: Spontaneous Pneumomediastinum in COVID-19 and Myasthenic-like Symptom Complications in Two Relatives: A Coincidence or Spike Toxicity with Thymic Response in Predisposed Individuals? Two Clinical Cases with a Comprehensive Literature Review

summary: Case series of three autism spectrum disorder patients who developed or experienced worsening neuropsychiatric symptoms following COVID-19 infection and long COVID. Reports immune activation markers (inflammatory and counter-regulatory cytokines) in peripheral blood monocytes and describes treatment challenges in managing post-COVID neuropsychiatric symptoms in ASD populations.
paper_authors: Harumi Jyonouchi; Lee Geng; Daniel A. Rossignol; Richard E. Frye
paper_title: Long COVID Syndrome Presenting as Neuropsychiatric Exacerbations in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Insights for Treatment

summary: This case series describes 19 post-COVID and post-vaccination syndrome patients with undifferentiated arthritis and suspected small fiber neuropathy, comparing clinical and pathological features in 8 skin-biopsy-confirmed neuropathy cases versus 10 neuropathy-negative controls. Over 12 months of follow-up, treated patients showed significant improvements in joint inflammation, fatigue, motor impairment, and neurological symptoms, though skin biopsy findings did not fully normalize.

paper_title: Small Fiber Neuropathy Associated with Post-COVID-19 and Post-COVID-19 Vaccination Arthritis: A Rare Post-Infective Syndrome or a New-Onset Disease?

summary: This paper presents two clinical case reports of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) with severe manifestations following COVID-19 exposure, focusing on diagnostic and clinical management challenges. It describes inflammatory involvement across gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, nervous, and respiratory systems but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.
paper_authors: Elena Vasichkina; Olga Kofeynikova; Svetlana Fetisova; Anastasia Y. Starshinova; Elizaveta Sheyanova; Tatiana Vershinina; Anton Ryzhkov; Aleksey Skripnik; Daria Alekseeva; Elizaveta Nechaeva; Anzhela Glushkova; Dmitry Kudlay; Tatiana Pervunina; Anna Starshinova
paper_title: Severe Course of COVID-19 and Long-COVID-19 in Children: Difficulties in Diagnosis

paper_authors: Kristina Bieksiene; Jurgita Zaveckiene; Kestutis Malakauskas; Neringa Vaguliene; Marius Zemaitis; Skaidrius Miliauskas
paper_title: Post COVID-19 Organizing Pneumonia: The Right Time to Interfere

summary: Case series of 10 patients with avascular necrosis and bone degeneration occurring immediately after acute COVID-19 infection. Paper describes clinical observations and steroid treatment response but is focused on acute infection complications, not persistent long COVID symptoms.

paper_title: Avascular Necrosis Bone Complication after Active COVID-19 Infection: Preliminary Results

summary: Case series of two immunocompromised patients with prolonged COVID-19 infection treated with convalescent plasma (CP). Both patients showed rapid clinical and virological recovery with symptom resolution after CP administration.

paper_title: Efficacy of Convalescent Plasma to Treat Long-Standing COVID-19 in Patients with B-Cell Depletion

summary: Two case presentations of paroxysmal finger hematoma (Achenbach's syndrome) occurring after COVID-19 recovery, hypothesizing SARS-CoV-2 as a triggering factor in microvascular pathology. paper_title: Paroxysmal Finger Hematoma—A Probable Vascular Disorder in Post-COVID-19 Condition: Two Clinical Case Presentations

summary: Case series of four patients who developed hemorrhagic cardiac tamponade in the recovery phase following COVID-19, with onset weeks to months after acute infection. Three cases required pericardiocentesis and anti-inflammatory treatment, with three patients discharged and one fatal outcome; histopathology showed fibrous pericarditis with inflammatory infiltrate.

paper_title: Hemorrhagic Cardiac Tamponade—An Unusual Threat in the COVID-19 Recovery Phase

summary: Case report of two immunocompromised transplant recipients with chronic COVID-19 treated with remdesivir, documenting transient RNA-dependent RNA polymerase mutations during treatment. The study provides evidence of potential remdesivir resistance development and suggests monitoring for viral resistance mutations in vulnerable populations receiving prolonged antiviral therapy.

paper_title: Transient SARS-CoV-2 RNA-Dependent RNA Polymerase Mutations after Remdesivir Treatment for Chronic COVID-19 in Two Transplant Recipients: Case Report and Intra-Host Viral Genomic Investigation

summary: An uncontrolled case series evaluating hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) in 5 long COVID patients with various comorbidities, assessing changes in oxidative stress and inflammation biomarkers via saliva and urine samples. Results showed reduced ROS production, lipid peroxidation, DNA damage, and inflammation markers post-treatment, particularly in athletes.

paper_title: Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy Counters Oxidative Stress/Inflammation-Driven Symptoms in Long COVID-19 Patients: Preliminary Outcomes

summary: A case series of 12 long COVID patients undergoing 12-week synchronous telerehabilitation combining therapeutic education, physical, and respiratory rehabilitation. The intervention resulted in significant improvements in fatigue, aerobic capacity, and limb/respiratory strength, though dyspnea showed no improvement.
paper_authors: Beatriz Carpallo-Porcar; Esther del Corral Beamonte; Carolina Jiménez-Sánchez; Paula Córdova-Alegre; Natalia Brandín-de la Cruz; Sandra Calvo
paper_title: Multimodal Telerehabilitation in Post COVID-19 Condition Recovery: A Series of 12 Cases

Rather than testing a treatment, it identifies a disease pattern and hypothesizes that local connective tissue damage in hypermobile patients, triggered by COVID-19, may lead to fibromyalgia syndrome.

paper_title: New Clinical Phenotype of the Post-Covid Syndrome: Fibromyalgia and Joint Hypermobility Condition

summary: Retrospective case series of 15 patients with post-COVID Guillain-Barré syndrome at a Croatian hospital in 2021, examining clinical presentation and treatment outcomes. Treatment with IVIG and/or plasma exchange resulted in improvement in 13 of 15 patients, with most patients having recovered from the acute COVID-19 infection prior to GBS onset.
paper_authors: Niko Dunkić; Marija Nazlić; Valerija Dunkić; Ivica Bilić
paper_title: Analysis of Post-COVID-19 Guillain–Barré Syndrome over a Period of One Year in the University Hospital of Split (Croatia)

summary: This paper studies anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgA antibody responses in 88 COVID-19 patients during acute infection and early recovery (4-41 days post-infection). While it mentions one patient with persistent symptoms seven months post-infection, the paper is primarily an immunological investigation of acute-phase IgA responses and does not study long COVID as its main focus or test any interventions for long COVID patients.
